member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.NpcType.Crablet
member.summary: The Crablet identity bit, which can also be included in an NPC’s filter for noticing other NPCs.

remarks.para: Value 32. In a TriggerRefProxy.npcType field this labels the character for identity-based threat scoring. In BehaviourBaseNav.agroOnNpcType it allows a candidate carrying this single bit through the inspected trigger-entry filter. The observer must also satisfy its usual collider, target and brain conditions; passing the filter is not an immediate attack command.

Assigning this identity does not spawn that NPC or replace the character’s model, weapons or behaviour. Threat scoring compares the stored identity, and existing threat can still be increased separately.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.TriggerType.Npc
member.summary: Enables NPC trigger dispatch and access to the brain cached from the proxy’s root GameObject.

remarks.para: Value 2. TriggerRefProxy.Start finds AIBrain on root itself and replaces its cache; aiManager exposes that cache only for this category. Start is Unity’s startup callback, a routine called before the first frame update. Supply a valid root with the NPC’s brain before startup; the enum does not create one.

The inspected GenGameControl_Trigger enter/exit handlers invoke their NPC events and proxy callbacks when ignoreEnemies is false. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Those notifications happen before disableOnTrigger turns off the trigger collider.

The inspected AI sensor paths use the cached brain to reject a dead target and validate its current pooled spawn identity. The behaviour’s trigger-entry path also checks npcType against its permitted mask. A category match does not guarantee an attack.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.TriggerType.Player
member.summary: Routes the proxy through the inspected player-trigger events and skips NPC brain validation in the sampled sensor entry path.

remarks.para: Value 0. GenGameControl_Trigger invokes its player enter/exit event for this category, then disables the trigger collider if disableOnTrigger is true. TriggerRefProxy.aiManager returns null and Start does not look for an NPC brain.

BehaviourBaseNav.OnTriggerEnter bypasses the NPC identity-mask test for this category, and SubBehaviourSensors.AddThreat does not perform its non-Player brain/death check. Other required target references and behaviour conditions still apply.
This label does not create a player rig or make an object controllable. Configure the proxy’s body references for the code that will read them.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.TriggerType.Proxy
member.summary: Uses category 1, for which the inspected player/NPC trigger dispatcher raises neither category’s enter/exit events.

remarks.para: TriggerRefProxy.Start does not look for a brain for this category, and aiManager returns null even if its private cache contains one. The enum’s generic-sounding name does not establish a universal AI-target fallback.

The inspected SubBehaviourSensors.AddThreat path expects a usable AI brain for every non-Player target. Because this category’s getter returns null, feeding it into that path can reach a failure rather than safely becoming an ordinary target. Use this label only with consumers that explicitly support it; the audited player/NPC dispatcher and sensor path do not provide that support.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GesturePose.Fist
member.summary: Reports the closed-fist pattern: all four fingers and the thumb are curled in the gesture check performed by .

remarks.para: These are the rules used when OpenController checks its already processed finger inputs. A curl input is a unitless amount of bend: 0 is the straight end of the scale and 1 is the curled end. The inputs can come from controller buttons and grip or from hand tracking, and some are smoothed over time. This label reports the detected pattern; choosing the enum value does not move the hand.

For this pattern, every processed curl input must be greater than 0.5. They do not have to reach 1. For example, index, middle, ring, little finger and thumb inputs of 0.8 all qualify. The hand can face any direction; the finger-pattern check does not require a particular pointing direction.

OpenController normally reuses its last gesture result until its next permitted check, set to 0.2 seconds after a completed check. This uses time unaffected by game slow motion. A new check happens on a later GetGesturePose call once that time has arrived; it is not a check scheduled for an exact rendered frame. Passing forceUpdate as true bypasses that wait but still uses the finger inputs already processed by controller updates. A finger pattern that matches none of the gesture rules can leave the previous label in place. The base BaseController implementation simply returns its stored label, so other controller implementations can behave differently.

A finger pattern that matches none of the gesture rules can leave the previous label in place. The base BaseController implementation simply returns its stored label, so other controller implementations can behave differently.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GesturePose.ThumbsDown
member.summary: Reports the thumb-out, fingers-curled pattern when the controller’s up direction is horizontal or points downward, in .

remarks.para: These are the rules used when OpenController checks its already processed finger inputs. A curl input is a unitless amount of bend: 0 is the straight end of the scale and 1 is the curled end. The inputs can come from controller buttons and grip or from hand tracking, and some are smoothed over time. This label reports the detected pattern; choosing the enum value does not move the hand.

The processed thumb curl must be 0.5 or less, while index, middle, ring and little-finger curls must each be greater than 0.5. The game then compares the controller object’s up direction, rotated into world space, with world up, the positive Y direction. A zero or negative upward component selects ThumbsDown; exactly horizontal therefore counts as down. For example, thumb 0.2, all four fingers 0.8, and a controller up direction tilted below horizontal qualify. This orientation test follows the controller object’s up axis rather than directly measuring the real thumb’s direction.

OpenController normally reuses its last gesture result until its next permitted check, set to 0.2 seconds after a completed check. This uses time unaffected by game slow motion. A new check happens on a later GetGesturePose call once that time has arrived; it is not a check scheduled for an exact rendered frame. Passing forceUpdate as true bypasses that wait but still uses the finger inputs already processed by controller updates. A finger pattern that matches none of the gesture rules can leave the previous label in place. The base BaseController implementation simply returns its stored label, so other controller implementations can behave differently.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.Corners.NegativeXNegativeYNegativeZ
member.summary: Allows the box’s left, lower, back corner region when included in BoxGrip.enabledCorners.

remarks.para: The corner is on the −X, −Y and −Z sides of the referenced BoxCollider’s center, measured along that box’s own rotated axes. These directions follow the box when it turns; they do not mean world left/right, height or north/south.

Combine this flag with other Corners values using | to allow more than one corner. BoxGrip.canBeCornerGrabbed must also be true. This permits the corner-grab region and its configured hand pose; it does not resize the box or force a held hand onto the exact vertex.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.Edges.NegativeXNegativeY
member.summary: Allows edge-style grabs where the negative X and negative Y faces meet, along the box’s Z direction.

remarks.para: Include this flag in BoxGrip.enabledEdges and enable canBeEdgeGrabbed. The axis signs are relative to the box collider’s center and orientation, so this edge turns with the box; they are not fixed world directions. The hand must still pass the zone checks. An accepted edge grab uses edgeHandPose, the saved hand-and-finger pose, and edgeHandPoseRadius, the radius in metres used to place the hand and choose its curl around the edge.

For an illustrative box of local size (1, 0.6, 0.4) at scale 1, this geometric edge has X = -0.5, Y = -0.3 meters relative to the center, with Z running from -0.2 to 0.2. These locate the edge, not a guarantee that every point on it accepts a hand.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.ButtonMode.ClickDown
member.summary: Produces a sensor-value pulse of 1 when a press is recognized, then normally returns to 0 on the following sensor read.

remarks.para: A press requires the adjusted travel reading to exceed 0.9 after release has rearmed the button. Release requires a reading below 0.1. The reading scales the current end-to-end joint travel to a fraction, multiplies it by 1.04, subtracts 0.02, then restricts it to 0 through 1. The press and release boundaries are therefore about 88.46% and 11.54% of current travel; equality does not trigger either transition.

Recognized pressing and releasing request their respective sounds. Initialization samples the starting state but returns 0 without requesting sounds. The pulse is a sampled number, not a separate event or a promise of exactly one rendered frame; its duration depends on the next sensor read. A connected CircuitSocket input can multiply this number before it becomes the final output.

The button's signed displacement is measured in meters along the Servo's configured joint-X direction. The joint is the physics connection controlling that movement; its current linear limit is the allowed travel in each direction from center, so the full travel is twice that limit. CircuitSocket samples during Unity's FixedUpdate physics step only while its Rigidbody (the physics-body component) is awake and the Servo has a live joint. If the body sleeps or the joint is absent, later reads pause; UpdateCircuit uses Time.fixedTime, seconds on Unity's physics clock.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.ButtonMode.ClickUp
member.summary: Produces a sensor-value pulse of 1 when a recognized press is released, then normally returns to 0 on the following sensor read.

remarks.para: The button first arms this release by reaching an adjusted travel reading above 0.9. It produces the pulse when that reading later falls below 0.1. The reading scales current end-to-end joint travel to a fraction, multiplies it by 1.04, subtracts 0.02, and restricts it to 0 through 1. These boundaries correspond to about 88.46% and 11.54% of current travel; equality preserves the state.

Pressing and releasing request their respective sounds even though the pulse occurs on release. Initialization returns 0 without requesting sounds. Pulse duration depends on later sensor reads, so it is not guaranteed to last exactly one rendered frame. A connected CircuitSocket input can multiply the sensor number before it becomes the final output.

The button's signed displacement is measured in meters along the Servo's configured joint-X direction. The joint is the physics connection controlling that movement; its current linear limit is the allowed travel in each direction from center, so the full travel is twice that limit. CircuitSocket samples during Unity's FixedUpdate physics step only while its Rigidbody (the physics-body component) is awake and the Servo has a live joint. If the body sleeps or the joint is absent, later reads pause; UpdateCircuit uses Time.fixedTime, seconds on Unity's physics clock.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.ButtonMode.ContinuousDown
member.summary: Reports sensor value 1 after a recognized press and keeps it until a recognized release returns it to 0.

remarks.para: Pressing requires an adjusted travel reading above 0.9, and releasing requires one below 0.1. Between those boundaries the remembered state stays unchanged, including at equality. The reading scales current end-to-end joint travel to a fraction, applies a 1.04 multiplier and a 0.02 subtraction, and is restricted to 0 through 1. The boundaries are about 88.46% and 11.54% of current travel.

Recognized transitions request press/release sounds; initialization sets the starting state without requesting them. This is a sensor number: a connected CircuitSocket input can multiply it before the final circuit output is published.

The button's signed displacement is measured in meters along the Servo's configured joint-X direction. The joint is the physics connection controlling that movement; its current linear limit is the allowed travel in each direction from center, so the full travel is twice that limit. CircuitSocket samples during Unity's FixedUpdate physics step only while its Rigidbody (the physics-body component) is awake and the Servo has a live joint. If the body sleeps or the joint is absent, later reads pause; UpdateCircuit uses Time.fixedTime, seconds on Unity's physics clock.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.ButtonMode.ContinuousFloat
member.summary: Reports the adjusted button travel as a continuous sensor value from 0 to 1, without click latches or press/release sounds.

remarks.para: The value is clamp(1.04 × (x + L) / (2 × L) − 0.02, 0, 1). Here x is the signed button displacement in meters along the Servo's joint X direction, and L is the current joint linear limit in meters, the allowed travel each way from its center. A joint is the physics connection controlling the button's motion. Clamp means restricting the result to 0 through 1; the multiplier and bias have no units. The limit must be nonzero.

The negative travel end gives 0, the center gives 0.5, and the positive end gives 1. This is adjusted travel rather than an unchanged raw analog value. It bypasses press/release thresholds and sounds in both initialization and later sensor reads. A connected CircuitSocket input can multiply it before it becomes the final output.

CircuitSocket reads this value during Unity FixedUpdate, its physics-step callback, only while its Rigidbody (physics-body component) is awake and the Servo has a live joint. A sleeping body or missing joint pauses later reads; UpdateCircuit uses Time.fixedTime in seconds on Unity’s physics clock.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.ButtonMode.Toggle
member.summary: Switches the stored sensor value between 0 and 1 on successive armed presses, and changes the button's physical travel to match.

remarks.para: A press above the adjusted reading of 0.9 flips the on/off latch and disarms further toggles. A release below 0.1 rearms the next press while retaining the output. The adjusted reading scales current end-to-end joint travel to a fraction, multiplies by 1.04, subtracts 0.02 and restricts it to 0 through 1. The boundaries are about 88.46% and 11.54% of the currently allowed travel; equality does not switch or rearm.

Switching on halves the physics joint's linearLimit (the allowed travel in each direction from center) and targetPosition (the position the joint requests), then shifts connectedAnchor, the joint's attachment point on the connected body, along the Servo's calibrated joint-X direction by half the current limit. Switching off reverses those changes. A joint is the physics connection controlling motion between physical objects, so this mode changes the button's mechanics as well as remembering an output.

Both switching on and switching off request the press sound; releasing requests the release sound. The constructor begins armed, and initialization can apply a qualifying toggle without requesting sound. A connected CircuitSocket input can multiply the latched sensor value before it becomes the final output.

The button's signed displacement is measured in meters along the Servo's configured joint-X direction. The joint is the physics connection controlling that movement; its current linear limit is the allowed travel in each direction from center, so the full travel is twice that limit. CircuitSocket samples during Unity's FixedUpdate physics step only while its Rigidbody (the physics-body component) is awake and the Servo has a live joint. If the body sleeps or the joint is absent, later reads pause; UpdateCircuit uses Time.fixedTime, seconds on Unity's physics clock.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.BallSocket
member.summary: Connects the selected bodies at one pivot while letting them turn freely around that pivot.

remarks.para: Value 2. This creates a physics joint, a connection that the physics simulation enforces between objects. It locks movement of the two joint attachment points along all three directions, but leaves turning around all three directions free. For example, a hanging object can swing and twist around its attachment.

The tool chooses one shared pivot rather than preserving a gap between the two clicked points. With two movable bodies it uses the second picked point as the pivot. If the second picked endpoint has no movable body, the tool swaps endpoint order: that fixed point supplies the world pivot, and the first movable body's anchor is converted to its local coordinates, meaning relative to that body. If the first picked endpoint has no movable body, there is no swap; the second movable body's picked point supplies the pivot, and the first fixed click does not set it. A fixed surface position is in world coordinates, meaning the shared scene coordinates.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.Elastic
member.summary: Connects the selected attachment points with a springy distance limit that pulls back when stretched.

remarks.para: Value 3. This creates a physics joint, a connection enforced by the physics simulation. It limits movement along all three directions, lets the bodies turn freely, and gives the distance limit a spring. Stretching beyond the limit makes the spring pull back; damping, resistance to motion, reduces bouncing.

At creation the tool measures d, the distance between the two selected attachment points in world coordinates, the shared scene coordinates. It sets the limit to max(0, d - 0.25): subtract 0.25 and use zero if the result is negative. Distances use Unity world units, normally metres. Points 2 metres apart therefore give a 1.75 metre spring limit; points 0.1 metres apart give a zero limit. This number is captured when the connection is created, rather than recalculated from the later separation.

The spring strength is 39.24 times m, where m is the mass in kilograms of the Rigidbody on the body that receives the joint. A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object simulated mass and movement. The resulting spring strength is in newtons per metre: each extra metre of stretch produces that much restoring force before the physics solver resolves the motion. The damping coefficient is 0.5 newton-seconds per metre. For a 1 kilogram body, the spring strength is 39.24 newtons per metre. Mass is sampled during joint creation.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.EntagleVelocity
member.summary: Connects the bodies with damped forces that resist their moving at different velocities.

remarks.para: Value 5. Keep the spelling EntagleVelocity when using this enum value in code. Velocity means both movement speed and direction. A physics joint, a connection enforced by the physics simulation, applies forces along its three movement directions to reduce relative velocity. These directions belong to the joint attached to the body, rather than fixed world directions. Its target relative velocity is zero metres per second.

All movement and rotation axes remain free. The connection uses damping, resistance to relative movement, without a position spring pulling the attachment points back together. The bodies can therefore remain separated and can turn independently. For example, dragging one connected crate encourages the other to travel with it, even though they are some distance apart.

At creation the tool samples m, the mass in kilograms of the Rigidbody on the body that receives the joint. A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object simulated mass and movement. For each movement direction it sets the damping coefficient to 200 times m in newton-seconds per metre and the maximum force to 50 times m in newtons. A 1 kilogram body therefore gets a damping coefficient of 200 newton-seconds per metre and a force cap of 50 newtons per direction. These are force settings, so other forces and the force cap can leave some relative movement. They do not promise instantly equal velocities. The sampled mass sets the initial values.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.EntangleRotation
member.summary: Keeps the bodies at the same relative orientation while leaving their movement unrestricted by the joint.

remarks.para: Value 4. This creates a physics joint, a connection enforced by the physics simulation. It locks turning around all three directions and leaves movement along all three directions free. Relative orientation means how one body is turned compared with the other body. The joint keeps the relative orientation captured when it is created; the two bodies can start facing different directions.

For example, if two separate props are turned a quarter-turn apart when connected, that difference is kept when one turns. Their attachment points can still move apart because this mode adds no distance limit or movement drive. When connected to a fixed surface instead of another movable body, the rotation is held relative to the world, meaning the shared scene coordinates.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.Remove
member.summary: Deletes one tracked connection selected on the first object hit by the tool.

remarks.para: Value 6. A tracked connection is a connection made by the Constrainer and recorded by its ConstraintTracker components. Pressing the tool selects the first hit object. Releasing in this mode chooses a tracker on that object and requests deletion of that connection, its visible connecting line, its attachment marker objects, and the two trackers that describe its ends.

If the object has several trackers, the tool chooses one using the direction in which its first firing point is aimed and the positions of the attachment markers. It does not delete every connection on that object in one use. An object with no tracker supplies no connection to remove. Holding in this mode does not select a second endpoint, so this is a single-object removal operation.

For example, a crate with two Constrainer connections needs separate removal operations to remove both. Deletion is requested through Unity object destruction; it is not a guarantee that every object has already disappeared at the exact moment the button is released.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.Tether
member.summary: Connects the selected attachment points with a distance limit that acts like a rope.

remarks.para: Value 0. This creates a physics joint, a connection enforced by the physics simulation. It limits movement along all three directions and leaves all turning directions free. The limit is the distance between the selected attachment points when the connection is created, measured in Unity world units, normally metres.

An attachment point is stored relative to its own movable body, so it follows that body. An endpoint on a fixed surface uses world coordinates, the shared scene coordinates. For example, endpoints initially 2 metres apart produce a 2 metre limit: they can come closer, while the joint resists separation beyond that limit. This mode has no spring at the limit. The stored limit is set at creation, rather than following the distance as the bodies move.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.ConstraintMode.Weld
member.summary: Locks the bodies together so they keep their relative position and orientation.

remarks.para: Value 1. This creates a physics joint, a connection enforced by the physics simulation, with movement and turning locked along all three directions. The joint captures how the bodies are placed and turned when connected. Their relative orientation means how one is turned compared with the other, so welding does not require them to face the same direction.

For example, welding a handle to a crate makes the handle move and turn with the crate while keeping their arrangement. With two movable bodies, the tool uses the second picked point as one shared joint location and converts that location into each movable body’s local coordinates, meaning relative to that body. With a bodyless or fixed endpoint, the builder receives only the movable body's selected point, converts it to world coordinates, and uses that location as the joint anchor. The movable point is held at its world position when the joint is created; the fixed endpoint's click does not determine the anchor.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.Blunt
member.summary: Classifies a hit as damage from a blunt impact, such as a club striking a target.

remarks.para: Its value is 2, a unitless flag: one on/off bit identifying this category. It describes the kind of hit; the attack’s separate damage value supplies the amount.

GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks. If its configured attack-type filter includes Blunt, an incoming hit containing this flag triggers its registered event actions and passes the hit’s damage value to them. For example, a filter set to Blunt accepts a hit classified as Blunt.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.Fire
member.summary: Classifies a hit as fire damage.

remarks.para: Its value is 8, a unitless flag: one on/off bit identifying this category. It describes the kind of hit; the attack’s separate damage value supplies the amount.

GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks. If its configured attack-type filter includes Fire, an incoming hit containing this flag triggers its registered event actions and passes the hit’s damage value to them. For example, a filter set to Fire accepts a hit classified as Fire.
Assigning this category describes the hit. Game code still has to apply the damage and create any flame effect; the flag itself is stored data.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.None
member.summary: Marks a hit with the None category, whose numeric value is 64 rather than zero.

remarks.para: This is a unitless flag with its own on/off bit. It is distinct from value 0, which has no bits set. For example, GenericAttackReceiver, a component that responds to incoming attacks, accepts a None hit when its configured filter includes 64. A filter of 0 accepts no hit in that receiver.

The category does not automatically make the hit’s separate damage amount zero. GenericAttackReceiver passes that amount to its registered event actions when the filter matches. Enemy_Health.OnReceivedDamage can also process the damage for this category after its normal checks allow the hit.
When a new ProjectileData asset is created, its AttackType field initially receives None. Saved asset settings can replace that initial value before the projectile uses it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.Piercing
member.summary: Classifies a hit as piercing damage, such as a projectile puncture.

remarks.para: Its value is 1, a unitless flag: one on/off bit identifying this category. It describes the kind of hit; the attack’s separate damage value supplies the amount.

GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks. If its configured attack-type filter includes Piercing, an incoming hit containing this flag triggers its registered event actions and passes the hit’s damage value to them. For example, a filter set to Piercing accepts a hit classified as Piercing.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.Slicing
member.summary: Classifies a hit as slicing damage from a cutting edge.

remarks.para: Its value is 16, a unitless flag: one on/off bit identifying this category. It describes the kind of hit; the attack’s separate damage value supplies the amount.

GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks. If its configured attack-type filter includes Slicing, an incoming hit containing this flag triggers its registered event actions and passes the hit’s damage value to them. For example, a filter set to Slicing accepts a hit classified as Slicing.

A GenericAttackReceiver filter combining Slicing and Stabbing has value 48 and accepts either category. Other receiving components can interpret combinations differently, so choose the filter for the component handling the hit.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType.Stabbing

remarks.para: Its value is 32, a unitless flag: one on/off bit identifying this category. It describes the kind of hit; the attack’s separate damage value supplies the amount.

GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks. If its configured attack-type filter includes Stabbing, an incoming hit containing this flag triggers its registered event actions and passes the hit’s damage value to them. For example, a filter set to Stabbing accepts a hit classified as Stabbing.

A GenericAttackReceiver filter combining Slicing and Stabbing has value 48 and accepts either category. Other receiving components can interpret combinations differently, so choose the filter for the component handling the hit.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Weight.HEAVY
member.summary: Identifies the heaviest weight category, with category code 2.

remarks.para: This is a category label, not a measurement: 2 is not a mass in kilograms, a force, or a multiplier. Selecting this value alone does not change an object’s physics mass.

For example, compare a Weight setting with Weight.HEAVY to recognize this category. The enum does not supply a numeric mass range for it; any rule that handles this category belongs to the code reading the setting.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.GripState.IDELING
member.summary: Reports the idle stage before a distant hand targets the object, or after force-pull cleanup.

remarks.para: OnFarHandHoverEnd sets this state when the object is not already attached to a hand. CancelPull and normal pull completion also restore it while cleaning up the temporary joint, a physics connection between the hand and object bodies, and saved pulling-hand references.
This is interaction status, not the component’s enabled flag. An enabled grip can be idle and ready for a new distant-hand selection. The identifier is spelled IDELING in the API.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.GripState.LONGHOVERING
member.summary: Reports that a distant hand has begun targeting an unattached object that can be force-pulled.

remarks.para: Far hover means the hand is selecting the object from a distance rather than touching its grip. OnFarHandHoverBegin writes this state when the host is not already attached to a hand. OnFarHandHoverUpdate checks the controller inputs that can start the pull coroutine, an action sequence that continues over several frames or physics steps.

There is no hover-duration timer in this state transition. The name does not by itself mean the hand waited long enough to arm a separate prompt. Ending the far hover returns to IDELING when the host remains unattached.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.GripState.PULLING
member.summary: Reports that the force-pull coroutine is drawing the object toward the selected hand.

remarks.para: CoPull is a coroutine, an action sequence continuing over several frames or physics steps. It enters this state, saves the receiving hand and locks that hand’s hover target to the grip. It creates a temporary ConfigurableJoint connecting the hand-side physics body to the object’s Rigidbody and updates pulling motion during the physics steps. A joint is a physics connection between two bodies.

This stage can continue while the object reaches the hand and starts attaching. It is not a signal that the object has already been grabbed. Normal completion or cancellation restores IDELING and removes the temporary pull connection.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.FIRE
member.summary: Is not mapped to a firing clip by the audited Gun.SetAnimationState implementation.

remarks.para: That method stores this enum value as animationState but its clip-selection switch has no FIRE case. Its completion coroutine also has no firing action for this value. Choose a supported slide sequence to animate the action; Fire performs the shot readiness checks and shot effects.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.FIRERETURN
member.summary: Is not mapped to a return clip by the audited Gun.SetAnimationState implementation.

remarks.para: The method stores this value as animationState but has no clip-selection case for it, and the checked completion coroutine has no associated slide-return action. SLIDERETURN is the supported forward-return sequence used by the normal gun cycle.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.NEUTRAL
member.summary: Displays the Animator's Neutral clip, used for the gun's resting pose.

remarks.para: Gun.SetAnimationState selects this clip on layer 0. Pool initialization displays it at the clip's end, normalized position 1; position 0 is the beginning. Reaching its endpoint records animation completion but does not perform a slide-pull or slide-return action. Selecting an animation is separate from directly changing the logical slide state. SetAnimationState displays a clip position; PlayAnimationState advances a timed sequence.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.NONE
member.summary: Stores an empty animation label without selecting another Animator clip.

remarks.para: Gun.SetAnimationState still writes animationState, but has no clip-selection branch for NONE. This value also marks that no completion endpoint is currently recorded. It does not itself hide the gun, clear ammunition or stop the Animator.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDELOCKED
member.summary: Displays the SlideLocked clip toward its locked-open visual pose.

remarks.para: Timed playback uses slideLockDuration in seconds. Selecting this animation alone does not set Gun.slideState to LOCKED or check whether the magazine is empty. Gun.SlideLocked sets LOCKED before starting the animation; its callers make the relevant empty-magazine checks. Completion of this clip does not automatically release the slide.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDELOCKEDREVERSED
member.summary: Runs the SlideLocked clip backward toward its beginning, normalized position 0; position 1 is its end.

remarks.para: PlayAnimationState uses slideLockDuration, the full lock-animation duration in seconds of game time, for the timed reverse sequence. SetAnimationState treats progress at or below 0 as its completed endpoint. The audited completion handler has no logical slide-unlock action for this value, so reversing the visual does not itself release the slide.

For a sequence starting partway through, remaining duration is (1 minus startPerc) times that full duration; startPerc is the unitless starting fraction of the sequence. Time advances in seconds of game time across frames.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDEPULL
member.summary: Moves through the SlidePull clip toward the rearward-stroke endpoint.

remarks.para: Normalized clip position is a unitless fraction: 0 is the clip beginning and 1 is its end. At normalized progress 1 or above, the gun schedules full-pull completion for the end of the frame. That completion cocks the hammer (makes it ready to strike), ejects the old chamber contents, tries to load the next round, and chooses a return or empty-slide lock.

Timed playback uses fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds of game time, times pullAnimationPerc, its independent unitless pull-stage multiplier. Their product is the full pull-stage duration. fireCurve receives elapsed sequence time divided by the remaining sequence duration, a unitless time fraction, and its output supplies a progress blend toward the clip endpoint. Manual override can display the same clip directly from the saved hand-pull fraction: 0 means unpulled and fully forward; 1 means fully pulled back.

returnAnimationPerc is the independent unitless return-stage multiplier. The pull and return multipliers are independent and need not sum to 1. The configured full pull-stage and return-stage durations add to fireDuration times (pullAnimationPerc plus returnAnimationPerc), so their sum need not equal the base firing period. This sum is a duration budget, not a promise of exact elapsed cycle time: sampling across frames, carried excess time and deferred endpoint work affect the actual timing.

For a sequence starting partway through, remaining duration is (1 minus startPerc) times that full duration; startPerc is the unitless starting fraction of the sequence. Time advances in seconds of game time across frames.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDEPULLREVERSED
member.summary: Runs the SlidePull clip backward when a partial pull is released before completing its rearward stroke.

remarks.para: Timed playback uses fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds of game time, times returnAnimationPerc, its independent unitless return-stage multiplier, for this full reverse stage. returnCurve receives elapsed sequence time divided by the remaining sequence duration and controls the progress blend toward the reversed endpoint. Normalized clip position is a unitless fraction: 0 is the clip beginning and 1 is its end. It finishes at normalized clip position 0; after the end-of-frame wait, the completion handler marks the slide RETURNED. This reversed completion does not eject a cartridge or run the full-pull loading operation.
The return-stage multiplier used here is independent of the pull-stage multiplier; the code does not force them to sum to 1.

For a sequence starting partway through, remaining duration is (1 minus startPerc) times that full duration; startPerc is the unitless starting fraction of the sequence. Time advances in seconds of game time across frames.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDERETURN
member.summary: Moves through the SlideReturn clip toward the fully forward endpoint.

remarks.para: Normalized clip position is a unitless fraction: 0 is the clip beginning and 1 is its end. At normalized progress 1 or above, end-of-frame completion marks the slide RETURNED and applies the return sound and firing-latch checks, meaning tests of the remembered trigger-press and firing flags. In the normal cycle, loading is attempted during full-pull completion or SlideRelease, before the return completes. Selecting this visual sequence directly, or cycling with a missing or empty magazine, need not yield a round; the return completion itself does not load one.

Timed playback uses fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds of game time, times returnAnimationPerc, its independent unitless return-stage multiplier. Their product is the full return-stage duration. returnCurve receives elapsed sequence time divided by the remaining sequence duration, a unitless time fraction, and its output supplies a progress blend toward the clip endpoint. Manual override samples this clip at 1 minus the saved hand-pull fraction: that pull fraction is 0 when unpulled and fully forward, and 1 when fully pulled back. For example, saved pull 0.25 displays the return clip at 0.75.

pullAnimationPerc is the independent unitless pull-stage multiplier. The pull and return multipliers are independent and need not sum to 1. The configured full pull-stage and return-stage durations add to fireDuration times (pullAnimationPerc plus returnAnimationPerc), so their sum need not equal the base firing period. This sum is a duration budget, not a promise of exact elapsed cycle time: sampling across frames, carried excess time and deferred endpoint work affect the actual timing.

For a sequence starting partway through, remaining duration is (1 minus startPerc) times that full duration; startPerc is the unitless starting fraction of the sequence. Time advances in seconds of game time across frames.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates.SLIDERETURNREVERSED
member.summary: Runs the SlideReturn clip backward toward its beginning, normalized position 0; position 1 is its end.

remarks.para: Gun.SetAnimationState uses the same return clip and recognizes 0 or below as completion. In the audited PlayAnimationState switch, this variant uses reversed playback without selecting returnCurve; its default full duration is 1 second of game time before start-position adjustment.
The audited completion handler has no logical slide action for this value. Do not assume reversing this clip performs a full pull or loads ammunition.

For a sequence starting partway through, remaining duration is (1 minus startPerc) times that full duration; startPerc is the unitless starting fraction of the sequence. Time advances in seconds of game time across frames.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CartridgeStates.NONE
member.summary: The chamber is empty; a trigger attempt can dry-fire, meaning it produces no live shot, when the slide is fully forward, the hammer is cocked (ready to strike) and the other Fire guards pass.

remarks.para: The empty-chamber Fire branch uncocks the hammer and requests dry-fire sound after its guards pass. EjectCartridge selects this state and clears chamberedCartridge. UpdateArt hides both chamber-round and spent-case art. Setting only this enum state does not spawn an ejected object.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CartridgeStates.SPENT
member.summary: A fired round’s case remains in the chamber; Fire does not emit another shot from it.

remarks.para: A successful Fire changes UNSPENT to SPENT while retaining the cartridge data. The gun shows spent-case art. EjectCartridge can spawn the case definition and then clears the chamber.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CartridgeStates.UNSPENT
member.summary: A live round is chambered and can produce a shot when the slide is fully forward, the hammer is cocked (ready to strike) and the other Fire guards pass.

remarks.para: PullCartridge selects this state after loading valid cartridge data. Fire changes it to SPENT after accepting a live shot; EjectCartridge uses the full-round spawnable, the full-round object definition used for spawning, if it is removed unfired. The chamber art displays the live round.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.FireMode.AUTOMATIC
member.summary: Continues firing while the trigger is held, as long as the gun’s firing cycle and ammunition permit.

remarks.para: This mode allows repeated Fire calls despite the hasFiredOnce latch, a stored true/false flag remembering an allowed firing attempt since trigger reset. Automatic mode bypasses that repeated-attempt restriction while retaining the readiness and ammunition checks. A shot still requires the slide to be fully returned, the hammer cocked, and an unspent round in the chamber. The gun’s slide and firing animation cycle determines when those conditions are ready again.

The trigger input is the controller’s unitless primary-interaction fraction, normally 0 when released and 1 when fully pressed. In ordinary trigger handling, firing is requested strictly above 0.5 only when isTriggerPulledOnAttach, the block for a trigger held during attachment, is clear. Input strictly below 0.3 clears that block, then the remembered firing-attempt flag. Holding the trigger through later ready cycles can therefore fire more shots without releasing it. Selecting this mode does not refill an empty gun.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.FireMode.MANUAL
member.summary: Requires the gun’s action to be cycled by hand between shots, as with a pump or bolt.

remarks.para: After a live shot, OnFire uncocks the hammer and makes the slide controller movable. Fire does not start the automatic slide-pull animation in this mode. Pulling the action cocks the hammer, ejects the previous cartridge, and tries to feed the next round if ammunition is available; the slide must return before another shot can pass the firing checks.

The trigger input is the controller’s unitless primary-interaction fraction, normally 0 when released and 1 when fully pressed. The trigger must also be released before another firing attempt. hasFiredOnce is a latch, a stored true/false flag remembering an allowed firing attempt since trigger reset. Normal input strictly below 0.3 first clears isTriggerPulledOnAttach, the block for a trigger held during attachment, then clears the remembered firing-attempt flag. Firing is requested strictly above 0.5 only when that attachment block is clear. Cycling the action and resetting the trigger are separate requirements; this setting does not identify a particular weapon model.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.FireMode.SEMIAUTOMATIC
member.summary: Allows one shot per trigger pull while the gun cycles its action automatically.

remarks.para: The trigger input is the controller’s unitless primary-interaction fraction, normally 0 when released and 1 when fully pressed. After a firing attempt sets hasFiredOnce, a latch or stored true/false flag remembering an allowed attempt since trigger reset, this mode rejects repeated Fire calls until trigger release clears that flag. Normal input requests firing strictly above 0.5 only when isTriggerPulledOnAttach, the block for a trigger held during attachment, is clear. Input strictly below 0.3 clears that block, then the remembered firing-attempt flag, so releasing only slightly may not reset the next shot.

A shot still requires the slide fully returned, the hammer cocked, and an unspent round in the chamber. A live shot starts the nonmanual slide-pull cycle. An allowed attempt with an open locked slide can close the slide first rather than discharge, so pressing the trigger is not a guarantee of a bullet.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.HammerStates.COCKED
member.summary: The hammer is ready to strike; Gun.Fire can proceed if the slide and chamber are also ready.

remarks.para: Charge and CompleteSlidePull select this state. A cocked hammer alone does not guarantee a shot: the slide must be forward, a live round must be chambered and the trigger/slide-grab rules must allow it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.HammerStates.UNCOCKED
member.summary: The hammer is not ready to strike, so Gun.Fire refuses a shot until the action is cocked again.

remarks.para: Manual-mode OnFire and an empty-chamber dry fire select this state. Charge or a completed full slide pull can cock the hammer. Pool initialization also starts uncocked before applying configured charging.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates.LOCKED
member.summary: The slide is held open, preventing the normal firing path until the lock is released.

remarks.para: SlideLocked enters this state, plays the slide-lock animation and sound, and can request magazine ejection when isMagEjectOnEmpty is enabled. Completing a pull can lock the slide when a magazine is present, no cartridge was loaded, and isSlideLockedOnEmpty is enabled.

SlideRelease acts only in this state: it tries to load a cartridge, changes the state to PULLED, and begins the forward-return animation. Fire also calls SlideRelease when the slide is locked and the magazine contains ammunition; that call releases the slide rather than immediately firing a shot.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates.PULLED
member.summary: The pull-back step has completed, but the gun has not yet finished returning the slide to its firing position.

remarks.para: CompleteSlidePull first cocks the hammer, then ejects the previous cartridge, then tries to feed another if one is available. It enters this state unless it locks the slide open. SlideRelease also enters it after releasing an open slide.

The state can remain PULLED while the slide visibly travels forward. Completion of the return animation changes it to RETURNED. It therefore describes an unfinished firing cycle, rather than guaranteeing that the visible slide is still at its rear endpoint.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates.PULLING
member.summary: The gun is in the pull-back phase of manually controlling the slide; normal firing is blocked.

remarks.para: A slide override means manually controlling the slide position. SlideOverride enters this state for non-MANUAL fire modes unless the slide is locked. Its amount is a unitless position fraction: 0 is the forward/start endpoint and 1 the rear pull endpoint. Update enters PULLING when that fraction moves away from zero and uses it to select a position in the pull-back animation, so the state can remain PULLING while the slide is held still. The forward-return animation uses 1 minus this amount; this does not mean every arbitrary assignment is clamped to the endpoint range.

Reaching the rear endpoint completes the pull, which first cocks the hammer, then ejects the previous cartridge, then tries to feed another if one is available. Releasing an incomplete pull instead plays the pull animation backward and returns the state to RETURNED without completing that rear-endpoint operation.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates.RETURNED
member.summary: The gun treats the slide as fully forward and allows its remaining firing checks to run.

remarks.para: Completing a forward return, or reversing an incomplete pull back to the start, enters this state. Charging the gun also sets it directly. Fire still checks the hammer, cartridge and other firing conditions; RETURNED alone does not mean that the gun contains ammunition or will fire.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates.RETURNING
member.summary: A forward-return phase recognized by the slide controls; normal firing remains blocked.

remarks.para: A slide override means manually controlling the slide position. Its amount is a unitless position fraction: 0 is the forward/start endpoint and 1 the rear pull endpoint. While that control is active, Update treats this state like PULLED and positions the forward-return animation using 1 minus the amount. This does not mean every arbitrary assignment is clamped to the endpoint range. Releasing that override starts the forward-return animation for non-MANUAL fire modes.

Do not use this value alone to detect visible forward motion: CompleteSlidePull and SlideRelease can start the return animation while keeping the logical state PULLED until completion changes it to RETURNED.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.index1
member.summary: Sets the orientation of the index finger’s first driven bone, nearest the palm, for this pose sample.

remarks.para: This quaternion is the bone’s local rotation: its orientation relative to its parent in the finger skeleton. It can include bending, spreading and twisting, so its four components are not four curl angles or values in degrees. HandPoseViewer records it from the corresponding first finger transform’s localRotation.

The hand pose animator blends this rotation with other samples and applies the result to index1_Transform.localRotation. Changing it alters the base direction of the index finger and therefore also moves the later bones below it in the finger hierarchy. Controller finger curl and pose transitions can further change the final displayed pose.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.index2
member.summary: Sets the index finger’s bend angle at its second driven bone for this pose sample.

remarks.para: The value is in degrees. ApplyPoseToTransforms converts the blended value to Quaternion.AngleAxis(angle, Vector3.forward) and assigns it as the corresponding bone’s localRotation. It is a rotation around the positive Z axis of the bone’s parent, the bone or object it is attached under; the direction that appears to curl inward depends on how that finger skeleton is oriented.

For example, 45 supplies a 45-degree rotation around that axis, while 0 means no rotation relative to that parent. Depending on how the finger model was built, zero does not necessarily look like a straight finger. This is the full local rotation used at this step, rather than an extra rotation added to the bone’s existing pose. The sample angle is blended with other samples, and controller curl or transitions can change the final value.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.index3
member.summary: Sets the index finger’s bend angle at its third driven bone, toward the tip for this pose sample.

remarks.para: The value is in degrees. ApplyPoseToTransforms converts the blended value to Quaternion.AngleAxis(angle, Vector3.forward) and assigns it as the corresponding bone’s localRotation. It is a rotation around the positive Z axis of the bone’s parent, the bone or object it is attached under; the direction that appears to curl inward depends on how that finger skeleton is oriented.

For example, 45 supplies a 45-degree rotation around that axis, while 0 means no rotation relative to that parent. Depending on how the finger model was built, zero does not necessarily look like a straight finger. This is the full local rotation used at this step, rather than an extra rotation added to the bone’s existing pose. The sample angle is blended with other samples, and controller curl or transitions can change the final value.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.invLeftHandle
member.summary: Stores the reverse placement: where the left hand belongs relative to the grip handle.

remarks.para: This SimpleTransform expresses a hand position and orientation in the stored handle frame, reversing the relationship described by leftHandle. It allows the pose system to place a hand from a known handle pose. Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters, and rotation is a quaternion.

GetHandInHandleNeutral reads this field from the first sample of the first radius group. It turns both position and orientation by the inverse of the asset’s HandleSpace rotation, then scales the position by the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize. That multiplier compares the avatar’s hand with the reference hand: 1 keeps the reference distance and 1.5 makes it 50 percent longer. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh this cache; SetHandSize must run again before this getter uses the new factor. HandleSpace supplies the axis orientation chosen by the asset’s primary and secondary axes.

This is separately stored data. The neutral getter reads it directly rather than recalculating it from leftHandle, so editing the forward transform alone does not update the neutral hand placement. The non-neutral GetHandInHandle method instead derives its placement from the animator’s current handle helper.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.invRightHandle

remarks.para: This SimpleTransform expresses a hand position and orientation in the stored handle frame, reversing the relationship described by rightHandle. It allows the pose system to place a hand from a known handle pose. Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters, and rotation is a quaternion.

GetHandInHandleNeutral reads this field from the first sample of the first radius group. That multiplier compares the avatar’s hand with the reference hand: 1 keeps the reference distance and 1.5 makes it 50 percent longer. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh this cache; SetHandSize must run again before this getter uses the new factor. HandleSpace supplies the axis orientation chosen by the asset’s primary and secondary axes.

This is separately stored data. The neutral getter reads it directly rather than recalculating it from rightHandle, so editing the forward transform alone does not update the neutral hand placement. The non-neutral GetHandInHandle method instead derives its placement from the animator’s current handle helper.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.leftArtHandle
member.summary: Stores the grip handle’s placement relative to the visible left hand for pose preview and art alignment.

remarks.para: This SimpleTransform contains the handle’s position and quaternion orientation in the art hand’s local frame. The art hand is the transform used to display the hand model while posing it. Changing this value moves or turns the previewed handle relative to that visible hand.

GetArtHandleInHand returns the matching field from the animator’s current blended pose. HandPoseViewer.ApplyPose combines it with the art hand’s world position and rotation to position the previewed object. It therefore describes handle-in-hand placement; it does not describe the hand relative to the handle.

Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters. Unlike the rig-handle getters, GetArtHandleInHand returns the stored result without applying handSizeMult, which scales reference distances to the avatar’s hand size, or HandleSpace, which gives the handle the orientation chosen by the asset’s axes. Use this field for the art-hand relationship rather than copying a scaled world offset into it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.leftHandle
member.summary: Stores where the grip handle sits relative to the left hand in this pose sample.

remarks.para: The SimpleTransform contains a local position and a quaternion orientation in the pose’s left hand rig frame: coordinates relative to the hand’s animation skeleton, the bones controlling its model. Moving its position shifts the handle relative to the palm, which changes how that hand lines up with a held grip. Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters; the quaternion describes orientation, not angles stored separately in X/Y/Z.

SolvePoseForHandle writes the blended position and orientation to the animator’s handle helper. GetHandleInHand scales the helper’s current local position, while GetHandleInHandNeutral scales this field’s position from the first sample of the first radius group. Both use the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize. It compares the linear size of that avatar’s hand with the reference hand: 1 uses reference size and 1.5 uses a hand 50 percent larger. A reference offset of 0.02 meters therefore becomes 0.03 meters at 1.5. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh this cache; SetHandSize must run again before these getters use the new factor. Their orientation also includes the HandPose asset’s HandleSpace rotation, built from its primary and secondary axes.

The ordinary weighted BlendPose path blends the sample positions but takes the rig handle rotation from the first sample of the first radius group. Editing a later sample’s rotation therefore does not guarantee that the normal solver will use it. Keep the corresponding inverse handle data consistent when authoring neutral hand placement.

This is the full local rotation used at this step, rather than an extra rotation added to the bone’s existing pose. The sample angle is blended with other samples, and controller curl or transitions can change the final value.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.nativePry
member.summary: Places this sample in the pitch, roll and yaw coordinates used to choose and blend hand poses.

remarks.para: X is the pitch coordinate, Y is roll and Z is yaw, in degrees. The animator compares its requested pitch/roll/yaw with these sample coordinates to calculate blend weights. Moving this point changes which hand orientations favor this sample; the fingers and handle placement come from the other fields in the selected samples.

These are coordinates in the pose solver’s angle space. ApplyRotationAnimationBlend derives them from a rotation’s axis multiplied by its angle in degrees, rotates that vector using the asset’s HandleSpace axis orientation, then applies the hand-side sign convention. They should not be treated as the ordinary X/Y/Z Euler rotation of a Unity transform.

For example, a sample at (30, 0, 0) is placed at a 30-degree pitch coordinate with zero roll and yaw coordinates. Its finger bones still use thumb1, index1 and the other rotation fields; nativePry is not assigned directly to a bone rotation.

SetHandPose builds its lookup points from the first radius group. Radius blending pairs samples in different groups by array index, so use the same coordinate layout and sample order across all radius groups. Changing only a later group’s nativePry does not relocate the lookup point.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.rightArtHandle
member.summary: Stores the grip handle’s placement relative to the visible right hand for pose preview and art alignment.

remarks.para: This SimpleTransform contains the handle’s position and quaternion orientation in the art hand’s local frame. The art hand is the transform used to display the hand model while posing it. Changing this value moves or turns the previewed handle relative to that visible hand.

GetArtHandleInHand returns the matching field from the animator’s current blended pose. HandPoseViewer.ApplyPose combines it with the art hand’s world position and rotation to position the previewed object. It therefore describes handle-in-hand placement; it does not describe the hand relative to the handle.

Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters. Unlike the rig-handle getters, GetArtHandleInHand returns the stored result without applying handSizeMult, which scales reference distances to the avatar’s hand size, or HandleSpace, which gives the handle the orientation chosen by the asset’s axes. Use this field for the art-hand relationship rather than copying a scaled world offset into it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData.rightHandle
member.summary: Stores where the grip handle sits relative to the right hand in this pose sample.

remarks.para: The SimpleTransform contains a local position and a quaternion orientation in the pose’s right hand rig frame: coordinates relative to the hand’s animation skeleton, the bones controlling its model. Moving its position shifts the handle relative to the palm, which changes how that hand lines up with a held grip. Position uses local Unity distance units, normally meters; the quaternion describes orientation, not angles stored separately in X/Y/Z.

SolvePoseForHandle writes the blended position and orientation to the animator’s handle helper. GetHandleInHand scales the helper’s current local position, while GetHandleInHandNeutral scales this field’s position from the first sample of the first radius group. Both use the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize. It compares the linear size of that avatar’s hand with the reference hand: 1 uses reference size and 1.5 uses a hand 50 percent larger. A reference offset of 0.02 meters therefore becomes 0.03 meters at 1.5. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh this cache; SetHandSize must run again before these getters use the new factor. Their orientation also includes the HandPose asset’s HandleSpace rotation, built from its primary and secondary axes.

The ordinary weighted BlendPose path blends the sample positions but takes the rig handle rotation from the first sample of the first radius group. Editing a later sample’s rotation therefore does not guarantee that the normal solver will use it. Keep the corresponding inverse handle data consistent when authoring neutral hand placement.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.HealthMode.InsantDeath
member.summary: Skips the player's ordinary post-hit regeneration and uses the special instant-death countdown when damage reaches zero health.

remarks.para: In Player_Health.TAKEDAMAGE, damage is still subtracted normally. Selecting this value does not itself make every positive hit fatal. For example, calling TAKEDAMAGE with 10 damage while current health is 50 leaves 40; the damage path starts dying when current health reaches zero or below.

When its Dying branch first runs, it sets isInstaDying and deathIsImminent, sets current health to -1, and starts the death-screen coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames. The countdown uses instaDeathTimeAmount in seconds of scaled game time, so slow motion can affect its wall-clock duration. When the sequence finishes, it calls Death if health is still zero or below. This branch does not send the OnDeathImminent(true) notification that the Mortal branch sends.

The normal damage path does not start its regeneration coroutine in this mode, and OnPuppetDeath skips the ordinary life-saving recovery. UpdateHealth provides a separate healing path while the player is alive and can stop the special countdown; this mode does not block every possible source of healing.
Use the spelling InsantDeath in code. Changing healthMode alone does not stop a regeneration or death sequence that was already running.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.HealthMode.Invincible
member.summary: Lets the player take damage while skipping the death countdown normally started at zero health.

remarks.para: Player_Health still subtracts damage from current health and can play damage feedback. When its Dying method is reached in this mode, it sets current health to zero and returns without starting the ordinary dying sequence. The post-hit damage path can still start health regeneration.

This protects against the death transition in that damage path. It does not cancel a death coroutine, a sequence continuing over several frames, that was started before the mode changed, and it does not prevent code from calling Death directly. Selecting the mode alone also does not refill health or revive a player whose alive flag is already false.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.HealthMode.Mortal
member.summary: Uses the player's normal damage, regeneration and recoverable dying sequence.

remarks.para: Damage reduces current health. When the player is not already dying, the damage path restarts regeneration after wait_Regen_t seconds of scaled game time. Reaching zero health begins a grace period governed by deathTimeAmount, also in seconds, rather than calling Death immediately.

The Dying method sets deathIsImminent to true before sending OnDeathImminent(true). It starts the death-screen countdown after that notification. This coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames, calls Death at the end if current health remains zero or below.

Additional hits while dying can reduce currDeathTime, the countdown's current duration, by deathTimeReduction seconds while that duration is greater than two seconds. The ordinary life-saving recovery can cancel the dying sequence and restore health; Mortal therefore allows death but does not make every lethal hit immediately irreversible.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.UsageSettings.armLf
member.summary: Scales the left arm's available muscle strength when these settings are applied to Health.

remarks.para: Health.SetUsage copies this settings value into the Health component. Health.UpdateMuscleStates then applies it to the physical rig, and the rig updates its joint motors. A joint motor applies physics forces to move body parts toward their target pose. Editing a local UsageSettings value takes effect after copying it into Health; the struct is not a live link to the rig.

The update copies it through usage_arm_lf into the left arm's PhysHand.armInternalMult. That factor contributes to the arm's joint-motor strength and its hand force/torque budgets; torque means twisting strength.

The available-strength factor A is computed from stun_arm_lf (the limb's available strength after stun), stun_spine (the spine's available strength after stun), and cur_arm_lf (the limb's current condition factor). These are unitless factors. Clamp means keeping a number between its lower and upper bounds. Health first clamps each stun factor to the range 0 to 1, multiplies both by the current-condition factor, then clamps that product to the range 0.02 to 1: A = clamp(clamp(stun_arm_lf, 0, 1) × clamp(stun_spine, 0, 1) × cur_arm_lf, 0.02, 1). It then computes the applied multiplier as A × armLf. For example, A = 0.8 and armLf = 0.5 produce an applied multiplier of 0.4.

This is a unitless multiplier: 1 preserves the strength available from the other factors and 0.5 halves this contribution. The constructor and SetUsage copy it without clamping. Availability is clamped before multiplication, so that clamp does not restrict this field to the same range.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.UsageSettings.hips
member.summary: Scales the pelvis and upper-body rotation support used during ball locomotion.

remarks.para: Health.SetUsage copies this settings value into the Health component. Health.UpdateMuscleStates then applies it to the physical rig, and the rig updates its joint motors. A joint motor applies physics forces to move body parts toward their target pose. Editing a local UsageSettings value takes effect after copying it into Health; the struct is not a live link to the rig.

Health copies this through usage_hips into the rig's _pelvisForceInternalMult. The pelvis means the hips, and ball locomotion is the rig's mode using its physical ball support. When ball locomotion is enabled, the rig's early update uses it for the knee-to-pelvis, knee-to-chest and knee-to-head rotation motors. These connections help turn the upper body toward the locomotion support's target orientations.

The applied pelvis multiplier is A × hips, where A is stun_spine, the spine's available strength after stun, clamped between 0 and 1. Both A and hips are unitless. For example, A = 0.8 and hips = 0.5 give 0.4 before the rig's other support and force multipliers are applied.

This is a unitless multiplier: 1 preserves the strength available from the other factors and 0.5 halves this contribution. The constructor and SetUsage copy it without clamping. Availability is clamped before multiplication, so that clamp does not restrict this field to the same range.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.DecalType.Collider
member.summary: Enables an impact mark whose projector is given the collider reported by the hit.

remarks.para: Value 0. A collider is the shape Unity uses to detect hits. The DecalProjector component places the visual impact mark onto that shape. The attack's world-space origin is the position stored in Attack.origin, measured in the world's coordinates. A Transform records an object's position, rotation and scale. After the surface data and impact particles are handled, ImpactProperties spawns the surface’s decal asset at the attack’s world-space origin and orients it toward the hit surface. It then supplies the attack’s collider, chosen surface material and tint to the decal projector.

If that collider has an attached Rigidbody, the spawn request uses the body’s Transform as the parent. A Rigidbody is an object’s physics body; parenting makes the spawned object follow that body’s movement. A collider without an attached body supplies no parent to this request. The struck collider is a separate projection target, so this setting does not mean the decal is always parented directly to its Transform.

A visible mark still requires usable loaded surface data, a successful decal-asset spawn, a valid hit collider and a DecalProjector on the spawned object. This value enables that path rather than guaranteeing a mark for every hit.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.DecalType.None
member.summary: Skips decal spawning and projection during impact handling while leaving the earlier particle-effect work enabled.

remarks.para: Value -1. The running impact handler checks this after its surface setup and particle-effect stage. Selecting None prevents it from starting the later decal stage; it does not turn this component’s whole impact response off.
The flag is read when that stage is reached, which can be after asynchronous work over later frames. Changing it does not remove marks already spawned.
