member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.Climbing
member.summary: Positions the foot assembly against detected climbing support while the rig moves along that support.

remarks.para: The climbing check uses hand-support information and a sphere cast, a test that sweeps a sphere through the scene to find a surface. The rig keeps a climbing contact point and surface normal, the direction pointing out from that surface, then adjusts the knee-to-pelvis joint target as movement continues.

Entering this state uses stronger X and Z position drives than Dangle. A drive applies spring-like correction toward the target, and a joint connects body parts in the physics simulation. The mode can change to Foothold when foot support increases, or return to Dangle when the climbing check no longer provides usable support. It is a specific foot-position mode, not a report of every grip or hanging situation.
X and Z are directions in the knee-to-pelvis connection’s own frame, which turns with it, rather than fixed scene directions.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.Dangle
member.summary: Uses softer foot-position correction while the hands provide support and the foot assembly has little support.

remarks.para: The normal selection test requires the two hands’ combined internal support score to exceed 0.8 and the footSupported score to be below 0.2. These are the rig’s internal hand-support and foot-support values; the thresholds describe this state-selection test. Being in mid-air alone does not necessarily select this mode.

Entering Dangle frees the knee-to-pelvis joint’s X and Z directions and uses a softer drive than the climbing states, allowing the foot assembly to hang and move toward its target. The rig checks for a climbing surface; with a suitable result it can reposition the foot and enter Climbing or Foothold. Regaining foot support can instead lead to ReturnStep.

The joint is the physics connection between the knee and pelvis. X and Z are directions in the knee-to-pelvis connection’s own frame, which turns with it, rather than fixed scene directions. A drive applies spring-like correction toward a requested position.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.Foothold
member.summary: Uses strong foot-position correction while transitioning from climbing support toward centered stepping.

remarks.para: This mode can follow Climbing when footSupported exceeds 0.5, or be selected while the rig positions the foot to climb onto a detected surface. footSupported is the rig’s internal foot-support value used for this state-selection test. It is not the generic state for every ordinary grounded foot.

The knee-to-pelvis joint uses strong X and Z drives, which apply spring-like correction toward its target. Movement checks run the ReturnStep centering routine while monitoring foot support and the rig’s internal StaticOneHand and StaticTwoHand hand classifications for static support. Depending on those checks, the rig can continue this placement, switch to ReturnStep or NeutralRoll, or return to Dangle.
The joint is the physics connection between the knee and pelvis. X and Z are directions in the knee-to-pelvis connection’s own frame, which turns with it, rather than fixed scene directions.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.HoldStep
member.summary: Maintains an offset foot placement while the rig continues checking where to take the next step.

remarks.para: The knee-to-pelvis joint allows X and Z movement and uses drives to hold its target; a drive applies spring-like correction toward a requested position. HoldStep updates that target using the input movement velocity over a physics update, preserving its Y target instead of immediately returning the foot offset to center.

Further movement and foot-surface checks can begin a new ReturnStep placement. A hand-supported, weak-foot-support condition can switch to Dangle. The word “hold” does not freeze the entire player or disable physics.
The joint is the physics connection between the knee and pelvis. X and Z are directions in the knee-to-pelvis connection’s own frame, which turns with it, rather than fixed scene directions.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.NeutralRoll
member.summary: Keeps the knee-to-pelvis connection centered for ordinary rolling locomotion.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the rig’s single physical foot assembly used beneath the two visible feet. Entering this state locks the knee-to-pelvis joint’s X and Z movement. A joint connects parts of the player’s body in the physics simulation; these axes belong to that joint, rather than being fixed world directions.

Movement checks can start a step or switch to Dangle when the hand/foot support test requires it. This is a stepping mode, not proof of continuous ground contact: disabling ball locomotion also selects NeutralRoll.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState.ReturnStep
member.summary: Gradually brings the foot assembly’s sideways and forward/back offset toward the centered knee-to-pelvis target.

remarks.para: The rig allows X and Z movement in the knee-to-pelvis joint, then smooths those target coordinates toward zero over physics updates while retaining the existing Y target. Zero here is the joint’s centered target, not world position zero; a joint is a physics connection between parts of the player’s body.

When that offset is sufficiently close to center, ReturnStep selects NeutralRoll, which locks those two joint directions. New surface checks can start another step before centering finishes, and the hand/foot support test can select Dangle instead. It is a gradual adjustment, not an instant teleport of the visible feet.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PlayerDamageReceiver.BodyPart.ArmLowerLf
member.summary: Labels a reported hit as affecting the left forearm between elbow and wrist.

remarks.para: Set PlayerDamageReceiver.bodyPart to this value on the receiver covering the left forearm. ReceiveAttack passes its current label to the receiver’s assigned Health component on each call. This identifies the region; it does not move the receiver or change its collider, the physics detection shape used to find hits.

In the inspected Health.OnReceivedDamage handler, an accepted hit passes incoming damage × 0.6 to TAKEDAMAGE, the routine that applies health damage. Incoming damage is measured in game health points, and 0.6 is a unitless multiplier; for example, an incoming 10-point hit passes 6 points. This happens only while alive is true and the attack’s backFacing marker is false; attacks with that marker true are ignored by this handler. Every listed non-head region uses this same multiplier; this label does not introduce a separate health pool or a special limb-stun rule in that handler.

When Health’s visual-damage option is enabled and the attack’s OrderInPool value is zero or negative, this value selects the stored left forearm position and orientation in the avatar’s reference pose to place visual hit data. The receiver first converts the hit position and surface-normal direction into its own local coordinates, meaning coordinates relative to that receiver. Keep the label matched to the actual receiver: choosing another region changes this visual mapping without relocating the detection shape. Whether a visible mark is drawn also depends on the visual-damage path and its configured renderers.

Every listed non-head region uses this same multiplier; this label does not introduce a separate health pool or a special limb-stun rule in that handler.

When Health’s visual-damage option is enabled and the attack’s OrderInPool value is zero or negative, this value selects the stored right forearm position and orientation in the avatar’s reference pose to place visual hit data. The receiver first converts the hit position and surface-normal direction into its own local coordinates, meaning coordinates relative to that receiver. Keep the label matched to the actual receiver: choosing another region changes this visual mapping without relocating the detection shape. Whether a visible mark is drawn also depends on the visual-damage path and its configured renderers.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.RoamMode.LEGACY
member.summary: Tries to send the NPC to a random point in an X/Z rectangle around its home position minus roamOffset.

remarks.para: This is the unitless RoamMode value 3. When RoamByMode runs in this mode, it first passes a random gate of Random.value <= 0.1, then chooses the X and Z offsets independently: X is between minus and plus roamRange.x, and Z is between minus and plus roamRange.y. For example, roamRange=(4, 2) allows up to 4 coordinate units sideways and 2 along world Z around homePosition - roamOffset. These are world-coordinate units; the native code does not establish meters. The search area is a rectangle, not a radius.

The code asks Unity's NavMeshAgent—the navigation component that finds routes across walkable ground—to calculate a route to the sampled point. If calculation succeeds, it asks the agent to use that point. If calculation fails, this branch records the sampled point in failedWPList, the list of points whose route calculation failed; it does not select an earlier point from usedWPList as a fallback. A later roaming tick reads the selected mode; assigning this enum value alone does not immediately run RoamByMode.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.RoamMode.WAYPOINTS
member.summary: Requests a route to one of the saved waypoint positions.

remarks.para: This is the unitless RoamMode value 2. A waypoint is a saved position the NPC may visit. After the current-path, stopping-distance, and wait-time checks allow a new choice, RoamByMode gets an index from the waypoint list and gives that position to SetPath. The NavMeshAgent is Unity's navigation component that finds and follows routes over walkable ground; requesting a route does not guarantee that the NPC reaches the destination.

waypointEvalMode selects the order: LINEAR advances through the list and wraps to its first position; PING_PONG reverses the list in place and needs at least two waypoints. With just one waypoint and its index 0 current (indexes count from 0), the next selection returns index 1, outside the list, so the caller fails before requesting a route; RANDOM chooses a random index. RANDOM_MIN_TIME gives each waypoint a next-eligible deadline using Unity's scaled game clock, Time.time, plus wpMinTime. This is the minimum re-selection wait in scaled game-time seconds, not time spent waiting at the current waypoint. The selector makes at most one try per array entry, although random tries can repeat an index. If no try finds an eligible waypoint, it still returns the last sampled index even when that index's deadline is in the future. This fallback does not renew that waypoint's deadline, although RoamByMode may still use its position for the route request.
A later roaming tick reads the selected mode; assigning this enum value alone does not immediately run RoamByMode.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.RoamMode.ZONE
member.summary: Samples an X/Z point from the assigned RoamArea and asks the navigation agent to find a route there.

remarks.para: This is the unitless RoamMode value 0. RoamArea.GetRoamTarget starts at the RoamArea object's world position, keeps its world Y height, and adds independent offsets along world X and Z. Each offset ranges from minus to plus half the matching roamScale component multiplied by uniformScale, a unitless multiplier. For example, with roamScale=(10, 6) and uniformScale=1, X varies by up to 5 and Z by up to 3 world-coordinate units; these are not established as meters. The area's rotation and object scale do not rotate or stretch these offsets.

After its current-path, stopping-distance, and next-roam-time checks, RoamByMode asks the NavMeshAgent—Unity's component for finding routes across walkable ground—to calculate a route to the sampled point. It calls SetPath for that point when calculation succeeds; if calculation fails, this method can choose a previously stored roam point instead. Assigning this enum value alone does not immediately run RoamByMode; a later roaming tick reads it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.RoamMode.ZONE3D
member.summary: Samples a world-space X/Y/Z point in the assigned RoamArea and stores it as ranRoamTarget.

remarks.para: This is the unitless RoamMode value 1. The sampled point is centered on the RoamArea object's world position. Each world-axis offset ranges from minus to plus half the matching roamScale3D component multiplied by uniformScale, a unitless multiplier. For example, roamScale3D=(10, 6, 4) with uniformScale=1 allows offsets up to 5 on X, 3 on Y, and 2 on Z in world-coordinate units; the native code does not establish meters. The area's rotation and object scale do not rotate or stretch these offsets.

After checking that the NavMeshAgent has no current path and that the next roam time has passed, this RoamByMode branch stores the candidate in ranRoamTarget and returns without calling SetPath. It therefore does not itself ask the navigation agent to route to this sample; this describes this method's branch only and does not establish whether other code reads the stored candidate. Assigning this enum value alone does not immediately run RoamByMode; a later roaming tick reads it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.WaypointEvalMode.LINEAR
member.summary: Advances through saved waypoint indexes in order, wrapping to index 0 after the last.

remarks.para: This is the unitless WaypointEvalMode value 0. A waypoint is a saved position the NPC can use as a route destination. The selector increments currWaypoint and resets it to 0 when it reaches the end of the waypoints array.

This choice is used only when the NPC is in waypoint roaming and needs a new route destination: an existing navigation path is handled first, and the next-roam wait must have passed. Unity's NavMeshAgent is the component that finds and follows a route over walkable ground. Changing this enum field alone does not choose a waypoint or replace the path already being followed.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.WaypointEvalMode.PING_PONG
member.summary: Reverses the saved waypoint order at the end so the patrol heads back; use at least two waypoints.

remarks.para: This is the unitless WaypointEvalMode value 1. A waypoint is a saved position the NPC can use as a route destination. When currWaypoint reaches the end of the waypoints array, the selector reverses that array in place and sets the index to 1. Code that reads the public array afterward sees the reversed order.

With a one-element waypoints array, if its only valid index 0 is current, this selector advances to index 1 and reverses the one-item array, leaving index 1 out of range. The caller checks the returned index against the array length and enters its failure branch instead of calling SetPath. This mode therefore needs at least two waypoints.

This choice is used only when the NPC is in waypoint roaming and needs a new route destination: an existing navigation path is handled first, and the next-roam wait must have passed. Unity's NavMeshAgent is the component that finds and follows a route over walkable ground. Changing this enum field alone does not reverse the array or replace the path already being followed.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.WaypointEvalMode.RANDOM
member.summary: Picks a saved waypoint index at random when waypoint roaming needs a new route; it may pick the same one again.

remarks.para: This is the unitless WaypointEvalMode value 2. A waypoint is a saved position the NPC can use as a route destination. The selector chooses a random index from waypoints and does not exclude currWaypoint, so the same position can be selected twice in a row.

This choice is used only when the NPC is in waypoint roaming and needs a new route destination: an existing navigation path is handled first, and the next-roam wait must have passed. Unity's NavMeshAgent is the component that finds and follows a route over walkable ground. Changing this enum field alone does not choose a waypoint or replace the path already being followed.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.WaypointEvalMode.RANDOM_MIN_TIME
member.summary: Prefers a random waypoint whose individual cooldown has expired, but falls back to the last draw after bounded tries.

remarks.para: This is the unitless WaypointEvalMode value 3. A waypoint is a saved position the NPC can use as a route destination. When a candidate is new or its deadline has expired, the selector records Unity's scaled game clock, Time.time, plus wpMinTime seconds as that index's next eligible time. This is a per-waypoint re-selection interval, not a promise to wait at the current waypoint; a still-cooling candidate returned by the fallback keeps its existing deadline.

When another destination is needed, the selector makes at most waypoints.Length random draws, checking each draw's saved deadline. Random draws may repeat the same index, so this does not guarantee that every distinct waypoint is checked. If no draw is eligible, it still returns the last sampled index even if its deadline has not passed.

This choice is used only when the NPC is in waypoint roaming and needs a new route destination: an existing navigation path is handled first, and the next-roam wait must have passed. Unity's NavMeshAgent is the component that finds and follows a route over walkable ground. Changing this enum field alone does not choose a waypoint or replace the path already being followed.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.Mode.Active
member.summary: Active physics simulation, where each PuppetMaster muscle (a physics-controlled body part and its joint drive) steers its Rigidbody toward the animated target pose; the poses can differ.

remarks.para: Enum value 0. A ragdoll is a character represented by physics-controlled body parts. PuppetMaster calls each body part and its connecting joint a muscle. In Active mode, Unity simulates each Rigidbody (the component that represents a physics body), and the joint drive steers that body toward the animated target pose; the simulated pose can differ from the target. The public mode field is the requested setting. PuppetMaster’s mode-switch routine applies it through a separate runtime mode, which the fixed-physics update and late-frame mapping check. Switching from Disabled to Active can raise mappingBlend over blendTime seconds. This blend controls how strongly the physics pose is copied onto the animated target transforms, which store each target body part’s position and rotation. This Mode is separate from PuppetMaster.State (Alive, Dead, or Frozen).

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.Mode.Disabled
member.summary: Disables the ragdoll and suspends all physics muscle simulation.

remarks.para: Enum value 1, selected in PuppetMaster’s public mode field to request disabling the ragdoll. When the mode-switch routine applies Active to Disabled, it lowers mappingBlend over blendTime seconds, reducing how much of the physics pose is copied onto the animated target transforms (the components that store each target body part’s position and rotation). After that blend reaches zero, it deactivates each muscle Rigidbody’s GameObject (the Unity object holding that physics body and its components) and marks the separate runtime mode Disabled. DisableImmediately skips the blend and deactivates those GameObjects directly. The mode request is not itself the transition. PuppetMaster.State (Alive, Dead, or Frozen) is a separate setting. The inspected Disabled-to-Active transition moves muscles toward their targets and raises the blend, but does not show a GameObject reactivation call.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.StunGroup.ArmLf
member.summary: Routes a mapped muscle's damage and stun to the left arm's separate health and recovery counters.

remarks.para: A muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Its pose-driving strength is how strongly it tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation. The left arm health is a unitless fraction, normally 1 for full health and 0 for depleted health. Organic means the isOrganic setting is enabled.

Assign this value to that muscle's entry in SubBehaviourHealth.muscles. For muscle indices after the first one, the limb's health and stun combine with the spine stun factor to affect its pose-driving strength. Organic limb attacks can also reduce overall health. GetStun reports this limb's stored health and the combined limb/spine recovery factor, not a duration in seconds.

The limb and shared spine recovery counters are unitless numbers that recover toward 1; raw values can be negative. GetStun limits each to 0 through 1, then multiplies them: lower factors mean weaker control. With spine counter 0.5, limb counter 0.8 and limb health 0.6, it returns 0.5 × 0.8 = 0.4 and separately outputs health 0.6. This query factor is not the final body strength.

For muscle indices 1 and later, UpdateMuscleStates also multiplies by limb health, limits that product to 0.02 through 1, and applies the limb usage multiplier, a unitless strength scale where 1 preserves the result and 0 removes it. Muscle index 0 instead uses the spine recovery factor times hips usage, regardless of its assigned group. This strength exception does not change damage routing.

For example, setting muscles[3] to ArmLf makes Stun, TakeDamage and GetStun calls with m = 3 use the left arm region. Here 3 is an index in the character’s physical-muscle list, rather than the group’s enum number. Supply a mapping aligned with that list; assigning the group does not create or locate a body part.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.StunGroup.Head
member.summary: Selects head-hit damage rules while applying stun to the shared spine counter.

remarks.para: A muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Its pose-driving strength means how strongly it tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation. The shared spine recovery counter is a unitless number that recovers toward 1 and can be negative after hits. For later Head muscles, that counter is limited to 0.02 through 1, then multiplied by spine usage, a unitless strength scale where 1 preserves the result and 0 removes it.

Assign this value to the head muscle's entry in SubBehaviourHealth.muscles. Direct attack health calculations use the extra head factor of 4.1, and a Piercing attack sends OnHeadShot before the general damage notification. Physical-strength updates for muscle indices 1 and later share the spine usage multiplier; index 0 uses hips usage instead. GetStun returns 1 and outputs health 1 for this group; it does not report a separate head health or timer.

For ordinary head Attack damage before the separate Blunt reduction, the health-fraction step is (D / H) × 4.1: D is damage in attack-damage points after the attack-type multiplier, and H is maxHitPoints, the full overall-health scale in damage points. Piercing is an attack category, such as a piercing projectile hit. With Piercing damage 10, type multiplier 1 and H = 100, the step is 0.41, so overall health 1 becomes about 0.59. Blunt head damage has an additional reduction.

After the head health and shared spine recovery counter have changed, a Piercing attack calls OnHeadShot listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine called by a notification. OnNPCDamage follows with the attack-damage amount after its type multiplier, before the score update and later kill check. In the example its payload is 10, rather than the 0.41 health-fraction step or 41 points. Neither notification supplies a head position or enemy identity.

GetStun’s returned 1 and health output 1 are fixed query placeholders for Head. They do not prove full actual health or no stun. There is no separate head health fraction or recovery counter in this health helper.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.StunGroup.Spine
member.summary: Routes a mapped muscle's damage to overall health and its stun to the shared spine counter.

remarks.para: A muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Torso pose-driving strength means how strongly it follows its intended animated position and rotation. The shared spine recovery counter is unitless, can be negative after hits, and moves toward 1 during active UpdateStun recovery. GetStun limits it to 0 through 1: 1 is the recovered contribution, and lower factors weaken torso and limb control.

Assign this value to a muscle's entry in SubBehaviourHealth.muscles. The spine recovery factor affects torso control and also contributes to arm and leg strength. GetStun returns the spine counter limited to 0 through 1 and outputs health 1; that health output is not the enemy's overall health fraction.
The health output 1 is a fixed query placeholder. For a muscle mapped to Spine, a spine counter of 0.4 and actual overall health of 0.7 produce return value 0.4 and health output 1, rather than 0.7.

For example, setting muscles[3] to Spine routes a query with m = 3 to this region; 3 is a physical-muscle index, not the enum value. For strength application, index 0 uses the spine counter limited to 0 through 1 times hips usage. Later Spine muscles use the spine counter limited to 0.02 through 1 times spine usage. These usage values are unitless strength scales: 1 preserves the calculated result and 0 removes it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.UsageSettings.armLf
member.summary: Sets the multiplier copied into the left arm's pose-driving strength when these settings are applied.

remarks.para: Pose-driving strength means how strongly the simulated left arm’s rotational drive turns it toward its intended animated pose.

This multiplier has no physical unit: 1 preserves calculated strength, 0.5 halves it, and 0 makes its final strength zero. It is not a reading of supported weight. A stun counter of 1 means recovered, while 0 or below contributes a zero stun factor; a limb health fraction of 1 is full and 0 is depleted.

UpdateMuscleStates multiplies the spine and matching limb stun factors, each limited to 0 through 1, by the limb's health fraction. It limits that product to 0.02 through 1, then multiplies by armLf. Thus armLf = 0 still makes the final strength zero despite that minimum.

SubBehaviourHealth.SetUsage copies this stored setting into the health object; UpdateMuscleStates applies the copied value later. Editing this settings value after the copy does not update the live enemy. SetUsage does not clamp the multiplier to 0 through 1.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState.Airborne
member.summary: Uses the regular horizontal speed calculation without a special airborne branch in the inspected ApplyMovement path.

remarks.para: The numeric value is a stored label, not a direct ground-contact measurement. ApplyMovement does not test ground contact from it and leaves maxVelocity, the base horizontal speed setting in meters per second, unboosted. Actual grounding checks in the inspected jump routine come from the physics rig separately.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState.FootClimb
member.summary: Uses the regular horizontal speed calculation without a foot-climbing branch in the inspected ApplyMovement path.

remarks.para: That method does not select footholds or start a special climbing action from this label. It follows the unboosted maxVelocity calculation, where maxVelocity is the base horizontal speed setting in meters per second. Other game code or mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState.HandClimb

remarks.para: Assigning this label to travState does not select a special hand-climbing action within that method. Other game code or mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState.Jog
member.summary: Doubles the base horizontal speed setting in RemapRig.ApplyMovement before other movement adjustments.

remarks.para: When travState is Jog, the movement calculation starts with twice maxVelocity, the base horizontal speed setting in meters per second. For example, maxVelocity = 3 makes this step start with 6 meters per second. Body-pose and movement-direction adjustments and acceleration smoothing still affect the result, so this does not guarantee an actual 6-meter-per-second velocity.
This is the only enum value distinguished by the inspected ApplyMovement speed calculation. The numeric enum value 1 is a label, not a speed.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState.Jump

remarks.para: The inspected Jump, JumpCharge, Jumping and JumpEnd methods use their own jump-enabled, jumping and stage fields. OnEarlyUpdate starts Jump from the controller's jump input, then advances Jumping when its separate jumping flag is set. Those inspected methods do not use this enum value to start a jump.
In ApplyMovement, this value leaves maxVelocity, the base horizontal speed setting in meters per second, unboosted, just like Walk.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState.ActiveRagdoll
member.summary: Lets the body move under physics while keeping its active body control enabled.

remarks.para: Value 2. When changing from OnFoot, the legs become physical: their Rigidbody components, which let Unity simulate moving objects, can respond to forces. Normal ball-based walking support is disabled, the shoulder and wrist have slightly tighter bend limits than during normal walking, and the shoulder no longer uses spring settings that push back at those limits or damping settings that reduce wobbling there, and selected hand/body collisions are enabled. A physics joint is a connection that limits or drives movement between body parts; the active joint control is left running.

When changing from Ragdoll, this state clears the shutdown flags for the torso, hands, and legs. For example, use this transition when a fallen body should regain active control without returning to ordinary walking. Entering from Seated does not perform the same setup, so leave a seat through its seat-release routine first.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState.OnFoot
member.summary: Uses the player’s normal standing and walking body mode.

remarks.para: Value 0. Returning from either ragdoll mode restores normal walking support and makes the legs kinematic. A kinematic Rigidbody is a body whose movement is controlled by the game instead of being pushed around by physics forces. The hand movement limits and selected hand/body collision rules are also restored for active play.

Returning from Ragdoll additionally clears the body’s shutdown flags. For a seated player, use the seat’s release routine: it removes the physics connection to the seat and requests OnFoot. Assigning this enum value alone does not remove that connection.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState.Ragdoll
member.summary: Makes the body fall and move under physics with much weaker active joint control.

remarks.para: Value 3. From OnFoot, this first makes the legs physical and disables normal walking support, then shuts down the torso, hand, and leg controllers. From ActiveRagdoll, it only performs that shutdown because the physical setup is already in place. A physics joint connects body parts; shutdown reduces its motor settings and clears movement targets, but does not set every motor setting to zero.

While this is the current mode, the rig manager skips the pose rigs’ early pass before the normal frame update, their physics-step pass when Unity calculates movement and collisions, and their late pass after the normal frame update. Those rigs normally translate tracked head and hand movement into body poses. This state check still allows the controller, physics rig, and ordinary once-per-frame pose update to run; separate conditions, such as a paused controller, can stop those updates. The mode itself therefore does not freeze the simulated body.

For example, changing from OnFoot to Ragdoll lets a falling body react to gravity and collisions with reduced active control. The reverse transition restores walking setup and clears the shutdown flags. A transition directly from Seated does not perform this ragdoll setup; release the seat first.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState.Seated
member.summary: Marks the player as using a registered seat.

remarks.para: Value 1. The seat’s registration routine requests this state, records the active seat, and builds a physics joint between the player’s pelvis and the seat body. A physics joint is a connection that limits or drives movement between two simulated bodies. This connection makes the player follow the seat, such as a moving vehicle seat.

The enum value alone does not create the seat connection. The physics rig’s body-state switch performs no physical setup when entering or leaving Seated; the seat routines do that work. Releasing the seat removes the connection, restores walking support, and requests OnFoot.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamStatus.DONE
member.summary: Marks that the main scene-load waits have passed; queued level-load callbacks run next.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine registered for the session to call at a particular point. The load routine writes DONE after its main scene-load waits, then invokes callbacks registered with AddDoLevelLoadCallback. A callback added after the session is already DONE runs immediately. The routine continues after this status change, so DONE does not mean Load has returned or that callback work has finished.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamStatus.LOADING
member.summary: Marks that a StreamSession has entered its scene-load path.

remarks.para: Load checks for NONE before writing LOADING. The routine then continues through asynchronous scene loading and setup. This value is a named stage code, not a percentage or an estimate of time remaining.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamStatus.NONE
member.summary: The default status of a new StreamSession, before its load path starts.

remarks.para: The StreamSession constructor does not assign the status field, so a newly constructed session uses the enum's zero value, NONE. Load checks for this value before it writes LOADING. Refresh creates a new session rather than copying the previous session's status.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Seat.AxisAssignment.LeanFwdBack
member.summary: Value 0: the seat-control option labeled for forward/backward leaning.

remarks.para: The primary and secondary inputs are each a pair of numbers: one up/down value and one left/right value. A Seat stores a saved response choice for each of those four values. The integer here identifies an enum option; it is not an input reading or movement amount.

The labels name possible seat-control responses. The saved native input and pose callbacks checked for this correction do not read the four saved assignment fields, so these callbacks do not establish which runtime effect each choice produces.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates.All
member.summary: Combines the Hide, Cull, and Despawn flag bits (1 | 2 | 4 = 7).

remarks.para: All is the combined mask Hide | Cull | Despawn, with value 7 (1 | 2 | 4 = 7). These are independent flags, not a choice of one strongest action. The enum constant itself does not set a status. A callback is a registered routine the manager calls when a status flag changes. When InactiveObjectManager processes an InactiveStatus record, it calls the registered callback routines for Hide, Cull, or Despawn only when that flag changed from its prior processed state.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates.Cull
member.summary: Represents the Cull flag; standard entity handlers can hibernate physics and disable its MarrowBehaviour components.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the manager or entity calls when a status flag changes. For a standard MarrowEntity, the registered culling resolve handler adds or removes the Culling hibernation source, one reason the entity's physics is suspended; it also disables or re-enables MarrowBehaviour components (attached scripts that run parts of the entity's game behavior) and notifies culling handlers, registered routines called about culling changes. When the entity changes from no hibernation reasons to at least one, each MarrowBody with HasRigidbody (a Rigidbody to simulate) freezes and sleeps that Rigidbody (Unity's simulated physics body); when the last hibernation reason clears, each Rigidbody's saved physics state is restored. It is woken only if it was awake before hibernation; a Rigidbody that was already asleep is put back to sleep. Clearing only Culling does not wake physics while another reason remains.

The apply handler can change the entity's GameObject, the Unity scene object whose active state is being reconciled. Here, resolved flags means the Hide, Cull, and Despawn state the manager has processed. The GameObject can remain active when culling is prevented or host/parasite attachment conditions apply. Cull therefore does more than hide renderers and does not guarantee every culled GameObject is inactive.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates.Despawn
member.summary: Represents the Despawn flag for lifecycle notifications and entity deactivation.

remarks.para: A Collider is Unity's shape used to detect contacts or overlaps. A Tracker is a per-Collider component associated with a MarrowBody (physical body); despawn handling calls its OnDeactivate method. A GameObject is the entity's Unity scene object whose active state is changed, not just a renderer. A pool is the system that keeps objects for reuse; pool teardown means the entity is leaving that reusable-object system, and pool initialization means it is entering it. The standard MarrowEntity's registered despawn handlers (routines called for this status change) process Despawn=true by first notifying despawn handlers, then deactivating each body Tracker, then reconciling GameObject activation from the resolved flags. When Despawn=false is processed, activation is reconciled first and registered spawn handlers run afterward.

The flag itself does not return an entity to its pool or obtain a new spawn. The separate MarrowEntity.Despawn method calls the entity's associated Poolee component's Poolee.Despawn method to request return through that pool lifecycle; the Despawn flag does not call it. These are separate operations.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates.Hide
member.summary: Represents the Hide flag; standard entity handlers notify hide handlers and reconcile GameObject activation.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the manager or entity calls when a status bit changes. For a standard MarrowEntity, applying Hide=true first calls registered hide handlers, then reconciles the GameObject (the whole Unity scene object, not just its renderers) with resolved flags. Applying Hide=false reconciles activation first, then calls the registered unhide handlers. Cull or Despawn can still keep the entity inactive. A custom InactiveStatus uses its own callbacks and can implement a different response.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates.None
member.summary: Represents a zero mask: none of the Hide, Cull, or Despawn request bits is set.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called when a status changes. When all three request bits are clear, the manager's Apply stage can reconcile a standard MarrowEntity's GameObject as active. Releasing the Culling hibernation source, the Culling reason for suspending physics, happens through the later false (off) resolve callback. Update processes Resolve and then Apply, and performs that release only when both queues of waiting statuses are empty; finishing this individual status alone does not bypass that gate. The manager performs that work through its processing stages; another reason for suspension can still keep physics asleep, and custom InactiveStatus callbacks (routines for status changes) choose their own response. The None constant itself does not run callbacks or change a status.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.HandSchematic.index1
member.summary: Supplies the measured index finger base position used to align the game’s hand rig with the model.

remarks.para: A pivot is a bone’s reference point. The proximal bone is the finger’s base near the palm, the intermediate bone is its middle section, and the distal bone is its end section. Distances here run between those reference points.

This Vector3 contains the index finger’s proximal bone-pivot position in metres in the calibrated hand schematic frame. Precomputation measures the finger base relative to the humanoid Hand pivot, applies the palm-alignment correction, and rotates it into the schematic frame. It is not the bone’s raw localPosition or a world-space position.

ArtRig compares the X component with the reference index finger position multiplied by handSizeMult, the avatar’s hand-size scale factor that scales the fixed reference hand to this avatar, then shifts the finger base by that difference. The inspected alignment uses X only; Y and Z remain stored measurements. Changing the stored vector does not automatically move an already configured finger, and precomputation replaces it from the model’s bones.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.HandSchematic.index2
member.summary: Reports the distance from the index finger’s proximal pivot to its intermediate pivot, in metres.

remarks.para: A pivot is a bone’s reference point. The proximal bone is the finger’s base near the palm, the intermediate bone is its middle section, and the distal bone is its end section. Distances here run between those reference points.

PrecomputeAvatar measures the straight-line distance between the humanoid proximal and intermediate bone positions and stores it in this schematic. This is a distance between two joint pivots, not a measurement to the fingertip or the visible finger mesh’s bounds.

Changing this stored number does not stretch the finger in the inspected ArtRig alignment: that code uses the finger-base position fields instead. Precomputation measures and replaces the number again from the model’s bones.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.SoftEllipse.XBias
member.summary: Shifts the center of the limb cross-section along its side-to-side axis by a fraction of its radius.

remarks.para: The shift is XRadius × XBias × eyeHeight, so the bias has no unit. Zero centers the profile. A positive value shifts toward the positive profile axis and a negative value shifts the other way. At radius 0.03, eye height 1.6 metres and bias 0.5, the center shifts 2.4 centimetres before mesh-generation scale factors.

The positive and negative edges are radius × (bias + 1) and radius × (bias - 1), scaled by eye height. Bias shifts the section without changing its total width. These are the limb profile’s cross-section axes rather than fixed world axes; the left-side calculation mirrors its X direction.

The shape calculation blends this value with neighboring profiles. Editing the stored description does not rebuild an existing collider or move the visible model’s bones; calibration must use the updated profile again.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.SoftEllipse.XRadius
member.summary: Sets the side-to-side half-size of an avatar limb cross-section, as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: An ellipse is an oval; this radius measures from its center to its edge along the profile’s X axis. Avatar’s limb-shape calculations multiply the radius by eyeHeight to obtain metres. For example, 0.03 at an eye height of 1.6 metres gives a 4.8-centimetre half-size, or 9.6 centimetres across with zero bias, before mesh-generation scale factors.

Increasing the radius makes the generated limb section thicker along that axis. XBias shifts its center by a fraction of this radius. The profile is blended with neighboring sections along the limb; it is not a global world-space axis.

The description supplies inputs for generated collision geometry. Changing a struct field alone does not replace an existing collider or resize the imported visible mesh; physics calibration must regenerate the shape.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.SoftEllipse.ZBias

remarks.para: The shift is ZRadius × ZBias × eyeHeight, so the bias has no unit. Zero centers the profile. The positive and negative edges are radius × (bias + 1) and radius × (bias - 1), scaled by eye height. Bias shifts the section without changing its total width. These are the limb profile’s cross-section axes rather than fixed world axes; the left-side calculation mirrors its X direction.
