For example, 0.03 at an eye height of 1.6 metres gives a 4.8-centimetre half-size, or 9.6 centimetres across with zero bias, before mesh-generation scale factors.

Increasing the radius makes the generated limb section thicker along that axis. ZBias shifts its center by a fraction of this radius. The profile is blended with neighboring sections along the limb; it is not a global world-space axis.

The description supplies inputs for generated collision geometry. Changing a struct field alone does not replace an existing collider or resize the imported visible mesh; physics calibration must regenerate the shape.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.OnDeath
member.summary: Records the puppet's death and notifies the brain's death listeners.

remarks.para: The physical puppet is the NPC's simulated body. During pool initialization, setup for an object managed for reuse in later spawns, the brain subscribes this handler to PuppetMaster's death notification. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; a coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue across later frames. The handler sets isDead to true, calls onDeathDelegate, then calls onNPC_DeathDelegate. Both callbacks receive this brain, and either can be absent.

If an arena entrance coroutine handle is stored, the handler then stops that coroutine and resets entranceTimer to 120 seconds. Calling this handler yourself only performs this bookkeeping: it does not request the puppet's death. It has no check that suppresses a repeated call, so calling it again can notify listeners again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.OnResurrection
member.summary: Records the puppet's return to life and notifies .

remarks.para: The physical puppet is the NPC's simulated body. The brain connects this handler to PuppetMaster's resurrection notification during pool initialization, setup for an object managed for reuse in later spawns. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. It sets isDead to false before invoking the callback with this brain. Calling the handler yourself does not revive the physical puppet, restore health, or restart the arena entrance countdown.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.SetAngularVelocity(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Adds a randomly directed spin to the NPC's physical body, with the added speed chosen between the two supplied values.
member.param: Lower end of the random angular-speed change, in radians per second.
Upper end of the random angular-speed change, in radians per second.

remarks.para: World space uses the scene's fixed axes regardless of which way the NPC faces. This chooses one random rotation axis in that space and passes the resulting vector to the MarrowEntity on this brain's GameObject with VelocityChange mode, which requests an addition to the spin rate for the next physics simulation step. The center of mass is the combined balance point weighted by each body's mass. Physics joints are simulated connections between body parts. The entity applies it to its physical rigidbodies, the parts moved by Unity's physics simulation, and also adds motion around their shared center of mass. If the entity cannot be found in its component cache, nothing is applied.

The method adds to existing motion. It does not set an exact final spin or continually maintain a speed. For example, passing 1 and 2 requests an added spin between 1 and 2 radians per second, about 57 to 115 degrees per second; joints and later physics can alter the resulting movement. Repeated calls add further changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.SetBaseConfig(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig)
member.summary: Stores the enemy configuration override on the brain's navigation behaviour and updates the brain's recorded death flag from that configuration.
member.param: Configuration to store, or null to clear the behaviour's override.

remarks.para: A configuration groups settings such as roaming, attacks, sensors, and the puppet's requested state. This method stores the reference; it does not immediately copy those settings into the behaviour or change PuppetMaster's physical state. BehaviourBaseNav.ApplyOverrideConfig is the separate operation that applies a configuration's values immediately.

With a valid behaviour, isDead becomes true only when the supplied configuration exists and its puppetState is Dead. Null, Alive, and Frozen configurations set the flag false. The method also sets _wasConfigSet, preventing pool initialization from clearing this override through its automatic reset. Pool initialization is setup for an object managed for reuse in later spawns. Calling SetBaseConfig again is allowed. With no valid behaviour, the method leaves the brain unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.SpawnGroupIgnore(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sends this brain and an ignore flag to listeners of .
member.param: True adds this brain to a connected SpawnGroup's ignored set; false removes it from that set.

remarks.para: SpawnGroup installs its listener when this NPC spawns and removes it when the NPC despawns. This call only raises the event. It does not directly despawn the NPC, disable its AI, or remove it from the group's living or dead collections. Other listeners can give the flag their own meaning, so a brain without a connected group does not gain a group-management effect from the name alone.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.StartArenaEntranceTimer(System.Single)
member.summary: Starts a countdown that requests PuppetMaster's Dead state when it runs out, providing a time limit for an NPC's arena entrance.
member.param: Countdown duration in unscaled seconds; the optional argument is 120 seconds.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue across later frames. This coroutine subtracts the elapsed unscaled frame time, then waits for the next frame. Unscaled time is independent of Unity's timeScale, so slowing the game does not stretch a five-second countdown into a longer countdown. Once a later check finds entranceTimer at or below zero, it sets puppetMaster.state to Dead and ends. A valid puppetMaster is required at expiry. A zero or negative starting time reaches that request without first waiting for another frame.

Starting again overwrites the shared entranceTimer and stores a new coroutine handle without stopping an older coroutine. Multiple running countdowns can therefore subtract from the same value. To restart an ordinary single countdown, call StopArenaEntranceTimer before starting it again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.StopArenaEntranceTimer
member.summary: Stops the stored arena entrance coroutine and resets its countdown value to 120 seconds.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue across later frames; its handle is the reference used to stop that work. This only acts when arenaEntranceRoutine is non-null. It does not start a replacement countdown and does not clear that handle, so a non-null handle is not proof that the timer is running. If StartArenaEntranceTimer was called repeatedly without stopping, this stops only the most recently stored coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.Awake
member.summary: Prepares one spawn-cancellation slot for each group and puts every assigned CrateSpawner into manual mode.

remarks.para: Manual mode lets the encounter control its spawners. The cancellation array is sized from spawnGroups at this point, so configure the groups before initialization. Null groups or null spawners are not skipped. Replacing the group array with a different-sized array later can leave cancellation slots out of step with group indices.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.CompleteEncounter
member.summary: Records encounter completion, releases its music override, and invokes once for that completion cycle.

remarks.para: It acts only while _complete is false. It stops all Unity coroutines attached to this component, sets _complete to true and _isEncounterActive to false, then requests the audio manager to stop the override if encounterMusic is assigned. The completion event has no arguments.

This method does not kill or despawn NPCs, complete individual groups, reset completeCount, or cancel the asynchronous encounter spawn loops. Those loops use cancellation tokens rather than Unity coroutines. ForceStopCompContext performs the separate forced group-completion and removal sequence, including PauseEncounter's cancellation request and its SERIES indexing limitation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.ForceStopCompContext
member.summary: Requests a pause, kills the groups' living NPCs, marks each group complete, starts their removal, and completes the encounter.

remarks.para: This is the ForceStopAndComplete Inspector context-menu action with killing enabled. It requests the groups' puppet death states, calls each group's CompleteGroup, and starts DespawnAllBrains with the group's delay enabled. The removal work can continue after this method returns; the encounter's completion event does not mean every NPC has already disappeared.

It uses PauseEncounter first. In SERIES mode after a group has completed, that pause can select the preceding group's cancellation slot rather than the loop started at completeCount. Do not assume the name guarantees immediate cancellation of every asynchronous operation.

The bulk DespawnAllBrains helper copies its dead and living brain sets into the same array starting at index zero for both copies. With both populations present, the second copy can overwrite some dead entries and leave empty slots. Its later removal processing can fail on those empty slots, so completing or resetting the encounter cannot promise that every NPC will successfully disappear, even after the asynchronous work has had time to run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.ForceStopContext
member.summary: Requests a pause, kills and removes the groups' NPCs, and resets the encounter so it can be started again.

remarks.para: This is the ForceStopAndReset Inspector context-menu action with killing enabled. It calls ForceStopAndReset(true), which requests living puppets' deaths, starts removal of all group brains without the group delay, starts dead-brain cleanup, clears each group's completion flag, and cleans up its spawn tracking.

After the group reset calls, _complete and _isEncounterActive are false, completeCount is zero, and OnEncounterReset is invoked without arguments. It does not clear isWarmed. Removal is asynchronous, so reset notification can arrive before all NPCs have disappeared. The SERIES cancellation-slot limitation described by PauseEncounter also applies.

The bulk DespawnAllBrains helper copies its dead and living brain sets into the same array starting at index zero for both copies. With both populations present, the second copy can overwrite some dead entries and leave empty slots. Its later removal processing can fail on those empty slots, so completing or resetting the encounter cannot promise that every NPC will successfully disappear, even after the asynchronous work has had time to run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.OnDestroy
member.summary: Requests cancellation of the encounter's stored spawn loops when Unity destroys the component.

remarks.para: PARALLEL mode checks every cancellation slot. SERIES mode checks slot zero when completeCount is zero, or slot completeCount minus one when the count is positive. SERIES starting uses slot completeCount, so these indices can differ after the first group. Sources that are null or already cancelled are skipped.

This callback does not perform the full force-reset sequence, invoke completion, or stop the encounter music override. It also does not cancel the separate warmup tasks, which do not receive these tokens.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.PauseEncounter
member.summary: Requests cancellation of encounter spawning, releases its music override, and clears the active flag while preserving completion progress.

remarks.para: PARALLEL mode cancels each stored group token. SERIES mode selects slot zero for completeCount = 0, otherwise slot completeCount minus one. For example, with one group completed, SERIES start uses group index 1 while pause cancels slot 0. That discrepancy can leave the later group's loop running.

Cancellation affects the loop and its cancellable waits; already spawned NPCs are not frozen, killed, or despawned by this method. Warmup tasks do not use these tokens. The method preserves _complete and completeCount, and StartEncounter can start again only if completion has not been recorded. It also leaves token-source references stored after cancellation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.Start
member.summary: Registers the groups' NPC assets and gathers their spawn settings, crate randomizers, and optional spawner toggles.

remarks.para: For a group with an EncounterProfile, this registers each NPCProfile's spawnable with AssetSpawner and gathers the group's AI settings. It examines each assigned spawner's GameObject for a SpawnerToggle and adds any found to the group's list. It enables useSpawnerToggle when the list count matches the spawner count.

This prepares spawning; it does not itself start the encounter's spawn loops. Unity normally calls Start once. Manually calling it again can append the same toggles again, so it is not a general refresh operation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.StartEncounter
member.summary: Starts or resumes group spawning and cues the encounter music, provided the encounter is neither active nor complete.

remarks.para: PARALLEL starts a loop for every group. SERIES starts the group at index completeCount, so an ordinary paused encounter retains its group progress. Starting a group sets it up, cancels its previous stored token if necessary, creates a new cancellation source, and starts asynchronous spawning governed by that group's limits and delays.

If encounterMusic is assigned, the shared audio manager receives volume, fadeInTime, fadeOutTime, and loop. The music cue requests timed release as well as looping. If playerEntity is a valid cached activator, the method also applies each group's configured investigation or aggression request toward its target reference. Calling this method again while active, or after completion, does nothing. It does not automatically run WarmupEncounter.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.WarmupEncounter
member.summary: Starts spawning an initial population of NPCs for the configured groups before the ordinary encounter loop runs.

remarks.para: Each warmup task sets up its group and spawns until the living count reaches maxAlive or the total spawned count reaches totalSpawn. It uses the group's EncounterProfile when available and ordinary spawners otherwise, with a short delay between completed spawn requests. This creates NPCs; it is more than loading assets.

PARALLEL warms every group; SERIES warms only the first group. isWarmed is set before the tasks finish and blocks later calls, so it is a request latch rather than a readiness check. PauseEncounter and OnDestroy do not cancel these warmup tasks through _spawnCTSs. ForceStopContext does not clear isWarmed for a second warmup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.CreateListFromSpline
member.summary: Rebuilds from the assigned spline's knot positions in world space.

remarks.para: A knot is a control point on the spline. This method clears the existing list first, then transforms each knot position using roamSpline's Transform, including its position, rotation, and scale. It adds one point per knot in spline order; it does not sample extra points along curved sections.

If roamSpline is missing, the list remains empty. objectPoints is not a fallback for this helper. The list supports closest-point lookup and the selected-object gizmo; spawning builds a separate runtime waypoint array directly from the spline or objectPoints.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.CreateRoamArea
member.summary: Creates a new child object with a RoamArea and assigns it as this settings component's roaming area.

remarks.para: It uses zone, or searches the parents for a Zone when none is assigned. With no zone it logs a message and creates nothing. With a zone it creates a new child every call, even if roamArea already refers to another object.

The new area's height initially matches this settings object's world height. If the zone has a BoxCollider, its local XZ center becomes the area's local XZ position, while its Y position is retained. The collider's local size is copied into the area's 2D and 3D dimensions. Those dimensions are not multiplied by the zone Transform's scale. Without a collider, the child and component still exist but this size-copy step is skipped.

ZONE and ZONE3D roaming pick targets from the assigned area's world position and dimensions. This helper does not change roamMode, turn on overrideRoam, or replace settings already copied to previously spawned NPCs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.GetClosestWaypoint
member.summary: Finds the spline knot nearest to this settings object's position, rebuilding the helper waypoint list first.
member.returns: Zero-based index of the nearest knot, or 0 when the rebuilt list is empty.

remarks.para: It measures straight-line 3D distance in world space, not walking distance along the navigation mesh or distance along the spline. Equal distances keep the earlier list entry. A result of 0 from an empty list does not identify a valid point. This helper uses roamSpline, not objectPoints, and does not itself change startWaypointIndex.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.GetStartIndexByDist
member.summary: Stores the nearest spline knot's index in .

remarks.para: This calls GetClosestWaypoint, which clears and rebuilds orderedWaypointList from roamSpline before comparing world-space 3D distances. With no points it stores 0. It changes the starting choice for a later spawn or reactivation setup, not a current NPC's path. Random waypoint evaluation can choose a different first point.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.GetZoneArea
member.summary: Copies the zone BoxCollider's XZ size and calculated center/displacement into the horizontal roaming helper fields.

remarks.para: It writes roamXz from the collider's local X and Z size, roamOffset from zone.worldPosition plus collider.center on X and Z, and spawnerOffset from this object's localPosition minus collider.center on those axes. The second component of each Vector2 represents Z.

This adds a local collider center directly to a world position without applying rotation or scale. For an unrotated zone at world (10, 0, 20) with collider center (2, 0, 3), roamOffset becomes (12, 23). These are the implemented calculations, not a general conversion of a rotated collider into world bounds.

If zone is unassigned, it searches parents for one. A valid zone is required; a missing BoxCollider causes the copy to be skipped. This does not create a RoamArea or reapply settings to existing NPCs. In LEGACY mode roamOffset is later subtracted from homePosition, so inspect the copied value rather than treating it as an absolute movement target.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.GetZoneArea3D
member.summary: Copies the zone BoxCollider's XYZ size and calculated center/displacement into the three-dimensional roaming helper fields.

remarks.para: It writes roamXyz from collider.size, roamOffset3D from zone.worldPosition plus collider.center, and spawnerOffset3D from this object's localPosition minus collider.center. The collider center is local, so direct addition does not rotate or scale it into world space. Unit scale and aligned axes are needed to interpret the copied size as the same dimensions as the world collider.

If zone is unassigned, it searches parents for one. A valid zone is required; with no BoxCollider the size/offset copy is skipped. This helper does not create a RoamArea. The audited spawn and reactivation paths do not read roamOffset3D or spawnerOffset3D to position the NPC or its roam targets.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.OnDrawGizmosSelected
member.summary: Shows the helper waypoint start or LEGACY roam rectangle when this settings object is selected in the Unity editor.

remarks.para: Drawing requires overrideRoam. WAYPOINTS draws a wire sphere at orderedWaypointList[startWaypointIndex] when the helper list is nonempty; the index must be valid. LEGACY draws a flat rectangle using roamXz, centered at this settings object's world position minus roamOffset.

The drawing does not rebuild the helper list or change an NPC's route. The LEGACY runtime center uses the NPC's homePosition minus roamOffset, so the drawing can differ when a separate homeTransform defines home. ZONE and ZONE3D do not get a rectangle from this callback.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.Cleanup
member.summary: Clears the group’s tracked NPCs and counters, unregisters its spawner listeners, and calls with this group.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

Also resets the spawner index to zero, removes the group’s own death and resurrection handlers from its stored callback fields, and sets isSetup to false. It leaves isComplete unchanged. Calling Cleanup again can invoke OnCleanup again; there is no once-only guard here.

This clears bookkeeping, not the NPCs in the scene. It neither kills nor despawns them, and it does not walk the existing NPCs to remove every listener previously attached to their brains. Delayed removal tasks and the encounter’s spawning tasks have their own lifecycle; clearing these sets does not cancel them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.CompleteGroup
member.summary: Marks this group complete, raises its completion callbacks, starts corpse cleanup, and unregisters its spawner listeners.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

The first call sets isComplete to true, invokes onComplete without arguments, then invokes OnGroupComplete with this group. With maxDead equal to zero it starts WaitAndDespawnAllDead; otherwise it starts DespawnToMaxDeadCount. It does not wait for those tasks to finish before returning.

Later calls do nothing while isComplete remains true. The method can be called even while NPCs are alive: it does not check IsAllDead, kill living NPCs, or cancel the encounter’s spawning task. It also leaves isSetup true, so Setup alone will not register the listeners again after this completion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.Despawn
member.summary: Requests removal of the tracked dead NPC with the lowest spawn-event ID.

remarks.para: An empty dead set does nothing. Selection uses the NPC’s pool spawn ID, not its death time or distance from the player. Equal IDs do not give a stable ordering through the set.

For a positive despawnInterval, the selected brain is removed from the group’s spawned, alive and dead sets immediately, then its body remains in the scene for that many scaled game seconds before the despawn effect and physical removal are requested. For a zero or negative interval this method takes its immediate effect/removal path. A delayed request returns before the body disappears.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.DespawnToMaxDeadCount
member.summary: Requests corpse removals until the tracked dead population is at or below .

remarks.para: While the dead set contains more than maxDead brains, it calls Despawn once, waits despawnInterval scaled game seconds, then checks the set again. Each selection therefore follows Despawn’s lowest-spawn-ID rule. The method returns a UniTask, which you can await to wait for this trimming loop.

A positive-delay Despawn stops tracking its selected brain before its body disappears, and the trimming loop waits separately rather than awaiting that brain’s removal task. Finishing the loop means its count test passed; it does not independently verify that every requested despawn has succeeded. Keep delay values nonnegative for the awaited delay calls; this method supplies no clamp or cancellation token.

A UniTask represents work that may continue over later frames. Awaiting it waits for that method’s task to finish; starting it without awaiting allows your caller to continue while the work is still pending.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.GetAISettings
member.summary: Builds an array containing the component on each assigned spawner’s GameObject.

remarks.para: The array has exactly spawners.Length entries in matching order. A missing SpawnAISettings logs an error and leaves that entry empty; it does not create a component. Calling this again replaces the array, which is useful after changing the spawner list.

SpawnProfileAsync uses the matching entry to assign an NPC profile’s overrideConfig before spawning. An empty settings entry is therefore not safe for that path. Setup does not call this collection method; Encounter.Start prepares it for groups with an encounter profile.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.GetCrateRandomizers
member.summary: Finds each spawner’s RandomizeCrate component, disables its automatic startup spawn, and caches it for group-controlled random spawning.

remarks.para: The component must be on the spawner’s own GameObject. For every found randomizer this sets spawnOnStart to false, even if that spawner is already in the cache. Existing dictionary entries are retained rather than replaced or cleared.

SpawnAsync checks this cache and asks a found randomizer to select and spawn a crate. SpawnProfileAsync follows its NPC profile instead. If you replace or remove a randomizer at runtime, this collection call alone does not remove its old dictionary entry.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.IsAllDead
member.summary: Tests whether the recorded death count has reached , the group’s completion target.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

The test is DeadCount >= totalSpawn. It does not inspect whether each currently tracked NPC is dead. With totalSpawn equal to zero it returns true immediately. Resurrection does not subtract from DeadCount, so reaching the target can remain true while an NPC is alive again.

For example, a target of three is reached when three death callbacks have been recorded. Repeated death callbacks can increase that counter even for a brain already in the dead set. Use the alive set’s count when your question is whether any tracked living NPC remains.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.IsOverMaxAlive
member.summary: Tests whether the tracked living population exceeds .

remarks.para: Compares the alive set’s current number of entries with maxAlive, using a strict greater-than test. With maxAlive = 4, four living brains returns false and five returns true.
This only reports the comparison; it does not spawn, kill or remove an NPC. The result reflects the group’s tracking, which can change before a delayed corpse removal finishes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.IsOverMaxDead
member.summary: Tests whether the tracked corpse population exceeds .

remarks.para: Compares the dead set’s current number of entries with maxDead, using a strict greater-than test. With maxDead = 2, two dead brains returns false and three returns true.
This only reports the comparison; it does not spawn, kill or remove an NPC. The result reflects the group’s tracking, which can change before a delayed corpse removal finishes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.IsUnderMaxAlive
member.summary: Tests whether the tracked living population has room below .

remarks.para: Compares the alive set’s current number of entries with maxAlive, using a strict less-than test. With maxAlive = 4, three living brains returns true and four returns false. A zero cap never leaves room.
This only reports the comparison; it does not spawn, kill or remove an NPC. The result reflects the group’s tracking, which can change before a delayed corpse removal finishes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.IsUnderTotalSpawned
member.summary: Tests whether is below the group’s total spawn target.

remarks.para: The comparison is SpawnCount < totalSpawn. With a target of six, five returns true and six returns false. A target of zero returns false for an ordinary zero count.

SpawnCount increases when an AI brain is registered on spawn, but removing an NPC whose puppet is still alive can decrease it. This is therefore the encounter’s spawn-progress check, not an irreversible count of everything ever created. Calling this method does not itself create an NPC.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.KillAlive
member.summary: Kills the tracked living NPC with the highest spawn-event ID through its puppet controller.

remarks.para: The puppet is the physics controller for the NPC’s body. This chooses one entry from _aliveBrains by its spawn ID, not by distance, health or death time. It calls that puppet’s Kill method; it does not directly despawn the body.

Call this only when there is a valid living brain with its behaviour and puppet references available. The native path has no empty-set success case: it reaches a failure path when no NPC can be selected.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.KillAll
member.summary: Requests the Dead puppet state for every NPC currently in the group’s living set.

remarks.para: This writes the desired physics-body state on each living brain’s puppet. It leaves already-dead NPCs alone and does not itself request their despawn effects or return their bodies to the object pool. Death notifications and corpse cleanup follow their own paths.
The group’s ignore set is not consulted here. Ignoring an NPC for group mental commands does not protect it from this call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.ResetVariables
member.summary: Clears all four brain sets, zeroes the death and spawn counters, and restarts spawner selection at index zero.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.
It leaves isSetup and isComplete unchanged. It also leaves spawner listeners, callback fields and cached settings/randomizers in place, and does not kill or despawn existing scene NPCs.

Use this when you deliberately want to erase the tracking and count history. It is not a complete encounter restart: for example, Setup still returns early if isSetup was already true, and CompleteGroup still returns early if isComplete was already true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.Setup
member.summary: Connects the group to its assigned spawners so spawned AI can be tracked and their deaths and resurrections can update the group.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

If isSetup is already true, the call returns. Otherwise it sets that flag first, adds its own death and resurrection handlers to the stored callbacks, sets _spawnerIndex to zero, and registers this group as a spawn listener on every assigned spawner. Supply valid spawners before calling it.

It does not clear the brain sets, reset the counters or completion flag, collect SpawnAISettings, or rebuild the randomizer cache. Cleanup clears the setup flag; CompleteGroup unregisters spawner listeners while leaving that flag true. Calling Setup after completion alone therefore does not reconnect them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.SpawnAsync
member.summary: Attempts one spawn from the group’s currently selected spawner, using its cached randomizer when one is available.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

Supply a nonempty spawners array and a valid _spawnerIndex, and run Setup when you want the group’s listener to track the result. This method does not check maxAlive, totalSpawn or isComplete, or wait initialGroupDelay or spawnInterval. Those limits and delays belong to Encounter’s loops.

It captures the current spawner, chooses a later _spawnerIndex for the next call, then runs the captured spawner’s optional shouldSpawn callback. A false result skips spawning but does not undo the index change. When useSpawnerToggle is true, it searches the toggle list for a permitted next index; no permitted entry means no spawn. This search does not replace the spawner already captured for this call. A standard SpawnerToggle supplies the separate callback that can veto a disabled current spawner.

With a cached RandomizeCrate it starts that component’s random spawn and returns without awaiting that request’s completion. Otherwise it awaits the spawner’s ordinary spawn task, then requests a spawn effect if useSpawnEffect is true and the result has a cached MarrowEntity. Awaiting this UniTask therefore has a different completion meaning on the randomizer branch.

A UniTask represents work that may continue over later frames. Awaiting it waits for that method’s task to finish; starting it without awaiting allows your caller to continue while the work is still pending.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.SpawnProfileAsync
member.summary: Attempts to spawn the NPC profile entry indexed by at the currently selected group spawner.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

It takes encounterProfile.npcProfileList[SpawnCount], replaces the selected spawner’s crate reference with that entry’s spawnable, and replaces its matching SpawnAISettings.overrideConfig with that entry’s baseConfig. It prepares the spawner, then checks its optional shouldSpawn callback. A veto leaves those assignments in place.

The profile list is not wrapped or clamped, so SpawnCount must be a valid list index. The spawners array, matching aiSettings entry and profile references must also be valid. This method does not enforce totalSpawn, maxAlive or the encounter delays itself. The normal Encounter loop performs those checks before calling it.

It captures the current spawner and settings before choosing the next _spawnerIndex. The toggle search chooses a next index, not a replacement for those captured references; the current spawner’s separate callback can still veto this call. A successful ordinary spawn is awaited before an optional spawn effect is requested. This path does not use the group’s cached RandomizeCrate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.WaitAndDespawnAllDead
member.summary: Stops tracking the currently dead NPCs, waits one , then requests their effects and despawns.

remarks.para: At the start it copies the dead set into a separate array and removes those brains from the group’s spawned, alive and dead sets. It waits the interval once in scaled game seconds, then processes that saved array. An NPC that dies after the snapshot is not added to this request.

The delay starts when this method is called, not when each NPC died. A saved NPC can therefore remain visible after the group’s dead set has become empty. The task does not recheck that each saved brain is still dead before despawning it; await the returned UniTask when you need to wait for its removal work.

A UniTask represents work that may continue over later frames. Awaiting it waits for that method’s task to finish; starting it without awaiting allows your caller to continue while the work is still pending.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.ClearFromSocket
member.summary: Immediately releases the remembered socket and restores the plug host’s interaction.

remarks.para: Call this while a valid socket is remembered. It removes the grab and release handlers from that socket’s proxy grip, or from the plug host when the socket has no proxy grip, and detaches the corresponding held grip or host. A handler is a method registered to run when a grab or release happens.

It calls Socket.Unlock, which first clears Socket.IsLocked and Socket.LockedPlug and then invokes the no-argument unlock delegate, so unlock listeners see the socket as unlocked and empty. ClearFromSocket then clears _lastSocket, releases the plug’s physics body from the socket’s body, unpacks it, makes the host movable again, and enables its interaction.

It marks exit complete and resets the reinsertion timer to zero. It performs no exit animation, adds no launch velocity, and does not call OnPlugExitComplete. For example, an insertion override can use this to consume a magazine immediately instead of animating it back out.

This is not a complete state reset: it does not clear the entry-request or physical-grip flags or destroy an existing guide joint. A joint is a physics connection that limits how objects can move relative to each other.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.EjectPlug
member.summary: Requests an animated exit from the remembered socket.

remarks.para: This requires a valid remembered socket. It removes this plug’s grab and release handlers from the socket proxy grip, when present, then sets the exit-request flag. The plug can remain seated and the socket can remain locked until later animation frames finish.

Update, Unity’s once-per-frame method, performs the movement and final release. Animated exit needs the plug’s proxyGrip and the socket’s proxy grip to be configured. The exit-complete hook runs only after successful release, hand transfer and interaction cleanup.
An entry request takes priority when both entry and exit flags are set. This method does not clear the entry flag or reset the shared animation-stage flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.ForceInSocket(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Socket)
member.summary: Seats the plug immediately in an unlocked socket and runs its insertion-complete hook.

remarks.para: If the target socket is already locked, this returns without replacing its plug. Otherwise it skips the usual hover, distance and angle checks: it detaches the plug host from held hands, disables its interaction, joins its physics body to the socket’s body and parents the host under the socket. Parenting makes its local position and facing relative to the socket.

The final plug pose, meaning position and facing, uses the socket’s endTransform when assigned. Otherwise it uses endDistance along the socket’s local +X axis, its right direction. endDistance is in local scene units, usually meters when the socket has unit scale. The host’s offset from the plug is included so an off-center plug component can still seat correctly.

The socket locks and raises its lock event before this plug’s local locked flag is set. Then the host snaps to its final pose, entry and second-stage flags clear, grab/release handlers are installed, and OnPlugInsertComplete runs. The plug entity’s mass and center of mass are refreshed after that hook. There is no wait for an animation frame.

Provide a configured socket with valid hosts and Marrow physics components. For example, this can put a starting magazine straight into a weapon. An insertion override can consume or remove it, so completion of this call does not guarantee that the override left it seated.

member.param: The configured destination socket; an already locked socket is left unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.OnHandFixedUpdate
member.summary: Requests hand alignment toward a nearby socket and starts insertion when the held plug passes the position and angle checks.

remarks.para: This is registered with a hand’s skeleton-update callback while the host has attached hands. A callback is a method another part of the game calls at a particular update point. It returns early if the plug has no hover candidates, is locally locked, is not held, or has no controller hand/grip pair. It uses the first pair to estimate the plug pose from the controller wrist, grip and hand pose.

It selects the closest hovered socket to that desired plug position, requiring a socket host with a Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physical motion and velocity. Changing the selected socket resets the hand-alignment weight and its smoothing velocity. The hand-pose calculation uses the hand animator’s prepared pose and cached size factor.

The ordinary alignment check compares the plug’s +X axis to the socket’s +X axis, keeps the desired point within twice effectiveRadius of the socket axis, and requires it on the approach side of a plane whose normal comes from the Socket.cutoffDirection Transform's local +X direction. If cutoffDirection is not assigned, socket-local +X supplies that normal and the accepted side is negative socket-local X. effectiveRadius is the plug’s width allowance in meters. The angle limit comes from the cosine cached during setup, not a fresh reading of minSwingAngle.

For an accepted alignment, the target correction weight is 1 minus the desired plug-to-socket distance divided by the magnitude of influenceRadius, with that ratio limited to 0–1. influenceRadius is the socket’s correction range in meters and should be positive and nonzero. Rejected alignment targets weight zero. The weight is smoothed and its cube is passed with the requested hand pose; for example, a smoothed weight of 0.5 requests a correction strength of 0.125.

Insertion additionally checks the actual plug point in the socket’s local coordinates. Let x be inward distance along local +X, and y and z the sideways coordinates. At unit socket scale these are meters. A point velocity is a Rigidbody’s velocity at a particular world position, including motion there from rotation. Let v be the plug host Rigidbody’s point velocity at the AlignPlug transform position minus the socket host Rigidbody’s point velocity at the Socket transform position, transformed into the socket’s local direction frame and projected onto socket-local +X; v is measured in meters per second (m/s). Let dt be fixedDeltaTime in seconds. The per-step allowance s = max(0, v × dt) is a distance in meters for that physics step. The gate requires max(-x, 0), abs(y) and abs(z) each to be at most s + 0.03 meters. Thus fast inward movement widens the 3 cm allowance. A very close fallback also permits insertion when desired distance is strictly below 5 cm, sideways distance is strictly below half effectiveRadius, and the axis angle is strictly inside the cached limit.

An occupied socket can receive an eject request for its existing alignment plug using a wider s + 0.12 meter position allowance; it stays occupied until that exit finishes. The exit-complete flag can also temporarily block reinsertion near the socket. A successful new insertion detaches the host, disables interaction, joins the physics bodies, parents and locks it, then sets the entry-request flag. The later per-frame Update moves it into place.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.OnPlugExitComplete
member.summary: Override this empty hook to react after animated socket release and hand transfer have finished.

remarks.para: A hook is a method you can override in a subclass to add behavior at a specific point. The default implementation does nothing. The animated exit calls it after snapping the exit pose, clearing the transition and local lock flags, unlocking the socket, separating the physics bodies and enabling the plug host’s interaction.

Before this hook, the plug Rigidbody receives the socket’s world velocity minus 1.25 meters per second along the socket’s world right direction, and copies its angular velocity. World directions are measured in the scene rather than relative to an object. If the socket proxy grip had a hand attached, that hand is transferred to the plug’s proxyGrip before the hook.

The remembered socket reference is still present on this exit path. ClearFromSocket performs immediate cleanup without calling this hook. For example, AmmoPlug’s override clears its magazine’s inserted state and calls the magazine’s ejection handler.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.OnPlugHoverBegin(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Socket)
member.summary: Adds a nearby socket to the candidates checked while the plug is held.

remarks.para: It appends the supplied socket to the hover list and enables hand-alignment checking. It does not choose that socket as the current target, lock it or insert the plug. The next eligible hand update chooses the nearest candidate.

This method itself allows duplicate entries. Normal socket enter notifications first check the socket’s own set of hovering plugs to avoid repeating the same enter. For example, entering two socket trigger areas gives the held plug two candidates to compare.

member.param: The socket whose hover area the plug has entered.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.OnPlugHoverEnd(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Socket)
member.summary: Removes one hover candidate and stops hand alignment when none remain.

remarks.para: It removes the first matching socket from the candidate list. When the list becomes empty, it clears the active flag and resets the hand-alignment weight to zero. It leaves the smoothing velocity and remembered socket alone.

This notification can also happen when a socket locks: the socket ends hover for all its candidates before marking itself locked. Ending hover therefore does not by itself mean a seated plug has been released.

member.param: The socket to remove from the current hover candidates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.OnPlugInsertComplete
member.summary: Override this empty hook to react after the plug reaches its exact seated pose.

remarks.para: A hook is a method a subclass can override to add behavior at this point. The default implementation does nothing. Both ordinary insertion and ForceInSocket call it after setting the final host position and facing, clearing entry and second-stage flags, and installing the grab/release handlers for the socket proxy grip or plug host.

The socket lock event has already run. The plug entity’s physics mass and center of mass are refreshed after this hook returns, so the hook runs before that refresh. A subclass may immediately remove or consume the plug; completion is not a promise that it stays seated.

For example, AmmoPlug’s override marks the magazine inserted and calls its insertion handler. On a socket configured to clear inserted ammunition, the AmmoPlug override first calls ClearFromSocket. It then invokes the Magazine’s inherited SpawnEvents.Despawn method, which passes its Poolee (the component that tracks this reusable scene object) to Poolee.Despawn. When the Poolee reports the Magazine is already in a pool, Poolee.Despawn asks AssetSpawner (the game’s pool manager) to dispatch it. With an AssetSpawner instance, the manager checks the Magazine’s matching pool and the registered SpawnPolicy for its Poolee; it can return the Magazine through that pool or invoke the registered policy. If the manager instance is missing, dispatch returns immediately. When the Poolee is not in a pool, Poolee.Despawn runs its despawn and deinitialize callbacks (registered cleanup routines), disables the Magazine’s scene object, and logs an error. This path targets the Magazine, not this plug.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.AddCartridge(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoGroup,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds rounds to one shared ammo-group reserve, registering the group first if necessary.
member.param: The group asset whose KeyName identifies the shared reserve.
Number of rounds to add to that reserve.

remarks.para: Every registered cartridge in this group uses the same reserve count. For example, adding 20 rounds to a group makes 20 additional rounds available to each cartridge type mapped to that group; it does not add a separate 20-round balance for each type.

The group is identified by AmmoGroup.KeyName. After adding, onAmmoUpdateCount receives that key and the requested count, followed by onAmmoUpdate. Registering a new group can also send notifications while its cartridges are processed.
The method adds count directly without checking that it is positive or limiting the result to a maximum. Supply a nonnegative quantity when depositing ammunition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.AddCartridge(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds rounds to the cartridge's shared ammo group, or to its individual reserve if it has no registered group.
member.param: The cartridge definition whose group or individual reserve receives the rounds.
Number of rounds to add.

remarks.para: For grouped cartridges, the inventory looks up CartridgeData.Name to find the group. Adding ammunition for one member increases the balance available to every cartridge mapped to that group. Ungrouped cartridges are counted separately by their CartridgeData object.

After the addition, onAmmoUpdateCount receives the group key, or an empty string for an ungrouped cartridge, and the requested count. Then onAmmoUpdate runs. The reported number is the amount passed to this call, not the new reserve total.
The method adds count directly without a positive-value check or maximum clamp. A negative value reduces the stored balance and can make it negative.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.ClearAmmo
member.summary: Sets the configured light, medium, and heavy shared reserves to zero, then sends ammo-update notifications.

remarks.para: This uses the KeyName of each of the three assigned AmmoGroup assets. It leaves other registered group balances and the separate reserves for ungrouped cartridges unchanged.

It calls onAmmoUpdateCount once for every entry in the group-count dictionary, passing that entry's key and its current balance. The three cleared groups report zero; any other groups report their retained balances. Then it calls onAmmoUpdate once.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.GetCartridgeCount(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData)
member.summary: Returns the shared-group balance for this cartridge, or its individual balance if it has no registered group.
member.param: The cartridge definition whose available inventory balance should be read.
member.returns: The group's stored round count, or the ungrouped cartridge's stored count; zero when that count has no entry.

remarks.para: A registered cartridge is identified by CartridgeData.Name and uses the entire count stored for its group. Two cartridges mapped to the same group therefore return the same balance; the inventory does not divide that balance between them.

For an ungrouped cartridge, the lookup uses the CartridgeData object itself. A missing balance returns zero. This reads inventory bookkeeping; it does not count cartridge objects in the scene or rounds inside a particular magazine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.GetGroupByCartridge(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData)
member.summary: Finds the registered ammo-group key for the cartridge's name, returning the text "null" when there is no mapping.
member.param: The cartridge definition whose Name is used to look up the registered group.
member.returns: The saved group KeyName, or the string "null" when the name is not mapped.

remarks.para: Registration maps CartridgeData.Name to AmmoGroup.KeyName. This method reads that saved mapping; it does not scan the current cartridge lists in the group assets. Changing a list after registration therefore does not automatically change this answer.
The missing-group result is a string containing the four letters null, not a C# null reference.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.RegisterAmmoGroup(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoGroup)
member.summary: Registers a shared reserve under the group's KeyName and assigns its listed cartridge names to that reserve.
member.param: The asset supplying a unique KeyName and the cartridge definitions that should share its reserve.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, registers the light, medium, and heavy groups. Adding rounds through the AmmoGroup overload also calls this method. Once a KeyName already exists, registration returns immediately without rescanning the cartridge list or resetting that group's balance.

For a new group, each listed CartridgeData.Name is added to the name-to-group mapping. An existing cartridge-name mapping is retained rather than replaced, so reusing a cartridge name in a different group does not move it to that group.

Register groups before adding their cartridges. Once a name is registered, cartridge queries and changes follow the shared balance instead of the separate ungrouped balance. Registration can invoke the ammo-update callbacks, registered code called to report an ammo operation, while processing the listed cartridges.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.RemoveCartridge(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData,System.Int32)
member.summary: Subtracts rounds from the cartridge's shared or individual reserve, stopping the stored balance at zero.
member.param: The cartridge definition whose group or individual balance should be reduced.
Number of rounds requested for withdrawal.

remarks.para: Registered cartridges subtract from the group selected by CartridgeData.Name; ungrouped cartridges subtract from their own object-keyed balance. Removing one grouped cartridge's rounds changes the balance available to every cartridge in that group. An ungrouped cartridge with no stored entry is ignored.

For example, withdrawing 5 rounds from a balance of 3 leaves zero. onAmmoUpdateCount still receives the requested count of 5, not the actual decrease of 3, the new total, or a negative number. It receives the group key, or an empty string for an ungrouped cartridge. onAmmoUpdate follows.
Supply a nonnegative quantity for a withdrawal. There is no positive-value check: subtracting a negative count increases the stored balance.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoPlug.OnPlugExitComplete
member.summary: Marks the linked magazine as removed and refreshes its visible cartridges when the alignment system completes removal.

remarks.para: This is a completion callback: a method the inherited AlignPlug code calls after its removal transition has finished. The normal alignment update has already released the socket and separated the magazine's interaction object before calling this method.

The method first sets magazine.isMagazineInserted to false, then calls Magazine.OnEject. That call clears the magazine's bullet-art hiding flag and refreshes the cartridge display from the remaining ammunition count. A cartridge is one complete round of ammunition. The refresh runs only when the first cartridge target is a live Unity object and the art is not being hidden. Zero rounds request both displays hidden; one round requests only the first active; two or more rounds request both cartridge-art references active. SetCartActive skips a null or destroyed art reference, so requesting both active does not guarantee that both cartridge models can be displayed.

For example, removing a magazine that still contains three rounds clears its inserted flag and requests both cartridge-art references active when the first cartridge target is live and art is not hidden. SetCartActive skips null or destroyed art, and this removal refresh does not require a live second target. This method updates the linked magazine after removal; the inherited alignment system performs the physical removal. Assign magazine before completion occurs. The inserted flag is changed before the display refresh, so a failing display refresh does not undo that earlier flag change.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoPlug.OnPlugInsertComplete
member.summary: Marks the linked magazine as inserted, hides its cartridge display, and handles sockets that consume the physical magazine after insertion.

remarks.para: This is a completion callback: a method the inherited AlignPlug code calls after seating the magazine's interaction object. The normal completion routine has ended its insertion-transition flags before this callback runs. Physical alignment and socket locking are handled by the inherited code.

The method first sets magazine.isMagazineInserted to true, then calls Magazine.OnInsert. That call sets the bullet-art hiding flag and hides the first displayed cartridge, plus the second when its display target is configured. A displayed cartridge is the visible model of an ammunition round. For a normal removable magazine, this keeps those models hidden while the magazine is seated.

After updating the magazine, the method checks the remembered socket. If it is a live Unity object and its IsClearOnInsert property returns true, the method calls ClearFromSocket, then requests the linked magazine's despawn. ClearFromSocket releases the socket, removes the alignment grip handlers, separates the interaction objects, and clears the remembered socket. Despawn asks the magazine's pooled object to leave play and return to storage for reuse. Thus a socket can consume the physical magazine immediately after the inserted flag and display have been updated.

The base Socket reports IsClearOnInsert as false. For the older AmmoSocket type, it is true when the linked gun has a live internalMagazine configuration, which describes the gun's built-in magazine. That getter does not read AmmoSocket.despawnOnInsert. Other socket types can supply their own IsClearOnInsert behavior.

Assign magazine before insertion finishes. The flag and display changes happen before the consuming-socket check; a later failure does not roll back those earlier changes. Completion can therefore be followed by a despawn request rather than leaving a visible magazine locked in the socket.

member.summary: Calculates a world-space chest pose and neck pose that respond to tracked height, movement lean, support, and avatar proportions.
member.param: Provides measured heights, bone offsets and neck movement limits.
Tracked head pose in world space.
Left-hand SimpleTransform parameter containing position and quaternion rotation values; this implementation does not read it.
Right-hand SimpleTransform parameter containing position and quaternion rotation values; this implementation does not read it.
Source rig with head and chest poses and the orientation reference.
Elapsed seconds used by the heading-correction smoothing.
Receives the calculated neck pose in world space.
Mantling weight, describing the pull-over-a-ledge posture; used only in the hand-dominant support branch.
Weight describing support through the feet.
Weight describing support through the hands.
Additional height adjustment in world units, normally meters, added before height normalization.
member.returns: Calculated chest position and quaternion rotation in world space.

remarks.para: The posture curve input is the head's height above this animation rig's root along the current player-up direction, plus spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset, divided by the avatar's calibrated skull-joint height. The curve result is an angle in degrees. It is smoothed into _t1UpOffsetLerp, then combined with lean and other posture corrections to rotate the upper spine; it is not a requested lift in meters.

The calculation also uses the input rig's chest and head orientation, the smoothed _dragUp direction, neck range-of-motion data, and saved horizontal heading history. Support inputs select standing/velocity, climbing, and mantling curve blends as described by SolveT1UpOffset. The returned chest and outNeck contain world positions and quaternion rotations; the caller applies them to the skeleton.

The signature supplies head and hand poses by reference, but callers should use the returned chest and outNeck as the verified outputs rather than assume a hand pose was changed. The live routine uses this rig's current movement and suppression history, so it is not an independent curve-evaluation utility.

SimpleTransform stores a position and an orientation. Its rotation is a quaternion, Unity’s four-component representation of orientation. The handLf and handRt parameters contain those values, but this implementation does not read either value. spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are height adjustments in the same distance units as the calibrated skull-joint height, normally meters; support weights are unitless values used by the solve blend. The returned chest pose and outNeck are outputs; smoothing and heading history are stored on this AnimationRig instance.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.OnEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Updates the animation skeleton for the current body state, then fades any saved transition pose back out.

remarks.para: OnFoot runs the torso, hand-proximity and leg solve. Seated uses a separate pose-copy and counter-tilt path once the active seat is ingress-aligned; until then it uses the on-foot path. ActiveRagdoll uses its own pelvis-relative spine and hand posing and SwingCounterCurveRagdoll. The input is manager.remapHeptaRig, and elapsed time comes from Time.deltaTime in seconds.

After the main pose is built, the method resets pelvisLocalAnimOff to the identity transform, copies eye-gaze data, and, if _sampleBlendWeight is positive, smoothly lowers that saved-pose weight toward zero. At a weight below 0.01 it clears the weight and its smoothing rate. RigManager normally skips this animation-rig pass in the fully Ragdoll state and returns early while its controller rig is paused.

Ingress-aligned means the seated input rig has completed its alignment with the player/world ingress frame, so the seated branch is permitted to run; before alignment the on-foot path remains active. Identity for a SimpleTransform means zero position and no added rotation (the identity quaternion), not a request to teleport the avatar.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.OnFootSolve(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig,System.Single)
member.summary: Builds the torso and stepping-leg pose from an input rig while the character uses the on-foot calculation.
member.param: Source joint poses in world space; the normal caller supplies manager.remapHeptaRig.
Elapsed update time in seconds.

remarks.para: It first aligns this rig's root with inRig.centerOfPressure and takes that transform's up direction as the player-up direction. It updates the procedural chest/pelvis, corrects hand proximity to the torso, updates SLZ_Body's leg-calculation inputs, and uses the returned foot and ankle poses to solve the leg joints.

The calculation reads physical pelvis velocity, acceleration, knee displacement, and hand/foot support through the manager. It requires the configured avatar, body, and joint references; it does not create them. Its pelvis offset output is working animation data that the outer OnEarlyUpdate resets after the pose pass.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.OnRigEnable(System.Boolean)
member.summary: On re-enable, resets the spine correction history and records the rig's current horizontal heading.
member.param: True to reset the pose history; false leaves it unchanged.

remarks.para: With reEnable = true, it takes the rig transform's world forward direction, keeps X and Z, normalizes that two-number heading, and stores it for both the upper-spine and pelvis heading histories. It zeroes their smoothed angle corrections and smoothing rates, the posture-angle corrections and their rates, and _lastInHeadSwing.
With reEnable = false this override returns without those changes. It does not recalculate avatar proportions or rebuild curves.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.ReapplyTorsoProximity(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig,System.Single)
member.summary: Adjusts the rig hands using the avatar's hand shape and the input pose's recorded proximity to the torso.
member.param: Provides the BodyPose proximity information used for the corrections.
Elapsed seconds used to ease the hand-shape input.

remarks.para: Each side first eases its stored grip/curl value toward that controller's secondary-interaction axis with a blend fraction clamped from 20 × deltaTime to the range 0–1. The avatar then supplies hand bounds for that value, so an opening or closing hand changes the shape used for proximity correction.

The method converts the hand-bound offsets into world space, applies HeptaRig.ApplyTorsoProximity using inRig.bodyPose, and writes the corrected position and rotation of this rig's two hand transforms. It is a pose correction, not a physics collision event or a general-purpose collision solver.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.SetAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Adapts this rig's bone spacing and stepping calculation to the supplied avatar.
member.param: Avatar whose measured body proportions and offsets should be used.

remarks.para: It stores the avatar, sets local positions for the spine, chest, neck, head and clavicle joints from that avatar's measured offsets, and calls the inherited body-scale calibration. It also tells SLZ_Body to reset and recalibrate its locomotion dimensions and footstep inputs.

The method moves the second key of the upper-spine and pelvis velocity curves to an avatar-dependent input value while preserving that key's output value. Those curves need at least two keys. Each replacement key retains its output value but resets its tangents, which describe the curve slope at that key. It does not regenerate all six posture curves on each avatar change. Keep the avatar, body and joint references assigned before using it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.SetBodyState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState)
member.summary: Captures the current joint rotations to soften transitions between OnFoot and ActiveRagdoll.
member.param: The requested destination state.
The previous state, used to decide whether the standing/active-ragdoll blend applies.

remarks.para: Only OnFoot → ActiveRagdoll and ActiveRagdoll → OnFoot run this override's transition setup. OnEarlyUpdate then fades the sampled pose's influence toward zero as the new pose takes over.
Transitions involving Seated or the fully Ragdoll state do not trigger this capture here. This method prepares the animation transition; RigManager owns the actual body-state change.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.SolveSacrumUpOffset(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Selects and blends the pelvis's posture-angle curves for the supplied normalized height and support weights.
member.param: Height divided by the appropriate calibrated avatar height; a dimensionless curve input, not elapsed time.
Mantling posture weight, used after the climbing blend when hands provide more support than feet.
Foot-support weight used for branch selection.
Hand-support weight used for branch selection and the climbing blend.
Normal caller's horizontal speed divided by upper-plus-lower leg length, in leg lengths per second; its numeric value is clamped to 0–1 for the velocity blend.
member.returns: Blended posture-angle target in degrees.

remarks.para: The baseline is the inherited sacrum up-offset curve evaluated at heightWeight. When velocityInLegs is positive and footSupported > handSupported, it blends toward the velocity curve using velocityInLegs clamped to 0–1. When handSupported > footSupported, it blends toward the climbing curve using 1.3 × handSupported clamped to 0–1; within that branch, a positive mantle then blends toward the mantling curve using 1.3 × mantle clamped to 0–1. Equal hand and foot support uses the baseline.

All chosen curves receive the same heightWeight. The result is an angular posture target in degrees, later smoothed and used in the pelvis rotation calculation. This method itself does not move a transform or smooth the value. An illustrative baseline of 10 degrees and velocity-curve value of 30 at the same input, blended with velocityInLegs = 0.5, produces 20 degrees.

The normal AdditivePelvis caller projects the chest-to-animation-root displacement along player up, adds spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset (both height adjustments in world-distance units, normally meters), then divides by the avatar's calibrated chest-joint reference height in the same distance units. The result is a unitless heightWeight. This helper does not clamp that input; configured curves must exist for whichever branch is used.

Mantling means pulling the body over a ledge; footSupported and handSupported are unitless support amounts, not distances or forces. The helper preserves its existing support-weighted branches and returns an unsmoothed angle target; AdditivePelvis smooths and uses that target for its rotation calculation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.Teleport(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Applies a world-position displacement to the rig and updates its locomotion and heading history for the supplied rotation change.
member.param: Position delta in world units, normally meters, and quaternion rotation delta to apply to locomotion/history.
Whether to clear this rig's cached movement, lean and spine-correction smoothing state.

remarks.para: The position in displace is added to the current rig-root world position; it is a movement delta, not an absolute destination. For example, a position delta of (1, 0, 0) shifts it one world unit along world X. The rotation is used to update locomotion heading around its reference position and to rotate the stored horizontal spine headings. This override does not simply assign displace as the root's new transform.

With zeroVelocity = true it also clears the stored posture/yaw corrections, their smoothing rates, and inherited movement/lean history, and reseeds movement headings. These are animation and locomotion records; this override does not zero every physics Rigidbody. RigManager's higher-level teleport coordinates the other rigs.

A quaternion is a four-component orientation representation, not three degree angles. A Unity Rigidbody is the physics body that owns mass, pose and velocity. zeroVelocity controls the documented motion-history/cache reset path; it does not imply that every animation field or every external body is cleared.

It also compares the measured finger-base positions with the fixed reference hand, scaled by handSizeMult, the avatar’s hand-size scale factor.
