member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.AttenuateCurrent(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Changes the assigned sound source toward a chosen volume without replacing its clip.

remarks.para: fadeTar is a source-volume value: 0 is silent and 1 is full source volume. The method limits this argument to 0 through 1. If the source is stopped and the target is above zero, it calls Play before setting up the volume change.

With a positive fadeInTime, measured in real seconds, it sets isFading and calculates fadePerSec as the absolute difference between the target and current source volume divided by fadeInTime. UpdateFade must then run once per frame. For example, changing volume from 0.8 to 0.2 over 3 seconds sets a speed of 0.2 volume units per second. This can make the sound louder or quieter.

A zero or negative duration sets the volume immediately and clears isFading. This immediate path does not stop playback when the target is zero; a gradual fade to zero stops the source when UpdateFade finishes. Assign ambMus first.

member.param: Desired source volume, limited to 0 through 1.
Requested transition time in real seconds; zero or less changes volume immediately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.FadeOut(System.Single)
member.summary: Starts fading the assigned sound source to silence, or stops it immediately when a gradual fade cannot start.

remarks.para: A gradual fade requires the source to be playing, its current volume to be above zero, and fadeOutTime to be positive. It sets isFading, calculates fadePerSec, then sets fadeTarget to zero. UpdateFade advances the fade each frame and stops playback when it completes.

The speed is the larger of 0.04 and the previous fadeTarget divided by fadeOutTime, in source-volume units per real second. The previous fadeTarget is the old requested volume, which can differ from the volume currently heard. Thus fadeOutTime is not a promise of the exact elapsed time. For example, with previous target 0.8, current volume 0.4 and duration 2 seconds, the speed is 0.4 per second and silence is reached after about 1 second of updates. A second FadeOut call after the target has become zero selects the minimum speed of 0.04.

If the source is already stopped, its volume is zero or lower, or the duration is zero or negative, this method stops it immediately, sets its volume and target to zero, and clears isFading. It retains the assigned clip. Assign ambMus first.

member.param: Requested fade time in real seconds, used with the previous target volume to calculate speed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.UpdateFade
member.summary: Advances the source volume for one frame and finishes the fade when it reaches the target.

remarks.para: Call once per rendered frame while a fade is active. Audio2dManager does this for its entries whose isFading flag is true. The method itself does not check that flag, so calling it manually still changes volume even when isFading is false.

The volume step is fadePerSec multiplied by the time since the previous frame, in real seconds. This time is unscaled, so game slow motion does not slow the fade while updates continue. With speed 0.2 volume units per second and a 0.05-second frame, the step is 0.01. It moves upward or downward toward fadeTarget and uses the target directly when the remaining difference fits within the step. Completion happens on a frame update, rather than at an exact sub-frame instant.

After setting the source volume, it checks whether that volume is approximately equal to fadeTarget. If so, it clears isFading first, then stops the source if its resulting volume is zero or lower. Assign ambMus before calling this method.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.Awake
member.summary: Creates six sound sources for overlapping ambience and music, then starts loading their mixer routing.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, called when this component is first set up. It replaces ambAndMusics with six new AmbAndMusic entries and creates an AudioSource, the component that plays a sound, on a child object for each entry. Each source starts with automatic playback disabled, looping enabled, and 2D sound, so its volume is not based on distance from a world position.

Entries 0 through 2 are for ambience; 3 through 5 are for music. The current indices start at 0 and 3. Mixer loading can finish later, after this initialization returns. Calling Awake again rebuilds the array and creates more child sources.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.CoFadeReverbData(System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a frame-by-frame sequence that blends the mixer's captured reverb values toward reverbObj.

remarks.para: The returned sequence is a coroutine: code that pauses and continues over several frames when Unity runs it. Calling this method alone creates the sequence; it does not start it. FadeToNewReverb starts it after capturing current mixer values into tempData.

fadeTime is measured in game seconds. Each update uses elapsed game time divided by fadeTime as a blend fraction, limited to 0 through 1 for the actual value calculation. Slow motion lengthens the fade in real time, and pausing game time pauses its progress. At halfway, each mixer value is halfway between its captured value and the target preset's corresponding value. The values keep the units of their individual mixer parameters.

The sequence reads reverbObj and tempData on each resumed frame. Keep their entries aligned with each other and with the mixer's parameter names. FadeToNewReverb supplies a positive duration in normal use; this sequence does not validate a manually supplied duration. A zero or negative fadeTime never starts the blend: its progress fraction stays at 0, so the captured starting values are rewritten every frame and the sequence never finishes.

member.param: Transition duration in game seconds.
member.returns: A sequence to run with Unity's coroutine system.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.FadeToNewReverb(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AudioReverbData)
member.summary: Starts blending the mixer's current reverb settings toward the supplied preset.

remarks.para: Reverb is the lingering reflected sound that makes a space sound like a room or hall. This method remembers the old preset in prevReverbObj, assigns the new preset to reverbObj, stops any previous reverb fade, then reads the mixer's current values into tempData. A new fade therefore starts from the values currently applied, including a partially finished earlier fade.

It chooses the duration from the fourth preset entry, normally DecayTime: how long the reverb lasts, in seconds. If the new decay time is shorter than the captured current value, the transition uses minFadeTime. Otherwise it uses the increase in decay time, capped at 5 seconds and raised to minFadeTime if needed. For example, an increase from 1 to 3 seconds gives a 2-game-second transition when minFadeTime is 0.35. If minFadeTime is above 5, that larger minimum wins.

The transition runs over several frames using game-scaled time, so slow motion stretches its real duration. The preset must be assigned, its parameter names must match the loaded mixer, and its parameter array must match the capture buffer's layout. The manager normally creates a 14-value capture buffer. This method starts the transition; it does not wait for completion.

member.param: Preset whose named reverb parameter values become the fade targets.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.GetParamVal(System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: Reads a named exposed parameter from the assigned audio mixer.

remarks.para: An exposed parameter is a mixer setting made accessible by name to game code. Its unit depends on that setting; for example, a volume parameter can use decibels, while a time parameter can use seconds. The supplied value initializes the output slot passed to the mixer read. This method ignores the mixer's success flag, so its return value alone does not tell you whether the name was found.
The mixer must be assigned. Use the mixer's GetFloat directly if you need to check whether the read succeeded.

member.param: Exact name of the exposed mixer setting.
Initial value supplied to the mixer read's output slot.
member.returns: The value left in the mixer read's output slot; no success flag is returned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.LoadMixers
member.summary: Loads the configured mixer if necessary and routes the six sources to its ambience and music output groups.

remarks.para: This starts asynchronous work, meaning it can pause while an asset loads and finish after the method returns. It checks the runtime MarrowSettings mixer asset, uses it immediately if already loaded, or waits for its load to complete. It then stores the mixer and assigns ambience routing to sources 0 through 2 and music routing to 3 through 5 when matching groups are found.

Awake, Unity's initialization callback, starts this work after creating the six source entries. If runtime settings or the configured mixer-asset reference are absent, the sequence finishes without routing sources. If the reference exists but its asynchronous load returns null (no mixer object), the continuation reaches a failing null-object check before looking up output groups; it does not take the absent-reference path. Assigning the mixer field later by itself does not reroute sources that already exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.OverrideCallback(System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a timed sequence that releases the music override and attempts to restore the remembered regular cue.

remarks.para: The returned sequence is a coroutine: code Unity can pause and resume over several frames. Calling this method only creates it. When first run, it sets a deadline to the current unscaled game time plus releaseTime, in real seconds, then waits frame by frame until that deadline is reached.

At the deadline it clears _isOverride before requesting the saved regular music. It uses a single clip when _overridenHasIntro is false, or an intro-plus-loop cue when both saved clips are available. It does not choose a playlist track or guarantee that the override source stops when there is no saved regular cue.

CueOverrideMusic starts this sequence for timed release with releaseTime equal to the override clip's length minus its requested fade-out time. For example, a 30-second clip and 2-second fade-out request release control after about 28 real seconds of resumed updates. The actual release occurs on a frame. Completion leaves the stored _overrideCallback reference assigned.

member.param: Real seconds to wait after the sequence first runs before releasing override control.
member.returns: A timed sequence for Unity's coroutine system.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.StopFadeRoutine
member.summary: Cancels the stored reverb-transition sequence and clears its handle.

remarks.para: A coroutine handle identifies work that Unity is continuing over several frames. If fadeRoutine is assigned, this method stops that work and sets the handle to null. It leaves the mixer values where the interrupted fade reached; it does not reset them to the old preset or jump them to the target. It does nothing when the handle is null. Ambience and music source-volume fades continue separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.StopMusic(System.Double,System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a stop of the selected regular music entry, rejecting older timestamped requests.

remarks.para: The timestamp is a number of real seconds since startup used to order requests. A timestamp strictly less than _timecodeMusic is ignored; an equal timestamp is accepted. An accepted request updates _timecodeMusic before handling override or playback state.

While _isOverride is true, this clears the remembered regular music and intro clips, so they will not be restored when the override ends. It returns without fading or stopping the override source and without cancelling the pending intro-to-loop sequence.

Otherwise it calls FadeOut on the entry selected by _curMus, then cancels and clears any pending intro-to-loop coroutine, a sequence that was waiting across frames to start a loop. Older entries already fading out are left to finish their own fades.

fadeOutTime is in real seconds, but is used to calculate a fade speed rather than an exact deadline. For a playing source above zero volume and a positive duration, the speed is the larger of 0.04 and that entry's previous requested target volume divided by fadeOutTime, in source-volume units per second. If the current volume differs from that old target, actual duration differs too. Other cases stop the selected source immediately. Update advances gradual fades each rendered frame.

member.param: Request-order timestamp in real seconds since startup; earlier timestamps are rejected.
Requested fade time in real seconds, used to calculate the source's fade speed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.StopMusic(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a stop of the selected regular music using the current realtime timestamp.

remarks.para: It passes the number of real seconds since startup to the timestamped StopMusic overload. If you previously supplied a future timestamp, this request can be rejected until that time is reached.

Without an override, the selected entry fades toward silence and its pending intro-to-loop sequence is cancelled. With an override, this only clears the remembered regular clips and leaves override playback running.

fadeOutTime is a requested number of real seconds. The underlying fade computes speed from the entry's old target volume, with a minimum of 0.04 source-volume units per second, so the exact duration can differ from the request. A zero or negative duration stops the selected regular source immediately when no override is active.

member.param: Requested fade time in real seconds; zero or less requests an immediate stop.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.StopOverrideMusic
member.summary: Releases override control and attempts to restore the remembered regular music cue.

remarks.para: If _isOverride is false, it does nothing. Otherwise it clears that flag first, stops the stored timed-release coroutine if one is assigned, and clears _overrideCallback. A coroutine is a sequence Unity was continuing over several frames.

It restores a saved single clip, or a saved intro and loop when both are available, using the remembered volume and fade settings. Restoring an intro cue can restart its intro. If no suitable saved cue exists, it makes no source-stop request, so this method does not guarantee that the override sound stops.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.Update
member.summary: Advances each active ambience or music volume fade once per rendered frame.

remarks.para: Unity calls Update every rendered frame while this component is running. It visits every ambAndMusics entry and calls that entry's UpdateFade only when isFading is true. The source-volume step uses real time since the previous frame, so slow motion does not slow these fades while updates continue.

The array, each entry and its sound source must be assigned. This method handles source volume; the reverb-transition coroutine, a sequence running across frames, advances separately using game-scaled time.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio3dManager.SetLowPassFilter(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a value for the configured mixer’s exposed parameter named LPF. It drives low-pass filtering only if the mixer asset maps LPF to that effect.

remarks.para: A low-pass filter allows lower frequencies through while reducing frequencies above its cutoff. An exposed mixer parameter is a named mixer setting that scripts can update. This method passes lpf to the configured mixer parameter named LPF. The value is a cutoff in hertz (cycles per second) only if that mixer exposes LPF as a cutoff; the mixer asset’s parameter graph is not established here. If it is a cutoff, lowering the value removes more high-frequency detail. For example, a value of 500 is a 500 Hz cutoff only under that condition.

The method writes the value directly and ignores the mixer’s success result. It does not clamp the value, fade to it, or tell the caller whether the write was accepted. Runtime settings and the loaded mixer asset must be available. Mixer loading initially writes 22000 to LPF, so a later loading pass can overwrite an earlier request.

member.param: Float passed to the exposed mixer parameter named LPF; it represents a cutoff frequency in hertz only if the configured mixer exposes LPF as a cutoff.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio3dPlugin.SLZ_Marrow_Plugins_IMarrowPluginLevelCallbacks_OnBeforeLevelLoad(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.LevelCrateReference)
member.summary: Requests registration of the configured reusable sound-object template and creates the shared if none is alive, on the normal callback path when the audio-player crate reference is nonnull.

remarks.para: The level-loading system calls this routine as a callback, a method invoked during that stage of loading. It reads the configured audio-player Spawnable from runtime MarrowSettings (the game's active settings asset). A Spawnable is a small settings value with two parts: a crate reference, which points to a content entry (a crate) in the game's asset warehouse by its barcode ID, and spawn-policy data, a separate settings asset used when objects are later taken from the pool. This callback uses only the crate reference: before handling the manager, it asks AssetSpawner to register that crate's reusable sound-object template with the object pool, the system that supplies reusable sound objects. Registration does not read the spawn-policy data. That data is used later, when a spawn request passes this Spawnable to the spawner (for example, Audio3dManager reads this same settings value when it plays a sound at a position): the spawner then reuses or creates a spawn policy from that data, and the policy takes the object from the pool. If the policy data is empty, that later spawn asks the pool directly. Runtime settings must be available.

Before handling the manager, the callback passes this settings Spawnable to AssetSpawner.Register. Register checks the crate reference before starting its separate registration work. If the reference is missing, registration fails immediately, so the callback does not continue to manager setup or return its usual completed task. With a present crate reference, Register looks up the crate right away, before this callback continues to manager setup. If that lookup fails, no pool is added, but the callback still continues to manager setup. If a matching pool already exists, the routine does not add another. Otherwise, it adds a pool entry and starts loading the template prefab (a saved object template). The lookup, check for an existing pool, and addition of a new pool all happen inside this callback, before manager setup. Only the template-prefab load can finish later; it may still be in progress when this callback returns, because the callback does not wait for it.

If the stored manager is missing or points to a destroyed Unity object, the plugin creates a new GameObject (a Unity scene object), adds Audio3dManager as a component (behavior attached to that object), stores the manager reference, and keeps the object alive across scene changes. An existing live manager is reused. The level argument does not choose a different template or manager in this routine. If the manager is newly added, its Awake initialization callback, Unity's setup routine, starts LoadMixers. That routine returns without populating its mixer-channel groups if runtime settings or the configured default-mixer reference is absent. If that reference is configured but its AudioMixer is not loaded, the routine can load it asynchronously before caching the groups. On its normal path, this level-load callback returns a completed task after requesting registration and handling the manager. Completion does not mean the template prefab has finished loading. It also does not wait for the separate mixer load or for an audio player to be spawned or begin playback.

member.param: Level-load context; this routine obtains its audio template from runtime settings instead.
member.returns: A completed task on the normal setup path after requesting template registration and handling the manager. It does not mean the template prefab or mixer has finished loading.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.Awake
member.summary: Registers this audio player for lookup by its object and saves the source settings that pool reuse will restore.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback. A GameObject is the Unity scene object this component is attached to. Awake adds the player and its GameObject to the shared component cache, a lookup table from objects to their AudioPlayer components. It then captures the assigned source's mixer group, volume, looping, pitch, minimum distance, spatial blend and Doppler level, and disables automatic source playback on startup.

Assign _source, the AudioSource component that plays the sound, before initialization. The saved values come from that moment; later changes to the live source do not recapture them. Calling Awake again overwrites those saved defaults. The inherited SpawnEvents.Awake callback then adds this player to the list of pool listeners kept by its Poolee, the component that tracks a pooled object. That list is how the pool's initialize and deinitialize calls reach this player, so the Poolee reference must be set; without it Awake fails after the other setup has finished.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this player from the shared object-to-audio-player lookup when Unity destroys it.

remarks.para: OnDestroy is Unity's destruction callback. It removes the player from the cache using its GameObject and clears the shared cache reference if that cache is now empty. Returning a reusable player to its pool is handled by separate pool callbacks; it does not mean the component was destroyed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.OnPoolDeInitialize
member.summary: Stops the source and clears its clip and playback-request flag when the pool deinitializes this player.

remarks.para: The object pool supplies reusable sound objects. Its deinitialization callback calls Stop on the assigned source, sets the source's clip to null, then clears _hasStartedPlaying. It leaves the saved default settings and the component-cache registration intact. The source must be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.OnPoolInitialize
member.summary: Restores the source settings saved for this reusable player.

remarks.para: The object pool invokes this setup routine when initializing a player for reuse. It writes the saved mixer group, volume, looping, pitch, minimum distance, spatial blend and Doppler level to the assigned source. Those defaults were captured by Awake, Unity's initialization callback; they are not newly read from the source here.
This routine does not start a clip, recapture defaults or clear _hasStartedPlaying. The pool's separate deinitialization routine stops the source, clears its clip and resets that flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.SetSpatialBlend(System.Single)
member.summary: Changes how much the assigned source uses distance and direction to place its sound in the world.

remarks.para: blend is a unitless mix: 0 requests 2D sound with no position-based placement, 1 requests fully 3D sound, and values between combine the two. For example, 0.5 mixes both modes. The method assigns one spatial-blend value, rather than editing a curve.

The source must be assigned. This changes the live source without updating the saved pool default. Pool initialization restores _defaultSpatialBlend, and a later Play call assigns its own spatial blend; an omitted Play argument uses 0.98.

member.param: Unitless 2D-to-3D mix, ordinarily 0 through 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.Stop
member.summary: Stops playback on the assigned source immediately.

remarks.para: It leaves the source's assigned clip and _hasStartedPlaying flag unchanged. If a Play request set that flag, Update normally asks to return the player to its pool on a later frame once it sees the source is stopped. That check requires positive game timeScale and an active object. Stop does not itself return the player to its pool.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.Update
member.summary: Asks to return the player to its pool after a playback request when its source is no longer playing.

remarks.para: Update is Unity's per-frame callback. It only checks while game timeScale is above zero, the object is active in the scene, and _hasStartedPlaying is true. If the assigned source then reports that it is not playing, it calls the base pool-return routine. A paused game, with timeScale zero, suspends this check.

The flag records a Play request before playback setup; it does not prove that a clip successfully began. A source stopped manually, paused so it reports not playing, or already finished can therefore satisfy this check. Playing the source directly without setting the flag does not enable this automatic return.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.PlayStep(System.Single)
member.summary: Stops the previous step and starts a randomly chosen walking or running footstep, with movement-dependent volume and time-scale-dependent pitch.
member.param: The caller's movement value. Despite the name, normal body locomotion supplies adjusted speed directly, while LiteLoco supplies squared speed. Values below 4 choose walking clips; values of 4 or more choose running clips.

remarks.para: Let x be the value passed to this method. In the normal body path, the game multiplies velocity magnitude (the size of the velocity vector) by 0.906 / the avatar's stored legLength value; SetAvatar calculates and caches this factor when setting the avatar. The inspected sources do not identify physical units for 0.906, legLength, or the resulting value passed to PlayStep. When the body changes from airborne to grounded, it doubles this value for the landing sound. LiteLoco instead squares the speed value passed to its footstep update before calling this method. PlayStep itself neither converts units nor squares x, so 4 is a threshold on the caller-supplied value, not one universal physical speed.

Walking uses walkOverride.audioClips when the override asset exists; otherwise it uses walkConcrete. Running similarly uses runOverride.audioClips or runConcrete. Each call picks a random array entry. The selected array must exist and contain at least one clip; an empty override does not fall back to the concrete array. This method does not inspect the ground's material.

Let m be volumeMult, a unitless multiplier (a number with no physical unit), and let clamp01(y) mean limiting y to the range 0 through 1. For x below 4, PlayStep passes m × (0.05 + 0.65 × clamp01(x / 4)) to the AudioSource volume setter (the call that changes the source volume). For x of 4 or more, it passes m × (0.3 + 0.5 × clamp01((x - 4) / 50)). These equations describe the number sent to the setter, not necessarily the value AudioSource.volume holds afterward. Unity documents AudioSource.volume as ranging from 0 to 1; this method does not show how Unity handles a request outside that range. PlayStep does not separately clamp m. The requested volume is a plain, unitless number, not a decibel value. With m = 1, the values requested for x = 2, x = 4, and x = 54 or higher are 0.375, 0.3, and 0.8. Crossing 4 therefore changes both the clip bank and the formula: the walking request approaches 0.7 × m just below 4, while the running request starts at 0.3 × m.

Pitch is r × (0.25 + 0.75 × clamp01(t)), where r is a new random playback-speed ratio from 0.9 to 1.1 and t is Unity's unitless game time scale. A pitch ratio of 1 means normal speed and pitch. At time scale 1, the resulting ratio is 0.9 to 1.1; at time scale 0, it is 0.225 to 0.275. Time scales above 1 do not raise this formula above its normal-speed range.

The source is stopped first, then its pitch and volume are set, then the chosen clip is assigned and Play is called. Repeated calls can cut off the previous step. This method requests playback immediately; it does not wait for completion or decide when the next foot touches the ground.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.SpawnAudio
member.summary: Requests a pooled sound player at the stored world point and applies the stored playback settings.
member.returns: A completion handle yielding the adopted AudioPlayer after setup and the playback request, or null if the pending flag was cleared before adoption.

remarks.para: This is an asynchronous operation: it can pause while the pool prepares the sound object and continue later without blocking the game. Its UniTask is a completion handle that callers can await. The calling playback routine sets _apIncoming before starting it. After the spawn completes, this method adopts and configures the player only if _apIncoming is still true. Otherwise it returns null. It does not itself set that flag or cancel the underlying spawn.

The spawn request takes _localPosition as a world-space point, in meters along the world X, Y and Z axes. After the wait the adopted player is detached from any parent. This path does not apply a later edit to _localPosition again after spawning, so changing that stored point during the wait does not move the already requested world spawn.

On adoption it stores the AudioPlayer reference and its current pool ID, then requests playback using the current stored clip, mixer group, volume, loop flag, pitch, minimum distance and spatial blend. Those playback settings are read after the wait, so a newer request can replace them while a spawn is pending. It is started by PlayAtPoint, which stores the loop flag as false before starting it, so the clip plays once. The loop flag is read as stored; this method does not force its value. It clears _apIncoming after requesting playback. Completion means that the request has been configured, not that the clip has finished or that audible sound has been confirmed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.SpawnAudioLoop
member.summary: Requests a pooled sound player at the stored world point and starts it at a random position in the clip.
member.returns: A completion handle yielding the adopted AudioPlayer after setup and the playback request, or null if the pending flag was cleared before adoption.

remarks.para: This is an asynchronous operation: it can pause while the pool prepares the sound object and continue later without blocking the game. Its UniTask is a completion handle that callers can await. The calling playback routine sets _apIncoming before starting it. After the spawn completes, this method adopts and configures the player only if _apIncoming is still true. Otherwise it returns null. It does not itself set that flag or cancel the underlying spawn.

The spawn request takes _localPosition as a world-space point, in meters along the world X, Y and Z axes. After the wait the adopted player is detached from any parent. This path does not apply a later edit to _localPosition again after spawning, so changing that stored point during the wait does not move the already requested world spawn.

On adoption it stores the AudioPlayer reference and its current pool ID, then requests playback using the current stored clip, mixer group, volume, loop flag, pitch, minimum distance and spatial blend. Those playback settings are read after the wait, so a newer request can replace them while a spawn is pending. It is started by LoopAtPoint, which stores the loop flag as true before starting it, so the sound repeats until stopped, beginning at the random position described below. The loop flag is read as stored; this method does not force its value. It clears _apIncoming after requesting playback. Completion means that the request has been configured, not that the clip has finished or that audible sound has been confirmed.

After calling Play, this variant chooses a random integer sample frame from 0 up to, but excluding, the clip's sample count and writes it to the source's timeSamples playhead. A sample frame is one time position across the audio channels. For example, frame 24,000 in a 48,000-frames-per-second clip is 0.5 seconds into the clip. This random offset is applied after the playback request. It is not read from _timecode. A valid assigned clip is required for this extra step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.SpawnLocalAudio
member.summary: Requests a pooled sound player at the stored point relative to its parent and applies the stored playback settings.
member.returns: A completion handle yielding the adopted AudioPlayer after setup and the playback request, or null if the pending flag was cleared before adoption.

remarks.para: This is an asynchronous operation: it can pause while the pool prepares the sound object and continue later without blocking the game. Its UniTask is a completion handle that callers can await. The calling playback routine sets _apIncoming before starting it. After the spawn completes, this method adopts and configures the player only if _apIncoming is still true. Otherwise it returns null. It does not itself set that flag or cancel the underlying spawn.

Before the wait, the parent Transform converts _localPosition into a world point for spawning. A Transform holds an object's position, rotation and scale. The parent must exist. After the wait, the spawned object is attached to the then-current _parent and placed at the then-current _localPosition. Coordinates use the parent's right, up and forward axes; at scale 1, one unit is one meter. Parent rotation and scale affect the world placement.

On adoption it stores the AudioPlayer reference and its current pool ID, then requests playback using the current stored clip, mixer group, volume, loop flag, pitch, minimum distance and spatial blend. Those playback settings are read after the wait, so a newer request can replace them while a spawn is pending. It is started by PlayAtLocalPoint, which stores the loop flag as false before starting it, so the clip plays once. The loop flag is read as stored; this method does not force its value. It clears _apIncoming after requesting playback. Completion means that the request has been configured, not that the clip has finished or that audible sound has been confirmed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.Stop
member.summary: Clears the pending-spawn flag and stops the managed source when its pool ID still matches.

remarks.para: The pending flag is cleared first. Then the existing AudioPlayer reference and current pool ID are checked; only a matching player has its AudioSource stopped. An AudioSource is the Unity component that plays a sound clip. This prevents stopping a pooled object that has since been assigned a different ID.

This method keeps the player reference, saved ID, clip and playback settings. It does not directly return the object to the pool. The AudioPlayer can request that return on a later update once it is stopped, active and the game time scale is above zero.

Clearing _apIncoming makes a later spawn completion skip adoption if the flag is still false. It does not cancel or wait for the pool operation. Starting another request can set the flag again; this shared flag is not a separate cancellation handle for each request.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.#ctor
member.summary: Allocates four audio-entry slots and a 14-value reverb buffer, with a default minimum reverb fade of 0.35 seconds.

remarks.para: This class is marked obsolete with a compiler error. Its replacement is Audio2dPlugin.Audio2dManager. These remarks describe the legacy class for existing content and inspection.

The audio-entry array initially contains four empty references; this constructor does not create the AmbAndMusic entries or their AudioSources. An AudioSource is Unity's component for playing sound clips. Supply valid entries before Awake, Unity's initialization callback, prepares their sources. The 14-value float buffer starts at zero.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.AmbAndMusic.UpdateFade
member.summary: Moves the source volume toward its fade target using this frame's scaled game-time step, then finishes the fade when the volume approximately reaches the target.

remarks.para: ambMus must contain a valid AudioSource, Unity's component that plays a sound clip. Let V be the source's current volume, T be fadeTarget, r be fadePerSec, and dt be Unity's scaled time since the previous frame in seconds. V and T are unitless source-volume values, and r is source-volume units per game second. With a nonnegative rate, the method moves V toward T by at most r × dt, setting T directly when that step reaches it. For example, V = 0.2, T = 0.8, r = 0.3 and dt = 0.02 produce volume 0.206.

The usual source-volume range is 0 for silence through 1 for full source level; it is not decibels or guaranteed perceived loudness. Use a nonnegative rate: a negative value can move away from the target. This method does not validate or clamp the stored target and rate itself.

The parent component normally calls this only when isFading is true. UpdateFade itself does not check that flag, so calling it directly can still change volume after the flag has been cleared. When the applied volume approximately equals the target, it clears isFading first, then stops the source if its volume is zero or lower. Positive target volume completes the fade without stopping playback.

This uses scaled game seconds. Pausing game time gives dt = 0 and prevents a positive-rate fade from advancing; slow motion slows its real-time progress. Completion is checked on frames, so a configured duration is not an exact wall-clock deadline.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.Awake
member.summary: Prepares 2D sound sources, routes the first four entries, and selects the initial ambience and music slots.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback. For every entry in ambAndMusics, it keeps the assigned AudioSource if it exists or adds one to this component's object. The array and each entry must exist. It disables automatic startup playback and the optional spatializer effect, enables looping, and sets spatial blend to 0 for nonpositional 2D sound.

With at least four entries, it assigns AmbientMixerGroup to entries 0 and 1 and MusicMixerGroup to entries 2 and 3. Mixer groups route sound through shared audio controls and effects. Extra entries receive source setup but are not routed by this first-four assignment. Setup then sets _curAmb to 0 and _curMus to 2. Cues need at least four valid entries to use both pairs.
This callback prepares the sources; it does not start their clips. The group references are applied here, so changing those fields later does not automatically reroute the existing sources.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.StopFadeRoutine
member.summary: Stops the stored reverb transition and clears its coroutine handle.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume over several frames; the handle identifies that started routine. If fadeRoutine is non-null, this method stops it and then clears the handle. With no handle, it does nothing.

The mixer keeps the last parameter values written by the transition. This method does not restore prevReverbObj, jump to reverbObj's target values, or stop music and ambience volume fades. It also leaves the target preset and captured starting buffer stored.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.Update
member.summary: Advances the volume fade of every audio entry whose fade flag is set.

remarks.para: Update is Unity's once-per-frame callback while this component is enabled. It visits ambAndMusics and calls each marked entry's UpdateFade. The array and entries must be valid. Entries without an active fade flag are skipped.

Each source volume moves toward its stored target by at most r × dt per frame, where r is its fade rate in unitless source-volume units per second and dt is Unity's scaled game-time step in seconds. For example, r = 0.5 and dt = 0.02 change volume by up to 0.01. Pausing game time makes dt zero and stops positive-rate fade progress; slower game time slows it down. The result is evaluated on frames, not an exact wall-clock deadline.

When the source volume approximately reaches the target, the entry clears its fade flag, then stops the source if its volume is zero or lower. This Update handles source volume fades; the intro wait, override release and reverb transitions run in their own coroutines.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip.#ctor
member.summary: Creates the per-hand contact dictionary and initially selects Pelvis as the body region for this grip.

remarks.para: The dictionary starts empty. ValidateGripScore adds contact records as hands are assessed. The constructor then performs the inherited Grip construction.
Pelvis is the constructor's initial value for bodyRb; a saved component can supply a different body-region setting.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip.Awake
member.summary: Registers this component in the grabbing system's lookup tables and prepares its initial grip distance and target transform.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: a routine Unity calls to prepare the component.

The lookup tables associate this GameObject with its HandReciever and Grip components so other grabbing code can find them. The method copies defaultGripDistance into the active distance and calculates its squared value for distance comparisons.
If targetTransform is unassigned, it uses this component's own Transform. This initializes the ordinary Grip settings; assign _physRig separately for the avatar-specific surface calculations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.Awake
member.summary: Initializes the inherited target grip, creates the per-hand zone cache, and selects the ring pose as the barrel’s initial hand pose.

remarks.para: Unity calls this during component initialization. The barrel part replaces _grabConfig with a new empty dictionary and copies ringHandPose into the inherited handPose field. Later valid zone checks choose a pose for each hand.
Calling Awake manually repeats that initialization and discards existing zone-cache entries. Set up the collider and pose references before the normal initialization callback.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.ClearHasBeenGrabbed
member.summary: Clears the saved last-grab timestamp to 0.

remarks.para: HasBeenGrabbed compares the current unscaled game-clock time, in seconds and unaffected by slow motion, with this timestamp. Clearing it usually makes that recent-grab query false once the game clock is at least 0.1 seconds, but the query does not separately reject a zero timestamp.

This method does not release a held object or clear the saved grip threshold and grab/release-transition flags. Near startup, when the game clock is less than 0.1 seconds, a zero timestamp can still satisfy the recent-grab comparison.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetAButton
member.summary: Returns false in the base implementation of the primary face button, commonly labelled A or X held state query.

remarks.para: The intended query is whether the primary face button, commonly labelled A or X is held. A controller subclass can replace this method to supply device input. The BaseController implementation returns false without reading the stored button or touch fields, so false here does not prove that a physical control is released or untouched.

Calling this query does not poll the hardware, open a menu, or consume a stored press. A press transition means a change into the pressed state; a release transition means a change out of it. A held-state query can stay true across several updates in an implementation that supports the control.

member.returns: False from the base implementation; a controller subclass may supply a different result.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetGesturePose(System.Single@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns the stored selection and writes an intensity of 0 in the base implementation.

remarks.para: This base method does not evaluate finger curls or refresh a timer. It returns the saved gesture selection; a fresh base component has the zero-valued OpenHand selection. The output intensity is always 0, a unitless value, regardless of that stored pose.

forceUpdate is ignored by the base method, including when it is true. OpenController replaces this method with gesture evaluation and a cache that normally refreshes no more often than every 0.2 seconds of unscaled game time, which slow motion does not change; its forceUpdate argument bypasses that wait. That behavior belongs to the controller subclass.

member.param: Receives 0 from the base implementation, rather than a confidence estimate.
Requests forced evaluation in supporting subclasses; has no effect in the base implementation.
member.returns: The stored GesturePose selection; OpenHand on a fresh base component.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetGrabbedState
member.summary: Returns the stored grab input-threshold condition.

remarks.para: This is a stored threshold condition, not proof that a scene object is held or has been let go. OpenController saves the grab condition when its unitless solved grip is strictly greater than 0.99. Its release condition is strictly below a threshold adjusted by how fast that solved grip changes; grip and its threshold have no physical units.

The release threshold is 0.5 plus a correction: take minus the solved-grip rate in units per unscaled second, multiply by 0.02 seconds, and clamp that correction between -0.4 and 0.4. For an unchanged grip, the correction is 0 and the release condition is grip below 0.5. A grip between the grab and release thresholds can make both conditions false.

The getter returns the previously computed condition without polling the device or recalculating it. IsGrabbed and IsReleased instead report the saved transitions into grab or release. StampController can copy these conditions from a source controller; a fresh base component starts with false.

member.returns: The saved grab threshold condition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetGripForce
member.summary: Returns the stored processed squeeze strength for the controller.

remarks.para: Despite the word force, this value is a unitless grip amount, normally 0 to 1: 0 means no processed squeeze and 1 full strength. It is not a measured force in newtons. The getter reads the saved number without sampling hardware or enforcing that range; a fresh base component starts at 0.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetGripVelocity
member.summary: Returns 0 from the base implementation of the grip-change-rate query.

remarks.para: A supporting controller subclass can report how fast the solved, unitless grip amount is changing per second. OpenController computes that rate as new solved grip minus the previous solved grip, divided by the elapsed unscaled frame seconds; slow motion does not change that time measurement. Positive means squeezing more, negative means releasing.

For example, a grip increase from 0.2 to 0.6 over 0.1 seconds gives a rate of 4 input units per second. The base implementation returns 0 instead of reading that stored rate. This is a squeeze-input rate, not movement of the controller in metres per second.

member.summary: Returns false in the base implementation of the quick-menu-tap query.

remarks.para: The base method does not inspect buttons or timing. A controller subclass must replace it to report a tap. OpenController’s update stores unscaled time on B-down and, on B-up, sets the tap flag when current unscaled time minus that stored time is strictly less than 0.2 seconds. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetRelativeVelocityInWorld
member.summary: Returns the zero vector from the base controller-velocity query.

remarks.para: The intended result is controller movement relative to the tracking head, expressed on the scene’s shared world axes in metres per second. OpenController supplies its stored velocity, calculated during a VR physics update from the change in controller-position-minus-head-position divided by the supplied timestep in seconds.

The base method returns (0, 0, 0) instead of measuring movement. Subtracting the head position means moving the controller and head together by the same amount contributes no relative movement; moving only the controller one metre on world X in half a second gives 2 metres per second on X in a supporting implementation.

member.returns: (0, 0, 0) from the base implementation; supporting subclasses can return world-axis metres per second.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.GetReleasedState
member.summary: Returns the stored release input-threshold condition.

remarks.para: This is a stored threshold condition, not proof that a scene object is held or has been let go. OpenController saves the grab condition when its unitless solved grip is strictly greater than 0.99. Its release condition is strictly below a threshold adjusted by how fast that solved grip changes; grip and its threshold have no physical units.

The release threshold is 0.5 plus a correction: take minus the solved-grip rate in units per unscaled second, multiply by 0.02 seconds, and clamp that correction between -0.4 and 0.4. For an unchanged grip, the correction is 0 and the release condition is grip below 0.5. A grip between the grab and release thresholds can make both conditions false.

The getter returns the previously computed condition without polling the device or recalculating it. IsGrabbed and IsReleased instead report the saved transitions into grab or release. StampController can copy these conditions from a source controller; a fresh base component starts with false.

member.returns: The saved release threshold condition.

member.summary: Provides an empty base hook for a controller vibration pulse.

remarks.para: Haptic feedback means a vibration you feel through the controller. The BaseController implementation ignores microFloat and returns without requesting vibration or changing its haptic component.
This empty method does not establish a physical unit or duration for microFloat. Do not rely on its name to mean microseconds. A controller subclass would need to supply behavior for this hook.

member.param: A pulse value accepted by this hook; ignored by the base implementation, which establishes no unit for it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.HapticAction(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Provides an empty base hook for a timed controller vibration request.

remarks.para: Haptic feedback means a vibration felt through the controller. The base implementation ignores all four arguments and returns without sending or scheduling a vibration, even when a Haptor component is assigned.

The request describes a delay and duration in seconds, frequency in hertz (vibration cycles per second), and unitless amplitude normally from 0 for no vibration to 1 for full strength. For example, delay 0, duration 0.1, frequency 100 and amplitude 0.5 describes an immediate tenth-second, half-strength request for a supporting controller implementation.
OpenController replaces this method and routes the request to the selected left or right XR device. The base hook itself does not clamp values, choose a device or report that any vibration completed.

member.param: Requested delay in seconds; ignored by the base implementation.
Requested vibration duration in seconds; ignored by the base implementation.
Requested vibration frequency in hertz, or cycles per second; ignored by the base implementation.
Requested unitless strength, normally 0 to 1; ignored by the base implementation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.HasBeenGrabbed
member.summary: Checks whether the saved grab timestamp is less than 0.1 unscaled seconds behind the current game clock.

remarks.para: The test subtracts the saved last-grab time from Unity’s current unscaled time, both in seconds; slow motion does not change this clock. It returns true only when that difference is strictly less than 0.1, so a difference exactly equal to 0.1 returns false. Reading it does not clear the timestamp.

OpenController saves a timestamp on a grab-input transition and clears it on release. ClearHasBeenGrabbed also sets it to 0. This query does not separately check for a nonzero timestamp or require that it be in the past; a fresh or cleared zero stamp can produce true during the first 0.1 seconds of the game clock. It reports recent input timing, not a current held object.

member.returns: Whether current unscaled seconds minus the saved timestamp is less than 0.1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.IsGrabbed
member.summary: Returns the stored grab input-transition flag.

remarks.para: This is an input transition flag, not a check that a scene object is currently held. OpenController records a grab transition when solved grip rises above 0.99 while its internal grabbed latch was clear. It records a release transition when grip falls below its velocity-adjusted release threshold while that latch was set.

The getter reads the last saved flag without recalculating thresholds or clearing it. During steady squeezing, IsGrabbed can be false even while GetGrabbedState remains true. During steady released input, IsReleased can likewise be false while GetReleasedState is true. StampController can copy these flags from another controller.

member.returns: The saved grab transition flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.StampController(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController)
member.summary: Copies selected interaction, grab and finger-curl query results from another controller into this controller’s stored input.

remarks.para: The source is read through its methods, so a source subclass’s implementations determine the copied values. The copy order is primary press/release/held and axis; secondary press/release/held and axis; grab/release-transition flags; grab/release-threshold conditions; last-grab timestamp; then index, middle, ring, pinky and thumb curls.

This is a snapshot at call time rather than a link to the source’s later input. It does not poll this controller’s hardware or recalculate the copied grip conditions. The axes and curls are unitless amounts; the saved grab timestamp is unscaled game-clock seconds, unaffected by slow motion.

The complete copy routine does not copy face/menu-button or touch flags, thumbstick/touchpad vectors, grip force, grip-change rate, movement velocity, controller type, handedness, rig or Haptor. For example, copying a source trigger value of 0.7 changes this controller’s saved primary axis to 0.7 while its thumbstick cache stays as it was. Supply a nonnull source; the routine does not handle null as an empty controller.

member.param: The source controller whose queried values are copied; must not be null.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.Blueprint.IsBundledDataCard
member.summary: Returns false, so the data-card packing code skips the separate bundled-asset reference for this blueprint.

remarks.para: A bundled asset is an asset stored in an asset bundle, a package of game content. The inherited DataCard packing and unpacking methods test this result before writing or reading their DataCardAsset reference. This override always returns false, so those particular steps are skipped.
This reports the card’s classification. Calling it does not create the blueprint’s objects or restore their signal connections.

member.returns: Always false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner.Awake
member.summary: Starts preparing the assigned blueprint’s object assets for later spawn requests.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s component initialization callback, a routine Unity calls to initialize the component. Here it starts asynchronous asset registration for every entry in Blueprint.spawnables. Asynchronous work can wait for assets and continue in later frames; this routine returns without waiting for all registrations to finish.

A blueprint stores a group of object choices, their relative positions and rotations, and their saved logic connections. Assign a nonnull Blueprint with an initialized spawnables array before initialization, and provide usable spawnable crate references in that array.

This initialization prepares assets; it does not create the blueprint’s objects or test ShouldSpawn. Request creation separately with SpawnBlueprint or SpawnBlueprintAsync. Replacing Blueprint afterward does not automatically repeat this preparation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner.DebugSpawnBlueprint
member.summary: Starts a blueprint spawn request from the Spawn Blueprint context menu, respecting ShouldSpawn.

remarks.para: ShouldSpawn is a callback, a routine called to decide whether this request may proceed. A missing callback allows the request; a callback returning false stops it before the new parent object is created. This context-menu path does not bypass that condition.

An allowed request creates a new parent object named after the blueprint’s Title, copies this spawner’s world position and rotation, and keeps the parent inactive while spawning the saved objects and restoring their logic connections. Those connections let the spawned objects send signals to one another. The parent becomes active after successful restoration; a reported missing crate reference, unresolved crate or failed restoration destroys the new parent.

The work can wait for assets and continue in later frames. This method starts the request and returns without waiting for completion. Repeated allowed calls start separate requests; the inspected spawning path has no already-spawned guard.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner.OnValidate
member.summary: The editor validation callback does not change the blueprint or object name in the inspected game implementation.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine Unity calls to perform an action. In the Unity editor, OnValidate is called when the component is loaded or its Inspector values change. This game implementation returns immediately while playing; otherwise it reads the object’s scene and returns without applying a configuration change.

Calling this routine does not register replacement blueprint assets, create objects, or run ResetName. This describes the inspected player implementation; the editor-only name-refresh code is not present there.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintVLSerializing.ReadJson(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.VoidLogicConnection,Il2CppNewtonsoft.Json.Linq.JObject)
member.summary: Attempts to read saved signal-wire data, but leaves the supplied connection and its existing edges unchanged. Record type: .

remarks.para: A VoidLogic connection describes wires for gameplay signals, such as connecting a button output to a device input. Each edge is one wire: from identifies its output endpoint and to identifies its input endpoint.

This native method requires json["edges"] to be a JObject, an object of named JSON properties. The connection writer instead produces a JArray, a JSON list, so its output fails this reader’s object-type requirement. A missing edges value or a null json also fails rather than supplying an empty connection.

After that requirement, it allocates a new local edge array and attempts to read each element’s from and to endpoint objects. Parsed endpoints are temporary: the array entries are cleared rather than receiving them, and the array is never assigned to vlc.edges or returned. The original edge array is not edited.

Each endpoint writes spawnableIndex, spawnableKey and portIndex. spawnableIndex is the zero-based position of the spawned object in the blueprint spawn list; 0 means the first object. spawnableKey is the text key used to find the signal component in that object’s bill of materials, its list of named parts. portIndex selects the numbered output on from or input on to; these indices are unitless counts, not distances or signal strengths.

The shared endpoint reader recognizes spawnableIndex and handle, not the writer’s spawnableKey, and converts portIndex without storing it. This overload is therefore unsuitable for restoring saved gameplay wires.

To load a saved connection, explicitly parse the writer’s edges array into records and assign the array to your connection. Only the separate connection Restore operation can reconnect the resulting records to the spawned objects. This method itself neither spawns objects nor connects live components.

member.param: Record passed by value; the native method does not restore the caller’s record.
JSON object to inspect; required object structure and mismatched key names are described above.

The port reader looks for spawnableIndex and handle rather than spawnableKey, and converts portIndex without storing it. Parse and assign both endpoints yourself when loading the writer’s from/to format; calling this method does not alter the live wire or restore the saved edge.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.AddPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigWeights)
member.summary: Adds weighted pose changes to this pose, using separate body-part weights and preserving its timestamp.

remarks.para: addPose supplies changes to apply to the current saved values. For an ordinary number or position component, result = current + change * weight: current is this pose's existing component, change is the matching component in addPose, and weight is the matching unitless rig weight. For example, current arm extension 0.6 plus change 0.2 at weight 0.5 becomes 0.7. A delta pose, such as one generated by subtracting a base pose, is suitable input.

Rotations combine the current quaternion with the added quaternion blended from identity by its weight. A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers; identity means no added rotation. The weighted added rotation is multiplied on the right of the current rotation, so it is a change in that orientation's local axes. Rotation weights are passed to an unclamped blend, and the method does not force weights into the range 0 through 1.

Head and neck use the head weight; chest and spine use chest; pelvis uses pelvis; each clavicle, the collarbone at the top of the shoulder, uses its shoulder weight. Arm reach, arm extension, hand rotation and torso-hand values use the matching hand weight. Leg reach, leg extension and foot rotation use the matching foot weight. All three position vectors, including both head positions, use rootPosition, while root orientation uses rootRotation. These names refer to the values in the supplied RigWeights object.

Hand separation uses the average of the left and right hand weights. The palm-to-palm direction, each palm-to-torso direction, and each two-component torso direction are blended toward their corresponding input directions and then normalized, meaning resized to length 1 when large enough. This differs from adding a distance: even a zero weight can normalize the existing direction. Extremely small three-component directions become zero.
Both addPose and weights must be non-null. This method edits the existing saved pose and does not move bones immediately. It leaves timestamp unchanged, so it does not record a new capture time.

member.param: The non-null pose containing the changes to add.
The non-null collection of unitless body-part strengths used for those changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.CopyPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose)
member.summary: Replaces every value in this pose with the supplied pose, including its timestamp.

remarks.para: The destination is this existing BodyPose object. Rotations, extensions, hand-proximity values, root and head positions, and timestamp are copied. The source pose object remains available, and no new pose object is created by this method.

The values keep their original units and reference frames. For example, a head position measured in skull-height units stays in those units; copying does not convert it to metres or adapt it to a different avatar.

To keep an earlier sample, create a separate BodyPose and copy the current pose into it before the current pose is refreshed. Later changes to the current pose's values will not change the copied values. Applying the copy to a rig is a separate step.

member.param: The non-null pose whose values replace this pose's values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.LerpPoseUnclamped(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose,System.Single)
member.summary: Stores a blend of two poses in this pose; the blend factor can also extend beyond either input, and the timestamp stays unchanged.

remarks.para: t is a unitless blend factor: 0 selects from, 1 selects to, and 0.5 gives the midpoint for ordinary numbers and vector components. For each such component, result = fromValue + (toValue - fromValue) * t. Here fromValue and toValue are that same component in the two input poses, and result is its new value in this pose.

The method does not limit t to 0 through 1. For example, blending an extension of 0.4 toward 0.8 with t = 1.5 produces 1.0. This extrapolation can produce values outside the range normally captured from a rig. t is not a duration in seconds.

Each rotation uses Unity's Quaternion.LerpUnclamped. A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers; this helper blends orientations rather than treating those numbers as angles in degrees. Direction vectors use ordinary component blending and are not normalized here, so the result can have a length other than 1.

Both inputs must be non-null and use matching units and reference frames. The method changes saved data without applying it to bones. It leaves this pose's timestamp exactly as it was, even when t is 0 or 1; set or copy a suitable timestamp separately if the result represents a new timed sample.

member.param: The non-null starting pose, selected at t = 0.
The non-null ending pose, selected at t = 1.
Blend factor; values outside 0 to 1 extrapolate beyond the endpoint poses.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.CheckZones(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Chooses a box-surface grab for this hand and saves the contact position, orientation, hand pose and pose radius.
member.param: The hand attempting to grab.
member.returns: True when a permitted geometric contact was selected and saved; false when the selected region or mode is rejected.

remarks.para: The calculation expresses the hand’s palm transform in the box collider’s oriented frame. It compares that position with the scaled box dimensions and edgePadding, considers sufficiently thin sections for a sandwich grab, and checks the allowed face, edge or corner for the selected region. The axes rotate with the box, rather than staying aligned with the world.

A successful selection saves the hand’s contact and local target in _grabConfig and its HandPose/radius in boxHandStates. Calling this method first removes the hand’s previous pose and pose/radius entry and clears the mode flags, so a failed check can discard a previous selection. It does not attach a joint or move the object.

The returned Boolean reports whether this geometric selection succeeded. ValidateGripScore separately copies that result into the saved isZoneValid flag and checks the hand’s facing direction; ordinary hover uses that saved flag. Calling CheckZones directly does not update isZoneValid and does not by itself guarantee that the grabbing system accepts the grip.

In this implementation, successful edge and face selections set the record’s isCorner flag, just as a corner selection does. The individual face/edge/corner enum fields are not filled by this calculation. Use the actual selected pose/radius and contact data rather than assuming those fields accurately identify the geometric region.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.GetDistanceBetweenFace(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.Faces)
member.summary: Returns the scaled box’s center-to-face distance along the selected axis.
member.param: The face defining the axis of measurement.
member.returns: The cached center-to-face distance in meters for any one of the six faces; zero for zero, combined or unsupported values.

remarks.para: PositiveX and NegativeX both return half the box’s width; the Y pair returns half its height, and the Z pair returns half its depth. For an illustrative scaled X size of 0.20 meters, either X face returns 0.10 meters. Despite the method’s name, this is not the full distance between opposite faces.

It reads the last _bounds produced by CheckZones or OnDrawGizmosSelected, the callback that Unity calls to draw the selected box and refresh its cached bounds. Each single face is supported, including NegativeZ. Zero or a combination of face flags returns zero; this helper expects one face.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.GetEdgePadding
member.summary: Returns the configured distance used to separate face interiors from edge and corner regions.

remarks.para: The result is edgePadding in meters. CheckZones subtracts half this value from each box half-size before testing the hand’s position. For an illustrative padding of 0.10 meters, the dividing boundary is 5 cm inside each outer face boundary.
This accessor simply returns the setting. It does not rebuild the bounds or choose a hand’s grab region.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.GetForcePullTransform(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)

remarks.para: It first runs UpdateForcePullTransform, which uses forceGrabFace and forceGrabTop to choose a fixed alignment on the box and applies sandwichHandPose. It then returns the target stored by the grip. The result describes where the hand should align; this method itself does not pull the object through space or attach it.
The primary and top settings refer to the collider’s oriented axes. They do not select whichever face the approaching hand happens to be closest to.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.OnDrawGizmosSelected
member.summary: Draws the box’s face, edge and corner grab regions in Unity’s scene view when this component is selected.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine Unity calls to draw the selected component in the scene view. It rebuilds _bounds from the referenced BoxCollider’s size and center, using this grip’s scale. Its drawing frame follows the collider’s rotation and position. It draws the inner boundary defined by edgePadding and colored regions for the enabled face, edge and corner masks when their corresponding grab modes are permitted.
These drawings help compare the configured grab regions with the physical box. The callback refreshes the bounds cache; it does not select a hand’s contact or attach a grip.

member.summary: Notifies the grip’s far-hover listeners that this hand has begun hovering over it from a distance.
member.param: The hovering hand.

remarks.para: The BoxGrip override invokes farHoverBeginHandDelegate with the hand when that delegate has listeners. Its own body does not calculate a force-pull target, test a nearby grab zone or attach the hand. Those actions have separate methods.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.OnHandAttachedUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Keeps a holding hand’s pose and finger-size setting matched to its saved box grab.
member.param: The holding hand.

remarks.para: When boxHandStates contains an entry for the hand, the method applies that entry’s HandPose and radius, then runs the inherited attached-hand update and reapplies the radius afterward. The saved radius is a size input for the hand animator, not a distance test.

It reuses the already selected entry rather than rerunning CheckZones. With no entry, it still runs the inherited update and uses a radius of zero afterward. Changing a pose or radius setting is therefore reflected after the appropriate contact selection refreshes the hand’s entry.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.OnHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Places the hovering hand’s target from its saved box contact, or uses the fixed force-pull alignment when overriding.
member.param: The hovering hand.
True to use fixed force-pull alignment and invoke inherited override grabbing; false to use the saved valid nearby contact.

remarks.para: With isOverride false, the method rejects disabled interaction and requires _grabConfig to contain a record whose isZoneValid flag is true. ValidateGripScore normally updates that flag. An invalid record restores the animator’s default hand pose and returns false. A valid record supplies localPosition/localRotation, which this method converts through the oriented, centered box frame into a world-space hand target.

With isOverride true, it instead calls UpdateForcePullTransform, bypassing the saved zone-validity test and using forceGrabFace, forceGrabTop and sandwichHandPose. It then passes the override to Grip’s hover method, whose override path can immediately attach through its quick-grab handling. This is more than a pose-preview switch.

For either path, the saved boxHandStates pose/radius is applied when available. The normal path returns the inherited hover method’s result after preparing the target; that result also depends on the controller’s grab/release state. A true return is not simply a new CheckZones result, and this normal update does not perform a fresh zone selection.

member.returns: False for rejected ordinary interaction or an invalid saved zone; otherwise the inherited hover result after the target and pose are prepared. The override path also invokes inherited attachment handling.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.UpdateForcePullTransform(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Sets this hand’s force-pull target using the configured primary face and top direction of the box.
member.param: The pulling hand.

remarks.para: The method refreshes the box dimensions by calling CheckZones, but does not require that check to return true. It then selects sandwichHandPose and saves a pose/radius entry for the hand. The radius for this force-pull path is the box’s half-size along forceGrabTop’s axis; the ordinary sandwich classifier uses its own calculated span.

The primary face chooses the target’s side and the top direction sets its roll around that side, with left/right hand orientation accounted for. Use one face for each setting on perpendicular axes, such as NegativeX and PositiveY. These settings are directions, whereas enabledFaces is a mask of allowed nearby regions.

Position starts at the primary face’s half-size measured from the collider Transform’s origin. If the top half-size is smaller than 0.05 meters, the method moves the target inward along the primary-face direction by 0.05 minus that half-size. For example, a 0.02-meter top half-size gives a 3 cm inward adjustment. Unlike ordinary hover’s centered frame, this force-pull position does not add the BoxCollider.center offset.
The result is stored as a world-space hand target. The method chooses alignment and pose; movement of the object and attachment are handled by the grabbing system.
