member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.CheckImpact(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single@,System.Single@)
member.summary: Accepts an impact unless it is weaker than the remembered impact while the supplied delay is still active.

remarks.para: Rejects only when time is strictly earlier than nextTime and impulse is strictly smaller than lastImpulse. Rejection leaves both reference parameters unchanged. Acceptance stores impulse in lastImpulse, stores time + duration in nextTime, and returns true. An equally strong impact is accepted during the delay and starts the delay again; an impact exactly at nextTime is accepted even if weaker.

time and nextTime are timestamps in seconds on the same clock; duration is a delay in seconds. The method uses the supplied time rather than reading Unity's clock. impulse and lastImpulse are the caller's numerical impact strengths and must use the same units; the method does not convert them. For example, with lastImpulse = 5, nextTime = 10 and time = 9, strength 4 is rejected but strength 5 is accepted. With duration = 0.2, that acceptance sets nextTime to 9.2 seconds.

member.param: Current impact strength, in the same units as lastImpulse.
Delay in seconds to add to time after acceptance.
Current timestamp in seconds on the same clock as nextTime.
Remembered strength; replaced with impulse when accepted.
End timestamp of the delay, in seconds; replaced with time + duration when accepted.
member.returns: True when accepted and both reference values are updated; false only for a weaker impact before nextTime.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.ProcessCollisionHaul(System.Single)
member.summary: Reports the collected collision through or and clears the reusable impulse data.

remarks.para: An enter is the start of a contact; a stay is a continuing contact. Impulse is the push delivered over time, measured in newton seconds. If any collected collision set _isEnter and an impulse was collected, the enter callback runs only when normal dot relativeVelocity is at least impactVelocityThresh. Here normal is the selected contact's unit direction, relativeVelocity is its relative movement in world metres per second, and dot means multiplying matching vector components and adding them. This gives a signed speed along the normal, not the full speed or its absolute value. Without the enter flag, a retained impulse flag selects the stay callback, with no velocity-threshold check. Only assigned callbacks run.

The argument is the collector's reusable RelevantCollision object, not a fresh copy. It holds the summed impulse from the collected contacts and the details of the individual collision with the largest impulse. Its point is in world coordinates, the level's shared axes, in metres; its normal is a direction with no units, and its relativeVelocity is in metres per second along those same axes. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body; the payload's rigidbody is the other body and can be null for a static surface. Copy any values you need to keep during the callback, a method called when the collector reports a collision: processing later clears totalImpulse and rigidbody, and future contacts overwrite the other details.

After callbacks return normally, both overloads reset the largest squared impulse to zero, clear the reusable payload's totalImpulse to the zero vector and set its rigidbody to null. They retain the other contact details. Only the branch with an enter flag and an impulse flag clears both flags. The stay branch keeps its impulse flag, so another processing call can report a stay even without a newly collected collision; its payload can then have zero impulse and a null rigidbody.

fixedDeltaTime is the caller's physics-step duration in seconds. This overload does not use it and does not update _pressureSensor. A physics step is one update of Unity's physical simulation; processing calls are made by the owning body's update code, rather than by this collector automatically every rendered frame.

member.param: Physics-step duration in seconds; unused by this overload.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.ProcessCollisionHaul(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Reports and clears collisions like , and saves their summed impulse multiplied by divByNewtons.

remarks.para: An enter is the start of a contact; a stay is a continuing contact. Impulse is the push delivered over time, measured in newton seconds. If any collected collision set _isEnter and an impulse was collected, the enter callback runs only when normal dot relativeVelocity is at least impactVelocityThresh. Here normal is the selected contact's unit direction, relativeVelocity is its relative movement in world metres per second, and dot means multiplying matching vector components and adding them. This gives a signed speed along the normal, not the full speed or its absolute value. Without the enter flag, a retained impulse flag selects the stay callback, with no velocity-threshold check. Only assigned callbacks run.

The argument is the collector's reusable RelevantCollision object, not a fresh copy. It holds the summed impulse from the collected contacts and the details of the individual collision with the largest impulse. Its point is in world coordinates, the level's shared axes, in metres; its normal is a direction with no units, and its relativeVelocity is in metres per second along those same axes. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body; the payload's rigidbody is the other body and can be null for a static surface. Copy any values you need to keep during the callback, a method called when the collector reports a collision: processing later clears totalImpulse and rigidbody, and future contacts overwrite the other details.

When an impulse flag is present, the selected callback runs first. After it returns, _pressureSensor is set to totalImpulse multiplied component by component by divByNewtons. Reading _pressureSensor inside that callback therefore sees its previous value; changing the payload's totalImpulse during the callback changes the result that is saved. With no impulse flag, this overload saves the zero vector.

totalImpulse is a world-space impulse vector in newton seconds, the force delivered over time. divByNewtons is a supplied scale, despite its name; this method does not calculate it from fixedDeltaTime. A scale of 1 / dt, where dt is the duration in seconds, produces average force in newtons. For example, an upward impulse of 0.4 newton seconds and dt = 0.02 seconds produce 20 newtons upward.

PhysicsRig, the component that simulates the player's physical body, supplies 1 / (m * g * dt), where m is the avatar's total mass in kilograms, g is the absolute vertical gravity acceleration in metres per second squared, and dt is the configured physics-step duration in seconds. A physics step is one update of Unity's physical simulation. The avatar is the player's in-game body. This produces a unitless fraction of body weight, not a force in newtons: with m = 10 kg, g = 10 m/s² and dt = 0.02 s, an upward impulse of 2 newton seconds gives an upward pressure value of 1. Other callers can supply different scales, so the stored value's units depend on that scale.

After callbacks return normally, both overloads reset the largest squared impulse to zero, clear the reusable payload's totalImpulse to the zero vector and set its rigidbody to null. They retain the other contact details. Only the branch with an enter flag and an impulse flag clears both flags. The stay branch keeps its impulse flag, so another processing call can report a stay even without a newly collected collision; its payload can then have zero impulse and a null rigidbody.

member.param: Physics-step duration in seconds; this method does not use it to derive the scale.
Scale multiplied by the summed impulse; its units determine the stored pressure units.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.IAttackReceiver.ReceiveAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Calls this receiver's attack response with the supplied hit details, which may trigger events or forward the hit into puppet behavior.
member.param: The incoming attack record, including its damage amount, hit geometry, attack type, and object references. The receiver decides which details affect its response.

remarks.para: This is the common entry point for attack receivers. The native interface declares the method without a shared response body; each receiver supplies its own behavior. Calling the proxy method invokes the existing object's native implementation.

The damage value is a game damage amount. Delivery alone does not guarantee that the same amount will be removed from health: a receiver can filter the attack, raise an event, or pass it to another system that applies its own damage rules. An event calls the functions attached to it. For example, GenericAttackReceiver forwards the unchanged damage value to AttackEvent only when the incoming attack type shares at least one enabled type with its attackType setting.

For a concrete example, a Blunt attack with damage 10 makes a GenericAttackReceiver configured for Blunt send 10 game damage units to its event. The same receiver configured only for Piercing ignores that attack. A plain AttackReceiver instead raises its OnAttackReceived event without checking that type or interpreting the damage amount.

Attack dispatch passes a copy of the attack record to the receiver. Object references in the copy still refer to the same objects. The dispatch callbacks examined here copy its values without converting coordinates or calculating new damage. Any later reaction, such as reducing health or starting an animation, belongs to the receiver and the systems it calls.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.ResetHits
member.summary: Resets hit data, then calls UpdateArray; material updates require a valid renderer array and entries.

remarks.para: This resets the impact manager's active hit count and next write position, clears CutPoint, then calls UpdateArray. UpdateArray sets NumberOfCuts to zero before its renderer loop. With a valid Renderers array and valid renderer/material entries where visited, that loop sends the hit manager's matrix array and zero hit count to each material. A shader is the drawing program used by a material; it must understand those hit properties for a visible mark to disappear. If Renderers is null, UpdateArray reaches a nonreturning error path after the stored hit data has been reset; that is not a successful no-upload return.

The old matrices remain in the hit array and CutPos; the reset changes the active counts rather than erasing every matrix slot. It also leaves Count_CUT, the next cut replacement index, unchanged. For example, if that index was 3, clearing and adding eight new cuts leaves 3 as the slot replaced by the following cut.

OnEnable, Unity's callback when this component becomes enabled on an active object, uses this same reset. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The call path needs a valid impactManager, CutPoint list, Renderers array, and valid renderer/material entries where visited. A missing renderer array or a null visited entry reaches the error path rather than completing a successful material refresh. This changes recorded visual data; it does not restore NPC health.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.UpdateArray
member.summary: Copies the recorded cuts into their cache and sends the hit manager's current data to the configured renderer materials.

remarks.para: First, NumberOfCuts becomes CutPoint.Count, and each cut matrix is copied into CutPos at the same index. A matrix is a table of numbers encoding an effect's position, orientation and shape. This preserves the list's index order; it does not reorder the cuts from oldest to newest after a replacement.

Next, this visits every material of every renderer in Renderers. For each material, impactManager writes its full hit matrix array to EllipsoidPosArray, then writes its active hit count to _NumberOfHits. This uses the renderer's material instances, which Unity can create for that renderer. It does not check isLODVisible before updating them.

This method prepares CutPos but does not send that cut array or NumberOfCuts to the materials. It also does not use the controller's four cached shader IDs for its hit upload; the impact manager uses its own IDs. Calling it therefore cannot by itself promise that cuts become visible.

AddToHitArray, AddToCutArray and ResetHits call this refresh after changing their data. If you edit CutPoint directly, a later refresh rebuilds its cache. Supply valid references and a CutPos array large enough for the list: the constructed array has eight slots, and directly adding more than eight list entries can make copying fail. Unused cache slots are left as they were.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.collectSkins
member.summary: Replaces Renderers with the skinned mesh renderers found on this object and its active children.

remarks.para: A skinned mesh renderer draws a mesh whose shape follows bones, such as an NPC's body. A GameObject is an object in a Unity scene. The search includes this component's own GameObject and recursively searches child GameObjects. It uses Unity's default child search, so inactive children are excluded; the object on which the search starts is still checked.

The result replaces the whole Renderers array, including any manually supplied entries. It does not append to the old array, gather ordinary MeshRenderer components, reset hits, or immediately upload material data. Call it when you want to rebuild this renderer selection, then use UpdateArray if the new selection needs the current hit data.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.isLODVisible
member.summary: Checks whether any renderer in Renderers is considered visible by Unity.
member.returns: True when the scan finds a renderer with isVisible true; otherwise false after a successful complete scan.

remarks.para: This scans the array from the last entry toward the first and returns as soon as a renderer's isVisible value is true. An empty array returns false. LOD means level of detail, but this routine does not inspect an LODGroup or select a mesh detail level.

Unity's visibility value can be true because a renderer is needed for shadows or, in the Unity editor, is seen by a Scene view camera. It does not specifically test what the player can see, whether a body part is unobstructed, or whether it has visual damage.

Provide a valid array and valid renderers: a missing array or an invalid entry reached during the scan can fail rather than be treated as invisible. This is a query; it does not switch renderers on or off or upload hit data.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Console.TokenParseContext.#ctor(System.Int32,Il2CppSystem.Type[])
member.summary: Creates shared console-conversion settings with an empty command set, the supplied expected-type array, and a suggestion-count threshold.
member.param: Threshold, in match entries, after which the command-name converter skips further non-exact suggestions. Defaults to 20; exact matches can exceed it.
Caller-supplied array of expected token types, in order, stored as the same array reference. An empty array supplies no type expectations; construction performs no type conversion.

remarks.para: A token is one piece of console input being interpreted, such as a command name. The new context starts with no eligible commands. Add the command wrappers you want the command-name converter to consider, or use the console plugin’s context after its command scan has populated the set. Constructing the context alone does not discover or run commands.

The expectedTypes array is stored by reference, so it is the same array object you supplied. Its entries are type descriptions, such as the type for a whole number or text; the constructor does not check the entries or convert input to those types. An empty array is valid and is what the console plugin supplies for its default context. The supplied integer threshold is stored unchanged; there is no minimum-value correction.

The softSuggestionLimit default is 20 match entries. In the command-name suggestion converter, exact matches and partial matches share a count. Exact aliases are checked before the limit gate, so exact entries can exceed the threshold when they occur first in a wrapper's alias order. Once the count has reached the limit, the first non-exact alias ends the scan of that wrapper's remaining aliases; a later exact alias on that wrapper can be skipped. For example, a threshold of 0 allows an exact alias only if it is encountered before a non-exact alias in that wrapper's alias list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.Swap1and2
member.summary: Exchanges the stored endpoint points, directions, and objects, then moves the first Marrow body into the second slot and clears the first.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody represents an object in the game’s physics system. This is not a general swap of two body references: the old second body reference is discarded, the old first body becomes the second, and the first becomes null, meaning no Marrow body.

The normal release path performs this rearrangement when the second endpoint has no Marrow body, so the movable body can host the connection and the other endpoint can act as a fixed world anchor. An anchor is the point where a physics joint, a connection limiting simulated movement, attaches.

The stored points and normal directions are exchanged without converting their coordinate frames. For example, when a movable object was picked first and a wall second, rearrangement puts the wall’s world-space point first and the movable object’s body-local point second. Calling the method does not create a joint or move either object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.DeleteConstraint
member.summary: Removes this constraint’s joint, visual endpoint helpers and both tracker components.

remarks.para: The normal Constrainer setup puts a tracker on each constrained object and gives both the same physics joint and visual line. A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives movement between objects. Calling this routine from either end requests removal of that shared connection; it does not require isHost to be true.

The requests run in this order: destroy this lineRenderer component if present, destroy this attachPoint’s entire GameObject if present, destroy the stored MarrowJoint if present, destroy the other tracker’s attachPoint GameObject and tracker component if that tracker is present, then destroy this tracker component. A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds components. The Constrainer creates separate helper GameObjects for the endpoint markers. It parents a marker to a selected object when that endpoint follows the object; a world-fixed marker can remain unparented. Removing either helper GameObject removes the helper, not its parent object, so the constrained objects remain in the scene.

These use Unity Destroy requests, whose actual removal is deferred until after the current Update loop. MarrowJoint’s OnDestroy routine then disconnects it from its bodies and removes its underlying ConfigurableJoint. This path destroys the MarrowJoint component directly; it does not call MarrowJoint.Destroy or run that method’s registered destroy-action list.

Missing line, own attachment or joint references are skipped. An existing otherTracker still needs an attachment transform: that nested reference is used without the same missing-object check. Keep the paired helper references intact for complete cleanup. This routine does not clear the stored fields before requesting destruction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.UpdateLines
member.summary: Copies the two attachment positions into the visual line’s two endpoints.

remarks.para: Vertex 0 is otherTracker.attachPoint.position; vertex 1 is this attachPoint.position. A vertex here is one endpoint of the drawn line. These are positions in world coordinates, normally measured in metres, rather than offsets relative to the line object. Configure the LineRenderer to use world space so that it interprets those numbers in the same frame.

The line renderer, counterpart tracker and both attachment transforms must exist, and the renderer needs at least two positions. The normal Constrainer setup creates and configures those references. This method neither creates missing pieces nor checks isHost or renderer visibility, so calling it directly can refresh the line even when automatic updates are skipped.

This updates the drawing only. It does not move the attachment objects, change the physics joint’s anchors, or measure a force. The per-frame Update routine separately does these endpoint writes only for a host whose line renderer reports itself visible.

This selects a physical side rather than the primary/secondary control role, and does not initialize or poll the controller.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.GetCrouch
member.summary: The signed input for lowering or raising the virtual body, separate from the player physically bending down.
member.returns: Signed cached body-height input; zero means no input from this axis.

remarks.para: On normal OpenControllerRig input, the secondary-axis X component is sideways and Y is up/down; both are unitless. abs(Y) measures the vertical amount without its direction, while abs(X) measures sideways amount without its direction. Input is accepted only when abs(Y) > 0.2 and abs(X) < 0.65. Then the value is sign(Y) × clamp((abs(Y) − 0.2) / 0.8, 0, 1): sign(Y) supplies the up/down direction and clamp limits the normalized amount to 0..1. With X = 0, Y = −0.6 gives −0.5 and Y = 0.6 gives 0.5; otherwise the cached value is zero. The bounds are strict, so equality does not pass.

RemapRig later uses this signed input for virtual body height: negative requests a lower target and positive requests a higher one. In CrouchHold, the per-update adjustment bound scales with 2 × deltaTime × the input amount × avatar agility; deltaTime is elapsed scaled game time in seconds, and avatar agility scales how quickly the height target can change. Current body height, physical support, and other height limits can restrict the result. This is a unitless adjustment request, not a distance or permanent height percentage.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.GetCrouchInput
member.summary: Whether the secondary axis currently requests a virtual body-height adjustment.
member.returns: The cached height-input flag, without clearing it.

remarks.para: On normal OpenControllerRig input, secondary-axis X is sideways and Y is up/down; both are unitless. abs(Y) measures how far the input moves vertically without regard to whether it is positive or negative. The cached flag is true only when abs(Y) > 0.2 and abs(X) < 0.65, for either vertical direction. For example, (0, −0.6) passes, while (0.7, −0.6) fails because the sideways amount is too large. This reports an input request, not the avatar’s current height or whether the player physically crouched.
RemapRig receives this flag alongside the signed value from GetCrouch for its later body-height calculation; the flag alone does not move the avatar.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.GetPrimaryAxis
member.summary: The processed two-dimensional movement input supplied to the locomotion rig.
member.returns: The cached processed movement vector.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. Touchpad devices have additional mappings.

A deadzone is the small region around a stick’s centered position whose deflection is treated as no input. Where MagnitudeRemapAxis is used, overall stick magnitude means the radial distance of the X/Y pair from center; that helper compares it with a lower threshold and linearly rescales the vector magnitude between configured thresholds. Separately, a configured AnimationCurve selects the movement-direction angle; it does not do the magnitude remap. The normal VR path then rotates movement into the center-of-pressure reference orientation, the orientation of the rig’s balance-reference transform. The stored components are unitless sideways and forward/back movement input in that frame, not velocity in meters per second.

RemapRig uses this vector with GetPrimaryAxisDirty to calculate movement. An active seat can take over the input: its base handler captures both offered axis vectors, and when the handler takes the input, OpenControllerRig clears both axis vectors to zero and clears the movement-active flag. This getter does not clamp components or promise a universal −1-to-1 range.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.GetPrimaryAxisDirty
member.summary: Whether the primary movement input passes the current device path's activity test.

remarks.para: In the normal OpenControllerRig paths this is an activity flag, not a comparison with the previous sample. Overall stick magnitude is the radial distance of the X/Y pair from center; the deadzone is the small centered region ignored as input. For example, the undefined-controller path sets the flag only when X² + Y² > 0.01, equivalent to radial magnitude > 0.1. Other device paths use MagnitudeRemapAxis, which compares radial magnitude with a lower threshold and linearly rescales the vector between configured thresholds; this is not an AnimationCurve response curve. The thresholds depend on device path.

A stick held steadily beyond its active threshold can keep this true even though its position has not changed. RemapRig uses it as the inputPressed argument for movement. An active seat’s input handler can take the input; OpenControllerRig then clears this flag and both axis vectors to zero. The getter only reads the flag; two reads before the next update return the same value.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. member.summary: The turning-angle change, in degrees, calculated for the current controller update.
member.returns: The cached turn delta in degrees.

remarks.para: OpenControllerRig writes this for both smooth turning and the smoothed release of a snap-turn request. In the smooth path it combines the smoothed sideways input, turn-speed setting, update duration, and time-scale correction. It is a per-update angle, not a torso bend, an absolute facing direction, or degrees per second.

RemapRig applies this angle around its up direction, pivoting at the physical rig's center-of-pressure position (its balance-reference point) when the player has no active seat. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.LootTableData.GetLootItem
member.summary: Rolls the table and selects a spawnable using cumulative item percentages.

remarks.para: Each call chooses a whole number from 1 through 99, with approximately equal chances. It reads items in array order and adds each entry's percentage to a running total that starts at 0. An entry wins when the roll is greater than the total before that entry and at most the total after adding its percentage. The percentages are numbers without physical units; they are not distances, seconds or size multipliers.

For example, a first entry with percentage 20 and a second with percentage 30 select the first for rolls 1–20 and the second for rolls 21–50. Rolls 51–99 return an empty spawnable description. There are 99 possible rolls, so 20 here covers 20 out of 99 chances rather than exactly 20 out of 100.

The method does not adjust the percentages to total 100. A total below 99 can leave rolls with no match; entries beyond an earlier total of at least 99 cannot win when all percentages are nonnegative. Decimal percentages still divide whole-number rolls, so a first entry with percentage 0.5 cannot win any roll. Negative percentages move the running total backward instead of being corrected to 0.

The returned spawnable is a description containing an object-template reference and a pool policy, the rules for limiting and reusing spawned objects. This call neither creates the object nor checks that the chosen description is usable. The caller decides whether and where to request a spawn. A missing items array causes an error; an empty array returns an empty description.

member.returns: The selected spawnable description, or an empty one with no object-template or pool-policy reference if no entry matches the roll.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Spawnable.IsValid
member.summary: Checks whether this spawn request has a crate reference with a nonempty, non-placeholder barcode.

remarks.para: A barcode is the text identifier used to look up an asset in the warehouse, BONELAB's asset catalog. This check returns false when crateRef is missing, its barcode is missing, or the barcode's text is empty or one of the reserved empty identifiers.

This is a check of the identifier only. It does not look up the crate, load its asset, inspect policyData, or create an object. For example, a nonempty identifier for an uninstalled mod can pass this check while a later spawn request fails to find its crate. A missing policyData does not make this check fail.

member.returns: if the crate reference has a barcode whose text passes the check above; otherwise, .

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.#ctor
member.summary: Sets the cartridge’s initial launch settings to 2 Unity world units per second (2 m/s only if this scene uses one Unity world unit per metre) and 100 radians per second, with an empty renderer array.

remarks.para: These are the component’s construction defaults: startSpeed is 2, startAxisSpeed is 100, and renderers contains no entries. Saved scene or prefab settings can replace these values when Unity creates the component. A prefab is a saved template for a scene object.

The constructor does not find the pool component or shell sound component. The speeds are base settings for ForceInDirection, which adds randomized movement and spin to the movement inherited from a supplied host Rigidbody, Unity’s component for simulated physical motion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.Awake
member.summary: Registers this cartridge with its assigned pool component so it can receive pool lifecycle calls.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s setup call when a component is first loaded or created. This method passes this cartridge to the assigned _poolee’s RegisterPoolable method. A pool reuses objects instead of creating a new object for every appearance; registering supplies this component’s pool callbacks, functions the pool calls at lifecycle steps.

The _poolee reference must already point to a valid pool component. Awake uses that reference directly and does not search for it. The registration method appends the cartridge to a list, so manually repeating Awake adds another registration rather than replacing the earlier one.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.Despawn
member.summary: Requests despawning through the cartridge’s linked MarrowEntity and that entity’s pool component.

remarks.para: The inherited marrowEntity reference is the component that groups this object’s gameplay and physics parts. It must be assigned. This method calls that entity’s Despawn method, which forwards to the entity’s assigned Poolee. It does not directly use this cartridge’s separate _poolee field, which is used for callback registration.

For an object belonging to a pool, Poolee forwards the request to the asset spawner’s despawn path. For an object outside a pool, Poolee sends its despawn event, calls pool deinitialization functions, disables the scene object and reports an error. The request therefore does not guarantee that an object outside a pool is returned to reusable pool storage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.MakeDynamic
member.summary: Clears the cartridge’s static-mode flag and enables its shell sound component when changing out of static mode.

remarks.para: If _isStatic is already false, this method returns without changing the sound component. Otherwise it first sets the flag to false, then enables shellSfx. A valid shellSfx reference is required for that change. For example, calling MakeDynamic after MakeStatic reverses that method’s sound-component disable.

Here dynamic describes this cartridge’s sound-component mode. This method does not change the Rigidbody, the component Unity uses to simulate physical movement, or change velocity, collisions or renderer visibility.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.MakeStatic
member.summary: Sets the cartridge’s static-mode flag and disables its shell sound component when changing into static mode.

remarks.para: If _isStatic is already true, this method returns without changing the sound component. Otherwise it first sets the flag to true, then disables shellSfx. A valid shellSfx reference is required for that change. MakeDynamic reverses this mode change.

Here static describes this cartridge’s sound-component mode. This method does not make a Rigidbody, Unity’s physical-motion component, stop moving or become fixed in place. It does not change collisions or renderer visibility. For example, selecting this mode alone does not stop a previously launched casing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.OnPoolDeInitialize
member.summary: Restores the cartridge’s sound-component mode if it was static, and clears the extra hide setting on its listed renderers.

remarks.para: This is a callback, a function the pool calls during deinitialization when finishing with this object. If _isStatic is true, the method first clears that flag and then enables shellSfx. If the flag is already false, it leaves the sound component’s enabled setting alone.

After that conditional sound reset, it calls SetRenderActive with true for every listed renderer, clearing forceRenderingOff, an extra setting that prevents a renderer from drawing. For example, an object hidden through SetRenderActive(false) can have that hide setting cleared before reuse. Clearing it does not turn on a separately disabled renderer or inactive scene object.

The renderer array must exist and all listed entries must be valid; an empty array needs no work. A valid shellSfx is needed when the flag was true. This callback does not restore launch speed settings, change the Rigidbody’s movement, or refill the renderer array.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.Reset
member.summary: Finds the ShellSFX sound component on the same scene object and stores it in shellSfx.

remarks.para: Reset is Unity’s editor setup call when adding or resetting a component. This implementation asks the same object for a ShellSFX component and replaces the shellSfx reference with the result. If no such component exists, the stored reference is empty.

This method only fills that sound reference. It does not reset the launch speeds, fill the renderer list, find _poolee or change the static-mode flag. For example, resetting this component can reconnect its sound reference while preserving the launch-speed settings already stored on it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.DisableNoClip(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Re-enables the cached player bodies' collision detection and clears the no-clip flag.

remarks.para: If the gun host has a Rigidbody-backed MarrowBody, it first asks the gun's Marrow entity to enable its trackers and colliders. An entity groups related game objects; trackers are its interaction-tracking components. It then sets detectCollisions to true on each cached _playerRbs entry and sets _noClipping to false after the loop.

A missing body array still allows the flag to be cleared, but the host must exist and any array entries must be valid. This method does not play the transition sound or clear the body array itself. The delayed grip-release cleanup calls it before clearing that array.
It does not check canNoClip. The supplied hand is not read by this implementation; the body cache already determines which player bodies are changed.

member.param: The reporting hand; this implementation uses the cached bodies rather than reading it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.EnableNoClip
member.summary: Disables collision detection on the cached player bodies and then marks no-clip active.

remarks.para: If the gun host has a Rigidbody-backed MarrowBody, it first asks the gun's Marrow entity to disable its trackers and colliders. It then sets detectCollisions to false on each _playerRbs entry. Only after all those writes does it set _noClipping to true.

The host and body array must be ready, with valid entries. Trigger-grip attachment normally builds the cache; invoking this before that setup can fail. This method does not check canNoClip, play the toggle sound or invoke OnFlyEnabled.

The regular held-input toggle checks canNoClip before enabling this state and requests the sound after the no-clip flag has changed. No-clip changes collision behavior; the flight movement calculation continues separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.CancelPull(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Ends the grip’s hover handling and clears its pull joint, event subscriptions, target hand, and pull bookkeeping.
member.param: The hand whose grip-hover handling should end; normally the current pull target.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The host is the physical object owning this grip. The joint is a temporary connection between bodies in Unity’s physics simulation. The hand proxy is the hand’s stand-in reference supplied to that host. Pass the hand involved in the pull so the grip can end that hand’s hover state. This method removes the pull-complete and hand-attached callbacks, requests destruction of tempJoint, clears tempJoint, sets state to IDELING, clears pullCoroutine and _pullToHand, and removes the host’s hand proxy.

It does not call StopCoroutine or unlock the hand’s hover target. To abort a pull from outside its coroutine, keep the current hand and coroutine references, stop that coroutine, unlock the hand with HoverUnlock, then call CancelPull with that hand. The other-hand attachment handler uses this sequence. Calling CancelPull alone clears the stored handle while its coroutine can still be scheduled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.CoPull(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Creates the physics-step coroutine that brings the grip’s host toward a hand, using direct motion updates and a temporary .
member.param: The hand whose moving handle target the object should approach.
member.returns: The pull coroutine; creating it alone does not start or track a pull.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this one pauses between physics steps. A joint is a connection between bodies in Unity’s physics simulation. A target transform describes the position and rotation the object should approach.

Run the returned sequence with StartCoroutine; Pull normally starts and records it for you. The host must provide a rigidbody, meaning a body in the physics simulation. The host is the physical object owning the grip; the hand proxy is its stand-in reference. Startup gives the host that hand proxy, records the target hand, selects the grip as its ordinary hover receiver, clears the distant hover receiver, then locks hover. That lock stores the grip in the hand’s AttachedReceiver and clears both hover receivers; the routine then sets state to PULLING.

The temporary joint is added to the Hand.rb GameObject and connected to the host rigidbody. All three linear and three angular motion axes are Free, allowing movement and rotation on those axes. autoConfigureConnectedAnchor is false, so Unity does not automatically choose the connection point on the other body. A GameObject is the scene object holding components such as the hand’s Rigidbody. This joint is temporary setup; the routine also applies force and directly changes the object’s velocity and rotation velocity each physics step. It calculates a target from the grip’s force-pull transform and the hand’s matching handle transform, including the hand point’s velocity, and curls the hand pose.

The stored pull distance starts at 6 meters. Predicted separation is the distance in metres, in the scene’s world coordinates, from the object’s center of mass (its balance point) to the target center of mass calculated from the grip and hand positions and rotations. The computed target includes the hand target point’s velocity in metres per second multiplied by fixedDeltaTime, the physics-step duration in seconds, to predict its movement over that step. Before hand attachment begins, the routine cancels when the predicted separation exceeds 1.3 times that 6-metre reference length, or about 7.8 metres (the unitless multiplier 1.3 and length 6 are multiplied with float precision), or when the controller’s secondary interaction button is no longer held. GrabLock is the hand flag that makes this routine abort; a hand with that flag set also causes cancellation. Once _isStartAttaching is true, the button and range checks no longer cause this cancellation, but GrabLock still does.

Near the hand, the routine requests a quick Grip.Snatch. Hand attachment sets _isStartAttaching; finishing the snatch sets _isDoneSnatching. Once completion is reported and more than 0.1 seconds of accumulated physics time have passed since the pull started, it returns to IDELING, clears the tracked coroutine and hand, and destroys the temporary joint. It waits with WaitForFixedUpdate between passes.

The movement force budget is maxForce multiplied by the host’s numerical mass in kilograms, limited to 0.1 through 1.1 for that multiplier. For a positive finite maxForce, some of this budget is reserved for upward gravity compensation. The routine does not safely clamp zero, negative or nonfinite maxForce values; these can make budget divisions or corrections invalid. Separate velocity updates mean this budget is not a guaranteed maximum object speed or a cap on every motion correction.

For a patch that changes the coroutine itself, inspect ForcePullGrip._CoPull_d__26.MoveNext. Its __1__state values are described below; the coroutine’s internal state is separate from ForcePullGrip.state.

item.description: Running or done.
First entry: saves the host in _host_5__3, sets _maxPullDistance_5__2 to 6 meters, records the hand, sets ForcePullGrip.state to PULLING, and creates pull setup.
Continues after WaitForFixedUpdate, adds fixedDeltaTime to _time_5__4, then repeats the motion and lifecycle checks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.Disable
member.summary: Stops this component from responding to the grip’s far-hover events and removes the grip’s FarHover option.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. The joint is a temporary connection between bodies in Unity’s physics simulation. Far-hover handlers are routines the grip calls for distant targeting. When _isEnabled is true and the grip exists, this unsubscribes the begin, end, and update handlers, then clears _isEnabled. Repeated calls while already disabled do nothing.

This method does not cancel an active pull or destroy its temporary joint. OnDisable is the callback Unity calls when this component becomes disabled; it separately unlocks the target hand and calls CancelPull before removing these subscriptions. To abort an ongoing pull yourself, retain its current hand and coroutine handle, stop that sequence, unlock the hand’s hover with HoverUnlock, then call CancelPull with that hand.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.Enable
member.summary: Adds the grip’s FarHover option and subscribes this component to its distant-hand targeting events.

It registers the begin, end, and update handlers, then sets _isEnabled. Repeated calls while already enabled do nothing. A missing grip prevents registration; Start normally obtains the Grip on this component’s GameObject and calls Enable.

member.summary: Checks the distant hand’s button input and starts a pull when the host is free and no pull coroutine is tracked.

Its handle is the reference Unity returns so code can stop it; the saved handle also prevents a duplicate start here. The host must not be attached. Input qualifies when the primary interaction button is pressed this update while the secondary is held, or the secondary is pressed this update while the primary is held. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.OnForcePullComplete(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Records snatch completion when the reporting hand matches the current pull target.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The grip calls this routine with the hand reporting snatch completion. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. A matching hand sets _isDoneSnatching. A different hand is ignored. The coroutine sees this flag during its next physics pass and performs completion cleanup once accumulated physics-step time since the pull started is greater than 0.1 seconds, rather than after a new 0.1-second delay from this notification; this callback itself does not destroy the joint or clear the coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.OnStartAttach(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Records attachment for the pull target, or aborts the pull if another hand attaches first.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The grip’s attachment event calls this routine with the attaching hand. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. For the hand in _pullToHand, this sets _isStartAttaching, allowing the coroutine to finish attachment without canceling when secondary input is released or predicted world-space separation from the object’s center of mass to the hand-derived target exceeds about 7.8 metres (6 metres times the unitless factor 1.3 with float precision). GrabLock, the hand flag that aborts this routine, can still cancel it. It is registered to the grip’s attachedHandDelegate, so it reports attachment beginning rather than predicting a distance. This notification occurs before later Grip attachment-flag and held-hand-list writes, so it does not prove that all attachment bookkeeping is finished.

If a different hand attaches, it stops the tracked coroutine, unlocks the original target’s hover, then calls CancelPull for that target. This protects against continuing to pull an object that another hand has taken.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.Pull(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Starts and tracks CoPull for the supplied hand when no pull coroutine is already tracked.
member.param: The hand to pull the object toward.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. Its handle is the reference Unity returns so code can stop that sequence. A nonnull pullCoroutine makes this call do nothing, preventing a second tracked pull. Otherwise it starts the coroutine and saves its handle.

This direct starter does not check _isEnabled, controller buttons, or whether the host is already attached. Normal far-hover input handling applies those checks before starting. CoPull can still cancel on its own later input and range checks. The grip, hand, and host physics references must already be set up.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._CoPull_d__26.MoveNext
member.summary: Advances the force-pull coroutine, moving and turning the object toward the receiving hand over successive physics steps.
member.returns: True when the coroutine has yielded and needs another step; false when pulling has finished or been canceled.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue on later physics steps. Here, yielding means pausing until WaitForFixedUpdate, the next physics update. Unity calls MoveNext to continue the routine, and its compiler-created iterator object remembers where it paused.

On first entry, this saves the grip’s host and receiving hand, starts with a 6-meter pull-distance limit, locks the hand’s hover target to the grip and enters the PULLING state. It subscribes to force-pull-complete and hand-attached callbacks, routines called when completion or hand attachment is reported, then creates a temporary ConfigurableJoint on Hand.rb connected to the object’s Rigidbody. A joint is a physics connection between two bodies.

The joint’s linear and angular motions are set to Free, meaning the axes have no fixed positional or angular limit. Automatic connected-anchor placement is disabled. Each step derives a desired object position and rotation from the grip handle and receiving hand, accounts for the velocity of the hand at that target point, curls the fingers and applies forces and turning adjustments to bring the object toward it.

maxForce is the base linear pulling-force limit in newtons, before the mass multiplier. The linear force budget is maxForce multiplied by the host’s numerical mass in kilograms, limited to a multiplier from 0.1 to 1.1. For example, a 0.5-kilogram host gives 0.5 × maxForce, while a 2-kilogram host uses 1.1 × maxForce. This helps the calculation account for object mass; it is not a new Rigidbody mass setting. The solver also reserves part of its force budget to counter gravity.

The saved time is elapsed physics time, increased by Time.fixedDeltaTime, the number of seconds in one physics step, after each WaitForFixedUpdate. Before attachment begins, the routine can cancel if the required controller input is released or the predicted hand-to-object separation exceeds 1.3 times the saved pull limit. The initial limit of 6 meters therefore gives a 7.8-meter separation check. This is an internal cancellation check, not the distance at which the player can select every object.

When attachment or cancellation ends the pull, cleanup removes the temporary connection and callback subscriptions and restores the idle state. A true return only means another coroutine step is pending; it does not mean the object was successfully grabbed.

Unity calls this method to continue the paused routine. To patch the actual force-pull steps, target this MoveNext implementation; ForcePullGrip.CoPull only creates the iterator object. The iterator’s __1__state records which entry path to take:

item.description: Executing a step or already finished; this value alone does not distinguish those cases.
First entry: performs pull setup, stores the host and distance limit, and selects PULLING.
Resumes after WaitForFixedUpdate, adds the elapsed physics-step time and continues the pull calculation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.AddInvalidModFile(System.Int64,System.Int64,Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Remembers one rejected mod.io file for a mod and saves that record, allowing subscription checks to skip that same file later.

remarks.para: modID identifies the mod; fileID identifies a particular uploaded file for it. For example, recording mod 101 with file 9001 makes that pair eligible to be skipped. File 9002 for the same mod does not match the record and can still be considered. Recording another file for mod 101 replaces its earlier file ID; this is one record per mod, not a list of every rejected upload.

The call first waits for LoadModSettings, changes invalidMods, copies the dictionary into the JSON entry named mod.io.invalid_mods with JObject.FromObject, then waits for WriteModSettings. JSON is a text format for saving named values. Await the returned task to wait for the save to finish; merely calling the method does not mean the file has already been written.

ModSettingsJSON must contain a settings object when the record is copied into it. A missing or blank settings file does not create that object. If it is still null, the dictionary can change before the call fails, leaving that change unsaved. The supplied cancellation token does not stop this implementation.

For patches, the compiler-generated state machine is the resumable routine that remembers which step is waiting. To change its behavior, patch its state machine's MoveNext method, ModDownloader._AddInvalidModFile_d__12.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are:
A waiting state is only needed when the operation has not already completed; it does not promise a particular number of game frames.

item.description: First entry. It awaits ModDownloader.LoadModSettings().
Continues after LoadModSettings. It updates the settings and awaits ModDownloader.WriteModSettings().
Continues after WriteModSettings. It finishes.
Done.

member.param: The numeric mod.io ID of the mod whose rejected-file record should be changed.
The numeric mod.io ID of the rejected upload for that mod.
Accepted but not checked or passed to the file operations in this implementation.
member.returns: A task to await until settings have been loaded, the record changed, and the save completed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.LoadModSettings
member.summary: Reads saved downloader settings and refreshes the in-memory records of rejected mod.io files.

remarks.para: The method reads mod_settings.json from Unity's persistent data folder, the game's folder for data kept between runs. It waits for the file read, decodes the bytes as UTF-8 text, then parses JSON, a text format for named values. Await the returned task before relying on the refreshed settings.

A missing file, whitespace-only text, or a parsed value that is not a JSON object leaves ModSettingsJSON and invalidMods unchanged. Those cases do not create a new settings object. A JSON object replaces ModSettingsJSON. Its mod.io.invalid_mods entry is converted to a dictionary from mod IDs to file IDs; if that entry is absent, the current invalidMods dictionary is cleared.

Loading can overwrite changes made only in memory. For example, an object with no mod.io.invalid_mods entry clears old rejected-file records, whereas deleting the settings file leaves those records unchanged. File-reading errors, malformed JSON, or data that cannot be converted to the required dictionary can fail the returned task.

For patches, the compiler-generated state machine is the resumable routine that remembers which step is waiting. To change its behavior, patch its state machine's MoveNext method, ModDownloader._LoadModSettings_d__10.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are:
A waiting state is only needed when the operation has not already completed; it does not promise a particular number of game frames.
In this load routine, any state other than 0 enters the initial file check.

member.summary: Deletes a mod's rejected-file record and saves the settings so later subscription checks can consider that file again.

remarks.para: modID is the mod.io ID of the mod. Removing its record removes the one saved file ID for that mod; it does not uninstall the mod, delete its uploaded file, or begin a download. Other requirements, such as the platform and a supported Marrow SDK version (the version of the tools used to build the mod), can still stop a later download.

The call first waits for LoadModSettings. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.WriteModSettings
member.summary: Replaces the saved settings file with the current ModSettingsJSON object.

remarks.para: ModSettingsJSON is the in-memory object of named settings values. The method turns that whole object into JSON text and creates or overwrites mod_settings.json in Unity's persistent data folder, the game's folder for data kept between runs. If the object is null, it finishes without opening or creating a file.

This call saves the JSON object as it stands. It does not automatically copy changes from the separate invalidMods dictionary. AddInvalidModFile and RemoveInvalidModFile perform that copy before saving. For example, directly adding a dictionary entry and then calling WriteModSettings is not enough to save that entry.

Writing continues asynchronously: the returned task lets you wait for the text write and cleanup to finish. The text writer is disposed first, then the file stream, closing the resources used to write the file. The method replaces the destination directly rather than first saving a replacement to a temporary file.

For patches that inspect cleanup state: __7__wrap3 and __7__wrap5 hold caught exceptions; __7__wrap4 and __7__wrap6 mark completed cleanup scopes. A caught exception is rethrown after the corresponding stream has been disposed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.LoadAndCheckLogin(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Loads local mod settings and checks whether an existing or saved mod.io access token can restore the user login.
member.param: Signal that can stop the settings read and token-check requests; it is combined with cancellation when this manager is disabled.
member.returns: A task yielding true when either token passes the authenticated-user request, or false when neither does. A false result does not clear an earlier true IsLoggedIn value.

remarks.para: An access token is a string that lets mod.io recognize the signed-in user. First this method reads mod_settings.json from Unity's persistent data directory, the folder where the game keeps files between runs, and replaces ModSettingsJSON with the loaded object or null. It reads the saved token from the mod.io.access_token entry. Missing settings or a missing entry give an empty saved token.

After loading, it checks ModIOAPI.Context.AccessToken first if that in-memory token is not null. If the check succeeds, it sets IsLoggedIn to true and returns true. If the token is absent or fails, it checks the saved token. A valid saved token sets IsLoggedIn to true and replaces the REST client's active token. For example, a still-valid saved token can restore login after restarting the game without showing a device-code prompt.

If neither check succeeds, the method returns false and leaves the existing IsLoggedIn flag unchanged. It also leaves the active client token unchanged on that failure path. Reading this flag later does not make another server request. This method does not start the interactive WebSocket login or raise the user-initiated login events.

The caller's cancellation token, a signal asking asynchronous work to stop, is linked with _enableCTS.Token, which is cancelled when this manager is disabled. Either signal can cancel the file read and validation work. The method disposes its temporary linked cancellation source on exit, including error cleanup. File or request errors can fail the returned task instead of producing a false result.
The check proceeds in this order:

item.description: It links the caller’s token with the manager’s enable token and waits for LoadModSettings. After the read, it stores the returned object or null in ModSettingsJSON and reads the saved token from mod.io.access_token, using an empty string when the entry is missing.

If the REST client’s active token is not null, it awaits ValidateAccessToken for that token. A valid token sets IsLoggedIn to true and returns true. If the active token is absent or fails validation, it awaits ValidateAccessToken for the saved token.

A valid saved token sets IsLoggedIn to true, replaces the REST client’s active token, and returns true. If neither token validates, the method returns false without clearing an earlier login flag or changing the active token.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.LoadModSettings(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Reads the local mod settings file and returns its parsed JSON object.
member.param: Signal passed to the asynchronous byte read to request cancellation.
member.returns: A task yielding the parsed JSON object, or null when the file is missing, blank, or contains a top-level value other than an object.

remarks.para: The file is mod_settings.json inside Unity's persistent data directory, where game files survive between runs. If it exists, the method reads its bytes asynchronously, so the game can continue while the read waits, decodes the bytes as UTF-8 text, and parses the text as JSON.

A missing file, empty or whitespace-only text, or JSON whose top level is not an object gives null. A non-object value also goes through the debug error logger; a visible message depends on Marrow debug logging being enabled for that thread. For example, {"mod.io.access_token":"saved-token"} produces an object, while an array such as [] gives null. Malformed JSON and file-read errors can fail the task.
This helper does not create or save a file, and returning an object does not itself assign ModSettingsJSON. LoadAndCheckLogin makes that assignment after waiting for the read.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.LogIn(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Starts mod.io device-code login, first trying to restore an existing login; the caller cannot await the final login result.
member.param: Signal requesting cancellation of the login work and the receive loop started by this attempt; disabling the manager also requests cancellation.

remarks.para: Device-code login lets the player authorize this game through a mod.io login page. The method returns UniTaskVoid, an asynchronous operation that yields no result and that its caller cannot await. Sending its login request is only one step: the later WebSocket responses supply the code prompt and final success or failure.

It links the caller's cancellation token with _enableCTS.Token, which is cancelled when the manager is disabled. It first invokes BeginUserInitiatedLogin, if subscribed, and waits for the task returned by that callback, then waits for LoadAndCheckLogin. A callback is a function subscribed to run when the event happens. It waits for the single task returned by the event delegate, rather than separately waiting for each subscriber's asynchronous work.

If token restoration succeeds, it skips the device-code handshake. It invokes CompleteUserInitiatedLogin, if subscribed, and waits for the returned task before cancelling and replacing _receiveLoopCTS. Without a completion callback, this already-logged-in path finishes without that cancellation-source reset.

Otherwise it connects the WebSocket, a connection through which the server can send later messages, and starts its receive loop on the thread pool, which runs work away from Unity's main thread. The receive loop has a separate linked cancellation source combining the caller token, the enable token, and the receive-loop token. The login method waits for a delay configured as one second, then switches to Unity's main thread, queues the device-login request, and sends the queued operation. The configured delay is not a promise of exactly one second of elapsed frame time.

If the login-check or handshake work throws, the method invokes FailUserInitiatedLogin when subscribed and awaits its returned task. It then passes the caught exception to the debug logger; if no failure callback is subscribed, it reaches that logger directly. A visible log message depends on Marrow debug logging being enabled for that thread. The failure callback receives no exception parameter. Errors thrown by callbacks can themselves interrupt this sequence. The temporary linked cancellation source is disposed when this method exits; the receive loop has its own lifetime.
The login proceeds in this order:

item.description: It links the caller’s cancellation token with the manager’s enable token. If BeginUserInitiatedLogin is subscribed, it invokes the callback and awaits the single task returned by the event delegate. It then waits for LoadAndCheckLogin.

If token restoration succeeds, it skips the device-code handshake. When CompleteUserInitiatedLogin is subscribed, the method awaits that callback’s returned task, then cancels and replaces the receive-loop cancellation source. With no completion callback, this shortcut ends without resetting that source.

If restoration fails, it awaits ModIOWebSocketAPI.ConnectAsync, starts the receive loop on the thread pool, then awaits UniTask.Delay with the configured one-second delay. It awaits UniTask.SwitchToMainThread, queues the device-login request through ModIOWebSocketAPI.EnqueueOperation, and awaits ModIOWebSocketAPI.SendOperationsAsync. The receive loop has its own linked cancellation signal from the caller, enable, and receive-loop tokens. The configured delay is not a promise of exactly one second of elapsed frame time.

If the login-check or handshake work throws, it invokes FailUserInitiatedLogin if subscribed and awaits the single returned task. It then reaches the conditional logger for the caught exception; with no failure callback, it reaches the logger directly. If a callback throws, that error can interrupt this sequence. The login method disposes its temporary linked cancellation source on exit, while the receive loop has a separate lifetime.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ValidateAccessToken(System.String,Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Checks an access token by asking mod.io for the authenticated user, without applying that token to the manager.
member.param: Candidate user access-token string to test; this method does not install it as the active token.
Signal passed to the authenticated-user request to request cancellation.
member.returns: A task yielding true if the authenticated-user API result has no error, or false for a blank token or an error result.

remarks.para: An access token is the string that identifies a signed-in user to mod.io. Null, empty, or whitespace-only tokens immediately give false without sending a request. For other strings, the method calls GetAuthenticatedUser with a temporary request context containing this manager's ModIOApiKey and the supplied token, and passes a retry-count setting of 5.

The result is true when the API result reports no error, and false when it reports an error. An exception that escapes the request can fail the task. This test does not replace ModIOAPI.Context.AccessToken or change IsLoggedIn; the caller decides whether a successfully tested token should become active. For example, testing a candidate saved token alone does not sign the manager in.

Non-null JSON object to receive thumbnailOverride, gameId, modId and modfileId.

remarks.para: JSON stores data as named values. The method first adds the inherited thumbnailOverride string, then gameId, modId and modfileId as integer values. These IDs identify the game, the mod within that game, and the specific downloadable file release. They are signed 64-bit identifiers and have no measurement units.

For example, a target with GameId 3809, ModId 123 and ModfileId 456 adds gameId: 3809, modId: 123 and modfileId: 456 alongside thumbnailOverride. The mod and file numbers in this example are illustrative identifiers.

Supply a non-null JSON object with space for these property names. The method adds each property in order. It does not write a file, start a download, or read or change the store parameter. Its effect is filling the JSON object so the surrounding object-store serialization can save it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModIOModTarget.Unpack(Il2CppSLZ.Serialize.ObjectStore,System.String)
member.summary: Loads this target’s thumbnail override and available mod.io IDs from the stored object identified by objectId.
member.param: Non-null object store containing the packed target data.
Text identifier locating the packed object in the store; it is separate from the numeric mod.io IDs inside that object.

remarks.para: An ObjectStore keeps packed objects as JSON and uses a text object ID to locate each object. This method first tries to load thumbnailOverride as a string, then gameId, modId and modfileId as signed 64-bit integers. It looks up each property independently under the supplied objectId.

A missing property leaves that existing field unchanged. For example, if this target already has ModfileId 456 and the stored object has no modfileId property, the value stays 456. Loading a partial record therefore does not reset all three IDs first.

The store must be non-null and contain the expected object structure. Stored ID values must be convertible to signed 64-bit integers. A lookup or conversion error can stop the method after earlier fields were already changed; there is no rollback of those earlier assignments. Loading these IDs does not contact mod.io or begin downloading the release.
