member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetSecondaryAxisInversedRotation
member.summary: Returns a reference up/down half-turn expressed in the frame formed by the grip axes.

remarks.para: Reference directions mean the ordinary local axes: forward is (0, 0, 1), and up is (0, 1, 0). The grip-axis frame is built by treating the configured primary axis as forward and the configured secondary axis as up, relative to targetTransform. The method expresses the reference half-turn in that frame.
With primary (0, 0, 1) and secondary (0, 1, 0), it is a 180-degree turn around local Z: up becomes down. It returns a rotation; it does not change the movement-axis fields.

member.returns: Rotation for the reference up/down half-turn in the grip-axis frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetSubColliders
member.summary: Fills additionalGripColliders with Collider components found on this GameObject and its children.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used by the physics simulation. This refreshes the additionalGripColliders array for grip-related collision handling. It is separate from Start’s gripColliders array, which only collects colliders directly on this GameObject.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetSwingLimit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Gets how far the hand pose allows its grip direction to tilt away from the grip’s primary axis.

remarks.para: The base implementation reads swingRotationLimit from GetHandPose, so a per-hand pose override can change the result. The angle is in degrees. Swing is sideways tilting; twist is rotation around the primary axis. Hand-target solvers use this value to restrict controller-driven rotation, and SolveHandleAmplify also uses it to limit the curve’s correction.

member.returns: Swing-angle limit in degrees from the selected hand pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetTargetInBase(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Gets this hand’s stored grip target relative to targetTransform’s position and orientation.

remarks.para: The result is a SimpleTransform value containing position and rotation. Zero position with identity rotation means targetTransform’s origin and orientation. Position offsets are in meters along that frame’s axes; this conversion uses position and rotation, not targetTransform’s scale. If the hand has no stored target, this creates one at targetTransform’s world pose, which becomes zero position and identity rotation in this frame.

member.returns: Per-hand target relative to targetTransform.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetTargetInHost(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Expresses this hand’s grip target relative to the host object when it reports a Rigidbody, or in world coordinates without a host or when the host reports no Rigidbody.

remarks.para: The host is the grabbable object owning this grip. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object simulated physics motion. With a host that reports a Rigidbody, the method converts targetTransform into the host’s position-and-rotation frame and composes the stored per-hand target. Without a host or when the host reports no Rigidbody, it composes that same target with targetTransform’s world pose. Position is measured in meters; these SimpleTransform calculations do not include scale. A missing stored target is treated as zero position and identity rotation without adding a cache entry.

member.returns: Target in the host’s frame when it reports a Rigidbody, or world space without a host or when the host reports no Rigidbody.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetTargetInWorld(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Converts this hand’s stored grip target into a world position and rotation.

remarks.para: It combines targetTransform’s current world pose with GetTargetInBase for this hand. Position is in meters, and scale is not part of the conversion. The target follows targetTransform when it moves or turns. This is a desired grip-handle pose, not a reading of the physical hand; a missing per-hand target is initialized by GetTargetInBase.

member.returns: Grip-handle target in world coordinates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetTwistLimit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Gets how far the hand pose allows rotation around the grip’s primary axis.

remarks.para: The base implementation reads twistRotationLimit from GetHandPose, including any per-hand pose override. The angle is in degrees. Twist turns around the grip direction, like turning a screwdriver; swing tilts away from that direction. The hand-target solvers use both limits when restricting controller rotation.

member.returns: Twist-angle limit in degrees from the selected hand pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.GetVirtualController(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Chooses the object-control solver for this grip and hand.

remarks.para: A VirtualController combines hand targets to decide how a held object should move. If the grip has a moving host with a Rigidbody, it returns that host’s VirtualController. Otherwise it uses the supplied hand’s virtual skeleton rig controller. This is the game’s motion solver, rather than the hand’s hardware input controller returned by GetController.

member.returns: Host motion solver, or the hand rig’s solver when there is no moving host.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.HandleAxisSpace
member.summary: Builds the grip’s reference orientation with its primary direction as forward and secondary direction as up.

remarks.para: The directions come from GetPrimaryAxis and GetSecondaryAxis with no hand supplied. They are relative to targetTransform’s orientation. For primary (0, 0, 1) and secondary (0, 1, 0), the result is identity rotation. Cylinder and sphere target calculations use this frame to interpret their limits; this method returns a quaternion without rotating the object.

member.returns: Rotation from the ordinary local axes into the grip-axis frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.HasGripFlag(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GripFlags)
member.summary: Checks whether this hand’s grip-state record contains every bit in the requested flag value.

remarks.para: For HOVER | ATTACH it returns true only when both bits are set. It tests bookkeeping, not whether a physics joint currently exists. The query creates a state record when necessary, and a zero flag value always matches.

member.returns: True when all requested bits are present.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnAttachedToHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Records a newly attached hand and locks its hover selection to this grip.

remarks.para: Hand.AttachObject calls this after choosing the held object. It notifies the host, marks the hand state active, invokes attachedHandDelegate, sets ATTACH, locks hovering, and adds the hand to attachedHands. The event runs before ATTACH and the list insertion in the base method. This records attachment; OnJointAttached handles the later physics-joint stage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes the destroyed grip from hand-lookup caches and unregisters it from its entity.

remarks.para: Unity invokes this when the component is destroyed. The Grip and HandReciever cache entries are removed so hands do not resolve this component afterward. If removing this entry leaves either shared cache empty, that cache’s stored reference is reset to null. If the cached MarrowEntity exists, it unregisters this grip as an event handler there.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnDetachedFromHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Clears this hand’s grip state, target, pose override, and object-control pairing after release.

remarks.para: Hand.DetachObject invokes this as part of releasing its held object. The base method marks the state inactive and invokes detachedHandDelegate before clearing ATTACH, deleting the state record, and removing the hand from attachedHands. It cancels any snatch, resets the hand pose and hover lock, notifies the host, disconnects the solver pair, and requests drop sound effects when HandSFX exists. Calling this callback alone does not perform all of Hand.DetachObject’s work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnDisable
member.summary: Releases attached hands and restores their normal hand and hover state when this component is disabled.

remarks.para: Unity calls this on disable. It uses Clear to cancel snatches, reset pose overrides, detach objects and joints, and unlock hovering for tracked attached hands. Returning this grip to its pool uses the same implementation through OnPoolDeInitialize.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnFarHandHoverBegin(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Notifies subscribers when distant-hand hover begins on this grip.

remarks.para: The base method invokes farHoverBeginHandDelegate with the supplied hand when subscribers exist. Distant hover is selecting an object for a possible force pull; this notification does not itself start the pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnFarHandHoverEnd(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Notifies subscribers when distant-hand hover ends on this grip.

remarks.para: The base method invokes farHoverEndHandDelegate with the supplied hand when subscribers exist. Distant hover is selecting an object for a possible force pull; this notification does not itself start the pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnFarHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Notifies subscribers when distant-hand hover continues on this grip.

remarks.para: The base method invokes farHoverUpdateHandDelegate with the supplied hand when subscribers exist. Distant hover is selecting an object for a possible force pull; this notification does not itself start the pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnGrabConfirm(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Applies the chosen hand pose and starts the grab’s attachment sequence.

remarks.para: It copies GetHandPose into the hand’s grip state, asks the animator to blend to it over 0.25 seconds, and clears the controller’s remembered grabbed notification. With targetTransform present it calls Snatch, passing isOverride as Snatch’s isQuick flag. Without targetTransform it directly requests a hand joint and object attachment. This method does not check input thresholds or compare competing grips.

member.param: Passed to Snatch as its quick-mode flag when a targetTransform exists.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandAttachedUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Updates this hand’s held-grip pose, joint settings, release input, and throwing history.

remarks.para: When a connected joint body exists, it records that body’s velocity relative to the player’s whole-body velocity plus its angular velocity. These samples feed the normal release’s throw calculation. It updates the finger-wrap radius from the hand state’s poseRadius and forwards controller squeeze to the physical hand. If a hand joint exists it calls the grip subclass’s UpdateJointConfiguration, then invokes attachedUpdateDelegate. It also handles release input and finger curl; controller-specific grab-toggle rules can alter when release occurs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandHoverBegin(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Starts the close-hover hand animation and notifies hover-begin subscribers.

remarks.para: The base method invokes hoverBeginHandDelegate with the hand, then calls the Boolean overload with isOverride false. That overload marks HOVER and starts the skeleton hand’s hover behavior.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandHoverBegin(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Marks close hover and prepares the hand’s skeleton hover behavior for this grip.

remarks.para: It sets HOVER and calls the skeleton hand’s OnGripHoverStart. When isOverride is true, or the controller reports a recent grab or release, it initializes the hand’s target at targetTransform’s current world pose. Calling this overload directly does not invoke hoverBeginHandDelegate; the one-argument overload does that first.

member.param: Forces initialization of this hand’s grip target when targetTransform is present.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandHoverEnd(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Ends close-hover animation and removes unused hand-specific grip state.

remarks.para: It tells the skeleton hand to stop hovering, invokes hoverEndHandDelegate, then clears HOVER. If ATTACH is still set, it preserves the attached hand’s pose and state. Otherwise it restores the default pose, resets the stored target to zero position and identity rotation in the grip frame, and removes the hand-state record.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Updates close-hover interaction and finger curling when this grip accepts the hand’s input.

remarks.para: It first calls the Boolean overload with isOverride false. If that returns false, this method stops without updating the animator or invoking hoverUpdateHandDelegate. On success, it scales the controller’s five finger-curl values toward zero using the square of the primary interaction axis, applies them to the animator, then invokes the hover-update event. Here the primary interaction axis is the controller’s unitless trigger amount, ordinarily 0 when released and 1 when fully pressed. For each incoming finger-curl value c and input a, the result is c × (1 − clamp(a × a, 0, 1)); clamp limits the squared input to the range from 0 to 1. The parenthesized factor is the unitless fraction of c to keep: a = 0 keeps c, a = 0.5 keeps 75% of c, and a = 1 makes it zero.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Checks whether ordinary close hover can continue, or starts a grab through the override path.

remarks.para: With isOverride false, a locally disabled grip or inactive component is rejected and its receiver is marked disabled. Otherwise it returns whether the controller reports a recent grab or the released state. With isOverride true it bypasses those availability checks, applies the hand pose, clears the remembered grabbed notification, and starts a quick snatch when targetTransform exists; it returns true. This overload alone does not invoke hoverUpdateHandDelegate.

member.param: Uses the direct grab path instead of the ordinary availability/input check.
member.returns: Whether the ordinary input check passes, or true after initiating the override grab.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnJointAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Registers the new hand-and-grip pair with the object-control solver and updates joint settings.

remarks.para: A joint connects the hand and object in the physics simulation. After that connection is prepared, this callback requests grab sound effects when HandSFX exists, adds the pair to GetVirtualController’s solver, and calls the subclass’s UpdateJointConfiguration. The base Grip joint-settings hook does nothing; specialized grips can configure it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnPoolDeInitialize
member.summary: Runs the same attached-hand cleanup as OnDisable when the grip is returned to its pool.

remarks.para: Pooling saves an object for reuse instead of destroying it. This cleanup cancels snatches, resets the hand pose and hover lock, and detaches tracked attached hands before the object is reused.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Provides a grip-specific hook during the attached hand’s runtime-skeleton physics update.

remarks.para: Hand.OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate calls this for the held Grip while the hand is outside its warmup phase. The base Grip method does nothing; subclasses can override it. It does not itself solve skeleton transforms or joint constraints.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.RemoveGripFlag(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GripFlags)
member.summary: Clears the selected interaction-state bits from this grip’s record for one hand.

remarks.para: Other bits stay set. For example, removing HOVER | FARHOVER preserves ATTACH. This changes the state record only; removing ATTACH does not detach the object or destroy its joint. Querying the hand state can create a record when none exists.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.RemoveHandPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Clears this hand’s grip-pose override and restores its animator’s default hand pose.

remarks.para: Future GetHandPose calls fall back to the grip’s handPose while no override is set. Restoring the animator’s default pose now is separate from choosing that fallback for later grip calculations. This does not detach the hand or change the grip-wide handPose field.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.RemoveTarget(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Removes this hand’s cached target offset from the grip.

remarks.para: A later GetTargetInBase or GetTargetInWorld call initializes the target at targetTransform’s origin and orientation again. This removes a stored SimpleTransform value; it does not destroy a scene Transform, detach the hand, or remove the hand-state record.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.SetEntity(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Stores the entity owning this grip and registers the grip as one of that entity’s event handlers.

remarks.para: Supply a valid MarrowEntity. The base method registers on the new entity immediately but does not unregister a previously assigned entity first. OnDestroy unregisters from the currently stored entity. Replacing the entity repeatedly therefore needs care with the previous registration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.SetHandPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose)
member.summary: Sets this hand’s grip-pose override and blends its animation toward that pose.

remarks.para: The override is stored in this grip’s per-hand state; other hands and the grip-wide handPose field are unchanged. The animator is asked to transition over 0.25 seconds. The pose also supplies the swing and twist limits returned for this hand, so it can affect allowed hand rotation as well as finger placement. RemoveHandPose clears the override.

member.param: Pose definition for this hand’s fingers and allowed grip rotation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.SetupConfiguration(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandJointConfiguration)
member.summary: Provides a subclass hook for preparing the settings used to connect a hand to this grip.

remarks.para: Start passes the hand receiver’s HandJointConfig into this hook. The base Grip implementation leaves it unchanged. Specialized grips write settings such as connection axes and movement limits; this parameter is runtime configuration data, not necessarily a configuration asset.

member.param: Hand-joint settings an override can modify before attachment.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.Snatch(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts attaching the hand to this grip, optionally moving the hand onto its target first.

remarks.para: It first attaches this grip’s GameObject as the hand’s held object, then starts CoSnatch to prepare and finish the joint. If this hand already has a recorded snatch coroutine for this grip, the call returns without starting another. Normal mode moves the skeleton hand toward the grip and waits across physics updates; quick mode skips that movement and wait. This moves the hand onto the grip rather than pulling a distant object toward the player.

member.param: Skips the skeleton-hand movement and wait when true; defaults to false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.SolveHandTarget(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Calculates the world-space pose the hand should reach at this grip, including allowed wrist rotation and the pose’s hand offset.

remarks.para: It starts from the stored grip-handle target, compares the controller’s handle rotation to it, applies soft swing and twist limits, updates the animator’s rotation blend, and adds the hand’s pose offset. The returned SimpleTransform contains position in world meters and world rotation; it is a desired pose, not the physical hand’s measured pose. SkeletonHand uses it while moving the hand onto a grip. This calculation does not itself write a joint anchor.

member.returns: Desired hand pose in world coordinates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.SolveHandleAmplify(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Calculates a wrist-dependent rotation correction for the two-hand object-control solver.

remarks.para: The curve’s horizontal input is signed sideways wrist bend in degrees from the hand’s virtual skeleton, rather than controller squeeze. Its vertical output is a correction angle in degrees, not a multiplier. The magnitude is limited by GetSwingLimit and stored in this hand state’s amplifyRotationInBase. The correction uses the third grip direction, secondaryMovementAxis crossed with primaryMovementAxis; positive curve values reverse that direction.

GameWorldSkeletonRig calculates this before the virtual object-control solver runs. In the two-hand calculation the solver applies the inverse correction to controller-handle rotations. For example, a curve value of 10 requests a 10-degree correction when the swing limit allows it; later blending and constraints can change the final object motion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.Start
member.summary: Collects this GameObject’s colliders and asks the grip subclass to prepare its hand-joint settings.

remarks.para: Unity calls this during startup after Awake. It replaces gripColliders with Collider components directly on this GameObject, then calls SetupConfiguration with HandJointConfig. Child colliders are collected separately by GetSubColliders into additionalGripColliders. The base Grip configuration hook does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.UpdateJointConfiguration(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Hook for a grip subclass to adjust the physics connection holding a particular hand to the object. The base Grip implementation does nothing.

remarks.para: Grip calls this after a joint is attached and during held-hand updates while the hand has a live joint. A joint is the physics connection that keeps the hand and object together; a subclass can change how strongly it pulls or when it breaks. CylinderGrip overrides this hook, including its squeeze-dependent break-force calculation. Calling the base implementation alone applies no springs, damping, or limits.

member.param: The hand whose current physics joint the subclass may update.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AmmoCount
member.summary: Returns how many rounds the magazine can currently supply, limited by the matching reserve ammunition.

remarks.para: The chambered round is separate and is not included. With 12 rounds in the magazine and only 5 matching rounds in AmmoInventory, this method returns 5. Negative reserve counts produce 0. Without an AmmoInventory reference, the reserve limit used here is 999.
A MagazineState with its cartridge list must already exist; this method does not return a safe zero for a missing magazine state.

member.returns: Usable magazine rounds after the reserve limit; excludes the chambered round.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CeaseFire
member.summary: Clears the trigger-press latch and the flag that remembers a shot during the current trigger press.

remarks.para: This lets a later Fire call count as a fresh press. It does not directly clear isFiring, release the physical trigger, or stop the slide animation. A slide return also checks the cleared trigger-press latch when deciding whether to end firing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.Charge
member.summary: Resets the gun to a forward slide and cocked hammer, clears the old chamber contents, and tries to load a new round.

remarks.para: A cocked hammer is ready to strike a round. This instant path marks the chamber empty before clearing the old cartridge data, so it does not spawn the old round or case as a loose ejected object. PullCartridge then takes a round from the magazine if one is available. The gun ends this operation with isFiring cleared.
This is the instant charging path used during configured loading; it does not play a full hand-driven slide stroke.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CheckGunRequirements
member.summary: Blinks the magazine or charging-handle helper to show the player what needs attention before firing.

remarks.para: It chooses the magazine hint when there is no magazine or no usable magazine ammo and no cartridge data remains in the chamber. Otherwise it can choose the charging hint when the hammer is uncocked or the slide is locked open.

Both selected helper renderers (Unity components that draw the visual hints) must exist, and another hint blink must not already be running. The charging hint is skipped only when the slide is not LOCKED and either the hammer is cocked or a manual gun has already fired during this press. A locked slide can therefore request the charging hint even for that manual gun. This method does not return a pass/fail result.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CompleteSlidePull
member.summary: Finishes a full rearward slide stroke: cocks the hammer, ejects the previous round or case, and attempts to take the next round from the magazine.

remarks.para: If loading succeeds, the new round is recorded as chambered here, before the forward return finishes. After cocking, ejection and the loading attempt, the first lock decision calls SlideLocked only when a magazine is present, cartridgeState is NONE, fireMode is not MANUAL and isSlideLockedOnEmpty is enabled. Otherwise it marks the slide PULLED.

The slide-grab blocking flag ends isFiring before the hammer is cocked. After the cock/eject/load attempt, an assigned slide controller is frozen in manual fire mode, before the first lock decision. Internal-magazine art is refreshed after the lock/return decisions, followed by the visible round/case selection.

When manual override is off, a second independent decision rechecks magazine presence, cartridgeState NONE and isSlideLockedOnEmpty, without the first decision's non-manual requirement. This second check can lock a manual gun. The first SlideLocked call can request magazine ejection, so the second check observes any synchronous change to magazine presence. If the conditions remain true, SlideLocked is called twice, including its lock sound and configured ejection request each time. Otherwise the second decision starts the forward return animation.

With manual override active, the second lock check is skipped and the return clip is displayed at 1 minus the saved pull fraction. This displays the return position directly; it does not start the ordinary timed return.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CompleteSlideReturn
member.summary: Marks the slide as fully forward and finishes the return sound and firing-state checks.

remarks.para: It does not take another round from the magazine; CompleteSlidePull or SlideRelease already performed that step. The release sound plays when the gun is not firing or uses manual fire mode. If firing is still marked active but the trigger-press latch was cleared, firing ends.
During manual override, it switches the visual animation back to slide pull at the saved pull amount, ready for the next stroke.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.EjectCartridge
member.summary: Starts spawning the chamber's live round or spent case at the ejection point when present, then clears the logical chamber.

remarks.para: UNSPENT chooses the cartridge data's full-round spawnable; SPENT chooses its empty-case spawnable. It starts the spawn operation first, then clears cartridgeState and chamberedCartridge without waiting for the loose object to finish spawning or launching. If the spawn result is already available, the operation can launch the object synchronously before that logical clearing; asynchronous spawning does not guarantee that the chamber clears first.

An empty chamber does not spawn an object. When the gun no longer has a magazine, its stored chamber-round and case art are also released. The remaining art visibility is refreshed for the now-empty chamber and any available next round.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.Fire
member.summary: Attempts a shot from a cocked gun with its slide fully forward, applying recoil, firing effects, and chamber-state changes when a live round is ready.

remarks.para: A live round becomes SPENT, then OnFire spends one matching reserve round when an inventory is assigned, starts projectile and muzzle-flare requests, and notifies listeners without awaiting the spawned objects. The firing sound and round/case art also update. Non-manual modes start the automatic slide cycle; manual mode requires the player to operate the action again.

A locked-open slide with usable magazine ammo is released instead of immediately firing. A slide that is not fully returned, an uncocked hammer, a slide-grab blocking flag, or an already-fired press in a non-automatic mode prevents a shot. An empty chamber with otherwise ready states plays dry-fire audio and uncocks the hammer.

This method assumes the gun's host, sound, animation and firing references were initialized. It can set firing/trigger latches before discovering a later reason to refuse the shot; calling it is not proof that a projectile was emitted.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.HasMagazine
member.summary: Returns whether the gun counts as having a magazine: an internal magazine always qualifies; otherwise the saved magazine-state presence flag decides.

remarks.para: This does not test whether the magazine contains rounds or whether a live round is chambered. For removable magazines, the MagazineState setter maintains the presence flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.InstantLoadAsync
member.summary: Refills an existing magazine and, when an ammo socket is assigned, asks it to load defaultMagazine without a manual insertion.

remarks.para: If an internal magazine or an existing magazine is present, it refills MagazineState first. With isCharged enabled it also clears the old chamber contents without spawning an ejected round or case, cocks the hammer and tries to take a new round. A newly force-loaded magazine uses OnMagazineInserted to finish the configured charging path.

Without an ammo socket, there is no socket operation to await. This method marks _wasInstaLoaded on entry; the insertion callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) clears that flag, so the flag alone does not prove loading has completed.

To patch the asynchronous loading sequence, inspect Gun._InstantLoadAsync_d__98.MoveNext. State -1 starts loading: it marks instant loading, refills/charges any available magazine, then awaits AmmoSocket.ForceLoadAsync if a socket exists. State 0 resumes after that await and finishes without another refill step. State -2 means the operation is done.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.MakeDynamic
member.summary: Re-enables collision shapes on the magazine host currently held by the ammo socket, if one exists.

remarks.para: These shapes let the attached magazine participate in physical contact again. The method does not change the gun's Rigidbody (Unity's component for simulated physics movement) into a different physics mode. A missing socket or magazine host makes this a no-op.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.MakeStatic
member.summary: Disables collision shapes on the magazine host currently held by the ammo socket, if one exists.

remarks.para: These shapes normally make the magazine collide with nearby objects. The method does not make the gun's Rigidbody (Unity's component for simulated physics movement) immovable. A missing socket or magazine host makes this a no-op.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnFire
member.summary: Starts projectile and muzzle-flare requests for the prepared chambered cartridge, spends one matching reserve round when an inventory is assigned, and calls firing listeners.

remarks.para: Fire normally calls this after turning the cartridge state from UNSPENT to SPENT and applying recoil. Calling OnFire directly bypasses Fire's slide, hammer and once-per-press checks; it does not perform those checks or apply that recoil itself.

chamberedCartridge supplies ProjectileData, the projectile definition and settings passed to the static ProjectileEmitter.Emit routine. When _ammoInventory is assigned, one matching reserve round is removed before that request. Emit uses firePointTransform and a valid proxyOverride, otherwise the host's trigger proxy. The onFireDelegate callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) receives this gun after projectile-emission and flare-spawn requests have started, without awaiting either object; projectile setup and flare loading can both still be pending.

In manual fire mode, it first uncocks the hammer and unfreezes an assigned slide controller, before reserve removal and the spawn requests. In the normal Fire path, GunShot audio and cartridge-art updates follow this notification. The gun must already have valid cartridge data and firing references.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnMagazineInserted
member.summary: Updates cartridge art after the ammo socket has supplied a magazine or added rounds to an internal magazine.

remarks.para: Normal insertion plays the magazine-insert sound. Instant loading suppresses that sound; if isCharged is enabled, it also clears the old chamber contents without spawning an ejected round or case, cocks the hammer and tries to load a fresh round. After the instant-loading branch, it clears _wasInstaLoaded whether or not isCharged was enabled.

The socket sets MagazineState or adds internal-magazine rounds before calling this. Calling this callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) alone does not insert a magazine or assign its inventory.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnMagazineRemoved
member.summary: Plays the magazine-drop sound and removes the next-round art, while keeping art for any cartridge still in the chamber.

remarks.para: If chamberedCartridge is absent, the chamber-round and case art are released too. Otherwise their visibility continues to follow cartridgeState, allowing a chambered live round or spent case to remain after the magazine is removed.
In the removable-magazine socket path, the socket calls this before setting MagazineState to null. This method itself does not clear that state or eject the chambered cartridge.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.PlayAnimationState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates,System.Single)
member.summary: Starts a timed gun animation, replacing the previous timed animation and advancing it across frames.

remarks.para: Forward SLIDEPULL uses fireCurve and the cached pull duration, fireDuration times pullAnimationPerc. Here fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds, and pullAnimationPerc is its unitless pull-duration share. SLIDEPULLREVERSED instead uses returnCurve and the return duration, fireDuration times returnAnimationPerc; returnAnimationPerc is the independent unitless return-duration share. Forward SLIDERETURN uses that same returnCurve and return duration. SLIDERETURNREVERSED uses the default full duration of 1 second with no curve selected. Both SLIDELOCKED variants use slideLockDuration in seconds. These reverse choices are not symmetric copies of their forward counterparts.

For example, startPerc = 0.5 begins halfway through the requested sequence and shortens its remaining duration. This is a fraction, not a percentage from 0 to 100. The method does not clamp it to the usual 0-to-1 interval.

Remaining time equals (1 minus startPerc) times the selected full duration; startPerc is the unitless sequence-start fraction. Reversed playback moves toward clip position 0; forward playback moves toward 1. The timed sequence advances across rendered frames, and recognized endpoint effects are deferred until the end of the frame. Pull completion can attempt loading; return completion itself does not load a round.

member.param: The sequence to run, such as slide pull, return, or lock.
Starting fraction of the sequence; 0 starts at the beginning and 0.5 starts halfway through.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.PullCartridge
member.summary: Takes the next usable round from the magazine and records it as a live chambered cartridge.

remarks.para: The gun first limits the magazine's cartridge list to AmmoCount, which accounts for available reserve ammo; the magazine state also respects its configured capacity. It then removes the last remaining cartridge from that list and assigns its data to chamberedCartridge. Successful loading sets cartridgeState to UNSPENT.

Without a magazine it only refreshes art. With no available cartridge, it assigns no cartridge data; callers such as the completed slide pull clear the old chamber first. This method does not deduct reserve ammo for a shot; OnFire does that later.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.RequiresChargingHandle
member.summary: Reports whether usable magazine ammo is waiting but the hammer is uncocked or the slide is locked open.

remarks.para: It returns false when AmmoCount is zero. With ammo available, an uncocked hammer returns true; a cocked hammer returns true only while the slide is locked. This is a readiness check, not a test for which kind of physical handle the gun model uses.

member.returns: True when usable magazine ammo exists and the tested hammer/slide states require charging or release.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SetAnimationState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates,System.Single)
member.summary: Selects a gun animation and shows it at a particular point, including the slide-completion logic when its endpoint is reached.

remarks.para: The animation fraction normally runs from 0 at the beginning of the clip to 1 at its end; 0.25 means one quarter through. Reversed variants finish at 0 instead of 1. The gun stores animationState, plays the appropriate neutral/pull/return/lock clip on animator layer 0, and schedules recognized completion work for the end of the frame.

This does not start a timed playback coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames). PlayAnimationState supplies the across-frame progression. Values are passed to Animator.Play without a 0-to-1 clamp, and enum values outside the handled clip states are stored without selecting a clip.

The lastCompletedAnimation guard suppresses repeated completion scheduling for the same state after its endpoint has been recorded. A call selecting a different state resets that guard before testing its endpoint. Recording the endpoint happens before starting the end-of-frame completion routine; it does not mean the deferred work has already finished.

member.param: The neutral, slide-pull, slide-return, or slide-lock state to display, including reversed variants.
Normalized clip position: for example, 0.5 displays its midpoint.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideGrabbed
member.summary: Records whether grabbing the slide should block firing, according to allowFireOnSlideGrabbed.

remarks.para: With allowFireOnSlideGrabbed false, _isSlideGrabbed becomes true and Fire refuses a shot while it stays true. With the option true, this blocking flag stays false. This method does not itself enter manual override or call OnSlideGrabbed; the slide-controller grab callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) does those additional steps.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideGrabbedReleased
member.summary: Clears the firing block that was recorded when the slide was grabbed.

remarks.para: This only clears _isSlideGrabbed. It does not resume an animation or invoke OnSlideReleased; the slide-controller release callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) handles those steps separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideLocked
member.summary: Holds the slide logically open, starts the slide-lock animation and sound, and can request automatic magazine ejection.

remarks.para: The previous timed animation is stopped. When isMagEjectOnEmpty is enabled, OnMagazineEjectDelegate is invoked after the slide-lock sound call; AmmoSocket normally subscribes its ejection method to that request. This method does not itself test whether the magazine is empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideOverride
member.summary: Lets manually supplied slide travel drive the gun's animation during subsequent updates.

remarks.para: For non-manual fire modes, a locked slide starts with saved pull amount 1; other slide states start at 0 and become PULLING. UpdateSlidePercentage then supplies the hand's pull fraction, which Update applies while override is active.

This does not set the separate slide-grab firing block or notify grab listeners. The normal slide-controller callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) performs those actions together.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideOverrideReleased
member.summary: Ends manual slide control and, where the slide state allows it, resumes a timed return from the saved pull position.

remarks.para: A partially pulling slide starts the reversed-pull sequence; a pulled or returning slide starts the forward return in non-manual fire modes. A fully returned or locked slide does not start either sequence here.
After selecting the continuation, the saved override fraction resets to 0 and manual override is disabled. This method does not clear _isSlideGrabbed by itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlidePull
member.summary: Plays the slide-pull sound while manual slide override is active.

remarks.para: Without manual override it does nothing. It does not start a slide animation, eject a cartridge, or cock the hammer. The normal controller pull callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) also calls SlideRelease, which is a separate operation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideRelease
member.summary: Releases a locked-open slide, tries to load a round, and starts moving the slide forward.

remarks.para: It does nothing unless slideState is LOCKED. It takes a cartridge through PullCartridge, clears isFiring and marks the slide PULLED. Without manual override it starts the timed return; with override it displays the return at 1 minus the saved pull fraction. Cartridge art is then refreshed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SpawnCartridge(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Spawnable)
member.summary: Starts spawning a loose cartridge or case at shellSpawnTransform, then throws it out using shellOrientationTransform.

remarks.para: The orientation transform's world right and up directions are passed to the cartridge's ejection force routine together with the gun's Rigidbody (Unity's component for simulated physics movement). This produces a separate loose object; it does not clear the logical chamber itself.

The spawned object's collision shapes are disabled during launch and re-enabled after a 33-millisecond delay. The delay is time-based, not a fixed count of rendered frames. A missing spawn result ends without launching anything; a valid result is expected to contain FirearmCartridge and its configured references.

member.param: The full-round or empty-case object definition to spawn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SpawnFlareAsync
member.summary: Starts spawning muzzleFlareSpawnable at firePointTransform and gives its Rigidbody (Unity's component for simulated physics movement) the gun's cached movement velocity.

remarks.para: The spawn position and rotation come from the firing point in world space. After loading, the spawned object is expected to have a Rigidbody so it can carry the saved velocity; otherwise the method logs an error.

Fire refreshes cachedVelocity when it finds the gun's Rigidbody. This routine reads the cache after the asynchronous spawn completes, so it is not a separate immutable snapshot for each outstanding flare.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.UpdateSlidePercentage(System.Single)
member.summary: Stores the manual slide-pull fraction for the next gun update.

remarks.para: During manual override, Update uses this fraction to position the pull animation, or 1 minus the fraction to position the return animation. For example, 0.25 means a quarter of the pull, not 25 meters or 25 percent passed as the number 25.
This method does not immediately move the animator or invoke OnSlideUpdate. It stores the value without clamping it to 0 through 1.

member.param: Pull fraction: 0 is fully forward, 1 is fully pulled back.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.DisableGunFire
member.summary: Blocks normal trigger-driven firing through this manager's permission flag.

remarks.para: Gun.Update checks the flag before requesting Fire from the held trigger grip. This method does not unload guns, stop a running slide cycle, or add a permission check to direct Gun.Fire calls. EnableGunFire clears this input-path block.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.EnableGunFire
member.summary: Allows normal trigger-driven firing to pass this manager's permission check again.

remarks.para: This only sets the stored permission true. The gun still needs its slide, hammer, cartridge and press-latch conditions (the remembered trigger-press flag records the initiating press) to allow a shot; it does not fire immediately or reload ammunition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.OnGunDropped(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun)
member.summary: Reports a qualifying hand release, notifies drop listeners, and reduces this gun's tracked grab count.

remarks.para: The hand's physics-rig entity must match _playerTag, and the gun must already be in _gunGrabCount, the dictionary storing each gun's accepted grab count. Otherwise no drop listener runs. Each listener receives the releasing hand and gun before the count is reduced.

When the count falls to zero or below, the manager removes the gun and unsubscribes its fire-event forwarding. Releasing one of two tracked hands still sends a drop notification but keeps fire forwarding for the remaining grab.
This is a bookkeeping callback, a routine called to report an action, not an operation that physically detaches a hand. It expects a valid hand, manager, physics rig and tag query.
_playerTag is the manager's configured matching rule for the entity belonging to the hand's physics rig. It is not automatically a local-player lookup or a test of the gun's tag.

member.param: The hand whose release is being reported; its rig must match the player query.
The previously tracked gun released by that hand.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.OnGunFire(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun)
member.summary: Forwards a gun-fire notification to every registered manager fire listener.

remarks.para: Each listener receives the supplied gun. The normal subscription is installed when the first qualifying grab of that gun is tracked and removed after its last qualifying release.
This method does not fire a projectile or check CanFireGun. Calling it directly forwards the supplied notification even if no actual shot occurred.

member.param: The gun included in the forwarded firing notification.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.OnGunGrabbed(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun)
member.summary: Reports a qualifying hand grab, notifies grab listeners, and begins forwarding shots from the gun on its first tracked grab.

remarks.para: The hand's physics-rig entity must match _playerTag; a nonmatching entity is ignored. Each listener receives the hand and gun before the grab count increases and before the first fire subscription is installed.

Every accepted call increases the count, including an additional hand on an already tracked gun. The count tracks notifications, so reporting the same grab twice is not deduplicated. This method does not attach a hand physically.
It expects a valid hand, manager, physics rig and tag query. Gun's host-attachment callback, a routine called to report the attachment action, normally reports the grab.
_playerTag is the manager's configured matching rule for the entity belonging to the hand's physics rig. It is not automatically a local-player lookup or a test of the gun's tag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.DryFire
member.summary: Plays the empty-trigger click and clicks the controllers holding the gun.

remarks.para: Chooses dryFire, or dryFireSlow during sufficiently slow game time, and requests sound at the GunSFX transform’s local origin so it follows the gun. The slow-motion list is considered when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less. A time scale of 1 is normal game speed, while 0.5 is half speed. An empty slow list falls back to the normal clips with time-dependent pitch adjustment.

After requesting audio, the method sends a click-style controller vibration to every hand attached to the cached _host that has a Haptor. Haptic feedback means controller vibration. The _host is the component that tracks attached hands. Start, Unity’s one-time setup routine before this enabled component’s first frame update, gets it from this GameObject and stores it. A Haptor is the controller’s vibration helper. A missing host skips vibration while still allowing audio playback.

This method does not check the chamber or consume ammunition; the gun’s firing logic decides when to call it. Calling it directly produces feedback even if the gun is loaded. Use an empty array to disable this sound. The playback helper returns for an empty normal list, including when a slow list is populated; a null normal array is not checked safely.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.GunError
member.summary: Has no built-in sound or other response in the shipped native implementation.

remarks.para: The native method is empty and returns immediately. Calling it does not log an error, repair the gun or play dryFire. A mod that wants an error effect must provide its own behavior rather than relying on this empty implementation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.GunShot
member.summary: Requests gunshot audio through the component’s reusable managed audio player.

remarks.para: Chooses fire, or fireSlow when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less, and plays at the GunSFX transform’s current world position. Time.timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed and 0.5 is half speed. This is a world-point request, unlike the handling sounds parented to the gun. _gunshotMap stores the playback helper used for these shot requests. If no valid AudioPlayer is ready, the request starts obtaining one and sound can begin on a later frame. Further requests while that player is being obtained replace the saved clip and playback settings, rather than queueing one separate sound per call.

One index is randomly selected using the normal fire list’s length, including when the slow list is used. Keep a populated fireSlow list at least as long as fire, preferably with a matching alternate at each index, to avoid an out-of-range selection. An empty fireSlow list falls back to fire with pitch adjusted for slowed time; a null slow list is not safe on the slow-time branch.

This method plays audio only; it does not launch a projectile, change ammo or apply recoil. Its body does not perform the controller-vibration loop used by the handling methods. Use an empty array to disable this sound. The playback helper returns for an empty normal list, including when a slow list is populated; a null normal array is not checked safely.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.Awake
member.summary: Registers this hand for component lookup and prepares the references and collider lists needed for grabbing and hover searches.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine called during component setup. Unity calls this during component initialization. It adds the hand to Cache, finds the PhysHand (the component that drives the physical hand and arm) and Rigidbody (an object whose movement Unity physics calculates) on the same GameObject, creates a 128-entry collider search buffer and an empty list of ignored collisions, and subscribes OnLevelLoad to the scene-stream session.
This prepares the hand for later updates; it does not attach an object or perform a hover search itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.CoJointBreakCooldown
member.summary: Cleans up a broken grab connection after waiting for the next physics update.

remarks.para: When the coroutine (a sequence that continues over several frames) first runs, it calls PhysHand.ClearJerk with 0.2. This caps the existing linear and angular strength-recovery multipliers at 0.2 and sets the shock factor to 1. These are unitless scaling values: the linear multiplier affects available muscle strength for moving the hand, while the angular multiplier affects rotational drive strength and the shock factor affects damping. The 0.2 is not a wait in seconds or a command to zero the hand's velocity. It then yields WaitForFixedUpdate to wait for the next physics update. After that wait it calls DetachObject and DetachJoint with a normal, non-quick release and no last grip.
OnJointBreak starts this coroutine automatically. Merely obtaining the returned iterator does not run the cleanup; it must be started as a coroutine.

member.returns: The coroutine that clears the held-object state and releases the remaining joint.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.CreateConfigurableJoint
member.summary: Adds a new physics joint to the hand and stores it in tempJoint for the grab setup code to configure.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection between two objects. This method only creates the component: it does not choose the connected object or apply the grip's joint settings. Calling it repeatedly creates additional components and replaces the tempJoint reference.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.DetachIgnoreBodyJoints
member.summary: Removes the extra connections between a held object and this hand's forearm and upper arm.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection. AttachIgnoreBodyJoints creates these two joints on the held object's host GameObject, connected to the arm rigidbodies; a Rigidbody is an object whose movement Unity physics calculates. This method destroys both and clears their stored references. They are separate from the arm's own driving joints and the main hand-to-object grab joint.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.DetachJoint(System.Boolean,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip)
member.summary: Releases the hand's grab joint and restores the collision pairs that were ignored while holding the object.

remarks.para: Uses joint when it still exists, otherwise tempJoint. If a joint exists, it starts the release coroutine (a sequence that continues over several frames) and immediately clears both stored joint references. The old component can therefore remain alive briefly after these fields become null.

A joint is a physics connection; its drives are the spring, damping and strength settings that pull it toward a target. A normal release sets the joint's movement and rotation axes free and removes its drives for approximately 0.08 seconds accumulated over fixed physics updates before destroying it. A quick release skips that waiting loop. Both paths temporarily disable the finger collider and remove the extra forearm/upper-arm connections. Completed cleanup requests re-enabling the finger collider; a later check against fingerColCheckMask enables it only when the checked finger box has no blocking overlap.

When lastGrip has grip colliders, the routine checks the hand collider against its first grip collider and moves the physical hand toward separating it from the grip, retaining its rotation and limiting the movement to 0.1 metres (ten centimetres). A deeper overlap may therefore remain. The ignored collision pairs are restored and their list cleared by DetachJoint itself.
This releases the physics connection. DetachObject separately clears the held-object reference and sends the receiver's release callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action).

member.param: True skips the 0.08-second joint-release waiting loop.
The released grip, used to check hand/object overlap; null skips that check.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.DetachObject
member.summary: Clears the hand's held-object state and tells the previous receiver that this hand released it.

remarks.para: First clears currentAttachedGO, then performs the inventory removal work and clears the inventory-slot association. If the previous object has a receiver, it calls that receiver's OnDetachedFromHand with this Hand. It then clears matching far hover through its setter, matching near hover through its setter, and matching AttachedReceiver, in that order. Finally it invokes the hand's onRecieverDetached event with the previous receiver. The receiver callback can still observe the old matching hover and reservation references; the final hand event sees them after clearing.

The receiver can perform its own release work in that callback (a routine called to perform or report an action). This method does not directly call DetachJoint; joint cleanup is a separate operation in Hand.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.DisableCollider
member.summary: Turns off physics collision detection for the hand Rigidbody and its lower-arm Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is an object whose movement Unity physics calculates. Changes Rigidbody.detectCollisions on Hand.rb and PhysHand.rbLower. It does not toggle the enabled property of the collider field. These bodies can therefore stop colliding while their collider components remain enabled.
The hand's Rigidbody, PhysHand and lower-arm Rigidbody must already be initialized.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.EarlyUpdateHeldObjectInputs
member.summary: Refreshes the held object's index-trigger input while filtering out a trigger press carried over from grabbing it.

remarks.para: First copies the controller's primary interaction button and analog axis through SetIndexButtonAndTrigger. If the trigger was already held when an object was attached, that call supplies false button states and a zero axis until the controller button is released.

The release poll clears the attachment flag after caching those zero values. Normal values resume on the next poll. This prevents the press that grabbed an object from also immediately activating its trigger action.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.EnableCollider
member.summary: Restores physics collision detection for the hand Rigidbody and its lower-arm Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is an object whose movement Unity physics calculates. Changes Rigidbody.detectCollisions on Hand.rb and PhysHand.rbLower. It does not toggle the enabled property of the collider field. These bodies can therefore take part in collision detection again.
The hand's Rigidbody, PhysHand and lower-arm Rigidbody must already be initialized.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.HoverLock

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnDestroy

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnJointBreak(System.Single)
member.summary: Starts delayed release cleanup when Unity reports that a joint on this hand broke.

remarks.para: Starts CoJointBreakCooldown, a coroutine (a sequence that continues over several frames). It first calls PhysHand.ClearJerk with 0.2. This caps the existing linear and angular strength-recovery multipliers at 0.2 and sets the shock factor to 1. These are unitless scaling values: the linear multiplier affects available muscle strength for moving the hand, while the angular multiplier affects rotational drive strength and the shock factor affects damping. The 0.2 is not a wait in seconds or a command to zero the hand's velocity. It then waits for the next physics update, detaches the object and releases any remaining grab joint through the normal, non-quick DetachJoint path. The breakForce argument does not change that cleanup.

member.param: Force value supplied by Unity's joint-break callback (a routine called to perform or report an action); this implementation does not use it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnLevelLoad
member.summary: Ends the hand's warmup period so its held-object and skeleton update hooks can run.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine) registers this with the scene-stream session. It clears m_IsWarmup; OnPhysRigUpdate and OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate skip their work while that flag is true. This callback (a routine called to perform or report an action) itself does not attach an object or update its pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnPhysRigEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Refreshes the held object's index-trigger input while filtering out a trigger press carried over from grabbing it.

remarks.para: First copies the controller's primary interaction button and analog axis through SetIndexButtonAndTrigger. If the trigger was already held when an object was attached, that call supplies false button states and a zero axis until the controller button is released.

The release poll clears the attachment flag after caching those zero values. Normal values resume on the next poll. This prevents the press that grabbed an object from also immediately activating its trigger action.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnPhysRigUpdate
member.summary: Updates hover selection and sends the held, near-hover and far-hover receivers their physics-rig update callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action).

remarks.para: Runs only after warmup ends. It first calls UpdateHovering. For an attached Grip, it compares the current animated handle rotation with the grip's desired rotation and supplies that difference to the hand animator's rotation blend.

Then calls OnHandAttachedUpdate on the current attached object's receiver, OnHandHoverUpdate on HoveringReceiver, and OnFarHandHoverUpdate on farHoveringReciever when each exists, passing this Hand to all three routines. The receivers decide what their callbacks do.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate
member.summary: Runs the held grip's skeleton physics hook and then the hand's skeleton-update delegate.

remarks.para: After warmup, looks for a Grip on the current attached GameObject and calls its OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate with this hand. Afterwards invokes onRTSkeleFixedUpdateDelegate with no arguments if set, including when no grip is attached. A delegate here is a callback: a routine called to perform or report an action.
This is a separate hook from OnHandAttachedUpdate, which OnPhysRigUpdate dispatches.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.SetGrabLock
member.summary: Sets GrabLock to true, making HasAttachedObject treat this hand as occupied even without an attached GameObject.

remarks.para: Only sets the lock flag. It does not select a receiver or create a physics joint. AttachObject clears GrabLock only after successfully finding a HandReciever for the new object. A failed receiver lookup leaves the flag unchanged, even though currentAttachedGO has already been stored.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.SetGripStrength(System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the physical hand's grip multiplier, which contributes to the torque available to turn its wrist toward a target.

remarks.para: Writes PhysHand.gripMult directly. Torque means twisting strength. In PhysHand.FixedUpdateArm, the budget supplied to the wrist-strength calculation is (1 + 0.25 × gripMult) × maxTorque × armInternalMult × forceMultiplier × situationalFactor. maxTorque is the configured wrist rotational-strength budget. gripMult, armInternalMult, forceMultiplier and situationalFactor are unitless scaling values; the other arm multipliers scale the budget for the current arm settings and state. The 0.25 is also unitless. The situational factor is normally 1, with a 0.3 branch under particular support/input conditions. ApplyTorque2 then adjusts the rotational drives further, so perc alone does not specify the final output. This affects rotational strength rather than directly setting the grab joint's drive or break force.

For example, perc = 0 contributes a factor of 1, and perc = 1 contributes 1.25 before the other factors. Zero therefore does not switch off all wrist torque. The value is a unitless amount, not a Newton value or a whole-number percentage, and this setter does not clamp it. PhysHand must be initialized.

member.param: Unitless grip multiplier to copy into PhysHand.gripMult; for example, 1 contributes 1.25 to the wrist-torque factor.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.SetIndexButtonAndTrigger
member.summary: Copies the controller's current primary interaction button and trigger axis into the hand's input cache.

remarks.para: Copies the button-down event, button-up event, held state and analog axis. GetIndexButton, GetIndexButtonDown, GetIndexButtonUp and GetIndexTriggerAxis then read those cached values.

While _isTriggerPulledOnAttach is true, it writes false to all three button values and zero to the axis instead. EarlyUpdateHeldObjectInputs clears that filter after the controller button is released. This method copies the analog value without clamping it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.UpdateHovering
member.summary: Selects a nearby interaction receiver, or a distant force-pull receiver when no near target qualifies.

remarks.para: Returns without changing targets if Controller is unavailable or hoverLocked is true. Otherwise predicts the hand and palm positions 0.015 seconds ahead using controller velocity, then searches a sphere with HoverSphereRadius. Its centre is shifted forward from the predicted palm by 0.8 times that radius.

Near candidates must have an enabled receiver, avoid ignoredRecievers and the object already held by this hand, and permit another hand when already held by otherHand. The selection uses the receiver's grip score plus distance, direction and relative movement. The current near receiver gets a small preference to reduce switching; the nearest collider does not automatically win.

If no near receiver qualifies and farHoverEnabled is true, it first checks alignment of the calculated aim. Only after those alignment checks pass does it search an aimed capsule whose endpoints lie 1 and 4 metres ahead of the predicted palm, with a 1-metre query radius. Further checks require an enabled receiver, its far-hover permission, the grip's ForcePull flag, suitable target angle and position, and an unobstructed line of sight; the other hand's held object is excluded. These checks narrow the candidates. These query dimensions do not guarantee that any object in that volume can be grabbed.

Updates farHoveringReciever first and HoveringReceiver second through their setters, sending hover-end and hover-begin callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action) when the targets change. Receiver callbacks receive this Hand; the hand's near-hover end/begin events receive the old/new receiver respectively. This method chooses targets; it does not itself start a force pull or attach a grab joint.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.WristToForearmAngle
member.summary: Reads this hand's signed sideways wrist-bend angle, in degrees, from the virtual skeleton rig.

remarks.para: The rig computes the left and right values while solving the arms. This method selects the value for handedness rather than calculating a new angle. It measures sideways deviation between the hand and forearm orientations, not trigger pull or finger curl.
The sign distinguishes opposite bend directions. If handedness is neither left nor right, it returns zero; otherwise manager and virtualHeptaRig must be available.

member.returns: The latest signed wrist deviation in degrees.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.ApplyPoseToTransforms
member.summary: Writes the solved finger rotations to the assigned finger bones.

remarks.para: Call SolvePose first to prepare _currentPoseData. This method writes the five finger-base rotations and the bends of their middle and end segments in each bone's local coordinates. Local coordinates are measured relative to the bone's parent.
It does not calculate a new pose or move the handle. All required finger segment references must be assigned; it does not substitute another bone when one is missing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.Awake
member.summary: Unity's initialization callback, which prepares finger overrides, an open-hand reference and the default pose. Shares its implementation with .

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform an action; Unity calls Awake when initializing this component. Awake shares its implementation with Initialize.

It creates five temporary finger-override slots, stores the fixed open-finger reference and calls SetHandPose(defaultHandPose, 0.1), where 0.1 is the blend duration in game-time seconds. Game-time seconds advance with the game’s time scale, so slow motion and a zero time scale change how quickly that duration elapses. Later SolvePose calls advance this blend using Time.deltaTime, the scaled time for that frame. The new override slots initially contain zero, so the first SetFingers call consumes open-finger overrides before later calls use ordinary inputs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.BlendOpenPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData)
member.summary: Returns a finger pose between the supplied open and closed shapes, using each finger's current curl.

remarks.para: For each finger, the method first clamps its current curl to 0..1 and maps it between that finger's _min and _max curl settings. With the default endpoints of 0 and 1, a curl of 0 gives the open shape and 1 gives the closed shape.

The result keeps the closed pose's handle data. When the selected pose is defaultHandPose, the thumb base always uses its ordinary thumb-curl factor, regardless of hoverFingers. For a nondefault pose, hoverFingers=false keeps the closed base rotation; true blends the thumb base using thumb curl + 0.25. The remaining finger bends still use their ordinary curl factors. This method returns data and does not write bone transforms.

member.param: The closed-finger shape and handle data to retain.
The open-finger shape to blend from.
member.returns: Pose data with finger rotations adjusted to the current curls.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.CurlOverride(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)

remarks.para: A nonnegative value replaces that finger's ordinary input for one SetFingers call, after which its override slot resets to -1. A negative value leaves the next ordinary input in control. To keep overriding a finger, queue the override again before each SetFingers call.
The method does not move a finger immediately. SetFingers consumes the targets and smooths the current curls; SolvePose and ApplyPoseToTransforms then update the visible fingers.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.ForceBlend(System.Single)
member.summary: Restarts the pose transition from the currently calculated hand shape.

remarks.para: It stores the requested duration, resets progress to zero, then copies _currentPoseData into the transition's starting snapshot. Later SolvePose calls advance the transition toward the newly calculated shape; the method does not select another HandPose asset or apply bone rotations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.GetArtHandleInHand
member.summary: Returns the solved visual handle's position and rotation relative to the hand-art frame.

remarks.para: The method selects the leftArtHandle or rightArtHandle stored in _currentPoseData according to handedness. It returns those stored values directly, without applying the avatar's hand-size scale factor or converting them into a world position.
A handle pose describes where and how the held object's handle fits within the hand. SolvePose or SolvePoseForHandle prepares the current data; this getter does not run a solve.

The hand-art frame means coordinates relative to hand2Art’s position and orientation: hand2Art is the Transform of the visible hand. A consumer combines this local handle pose with that Transform’s world position and rotation to place the visual handle in the scene. This getter itself only returns data.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.GetHandInHandle
member.summary: Calculates the hand's placement relative to the current handle.

remarks.para: It measures hand2Art's world position in handle's local coordinates, rotates that offset by the inverse of the active pose's handle-axis rotation and scales it by _handSizeMult. _handSizeMult is the animator’s cached unitless hand-size scale factor, which scales the fixed reference hand to the avatar. It was copied by the last SetHandSize call; later Avatar edits change this cache only after SetHandSize runs again.

Its rotation uses the inverse-hand reference stored in the active asset's first sample in its first size group. The result is local placement data, rather than a world position, and the method does not change scene transforms.

The active pose's handle-axis rotation uses primaryAxis as forward and secondaryAxis as up. Its inverse undoes that axis rotation. Local handle coordinates describe offsets from the handle using its axes, converted into the pose convention as described above. Returned position distances are in metres.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.Initialize
member.summary: Prepares the temporary finger overrides and fixed open-hand reference, then selects the configured default pose.

remarks.para: This is the same setup routine used by Awake, the initialization callback—a routine Unity calls to prepare this component. It creates a new five-slot override array and calls SetHandPose with defaultHandPose and a transition lasting 0.1 game-time seconds. SolvePose advances it using Unity Time.deltaTime, the elapsed game-time seconds for the frame, so its real-time speed follows the game’s time scale.

New override slots are zero, so the next SetFingers call consumes open-finger overrides. Repeating Initialize also replaces those slots. SetHandPose returns early if the default asset is already selected; this call therefore does not guarantee rebuilding an already active asset's sample caches.

member.summary: Sets the grip size used to choose and blend pose samples, adjusted for the avatar's hand size.

remarks.para: It multiplies newRadius by _handSizeMultInv, the cached reciprocal of the avatar's hand-size scale factor. That unitless factor scales the fixed reference hand to the avatar; using its reciprocal converts the supplied size back to the reference hand’s scale. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.SetHandSize(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Positions the assigned hand bones using the avatar's hand scale and measured finger-base offsets.

remarks.para: It copies the avatar's hand-size scale factor, which scales the fixed reference hand to that avatar, and its reciprocal. The thumb and the middle/end segments use scaled reference positions. For the other four finger bases, X comes from the scaled reference hand while Y and Z come from the avatar's measured base offsets. These are local bone positions in metres, relative to each bone's parent using that parent's axes.

It also copies the avatar's left and right palm-alignment corrections: metre displacements from the measured palm center to the fixed reference palm center, expressed in the calibrated hand frame. That frame measures displacement from the avatar's hand-bone origin and rotates it into the game's reference-hand orientation using measured finger geometry, rather than world axes. Assign the required finger segment references before calling it; the method does not find missing bones or resize an object's collider.
The hand-size scale and its reciprocal are unitless. Those copied values and palm corrections stay cached until SetHandSize runs again; later Avatar edits do not update them automatically.

member.param: Avatar supplying the hand-size scale factor, finger-base measurements and palm-alignment corrections.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.SolvePose
member.summary: Calculates the finger pose and handle placement from grip size, hand rotation and current finger curls.

remarks.para: The method selects and blends pose samples, adjusts the fingers between their open and closed shapes, and stores _currentPoseData. While a pose transition is active it advances progress using the frame duration and blends from the saved starting shape. It then writes handle's local position and rotation.

It does not apply the finger bone rotations; call ApplyPoseToTransforms afterward. With no pose selected it returns without solving. Select a new asset using SetHandPose so its sample lookup and transition are prepared; writing pose directly does not perform that setup.

The grip-size input is a distance in reference-hand metres, prepared by SetCylinderRadius from the supplied world-size distance using the cached inverse hand-size factor. That unitless factor converts the avatar's hand scale to the fixed reference hand. Current finger curls are unitless amounts, normally 0 for open and 1 for closed. Hand-rotation coordinates are a rotation-axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in degrees, expressed in the selected pose's handle-axis convention: First rotate the axis-times-angle vector using the pose's primaryAxis as forward and secondaryAxis as up. If its components are x, y and z in degrees, LEFT uses pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z; RIGHT uses pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z. They are not conventional Euler X/Y/Z angles. handle's local position is a metre offset from its parent using that parent's axes; its local rotation is orientation relative to that parent. Frame duration means Unity Time.deltaTime, the elapsed game-time seconds since the previous frame; the game's time scale changes how quickly this clock advances in real time.
