member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.DisableInteraction
member.summary: Prevents this receiver from qualifying for automatic near- and far-hover selection.

remarks.para: The base implementation clears the receiver's local interaction flag. Hand.UpdateHovering checks IsEnabled before considering a candidate, so the change takes effect when the hand next searches.

This method does not release an existing attachment or immediately send hover-end callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action). Derived receiver types can add their own behavior. EnableInteraction restores the local permission, though the host can still block interaction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.EnableInteraction
member.summary: Allows this receiver to qualify for hover selection again, provided its host also permits interaction. Re-enables its local permission after .

remarks.para: The base implementation sets the local interaction flag to true. IsEnabled also checks Host.IsInteractionDisabled when a host exists, so enabling the receiver does not override a disabled host.

A later Hand.UpdateHovering search can choose the receiver if its other distance, direction and grip checks pass. This method itself does not select a target, attach an object or send a hover-begin callback (a routine called to perform or report an action).

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.GetHostTransform
member.summary: Returns a snapshot of the host's position and rotation, or an identity transform when no host is assigned.

remarks.para: Delegates to Host.GetHostTransform. For the ordinary InteractableHost, its world position in metres and world rotation are copied only when its associated MarrowBody component reports HasRigidbody = true. A Rigidbody is the simulated physics body whose movement Unity calculates. If the MarrowBody component is missing or its flag is false, that host returns identity too: position (0, 0, 0) at the world origin, with a rotation that adds no turn. Other IGrippable implementations supply their own result. A SimpleTransform stores these two values; it does not stay linked to the moving GameObject.

With no Host, returns position (0, 0, 0), at the world origin, and identity rotation, which adds no turn. Check HasHost when that fallback would be mistaken for an actual object at the world origin. Changing the returned snapshot does not move the host.

member.returns: The host-supplied position and rotation snapshot; ordinary InteractableHost uses world space.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.OnJointAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Receives notification after the hand has finalized its prepared grab joint and applied this receiver's movement settings.

remarks.para: Hand.AttachJoint moves tempJoint into joint and clears tempJoint before applying motion limits, drive settings, linear limit, break force and break torque from HandJointConfig. Drives use spring strength and damping to pull the connection toward a target. Spring strength controls how strongly the connection pulls toward its target; damping resists that movement to reduce bouncing. Here, the linear limit is a boundary for allowed positional movement on axes set to Limited, measured in metres; the configured limit spring can soften that boundary. Break force is the pulling-strength threshold that breaks the connection, measured in newtons (N), and break torque is the twisting-strength threshold that breaks the connection, measured in newton-metres (N·m). For torque to break the joint, the rotation axis where the twist is applied must be Locked (no turning) or Limited (turning only within its allowed range); a Free axis supplies no rotational constraint. It calls this method after those settings have been applied.

A joint is a physics connection between the hand and an object. This hook is separate from OnAttachedToHand, which reports the held-object association. Creating an unconfigured joint alone does not call this hook.

The base HandReciever implementation is empty. Receiver types such as Grip override this callback, a routine called to perform or report an action, to handle their own interaction. Calling the base method alone performs no grab, release or visual effect.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.Awake
member.summary: Connects this hand’s collision-sound routines to the assigned collision collector.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback: a routine Unity calls to prepare the component. It adds OnSignificantCollisionEnter and OnSignificantCollisionStay as listeners on _collisionCollector, so processing the collector’s contact data can call this component’s impact and sliding routines.

Assign _collisionCollector before initialization; this method does not search for and fill that reference. It subscribes the routines without removing other listeners. OnDestroy removes these subscriptions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.BodySlot
member.summary: Requests a randomly selected body-slot cue at the hand’s current position.

remarks.para: InventorySlotReceiver calls this for storing and retrieving an item. The method requests one clip from bodySlot at volume 1, with a small randomized pitch variation. Volume is a unitless playback setting; 1 requests the normal full setting. It provides the sound notification; it does not itself insert, remove or attach an inventory item.

It also sets _nextImpactTime to the current unscaled time plus 0.2 seconds. That filters some weaker collision sounds immediately afterward; equal or stronger impacts can still pass the separate impact check.
Unscaled time is Unity’s clock in seconds that advances at real-time speed, so slow motion does not stretch this deadline.

This requests playback at the hand’s scene position captured when the method is called: its location in the whole scene, rather than an offset relative to the hand. The audio player may still need to be created, so the sound can start later. The 0.2-second impact deadline is set after this request is issued; it does not wait for the sound to become audible.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.Drop
member.summary: Requests the configured release cue at the hand and requests a release haptic click when the attached hand has a Controller with a Haptor vibration sender.

remarks.para: It randomly selects one clip from drop, passes volume 0.5 and a base pitch of 1 with variation, and requests it at this component’s world position. When the attached hand has a Controller with a Haptor vibration sender, it sends Haptic_Click with the release setting. A haptic click is a short controller vibration.

Grip’s detachment routine calls this sound notification. Calling Drop directly does not detach the object or destroy a joint. After finding the Controller, it sets the impact deadline to unscaled time plus 0.2 seconds, even when that Controller has no Haptor, while the impact check can still admit equal or stronger hits early.
Unscaled time is Unity’s clock in seconds that advances at real-time speed, so slow motion does not stretch this deadline.
A physics joint is the connection that holds the grabbed object to the hand. Drop supplies the release cue; the detachment code handles that connection.

This requests playback at the hand’s scene position captured when the method is called: its location in the whole scene, rather than an offset relative to the hand. The audio player may still need to be created, so the sound can start later. After this request is issued and the attached hand’s Controller is found, the 0.2-second impact deadline is set; it does not wait for the sound to become audible.

Volume is a unitless playback setting; 0.5 requests half that setting, rather than guaranteeing half the perceived loudness. Base pitch is a unitless playback-speed factor: 1 is the clip’s original rate before the audio player’s random variation and game-speed adjustments.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.FixedUpdate
member.summary: Coordinates collision processing across physics steps and records the hand’s speed relative to the chest.

remarks.para: FixedUpdate is Unity’s physics-step routine. With an awake Rigidbody, it processes the collector and samples velocity only if _fixedRan was already true, then sets that flag true. Thus the first physics step after Update has cleared the flag marks work pending; additional physics steps can process the accumulated contacts.

The velocity sample is the squared length of hand Rigidbody velocity minus chest Rigidbody velocity. Both are world-space velocities in meters per second, so the stored value is in square meters per square second. Moving the whole player together does not increase it just because both bodies share that movement.
Contact processing happens before the new speed sample is stored, so the impact routines use the previous cached sample during that processing. A sleeping hand body skips this work.

A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation. An awake body is being processed by physics; a sleeping body is temporarily inactive so physics can skip unnecessary work until it wakes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.ForcePull(System.Single)
member.summary: Chooses and requests the short or long force-pull cue from a mass-times-distance input.

remarks.para: The normal ForcePullGrip caller supplies object Rigidbody mass in kilograms multiplied by the predicted hand-to-target separation in meters. Its separation calculation includes one physics step of hand-point movement. The value is not normalized to 0–1, and a heavy nearby object can select the long clip just as a lighter distant object can.

The method multiplies the input by 0.05 to obtain its sound-control value. A value below 0.18 selects forceGrab; otherwise it selects forceGrabLong. That places the changeover at about 3.6 for the mass-times-distance input. The short branch passes three times that value as a unitless playback-volume setting, where 0 is silent and 1 is the normal full setting; it divides 0.12 by the sound-control value for base pitch, then limits pitch to 0.5–1.5. The long branch passes twice the value as the same playback-volume setting; it divides 0.3 by the sound-control value for base pitch, then limits pitch to 0.2–1.5. HandSFX passes the calculated volume request through without clamping it, and the setting does not guarantee a particular perceived loudness.

For an illustrative input of 2, the short branch requests volume 0.3 and base pitch 1.2. An input of 4 requests the long clip at volume 0.4 and base pitch 1.5. The audio manager also adjusts pitch with timeScale. The sound is requested at the hand; this method does not apply force to the object. It sets the impact deadline to unscaled time plus 0.2 seconds.
Unscaled time is Unity’s clock in seconds that advances at real-time speed, so slow motion does not stretch this deadline.
timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 0.5 is half speed, and 0 pauses game time.
A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation; its mass supplies the kilogram part of the normal caller’s input.

This requests playback at the hand’s scene position captured when the method is called: its location in the whole scene, rather than an offset relative to the hand. The audio player may still need to be created, so the sound can start later. The 0.2-second impact deadline is set after this request is issued; it does not wait for the sound to become audible.
Pitch is a unitless playback-speed factor: 1 is the clip’s original rate before the audio manager’s timeScale adjustment.

member.param: Object mass in kilograms multiplied by hand-to-target distance in meters in the normal caller, giving a kilogram-meter input. This method uses that number to choose and scale its sound; it is not a normalized weight or a distance alone.

After this request is issued and the attached hand’s Controller is found, the 0.2-second impact deadline is set; it does not wait for the sound to become audible.

member.param: Dimensionless playback volume passed to the sound player: 1 uses the normal volume and, for example, 0.5 requests half that setting. This method does not clamp the argument.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this component’s impact and ongoing-contact listeners when Unity destroys the component.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDestroy when this component is destroyed. It removes this component’s OnSignificantCollisionEnter and OnSignificantCollisionStay routines from the assigned collision collector, matching the subscriptions made during Awake, Unity’s initialization routine.
A listener is a routine registered to be called when the collector reports a contact. Removing these two listeners does not clear other components’ listeners or destroy the collision collector.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.OnSignificantCollisionEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision)
member.summary: Handles a collected empty-hand contact as an impact, fist attack, slap or backhand sound.

remarks.para: The routine skips a hand that has a recorded attached object, has GrabLock set, or has a prepared tempJoint. It examines movement into the contact surface, cached hand-versus-chest speed and impulse strength. An impulse is the push delivered during a collision, measured in newton-seconds. The collector’s impact check suppresses a weaker repeat before its deadline but allows an equal or stronger impact.

An accepted impact can request controller vibration. For the stronger contact branch, a strongly pressed secondary-interaction input leads to PunchAttack; success selects punch audio, while rejection uses fallbackImpact. With that input below the fist branch, the side of the hand facing the contact chooses slap or backhand audio. Less suitably oriented contacts use fallbackImpact.

PunchAttack sends the game’s attack message; the sound selection happens here. A punch/slap/backhand sound alone does not prove that a target lost health. The method also saves the contact’s velocity along the surface for later slide calculations.

tempJoint is the temporary physics connection prepared by the hand during grabbing. A collider is an invisible physics shape, and a Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation. The contact’s relative velocity is in meters per second, and its world contact position is measured in meters in the scene’s coordinates.

Hand.HasAttachedObject includes GrabLock, the flag blocking a new grab, as well as a held GameObject, the Unity scene object carrying components. Either state suppresses this contact routine. An accepted repeat-impact check saves the raw collision impulse and sets the next deadline to the current unscaled clock plus 0.25 seconds; this clock advances in seconds at real-time speed independently of slow motion.

member.param: The collector’s chosen contact, including total impulse, relative velocity, surface point and outward normal, and the contacted collider and Rigidbody. Positions and directions are in world space.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.OnSignificantCollisionStay(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision)
member.summary: Measures how an empty hand moves along a contacting surface and supplies that motion to the slide sound routine.

remarks.para: It skips a hand with an attached object, GrabLock set, or a prepared tempJoint. It removes the part of relative velocity pointing into or away from the surface, leaving motion parallel to the surface. The surface-parallel vector remains in world coordinates, the axes of the whole scene. Its length is sliding speed in meters per second.

It compares the new surface-parallel velocity with _lastRelVelPlane and divides the change by the physics-step duration in seconds. That gives relative acceleration in meters per square second; Slide receives its squared length. The method stores the new velocity before calling Slide, so the next comparison uses this contact sample.

It also supplies the magnitude of the contact’s total impulse, the collision’s push measured in newton-seconds. A resting hand with steady contact does not automatically start a new scrape: Slide uses an acceleration and timing gate to start or retrigger its clip.
tempJoint is the temporary physics connection prepared by the hand during grabbing. Its existence suppresses this empty-hand scrape calculation.

Hand.HasAttachedObject includes GrabLock, the flag blocking a new grab, as well as a held GameObject, the Unity scene object carrying components. Either state suppresses this routine even before the temporary-joint check.

member.param: The current collected contact. Its relative velocity and normal determine motion along the surface; its totalImpulse supplies the collision push magnitude.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.PunchAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Builds a blunt melee attack message for an eligible contact and sends it to the contacted body’s attack receivers.

remarks.para: The contacted collider’s layer must be included in meleeAttackMask and relVelSqr must be at least 0.9. The normal caller supplies the cached squared speed of the hand relative to the chest, rather than the collision record’s own relative-velocity squared. A collider is an invisible shape used by the physics system to check contact.

The method calculates damage from the supplied impact intensity and hand mass, capped by the avatar’s upper-body strength statistic, which serves as the maximum damage for this calculation. It includes the contact point, outward surface direction and collider in the message. It also includes the character reference found through Hand.triggerRefProxyObject so receiving code can identify the source of the hit.

The message is dispatched to IAttackReceiver components on the contacted Rigidbody’s GameObject. The return value reports that this dispatch was attempted, not that a listener existed or applied damage. This method does not play the punch, slap or backhand clip; OnSignificantCollisionEnter makes the audio choice after its result.

A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation; the hand mass used here is in kilograms. A GameObject is a Unity scene object carrying components, such as the contacted physics body and its attack receivers.

The caller starts with raw collision impulse in newton-seconds divided by hand mass in kilograms, a ratio with speed units of meters per second. It subtracts the fixed number 1 to create the game’s numeric attack-control value passed here. This calculated value is distinct from the raw collision impulse.
The contact point is measured in meters in the coordinates of the whole scene. The outward surface normal is a direction pointing away from the contact surface; it is not a position or a speed.

member.param: The collected contact supplying the struck collider and Rigidbody, world-space contact point and surface normal.

The mass-normalized impact intensity used by the normal caller: collision impulse magnitude divided by the hand’s mass, then reduced by 1. Despite this parameter’s name, that caller does not pass raw impulse in newton-seconds.
Squared hand-versus-chest speed in the normal caller, in square meters per square second. The attack layer/speed test rejects values below 0.9.
member.returns: True after attempting attack-message dispatch; false when the layer or speed test rejects the contact. True does not guarantee a receiver or health damage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.Slide(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Adjusts an existing scrape sound and requests a slide clip when contact motion changes sharply enough.

remarks.para: When _mapSlide is already playing, sliding speed and impulse relative to hand mass determine its target volume. Each call moves volume toward that target by at most 0.05, avoiding a large immediate jump. Speed also raises pitch, and slow motion lowers it. These adjustments occur even when a new clip is not allowed yet.

A new playback requires relAccelSqMg of at least 400 and unscaled time at or beyond _nextSlideTime. In the normal caller, 400 means an acceleration magnitude of 20 meters per square second because the supplied value is squared. The method requests one randomly selected, non-looping slide clip at the hand’s local origin and advances the next-request deadline by 0.3 real-time seconds. A new audio player may still be loading before the sound starts.

The managed playback call explicitly uses non-looping playback. Repeated contacts can retrigger and adjust a scrape, but this method does not start an indefinitely looping sound. It produces audio rather than changing the surface’s physical friction.
Unscaled time is Unity’s clock in seconds that advances at real-time speed, so slow motion does not stretch this deadline.
A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation. Its hand mass is in kilograms in the impulse-to-mass calculation.

Volume uses a unitless 0–1 control, so the maximum change of 0.05 is five hundredths of that control per call. Pitch is a unitless playback-speed factor, with 1 meaning the clip’s original rate. The normal caller’s surface-parallel velocities use world coordinates, the axes of the whole scene, rather than the hand’s axes.

member.param: Length of surface-parallel relative velocity, in meters per second in the normal contact caller. A larger value raises the target volume and pitch.
Magnitude of the contact’s total impulse, in newton-seconds. The method divides it by the hand Rigidbody mass to scale the sound’s response. It is not the contact force in newtons.

Squared acceleration magnitude, in square meters per fourth-power second. The normal caller subtracts the previous surface-parallel velocity from the new one, divides by the physics-step duration in seconds, then takes the squared length. For example, an acceleration magnitude of 20 meters per square second gives 400.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.Start
member.summary: Caches the hand’s physics body and initializes its first impact deadline.

remarks.para: Start is the Unity routine called after initial component setup. It gets the Rigidbody from this GameObject and stores it in _rb. A Rigidbody is the body the physics simulation moves and collides.

It sets _nextImpactTime to unscaled time plus 5 seconds and caches a named layer index in _enemyLayer. The layer cache is not read by the inspected HandSFX methods. The impact deadline is not an absolute five-second mute: the impact check can admit a hit whose impulse is at least the previous accepted impulse.
Unscaled time is Unity’s clock in seconds that advances at real-time speed, so slow motion does not stretch this deadline.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.Update
member.summary: Processes pending hand contacts after physics has run, then refreshes the hand-versus-chest speed sample.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s rendered-frame routine. A sleeping Rigidbody is temporarily inactive in physics calculations until awakened; in that state, or when _fixedRan is false, Update returns. Otherwise it asks the collector to report its gathered contact, then reads the hand and chest velocities, clears _fixedRan, and stores their new squared velocity difference.

The impact and slide routines are called while the pending flag is still true and before this method writes the new speed sample. A frame with no pending physics work does not process contacts again. A sleeping-body return leaves the flag unchanged.

A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation. The refreshed sample is the squared length of hand world velocity minus chest world velocity, in square meters per square second (m²/s²).

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.AfterFixedSensorUpdate(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Processes the collected head contacts, then measures how quickly the head is rotating relative to the chest.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. The PhysicsRig, which controls the character’s simulated body, calls this after its physics update. The collision collector calls its registered contact routines first; afterward this method stores the squared length of head angular velocity minus chest angular velocity. Angular velocity describes rotation speed and direction in world coordinates, measured in radians per second; its squared length is measured in rad²/s².

Because the measurement is stored after the contact routines run, headbutt detection during those routines uses the previously stored measurement. The collector, head Rigidbody, PhysicsRig, torso and chest Rigidbody must be assigned.

member.param: Length of the physics step in game-time seconds, forwarded to the collision collector.

Multiplier that converts the collector’s summed collision impulse into its unitless support sensor. The PhysicsRig supplies 1 / (absolute vertical gravity × avatar mass × physics-step duration), with gravity in m/s², mass in kg and duration in game-time seconds; the multiplier therefore has units of 1/(N·s).

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.Awake
member.summary: During Unity initialization, finds this object’s Rigidbody, routes mouth audio to the vocal mixer and connects the head contact routines.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body, and an AudioSource is the scene component that plays audio clips. Awake is Unity’s initialization callback: a routine Unity calls while setting up the component. It replaces _rbHead with the Rigidbody found on the same scene object, sets the assigned mouthSrc output to Audio3dManager.npcVocals, and registers the enter and stay routines on the assigned collision collector.

Assign mouthSrc and _collisionCollector before initialization. This method does not find the mouth AudioSource, low-pass filter or PhysicsRig for you. A contact callback is a routine the collector calls to report a contact; the registered stay routine is empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.BigDamageVocal
member.summary: Attempts to play a random heavy-damage vocal when the speech-blocking deadline has passed.

remarks.para: The current avatar’s bigPain sound data supplies its audioClips array when that data asset exists; otherwise the bigDamage array on this component is used. An empty selected array produces no sound. An empty avatar array does not fall back to this component’s array. The PhysicsRig and its avatar must exist, and the selected array must not be null.

The call is skipped while the game-time clock is before _speachEnd, the speech-blocking deadline. Otherwise it sets mouthSrc volume to 1, its full-volume setting, then sets the pitch multiplier to 0.25 + 0.75 × the game’s unitless time-scale factor, clamped between 0 and 1 (1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed). It next chooses a random clip, updates the mouth filter and starts playback. For example, time scale 0.5 gives pitch 0.625, lowering the pitch and slowing playback.
This helper does not advance the speech deadline or wait for another damage vocal to finish. A later eligible vocal can replace its sound on the same mouth AudioSource.
This method does not select itself from a damage threshold. The inspected Health.TAKEDAMAGE routine calls SmallDamageVocal with the damage amount.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.BluntAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision,System.Single)
member.summary: Sends a blunt headbutt attack to receivers on the collided Rigidbody’s scene object when the collider’s layer is allowed.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. The collision’s collider is the physical shape that was hit. Its scene-object layer must be included in meleeAttackMask. The attack records the world-space contact point and normal, uses the opposite normal as its direction, and includes proxy as the source reference.

Attack damage is clamped between 0 and 1 after calculating head mass × impulseNormed × 0.02 − 0.16, where head mass is in kg and impulseNormed is the impact-strength value described below; 0.02 and 0.16 are this method’s fixed tuning constants. IAttackReceiver is the interface a component implements to handle an incoming Attack. The method attempts to call IAttackReceiver handlers on the other Rigidbody’s scene object. It does not play a sound; the collision-enter routine plays headbutt audio afterward when this returns true.

The true result does not confirm that a receiver existed or accepted damage. The result of the receiver-dispatch operation is not checked. The collision, its collider, its Rigidbody and the cached head Rigidbody must exist.

member.param: Collected contact with the struck collider and Rigidbody, a world-space contact point and normal, and the summed collision impulse.

Impact strength used to scale attack damage. The collision-enter caller calculates summed impulse magnitude in N·s divided by head mass in kg, then subtracts 1 from that numerical speed-change value in m/s.
member.returns: if the collider layer is excluded; after attempting receiver dispatch, even if no receiver handled the attack.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.DoubleJump
member.summary: Attempts a quiet random double-jump vocal from this component’s doubleJump bank.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.JumpEffort
member.summary: Attempts a jump grunt with a two-second cooldown unaffected by slow motion.

remarks.para: The current avatar’s bigEffort audioClips array is selected when that data asset exists; otherwise jumpEffort is used. The call is skipped while game time is before the speech-blocking deadline, for an empty selected bank, or when less than 2 seconds have passed on Unity’s unscaled-time clock since _lastJumpEffort. This clock is unaffected by slow motion. Start initially records the clock, so the first grunt is also held back for 2 seconds.

On an eligible attempt, the timestamp is updated before configuring playback. A random clip is played on mouthSrc at volume 0.2. Pitch is 0.25 + 0.75 × the game’s unitless time-scale factor, clamped between 0 and 1 (1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed); the mouth filter is updated before playback. The speech deadline is not extended. RemapRig.Jump requests this grunt as part of jumping.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.OnDestroy
member.summary: During Unity’s destruction callback, removes the head contact routines from the currently assigned collision collector.

remarks.para: The routines were registered by Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, to report new and continuing contacts. This method removes both registrations from the collector referenced at destruction time. It does not stop or destroy the mouth or impact audio player.

Keep _collisionCollector pointing to the collector used during initialization. Changing that field alone does not move the registrations; destruction would attempt removal from the new collector and leave the old registrations behind.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.OnSignificantCollisionEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision)
member.summary: Tests a new head contact for a headbutt attack and plays a separate impact sound when the attack dispatch passes.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. Contacts against a Rigidbody in the character’s selfRbs set are ignored. For a contact whose relative velocity along the contact normal is at least 0.5 m/s, the summed impulse magnitude is tested by a 0.25-second unscaled-time filter: a strictly weaker impulse is skipped until the deadline; an equal or stronger one passes and refreshes the saved impulse and deadline.

A headbutt additionally needs another Rigidbody, normal-relative speed above 1.33 m/s, impact strength above 2, and cached squared head-minus-chest angular velocity above 6 rad²/s². The incoming surface direction, opposite the contact normal, must be within about 60 degrees of a direction tilted about 30 degrees upward from the head Rigidbody’s local forward direction. Impact strength is summed impulse magnitude in N·s divided by head mass in kg, minus 1 from that numerical speed-change value in m/s. BluntAttack must also allow the collider’s layer and attempt receiver dispatch.

The resulting impact audio uses the managed impact player at this component’s local origin, with headbuttClips and the slow-motion alternative bank. It does not use mouthSrc or request a damage grunt. After processing a contact, the relative velocity along the surface is stored in _lastRelVelPlane; self contacts and contacts rejected by the impulse filter return before updating that vector.

member.param: Collected head contact, including the other collider and Rigidbody, world-space contact normal and relative velocity, and summed collision impulse.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.RecoveryVocal
member.summary: Attempts to play a random recovery vocal when the speech-blocking deadline has passed.

remarks.para: The current avatar’s recovery sound data supplies its audioClips array when that data asset exists; otherwise the recovery array on this component is used. An empty selected array produces no sound. An empty avatar array does not fall back to this component’s array. The PhysicsRig and its avatar must exist, and the selected array must not be null.

The call is skipped while the game-time clock is before _speachEnd, the speech-blocking deadline. Otherwise it sets mouthSrc volume to 1, its full-volume setting, then sets the pitch multiplier to 0.25 + 0.75 × the game’s unitless time-scale factor, clamped between 0 and 1 (1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed). It next chooses a random clip, updates the mouth filter and starts playback. For example, time scale 0.5 gives pitch 0.625, lowering the pitch and slowing playback.
This helper does not advance the speech deadline or wait for another damage vocal to finish. A later eligible vocal can replace its sound on the same mouth AudioSource.
Player_Health requests this sound in its life-saving recovery and health-recovery paths. Calling this helper alone does not restore health.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.SmallDamageVocal(System.Single)
member.summary: Attempts a damage grunt whose volume and audible near-distance depend on the damage amount.

remarks.para: Damage below 0.25 is ignored. The call is also skipped while game time is before _speachEnd, the speech-blocking deadline. The current avatar’s smallPain audioClips array takes priority over smallDamage when that data asset exists; an empty selected array produces no sound, while a null array is invalid. An empty avatar bank does not use the fallback.

For an eligible call, mouthSrc volume is the smaller of damage and 1. Its minDistance, the distance within which the sound keeps its near-source volume, is the larger of damage and 1 in metres. For example, damage 0.5 gives volume 0.5 and minDistance 1 m; damage 2 gives volume 1 and minDistance 2 m. Damage is a game health amount, not a percentage or a distance; the method reuses its numerical value for these audio settings.

A random clip is selected. Pitch is 0.25 + 0.75 × the game’s unitless time-scale factor, clamped between 0 and 1 (1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed); time scale 0.5 therefore gives pitch 0.625. The mouth filter is updated before playback. This method leaves the speech deadline unchanged, so another eligible vocal can replace this sound.

member.param: Damage amount in the game’s health units. Health.TAKEDAMAGE forwards the same amount it subtracts from health; values below 0.25 do not trigger this grunt.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.Start
member.summary: Starts the two-second jump-grunt delay during Unity’s first active-frame setup.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s setup routine called before the component’s first regular active-frame update. It stores Unity’s unscaled-time clock in _lastJumpEffort. JumpEffort compares that timestamp with the same clock, so slow motion does not stretch its two-second delay.

It also stores unscaled time plus 5 seconds in _lastImpactTime. The audited HeadSFX methods do not read that second timestamp, so it does not impose a five-second impact grace period on their headbutt path. The active impact filter instead uses _lastImpulse and _nextImpactTime.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.UpdateLowPass
member.summary: Rebuilds the mouth filter’s distance curve according to whether the mouth faces toward the main camera.

remarks.para: An AudioSource is the scene component that plays audio clips. A low-pass filter removes higher sound frequencies, making the voice more muffled. This method compares the mouth AudioSource’s world forward direction with the direction from its position to the main camera. Facing the camera raises the near curve level to about 0.56; facing away lowers it to about 0.22, with side-on facing between them. These are unitless low-pass curve levels, not frequencies in hertz.

The new curve has two keys: input 0 uses that near level, and input 500 uses one quarter of it. Unity rescales the curve input over mouthSrc.maxDistance, the distance over which the source’s distance effects are applied; the key input 500 is not a claim of 500 metres. This replaces the previous custom cutoff curve.
Speak and the vocal helpers call this while preparing playback. It is not continuously updated as the camera moves during a clip. A main camera, mouthSrc and mouthLowPass must exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.AttachHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Registers a hand with this grippable's attachment tracking.

remarks.para: InteractableHost adds the hand to its attached-hand list before calling its attachment listeners, the functions configured to run when a hand attaches. This changes HandCount; the actual hand-to-grip physics connection is managed by the grip and hand routines.

When the host is nonstatic and ignoreBodyOnGrab is enabled, it can also create extra connections between the held body and parts of the player body. A joint is a connection between two objects in the physics simulation. Register the hand once for each attachment.
Each attachment listener receives this host and the supplied hand, after the hand has been added to the host list and before these extra joints are created.

member.param: The hand being registered as attached to this grippable.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.DetachHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Removes a hand from this grippable's attachment tracking and reports its release.

remarks.para: InteractableHost remembers the supplied hand for GetLastHand, removes it from the attached-hand list, then calls its release listeners, the functions configured to run when a hand detaches. If the list is already empty, the call returns without changing that remembered hand.

After the listeners run, releasing the last registered hand removes the host's extra player-body joints when they exist. A joint is a physics connection between objects. This bookkeeping method does not itself perform the hand's normal grip-joint release; the grip and hand release routines handle that.

Each release listener receives this host and the supplied hand. It runs after the list removal attempt and before the last-hand extra-joint cleanup; this method does not first validate that the supplied hand was in the list.

member.param: The hand to remove from the attachment list and remember as the latest detach argument.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.DisableColliders
member.summary: Turns off the collision shapes managed by this grippable.

remarks.para: A collider describes a shape used for collision tests. InteractableHost sets enabled to false on every collider in its MarrowBody collider array. This affects those shapes rather than simply setting the grab-availability flag.
The host must have a configured body and collider array. The method does not detach held hands or change IsInteractionDisabled; use the separate interaction controls for grab availability.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.DisableInteraction
member.summary: Marks this grippable as unavailable to its hand interaction receivers.

remarks.para: InteractableHost sets IsInteractionDisabled to true. A hand receiver is a component that handles a hand's hover and grab actions; its IsEnabled check rejects the host while this flag is set.
This method does not turn off collision shapes or release attached hands. DisableColliders and ForceDetach perform those separate operations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.EnableColliders
member.summary: Turns on the collision shapes managed by this grippable.

remarks.para: A collider describes a shape used for collision tests. InteractableHost sets enabled to true on every collider in its MarrowBody collider array, including entries that were previously disabled.
The host must have a configured body and collider array. This does not clear IsInteractionDisabled; use EnableInteraction as well if grabbing was disabled separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.EnableFarHover
member.summary: Allows this host's hand receivers to report that distant targeting is enabled.

remarks.para: Far hover means a hand targets the object from a distance before holding it. InteractableHost sets IsFarHoverEnabled to true, and its hand receivers read that flag.
This does not start a force pull, attach a hand or clear the separate interaction-disabled flag. Other targeting checks still decide which object the hand selects.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.EnableInteraction
member.summary: Clears the host-level block on hand interaction receivers.

remarks.para: InteractableHost sets IsInteractionDisabled to false. A hand receiver handles hover and grab actions; clearing this host flag lets its IsEnabled check pass when the receiver itself is also enabled.
It does not turn collision shapes back on or attach a hand. Use EnableColliders when those shapes were disabled separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.ForceDetach(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Releases the hands holding this host's registered grips.

remarks.para: InteractableHost first removes its extra player-body connections, then asks each registered Grip to release its attached hands. A joint is a connection in the physics simulation; the grip release also clears hand/object association and grip tracking.

The normal cleanup sequence aims for about 0.08 seconds of accumulated physics-step time. A physics update is one step of the game’s movement and collision simulation. Cleanup finishes on a later physics update once that accumulated time reaches or exceeds the target, so completion need not occur exactly 0.08 real-time seconds after the call. With isQuick true, it skips that waiting loop. With false, movable hosts normally use this sequence; static hosts or hosts without a Rigidbody still request the quick path. This is joint cleanup, rather than waiting for a release animation.
A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object’s movement and rotation in the physics simulation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.Freeze

remarks.para: The built-in InteractableHost implementation calls DestroyJoints, which removes these extra connections when its body reports a Rigidbody and the auxiliary pelvis connection exists. They are the connections it can create to the player's foot and torso/head bodies when ignoreBodyOnGrab is enabled; a joint connects two physics objects.
It does not set the held Rigidbody to be immovable, clear the attached-hand list or run the full ForceDetach release. Other implementations of this interface can supply their own freeze behavior.
A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object’s movement and rotation in the physics simulation.

remarks.para: A Grip defines a place and behavior for holding an object. The host can have several grips; this method selects the first entry in its grip list, rather than choosing the grip nearest a hand or the one currently held.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.GetHostGameObject

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.GetHostTransform
member.summary: Returns a position-and-rotation snapshot for the host.

remarks.para: InteractableHost copies its world position and rotation into a SimpleTransform when its body reports HasRigidbody. World coordinates locate the object within the scene. Otherwise this implementation returns zero position and identity rotation, rather than the host's actual scene placement.
This is a copied value, not a live Transform component. Editing the returned position or rotation does not move the host; use GetTransform for its scene Transform.

A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object’s movement and rotation in the physics simulation. The copied position is in world-space metres. The fallback position (0, 0, 0) is the world origin; identity rotation means no rotation relative to the world’s axes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.GetLastHand

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.RemoveProxy
member.summary: Requests clearing the host's cached trigger-proxy reference after a grab.

remarks.para: InteractableHost first stops any older sleep check. It clears LastGrabbedProxy immediately when the object’s own activeSelf flag is false. Being inactive only because a parent is inactive does not satisfy that test. Otherwise it starts a coroutine, a sequence that continues over several physics updates, which clears the reference when the body’s Rigidbody is sleeping.

Sleeping means the physics body is at rest and no longer being actively simulated. On the sleep-check route, a host without HasRigidbody ends the check without clearing the reference. A static host, failed Rigidbody lookup or null Rigidbody can fail rather than complete the check. Clearing the reference does not destroy the TriggerRefProxy component or release a hand.

This operation forgets that reference; it does not delete the helper component. A physics update is a step of the game’s movement and collision simulation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.Awake
member.summary: Registers this surface component so impact code can find it from its GameObject. See .

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components.
Awake is Unity's initialization callback: a routine Unity calls to perform initialization. It obtains the shared Cache and adds this GameObject/component pair.

It does not load SurfaceData or register the effect assets. That separate setup is performed when the attack-response path first needs it. Registration remains until OnDestroy removes the pair, rather than being limited to currently enabled objects.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.GetMaterialFromAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType)
member.summary: Randomly chooses a decal material entry from the loaded surface's blunt or bullet collection. See .

remarks.para: Blunt, Slicing and Stabbing choose BluntDecal. Piercing and the other numeric cases choose BulletDecal. The selection is a random array entry, not a search for a best matching hardness level.

A decal is a surface mark such as a bullet hole. A MaterialLevel contains the decal material, size, optional atlas and whether to use the surface tint as vertex color. An atlas is a sheet containing several decal images; vertex color is a color applied to the decal's mesh points to tint it. The decal consumer copies the size into its meter-based decal width/diameter setting and uses the atlas if assigned.

If _isSurfaceDataLoaded is false, this method returns a default empty MaterialLevel without loading anything. When loaded, _cachedSurfaceData and the selected collection must exist and contain an entry; an empty collection is not handled as a clean no-decal choice.

member.param: Chooses the blunt collection for Blunt/Slicing/Stabbing; the other cases use the bullet collection.
member.returns: A random decal entry, or the default empty entry while surface data is not marked loaded.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.GetMegaPascals
member.summary: Returns the configured surface hardness number multiplied by megaPascalModifier. See .

remarks.para: It first tries the valid SurfaceDataCard reference and reads that card's megaPascal value. If the card cannot be resolved, it tries legacy surfaceData.megaPascal. With neither available, the base value is 100. Every branch multiplies by megaPascalModifier.

The result is megapascals, a pressure unit equal to one million pascals, or one newton per square millimeter. The modifier is dimensionless. For an illustrative base hardness of 100 MPa and modifier 0.5, the reported result is 50 MPa.

In the checked stabbing path, hardness times the stab tip's area in square millimeters supplies an opposing force in newtons. With normal positive spring settings and a nonnegative tip area, increasing hardness lowers the unclamped initial-depth target. The final depth is limited to zero through maxDepth, the tip’s configured maximum penetration depth in meters, so it can stay unchanged at either limit. The value retains its other role: the value is also cached for the stab joint's later damping. The stab joint is a physics connection holding the blade to the struck object; damping resists their relative motion. This getter does not await effect-data loading or change collision materials.

member.returns: The chosen base hardness times megaPascalModifier, in megapascals.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.GetPenetrationResistance
member.summary: Returns the configured coefficient used by the checked projectile path to resist passing through a collider.

remarks.para: It reads SurfaceDataCard.PenetrationResistance when a valid card can be resolved, otherwise legacy surfaceData.PenetrationResistance, otherwise 1. It does not multiply by megaPascalModifier or calculate the value from megapascal hardness.

This coefficient is dimensionless. In the speed calculation below, resistance is this returned coefficient, startSpeed is the projectile's stored starting speed, and currentSpeed is its speed just before this hit. A collider is the shape Unity tests for collisions; a raycast tests a line against that shape, here looking backward for an exit. In the audited Projectile.Update path, a value of 1 or more stops the projectile at the hit. A smaller value permits a reverse collider raycast looking for an exit within 1 meter; passing that test reduces currentSpeed by resistance times startSpeed.

currentSpeed and startSpeed are projectile speeds in meters per second, so the product subtracts a speed. For an illustrative start speed of 100 m/s, current speed 80 m/s and coefficient 0.25, a successful exit leaves 55 m/s. A coefficient below 1 does not guarantee passage: the exit test and remaining positive speed still matter.
The source assets show an Inspector range, but this getter does not clamp the returned value. It also does not wait for the visual-effect SurfaceData asset to load.

member.returns: The card or legacy penetration coefficient, or 1 when neither source is available.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this component's GameObject entry from the shared impact lookup cache.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components.

Unity calls this destruction callback when the component is destroyed. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. After removing the GameObject/component pair, it clears the static _cache reference if that cache is empty.
A later Cache access can create a new cache. This method handles lookup cleanup; it does not unload the cached surface asset or act as an ordinary disable callback in the checked body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.ReceiveAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Starts the surface's asynchronous impact-effect and optional decal response.

remarks.para: A decal is a surface mark, such as a bullet hole. A collider is the shape Unity tests for collisions. World space uses the level's coordinates. A prefab is an object template whose components can add behavior.

It copies the attack payload into the ReceiveAttackAsync operation and returns without waiting for that operation to finish. The response first completes lazy surface setup if needed, then requests the configured impact-effect object at attack.origin in world space.

When the effect is available, it applies the surface particle tint if ParticleTint exists and orients spread from the attack normal/direction if ParticleSpreadManager exists. Unless decalType is None, it then requests the decal object, selects a material entry from the attack type and projects onto the supplied collider.

The payload's origin is the world hit point in level-space length units, conventionally meters; normal points perpendicular to the hit surface and direction gives the attack direction. Both are unitless world-space directions used to orient the effect at that world-space origin; collider identifies the hit geometry. The checked response does not apply attack.damage to health or directly issue an audio-player call. Any additional behavior inside the requested effect prefab belongs to that asset's components.

Missing usable surface data finishes without spawning these effects. Missing optional tint/spread/projector components skips their corresponding setup. Asset loading and pool requests can continue after this call returns.

member.param: The copied hit payload: world point and orientation, hit collider and attack type; its damage is not applied by this surface-effect response.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.ReceiveAttackAsync(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Runs the surface setup, impact-effect spawn and optional decal projection for a copied attack. See .

remarks.para: A decal is a surface mark, such as a bullet hole. A collider is the shape Unity tests for collisions. World space uses the level's coordinates; attack.origin is a position in level-space length units, conventionally meters.

If _isSetup is false, it awaits SetupSurfaceData. If no usable data is marked loaded afterward, it finishes. Otherwise it requests impactEffectSpawnable at attack.origin with identity rotation (no initial turn), then after that object becomes available applies optional particle tint and spread orientation.

The decal step comes after the impact effect and is skipped for decalType.None. It requests bulletDecalSpawnable at the world hit point, oriented from the negative surface normal and a tangent derived from the attack direction. The normal points perpendicular to the surface; the tangent lies along that surface. The normal, tangent and attack direction are unitless world-space directions. A Rigidbody is Unity's component that moves an object through physics. If the hit collider has an attached Rigidbody, that body's transform is supplied as the spawn parent, making the decal follow that object's position and rotation.

After the decal object is available, a valid hit collider and DecalProjector let it choose a random MaterialLevel for the attack type, apply the surface tint when that entry requests it and build the projected decal. Missing optional components skip their setup. It does not apply health damage.

This UniTaskVoid operation can pause for asset/pool work, but is not an IEnumerator coroutine to start with StartCoroutine. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over frames; this response instead uses asynchronous tasks to resume when its awaited work completes.

member.param: The hit payload copied into this operation; its point/orientation/type/collider drive visual setup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.SetupSurfaceData
member.summary: Loads the surface effect data and prepares its impact and decal assets for later pool spawns. See .

remarks.para: Pool registration asks the reusable-object system to prepare each configured effect or decal object template for later spawning. Collider.sharedMaterial is the collision shape’s friction and bounce material setting.

If _isSetup is true, it returns immediately. Otherwise, only when _isSurfaceDataLoaded is false does it try to resolve the warehouse SurfaceDataCard and asynchronously load its SurfaceData asset. It stores that object in _cachedSurfaceData first, then sets _isSurfaceDataLoaded according to whether the object is usable.

If that loading attempt did not yield usable data, it tries the legacy surfaceData reference. If data was already marked loaded, it reuses _cachedSurfaceData without resolving or loading the card again. Once usable data is available, it awaits registration of impactEffectSpawnable, then bulletDecalSpawnable. Only after those steps does it set _isSetup true.

If neither source supplies usable data, the setup attempt still ends with _isSetup true and _isSurfaceDataLoaded false. Later attack calls then skip setup until the state is deliberately invalidated; the flag does not mean loading succeeded.

The returned UniTask represents completion of this setup attempt and can be awaited. It is not an IEnumerator coroutine; a coroutine is a sequence that resumes over frames, while this task resumes after its asynchronous asset work completes. It does not assign Collider.sharedMaterial in the checked setup path.

member.returns: A task that completes when the setup attempt and any required asset registrations finish.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.Awake
member.summary: Runs Unity’s initialization callback to cache the physics and sound settings for this component.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Unity calls Awake during component initialization; this implementation performs the same setup as Initialize.

Finds the Rigidbody on this same GameObject. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in the physics simulation. If found, it also looks up that object’s MarrowBody, the Marrow wrapper used here to check whether its entity is hibernating. Hibernating is Marrow’s temporary sleeping/frozen physics state. Stores Rigidbody.mass in _mass, in kilograms; without a Rigidbody it stores the fallback 20 kilograms.

Copies pitchMod into the internal playback pitch _pitchMod, stores minVelocity squared in _minVelSquared, and sets _altColliders according to whether altImpactColliders contains any entries. pitchMod is a unitless pitch multiplier, with 1 meaning normal pitch. minVelocity is the signed approach-speed threshold perpendicular to the first contact surface, in metres per second; its squared cache has units (metres per second)². These are setup caches. Later edits to Rigidbody.mass, pitchMod, or the collider array’s empty/nonempty status do not automatically repeat this setup. minVelocity itself is read directly during collisions.

The alternate-collider array must exist, even if empty: setup reads its length. The host and initial sound-delay state are filled by Start. Repeating Initialize refreshes the setup values, including resetting any pitch previously calculated by SetPitchMultiplier.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.CheckImpact(System.Single)
member.summary: Accepts an impact if its local sound delay has expired or it is at least as strong as the previous accepted impact.

remarks.para: This is a time-and-strength check. It returns false only while Time.fixedTime is earlier than _nextImpactTime AND the supplied value is smaller than _lastImpactImpulse. Equal or larger values can pass during the delay. A passing call first stores the supplied value, then sets _nextImpactTime to the current physics time plus 0.24 seconds. A rejected call leaves both values unchanged.

The physics clock is measured in scaled game seconds. In collision processing the value being compared is a speed in metres per second: collision impulse magnitude divided by this component’s cached mass, with a fallback when the impulse is zero. That fallback uses the signed relative speed d perpendicular to the first contact surface. It uses d when no other Rigidbody exists, or d × otherMass / (otherMass + cachedMass) when one exists; otherMass is the other body’s current mass and cachedMass is this component’s cached mass, both in kilograms. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in the physics simulation. Despite the parameter name, the collision path does not compare a force in newtons here.

This method neither checks minVelocity nor plays a sound. The collision path first compares the signed relative approach speed perpendicular to the first contact surface against minVelocity, both in metres per second, and fires OnSignificantCollision, then uses this local rule or the manager’s shared rule. For example, after accepting 4 m/s, a later 3 m/s impact within 0.24 seconds is rejected, while another 4 m/s impact can pass immediately.

member.param: Strength to compare with the previous accepted value; the collision path supplies a speed in metres per second.
member.returns: True after updating the local strength and time caches; false if both the delay and smaller-strength conditions hold.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.DestructionEvent(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a destruction sound at this object’s world position and raises its local collision-sound suppression state.

remarks.para: Chooses a random clip from the first nonempty set in this order: destruction, impactHard, impactSoft. With existing but empty arrays throughout, it returns without playing or changing the delay state. This routine requests audio; the actual object destruction belongs to its caller.

For the input V, the sound volume is 0.3 + 0.7 × V. V is a unitless loudness input, and 0.3 and 0.7 are fixed coefficients in this calculation. The same input separately sets the 3D audio minimum distance to max(V, 1), in metres: this is the near-distance setting the 3D audio system uses when making a sound quieter as the listener gets farther away. For example, V = 0.5 gives volume 0.65 and minimum distance 1 metre. The volume calculation does not clamp V to 1.

Uses the hard-interaction audio mixer and a base pitch of 1, randomly varied by ±0.25. The audio helper then multiplies that pitch by 0.75 × T + 0.25, where T is the unitless game time scale: 1 is normal speed. At T = 0.5 this last factor is 0.625. This destruction call uses that base pitch directly, rather than reading the cached _pitchMod.

Before requesting playback, multiplies the stored _lastImpactImpulse by 10 and sets _nextImpactTime to Time.fixedTime + 0.3 seconds. Those are the component’s local sound-gating values. Ordinary collisions using a manager consult the manager’s separate shared values. The method itself does not wait for a previous delay to expire.

member.param: Unitless loudness input V; playback volume is 0.3 + 0.7 × V, while minimum distance is max(V, 1) metres. The optional argument is 1.

member.summary: Refreshes the cached body, mass, pitch and alternate-surface setup used by impact sounds.

remarks.para: Finds the Rigidbody on this same GameObject. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in the physics simulation. If found, it also looks up that object’s MarrowBody, the Marrow wrapper used here to check whether its entity is hibernating. Hibernating is Marrow’s temporary sleeping/frozen physics state. Stores Rigidbody.mass in _mass, in kilograms; without a Rigidbody it stores the fallback 20 kilograms.

Copies pitchMod into the internal playback pitch _pitchMod, stores minVelocity squared in _minVelSquared, and sets _altColliders according to whether altImpactColliders contains any entries. pitchMod is a unitless pitch multiplier, with 1 meaning normal pitch. minVelocity is the signed approach-speed threshold perpendicular to the first contact surface, in metres per second; its squared cache has units (metres per second)². These are setup caches. Later edits to Rigidbody.mass, pitchMod, or the collider array’s empty/nonempty status do not automatically repeat this setup. minVelocity itself is read directly during collisions.

The alternate-collider array must exist, even if empty: setup reads its length. The host and initial sound-delay state are filled by Start. Repeating Initialize refreshes the setup values, including resetting any pitch previously calculated by SetPitchMultiplier.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.OnJointBreak(System.Single)
member.summary: Responds to Unity’s joint-break notification by requesting a break sound and controller vibration.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation. This callback, a routine called to report an action, selects the first nonempty clip set in this order: jointBreak, impactHard, impactSoft. With all three arrays present but empty, the playback helper returns without a sound or vibration.

With a clip set, JointBreakFx first multiplies the local _lastImpactImpulse by 10 and sets _nextImpactTime to the physics clock plus 0.3 seconds; this clock counts scaled game seconds. It then plays a random clip at this component’s world position through the hard-interaction mixer, using jointBreakVolume and the cached _pitchMod. jointBreakVolume is unitless playback volume; _pitchMod is the unitless base pitch multiplier, with 1 meaning normal pitch. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, or Initialize copies that pitch value from pitchMod; SetPitchMultiplier can replace the cached value afterwards. Random pitch variation is ±0.25 before the audio helper’s time-scale adjustment.

After requesting playback, it sends a hit vibration to each hand holding the cached interactable host, if present. The supplied breakForce is not read by this implementation, so it does not scale the sound or damage. The helper’s minimum-distance setting is max(jointBreakVolume, 1) metres. This is the near-distance setting used by 3D audio when making sound quieter as the listener gets farther away.

member.param: Value supplied with Unity’s joint-break notification; this implementation does not use it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.ReceiveAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Provides an empty base attack-receiver implementation.

remarks.para: Calling this implementation returns without playing impact audio, applying damage, or adding a physical reaction. Collision-enter handling and DestructionEvent are separate paths. A derived implementation may supply its own response.

member.param: Attack information supplied by the sender; the base implementation ignores it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.SetPitchMultiplier(System.Single)
member.summary: Calculates and stores the pitch used by later collision and joint-break sounds.

remarks.para: For an input v other than exactly 3, stores P = (0.7 + 0.9 / v) × pitchMod, equivalently the native calculation ((1 / (v / 3) − 1) × 0.3 + 1) × pitchMod. P and pitchMod are unitless pitch multipliers; 1 is normal pitch before random variation and game-speed adjustment. The numbers 3 and 0.3 are fixed reference and adjustment coefficients. Exactly v = 3 is a special case that stores P = 1, even if pitchMod differs from 1.

In the fragment-spawning caller, v is the sum of the spawn point’s three unitless transform scale components. Scale (1, 1, 1) gives v = 3. With pitchMod = 1, scale (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) gives v = 1.5 and stored pitch 1.3; scale (2, 2, 2) gives v = 6 and stored pitch 0.85. This is a size-related pitch adjustment, not an input in metres or kilograms. SpawnFragment.EnableSound can also pass its supplied numeric input.

Updates _pitchMod, leaving the public pitchMod unchanged. Later collision and joint-break playback randomly varies the cached pitch by ±0.25, then applies the factor 0.75 × T + 0.25, where T is the unitless game time scale, with 1 meaning normal speed. Initialize copies pitchMod into the cache again. The calculation has no input clamp and divides by v outside its special case.

member.param: Numeric input v to the pitch calculation; fragment spawning supplies the sum of the three unitless spawn-point scale components.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.Start
member.summary: Sets the local startup sound delay and finds the interactable host for held-hand effects.

remarks.para: Unity calls Start before the component’s first frame update. This callback is a routine called to perform initialization. It stores _lastImpactImpulse = 100,000,000 and _nextImpactTime = Time.fixedTime + 2 seconds, then looks up the InteractableHost on this same GameObject and caches it in _host. The large stored number is a startup suppression value, not a measured impact.

For ordinary collision strengths, the local time-and-strength rule suppresses collision sound, held-hand vibration and collision-generated blunt attacks during those first two scaled physics seconds. OnSignificantCollision still fires after its velocity test and before that sound gate. A valid manager uses its own shared gate instead. The host lets later sounds find hands holding the object and supplies the last grabber’s proxy for blunt attacks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.OnFrameStart

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.OnPostNewInputUpdate

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.Refresh
