member.summary: Sets the full-update request flag to false; the inspected HandActionMap continues updating without checking it.

remarks.para: In the complete inspected XRHand and HandActionMap methods, the flag is stored but HandActionMap never reads it before updating bone arrays and finger curl. Changing it therefore does not stop or start those updates on that provider. This finding does not cover every other provider or mod.
This method does not clear the cached bone arrays or curl values, and does not switch off the tracking hardware.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.AttachHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Registers a hand with this host, notifies attachment listeners, and optionally prevents the held object from colliding with the player's torso and locomotion body.

remarks.para: This is part of the grab process, rather than a complete command to make a hand grab an object. It adds the hand to the host list first, then calls onHandAttachedDelegate with this host and that hand. Listeners can already see the increased HandCount, but the optional body connections have not been created yet.

When IsStatic is false and ignoreBodyOnGrab is true, it creates six physics joints if the pelvis connection is missing. A joint connects two bodies in the physics simulation. These connections leave all movement and rotation directions free; they serve to ignore collisions between the object and those player body parts. The regular hand-to-grip joint is handled elsewhere.

In the normal grip attachment path, the host notification precedes updating LastGrabbedProxy and the grip's own hand list, so IsAttached can still reflect the earlier grip state. The hand is added without checking for duplicates. Call this once per actual attachment; calling it twice can inflate HandCount and repeat the notification.

member.param: The hand whose attachment is being registered.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Awake
member.summary: Registers this host in the shared lookup cache, connects its grips to it, and enables host interaction.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: a routine Unity calls while setting up the component. It walks this object and its children, records Grip and ForcePullGrip components, and sets each discovered Grip's Host to this host. A child with its own InteractableHost starts a separate group, so this walk stops before entering that child.

This builds the grip lists during setup. Adding another grip later does not automatically update these lists through this method. Calling Awake again can append duplicates. It also registers each collected Grip with this host's MarrowEntity and finally clears IsInteractionDisabled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.ClearAttachedHandsForDespawn
member.summary: Clears the host's recorded hands and its virtual controller's hand-and-grip pairs before reuse or despawning.

remarks.para: A virtual controller combines the hands holding an object to calculate where the held object should move. This method clears its pair list first, then the host's hand list. It requires an initialized VirtualController and pair list.

This is bookkeeping cleanup. It does not run the normal detach notifications, release the hands' own grip connections, or clear GetLastHand. Use it within the full despawn cleanup process, rather than as a replacement for ForceDetach.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.CoCheckForSleep
member.summary: Creates the waiting sequence that clears grab attribution when this host's physics body goes to sleep.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue across several frames. Calling this method returns the sequence; RemoveProxy starts it. It checks the body immediately and then after each physics update while the body remains awake. Physics sleep means the simulation has stopped actively updating a settled body.

When the body is sleeping, it clears LastGrabbedProxy and finishes. A host without a Rigidbody ends the sequence without clearing that reference. A host marked IsStatic despite having a body cannot supply Rb to this path and is not a valid setup for it. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

member.returns: A sequence to run as a Unity coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.DestroyJoints
member.summary: Immediately removes the six extra connections that stop the held object colliding with the player's body.

remarks.para: These are the monofoot, pelvis, spine, chest, neck and head connections created for ignoreBodyOnGrab. A physics joint connects two simulated bodies; these particular joints leave movement and rotation free. They are separate from the ordinary joint holding a hand to a grip.
The cleanup only runs when HasRigidbody is true and the pelvis connection exists. It destroys the components immediately, but does not clear the hand list or send detach notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.DetachHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Removes a hand from this host's records and cleans up the extra player-body connections when no recorded hands remain.

remarks.para: When the host list is already empty, this does nothing. Otherwise it first stores the supplied hand as GetLastHand, then removes one matching list entry, then calls onHandDetachedDelegate with this host and the supplied hand. The callback is a routine called to report the detach; it runs before the final body-joint cleanup.

If the list becomes empty and the pelvis connection exists, it schedules destruction of the six collision-ignore joints and clears their stored references. A joint connects simulated bodies; these extra joints are separate from the hand's own grip joint. Removing the hand from this list does not by itself perform the whole physical release.
The removal result is not checked. Supplying a hand that was never registered can still change GetLastHand and send a notification while the list is nonempty.

member.param: The hand whose attachment record is being removed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.DisableColliders
member.summary: Turns off every collider listed by this host's MarrowBody.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape the physics system can detect and collide with. This uses the body's Colliders array; it does not search all child objects. The body, array and each collider must exist.
Disabled shapes stop participating in collision detection. This does not detach held hands or change IsInteractionDisabled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.DisableFarHover
member.summary: Blocks this host in the hand's distant-target search.

remarks.para: Distant hovering is aiming at an object from too far away to grab it directly, as a first step toward force pulling. This only changes IsFarHoverEnabled. The hand's search also requires an enabled receiver, an eligible grip, and its normal direction and visibility checks.
Changing this permission does not directly release a held hand or cancel an already running force pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.DisableInteraction
member.summary: Blocks the host's enabled hand receivers to take part in normal hand targeting.

remarks.para: It sets IsInteractionDisabled to true. A hand receiver is the component that handles a nearby or distant hand target. Its enabled check reads this host flag, and normal hand searches skip disabled receivers.
This does not change collider settings or force currently attached hands to release. An individual receiver can remain disabled even when the host allows interaction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.EnableColliders
member.summary: Turns on every collider listed by this host's MarrowBody.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape the physics system can detect and collide with. This uses the body's Colliders array; it does not search all child objects. The body, array and each collider must exist.
Every listed collider is enabled, including ones that were disabled before DisableColliders. The method does not remember and restore an earlier mix of enabled and disabled shapes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.EnableFarHover
member.summary: Allows this host in the hand's distant-target search.

remarks.para: Distant hovering is aiming at an object from too far away to grab it directly, as a first step toward force pulling. This only changes IsFarHoverEnabled. The hand's search also requires an enabled receiver, an eligible grip, and its normal direction and visibility checks.
Changing this permission does not directly release a held hand or cancel an already running force pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.EnableInteraction
member.summary: Allows the host's enabled hand receivers to take part in normal hand targeting.

remarks.para: It sets IsInteractionDisabled to false. A hand receiver is the component that handles a nearby or distant hand target. Its enabled check reads this host flag, and normal hand searches skip disabled receivers.
This does not change collider settings or force currently attached hands to release. An individual receiver can remain disabled even when the host allows interaction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.ForceDetach(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Releases the hands holding this host's recorded grips and removes the extra player-body connections.

remarks.para: It first calls DestroyJoints, then asks every Grip in the host's setup list to release its hands. Each grip removes the attachment records through the normal release path.

With isQuick true, the hand skips the normal short wait before destroying its grip joint, the physics connection holding it to the object. With isQuick false, the normal path waits using physics updates toward a configured 0.08 seconds; this can finish later than exactly 0.08 seconds because updates occur in steps. Static hosts and hosts without a Rigidbody also request quick release.

member.param: True to skip the normal brief physics-step wait before removing each hand joint.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Freeze
member.summary: Removes the host's extra player-body collision-ignore connections through DestroyJoints.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects two simulated bodies. These joints normally let the held object overlap the player's torso and locomotion body without colliding with them. This method does not lock the object's position, stop its Rigidbody motion, clear the hand records, or send release notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.GetForcePullGrip
member.summary: Returns the first recorded ForcePullGrip, which handles pulling an object toward a distant hand.

remarks.para: The list is collected during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. This does not choose the nearest grip, check whether pulling is currently allowed, or search for a newly added component.

member.returns: The first recorded force-pull grip, or null when the list is empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.GetGrip
member.summary: Returns the first Grip recorded for this host, or null when none was collected.

remarks.para: A grip describes a place and pose for the hand to hold. The order comes from the host's object-and-child walk during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. This is not a search for the nearest or currently held grip.

member.returns: The first recorded grip, or null when the list is empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.GetHand(System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns a hand from this host's attachment records by its zero-based list position.

remarks.para: Index 0 is the first remaining hand in attachment order; index 1 is the next. For two recorded hands, use 0 or 1. An empty list or an index at least HandCount returns null.
Use a nonnegative index. A negative index is not rejected by this method's upper-bound check and can reach the list's error check when the list is nonempty.

member.param: A nonnegative position in the host's hand list; the default is 0.
member.returns: The recorded hand at that position, or null for an empty list or an index at least HandCount.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.GetHostTransform
member.summary: Returns a snapshot of this host's world position and rotation when its MarrowBody reports a Rigidbody.

remarks.para: The position is measured in meters along the world's axes. The rotation is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. This is a copied pose, not a live Transform reference: later movement does not change the returned snapshot.
Without a reported Rigidbody, it returns position (0, 0, 0) and identity rotation, meaning no rotation, even if the object's Transform is elsewhere. The test uses HasRigidbody rather than IsStatic.

member.returns: A copied world pose, or the zero-position, unrotated pose when HasRigidbody is false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.GetLastHand
member.summary: Returns the hand most recently passed to DetachHand while the host had recorded hands.

remarks.para: This is release history, not the newest grab. It starts as null. AttachHand and ClearAttachedHandsForDespawn do not update or reset it. An unregistered hand passed to DetachHand can also become this value if the list was nonempty.

member.returns: The last recorded detaching hand, or null before any such call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this host from the shared lookup cache when Unity destroys the component.

remarks.para: This is Unity's destruction callback, a routine Unity calls during removal. If that leaves the cache empty, it clears the shared cache reference; a later Cache request can create a new empty cache.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.RemoveProxy
member.summary: Clears this host's stored grab attribution immediately on an inactive object, or waits for physics sleep on an active object.

remarks.para: LastGrabbedProxy identifies the player or entity credited with handling the object. It can remain useful after release, for example while a thrown object is still moving. This method first stops the previous sleep-check coroutine, a sequence that can pause across frames.

If the GameObject's own activeSelf flag is false, it clears LastGrabbedProxy immediately. Otherwise it starts CoCheckForSleep, which checks now and after physics updates, clearing the reference once the body is sleeping. It does not remove a component from the object. A host with no reported Rigidbody finishes that check without clearing the reference.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Reset
member.summary: Copies the GameObject's editor Static setting into this host's IsStatic flag.

remarks.para: Reset is a Unity editor callback, a routine called when the component is first added or reset in the editor. It does not reset all grip settings. At runtime, Start recalculates IsStatic from whether the host's MarrowBody reports a Rigidbody.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Start
member.summary: Sets IsStatic according to whether this host's MarrowBody reports a Rigidbody.

remarks.para: Start is Unity's startup callback, a routine called before the enabled component's first frame update. It writes IsStatic = false when HasRigidbody is true, and true otherwise, replacing the earlier serialized or editor value.

A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. This flag affects how interaction code treats the object; Start does not add a Rigidbody, make one immovable, or change its constraints.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.DisableCollisionAll
member.summary: Turns off every collider listed by the MarrowBody of each host in .

remarks.para: A collider is a shape the physics system detects and collides with. This uses each host's body collider array, rather than searching every child object or using only grabbedHosts. An empty hosts array does nothing. The array, each host, each MarrowBody and its collider entries must exist; missing entries are not skipped.
The disabled shapes stop participating in collision detection. This does not release held hands, change the hosts' interaction flags, or send hand notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.DisableInteractionAll
member.summary: Stops enabled hand receivers on every configured host from taking part in normal hand targeting.

remarks.para: This sets IsInteractionDisabled to true on every entry in hosts, including entries not currently grabbed. A hand receiver is the component a hand search checks before offering its host as a target. Its own enabled setting must also permit interaction; its enabled check reads this host flag, and normal hand searches skip receivers that fail either requirement.

It does not toggle colliders, release hands already holding the object, or send hand notifications. An individual receiver can remain disabled even when its host permits interaction. Use a nonnull hosts array without missing entries; an empty array does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.EnableCollisonAll
member.summary: Turns on every collider listed by the MarrowBody of each host in .

remarks.para: A collider is a shape the physics system detects and collides with. This uses each host's body collider array, rather than searching every child object or using only grabbedHosts. An empty hosts array does nothing. The array, each host, each MarrowBody and its collider entries must exist; missing entries are not skipped.

Every listed shape is enabled, including a collider that was already disabled before DisableCollisionAll. This does not restore a saved mix of earlier settings, change interaction flags, or send hand notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.EnableInteractionAll
member.summary: Allows enabled hand receivers on every configured host to take part in normal hand targeting.

remarks.para: This sets IsInteractionDisabled to false on every entry in hosts, including entries not currently grabbed. A hand receiver is the component a hand search checks before offering its host as a target. Its own enabled setting must also permit interaction; its enabled check reads this host flag, and normal hand searches skip receivers that fail either requirement.

It does not toggle colliders, release hands already holding the object, or send hand notifications. An individual receiver can remain disabled even when its host permits interaction. Use a nonnull hosts array without missing entries; an empty array does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.ForceDetachAll
member.summary: Asks every configured host to release the hands holding its recorded grips.

remarks.para: This visits hosts, rather than only grabbedHosts, and calls each host's ForceDetach with isQuick set to false. Host ForceDetach calls DestroyJoints before it releases each grip collected during setup. DestroyJoints removes the six auxiliary player-body joints only when HasRigidbody is true and the pelvis-joint reference is nonnull. HasRigidbody is the MarrowBody setup marker, not a fetched live Rigidbody reference. A grip is a place and pose for a hand to hold.

The normal release path can wait toward a configured 0.08 seconds using physics updates before destroying the hand joint. A joint connects simulated bodies. A coroutine, a sequence that pauses and continues across frames, handles that wait; this method does not wait for it to finish. The actual time can be longer because physics updates occur in steps. When releasing a grip, Grip.ForceDetach uses quick cleanup if the grip has no host, if its host's IsStatic flag is true, or if the host's MarrowBody HasRigidbody setup marker is false.
Use a nonnull hosts array without missing entries. An empty array does nothing. This releases existing attachments; it does not disable future grabbing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.OnDetachedHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Notifies the manager's detachment listeners, then removes one matching host entry from grabbedHosts.

remarks.para: During startup, the manager subscribes this routine to each configured host's detachment delegate. In that normal path the host has already attempted to remove the hand from its own list and recorded GetLastHand. The manager's onHandDetached callbacks, routines called to report the action, run before grabbedHosts is changed.

Only one matching entry is removed. If two hands produced two entries for a box, releasing one normally leaves one entry. The notification still runs if the host is absent from the manager list. Calling this method directly reports a release; it does not physically detach the hand or check membership in hosts.

member.param: The host whose release is being reported and whose first matching list entry is removed.
The detaching hand passed to the listeners.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.OnHandAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Notifies the manager's attachment listeners, then adds one record of the supplied host to grabbedHosts.

remarks.para: During startup, the manager subscribes this routine to each configured host's attachment delegate. In that normal path the host has already added the hand to its own list, but the manager has not yet added the host to grabbedHosts when onHandAttached runs. A callback is a routine called to report an action.

Each call appends one host entry without checking whether it is already present. Two hands holding the same box can therefore create two entries for that box. Calling this method directly reports and records an attachment; it does not physically make the hand grab, or check that the host belongs to hosts.

member.param: The host whose attachment is being reported and appended to grabbedHosts.
The attaching hand passed to the listeners.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.Destroy
member.summary: Removes the separate anchor object and physics joint created for this contact.

remarks.para: The contact owns a scene object containing its kinematic Rigidbody and ConfigurableJoint. This method schedules that object and joint for destruction through Unity’s normal Destroy operation, which completes after the current update rather than deleting them immediately.

The existing host Rigidbody stays in the scene. Removing the contact removes this connection that limits or drives the host’s motion. The method checks whether its owned objects still exist before requesting their destruction; it does not clear the stored references.

A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. Kinematic means code controls the anchor’s position and rotation instead of forces moving it. The ConfigurableJoint is the physics connection from that anchor to the host.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.Disable
member.summary: Temporarily deactivates the contact’s anchor object while saving its current world rotation for Enable.

remarks.para: First, it saves the anchor object’s rotation in scene coordinates in _disabledRotation. It then resets that object’s Transform and Rigidbody rotation to the host’s current world rotation combined with _startRotation, the contact’s original rotation relative to the host. Finally, it deactivates the anchor scene object, taking this joint out of the active simulation.
The saved rotation is a world orientation, not an angle relative to the joint. Enable restores it after reactivating the object. This method does not save or change the anchor’s position.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body; a Transform stores a scene object’s position and rotation. The joint is the physics connection between this separate anchor and the host.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.Enable
member.summary: Reactivates the contact’s anchor object and restores its saved world rotation.

remarks.para: The scene object is activated first. After that, the method writes _disabledRotation to both its Transform and Rigidbody. This is the orientation saved by the latest Disable call; construction initially fills the same cache with the anchor’s starting world rotation.

If activation calls OnEnable, Unity’s routine for a component becoming active, that routine runs during activation and before the saved orientation is restored. Position is left as it is. The existing host object is not activated or moved by this method.
A Transform stores the scene object’s position and rotation; a Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. Both receive the restored orientation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.FreeDirection
member.summary: Allows unrestricted sliding along the contact joint’s X axis.

remarks.para: It changes _joint.xMotion to Free. In a SplineJoint, moving the contact frames along the path lets this direction act as the direction of travel. The Y and Z sliding settings, rotation settings and drive strengths keep their existing values.
Free removes the positional limit on X; a configured drive can still push or resist motion on that axis. If X is already Free, the method returns without setting it again.

A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor. Its X direction is local right, used as the direction of travel along the path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.LimitDirection(System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Restricts sliding along the joint’s X axis using a maximum distance from the anchor.
member.param: Maximum linear distance in meters used by the joint’s limited sliding axes.
Unused in this implementation; true and false produce the same settings.

remarks.para: It changes xMotion to Limited and stores limit in the joint’s linearLimit. For example, 0.05 meters supplies a 5-centimeter distance limit. Limited allows travel within the boundary; it does not set the axis to Locked.

isForward is unused in this implementation, so changing it does not choose an end of the path or reverse the allowed direction. The method preserves the limit’s bounciness and contact-distance tolerance and leaves Y/Z motion settings alone. The ConfigurableJoint has one shared linearLimit, so any other linear axes already set to Limited use that same distance.

A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor. Its X direction is local right, used as the direction of travel along the path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.SetAngularXDriveMaxForce(System.Single)
member.summary: Limits how strongly the contact’s rotation drive can turn around X.
member.param: Maximum drive torque in newton-meters.

remarks.para: maximumForce is the cap on the drive’s turning force, called torque, measured in newton-meters. A larger cap allows a stronger spring or damping correction before the drive reaches that cap. Setting the cap does not itself supply a desired rotation or turning speed.

The axis names refer to the joint’s own frame, which turns with the contact. X is the twist direction, meaning rotation around the joint’s main axis. These angular drive settings apply when the joint uses its X and Y/Z rotation-drive mode. Locked axes and rotation limits still restrict what motion the drive can produce.

Only angularXDrive.maximumForce is changed; the drive’s other strength settings are preserved. An approximately equal value causes an early return. This method copies the input without adding its own clamp.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.SetAngularXDrivePositionDamper(System.Single)
member.summary: Sets how strongly the rotation drive corrects differences from its desired turning speed around X.
member.param: Angular damping coefficient in newton-meter-seconds per radian: correction strength per difference in turning speed.

remarks.para: damperForce is a damping coefficient, in newton-meter-seconds per radian, copied to JointDrive.positionDamper. Damping generates a turning correction from the difference between target and current angular velocity. With a zero speed target, it resists turning and helps a spring settle instead of repeatedly swinging past its target. With a nonzero target, it can help drive the rotation toward that speed.

The axis names refer to the joint’s own frame, which turns with the contact. X is the twist direction, meaning rotation around the joint’s main axis. These angular drive settings apply when the joint uses its X and Y/Z rotation-drive mode. Locked axes and rotation limits still restrict what motion the drive can produce.

Only angularXDrive.positionDamper is changed; the drive’s other strength settings are preserved. An approximately equal value causes an early return. This method copies the input without adding its own clamp.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.
A radian is an angle unit: 1 radian is about 57.3 degrees. This coefficient sets the correction strength for a difference in turning speed, measured in radians per second.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.SetAngularXDrivePositionSpring(System.Single)
member.summary: Sets how strongly the rotation drive pulls the connected body toward its desired relative rotation around X.
member.param: Angular spring stiffness in newton-meters per radian: restoring strength per difference from the desired orientation.

remarks.para: springForce is a spring stiffness coefficient, in newton-meters per radian, copied to JointDrive.positionSpring. The physics solver uses the difference between the current and desired orientation to calculate restoring torque. A larger stiffness asks for more turning force for the same angular error, subject to the drive’s maximumForce cap. This is a strength setting, not a rotation angle or an immediate turn.

The axis names refer to the joint’s own frame, which turns with the contact. X is the twist direction, meaning rotation around the joint’s main axis. These angular drive settings apply when the joint uses its X and Y/Z rotation-drive mode. Locked axes and rotation limits still restrict what motion the drive can produce.

Only angularXDrive.positionSpring is changed; the drive’s other strength settings are preserved. An approximately equal value causes an early return. This method copies the input without adding its own clamp.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.
A radian is an angle unit: 1 radian is about 57.3 degrees. The per-radian coefficient describes correction strength for an angular difference, rather than a number of degrees.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.SetAngularXDriveSpeed(System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the desired turning speed around the joint’s X axis.
member.param: Desired angular speed around joint X, in radians per second.

remarks.para: speed is an angular-velocity target in radians per second, written to targetAngularVelocity.x. For an illustrative value, 1 radian per second is about 57.3 degrees per second; a negative value requests the opposite direction. The target normally uses the joint’s local frame, which turns with the contact. If configuredInWorldSpace is enabled on _joint, Unity instead interprets the velocity target in scene coordinates.

The existing Y and Z angular-velocity targets are preserved. If the X target is already approximately equal, the method returns. This sets a goal for the angular drive; its damping strength, torque cap, drive mode and allowed rotation determine the resulting motion. It does not directly set either physics body’s current angular velocity.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.

The axis names refer to the joint’s own frame, which turns with the contact. The Y/Z setting is shared by both sideways rotation axes. These angular drive settings apply when the joint uses its X and Y/Z rotation-drive mode. Locked axes and rotation limits still restrict what motion the drive can produce.

Only angularYZDrive.positionDamper is changed; the drive’s other strength settings are preserved. An approximately equal value causes an early return. This method copies the input without adding its own clamp.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.
A radian is an angle unit: 1 radian is about 57.3 degrees. This coefficient sets the correction strength for a difference in turning speed, measured in radians per second.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.SwingTwistSpringStabilization
member.summary: Updates the rotation-spring target to center sideways tilt while following the contact’s current twist.

remarks.para: Twist means turning around the joint’s X axis. Swing means tilting that axis sideways through Y/Z rotation. The routine compares the contact anchor’s world rotation with the connected host’s rotation, accounting for _startRotation, the initial contact rotation relative to the host, and the joint’s cached axis frame.

From that relative orientation, it takes the current up direction projected into the joint’s Y/Z plane and builds an X-axis-only target rotation. This gives the swing springs a centered sideways orientation while the target follows the current twist. It writes ConfigurableJoint.targetRotation; the springs and damping in the physics simulation produce any resulting turn. The bodies are not directly rotated here.

The calculation is skipped when angular X is Locked, when both angular Y and Z are Locked, or when either Y or Z angular limit is greater than 90 degrees. Otherwise it uses the stored limits as a condition only: it changes neither those limits nor any spring, damper or force setting.
A joint is the physics connection between the existing host body and the separate anchor body. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions, which turn with the anchor.

Construction makes the anchor body kinematic, meaning code controls its pose rather than forces moving it. WakeUp does not change that setting, move the anchor, or reactivate a scene object disabled by Disable.
