member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.AddEntityToTag(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Appends an entity to the lookup list for one exact tag ID.

remarks.para: The tag ID is the BoneTag barcode ID string: the identifier used to distinguish that tag asset, rather than its display name. If this ID has no list yet, the helper creates one; it then appends the entity to the end. It does not check whether that entity is already in the list, so two calls can produce two entries for the same entity.

This is the manager's internal list-editing helper. It changes the lookup index only: it does not add the entity to _entities or edit the entity's Tags. For example, adding a crate here can make the tag lookup return the crate even though the crate's own tag list was not changed. RegisterEntity is the ordinary operation that records an entity and indexes its existing tags together.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.RegisterEntity(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Records an entity and adds it to lookup lists for the tags currently in its Tags list.

remarks.para: If the entity is already in _entities, this method returns immediately. Otherwise it first adds the entity to that set, then reads each BoneTagReference in entity.Tags.Tags and appends the entity under that reference's barcode ID. An entity with an empty tag list is still registered. Duplicate tag references can put the same entity into a tag list more than once, even though _entities stores it only once.

Registration takes the tags present at this call; it is not a live link that follows later tag edits. Calling RegisterEntity again on an already registered entity does not refresh the lists. To change tags consistently, call UnregisterEntity while the old tags are still present, edit the tags, then call RegisterEntity. Editing first can leave the old lookup entries behind, because UnregisterEntity also reads the current tags.

The manager reads the references already in Tags.Tags. It does not expand tag inheritance itself. Inherited references are tag references copied from the source tag list selected by TagList.InheritTags. TagList.UpdateCache can copy missing references from that source into this list before registration. TagList.UpdateCache can add inherited references to that list beforehand, and those references can then be registered like the others. Updating a tag cache after registration does not itself rebuild this manager's lists.

MarrowEntity normally calls this during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Registration makes the object findable by these lookup lists; it does not spawn, move, or activate it. Supply a valid entity with a valid Tags list and tag references: membership is added before the tags are read, so invalid tag data can interrupt the operation after that first step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.RemoveEntityFromTag(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Removes one occurrence of an entity from the lookup list for one exact tag ID.

remarks.para: The ID is the tag's barcode ID string. A missing ID does nothing. If a list exists, the helper removes one matching entry and deletes the ID from _tagIDToEntity if the list is then empty. Other entities in that list keep their order.

This edits only that lookup list; it does not remove membership from _entities or edit the entity's Tags. If the same entity was appended twice for this ID, one call leaves the other occurrence. Use UnregisterEntity for normal removal of a registered entity using its current tags.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.SLZ_Marrow_Plugins_IMarrowPluginLevelCallbacks_OnBeforeLevelLoad(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.LevelCrateReference)
member.summary: Clears entity membership and tag lookups before a level is loaded.

remarks.para: This is a level-loading callback, a routine called to perform or report an action. It first clears _entities, then clears _tagIDToEntity, and returns an already completed UniTask, the task value used by the loading system. Both clears happen during the call; this method does not wait for another frame.

The clear forgets the old registry entries. It does not destroy or despawn those objects, and it keeps the cached manager itself. New registration calls can populate the emptied collections. The supplied level reference does not change which entries are cleared; this implementation clears both entire collections.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.TryGetFirstEntityWithTag(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.BoneTag,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity@)
member.summary: Returns the first entity in a tag's lookup list whose IsDespawned status is false.
member.param: Valid tag asset whose exact barcode ID is searched.
First entry whose IsDespawned status is false, or null when the search returns false.
member.returns: True when an eligible list entry is found; false when the ID is absent or all its entries are marked for despawn.

remarks.para: The search uses the supplied BoneTag's exact barcode ID. It walks that ID's list from the beginning, skips entries whose IsDespawned property is true, and returns the first remaining entity. It returns false and writes null to entity if the ID is missing or every entry is skipped. Pass a valid BoneTag; a null tag is not handled as an ordinary no-match result.

First means list order, which registration and AddEntityToTag append to. It does not mean nearest, newest, or most suitable. For example, if crates A and B were added in that order, A is returned while its IsDespawned status is false; B can be returned when A is marked for despawn.

IsDespawned reads the entity's requested despawn flag when it has an inactive-state record. A request can therefore make this lookup skip an entity without proving that its physical disappearance has finished. This search does not separately test culling, hiding, general GameObject activity, or IsDestroyed. Culling and hiding are other inactive-state flags and are not the despawn flag.

The lookup searches the manager's stored index rather than rereading each entity's current tags. Tag edits and direct collection changes can make that index disagree with the entity's own Tags or _entities membership; use the registration sequence described by RegisterEntity when changing tags.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.UnregisterEntity(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Removes a registered entity and removes its entries for the tags currently in its Tags list.

remarks.para: If the entity is not in _entities, this returns without changing any tag list. Otherwise it first removes membership, then reads the entity's current tag references. For each reference it removes one occurrence from that barcode ID's list, deleting the ID when its list becomes empty.

It does not scan every lookup list or remember the tags used during registration. If an entity was registered with tag A and its tags were changed to B first, unregistering looks under B and can leave the old entry under A. Unregister before editing the tags, then register after the edit. Likewise, an extra entry added directly under an unrelated ID is not automatically found and removed here.

MarrowEntity calls this during OnDestroy, Unity's destruction callback; a callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The entity sets IsDestroyed to true before calling UnregisterEntity. This method itself removes registry entries and does not destroy or despawn the object. Valid tag data is needed for cleanup to finish: membership is removed before the tag list is read.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityCullable.OnEntityCull
member.summary: Lets a registered component pause its custom work while the game processes a new entity-culling request.

remarks.para: Culling is the game suspending an entity’s normal processing while it is inactive. MarrowEntity calls this routine from its culling handler after requesting physics hibernation for the culling reason and disabling its MarrowBehaviour components, the entity’s configured game-script components. Hibernation pauses the entity’s simulated bodies while a reason for pausing remains active. This pause notification happens before the game finishes recording and applying the new culling state; it does not mean the GameObject has already been disabled. A GameObject is the Unity object holding components. Its activation is handled in the later apply stage. The manager marks the cull transition completed before this notification, then records the resolved state afterward.

Implement the work specific to this component, such as pausing its animator or stopping its extra updates. An Animator is the Unity component that runs animations. For example, Gun.OnEntityCull disables the gun component and its animator while preserving the animator controller’s state. Pair that work with OnEntityUncull so it can be resumed.

The receiver must be in MarrowEntity’s registered culling-handler list. RegisterEventHandler adds it without immediately calling this method. Calling this routine yourself runs the component’s implementation. The interface does not automatically change the entity’s culling state; an implementation can explicitly request such a change.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityCullable.OnEntityUncull
member.summary: Lets a registered component resume the work it paused for entity culling.

remarks.para: The game sends this resume notification during completion after all hide, cull and despawn requests for the entity are cleared. Clearing culling alone can leave it waiting while another inactivity request remains. Pending queued changes must also finish before the normal update reaches completion. The manager clears the completed-cull flag before this resume notification. It first removes the culling reason for physics hibernation and enables its MarrowBehaviour components, the entity’s configured game-script components, then calls the registered receivers. Another hibernation reason can still keep the physics bodies paused.

Restore the component-specific state paused by OnEntityCull. For example, Gun.OnEntityUncull re-enables the gun component and animator. An Animator is the Unity component that runs animations. This interface has no default implementation and does not supply a new entity or reset its gameplay data.

UnregisterEventHandler removes a receiver from future calls. Calling OnEntityUncull directly runs that receiver’s routine. The interface does not automatically remove the entity’s culling or hibernation reasons; an implementation may explicitly call the entity’s state routines.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityDespawnable.OnEntityDespawn
member.summary: Lets a registered component clean up its per-spawn behavior when its entity enters the despawned state.

remarks.para: This callback, a routine called to perform an action or report an event, has no arguments. MarrowEntity calls it while applying the despawn transition, before its trackers send their deactivation notifications and before it recalculates whether its GameObject should be active. A tracker links a collision shape, the shape Unity uses to detect contact, to the entity’s physics parts. A GameObject is Unity’s object that holds components. Physical tracker disabling can already have happened earlier in pooled deinitialization; the later tracker step sends notifications. The despawn request was recorded earlier; the manager records the newly applied state after these callbacks finish.

Register the implementing component with MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler so the entity can call it, and unregister it when that relationship ends. For example, your implementation can stop a temporary effect or discard references that belong to this spawn. This is the notification point for your cleanup; use the entity's despawn operation to request removal rather than treating this interface method as the removal command.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityDespawnable.OnEntitySpawn
member.summary: Lets a registered component restore its per-spawn behavior when its entity leaves the despawned state.

remarks.para: This callback, a routine called to perform an action or report an event, has no arguments. MarrowEntity first recalculates whether its GameObject, the Unity object holding its components, should be active, then calls registered spawn handlers. Separate hide or cull requests, which temporarily keep an entity out of active use, can still keep the object switched off; this notification does not promise that it is visible. The manager records the newly applied despawn state after the callbacks finish.

Register the implementing component with MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler and remove the registration when it is no longer needed. For example, an implementation can reset a temporary effect or prepare state for this reuse of the object. The notification belongs to the applied despawn-state transition, rather than being a signal on every rendered frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityHideable.OnEntityHide
member.summary: Lets a registered component react when the entity’s managed hide state is applied.

remarks.para: Implement this routine to pause or clean up work specific to your component while the entity is hidden. For example, a custom component could pause an extra effect here and restore it in OnEntityUnhide. The interface supplies no default implementation and does not destroy the entity or reset its gameplay data.

MarrowEntity’s hide-application handler calls the registered receivers first, then updates whether its GameObject is active. A GameObject is Unity’s object containing the entity and its components; deactivating it also stops the normal activity of its components. The hide request has already been resolved as hidden when this routine runs.

The notification is processed through the inactivity manager, rather than being sent directly by MarrowEntity.Hide. If Hide is called with doApplyImmediately=true, it can deactivate the GameObject before the manager delivers this notification. Do not assume that the object is still active inside OnEntityHide.

Register the receiver with MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler. Registration avoids duplicate entries but does not immediately call this routine for an already-hidden entity. Calling OnEntityHide yourself only runs your implementation; it does not set MarrowEntity’s hide state.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityHideable.OnEntityUnhide
member.summary: Lets a registered component restore the work it paused when the entity was hidden.

remarks.para: MarrowEntity’s hide-application handler first updates the GameObject’s active state using the resolved inactivity flags, then calls the registered OnEntityUnhide routines. The hide flag has been cleared at this point. Another inactivity reason, such as despawning or a culling state that disables the object, can still keep it inactive; this call alone does not guarantee that the object is active or visible.

Restore the component-specific work paused by OnEntityHide, such as resuming a custom effect. This interface has no default restoration behavior. Hiding and unhiding use the existing entity rather than creating a replacement or healing it.

These calls are delivered when the manager applies a hide-state change, not immediately on registration. Remove the receiver with MarrowEntity.UnregisterEventHandler when it should stop receiving them. Calling OnEntityUnhide directly only runs the implementation and does not clear the entity’s own hide flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityPoseable.OnWritePose
member.summary: Called after the owning MarrowEntity finishes applying the supplied body pose entries.

remarks.para: A pose is the arrangement of an entity's body parts: their positions and orientations. WritePose applies the stored entries to body transforms, the Unity objects holding those positions and orientations, and then calls OnWritePose on the entity's registered pose handlers. This callback, a routine called to perform or report an action, is a notification that the pose was applied; it is not a request to capture or save the old arrangement.

The callback runs within the WritePose call, after its body-transform loop and in the order of the registered handler list. It does not wait for another frame or for the physics simulation to settle. If the input contains fewer entries than the entity has bodies, only the corresponding initial bodies were changed before notification. A failure while applying the entries can prevent this notification from being reached.

Register your handler with the MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler overload for IMarrowEntityPoseable to receive this call, and use the matching UnregisterEventHandler when it should stop receiving it. Registering the same handler again does not add a duplicate. The method receives no pose argument and returns no data, so an implementation can read the owning entity's newly placed body transforms to refresh its own dependent data. Reading a pose through the inspected ReadPose method does not call this notification.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowCollisionManager.SLZ_Marrow_Plugins_IMarrowPluginLevelCallbacks_OnAfterLevelUnload
member.summary: Clears the shared collision-ignore bookkeeping after the level unloads.

remarks.para: The plugin system calls this callback, a routine called to perform or report an action, after level unload. It clears _ignoreCounts first, then _colliderToColliderMap, then _colBsToRemove. These are static collections shared by the manager, so their old-level entries are discarded together.

This implementation clears the records and returns an already completed UniTask, the task result used by the plugin API. It does not wait across frames or loop through collider pairs to call Physics.IgnoreCollision(false). To explicitly restore tracked collisions for a particular collider, ClearManagedIgnoresFor performs that separate operation.

member.returns: An already completed task after the three bookkeeping collections have been cleared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Activate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus)
member.summary: Sets the entity’s GameObject active or inactive from the combined, resolved hide, cull and despawn requests.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the scene object that holds this component. This method reads the supplied status after the inactive manager has resolved its requests. A resolved Hide or Despawn request makes the GameObject inactive. A Cull request also makes it inactive unless PreventDisableOnCull was enabled, it has packed parasite entities, or its stored host-entity reference exists. A packed parasite entity is another entity recorded as attached within this host.

These exceptions only protect against culling. They do not override Hide or Despawn. The method changes GameObject.activeSelf only when needed and returns immediately for an entity marked destroyed. It leaves the status flags unchanged; physics hibernation and behaviour enable changes happen in the other culling routines.

member.param: The manager’s status containing the resolved Hide, Cull and Despawn requests to apply.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.AddRuntimeJoint(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint)
member.summary: Adds a dynamically created joint to the entity’s cleanup list.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives motion between objects. This method records the supplied MarrowJoint in RuntimeJoints unless it is already listed. It does not create the connection, change its owner, or change any of its physics settings.

Ghost(true) removes these entries, then asks each joint to destroy itself. MarrowJoint.Destroy only performs destruction when IsCreatedAtRuntime is true; adding a joint here does not set that flag. Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize follows a separate path that removes the entries and requests Unity destruction of their wrappers without that flag guard. Unity completes destruction later, so these requests do not promise that the connection is already gone when the request returns. The separate Joints array holds the joints saved with the entity rather than these runtime additions.

member.param: An existing MarrowJoint to include in runtime cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Awake
member.summary: Registers the entity with the game’s lookup systems and prepares its pool, inactive-state and pose bookkeeping during Unity initialization.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback: a routine Unity calls when setting up this component. It adds the entity to the GameObject-to-entity cache and EntityManager, allocates one teleport-cache entry per body, and creates the inactive status with routines for culling, hiding and despawning.

It then registers this entity with its Poolee, the component that manages reuse of the scene object through a pool. Finally, it records each body’s current local position and rotation in the default pose cache. Here local means relative to that body’s immediate parent in the scene hierarchy. Pool reset uses this starting pose later.

If the current level session is still loading, it also subscribes OnLevelLoadComplete to the loading-complete event. The routine expects the body array and Poolee references to have already been prepared; it does not rebuild them by running Validate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.CleanupIgnoredCollisions
member.summary: Removes managed collision-ignore pairs involving the entity’s solid body colliders.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape used by the physics simulation to detect contact. IgnoreCollision can temporarily prevent two such shapes from colliding. This cleanup visits each body’s solid Colliders array and asks MarrowCollisionManager to restore collisions for every managed pair involving each shape, removing the manager’s saved pair and request-count records.

This is a full cleanup for those pairs, rather than releasing one counted ignore request. Other systems’ managed requests for the same pairs are removed too. Trigger arrays are not visited, and the routine does not change collider enabled states or global layer collision rules.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ClearGhost
member.summary: Restores body colliders, trigger volumes and tracker objects, and makes existing Rigidbodies dynamic.

remarks.para: Solid colliders are physics contact shapes; triggers are shapes that report overlaps without blocking motion. Each body’s saved enabled values are restored for its colliders and triggers. Trackers, the scene objects used to report body contact or zone presence, receive an enable request; their activation still depends on the entity’s IsTrackersEnabled flag. Rigidbodies that exist are set to isKinematic = false, allowing the physics simulation to move them. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

This helper does not clear IsGhosting or change the entity’s IsCollidersEnabled, IsTriggersEnabled or IsTrackersEnabled flags. It also does not recreate joints destroyed by Ghost(true). Its name therefore does not mean it performs the complete entity-level Ghost(false) transition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ClearHibernation
member.summary: Clears every hibernation source on this entity and restores bodies that have saved hibernation settings.

remarks.para: Hibernation temporarily freezes a body’s physics while saving settings needed to restore it. This helper clears the entity’s source mask first. It then restores saved Rigidbody settings, or the saved cached Rigidbody movement and rotation locks used when that component is recreated for a body without a Rigidbody, for each body marked hibernating. Each body’s hibernating flag is cleared before its mass is recalculated. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

Unlike Hibernate(false, source), this removes all sources at once. It operates on this entity’s body array and does not recursively clear the source masks on packed parasite entities. It also does not activate the entity’s GameObject or re-enable its behaviours.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Despawn
member.summary: Asks the entity’s Poolee to remove this instance from use through the spawning and pooling system.

remarks.para: A pool keeps scene objects so they can be reused instead of recreated. This method forwards to the associated Poolee, which handles despawn notifications and pool deinitialization. For a pool-managed instance, Poolee passes the request to AssetSpawner and the instance’s pool or spawn policy.

The fallback for an instance without pool membership calls the Poolee despawn event, deinitializes its registered poolable components, then deactivates its GameObject and logs an error. This method is therefore a lifecycle request rather than an unconditional immediate destruction of the scene object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.EnableColliders(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Temporarily disables the entity’s solid physics contact shapes, or restores their saved enabled states.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape. Solid colliders can block motion and produce physical contact.

With isEnabled = false, each body saves each solid collider’s current enabled value and disables it. With true, it restores those individually saved values. A shape that was disabled before the disable request therefore remains disabled when restored; true does not turn every shape on.

The method returns when IsCollidersEnabled already matches the requested Boolean. Otherwise it completes the body updates before writing that flag. The flag records the last normal request, rather than reporting every shape’s actual state: Ghost and forced helpers can change shapes without updating it. Assigning the flag directly does not perform these body updates.

member.param: False saves and disables these shapes; true restores their saved enabled values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.EnableTrackers(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Changes the entity’s tracker-enable request and updates the body tracker objects when that request changes.

remarks.para: Trackers are scene objects that report body collider activity to systems such as zones. A collider is an invisible physics shape. If IsTrackersEnabled already matches isEnabled, this method returns. Otherwise it stores the new flag first, then calls ForceEnableTrackers to update every body and its packed bodies.

A tracker GameObject is made active only when both the entity’s stored tracker flag and the supplied enable request are true. On a change to inactive, its deactivation routines are called after the object is switched off. These routines receive the tracker’s Collider, rather than the enable Boolean. Disabling also removes the entity’s associations from zone-culling bookkeeping. Assigning IsTrackersEnabled directly changes the stored request without doing this work.

member.param: True permits tracker objects to be activated; false switches them off and clears zone-culling associations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.EnableTriggers(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Temporarily disables the entity’s overlap-reporting trigger shapes, or restores their saved enabled states.

remarks.para: A trigger is an invisible collider that reports overlaps without blocking motion.

With isEnabled = false, each body saves each trigger collider’s current enabled value and disables it. With true, it restores those individually saved values. A shape that was disabled before the disable request therefore remains disabled when restored; true does not turn every shape on.

The method returns when IsTriggersEnabled already matches the requested Boolean. Otherwise it completes the body updates before writing that flag. The flag records the last normal request, rather than reporting every shape’s actual state: Ghost and forced helpers can change shapes without updating it. Assigning the flag directly does not perform these body updates.

member.param: False saves and disables these shapes; true restores their saved enabled values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ForceEnableColliders(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Always saves and disables, or restores, the entity’s solid contact collider shapes.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape used by physics. This helper visits all matching shapes even when the entity’s stored IsCollidersEnabled request already equals isEnabled. It leaves that entity flag unchanged.

False copies each shape’s current enabled value into its saved-state array before disabling it. True restores those saved values, including false for shapes that were already disabled. Calling false twice overwrites the first saved states with the currently disabled states, so a later true may keep the shapes disabled. This is a forced pass through the save/restore operation, rather than a command that overrides every shape to enabled.

member.param: False saves current enabled values and disables the shapes; true restores the saved values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ForceEnableTrackers(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Always updates body tracker objects, bypassing the normal enable-request early return.

remarks.para: Trackers are scene objects that report collider activity to systems such as zones. A collider is an invisible physics shape. This method requests tracker activation on every body and recursively on its packed bodies. A tracker object becomes active only if isEnabled and its entity’s IsTrackersEnabled flag are both true. Passing true while that stored flag is false therefore leaves it inactive.

When a tracker changes from active to inactive, its deactivation routines run after the GameObject is switched off. These routines receive the tracker’s Collider, rather than the enable Boolean. With false, the method also clears the entity’s zone-culling associations after updating the bodies. It never changes IsTrackersEnabled itself; EnableTrackers updates that flag before calling this helper.

member.param: Enable request combined with each tracker’s entity flag; false always requests inactive tracker objects.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ForceEnableTriggers(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Always saves and disables, or restores, the entity’s overlap-reporting trigger collider shapes.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape used by physics. This helper visits all matching shapes even when the entity’s stored IsTriggersEnabled request already equals isEnabled. It leaves that entity flag unchanged.

False copies each shape’s current enabled value into its saved-state array before disabling it. True restores those saved values, including false for shapes that were already disabled. Calling false twice overwrites the first saved states with the currently disabled states, so a later true may keep the shapes disabled. This is a forced pass through the save/restore operation, rather than a command that overrides every shape to enabled.

member.param: False saves current enabled values and disables the shapes; true restores the saved values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.GatherMarrowBehaviours
member.summary: Rebuilds the list of MarrowBehaviour components that culling will switch off and on.

remarks.para: It searches the entity’s GameObject and active child objects for MarrowBehaviour components, replaces _behaviours with that result, and assigns this entity to every collected component’s Entity reference. Inactive child GameObjects are excluded by this search.

OnCullResolve later disables every collected behaviour when culling starts and enables every one when culling ends. This helper does not itself enable or disable them, and it does not register their cull, hide or despawn listener interfaces automatically.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.GetCenterOfMassInWorld
member.summary: Calculates a mass-weighted average of the body center positions in scene coordinates.

remarks.para: For each body, it uses that body’s stored CenterOfMass value: a meter offset from the body’s origin along its local axes, rotated by its current Transform rotation and added to its current scene position. The offset is not multiplied by the Transform scale. The method weights that position by the body’s current Rigidbody mass; a body without a Rigidbody contributes zero mass. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

It adds position times mass for all bodies, then divides by their total mass. For example, a 1-kilogram body centered at X = 0 meters and a 3-kilogram body centered at X = 4 meters give an average X of 3 meters. The result is a world position in meters, rather than an offset from the entity root.

The body list and its entries must exist, and the total contributing mass must be nonzero. There is no fallback position for an empty list or zero total mass. The calculation uses MarrowBody’s serialized CenterOfMass values, rather than directly querying Rigidbody.worldCenterOfMass. This method does not refresh those stored values from the Rigidbody.

member.returns: The mass-weighted body-center position in world coordinates, in meters.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Ghost(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Switches the entity and its packed parasite entities between ghost physics and normal body processing.

remarks.para: The method returns if IsGhosting already equals isGhosting. Otherwise it writes IsGhosting first. Entering ghost mode disables body solid colliders, trigger shapes and tracker objects, and sets existing Rigidbodies to kinematic so ordinary physics forces do not move them. Leaving ghost mode restores saved collider and trigger enabled values, requests tracker activation, and makes those Rigidbodies dynamic. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives motion between objects.

The same ghost request is then applied to each packed parasite entity, meaning another entity recorded as attached inside this host. On entering ghost mode, the method additionally requests Cull(false), removes zone-culling associations, and removes each RuntimeJoints entry before asking that joint to destroy itself. MarrowJoint.Destroy only performs destruction when IsCreatedAtRuntime is true; merely being in RuntimeJoints does not set that flag. Destruction is requested through Unity, which completes it later. It does not destroy the separate serialized Joints array, and leaving ghost mode does not recreate destroyed runtime joints.

IsCollidersEnabled, IsTriggersEnabled and IsTrackersEnabled are not updated here. Tracker activation still depends on the stored tracker flag. Leaving ghost mode sets isKinematic to false rather than restoring a body’s previous kinematic value; collider restoration uses saved per-shape values rather than enabling every shape.

member.param: True enters ghost physics and requests runtime-joint cleanup; false restores body processing without recreating destroyed joints.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Hibernate(System.Boolean,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.HibernationSources)
member.summary: Adds or removes a reason for freezing the entity’s physics, waking it only when no reasons remain.

remarks.para: source is a set of flags: Default = 1, Culling = 2 and Loading = 4. True adds the supplied bits to the hibernation mask; false removes those bits. The mask changes before any bodies are updated. Bodies are updated only when the overall state changes between no sources and at least one source. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

For example, if both Loading and Culling are present, removing Loading leaves the bodies hibernating because Culling remains. Calling false is therefore a request to release one system’s reason, rather than an unconditional wake-up.

Entering hibernation saves each Rigidbody’s restoration settings, freezes all position and rotation constraints, sets its sleep threshold to positive infinity and calls Sleep. The sleep threshold is the energy-per-unit-mass cutoff below which a Rigidbody can sleep; positive infinity is the threshold value assigned here, not a wait duration. Waking restores the saved settings, clears the body’s hibernating flag and recalculates its mass. For a body without a Rigidbody, the corresponding helper saves or restores the cached Rigidbody movement and rotation locks used when that component is recreated.

On an overall state transition, each packed parasite entity receives the same freeze/wake Boolean using its Default source. Individual source changes that leave this entity hibernating do not perform another body or parasite pass. This routine does not deactivate the entity’s GameObject or disable its behaviour components.

member.param: True adds the source reasons; false removes them, waking only if no reasons remain.
The hibernation-reason flags to add or remove; Default, Culling and Loading can be combined.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Hide(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Changes the entity’s hide request and optionally switches its GameObject immediately.

remarks.para: The method compares isHidden with the current requested Hide bit and returns if they already match. Otherwise it ensures the inactive status exists, then asks InactiveObjectManager to write the Hide request and queue it for processing. IsHidden consequently reports the new request before the normal apply routine runs.

The manager later calls OnHideApply, a callback routine that reports the change to registered hideable listeners and updates the entity’s GameObject using the combined resolved Hide, Cull and Despawn reasons. Hiding is object deactivation here, rather than changing individual renderer visibility settings.

With doApplyImmediately = true, this method directly calls GameObject.SetActive(!isHidden) after submitting the request. That immediate toggle does not invoke the hideable listeners itself and does not check other inactive reasons; the later manager pass still applies the combined state. Because the equal-request early return happens first, this option does nothing when the Hide request already matches.

member.param: True requests hiding; false removes the Hide request.
Also toggle this GameObject immediately after a changed request, before normal manager application.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IgnoreCollision(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds or releases managed requests to ignore contact between the two entities’ solid body shapes.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape. This overload pairs every solid collider in otherEntity’s bodies with every solid collider in this entity’s bodies, passing each pair to MarrowCollisionManager. Trigger arrays are not included.

True adds one ignore request per pair; false releases one. The manager counts requests so that a pair remains ignored while another request is still outstanding. For example, after two true calls, one false call leaves a request remaining. Balance temporary requests rather than repeatedly calling true every update.

These requests change contact between specific shapes. They do not disable the shapes, change global layer collision rules, or guarantee that releasing a request produces contact if some other physics setting still prevents it.

member.param: The other entity whose solid body colliders are paired with this entity’s solid colliders.
True adds one ignore request for every pair; false releases one request.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.InitializeInactiveState
member.summary: Creates the shared hide, cull and despawn status and connects the entity’s routines to its processing stages.

remarks.para: The method does nothing after _hasInactiveState is true. On the first call, it creates an InactiveStatus and attaches OnCullResolve to cull resolution, and OnCullApply, OnHideApply and OnDespawnApply to their respective apply stages. These are callbacks: routines the inactive manager calls to perform or report a state change.

Only after those connections are made does it set _hasInactiveState to true. The newly created status initially has no requested inactive reasons. This setup does not itself request hiding, culling or despawning, or switch off the entity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnCullApply(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Applies the entity GameObject’s activation state after the manager resolves culling and the other inactive reasons.

remarks.para: This is an inactive-manager callback: a routine called to perform part of a state change. It forwards the supplied status to Activate, which checks all resolved Hide, Cull and Despawn reasons and the exceptions that allow a culled root to remain active.

The isInactive Boolean is unused by this implementation. It does not perform the physics or behaviour changes itself; those happen in OnCullResolve. During the normal manager path, the resolved flags already describe the new state, and the applied flags are updated only after this callback returns.

member.param: The inactive status whose combined resolved reasons determine GameObject activation.
The manager’s cull-state Boolean; ignored by this forwarding implementation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnCullResolve(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Freezes or releases culling physics, switches the collected behaviours, then tells culling listeners about the transition.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine invoked by the inactive manager while processing cull transitions. With true it adds the Culling hibernation source, disables every collected MarrowBehaviour, then calls OnEntityCull on the registered cullable listeners. With false it removes the Culling source, enables all collected behaviours, then calls OnEntityUncull. Removing Culling only wakes physics if no other hibernation source remains.
Listeners run after the hibernation request and behaviour changes. The routine does not switch the root GameObject active or inactive; the apply stage handles that separately.

In the manager’s entering-cull path, the requested Cull bit is already set and the manager sets the completed Cull bit before this callback, but resolved flags are copied from the request only afterward. The leaving callback is delayed until the manager’s completion stage and all Hide, Cull and Despawn requests are clear. The manager clears the completed Cull bit before calling the leaving routine. Removing only Cull while Hide or Despawn remains can therefore leave the behaviours disabled until that later completion.

member.param: The status supplied by the manager; this routine uses the transition Boolean rather than reading its flags.
True performs entering-cull changes; false releases those changes when completion is permitted.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnDespawnApply(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Reports a resolved despawn transition and updates tracker notifications and GameObject activation.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine invoked by the inactive manager during its apply stage. With true, it first calls OnEntityDespawn on all registered despawnable listeners, then invokes OnDeactivate on every body tracker, and finally calls Activate with the combined resolved status. A tracker is a scene object that reports its collider activity to contact or zone systems; a collider is an invisible physics shape. These tracker deactivation routines receive that tracker’s Collider. Tracker deactivation here reports through the tracker’s registered routines; this loop does not itself toggle the tracker GameObjects.

With false, it calls Activate first, then calls OnEntitySpawn on the despawnable listeners. Other resolved inactive reasons may still keep the GameObject off. The manager’s resolved flags already hold the transition while these listeners run; its applied flags are copied afterward.
This callback does not itself return the instance to a pool or destroy it. Despawn through Poolee and the pool lifecycle perform that separate work.

member.param: The combined resolved inactive reasons used for the final GameObject activation decision.
True reports despawning before activation changes; false updates activation before reporting spawning.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes the destroyed entity from lookup systems and zone-culling bookkeeping.

remarks.para: OnDestroy is a Unity lifecycle callback: a routine Unity calls when destroying this component. It first removes the GameObject-to-entity cache entry, releasing the shared cache reference when that cache becomes empty. It then marks IsDestroyed true, unregisters from EntityManager, and clears the entity’s zone-culling associations.

The destroyed flag is therefore set after cache removal and before manager unregistering and zone cleanup. This routine does not explicitly clear the listener lists or deregister this entity from its Poolee; those operations should not be assumed from this callback.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnHideApply(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Notifies hideable listeners and sets GameObject activation for a resolved hide transition.

remarks.para: This is an inactive-manager callback, meaning a routine called to apply a state change. With true it calls OnEntityHide on registered hideable listeners first, then calls Activate to apply the combined resolved Hide, Cull and Despawn state. With false the order is reversed: activation is updated first, then OnEntityUnhide is called.

Listeners therefore run before the root activation update when hiding, and after it when unhiding. Unhiding does not guarantee an active GameObject if another resolved inactive reason still applies. The manager has already updated resolved flags at this stage; it copies those flags to applied only after the callback returns.

member.param: The manager’s combined resolved inactive reasons used by Activate.
True reports hiding before updating activation; false updates activation before reporting unhiding.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnLevelLoadComplete
member.summary: Releases the Loading reason for physics hibernation when level loading finishes.

remarks.para: This routine is connected to loading completion during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback. A callback is a routine called when an action or event occurs. It calls Hibernate(false, Loading), removing only the loading system’s freeze reason.

Bodies wake only if that was the final hibernation source. A remaining Culling or Default source keeps them frozen. This does not activate the entity’s GameObject, enable behaviours, or forcibly clear every sleep reason.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnPoolDeInitialize
member.summary: Resets this instance for reuse, turns off tracker objects, then requests the despawned inactive state.

remarks.para: This is a Poolee lifecycle callback: a routine called when its pool deinitializes the instance. A pool stores scene objects for later reuse. First Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize removes runtime connections, restores body and joint settings, unpacks bodies and restores the starting body pose and root scale.

After that full physics reset, it calls ForceEnableTrackers(false), switching off tracker objects and clearing zone-culling associations. Finally it submits inactive requests in this order: Hide(false), Cull(false), Despawn(true). Those calls change request bits immediately and queue the later resolve/apply callbacks.

This routine does not directly destroy the root scene object. It prepares and marks the instance for the pooling system’s later use. The stored IsTrackersEnabled flag is not changed by the forced-off tracker pass.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnPoolInitialize
member.summary: Clears the despawn request, enables body tracker requests, and adjusts mass for a changed root scale.

remarks.para: This is a Poolee lifecycle callback, a routine called during pool initialization of an instance. A pool stores scene objects for reuse. It first submits Despawn(false) to the inactive manager, then requests tracker activation for each body. The request flag changes immediately; the manager’s spawn notifications and activation changes occur in its later apply stage.

It then compares the entity Transform’s local scale with the original scale recorded by Validate. If they differ beyond the native comparison tolerance, it stores the unitless volume ratio (current X/original X) × (current Y/original Y) × (current Z/original Z) in ScaleRatio and calls ResetMass. Each local-scale component is a unitless size factor along that axis relative to the root’s parent. For uniform scale doubled on all three axes, the ratio is 8, so saved masses are multiplied by 8.

Tracker activation still depends on IsTrackersEnabled. If the scale is approximately unchanged, the scale/mass part returns without replacing an existing ScaleRatio or recalculating mass. Pool initialization does not capture a new starting pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.OnPoolSpawn
member.summary: Adds the Loading physics-hibernation reason if this instance spawns during level loading.

remarks.para: The routine checks the current SceneStreamer session. If that session is in its loading state, it calls Hibernate(true, Loading) so the bodies remain frozen while the level is being prepared. Hibernate saves restoration settings and freezes Rigidbody motion on the transition into hibernation. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

When loading finishes, OnLevelLoadComplete removes that reason; another source can still keep the bodies frozen. If the session is not loading, this spawn routine returns without adding or clearing any reason. OnPoolSpawn is the pool’s callback, a routine called when an instance is brought into use.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Pack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody)
member.summary: Attaches a body under one of this entity’s host bodies and removes that body’s independent Rigidbody and joint components.

remarks.para: hostBody must be in this entity’s Bodies array; otherwise the method returns. It hibernates parasiteBody temporarily, then asks the host body to pack it. A parasite is the body being attached, which can belong to this entity or another one. The body helper marks it packed, records its host, and requests Unity Object.Destroy for Joint components on the parasite body’s GameObject and for its Rigidbody. Unity completes those component removals after the current Update loop. The helper immediately clears the body’s Rigidbody reference and HasRigidbody flag, while retaining settings for later recreation. Its Transform is parented to the host body. The body packing helper returns without repeating these operations when the body is already marked packed. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives motion between objects.

The method then releases that body’s temporary hibernation state and recalculates mass through its host. For a body outside this entity’s array, it also records the other entity in _parasites if newly encountered, applies this host’s ghost Boolean, and applies its hibernation Boolean with the host’s current source mask. These are lifecycle and physics changes, rather than a transfer of the removed joint components.

The receiver’s _hostEntity reference is set from hostBody.Entity before packing, so this reference can point to the receiver itself. The native packing helper saves the parasite’s previous Transform parent on the host body’s _lastParent field, whereas Unpack later reads the parasite body’s field. Do not assume this pair automatically preserves and restores the original parent; that asymmetric cache use matters when arranging the hierarchy.

member.param: A member of this entity’s Bodies array that will hold the packed body.
The body to attach beneath the host and remove from independent Rigidbody processing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_Awake
member.summary: Saves each body’s starting position and rotation relative to its immediate parent for pool reset.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to set up a component. This physics setup helper allocates a default-pose array matching Bodies and fills it from each body Transform’s localPosition and localRotation. The position is a local offset in Unity distance units, conventionally meters; the rotation is an orientation represented by a quaternion, Unity’s four-number representation of a 3D orientation.

These values use each body’s immediate parent in the hierarchy, rather than the entity root’s frame. Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize later writes them back as local positions and rotations. Scale, velocity and Rigidbody settings are not stored in this pose cache. Calling the helper again replaces the cache with the bodies’ current pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnCullDisabled
member.summary: Adds the Culling reason for freezing the entity’s physics bodies.

remarks.para: This helper calls Hibernate(true, Culling). Entering hibernation saves the body settings needed for restoration, freezes Rigidbody movement and puts the bodies to sleep. If the entity is already hibernating for another reason, it adds the Culling bit without repeating the body transition. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.
It only makes the physics hibernation request. It does not deactivate the root GameObject or disable MarrowBehaviour components; the other culling routines handle those changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnCullEnabled
member.summary: Removes the Culling reason for physics hibernation, waking bodies if no other reasons remain.

remarks.para: This helper calls Hibernate(false, Culling). For example, a body still held by the Loading source stays frozen after Culling is removed. When removing Culling leaves no sources, the body helper restores saved Rigidbody settings and recalculates mass. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.
It does not activate the entity’s GameObject or enable its behaviour components. Those operations belong to the other culling stages.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnLevelLoadComplete
member.summary: Releases the Loading reason for physics hibernation when level loading finishes.

remarks.para: This routine is connected to loading completion during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback. A callback is a routine called when an action or event occurs. It calls Hibernate(false, Loading), removing only the loading system’s freeze reason.

Bodies wake only if that was the final hibernation source. A remaining Culling or Default source keeps them frozen. This does not activate the entity’s GameObject, enable behaviours, or forcibly clear every sleep reason.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize
member.summary: Removes temporary physics attachments and restores the entity’s saved body, joint, pose and scale settings for reuse.

remarks.para: First it removes RuntimeJoints and requests destruction of their wrappers, exits ghost mode when needed, and unpacks any packed member bodies. It then restores the tracker-enable request, clears the entity hibernation sources, restores saved hibernation settings on bodies that need them, enables tracker requests, makes existing Rigidbodies dynamic, and restores saved collider and trigger enabled values. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with configurable movement limits and drive strengths.

Next it clears managed collision-ignore pairs on body solid colliders, despawns recorded parasite entities, clears the receiver’s stored host-entity reference, and writes each member body’s starting local position and rotation from the default pose cache. Local here means relative to that body’s immediate parent; the positions are meter offsets along the parent’s axes. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback—a routine called when setting up a component—captured this starting pose.

Finally it restores the saved ConfigurableJoint settings and marks each joint for connected-anchor setup during the next applicable body-enable pass. The connected anchor is the joint’s attachment point on the other Rigidbody, expressed in that body’s local coordinates; when no Rigidbody is connected, Unity interprets the point in world coordinates. These position offsets are measured in meters. The method then restores stored Rigidbody settings, resets the root Transform’s local scale to _originalScale recorded by Validate, and sets the unitless ScaleRatio to 1. The later Rigidbody restoration can replace the earlier temporary dynamic settings.

This is the physics-reset part of OnPoolDeInitialize. That outer callback subsequently switches tracker objects off and submits the inactive requests for despawning. This helper does not itself perform that final tracker-off pass or change the entity’s IsCollidersEnabled and IsTriggersEnabled request flags.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnPoolInitialize
member.summary: Recalculates the volume multiplier and body masses when the root’s local scale differs from its recorded original scale.

remarks.para: ScaleRatio is unitless: (current X scale/original X scale) × (current Y scale/original Y scale) × (current Z scale/original Z scale). Each scale component is a unitless size factor along an axis relative to the root’s parent, taken from the root’s Transform.localScale, with the original saved by Validate. Uniform scale doubled gives 2 × 2 × 2 = 8; saved body masses are multiplied by that volume ratio. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

The new ratio is stored before ResetMass runs. ResetMass then updates eligible active, nonhibernating Rigidbody bodies and recalculates their inertia, the physics quantity that controls resistance to turning.

The comparison permits a small numerical tolerance. If all scale components are approximately unchanged, this helper returns without setting ScaleRatio back to 1 or resetting mass. It does not apply a new Transform scale itself, capture a new pose, or validate the original-scale reference for zero components.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Physics_OnSpawn
member.summary: Adds the Loading physics-hibernation reason if this instance spawns during level loading.

remarks.para: The routine checks the current SceneStreamer session. If that session is in its loading state, it calls Hibernate(true, Loading) so the bodies remain frozen while the level is being prepared. Hibernate saves restoration settings and freezes Rigidbody motion on the transition into hibernation. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

When loading finishes, OnLevelLoadComplete removes that reason; another source can still keep the bodies frozen. If the session is not loading, this spawn routine returns without adding or clearing any reason. OnPoolSpawn is the pool’s callback, a routine called when an instance is brought into use.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.PreventDisableOnCull(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets whether resolved culling is allowed to deactivate this entity’s root GameObject.

remarks.para: True stores an exception that Activate checks when deciding whether a Cull request should switch the GameObject off. False removes that exception. This setter only stores the choice; it does not immediately recalculate activation or change a current cull request.
The exception does not block physics hibernation, behaviour disabling or cull listener notifications. It also does not override resolved Hide or Despawn requests, which can still deactivate the root.

member.param: True protects root activation from Cull; false lets Cull deactivate it when other exceptions do not apply.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ReadPose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntityPose@)
member.summary: Captures the bodies’ positions and rotations relative to the entity root into an existing pose object.

remarks.para: outputPose must already refer to a MarrowEntityPose object. Although the parameter is passed by reference, this method does not allocate that object: it replaces its bodyPoses array with a new array matching Bodies, in the same body order.

It takes the entity root’s current world position and rotation as the reference. Each stored position is the world displacement from that root, rotated into the root’s axes, in meters. Each stored rotation is the body’s orientation relative to the root. These scale-free position/rotation records do not divide by the root’s scale and differ from Transform.localPosition when a body has another immediate parent.

Velocity, mass, Rigidbody constraints, scale and other physics settings are not captured. WritePose later places these relative positions and rotations around the entity root’s then-current world pose.

member.param: An existing pose object whose bodyPoses array will be replaced with one root-relative position/rotation record per body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityCullable)
member.summary: Adds a listener for this entity’s cull and uncull notifications.

remarks.para: A listener supplies callback routines: functions the entity calls to report an action or state change. This overload stores the supplied listener for OnEntityCull and OnEntityUncull. Registering the same listener again does not add a duplicate, and registration itself sends no immediate notification or current-state update.

The OnEntityCull and OnEntityUncull routines run after the hibernation request and collected behaviour enable/disable changes in OnCullResolve. Uncull completion can wait until all inactive requests have cleared.

member.param: The listener whose OnEntityCull and OnEntityUncull routines should receive this entity’s notifications.

Registering the same listener again does not add a duplicate, and registration itself sends no immediate notification or current-state update.
OnEntityDespawn runs before tracker deactivation notifications and root activation changes; OnEntitySpawn runs after the root activation decision in OnDespawnApply.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.IPoolable)
member.summary: Adds a listener to the Poolee’s initialization, spawn and deinitialization notifications.

remarks.para: Poolee manages this object’s pooling lifecycle; a pool keeps an instance for reuse. The listener supplies OnPoolInitialize, OnPoolSpawn and OnPoolDeInitialize callbacks, meaning routines the Poolee calls at those lifecycle stages. This entity overload forwards the listener to its associated Poolee.

The Poolee appends the listener without checking for duplicates and does not immediately invoke a callback. Registering the same listener twice can make it receive a lifecycle notification twice. This differs from this entity’s cull, hide, despawn and pose listener overloads, which avoid duplicate entries.

member.param: The listener implementing initialization, spawn and deinitialization routines for the associated Poolee.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.RemoveRuntimeJoint(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint)
member.summary: Removes a joint from the entity’s runtime cleanup list without destroying the connection.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives object movement. This method only removes the supplied MarrowJoint from RuntimeJoints. If it was absent, the list is unchanged. The method does not destroy the joint component, disable it, change its owner, or disconnect its physics bodies.

Ghost(true) and Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize process the joints remaining in this list. After removal, this list no longer causes that joint to be cleaned up; code responsible for the joint must handle any required teardown separately.

member.param: The existing joint to stop tracking for runtime cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ResetMass
member.summary: Updates eligible bodies’ mass from the saved mass and volume scale, restores their saved center offset, and recalculates resistance to turning.

remarks.para: For each packed body with a recorded host, mass reset is redirected through that host. Otherwise it updates only a body that has a Rigidbody, is not hibernating and has an active GameObject in the hierarchy. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

The mass in kilograms becomes the saved RigidbodyInfo mass times ScaleRatio. ScaleRatio is the unitless volume ratio: the product of the entity root’s current/original local scale on X, Y and Z, normally refreshed during pool initialization. Each local-scale component is a unitless size factor relative to the root’s parent; the original was recorded by Validate. For example, a saved 2-kilogram mass and a ratio of 8 produce 16 kilograms. This routine reads the ratio already stored; changing the root scale alone does not recalculate that ratio here.

The saved RigidbodyInfo center-of-mass offset, measured in meters from that body’s origin along its local axes, is converted through the current Transform and back before being assigned. This saved setting is separate from MarrowBody’s stored CenterOfMass value used by GetCenterOfMassInWorld. It is not multiplied by ScaleRatio. The routine then asks the Rigidbody to recalculate its inertia tensor, the physics quantity controlling resistance to turning, from its current geometry and mass; it does not multiply a saved inertia tensor by the ratio.

When IsTrackersEnabled is true and IsGhosting is false, nontrigger tracker GameObjects are temporarily switched off while the inertia is recalculated and restored afterward. A collider is an invisible physics shape; a nontrigger shape produces physical contact rather than only reporting overlaps. On an actual active-to-inactive change, the tracker’s deactivation routines receive its Collider after the object is switched off. The body arrays and saved settings must already be prepared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.SetActive(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Directly switches this entity’s GameObject active or inactive.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the scene object containing the entity. This method calls its SetActive operation with isActive. Deactivation makes that object and its children inactive in the scene hierarchy; reactivation still depends on the parent object being active.

It does not edit the entity’s hide, cull, despawn or hibernation request flags, or separately set behaviour and body enable values. The inactive manager can later make another activation decision from its resolved requests. Use Hide or the appropriate lifecycle operation when those state notifications are also needed.

member.param: The activeSelf value to request on the entity’s GameObject.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.SetPhysicsDefaults
member.summary: Saves the current Rigidbody and ConfigurableJoint settings as the values to restore during pool reset.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object simulated mass and movement. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with configurable motion limits and drive strengths. This method copies each existing saved joint’s current configuration into its ConfigurableJointInfo and records the joint’s reference frame: its anchor position on its own Rigidbody and the connected anchor position on the other Rigidbody, both measured in meters. If no Rigidbody is connected, Unity interprets the connected anchor in world coordinates rather than in another body’s frame. A later body-enable pass uses this saved frame to configure the joint. It also copies each Rigidbody-backed body’s current settings into its stored RigidbodyInfo.

Physics_OnPoolDeinitialize later restores those records, and ResetMass uses their saved masses and center offsets. Calling this after changing physics settings makes those settings the new restore baseline. The method does not capture body positions and rotations into the default pose cache, rebuild body or joint lists, or record a new original root scale.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.SpawnEvents_Awake
member.summary: Registers this entity to receive lifecycle routines from its associated Poolee during startup.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to set up a component. This helper passes the entity itself to Poolee.RegisterPoolable so that Poolee can call its OnPoolInitialize, OnPoolSpawn and OnPoolDeInitialize routines during reuse of the scene object.

The helper does not discover or register other listener components. Poolee registration appends without a duplicate check, so repeatedly calling this helper can add repeated registrations; the main Awake routine already performs the entity’s registration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Unpack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody)
member.summary: Removes a packed body from its recorded host and recreates its independent Rigidbody when needed.

remarks.para: hostBody must belong to this entity’s Bodies array; otherwise the method returns. If parasiteBody is packed, it clears the packed flag first, switches its trackers off, removes it from its recorded host’s packed-body list and recalculates that host’s mass. It then clears the body’s host reference, recreates a missing Rigidbody from its saved settings, and recalculates the body’s mass. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion.

Next it assigns the body Transform’s parent from parasiteBody._lastParent and requests tracker activation again. The packing helper stores the previous parent on the host body instead, so this method uses whatever parent reference is present on the parasite; this native asymmetry means restoring the actual original hierarchy is not guaranteed. Destroyed joint components are not recreated by this method.

For a body outside this entity’s array, if no body still packed into any body in this entity’s Bodies array belongs to the same parasite entity, that entity is removed from _parasites. It receives Ghost(false) and Hibernate(false, Default); other hibernation reasons can remain. Finally this receiver’s stored _hostEntity reference is cleared.

member.param: A body in this entity’s array used to authorize the unpack operation.
The packed body to remove from its recorded host and restore from its saved Rigidbody settings.
