member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Validate
member.summary: Rebuilds the entity’s component references and ownership links, adding missing wrapper components where needed.

remarks.para: This setup routine records the root Transform’s current local scale as _originalScale, finds or adds a Poolee on the entity GameObject, rebuilds Bodies and Joints from the active child hierarchy, and gathers MarrowBehaviour components. A Poolee manages reuse through a pool; MarrowBody and MarrowJoint wrap Unity physics components with the game’s extra settings and bookkeeping. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with configurable movement limits and drive strengths.

Body and joint validation can add wrappers for existing Rigidbodies or ConfigurableJoints, update saved setup information, and immediately destroy invalid wrappers that no longer have their required physics component. Collected behaviours have their Entity reference set to this entity.

This changes the object’s setup rather than just returning a valid/invalid answer. The hierarchy searches exclude inactive child GameObjects. It does not populate the default starting-pose array; Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, performs that later pose capture.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ValidateBodies
member.summary: Rebuilds Bodies from active-child Rigidbodies and prepares a MarrowBody wrapper for each one.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody provides simulated mass and motion. A MarrowBody adds the game’s saved settings, collider and tracker bookkeeping around that Rigidbody. This method searches the entity object and active child objects for both kinds of component. It removes null wrapper entries and immediately destroys wrappers recorded as having no Rigidbody.

For each discovered Rigidbody, it reuses a wrapper pointing to that Rigidbody or adds a new MarrowBody on the same GameObject. It runs the body setup with this entity as owner and removes the Rigidbody’s HideInInspector flag so the component can be inspected. The resulting wrappers replace the Bodies array; inactive child GameObjects are excluded.

It then considers those bodies for AnchorBody. If the current anchor is absent, the first candidate is selected; a Rigidbody-backed candidate replaces an existing Rigidbody-backed anchor only when its mass in kilograms is strictly greater. The old anchor is not cleared before the scan, so an existing heavier anchor can remain even if it is outside the rebuilt list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ValidateJoints
member.summary: Rebuilds Joints from active-child ConfigurableJoints and prepares their MarrowJoint wrappers.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection that can restrict movement or use drive forces to seek a position or rotation. A MarrowJoint stores the game’s associated joint settings and ownership information. This method searches the entity object and active children for both kinds, discards null references, and immediately destroys MarrowJoint wrappers without a corresponding ConfigurableJoint.

For each discovered ConfigurableJoint it finds the matching wrapper or adds a MarrowJoint on that GameObject, then invokes the wrapper’s setup with the joint and this entity as owner. It removes HideInInspector from the underlying physics joint and replaces the Joints array with the prepared wrappers. Inactive child GameObjects are excluded.
RuntimeJoints is a separate cleanup list; rebuilding Joints does not rebuild that cleanup list or destroy its entries merely by replacing the serialized Joints array.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ValidatePoolee
member.summary: Finds or adds a Poolee on the entity’s own GameObject and saves that reference.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages the scene object’s initialization, spawning and deinitialization through the pooling system, which keeps objects for reuse. This helper looks on the GameObject containing this entity, adds the component if missing, and stores the result when it differs from the current _poolee reference.
It does not search children, register lifecycle listeners, initialize the pool, or despawn the object. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, later registers this entity with the prepared Poolee.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ValidatePoseCache
member.summary: Scans Bodies for a Rigidbody-backed anchor with greater mass than the current .

remarks.para: This setup scan does not clear the existing anchor. If that reference is missing, it takes the first body. When both the candidate and current anchor have Rigidbodies, it replaces the current anchor only if the candidate’s mass is strictly greater. Equal masses keep the existing selection, and an existing heavier anchor can survive even when it is not in Bodies. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. The mass compared in this scan is measured in kilograms.

Despite the method’s name, it does not allocate or fill a pose cache. Physics_Awake records the starting body poses during Unity initialization. The chosen anchor is used by Teleport as its body reference for positioning the rest of the entity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.WritePose(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntityPose)
member.summary: Places bodies at the supplied positions and rotations relative to the entity root, then notifies pose listeners.

remarks.para: inputPose.bodyPoses should match the entity’s Bodies array in order and count. Each stored position is a displacement in meters along the entity root’s axes. The method rotates it by the root’s current world rotation and adds the root’s world position. Each stored orientation is similarly combined with the root’s current rotation. Root scale is not multiplied into these stored displacements.

The resulting scene positions and rotations are assigned to the body Transforms. These records use the entity root’s frame rather than each body’s immediate parent frame. ReadPose creates records with this same scale-free convention.

After all supplied records are written, each registered poseable listener receives OnWritePose, a callback routine reporting that the write has finished. A short record array leaves later bodies untouched and still sends that notification; an array longer than Bodies can fail partway through the writes. The routine does not restore velocities, Rigidbody settings, scale or mass from the pose.

member.param: The pose containing root-relative meter displacements and orientations in the same order as Bodies.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.Awake
member.summary: Captures an assigned physics joint's settings, connects this component to its participating bodies and records its reference pose.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine called while the component is being set up. When a valid ConfigurableJoint is assigned, it copies that joint's current settings into _defaultConfigJointInfo, registers with each assigned body, then calls ReadJointSpace. A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict movement and drive bodies toward targets.
With no valid assigned joint, this setup path does nothing. Later assigning references alone does not repeat this capture or body registration; CreateJoint is the separate runtime creation path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.Build(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ConfigurableJointInfo)
member.summary: Creates a missing Unity ConfigurableJoint on BodyA and applies the supplied settings.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement. A GameObject is an object in the Unity scene that holds components. This direct Build call requires valid references but does not test whether BodyA is active/enabled; that gate belongs to the higher-level OnBodyEnable path.

It returns without rebuilding when a valid joint already exists. Otherwise BodyA and its GameObject must be valid. It adds the engine joint, copies the configuration into it, connects BodyB's Rigidbody when that body has one, and calls WriteJointSpace. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for simulated physical movement; without a connected body the new engine joint is attached to the fixed scene.

This helper does not set the runtime-created flag or register with the bodies. The higher-level CreateJoint path handles that setup. The configuration must be assigned; it includes movement modes, anchors, limits, targets and drives rather than merely a rotation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.CreateJoint(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ConfigurableJointInfo,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody)
member.summary: Sets up a runtime physics connection between the supplied bodies when this component has no valid joint yet.

remarks.para: The starting orientation is a quaternion, an orientation value, captured from BodyA relative to BodyB only when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is relative to the fixed scene. Capture writes it into startRotation. This frame choice follows the ConfiguredInWorld getter: while the engine joint is missing, it reads the separate _cjTempInfo fallback rather than directly reading the newly supplied configuration's world-space flag.

It first marks IsCreatedAtRuntime true, saves BodyA, BodyB and the supplied configuration reference, registers this component with each assigned body, records the reference pose, then runs OnBodyEnable. That last step builds the engine joint only when BodyA is active/enabled and any assigned BodyB is active/enabled. An inactive body can therefore delay actual construction.

The configuration object is stored by reference, not cloned; ReadJointSpace writes its captured startRotation. A valid BodyA and configuration are required. If an engine joint already exists, this method leaves the current setup unchanged. Runtime-created joints use removal/break handling rather than the scene-joint rebuild path.

member.param: Settings object saved as the runtime connection's configuration; capture updates its startRotation.
Body whose GameObject receives the Unity joint.
Other participating body, or no body for a connection to the fixed scene.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.Destroy
member.summary: Notifies destroy listeners and schedules removal of a runtime-created joint and its MarrowJoint component.

remarks.para: The six motions are movement along joint X, Y and Z and turning around those axes. Drives act like motors pushing or turning the bodies toward targets; zeroing them removes their drive settings. These directions belong to the configured joint frame and need not match the fixed scene axes.

It acts only when IsCreatedAtRuntime is true. If the engine joint is valid, it first frees all six motions, zeros its drives and clears its connected body. Then each registered destroy callback, a routine called to report or perform an action, receives this MarrowJoint. The callback list is cleared after dispatch, removal is requested for both components, and _configurableJoint is cleared last.

Listeners run before the saved joint reference is cleared, although the physical connection has already been neutralized. This method does nothing for a joint whose runtime-created flag is false. Unity's later OnDestroy cleanup disconnects body registrations; a break-cleanup request uses a separate break-listener path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.FreeAllConstraints
member.summary: Allows unrestricted movement along all three joint axes and rotation around all three axes.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement. Free means that the corresponding motion limit does not restrict that direction; it does not clear the drive settings.
It sets X, Y, Z and angular X, Y, Z motion modes to Free. These directions are the configured joint axes, which need not match the fixed scene axes. The ConfigurableJoint must be assigned.
The joint component, connected body and drive settings remain. Freeing the motion limits does not zero a motor drive or destroy the joint, so a configured drive can still push toward its target.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.JointCleanupCheckAsync
member.summary: Waits for an Update continuation, then repairs a missing scene joint or reports a runtime joint's break and removes its component.

remarks.para: Update is a stage of the game's repeated frame processing. A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement. breakForce is the force break threshold in newtons. Setting it to infinity prevents force alone from exceeding that threshold; the turning-force break threshold, breakTorque in newton-meters, is not changed by this cleanup policy.

This asynchronous sequence pauses and resumes through the game's Update processing. It is not a fixed time delay or a promise of exactly one rendered frame. After the wait, a still-valid ConfigurableJoint requires no cleanup.

If the joint is missing and IsCreatedAtRuntime is false, it changes the stored default breakForce to positive infinity and rebuilds from that configuration. It does not also change breakTorque. If the flag is true, it calls each break callback, a routine registered to report or perform work for the break, with this MarrowJoint, clears the break-listener list, then requests removal of the MarrowJoint component.

That runtime branch does not call the explicit Destroy method or its destroy-listener list. It checks for a missing joint after the wait; calling this routine alone is not proof that a break happened.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.OnBodyDisable
member.summary: Saves the live joint's connection settings and neutralizes it when a participating body is disabled.

remarks.para: Motion modes choose whether movement along each joint X/Y/Z axis and rotation around it is locked, limited or free. Drives act like motors pushing or turning bodies toward targets. The saved six modes and six drives therefore describe the restrictions and motor settings being temporarily removed.

It acts only while _hasBeenEnabled is true, and clears that flag before doing any joint work. For a valid engine joint it saves the connected Rigidbody, six motion modes and six drives into _disableJointInfo, then frees every motion, zeros the drives and disconnects the connected body. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for simulated physical movement.

The engine joint component is retained for later restoration. This snapshot is distinct from the full default configuration. Repeated disable notifications do nothing until a qualifying OnBodyEnable sets the flag again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.OnBodyEnable
member.summary: Builds or restores the joint once its participating bodies can be active together.

remarks.para: BodyA hosts the physics connection; BodyB is the other body, or absent for a connection to the fixed scene. Drives act like motors pushing or turning toward targets. A connected anchor is the connected-side attachment point; automatic configuration lets Unity calculate it.

It acts only while _hasBeenEnabled is false, BodyA is valid and active/enabled, and any assigned BodyB is active/enabled. It sets _hasBeenEnabled true before building a missing engine joint or restoring saved disable-state motions, drives and connected body into an existing one only when the saved disable snapshot is valid.

For an existing joint, it then either recaptures the reference pose or refreshes the engine joint using the stored pose. If _doResetConnectedAnchor is true, automatic connected-anchor configuration is enabled and BodyB is absent, it recaptures the reference with ReadJointSpace; otherwise it uses WriteJointSpace. A missing joint is built with Build, which refreshes it with WriteJointSpace. Repeated enable reports while the flag is already true do nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this component from its bodies' joint registrations and requests destruction of any remaining Unity joint.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement.

Unity calls OnDestroy when this component is being removed. It disconnects BodyA and BodyB registrations first, then destroys a valid stored ConfigurableJoint. It does not itself dispatch the explicit Destroy method's listener list; runtime break cleanup has its own separate notification path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.OnJointBreak(System.Single)
member.summary: Starts the deferred missing-joint cleanup when Unity reports a broken joint.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement. Update is a stage of the game's repeated frame processing, where the deferred cleanup check resumes.

It starts JointCleanupCheckAsync rather than rebuilding or removing the component immediately. That sequence resumes through Update, checks whether the ConfigurableJoint is actually missing, then chooses scene-joint repair or runtime break-listener removal. The received breakForce value is not used to choose that branch or forwarded to listeners.

member.param: Force value in newtons supplied by Unity's break notification; this routine does not inspect or forward it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.ReadJointSpace
member.summary: Captures BodyA's position and rotation relative to BodyB or the fixed scene, and refreshes the joint-orientation caches.

remarks.para: ToJointSpace describes the saved default axis/secondaryAxis orientation in BodyA's local frame, which turns with that body. ToJointSpaceInv reverses that orientation conversion. ToJointSpaceFromDefault combines the captured starting orientation with the local joint-axis orientation. These caches are quaternion orientation values.

The reference is BodyB's scene position and rotation when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is the fixed scene frame. Position is in meters. Rotations are quaternions, orientation values rather than three angle values; the conversion uses position and rotation without scale.

It first clears _doResetConnectedAnchor, then saves that relative pose in _jointSpace, writes the captured rotation into both StartRotation and the default configuration's startRotation, then calculates ToJointSpace from the default axis/secondaryAxis, its inverse, and ToJointSpaceFromDefault. It reads the current bodies; it does not move them.

For example, BodyA 1 meter along BodyB's right direction is saved with relative position (1, 0, 0). Changing an individual cached quaternion does not recapture this whole group; this routine refreshes them together.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.RestoreStartRotation
member.summary: Refreshes the joint reference from its stored pose, or recaptures it for the special connected-anchor reset case.

remarks.para: A connected anchor is the connected-side attachment point; automatic configuration lets Unity calculate it. The starting orientation is a quaternion, an orientation value, captured from BodyA relative to BodyB only when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is relative to the fixed scene. WriteJointSpace uses that chosen reference frame to reconstruct the stored pose.

With a valid ConfigurableJoint, it calls ReadJointSpace only when _doResetConnectedAnchor is true, autoConfigureConnectedAnchor is enabled and BodyB is absent. That capture clears the reset flag. Otherwise it calls WriteJointSpace, which temporarily uses the stored pose in its chosen BodyB-or-fixed-scene reference frame and restores BodyA's original scene pose before returning.
A missing engine joint makes this a no-op. It does not simply assign StartRotation to a body, and changing that cached quaternion alone does not update _jointSpace.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.SetAngularXDrive(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Applies the angular X drive by multiplying its saved baseline spring, damping and force cap by three independent factors.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection between bodies, and a drive acts like a motor pushing or turning them toward a target. Torque means turning force. Orientation error is the difference from the wanted orientation, and angular velocity means turning speed and direction; its error is the difference from the wanted angular velocity. Angular X and Y/Z refer to the configured joint axes, which need not match the fixed scene axes.

The drive turns the joint toward its rotation/angular-velocity target. Spring supplies restoring torque for orientation error, damper responds to angular-velocity error and maximumForce caps torque. The selected rotationDriveMode chooses Slerp or the angular X/YZ drives; this setter does not change that mode. For angular driving, the force cap is a torque in newton-meters; spring and damper are the engine's angular restoring and damping coefficients.

The baseline is angularXDriveBase. Applied spring = baseline positionSpring times springMult; damping = baseline positionDamper times damperMult; cap = baseline maximumForce times maxForceMult. All three multipliers are unitless: 1 keeps the corresponding baseline, 0.5 halves it and 0 zeros it. For example, baseline spring 100 with springMult 0.5 produces 50 in the same coefficient units.

Each call starts from the saved baseline, not the last applied result, so repeated 0.5 calls do not keep halving the drive. This does not change the baseline, targets, motion limits or drive mode. A valid live ConfigurableJoint is required; this wrapper does not clamp the multipliers.

member.param: Unitless factor multiplying the saved restoring-strength coefficient.
Unitless factor multiplying the saved velocity-damping coefficient.
Unitless factor multiplying the saved drive force/torque cap.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.WriteJointSpace
member.summary: Uses the stored reference pose to refresh the engine joint while restoring BodyA's original scene pose before returning.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is Unity's physics connection that can restrict or drive body movement.

The reference is BodyB's scene position and rotation when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is the fixed scene frame. Position is in meters. Rotations are quaternions, orientation values rather than three angle values; the conversion uses position and rotation without scale.

It saves BodyA's current scene position/rotation, temporarily puts it at the pose reconstructed from _jointSpace, toggles the ConfigurableJoint's swapBodies flag and restores that flag, then restores BodyA's original position/rotation. This is not a permanent teleport to the saved pose.
A valid engine joint and BodyA are required. Restoring the body pose is part of this successful sequence; assigning _jointSpace alone does not execute it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapStateHelper.OnDisable
member.summary: Asks the overlap manager to end recorded overlaps involving this GameObject when the helper is disabled.

remarks.para: A GameObject is Unity's container for a scene object and its components. A collider is the shape used to detect contact; a trigger is a collider that reports overlap without blocking movement. OnDisable is Unity's callback when this component becomes disabled, including when its GameObject becomes inactive. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This method gets OverlapTriggerManager.Instance and, if that returns a manager, passes the helper's own GameObject to DisableOverlap.

The manager holds the overlap records: counts of contacts between a trigger GameObject and another GameObject. Cleanup uses those existing records to reduce each affected positive count to zero. A pair with several recorded collider contacts is ended as a whole instead of leaving the remaining count behind. If there is no matching recorded pair, this call does not invent an overlap or exit for it.

When the last recorded count for a pair is cleared, the manager queues exit notifications for the OverlapTrigger components on the trigger GameObject. Their OnOverlapExit callbacks receive the pair's other GameObject when the manager drains its event queue. In the usual case where the helper is on that other object, this argument is the helper's GameObject. If the helper was placed on an object that also has OverlapTrigger, its own trigger relationships can also be ended, with each partner as the argument. Count changes and pair cleanup occur during the disable cleanup; those callbacks are dispatched through the queue afterward, rather than called directly by this helper.

For example, a crate already recorded inside a trigger can be made inactive. This helper asks the manager to end the recorded crate overlap even though the crate did not physically move out of the trigger volume. Disabling the helper component itself also requests that cleanup without directly disabling the crate's colliders.

This operation only handles the manager's recorded relationships for the supplied object. It does not clear unrelated overlaps or cancel notifications that were already queued. Notification timing follows the manager's queue processing, so it is not a promise of an exact one-frame delay. If Instance returns null, the helper makes no cleanup call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTrigger.OnDisable
member.summary: Asks the overlap manager to end the recorded overlaps involving this trigger's GameObject when the component is disabled.

remarks.para: A GameObject is an object in Unity's scene. A recorded pair links this scene object with one partner scene object. OnDisable is Unity's disable callback, a routine called to perform or report an action when the component is disabled or its GameObject becomes inactive. It gets OverlapTriggerManager.Instance and, if that returns a manager, calls DisableOverlap with this component's own GameObject.

For recorded relationships where this GameObject is the trigger, the manager clears each current positive pair count by processing as many exits as the recorded count requires. It also checks relationships where this GameObject was another trigger's partner. Missing records do not create new exits. Cleanup concerns the GameObject's recorded relationships, so it can affect the other OverlapTrigger components on the same GameObject as well.

At the final count for a pair, the manager queues OnOverlapExit notifications with that pair's other GameObject. Pair counts are reduced and entries removed during cleanup, before those queued callbacks are dispatched by the manager. The call does not itself move an object out of the volume, and it does not directly call the exit callback.

For example, disabling a trigger with a crate recorded inside it ends the recorded crate relationship and queues an exit report naming the crate. The manager's queue dispatcher does not check the recipient component's enabled state before calling OnOverlapExit, so a disabled trigger can still receive that queued notification. Already queued enter or exit notifications are not cancelled by this cleanup.

Timing follows the manager's event-queue processing rather than a fixed number of frames. If Instance returns null, this method makes no cleanup call. It does not rebuild overlap records when the component is later enabled; subsequent overlap reports are needed to populate the manager again.

A finalizer is an automatic cleanup routine the runtime can call after an object is no longer reachable. Its timing is not tied to a particular game frame. This is not the operation that clears a disabled object’s overlaps or sends pending enter/exit notifications. Do not call it as a manual overlap reset: DisableOverlap performs pair cleanup, while normal updates deliver queued notifications.

remarks.para: The constructor registers this routine with Marrow’s normal update stage. It repeatedly removes the next queued record and calls the saved trigger’s OnOverlapEnter for an enter record or OnOverlapExit for an exit record, passing the saved other GameObject. A GameObject is the Unity object holding an object’s components.

The overlap counts and helper associations are updated when contacts are reported, before these routines are called. Dispatching a queued enter therefore does not mean the pair is still present now: an exit may already have been recorded behind it in the queue.

The loop continues until the queue is empty. An event added while a receiving routine is running can be processed in the same drain; the method does not promise a delay of exactly one frame. It does not check whether a recipient is enabled before invoking its routine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.Awake
member.summary: Captures the attached physics body’s original pose and mass, then applies its spin limit and rotational-inertia settings. Its active settings are the spin limit from and rotational-inertia multiplier from .

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. A kinematic body has its movement controlled by scripts instead of ordinary physics forces. The center of mass is the body’s balance point.

The saved position and rotation are relative to the object’s parent. The saved mass is the Rigidbody’s current mass in kilograms, before this component’s enable-time scale adjustment. A Rigidbody is required on the same object; this routine does not add one.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) writes max(maxAv, 60) to the body’s maximum angular velocity, in radians per second. Here maxAv is the requested spin limit in those units, and iTensorMult is the extra unitless inertia multiplier. If iTensorMult differs approximately from 1, it multiplies all three components of the current inertia tensor, which describes resistance to rotation. If disableITCalc is true and the body is not kinematic, it first reassigns the current inertia tensor and center of mass so they become explicit values.

These settings are applied during initialization. Changing the fields later does not automatically repeat Awake, and manually repeating it would recapture the current pose/mass and could multiply an already adjusted inertia tensor.

member.param: True to ignore the listed pairs; false to allow them to collide again under the other physics rules.

remarks.para: A collider is the shape physics uses to detect contact. For each collider in localColliders, this routine calls Physics.IgnoreCollision with every collider in collidersToIgnore. remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. A collider is the shape physics uses to detect contact.

It gathers colliders with GetComponentsInChildren and enables collision ignoring for the gathered pairs. This includes the root object and active descendants, not just colliders assigned to this Rigidbody; inactive child objects are not included in this search.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.OnEnable
member.summary: Stops the physics body whenever this component becomes enabled, with optional pose reset and scale-based mass adjustment.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

It looks up the Rigidbody on the same object if the cached reference is missing, and returns if none is found. With resetOnEnable enabled, it restores the saved parent-relative position/rotation, then copies the resulting world position/rotation to the Rigidbody. A moved or changed parent can therefore produce a different world reset pose.

With scaleMass enabled, it assigns _nativeMass × lossyScale.x × lossyScale.y × lossyScale.z. Here _nativeMass is the initially captured mass in kilograms, and the lossyScale components are the extra unitless multipliers for the object’s effective world scale, including its parents. For example, a saved mass of 2 kg and scale (2, 2, 2) request 16 kg. This uses the saved mass each time rather than repeatedly multiplying the current mass.

Regardless of both switches, a present Rigidbody has its linear and angular velocity set to zero. Disabling pose reset therefore does not preserve its previous motion. This routine does not reapply maxAv, iTensorMult or the center-of-mass override.

member.summary: Adds a random change in spin to the physics body.
member.param: Lower bound for the sampled angular-velocity change, in radians per second.
Upper bound for the sampled angular-velocity change, in radians per second.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. rb is the cached reference to that physics component.

This overload chooses a value between the two supplied bounds and a direction from a random rotation, then calls AddTorque with ForceMode.VelocityChange. The bounds describe the scalar angular-velocity change in radians per second. One radian is about 57.3 degrees. A negative sample reverses the chosen direction; its absolute value is the magnitude.

It adds to existing rotation rather than assigning a final angular velocity. For example, bounds of 2 and 2 request a change of 2 radians per second around a randomly chosen world direction. The physics simulation applies the accumulated change on its next step; constraints and spin limits can affect the resulting motion.

Both float overloads share this behavior. Despite the SetVelocity name, that float overload changes spin rather than linear travel. A cached Rigidbody is required; the helper does not look one up or safely skip a missing body. The Rigidbody’s GameObject, Unity’s object holding the components, must be active; this AddTorque call has no effect while that object is switched off.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.SetCenter
member.summary: Moves the body’s balance point to the position specified by .

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. rb is the cached reference to that physics component.

The center of mass is the point around which the object’s mass is balanced; moving it changes how the physics body balances and responds to rotation. This routine reads the override’s world position, converts it with the Rigidbody transform’s InverseTransformPoint, and assigns that result as centerOfMass. It does not simply copy the override’s own localPosition.

For example, with body scale 1, an override 10 cm below the body’s origin requests a center 10 cm below it. The conversion includes transform scale, while Unity’s centerOfMass property uses the body’s position and rotation without reflecting scale, so a scaled body may not place its physical center exactly at the override’s world point.

Missing rb or comOverride makes this a no-op. Start (the routine Unity calls for this component’s first startup) applies it once; moving the override later requires another call to update the body. The routine does not move the object itself.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. A drive applies push/pull force or turning force through that joint to move toward a target.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. A drive applies push/pull force or turning force through that joint to move toward a target.

This changes angularYZDrive, which rotates around contact Y and Z; it does not change sideways translation. The cap is in newton metres (N·m), the strength of a turning force, and limits the corrective torque rather than setting a tilt angle.

This updates every existing contact, not the saved SplineJoint configuration field. A later RefreshContactConfig reapplies the saved field and can replace this change. It does not create contacts or unlock restricted motion. The angular X/YZ drives act when the contact joint uses its X & YZ rotation-drive mode; this setter does not change that mode.

member.param: Per-contact drive cap in the units described above.

member.summary: Sets how strongly each contact’s tilt drive corrects angular-speed error.

remarks.para: The damping coefficient is newton metres of turning-force strength per radian-per-second speed error (N·m·s/rad). Torque means the strength of a turning force, measured in newton metres. A radian is an angle unit; one radian is about 57.3 degrees.

A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. A drive applies push/pull force or turning force through that joint to move toward a target.

This changes angularYZDrive, which controls rotation around contact Y and Z, rather than the linear Y/Z drives. Damping corrects desired minus current angular speed; its coefficient is in N·m·s/rad. The torque cap still limits the result.

This updates every existing contact, not the saved SplineJoint configuration field. A later RefreshContactConfig reapplies the saved field and can replace this change. It does not create contacts or unlock restricted motion. The angular X/YZ drives act when the contact joint uses its X & YZ rotation-drive mode; this setter does not change that mode.

member.param: Speed-error damping coefficient in the units described above.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.Solve
member.summary: Updates the contact targets and path-end restrictions along the path for the configured one-, two-, or four-contact layout.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body whose movement and rotation Unity physics simulates.
A Contact is a generated physics body joined to the main Rigidbody; the joint constrains how the two bodies can move relative to each other.

One finds the nearby path point for the body anchor and requests a contact position and orientation there. Its spring-target correction centres sideways tilt while following the current twist around the travel direction. Two calculates a front/back pair. Four adds side-to-side target offsets using _size.x, the configured full width in metres. Open path ends switch the corresponding contact’s travel motion from free to limited.

Normally Update calls this only while the main Rigidbody is not sleeping, but this routine itself has no sleep check. The contact pose update can skip changes smaller than about one millimetre, including a rotation-only change with no positional displacement.

In Two and Four, if the body’s configured travel axis points opposite the calculated path direction, the solver also directly repositions and turns the main Rigidbody at the rear path target. Existing contact indices must match the configured count, and the saved path index must be valid.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.Update
member.summary: Runs the path solver each Unity frame while the configured Rigidbody is not sleeping.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. Update is the routine Unity calls once per ordinary rendered frame while the component is enabled; it is separate from a fixed physics step, one step of movement and collision simulation.

Sleeping means Unity physics has temporarily stopped updating a resting body. When IsSleeping is true, this returns without calling Solve; it does not wake the body. Otherwise Solve updates the existing contact constraints. A valid Rigidbody reference is required.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.Awake
member.summary: Registers this tracker for collider lookup and records whether its body and entity references exist during Unity initialization.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback: a routine Unity calls when setting up a component. It adds this Tracker to the shared cache under its GameObject, the scene object containing it. A collider is an invisible physics shape. Zones later use an overlapping collider’s GameObject to find the tracker and identify its owning body and entity.

After registration, it sets hasBody from the stored Body reference and hasEntity from the stored Entity reference, using Unity’s check that the referenced object still exists. These are snapshots taken at this point. Validate or later field assignment can change the references without refreshing the two flags.
This routine does not assign owner bodies, fill in a missing collider, or resize the tracking shape. Validate performs that separate setup, using the body and entity its caller supplies.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.CanUpdateValues(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns whether two scalar values differ by more than 0.0001.

remarks.para: The test uses the absolute difference, so it treats an increase and a decrease equally. A difference equal to or below 0.0001 returns false. For example, original = 0 and updated = 0.0001 do not pass, while updated = 0.0002 does. The threshold has the same units as the two values; it is not a percentage or a time delay.

Tracker validation uses this comparison for scalar collider dimensions, such as radius and capsule height, to avoid rewriting nearly unchanged values. For those dimensions the values are local distances, conventionally in meters before the object’s Transform scale is applied. The helper only answers the comparison; it does not change a collider itself.

member.param: The current scalar value, in the same units as updated.
The proposed replacement scalar value.
member.returns: True when the absolute difference is strictly greater than 0.0001; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.OnDeactivate
member.summary: Calls the tracker’s registered disable-notification routines with its current collider.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine registered to perform or report an action. This method calls the entries in _onDisableActions from the end of the list toward the beginning, passing Collider as the sole argument to each. A collider is an invisible physics shape. The method does not itself disable that shape or its GameObject, and it does not automatically clear the list afterward.

The body’s normal tracker-disable helper calls this after a tracker GameObject changes from active to inactive. Entity despawn processing can also call it as a notification without this method changing the object’s active state. It is not a Unity OnDisable callback that automatically runs on every possible way of disabling a collider.

Zones register a routine when a tracker enters them. This notification lets an active zone process departure, reduce its body and entity overlap counts, and send exit notifications as those counts reach zero. A routine can unregister itself during the call; repeated OnDeactivate calls can notify routines that remain registered again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this tracker’s lookup entry and clears its registered disable routines during component destruction.

remarks.para: OnDestroy is a Unity lifecycle callback: a routine Unity calls when destroying the component. It first removes this Tracker from the shared cache entry for its GameObject. If the cache becomes empty, it clears the shared _cache reference. A later Cache access can create a fresh empty cache.

It then clears _onDisableActions. This destruction routine does not call those routines before clearing them; OnDeactivate is the separate notification operation. Any deactivation notification that happened earlier belongs to its own call path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.Validate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Builds or updates the tracker’s overlap-detection shape and assigns the supplied body, entity and tracking layer.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape. This setup routine stores body and entity, renames the tracker object using the body name and tracking category, and finds a collider on the tracker’s own GameObject. It reuses that collider if its type matches the chosen shape, or adds the required BoxCollider, SphereCollider or CapsuleCollider. An existing collider of another type is not removed by this routine.

The selected collider is set to be a trigger: it reports overlaps without acting as a solid obstacle. Its dimensions come from settings and the body’s saved bounds, which are a box containing the body’s solid shapes. The normal body setup creates this tracker as a child of the body with zero local position and no extra local rotation.

Bounds mode uses a BoxCollider and writes the body Bounds center and size directly. Those Bounds values include the body’s current per-axis scale but remain offsets and lengths along the body’s axes, rather than a box center translated to its world position. Box mode also uses body Bounds, dividing each center and size component by the tracker’s matching lossyScale component before storing them. The settings.size vector is not used by either box branch.

Sphere and Capsule modes use settings.center, dividing X, Y and Z by the tracker’s matching lossyScale factors to get the local collider center. These input center components are distances along the tracker’s axes. lossyScale is a unitless size factor on each axis including parent scaling: 1 means normal size and 2 means twice the size. A desired offset of 0.1 meters along an axis with scale 2 is therefore stored as a 0.05-meter local offset.

A Transform is the component that stores an object’s position, rotation and size. In the following formula, scaleX, scaleY and scaleZ are the X, Y and Z components of this tracker’s Transform.lossyScale. For Sphere and Capsule, the stored local radius is settings.radius times the largest of 1/scaleX, 1/scaleY and 1/scaleZ. Capsule height uses settings.height times that same factor, and settings.direction chooses its X, Y or Z length axis. Radius is the distance from the shape center to its side; capsule height is its total end-to-end length. With uniform scale 2, a radius input of 0.1 meters becomes a local radius of 0.05 meters. Different scale factors on different axes use the native largest-reciprocal rule; this is not a promise of an exact world-size shape under every uneven scale.

Dimension writes are skipped for differences at or below 0.0001 local distance units. Center and size vector comparisons use the difference between the vectors’ lengths, not the distance between their endpoints: two different vectors of equal length can therefore be considered unchanged. Scalar radius and height comparisons use their ordinary absolute difference.

The single tracking categories Entity, Being and Observer assign the matching EntityTracker, BeingTracker or ObserverTracker Unity layer. A layer is a numbered category used to filter physics interactions. Combined or other category values do not set a layer in this implementation. This routine does not activate the tracker from settings.isActive, and it does not refresh the hasBody or hasEntity snapshots made during Awake, Unity’s initialization routine.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physics movement. A capsule is a cylinder with rounded ends.

member.param: The shape type, tracking category, center, radius, capsule height and capsule direction used for setup.
The owning MarrowBody, which groups a Rigidbody and its shapes and supplies the body bounds.
The owning MarrowEntity, which groups the game object’s bodies and interaction state.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig.OnAwake
member.summary: Records the physics clock time when the rig is initialized.

remarks.para: RigManager calls this hook during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback: a routine called to perform initialization. It stores Time.fixedTimeAsDouble in _lastFixedTime. That clock is measured in seconds at physics-step times; the value is a time marker, not the length of one step.

OnUpdate later compares the physics clock with this marker to decide whether a newer animated skeleton needs to be copied into lastRig. This hook does not take a skeleton snapshot or fill the two BodyPose buffers.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig.OnEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Saves the previous tracked body pose, then captures the latest pose remapped to the avatar.

remarks.para: The order matters: it first copies _updateBodyPose into _lastUpdateBodyPose, then copies manager.remapHeptaRig.bodyPose into _updateBodyPose. A BodyPose is a group of body rotations, limb-extension values and other pose data. The remap rig supplies that data after adapting the tracked pose to the avatar’s proportions.

These are content copies into the existing buffers, including their timestamps, not swaps of the two references. Keep the buffers distinct and assigned. OnFixedUpdate later blends their contents at the physics step’s time; it computes its fraction from the controller rig’s timestamps rather than these buffers’ timestamp fields.

This is a callback, meaning a routine called to perform an update action. RigManager dispatches it in its early-update sequence for rigs registered in remapRigs. The normal manager sequence skips that rig dispatch while the controller rig is paused and in its Ragdoll body-state branch, the limp body state controlled by physics; calling the hook directly does not perform those manager checks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig.OnUpdate
member.summary: Refreshes the saved animated skeleton once the physics clock has advanced.

remarks.para: World positions are measured in metres. Time.fixedTimeAsDouble is the physics-clock time in seconds.

If Time.fixedTimeAsDouble is less than or equal to _lastFixedTime, it returns without copying the skeleton. Otherwise it places this component’s transform at animationRig.centerOfPressure’s world position and rotation, then copies the animation rig’s supported body transforms into lastRig.

The centerOfPressure reference, pelvis and both hands are copied in scene world position and rotation. The other supported torso, arm and leg transforms are copied by their local rotations, meaning relative to their parent transforms. After all those copies succeed, _lastFixedTime is updated to the current physics-clock time.

This callback is a routine called to perform the frame-update action through RigManager. It prepares a saved skeleton for later physics interpolation; it does not itself blend poses every rendered frame. lastRig, the animation rig and their required transforms must already be assigned. The normal manager stops its frame-update dispatch while the controller rig is paused.
A Transform stores an object’s position and rotation. Here centerOfPressure is the rig reference whose position and orientation anchor this body snapshot.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig.Reset
member.summary: Finds or creates the rig’s body-part child objects and assigns their transform references.

remarks.para: This override is the Unity reset callback, a routine called for the component’s reset action, and runs the base Rig.Reset operation. That operation looks for the expected skeleton children, creates missing objects in the rig hierarchy, and stores references for the supported body parts and centerOfPressure, the configured reference whose position and orientation anchor the rig. A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale.

It is a hierarchy-setup operation rather than a reset of _lastFixedTime or the saved BodyPose contents. Calling it does not replace lastRig with a newly captured prior pose. Existing matching children are reused instead of recreated.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.FlipSlot(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Selects the mirrored body-slot angles and the left or right forearm region for special slots.
member.param: Whether body weapon slots should be mirrored.
True selects the left forearm for ready special-item containers; false selects the right forearm.

remarks.para: The two choices are independent. For ready containers in bodySlots, flipped = true writes the negative of the angle cached by SlotContainer.Awake, Unity's initialization callback; false restores that cached angle. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The angle is degreesFromCenter, measured in degrees around the body. Only containers with flippable enabled change their angle. For example, an originally cached 90-degree angle becomes -90 when flipped and returns to 90 when restored; repeated true calls do not keep toggling it.

For ready containers in specialItems, specialItemsFlipped = true selects ArmLowerLf, the left forearm, and false selects ArmLowerRt, the right forearm. This branch changes bodyRegion and does not check the container's flippable flag. It selects those two regions even if the container was originally configured for another region.

This method changes slot placement settings. It does not itself move or rotate a scene object: PhysicsRig.SetBodySlot later processes the arrays and uses those settings to position their containers for an avatar. Supply valid arrays and entries, and initialize the containers before applying the choices. Containers whose ready flag is false are skipped; an empty array is allowed, but a null array or null entry is not treated as an empty group.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.RegisterSlot(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot)
member.summary: Adds a named to the lookup used for its insertion and removal callbacks.
member.param: Unique name identifier of the inventory slot.
The slot instance to register.

remarks.para: Creates the name-to-slot dictionary on the first call if it does not yet exist. If the name is already present, its existing slot is retained: registering a different slot with the same name does not replace it. For example, register a valid slot under the illustrative name "ToolHolster" before subscribing to that name.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.SubscribeToInsert(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.SlotDelegate)
member.summary: Adds a callback to the named slot's item insertion notification.
member.param: Name of the target slot.
Delegate invoked when an item is placed into the slot.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callback receives the InventorySlot that changed, rather than the item GameObject. A GameObject is an object in Unity's scene; read slot.itemGameObject to obtain the newly stored object. InventorySlot.Insert writes that reference first, then invokes insertion listeners synchronously, before Insert returns.

Register the name first. With an existing dictionary, an unknown name does nothing; it is not remembered for later registration. A missing dictionary or a name mapped to a null slot is not a safe no-op. Repeated subscriptions add repeated listener entries, so pair subscriptions with matching unsubscriptions when your listener is no longer needed.

If Insert replaces an existing item, it reports removal of the old item before writing the new reference and reporting insertion. That replacement path expects a removal listener to exist; an occupied slot without one can fail before storing the new item. Subscribing to insertion alone does not remove that native limitation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.SubscribeToRemove(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.SlotDelegate)
member.summary: Adds a callback that observes the named slot's old item when removal is reported.
member.param: Name of the target slot.
Delegate invoked when an item is removed from the slot.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. It receives the InventorySlot, rather than an item argument. Its itemGameObject still refers to the old item while the callback runs: InventorySlot.Remove reports removal first, then clears that reference. A GameObject is an object in Unity's scene. Read or save the old reference inside the callback if you need it afterward.

InventorySlot.Insert also reports removal when it replaces an existing item. That removal callback runs before the new reference is stored; afterward, insertion listeners observe the new item. These notifications run synchronously in the slot methods, rather than waiting for a later frame. Ordinary Remove does not report removal for a slot already considered empty.

Register the name first. If the dictionary exists but the name is unknown, this call does nothing and does not wait for future registration. A missing dictionary or a name mapped to a null slot is not a safe no-op. Repeated subscriptions add repeated listener entries; unsubscribe the matching callback when it is no longer needed.

Delegate previously registered for insertion events.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Pass the same delegate you subscribed, such as a saved listener routine for "ToolHolster". This removes a matching listener occurrence; repeated registrations of that delegate require matching removals if you want none left. It does not empty the holster or undo an item insertion.

The method looks up the slot currently registered under the name. If the dictionary exists and the name is absent, it does nothing. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.Remove
member.summary: Reports removal of a live recorded item, then clears this slot’s item reference.

remarks.para: When itemGameObject is a live Unity object and a removal callback is assigned, slotRemoveEvent runs first. It receives this InventorySlot, so listeners can read itemGameObject to inspect the old item before the field is cleared.

After notification returns, itemGameObject becomes null. With no live item or no listener, the notification is skipped and the field is still cleared. Calling Remove on an empty slot does not send another removal report.

This routine clears the record; it does not destroy the GameObject, move it, or disconnect a physical grab joint (a physics connection holding the hand to the object). Those actions belong to the systems using the slot. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.AddSubscription``1(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReference{``0})
member.summary: Queues a reference under its target ID for a later pass.
member.typeparam: The object type expected by the reference.
member.param: The reference to queue, with its UniqueId already set to the target object's ID text.

remarks.para: A late reference stores an object's ID so the object can be found after it becomes available. This method adds the reference to the waiting group for its UniqueId. The group is a set, so adding the same reference instance again under the same ID does not create a duplicate.

Adding a subscription does not look up the object, set ReferenceLinked, or invoke its linking event. A separate linking pass must run after the target has been indexed. For example, queue a reference for door-switch-01, load the table containing that ID, then run LinkSubscribedLateReferences.
The reference and its ID must be supplied. Changing UniqueId after adding it does not move the existing waiting entry to a different group.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.LinkSubscribedLateReferences
member.summary: Delivers indexed objects to waiting late references and removes each processed ID group from the subscription queue.

remarks.para: The pass takes a snapshot of the currently waiting ID strings, then checks the object cache for each ID. A missing ID stays queued for a later pass. A found ID causes every reference in that group to receive its LateReferenceDidLink callback with the cached object and the table recorded for that ID. A callback is a function called when another operation reaches this step.

For the built-in LateReference<T>, a compatible object is stored in Object first, ReferenceLinked becomes true second, and OnLateReferenceLinked runs last. That event receives the export table and the late-reference instance, so its second argument identifies the reference that linked.

After all callbacks in a found group return, the manager removes the entire group. This also happens when a typed reference rejected the cached object because it was the wrong type. Such a reference can remain unlinked while no longer waiting in the queue. For example, two references waiting for one ID share a group; finding that ID processes both and removes the group even if only one expects the cached object's type.

The group's queue entry still exists while its callbacks run. A callback failure or a missing table entry can stop the pass before that group is removed, after earlier callbacks have already changed their references. The pass uses stored cache entries; it does not perform a new scene search or a separate destroyed-object check.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.LoadTable(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.SceneExportTable)
member.summary: Indexes an existing scene export table's ID-to-object pairs so later queries and linking passes can find those objects.
member.param: The scene table whose Exports collection contains the ID strings and existing object references to index.

remarks.para: An export table is a list of IDs paired with objects. For each pair, the manager first records the table as the owner of that ID, then records ID-to-object and object-to-ID lookups. The table index is keyed by each exported object's ID, rather than the scene's name.

If an ID already has an indexed table, the method logs the duplicate and skips that pair's object-cache writes. The first indexed ID wins. For example, loading a second table with door-switch-01 does not replace the first table's object for that ID.

This call indexes objects that already exist. It does not load a Unity scene, create the objects, or run LinkSubscribedLateReferences. SceneExportTable calls it from Awake, Unity's initialization call. For manual setup, load the table before running a separate linking pass.

Use usable object references and nonblank IDs that are unique across the tables being indexed. A null object can fail while writing the reverse lookup after its ID and forward lookup were already added. The method does not roll back those earlier writes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.Register(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.ExportTable,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReference)

remarks.para: For each exported pair, the method removes the ID's table entry, the ID-to-object entry, and the object's reverse ID entry. It continues with the object-cache removals even if the table-index removal reported that the ID was absent. SceneExportTable calls this when its component is destroyed.

The method does not check that the indexed owner is the supplied table. If table A loaded an ID and table B's duplicate was rejected, unloading B can still remove A's entries for that ID. Keep exported IDs unique across loaded tables.

Cleanup reads the table's current pairs, rather than a saved copy from LoadTable. Changing Exports after loading changes which entries are removed and can leave earlier pairs cached. Unloading the table does not itself destroy its exported objects, clear already-linked references, or queue those references again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.VacuumLinks
member.summary: Purges scene-object lookup entries whose Unity object was destroyed or whose ID is blank, returning the number of distinct IDs collected when cleanup completes.
member.returns: The number of distinct ID strings collected from the forward object cache, excluding the number of reverse object keys removed. The method can throw during reverse cleanup before returning this count.

remarks.para: The first stage collects IDs whose cached object compares equal to Unity null, including destroyed objects, or whose ID is empty or contains only whitespace. It then removes those IDs from the table index and the ID-to-object cache. An ID meeting both conditions is counted once.

The second stage tries to remove destroyed-object keys from the object-to-ID cache. It removes keys while walking that dictionary's live key collection. Removing a key changes the dictionary's version, so the next iterator step can throw a collection-modified exception. Forward removals and the first reverse removal may already have happened when that exception occurs.

A live object whose ID was blank is not removed from the reverse cache by the destroyed-object test. This cleanup does not edit the original export tables, destroy objects, clear waiting subscriptions, or unlink references that already stored an object.

For example, if one destroyed object has two cached IDs, the first stage collects two IDs. Its intended return is 2, even though the reverse cache has only one key for that object; reverse cleanup can interrupt the method before it returns.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.CheckBulletArt
member.summary: Refreshes the two cartridge display models to match the magazine’s current round count.

remarks.para: The round count is the number of cartridge entries in magazineState, measured in whole rounds: zero requests both models hidden, one requests only the first shown, and two or more requests both shown. These models decorate the magazine opening; showing one does not add a usable round.

The method returns without changing the models when firstCartridgeTarget is missing or _isArtHidden is true. Missing cached cartridge objects are skipped. It does not create new models, and it does not check isMagazineInserted or ignoreSecondBulletSpawn directly.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.
For example, after initialization finishes, refreshing a magazine with one round shows the first model and hides the second. Refreshing with zero rounds hides both.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.Claim
member.summary: Marks this magazine as claimed so later grab handling skips its first-claim inventory work.

remarks.para: This sets _isMagazineClaimed to true. It does not transfer ammunition, change the magazine’s round list, or register it with an ammo receiver.

The grab handler separately registers an unclaimed magazine with a player ammo receiver when available and adds its configured capacity to the available ammo inventory when available. Capacity means magazineState.magazineData.rounds, in whole rounds, even if the magazine currently contains fewer rounds. Calling Claim() before grabbing suppresses those first-claim actions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.HideBulletArt
member.summary: Suppresses count-based display refreshes and requests the cartridge models hidden.

remarks.para: This sets _isArtHidden to true before hiding the cached first model. It also requests the cached second model hidden when secondCartridgeTarget, the second display marker, exists. Missing cached models are skipped.

While the flag is true, CheckBulletArt() does nothing. This method changes neither the stored ammunition nor isMagazineInserted. Newly finishing initialization can still activate a model without checking this flag.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.Initialize(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData,System.Int32)
member.summary: Starts setting the magazine’s ammunition and loading its cartridge display models.

remarks.para: This starts InitializeAsync and discards its task, the handle that can be awaited to know when loading has finished. The method can return while model spawning is still pending.

Use await magazine.InitializeAsync(cartridgeData, count) when the next operation needs the models to have finished loading. A magazine already marked initialized does not start a second initialization or replace its contents.

For an ordinary nonnegative capacity, a negative requested count becomes zero and a request above capacity becomes capacity. Capacity is the configured maximum number of rounds in magazineState.magazineData.rounds.

member.param: The ammunition settings whose cartridge model is loaded and whose entries fill the magazine.
Requested starting ammunition, in whole rounds; limited to zero through the configured magazine capacity for a nonnegative capacity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.InitializeAsync(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData,System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets the magazine’s starting ammunition and waits for its requested cartridge display models to finish loading.

remarks.para: The returned UniTask is an awaitable completion handle. Loading may pause this operation without stopping the game. If _isInitalized is already true, this call does nothing; it does not wait for a previous call that is still loading.

On first entry, the method sets _isInitalized before changing the ammunition or requesting models. It replaces the cartridge list with count copies of cartridgeData. With a nonnegative configured capacity, negative counts become zero and counts above capacity become capacity. Capacity is magazineState.magazineData.rounds, measured in whole rounds. The ammo-change callback, a function notified when the count changes, receives the resulting total before the new models are loaded.

The cartridge settings supply cartridgeSpawnable, the description of the cartridge model to load. It is registered before testing the display markers. A first model is requested only when firstCartridgeTarget exists. A second requires secondCartridgeTarget and ignoreSecondBulletSpawn false; it can be requested even if the first marker is missing. Missing markers can allow completion without a pause.

Each successful spawn is positioned and rotated to its marker’s world pose, meaning its location and facing in the whole scene, and packed into the magazine’s physical object group. The marker is read again after loading. The cartridge is marked as decorative art and its grip behavior is disabled when first converted to art; a player does not grab these display rounds as separate ammunition.

Each newly obtained model is stored and activated without rechecking the current round count or _isArtHidden. There is no final count refresh here. For example, after awaiting initialization with zero rounds, call CheckBulletArt() to request both models hidden, provided the first marker exists and refreshes are not suppressed. A loading failure does not clear the started flag, so that flag alone does not show that setup succeeded.

To patch this asynchronous behavior, use the state machine’s Magazine._InitializeAsync_d__22.MoveNext method. A state machine stores where a paused operation should continue. Its __1__state values are listed below.

item.description: First entry: marks initialization started, replaces the ammunition, notifies count listeners, and registers the cartridge model description. Starts the first model when its marker exists, or proceeds to the second-model check.

Continues after the first model spawn. Applies that model at the first marker’s current world pose, stores and activates it, then starts the second model if its marker exists and spawning it is allowed.
Continues after the second model spawn. Applies that model at the second marker’s current world pose, stores and activates it, then completes.
Done: the operation has completed or ended with an error.

member.param: The ammunition settings to store for each starting round and the source of the cartridge display model.
Requested starting ammunition, in whole rounds; limited to zero through the configured capacity for a nonnegative capacity.
member.returns: An awaitable task that finishes after the requested display models have been processed, or reports a setup/loading error. A call made after initialization has already started completes without joining the earlier operation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.IsClaimed

remarks.para: This returns _isMagazineClaimed as stored. It does not check which object is holding the magazine, whether it is inserted, or whether an inventory transfer actually succeeded.
Claiming can happen through Claim(), grab handling, or player-pouch magazine creation. Pool setup resets the flag.

member.returns: when the claimed flag is set; otherwise .

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.OnEject
member.summary: Allows count-based cartridge display updates again and immediately refreshes the models.

remarks.para: The ammo plug calls this when its exit finishes. It first sets isMagazineInserted to false, then calls this method. Calling OnEject() directly does not change that insertion flag or physically eject the magazine.

This method clears _isArtHidden and calls CheckBulletArt(). The round count is the number of cartridge entries in magazineState, measured in whole rounds: zero requests both models hidden, one requests only the first shown, and two or more requests both shown. These models decorate the magazine opening; showing one does not add a usable round.
A missing first display marker prevents the refresh. Visibility requests can finish later for models managed as physical object groups.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.OnInsert
member.summary: Suppresses cartridge display refreshes and requests the exposed cartridge models hidden after insertion finishes.

remarks.para: The ammo plug calls this at insertion completion, after setting isMagazineInserted to true. This method itself sets _isArtHidden and requests the first model hidden; it requests the second hidden only when the second display marker exists.

Calling this method directly does not move the magazine into a gun, set the insertion flag, or change ammunition. Missing model references are skipped. After this call, AmmoPlug checks the socket’s IsClearOnInsert predicate. The inspected AmmoSocket override returns true when its assigned Gun’s internalMagazine field is non-null. This field holds a MagazineData object for the Gun’s internal magazine. The predicate does not read the public Boolean despawnOnInsert field. When true, insertion completion clears the plug from the socket and calls DespawnOnJointBreak.OnJointBreak, which despawns the pooled magazine.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.OnPoolDeInitialize
member.summary: Removes magazine listeners and receiver tracking, clears cached display references, and resets initialization for reuse.

remarks.para: An object pool stores objects for later reuse. This cleanup removes the grab listener from grip when it exists, removes the ammo-count listener from magazineState, and removes this magazine from the cached ammo receiver’s active-magazine list when that receiver exists.

It then clears both cached cartridge-art references, runs the ammo plug’s despawn cleanup, and clears _isInitalized. The plug cleanup clears its socket relationship and internal insertion state and destroys its stored physics joint, the connection that constrains two physical objects.

Clearing a cartridge reference does not itself despawn that cartridge object. This magazine method contains no separate cartridge-art despawn call. It also leaves the hidden, claimed, inventory-cache and insertion fields for their later setup or plug-completion paths rather than explicitly resetting each one here.
The state object and ammo plug are required for this cleanup to finish; missing required setup can stop it before initialization is reset.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.OnPoolInitialize
member.summary: Connects grab and ammo-count listeners, refills the magazine, and resets its per-spawn tracking flags.

remarks.para: An object pool keeps objects ready to be reused. Setup subscribes the grab handler to grip when present and the visual-refresh handler to magazineState’s count callback, a function notified when ammunition changes.

It refills the cartridge list to magazineState.magazineData.rounds, the configured capacity in whole rounds, using the state’s current cartridge settings. Refill notifies listeners with the resulting count before the reset below.
It then clears isMagazineInserted, _isArtHidden, _isMagazineClaimed, _lastAmmoInventory, and _lastAmmoInventoryReceiver. Resetting a visibility flag does not perform a second visual refresh.

When its pooled-object record says it is outside the pool and cartridge settings exist, it starts InitializeAsync with those settings and configured capacity without waiting for visual loading to finish. It does not clear _isInitalized here; normal pool cleanup clears that flag first.
The magazine state, capacity settings and pooled-object record must be configured. The ammo plug and interaction host are needed by their cleanup and art-attachment paths.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.ShowBulletArt
