remarks.para: This clears _isArtHidden and calls CheckBulletArt(); it does not show both models unconditionally. The round count is the number of cartridge entries in magazineState, measured in whole rounds: zero requests both models hidden, one requests only the first shown, and two or more requests both shown. These models decorate the magazine opening; showing one does not add a usable round.
The refresh requires a first display marker, and missing cached models are skipped. The method does not spawn missing art or clear isMagazineInserted.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.AddCartridge(System.Int32,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData)
member.summary: Appends rounds of the requested ammunition type, stopping at the magazine’s configured capacity.

remarks.para: Capacity means magazineData.rounds, a whole number of rounds. With a nonnegative capacity, this adds at most the space between the current list count and that capacity. Existing rounds keep their ammunition types and order. A zero or negative count does not remove rounds, and this method does not trim a list that is already over capacity.

Each new entry refers to cart, the shared data asset describing that ammunition type. If cart is null or Unity treats its object as destroyed, each new entry instead uses the current cartridgeData default. This does not change cartridgeData or make separate copies of either asset.

After adding entries, this calls onAmmoChange once if a callback is assigned. A callback is a function registered to receive a notification; here it receives the actual whole-number list count. This call happens immediately, after the additions, even if the magazine was full or count was zero or negative. It does not wait for a later frame.

For example, a six-round magazine containing three type-A rounds can receive AddCartridge(2, typeB). It then contains three A entries followed by two B entries, and PullCartridge takes a B entry first. Use a configured magazineData asset and a non-null backing list.

member.param: Requested number of rounds to append, as a whole-number count. Available capacity limits positive requests; zero or negative requests add nothing.
Ammunition-type data for the new entries. A null or destroyed Unity object selects the current cartridgeData default instead.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.ClearMagazine
member.summary: Removes every loaded entry, resetting to zero.

remarks.para: Clears the existing list in place, so references to that same list see it become empty. The magazineData configuration and cartridgeData default are retained.

This method does not call onAmmoChange, the optional function for count notifications. A listener that refreshes visuals from that callback will not receive a notification from this clear operation. GetCartridgeData can still return the configured default afterward, although no rounds remain.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.GetCartridgeData
member.summary: Returns the last loaded ammunition-type entry without removing it, or the configured default when the magazine is empty.

remarks.para: The last entry is the one PullCartridge will remove next. For mixed ammunition, this is the most recently appended type that has not yet been removed.

An empty list returns cartridgeData, the shared default ammunition definition, rather than evidence that a round is available. For example, after ClearMagazine, this can return type A while AmmoCount is zero. A null last entry or null default produces null; the method does not skip a null last entry to find another round.
Reading the entry leaves the list unchanged and does not call onAmmoChange, the optional count-notification function.

member.returns: The last loaded CartridgeData reference, or the current cartridgeData default when the list is empty. Either can be null.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.Initialize(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData,System.Int32)
member.summary: Replaces the loaded rounds with the requested ammunition type and starting count, and stores that type as the default for later fills.

remarks.para: Assign magazineData before calling this method. Its rounds field is the capacity, measured as a whole number of rounds; use a nonnegative capacity. The requested ammoCount is limited to zero through that capacity. The method stores catridgeData in cartridgeData, clears the existing list in place, then adds that same shared asset reference once for every starting round.
For example, with a six-round capacity, Initialize(typeA, 9) loads six type-A entries. Initialize(typeA, -2) loads none but still stores type A as the default. Existing mixed ammunition is discarded.

When rebuilding finishes, this immediately calls onAmmoChange once if assigned, passing the actual list count, even when that count is zero or unchanged. A callback is a registered notification function; it sees the rebuilt list before this method returns.
A null ammunition asset is not rejected: its null entries still count toward AmmoCount. Supply valid ammunition data if later code needs to use its projectile or round assets.

member.param: Shared definition of the ammunition type to store as the default and place in every new list entry. This parameter name is spelled catridgeData in the API.
Requested starting count in whole rounds, limited to zero through magazineData.rounds for a nonnegative capacity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.PullCartridge
member.summary: Removes and returns the last loaded ammunition-type entry, reducing by one when an entry exists.

remarks.para: The list works like a stack: rounds appended last are taken first. For example, adding two type-B entries after three type-A entries makes the next two pulls return B, then the next pull return A. This removes stored ammunition data; a gun handles its chamber separately.

A successful removal does not call onAmmoChange, the optional count-notification function. On an empty-list call, it instead calls that function with zero if assigned, then returns null. That notification happens immediately before the empty call returns.

A stored null entry is also removed and returned as null, while the list count still falls by one. Therefore a null return alone cannot tell whether an entry was removed; compare the count if that distinction matters. The empty case does not return the cartridgeData default.

member.returns: The removed CartridgeData reference, or null if the list was empty. A removed null entry also returns null.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.Refill
member.summary: Replaces all loaded rounds with the current default ammunition type up to the configured capacity.

remarks.para: Clears the existing list in place, then fills it with repeated references to cartridgeData, the shared default ammunition definition. Capacity is magazineData.rounds, measured as a whole number of rounds. A capacity of zero or less leaves the list empty; use a nonnegative capacity for normal magazine setup.

This rebuilds the whole load rather than preserving mixed ammunition. For example, if a six-round magazine contains some type-B rounds but cartridgeData is type A, Refill replaces the load with six A entries. Changing cartridgeData alone does not replace rounds already loaded.

After the rebuild, this immediately calls onAmmoChange once if assigned, passing the actual count even if the magazine already had that many rounds. A callback is a registered notification function; listeners see the completed rebuild.

Assign magazineData before calling. The list is cleared before this method checks that configuration, so a missing configuration can cause a failure after the old rounds have already been removed. This state operation does not check or subtract an inventory reserve.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.SetCartridge(System.Int32)
member.summary: Adjusts the loaded round count, appending default-type rounds or removing the last entries as needed.

remarks.para: With a nonnegative capacity, the target is limited to zero through magazineData.rounds, the configured whole-number round capacity. Growing the list appends references to cartridgeData, the current default ammunition definition. Shrinking it removes entries from the end, preserving the types and order of the entries that remain.

If the requested count already equals the current list count, the method returns immediately: it does not check capacity or call onAmmoChange. Otherwise it adjusts the list and immediately calls that optional notification function once with the actual count, even if limiting the request leaves the count unchanged.

For example, in a full six-round magazine, SetCartridge(6) sends no notification, but SetCartridge(99) keeps six rounds and sends a notification with six. If the capacity was changed below the current count, requesting that unchanged current count also leaves the over-capacity list alone.
Use a configured magazineData asset and a non-null backing list. This changes the number of entries without making every existing entry match the current default type.

member.param: Desired loaded count in whole rounds. A request equal to the current count returns immediately; other requests are limited by zero and the configured nonnegative capacity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.CheckVersionCompatibility(Il2CppSystem.Version)
member.summary: Checks whether the supplied SDK version falls between this runtime’s minimum and current versions, comparing only major and minor numbers.

remarks.para: A version such as 1.2.7 has major number 1, minor number 2, and patch number 7. The check compares major numbers first, then minor numbers if the major numbers match. It ignores patch and revision numbers. Both ends of the range are included.

With the default cached versions in this build, the range is 0.6 through 1.2. For example, 0.6.0 and 1.2.99 pass, while 0.5.99 and 1.3.0 fail. A version newer than the runtime can therefore fail this check. This reports the version rule; it does not load content or test whether every asset works.

The minimum and current versions are cached parsed Version objects, meaning objects that store the numbered parts separately. Empty caches are filled from 0.6.0 and 1.2.0 when needed. A null otherVersion cannot be compared and causes an exception.

member.param: Numbered version object to compare; must not be null.
member.returns: True when the major/minor version is at or above the cached minimum and at or below the cached current SDK version; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.CheckVersionCompatibility(System.String)
member.summary: Parses version text and checks its major and minor numbers against this runtime’s supported range.

remarks.para: Use numeric version text such as 1.2.0. Major is the first number, minor the second, and patch the third. The check includes both ends of the minimum-to-current range and ignores patch and revision numbers. The default range in this build is 0.6 through 1.2.

For example, 1.2.99 returns true, 1.3.0 returns false, and text such as hello cannot be parsed and returns null. Null means the method could not produce a yes-or-no compatibility result; it is different from false, which means a parsed version failed the range check. The overload catches an exception from parsing or checking and returns that empty result.
The return type is a nullable Boolean: a true/false value that can also be absent. No content is loaded by this check.

member.param: Version text to parse and compare.
member.returns: True for an included major/minor version, false for a parsed version outside the range, or null when parsing or checking fails.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.PrecachePaths
member.summary: Computes and stores all four mod-related paths during Unity’s runtime startup.

remarks.para: Unity runs this method automatically during subsystem registration, an early startup step that prepares runtime systems. It combines Application.persistentDataPath, the game’s folder for saved data that remains between runs, with Mods, ModsStaging, com.unity.addressables, and settings_mods.json.

The results replace the cached runtime-mods directory path, staging directory path, asset-cache directory path, and mod-settings file path. For example, if the persistent-data folder were /GameData, the runtime-mods path would be /GameData/Mods. Use the platform’s normal path separator when forming a real path.

Caching means saving the computed strings for later calls. This method computes paths without creating directories or reading the settings file. The RuntimeModsPath and InstallStagingPath getters separately create their directories if missing when read.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.SanitizeID(System.String)
member.summary: Removes every character except ASCII letters, digits, and periods from an identifier.

remarks.para: ASCII letters here mean A through Z and a through z; digits mean 0 through 9. Case and periods are preserved. Spaces, underscores, hyphens, slashes, and letters outside that set are deleted rather than replaced.

For example, My Mod_2! becomes MyMod2, while Maker.Item stays Maker.Item. A null or empty input is returned unchanged. An input containing only removed characters can become empty. Cleanup does not check uniqueness or all the separate rules for a valid content identifier.

member.param: Identifier text to clean; null and empty text are returned unchanged.
member.returns: The input with everything except ASCII letters, digits, and periods deleted, or the original null or empty input.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.SanitizeName(System.String)
member.summary: Deletes filename-invalid characters, square brackets, and hyphens from a name.

remarks.para: On the first call, the method asks the platform for its invalid filename characters, adds [, ], and -, and saves that character list for later calls. It splits the name at any listed character and joins the remaining pieces with no separator, so removal does not insert spaces or underscores.

For example, Puzzle-[Pack] becomes PuzzlePack. Characters absent from the list keep their case and spacing. Which other characters are removed depends on the platform’s filename rules. This returns cleaned text rather than creating a file or renaming an existing object.

An empty string stays empty, and a name containing only removed characters can become empty. Null is not accepted. This cleanup does not check path length, reserved filenames, or whether the cleaned name is unique.

member.param: Name to clean; must not be null.
member.returns: The name with all listed characters deleted. The result can be empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectStoreMarrowExtensions.WithMarrowDefaults(Il2CppSLZ.Serialize.ObjectStore.ObjectStoreBuilder)
member.summary: Returns an object-store builder configured to recognize Marrow’s built-in types and older saved type names.
member.param: The builder configuration to copy and configure before creating the object store. Its earlier built-in-type and type-rename collections are replaced by the Marrow defaults.
member.returns: The builder value carrying the Marrow type identifiers and rename mappings. Use this returned value when calling Build.

remarks.para: An object store converts supported objects to saved data and resolves their references when reading that data. A type is the kind of object, such as an AvatarCrate. The builder collects the settings used to create the store; this method configures those settings rather than creating the store immediately.

The defaults register 16 built-in types, including Crate, AvatarCrate, SpawnableCrate, LevelCrate, Pallet, and mod-listing types. They pair each type with a stable text identifier and supply mappings from older saved type names to those identifiers. For example, a registered older Crate type name can resolve through the identifier "crate#0" to the current Crate type. These identifiers are text labels, not measurements or objects spawned into the level.

The method replaces the builder’s previous built-in-type and rename collections; it does not merge them with earlier custom entries. Its other settings, including the saved-data document, remain in the returned builder. Apply custom replacements afterwards if needed. Calling it on a builder does not update an object store that was already built.
Keep the returned builder value, then build the store from it. For example:
This prepares saved-data type recognition. It does not load an avatar asset, spawn gameplay objects, or convert every possible old data format.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.#ctor
member.summary: Creates an OpenController with each saved finger curl starting at 0.2.

remarks.para: A finger curl is a unitless bend amount: 0 means open and 1 means fully curled. The constructor initializes all five finger values to 0.2; later input updates replace them.
The controller still needs its left/right handedness, controller rig, and game input sources to be set up before the normal update methods can use them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.CacheInputs
member.summary: Copies this hand’s controller input into the saved button and axis values that the getters return.

remarks.para: It selects the game input source for the configured left or right hand. If game input is not initialized, the handedness is neither left nor right, or that hand has no controller source, it returns without replacing the saved inputs. This is a copy of the input source’s current values, rather than a fresh device poll for each getter.

Index controllers and Vive Wands copy the source trigger amount and button flags directly. Oculus Touch, Windows MR, Touch Pro, Undefined, and other controller-type values use triggerAmount = clamp(1.3 × rawTrigger - 0.1, 0, 1). rawTrigger is the unitless source trigger pull, triggerAmount is the saved pull, and clamp limits the result to 0–1. For those types the saved button turns on only above 0.55 while previously off, and stays on only above 0.5 while previously on. This gap avoids flickering near one cutoff.

Vive Wands clear the A-button flags and map the source A-button flags into B/menu. They also leave the saved touchpad axis unchanged, although touchpad click flags are copied. Thumbstick touch is true if its source reports touch or the stick is moved more than 0.5 from its center; exactly 0.5 does not satisfy that movement test.
Button amounts and stick/pad coordinates are unitless input values. Grip force is copied here, then SolveGrip turns that saved value into the gameplay squeeze strength.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.CheckMenuTap
member.summary: Records a short B/menu press as a tap when menu-tap detection is enabled.

remarks.para: The controller rig must exist. When its IsMenuTapDisabled flag is false, a B-button down flag saves the current unscaled time: seconds that continue independently of the game’s slow-motion time scale. A B-button up flag sets the tap result to whether the elapsed time is strictly less than 0.2 seconds. A press lasting exactly 0.2 seconds fails this test.

An enabled check without a B release clears an earlier true tap. While IsMenuTapDisabled is true, this method leaves both the timer and tap result unchanged, so clearing is not guaranteed on the next rendered frame. OnUpdate performs the same check after refreshing input.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.ClearHasBeenGrabbed
member.summary: Resets the saved recent-grab time to zero.

remarks.para: HasBeenGrabbed checks whether current unscaled time minus this saved time is less than 0.1 seconds. Unscaled time is seconds since the game started, independent of slow motion. Resetting the timestamp does not clear the separate grab/release flags or the latch that remembers whether a grab is active.

Because the timestamp becomes zero, the recent-grab check can still be true during the first 0.1 seconds of unscaled game time. After that initial interval, resetting it makes that check false until another grab is recorded.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.GetGesturePose(System.Single@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a cached selected from finger bends and hand direction.
member.param: Receives the saved unitless positional weighting for the pose; it is not a confidence score.
True to bypass the 0.2-second gesture cache deadline and re-evaluate using the saved curls and current transforms.
member.returns: The selected or previously retained gesture pose.

remarks.para: A curl above 0.5 counts as curled; 0.5 or below counts as open. The curls are unitless bend amounts, normally 0–1. All five open selects OpenHand; only the thumb open with the four fingers curled selects ThumbsUp. An open index with curled middle/ring/pinky selects IndexPoint regardless of the thumb. A curled thumb/index/ring/pinky with open middle selects MiddleFinger. A curled thumb/ring/pinky with open index/middle selects PeaceSign. All five curled selects Fist. An unmatched combination leaves the previous pose selected.

For the thumbs-up pattern, the controller’s upward direction is compared with Unity world up. If it points sideways or downward relative to world up, the selected pose becomes ThumbsDown. This test concerns controller orientation, rather than the thumb’s world position.
When recalculating a pose, the method reads m_head from the assigned controller rig for its world-space comparisons. The rig and head must be available for recalculation.

poseIntensity is a unitless position-based weighting, not a recognition confidence score. For OpenHand, IndexPoint, MiddleFinger, PeaceSign, and the thumbs-up pattern, the distance from the rig head to the controller maps 0.2–0.5 Unity world units to a 0–1 factor. Head-forward alignment maps 0.7–0.95 to another 0–1 factor, and the two factors are multiplied. Alignment is the dot product of the unit-length head-to-hand direction and the head’s forward direction: 1 means the same direction, 0 means sideways, and -1 means opposite. Each remap is limited to its output endpoints. Fist reverses both factors to 1–0. The native function does not apply a separate distance-unit conversion.

For a left- or right-hand controller, OpenHand and Fist also multiply an orientation factor from world up dotted with the rig hand’s sideways axis, reversed for the right hand. The native remap uses literal input bounds 170–80 on this unit-vector dot product; these bounds are not degrees. A dot product in -1–1 lies outside that range, so the factor clamps to 1 for OpenHand and 0 for Fist instead of varying continuously with orientation. The value can be zero even when a pose is selected, and a cached ThumbsDown result can retain the previous intensity.

Unless forceUpdate is true, calls before the saved deadline return the previous pose and intensity. Recalculation sets the next deadline 0.2 unscaled seconds later; unscaled time is independent of slow motion. Recalculation reads already processed curls and scene transforms, so forceUpdate does not itself refresh the physical controller input.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.GetGripForce
member.summary: Returns the processed squeeze strength used by gameplay.
member.returns: The saved unitless gameplay squeeze strength, normally from 0 to 1.

remarks.para: This is a unitless input strength, rather than a force measured in newtons. CacheInputs first copies source grip force, but SolveGrip then replaces it with a controller-specific value.

For Index, the processed strength is clamp((rawForce - 0.01) × 1.4, 0, 1). rawForce is the unitless source squeeze pressure, and clamp limits the result to 0–1. The default and Windows MR paths blend the real or simulated middle-finger curl with its product with trigger pull: strength = 0.5 × middleCurl + 0.5 × triggerPull × middleCurl. Vive Wands use their simulated grip curl and trigger-button state in a separate blend. These processed strengths can differ from the combined solved-grip amount.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.GetGripVelocity
member.summary: Returns how quickly the combined squeeze amount changed during the last update.
member.returns: The saved change in solved grip per unscaled second.

remarks.para: It is calculated as (newGrip - previousGrip) / deltaTime. newGrip and previousGrip are unitless combined squeeze amounts from 0 to 1; deltaTime is the elapsed unscaled update time in seconds, independent of slow motion. The result is squeeze units per second, not hand movement in metres per second.

Positive values mean closing; negative values mean opening. For example, moving from 0.2 to 0.6 over 0.02 seconds gives 20 squeeze units per second. OnUpdate uses this rate to shift the release cutoff.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.GetIndexCurlAxis
member.summary: Returns the processed bend amount of the index finger.
member.returns: The saved unitless index curl, normally from 0 to 1.

remarks.para: The usual scale is unitless: 0 is open and 1 is fully curled. These are processed input values for finger poses and grip/gesture calculations, rather than joint angles in degrees.

Depending on the controller type, this comes from the saved trigger pull, trigger touch, or tracked index curl combined with trigger pull. Hand tracking adds four times the saved trigger amount before limiting the curl to 0–1, then adjusts it using the middle finger.
ProcessFingers refreshes this value during OnUpdate. GetGesturePose reads the saved curls; calling this getter does not refresh tracking or bend a finger by itself.

member.summary: Returns whether the latest combined squeeze amount passes the speed-dependent release test.
member.returns: True if the saved solved grip is below the current release cutoff; otherwise false.

remarks.para: The release test uses solved grip, a unitless squeeze amount from 0 (open) to 1 (fully closed), and grip velocity, its change per second. The cutoff is 0.5 + clamp(-0.02 × gripVelocity, -0.4, 0.4). Here 0.02 is a response time in seconds, and clamp keeps its result between the two stated limits. A faster opening movement raises the cutoff; a faster closing movement lowers it. The grip must be strictly below the cutoff.
This test can be true even when no grab was active. IsReleased is the separate one-update flag that requires a previous grab. The input test does not prove that an object has been dropped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.HasBeenGrabbed
member.summary: Returns whether the saved grab timestamp is less than 0.1 unscaled seconds old.
member.returns: True if the timestamp difference is strictly below 0.1 seconds.

remarks.para: Unscaled time is seconds since the game started, independent of slow motion. The check is currentTime - savedGrabTime < 0.1, where both times are in unscaled seconds. Exactly 0.1 seconds does not count. This is a brief recent-input window rather than a test for holding an object.

OnUpdate records the timestamp when a new grab starts, and resets it to zero when a latched grab is released. ClearHasBeenGrabbed also writes zero. There is no separate check for a nonzero timestamp, so the result can be true in the first 0.1 seconds even before a grab.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.IsGrabbed

remarks.para: OnUpdate sets this flag when the unitless solved grip is strictly greater than 0.99 and the controller has not already latched a grab. It then records the unscaled grab time and sets the latch. Unscaled time is seconds independent of slow motion.

The flag is recomputed on the next OnUpdate. Calling this getter does not consume it, so several reads in the same update can all return true. Another grab requires the release test to clear the latch first. This input flag does not confirm that an object was successfully grabbed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.IsReleased
member.summary: Returns the saved flag for releasing a previously latched grab during the latest update.
member.returns: True if the latest update released a latched grab; otherwise false.

remarks.para: The release test uses solved grip, a unitless squeeze amount from 0 (open) to 1 (fully closed), and grip velocity, its change per second. The cutoff is 0.5 + clamp(-0.02 × gripVelocity, -0.4, 0.4). Here 0.02 is a response time in seconds, and clamp keeps its result between the two stated limits. A faster opening movement raises the cutoff; a faster closing movement lowers it. The grip must be strictly below the cutoff.

OnUpdate sets this flag only when that test passes while the grab latch is set. It then resets the recent-grab time and clears the latch. The next update recomputes the flag; reading it repeatedly does not consume it.
This describes releasing grab input. It does not confirm that an object has completed a drop or detach operation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.OnUpdate
member.summary: Refreshes saved inputs, processes finger bends, and updates the grab, release, and menu-tap flags.

remarks.para: The order is CacheInputs, ProcessFingers, SolveGrip, the menu-tap check, then grab/release tests. This is an overridable game method named OnUpdate; Unity’s automatic frame callback is Update. A callback is a method another system invokes at a particular step, so this method does its work only when the game calls it.

Finger processing creates unitless curls, normally 0 open to 1 fully bent. SolveGrip produces the combined squeeze amount and its change per unscaled second, independent of slow motion. A squeeze strictly above 0.99 starts a grab only when the grab latch is clear; it records the time and then sets that latch.

The release test uses solved grip, a unitless squeeze amount from 0 (open) to 1 (fully closed), and grip velocity, its change per second. The cutoff is 0.5 + clamp(-0.02 × gripVelocity, -0.4, 0.4). Here 0.02 is a response time in seconds, and clamp keeps its result between the two stated limits. A faster opening movement raises the cutoff; a faster closing movement lowers it. The grip must be strictly below the cutoff.

A release while latched resets the saved grab time and then clears the latch. The one-update flags are recomputed here, but getters do not consume them. The controller rig must be assigned for the normal menu-tap and grab/release update work; a missing rig reaches the method's failure path. The stored _runUpdates Boolean is not checked by this method.
This update does not run GetGesturePose. Gesture classification occurs when that method is requested, subject to its own cache deadline.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.ProcessFingers
member.summary: Selects a controller-specific method for updating saved finger bends and thumb touch.

remarks.para: It requires initialized game input and a left/right controller source. Finger bends are unitless curls, normally 0 open to 1 fully bent; these values later feed grip and gesture calculations.

Index uses the matching tracked hand when it exists, reports tracking, and _noFingies is false. Otherwise it falls back to controller-based estimates. The other controller types do not use this hand-tracking branch.

Vive Wands and Windows MR use the saved trigger for the index finger. Their grip-button input drives the other three fingers toward 0 or 1 at up to 20 curl units per unscaled second. Unscaled time passes independently of slow motion. Other types use trigger/touch and analog-grip estimates.

The thumb is simulated from controller-specific touch inputs and moves toward open/closed at up to 25 curl units per unscaled second. Turning off the tracked-hand branch does not turn off these simulated finger updates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.ProcessHandTrackedFingers(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand)
member.summary: Combines tracked finger bends with trigger and touch input to update the saved finger curls.
member.param: The game input source supplying this hand’s trigger and touch states. Required on branches that read its touch sensors.
The tracked hand source supplying finger curls. A missing or untracked hand leaves the saved curls unchanged.

remarks.para: It returns without updating if hand is missing or does not report tracking. The normal dispatcher uses this path for Index controllers. XR here is the game’s device-input data: controller supplies trigger/touch values and hand supplies tracked finger curl amounts.

Let T be the saved unitless trigger amount and I, M, R, and P be the hand’s unitless index, middle, ring, and pinky curls. First, I = clamp(handIndex + 4 × T, 0, 1); M, R, and P start at the matching tracked curls. The method then raises neighboring-finger minimums in sequence: I = max(I, (M - 0.8) × 0.5); M = max(M, (clamp(I - 0.9, 0, 1) + clamp(R - 0.9, 0, 1)) × 0.5); R = max(R, (clamp(M - 0.6, 0, 1) + clamp(P - 0.6, 0, 1)) × 0.5); P = max(P, (R - 0.7) × 0.5). Each resulting curl is capped at 1. The 4, 0.5, and other constants scale unitless curl amounts; they are not angles or distances.

The thumb is simulated from thumbstick, A/B, or touchpad touch, rather than copied from the tracked thumb curl. It moves toward 1 when touched and toward 0 otherwise, at up to 25 unitless curl units per unscaled second; unscaled time is independent of slow motion.
This method updates curl values for grip and gesture calculations. It does not copy tracked joint positions or rotations onto a hand skeleton.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.ProcessNonHandTrackedFingers(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController)
member.summary: Estimates finger bends from controller trigger, grip, and touch input.
member.param: The required game input source supplying trigger touch, grip amount, and A/B touch states.

remarks.para: The controller source must exist. A trigger-touch report moves an extra index bend toward 0.3 at up to 10 curl units per unscaled second; without touch it moves toward 0. The saved index curl is the trigger pull plus that extra bend, limited to 0–1.

Middle, ring, and pinky all receive clamp(1.3 × rawGrip - 0.1, 0, 1). rawGrip is the source’s unitless grip amount, and clamp limits the result to 0–1. For example, rawGrip 0.5 gives each of these three fingers a curl of 0.55.

The thumb-touch flag combines source A/B touch with inferred thumbstick touch. It moves thumb curl toward 1 or 0 at up to 25 curl units per unscaled second. A curl is a unitless bend amount, with 0 open and 1 fully curled; unscaled seconds pass independently of slow motion. These estimates update saved values for grip/gesture calculations rather than reading real finger joint angles.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.SolveGrip
member.summary: Combines the saved input into a gameplay squeeze amount, squeeze strength, and rate of change.

remarks.para: The solved grip is a unitless 0–1 amount used by grab/release tests. For the default path, solvedGrip = clamp(T + M, 0, 1), where T is saved trigger pull and M is processed middle-finger curl. Its processed grip strength is 0.5 × M + 0.5 × T × M. For example, T = 0.6 and M = 0.5 give solvedGrip = 1 and strength = 0.4. Windows MR substitutes its simulated grip curl H for M in both formulas. Vive Wands use solvedGrip = clamp(T + V, 0, 1), where V is their simulated grip curl; their processed strength is clamp(0.5 × V + 0.5 × V × Q, 0, 1), where Q is 0.2 while the trigger button is held and T - 0.2 otherwise.

For Index controllers, first calculate processed pressure P = clamp((sourceGripForce - 0.01) × 1.4, 0, 1). Let I, M, R, and K be the four processed finger curls, with K meaning pinky, and let U = min(I, M, R, K). Then solvedGrip = clamp(((0.5 × thumbCurl + I + M + R + K - U) × 0.33333) + 10 × P + 2 × T, 0, 1). The 0.5 thumb factor, one-third finger blend, 10 pressure multiplier, and 2 trigger multiplier operate on unitless amounts; P is also the saved processed grip strength for this type. Subtracting U keeps the least-curled finger from contributing to this part of the squeeze calculation.

It also replaces the saved grip-force value with a processed unitless strength. This is not a force in newtons. Finally, gripVelocity = (newGrip - previousGrip) / deltaTime, where the grip values are unitless squeeze amounts and deltaTime is elapsed unscaled update time in seconds. Positive velocity means closing; negative means opening. OnUpdate uses both solved grip and this rate to decide grab/release input states.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.AssignTrackingPucks
member.summary: Copies available body-tracking bone poses into the configured tracker transforms, then captures their alignment to the rig.

remarks.para: This implementation uses MarrowGame’s XRBody data, not a search for SteamVR puck names or serial numbers. It returns without assignment when that body device is absent, disconnected, or lacks body-tracking permission. The tracker transforms must already be assigned; the method does not create them.

For configured tracked chest, pelvis, shoulder and elbow points, it copies the corresponding bone-array position and rotation into the tracker’s local pose, meaning relative to its parent. Positions are tracking-space distances, normally metres before parent scaling; rotations are quaternions, four numbers describing orientation. The selected array entries must exist.

After those copies it calls CaptureTrackedOffsets, which aligns calibration children with the current rig. That helper also handles configured feet and knees, but this assignment method does not itself fill the foot or knee trackers from the bone arrays. Call it with the rig and tracker hierarchy in the calibration pose you intend to capture.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.CaptureTrackedOffsets
member.summary: Aligns the first child of each configured tracker with the corresponding body point in the rig.

remarks.para: For chest and pelvis it places the tracker’s first child at the current rig point expressed in the tracker’s local coordinates, and assigns the method’s fixed orientation correction. Feet and knees also capture position relative to their tracker, with a rotation correction derived from the relevant rig segment. Shoulder children capture the current rig shoulder position in their tracker’s local coordinates; elbow children use zero local position. Both receive fixed orientation corrections. A quaternion is four numbers describing an orientation.

This is a setup snapshot: later movement of a tracker carries its child with it through Unity’s parent-child transform hierarchy. Local positions are distances, normally metres before parent scaling. Capturing again replaces these child poses using the rig’s current pose; it does not average several samples or move a physical tracker.

The method sets _hasAssignedOffsets to true before checking the optional tracked points and before completing their captures. A missing tracked point skips its branch. A present point requires its tracker, the first child and the needed rig transforms; those references are not created here. A true flag therefore does not prove that every point exists or that capture finished successfully.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.CheckHeadsetLimits
member.summary: Keeps the headset inside a large local-position box and reports unusually fast horizontal movement or yaw.
member.returns: True when one of the checked horizontal-motion or yaw thresholds is exceeded; otherwise false.

remarks.para: It clamps headset.localPosition to X and Z between −20 and 20, and Y between −3 and 10. These are local distances, normally metres before the parent’s scale is applied. Clamping position is separate from the returned warning: touching or exceeding that box alone does not make the return value true.

Using Time.unscaledDeltaTime, the real elapsed seconds for this frame, it estimates horizontal speed and acceleration from the saved headset pose and previous velocity. It also removes head tilt to measure yaw, the turn about the upward direction, in degrees per second and degrees per second squared. Excessive acceleration makes it keep the earlier velocity estimate rather than replacing that estimate with the new spike.

The warning is true for horizontal speed greater than 10 metres per second, horizontal acceleration magnitude greater than 480 metres per second squared, absolute yaw speed greater than 2,000 degrees per second, or absolute yaw acceleration greater than 100,000 degrees per second squared. Vertical speed is not included in those horizontal tests. This method needs the headset and a valid elapsed-time sample; it does not pause the game or repair every tracking problem.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnAwake
member.summary: Registers the readiness routine, connects the controllers to this rig, and initializes its tracking avatar.

remarks.para: RigManager invokes this hook during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback: a routine called to initialize components. It registers OnMarrowReady with MarrowGame, then runs ControllerRig.OnAwake to give both controller components a reference back to this rig.

The assigned player becomes this rig’s avatar reference. It is precomputed from the manager’s current avatar eye height in metres. The measurement refresh copies selected player shape factors into the manager’s calibration avatar, then refreshes the player’s own measurements. The calibration avatar is the recipient of those factors. This prepares the tracked body’s proportions; it does not launch a tracking update or capture every tracker offset.

There is also a branch to apply a successfully queried headset IPD, the distance between the eyes, to Camera.main.stereoSeparation. In the audited build the display’s TryGetIPD helper returns false, so this branch does not apply a separation. The manager, player, controllers and XR display references still need to be assigned for the setup that uses them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this rig’s camera-render routine and clears the shared platform-pause listeners.

remarks.para: Unity calls this routine when the component is destroyed. It removes one matching OnBeginCameraRendering delegate from RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering. OnMarrowReady adds the same callback each time it runs and has no duplicate-registration guard, so if readiness ran repeatedly, one removal can leave other copies registered and they may continue updating this rig. A callback is a routine invoked for the camera-render action.

It then sets the entire static OnPauseStateChange Action to null. This clears every listener stored there, including listeners installed by other components or mods; it is not merely an unsubscribe of this rig’s own handler. The audited routine does not remove a separate collection of tracker subscriptions or reset the global time and audio pause state.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Samples VR controls and tracked poses, handles platform pause, and prepares the tracked body and movement inputs for this frame.

remarks.para: RigManager dispatches this callback, a routine called to perform its early-frame update action. Platform pause is checked before the base ControllerRig refreshes the effective pause state. Normal control and pose work can then be skipped while that effective state is paused; reading a cached axis or button does not force a fresh sample.

Supported device branches map the controllers’ axes, buttons and touch states into the rig’s control roles. An active Seat is offered both axis vectors first; when its input handler returns true, this routine zeroes both axis caches and clears _axisPrimaryDirty. The base Seat handler stores the offered vectors and returns true, so seat input is taken before ordinary walking input continues.

Thumbstick touch and a button press are different values. For OpenController, the touch cache is true when the XR device reports JoystickTouch or when its stick deflection magnitude is greater than 0.5; it is not exclusively a raw touch-sensor reading. Primary button edges and touch are passed to TimeInput, and the primary stick also participates in jog selection.

The pose portion uses current device poses when available and remembered head-relative controller poses as fallbacks. Controller targets fade their saved position/orientation difference when tracking changes to avoid an immediate jump. The headset uses a separate reacquisition alignment of the tracking root with its remembered pose. The routine refreshes available body tracking, then runs OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate to fit the body and save its pose. Active movement is finally rotated using directionMasterTransform, the selected direction reference, and the body-support reference orientation. These axes are unitless control input, not metres or speed. A transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale. The body-support reference is the rig’s center-of-pressure transform, its balance-reference point; that transform’s orientation supplies the body axes used for movement.

The pause event is called after the local pause flag changes. On entering platform pause, the time pause and tracking-state reset occur after that event; on resuming, the time unpause occurs first and a positive frame delta is required before the flag and event become false. OnPauseStateChange describes the full listener-visible order.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnMarrowReady
member.summary: Registers the late camera-render update after MarrowGame reports that initialization is ready.

remarks.para: OnAwake registers this routine during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, meaning a routine called to initialize the component. When MarrowGame runs the readiness routine, it subscribes this rig’s OnBeginCameraRendering to the render pipeline’s beginCameraRendering callback, a routine called for a camera-render action.

For Camera.main, the render routine refreshes tracked VR devices and hand offsets, updates headset rotation, and updates headset position on its paused branch. It invokes onLastCameraUpdate after that camera’s update path. Other cameras are ignored by that routine.

The readiness code also checks available display refresh rates and contains a request for the largest positive rate. In this audited build TryGetAvailableRefreshRates returns false and no array, and SetRefreshRate is an empty routine. Calling OnMarrowReady therefore does not change the display’s refresh rate here. OnDestroy removes this rig’s render delegate; calling readiness repeatedly can register it repeatedly.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnRealHeptaAwake
member.summary: Sets the tracking avatar reference, prepares the player from the manager avatar’s eye height, copies selected player shape factors into the calibration avatar and refreshes the player’s measurements.

remarks.para: It assigns player to the rig’s avatar reference, calls that player’s PrecomputeAvatar with the manager avatar’s eye height in metres, then calls RefreshBodyMeasurements with the manager’s calibration avatar. That refresh copies selected player shape factors into the calibration avatar, then refreshes the player’s own measurements. The calibration avatar receives those factors. The resulting player measurements are used when fitting the tracked body to the selected avatar.

This is an initialization helper, not a separate Unity Awake message. Awake means Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to initialize components. OpenControllerRig.OnAwake includes these same measurement operations along with its readiness and controller setup. Calling this helper alone does not register the camera-render routine or capture tracker children; manager and player references must already exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate(System.Single)
member.summary: Adjusts the tracking root’s height, filters the hand poses, solves the tracked body, and records its body-pose data.
member.param: Elapsed update time in seconds; the normal caller supplies Time.deltaTime.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate calls this with the current frame’s delta time in seconds after processing device poses. It takes the tracking root’s upward direction as playerUp and chooses a body-height reference: pelvis when configured, otherwise chest when configured, otherwise head. It compares that reference with the player’s body measurements and applies an accumulated vertical correction through _adaptiveY.

It first clamps the reference height to the allowed geometric range. The distance budget spent from _adaptiveJuice then limits the further move from that clamped height toward the preferred height. The clamping contribution can make the total correction larger than the budget spent. That budget decays at 0.6 times the player’s eye height per second. Suitable upright poses also allow adjustment based on the magnitude of the signed virtual-height input and the player’s chest height. These distances are in metres at the game’s usual scale, not a physical spring force.

It preserves the tracking root’s local X and Z positions while writing its local Y correction. It filters the left and right rig-hand transforms against the corresponding controller poses to reduce small positional and rotational changes, then calls UpdateHeptaBody. The resulting BodyPose stores body rotations, head/root relationships and limb-extension data for later rig updates.

This is a callback in the manager-driven update sequence: a routine called to perform the update action. It requires the configured player, root, manager, controller and body-part references. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for a body controlled by physics. This routine is not a request for Unity’s physics engine to move a Rigidbody, and direct calls do not supply the outer pause checks performed by OnEarlyUpdate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnStart
member.summary: Selects the movement-direction reference from and touchpad curve from , then seeds saved headset, controller and body-position data.

remarks.para: RigManager calls this start hook after initialization. It sets the rig head’s local height from the current avatar’s skull height, a local distance normally in metres before parent scaling, chooses directionMasterTransform from directionMode, and chooses touchPadCurve from curveMode. The curve mapping is the same one used by SetTouchPadCurve.

It saves the current headset local pose and each controller’s pose relative to the headset. These remembered poses support the fallback used when tracking is unavailable. It also seeds body-position differences from the avatar’s bones and gives _adaptiveJuice a two-metre initial correction budget in this start-setup path; it does not capture all tracker calibration children.

If Custom mode is selected while CustomDirection is missing, the stored directionMode is changed to Head after the original reference selection. That branch does not select a new directionMasterTransform a second time. Configure CustomDirection before setup, or call SetDirectionMasterTransform with a valid selection when changing it later.

The necessary headset, controller, manager, avatar-bone and rig references must be configured. This is a callback, meaning a routine called to perform the start action, not a continuous device-polling loop.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnUpdate
member.summary: Corrects the rig root from the current and saved body poses when the physics clock advances, then saves the current pose.

remarks.para: The root-correction and snapshot block runs only when Time.fixedTimeAsDouble, the physics clock in seconds, is greater than _lastFixedTime. It uses current and last BodyPose rotation and head-position differences to adjust this component’s world rotation and position relative to the animation rig’s head. It is not a new interpolation of every tracked joint on every rendered frame.

Its unitless timing fraction is (currentSampleTime − physicsTime) / (currentSampleTime − previousSampleTime). The sample times are the current and last controller BodyPose timestamps in seconds; physicsTime is Time.fixedTimeAsDouble in seconds. A non-positive sample interval gives fraction zero. The native calculation does not clamp the fraction, so a physics time outside the sampled interval can produce a value outside zero to one.

After the root adjustment, it stores the current physics-clock time in _lastFixedTime and copies the current BodyPose contents into lastBodyPose. This content copy preserves the existing destination object rather than replacing its reference. Later calls at the same physics time skip this correction and copy.

After that gated block it computes sternum and pelvis reference points in world space and requests a green Debug.DrawLine between them. This line request is not guarded by drawDebugBodyBones in the audited routine. Manager, player, pose buffers and the required transforms must already exist. RigManager dispatches the update callback, a routine called to perform the frame-update action.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.ProcessesWristOffset
member.summary: Selects runtime hand-offset presets from the detected right controller model and clears both XR hands’ full-update mode flags.

remarks.para: The right XR controller’s model selects a pair of hard-coded left/right position and quaternion-rotation offsets. Undefined, OculusTouch and WindowsMR use one preset; Index and ViveWands each use another. An unhandled model leaves the offsets unchanged and returns. Each preset has three position components and four quaternion components describing orientation rather than degrees on three axes. OnEarlyUpdate consumes these runtime presets: it rotates each preset’s position by the controller’s tracked rotation and adds the tracked position, then combines the tracked rotation with the preset rotation. The preset position is a distance in controller axes, normally metres before parent scaling.

For a handled model it writes leftHandOffset, calls the left XR hand’s StopFullUpdate, writes rightHandOffset, then calls the right hand’s StopFullUpdate. It needs the right controller and both XR hand references for that path. StopFullUpdate clears that XR hand’s full-update mode flag. The method does not set _hasLeftHandOffset or _hasRightHandOffset.

These writable runtime presets are separate from the constructor’s readonly OculusHandOffsetLf and OculusHandOffsetRt values. The audited OpenControllerRig pose routines read the runtime presets when building controller targets; those routines do not consume the readonly constructor presets. The complete HandActionMap update path checked continues processing hand poses without testing the cleared full-update mode flag, so clearing it does not establish that all XR-hand updates stop. The actual visible hand pose also depends on tracking, fallback selection, transition blending and the later hand filter.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.RefreshBodyTrack
member.summary: Refreshes permitted XR body data and uses a slowly averaged head alignment to correct the configured chest and pelvis trackers.

remarks.para: It returns without refreshing when the XR body device is absent, disconnected or lacks permission. Otherwise it updates that device, compares its head bone position with headset.localPosition, and rotates the difference into the headset’s axes. It updates _averageSkullLocal as 0.998 times the old average plus 0.002 times the new difference on each call. Those weights are unitless and are applied per call, not per second.

The difference between that average and the current sample is rotated back into the headset’s parent tracking space. Once _hasAssignedOffsets is true, this position correction is added to the body-array chest and pelvis positions before those tracker transforms receive local positions and rotations. Configured shoulder and elbow tracker transforms receive their corresponding body-array poses without this added head correction.

The average is updated before the _hasAssignedOffsets check, so it can accumulate while tracker pose writes are disabled. Setting the flag false skips those later writes; it does not disconnect the device or stop the averaging step. The necessary bone-array entries and tracker references must exist for enabled branches.

The local distances are normally metres before parent scaling. Captured calibration child poses follow their tracker parents through Unity’s transform hierarchy. This routine does not locate SteamVR puck serial numbers or write every configured foot and knee point from the body arrays.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.Reset
member.summary: Sets up the base rig’s body-part hierarchy and finds the on this GameObject for .

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity object that holds components. Unity calls Reset for the component’s reset action, such as when it is first added in the editor or reset through the Inspector. This override runs the base rig reset, then GetComponent for RealHeptaAvatar on the same GameObject and stores the result in _player.

The base rig operation finds or creates its expected body-part child objects and records their transform references. This override does not automatically add a missing RealHeptaAvatar: the component lookup can leave player null. It also does not capture tracker offsets or rerun the full OnAwake setup. Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to initialize the component.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.SetAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Rescales the tracking root and updates the tracking avatar’s body measurements to fit the supplied avatar’s eye height.
member.param: Avatar whose eye height is used to rescale and recompute the existing tracking player.

remarks.para: The new uniform tracking-root scale is suppliedEyeHeight / (realWorldHeight / heightPercent). suppliedEyeHeight is the supplied avatar’s eye height in metres; realWorldHeight is player’s stored real-world height in metres; heightPercent is player’s unitless total-height-to-eye-height conversion ratio: refreshed total height equals heightPercent × eyeHeight, where eyeHeight is player’s eye height in metres. The result is a unitless scale. _adaptiveY is the accumulated local-Y correction distance of the tracking root. It multiplies _adaptiveY by newScale / oldRootYScale, where both scale values are unitless, before assigning the new scale to all three root axes.

It precomputes player using that supplied eye height, copies selected player shape factors into the manager calibration avatar and refreshes player’s own measurements, updates the rig’s shoulder/spine geometry and runs CalibratePlayerBodyScale. It places the rig feet at local X positions −0.2 and +0.2 with Y and Z zero, in local distances normally measured in metres before scaling.

It raises _adaptiveJuice to at least abs(newEyeHeight − oldEyeHeight) + 0.3 × newEyeHeight. Both eye heights are player’s metre-valued eye heights before and after recalculation; 0.3 is a unitless multiplier. This supplies a distance budget in metres for later height correction, not a force or instantaneous body jump.

The player, manager, tracking root and relevant body transforms must already be configured. This method uses the supplied avatar’s measurements; it does not replace player with the supplied object or recapture the tracker calibration children. The native routine has no protection for a zero height ratio or old root Y scale.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.SetDirectionMasterTransform(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.DirectionMode)
member.summary: Chooses the transform whose facing direction will guide movement without changing .
member.param: Controller, Head or Custom reference to select for subsequent movement processing.

remarks.para: Controller selects the left controller transform when isRightHanded is true and the right controller transform when it is false. Head selects the rig’s head transform. Custom copies CustomDirection into directionMasterTransform. An unrecognized enum value leaves the previous reference unchanged.

OnEarlyUpdate uses the selected transform’s rotation to orient active primary movement input relative to the body-support reference. Rotating a selected transform changes the direction used by later samples; merely changing CustomDirection after selection does not replace the cached reference. Call this method again with Custom to select the replacement.

Controller and Head selection require their referenced component or transform. Custom does not reject null here, so configure it before a later movement update uses it. The method selects a reference; it does not itself move or turn the avatar, and it does not change the saved directionMode enum.

A transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale. The body-support reference is the rig’s center-of-pressure transform, its balance-reference point; that transform’s orientation supplies the body axes used for movement.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.SetTouchPadCurve(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.CurveMode)
member.summary: Selects the stored curve that remaps touchpad input directions without changing the curve’s keys or the saved curveMode.
member.param: Which configured direction-remapping curve to use on subsequent touchpad evaluations.

remarks.para: Linear selects curve_Linear, Poles selects curve_Poles, GenesisDpad selects curve_Genesis, Dpad selects curve_Dpad, SmoothGenesis selects curve_SmoothGenesis, and SmoothDpad selects curve_SmoothDpad. It copies the selected curve reference into touchPadCurve. An unrecognized value leaves the active reference unchanged.

The touchpad helper measures the input’s signed angle from the upward 2D direction in degrees, evaluates that angle on the selected curve, then interprets the curve result as an output angle in degrees. It reconstructs the two input components from that angle while keeping the original vector magnitude. Thus the curve changes directional response rather than directly setting movement speed or a physical rotation of the avatar.

The selected curve must be assigned before a touchpad path evaluates it. Changing this selection affects future curve evaluations; it does not rewrite curveMode or automatically select a new curve when that enum field changes. OnStart also selects the initial reference from the saved enum.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.SmoothRotate(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Calculates a smoothed yaw amount for later movement processing and stores it in the rig’s turn cache.
member.param: Signed, unitless side input; its sign chooses turn direction.
Elapsed seconds used to convert the calculated turn speed into this update’s degree amount.

remarks.para: It smooths the saved _smoothInput toward the supplied signed, unitless input using a 0.04-second SmoothDamp setting and Unity’s current Time.deltaTime, then stores the new smoothed input. SmoothDamp moves a value gradually toward its target while keeping its change-rate history. The separate deltaTime argument is then used to calculate the stored degree amount for this update; the method does not directly rotate a transform.

The stored amount is deltaTime / (0.3 × (1 − timeScale) + timeScale) × smoothedInput × (48 × degreesPerSnap + 60). deltaTime is the supplied seconds; timeScale is Unity’s unitless game-time multiplier; smoothedInput is the unitless filtered side input; degreesPerSnap is the stored degree-valued turning setting that this routine also uses in its speed formula. The final speed factor is interpreted in degrees per second and the result in degrees by the later turn consumer.

Positive and negative input request opposite turns. RemapRig later uses the cached degree amount to turn around the physics rig’s support point, subject to its update checks and absence of an active seat. A subsequent turning update can overwrite this cache; calling the method does not guarantee an immediate visible turn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.SnapRotate(System.Boolean,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Queues one signed snap angle for an armed press and releases the queued turn gradually into the turn cache.
member.param: True for a requested snap press; a false call rearms the next press.
Elapsed update time in seconds for releasing the queued turn.
Signed horizontal input used only to choose the snap direction.

remarks.para: inputPressed false arms _secondaryFlickReady again. When inputPressed is true and that flag is armed, it clears the flag and adds one signed angle to _twistDebt: snapDegreesPerFrame values 1, 2, 3 and 4 select 15, 30, 45 and 90 degrees. Other values also use 15 degrees in this helper. x less than zero makes the angle negative; x zero or positive makes it positive. Repeated true calls do not queue another angle until a false call rearms the flag.

The debt is smoothed toward zero and the amount removed this call is written to _smoothTwist in degrees. The smoothing duration is 0.01 + 0.2 / degreesPerSnap seconds: degreesPerSnap is the stored degree-valued turning setting used as the divisor here, not the angle selected by snapDegreesPerFrame. The supplied deltaTime in seconds is adjusted by the current unitless timeScale in that smoothing calculation.

The method itself does not test a thumbstick threshold or rotate the avatar; the input-processing caller decides when inputPressed is true. RemapRig later consumes the degree amount, subject to its checks including no active seat. A queued snap can span several updates rather than instantly applying its entire angle. Required turning settings should not be treated as validated by this helper; it has no zero-divisor guard for degreesPerSnap.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.TimeInput(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Handles a slow-motion press and a delayed return/toggle after release and loss of stick touch.
member.param: Mapped slow-motion button press edge.
Mapped slow-motion button release edge.
Current primary-stick touch/activity cache used to postpone an armed toggle.

remarks.para: Down is processed first. A down input clears any pending delayed toggle, then returns immediately if TimeManager’s time-control flag is inactive or its step is above two, skipping touch and release processing. Otherwise it calls DECREASE_TIMESCALE and requests decelTime audio. This is a step request, not a continuous ramp driven by holding the button.

An already pending toggle is processed second. While it is armed, touch true keeps moving its deadline 0.25 seconds into the future. On a later call with touch false and unscaled time strictly beyond the deadline, it clears the armed flag before calling TOGGLE_TIMESCALE and requesting accelTime audio. Up is processed last: an up input at a positive time-control step arms a delayed toggle and sets its deadline to Time.unscaledTime plus 0.25 seconds. A newly armed release is not tested for expiry until a later call. Unscaled seconds measure real elapsed time through slow motion.

OnEarlyUpdate supplies the mapped primary A-button down/up edges and the primary stick touch cache. For OpenController, that touch cache can be true from reported JoystickTouch or stick deflection magnitude greater than 0.5, so moving the stick can postpone the toggle without a separately reported touch. The three inputs are separately supplied booleans, but the down-path immediate return can prevent the other inputs from being processed that call. This method does not poll the device itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.UpdateHeptaBody(System.Single)
member.summary: Fits the torso, pelvis and legs from the tracked head and hands, using configured body trackers when available.
member.param: Elapsed update time in seconds for the body solver and its positional smoothing.

remarks.para: The solver starts from a head reference built from the headset’s world position and rotation plus the player’s rotated skull-camera offset, the local displacement connecting the headset camera and skull reference. Body dimensions come from player. It writes the rig’s body-part transforms; it does not apply forces to physical joints or create missing tracker objects. A physical joint is a connection that constrains how physics bodies move relative to each other.

Without assigned tracker calibration, a connected body device and body permission, it uses the HeptaRig chest/pelvis solving path. With the required tracking setup, configured chest, pelvis, shoulder and elbow references guide the relevant body geometry, while missing optional roles use their fallback calculations. Tracker calibration children supply the relation between measured tracker poses and body points.

When both tracked feet are configured in the tracked-body path, each foot position relative to the moving head reference is passed through the positional Gimbal smoother. It keeps velocity history in metres per second, a velocity-smoothing derivative, meaning how quickly its smoothed velocity is changing, in metres per second squared, and an additive offset in metres along world axes. The foot call limits that offset’s magnitude to 0.05 metres and uses a 0.1-second velocity smoothing duration. This reduces abrupt target motion rather than simulating a physical spring.

OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate calls this after adapting root height and filtering the hands, then captures the resulting BodyPose for later stages. deltaTime supplies elapsed seconds to time-dependent solving. Required player, headset and rig-part references must exist; the method’s conditional tracker paths do not make every missing body transform safe.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.ArmMantle
member.summary: Calculates how strongly this arm can help push the body up while the palm braces below the shoulder.

remarks.para: The result is a unitless number from 0 to 1. It multiplies three factors: hand support, the hand’s vertical distance below the shoulder, and how much the palm faces world down. Each factor is limited to 0 through 1. Support below 0.2 returns 0 immediately.

The height factor is (heightGap / armLength - 0.4) / 0.3, limited to 0 through 1. heightGap is the upper-arm body’s world Y position minus the hand body’s world Y position, in meters. armLength is the avatar’s cached overall arm length in meters. The support factor is (support - 0.2) / 0.4, limited to 0 through 1; support is the unitless hand-load estimate stored in handSupported. The facing factor is 1.5 times the palm’s forward direction dotted with world down, limited to 0 through 1; the dot product measures alignment, with 1 meaning straight down.

For an illustrative 0.60-meter arm with the hand 0.33 meters below the shoulder, support of 0.4, and a palm facing straight down, the result is 0.5 × 0.5 × 1 = 0.25. Calling this method returns the calculation. ReadSensors is the routine that also saves it into armMantle for later muscle-force calculations.

member.returns: A 0-to-1 assistance weight, with 0 meaning no assistance from this calculation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.CalibrateArmColliders(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Rebuilds the arm’s collision shapes and sizes the palm, fingers, and inventory plug to the supplied avatar.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape that the physics simulation uses to detect contact. This replaces the upper-arm and forearm mesh colliders with generated avatar meshes and makes both convex, meaning they have no inward dents. It also sets the palm and finger box sizes and their local positions from the avatar’s cached palm width and length, in meters.

isRight selects the matching palm offsets and mirrors the sideways placement for the right hand. The inventory plug is sized from the avatar’s cached arm length: its radius is 5% of that length and its height is 50%. For a 0.60-meter arm, those values are 3 cm and 30 cm. These are setup changes to the existing collider references; changing the avatar’s measurements afterward requires another calibration call.

member.param: Avatar whose already-calculated arm and palm measurements supply the collision shapes.
True selects right-hand measurements and mirrored placement; false selects the left hand.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.CalibrateArmJoints(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Moves the arm joints’ attachment points to match the avatar’s elbow, wrist, and palm measurements.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects two bodies. Its anchor is an attachment point in one body’s local coordinates; its connected anchor is the matching point in the other body’s coordinates. These positions are in meters. This updates the elbow’s connected anchor, both wrist attachment points, and the hand-side attachment points of the chest and support connections.

isRight chooses the right palm-position offset; otherwise it uses the left. The sizes come from the avatar’s cached upper-arm, forearm, and wrist-to-hand measurements. This method sets attachment positions, not spring strength or angular limits. Re-run it when those cached avatar measurements change.

member.param: Avatar with the cached arm lengths and palm-position offsets to apply.
True uses the right palm-position offset; false uses the left.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.CalibrateJoints(System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets the arm’s base muscle strength and joint drives, then activates the chosen hand-support rotation drive.

remarks.para: A joint drive acts like a motor: its spring pulls toward a target, its damping resists movement, and its maximum force limits how hard it can push or twist. avatarArmMult and gripMult are unitless strength inputs. Doubling avatarArmMult doubles the configured shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand-to-chest base spring and damping coefficients, along with the directional hand-force limits. The wrist’s base maximum force stays at 1 before its extra multipliers.

This stores maxTorque as 30 × gripMult, a torque scale in newton-meters. It also sets newtonDamp to 100 × avatarArmMult, in newtons. Shoulder and elbow angular drives apply an additional maximum-force multiplier equal to _forceMultiplier × armInternalMult; those two values are unitless arm-strength scales. Wrist angular drives use maxTorque as their additional maximum-force multiplier.

With monofootEnabled false, the hand-to-chest rotation drive is activated and the support-hand rotation drive is set to zero. With true, the support-hand rotation drive is activated and the chest rotation drive is set to zero. This flag selects the rig’s single-foot support mode. Later drive updates can replace the applied settings.

member.param: Unitless scale for base arm drive coefficients and directional hand-force limits.
Unitless scale for maxTorque and the two hand-support base rotation drives.
Selects the support-hand rotation drive when true, or the hand-to-chest rotation drive when false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.CalibrateLimbGrips(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Fits the grab targets on the upper arm and forearm to the avatar’s arm length and thickness.

remarks.para: This positions the two cylinder-grip targets, sets their half-lengths, and replaces their radius curves. A hand target is the position the game wants a grabbing hand to reach. The upper-arm target sits 57% of the upper-arm length along its local Z axis and has a half-length of 32% of that length. The forearm target sits 54% of the forearm length along local Z and has a half-length of 40%.

Each radius curve maps signed distance along the grip, in meters, to radius in meters. The upper-arm curve has keys at -17% and +23% of upper-arm length, with radii calculated from upper-arm and elbow thickness. The forearm curve has keys at -34% and +26% of forearm length, with radii calculated from forearm and wrist thickness. Thickness values are the avatar’s stored sideways ellipse radii as fractions of eye height, multiplied by its cached eye height in meters.

isRight mirrors the upper-arm target’s sideways offset. For an illustrative upper-arm length of 0.30 meters, the half-length becomes 9.6 cm and the radius-curve key positions become -5.1 cm and +6.9 cm. This writes setup values; it does not enable variable-radius mode on the grips.

member.param: Avatar supplying cached arm lengths, eye height, and arm-section thickness settings.
True mirrors the upper-arm target sideways for the right arm.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.CheckFingerEnable
member.summary: Enables finger collisions once the front half of the finger box is clear of the configured obstacle layers.

remarks.para: It checks an oriented box matching the finger collider’s front half, using the collider’s local Z direction and fingerColCheckMask. The mask chooses which physics layers count as obstacles, and trigger-only shapes are ignored. If the check finds nothing, the pending enable flag is cleared before the finger collider is enabled.

The method itself does not require a pending request. Normal UpdateColliders calls perform this check only while EnableFingerCollider has left a request pending. A failed clearance check leaves the request and collider state unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.ClearJerk(System.Single)
member.summary: Lowers the stored force and rotation response factors to a chosen ceiling and briefly boosts rotation damping.

remarks.para: For each factor, the new value is the smaller of its current value and newJerk. The input is unitless; it is not acceleration or physical jerk. For example, a ceiling of 0.2 changes factors of 0.8 and 0.1 to 0.2 and 0.1. The default ceiling of 0 clears positive factors.

This also sets the temporary shock factor to 1. The normal rotation solver uses that factor to raise damping, then moves it toward 0 by 8 times the physics-step duration in seconds on each update. Saved target positions, velocities, and force history are left alone.

member.param: Unitless ceiling for both stored response factors; each is only lowered, never raised.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.DisableFingerCollider
member.summary: Immediately turns off the finger collision box and cancels any pending request to turn it back on.

remarks.para: The configured finger box is an invisible, box-shaped physics contact detector. This changes the collider’s enabled state to false and then clears _fingerEnableFlag. Use EnableFingerCollider to request a later safe re-enable after the box has space.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.EarlyUpdateArm
member.summary: Refreshes the shoulder and elbow joint strength when the arm’s combined strength multiplier changes.

remarks.para: A joint drive is the physics motor that pulls an arm segment toward its target rotation. The combined, unitless multiplier is _forceMultiplier × armInternalMult. This scales the maximum force of the shoulder’s angular X and YZ drives and the elbow’s angular X drive, while keeping spring and damping multipliers at 1.
