It saves the combined multiplier into _lastForceMult after applying the settings. If shutdown is true or the saved value already matches, it does nothing. It does not refresh the wrist drives.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.EnableFingerCollider
member.summary: Requests that the finger collision box be turned back on after a clearance check.

remarks.para: This only sets _fingerEnableFlag. It does not immediately enable the collider. During later UpdateColliders calls, a clear front-half box test against fingerColCheckMask enables the finger collider and clears the request. Obstacles can delay that change across several updates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.IgnorePhysHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Changes collision filtering between this hand’s selected arm shapes and another hand’s shapes.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape used to detect physical contact. This toggles 13 pairs involving the finger box, palm box, forearm mesh, and upper-arm mesh. Finger and palm pairs cover all four shapes on the other arm; forearm pairs cover the other fingers, palm, and forearm; upper-arm pairs cover the other fingers and palm.

It does not change upper-arm versus upper-arm or upper-arm versus forearm pairs, and it does not include either inventory plug. ignore = true prevents the listed pairs from colliding; false restores those pairs. Both PhysHand references and their configured colliders must exist.

member.param: Other hand whose finger, palm, forearm, and upper-arm collision shapes are paired with this arm.
True disables collisions for the listed pairs; false allows them again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.RelaxTorqueMult(System.Single)
member.summary: Returns a reduced rotation-strength multiplier when this empty hand relaxes while the other hand supports the body.

remarks.para: The result is 0.3 only when this hand’s physical state is Empty, grip is below 0.5, its support estimate is below 0.2, and the other hand’s support estimate is above 0.3. Otherwise it is 1. The support estimates are unitless load signals, not percentages of body mass.

The method only calculates the factor. FixedUpdateArm contains the same choice when setting its rotation-strength input. Exactly 0.5 grip, 0.2 own support, or 0.3 other support does not satisfy the corresponding strict comparison.

member.param: Controller squeeze input, normally 0 to 1; values below 0.5 can allow relaxation.
member.returns: 0.3 when all relaxation conditions hold; otherwise 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.ResetHand
member.summary: Tries two collision sweeps to move the hand body to a contact position using the forearm’s current pose.

remarks.para: A sweep checks where a moving collision shape first hits something. This uses the forearm transform and its forward direction to choose the two searches. If a sweep hits, it places the hand at that hit distance. If neither hits, it restores the hand’s original position.
The upper-arm and forearm bodies are reference points for the search; this method changes only the hand body’s position. It does not rebuild the whole arm or reset its rotation and velocities.

member.returns: True if either sweep found a contact and placed the hand there; false if neither hit and its old position was restored.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.SetFriction(System.Single)
member.summary: Switches the palm and finger collision materials according to squeeze and hand support.

remarks.para: A physics material controls contact friction and bounce. When _isHighFriction is false, grip above 0.5 or support above 0.2 first sets the flag true, then assigns _highFriction to the palm and then the fingers. When the flag is true, grip below 0.5 together with support below 0.1 first clears the flag, then assigns _lowFriction to the palm and then the fingers. Support is a unitless load estimate.

The different support thresholds stop rapid switching near one boundary. At grip exactly 0.5, grip alone cannot turn high friction on, but support above 0.2 still can. Grip exactly 0.5 prevents turning it off. Support exactly 0.2 does not turn high friction on by itself, and exactly 0.1 does not turn it off. This selects whole material assets; it does not blend their friction coefficients. FixedUpdateArm also performs this selection.

member.param: Controller squeeze input, normally 0 to 1; 0.5 is the strict switching boundary.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.SetFrictionLow
member.summary: Applies the low-friction material to both arm meshes and the palm, and the natural material to the fingers.

remarks.para: A physics material sets contact friction and bounce. This clears _isHighFriction after assigning the materials. The finger box deliberately receives _naturalFriction. If the upper-arm mesh already has _lowFriction, the method returns immediately without checking the other shapes or correcting the flag.
Later FixedUpdateArm calls may select another palm and finger material according to squeeze and support.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.SetFrictionNatural
member.summary: Applies the natural-friction material to the upper arm, forearm, palm, and fingers.

remarks.para: A physics material sets contact friction and bounce. This clears _isHighFriction after assigning all four shapes. If the upper-arm mesh already has _naturalFriction, it returns immediately without checking the other shapes or correcting the flag. Later arm updates can change the palm and finger materials again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.SetRangeOfMotionActive
member.summary: Sets wider shoulder and wrist rotation limits for the arm’s physics joints.

remarks.para: A joint connects two bodies in the physics simulation. In the joint’s own axes, the shoulder’s X limits become -95 to +95 degrees, with Y and Z each limited to 90 degrees on either side. The wrist’s X limits become -90 to +90 degrees, with Y and Z each limited to 90 degrees on either side.

This also sets the shoulder’s X and YZ limit springs to 1000 and their dampers to 100. A limit spring resists motion past the allowed angle, and a damper resists movement there. The elbow settings are left alone; calling this does not itself rotate the arm.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.SetRangeOfMotionNatural
member.summary: Restores the narrower shoulder and wrist rotation limits and removes the shoulder’s limit-spring resistance.

remarks.para: A joint connects two bodies in the physics simulation. In its own axes, the shoulder’s X limits become -82 to +82 degrees, with Y and Z each limited to 80 degrees on either side. The wrist’s X limits become -85 to +85 degrees, with Y and Z each limited to 70 degrees on either side.
This sets both shoulder limit springs and dampers to 0. It does not change the elbow limits or move the bodies into a particular pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.UpdateArmDrives(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Scales the shoulder, elbow, and wrist motors that pull the arm toward its target rotations.

remarks.para: A drive is a physics motor inside a joint. Its spring pulls toward the target, damping resists movement, and its maximum force limits the push or twist. Each argument is a unitless multiplier of the drive’s saved base value: 1 preserves it, 0 removes that part, and 2 doubles it.

This updates the shoulder’s angular X and YZ drives, the elbow’s angular X drive, and the wrist’s angular X and YZ drives. For the wrist, the maximum-force multiplier is also multiplied by maxTorque, the stored rotation-strength scale. If slerpForceMult already equals _lastForceMult, the entire call is skipped, even when only spring or damping was changed. Successful updates save slerpForceMult into that cache.

member.param: Unitless multiplier for maximum force; the wrist also multiplies this by maxTorque.
Unitless multiplier for the saved spring strength.
Unitless multiplier for the saved damping strength.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.UpdateArmSupportDrives(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Scales the hand-to-chest position motors and the selected hand-support rotation motor.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects two bodies; its drive acts like a motor pulling toward a target. This always updates the hand-to-chest X, Y, and Z position drives. It updates the support-hand rotation drive when monofootEnabled is true, or the hand-to-chest rotation drive when false. The flag selects the rig’s single-foot support mode.

The three multipliers scale saved base maximum force, spring strength, and damping separately. They are unitless: 1 keeps a base value and 0 removes that part. This does not disable or refresh the other rotation drive; calibration or the support-switch routines handle that separately.

member.param: Unitless multiplier for each selected drive’s saved maximum force.
Unitless multiplier for each selected drive’s saved spring strength.
Unitless multiplier for each selected drive’s saved damping.
True chooses the support-hand rotation drive; false chooses the hand-to-chest rotation drive.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.ZeroTargets
member.summary: Resets the arm joint motors to neutral rotation targets and clears their requested angular speeds.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection, and its target is where its motor tries to move a body. This assigns identity rotation—the neutral, unturned rotation in the joint’s coordinates—and zero target angular velocity to the shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand-to-chest, and support-hand joints.

It also zeroes the hand-to-chest joint’s target position and target linear velocity. It does not zero the actual bodies’ velocities, teleport the arm, or reset drive strength. Later target updates can replace these values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.#ctor
member.summary: Creates the torso component with strength scales of 1 and a damping-to-spring scale of 0.1.

remarks.para: The constructor sets _spineForceMult and _spineInternalMult to 1, and _slerpDamperMult to 0.1. These are unitless scales. Unity can later replace serialized values with the settings saved on the component in the scene or prefab, a saved object template.

Construction does not create the Rigidbody, Servo, collider or grip objects. A Rigidbody is a physically simulated body; a Servo controls a physics joint connecting bodies; a collider supplies the collision shape; a grip supplies hand-interaction behaviour. Assign the required existing components before calling the torso's setup and update methods.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.EarlyUpdateSpineJoints
member.summary: Refreshes the four internal spine angular drives when their remembered scale settings differ.

remarks.para: Returns immediately when shutdown is true. Otherwise it compares the effective force scale and the damping field with their saved values. PhysicsRig, the component that simulates the player's body, calls this during its early update when that rig is running; calling this method alone does not start a repeating update.

These are the four servos joining head to neck, neck to chest, chest to spine, and spine to pelvis. A servo controls a physics joint, a connection that lets Unity apply forces between simulated body parts. Its angular drive turns the parts toward a requested pose; the spring pulls toward that pose, damping resists turning motion, and the maximum-force setting caps the drive.

The effective runtime scale is _spineInternalMult multiplied by _spineForceMult. Both numbers have no units; 1 keeps the calibrated maximum-force setting and 0.5 halves it. The scale changes the angular drive's maximum-force setting rather than its spring or damping settings during this early update.

The comparison uses _lastSpineForceMult for the previously applied force scale and _lastSlerpDamperMult for the previously recorded _slerpDamperMult. If both match, no drive is written. After all four writes return normally, both saved values are updated. A change to _slerpDamperMult triggers this refresh but the refresh uses a damping scale of 1; it does not rebuild the calibrated damping from the new field value.

CalibrateJoints must first supply the servos' base drive settings for the avatar, the player's in-game body. For example, changing _spineInternalMult from 1 to 0.5 with _spineForceMult at 1 makes the next refresh use half the stored base maximum force. It does not rebuild the collision shapes or immediately put the body in a new pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.OnAwakeInitialize
member.summary: Stops the head and neck colliders from colliding with the two spine colliders.

remarks.para: Disables four collision pairs: cHead with cSpine, neckCol with cSpine, cHead with cSpineLow, and neckCol with cSpineLow. A collider is the shape Unity checks for physical contact. Disabling a pair lets these parts overlap without pushing against one another through that pair; it does not disable either collider against the rest of the level.

The project's PhysicsRig.OnAwake initialization method calls this helper after the torso references have been configured. This method is a helper called by that setup, and all four collider references must already identify the intended body parts. It does not find them, calibrate their sizes or ignore every torso pair.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.SetFrictionLow
member.summary: Applies the configured low-friction material to the six torso collision shapes when the pelvis has a different material.

remarks.para: Checks cPelvis.sharedMaterial first. If it already matches _lowFriction, the method returns without checking or changing the other shapes. Otherwise it assigns that same material reference to cPelvis, cSpineLow, cSpine, cChest, neckCol and cHead in that order.

A physics material supplies contact settings such as sliding friction and bounce; the configured asset determines the values. The method does not change body mass or joint strength. Supply all six collider references before this path runs; missing references can fail after earlier shapes have already been changed.

For example, if cPelvis already has _lowFriction but cChest was changed to another material separately, calling this method leaves cChest as it is. Changing the stored material reference alone also does not apply it to any collider.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.SetFrictionNatural
member.summary: Applies the configured natural-friction material to the six torso collision shapes when the pelvis has a different material.

remarks.para: Checks cPelvis.sharedMaterial first. If it already matches _naturalFriction, the method returns without checking or changing the other shapes. Otherwise it assigns that same material reference to cPelvis, cSpineLow, cSpine, cChest, neckCol and cHead in that order.

A physics material supplies contact settings such as sliding friction and bounce; the configured asset determines the values. The method does not change body mass or joint strength. Supply all six collider references before this path runs; missing references can fail after earlier shapes have already been changed.

For example, if cPelvis already has _naturalFriction but cChest was changed to another material separately, calling this method leaves cChest as it is. Changing the stored material reference alone also does not apply it to any collider.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.ZeroTargets
member.summary: Sets the four internal spine joints to their neutral rotation targets with zero requested angular velocity.

remarks.para: These are the four servos joining head to neck, neck to chest, chest to spine, and spine to pelvis. A servo controls a physics joint, a connection that lets Unity apply forces between simulated body parts. Its angular drive turns the parts toward a requested pose; the spring pulls toward that pose, damping resists turning motion, and the maximum-force setting caps the drive.

Writes each joint's targetRotation to the identity quaternion and targetAngularVelocity to the zero vector, in head-neck, neck-chest, chest-spine and spine-pelvis order. A quaternion is Unity's rotation value; identity is the neutral rotation value, not four zero quaternion components. Unity interprets that target using the joint's configured target-space and connected-body settings. Angular velocity means turning speed, measured in radians per second, so zero requests no target turning.

This changes the joints' requests rather than setting the bodies' current positions, rotations or velocities. The joint drives can move the simulated body toward the targets later. It does not clear linear position targets or the three longer head/chest/pelvis joints, and it does not rebuild Servo's saved starting rotations.

All four servos and their joints must be assigned. The method still runs with shutdown true; PhysicsRig.ShutdownRig uses it after changing the drive scales. If the torso later resumes normal target updates, UpdateSpineTargets can replace these neutral requests.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.CalibrateJoints(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Calculates and saves the strength settings that help the monofoot support the pelvis, chest and head.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the rig's single rolling ground-support ball and the support body above it. A servo is a controller that pushes a physics joint toward a target; a physics joint connects two simulated body parts and limits or guides their movement. This method saves spring strength, damping and force caps for the monofoot-to-pelvis, chest and head servos. The spring pulls toward the target, damping resists unwanted motion, and the cap limits the drive's push.

The saved rotational settings depend on the supplied avatar's stored body-part masses in kilograms and torso or neck lengths in metres. The vertical pelvis setting combines that avatar's pelvis height with the total mass of the avatar currently assigned to this rig, so normally supply the rig's current avatar. The rig's pelvis force multipliers scale the rotational settings without units; its mono damper multiplier scales damping.

This is setup work: saving a base setting does not immediately replace the live joint drive. OnEarlyUpdate applies the rotational settings with current support factors, and UpdateKnee applies the vertical setting. Run calibration again after changing the relevant avatar measurements or rig multipliers.

member.param: Avatar whose already stored masses and body measurements supply the calibration values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.CheckBodyMassDistribution
member.summary: Chooses a and applies the matching mass split when the support mode needs to change.

remarks.para: With ball locomotion off, an assigned seat selects Seated; without a seat the rig selects Natural. These states choose how much mass is assigned to the torso and monofoot, the single rolling support ball and the support body above it. They do not themselves make the player sit or change the legs between simulated and kinematic movement. Kinematic means game code places a body instead of letting forces move it.

With ball locomotion on, the choice uses footSupported, the rig's dimensionless measure of ground support, and bodyMassNaturalHold, a flag that holds the less stable NaturalMono split. Starting from Natural or Seated, support below 0.65 selects NaturalMono; otherwise it selects StableMono, unless the hold flag is set. NaturalMono switches to StableMono at support 0.70 or above when the hold flag is clear. StableMono switches back at support 0.60 or below, or when the hold flag is set.

The different switch thresholds stop small changes near one boundary from repeatedly moving mass back and forth. For example, a StableMono rig with support 0.65 keeps its current split. Each selected change is followed by SetBodyMassDistribution, which writes the actual body masses in kilograms.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.CheckDoubleJump(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Arms a follow-up jump while the feet have support, then accepts an upward impulse request once the jump is armed and its cooldown has ended.

remarks.para: If the jump is not armed and footSupported is greater than 0.1, this call arms it, sets a launch-window timestamp to the current physics time plus 0.5 seconds, and returns false. footSupported is the rig's dimensionless ground-support measure, calculated from the upward contact impulse compared with avatar weight over a physics step and then smoothed. It is not a percentage. A later call may accept the impulse even while the feet still have support; becoming airborne is not a requirement checked here.

An armed request is rejected while the current physics time is earlier than the saved cooldown timestamp. Equality is allowed. An accepted request clears the armed flag, adds newtonSecond to the pending upward impulse, and sets the next cooldown timestamp to now plus cooldown. For example, accepting 20 Newton-seconds with cooldown 1 stores 20 additional Newton-seconds and prevents another accepted request before one second of physics time has passed.

The impulse is stored for later locomotion processing rather than applied all at once here. That processing releases it in portions and reduces its effect as the pelvis's upward speed approaches 10 metres per second. OnAfterFixedUpdate also clears an armed jump when the launch-window time has passed and footSupported is greater than 0.25; the 0.5-second timestamp is not an unconditional expiry checked by this method.

member.param: Amount to add to the pending upward impulse, in Newton-seconds. One Newton-second is a push of one Newton lasting one second.
Seconds of physics time before the next armed request can be accepted. The default is 1 second.
member.returns: True when this call added the impulse request; false when it only armed the jump or rejected the request.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.DisableBallLoco
member.summary: Turns off rolling-ball support, disables the monofoot bodies' collision detection, and moves their support links back toward the torso.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the shared rolling support beneath the player, separate from the visible left and right feet. This method clears the ball-locomotion flag, zeroes the monofoot support servos' rotational drives, and reconnects arm support to the chest. A servo drives a physics joint, a connection that guides simulated body parts toward a target.

It requests a smaller ball radius, 0.055 times the avatar's eye height in metres times 1.05, and immediately applies that radius without a growth collision check. It updates the mass split, selects NeutralRoll, updates the vertical knee target, and places the monofoot knee and ball bodies at the pelvis. Their collision detection is disabled, and the capsule between them is collapsed.
The separate physical legs keep their existing simulation mode. RagdollRig performs the accompanying switch to simulated legs when entering a ragdoll.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.EnableBallLoco
member.summary: Turns on rolling-ball support, connects arm support to the monofoot, and prepares the ground-support and stepping systems.

remarks.para: The monofoot is one rolling ground-support ball with a support body above it. This method sets the ball-locomotion flag first, rebuilds the arms' support connections to those bodies, and enables collision detection on the monofoot knee and ball. A physics joint is the connection used to guide one simulated body part relative to another.

It requests the usual ball radius: the avatar's eye height in metres times 0.055 times 1.3. It checks the mass split, starts a ground query and return-step setup, and resets the ground-support system. The flag describes which locomotion path is enabled; it does not mean the ball is touching the ground.

This method keeps the separate legs' current simulation mode. UnRagdollRig switches them to kinematic movement before enabling ball support. Kinematic means the game places a body instead of letting forces move it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.KinematicLegs
member.summary: Makes both separate legs follow game-controlled poses instead of responding to physics forces.

remarks.para: Each leg has simulated upper-leg, lower-leg and foot bodies. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for such a simulated body. Kinematic mode tells Unity that game code controls the body's position and rotation, so forces do not move it.

Both legs have their joint movement released and their drive spring and damping values set to zero. A physics joint connects two body parts; its drive is the push that normally moves the parts toward a target. The leg bodies become kinematic and switch to their configured no-collision layer, and the rig records that its legs are kinematic.
This affects the two anatomical legs, not the shared monofoot ball. Their visible poses can then be placed from the rig's tracking targets during OnAfterFixedUpdate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.LadderForce
member.summary: Adds a rung-based correction to the pelvis's velocity, pushing it away from a point calculated near the monofoot.

remarks.para: The calculation uses the rung transform and width last supplied by UpdateLadderInfo. It expresses the monofoot ball's centre in the rung's local axes, chooses a point at local Y zero, and clamps local Z between minus and plus rungWidth. Here rungWidth is the stored limit in metres on each side along the rung's local Z axis. Local coordinates move and turn with the rung; the resulting correction is converted to world coordinates.

The push points from that selected point toward the pelvis, with a 0.2-metre dead zone on the world X and Z components. It adds a change in velocity, measured in metres per second, directly to the pelvis. An upward change therefore depends on the relative positions; the direction is not always world up.

The change scales with avatar total mass divided by pelvis mass, both in kilograms, the vertical gravity strength in metres per second squared, and Unity's fixed physics timestep in seconds. It also scales with the ladder fade factor, a number normally between 0 and 1 with no physical units: 0 removes this correction and 1 allows its full strength. ApplyFeetForce moves that blend toward the current contact request by up to 4 per second of physics time, then clears the request. Fresh ladder contact requests 1; without a refreshed request the target is 0, so repeated contact refreshes the blend. The correction becomes weaker as the ball moves outside the rung's vertical or width bounds. This method expects a valid stored rung transform. It does not check a hand's grip or apply velocity-dependent damping.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnAfterFixedUpdate
member.summary: Reads the completed physics step, updates body-motion measurements and contacts, and places legs that are following game-controlled poses.

remarks.para: This is a rig update hook: the rig manager calls it as part of the update sequence after a physics step. A physics step is one fixed-duration update in which Unity moves simulated bodies and resolves collisions. If the pelvis Rigidbody is sleeping, meaning Unity has paused an idle body's simulation until it is disturbed, this hook returns immediately.

It saves each physical leg's latest transforms. When the legs are kinematic, meaning placed by game code rather than forces, it positions their hips, knees and feet from the virtual rig's target pose and synchronizes the corresponding physics bodies. It then reads hand sensors, updates head collision sounds, processes collision collectors, and calculates whole-body velocity in world metres per second and acceleration in world metres per second squared.

It places the centre of pressure, the reference point representing ground or climbing support, using the monofoot's current position, radius and contact direction. These contact and measurement operations happen before the shutdown check. After that check, the active path measures the physical body's difference from its virtual target. With ball locomotion enabled it also reads ground support, updates motion relative to the ground, smooths the support amount, and updates crouch measurements and double-jump readiness.

The ground readings include a world-space slip velocity, the ball's velocity at its contact point minus the supporting ground's velocity there, in metres per second. skidSpeed is the magnitude of that vector. groundAngVelocity is the support-weighted average of the ground bodies' rotation rate around world Y, in radians per second. footSupported has no physical units. Its target is upward contact impulse divided by (avatar total mass times vertical gravity magnitude times the fixed-step duration). Here impulse is the collected world-Y push over the completed step in Newton-seconds, mass is the assigned avatar's stored total mass in kilograms, gravity magnitude is the absolute world-Y gravity in metres per second squared, and duration is Unity's fixed physics timestep in seconds. It moves toward that target, increasing by at most 12 per second and decreasing by at most 6 per second of physics time. There is no clamp to 1, so the smoothed amount can exceed 1 and is not a percentage.

The double-jump armed flag is cleared only when physics time is later than its saved launch-window timestamp and footSupported is greater than 0.25. These measurements describe the completed step; setting a configuration value elsewhere does not immediately replace them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnAwake
member.summary: Prepares hand and body physics, self-collision rules, ground-query storage and the initial poses saved for later rig switching.

remarks.para: This is the rig's initialization hook. The Unity name Awake normally means an initialization callback, a method the engine calls during setup; this OnAwake method is a rig hook that performs the PhysicsRig setup. It assigns the rig manager to both hands, initializes torso and soft-body physics, allocates space for 32 ground-query hits, and initializes the ground-support component.

It sets selected collision-ignore pairs between the rig's own colliders so its hands, arms, torso, legs and monofoot interact as intended. A collider is the invisible shape Unity uses for contact tests. Some self-contact pairs remain enabled, so the whole rig is not simply made unable to collide with itself. Its own torso grips are also excluded from the hands' grip queries, and its body Rigidbodies are added to a set used by queries that exclude the player. A Rigidbody is a physics-simulated body.

It records initial positions and rotations for the torso, arms and monofoot relative to each transform's parent, plus leg rotations relative to the pelvis or the preceding leg segment. A transform stores position and orientation; its parent is the object it belongs under in Unity's hierarchy. Positions use the parent's axes and Unity distance units, normally metres when the rig and its parents have scale 1, meaning they are not enlarged or shrunk. The rotations are quaternions, four-number descriptions of orientation whose components are not degree angles. These initial poses are applied when the rig is disabled; separate cached poses remember where it was just before disabling. If an art-output component is assigned, its setup hook is called too.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Updates hand and body joint controllers and applies the monofoot's saved rotational support strengths.

remarks.para: This update hook returns immediately while the rig's shutdown flag is set. Otherwise it updates both hands, torso joint controllers and arm controllers. It updates leg controllers when the legs are physical rather than kinematic, meaning forces can move them instead of game code placing them.

With ball locomotion enabled, it applies the saved monofoot-to-head, chest and pelvis rotational drives. A drive is the spring-and-damping push that guides a physics joint toward its target orientation; a physics joint connects two simulated parts. The saved spring strength, which pulls toward the target, and damping, which resists rotation, are applied unchanged. Only the maximum rotational push, or torque cap, is scaled by support. The support amount S is the sum of stored foot, left-hand and right-hand support, limited to 0 through 1; it has no physical units, with 0 meaning no support contribution and 1 meaning full support. The override O is overrideKneePelForce limited to the same range. The cap multiplier is (S + (1 - S) times O) times pelvisForceMult times pelvisForceInternalMult. Both named pelvis factors are the rig's unitless force multipliers. At S = 0 the override supplies the support part of the cap; at S = 1 that part is 1 regardless of the override.
CalibrateJoints saves these base strengths during setup; this hook turns them into current joint settings using the support state. It does not recalculate avatar measurements each frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnLateUpdate
member.summary: Updates the optional visual body output to follow the physical rig after the main update stage.

remarks.para: When the pelvis physics body is awake and an art-output component is assigned, this hook calls that component's regular output update and then its late update, in that order. The art output is the part that presents the visible body from the physical rig's state.
If the pelvis Rigidbody is sleeping, meaning Unity has paused an idle simulated body, this hook skips both calls. An absent art-output component is also skipped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnRigDisable
member.summary: Saves the current body poses for re-enabling the rig, then restores the initial poses recorded during setup.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object's position and orientation; its parent is the object it belongs under in Unity's hierarchy. Before changing the transforms, this hook overwrites the cached pelvis, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, monofoot knee and ball, shoulders, elbows and hands. Each saved position and rotation is relative to that transform's parent. Positions are in Unity distance units, normally metres when the rig and its parents have scale 1, meaning they are not enlarged or shrunk.

The six separate leg caches save rotations relative to another body part: each hip relative to the pelvis, each knee relative to its same-side hip, and each foot relative to its same-side knee. A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation; its components are not angles in degrees.

After saving those values, it applies the initial poses captured by OnAwake. OnRigEnable with reEnable true later restores the cached pose. The caches are snapshots taken at disable time, not fresh data for every physics step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnStart
member.summary: Starts the rig with ball locomotion and game-controlled legs, then configures the monofoot physics bodies.

remarks.para: This startup hook sets the ball-locomotion flag, makes both separate legs kinematic, and applies the requested monofoot ball radius without checking for blocked growth. Kinematic means game code places the leg bodies instead of letting physics forces move them.

It sets the number of passes used to resolve velocity constraints to 20 for each monofoot body per physics step. Velocity constraints are the collision and joint rules that limit how the simulated bodies can move. It also sets the knee body's rotational inertia, how hard it is to spin, to 0.5 on each axis, in kilogram-metres squared when the rig uses metre-based physics units. The ball body's maximum angular speed is set to 300 radians per second. These are startup settings on the physics bodies, not live measurements of their movement.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.OnUpdate
member.summary: Updates arm placement, hands, monofoot contact shapes and the rig's automatic fall or recovery checks during a frame.

remarks.para: This is the per-frame rig hook, separate from the fixed-duration physics steps. It returns if the pelvis Rigidbody is sleeping, meaning Unity has paused an idle body. It first adjusts the collarbone rotations from the current shoulder and chest positions; that adjustment occurs before the shutdown check.

On the active path it updates both hands and their finger contact shapes, adjusts the monofoot colliders, and updates the physical head orientation relative to the eye-gaze direction. A collider is the invisible shape that determines which surfaces touch.

Without an assigned seat it also checks whether the rig should move between upright and active-ragdoll states. The choice uses either the manual fall control or the configured automatic fall/recovery checks, including body tilt and rotation speed. The hook works from the current rig pose and inputs; it does not simply replay a startup pose.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.PhysicalLegs
member.summary: Returns both separate legs to force-driven physics movement and restores their normal joint constraints and collision layers.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body Unity simulates with forces and collisions. This method makes the upper-leg, lower-leg and foot bodies dynamic instead of kinematic. Kinematic means game code places the bodies; dynamic means the physics simulation moves them. Their physics joints, connections between body parts, regain the normal locked or limited movements, and their configured player collision layers are restored.

The native leg operation restores linear and angular velocities from the difference between each body's current pose and its saved pose over Unity's fixed physics timestep. Linear velocity is in world metres per second; angular velocity is in world radians per second. Although this wrapper passes the pelvis velocity, that value does not supply the restored velocities in this build.
It then clears the rig's legs-kinematic flag and updates both legs' joint targets from the rig's body transforms. Ball-locomotion mode is changed separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.ProcessSlotContainer(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer)
member.summary: Fits one inventory-slot container to an avatar body region and assigns the physics body that the slot follows.

remarks.para: A slot container holds inventory attachment points, such as holsters. The container's bodyRegion chooses the torso or a left/right upper or lower arm or leg. A transform stores the container's position and orientation. Its parent is the body segment it belongs under, so its local pose follows that segment. This method changes its transform parent to the corresponding rig segment, calculates its position from the avatar's stored body shape, applies a local orientation, and assigns its root Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is the simulated body that lets the attachment follow physical movement.

For torso slots it uses regionY as a dimensionless position along the torso and degreesFromCenter as an angle around it, in degrees. The hardDimentions values describe the container's width and height in metres; the placement calculation accounts for that space when fitting it against the avatar's body shape. Left and right limb regions mirror the local orientation as needed.

The result is a local position in Unity distance units, normally metres, and a local orientation relative to the chosen body segment. Changing the slot's configuration fields alone does not run this fitting calculation; call this method or SetBodySlot to apply the fit to an already configured rig.

member.param: Avatar whose already stored body dimensions and shape are used to fit the slot.
Existing inventory-slot container whose parent, local pose and root physics body will be updated.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.RagdollRig
member.summary: Switches the rig to physical legs and ragdoll-style hand contact while turning off rolling-ball support.

remarks.para: It first makes both legs physical and updates their joint targets, then disables ball locomotion. Physical legs are moved by Unity's simulated forces and collisions. Each hand receives its natural range of motion and is set to apply its forces through its joint, the physical connection between body parts.

It selects the natural friction materials on the torso, legs, arms and hands. It also re-enables the hand-versus-body and hand-versus-hand collider pairs changed by this method. A collider is an invisible contact shape. The false ignore flags here mean that those contacts are allowed, so the hands can physically meet the ragdoll body.

Torso collision sounds are enabled after the contact changes. This method prepares the active ragdoll configuration; ShutdownRig is the separate operation that marks the controllers shut down and weakens their drives.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.Reset
member.summary: Finds or creates the rig's body-transform references and fills in the hand and monofoot component references.

remarks.para: A transform is an object's position and orientation record. This is a setup helper. The base rig operation finds its named body transforms and creates missing transform objects. PhysicsRig then finds the hand components for the left and right hand objects and adds them if needed.

For the already assigned monofoot knee and ball objects, it finds or adds their Rigidbody components and saves those component references. The two monofoot objects must already be assigned. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that lets an object participate in simulated movement.

Despite its name, this method is not a command to return an already moving body to its rest pose or reset joint limits. Use the rig's pose or teleport operations when the intended change is physical placement.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.ResetHands(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Handedness)
member.summary: Starts a short, staged reset of the selected physical hand or hands, detaching their current attachments first.

remarks.para: The reset runs as a coroutine, a routine that can pause and continue on a later update. Only one hand-reset coroutine can run on this rig at a time; a call made while one is already running does not start another reset or add the other hand.

Attachment joints are physics connections that hold a hand to an object or attachment. The selected hands detach their held objects and attachment joints immediately. After waiting for a fixed physics update, their hand bodies' collision detection is disabled and each physical hand's ResetHand operation is called. The coroutine then waits for a configured 0.1 seconds of Unity game time before restoring collision detection and clearing its running handle.

The wait ends when Unity schedules the coroutine to resume, so the total reset is not guaranteed to take exactly 0.1 seconds of wall-clock time. For Both, each stage processes the right hand before the left. The method returns after starting the routine, before the later reset stages finish.

member.param: Left, Right or Both selects the hands to detach and reset.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Fits the physical body, contact shapes, joint controllers, mass split and inventory slots to the supplied avatar's stored measurements.

remarks.para: The avatar supplies the prepared body measurements and mass values. This method stores it as the rig's current avatar and sends those values to the torso, arms, legs and soft-body setup operations. A collider is an invisible contact shape; a physics joint connects body parts and guides or limits their movement. The calibration calls fit those shapes, joint settings and grip attachment points to the new body.

It requests a monofoot ball radius from the avatar's eye height in metres and applies it immediately if ball locomotion is enabled. When replacing an existing avatar, it first scales the current vertical knee-joint target by the new eye height divided by the old eye height, so that target carries across the size change. It also updates shoulder and palm attachment positions, actual body masses in kilograms, and inventory-slot placement.

If the avatar has a valid surface-data reference that can be resolved, the method requests that asset and supplies a callback, a function invoked when the load completes. That callback assigns the returned surface data to the rig's impact-property components. Starting the load does not mean its result has already been applied when SetAvatar returns. The method also assigns the avatar's impact properties or their fallback on its immediate path.

Some joint operations save base controller settings that later update hooks apply using current support. This is an avatar setup operation, not a fresh calculation of the avatar's original skeleton measurements.

member.param: Avatar to assign, with its body measurements, masses and asset references already prepared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetBodyMassDistribution
member.summary: Writes the torso, arm, leg and monofoot body masses for the rig's current mass-distribution state.

remarks.para: All masses are in kilograms. Let M be the assigned avatar's total mass and L be its stored mass for one whole leg. Each arm receives 0.07317 times M, including the hand. The combined monofoot knee-and-ball mass is 0.02 times M in Natural, 0.12 times M in NaturalMono, 0.34 times M in StableMono, and twice L in Seated.

The ball receives 56.25 percent of that combined monofoot mass and its knee receives 43.75 percent. The torso receives M minus both arm masses minus the monofoot mass; Natural additionally subtracts both separate leg masses. For example, with M equal to 100 kg and StableMono selected, the monofoot gets 34 kg: 19.125 kg on the ball and 14.875 kg on the knee. Each arm gets 7.317 kg and the torso gets 51.366 kg.

The torso helper splits its assigned amount among the head, neck, chest, spine and pelvis. Each arm helper splits its amount among upper arm, lower arm and hand. Both separate legs are assigned L through their leg helpers in every state. Kinematic legs, which game code places instead of forces moving them, remain outside normal force-driven simulation; do not add every stored Rigidbody mass to infer the currently simulated total. A Rigidbody is one body Unity simulates.

The helper calls also rebuild rotational inertia settings, which control how hard each body is to spin. The method applies the already selected state; CheckBodyMassDistribution is the separate operation that chooses a state from current support.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetBodySlot(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: Refits the rig manager's inventory and body-slot containers to the supplied avatar.

remarks.para: The method walks both slot-container arrays owned by the rig manager's inventory and calls ProcessSlotContainer for each entry. Each container is an existing group of inventory attachment points, such as holsters.

The fitting operation selects a body segment, changes the container's parent and local pose, and assigns the simulated body it follows. Local means relative to that body segment rather than a fixed location in the world. Positions follow the avatar's stored shape in Unity distance units, normally metres; orientation configuration uses degrees.
Use this after changing the avatar dimensions or slot placement settings when those changes need to be applied to all configured slots.

member.param: Avatar whose stored body shape and dimensions should be used for both sets of slot containers.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetBodyState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState)
member.summary: Applies the leg, ball-support and shutdown operations required by the supplied body-state transition.

remarks.para: From OnFoot to ActiveRagdoll it calls RagdollRig. From OnFoot to Ragdoll it calls RagdollRig and then ShutdownRig. RagdollRig changes the leg and contact configuration; ShutdownRig separately marks the controllers shut down and weakens their drives.

From ActiveRagdoll to OnFoot it calls UnRagdollRig, and from ActiveRagdoll to Ragdoll it calls ShutdownRig. From Ragdoll to OnFoot it calls UnRagdollRig first and TurnOnRig second; from Ragdoll to ActiveRagdoll it calls TurnOnRig.

Transitions from Seated, and transitions whose destination is Seated, have no matching action here. This method does not assign the rig manager's current body-state value. The two arguments describe the transition to apply; passing a destination alone does not establish the correct previous state.

member.param: Requested destination state: OnFoot, Seated, ActiveRagdoll or Ragdoll.
State the rig is transitioning from, used to select the necessary operations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetFootballSize(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a monofoot ball radius based on avatar eye height, for the later collider-resizing operation to apply.

remarks.para: The football is the rig's rolling ground-support sphere. The requested radius in metres is eyeHeight times 0.055 times max(mult, 1.05). eyeHeight is the current avatar's stored height from its floor reference to its eyes, in metres. mult is a scale factor with no units, and values below 1.05 use 1.05 instead.
For an eye height of 1.6 metres and mult 1.3, the request is a radius of 0.1144 metres, or 11.44 centimetres. This is a radius, so the ball's diameter would be twice that.

The method only stores the request. UpdateFootballRadius performs the actual resize, and UpdateMonofootColliders retries a differing request while ball locomotion is enabled. A checked growth request can remain unapplied if nearby geometry blocks it, so the requested radius and the collider's current radius can differ.

member.param: Dimensionless radius multiplier. The effective minimum is 1.05.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetFrictionLow
member.summary: Selects the rig's low-friction contact materials on the torso, legs, arms and hands.

remarks.para: A physics material supplies the friction values used when invisible collider shapes touch. Less friction generally lets those body parts slide more easily against another surface; the actual result depends on the configured materials.

The torso's contact shapes and all three contact shapes on each separate leg receive their low-friction material. Upper arms, lower arms and the main hand shapes receive the hand system's low-friction material, while finger shapes keep its natural material.

This method changes the player's body materials. It does not resize the monofoot or assign a material to its rolling ground sphere. Each body helper can return early if its representative collider already has the selected material, so the method is a mode switch rather than a repair pass for every individually edited collider.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetFrictionNatural
member.summary: Selects the rig's natural contact materials on the torso, arms, hands and most separate-leg shapes.

remarks.para: A physics material supplies friction settings for a collider, the invisible shape used for contacts. The natural material is the rig's configured material for ordinary physical body contact, including its ragdoll configuration.

The torso's shapes and the upper and lower segments of each leg receive their natural material. The end shape on each leg, its foot, still receives the leg system's low-friction material. Both arms and all hand and finger shapes receive their hand system's natural material.

The rolling monofoot ground sphere is not changed by this method. Each helper may skip its assignments if its representative collider already has the natural material, so changing another collider by hand is not guaranteed to be undone by a repeated call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SetKneePelvisLimit(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the monofoot knee-to-pelvis joint's vertical travel range and rescales its existing vertical target to that range.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects two simulated body parts and limits or guides their relative movement. This method sets the linear travel limit to the half-range (maxCrouchMeters - minCrouchMeters) / 2. Both inputs are distances in metres for the monofoot's vertical crouch range, not changes to headset height.

The centre is minCrouchMeters plus that half-range, in metres. It saves the requested ball radius minus that centre, also in metres, for UpdateKnee. The requested radius is the saved resize request and can differ from the actual collider radius. It also rescales the current joint target's Y component by the new half-range divided by the old linear limit. The X and Z target components are kept. For example, a range from 0.3 to 1.3 metres has a half-range of 0.5 metres and a centre of 0.8 metres.

Changing this constraint does not instantly place the pelvis at either bound. The joint solver and later target updates determine the body's movement. Supply an ordered range on a configured joint with an existing nonzero linear limit; this method does not validate or repair those values.

member.param: Lower distance bound of the monofoot's vertical crouch range, in metres.
Upper distance bound of that range, in metres.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.ShutdownRig
member.summary: Marks the rig and its body controllers shut down, weakens their drives and clears active pose targets.

remarks.para: The rig's shutdown flag is set first, followed by shutdown settings on the torso, hands and legs. The method reduces torso and arm drive strengths, clears their targets, and removes arm-support drive force. A drive is the spring-and-damping push that guides a physics joint, a connection between simulated body parts.

The shutdown flag makes active update paths skip their usual pose-driving work. This does not turn the body into a frozen object: the Rigidbody simulation and physical contacts can continue. A Rigidbody is the component Unity moves with gravity, forces and collisions.

RagdollRig separately changes legs, ball support, hand motion and contact materials. SetBodyState calls both operations, in that order, when moving from OnFoot to the fully shut-down Ragdoll state. TurnOnRig clears the shutdown flags so normal updates can resume.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.SwitchStepState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.StepState)
member.summary: Changes the monofoot stepping state and adjusts the knee-to-pelvis joint for rolling, stepping, hanging or climbing.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the shared rolling ground support. Its knee-to-pelvis physics joint connects that support to the body. Before saving the new state, this method performs cleanup for the old state, such as clearing a return-step flag or restoring the usual horizontal drives after hanging or climbing.

Entering NeutralRoll locks horizontal X and Z joint movement. HoldStep and ReturnStep allow horizontal movement; HoldStep also applies strong horizontal holding drives. Dangle allows movement with weaker drives for hanging. Climbing and Foothold allow movement with stronger support drives. A drive is the spring-and-damping push toward a target.

Leaving Dangle or Climbing can reset the horizontal target from the current pelvis and monofoot geometry; leaving Climbing also recentres the protective sphere's horizontal offset. The method writes the new step-state value after these constraint and target changes. Calling it with the current state can still run those operations; it has no same-state early return.

member.param: Destination monofoot state: NeutralRoll, HoldStep, ReturnStep, Dangle, Climbing or Foothold.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.Teleport(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Moves the rig's body parts by a world-space offset and rotates them around the rig's centre of pressure, then synchronizes their physics bodies.

remarks.para: displace contains a translation and a rotation change. Its position is an offset in world metres, not an absolute destination. Its rotation is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation, describing the turn to apply. The pivot is the existing centre of pressure, the rig's ground or climbing support reference point.

A direct child transform stores the position and orientation of an object placed immediately under the rig in Unity's hierarchy. For each direct child transform of the rig, the method translates the support pivot by the offset and rotates the child's position around that translated pivot. It applies the rotation change to the child's orientation, then copies the resulting transforms to the configured torso, arm, leg, monofoot and soft-body physics bodies. With an identity rotation, which means no turn, an offset of (0, 1, 0) moves those body parts one metre up.

With zeroVelocity false, this method leaves the stored velocities alone. With true it clears the torso bodies' linear and angular velocities, both monofoot bodies' linear velocities, the monofoot ball's angular velocity, both hands', forearms' and upper arms' linear and angular velocities, and the listed soft-body velocities. It also clears the rig's whole-body and pelvis velocity/acceleration readings. The monofoot knee body's angular velocity and the separate anatomical leg velocities are not cleared by this method, so true does not guarantee every part is motionless.

member.param: World translation offset in metres and rotation change around the current support pivot.
Whether to clear the specific body velocities and rig-motion readings described in the remarks. The default is false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.TeleportToPose
member.summary: Snaps the configured torso, arms and monofoot to positions and orientations taken from the rig manager's prepared virtual pose.

remarks.para: The virtual rig is the target body pose already built from tracking and avatar setup; this method directly places the torso and arms from that prepared pose instead of gradually pulling them toward it through physics joints. A physics joint is a connection that normally guides or limits two simulated parts.

It directly writes the configured torso, arm and monofoot Rigidbody poses and the matching body transforms. The physical chest uses the virtual neck's position and the virtual chest's rotation. The monofoot is placed from the virtual rig root, with the current ball radius lifting the ball's centre; it does not use the target anatomical feet. This method does not copy anatomical-leg poses. A Rigidbody is the body Unity simulates. Placement is in world metres and world orientation. The monofoot is the shared rolling ground support, distinct from the target left and right feet.

The method uses the virtual rig's already calculated body positions rather than reading raw controller or headset input. It does not clear the physical bodies' linear or angular velocities, so existing movement can continue after the snap.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.TurnOnRig
member.summary: Clears shutdown flags on the rig, torso, hands and legs so their active update paths can run again.

remarks.para: Shutdown is a controller state that makes the rig skip normal pose-driving updates. This method clears that state on the PhysicsRig and its torso, both physical hands and both physical legs.

It does not immediately recalculate drive strengths or change the ball-support, collision-material or leg-simulation configuration. Subsequent active update hooks apply the controller settings for the current configuration. SetBodyState uses this after UnRagdollRig when returning from a shut-down ragdoll to OnFoot.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UnRagdollRig
member.summary: Restores game-controlled legs, rolling-ball support and the active hand-contact configuration after a ragdoll.

remarks.para: It first makes both separate legs kinematic, meaning game code places them instead of physics forces moving them, then enables ball locomotion. The monofoot is the shared rolling support used in that mode.

Both hands receive their active range of motion, stop routing forces through the ragdoll hand-joint setting, and have their arm-support drives cleared for the active system to update. A physics joint connects simulated body parts; a drive pushes that connection toward a target. The method selects low-friction body materials and restores the specified hand-versus-body and hand-versus-hand collision-ignore settings, while several forearm-versus-torso contact pairs remain allowed.

Torso collision sounds are disabled after these changes. The rig's shutdown flag is handled separately: when returning from the shut-down Ragdoll state, SetBodyState calls this first and TurnOnRig afterward so the active updates can resume.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UpdateFootballRadius(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Applies the requested rolling-ball radius and moves the monofoot support bodies to keep the ball's bottom at the same height.

remarks.para: The football is the rig's rolling ground-support sphere. The method compares its actual collider radius with the requested radius, both in metres. It resizes the protective sphere above the ball, updates the ball radius and saved circumference, and recalculates the monofoot knee-to-pelvis travel range.

When runCheck is true, growth is tested before any resize is applied. The two sphere-overlap checks use the configured football collision mask, ignore trigger-only colliders, and leave a 0.005-metre margin inside the requested ball and protective sphere. If either check finds an overlap, the method returns with the old sizes and positions. Shrinking skips these checks even when runCheck is true. With runCheck false, growth is applied without this obstruction test.

On a successful resize it shifts both the monofoot knee and ball upward by requested radius minus old radius, in world metres. For example, growth from 0.10 to 0.12 metres moves them up 0.02 metres while keeping the ball's bottom at its previous world height. The saved circumference becomes two times pi times the new radius, measured in metres, for later rolling-motion calculations.
A request is therefore not proof of a successful resize. UpdateMonofootColliders can retry it later while ball locomotion is enabled.

member.param: Whether to reject growth that fails the two overlap tests. It has no obstruction-check effect on shrinking, and defaults to false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UpdateKnee(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Updates the monofoot knee-to-pelvis vertical drive and target so it can support the body at the requested crouch offset.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the rolling support below the player. Its knee-to-pelvis physics joint connects that support to the pelvis; the joint's vertical drive is a spring-and-damping push toward a target. This method adjusts the live drive strength using the actual pelvis height above the ball and the avatar's stored pelvis height, both in metres.

feetTar is an added target offset in metres along the joint's Y axis. The target is calculated as targetY = cachedOffset - actualRadius + feetTar + ((avatarMass - kneeMass - ballMass) times gravityMagnitude) / spring - climbingOffset. All distance terms, including targetY, are in metres along the joint's Y axis. cachedOffset is the requested ball radius minus the crouch-range centre saved by SetKneePelvisLimit; that request can differ from actualRadius, the live ball collider's radius. avatarMass is the assigned avatar's stored total mass in kilograms. kneeMass and ballMass are the current masses of the two monofoot Rigidbodies, also in kilograms; a Rigidbody is a body moved by Unity physics. gravityMagnitude is the absolute vertical gravity in metres per second squared. spring is the joint's live vertical spring strength in Newtons per metre. The gravity term is therefore a distance in metres that compensates for the mass above the monofoot. climbingOffset is the stored climbing correction in metres: a positive value lowers the target Y, and a negative value raises it. A larger positive feetTar increases the joint's target Y by that many metres; it does not instantly lift the physical foot or pelvis by that amount.

The method derives the target's Y velocity as the new target minus the previous target, in metres, divided by Unity's fixed physics timestep, in seconds. The result is metres per second in the joint's axes. It preserves the target's X and Z components.
In this build the supplied deltaTime argument is ignored: the velocity calculation reads Unity's fixedDeltaTime directly. A different argument value therefore does not change the timestep used here.

member.param: Extra vertical joint-target offset in metres, combined with the stored crouch range and other support corrections.
Nominal fixed-step duration in seconds. This build ignores this argument and uses Unity's configured fixed timestep.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UpdateLadderInfo(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LadderInfo)
member.summary: Stores the supplied ladder-rung information and signals ladder contact for the next locomotion update.

remarks.para: The entire LadderInfo value is copied, including its source, rung transform, rung count and number, width and radius. The source and counts describe the ladder interaction; the transform supplies the rung's position and axes, while its width and radius are stored distances in metres.

The method then sets the rig's on-ladder indicator. This is a contact request for locomotion processing, not a test that a hand currently holds the rung. The indicator requests a ladder fade of 1. The fade is a blend normally between 0 and 1 with no physical units: 0 removes LadderForce's correction and 1 allows its full strength. ApplyFeetForce eases it toward the indicator by up to 4 per second of physics time, then clears the indicator. Without a refreshed contact request its next target is 0. Continued ladder contact must supply fresh information to keep requesting it.
No force is applied and no climbing target is calculated by this method. LadderForce uses the saved rung geometry when called.

member.param: Rung interaction information to copy into the rig; its rung transform must be valid for later rung-based calculations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UpdateMonofootColliders
member.summary: Fits the monofoot's connecting capsule to the current pelvis position and retries a requested ball resize.

remarks.para: The monofoot is the rig's shared rolling support below the player. A capsule collider is an invisible pill-shaped contact volume. While ball locomotion is enabled, this method aims that capsule from its base toward a point 0.05 metres below the pelvis along the pelvis's own up/down axis.

The capsule's orientation follows that world-space direction, and its height and local centre are adjusted to cover the distance while accounting for its current radius. It therefore changes as the pelvis moves or tilts relative to the monofoot.

If the requested football radius differs from the rolling sphere's actual radius, it calls UpdateFootballRadius with growth checks enabled. Nearby geometry can prevent growth, leaving the request pending for a later call. With ball locomotion disabled, this method returns without changing these colliders.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.UpdateTotalDerivatives
member.summary: Recalculates whole-body linear velocity and acceleration from the torso, arms and monofoot bodies.

remarks.para: It adds the linear momenta reported by the torso and both arms, then adds the monofoot knee and ball masses times their velocities. Momentum is mass in kilograms times velocity in metres per second. The resulting vector is divided by the assigned avatar's total mass in kilograms to produce wholeBodyVelocity in world metres per second.

It then computes wholeBodyAccel as the new wholeBodyVelocity minus its previous value, divided by Unity's fixed physics timestep in seconds. The result is world metres per second squared. For example, changing from 1 to 2 metres per second along an axis over a 0.02-second step produces 50 metres per second squared along that axis.

This calculation has no separate leg-momentum contribution and does not calculate angular momentum. It uses the avatar's stored total mass as its divisor rather than adding up every body's current Rigidbody mass. A Rigidbody is one body Unity simulates. OnAfterFixedUpdate calls this after reading the completed physics step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PlayerDamageReceiver.ReceiveAttack(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Converts an attack's hit position and surface normal into this body part's local coordinates, then sends the attack and to the assigned health component.
member.param: The attack payload containing damage amount, type, impact direction, hit origin, and surface normal (the direction perpendicular to the contacted surface at the hit point). Supply origin and normal in world coordinates; the method converts those two fields to this receiver's local coordinates in the copy sent to health.

remarks.para: World coordinates describe positions and directions relative to the scene. Local coordinates describe them relative to this body part's position and rotation. The receiver uses its Transform, Unity's position, rotation, and scale information, to convert attack.origin as a point and attack.normal as a direction. The point conversion includes scale; the normal conversion uses rotation without applying position or scale. The separate attack.direction field is forwarded unchanged, along with the damage, type, and other attack information.

For example, with no rotation and scale 1, a receiver at world position (10, 0, 0) converts an origin at (11, 0, 0) to local position (1, 0, 0). Unity's world distance units normally represent metres. With scale 1, that example is a point one metre along the receiver's local X axis. A scaled body part changes the local position values, so they are not always the same distances as the incoming world values.

The method calls health.OnReceivedDamage with the converted attack and the current bodyPart setting. It does not test whether this receiver is enabled, so a direct call still forwards an attack when the component's enabled switch is off. The health reference must already be assigned; the method does not look for one or quietly skip a missing reference.

The normal Health handler, also used by Player_Health, ignores attacks marked backFacing. For a living player, it requests damage equal to D × S, where D is the incoming attack.damage in game health points and S is a unitless body-part multiplier: 4.1 for Head and 0.6 for every other part. Thus D = 10 requests 41 points for Head or 6 points for Chest. Health rules decide the final health change; forwarding an attack alone does not guarantee that many points are lost.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.ApplyKillDamage
member.summary: Sends damage equal to maximum health plus 10 health points.

remarks.para: For example, a maximum of 100 means this sends 110 health points of damage. It follows the normal damage and health-mode rules: Mortal mode can start the death-save sequence, instant-death mode starts its own death animation, and Invincible mode does not start either fatal sequence.
This is not a direct call to Death. It does not promise an immediate kill, slow motion in every mode, or a fatal result if another caller has raised current health above the amount sent.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.CoBrightenDeathSave
member.summary: Creates the recovery sequence that reopens the damage overlay over one scaled second.

remarks.para: A shader is the material's drawing program. The renderer is the component that draws the overlay. A material property block buffers drawing settings; Renderer.SetPropertyBlock applies those settings to that renderer.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. This method creates its iterator, the object that remembers its progress; calling it alone does not start the sequence. Start it with StartCoroutine. LifeSavingDamgeDealt and UpdateHealth use it after recovery or cancellation of an instant-death sequence.

It reads the starting shut-eyes shader value, then blends that value toward 0 once per frame and applies the material property block to the overlay renderer. Progress is elapsed scaled seconds divided by 1 second, limited to 0 through 1. Slow motion therefore stretches the real-world wait. It writes shutEyesID, not brightenID, and does not itself award health or check a death-save score.

member.returns: An iterator to run with StartCoroutine; creating it does not change the overlay yet.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.CoFadeVignette
member.summary: Creates the sequence that shows damage according to current health, then removes the overlay after health reaches its maximum.

remarks.para: A shader is the material's drawing program. The renderer is the component that draws the overlay. A material property block buffers drawing settings; Renderer.SetPropertyBlock applies those settings to that renderer.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. Calling this method creates an iterator; StartCoroutine runs it. On first execution, isFadingVignette becomes true before the overlay renderer is enabled. While current health is below maximum, each update recalculates its shape settings and blends darkRed toward brightRed using current health divided by maximum health, a unitless fraction limited to 0 through 1.

The inner shader setting ranges from 0.7 at zero health to 0.35 at full health; the outer setting ranges from 0.5 to 0.15. These are shader control values, not proven distances in meters or pixels. Once health reaches maximum, it starts from 0.35 and 0.15 and moves each toward 0 by 0.01 per update. Both phases wait routineTickRate scaled seconds between updates, so they can take longer in real time during slow motion.

On normal completion it clears isFadingVignette before disabling the renderer. Stopping the coroutine early does not run that final cleanup, so the flag alone is not proof that a sequence is still running. This method does not regenerate health.

member.returns: An iterator to run with StartCoroutine; creating it does not enable or update the overlay yet.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.CoWaitAndGoToRespawn
member.summary: Creates the sequence that teleports to the checkpoint first, then respawns after about one unscaled second, with a hibernation hold.

remarks.para: The physics rig is the player's simulated body. Its physics entity groups the objects making up that body. Hibernation temporarily freezes or sleeps their physics; checking IsHibernating observes the reported state and does not itself wake the body.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. Calling this method creates its iterator; start it with StartCoroutine, for example StartCoroutine(CoWaitAndGoToRespawn()). Death selects this path when reloadLevelOnDeath is false. Creating the iterator alone does not teleport anyone.

On first execution it asks TimeManager for its normal time-scale target, teleports through the inherited TeleportToCheckpoint routine, and starts an elapsed timer at zero. Each later frame adds unscaled delta time: seconds between frames unaffected by slow motion. While the physics rig entity reports IsHibernating, it caps that timer at 0.9 seconds. When the stored timer reaches at least 1 second, the next execution calls Respawn and finishes. Prolonged hibernation can therefore postpone respawn beyond one real-world second.

Respawn restores full health through SetFullHealth. The checkpoint teleport needs an initialized rig and checkpoint pose; this sequence also requires the rig's physics entity. It does not wait one second before the initial teleport.

The state-machine object remembers which step the sequence reached, and MoveNext runs its next piece. To change the sequence itself, patch its state-machine MoveNext method, Player_Health._CoWaitAndGoToRespawn_d__84.MoveNext. Its state values are:

item.description: First entry. Requests the normal time-scale target, teleports to the checkpoint, and sets the elapsed timer to zero.
Continues after yielding a frame. Checks the elapsed timer, adds unscaled frame time, applies the hibernation cap, and yields again unless the timer has already reached one second.
Running or done. Entry states other than 0 or 1 return false.

member.returns: An iterator to run with StartCoroutine; it remembers the elapsed time between frames.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.CoWaitAndReloadScene
member.summary: Creates the sequence that waits one scaled second, then requests a reload through SceneStreamer. selects this path in Death.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. Calling this method only creates its iterator; StartCoroutine runs it. Death checks reloadLevelOnDeath before choosing this sequence. Once started, the sequence itself does not recheck that flag.

The wait uses WaitForSeconds(1), so slow motion can make it take longer than one real-world second.
