member.summary: Marks the player dead, reports the death, then starts the selected reload or checkpoint-respawn sequence.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues on later frames.

First the inherited Death routine stops this component's coroutines, clears deathIsImminent, sets alive to false, and calls the death-vocal routine. When the inherited _testRagdollOnDeath setting is enabled, it also requests the rig's Ragdoll body mode. A ragdoll is the character body driven by physics; this request alone does not prove the physical transition has completed. Only after that does OnPlayerDeath run. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; these callbacks see the changed alive and deathIsImminent flags.

After the callbacks return, reloadLevelOnDeath is read: true starts a one-scaled-second wait followed by a reload request; false starts immediate checkpoint teleport followed by the unscaled respawn wait. A death callback can therefore change the flag before this choice. This method starts the later sequence rather than waiting for a completed reload or respawn.
Clearing deathIsImminent here does not raise OnDeathImminent(false). The checked Death body does not instantiate fx_death, and it does not clear every private coroutine flag or handle.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.Dying(System.Single)
member.summary: Handles fatal health according to the current mode, including the Mortal death-save window and the separate instant-death animation.

remarks.para: Scaled seconds are seconds on the game clock, affected by the game's time scale; during slow motion they pass more slowly than real-world seconds.

In Mortal mode, first entry sets deathIsImminent to true, optionally requests slow motion, and starts the named low-pass timing routine. OnDeathImminent(true) then calls listeners before the old regeneration, ordinary vignette and death routines are stopped and the new death animation is started. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Those listeners see the flag already set, but cannot assume the new animation has initialized currDeathTime yet.

The animation begins with deathTimeAmount scaled seconds as its duration denominator. Each frame adds scaled frame seconds divided by currDeathTime to unitless progress; when progress reaches 1, it calls Death only if health is still at or below zero. An additional Dying call during an existing Mortal window subtracts deathTimeReduction from that denominator only when it is greater than 2 seconds. This speeds future progress; it is not subtraction from a remaining-time countdown.

In instant-death mode, the first call sets isInstaDying and then deathIsImminent, calls the dying-vocal routine, sets current health to -1, and starts the animation with instaDeathTimeAmount. That branch does not request slow motion or raise OnDeathImminent(true). Further calls return while isInstaDying is true. Invincible mode instead sets current health to zero and starts no fatal animation.

The Mortal recovery path is OnPuppetDeath calling LifeSavingDamgeDealt. The checked path does not test playerDamageScore or whether the player caused that puppet's death. Dying itself does not check for zero health before starting a sequence; its normal caller supplies that condition. Initialized audio and vignette references are required for the sequences that use them.

member.param: Damage supplied by the caller; this override does not use the value to choose or time the fatal sequence.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.LifeSavingDamgeDealt
member.summary: Performs a death save: clears imminent death, restores half maximum health, and starts visual recovery and regeneration.

remarks.para: wait_Regen_t is the configured delay before regeneration begins, measured in scaled game-clock seconds; slow motion makes that delay take longer in real time.

First it increments playerDeathSaves and clears deathIsImminent. It requests TimeManager's normal time-scale target, replaces the named low-pass timing routine, and calls the recovery-vocal routine. OnDeathImminent(false) runs next, before the old death routine is stopped and before health is restored. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; these listeners see the incremented count and cleared flag, but may still see fatal health.

After the callbacks, it stops the death routine, starts the shut-eyes recovery animation, and writes current health = maximum health × 0.5. Here maximum health is measured in health points and 0.5 is a unitless half-health multiplier: a maximum of 100 restores 50. It starts the damage-overlay sequence, replaces regeneration, sets regenerating to true before the regeneration wait, and starts regeneration using wait_Regen_t.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. The animations and regeneration continue after this method returns. This public method does not itself check alive, health mode, score, puppet attribution, or whether death was imminent; OnPuppetDeath supplies its own imminent-death/mode check. Calling it directly still increments the count, and it does not set alive to true.
If regeneration enters or resumes its healing phase while alive is false and current health is below maximum, it loops without pausing and can block the game.

remarks.para: A shader is the material's drawing program. A blend shape is a stored alternate mesh shape; weight 0 requests the unmodified base shape.

This method stores that renderer in vigRend, parents the clone to the main camera, and sets local position to (0, 0, 0), local scale to (1, 1, 1), and local rotation to identity, meaning no extra rotation relative to the camera.

It creates a new MaterialPropertyBlock, a buffer of shader settings for this renderer, resets four float settings to zero, and sets mesh blend-shape number 0 to weight 0. It instantiates the existing template rather than generating a new mesh or material definition.

Awake, Unity's initialization callback, arranges this setup through the level-load callback or a delayed call. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. remarks.para: The inherited route ignores attacks marked backFacing. For other attacks, it sends health damage only while alive: attack.damage × 4.1 for Head, or attack.damage × 0.6 for any other body-part value. attack.damage is an amount in health points; 4.1 and 0.6 are unitless multipliers. For an attack amount of 10, that means 41 head damage or 6 damage elsewhere.

The optional inherited visual-damage path is called separately before the alive check. The Player_Health override copies the attack payload and delegates to the base routine; it does not add collision multipliers or an impact layer-mask filter. The resulting TAKEDAMAGE call supplies the player damage report and score update.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called when an event occurs. The returned delegate holds the combined list of callbacks; combining them does not call the routines or make the player die. Assign the result back to the event, normally with +=, to subscribe.

The result keeps the left-hand callbacks first, then appends the right-hand callbacks in their existing order. Repeated registrations are retained: combining [A, B] with [C] gives [A, B, C], and adding A twice keeps two copies. Combining the lists does not run any callback.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called when an event occurs. This returns the callback list after delegate removal; it does not invoke the routines or change the player's health. Assign the result back to the event, normally with -=, to unsubscribe. The result can be null; some empty-list results remain non-null in this implementation.

For a callback list containing at least two entries, subtracting one callback removes its last matching occurrence; earlier copies remain. For two callback lists, it normally removes the last matching consecutive sequence. With no match, the source is returned unchanged. This runtime also has a special case: a single callback minus a list containing that callback returns null. For example, single A minus [B, A] returns null. Removing independently built matching lists can instead return a non-null delegate holding an empty callback list. For example, [A, A] minus [A] leaves [A], so one -= does not undo two += registrations.

Removing a callback list can leave a list containing only one callback. In this implementation, subtracting that matching single callback next throws InvalidOperationException, an error saying this removal operation is invalid for that stored list. For example, [A, B, C] minus the list [B, C] leaves the one-entry list [A]; subtracting single A from that result then throws instead of returning null.

member.returns: The delegate after removal. The result can be null; some empty-list results remain non-null in this implementation.

remarks.para: A shader is the material's drawing program. The renderer is the component that draws the overlay. The four controls are brightenID, shutEyesID, innerID and outerID. Their integer IDs select shader properties; zero here is the float value written to each selected property, not a replacement property ID.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.STARTDATA
member.summary: Sets full current health and the alive flag, then moves this component's scene object to a selected spawn-point position and rotation.

remarks.para: It first copies maximum health to current health, sets regenerating to false, and sets alive to true. It then reads spawn_points. An empty array skips the move; a null array or a null selected Transform is not handled as a harmless empty list. A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale.

Array indices start at 0, and count is the number of entries in spawn_points. With more than one entry, it chooses an integer in [0, count - 1), so the final array entry is excluded. For three entries it can choose index 0 or 1, never 2; a single-entry array selects index 0. The chosen position and rotation are world coordinates, relative to the scene rather than the player's local axes.

The move writes this component's GameObject Transform directly. A GameObject is a scene object with components attached. This body does not use the full rig checkpoint-teleport routine or instantiate prop_Hero. Unity Start uses the same initialization body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.SetFullHealth
member.summary: Stops this component's coroutines, resets the vignette float controls, clears imminent death, and restores maximum health and the alive flag.

remarks.para: The order is StopAllCoroutines, request TimeManager's normal time-scale target, ResetVigMaterial, clear deathIsImminent, then the inherited full-health reset. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames; stopping all of them also interrupts a pending reload or checkpoint-respawn sequence owned by this component.

The inherited reset writes current health to maximum, sets alive to true, restores its limb/stun values, and clears stunActive and its stored visual-hit lists. This method does not teleport the player.

It does not raise OnDeathImminent(false), clear isInstaDying, regenerating or isFadingVignette, or erase the saved coroutine handles. Those flags and handles can therefore remain stale after the routines have stopped. ResetVigMaterial clears four float values but does not explicitly disable the renderer or reset its color.

Despite the method name, this body does not check health mode. It does not enable instant death, heal the player, or start regeneration. At or above maximum health it leaves the existing sequence alone.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.StartHealthRegnerationAndVignette(System.Single)

remarks.para: It stops and replaces the vignette routine only if current health is below maximum. It stops and replaces the regeneration routine regardless of health mode or whether health is already full. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames, so this method starts the sequences and returns before their work finishes.

The regeneration wait uses scaled frame time, so a delay of 3 seconds at a constant half-speed time scale takes roughly 6 real-world seconds, with frame scheduling rounding. Once the wait finishes, regeneration sets its own regenerating flag, calculates a duration from the starting health, and increases health toward maximum while the player is alive. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.TAKEDAMAGE(System.Single)

remarks.para: wait_Regen_t is the configured delay before regeneration begins, measured in scaled game-clock seconds; slow motion makes that delay take longer in real time.

After that health processing, if death is not imminent, instant-death mode restarts the ordinary vignette when below maximum; other modes can restart the vignette and replace the regeneration routine using wait_Regen_t. A damage argument of 2.9 adds 2 to the score. This public method has no alive guard of its own, so a damage report is not proof that positive health was actually lost.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.TELEPORTONESECOND
member.summary: Starts , which teleports to the checkpoint immediately and delays the health-restoring respawn.

remarks.para: The physics rig is the player's simulated body. Its physics entity groups the objects making up that body. Hibernation temporarily freezes or sleeps their physics; checking IsHibernating observes the reported state and does not itself wake the body. Unscaled seconds measure elapsed frame time unaffected by the game's slow-motion time scale.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. This method starts it directly; no separate StartCoroutine call is needed. The sequence requests the normal time-scale target and teleports on its first execution, then waits about one unscaled second before Respawn, with a 0.9-second timer cap while the physics entity is hibernating.
The method does not check whether the player is dead or whether reloadLevelOnDeath is enabled. Its name does not mean that teleport waits one second.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.ToggleInstantDeathMode(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables instant-death mode, or restores the previously saved health mode and full current health when disabled.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues on later frames.

Passing true saves the current health mode in prevHealthMode, then selects instant death. Passing false resets the vignette float controls, writes maximum health to current health, and restores prevHealthMode. This is not necessarily Mortal mode: the saved mode can be Invincible or even instant death.

Repeated true calls overwrite the saved mode, so a second true call while already in instant death can make false restore instant death again. The false path does not stop active coroutines, clear deathIsImminent or isInstaDying, or set alive to true; it is not the same complete reset as SetFullHealth.

member.param: True saves the current mode and selects instant death; false restores that saved mode and full current health.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.UpdateHealth(System.Single)
member.summary: Adds a fraction of maximum health only while the player is alive in instant-death mode, and can cancel that mode's active death animation.

remarks.para: The added amount is perc × maximum health: perc is a unitless fraction and maximum health is measured in health points. For example, with maximum 100 and current 40, perc = 0.2 adds 20 and leaves 60. This uses fractions, so 0.2 means 20%; passing 20 does not mean 20%.

If isInstaDying is true, it clears that flag first, stops the death routine, starts the shut-eyes recovery animation, and calls the recovery-vocal routine before applying the health change. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. Even perc = 0 can therefore cancel that animation without raising health.

It calls SetFullHealth if the added amount is at least maximum health or the resulting sum exceeds maximum. A sum exactly equal to maximum takes the direct-write path instead: from 40 of 100, perc = 0.6 writes 100 without the full reset, while 0.7 calls SetFullHealth. Smaller direct gains do not clear deathIsImminent. Negative fractions are not rejected or lower-clamped and can reduce health. Outside the alive/instant-death guard it does nothing.

member.param: Unitless fraction of maximum health to add; for example, 0.25 adds one quarter of maximum health.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Plugins.IMarrowPlugin.OnMarrowPluginLoad
member.summary: Provides a registered plugin’s load-stage initialization, whose returned task the framework waits for before marking that plugin loaded.

remarks.para: A plugin is an extra piece of code that adds a feature. A callback is a method the framework calls at a particular stage. This callback receives no arguments and returns a UniTask, a completion handle for work that can finish now or continue later.

The default implementation performs no plugin-specific setup and returns UniTask.CompletedTask, which is already finished. A plugin can supply its own implementation when it needs initialization work.

When the load stage is dispatched, the framework calls this method for the registered plugin and waits for its returned work to finish before setting that plugin’s loaded flag. If the work is still pending, the framework continues when that task reports completion; this method has no fixed delay or promised number of frames. A frame is one pass through the game’s update loop.

The inspected load dispatcher skips a plugin already marked running. Its guard checks running state, rather than whether a previous load callback completed, so do not assume this method can only be called once. Calling the method yourself also does not set the framework’s loaded flag; that bookkeeping belongs to the dispatcher.

For example, an implementation can prepare lookup data and await an asset-loading operation before returning. Await means continue after that operation finishes. Return the task for the initialization work that must finish; if no work is needed, return UniTask.CompletedTask. This load callback is a separate stage from the plugin’s start, stop and game-level callbacks.

member.returns: A UniTask representing completion of this plugin’s load-stage work. The framework waits for it before marking the plugin loaded; the default implementation returns an already-completed task.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Plugins.IMarrowPluginLevelCallbacks.OnAfterLevelUnload
member.summary: Runs a plugin callback after a level unloads.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the plugin manager calls at one step of a level change. Use this no-argument callback to release plugin state tied to the level that was unloaded. It returns a UniTask, a completion signal for the callback's work. That work may finish immediately or later. The plugin manager waits for each callback's returned task before it advances to the next callback. The default interface body returns an already-completed task.

In the inspected StreamSession.Load path, the manager awaits OnBeforeLevelUnload, then waits for UnloadAllOtherScenes to finish unloading every scene except the incoming scene, and then invokes and awaits this callback. That path proceeds to crate-asset cleanup after the after-unload dispatch. This ordering describes that scene-streaming path.
For example, the MarrowCollisionManager implementation clears its managed collision-ignore counts, collider-pair map, and pending collider-removal list in this callback.

member.returns: A UniTask that completes when this plugin's after-unload work finishes; the default interface body returns an already-completed task.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Plugins.IMarrowPluginLevelCallbacks.OnBeforeLevelUnload
member.summary: Runs a plugin callback before a level unloads.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the plugin manager calls at this level-change step. Use this no-argument callback to finish plugin work while scenes from the departing level are still present. The method does not receive a LevelCrateReference or another level argument. It returns a UniTask, a completion signal for the callback's work; the plugin manager waits for each callback's returned task before it advances to the next callback. The default interface body returns an already-completed task.

In the inspected StreamSession.Load path, the incoming scene is loaded first. The manager then invokes and awaits this callback before calling UnloadAllOtherScenes. That method unloads the other scenes and awaits all of their unload tasks before returning; the manager then invokes OnAfterLevelUnload. This ordering describes that scene-streaming path.

member.returns: A UniTask that completes when this plugin's before-unload work finishes; the default interface body returns an already-completed task.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay.#ctor

remarks.para: The constructor sets secondsUntilDisable to 1.0. The wait starts when the pool calls OnPoolInitialize and uses scaled game time: slow motion makes it take longer in real time, and pausing the time scale stops the clock.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay.OnPoolInitialize

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay.Update

remarks.para: A Poolee is a component attached to a pooled GameObject. A callback is a routine the game calls at a particular lifecycle moment. After those calls return, Despawn removes the reference from _spawned and adds it to _despawned. Unless skipDisable is true, it then deactivates the GameObject. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ProjectileEmitter.Register(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData)
member.summary: Registers the projectile's spawnable crate with so that later emissions of this data can spawn it.

remarks.para: Only the data's spawnable crate reference is read; the spawn policy stored next to it plays no part in registration. The reference is handed to the shared asset pool, which looks the crate up in the asset warehouse by its barcode (the code that names an asset) and, when that barcode is not pooled yet, creates the pool — the container object that later spawns of this crate go through — then starts loading the crate's prefab (the saved template Unity loads to create a crate object). If the crate is already pooled, the call does nothing; nothing is registered twice. If the warehouse does not know the barcode, the call also finishes silently and creates nothing.

Timing: Register starts the asynchronous prefab load without exposing its completion, so the load may still be pending when Register returns. Registration itself is synchronous up to that point — when the warehouse knows the crate, the pool entry already exists by the time Register returns, even though the prefab may still be loading. Register returns no result and reports no status; besides the exceptions below, an unknown barcode or an already-pooled crate completes silently.

Pass a non-null ProjectileData whose spawnable crate reference is assigned: a null argument, or a null crate-reference object, raises an exception and registers nothing. A non-null crate-reference object with a barcode the warehouse does not know instead completes silently and creates nothing. Typical use is one call during setup before any firing — for example, TurretHeadController calls Register from Awake only in its Cartridge fireType branch (value 0); its GachaLauncher branch (value 1) registers separate Spawnable values directly with AssetSpawner. Awake is Unity’s setup routine for this script component. Unity calls it once when an active object loads the component; if the object is inactive then, Unity calls it the first time the object becomes active. Emit never performs registration itself, so data that was skipped here is not made spawnable by firing.

member.param: The projectile asset to register; only its spawnable crate reference is read.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.GetAnimContactPoint
member.summary: Samples the chosen animation and logs the selected bone’s position relative to the contact animator.

remarks.para: This component’s Get Animation Contact Point context-menu helper in the Unity editor has no return value. An Animator is Unity’s component that plays animation. The method caches contactAnimController’s current runtime controller, finds the first clip whose name exactly matches contactAnimName, and samples that clip using contactBoneRef and contactPointFrame.

The selected point is in the contact animator transform’s local coordinates: the animator’s origin and rotation define the axes, and its scale is removed. It is not a world-space contact point. These values have no separately established physical unit. If the project uses a 1 Unity unit = 1 metre scale, the coordinates are numerically metres; this method applies no separate metre conversion.

Sample time is f / R seconds, where f is contactPointFrame, a numbered animation frame, and R is the clip’s frame rate truncated to an integer in frames per second. For f = 30 and R = 30, the chosen sample is at 1 second. This animation frame number is different from a live game-update frame.

The helper also samples and logs every numbered frame before the integer total R × L, where L is clip length in seconds. Sampling changes the animator object’s pose, its arrangement of body parts; the tool does not restore the initial pose afterward. Supply a valid humanoid bone, animator, controller, matching clip and usable frame rate. A missing name logs a warning and the subsequent null-clip sample can fail.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.RemoveMusclesOfGroup(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.Group)
member.summary: Removes matching muscles and their descendants from the puppet’s controlled muscle list.

remarks.para: A muscle is a physics-controlled body part, and a physics joint is the component connecting simulated body parts. The method searches for the requested group, obtains a matching muscle’s joint and requests recursive removal, then restarts its search against the changed list.

Recursive removal includes that muscle’s descendants, so children with another group can also be removed. The call uses normal removal with animated target bones attached to their corresponding physical bodies, and does not request animation blockers. The physical parts can remain in the scene; removal does not mean deleting every body object.

For example, removing an arm group can also remove controlled hand muscles below that arm. The puppet must already be initialized, with valid muscle properties and usable joints for matching entries. If a matching entry cannot supply a joint, the search can repeat without making progress.

member.param: Exact body-part group stored in each visited muscle’s properties.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.AddThreat(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy,System.Single)
member.summary: Adds an eligible candidate’s threat score and requests aggressive behavior if that changes the sensor’s selected target.

remarks.para: trp identifies a candidate through its TriggerRefProxy, a reference that connects the candidate to its body and AI information. threat is a unitless change in targeting priority, not damage or seconds. The sensor adds it to the stored score, or to the candidate’s initial score when registering a new candidate.

The method ignores the owner’s own proxy, a dead owner, and non-player candidates whose NPC-type flags are not included in agroOnNpcType, the allowed set of NPC categories. The sensor can also reject a missing or dead candidate. Increasing the score does not necessarily select that candidate: the following state work runs only when the sensor reports that its selected target changed.

After a changed target, it wakes a frozen puppet through its resurrection request, measures the selected target’s head-to-agent distance in world-space meters, and raises the target and home aggression limits to at least that distance plus 20 meters. If the prior decision state is Rest or Roam, it saves that state. An active entity requests Agroed immediately; a culled entity, temporarily suspended by the game, saves Agroed for its later unculling instead.

member.param: Candidate reference to add targeting priority toward.
Unitless amount added to the candidate’s threat score; not damage or a time.

remarks.para: This is an override hook: a more specific NPC class can replace it with its own action. The base implementation has an empty body and changes no state, animations or movement.

An Animator is the component that runs an animated character’s controller. Any animation or visual change requires the NPC’s replacement for this hook; the base does not start an animation or restore a mesh.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.ApplyOverrideConfig(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig)
member.summary: Stores and copies the supplied enemy configuration, then forces that configuration’s movement-state setup.

remarks.para: The copy updates this behavior’s stored ranges, speeds, attack settings, colors and health/sensor settings. It also writes the puppet’s requested Alive, Dead or Frozen state. The override becomes the stored overrideConfig reference; it is not a clone of the asset.

After copying, it calls the NPC’s movement-state implementation with the configuration’s selected state, a 2-scaled-game-second cooldown and forceSwitch = true. A movement state describes actions such as standing, walking or getting up. Copying values and requesting state setup does not guarantee that a path, animation, death or freeze has already completed.

The configuration and this behavior’s puppet, sensor, health and nested configuration references must exist. A failure can happen after some values have already been copied. Stored colors do not by themselves recolor renderers here.

member.param: Existing configuration asset whose stored settings should be copied into this behavior.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.BlockCollisions(System.Single)
member.summary: Stores the absolute game-time deadline used to skip part of collision-reaction processing.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

The argument is copied directly into _blockCollisionsUntil. It is not added to the current time. To request a two-second window, pass Time.time + 2; passing 2 alone means the deadline at game time 2 seconds, which can already be in the past.

In PowerLegs, the relevant non-hand collision path skips investigation, stun and pain reactions while Time.time is strictly earlier than that deadline. Equality allows that path to continue. Impact-sound setup occurs before the check, and hand melee processing has a separate path. This setting does not switch off physical collisions.

member.param: Absolute deadline in scaled Time.time seconds; use Time.time plus the desired delay.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.CheckTarget
member.summary: Refreshes target data, drops a target outside the aggression limits, and reports whether a target remains.

remarks.para: The sensor first checks its current target. For an NPC target, that can remove one whose root is inactive, whose AI reports death, or whose saved spawn identity no longer matches. Its required current-target references must exist when that check runs; a null current target is not universally handled as a safe false result.

For a remaining target, this method saves the world-space vector from eyeTran, the owner’s eye reference, to the target’s head physics body. It saves that vector’s length in meters and its unitless normalized direction. It removes the selected target when that length is strictly greater than breakAgroTargetDistance, the allowed target separation in meters, or when the owner’s horizontal world X/Z distance from homePosition exceeds breakAgroHomeDistance, the allowed home distance in meters. Equality with either positive limit is allowed.

Removing one target can leave another selected target. The return value checks whether any selected target remains afterward, rather than whether the original candidate survived the checks. When none remains, it calls the NPC’s ReturnToPreAgro hook before returning false; that hook is empty in this base class.

member.returns: true when a selected target remains after the checks; otherwise false, after requesting the return hook.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.ClearPath
member.summary: Clears a route when the agent is on the navigation map and requests Standing if it was Walking.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

If the agent is off the map, the method first tries to bind it by warping it to its current world position. If this establishes the previously missing home binding, that world position becomes homePosition. A successful binding lets it reset the agent’s path; an unsuccessful attempt leaves no guaranteed cleared path.

When locoState is Walking, it calls the NPC’s movement-state implementation for Standing. It does not directly zero the physical bodies’ velocities or set the agent’s stopped flag, so clearing a route is not a guarantee that the puppet instantly stops.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.ClearState
member.summary: Clears sensor targets, requests the Rest decision state, and replaces the waypoint array with an empty array.

remarks.para: The sensor’s selected target, candidate list and threat records are cleared before the Rest-state request. Rest means the NPC’s resting decision mode; its detailed settings come from the specific NPC’s state implementation.

The waypoint positions are then replaced by a new empty array. This method does not reset locoState, the separate movement mode, or rebuild the navigation agent. Provide the initialized sensor helper.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.DealMeleeDamage(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.MuscleCollision,System.Single)
member.summary: Sends a fixed blunt attack to receivers on the collided physics body when the contact passes the melee gates.

remarks.para: m describes the collision for one simulated body part. impulse is the processed collision-strength number: values below 1 return without sending an attack, while exactly 1 passes this gate. Its producer has fallback calculations with different physical units, so it should not be treated as a single raw force measurement. The collided object’s layer must be included in meleeAttackMask, the set of object categories allowed for this melee path.

The method builds a Blunt attack with 1.5 damage points from the collision’s first contact and the owner’s self proxy, the reference identifying who attacked. It sends that Attack value to IAttackReceiver handlers on the collided Rigidbody’s object. A Rigidbody is a body whose movement is controlled by the physics simulation. Larger impulse values do not increase the fixed damage here. A receiving handler decides what damage actually results.

After dispatch, it calls hit-sound setup. If the sensor’s selected target and self proxy have the same NPC category, it moves the owner’s unitless aggression score toward 0 by 0.1 times placability, its unitless calming multiplier. It then clears meleeAttackActive, the flag marking the attack window. Early returns skip this ending. The collision, its first contact and physics-body/sensor/sound references used on this path must exist.

member.param: Collision data with the struck body part’s index and Unity collision contact information.
Processed contact-strength score; at least 1 is required, and it does not scale the fixed attack damage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.DisableNav
member.summary: Saves the agent’s destination and stopped flag, then disables its navigation component.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

Before disabling, it copies the world-space destination, measured in meters, into _cachedDestination. It also copies the agent’s stopped flag into _isNavAgentStopped when on the NavMesh; off the map it saves false instead. These fields are saved snapshots, not live state readings.

A missing or destroyed agent makes this method return without doing anything. EnableNav restores the saved settings when navigation is enabled again. Disabling this component does not directly disable this behavior or every physics body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.EnableNav
member.summary: Enables navigation and restores the destination and stopped flag saved by DisableNav.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

It enables the agent first, submits _cachedDestination as a world-space position in meters, then applies _isNavAgentStopped. A saved true flag leaves the enabled agent stopped; enabling does not always resume movement. Setting a destination requests a route, not successful arrival.
A missing or destroyed agent makes this method return. The saved fields must describe the settings you want restored; they are not automatically refreshed from a live disabled agent.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.GetNextWaypoint
member.summary: Updates the waypoint index using the configured selection mode.

remarks.para: An index is the zero-based position in waypoints: 0 selects its first world-space point. LINEAR increments currWaypoint and wraps to 0 at the array’s end. PING_PONG increments it too, but at the end reverses the actual waypoints array in place and sets the index to 1. Use at least two points for that reversed index to be valid.

RANDOM chooses an index from 0 through the last point. RANDOM_MIN_TIME tries at most as many random picks as there are points. Each index’s saved allowed time is compared with Time.time, in scaled game seconds. A new or expired index is recorded with its next allowed time set to now plus wpMinTime, the minimum intended wait in seconds. Equality allows reuse. Random retries can repeat the same index; when all attempts fail, the last rejected index still remains, so this is not a guaranteed minimum wait.

The routine returns the updated currWaypoint and can mutate the array or timing dictionary. It does not itself request a path. An empty array does not supply a valid waypoint, and an unknown selection mode logs an error and retains the stored index.

member.returns: Updated zero-based currWaypoint; the caller must still have a valid waypoint at that index.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.KillEnd
member.summary: Clears navigation and targeting records before sending the death-finished notification.

remarks.para: It calls ClearPath, saves the current animated-root position offset, disables the navigation agent and clears the melee attack flag. It removes the roam-area reference, clears used and failed roaming-point lists and waypoint timing records, then clears sensor targets and resets the overlap counter.

A configured OnDeath UnityEvent runs after those steps, with no arguments. A listener is a callback, a routine called to handle a notification. Calling this method alone does not check a completed death or call OnDeathStart first; normal death-sequence code is responsible for arranging that order. There is no once-only notification guard here, and required puppet/agent/list/dictionary/sensor references can fail before the event.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.KillStart
member.summary: Clears the melee attack window and disables the detection sphere before sending the death-start notification.

remarks.para: It sets meleeAttackActive to false, sets the sensor’s sphere radius to 0, disables that collider and resets its center to zero. A collider is the invisible detection shape that reports overlaps or contacts.

After that cleanup, a configured OnDeathStart UnityEvent calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a callback, a routine called to handle a notification. This routine does not itself request the puppet’s death or guarantee that the puppet is dead. Its sensor and sphere references must exist; a failure can prevent the notification.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnDrawGizmos
member.summary: Draws optional editor markers for navigation paths, roaming points and target directions.

remarks.para: Gizmos are debug shapes displayed by Unity’s editor. The navigation display requires this behavior to be enabled and displayNavpath to be true; it draws path corners and lines, destination markers and, while roaming, waypoint or used/failed point markers. LEGACY roaming also draws its rectangular search area.

The separate displayCrabCones flag enables target-direction and orientation lines when the needed target/self references exist. The method draws information and does not select targets, request routes or move bodies. The selected displays require their initialized navigation, sensor and point-list references.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnEntityCull
member.summary: Saves animation settings for culling, freezes a living puppet, and disables navigation.

remarks.para: Culling here is the entity system temporarily suspending an entity. If the puppet is already in its killing sequence, this method first finishes its special cull-time death work. It then saves the Animator’s controller settings and current base-layer state for later restoration. An Animator runs the animated character’s controller.

If the puppet still reports Alive, its cull-time freeze routine disables animation, calls behavior freeze hooks, writes the requested and active Frozen state, and invokes the freeze notification. After that, this method calls the NPC’s DisableNav hook; the base hook saves the destination and stopped flag before disabling the agent. Required puppet and animation references must exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnEntityUncull
member.summary: Restores navigation and saved animation settings, then applies any decision state saved while culled.

remarks.para: Unculling is the entity system bringing a suspended entity back into use. The method first calls EnableNav, then restores the Animator’s saved culling settings and base-layer state. If the puppet reports Frozen, it configures a 1-scaled-game-second delay for its next Alive-to-Frozen transition and requests resurrection before handling the saved decision state. Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion.

When applyCachedMental is true, it clears that request flag, calls the NPC’s state implementation with cachedMentalState, then resets the cached state to Rest. It does not apply a cached state when the flag is false. Resurrection is requested here; the method alone does not prove that all body-state transitions have finished.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnInitiate
member.summary: Sets up navigation, sensor, sound and health helpers and records the initial home position.

remarks.para: This setup hook registers the behavior with the puppet’s entity and records its own physics bodies. A Rigidbody is a simulated body; those bodies are saved for later self-collision checks. If prefabConfig is missing, it creates a configuration snapshot from the current stored settings.

It finds the parent object’s NavMeshAgent, the component that plans paths over the game’s walkable-surface map. It turns off that component’s automatic position, rotation and up-axis updates, saves whether it is on the map and takes its world position in meters as homePosition. Sensor, sound and health setup follows; health fractions and recovery counters are initialized to 1.

It saves scaled game-clock values, which follow slow motion, and puts the collision-reaction deadline 1.5 seconds ahead, creates the material-color helpers, clears the forced-decision flag, and initializes movement/jump timing. This hook needs the puppet/entity hierarchy, nonnull body list and initialized helper references. It does not apply overrideConfig in this base body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnReactivate(System.Int32)
member.summary: Restores saved animation parameters and performs the main reactivation reset only for phase 0.

remarks.para: Every phase first restores the puppet’s ordinary saved Animator parameters, the values controlling its animations. Phase 1 only logs a message after that; other nonzero phases have no additional base reset. The completion callback described below belongs to phase 0.

Phase 0 resets the eye reference’s local rotation, saves the first animated muscle target’s root offset and inverse local rotation, synchronizes navigation with the physical root, resets visible damage, enables the agent, clears its velocity and synchronizes its next position. It restores emission colors, captures the agent’s current world position in meters, and overwrites homePosition with it. If homeIsPost is true, it requests SetPath using that same newly captured position; otherwise it writes that same position directly into homePosition. The path request is to the current position, not to a previous home.

It forces the current movement-state setup, saves the current decision state before requesting Rest, clears investigation/forced-decision flags and resets timing markers. Sensor support values and the grounded flag are reset; sound respawn setup runs. Remaining health fractions become 0 when the puppet currently reports Dead and 1 otherwise. Recovery counters become 1 and the stun-active flag is cleared, so this reset alone does not guarantee a dead puppet becomes alive.

Finally it clears the melee attack flag, sets the collision-reaction deadline to Time.time + 3 scaled game seconds, a clock that follows slow motion, and invokes a configured OnPostReactivate callback with this behavior as its argument. A callback is a routine called to handle a notification. Required setup references must exist; an earlier failure prevents this ending. A frame is one game update, and this routine itself has no multi-frame wait.

member.param: Reactivation phase: 0 performs the main reset and completion callback; 1 only adds logging after parameter restoration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnReadBehaviour
member.summary: Caches the animated root’s position offset and estimates its rotation contribution for navigation.

remarks.para: The first muscle’s target is its animated bone. The method saves that bone’s world position minus the animated target root’s world position into _animatedRoot. The three components are world-axis distances in meters; this is a current offset, not accumulated movement or the physical body’s position.

A quaternion stores an orientation using four unitless numbers. Each local rotation sample is measured relative to the bone’s parent. The method combines the saved inverse rotation with the current rotation to measure the animation’s change in the previous bone orientation’s axes. It converts the shortest rotation angle to degrees, divides by the frame’s deltaTime in scaled game seconds, affected by slow motion and saves the negative X component of that rate in _animatedRotVel. A frame is one game update.

It then replaces _localAnimatedRoot with the inverse of the current local rotation for the next read. These saved values help SetNavAgentToPhysics remove animated bone offsets from the physical body’s pose and predict navigation rotation. The puppet needs a first muscle target and target root; the computed rate is not a measured Rigidbody angular velocity.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.PredictiveAimWildGuessAtImpactTime
member.summary: Picks a fallback projectile travel-time guess of 1, 2, 3 or 4 seconds.

remarks.para: It takes no distance, speed or target information and picks an integer randomly before returning it as a float. It does not measure a likely impact time.

PredictiveAim uses the same random-time choice in its fallback when an interception solution is unavailable. That estimate helps form a guessed launch direction; it does not promise the projectile will hit or arrive after the chosen time.

member.returns: Random float-valued time guess: 1, 2, 3 or 4 seconds.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.ProcessTargetRelativePathing(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a reachable destination toward or away from the target, with an optional side offset.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

All four arguments are distances in meters. Let D be targetDistance, the stored target-separation number last refreshed by target logic. The method keeps the current route when D is between clamp(idealDistance − nearBuffer, 0.3, 200) and idealDistance + farBuffer, including both boundaries. clamp limits its first value to 0.3–200 meters. This stored separation can be an eye-to-target-head distance; it is not a newly measured horizontal distance from the agent.

Outside that band, it forms a horizontal world X/Z direction from the agent’s nextPosition toward the target head and offsets that position by D − idealDistance along the direction. A negative offset retreats; a positive one advances. Positive orbitMeters adds a perpendicular side offset, tries a path on that side, and tries the opposite side if the first calculation fails. Zero or negative orbitMeters adds no side offset.

For example, D = 8 and idealDistance = 5 produces a 3-meter forward offset before any side offset. It requests SetPath only after a successful path calculation, and only with a target and Standing or Walking movement state. If the current route is already nearer its end than stoppingDistance, the method clears it and returns first. A requested destination is not guaranteed arrival or continuous circling.

member.param: Preferred target separation in meters, used to calculate the destination offset.
Meters subtracted from idealDistance for the lower permitted separation, limited to 0.3–200 meters.
Meters added to idealDistance for the upper permitted separation.
Positive perpendicular side offset in meters; zero or a negative value adds none.

member.summary: Provides the override hook for returning to an earlier decision state; this base implementation does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.RoamByMode
member.summary: Selects a roaming point and, for the path-submitting modes, requests navigation toward it.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

WAYPOINTS keeps a complete route until the remaining route distance is strictly below stoppingDistance, then clears it and waits roamWaitDuration scaled game seconds. An incomplete route is cleared too. Once there is no path and Time.time is strictly later than nextRoamTime, it selects the next zero-based waypoint index and requests SetPath for that world-space position.

ZONE similarly waits for no path and an expired wait, then asks roamArea for a world-space point. It checks whether a route can be calculated before requesting it and records successful or failed points. If calculation fails and there are more than one successful saved points, it can request one of those instead. ZONE3D only saves the area’s 3D roaming point in ranRoamTarget in this base method; it does not submit SetPath.

LEGACY tries a new point when its random 0–1 value is at most 0.1. Its rectangle is centered at homePosition minus roamOffset, with X within plus/minus roamRange.x meters and Z within plus/minus roamRange.y meters. These are world-axis half-widths, not minimum/maximum radii. It tries a path and records the result; this chance is per call, not an exact seconds timer.

The selected mode needs its area, agent, point arrays and result lists. WAYPOINTS with no points logs an error and returns. A missing area is logged for area modes but can still fail later. Selecting or submitting a point does not guarantee successful travel.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.SetAgro(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy)
member.summary: Updates the supplied candidate’s targeting record and requests the Agroed decision state.

remarks.para: It requests resurrection when the owner currently reports Frozen. The sensor then adds enough extra unitless threat to put a known candidate one point above the current leader’s stored score; with no candidates it adds 2. A new candidate also has its own initial threat score.

The method measures the sensor’s selected target head-to-agent world distance in meters, not necessarily the supplied candidate’s distance. It stores that separation and raises breakAgroTargetDistance and breakAgroHomeDistance to at least that distance plus 20 meters. These are the target-distance and owner-home leash limits.

When the prior decision state is Rest or Roam, it saves that state for a later return. If the entity is active, it calls the NPC’s Agroed state setup. If culled, temporarily suspended by the game, it instead sets applyCachedMental and saves Agroed for unculling. This method does not itself fire a weapon, require immediate combat range or prove an attack completed. The owner, sensor, selected head body and navigation references must exist.

member.param: Candidate’s TriggerRefProxy, which links its body and AI information.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.SetHomeIsPost(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets whether subsequent SetPath requests are restricted to within 1 meter of homePosition.

remarks.para: With isPost true, SetPath rejects a destination whose three-dimensional world-space distance from the stored home position is greater than 1 meter; exactly 1 meter is allowed. With false, that restriction is skipped.

The method only stores this flag. It does not move the NPC home, replace the home position or cancel a route already running. Its restriction belongs to SetPath rather than every possible way of moving the body.

member.param: true to restrict later SetPath destinations to the 1-meter home area; false to skip that restriction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.SetNavAgent(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Copies speed, turning, acceleration and stopping settings into the existing navigation agent.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

speed is the configured movement speed in meters per second; angSpeed is the turning-speed setting in degrees per second. accel is speed change per second, measured in meters per second per second, and stopDistance is the allowed distance from a destination at which the agent can stop, in meters.

For example, speed = 2 and accel = 4 configure a 2-meter-per-second speed and a 4-meter-per-second-per-second acceleration. These are agent settings, not a command that instantly changes every physical body’s measured velocity. The agent must already exist; the method does not create it or submit a path.

member.param: Navigation movement-speed setting in meters per second.
Navigation turning-speed setting in degrees per second.
Acceleration setting in meters per second per second; defaults to 2.
Stopping distance in meters from the requested destination; defaults to 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.SetNavAgentToPhysics(System.Single)
member.summary: Aligns the navigation object to the physical root while removing saved animation offsets and predicting ahead by deltaTime.

remarks.para: The root body is the puppet’s first simulated body part, obtained as a Rigidbody, a body moved by physics. The method sets the agent object’s world position to root position plus agent velocity times deltaTime minus _animatedRoot. Here all positions and the saved animated-bone-to-animated-root offset are in meters, velocity is in meters per second, and deltaTime is scaled game seconds, affected by slow motion. This positions the navigation object rather than teleporting the physical body.

It also removes the saved animated local rotation from the root body’s rotation, straightens the result to world up, and applies a further world-up turn equal to the sum of _currentRotVel and _animatedRotVel times deltaTime. Those two stored turn rates are in degrees per second: steering smoothing and the animated local-rotation contribution. World up is the vertical world Y axis. Quaternions are four-number unitless representations of orientation.

At the default deltaTime of 0, no velocity or turn-rate prediction is added; the saved animation offsets still matter. If the first body cannot supply a Rigidbody, this method returns. The body list, animated samples and navigation agent must otherwise be set up before synchronization.

member.param: Scaled game seconds to predict using stored velocity and turn rates; 0 adds no prediction.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate.op_Addition(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate)
member.summary: Combines two collision-impulse callback lists without invoking their callbacks.
member.param: The existing delegate; its callbacks stay first.
The delegate whose callbacks are appended after a.
member.returns: The combined delegate. If one operand is null, the other operand is returned; if both are null, the result is null.

remarks.para: A callback is a method that a delegate can call later. This delegate’s handler signature is void Handler(MuscleCollision m, float impulse): m is collision information, and impulse is the float supplied by the collision path. A delegate that stores several callbacks keeps them in an ordered callback list.

The result keeps every callback from a first, followed by every callback from b; repeated callbacks stay in the list. For example, [RecordA] + [RecordB, RecordC] returns [RecordA, RecordB, RecordC]. Combining builds the list; it does not call a handler or update BehaviourPuppet.OnCollisionImpulse by itself.

To register a handler on that field, use puppet.OnCollisionImpulse += HandleCollision; C# stores the combined result back into the field. This operator does not inspect or change the future impulse argument, so it adds no physical unit or coordinate frame to that value.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate.op_Subtraction(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.CollisionImpulseDelegate)
member.summary: Removes a matching callback or callback sequence from a collision-impulse delegate list.
member.param: The delegate containing callbacks from which to remove.
The callback or callback list to remove from a.
member.returns: The remaining delegate. The result can be null or a non-null empty list; one reachable stored-list case throws an invalid-operation error described below.

remarks.para: A callback is a method a delegate can call later. Two callbacks match when they use the same method on the same target object (the object on which the method runs). When a delegate stores several callbacks, their order is kept in a callback list.

If a is null, the result is null; if b is null, a is returned unchanged. Removing a matching single callback from an ordinary single-callback delegate returns null; if it does not match, a stays unchanged. From a stored list with at least two entries, removing one callback removes its last matching occurrence, so earlier copies remain. For example, [RecordA, RecordB, RecordA] - [RecordA] returns [RecordA, RecordB].

For two stored callback lists, removal normally finds the last matching consecutive sequence: the requested callbacks must appear next to each other in the same order. If there is no full sequence match, a is returned unchanged. A special case in this build is a single callback A minus a list [B, A]: it returns null if A appears anywhere in that list, even though the whole list is not present in the single-callback source.

Two separately stored lists with the same callbacks in the same order can produce a non-null delegate whose callback list is empty. Null is therefore not the only result that means no callbacks remain.

A sequence removal can leave a stored one-entry callback list. For example, [A, B, C] - [B, C] leaves the stored list [A]. Subtracting single callback A from that one-entry stored list throws InvalidOperationException, an error meaning this removal is not valid for that stored-list state. This differs from an ordinary delegate created with only callback A: subtracting A from that ordinary single-callback delegate returns null.

To unregister from the field, use puppet.OnCollisionImpulse -= HandleCollision; C# stores the returned delegate back into the field. The subtraction operator changes only the callback list: it does not invoke handlers, inspect collision data, or change the float impulse value or assign it physical units.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.CalculateMappedVelocity
member.summary: Calculates linear and angular velocities of the mapped muscle based on delta position and rotation since last update.

remarks.para: Samples the animated target Transform's world position and rotation; a Transform stores an object's position and rotation, and world space means the scene's shared reference frame. It divides the position change by positive elapsed Time.time seconds to produce mappedVelocity in metres per second, and converts the rotation change to Euler angles in degrees before dividing by the same interval to produce mappedAngularVelocity in degrees per second. Time.time is Unity's game-time clock, measured in seconds. Only that positive-interval branch advances lastWriteTime. With a zero or negative interval, velocity division is skipped, the velocity values stay unchanged, and the old time sample is retained. In either case, the previous target position and rotation caches are refreshed.

member.summary: Initializes the profile for one simulated muscle, with settings for following its animated target and driving it through a physics joint.
member.param: Scales the strength of the physics joint that drives this body part toward its target pose. It is a dimensionless multiplier; the profile metadata describes 0 to 1, but this constructor stores the supplied value.

Scales how much the simulated body part follows the pose of its animated target. It is a dimensionless multiplier; the profile metadata describes 0 to 1, but this constructor stores the supplied value.

Scales the physics joint's base damping, which resists wobble while it drives the body part. Per-muscle runtime state can add a separate damping term. It is a dimensionless multiplier; the profile metadata describes 0 to 1, but this constructor stores the supplied value.
Whether target mapping also follows the animated target's position, in addition to its rotation.

The category PuppetMaster uses to find this simulated muscle for group-wide weight settings. Categories include Hips, Spine, Head, Arm, Hand, Leg, Foot, Tail, and Prop. The optional default 0 is Hips.

remarks.para: The constructor first initializes the three weight/damper fields to 1.0, then stores the supplied , , , , and values. The native body does not show clamping, validation, or initialization of the ignored-index array.

These weights and the damper are dimensionless multipliers, not physical units. At use time, target mapping combines this profile value with master and per-muscle state multipliers. muscleWeight scales the joint drive strength; muscleDamper scales the drive's base damping, while runtime state can add a separate damping term. mapPosition enables mapping position as well as rotation. A muscle is one simulated body part; its animated target supplies the pose it follows, and its physics joint is the connection whose drive applies movement. A value of 1.0 is the full profile multiplier represented by the constructor's initial writes; the documented range metadata is not evidence that the native body clamps out-of-range inputs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.Read
member.summary: Caches the animated target rotation for driving the muscle joint.

remarks.para: Reads the connected ConfigurableJoint and caches the animated rotation for later drive calculations. A joint links two physics bodies; a Rigidbody is Unity's physics-body component, and a Transform stores an object's position and rotation. With a connected body, directTargetParent=true caches target.localRotation, the animated target's orientation relative to its immediate Transform parent. When false, it caches targetLocalRotation: inverse(targetParentRotation * toParentSpace) * target.rotation. Here targetParentRotation is the selected animated parent's world rotation, toParentSpace is the unitless rotation offset established during initialization between that parent and the physical connected body, and target.rotation is the animated target's world rotation. The combined reference uses that connected-body offset rather than only the animated parent. With no connected body, the observed Props.group==0 branch caches the animated target's world rotation; other observed group branches leave this cache unchanged.

member.summary: Returns the current stun contribution to physical control for the selected muscle and reports its limb health.

remarks.para: A physical muscle here is a physics-controlled body part. StunGroup names the body regions to which those parts are mapped for damage and recovery. The unitless recovery counter is 1 when recovered; 0 or below contributes a zero factor after limiting it to 0 through 1. The returned contribution does not include limb health or usage multipliers, so it is not the complete pose-driving strength.

The return value is a number from 0 to 1, not a duration in seconds. For a spine muscle it is the spine stun counter limited to that range. For an arm or leg it is the product of the spine and selected limb counters, each limited to 0 through 1. For a head or unrecognized group it returns 1.

The health output is the selected arm or leg's stored health fraction; spine, head, and unrecognized groups output 1. A normal limb value of 0.5 means half health, but the output is not clamped if a mod writes values outside 0 through 1. For spine counter 0.5 and left-arm counter 0.8, a left-arm query returns 0.4 and separately reports that arm's health.
m is an index into muscles, not a StunGroup enum number. The mapping array must exist and contain that index.

member.param: Index of a puppet muscle in the muscles mapping array.
Outputs the selected limb's stored health fraction, or 1 for spine, head, or an unrecognized group.
member.returns: A control factor from 0 to 1; head and unrecognized groups return 1.

remarks.para: The six values are multipliers with no physical units. A value of 1 keeps the strength calculated from health and stun, 0 disables that region's pose-driving strength, and 0.5 halves it. Values are stored without a 0-to-1 clamp.

SetUsage only stores the multipliers. UpdateMuscleStates later combines them with health and stun and copies the results into the puppet's physical-control settings. It does not heal limbs or clear stun. The float overload's order is hips, spine, left leg, right leg, left arm, right arm.

member.param: Hip pose-driving multiplier; 1 keeps calculated strength and 0 disables it.
Spine and head pose-driving multiplier.
Left-leg pose-driving multiplier.
Right-leg pose-driving multiplier.
Left-arm pose-driving multiplier.
Right-arm pose-driving multiplier.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.Stun(System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Processes a collision impact against the selected muscle's body region, reducing control and applying collision damage.

remarks.para: A physical muscle is a physics-controlled body part mapped to a named damage region. Collision impulse means the shove delivered during contact; the processed strength supplied here can have the different producer scales described below.

m selects an entry in muscles, which maps the muscle to spine, head, or a particular limb. The stun argument is processed impact strength, not seconds. A region's minimum-impact setting is subtracted; a strength below that threshold is rejected, and equality leaves zero excess strength. The supplied value normally comes from collision impulse in newton-seconds, but some enemy collision adjustments and zero-impulse fallback calculations use different scales.

Accepted impacts push a region's stun counter toward -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery), where maxStunSeconds is the configured below-zero recovery interval in game seconds and stunRecovery is counter units regained per game second. Counters normally recover toward 1. Head impacts affect the shared spine counter. Collision damage also lowers overall or selected limb health, with different organic and non-organic rules.

stunActive is set true before the threshold check, even when the impact is rejected. For a processed impact that reaches the scoring path, OnNPCDamage runs after health changes and before damageScore increases. If overall health is then depleted, PuppetMaster.Kill is called to request death and this method returns 0. The return is otherwise the calculated collision-damage amount, not the new counter or elapsed stun time.

member.param: Index of the hit muscle in the muscles mapping array.
Processed collision-impact strength; this is not a duration.
member.returns: Calculated collision damage, or 0 for a rejected impact or after a death request; not a stun duration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.TakeDamage(System.Int32,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack)
member.summary: Applies an attack's damage-type rules to the selected body region and lowers its health and stun counters.

remarks.para: m indexes muscles to choose a region; a physical muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Piercing uses pierceMult, Blunt uses bluntMult, and both Slicing and Stabbing use stabMult. These initial multipliers have no physical units. Health is stored as unitless fractions: 1 means full and 0 depleted. Calculations divide processed damage by maxHitPoints, the damage-point scale for overall health, or maxAppendageHp, the damage-point scale for a single arm or leg. Stun counters are unitless recovery values: 1 means recovered, and 0 or below suppresses their contribution to pose strength. Head hits have an extra factor of 4.1; blunt hits have further stun-dependent reductions. Collision minimum-impact thresholds are not checked here.

stunActive is set true before rejection checks. For a piercing attack mapped to Head, OnHeadShot runs after the health/counter changes, then OnNPCDamage runs, then damageScore increases. The damage notification carries the processed attack amount, which can differ from the actual health loss; a head's 4.1 factor is not multiplied into this payload.

After the damage notification and score update, depleted overall health causes a PuppetMaster.Kill death request and a return of 0. Other rejected paths also return 0. Therefore a return of 0 does not prove that no health changed or no notification fired. An already-depleted non-organic limb can reject further limb damage. The muscles array must exist and include m.

member.param: Index of the hit muscle in the muscles mapping array.
Damage points, attack type, and hit information to process.
member.returns: Processed attack damage for reactions and scoring, or 0 for a rejected path or after requesting death; not necessarily health lost.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.UpdateMuscleStates(System.Single)
member.summary: Copies body-region strength calculated from health, stun, and usage multipliers into the puppet's physical-control settings.

remarks.para: A physical muscle is a simulated body part. Pose-driving strength means how strongly a simulated body part tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation. Clamp means limiting a number to the stated minimum and maximum.

For an arm or leg, the calculated strength is the spine stun counter limited to 0 through 1, times that limb's stun counter limited to 0 through 1, times its stored health fraction. The product is limited to 0.02 through 1, then multiplied by that region's usage value. These are numbers with no physical units. A stun counter of 1 means fully recovered; 0 or below supplies a zero stun factor. Limb health 1 means full and 0 means depleted. Usage 1 keeps calculated strength and 0 disables it. For spine stun 1, limb stun 0.5, health 1, and usage 0.5, the final multiplier is 0.25.

The first puppet muscle receives clamp(spine stun, 0, 1) × usage_hips. Other muscles mapped to Spine or Head receive clamp(spine stun, 0.02, 1) × usage_spine. The 0.02 floor keeps a little calculated strength even when health or stun is zero; usage 0 can still make the final multiplier zero. It changes pose-driving strength, not the body's mass or health.
The footSupported argument is ignored by this implementation. The owner must already supply a valid puppet, its physical-muscle list, and a muscles mapping covering the entries that are visited.

member.param: Unused by this implementation; it does not change the calculated muscle strength.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.UpdateStun
member.summary: Advances active stun counters toward 1 using elapsed game time and reports whether recovery still needs updates.

remarks.para: While stunActive is true, each counter advances by stunRecovery × deltaTime toward 1. stunRecovery is counter units per scaled game second; deltaTime is game seconds elapsed since the previous frame. When all five counters are at least 1, stunActive becomes false before returning false.

When stunActive is already false, this returns false without changing counters. A true result means at least one counter has not fully recovered; it is not proof the whole enemy cannot move. Negative counters can need extra time to reach 0 before strength begins returning, and 0-to-1 recovery continues afterward.

This completion test also accepts edited counters above 1. For example, with all five counters at 1.2 and a recovery rate of 0, the update leaves their values unchanged but clears stunActive before returning false.

member.returns: True while at least one counter still needs recovery; false when inactive or after all counters reach 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.UsageSettings.#ctor(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a stored set of six multipliers controlling how strongly body regions follow their intended poses.

remarks.para: Argument order is hips, spine, left leg, right leg, left arm, right arm. The multipliers have no physical units: 1 keeps calculated strength, 0.5 halves it, and 0 makes the region's final strength zero. For example, UsageSettings(1, 1, 1, 1, 0.5, 1) preserves the other regions and halves the left arm's calculated strength.

Construction stores values without a 0-to-1 clamp and does not change an enemy. SubBehaviourHealth.SetUsage copies the settings; UpdateMuscleStates later combines them with health and stun and applies the strength settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RealHeptaAvatar.PrecomputeAvatar(System.Single)
member.summary: Scales reference body measurements and local-position vectors by eyeHeight / , fills inherited Avatar values, and loads default hand-configuration data; this precompute step does not call RefreshBodyMeasurements or its callback.
member.param: The target standing eye height in meters. PrecomputeAvatar scales the reference measurements by eyeHeight divided by _eyeHeightDefault.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar computes scale = eyeHeight / _eyeHeightDefault, stores the supplied eye height, and derives total height by scaling _heightDefault. It scales the default local-position vectors and palm dimensions, copies proportion settings into the inherited Avatar, generates its spine curve, and loads default left and right HandSchematic hand-configuration data. This seeds the measurements; it does not run RefreshBodyMeasurements or OnRefreshBodyMeasurements.
Stored local-position vectors use avatar/Animator-root-aligned axes; they are not world-space positions or coordinates relative to an arbitrary child transform.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RealHeptaAvatar.RefreshBodyMeasurements
member.summary: Recomputes this avatar’s derived body dimensions and torso shape from its stored proportions, then invokes its measurement callback if one is registered.

remarks.para: The refresh first derives total height as heightPercent multiplied by eyeHeight. It derives skull, chest, pelvis, clavicle, arm, leg, and wrist-segment measurements from stored proportions and eyeHeight, and also computes footLength, armPercent, shoulderToPalmPercent, and palmOffsetLength. It then builds the torso shape curves, recomputes body mass and base stats, and calls OnRefreshBodyMeasurements last when the callback is non-null. A callback is a registered method the avatar calls to report that refresh.

remarks.para: For a non-null argument, this method copies eleven values from this RealHeptaAvatar: chest, waist, and hip width and front/back depth ratios, plus front/back sternum depth ratios. The copy runs from this receiver into calibrationAvatar; it does not copy the full skeleton or all measurements. After the optional copy, the method always invokes the inherited Avatar refresh dispatch with this receiver and the argument; a null argument skips only the copy.
