member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug.DestroyJoint
member.summary: Asks Unity to destroy the physics joint connecting this plug to its selected socket.

remarks.para: The joint is a MarrowJoint component that connects the plug's body to the socket's body. The plug creates it when it attaches. This method calls Unity's Destroy function with a requested delay of zero seconds. Unity schedules the actual removal after the current Update loop (the current round of update callbacks). It only asks Unity to destroy that joint: it does not clear the stored joint field, IsAttached, or _attachedSocket, and it does not perform the attachment-state updates and notifications in Detach. Use Detach to update attachment state when the plug is attached and unbound.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug.Detach
member.summary: Detaches this plug only while is true and is false.

remarks.para: If IsAttached is false, or IsBound is true, this method returns without detaching. Otherwise it clears the attached state, asks Unity to destroy the physics joint, and restores the host's distant-hover interaction (far-hover).

It then calls OnSocketDetached on each registered IPlugable, notifies the socket, remembers that socket in _lastDetachedSocket, and clears _attachedSocket. A socket can be configured to bind automatically when a plug attaches; unbind it before detaching a bound plug.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.Bind
member.summary: Binds the attached , disabling its normal interaction, or arms this socket to bind the next plug that attaches.

remarks.para: If no plug is attached, this sets a one-shot auto-bind request. On the next attach, onPlugAttached runs first; the socket binds the plug after that callback returns.
Binding does not detach the plug. To remove a bound plug, call Unbind before Detach; a bound plug ignores the detach request.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.Detach
member.summary: Asks this socket's tracked to detach; the Plug requests destruction of its physics joint.

remarks.para: The plug must be attached and unbound. If it is bound, its detach path does nothing; call Unbind first. The socket also needs to be tracking that plug.
A physics joint is the connector that holds the plug and socket bodies together in the physics simulation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.Unbind
member.summary: Clears the bound state of the attached plug without detaching it.

remarks.para: When the plug is attached and bound, this clears both bound flags and then raises onPlugUnbound. If no plug is attached, it cancels a pending auto-bind request instead.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.ApplyRotation(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Turns the rig around its support point by the supplied angle plus any degrees queued by .

remarks.para: The support point is the physics rig's center of pressure: the point used to represent where the body is supported. The turn uses the remap rig's own up direction as its axis. With an upright rig, this is a left or right turn around the feet.
The supplied angle and the queued angle are added. After a nonzero turn, the queue is cleared. For example, 10 supplied degrees and 20 queued degrees produce one 30-degree turn.

An active seat prevents the turn and leaves the queue waiting. A total angle of exactly zero also returns without clearing the queue. The deltaTime argument is not used by this method; the angle is already an amount to turn, rather than a turning speed.

member.param: Frame duration in seconds. This method does not use it.
Angle to add to the queued turn, in degrees. Positive and negative values turn in opposite directions around the rig's up axis.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.CrouchHold(System.Single,System.Boolean@,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adjusts the feet-height control for crouching or rising, and adds extra spine-crouch control when the hands are supporting a pull-up.

remarks.para: Negative crouchRate values lower the target; positive values raise it toward the avatar's extended standing pose. The size of the change depends on the frame duration and the avatar's stored speed rating. The feet-height value then eases toward that target, so a change in input need not finish in one frame.

The target is measured in metres and accounts for the difference between the avatar's stored chest height and the current neck-to-support-point height, measured along the rig's up direction. It is an offset control, rather than an absolute world height or a percentage.

The hand-support test can make this method run even when crouchInput is false. It requires foot support below 0.2 and a positive sum of the two hands' pull-up scores. Otherwise, false crouchInput leaves all controls and feetOverride untouched.

If a jump sequence is active, this processing cancels it, releases its mass hold, and restores the cached support-radius multiplier to 1.3. Processed crouch or hand-support control then sets feetOverride to true so the later ordinary feet-recovery step does not replace this frame's result. This method never clears feetOverride to false.
The support point mentioned here is the center of pressure, the physics body's reference point for support through the ground.

The mass hold keeps the physics rig's natural mass-distribution mode selected while its ball-based movement mode is enabled. Mass distribution means how body mass is divided among the physical parts. Clearing the hold lets foot support choose that mode again; it does not directly set a new mass in kilograms.

member.param: Duration of this update in seconds, used to scale the target movement and smoothing.
A shared result flag. Set to true when crouch or hand-support control handles the feet this frame; left unchanged when neither condition applies.

Signed transition factor, scaled by the avatar's speed rating. For example, -1 requests lowering and 1 requests rising. Its magnitude controls how quickly the target changes; it is not a height in metres.
Whether to process the requested crouch or rise. A qualifying hand-supported pull-up also enables processing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.GetAcceleration
member.summary: Returns the cached rate of change of the rig's smoothed horizontal movement velocity.

remarks.para: The returned two-number vector uses x for world X and y for world Z, both in metres per second squared. Its y component is forward or backward along world Z, not upward movement.

The value comes from the movement smoother's saved rate of change. It is copied at full size for ordinary movement and multiplied by 0.3 on an update that consumes a virtual-controller movement request. It is not a measurement of the body's actual physics acceleration. A seated update or Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled clears this cache.

member.returns: The last cached horizontal movement change-rate, in metres per second squared, with components for world X and world Z.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.GetVelocity
member.summary: Returns the rig's cached horizontal movement speed and direction.

remarks.para: The returned two-number vector uses x for world X and y for world Z, in metres per second. For example, (2, 0) means 2 metres per second toward positive world X, regardless of where the player is looking.

The early update moves the rig root by this velocity multiplied by the frame duration. The movement calculation can include controller movement input, navigation-agent travel, and pending virtual-controller corrections. This is the remap root's movement control, not a reading of the physical torso's velocity, and it does not include vertical jump speed.

member.returns: The last cached movement velocity in metres per second: x is world X, and y is world Z.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.Jump
member.summary: Starts the jump-pose sequence when jumping is enabled, invokes , and attempts an extra jump when is enabled.

remarks.para: When jumpEnabled is false, this method does nothing. Otherwise it first invokes onPlayerJump, if a handler exists. A handler is a function notified about the event; it receives no jump data. The jumping flag and stage are changed only after the handler returns, so a handler sees the state from before this call.

The method then marks the sequence active, selects stage 0, clears the feet-smoothing rate of change, and prepares the target from the avatar's chest height and current neck-to-support-point height. Both heights are distances in metres measured along the rig's up direction; the center of pressure is the body's support reference point. The starting cycle value can be negative, depending on the current feet offset. It plays the effort sound and enables the physics rig's body-mass hold.

If doubleJump is enabled, it asks the physics rig to accept an extra-jump request using doubleJumpPower and a 1-second cooldown. The extra-jump sound plays only when that request is accepted. This call does not itself assign an upward torso velocity or prove that the player has left the ground.
Calling Jump again while its sequence is already active still invokes the event and restarts stage 0; there is no already-jumping guard in this method.

The mass hold keeps the physics rig's natural mass-distribution mode selected while its ball-based movement mode is enabled. Mass distribution means how body mass is divided among the physical parts. Clearing the hold lets foot support choose that mode again; it does not directly set a new mass in kilograms.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.JumpCharge(System.Single,System.Boolean@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Eases the feet-height control toward a jump-preparation pose while charge input is enabled.

remarks.para: This changes the preparation pose; it does not build up jumpVelocity as time passes. The target combines the saved crouch target, a correction for the current neck-to-support-point height, and a lowering amount equal to one quarter of the avatar's standing pelvis height. Those heights and the resulting offset are in metres.

The feet offset eases toward this target using a saved rate of change, and the extra spine-crouch control eases toward zero. If a jump sequence is already active, preparation cancels it, releases its body-mass hold, and restores the cached support-radius multiplier to 1.3.
False chargeInput returns immediately, leaving feetOverride and the pose controls unchanged. A processed charge sets feetOverride to true so ordinary feet recovery does not take over this update.
The support point mentioned here is the center of pressure, the physics body's reference point for support through the ground.

The mass hold keeps the physics rig's natural mass-distribution mode selected while its ball-based movement mode is enabled. Mass distribution means how body mass is divided among the physical parts. Clearing the hold lets foot support choose that mode again; it does not directly set a new mass in kilograms.

member.param: Duration of this update in seconds for the preparation-pose adjustment.
Set to true when preparation handles the feet; left unchanged when chargeInput is false.
Whether to apply the preparation pose. Defaults to true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.JumpEnd
member.summary: Stops the jump-pose sequence and releases the physics rig's jump mass hold.

remarks.para: It clears the jumping flag, clears bodyMassNaturalHold on the physics rig, and calls the support-radius setup with a multiplier of 1.3. That number is a size multiplier, not a 1.3-metre radius.
It does not reset the saved jump stage, cycle time, flight-time estimate, feet offset, or horizontal movement velocity. Ending this control sequence does not establish that the body has landed.

The mass hold keeps the physics rig's natural mass-distribution mode selected while its ball-based movement mode is enabled. Mass distribution means how body mass is divided among the physical parts. Clearing the hold lets foot support choose that mode again; it does not directly set a new mass in kilograms.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.Jumping(System.Single,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Advances the jump's feet and spine pose through push-off, tuck, and recovery stages.

remarks.para: Each call adds deltaTime seconds to the cycle clock and sets feetOverride to true. Stage 0 extends the feet control toward the avatar's toe-stretched pose. It enters stage 1 only when the physics rig reports leaving support this frame and the torso's upward speed relative to the ground exceeds one quarter of the configured jumpVelocity. Here jumpVelocity is the upward-speed threshold setting in metres per second. The relative upward speed is the torso's world-Y speed minus the ground's world-Y speed, also in metres per second.

At that transition it predicts a flight duration from upward speed and gravity, resets the cycle clock to zero, and changes the cached lower-body support-radius multiplier to 1.1. The torso speed comes from its Rigidbody, Unity's component that lets physics move an object.

Stages 1 and 2 sample JumpCurve using progress = cycleTime / predictedDuration. Here cycleTime is the running cycle clock in seconds, predictedDuration is the saved predicted flight duration in seconds, and progress is their unitless ratio. The curve changes the feet-offset target and extra spine-crouch control. The feet offset moves toward its target by at most 8 metres per second times the duration of this update. This method adjusts the pose controls rather than directly damping the torso's flight velocity.

After the cycle exceeds half the predicted duration, stage 1 switches to stage 2 and sets the cached support-radius multiplier to 1.4. The cycle clock keeps running. Stage 2 ends the sequence only after progress exceeds 1.3. Stage 0 can also end through its avatar-height-dependent timeout if the leaving-support condition never succeeds. These stage changes are timed controls, not proof of touching the ground.

member.param: Duration of this update in seconds. Added to the cycle clock and used to limit feet-offset movement.
Set to true on every call, indicating that the jump controls handle this update's feet position.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.MantleGesture(System.Single@)
member.summary: Checks whether the saved hand-support scores request a pull-up while the feet have little support.

remarks.para: It returns true when footSupported is below 0.2 and the left and right hands' armMantle scores add to a positive number. These are dimensionless control scores: they have no metre or second unit. One hand can supply the positive score; both do not have to contribute.

For a successful test, mantle = handSum × clamp((0.2 - footSupport) / 0.2, 0, 1). Here handSum is the sum of the two hand scores, footSupport is the physics rig's foot-support score, and clamp limits the factor to the range 0 to 1. For example, handSum of 1 and footSupport of 0.1 produce mantle of 0.5.

If foot support is 0.2 or greater, the output is zero. With less support but a nonpositive hand sum, the output is that unscaled sum and the result is false. The method reads existing scores; it does not search for a ledge or measure how far a climb has progressed.

member.param: Output strength of the hand-supported pull-up request. A successful result scales the summed hand scores down as foot support approaches 0.2; this is not elapsed climb progress.
member.returns: True when foot support is below 0.2 and the summed hand scores are positive; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.MoveSpineCrouchOffTowards(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Moves the saved extra spine-crouch control toward a target and copies the changed value to the animation rig.

remarks.para: The control is a unitless number supplied by the crouch and jump pose calculations. This method changes that number; it does not directly move a spine bone by a distance in metres.

For a nonnegative rate, each call changes the control by at most rate × deltaTime. Here rate is control units per second and deltaTime is the update duration in seconds. For example, rate 2 and a 0.02-second update allow a change of 0.04 toward the target, without going past it.

If the saved control is already approximately equal to the target, the method leaves it and the animation rig's value untouched. Otherwise it saves the new control and forwards it as the animation rig's spineCrouchOffset. The default rate is 6.5 when the caller does not supply another value.

member.param: Desired extra crouch control, with no distance unit.
Duration of this update in seconds.
Maximum control change per second. Use a nonnegative value to approach the target; defaults to 6.5.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.Reset
member.summary: Sets up the rig's named body transforms through the base rig reset routine.

remarks.para: The base routine finds or creates the transform objects that represent parts such as the head, chest, spine, pelvis, arms, legs, and center of pressure. A transform stores an object's position, rotation, and size, and the routine arranges these objects under the rig's hierarchy.

This override only calls that setup routine. It does not clear RemapRig's movement velocities, jump state, turn queue, or procedural pose offsets. Calling Reset is therefore not a way to stop the player's current movement or cancel a jump.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.SetAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar)
member.summary: When given a non-null avatar, applies its stored body dimensions to this rig and updates its movement and navigation settings.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, rotation, and scale. The navigation agent is Unity's component that plans and follows routes over walkable navigation surfaces.

The supplied avatar reference is stored first. When it is non-null, the rig's maximum movement speed is twice the avatar's speed rating and its maximum acceleration setting is seven times the avatar's agility rating. The resulting movement settings are used as metres per second and metres per second squared; the avatar ratings are input tuning numbers.

For a non-null avatar, this places the rig's spine, chest, neck, head, and shoulder reference transforms using dimensions and offsets already stored on the avatar, then calibrates the shoulder, elbow, hip, knee, and foot reference positions to the avatar's limb measurements. If a testAdditiveRig exists, it receives the avatar too. This method does not directly set physical joint limits; a physics joint is the connection that constrains how two physics bodies move relative to each other.

The navigation agent receives body-size settings, a speed of twice the newly calculated maximum movement speed, and an acceleration of ten times the newly calculated maximum acceleration setting. When a non-null avatar is supplied, this setup path requires the rig reference transforms and navigation-agent reference to already exist.

These are setup-time calculations. Changing the avatar's speed, agility, or body measurements afterward does not rerun this method or automatically rebuild these saved movement settings and transform placements.

member.param: Avatar whose stored measurements, speed rating, and agility rating configure this rig. A non-null avatar is required for successful setup. Passing null stores a null reference, skips avatar setup, and then reaches the method's failure path.

remarks.para: The position in displace is a movement amount in metres, not a destination. For example, position (1, 0, 0) moves the root 1 metre toward positive world X from wherever it is now. The rotation stored in displace is ignored by this method.

With zeroVelocity true, it clears currentVelocity and currentAcceleration. These are the remap movement control caches; it does not clear the effectiveAcceleration value retained by the movement smoother, the queued turn, or the velocities of physical body parts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.Gimbal(System.Single,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Smooths changes in a scalar target by returning the target plus a limited, gradually fading offset.

remarks.para: A scalar is one number, such as a distance or an angle. This helper does not wrap angles at 360 degrees. Keep lastTarget, gimbaledVelocity, gimbalAccel, and gimbleOffset between calls: they are the saved history, and the method changes them through the ref parameters. Initializing lastTarget to the first target avoids treating the starting value as a sudden jump.

With positive deltaTime and maxOffset, targetSpeed = (target - lastTarget) / deltaTime. Here targetSpeed is the target's change per second, target is this call's requested number, lastTarget is the previous saved target, and deltaTime is this step's duration in seconds. The method smooths targetSpeed into gimbaledVelocity, adds (gimbaledVelocity - targetSpeed) × deltaTime to gimbleOffset, then multiplies that offset by 1 - lerpRate × deltaTime. Finally it limits gimbleOffset to the range from -maxOffset to +maxOffset, saves target in lastTarget, and returns target + gimbleOffset.

Use one consistent unit for target, lastTarget, gimbleOffset, and maxOffset. If target is in meters, gimbaledVelocity is meters per second and gimbalAccel is meters per second squared. lerpRate is per second; smoothTime is in seconds and controls the approximate response of the speed smoothing, not an exact number of frames.

For example, target = 0.20 meters and maxOffset = 0.02 meters keep the returned value between 0.18 and 0.22 meters when both maxOffset and deltaTime are positive. The fading multiplier is not limited to 0–1: lerpRate = 50 per second and deltaTime = 0.02 seconds make it zero, while a larger product can reverse the offset before the final limit.

If maxOffset is zero or negative, the method returns target without changing the saved history. With positive maxOffset but zero or negative deltaTime, it returns target plus the existing gimbleOffset without updating or limiting that offset.

member.param: The requested scalar value for this call, in the caller's chosen unit.
Saved target from the previous processed call, in the same unit as target; replaced by target after a positive-time update.
Saved smoothed target speed, in target units per second; updated by the speed smoother.
Saved rate of change of gimbaledVelocity, in target units per second squared; updated by the speed smoother.
Saved offset added to target, in target units; updated, faded, and limited during a positive-time update.
Offset fading rate per second. The method uses the multiplier 1 - lerpRate × deltaTime without limiting that multiplier.
Duration represented by this call, in seconds.
Maximum absolute offset in target units. Zero or negative disables the offset; the default is the largest finite float.
Approximate response time of the target-speed smoother, in seconds; defaults to 0.1 seconds.
member.returns: The target plus the saved offset when maxOffset is positive, or the unchanged target when maxOffset is zero or negative.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.OnAfterFixedUpdate
member.summary: Provides a callback for a previous physics step before the manager starts its next fixed or regular update.

remarks.para: A callback is a method the manager calls at a particular point in its work. The manager records that a fixed update ran. At the beginning of a later FixedUpdate or Update, it checks that record and calls this hook before running the next set of rig updates. This is not an immediate call at the end of physics simulation.

When these calls are delivered, the manager first sends an available Seat component its separate OnPlayerAfterFixedUpdate notification. A Seat is a scene component for sitting, rather than a Rig subclass. The manager then calls this Rig hook on the controller rig, its enabled remapping pass, and the physics rig. A fixed step is one scheduled physics update; several can happen between displayed frames. The manager's regular Update clears the pending record after delivering these callbacks.

This hook is a callback: a method the manager calls at a particular point in its work. The base Rig implementation is empty. A derived rig, meaning a more specific rig class, overrides this method to do its own work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.Reset
member.summary: Finds the rig's main bone transforms, creating missing child objects, and stores its center-of-pressure transform.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object's position, rotation, and scale. This method looks for named children directly under the rig object for the head, neck, chest, spine, pelvis, both shoulders, elbows, hands, hips, knees, feet, and center of pressure. When a child is missing, it creates a GameObject with that name and parents it directly to the rig object, then saves the transform reference.

It does not build a shoulder-to-elbow-to-hand parent chain: each newly created object is a direct child of the rig. It also does not find or create the jaw or either clavicle, so those references need separate setup. The center-of-pressure result is a named transform reference; this method does not calculate a pressure point from physics contacts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.SampleSpinePose
member.summary: Returns a world-space pose at the pelvis, with rotation blended equally between the pelvis and spine.

remarks.para: The returned position is the pelvis's position in world space: coordinates measured from the scene's origin, in meters for normal BONELAB scaling. The rotation comes from Quaternion.LerpUnclamped with a blend value of 0.5 between the pelvis and spine world rotations. A quaternion is Unity's four-number way to store a rotation; this is a rotation blend, not a component-by-component average of angles.

For example, rotating the spine while leaving the pelvis unchanged can change the returned rotation, but the returned position still comes from the pelvis. Both transform references must be set. This method only samples them; it does not move either bone.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.InternalTeleport
member.summary: Applies the stored teleport destination to the controller, remap stages, and physical body.

remarks.para: The stored destination contains a feet position in world-space meters and an orientation. The move is measured from the physical rig’s center-of-pressure position, its reference point beneath the body. The method also straightens the rig against world up and turns it toward the stored facing direction. If the player occupies a seat, it exits that seat first.

During normal operation EarlyUpdate, the manager’s early per-frame pass, calls this after the queued avatar change and before the queued body-state change. That caller clears the pending teleport flag afterwards. Calling InternalTeleport directly applies the stored data immediately; it does not check or clear that flag itself, so a still-pending request can be processed again.

The stored zeroVelocity option is passed to each rig’s teleport routine. It requests clearing motion as part of the move. For example, an ordinary Teleport request can place the feet at world position (0, 0, 5), then this method performs that move in the next early pass.

member.summary: Queues an existing instance for the next early avatar-switch pass.

remarks.para: The call stores the candidate and marks an avatar change pending. It does not load an avatar crate or immediately change the avatar getter. The early pass requires the candidate’s Animator and either its LeftEye bone or its eyeCenterOverride, a reference used to place the eyes when eye bones are missing. An Animator is the Unity component that connects animation poses to the model’s skeleton. If accepted, the candidate is used to fit the rigs, the body bones and code that position them. A later request made before that pass replaces the stored candidate.

For example, after SwapAvatar(myAvatar), avatar can still return the old body until the early pass runs. This method does not invoke onAvatarSwapped or onAvatarSwapped2; those notifications belong to the asynchronous crate-switch path, which loads and waits over time.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.Load
member.summary: Loads this session’s level content and prepares the player, returning a UniTask that callers can await to wait for the operation to finish.

remarks.para: A UniTask is a completion object: awaiting it lets your routine continue after this operation finishes. Load can pause across frames while a scene load or a wait condition is incomplete. It first uses _loadLevel for the loading scene, then loads persistent content from _level. Player-marker spawn work happens before the level-load notification.

Load waits until the registered load-dependency count is below 1. Its texture-count wait runs only when Unity’s streaming-mipmap memory budget is nonzero; a zero budget skips that wait. A texture is an image used on surfaces, and mipmaps are smaller versions of that image used at lower detail. When the wait runs, no more than 4 textures may be loading and fewer than 5 may be waiting to load. For example, counts of 4 loading and 4 pending pass; 5 loading or 5 pending do not. These are counts, not elapsed-time limits.

A later wait requires ZoneManagerPlugin.InactiveManager.ApplyCount to be below 1. InactiveManager handles pending changes to inactive objects, and ApplyCount counts changes waiting in its apply queue. A count of zero means that queue is empty. Load expects the manager to exist; a missing manager follows a failure path rather than passing the wait.

Load sets Status to DONE (StreamStatus value 2), safely invokes any queued _doLevelLoad callbacks, then clears that stored batch. A callback is a routine the session calls at a loading phase. DONE marks this notification point; afterward Load still awaits the after-level-load plugin work, waits 11 frames, unloads the loading scene, and restores loading settings before the UniTask completes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.LoadPersistentScenes
member.summary: Loads the persistent game areas listed by this session’s primary level reference, waits for their scene-load queue, makes the main Scene active, and returns it.

remarks.para: A Scene is a loaded game area. The method looks up the crate named by _level in AssetWarehouse, the game’s crate registry. It adds that crate’s main scene asset and every listed extra MarrowScene asset to _persistentQueue. MarrowScene is the scene-asset record, and each asset is queued by its GUID, its unique asset ID.

SceneLoadQueue collects these requests and loads them together. The method awaits its completion, retrieves the main scene by its saved GUID, tells Unity’s SceneManager to make it the active scene, and returns that Scene. Here the main scene is the root asset. This method reads _level; _loadLevel separately chooses Load’s initial loading scene.

member.summary: Unity’s initialization callback adds hand-switching support for a small sphere, performs base grip setup, and caches the normal hand pose.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine Unity calls to perform initialization. First, radius below 0.05 m, or 5 cm, adds SwitchHands to the interaction options. It then runs Grip’s setup: registers the grip in component caches, copies defaultGripDistance into the active distance and squared-distance values, and uses this component’s Transform as targetTransform if none is assigned. Finally, a valid configured handPose is cached as the normal pose for flipped-pose selection.

These are initialization changes, not continuous synchronization. This routine does not read autoConfigure or overwrite dynamicFriction or staticFriction. Changing radius later does not make Awake rerun its hand-switch option check.
defaultGripDistance is the initial palm-to-sphere scoring-gap threshold, measured in metres. A Transform is Unity’s component that holds an object’s position, rotation, and scale.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.CheckHandPriority(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandGripPair@,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandGripPair@)
member.summary: Can swap the primary and secondary hand/grip pairs when both use the same grip and their targets align.

remarks.para: Each pair records a hand and its grip. If the two grip references differ, it leaves both pairs unchanged. Otherwise it compares their stored target poses relative to that grip. It proceeds only when their rotated forward directions pass the strict alignment test: the direction dot product must be at least 1; for unit direction vectors, 1 means they point the same way.

It keeps the order when the primary target is ahead of the secondary along the primary target’s forward direction. Otherwise it swaps both whole pairs, including when their positions are equal along that direction. For an illustrative pair of identically oriented targets, a secondary target 0.10 m farther forward becomes primary. This method does not score grips, attach a hand, or change the stored target poses.

member.param: The current primary pair, replaced with secondary if the swap conditions pass.
The current secondary pair, replaced with primary if the swap conditions pass.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.ClampHandleInTarget(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform)
member.summary: Centers a handle in the target’s frame and limits how far its primary axis can swing.

remarks.para: The input is a position-and-rotation pose relative to targetTransform. The result’s position is always zero in that frame, even for a large radius. Zero means the target’s center, not world origin.

The routine aligns the handle’s configured primary direction with the grip’s primary direction, then allows the original rotation back only as far as rotationLimit permits. rotationLimit is an angle in degrees. For example, a 30-degree limit bounds an otherwise 60-degree swing to 30 degrees. This helper returns a pose; it does not move a hand, change a Rigidbody, or create a joint.

member.param: The handle pose already expressed relative to targetTransform, using meter offsets and a rotation.
member.returns: A target-relative pose centered at zero with the primary-axis swing constrained.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.FreeJoint(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Records the hand as free to rotate, centers its target, and updates the connection anchors.

remarks.para: The hand is added to _isJointFree before any anchor callback or target adjustment. The existing target rotation is retained while its target-relative position is set to zero. The hand-side anchor is rebuilt from the animator’s current handle pose, including the large-sphere offset when required; the connected anchor is then updated from the grip’s host-relative target.

Free mode is recorded per hand in _isJointFree. UpdateJointConfiguration later sets that hand joint’s rotational restoring drive to zero while free, or a strong restoring drive while locked. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and the held object; a drive applies spring-like correction toward its target. Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.

Large-sphere calculations use excess = max(radius − _maxRadius, 0). radius is the inherited sphere radius in meters, _maxRadius is this grip’s radius threshold in meters, and excess is the resulting meter amount used to scale the chosen unitless direction vector. For illustrative values of radius 0.10 m and _maxRadius 0.04 m, excess is 0.06 m, giving a 6 cm displacement when that direction is a unit vector. This threshold does not clamp the sphere radius.

Hand.UpdateAnchor can invoke its anchor-change callback before writing the joint anchor, so a callback listener already sees IsJointFree as true. Calling this routine again repeats the target and anchor work even when the hand was already in the set.

An anchor is a joint connection point: the hand-side anchor belongs to the hand, and the connected anchor belongs to the held target. Here, targetTransform is the grip’s position-and-rotation reference whose origin is used for the zero target-relative position.

member.param: The hand whose free-mode membership and connection anchors are updated.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.GetForcePullHandTransform(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Returns the neutral handle pose relative to the hand, with an extra offset for a large sphere.

remarks.para: The pose comes from the hand animator using this grip’s selected hand pose. Its position is measured in meters in the hand’s frame, and its rotation is relative to the hand. It is intended for lining the grip up with the hand during force pulling; the result is not already in world coordinates.

Large-sphere calculations use excess = max(radius − _maxRadius, 0). radius is the inherited sphere radius in meters, _maxRadius is this grip’s radius threshold in meters, and excess is the resulting meter amount used to scale the chosen unitless direction vector. For illustrative values of radius 0.10 m and _maxRadius 0.04 m, excess is 0.06 m, giving a 6 cm displacement when that direction is a unit vector. This threshold does not clamp the sphere radius.

For a large sphere, the additional displacement follows the grip’s tertiary direction, meaning its third configured axis, rotated by the neutral handle orientation and reversed for the right hand. This call returns the desired pose and does not start a force pull or apply a force.

member.param: The hand whose animator and hand side define the neutral local pose.
member.returns: The neutral handle pose in hand coordinates, including the large-sphere offset when applicable.

remarks.para: For radius at or below _maxRadius, it returns the current per-hand target in world coordinates. For a larger sphere, it constructs a target-relative offset along the tertiary direction, the grip’s third configured axis, reverses it for the left hand, and composes it with targetTransform’s world position and rotation.

Large-sphere calculations use excess = max(radius − _maxRadius, 0). radius is the inherited sphere radius in meters, _maxRadius is this grip’s radius threshold in meters, and excess is the resulting meter amount used to scale the chosen unitless direction vector. For illustrative values of radius 0.10 m and _maxRadius 0.04 m, excess is 0.06 m, giving a 6 cm displacement when that direction is a unit vector. This threshold does not clamp the sphere radius.

member.summary: Builds a neutral rotation for the hand while copying the position returned by the host-target helper.

remarks.para: The rotation is targetTransform’s world rotation, with the left hand’s configured axis-frame flip applied; the right hand uses the unflipped rotation. A neutral pose is an alignment target rather than the hand’s current physical pose.

The position is copied from GetTargetInHost without converting it back to world coordinates. When Host is assigned and its HasRigidbody property is true, GetTargetInHost uses the Host’s Transform to express the target relative to Host. If Host is null or HasRigidbody is false, it composes the stored target through targetTransform into world coordinates. HasRigidbody reports whether the host has a physics body; this helper checks that report, not the separate Rb property that returns the body itself. This method computes rotation separately in world coordinates, so position and rotation use different frames only when an assigned Host reports HasRigidbody as true. Despite the method name, do not assume the position can always be used as a world location.

Here, Host means the grippable object assigned to this grip. A Transform is Unity’s component that holds an object’s position, rotation, and scale. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

remarks.para: This is a membership query, not a measurement of whether a Rigidbody is rotating or the live joint has already applied its zero restoring drive. FreeJoint adds the hand before anchor updates; LockJoint removes it before target updates. Detachment also removes the hand.

Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.OnAttachedToHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Performs base attachment handling, then suppresses automatic updates of this hand’s two grip anchors.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called to report attachment. Base Grip attachment runs first, including marking the hand state active, invoking the optional base attachment action, setting the Attached grip flag, locking hover, and adding the hand to attachedHands. Only after that base work does SphereGrip set isIgnoreAnchorUpdate and isIgnoreConnAnchorUpdate true in the hand state.

A listener in the base attachment action therefore runs before SphereGrip writes these two ignore flags and before the base Attached flag is set. The connected-anchor permission query becomes false after isIgnoreConnAnchorUpdate is set. FreeJoint can still explicitly rebuild the anchors; suppressing automatic update does not remove the physical connection.
An anchor is a joint connection point: one belongs to the hand, and the connected anchor belongs to the held target.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.OnDetachedFromHand(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Removes the hand from free mode and clears the anchor-ignore flags before base detachment reports.

remarks.para: In order, it removes the hand from _isJointFree, obtains the hand state, clears isIgnoreAnchorUpdate and isIgnoreConnAnchorUpdate, then calls Grip’s detach handling. The base handler marks the state inactive before invoking its optional detached action, then performs further hover and state/list cleanup.

A listener in that base detached action sees the hand already outside the free set and the two ignore flags already false. This callback is a routine called to report a detach; calling it is not itself a replacement for the hand’s complete object/joint-release operation.

Free mode is recorded per hand in _isJointFree. UpdateJointConfiguration later sets that hand joint’s rotational restoring drive to zero while free, or a strong restoring drive while locked. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and the held object; a drive applies spring-like correction toward its target. Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.OnHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Chooses the normal or flipped hand pose when configured, then runs the base hover-pose update.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called while a hand hovers. If handPoseOnFlippedPrimaryAxis is assigned, TargetGrip’s pose selection examines hand orientation and chooses the normal or flipped pose; SphereGrip assigns that pose before base hover work. The flipped selection depends on the inherited primary/tertiary flip options, not simply on entering the sphere’s radius.

The base hover routine first calls this grip’s boolean hover/grab overload with isOverride false. That call stores the radius-dependent target and checks the ordinary grab request. Only if it returns true does the base routine continue with finger-curl preview updates and the optional hover-update action. The normal/flipped pose selection above happens before that check.

member.param: The hovering hand whose pose is selected and previewed.

member.summary: Stores a radius-dependent hover target, then asks the base grip to evaluate or perform the requested grab.

remarks.para: The current hand handle is expressed relative to targetTransform. For radius at or below _maxRadius, the target position is centered and retains the handle orientation. A larger sphere positions the target at the excess-radius distance along the center-to-handle direction and adjusts its orientation for the hand side. The result is stored in world coordinates before base hover/grab checks run.

Large-sphere calculations use excess = max(radius − _maxRadius, 0). radius is the inherited sphere radius in meters, _maxRadius is this grip’s radius threshold in meters, and excess is the resulting meter amount used to scale the chosen unitless direction vector. For illustrative values of radius 0.10 m and _maxRadius 0.04 m, excess is 0.06 m, giving a 6 cm displacement when that direction is a unit vector. This threshold does not clamp the sphere radius.

With isOverride false, the inherited routine checks availability and the controller’s grab request. With true, it runs the inherited forced quick-grab path, which can attach the hand and bypass the ordinary disabled/inactive check. This flag therefore has action consequences beyond changing a preview. The cached target has already been written even if the ordinary path later returns false.

member.summary: Performs base joint attachment work, then chooses free or locked rotational behavior.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called after the hand joint attaches. Base Grip work runs first, including joining the virtual-controller hand/grip pair and updating the joint configuration. SphereGrip then chooses its mode.

For a grip whose host has a Rigidbody and radius is at most 0.05 m, or 5 cm, an unheld secondary interaction button chooses FreeJoint. A held button chooses LockJoint. Larger spheres and grips without a Rigidbody choose LockJoint. The threshold here is a fixed radius test and does not use _maxRadius.

Free mode is recorded per hand in _isJointFree. UpdateJointConfiguration later sets that hand joint’s rotational restoring drive to zero while free, or a strong restoring drive while locked. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and the held object; a drive applies spring-like correction toward its target. Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.
Because the initial configuration update occurs before this free/lock decision, the live restoring drive may still reflect the previous membership until a later configuration update.
The host is the grippable object that owns this grip. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Refreshes a free hand’s desired world orientation during the runtime skeleton’s physics update.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called during a skeleton physics update. It does work only when the hand has a live joint and is recorded in _isJointFree. It starts with the controller-handle orientation. If rotationLimit is below 180 degrees, it constrains the controller’s primary direction toward the target’s primary direction within that angular limit; 180 degrees or more leaves that orientation unrestricted by this step.

The stored world target position is targetTransform.position. The result is written to the grip’s desired target for this hand; this callback does not itself change free-set membership or apply a new live drive. Free rotation can therefore still use limited, continually updated hand positioning.
A joint is the physics connection between the hand and held object; its rotational drive applies spring-like correction toward a target orientation.

member.param: The hand with a live joint whose free-mode target is refreshed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.SetupConfiguration(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandJointConfiguration)
member.summary: Fills a hand-joint configuration with fixed position and the sphere’s permitted angular motion.

remarks.para: This modifies the supplied configuration object rather than applying it to an existing live joint. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and object. The grip’s primary and secondary directions define its axes; all three linear directions are locked, connected-anchor automatic setup is disabled, and angular X is free.

Angular Y and Z are limited by rotationLimit when it is below 180 degrees, and are free at 180 degrees or more. The angular limit values are in degrees. The configuration selects spherical rotational drive mode and removes angular-limit spring correction. Its later live drive strength is chosen by UpdateJointConfiguration from the free-hand set.

The routine writes these settings directly and does not read autoConfigure, dynamicFriction, or staticFriction. Calling it again replaces those settings in the passed configuration; it does not grant a new hand attachment.
The connected anchor is the connection point on the object attached to the hand. A rotational drive applies spring-like correction toward the target orientation.

member.param: The configuration object to fill before applying it to a hand joint.

The requested target position is retained; this method does not clamp that position to a sphere surface or use the friction fields.

The checked implementation also accesses the supplied hand’s physical body, live joint, and connected body while calculating. Those references must exist even though this routine returns a pose rather than applying it. It does not change its result based on applyOffsetBlending.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.DECREASE_TIMESCALE
member.summary: Requests the stored step plus 1, clamped to the helper range, when slow motion is enabled.

remarks.para: This adds 1 to the stored index, clamps the result from 0 through max_timeScaleStep, and requests that step's intensity transition. The initial helper range is 0 through 3. Index 0 means normal intensity 1; each larger index doubles the unitless intensity, and Unity's timeScale is its reciprocal. For example, index 1 applies 0.5 speed and index 3 applies 0.125 speed. With the initial maximum of 3, index 3 stays there. STEP_TIMESCALE can store an index outside the helper range: for example, stored index 10 becomes 3 after this request, rather than moving deeper into slow motion.

When enabled, this method raises OnSlowTime with the resulting step as a float after writing the step, even if the step was already at its limit. When slow motion is disabled, it returns without changing the step or raising the event.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.DROP_TIMESCALE
member.summary: Starts easing toward the strongest configured slow motion when slow motion is enabled.

remarks.para: The default maximum intensity is 8, which corresponds to Unity's timeScale of 1/8. This sets that intensity as the target and snapshots the starting intensity; the time-update handler moves toward the target over time. It leaves the step index and slowMoEnabled flag alone, and does not raise OnSlowTime. If slow motion is disabled, this method does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.INCREASE_TIMESCALE
member.summary: Requests the stored step minus 1, clamped to the helper range, to ease toward its matching speed.

remarks.para: The initial helper range is 0 through 3, with 0 representing normal speed. This subtracts 1 from the stored index, clamps the result from 0 through max_timeScaleStep, then requests the matching intensity transition. STEP_TIMESCALE can store an index outside that range, so this can select a range boundary instead of simply lowering the stored value by one. For example, with maximum 3, stored index -5 becomes 0 and stored index 10 becomes 3. It does not raise OnSlowTime.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.PAUSE
member.summary: Sets Unity's scaled game time to zero and saves the previous time scale for UNPAUSE.

remarks.para: Calling this while already paused has no effect. The manager marks itself paused, stores the current Unity timeScale, then sets timeScale to 0; scaled time stops advancing, while the saved value remains available for restoration. This does not reset the slow-motion step or its target.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.RESET_TIMESCALE
member.summary: When the cached time scale differs from 1, clears the transition and restores normal Unity time.

remarks.para: If the cached scale is already 1, this method returns without changing anything. Otherwise it stores 1 and clears the transition flag; it does not change the stored step index or slowMoEnabled. When not paused, it also applies Unity timeScale = 1 and sets fixedDeltaTime to 1 divided by the recommended physics frequency. Physics frequency is the number of physics steps per second, so fixedDeltaTime is the seconds per step. While paused this method leaves Unity timeScale at 0; UNPAUSE later restores the saved value of 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.RISE_TIMESCALE
member.summary: Starts easing the current intensity back toward 1, which is normal speed.

remarks.para: This sets the transition target to intensity 1 and records the current intensity as the starting point. It does not change the stored step index or the slowMoEnabled flag. The regular time-update handler applies the transition when its slow-motion and pause gates allow it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.SET_TIMESCALE(System.Single)
member.summary: Applies a slow-motion intensity directly, using its reciprocal as Unity's timeScale.
member.param: A unitless multiplier: 1 is normal speed, and larger values mean slower simulation.

remarks.para: The value is clamped from 1 to the configured maximum, initially 8. For example, intensity 4 applies timeScale 0.25. If slow motion is disabled, requests above 1 are ignored; a request of 1 or less is still accepted and becomes normal speed. This sets the scale immediately rather than starting an eased transition, does not change the step index or raise OnSlowTime, and only writes Unity timeScale when the manager is not paused. When applied, fixedDeltaTime becomes timeScale divided by the recommended physics frequency; frequency means physics steps per second, so fixedDeltaTime is seconds per step.

remarks.para: The usual helper-managed indexes are 0 through 3: their target intensities are 1, 2, 4, and 8, so their Unity time scales are 1, 0.5, 0.25, and 0.125. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.TOGGLE_TIMESCALE

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.Awake
member.summary: Requests registration of this node with the VoidLogic manager, using the nearest owning MarrowEntity.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: Unity calls it when it initializes this component. The base implementation searches this object and its parents for a MarrowEntity, which identifies the owning game entity when present, then passes the node and search result to the VoidLogic manager.

The manager records a pending registration request. Returning from Awake does not prove that the node already has a built subgraph or initialized signal state. A derived node that replaces this routine should call the base implementation if it needs this registration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.OnDestroy
member.summary: Requests removal of this node from the VoidLogic manager when Unity destroys the component.

remarks.para: OnDestroy is a routine Unity calls during component destruction. The base implementation submits a removal request to the manager; graph cleanup is processed later. It does not immediately clear this node's saved connection array.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.OnDisable
member.summary: Queues a request to disable this node in the logic graph when Unity disables the component.

remarks.para: OnDisable is a routine Unity calls when the component or its object becomes disabled. The manager later marks the registered node's cached NodeState.Enabled flag false. The subgraph, a group of connected logic components, checks that flag before running the node's calculations.
The request preserves saved input connections. The flag changes when the manager processes the request, rather than inside this routine itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.OnEnable
member.summary: Queues a request to enable this node in the logic graph when Unity enables the component.

remarks.para: OnEnable is a routine Unity calls when the component becomes enabled on an active object. The manager later marks the registered node's cached NodeState.Enabled flag true and marks its subgraph for recalculation. A subgraph is a group of connected logic components.
This request does not calculate an output immediately. It takes effect when the manager processes it and finds the node in its registered group.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode.SLZ_Marrow_VoidLogic_IVoidLogicSensor_ReadSensors(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.NodeState@)
member.summary: Measures the shaft's travel and saves a continuous value for the next Power calculation.

remarks.para: The logic system calls this sensor method through IVoidLogicSensor, the common interface for nodes that measure something in the scene. NodeState is the node's saved working data; the method changes the supplied data directly. It also marks the node's connected group of logic components as needing calculation when that group exists.

The saved value is p = 1 - d² / L². Here d is the current full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, from the joint's object to _endTransform; L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. Both distances use positions in the scene, rather than positions relative to a parent. The value p has no unit: it is 0 at the setup distance, 1 at the endpoint and 0.75 halfway along a straight path. It is not clamped; a distance larger than L gives a negative value. A zero setup distance makes the division invalid.

A missing Rigidbody, the component that lets physics move the shaft, leaves the saved value unchanged. After the first attempted measurement with a valid body, later reads also leave it unchanged while that body sleeps, meaning physics has paused its motion because it is resting. This method does not change _isPressed. Calculate later multiplies the saved value by the incoming Power signal; no readable input produces output 0.

member.param: The node's saved working data, supplied by reference so this method can store the measured travel value in it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.TryConnectPortToInput(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.OutputPortReference,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Saves a source signal or constant number into the volume's single Power input and reports the connection change to the logic manager.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a numeric signal. Only input index 0 is accepted. Other indices return false and leave the saved connection unchanged. For index 0, the supplied reference replaces _previousConnection before the manager is notified.

True means that this input index accepted the reference and the manager notification returned. It does not prove the reference can currently supply a value or that a damage tick has happened. Each later damage attempt reads the saved reference; an unreadable signal supplies 0 to the volume's Power mapping.

member.param: The source output reference, or an inline constant number, to save into Power input 0.
The target input index. Use 0 for Power; every other index is rejected.
member.returns: True for an accepted index 0 after notification returns; false for any other index.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.TryGetInputConnection(System.UInt32,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.OutputPortReference@)
member.summary: Copies the saved Power connection and reports whether it can be treated as a valid reference.

remarks.para: Only input index 0 is supported. For that index, connectedPort receives _previousConnection even if the reference is invalid; the return value is then its validity check. A constant number stored directly in the reference counts as valid. A node reference needs an existing object that supplies VoidLogic output signals.

For any other index, connectedPort is cleared to an empty reference and the method returns false. Validity does not guarantee a live graph value is available or that an attack will reach a receiver. This method reads the connection without applying damage.

member.param: The input index to inspect. Index 0 is Power.
Receives the saved reference at index 0, whether valid or invalid; receives an empty reference for other indices.
member.returns: True if index 0 has a valid source reference or inline number; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.Update
member.summary: Checks once per game frame whether a damage pass is due, then processes the tracked targets in order.

remarks.para: Update is the routine Unity calls once per game frame. A pass needs at least one tracked Rigidbody, the component that gives an object physics movement, and elapsed real time of at least _tickFrequency seconds since _lastTickTime. This clock is time since the application started and continues advancing independently of Unity's Time.timeScale, the game-speed setting. The frequency field is an interval in seconds, not ticks per second.

A due pass first processes the first _playerDamageRecievers entry with multiplier 1, if there is one. It then processes every _objectDamageRecievers entry with multiplier 1. Finally it visits the tracked bodies, skips bodies listed as player receivers, and processes the others with multiplier 0.08. A destructible that remains in this final pass can therefore receive an additional smaller attack; other player-list entries do not each receive the first entry's full-strength call.

Each attempt reads Power again, maps it to a damage multiplier, checks source range and applies any speed and distance modifiers before sending an Attack, the damage message received by the target. A rejected attempt is skipped, rather than guaranteeing damage to every object inside the trigger. The trigger is a collision shape that detects entry and exit without blocking motion.

After the pass, dead character bodies collected during processing are removed from tracking and _lastTickTime is set to the current real-time clock. A slow frame produces one pass, with no loop to replay missed intervals. For example, an interval of 0.25 seconds makes a pass eligible after a quarter second; actual calls wait for a game frame and do not happen at exact fixed instants.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.TryConnectPortToInput(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.OutputPortReference,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Stores the supplied output reference as this adapter’s only input and requests a graph connection update.
member.param: The source output reference or inline constant to store.
The target input index. Use 0; all other indices are rejected.
member.returns: True after storing the reference at input 0 and submitting the manager notification on the normal return path; false for any other input index. True does not certify a readable source or a completed graph rebuild.

remarks.para: Input indices start at zero. Only inputIndex 0 is supported. For any other index, the method returns false without changing the stored connection. At index 0 it replaces _previousConnection before notifying the VoidLogic manager.

OutputPortReference identifies a source node and output index, or supplies an inline constant, a number stored directly in the reference. This method does not check that the reference can currently supply a value: accepting it is different from reading it successfully. A disconnected reference can therefore still be stored with a true return.

The manager queues a connection update for later graph processing only when the input node is a live Unity object. If that check fails, TryConnectPortToInput can still return true after the manager call returns, even though no queue entry was added. For example, connect a button’s Power output to input 0 so later adapter actuations, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, can respond to that number. A true return does not mean an event has already fired.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.TryGetInputConnection(System.UInt32,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.OutputPortReference@)
member.summary: Copies this adapter’s stored input reference and reports whether that reference is valid.
member.param: The input index to query. The only supported index is 0.
Receives the stored reference for input 0, including an invalid one; receives an empty reference for any other index.
member.returns: True when input 0 contains an inline constant or a reference to a live source node; false otherwise. This checks the reference, not whether the source has a readable cached output.

remarks.para: For inputIndex 0, connectedPort receives _previousConnection even if the method returns false. The validity check accepts an inline constant, or a live Unity object implementing IVoidLogicSource, the common interface for a node that supplies an output number. It does not check the source’s graph cache or whether its output index can be read.

For any other index, connectedPort is cleared to an empty reference and the method returns false. For example, querying index 1 fails because this adapter has only input 0. A true result at index 0 describes the reference, not proof that the adapter is enabled or that a callback, a method run by an event, has executed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Crate.CreateCrate(Il2CppSystem.Type,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Pallet,System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new crate description with the supplied owner, title, and main asset reference.

remarks.para: This factory accepts exactly SpawnableCrate, LevelCrate, AvatarCrate, and VFXCrate. Other types, including custom subclasses, return null. The generic overload uses T as that type. It creates a Unity data object (a ScriptableObject) that describes the crate; it does not load or place the referenced asset in a scene, append the crate to Pallet.Crates, or register it with the warehouse.

When generateBarcode is true, it calls GenerateBarcode after assigning the owner and title. That common routine creates or replaces the crate’s Barcode object when it is absent or invalid before calling GenerateBarcodeInternal. The owning pallet and its Barcode object must be present, and the title must be nonnull for this generation path. With generation disabled, those assignments alone do not build a new ID.

The chosen type’s MainAsset setter is used. A plain MarrowAsset reference is converted to the expected GameObject or scene reference; a different specialized asset-reference type must be compatible with the chosen crate.

member.param: The owner recorded on the new description.
The display title; also used for barcode generation.
The main asset reference, compatible with the chosen crate type.
Whether to generate an identifier after assigning the owner and title.
Exactly SpawnableCrate, LevelCrate, AvatarCrate, or VFXCrate.
member.returns: The new description, or null when the requested type is not supported.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Crate.GenerateBarcodeInternal(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Builds the crate’s ID from its pallet ID, crate-type name, and title.

remarks.para: The three segments are the owning pallet’s full ID, GetCrateName for this crate’s runtime type, and the title with periods removed. Barcode.GenerateID then cleans the segments and joins them. For example, pallet Creator.Package, a SpawnableCrate, and title Toy. Gun produce Creator.Package.Spawnable.ToyGun with the initialized period separator.

An already valid ID is preserved unless forceGeneration is true. The owner, its Barcode, this crate’s Barcode, and a nonnull title must be present even when the later GenerateID call decides to preserve the existing ID. Changing the title or owner does not run generation automatically.
This changes identifier text; it does not update warehouse dictionary keys or register the crate. Keep identifier changes separate from a barcode already serving as a registered dictionary key.

member.param: True replaces a valid existing ID; false preserves it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Crate.GetCrateName(Il2CppSystem.Type)
member.summary: Returns the cached type-name segment used when a crate barcode is generated.

remarks.para: For a type not already in CrateNames, it takes Type.Name, removes every occurrence of the case-sensitive text Crate, caches the result, and returns it. For example, AvatarCrate becomes Avatar and SpawnableCrate becomes Spawnable. This is a type-name segment, not the crate’s display Title.
Existing entries are returned as-is, so editing the shared CrateNames dictionary changes later calls and later barcode generation for that type. The type must be nonnull.

member.param: The nonnull type whose name segment is needed.
member.returns: The cached name, or Type.Name with Crate removed when first computed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Crate.LoadAssetAsync
member.summary: Waits for the crate’s MainAsset loader and returns its loaded Unity object.

remarks.para: The crate-level routine uses the virtual MainAsset property, so derived crate types select their own reference. MainAsset must be present. This routine does not register a crate, select an avatar, or instantiate a prefab copy in the scene; it forwards the asset loader’s result.

The returned task is an asynchronous result that carries the loaded object when loading finishes; await it before using the object. Completion follows the loader’s asynchronous operation, not a fixed number of frames.

member.returns: A task completing with the object returned by the main asset loader.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.GetCrateReference
member.summary: Returns the selected , or creates one from .Barcode when useQuery is true.

remarks.para: AssetWarehouse is the game's loaded catalog of crate descriptions. This method returns null while that catalog is not ready. Otherwise, when useQuery is false it returns the existing spawnableCrateReference; when true it requires a nonnull crateQuery and creates a new reference from that query's Barcode, the warehouse ID used to identify a crate.

This only returns a reference: it does not call CrateQuery.RunQuery, read tempBarcode, load a prefab, or confirm that the Barcode resolves to a SpawnableCrate. To use a RunQuery result, copy tempBarcode into crateQuery.Barcode, then call SetSpawnable.

member.returns: The selected , or null while the warehouse is not ready.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.ReSpawnSpawnable
member.summary: Starts an asynchronous pool spawn using the saved crate and policy at this spawner’s world position and rotation.

remarks.para: It calls SpawnSpawnableAsync and discards the returned task, so this method can return before the object is ready. Use the asynchronous method when code needs the resulting Poolee, the component that manages a scene object’s pool lifecycle.

It performs the same request even with manualMode enabled. The saved reference must resolve to a SpawnableCrate, and shouldSpawn can reject the request. Pool policy can also prevent a spawn or reuse an existing object.
Despite the name, ReSpawnSpawnable uses the same implementation as SpawnSpawnable. It does not first despawn an object previously produced by this spawner.

member.summary: Adds a receiver for notifications that an object from this spawner is being recycled for reuse.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report or perform an action. OnRecycle receives the affected object’s GameObject. In the checked reuse policy it runs before the object is despawned and another spawn is requested.

An already registered listener is not added again, and registering does not replay earlier events. Supply a nonnull listener and remove it with the matching UnregisterSpawnEventListener when it should stop receiving notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.SetSpawnable
member.summary: Refreshes the saved crate-reference and pool-policy pair used by later spawn requests.

remarks.para: It takes the current GetCrateReference result and policyData and replaces _spawnable. For example, after choosing a different spawnableCrateReference, call SetSpawnable so subsequent SpawnSpawnableAsync requests use that reference.

This does not load a prefab, spawn an object, register a pool, or rerun CrateQuery. Warehouse readiness lets GetCrateReference return a reference, but does not prove the referenced Barcode identifies a SpawnableCrate. The pool for the selected crate's Barcode must already be registered with AssetSpawner; without that registration, a later spawn request can return null. Changing the public crate or policy fields alone does not replace this saved pair, although editing an already shared reference object can affect its Barcode.

member.summary: Starts an asynchronous pool spawn using the saved crate and policy at this spawner’s world position and rotation.

remarks.para: It calls SpawnSpawnableAsync and discards the returned task, so this method can return before the object is ready. Use the asynchronous method when code needs the resulting Poolee, the component that manages a scene object’s pool lifecycle.

It performs the same request even with manualMode enabled. The saved reference must resolve to a SpawnableCrate, and shouldSpawn can reject the request. Pool policy can also prevent a spawn or reuse an existing object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.SpawnSpawnableAsync(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a UniTask<Poolee> for a pool spawn at this spawner's position and rotation in the overall scene. Await it to receive the Poolee component that manages the pooled object.

remarks.para: It uses _spawnable, the crate-reference and policy pair saved by Awake or SetSpawnable. Awake is Unity's initialization callback. A missing reference, a reference that does not resolve to a SpawnableCrate, or a shouldSpawn routine returning false completes with null before requesting a pool object. manualMode does not block a direct call.

The active stream session is required. After the crate and optional shouldSpawn check pass, this method registers a scene-load dependency, requests AssetSpawner.SpawnAsync, and waits for it. The request uses the spawner's world position and rotation, no parent, no explicit scale override, and the saved policy. It may reuse an object instead of instantiating a new one.

Pool spawn listeners run inside AssetSpawner before this method resumes. On normal completion, this method removes the scene-load dependency first. A nonnull result then invokes onSpawnEvent, if assigned, with this spawner and the result's GameObject before completing the task. A null pool result logs a warning and returns null. It does not wait a fixed number of frames.
The isHidden argument is unused in the checked wrapper and state machine; true does not request a deactivated or hidden spawn.
To patch the asynchronous behavior, inspect CrateSpawner._SpawnSpawnableAsync_d__26.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are described below.

item.description: First entry. Resolves the crate and checks the optional spawn predicate. Awaits AssetSpawner.SpawnAsync at the spawner's position and rotation with its configured options.
Continues after AssetSpawner.SpawnAsync. Returns the spawned Poolee.
Done.

member.param: Unused in this implementation; it does not deactivate or hide the returned object.
member.returns: The spawned Poolee, or null when the saved crate is unavailable, shouldSpawn rejects the request, or the pool returns no object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.LoadAssetAsync``1(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Waits for this reference’s existing operation or starts a new load of TObject and returns its result.

remarks.para: When the stored handle is already loading or done, this routine converts and awaits that operation for TObject. Otherwise, it calls the virtual loader; the base loader starts an Addressables load using AssetGUID and stores its handle. Repeated requests on the same reference can share that operation.

The supplied cancellationToken is forwarded when a new load path starts. The checked reused-handle path passes an empty token instead, so a supplied cancellation request is not forwarded when reusing a pending or completed operation. This method does not promise that cancellation stops the underlying asset-system operation.

member.returns: A task yielding the requested asset result, or reporting a loading, cancellation, or incompatible-type failure.

member.summary: Loads or reuses the asset and calls the supplied routine with the result as TObject.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This callback takes the asset result. If IsDone is already true, the method reads Asset, casts it to TObject, and invokes the callback synchronously before returning.
