member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.Awake
member.summary: Registers the grip with the usual grip lookup tables and uses this object’s own Transform as its grip reference.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s setup call when a component first loads. This override runs Grip’s setup, then stores this component’s own Transform in targetTransform. A Transform describes an object’s position, rotation and scale.

The stored reference identifies the object whose coordinate system is used for grip targets. It keeps referring to that object as the object moves; it is not a snapshot of one position. A separately assigned targetTransform is replaced during this setup.
The world-surface tracking records for individual hands are created later, when those hands are scored for this grip.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.OnHandHoverUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Updates this hand’s hover target from its cached surface hit, then rebuilds the colliders used during hand attachment.

remarks.para: This call needs an existing entry for the hand in genericHandStates and a true isRaycastHit flag in that entry. If the entry is missing or that flag is false, it returns before changing the target, rebuilding the collider list or running Grip’s normal hover update. It uses the recorded hit; it does not perform a new raycast here. A raycast tests a line against collision shapes.

The cached point and directions are interpreted relative to this WorldGrip object. It converts the surface point into a world position, measured in metres, and converts the surface normal and back-of-hand direction into world directions. A surface normal points straight out of a surface. It turns the cached hand orientation so the back-of-hand direction lines up with the opposite of the surface normal, then stores the resulting hand target through SetTargetInWorld. Internally, a quaternion is the four-number representation of that orientation.

For example, a point accepted on a tabletop becomes the hand’s hover target. The cached local point is transformed using the WorldGrip object’s current Transform, so moving that object changes the world position calculated from the point.

After storing the target, it clears ignoreColliders and appends the recorded nearby colliders from every hand entry, up to each entry’s targetColliderCount. It copies that list into additionalGripColliders, then calls Grip’s hover update. That inherited update can update the finger pose and then call the registered hover-update functions with this hand when its own input checks allow it. These functions are the notification’s listeners. Repeated colliders are copied as repeated entries.

member.param: The hovering hand whose saved surface hit supplies the new target.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.SetupConfiguration(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandJointConfiguration)
member.summary: Prepares hand-joint settings that hold position at the world grip while allowing limited rotation.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that restricts how a physics-controlled object can move. This method changes the supplied settings object. Grip’s Start setup call uses it before the hand pipeline applies those settings to a joint; calling it alone does not change an already created hand joint.

It copies the grip’s primary and secondary movement directions into the joint’s axis and secondaryAxis. These are directions in the grip’s reference frame, not positions in metres. All three position axes are set to Locked. All three rotation axes are set to Limited; this method selects that motion mode, while the hand’s pose limits supply the permitted angles during joint updates.

It selects separate X and YZ rotation drives, disables automatic calculation of the connected anchor, and sets swapBodies to false. An anchor is a joint attachment point. Disabling automatic connected-anchor calculation uses the supplied connected attachment point when the settings are applied. With no connected physics body, that point is in world coordinates. Keeping swapBodies false preserves the normal order in which the physics engine processes the connected bodies. It clears the spring and damping of both angular limit springs. These limit springs govern the response at a rotation boundary; they are separate from the drives that pull rotation toward a target.

The X position drive is given positionSpring = 0, positionDamper = 150 and maximumForce = 0.25. These are Unity drive coefficients: spring pulls toward a target, damping resists motion, and maximumForce caps the drive’s effort. Position is already locked by the motion settings.

It stores projectionDistance = 0.1 metres and projectionAngle = 180 degrees, but selects projectionMode = None. Projection is the joint’s extra correction for excessive separation or rotation, so those thresholds are inactive in this prepared configuration.

For example, the attachment can hold a hand at a tabletop grip point while still allowing the wrist to turn within the hand pose’s angular limits. Anchor positions and numeric rotation limits already present in the supplied settings are not rewritten by this method.

member.param: The hand-joint settings object to prepare for this grip.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.UpdateJointConfiguration(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Updates an existing hand joint’s rotation limits and rotation-drive strength from its hand pose, grip input and avatar strength.

remarks.para: This works on the hand’s existing ConfigurableJoint, a physics connection with separate movement and rotation controls. It needs the hand’s controller, rig manager, current avatar and saved Grip hand state with a hand pose. The normal Grip pipeline calls it after joint attachment and during attached-hand updates when a joint exists.

The saved hand pose supplies twistRotationLimit and swingRotationLimit, both measured in degrees. Twist is rotation around the joint’s X axis: its low limit is minus twistRotationLimit and its high limit is plus twistRotationLimit. Swing is rotation around the other two joint axes: both use swingRotationLimit. These axes belong to the joint’s configured reference frame.

Both angular drives receive the same three coefficients. Let s be the controller’s current GetGripForce value, a unitless grip input, and let g be the current avatar’s stored grip-strength multiplier, also unitless. The spring coefficient is (450 × s + 1500) × g, the damping coefficient is (36 × s + 120) × g, and the maximumForce coefficient is (25 × s + 25) × g. These are the Unity angular-drive settings: spring pulls orientation toward its target, damping slows unwanted rotation, and maximumForce caps the drive’s turning effort.

For example, with s = 0 and g = 1, the three coefficients are 1500, 120 and 25. With s = 1 and g = 1, they are 1950, 156 and 50. Doubling g doubles all three. This method uses the supplied input values directly; it does not clamp them to these example endpoints.

The hand pose is read from Grip’s stored hand state. The controller input and the avatar’s stored strength are read again on each call. The method changes rotation limits and drive coefficients; it leaves the joint’s target position and target rotation unchanged.

member.param: The attached hand whose existing joint, controller input and stored hand pose are used.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneBodyListenable.OnZoneBodyEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody)
member.summary: Reports this body's accepted Tracker-overlap count changing from zero to one.
member.param: The body associated with the entering collider's Tracker, rather than the entire entity.

remarks.para: In Unity, a component is a piece of data or behavior attached to a GameObject. A Tracker is the component on the collider's GameObject that links the collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity. The Zone uses a lookup table keyed by GameObject to find the Tracker. A GameObject is a Unity object in the scene, and a collider is a shape Unity uses for collision detection. A body is a physical part of an entity and can have several colliders. The Zone counts accepted overlaps for each distinct Tracker associated with a body. If two distinct Trackers on a body's colliders are accepted, the first changes the body count from zero to one and produces this callback; the second increases the count without producing another body enter. A repeated callback for the same Tracker is deduplicated.

The entering collider must be found in the Tracker cache, its Tracker must identify both a body and an entity, and the Zone must be active and enabled. Register with the Zone's body-listener overload before the overlap begins: registration does not replay existing enters.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneBodyListenable.OnZoneBodyExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowBody)
member.summary: Reports that this body's accepted Tracker-overlap count reaches zero after its final counted overlap is removed.
member.param: The body whose accepted overlaps have fallen to zero.

remarks.para: In Unity, a component is a piece of data or behavior attached to a GameObject. A Tracker is the component on the collider's GameObject that links the collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity. The Zone uses a lookup table keyed by GameObject to find the Tracker. If two distinct Trackers for one body overlap the Zone, removing only one does not produce this callback. It fires when the body's accepted Tracker-overlap count reaches zero after the final counted overlap is removed, so it describes the body's overall Zone membership rather than each individual collider exit.

Zone disable cleanup can produce exits. A Tracker's GameObject can also be deactivated. Zone.Awake, Unity's initialization callback for the Zone, creates the Zone.OnTrackerDisable callback: a routine the Zone registers on each accepted Tracker to handle deactivation. Tracker.OnDeactivate invokes that registered routine with the Tracker's Collider. MarrowBody tracker-deactivation paths and MarrowEntity despawn call Tracker.OnDeactivate, so an exit does not necessarily mean the body physically moved across the boundary. If exit processing is requested while enter callbacks are being dispatched, the Zone can defer it until that enter processing finishes. It stores only one deferred Tracker exit: another eligible exit before dispatch finishes overwrites the saved Tracker, and only the last saved exit is processed afterward. The overwritten exit is not replayed by this deferral mechanism.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkListenable.OnZoneLinkEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link has become active for the activator as either its primary link or a linked secondary neighbor.
member.param: The entity whose tracked zone activation changed, such as the player.

remarks.para: Primary is the manager's selected active link. Its outgoing linked neighbors become secondary. For example, if A links to B, activating A can produce B's link-enter callback even while the player is outside B's trigger.

The combined enter is sent when the manager changes that activator/link state from inactive to active. It does not repeat merely because an already active link changes between primary and secondary. Registering a listener does not immediately replay its current activation.
The manager writes this link’s combined state as active for this activator before it dispatches OnZoneLinkEnter, so listeners observe the post-transition active state for this link and activator.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkListenable.OnZoneLinkExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link is no longer active through either the primary or secondary role for this activator.
member.param: The entity whose activation of this link ended.

remarks.para: This follows the manager's combined activation state, not every physical trigger exit. A link that stops being primary but stays secondary remains active and does not produce this combined exit. The manager can also retain the last active link when an activator leaves all tracked links, so leaving a trigger does not guarantee an immediate activation exit.
State is tracked separately for each activator. An exit for one entity does not establish that another entity has stopped activating the link, or that all objects in the zone have been disabled.
The manager writes this link’s combined state as inactive for this activator before it dispatches OnZoneLinkExit, so listeners observe the post-transition inactive state for this link and activator.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable.OnZoneLinkPrimaryEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link has become the manager's selected primary link for the activator.
member.param: The entity whose primary zone selection changed.

remarks.para: Primary describes the link's role for that entity. The manager tracks the links active for each entity and selects one as that entity’s primary link. This is not a callback for a special entity called the primary activator, nor for every zone the entity physically overlaps.

The callback follows a false-to-true primary-state change. A link already active as a secondary neighbor can become primary and produce this callback without another combined OnZoneLinkEnter. Registering a listener does not replay the existing primary state.
Before dispatching this callback, the manager writes this activator’s current primary state for the link. Listener code that checks the role during the callback sees the new primary state.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable.OnZoneLinkPrimaryExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link has stopped being the selected primary link for the activator.
member.param: The entity for which this link lost its primary role.

remarks.para: The link can remain active as an outgoing secondary neighbor of the newly selected primary: the manager also keeps that connected link active for the same activator while it is not selected as primary. In that case this primary exit happens without a combined activation exit. A different primary can be selected while zones overlap, so this notification is not simply a physical trigger exit.

The manager tracks the role separately for each activator and can retain its last active link after leaving all tracked links. This callback therefore does not establish that every entity has left or that every object in the area has been disabled.
Before it dispatches this callback, the manager writes this activator’s updated current primary state for the link, so listener code sees that the link is no longer primary.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkSecondaryListenable.OnZoneLinkSecondaryEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link has become an active outgoing neighbor of the activator's selected primary link.
member.param: The entity whose selected primary link now activates this neighboring link.

remarks.para: For example, if A lists B in its zoneLinks and the player makes A primary, B becomes secondary for that player. The player need not be physically inside B. A farther link C in a chain from B is not automatically secondary unless the selected primary also has an outgoing link to C.

Secondary describes the link's role, not a special secondary entity. The manager sends this callback when the secondary flag changes from false to true. Combined activation and primary status are tracked separately for the same activator.
During the state solve, the manager writes this link’s current secondary state as true before it dispatches this callback, so a listener that reads the state sees the updated value.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkSecondaryListenable.OnZoneLinkSecondaryExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Reports that this link has stopped being an active outgoing neighbor of the activator's selected primary link.
member.param: The entity for which this link lost its secondary role.

remarks.para: The link may have become primary itself. In that case it remains active in the combined channel while this secondary exit is sent. The notification therefore does not guarantee that the entity physically left the zone or that the area's objects were disabled.
The manager keeps separate state for each activator, so another entity can still activate the link. The callback follows a true-to-false secondary-state change during a state solve.

During the state solve, the manager writes this link’s current secondary state as false before it dispatches this callback. The link may still be active as the primary link, so the combined active state can remain true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.Clear
member.summary: Erases all requested, resolved, applied, and recorded inactive callback flags without running any callbacks.

remarks.para: This zeros the request, resolved, applied, and completed masks without calling callbacks or changing object effects. If a callback already made the object inactive, Clear erases the mask differences the manager needs to reverse that effect. A later manager false request can enqueue the status, but Resolve sees no request/resolved difference and creates no apply or completion callback to undo it. When normal callbacks must reverse effects, use InactiveObjectManager.Hide, Cull, or Despawn with false for each requested channel and let the manager process those requests. Use Clear only when you intend a bookkeeping reset without lifecycle releases.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.Cull(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets or clears only the culling bit in this status's requested state.
member.param: True to request culling; false to clear that request. Defaults to true.

remarks.para: This method edits only the requested Cull bit; it does not queue the status, call callbacks, or change an object directly. For a standard MarrowEntity, after manager processing, a Cull request adds the Culling hibernation source (one reason physics is suspended) and disables MarrowBehaviour components (the entity's game-behavior components). Clearing request bit Cull does not immediately release that source: the later false OnCullResolve callback waits until Hide, Cull, and Despawn request bits are clear and the resolved Cull bit is clear. A still-requested Hide or Despawn can therefore defer release. In Update, Complete also waits until the resolve and apply queues are empty. Even after the Culling source releases, another hibernation source can keep physics asleep. Use InactiveObjectManager.Cull(thisStatus, isInactive) when you want to update and queue the request together. Hide and Despawn request bits remain unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.Despawn(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets or clears only the despawned-state bit in this status's requested state.
member.param: True to request the despawned state; false to clear that request. Defaults to true.

remarks.para: An object pool is the game's reuse system for keeping objects available for later use after removal from active play. This method changes only the status request; it does not queue work or remove or spawn an object from that pool. Use InactiveObjectManager.Despawn(thisStatus, isInactive) to update and queue the status's lifecycle callbacks. Hide and Cull request bits are independent and remain unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.Hide(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets or clears only the hiding bit in this status's requested state.
member.param: True to request hiding; false to clear that request. Defaults to true.

remarks.para: This does not hide a GameObject or queue callbacks. Use InactiveObjectManager.Hide(thisStatus, isInactive) to update the request and queue it together. For example, Hide(false) clears the request reported by IsHidden immediately, even if the object is still hidden because processing has not happened or another inactive channel remains.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.IsActive
member.summary: Returns whether none of the three inactive channels is currently requested.
member.returns: True when request contains no Hide, Cull, or Despawn flag.

remarks.para: GameObject.activeSelf reports whether this Unity scene object itself is active. This method checks desired request state, not activeSelf or whether callbacks have finished. After clearing the requests it can return true while application is still queued. Conversely, an inactive request can make it return false before the object changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.IsCulled
member.summary: Returns whether culling is currently requested for this status.
member.returns: The Cull flag in request, rather than the applied state.

remarks.para: The result changes as soon as the requested bit changes. For a standard MarrowEntity, processing Cull hibernates its physics and disables its MarrowBehaviour components (game-behavior components). This query reads only the requested bit; it does not confirm that either effect or its callbacks have run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.IsDespawned
member.summary: Returns whether the despawned-state channel is currently requested.
member.returns: The Despawn flag in request, rather than proof of pool removal.

remarks.para: An object pool is the game's reuse system for keeping objects available for later use after removal from active play. This is a status query: it does not confirm that the object entered or left the pool, or wait for lifecycle callbacks, so it can change before the object response is applied.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.IsHidden
member.summary: Returns whether hiding is currently requested for this status.
member.returns: The Hide flag in request, rather than actual visibility or GameObject activation.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components; its active state is distinct from whether its renderers are visible. For example, a queued request to hide can make this true before the hide callback runs. Clearing the request can make it false while other inactive channels or unprocessed work still keep the object inactive.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.RecycleDecorator.OnDisable
member.summary: When Unity disables this component, it removes this decorator from the currently assigned spawner's recycle listener list.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDisable automatically when this component becomes disabled. The hook reads the current _crateSpawner reference; it does not remember the previous spawner. If you change the field while this component is enabled, disabling it can leave the old spawner's registration in place. Remove the old registration before changing the source.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.RecycleDecorator.OnEnable
member.summary: When Unity enables this component, it registers with its assigned for later recycle notifications.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable automatically when this component becomes enabled. Assign _crateSpawner before enabling it. The base hook uses that stored reference instead of searching for a component, and it adds this decorator only if it is not already in the spawner's recycle listener list.

Registration does not call OnRecycle for objects already in the pool and does not recycle or remove an object. Override OnRecycle to respond when the spawner later reports a recycled GameObject (the Unity scene object being reported).

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.SpawnDecorator.OnDisable
member.summary: Unsubscribes this decorator from its configured CrateSpawner's later spawn and despawn notifications.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDisable when this component stops being enabled and active. This removes the listener without despawning anything or calling OnDespawn. It uses the current _crateSpawner reference, so changing that reference while subscribed does not remove the listener from the old spawner.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.SpawnDecorator.OnEnable
member.summary: Subscribes this decorator to its configured CrateSpawner's later spawn and despawn notifications.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable when this component becomes enabled and active. Assign a valid _crateSpawner before then; this method uses that reference rather than finding a component for you. The same decorator is added only once, and subscribing does not report objects that already spawned.
The spawner later calls OnSpawn or OnDespawn with the affected GameObject. These are callbacks: routines called to report an action. Override them to give your decorator a response.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.Awake
member.summary: Creates the routine that handles a tracked collider being disabled.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: a routine Unity calls to set up this component. It prepares the tracker-disable callback, a routine called to report that an overlapping tracker has stopped being active. The zone attaches it to newly accepted trackers so disabling one can be handled like leaving the zone.
The overlap collections are created during construction, not by Awake. This initialization does not scan the trigger or report existing overlaps.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.OnDisable
member.summary: Attempts to process exits for the zone's recorded trackers when this component stops being enabled and active.

remarks.para: It copies the tracked set into _trackerExitBuffer before processing entries, allowing normal exit processing to remove set members without changing the set being copied. Existing valid Unity trackers are passed to ProcessTriggerExit, then the buffer is cleared.

Cleanup can send exit reports without physical movement. Exit processing still requires both a body and an entity. Destroyed entries are skipped. Exits during enter dispatch use a single saved tracker slot, so disabling is not an unconditional clear of every tracking collection or listener registration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.ProcessTriggerExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker)
member.summary: Removes an accepted from this zone, updates its body and entity counts, and sends the applicable exit reports.
member.param: The previously accepted tracker whose counted overlap should end.

remarks.para: The tracker must still report both a body and an entity and be present in _trackerOverlap. During enter dispatch, its exit is saved for the end of that enter call, without waiting for another frame. There is one pending tracker slot; a later deferred request replaces the earlier reference. Only the most recent deferred tracker is processed when enter dispatch ends. If its saved reference replaced an earlier tracker, that earlier tracker is not processed by that pass and can remain in _trackerOverlap and its body/entity counts until another valid exit or cleanup removes it.

An immediate exit first removes the tracker from the set and sets _isProcessingExitEvents true. It decrements the entity count and reports entity exit if the last overlap ended, then does the same for the body. It removes the tracker-disable callback, reports tracker exit, and clears _isProcessingExitEvents on normal completion. Entity and body entries are removed before their exit reports.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the reports tell listeners that tracking ended, through physical exit, tracker disabling, or zone disabling. Calling this method directly does not move the object. Unlike the trigger wrappers, this method does not test whether the zone is enabled and active.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.RegisterZoneEventListener(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneBodyListenable)
member.summary: Subscribes a listener to this zone's later enter and exit reports.
member.param: The listener implementing this overload's zone-report interface.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Implement OnZoneBodyEnter(MarrowBody body) and OnZoneBodyExit(MarrowBody body); both callbacks receive the physical body. It is added only once to this interface's list, and registration does not replay enter reports for overlaps already recorded.

A body is a physical part of an entity. Body enter is reported for its first accepted tracker; exit is reported when its last counted tracker leaves. Supply a valid listener; dispatch does not skip null entries.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.RegisterZoneEventListener(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneEntityListenable)
member.summary: Subscribes a listener to this zone's later enter and exit reports.
member.param: The listener implementing this overload's zone-report interface.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Implement OnZoneEntityEnter(MarrowEntity entity) and OnZoneEntityExit(MarrowEntity entity); each callback receives the whole entity, which may contain several bodies. It is added only once to this interface's list, and registration does not replay enter reports for overlaps already recorded.

An entity is a whole object that can contain several physical bodies. Entity enter is reported for its first accepted tracker and exit for its last counted tracker. Supply a valid listener; dispatch does not skip null entries.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone.RegisterZoneEventListener(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneTrackerListenable)
member.summary: Subscribes a listener to this zone's later enter and exit reports.
member.param: The listener implementing this overload's zone-report interface.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Implement OnZoneTrackerEnter(Tracker tracker) and OnZoneTrackerExit(Tracker tracker); each callback receives the accepted tracker whose zone membership changed. It is added only once to this interface's list, and registration does not replay enter reports for overlaps already recorded.

A tracker associates a collision shape with its body and entity. Each accepted tracker gets its own reports, even if others belong to the same body or entity. Supply a valid listener; dispatch does not skip null entries.

remarks.para: Removal sends no exit report, changes no overlap counts, and does not undo the listener's earlier work. If an object implements several zone-listener interfaces, remove it separately from each list it joined.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneChunkLoader.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes both inherited link-event options as selected.

remarks.para: The constructor writes 3 to the inherited ZoneLinkItem._eventTypes field: Primary is 1 and Secondary is 2. When enabled with a linked zone, the base OnEnable subscribes this component to both event lists. This sets event subscriptions; it does not load chunks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneChunkLoader.OnPrimaryEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Requests each configured SceneChunk when the zone manager selects this link as primary for an activator.
member.param: The entity accepted by the linked ZoneLink's activatorTags filter; this override does not inspect it.

remarks.para: The linked ZoneLink's activatorTags filter decides whether an entering entity is accepted. Primary is a link state: the zone manager selects one link by priority for an accepted activator within its connected group of zone links. The inherited event mask controls normal subscription. This override does not check that mask, so a direct call also requests the chunks.

A callback is a routine invoked to perform an action. This callback starts one asynchronous load request for each array entry and returns without waiting for loading to finish. Requests may be queued or collected into loader batches; do not assume every listed chunk is loaded in one batch. A batch is the set of chunks the shared scene loader wants active in that pass. Chunks omitted from the desired active set can be unloaded before new chunks are loaded.

A SceneChunk groups one or more scene layers managed as one loadable chunk. When its load step runs, it sets IsChunkLoaded to true, updates its ZoneCullers (components that manage entities and level assets in the chunk's zone), calls registered IChunkLoadable.OnChunkLoad handlers, and then invokes its configured onChunkLoad event. Use the flag, interface callback, or event to observe that chunk's load step; the request itself does not mean scenes are already available.
Supply a nonnull chunks array with valid entries; this loop does not skip null entries. This class does not request an unload when its link later stops being primary.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.OnEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Invokes first, then may invoke while this component's flag is still false.
member.param: The whole MarrowEntity reported by the Zone. The regular event receives it when assigned; the one-shot event receives it only if the flag remains false after the regular event returns.

remarks.para: An event calls its attached listener routines, also called callbacks. OnEnter first invokes onZoneEnter when assigned, then checks _hasZoneEntered. If the flag is false, it invokes onZoneEnterOneShot when assigned and writes the flag true after those listeners return, even when the one-shot event is absent. One-shot listeners therefore normally see the flag before that final write.

A regular listener can change the flag before the check. A nested entry before the final write can invoke the one-shot event again, so this is not a strict once-only guarantee under re-entry. Exit and disable do not reset the flag.
In normal delivery, the inherited ZoneItem first tests activatorTags against the entity. A direct call to this override skips that filter and does not create a collider overlap.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.OnExit(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Invokes the optional event with the whole MarrowEntity supplied by the Zone.
member.param: The whole entity reported as leaving this Zone.

remarks.para: A Tracker is the Zone's record linking one Collider, the shape used for overlap detection, to its MarrowBody and whole MarrowEntity. The Zone reports entity exit after that entity's last tracked collider leaves or is removed during cleanup. Disabling a Tracker or the Zone can cause cleanup exit reports without physical movement.

Before normal delivery reaches this method, ZoneItem rechecks its inherited activatorTags filter. This is a MarrowQuery configured with tag and crate rules, evaluated against the entity at exit time. A direct call to OnExit bypasses that filter. This method only reports the exit; it does not move or remove the entity and does not clear the one-shot flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.Awake
member.summary: Registers this link and its configured outgoing connections in the shared zone-link manager.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: the routine Unity calls to set up this component. Each zoneLinks entry registers a directed connection from this link to that entry. An empty array registers this link in the manager without adding outgoing connections from this array.

Registering the link or a connection also makes the manager recalculate graph-derived roles for activators it is already tracking. Adding a connection can therefore change existing primary or secondary roles and notify listeners without a new physical Zone entry.

Configure a nonnull array and valid target links before Awake. Entity reports are subscribed separately by OnEnable; registration itself does not make an entity enter. Later changes to the array alone do not rebuild the registered connections.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes this link and its connections from the manager's connection graph and from tracked activators' priority lists, then recalculates roles only from links that remain active.

remarks.para: The manager removes this link and references to it from its map of directed ZoneLink connections, removes it from each tracked activator's ordered list of active links, then recalculates roles only in groups reached from that activator's remaining active links. An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed activatorTags. A connected group contains links joined through incoming or outgoing connections; its highest-ranked active link is primary, and that primary's direct outgoing neighbors are secondary. A link is combined-active when either role is active.

If this was an activator's only active link in its group, there is no remaining active link to start that group's recalculation. Former secondary neighbors keep their secondary and combined flags, and their listeners receive no exit callback from this teardown. For example, if A was the only active link and its connection made B secondary, destroying A leaves B marked secondary and combined-active. Former neighbors disconnected from every remaining active link can likewise be missed. A callback is a routine called to report a state change.

This is connection-graph teardown. OnDisable separately removes the Zone listener. Do not assume destruction produces a physical exit or guarantees an exit callback on every removed-link listener; effects follow the manager's remaining state calculations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.OnDisable
member.summary: Unsubscribes this link from its configured Zone, the trigger area that supplies whole-entity enter and exit reports.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDisable when this component stops being enabled and active. It removes this listener using the current _zone reference.

This method does not unregister the link from the manager's connection graph, clear link listeners, or explicitly deactivate existing activator roles. It sends no synthetic entity exit. Keep the configured reference consistent across subscription and teardown; changing it alone leaves the old subscription.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.OnEnable
member.summary: Subscribes this link to its configured Zone trigger area's later whole-entity enter and exit reports.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable when the component becomes enabled and active. Assign a valid _zone before then; this method uses the reference rather than finding a Zone automatically.

Zone registration adds this entity listener only once and does not replay entities already recorded inside. If the listener is added after an entity is already inside, it receives no immediate enter report; it receives only later Zone reports. Matching reports later pass through activatorTags before reaching the link manager. Link event listeners are a separate set of registrations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.Reset
member.summary: During setup, finds the Zone trigger area on this GameObject and stores it as the source of entity reports.

remarks.para: Unity uses Reset for editor setup when a component is added or reset in the Inspector. A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components. GetComponent is Unity's lookup for a component attached to that same GameObject; Reset does not search parents or neighboring objects.
Reset only assigns _zone, the report source. It does not move an existing subscription, rebuild zoneLinks connections, or recompute activation, so use it during setup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ComputeBaseStats
member.summary: Replaces the avatar’s cached strength, speed, vitality, intelligence and agility ratings using its current measured body proportions and mass.

remarks.para: These are relative game ratings, not meters per second, kilograms or newtons. For example, intelligence is forehead half-width divided by the reference ratio 0.044. Upper-body strength depends on chest and shoulder size, arm thickness, total mass, eye height and arm length; longer arms appear in its denominator. Grip strength uses hand size and forearm/wrist thickness.

This reads measurements already stored on the Avatar. It does not measure the Animator’s bones, rebuild collision shapes or recalculate mass first. RefreshBodyMeasurements performs the mass calculation before calling it. Direct changes to cached stat fields are overwritten by another calculation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ComputeMass(System.Single)
member.summary: Estimates the masses of the head, chest, pelvis, each arm and each leg from the current body dimensions, then stores their total.
member.param: 0-to-1 blend from the shape estimate toward 82 kg, before the torso-shape multiplier.

remarks.para: The shape estimate uses torso dimensions and bulge depths, plus limb thickness and measured segment lengths. Results represent kilograms and feed later physics-rig mass distribution. The rig can distribute them differently: its physical arm mass is derived from total mass. An arm or leg result here is for one limb; the total includes both sides.

normalizeTo82 is a blend amount, clamped from 0 to 1. At 0 the calculation retains its shape-based estimate; at 1 it blends toward 82 kg before applying an additional torso-shape factor between 0.7 and 1. Therefore 1 does not guarantee an 82 kg final total. For a hypothetical raw estimate of 100 kg and a torso factor of 1, 0.5 gives 91 kg.

This changes cached mass values only. It does not set existing Rigidbody masses, recalculate base stats or rebuild measurements. It requires the breast, upper-back, abdomen, lower-back and butt bulge objects used by the estimate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.EllipsePerimeterFromAxes(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Estimates the distance around an ellipse from its two center-to-edge radii.
member.param: One center-to-edge radius of the ellipse.
The other center-to-edge radius, in the same unit.
member.returns: The approximate perimeter, in the same unit as the inputs.

remarks.para: An ellipse is a stretched circle. Supply the half-width and half-height, not the full diameters, using the same unit for both. The result has that unit. Inputs of 0.10 m and 0.10 m describe a circle with radius 10 cm and return about 0.628 m.
The approximation is π × [3(a + b) − √((3a + b)(a + 3b))]. The code does not check for positive radii or reorder the inputs; use valid lengths.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.GetSpineInWorldForGizmos(System.Single,System.Single,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Utilities.SimpleTransform)
member.summary: Returns a world-space position and rotation along the head–sternum–hips path used to draw the avatar’s body guides.
member.param: Path coordinate: sternum 0, hips 1; between −1 and 0 blends head to sternum, and −1 or below selects the head-top extension.
Eye-center height in meters, used to turn HeadTop and CrotchBottom ratios into distances.
World-space head position and rotation.
World-space upper-chest position and rotation.
World-space hip-center position and rotation.
member.returns: A world-space transform for the drawing helper.

remarks.para: The path coordinate is unusual: 0 is the sternum and 1 is the hip center. Inputs strictly between −1 and 0 blend the head and sternum transforms; between 0 and 1 it blends sternum and hips. At −1 the separate head-top extension branch already applies. For example, 0.5 gives the midpoint from sternum to hips, including blended rotation.

At values at or below −1, it uses the head orientation and adds HeadTop × eyeCenterHeight along head up. Above 1 it extends below the hips by CrotchBottom × eyeCenterHeight × (yPerc − 1), capped at the full crotch extension at 2. This helper does not sample the detailed spineZ curve.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.PrecomputeAvatar
member.summary: Measures the model’s humanoid bones once and caches the dimensions and orientation corrections needed to fit the game’s body rig to it.

remarks.para: The routine asks the Animator for its default pose, records its humanoid bones in artTransforms, finds the eye center, and measures bone positions and limb proportions. It builds the spine curve and cached body-segment offsets, captures corrections in artOffsets and poseOffsets, measures the hands, and prepares visibility bounds for the body, head and hair renderers.

PreComputed is checked first. If it is already true, this base routine returns without repeating the work; successful completion sets it to true. Clearing that flag allows another measurement, but the routine restores the Animator’s default pose and replaces caches, so do this during setup rather than expecting an in-place adjustment during animation.

This is not a complete physics-rig rebuild. RefreshBodyMeasurements derives lengths, torso curves, mass and ratings from the cached proportions; PhysicsRig.SetAvatar separately creates or calibrates body collision shapes and joints. Required humanoid bone references and the measurement objects must be present.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.PrecomputeAvatar(System.Single)
member.summary: Provides a virtual eye-height setup hook whose base Avatar implementation does nothing.
member.param: Requested eye height passed to an override; ignored by the base implementation.

remarks.para: The base implementation returns immediately and does not store eyeHeight or scale the avatar. A derived Avatar can override the hook. To perform the base model measurement, use the parameterless PrecomputeAvatar overload; passing a height to this overload alone does not produce that work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.RefreshBodyMeasurements
member.summary: Updates derived body lengths, torso curves, mass and base stats from the avatar’s stored proportions and eye height.

remarks.para: It converts normalized bone lengths into meters, updates overall arm lengths and body heights, regenerates the torso width/front/back curves, computes mass with normalizeTo82 = 0.5, and then recalculates the stat ratings. OnRefreshBodyMeasurements is invoked afterward if it has subscribers.

This does not re-read the Animator’s bones or replace the spine curve measured by PrecomputeAvatar. It also does not rebuild an already mounted physics rig’s collision shapes or joints. Use it when the measured proportions already exist and derived caches need updating.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.SoftBulge.Copy(Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.SoftBulge)
member.summary: Replaces this bulge’s shape and rigidity settings with another bulge’s values while keeping its assigned bones.
member.param: The non-null bulge whose numeric settings will be copied into this instance.

remarks.para: Copies the apex position and depth, upper/lower and inner/outer extents, corner roundness, swell amounts, and rigidity. This lets an existing bulge use another shape or preset without replacing its primaryRt and secondaryLf bone references. The source bulge is unchanged.

The method changes stored settings only. It does not generate a mesh, rebuild an existing collider, or recalculate avatar mass. Those systems must use the updated settings again to update their results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.IsSoundAggroWhenInSecondaryZone
member.summary: Reports whether a linked secondary zone may add a sound-related threat to this NPC's navigation behaviour.

remarks.para: When ZoneAggro passes an alert to its linked zones, a secondary-zone call skips this brain if the value is false. If true, the secondary zone is allowed to ask the behaviour to add threat toward the alert's TriggerRefProxy, the reference identifying the potential target. Threat is a priority score for a potential target in the NPC's sensor tracking. Other checks can reject the request, and a score change does not guarantee a new selected target or an immediate attack. The primary-zone call does not check this flag.

This read-only property reads behaviour.isSoundAggroWhenInSecondaryZone. It returns true when behaviour is missing or destroyed; that fallback does not supply the missing behaviour needed to process the threat.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.MentalState
member.summary: Reports the navigation behaviour's current decision state, such as resting, roaming, investigating, or responding to a target.

remarks.para: This reads behaviour.mentalState; it does not request a state change. If behaviour is missing or destroyed, it returns Rest. That fallback describes the missing-controller case and does not prove that the NPC is alive or idle. Use isDead separately when inspecting the brain's recorded death status.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.OnGroupDeregister
member.summary: Event through which sends this brain and its requested ignore flag to group-management listeners.

remarks.para: The arguments are the AIBrain that raised the event and the exact boolean supplied to SpawnGroupIgnore. SpawnGroup's listener adds the brain to its ignored set for true and removes it for false. Despite the event's name, raising it is not itself a despawn or a removal from the group's living and dead collections.

Awake, Unity's automatic initialization callback for this component, replaces this field with a newly created event, so attach runtime listeners after the brain has initialized. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. A SpawnGroup adds its listener on spawn and removes it on despawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain._wasConfigSet
member.summary: Records that this brain's configuration was set for the current pool lifecycle, so automatic initialization does not clear it.

remarks.para: Pooling manages the same object for reuse in later spawns. OnPoolInitialize performs its pool setup, and OnPoolDeInitialize performs its pool cleanup. With a valid behaviour, SetBaseConfig sets this flag even when its argument is null. OnPoolInitialize clears the behaviour's override only if this flag and dontClearBaseConfig are both false; that automatic clear also sets the flag. OnPoolDeInitialize resets the flag to false for the next reuse.
This is a reset guard, not a ban on calling SetBaseConfig twice. Setting it directly does not apply a configuration or synchronize the puppet's state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.arenaEntranceRoutine
member.summary: Stores the coroutine handle used to cancel the countdown started by .

remarks.para: A coroutine is work that can pause and continue on later frames. StartArenaEntranceTimer replaces this handle each time it starts one. StopArenaEntranceTimer and OnDeath stop the coroutine referred to by this handle and reset entranceTimer, but do not clear the handle. Natural completion does not clear it either, so test the lifecycle rather than treating a non-null value as an active-timer flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.behaviour
member.summary: Connects this brain to the controller that makes the NPC's navigation and combat decisions.

remarks.para: MentalState and IsSoundAggroWhenInSecondaryZone read this controller's state and alert setting. SetBaseConfig stores an override on it, and spawn-group logic uses it to request investigation or aggression. AIBrain.Reset searches the brain's children for this reference.

The brain's death and resurrection notification routines run from puppetMaster notifications. Its stored isDead flag is also written by SetBaseConfig without running those routines. Replacing behaviour alone does not copy settings into the new controller or reconnect the physical puppet's death notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.dontClearBaseConfig
member.summary: Prevents pool initialization from automatically clearing the navigation behaviour's configuration override.

remarks.para: When this and _wasConfigSet are both false, OnPoolInitialize clears behaviour.overrideConfig and records that a configuration reset was performed. Turning this on skips that step, leaving the existing override and brain death flag unchanged by that step. Pooling means reusing the same NPC object for later spawns.
This flag does not apply the stored configuration immediately. AIBrain.Reset only refreshes component references, and SetBaseConfig can still replace or clear the override regardless of this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.entranceTimer
member.summary: Stores the remaining unscaled seconds before the arena entrance coroutine requests the puppet's death.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue across later frames. unscaledDeltaTime is the seconds elapsed for the current frame without game-speed scaling. StartArenaEntranceTimer writes the requested duration; repeated starts can leave several coroutines subtracting from this same value. While the coroutine is running, it subtracts unscaledDeltaTime once per resumed frame and finishes when a check finds this value at or below zero. For example, changing a running timer to 5 requests roughly five more seconds, independent of game-speed scaling. Changing this value alone does not start a coroutine.

The subtraction can leave a slightly negative value before the following check. StopArenaEntranceTimer and OnDeath reset it to 120 if a coroutine handle is stored; 120 is also the constructor's initial value. A value of 120 therefore does not by itself mean that a countdown is running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.isDead
member.summary: Stores this brain's recorded death status, which spawn-group logic uses when deciding how to handle the NPC.

remarks.para: OnDeath sets it true and OnResurrection sets it false before notifying listeners. SetBaseConfig also writes it from the configuration's puppetState: only Dead sets it true. The normal automatic configuration clear during pool initialization writes false.

This is a stored flag, not a live query of health or PuppetMaster.state. Changing it directly does not kill or revive the puppet or run the death/resurrection notification routines. SpawnGroup reads it when choosing the living or dead collection for a new NPC and when deciding whether to request investigation or aggression.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.onDeathDelegate
member.summary: Callback invoked with this brain after records it as dead.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Pooling manages the same NPC object for reuse in later spawns; pool deinitialization is its cleanup. It runs before onNPC_DeathDelegate and before the arena entrance timer is stopped. Add your callback with += to preserve existing listeners, such as a SpawnGroup's death tracking. Pool deinitialization clears this field, so a subscription needed for a later pooled spawn must be added again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.onNPC_DeathDelegate
member.summary: Second death callback, invoked with the same brain immediately after .

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Pooling manages the same NPC object for reuse in later spawns; pool deinitialization is its cleanup. OnDeath has already set isDead to true when this runs. This is another notification of that brain's death, not a callback for a different NPC. Use += and -= to add and remove a listener without replacing others.
Unlike onDeathDelegate and onResurrectDelegate, this field is not cleared by AIBrain.OnPoolDeInitialize. Manage your subscription's lifetime if it should not continue into later pooled reuse.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.onResurrectDelegate
member.summary: Callback invoked with this brain after records it as alive again.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Pooling manages the same NPC object for reuse in later spawns; pool deinitialization is its cleanup. isDead is already false when listeners run. Add a listener with += to preserve other listeners, including a SpawnGroup's living/dead tracking. AIBrain.OnPoolDeInitialize clears this field, so subscriptions do not automatically survive the next pooled spawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.puppetMaster
member.summary: Connects the brain to the NPC's physics puppet, whose simulated body parts and joints let it move and fall as a ragdoll.

remarks.para: Physics joints are simulated connections between body parts. Pooling manages the same NPC object for reuse in later spawns; initialization is its pool setup and deinitialization its pool cleanup. AIBrain.Reset searches the children for this component. Pool initialization subscribes the brain's death and resurrection handlers to it, and pool deinitialization removes those subscriptions. The arena entrance timer uses this reference when it requests the Dead state.
Changing the reference directly does not transfer subscriptions from the previous puppet. Set up the references before initialization so notifications and the timer refer to the intended NPC.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.OnComplete
member.summary: Event invoked without arguments after records completion and clears the active flag.

remarks.para: It fires only when CompleteEncounter changes _complete from false to true. Repeated completion calls are ignored until a reset clears that latch. Normal spawning calls completion when group progress is finished; forced completion can invoke it without waiting for the player to defeat the NPCs.

This notification does not guarantee that all NPCs have despawned or that every asynchronous task has stopped. CompleteEncounter itself does not cancel the group tokens, and forced removal can still be running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.OnEncounterReset
member.summary: Callback invoked without arguments after ForceStopAndReset clears encounter progress and resets its groups.

remarks.para: When it runs, completeCount is zero, _complete and _isEncounterActive are false, and the groups' cleanup calls have been made. NPC removal can still be running asynchronously, and isWarmed remains unchanged. PauseEncounter alone and CompleteEncounter do not invoke this callback. Use += and -= to manage your listener without replacing others.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter._complete
member.summary: Completion latch that blocks and suppresses repeated completion events.

remarks.para: CompleteEncounter sets it true; ForceStopAndReset clears it. Pausing leaves it unchanged. Writing the flag directly does not fire OnComplete, reset the groups, remove NPCs, or cancel their asynchronous loops. In particular, those loops do not use this flag as their cancellation condition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter._isEncounterActive
member.summary: Tracks whether encounter starting has been accepted, preventing another start while the encounter is marked active.

remarks.para: StartEncounter sets it before cueing music and starting groups. PauseEncounter, CompleteEncounter, and ForceStopAndReset clear it. WarmupEncounter does not set it.

This is a stored lifecycle flag, not proof that every spawn task is currently running or stopped. Changing it directly does not cancel tasks, remove NPCs, or change music. The SERIES pause indexing discrepancy can leave a task running even after this flag becomes false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter._spawnCTSs
member.summary: Stores the per-group cancellation sources used to request that asynchronous encounter spawning stop.

remarks.para: A cancellation source supplies a token that a task checks while waiting and looping. Awake creates an array matching spawnGroups, initially with empty slots. Starting a group cancels its older source and stores a new source at that group's index. Pausing and destruction request cancellation; they do not clear these references.

PARALLEL cancellation checks all slots. SERIES cancellation selects completeCount minus one when positive, otherwise zero, while SERIES starting selects completeCount. These sources do not control WarmupEncounter's separate tasks. Replacing the array or its sources directly does not reconnect tokens already held by running tasks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.completeCount
member.summary: Counts groups credited as complete and selects the next group in SERIES spawning.

remarks.para: It counts groups, not defeated NPCs or completed runs. If there are three groups, values 0, 1, and 2 select the first, second, and third group when SERIES starts; reaching the array length triggers normal encounter completion. ForceStopAndReset returns the count to zero.

A group normally receives credit once when its completion flag is false. In PARALLEL mode, checking completion also credits unfinished non-hostile groups. Changing the count directly does not complete those groups and can select an invalid array index. PauseEncounter and OnDestroy use the preceding index when the count is positive, a separate limitation from the next-group selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.encounterMusic
member.summary: Music clip requested as a temporary override when the encounter starts.

remarks.para: With a valid clip, StartEncounter sends it to the shared Audio2dManager together with volume, fadeInTime, fadeOutTime, and loop. It requests automatic override release after the clip's length minus fadeOutTime, even when looping is enabled. PauseEncounter and CompleteEncounter also request release if this field is still assigned.

Setting the field alone does not start playback or replace an already playing clip. Leaving it unassigned skips the encounter's cue and its music-release calls. Releasing the override lets the audio manager restore its saved background cue when one is available; it is not a promise that all music becomes silent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.encounterPasted
member.summary: No runtime gameplay effect was found for this shared flag in the audited Encounter code.

remarks.para: The flag is static, so it is shared across Encounter instances rather than stored separately on each encounter. The complete native Encounter methods and its two asynchronous task bodies audited here do not read or write it to control spawning, reset, completion, or music. Editor tooling, other game classes, and mods were not exhaustively checked. A working paste operation or tuning use was not established from this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.fadeInTime
member.summary: Requested time in unscaled seconds for encounter music to rise toward when its cue starts.

remarks.para: For a new clip, the audio channel starts at zero volume and moves toward the target on each frame using unscaledDeltaTime. Game-speed scaling does not stretch this fade. A nonpositive time assigns the target immediately. For example, target volume 0.5 over 2 seconds requests a rise of 0.25 volume units per second.

New-clip fades have a minimum rise rate of 0.04 volume units per second. For example, a target of 0.02 over 3 seconds instead reaches that target in roughly half a second. Reusing a currently playing clip uses a separate attenuation path. The Inspector's 0-to-10 range is not an Encounter runtime clamp, and editing this field alone does not adjust an already running fade.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.fadeOutTime
member.summary: Requested outgoing-music fade time when the encounter cue begins, and the amount of time subtracted from the clip length to schedule automatic override release.

remarks.para: This is measured in seconds. CueOverrideMusic passes it to the previous music channel's FadeOut and schedules an unscaled-time release after clip.length minus fadeOutTime. For example, a 30-second clip with fadeOutTime = 5 schedules release roughly 25 unscaled seconds after the cue starts, including when loop is true.

It does not directly set a fresh fade duration when PauseEncounter or CompleteEncounter releases the override: restoring the background cue uses that cue's saved fade settings. Channel fade rates and the current volume can also change the actual fade duration. The Inspector range is 0 to 10, but Encounter itself does not clamp the field to that range. Changes are read on the next encounter music cue.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.isWarmed
member.summary: Records that has already been requested, preventing another request.

remarks.para: WarmupEncounter sets this true before its spawn tasks finish. It does not mean that all NPCs have spawned or all assets are ready. PARALLEL requests every group's warmup; SERIES requests only the first group. The encounter's force-reset path does not clear this flag.

Changing it to false does not cancel earlier warmup tasks or remove their NPCs. A later WarmupEncounter call can then launch another warmup request, so manage that lifecycle rather than using this as a readiness test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.loop
member.summary: Requests looping playback for a newly cued encounter music clip.

remarks.para: The cue passes this to the AudioSource's loop setting. The encounter also requests timed release after clip.length minus fadeOutTime, so true does not guarantee that the override will repeat for the whole fight. This field controls music playback, not repetition of the spawn groups.

It is read when the encounter cues music; changing it alone does not update the current AudioSource. If the audio manager reuses an already playing identical clip instead of cueing a new one, its early-return or attenuation path may leave the existing loop setting in place.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.playerEntity
member.summary: Stores the entity that entered the encounter's linked zone, so a later parameterless start can direct group behavior toward that activator.

remarks.para: OnEnter assigns the entering MarrowEntity before attempting to start. StartEncounter uses this cached entity, when valid, to find a child TriggerRefProxy, the target reference used for investigation or aggression requests. Each group's mentalMode decides which request is made.

This is the cached activator, not an automatic global-player lookup. Setting it directly does not immediately redirect NPCs. StartEncounter(activatorEntity) uses its supplied entity for that call and does not store it in this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.spawnGroups
member.summary: Groups whose NPC populations, spawn limits, and progression are coordinated by this encounter.

remarks.para: PARALLEL starts every array entry. SERIES starts the entry at completeCount and advances when the current group receives completion credit. Each group supplies its own spawners, optional NPC profiles, living/dead limits, delays, and target-response mode.

Configure the array before Awake: that callback sizes _spawnCTSs to match it and sets the spawners to manual mode. Start gathers asset and toggle information from these groups. Null entries are not silently skipped, and growing or reordering the array during a run does not automatically rebuild cancellation sources or retarget existing tasks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.spawnOrder
member.summary: Selects whether all groups start together or groups start one at a time as completion advances.

remarks.para: PARALLEL starts every group loop; group limits and delays still determine when individual NPCs appear. SERIES starts spawnGroups[completeCount] and starts the next group after completion credit advances that count. A three-group example begins at index 0, then 1, then 2.

Warmup follows the same choice by warming every group in PARALLEL and only the first group in SERIES. PauseEncounter and OnDestroy cancel all slots in PARALLEL, but use the preceding slot in SERIES once completeCount is positive. Changing the mode during a run does not reorganize tasks already started under the previous mode.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter.volume
member.summary: Target AudioSource volume for the encounter music cue.

remarks.para: Use the ordinary 0-to-1 volume scale: 0 is silent and 1 is the source's full volume before mixer and user-volume settings. For example, 0.5 requests a target of 0.5, reached according to fadeInTime. This is not a percentage stored as 50 or a decibel value.

The Inspector limits editing to 0 through 1, but Encounter itself forwards the value; the audio manager uses different paths for a new clip and an already playing clip. Do not rely on the Inspector attribute as a universal runtime clamp. Editing this field alone does not change an existing cue's stored target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings._behaviours
member.summary: No effect of this stored behaviour list was verified in the audited SpawnAISettings methods.

remarks.para: The complete class methods checked here do not populate or read this list when applying settings. OnSpawn and PostReactivate instead find the spawned AIBrain and use its behaviour directly. Editing this list is therefore not a verified way to apply these settings to more NPCs. External game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings._playerObject
member.summary: No player-targeting effect of this reference was verified in the audited SpawnAISettings methods.

remarks.para: The checked class methods do not read or assign this field to direct investigation, aggression, or roaming. SpawnAISettings applies configuration to the brain found on the spawned object; setting _playerObject does not perform a verified player lookup or target command in those paths. External game and mod consumers remain outside this finding.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.homeIsPost
member.summary: Enables the navigation behaviour's post-home path request during its reactivation setup.

remarks.para: This flag is copied to the behaviour on spawn and after reactivation, whether or not overrideRoam is enabled. BehaviourBaseNav.OnReactivate uses a true post flag to request a path to its recorded home during that setup.

When homeTransform is assigned, SpawnAISettings separately writes its world position as home and requests a path there for either flag value. The flag does not make the NPC immobile or stop later roaming and combat decisions. Editing it alone does not update a behaviour that has already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.homeTransform
member.summary: Sets the world position recorded as the spawned NPC's home and requests navigation toward it during setup.

remarks.para: OnSpawn and PostReactivate read this Transform's current position and call SetHomePosition with goToHome enabled and the homeIsPost flag. This requests a path rather than teleporting the body. The recorded home is also the reference for LEGACY roaming and the navigation behaviour's horizontal home-distance check during target pursuit.

A missing Transform leaves the existing home position alone in these settings passes. Moving or replacing the Transform is read on the next spawn/reactivation setup, not continuously followed each frame. Rotation and scale of the home Transform do not define the roam axes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.investigateTimeout
member.summary: No investigation-duration effect was verified for this field in the audited SpawnAISettings setup paths.

remarks.para: OnSpawn and PostReactivate do not pass this value to BehaviourBaseNav.Investigate or copy it into a timer. The checked SpawnGroup spawn and post-reactivation paths use that group's own investigateTimeout for its investigation requests. Changing this field is therefore not a verified way to make those requests last longer.

This finding covers the complete SpawnAISettings class and the checked SpawnGroup paths, not all external code or mods. The constructor stores a value, but working units, a tuning range, and serialized defaults for a functional consumer were not established here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.isSoundAggroWhenInSecondaryZone
member.summary: Sets whether linked secondary-zone alerts may add threat to the spawned NPC.

remarks.para: OnSpawn and PostReactivate copy this flag into behaviour.isSoundAggroWhenInSecondaryZone even when overrideRoam is false. ZoneAggro checks the brain's corresponding getter when forwarding an alert to a linked secondary zone: false skips that NPC, while true permits AddThreat toward the alert's target reference.

The primary-zone call does not check the flag. Accepting a threat is not a guarantee of an immediate attack or immunity from every other source of aggression. Editing the spawn setting alone does not change an already configured behaviour until it is applied again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.objectPoints
member.summary: Provides waypoint objects for WAYPOINTS roaming when no valid roamSpline is assigned.

remarks.para: With overrideRoam enabled, OnSpawn and PostReactivate copy the nonempty array into the behaviour's waypoint-object reference and snapshot each object's current world position into its numeric waypoint array. The array order is the route order used by linear and ping-pong evaluation. A valid spline takes priority over these objects.

Entries must refer to real objects; missing entries are not skipped. Moving an object is captured by a later setup pass; these passes do not continuously rebuild positions every frame. orderedWaypointList and GetClosestWaypoint are spline helpers and do not read this fallback array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.orderedWaypointList
member.summary: Stores world-space spline-knot positions for closest-waypoint lookup and the selected-object drawing.

remarks.para: CreateListFromSpline clears and rebuilds it with one transformed position per knot. GetClosestWaypoint rebuilds it automatically before searching. The positions are meters in world space, and the list order follows knot order.

This settings list is not the input used to build a spawned NPC's runtime route. OnSpawn and PostReactivate independently read roamSpline or objectPoints. Editing only this list changes the helper/drawing data, not that runtime waypoint setup, and the next rebuild overwrites the edit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.overrideConfig
member.summary: Applies a replacement enemy profile to the spawned navigation behaviour during spawn and post-reactivation setup.

remarks.para: When assigned, the setup calls BehaviourBaseNav.ApplyOverrideConfig, which copies movement, combat, sensor, and health settings and writes the profile's requested puppet state. A missing profile skips this step. The separate home/sound settings are applied afterward, and enabled roaming overrides can replace the profile's roam settings.

When a SpawnGroup spawns an NPC from an EncounterProfile, it replaces this field with that selected NPCProfile's baseConfig before spawning. An edit can therefore be overwritten by profile selection. Changing the reference alone does not reconfigure an NPC that has already spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.overrideRoam
member.summary: Enables copying this component's roaming mode, speed, route or range, and wait settings into the spawned navigation behaviour.

remarks.para: OnSpawn and PostReactivate apply the optional enemy profile, sound flag, and home settings first. If overrideRoam is false, they stop before applying the roaming-specific fields. If true, roamMode selects the setup branch, wpWaitDuration is copied, and the behaviour is requested to enter roaming through SetRoam.

ZONE and ZONE3D need an assigned RoamArea for the base target picker. WAYPOINTS builds positions from a spline or waypoint objects. LEGACY uses roamXz and roamOffset. Changing the flag alone does not undo settings already copied into a spawned NPC.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamArea
member.summary: Defines the region from which the navigation behaviour chooses random targets in ZONE and ZONE3D roaming.

remarks.para: When overrideRoam is enabled, those two modes copy this reference to the behaviour. RoamArea.GetRoamTarget chooses a world-axis XZ rectangle at the area's world height; GetRoamTarget3D also varies Y. The full widths come from that area's dimensions multiplied by its uniformScale, centered on its Transform's world position.

These target calculations do not rotate the random region with the area's Transform or multiply dimensions by Transform scale. For an area with XZ size (10, 6) and uniformScale 1, targets range up to 5 meters each way along world X and 3 meters along world Z. The SpawnAISettings roamXz/roamXyz copies do not resize this area's geometry. Assign a valid area; the base picker does not provide a safe missing-area fallback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamMode
member.summary: Chooses whether a configured NPC roams in a 2D area, a 3D area, a waypoint route, or the legacy home-centered rectangle.

remarks.para: With overrideRoam enabled, ZONE uses roamArea's XZ targets, ZONE3D uses its XYZ targets, WAYPOINTS uses spline knots or objectPoints, and LEGACY samples a rectangle with full dimensions roamXz centered on homePosition minus roamOffset. RoamArea axes are world axes; spline knots are transformed into world positions.

The mode is copied during spawn and post-reactivation, after that branch's SetRoam setup. Editing this field alone does not change an existing behaviour. Ensure the required source is available for the selected mode; changing the enum does not create an area or a route.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamOffset
member.summary: Shifts the LEGACY roaming rectangle by subtracting this XZ offset from the NPC's recorded home.

remarks.para: The vector's first component is world X and its second is world Z, in meters. With home at (10, 0, 20) and roamOffset = (2, 3), the rectangle's center is (8, 0, 17). Positive values move the center toward negative world axes; this is not a local direction rotated by the spawner.

It is copied only for enabled LEGACY roaming. GetZoneArea overwrites it with zone.worldPosition plus the collider's local center, so that helper's result is still subtracted from home. The editor rectangle instead uses this settings object's position as its reference, which can differ from an assigned homeTransform. Changes are copied on spawn/reactivation, not continuously.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamOffset3D
member.summary: Stores the XYZ center value calculated by GetZoneArea3D; no target-offset effect was verified in this component's spawn setup.

remarks.para: The helper overwrites it with zone.worldPosition plus BoxCollider.center, adding components directly without rotating or scaling the local collider center. OnSpawn and PostReactivate do not read it to move a ZONE3D target region. That base mode instead picks from roamArea's own position and dimensions.

The checked SpawnAISettings and SpawnGroup setup paths do not establish another gameplay consumer. External code and mods were not exhaustively checked, so this is a limited finding rather than a game-wide unused claim.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamSpeed
member.summary: Sets the navigation speed requested by the roaming override, in meters per second.

remarks.para: When overrideRoam is true, setup passes this speed to SetRoam, which stores it in the behaviour.
