The checked PowerLegs and Omniwheel state transitions send that value to NavMeshAgent.speed for roaming, and also use it for some resting/investigating movement. The physical NPC can move more slowly because navigation, collisions, and its body simulation still affect movement.

For example, 2 requests a navigation speed of 2 meters per second. This does not set the separate combat speed. The Inspector tooltip lists LegBehaviours 1.35, Omni 2.5, and Crablet 1 as reference values; they are not automatic per-enemy defaults chosen by this component. Changes apply on spawn/reactivation rather than immediately to all existing NPCs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamSpline
member.summary: Supplies the knot positions for WAYPOINTS roaming, taking priority over objectPoints when assigned.

remarks.para: With overrideRoam enabled, OnSpawn and PostReactivate create one world-space waypoint per spline knot by applying the SplineContainer Transform to its local position. Moving, rotating, or scaling the container changes those positions when setup runs again.

The runtime route is a list of control-point positions, not continuous travel along the spline's curved shape or a dense sampling of its handles. CreateListFromSpline separately builds the helper list used for closest-point lookup and drawing. A valid but empty spline does not fall back to objectPoints.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamXyz
member.summary: Supplies XYZ roam dimensions that ZONE3D setup copies into the behaviour as half-widths.

remarks.para: With overrideRoam enabled and ZONE3D selected, each component is halved before SetRoam stores the behaviour's roamRange3D. For example, (10, 4, 6) becomes half-widths (5, 2, 3). These are distance values in meters under the game's world-distance convention, not percentages or speeds.

The audited base ZONE3D target picker chooses positions from roamArea's own dimensions and world position instead of this copied range. Changing roamXyz therefore does not resize that area. GetZoneArea3D can overwrite this field from the zone collider's local size without applying Transform scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.roamXz
member.summary: Sets the full XZ dimensions of LEGACY roaming and supplies the range copied by the other horizontal roaming setup branches.

remarks.para: In LEGACY mode with overrideRoam enabled, setup halves the X and Z values before random sampling around homePosition minus roamOffset. For roamXz = (10, 6), targets range up to 5 meters along world X and 3 meters along world Z on either side of that center. The Vector2's second component represents Z, and the values are meters, not radius or speed.

ZONE setup also copies half these dimensions into behaviour.roamRange, but its base target picker uses roamArea's geometry. WAYPOINTS copies the full values through SetRoam while actual destinations come from the waypoint array. Changing this field does not move spline knots or resize roamArea. GetZoneArea overwrites it from the collider's local XZ size.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.spawnAIPasted
member.summary: No runtime gameplay effect was found for this shared flag in the audited SpawnAISettings code.

remarks.para: This static boolean is shared by all instances. The complete native class methods and checked SpawnGroup spawn/settings paths do not read or write it to apply profiles, home positions, sound alerts, or roaming. A working paste operation was not established. Editor tools, other game classes, and mods remain outside this audit's absence finding.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.spawnerOffset
member.summary: Stores the local XZ displacement calculated by GetZoneArea between this settings object and the zone collider's center.

remarks.para: The helper computes (this.localPosition.x minus collider.center.x, this.localPosition.z minus collider.center.z). With matching parent axes and unit scale, this is the horizontal displacement in meters from that local collider center. Different parents or scales can make that interpretation misleading.

The audited OnSpawn and PostReactivate methods do not read it to relocate NPCs or center their roam targets. LEGACY target positioning reads roamOffset instead. No external gameplay consumer was established in the checked SpawnGroup paths; other classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.spawnerOffset3D
member.summary: Stores the local XYZ displacement calculated by GetZoneArea3D between this settings object and the zone collider's center.

remarks.para: The helper writes this.localPosition minus collider.center component by component. It does not convert either vector through a Transform, so interpret it as a common local-space displacement only when the settings object and collider share compatible parent coordinates. At unit scale the distance convention is meters.

This field is not read by the audited spawn/reactivation setup to move the NPC or its ZONE3D region. Those target coordinates come from home/waypoints or roamArea. The checked class/group consumers do not establish another effect; external classes and mods remain unverified.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.startWaypointIndex
member.summary: Chooses the initial route entry for ordered WAYPOINTS roaming when settings are applied.

remarks.para: This is zero-based: 0 means the first point, 1 the second. Enabled WAYPOINTS setup writes the behaviour's current index as startWaypointIndex minus one, so LINEAR or PING_PONG advances to the requested entry on its next selection. Random modes choose a random entry instead.

GetStartIndexByDist replaces it with the closest spline-knot index. The helper gizmo uses it directly to index orderedWaypointList, so keep it valid for that list as well as the runtime route. It is not clamped to the route length, and changing the settings field does not immediately change an existing NPC's current waypoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.waypointEvalMode
member.summary: Chooses how the next destination is selected in enabled WAYPOINTS roaming.

remarks.para: LINEAR walks forward through the route and wraps to the beginning. PING_PONG reverses the runtime waypoint array at the end and continues from index 1, avoiding an immediate repeat of the endpoint; it needs enough points for that index. RANDOM chooses any index and can repeat the same point.

RANDOM_MIN_TIME tries random indices whose stored selection cooldown has expired, using waypointMinTime. It makes at most as many attempts as there are waypoints, with possible repeat samples, so it can still return a recently selected point if all attempts fail. The mode is copied at spawn/reactivation, not applied continuously from this component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.waypointMinTime
member.summary: Sets the requested cooldown before a waypoint is selected again in RANDOM_MIN_TIME evaluation.

remarks.para: Enabled WAYPOINTS setup copies this only when waypointEvalMode is RANDOM_MIN_TIME. The behaviour records an eligible selection's next allowed time as Time.time plus this duration, so it uses scaled game seconds. For example, 15 asks later choices to prefer other points for the next 15 game seconds; the timestamp is set when selected, not when reached.

The picker makes only a limited number of random attempts and can return its last sampled point even if still on cooldown. This is not a strict guarantee that revisits cannot happen earlier. It does not set how long the NPC stands at a waypoint; wpWaitDuration controls the applicable path-finish wait.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.wpWaitDuration
member.summary: Sets the delay before choosing another destination after the base ZONE or WAYPOINTS path is cleared at arrival or failure.

remarks.para: With overrideRoam enabled, setup copies this into behaviour.roamWaitDuration. In the checked base ZONE and WAYPOINTS branches, reaching inside the navigation agent's stopping distance or detecting an incomplete path clears it and stores nextRoamTime = Time.time plus this value. Another target is chosen after that time has passed.

The duration is in scaled game seconds. For example, 2 requests a two-game-second wait after that path-clear step; navigation updates can add scheduling delay. It is not the minimum time before revisiting a particular point, and the checked LEGACY and ZONE3D branches do not establish the same path-finish wait behavior. Edits are copied on spawn/reactivation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnAISettings.zone
member.summary: Zone from which the area-building helpers obtain their parent object and BoxCollider geometry.

remarks.para: CreateRoamArea, GetZoneArea, and GetZoneArea3D use this reference, searching the settings object's parents for a Zone if it is unassigned. CreateRoamArea adds its child under this zone. The copy helpers use collider local size/center and direct position arithmetic, so rotated or scaled zones are not automatically converted into matching world bounds.

Assigning this reference alone does not create an area, start an encounter, or relocate a spawned NPC. The audited spawn/reactivation setup consumes roamArea or the explicit route/range fields rather than querying the zone each frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.DeadCount
member.summary: The number of death notifications recorded toward this group’s completion target.

remarks.para: Increases once per invocation of the group’s death handler, after OnDeathEvent runs. Resurrection and corpse despawn do not subtract from it. ResetVariables and Cleanup set it to zero.

It is a count of recorded death notifications, not the current number of corpses. A brain spawned already dead enters the dead set without adding a death notification, and a repeated notification can increment this counter even if that brain is already in the set. IsAllDead and the normal encounter loop compare it with totalSpawn to decide when the group has met its completion target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.OnCleanup
member.summary: Callback invoked with this group after clears its tracking and unregisters its spawners.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

At callback time the sets and counters have been cleared, _spawnerIndex is zero and isSetup is false. isComplete is left unchanged. Cleanup has no once-only guard, so another call can raise this callback again.
This notification means group bookkeeping was cleared. It does not mean every NPC body has disappeared or every asynchronous encounter/removal task has stopped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.OnDeathEvent
member.summary: UltEvent invoked with the dying member’s AIBrain when the group handles a death notification.

remarks.para: The brain has been added to _deadBrains and removed from _aliveBrains before this event runs, and the group’s PostReactivate listener has been removed from its behaviour. DeadCount increases after the event returns, so reading it inside the event still gives the earlier count.
This event does not itself despawn the corpse. The handler does not deduplicate notifications by whether the dead set already contained that brain.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.OnGroupComplete
member.summary: Callback invoked with this group during its first call while it is incomplete.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

isComplete is already true and onComplete has already run. This callback runs before CompleteGroup starts corpse cleanup and unregisters its spawners. It can therefore inspect or react to completion while bodies and listeners are still present.

The callback is not raised by a direct write to isComplete. The parallel encounter completion path can directly credit a non-hostile group by setting that flag, so the flag alone does not prove this callback ran.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.OnGroupSpawned
member.summary: Callback invoked with the newly reported GameObject and this group before the object is registered as a tracked NPC.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

The group checks for an AIBrain and a pooled-object component, then invokes this callback before deciding whether both were found. It can therefore run for a spawned object that will not become an AI member.

The group’s listener attachments, mental command and SpawnCount increment occur later. For example, reading SpawnCount here shows the count before this object’s increment. Use the GameObject argument for the reported object and the SpawnGroup argument for the group receiving its spawn notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.SpawnCount
member.summary: The group’s spawn-progress counter, used for its total-spawn limit and next NPC-profile entry.

remarks.para: Increases when the group registers a spawned object with both an AIBrain and a pooled-object component. Removing an NPC whose puppet state is still Alive subtracts one when the counter is positive; removing a dead puppet does not. Cleanup and ResetVariables zero it.

The encounter compares it with totalSpawn to decide whether another NPC may be requested, and SpawnProfileAsync uses it as the next NPC-profile list index. It is not the living population, the current tracked-set size, or a permanent lifetime spawn total. OnGroupSpawned runs before the registration increment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._aliveBrains
member.summary: The set of tracked brains currently classified as living, used to decide whether the encounter has room for another NPC.

remarks.para: Successful spawn registration adds a brain here when its isDead flag is false. Death removes it; resurrection adds it back. Despawn handling, requested delayed removal, Cleanup and ResetVariables can also remove entries.

maxAlive comparisons read this set’s size. KillAll and KillAlive select their targets from it. The set is bookkeeping rather than a fresh scene search; editing it does not physically spawn, resurrect or kill an NPC.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._crateRandLookup
member.summary: Spawner-to-randomizer cache that lets ordinary group spawning choose a randomized crate.

remarks.para: GetCrateRandomizers adds found RandomizeCrate components from the spawners’ GameObjects. SpawnAsync uses a matching entry instead of its ordinary awaited spawn path. SpawnProfileAsync follows the NPC profile rather than this cache.

The collection method does not replace existing entries or clear stale ones; Cleanup and ResetVariables also leave this dictionary intact. Replacing a spawner’s randomizer therefore requires attention to this cached mapping, not just a new component on its GameObject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._deadBrains
member.summary: The set of tracked brains classified as dead and available for the group’s corpse-removal requests.

remarks.para: Spawn registration can add an already-dead brain; death adds a living brain here; resurrection removes it. The set’s size is compared with maxDead. It is different from DeadCount, which records death notifications.

A delayed Despawn or WaitAndDespawnAllDead removes selected entries from this set before their bodies disappear. An empty set therefore does not guarantee that every corpse has already been physically removed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._deadCount
member.summary: The number of death notifications recorded toward this group’s completion target.

remarks.para: Increases once per invocation of the group’s death handler, after OnDeathEvent runs. Resurrection and corpse despawn do not subtract from it. ResetVariables and Cleanup set it to zero.

It is a count of recorded death notifications, not the current number of corpses. A brain spawned already dead enters the dead set without adding a death notification, and a repeated notification can increment this counter even if that brain is already in the set. IsAllDead and the normal encounter loop compare it with totalSpawn to decide when the group has met its completion target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._ignoredBrains
member.summary: Brains skipped by the group-wide mental command that applies aggression or investigation to existing members.

remarks.para: The brain’s SpawnGroupIgnore event adds it when the argument is true and removes it when false. MentalAllGroup checks this set while visiting registered living brains.

Ignoring a brain does not remove it from the alive, dead or spawned sets and does not exempt it from their count limits, death bookkeeping, KillAll or KillAlive in the inspected group code. The spawn and PostReactivate mental-command paths do not consult this set. Cleanup and ResetVariables clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._onCrateDespawned
member.summary: Callback attached to a successfully registered NPC’s pooled object to receive its GameObject when that object despawns.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

OnSpawn combines the current value into the pooled object’s despawn callback; OnDespawn removes the current value from that callback. This is separate from registering the group itself as a listener on its CrateSpawners.

The inspected SpawnGroup constructor and Setup do not assign this field. Supplying or replacing a callback affects later attachments; replacing the field does not automatically replace the value already attached to an existing pooled object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._onDeath
member.summary: Stored AIBrain callback that Setup adds the group’s death handler to and OnSpawn attaches to registered brains.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

The group handler moves the brain from the alive set to the dead set, removes its PostReactivate listener, invokes OnDeathEvent with that brain, then increments DeadCount. It does not directly despawn the body.

Cleanup removes the group handler from this stored callback. Brains already subscribed received the earlier delegate value; changing this field alone does not rewrite their subscriptions. OnDespawn removes the field’s current value from the departing brain.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._onResurrect
member.summary: Stored AIBrain callback whose group handler moves a resurrected NPC back into the living set.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

Setup adds the group’s handler, and OnSpawn attaches the stored callback to the brain’s resurrection notification. The handler adds that brain to _aliveBrains and removes it from _deadBrains; it does not decrement DeadCount or create a new spawn.

Cleanup removes the group handler from this field, and OnDespawn removes its current value from the brain. Changing the field does not automatically update delegate values already copied into existing brains.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._spawnCount
member.summary: The group’s spawn-progress counter, used for its total-spawn limit and next NPC-profile entry.

remarks.para: Increases when the group registers a spawned object with both an AIBrain and a pooled-object component. Removing an NPC whose puppet state is still Alive subtracts one when the counter is positive; removing a dead puppet does not. Cleanup and ResetVariables zero it.

The encounter compares it with totalSpawn to decide whether another NPC may be requested, and SpawnProfileAsync uses it as the next NPC-profile list index. It is not the living population, the current tracked-set size, or a permanent lifetime spawn total. OnGroupSpawned runs before the registration increment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._spawnedBrains
member.summary: The set of registered AI brains that the group has not yet removed from its tracking.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

Successful registration adds a brain whether alive or dead. Death and resurrection change the alive/dead sets without removing it here. Despawn handling and requested delayed removals remove it; Cleanup and ResetVariables clear the set.

This is not an archive of every NPC ever spawned. It can also stop containing an NPC before a delayed physical despawn finishes. Manually editing the set does not adjust SpawnCount or automatically connect and disconnect the NPC’s callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup._spawnerIndex
member.summary: The array index captured for the current spawn attempt and advanced to select a later attempt’s spawner.

remarks.para: Setup, Cleanup and ResetVariables set it to zero. Ordinary selection captures spawners[index], then stores (index + 1) modulo the number of spawners. For example, three spawners are selected 0, 1, 2, then 0 when toggles are not used.

With useSpawnerToggle the search stores a permitted next index, but the current spawner was already captured. A spawner’s shouldSpawn veto can therefore consume an index step without producing an NPC. Keep the index within the nonempty spawners array and keep profile settings in matching order.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.aiSettings
member.summary: The per-spawner settings components whose overrideConfig is replaced with each selected NPC profile’s base configuration.

remarks.para: GetAISettings creates this array from components on the spawners’ own GameObjects, using the same length and indices as spawners. A missing component leaves an empty entry and logs an error.

SpawnProfileAsync captures the settings entry beside the current spawner and changes its overrideConfig before requesting the spawn. This array contains shared component references, not separate copies of the settings, and is not rebuilt automatically whenever the spawners array changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.despawnInterval
member.summary: The wait, in scaled game seconds, between a corpse-removal request and its physical despawn.

remarks.para: The interval is read when delayed removal is requested; no per-NPC death timestamp is used. Despawn uses its delayed path only when this value is positive. That path removes the selected brain from tracking first, then waits before requesting the despawn effect and body removal.

WaitAndDespawnAllDead waits once for its snapshot; DespawnToMaxDeadCount waits between removal requests. Those awaited paths pass the value to UniTask.Delay without a nonnegative clamp. For example, an interval of two means roughly two game seconds after the request, which takes longer in real time when the game’s time scale is reduced.

A UniTask represents work that may continue over later frames. Awaiting it waits for that method’s task to finish; starting it without awaiting allows your caller to continue while the work is still pending.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.encounterProfile
member.summary: Optional ordered NPC list that supplies each profile spawn’s crate and AI base configuration.

remarks.para: The normal Encounter loops choose SpawnProfileAsync when this profile is valid, and ordinary SpawnAsync otherwise. A profile spawn reads npcProfileList[SpawnCount], assigns that entry’s spawnable to the chosen spawner, and assigns its baseConfig to the matching SpawnAISettings.overrideConfig.

Keep totalSpawn and the profile list’s valid indices consistent. The inspected runtime paths do not automatically resize the list or clamp the index, and Encounter.Start prepares profile assets/settings without assigning totalSpawn from the list length. The original Inspector tooltip’s “locked by encounter profile” wording is not a runtime guarantee.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.hostileGroup
member.summary: Controls whether a group must earn its own completion credit during a parallel encounter’s completion check.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

When a parallel encounter credits a completed group, it also marks incomplete groups with hostileGroup false as complete and adds them to its completion count. This direct flag change skips those groups’ CompleteGroup callbacks and cleanup.

This flag does not issue an aggression command in the inspected spawn paths. mentalMode and the stored playerProxy decide whether a newly registered or reactivated living NPC is told to investigate or become aggressive. A non-hostile completion credit also does not itself cancel that group’s already-running loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.initialGroupDelay
member.summary: The initial wait, in scaled game seconds, when the encounter starts this group’s normal spawning loop.

remarks.para: The loop waits this interval before its repeated checks; it then has a 0.15-second polling wait before checking completion, corpse limits and spawn room. For example, two means a two-game-second initial wait, not an immediate first spawn exactly at two real-time seconds.

A new normal group loop starts this wait again. WarmupLoop and direct SpawnAsync/SpawnProfileAsync calls do not read this delay. The delay uses the encounter’s cancellation token and is not clamped by the group.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.investigateTimeout
member.summary: The investigation time request, in scaled game seconds, sent to living NPCs when the group uses INVESTIGATE mental mode.

remarks.para: The group samples playerProxy.feetTran.position in world space and calls the NPC behaviour’s Investigate with that fixed position and this duration. An accepted request stores an expiry of Time.time plus the duration. For example, four requests an expiry four game seconds after acceptance.

Investigate can ignore a request while the NPC is in certain mental states or its previous investigation timer has not expired. This value is not a guaranteed stopwatch for stopping all movement, and changing it alone does not send a new command. Spawn, PostReactivate and MentalAllGroup supply it when they actually issue an investigation request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.isComplete
member.summary: The latch that records whether this group has already received completion credit.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

CompleteGroup sets it before invoking onComplete and OnGroupComplete, then starts corpse cleanup and unregisters spawners. Calls to CompleteGroup while it is true do nothing. A parallel encounter can also directly set it for a non-hostile group without running those callbacks.

It is not proof that all NPCs are dead or removed, or that every spawn/removal task has stopped. Cleanup and ResetVariables leave it unchanged; the encounter’s reset path explicitly clears it. Setting the field yourself does not perform CompleteGroup’s effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.isSetup
member.summary: The guard that prevents Setup from registering the group’s spawner listeners and handlers more than once.

remarks.para: Setup sets it true before adding handlers and registering the spawners. It is a setup-attempt flag, not a check that every later reference or listener is still valid. Cleanup clears it.

CompleteGroup unregisters the spawners while leaving it true, and ResetVariables also leaves it true. A later Setup call therefore returns until this guard has been cleared as part of deliberate cleanup. Writing true manually skips setup work rather than performing it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.maxAlive
member.summary: The living-population threshold below which the normal encounter and warmup loops may request another NPC.

remarks.para: Both loops compare the size of _aliveBrains with this whole-number cap and require the size to be strictly smaller. For example, a cap of three allows a request at two tracked living NPCs and holds it back at three. A zero cap leaves no room.

This is a gate on those loops, not an automatic kill or hard scene-wide population clamp. Direct SpawnAsync/SpawnProfileAsync calls do not check it. Other spawning, delayed work and manually changed tracking can make the actual population differ from the limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.maxDead
member.summary: How many dead brains the group may retain in its tracking before corpse cleanup is requested.

remarks.para: Excess means _deadBrains.Count is strictly greater than this whole-number threshold. For example, two permits two tracked corpses; a third makes IsOverMaxDead true. The normal encounter loop checks this and requests removal, including a 0.5-game-second wait on its ordinary excess-corpse path.

On completion, zero selects one delayed bulk removal of the current dead snapshot; a positive value selects trimming toward this count. Positive-delay removal stops tracking a selected brain before its body disappears, so this threshold is not an immediate limit on all visible corpses. Changing it alone does not invoke cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.mentalMode
member.summary: Chooses whether the group leaves an NPC’s mental state alone, asks it to investigate the stored target position, or makes that target a threat.

remarks.para: NONE leaves the mental state unchanged. INVESTIGATE samples playerProxy.feetTran.position as a world-space destination and sends investigateTimeout with the request. AGRO calls SetAgro with the stored proxy, which adds threat and requests the aggressive state; it does not guarantee an immediate attack.

The spawn and PostReactivate paths apply this only to living brains and require a valid stored playerProxy. MentalAllGroup stores a supplied proxy and applies the selected mode to existing living brains except those in _ignoredBrains. Merely changing this mode field does not send a command or continuously update every NPC.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.onComplete
member.summary: UltEvent invoked without arguments at the start of the group’s first completion transition.

remarks.para: CompleteGroup sets isComplete true, invokes this event, then invokes OnGroupComplete with the group. Corpse-removal requests and spawner unregistration follow those notifications, and the method does not await the removals.

It is not raised again while isComplete is true, or merely because a caller writes the flag. A parallel encounter’s direct completion credit for a non-hostile group can set the flag without invoking this event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.playerProxy
member.summary: The stored target reference used for this group’s investigation and aggression requests.

remarks.para: MentalAllGroup stores its supplied proxy here before applying the current mentalMode to existing living brains. Spawn and PostReactivate later reuse it. It is not necessarily a global player singleton: Encounter’s mental command obtains a child TriggerRefProxy from the supplied activator.

INVESTIGATE samples the proxy’s feetTran.position in world space for a destination; AGRO passes the proxy itself as the threat target. Replacing this field alone does not retarget NPCs already given commands. The spawn/reactivation paths skip their mental command when the stored proxy is not Unity-valid.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.spawnInterval
member.summary: Extra wait, in scaled game seconds, before a normal encounter loop requests another NPC after its spawn counter is positive.

remarks.para: The loop first finds room below maxAlive and totalSpawn. If SpawnCount is greater than zero, it waits this interval, then requests the spawn. With SpawnCount zero it skips this particular wait. The loop also spends time polling, awaiting the spawn and sometimes handling excess corpses, so this is not a promise of one spawn at exact regular intervals.

Direct SpawnAsync/SpawnProfileAsync calls do not apply it. WarmupLoop uses its own 0.1-second wait between operations instead. For example, an interval of one adds one game second before eligible later spawn requests; lowering the game time scale stretches that wait in real time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.spawnerToggles
member.summary: The index-matched SpawnerToggle list searched to select a permitted later spawner when useSpawnerToggle is enabled.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

Encounter.Start appends found SpawnerToggle components in spawner order and enables useSpawnerToggle when their count matches the spawner count. It does not clear this list first. Missing entries or repeated preparation can therefore break the expected matching arrangement.

The group scan reads each toggle’s shouldSpawn bool while choosing the next index. The current spawner has already been captured, and its own shouldSpawn callback separately decides whether it may spawn. The standard toggle’s Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, installs that callback, so a disabled current spawner can be skipped while the next call uses the newly selected index.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.spawners
member.summary: The ordered CrateSpawners that supply this group’s NPCs and notify it about their spawn lifecycle.

remarks.para: Setup registers the group with every assigned spawner. SpawnAsync and SpawnProfileAsync capture the current _spawnerIndex and advance selection for later attempts. Use a nonempty array with valid references for spawning; profile settings and enabled-toggle entries must line up with these indices.

When groups run in parallel, give each group its own spawners, as the Inspector tooltip requests. Profile spawning changes a spawner’s crate reference and its settings component’s overrideConfig, and more than one registered group can receive its spawn notifications. Sharing those objects can therefore interfere with each group’s selection and bookkeeping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.totalSpawn
member.summary: The group’s whole-number target used to stop further spawn requests and decide when enough deaths have been recorded for completion.

remarks.para: The normal and warmup loops request more NPCs while SpawnCount is below this value. The normal loop awards completion when DeadCount reaches it. These are separate counters: a living despawn can reduce SpawnCount, and resurrection does not reduce DeadCount.

For example, a target of six with maxAlive three ordinarily fills up to three living members at once and requests replacements as room opens until its spawn-progress target is reached. Death notifications then drive the completion test. A zero target makes IsAllDead true immediately and gives the loops no initial spawn room.

When using an encounter profile, keep the target consistent with its NPC list. The profile path indexes that list directly with SpawnCount; the inspected runtime preparation does not automatically set this value to the list length. The Inspector tooltip describes profile locking, but does not establish a runtime clamp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.useSpawnEffect
member.summary: Requests the crate’s spawn effect when a group spawn produces an object with a cached MarrowEntity.

remarks.para: On the ordinary awaited SpawnAsync and SpawnProfileAsync paths, the group checks the returned pooled object for a MarrowEntity and calls its spawn effect only if this flag is true. The cached-randomizer path passes the same flag into RandomizeCrate’s spawn request.

This controls the spawn-side effect request. The group’s inspected corpse-removal paths request despawn effects independently and do not check this flag. Changing it does not replay an effect on an NPC already spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup.useSpawnerToggle
member.summary: Enables searching the matching toggle list for the spawner index to store for a later spawn attempt.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here the group stores those routines so spawn, death, resurrection or completion notifications can trigger the matching work.

The group captures the current spawner before searching forward through spawnerToggles. A permitted entry updates _spawnerIndex for the next call; if no entry permits spawning, this call exits. The search itself does not replace the current captured spawner.

The captured spawner’s optional shouldSpawn callback is checked separately in both spawn methods, even when this flag is false. The standard SpawnerToggle installs such a callback, so turning this group flag off does not necessarily bypass a disabled spawner. Supply a correctly ordered toggle list with an entry for every spawner before enabling the search.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy._aiManager
member.summary: The NPC brain cached from when this proxy initializes.

remarks.para: For triggerType Npc, Start replaces this reference with the AIBrain component on root itself. Start is Unity’s startup callback: a routine Unity calls before the component’s first frame update. The lookup does not prefer a brain previously stored here and does not search root’s children.

The aiManager getter exposes this cache only while triggerType is Npc; it returns null for Player and Proxy even if this field contains a brain. Changing root later does not automatically repeat the lookup. This field’s native declaration is private and has no SerializeField attribute in the supplied dump, so it is not established as an Inspector-configured preference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.aiManager
member.summary: Returns the cached AI brain for an Npc proxy, and null for every other trigger category.

remarks.para: Start fills the cache by finding AIBrain on the root GameObject when triggerType is Npc. Start is Unity’s startup callback, a routine called before the first frame update. The getter does not search for a brain or refresh it; an NPC can still return null before setup or when root has no AIBrain.

Player and Proxy categories both return null, even when _aiManager contains a value. Sensors use the NPC brain to check death and pooled spawn identity, so set the category and root correctly before startup. Switching category or root alone after startup does not discover a new brain.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.chestTran
member.summary: A supplied chest-position reference; the inspected trigger and targeting paths do not use it as a primary volume-test point.

remarks.para: A Transform records a scene object’s position, rotation and scale. This field stores a reference to such an object rather than creating or moving a chest. The proxy’s Start leaves it as supplied by the character setup.

GenGameControl_Trigger’s inspected enter/exit handlers react to the entering collider and its attached Rigidbody’s proxy, while BehaviourBaseNav.CheckTarget reads targetHead and the inspected SpawnGroup investigation commands read feetTran. None of these paths tests chestTran to decide entry or priority. Other external scripts were not exhaustively searched; the old primary-body-point claim is not established by this evidence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.feetTran
member.summary: The world-space destination marker sampled when a spawn group asks an NPC to investigate this proxy’s position.

remarks.para: A Transform records an object’s position, rotation and scale. The SpawnGroup spawn and PostReactivate mental-command paths read feetTran.position in world space when they issue an INVESTIGATE request. Assign a marker at the position you want those NPCs to investigate, commonly near the character’s feet.

The request captures that position at command time; moving or replacing this marker does not continuously move an already-stored investigation destination. It also does not teleport the character. Those group paths require a valid feet Transform and do not fall back to the chest or head.

The inspected GenGameControl_Trigger enter/exit handlers use collider contact and triggerType, not a feet-position sanity check. This finding concerns those handlers and the inspected group commands; it is not a claim about every external trigger script.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.legacyProxy
member.summary: An additional Transform reference whose effect was not found in the inspected proxy, trigger and AI-targeting paths.

remarks.para: A Transform records an object’s position, rotation and scale. The proxy’s Start leaves this reference as supplied; it does not automatically synchronize it with root or use it as a fallback for missing body references.

The inspected proxy class, GenGameControl_Trigger enter/exit handlers, BehaviourBaseNav.CheckTarget and SpawnGroup investigation commands do not read legacyProxy. External scripts and editor setup were not exhaustively audited. The previous instruction to replace it with root was not verified: root is a GameObject used for brain lookup and NPC activity checks, so the two references have different types and demonstrated roles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.lfHandRb
member.summary: The supplied left-hand physics-body reference; assigning it does not change which collider the inspected trigger handlers recognize.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body simulated by Unity’s physics system. This field points to the character’s left-hand body rather than creating a hand, attaching a collider, or moving it. TriggerRefProxy.Start does not discover or assign it.

The inspected GenGameControl_Trigger enter/exit handlers find a proxy from the contacted collider’s attached Rigidbody GameObject and then read triggerType. They do not consult either stored hand reference for a separate hand-contact volume check. The sampled AI target check uses targetHead and the sampled group investigation commands use feetTran. External hand-interaction scripts were not exhaustively audited, so this is a scoped correction of the previous trigger-check claim.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.npcType
member.summary: The NPC identity value compared when AI computes a newly noticed target’s initial threat.

remarks.para: SubBehaviourSensors.InitialThreat gives zero initial threat when the target and self proxy have exactly equal npcType values; different values receive a distance-based score. AddThreat can still add further threat, so matching identities do not make an NPC immune to aggression.

The older TriggerRefProxyUtilities.HostilityTowards also compares this value, including a special rule when the source proxy’s teamNumber is zero. NpcType is a flags enum, but these two inspected scoring functions compare the whole value for equality rather than checking whether combined values share a flag. For example, FordHair and FordShortHair are different values even though both names describe Ford variants.
This is a label for the scoring rules, not a request to load an NPC model or replace its behaviour. Changing it does not clear existing sensor threat entries or immediately retarget all NPCs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.root
member.summary: The character GameObject searched for an NPC’s brain and checked for an active NPC target.

remarks.para: For triggerType Npc, the proxy’s Start callback finds AIBrain on this exact GameObject, not on its children, and replaces _aiManager. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this startup call prepares the cached brain. Assign the NPC object that actually holds AIBrain before startup.

SubBehaviourSensors.CheckTarget reads root.activeSelf, the object’s own active setting, when validating an NPC target. An inactive root causes that target to be removed. The cached brain is not refreshed simply by changing root later.

This reference is distinct from the GameObject holding the TriggerRefProxy component. GenGameControl_Trigger finds the proxy on the entering collider’s attached Rigidbody GameObject; root is not used as a parent-search fallback in that lookup. The inspected code does not establish the old claim that root automatically rejects all self-trigger contacts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.rtHandRb
member.summary: The supplied right-hand physics-body reference; assigning it does not change which collider the inspected trigger handlers recognize.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body simulated by Unity’s physics system. This field points to the character’s right-hand body rather than creating a hand, attaching a collider, or moving it. TriggerRefProxy.Start does not discover or assign it.

The inspected GenGameControl_Trigger enter/exit handlers find a proxy from the contacted collider’s attached Rigidbody GameObject and then read triggerType. They do not consult either stored hand reference for a separate hand-contact volume check. The sampled AI target check uses targetHead and the sampled group investigation commands use feetTran. External hand-interaction scripts were not exhaustively audited, so this is a scoped correction of the previous trigger-check claim.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.targetHead
member.summary: The head physics body whose world position is used to measure an AI target’s direction and distance.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body simulated by Unity’s physics system. BehaviourBaseNav.CheckTarget reads this Rigidbody’s world position and subtracts the observing NPC’s eye position to find the full 3D direction and distance to the target. Replacing this reference changes the point that calculation follows; it does not move the character’s actual head.

The check reads the current body position each time it runs. Supply a valid body when the proxy is used as a target; this path has no chest or feet fallback when targetHead is missing. The proxy’s own Start does not find or assign the head for you.
The sampled trigger enter/exit code identifies the proxy from the contacted Rigidbody’s GameObject and category. It does not make this head reference a “most sensitive” trigger-volume point.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.teamNumber
member.summary: The team label used by the older hostility helper, whose zero-team rule differs from its ordinary team comparison.

remarks.para: In TriggerRefProxyUtilities.HostilityTowards, a source proxy with a nonzero teamNumber gives zero hostility toward a matching team. Different teams get a distance-based score, with an additional reduction when their npcType values match.

A source teamNumber of zero instead compares npcType: the same identity gives zero hostility and a different identity gives one, regardless of the other proxy’s team number. For example, two proxies both labelled team zero can still score as hostile when their NPC identities differ. The rule depends on which proxy is the source of the comparison.

The inspected SubBehaviourSensors.InitialThreat does not read teamNumber; it compares NPC identity and distance. This field therefore is not a universal friend-or-foe switch for every AI path, and changing it does not itself clear recorded threat or order an attack.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy.triggerType
member.summary: Selects which trigger category this proxy reports and whether it exposes an NPC brain.

remarks.para: Player is 0, Proxy is 1, and Npc is 2. GenGameControl_Trigger sends its player enter/exit events for Player and its permitted NPC enter/exit events for Npc; its inspected handlers do not dispatch either category’s events for Proxy. Npc startup fills the brain cache; aiManager returns null for the other two categories.

Changing this label does not turn an object into a player rig or build an NPC brain. The inspected AddThreat sensor path expects a usable AI brain for a non-Player target, while a Proxy-category aiManager returns null. Proxy is therefore not a universally safe substitute category for an ordinary AI target. Configure the category and required root references before startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._exitTime
member.summary: Accumulated unscaled seconds that narrow the near-socket reinsertion guard.

remarks.para: Immediate clear and completed animated exit reset this to zero. Eligible hand updates use the old value to choose a guard size, then add unscaledDeltaTime, the time since the previous update without the game’s slow-motion multiplier. A callback that returns before reaching the active _isExitComplete guard does not increase it; the timer increment occurs before that guard can return.

For time t in unscaled seconds, the guard distance is (0.032 socket-local distance units) + (0.1 socket-local distance units) × (1 - clamp((4 per second) × t, 0, 1)). clamp limits its input between zero and one. The 4-per-second factor reaches the clamp limit at 0.25 seconds, so the guard shrinks from 0.132 to 0.032 socket-local units; at unit socket scale that is 13.2 cm shrinking to 3.2 cm.

While exit-complete is set, reinsertion returns early if max(-x, 0), abs(y) and abs(z) are each within that distance. Here x, y and z are the actual plug point in the socket’s local coordinates, with +X pointing inward. Moving outside the guard clears exit-complete, so this is a shrinking position guard rather than an animation timer or a guaranteed waiting period.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._handAttachedCount
member.summary: Stored attach-minus-detach count that controls the hand-alignment callback subscription.

remarks.para: When a hand attaches while the old count is below one, the plug subscribes its alignment callback to that hand’s skeleton update, then increases the count. Detaching decreases it first; a count of zero or less removes the callback from the hand supplied with that detach notification. A callback is a registered method that runs when the corresponding update occurs.

This is notification bookkeeping, not a live count read from the host. It is not clamped at zero, so balanced attach/detach notifications matter. Despawning resets it to zero. Writing the count directly does not add or remove callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isActive
member.summary: Allows held-plug alignment while at least one socket hover candidate remains.

remarks.para: Hover begin sets this true. Hover end sets it false only when the candidate list becomes empty, and despawning clears it. The hand-alignment method returns immediately while it is false.
Socket locking ends candidate hover notifications, so this can become false even while the plug is seated. The per-frame entry and exit animations use their own request flags rather than this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isEnterTransition
member.summary: Requests the per-frame alignment and seating sequence for the remembered socket.

remarks.para: Normal insertion sets this after locking the socket. Releasing the socket proxy grip, or releasing the last directly attached host hand, can also set it to reseat the plug. The per-frame Update checks entry before exit, so entry wins if both requests are true.

Entry first lines up the plug with the socket mouth, then moves to endTransform or endDistance along socket-local +X. Position movement is 1.25 local units per scaled second, usually meters per second with unit socket scale. Scaled time follows game speed, so slow motion slows this movement. Final seating clears the flag before the insertion-complete hook.
The flag can be true before any movement frame has run. Writing it alone does not lock a socket, prepare the physics bodies or install the needed grab handlers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isExitComplete
member.summary: Marks a completed release so nearby hand updates can suppress immediate reinsertion.

remarks.para: Immediate ClearFromSocket and successful animated exit set this true and reset the guard timer. A held-plug update keeps it true while the actual plug point stays inside the shrinking near-socket guard; leaving that guard clears it and allows insertion checks to continue.

The guard starts at 0.132 socket-local units and narrows to 0.032 over 0.25 accumulated unscaled seconds, usually 13.2 cm to 3.2 cm at unit scale. Despawning clears the flag. It is not a permanent record that the plug has ever been ejected, and immediate clear can set it without running an exit animation or completion hook.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isExitTransition
member.summary: Requests the per-frame exit sequence through the socket’s proxy grip.

remarks.para: EjectPlug and grabbing the socket proxy grip set this flag. A later Update moves the host to the socket mouth, then moves the plug proxy-grip pose toward the socket proxy-grip pose. Position moves at 1.25 local units per scaled second; the second stage turns by up to 720 degrees per scaled second. Local units are usually meters with unit socket scale, and scaled seconds follow game speed.

The second stage completes within 0.01 local units of its target position and about 2.29 degrees of target facing. It then clears this flag, unlocks and separates the plug, transfers any held proxy hand, and invokes the exit-complete hook. Both proxy grips must be configured for this path.

Releasing the socket proxy grip cancels this request and requests entry instead. Entry takes priority if both flags are true. A true request flag does not prove the socket is already unlocked or that an exit has completed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isLocked
member.summary: Local seating flag that prevents the held-plug method from starting another insertion.

remarks.para: Insertion and ForceInSocket set this after calling the socket’s Lock method. Immediate clear and completed animated exit clear it. The physical-grip cleanup path can also clear it without calling the socket’s Unlock method.

It is separate from Socket.IsLocked: during the socket lock event the socket is already locked but this flag has not yet been set. Direct host grabbing can allow physical movement while the remembered socket remains locked. Writing this field does not lock or unlock the socket.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isPhysicsGrip
member.summary: Marks direct host grabbing that lets the seated plug move through a physics guide joint.

remarks.para: For a socket without a proxy grip, grabbing the seated plug host sets this flag, separates its physics body from the socket’s packed body and makes it movable. It creates a ConfigurableJoint, a physics connection that guides sliding along the plug’s +X axis while restricting sideways motion.

Releasing the last host hand clears it and requests reseating. Per-frame cleanup can clear it and destroy the joint when the plug passes the socket mouth or gets sufficiently close to the socket origin. Despawning also clears it. This flag comes from direct host grabbing; holding the socket proxy grip follows the animated exit path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._isStageTwoAnimation
member.summary: Selects the second movement stage of either entry or exit.

remarks.para: During entry, stage one aligns the plug with the socket mouth; stage two moves it to the final endTransform pose or endDistance along socket-local +X. During exit, stage one moves back to the mouth; stage two aligns the plug proxy grip with the socket proxy grip.

The per-frame animation sets this when the first stage reaches its position target. Entry stage one also checks facing. Completing entry or exit clears it, as do immediate clear and despawning. It is shared by both directions and is not a 0–1 progress value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._joint
member.summary: Runtime physics guide created when the seated plug host is grabbed directly.

remarks.para: This ConfigurableJoint is added to the plug host’s GameObject. A joint is a physics connection that limits movement between bodies. Its main axis follows the plug’s local +X direction expressed in the host’s coordinates. Sliding on that axis is limited; sideways movement and sideways bending are locked, while twisting about the axis is free.

The linear limit is the socket’s endDistance, and the target position is half that distance along the joint axis. Distances use scene units, usually meters at unit scale. It connects to the socket host’s Rigidbody when available; a Rigidbody is Unity’s physical-motion component. Otherwise the joint is connected to the world.

Last-hand release and the physical-grip cleanup path destroy the joint. Despawning destroys it and clears this stored reference. Immediate ClearFromSocket does not destroy it, and a stored reference can outlast destruction because those other paths do not explicitly assign null.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._lastSocket
member.summary: Remembered alignment target that later insertion, exit and cleanup methods operate on.

remarks.para: While the plug is held, alignment updates select the nearest eligible hovered socket to the controller-derived desired plug position. Changing this selection resets the correction weight and its smoothing velocity. ForceInSocket also writes the supplied socket here.

It can refer to a candidate before insertion, a seated socket, or the socket just left after animated exit. The animated exit keeps this reference; ClearFromSocket and despawning clear it. Hover begin alone does not select it, and hover end alone does not clear it.
A nonnull remembered target therefore does not prove that it currently contains this plug. Methods such as EjectPlug and ClearFromSocket require a valid reference with the corresponding socket setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._minSwingAngleCos
member.summary: Cached cosine threshold for accepting the plug’s axis angle during hand alignment.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, stores cos(minSwingAngle × π / 180). minSwingAngle is the configured angle in degrees; π / 180 converts degrees to radians for the cosine. The stored result has no distance or time unit.

The hand update compares this value with the dot product of the plug and socket +X directions. For unit directions, that dot product is the cosine of their angle: 1 means matching directions and 0 means a 90-degree angle. The ordinary check accepts equality. The very-close insertion fallback requires a strictly larger dot product.

At the default 45-degree setting, the cache is about 0.7071. Changing minSwingAngle after Awake does not automatically refresh this cache. Writing the cache directly changes the next axis check without moving or inserting the plug by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._perc
member.summary: Smoothed weight for the requested hand-position and facing correction near a socket.

remarks.para: For acceptable axis and approach alignment, its target is 1 - clamp(d / abs(r), 0, 1). Here d is the desired plug-to-socket distance in meters, r is the socket’s influenceRadius in meters, abs gives its magnitude, and clamp limits the ratio to 0–1. Configure r positive and nonzero. Failed alignment targets zero.

SmoothDamp, a gradual change that keeps a stored rate of change, updates this weight with a 0.1-second smoothing time and scaled update time. The smoothing time controls how it approaches the target; it is not a promise of completion after exactly 0.1 seconds.

The requested hand correction receives this weight cubed. For example, 0 means no correction, 0.5 produces 0.125, and 1 produces full requested correction. The weight has no unit. A changed socket target, the last hover ending, or despawning resets it to zero.
This is independent of the entry and exit animation stages. Reading it does not tell you how far the plug has traveled into or out of the socket.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._sockets
member.summary: Current hover candidates from which held-plug alignment chooses its nearest socket.

remarks.para: Hover begin appends a socket and activates alignment. Hover end removes the first matching socket; removing the last candidate deactivates alignment and clears its correction weight. Despawning empties the list.

This is a changing runtime list of nearby sockets, not an allowed-socket configuration. Direct hover-begin calls can add duplicates, although normal socket notifications guard against duplicate plug enters. The hand update skips candidates whose socket host lacks a usable Rigidbody, Unity’s physical-motion component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug._speed
member.summary: Stored rate of change used to smooth the hand-alignment weight.

remarks.para: SmoothDamp, a gradual change with a remembered velocity, reads and writes this while bringing the correction weight toward its distance-based target. Its unit is weight change per scaled second: weight itself is unitless, and scaled seconds follow the game’s speed setting.

It starts at zero and resets when the selected socket changes or the plug despawns. Ending the last hover resets the correction weight but does not reset this rate. It is not the plug’s travel speed: per-frame insertion and exit position movement use a separate 1.25 local units per second rate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.minSwingAngle
member.summary: Configured angle limit, in degrees, between the plug and socket +X axes for insertion alignment.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, converts this to a cosine threshold. The Inspector setting is an angle in degrees, while the cached threshold is a unitless cosine. The default is 45 degrees, and the Inspector slider shows 30–90 degrees. A smaller angle requires straighter alignment; a larger angle permits more tilt. For example, a 45-degree setting accepts an ordinary axis check at 45 degrees but rejects 60 degrees.

The Inspector range does not clamp values written by code. The hand update reads the prepared cosine threshold, so changing this field after Awake does not automatically change the active angle check.
Passing the angle check alone does not seat the plug. Distance, approach side, hover eligibility, socket occupancy and the reinsertion guard also affect insertion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AlignPlug.proxyGrip
member.summary: Assigned plug grip used as the animated exit target for hand transfer.

remarks.para: This is a Grip reference you configure on the plug; this field does not spawn a grip. It is separate from the socket’s proxy grip. During the second exit stage, the host moves so this plug grip lines up with the socket grip’s pose, meaning its position and facing.

At successful exit, a hand attached to the socket grip is redirected to this plug grip. Configure both grips for that animated path. Directly grabbing a seated host on a socket without a proxy grip instead creates a physics guide joint through a separate path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoGroup.KeyName
member.summary: Identifies the shared ammunition count that reads and changes for this group.

remarks.para: This is a text key, a name used to find an entry in the inventory's stored counts. Different AmmoGroup assets with the same key refer to the same whole-round count. For example, if the registered key is ExampleLight, adding 20 rounds through one group and 10 through another with that key increases the shared count by 30.

The inventory registers its light, medium and heavy groups during Awake, Unity's initialization routine before normal component startup. Adding ammunition through an AmmoGroup also tries to register it. If the key is already registered, registration returns immediately and does not read that later group's cartridges list. Use different keys for ammunition that should have separate counts.

Registration saves each listed cartridge's name as a lookup to this key. Cartridge-based additions, removals and count queries then use that saved lookup. Changing KeyName later does not rename the old stored count or refresh those saved cartridge mappings; a group-based addition can instead register the new key.

The constructor starts this key as empty text. Set a deliberate, non-null key before registration. Empty text is still a shared key, so leaving several groups empty makes their names collide. This field does not contain the number of rounds or the Unity asset's file name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoGroup.cartridges
member.summary: Lists the ammunition descriptions whose inventory operations should use this group's shared count.

remarks.para: A CartridgeData asset describes a cartridge type. When a new group key is registered, AmmoInventory reads this array and saves each cartridge's Name as a lookup to the group's KeyName. Array indices start at zero, but their order does not give each cartridge a separate count. These entries identify types; the inventory stores the changing whole-round count elsewhere.

For example, if cartridge A and cartridge B belong to the same registered group, adding 20 rounds of A and 10 rounds of B raises their shared reserve by 30. A count query for either type reads that same reserve. Removing one round through A lowers the amount available through B too.

The array and every listed cartridge must be assigned before registration. An empty array registers the key without any cartridge mappings. If another group already registered the same KeyName, this array is skipped entirely. If a cartridge name already maps to another key, registration reports the conflict and keeps the earlier mapping.

The inventory registers its configured groups during Awake, Unity's initialization routine before normal component startup, and also attempts registration when ammunition is added through a group. It caches the mappings then. Editing this array later does not refresh an already registered key. CartridgeData.Name itself is cached from the asset's name when first needed, so changing an asset's visible name later may not change that lookup name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.Instance

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, assigns this reference only when no live inventory is already selected. Creating another AmmoInventory does not replace the existing reference or destroy the extra component. Before an inventory has initialized, this reference can be null.
InventoryAmmoReceiver uses this reference to read available ammunition and subscribe to updates that refresh the visible ammo supply.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory._AmmoCountsByCartridge

remarks.para: AmmoInventory's add, remove, count-query, registration, and clear methods do not read or update this dictionary. Use AddCartridge and RemoveCartridge to change those balances and send the corresponding update callbacks, registered code called to report an ammo operation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory._cartridgeCounts
member.summary: Individual round balances for cartridge definitions that are not assigned to a registered ammo group.

remarks.para: The keys are CartridgeData objects, not name strings. AddCartridge creates an entry when an ungrouped cartridge is first added; GetCartridgeCount reads it and RemoveCartridge reduces it without going below zero.

Grouped cartridges use _groupCounts instead. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, replaces this dictionary with an empty one, and ClearAmmo does not clear it. Changing it directly bypasses the update callbacks, registered code called to report an ammo operation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory._cartridgeToKey
member.summary: Maps each registered cartridge Name to the KeyName of the shared reserve used for its ammunition.

remarks.para: RegisterAmmoGroup builds this mapping from each group's cartridge list. AddCartridge, RemoveCartridge, GetCartridgeCount, and GetGroupByCartridge consult it to choose the group balance. A cartridge name absent from the mapping uses an individual CartridgeData balance instead.

Because the key is a name string, separate CartridgeData assets with the same Name resolve to the same registered group. Existing mappings are retained on registration, and editing an asset's cartridge list later does not rebuild them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory._groupCounts
member.summary: The number of inventory rounds available in each registered shared ammo group, indexed by its KeyName.

remarks.para: Every cartridge name mapped to a group reads and changes this same balance. For example, a balance of 30 is one shared 30-round supply, not 30 separate rounds for each listed cartridge type.

AddCartridge and RemoveCartridge update these balances and send callbacks, registered code called to report an ammo operation. Direct dictionary edits bypass those notifications. ClearAmmo resets only the groups currently assigned as lightAmmoGroup, mediumAmmoGroup, and heavyAmmoGroup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.onAmmoUpdate
member.summary: Callback for refreshing ammunition displays after an inventory add, removal, or clear operation.

remarks.para: A callback is a function you attach so it runs when an operation finishes. This one takes no arguments. Read the relevant balance with GetCartridgeCount when it runs. InventoryAmmoReceiver subscribes to this callback to refresh its visible ammo supply.

Add and removal operations invoke it after onAmmoUpdateCount, even if the requested count is zero or the removal is limited by an empty balance. Removing an ungrouped cartridge with no entry returns without either callback. ClearAmmo calls it once after its per-group notifications. Registering a new group can also invoke it while processing cartridges.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoInventory.onAmmoUpdateCount
member.summary: Reports an ammunition operation with a group key and a count whose meaning depends on the operation.

remarks.para: This callback holds registered code called to report an ammo operation. For AddCartridge and RemoveCartridge, the string is the affected group KeyName, or an empty string for an ungrouped cartridge. The integer is the count passed to that method. Both adding 5 and removing 5 report 5; it is not a signed change or the resulting balance. A removal that is limited to zero still reports the requested quantity.

ClearAmmo instead reports each registered group's current stored balance after resetting the configured light, medium, and heavy groups. Those groups report zero; other groups can report their retained balances. Registration can also send notifications through its internal removal calls.
To display the current ammunition total, query GetCartridgeCount rather than treating this callback's integer as the total. The general onAmmoUpdate callback follows these notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AmmoPlug.magazine
member.summary: The whose inserted state and visible cartridges this plug updates.

remarks.para: The insertion and removal completion callbacks use this reference. A callback is a method the alignment system calls when a stage finishes. Insertion sets this magazine's isMagazineInserted flag to true and hides its displayed cartridge models. Removal clears the flag and refreshes those models from the remaining round count. A round is one complete cartridge of ammunition.

Configure this public field for the Magazine represented by the plug, and keep the magazine's own magazinePlug reference consistent with that pairing. The inspected AmmoPlug constructor and inherited Awake do not search for or fill the field. Awake is Unity’s initialization callback for a Unity component. A missing magazine causes either completion callback to fail.

Assigning this public field changes only the stored reference that future completion callbacks read. It does not itself run the insertion or removal callback. For a socket whose IsClearOnInsert returns true, the insertion callback also requests this magazine's despawn after updating its inserted flag and display.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.SwingCounterCurveRagdoll
member.summary: Maps the active-ragdoll pose's calculated tilt angle to a counter-rotation angle in degrees.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate uses this in the ActiveRagdoll state, rather than the fully Ragdoll state. Its horizontal input is the angle, in degrees, between the tracked rig's up direction and the up direction after the branch's pelvis-relative orientation calculation. Its output is passed to an axis-angle rotation used in the spine-pose correction.

It is not a count that increases over time. An illustrative input of 30 degrees and curve output of 15 supplies a 15-degree counter-rotation before the rest of that branch's pose composition. Changing a key changes the correction at that tilt; the field does not itself switch the body into a ragdoll state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.SwingCounterCurveSeated
member.summary: Maps seated rig tilt in degrees to the head's counter-tilt correction in degrees.

remarks.para: In the aligned-seated branch, OnEarlyUpdate measures the angle between the input rig's player-up direction and world up, evaluates this curve at that angle, and applies the result around the axis that counteracts the rig tilt when setting the head rotation. Horizontal curve input is an angle, not time or an accumulated swing count; vertical output is the correction angle.

For example, an illustrative key at input 20 with output 10 supplies a 10-degree counter-rotation when the measured tilt is 20 degrees. Increasing that output increases the counter-tilt for that input. This branch needs the active seat to be ingress-aligned; otherwise the on-foot solve runs. The exact parallel/antiparallel-up case skips this curve evaluation in that branch.
The field retains the old serialized name SwingCounterCurve for scene-data compatibility. That old name does not change the current angle-input behavior.

The seated curve is evaluated only after the input rig is ingress-aligned: aligned means its seated ingress pose has been brought into the expected player/world frame. The curve input remains the measured tilt angle in degrees, not an alignment timer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._blendToSampleTime
member.summary: The smoothing duration used while fading the saved transition pose's weight toward zero.

remarks.para: This is the smoothTime argument in seconds for the _sampleBlendWeight SmoothDamp calculation. SetBodyState writes 0.25 when transitioning between OnFoot and ActiveRagdoll. A longer positive duration generally makes the saved rotations lose influence more slowly; it is not a countdown decremented each frame or a promise that blending ends after exactly that duration.
OnEarlyUpdate uses it with the current weight and _sampleBlendWeightV. Another eligible body-state transition overwrites the duration with 0.25 again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._body
member.summary: The configured component that calculates stepping-leg animation for this rig.

remarks.para: SLZ_Body owns the locomotion and footstep data used by OnFootSolve. AnimationRig startup calls its OnStart, SetAvatar forwards avatar calibration, and the on-foot solve asks it for foot/ankle poses and a working pelvis offset.

body returns the stored _body reference directly. The reference must point to an already configured component; replacing it alone does not initialize its footstep state or recalibrate it for the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._currentSwing
member.summary: Stored swing value that does not drive the swing-counter curves in the audited animation update.

remarks.para: Startup resets this to zero. OnEarlyUpdate evaluates SwingCounterCurveSeated and SwingCounterCurveRagdoll directly from calculated tilt angles and uses those results for counter-rotation; it does not accumulate those results into this field.

The audited AnimationRig pose paths do not use this field as a curve input or as a turn-smoothing rate. Changing it therefore does not retune those verified swing-counter calculations. This statement concerns the audited rig implementation, not every possible external proxy consumer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._dragUp
member.summary: The smoothed world-space direction toward which movement makes the body lean.

remarks.para: UpdateHeptaBody2 replaces it with BodyVelocity's result. That calculation combines world-up with horizontal velocity and acceleration contributions, smooths the direction, and normalizes it; its components are unitless direction components, not meters per second or a force.

The chest and pelvis solves use rotations from the current player-up direction toward this direction to alter posture. OnFootSolve also converts it into the input orientation reference for locomotion adjustments. Editing the field is temporary because the next body-velocity calculation replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._lastInHeadSwing

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._lastSacrumFwdV2
member.summary: The previous flattened forward heading used to measure the pelvis's turn between additive solves. Related state: .

remarks.para: The two components are world X and world Z from a forward direction, not X and Y positions. The additive solve compares this heading with its newly calculated heading using signed angles, then stores the new heading for the next call. This history helps the horizontal turn correction respond without treating every solve as a fresh pose.

Startup and re-enable initialize it from the rig transform's normalized horizontal forward direction. Teleport rotates the stored heading with the supplied rotation delta. This is calculated direction history, so assigning it does not directly turn a joint and later solves replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._lastT1FwdV2
