remarks.para: The two components are world X and world Z from a forward direction, not X and Y positions. The additive solve compares this heading with its newly calculated heading using signed angles, then stores the new heading for the next call. This history helps the horizontal turn correction respond without treating every solve as a fresh pose.

Startup and re-enable initialize it from the rig transform's normalized horizontal forward direction. Teleport rotates the stored heading with the supplied rotation delta. This is calculated direction history, so assigning it does not directly turn a joint and later solves replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._lfCurlLerp
member.summary: The smoothed left-controller grip value used to choose the avatar's hand shape for torso-proximity correction.

remarks.para: ReapplyTorsoProximity reads the controller's secondary-interaction axis; the audited base/controller implementation returns its solved-grip value. It eases this cache toward that input with blend fraction clamp(20 × deltaTime, 0, 1). For an illustrative 0.01-second update, it moves 20% of the remaining difference.

The cache is passed to Avatar.GetHandBounds for the left hand, and those bounds help reposition the rig hand relative to the torso. It is a unitless input blend, not an elbow angle or force. The method overwrites it on later calls; changing it does not simulate a controller button press.
deltaTime is elapsed frame time in seconds. Thus 20 × deltaTime is a per-second smoothing rate converted to a unitless blend fraction and clamped to 0–1; at 0.01 seconds it is 0.2.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._pelvisLocalAnimOff
member.summary: The current working pelvis position-and-rotation offset produced by the stepping-leg calculation.

remarks.para: SLZ_Body.SolveLegs writes this SimpleTransform through a reference during the on-foot solve. Its position describes a local animation displacement in world-distance units, normally meters, and its rotation is a quaternion, a value that records an orientation. Local here means the stepping coordinate frame of SLZ_Body.locomotion.neutralRoot, the transform used as the reference for its foot calculations. The quaternion records a rotation correction around that frame's axes. The additive pelvis path reads the stored rotation as a posture correction, blending from identity with a factor of 0.5 + 0.5 × the chest-suppression weight.

pelvisLocalAnimOff returns a copy of the same storage as _pelvisLocalAnimOff. OnEarlyUpdate replaces that storage with the identity transform at the end of the pose pass. This is temporary solve output, not an Inspector offset that remains applied across updates; reading it after the outer pass normally sees the reset value.

suppressChestVelocityTwist is a unitless 0–1 weight. The additive rotation uses the identity quaternion as its neutral orientation and the factor 0.5 + 0.5 × weight; neutralRoot supplies the stepping coordinate frame. The field is temporary solve output and is reset at the documented pass boundary.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._rtCurlLerp
member.summary: The smoothed right-controller grip value used to choose the avatar's hand shape for torso-proximity correction. Related state: .

remarks.para: ReapplyTorsoProximity reads the controller's secondary-interaction axis; the audited base/controller implementation returns its solved-grip value. It eases this cache toward that input with blend fraction clamp(20 × deltaTime, 0, 1). For an illustrative 0.01-second update, it moves 20% of the remaining difference.

The cache is passed to Avatar.GetHandBounds for the right hand, and those bounds help reposition the rig hand relative to the torso. It is a unitless input blend, not an elbow angle or force. The method overwrites it on later calls; changing it does not simulate a controller button press.
deltaTime is elapsed frame time in seconds. Thus 20 × deltaTime is a per-second smoothing rate converted to a unitless blend fraction and clamped to 0–1; at 0.01 seconds it is 0.2.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumToVelLerp
member.summary: The smoothed horizontal heading correction, in degrees, applied to the pelvis.

remarks.para: The additive pelvis calculation compares flattened forward headings with signed angles and uses the previous _lastSacrumFwdV2 heading to account for motion between solves. It then smooths the correction and applies it as a rotation around world up. This is a turn-angle history value, not a linear velocity or a 0–1 blend weight.

Its paired ToVelVel field is the smoothing rate. Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity clear both. Editing the value can affect a transient pose, but later additive solves recalculate it from the current headings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumToVelVel
member.summary: The smoothing rate for the pelvis's horizontal heading correction. Related state: .

remarks.para: The additive solve passes this by reference to SmoothDamp when updating _sacrumToVelLerp. It is an angular rate in degrees per second, retained so the turn correction changes smoothly. It does not directly rotate a Rigidbody or set the body's movement speed.
The next smoothing call updates it. Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity clear it together with the corresponding correction angle.
The referenced Rigidbody term is Unity’s physics body; this cache is not that body’s velocity. The value is the animation angular-rate history used by SmoothDamp, in degrees per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumUpOffsetCurveClimb
member.summary: The climb-posture curve that maps normalized height to a pelvis angle in degrees. Related state: .

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized chest height: project the world-space chest-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated chest-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the pelvis rotation. SolveSacrumUpOffset selects this curve when hand support exceeds foot support; its blend weight is 1.3 × hand support clamped to 0–1. Here, hand support means a unitless amount of support through the hands, not a distance or force. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.
This is a configured curve input to subsequent solves. The curve result is not clamped to a degree range in the helper, and branches that select it need an assigned curve.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are distances in the solve’s calibrated distance units (metres at unit scale), while the curve output is an angle in degrees. The denominator is the calibrated chest reference height; the velocity curve’s leg-relative speed is movement speed divided by combined leg length.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumUpOffsetCurveMantle
member.summary: The mantle-posture curve that maps normalized height to a pelvis angle in degrees. Related state: .

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized chest height: project the world-space chest-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated chest-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the pelvis rotation. SolveSacrumUpOffset selects this curve when hand support exceeds foot support and mantle is positive; after the climbing blend, its blend weight is 1.3 × mantle clamped to 0–1. Here, mantle is the unitless amount of pulling the body over a ledge; a positive mantle value is the blend operand. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.
This is a configured curve input to subsequent solves. The curve result is not clamped to a degree range in the helper, and branches that select it need an assigned curve.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are distances in the solve’s calibrated distance units (metres at unit scale), while the curve output is an angle in degrees. The denominator is the calibrated chest reference height; the mantle branch is the ledge-pull branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumUpOffsetCurveVelocity
member.summary: The velocity-posture curve that maps normalized height to a pelvis angle in degrees.

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized chest height: project the world-space chest-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated chest-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the pelvis rotation. SolveSacrumUpOffset selects this curve when foot support exceeds hand support and the leg-relative speed is positive; its blend weight is that speed clamped to 0–1. Here leg-relative speed means horizontal movement speed in meters per second divided by the avatar's total upper-plus-lower leg length in meters, giving leg lengths per second. Its numeric value is clamped for the blend; for example, 0.5 means movement at half a leg length per second. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.

SetAvatar moves the second key's input coordinate for the avatar while preserving its output value. Provide at least two keys; an avatar refresh can overwrite that key's input coordinate and resets its slope settings.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are distances in the solve’s calibrated distance units (metres at unit scale), while the curve output is an angle in degrees. Leg-relative speed means horizontal movement speed divided by the avatar’s combined leg length, giving leg-lengths per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumUpOffsetLerp
member.summary: The smoothed posture-curve angle currently used by the pelvis solve.

remarks.para: The additive pelvis path moves this toward the corresponding SolveSacrumUpOffset result using SmoothDamp with a 0.15-second smoothing time. The value is in degrees and feeds an axis-angle rotation together with other lean and posture corrections; it is not a stored vertical distance.

Its paired UpOffsetVel field records the rate used by the smoother. Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity clear both values. A manual change can affect a following solve, but the smoother will continue replacing it toward the calculated target.
The paired UpOffsetVel value is the smoothing rate, and the smoothed value is later consumed as an axis-angle posture correction. Its angle is in degrees; it is not a vertical distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sacrumUpOffsetVel
member.summary: The smoothing rate for the pelvis's posture-curve angle. Related state: .

remarks.para: SmoothDamp receives this by reference while updating _sacrumUpOffsetLerp and replaces it with the new rate. Because the smoothed quantity is an angle and elapsed time is in seconds, this is degrees per second. It carries momentum between smoothing steps; it is not the physical speed of the spine or a separate target.
Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity reset the paired angle and rate to zero. Setting the rate alone changes transient smoothing behavior until the next calculation updates it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sampleBlendWeight
member.summary: The remaining influence of the joint rotations saved for a body-state transition.

remarks.para: SetBodyState sets this to 1 after capturing the current rotations when entering or leaving ActiveRagdoll from OnFoot. OnEarlyUpdate smoothly lowers it toward 0 and blends the newly solved rotations toward the saved rotations using this weight. Thus 1 retains the saved pose, while 0 leaves the current solve's pose. It is unitless.
Below 0.01 the update clears both this weight and its smoothing rate. This is a calculated transition value, not a permanent animation-layer setting; later transitions replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._sampleBlendWeightV
member.summary: The smoothing rate used to fade the saved-pose blend weight.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate passes this by reference to SmoothDamp when moving _sampleBlendWeight toward zero. Its units are blend-weight units per second, not meters per second. The smoother updates it each active blending step; a negative rate can represent a falling saved-pose weight.
The update clears it with the weight once the weight falls below 0.01. Changing this field alone does not capture a pose or start a body-state transition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._stateBlendSample
member.summary: Saved joint rotations that briefly preserve the previous pose during an OnFoot/ActiveRagdoll transition.

remarks.para: SetBodyState fills this Quaternion array through Rig.SampleRigPose; OnEarlyUpdate later passes it to Rig.BlendToSampledRigPose with _sampleBlendWeight. A quaternion represents an orientation, not a position. The sampler stores the pelvis world rotation and the other sampled joints' rotations relative to their parent joints.

The constructor supplies space for 19 sampled rotations. This snapshot is generated transition history, not an Animator clip, and it does not contain joint positions. The next eligible transition replaces its contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._suppressChestVelocityTwist
member.summary: Temporarily reduces movement-driven chest lean and adjusts the pelvis posture correction while the weight is refreshed.

remarks.para: This is a unitless weight. The public suppressChestVelocityTwist setter clamps it to 0–1 and marks it freshly updated. One chest lean-blend factor includes 1 - 0.5 × weight, so increasing it from 0 to 1 reduces that factor from 1 to 0.5; it is not a switch that stops all torso movement. The pelvis-animation rotation blend also changes from 0.5 to 1 as this weight rises.

HandgunVirtualController and RifleVirtualController refresh the public property while solving aiming. In the on-foot body update, the freshly updated flag first prevents decay for one solve, then an unrefreshed dirty weight loses deltaTime each later solve until it is clamped back to zero when the subtraction would make it negative. For example, an unrefreshed weight of 0.5 falls by about 0.1 over a subsequent 0.1-second solve.

_suppressChestVelocityTwist exposes the raw stored weight; writing it directly bypasses the setter's clamp and freshness flags. Use the public property when requesting the verified temporary-suppression behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._suppressionDirty
member.summary: Records that the temporary chest-suppression weight should be allowed to fade when it is no longer refreshed.

remarks.para: The public suppression setter sets this flag together with _suppressionFreshlyFilthy. UpdateHeptaBody2 checks it, waits out the freshly updated solve, then subtracts elapsed seconds from the stored weight on later solves. It clears the flag when that decay takes the weight strictly below zero and resets the weight to zero.

This flag controls the lifetime of a temporary pose weight. It does not mean a cache or curve needs rebuilding. Changing it directly can change whether the weight decays, without performing the setter's other steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._suppressionFreshlyFilthy
member.summary: Marks a fresh suppression request so the next on-foot body solve skips its decay once.

remarks.para: The public suppression setter sets it true and also sets _suppressionDirty. UpdateHeptaBody2 clears this fresh flag on its first flagged solve. Only later solves without a new request subtract deltaTime from the suppression weight.
Refreshing the property again renews this one-solve hold. This flag is about request timing, not recomputing suppression caches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._t1UpOffsetCurveClimb

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized head height: project the world-space head-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated skull-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the upper-spine/chest rotation. SolveT1UpOffset selects this curve when hand support exceeds foot support; its blend weight is 1.3 × hand support clamped to 0–1. Here, hand support means a unitless amount of support through the hands, not a distance or force. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.
This is a configured curve input to subsequent solves. The curve result is not clamped to a degree range in the helper, and branches that select it need an assigned curve.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are calibrated distances, while the curve output is an angle in degrees. The denominator is the calibrated skull reference height; the selected branch is the hand-supported climb posture.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._t1UpOffsetCurveMantle
member.summary: The mantle-posture curve that maps normalized height to a upper-spine/chest angle in degrees.

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized head height: project the world-space head-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated skull-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the upper-spine/chest rotation. SolveT1UpOffset selects this curve when hand support exceeds foot support and mantle is positive; after the climbing blend, its blend weight is 1.3 × mantle clamped to 0–1. Here, mantle is the unitless amount of pulling the body over a ledge; a positive mantle value is the blend operand. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.
This is a configured curve input to subsequent solves. The curve result is not clamped to a degree range in the helper, and branches that select it need an assigned curve.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are calibrated distances, while the curve output is an angle in degrees. The mantle branch is the ledge-pull posture, and the denominator is the calibrated skull reference height.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._t1UpOffsetCurveVelocity
member.summary: The velocity-posture curve that maps normalized height to a upper-spine/chest angle in degrees.

remarks.para: Horizontal curve input is normalized head height: project the world-space head-to-animation-root displacement along the current player-up direction, add spineCrouchOffset and the supplied knee height adjustment, and divide by the avatar's calibrated skull-joint height. Input 1 means that adjusted height equals the reference height; 0.5 means half. It is not a time in seconds.

Vertical curve output is an angle in degrees used as a target contribution to the upper-spine/chest rotation. SolveT1UpOffset selects this curve when foot support exceeds hand support and the leg-relative speed is positive; its blend weight is that speed clamped to 0–1. Here leg-relative speed means horizontal movement speed in meters per second divided by the avatar's total upper-plus-lower leg length in meters, giving leg lengths per second. Its numeric value is clamped for the blend; for example, 0.5 means movement at half a leg length per second. Increasing a key's output adds a larger angle contribution at that height, after blending and smoothing; it does not directly add that many meters of vertical movement. An illustrative key at input 0.5 with output 30 contributes a 30-degree target when this curve is fully selected.

SetAvatar moves the second key's input coordinate for the avatar while preserving its output value. Provide at least two keys; an avatar refresh can overwrite that key's input coordinate and resets its slope settings.

spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are calibrated distances, while the curve output is an angle in degrees. Leg-relative speed is horizontal movement speed divided by combined leg length, in leg-lengths per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._t1UpOffsetLerp
member.summary: The smoothed posture-curve angle currently used by the upper spine solve.

remarks.para: The additive upper spine path moves this toward the corresponding SolveT1UpOffset result using SmoothDamp with a 0.15-second smoothing time. The value is in degrees and feeds an axis-angle rotation together with other lean and posture corrections; it is not a stored vertical distance.

Its paired UpOffsetVel field records the rate used by the smoother. Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity clear both values. A manual change can affect a following solve, but the smoother will continue replacing it toward the calculated target.
The paired UpOffsetVel value is the smoothing rate, and the smoothed value is later consumed as an axis-angle posture correction. Its angle is in degrees; it is not a vertical distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig._t1UpOffsetVel
member.summary: The smoothing rate for the upper spine's posture-curve angle. Related state: .

remarks.para: SmoothDamp receives this by reference while updating _t1UpOffsetLerp and replaces it with the new rate. Because the smoothed quantity is an angle and elapsed time is in seconds, this is degrees per second. It carries momentum between smoothing steps; it is not the physical speed of the spine or a separate target.
Startup, re-enable, and Teleport with zeroVelocity reset the paired angle and rate to zero. Setting the rate alone changes transient smoothing behavior until the next calculation updates it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.body
member.summary: The configured component that calculates stepping-leg animation for this rig.

remarks.para: SLZ_Body owns the locomotion and footstep data used by OnFootSolve. AnimationRig startup calls its OnStart, SetAvatar forwards avatar calibration, and the on-foot solve asks it for foot/ankle poses and a working pelvis offset.

body returns the stored _body reference directly. The reference must point to an already configured component; replacing it alone does not initialize its footstep state or recalibrate it for the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.pelvisLocalAnimOff
member.summary: The current working pelvis position-and-rotation offset produced by the stepping-leg calculation.

remarks.para: SLZ_Body.SolveLegs writes this SimpleTransform through a reference during the on-foot solve. Its position describes a local animation displacement in world-distance units, normally meters, and its rotation is a quaternion, a value that records an orientation. Local here means the stepping coordinate frame of SLZ_Body.locomotion.neutralRoot, the transform used as the reference for its foot calculations. The quaternion records a rotation correction around that frame's axes. The additive pelvis path reads the stored rotation as a posture correction, blending from identity with a factor of 0.5 + 0.5 × the chest-suppression weight.

pelvisLocalAnimOff returns a copy of the same storage as _pelvisLocalAnimOff. OnEarlyUpdate replaces that storage with the identity transform at the end of the pose pass. This is temporary solve output, not an Inspector offset that remains applied across updates; reading it after the outer pass normally sees the reset value.

suppressChestVelocityTwist is a unitless 0–1 weight. The additive rotation uses the identity quaternion as its neutral orientation and the factor 0.5 + 0.5 × weight; neutralRoot supplies the stepping coordinate frame. The field is temporary solve output and is reset at the documented pass boundary.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.spineCrouchOffset
member.summary: Adds a height adjustment to the curve input used to calculate upper-spine and pelvis posture.

remarks.para: This is a distance in world units, normally meters. Both additive spine solves add it to their projected height before dividing by the appropriate avatar height. For an illustrative reference height of 1.6 meters, adding 0.08 meters raises the normalized curve input by 0.05.

It changes which point is sampled on the posture curves; the resulting curve values are angles, so the visible effect depends on the curve shape. The code does not directly move the spine upward by this many meters. Changing it is read on the next relevant solve and is separate from the calculated posture caches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AnimationRig.suppressChestVelocityTwist
member.summary: Temporarily reduces movement-driven chest lean and adjusts the pelvis posture correction while the weight is refreshed.

remarks.para: This is a unitless weight. The public suppressChestVelocityTwist setter clamps it to 0–1 and marks it freshly updated. One chest lean-blend factor includes 1 - 0.5 × weight, so increasing it from 0 to 1 reduces that factor from 1 to 0.5; it is not a switch that stops all torso movement. The pelvis-animation rotation blend also changes from 0.5 to 1 as this weight rises.

HandgunVirtualController and RifleVirtualController refresh the public property while solving aiming. In the on-foot body update, the freshly updated flag first prevents decay for one solve, then an unrefreshed dirty weight loses deltaTime each later solve until it is clamped back to zero when the subtraction would make it negative. For example, an unrefreshed weight of 0.5 falls by about 0.1 over a subsequent 0.1-second solve.

_suppressChestVelocityTwist exposes the raw stored weight; writing it directly bypasses the setter's clamp and freshness flags. Use the public property when requesting the verified temporary-suppression behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.LeftAnimatorHand
member.summary: Returns the left hand’s pose animator, which turns finger input into the reference hand pose copied to the model.

remarks.para: ArtOutputUpdate passes the left hand’s input finger values to this component, solves its pose and applies the result to the reference hand transforms. SetArtOutputAvatar also fits that reference hand to the avatar’s measured hand size.
Reset finds or adds the component on m_handLf and stores it in _leftAnimatorHand. The getter returns that stored reference; it does not find a component each time.

member.returns: The stored left HandPoseAnimator component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig._eyeDamper
member.summary: Controls how much the eye helpers turn toward the gaze target when the avatar uses an eye-center override.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless rotation blend: 0 leaves the eyes at their neutral forward local rotation, 1 applies the full calculated look rotation, and intermediate values reduce the gaze turn. ArtOutputUpdate blends from neutral each frame; this is not a time delay or a smoothing speed.

SetArtOutputAvatar recalculates and clamps the value to 0–1 from the avatar’s camera-to-head and right-eye offsets when both humanoid eye bones and the override are present; otherwise setup assigns 1. Setup replaces a manual value. Without an eye-center override, the inspected update applies the full look rotation directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.armLowerTwistLf
member.summary: Carries the left forearm’s simulated twist into the art rig’s visual pose.

remarks.para: This is an art-rig helper transform. MountRig attaches it to the matching physical forearm frame. Each ArtOutputUpdate copies the corresponding PhysSoftBody part’s local rotation into it, so a calibrated child helper can pass that rotation to the model’s optional twist bone.

remarks.para: ArtOutputUpdate solves carpalLf from the wrist and corrected hand poses, using the avatar’s measured wrist-to-hand segment. This child helper adds the avatar’s arm-orientation correction to that solved bridge.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.artEyeLf
member.summary: Supplies the calibrated rotation that aims the model’s left eye at the physics rig’s gaze target.

remarks.para: ArtOutputUpdate aims eyeLf using eyeGaze and the eye’s measured position relative to the head. This child helper adds the avatar’s saved eye-orientation correction; with an eye-center override the gaze turn can be reduced by _eyeDamper, the neutral-to-look rotation blend.

Late output copies this helper’s world rotation to the humanoid left eye bone when it exists. That output changes the bone’s rotation only. Assign the calibration helper in the eye hierarchy so it follows the posed eye reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.artFingerLf11
member.summary: Supplies the calibrated pose copied to the left index finger’s proximal bone.

remarks.para: The proximal bone is the finger’s base near the palm; the distal bone’s pivot is not the fingertip. This field points to a pose helper in the art hand hierarchy. Late output copies its world position and rotation to the matching left index bone in Avatar.artTransforms.

The reference hand receives its pose from the hand animator, which turns finger input into bone rotations. Avatar setup applies the recorded hand calibration to these offset helpers so that the posed reference hand fits the model. Keep the helper in the matching finger chain; assigning another transform redirects the pose copied to this joint.
Setup also corrects the base helper’s local position using the measured finger-base layout and the fixed reference hand scaled to this avatar’s hand size.

remarks.para: The intermediate bone is the finger’s middle section; the distal bone’s pivot is not the fingertip. This field points to a pose helper in the art hand hierarchy. Late output copies its world position and rotation to the matching right index bone in Avatar.artTransforms.

The reference hand receives its pose from the hand animator, which turns finger input into bone rotations. Avatar setup applies the recorded hand calibration to these offset helpers so that the posed reference hand fits the model. Keep the helper in the matching finger chain; assigning another transform redirects the pose copied to this joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.artShoulderLf
member.summary: Supplies the corrected pose written to the avatar’s left shoulder bone.

remarks.para: This is an intermediate transform in the ArtRig, not the Avatar model’s bone reference. SetArtOutputAvatar applies the model’s stored rotation correction here so a model whose bone axes differ from the physics rig can still face the right way.

MountRig parents this helper under the physics rig’s left clavicle, or collarbone, transform. Setup applies the model’s shoulder position and rotation corrections, so the pose includes the physics shoulder chain and the model’s own bone alignment.

ArtOutputLateUpdate copies this helper’s world position and rotation to the corresponding cached Avatar bone while that avatar GameObject is active. Moving or rotating this helper therefore changes the pose sent to the visible skeleton; editing the visible bone directly can be overwritten on the next output pass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.artThumbLf1
member.summary: Supplies the pose for the left thumb’s base segment, nearest the palm.

remarks.para: This is the ArtRig output helper corresponding to the Avatar’s humanoid thumb Proximal bone. Those names mean base, middle and end segments; the end segment is still a bone, not a separate fingertip marker.

Avatar setup applies the same finger-axis alignment correction to all three thumb helpers, calculated from this hand’s index finger base segment. It also adjusts this base helper’s local position using the avatar’s thumb-base hand measurement minus the scaled reference-hand position. The hand pose system supplies the finger pose, and ArtOutputLateUpdate copies this helper’s world position and rotation to the avatar’s matching thumb bone.

The reference-hand position is the fixed thumb-base displacement used by the rig’s neutral hand layout. Its size is multiplied by handSizeMult, a unitless ratio comparing the avatar’s hand size with that reference hand: 1 is reference size and 2 doubles the reference layout. Subtracting this scaled reference displacement from the measured thumb-base displacement gives the local adjustment in distance units, normally meters.
Use the matching hand and segment when assigning the helper. Model-bone edits made afterward can be overwritten by the next art output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.artToeLf
member.summary: Supplies the corrected world pose written to the avatar’s left toe bone.

remarks.para: This is an intermediate transform in the ArtRig, not the Avatar model’s bone reference. SetArtOutputAvatar applies the model’s stored rotation correction here so a model whose bone axes differ from the physics rig can still face the right way.

The toe helper chain follows toeLf, which is attached to the physics foot and positioned from the avatar’s measured foot-to-toe offset. Setup gives this output helper the model’s toe rotation correction.

ArtOutputLateUpdate copies this helper’s world position and rotation to the corresponding cached Avatar bone while that avatar GameObject is active. Moving or rotating this helper therefore changes the pose sent to the visible skeleton; editing the visible bone directly can be overwritten on the next output pass.
This member drives a skeleton bone. The audited ArtRig code does not use it to find a ground contact or change the foot’s collision shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.carpalLf
member.summary: Receives the calculated left wrist-to-palm transition pose.

remarks.para: Carpal means the wrist-bone region. ArtOutputUpdate calls SolveCarpal using wristLf, the left hand pose shifted by Avatar.palmLfPosOffset, and half of Avatar.carpalLength. The solver places this helper between the wrist and palm and blends their rotations halfway.

Avatar.palmLfPosOffset is a cached alignment correction from the measured palm layout toward the reference palm layout, expressed in the hand’s axes and in distance units, normally meters. ArtOutputUpdate rotates that correction by the current hand-helper rotation and adds it to the hand’s world position. This corrected position is the hand endpoint used by the carpal solver; the hand rotation is retained.

carpalLength is the avatar’s cached wrist-to-hand length, measured from the optional right wrist reference to the right humanoid Hand bone and shared by both sides. It uses distance units, normally meters, and is zero when that optional wrist reference is absent. The wrist-forward and hand-backward projections each use half of this length.

The solver averages the wrist/palm midpoint with one endpoint projected forward from the wrist and another projected backward from the palm. Those projections each use half this shared cached wrist-to-hand length. The result is a world-space pose that allows the wrist region to bend between the forearm and hand.

The artCarpalLf output helper then supplies the pose copied to the avatar’s optional carpal transform. This is a calculated pose destination; it does not point at a collection of physical wrist bones. Its pose is overwritten on updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.eyeLf
member.summary: Receives the left eye’s calculated gaze rotation before it is passed to the avatar.

remarks.para: MountRig parents this helper under the physics head; SetArtOutputAvatar places it at the avatar’s measured head-relative eye position. ArtOutputUpdate constructs a look rotation from PhysicsRig.eyeGaze while accounting for eye spacing, so the two eyes can turn toward the same nearby target.

For avatars with eyeCenterOverride, the desired local rotation is blended from neutral, meaning no extra local rotation relative to the helper’s parent, using _eyeDamper. This unitless blend fraction uses 0 for neutral forward gaze and 1 for the full calculated gaze rotation; values between them reduce how far the eye turns. It does not smooth motion over time. The artEyeLf correction helper then supplies the world rotation copied to the avatar’s optional eye bone.
Assign the ArtRig gaze helper here, not the model’s eye bone. Runtime gaze updates overwrite its local rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.l1Vert
member.summary: Receives the intermediate torso rotation used to fit an avatar’s additional chest joint.

remarks.para: This lower-back helper is initially mounted under the physics spine. SetArtOutputAvatar reparents it under the physics chest for avatars without UpperChest, or under the physics spine for avatars with UpperChest, and sets its neutral position from the avatar’s measured torso segments.

l1Y and WaistY are unitless locations down the sternum-to-hips torso path: 0 is the sternum, or breastbone, and 1 is the hips. l1Y is calculated for the cached Chest landmark; WaistY marks the waist on the same path. They are fractions along that torso span, rather than distances in meters or world-Y coordinates.

Only when hasUpperChest is true, ArtOutputUpdate sets this helper’s world rotation from neighboring physics frames. At or above the waist (l1Y ≤ WaistY), it blends chest toward spine by l1Y / WaistY, limited to 0 through 1. Below the waist, it blends spine toward pelvis by (l1Y − WaistY) / (1 − WaistY), also limited to 0 through 1. A fraction of 0 uses the first rotation, 1 uses the second, and 0.5 lies halfway between them. A zero denominator uses the native zero-fraction fallback.

L1 names the first lumbar, or lower-back, landmark in this rig. Assign the intermediate ArtRig helper, not a measured anatomical bone on the model. Setup replaces its parent and local pose; applicable updates replace its world rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ArtRig.l3Vert
member.summary: Provides a lower-torso positioning helper fitted to the avatar’s measured spine shape.

remarks.para: MountRig parents this helper under PhysicsRig.m_spine. SetArtOutputAvatar combines the avatar’s measured t1Local, l1Local and l3Local torso segments, which together run from Neck to Spine, then subtracts the curved torso reference chain from sternum through underbust and waist to high hips. Sternum is the breastbone at the front of the chest; these named sections mark positions down the torso.

The result is a position offset in the parent spine frame, in world-distance units, normally meters, rather than a vertical height percentage. Setup replaces this local position. The audited ArtOutputUpdate does not independently interpolate this helper’s rotation from l3Y; the dynamic interpolation there uses l1Vert and l1Y.
L3 names the third lumbar, or lower-back, helper landmark. This field points to the ArtRig helper, not directly to a model bone or Rigidbody.

member.summary: Positions the ArtRig’s left toe output relative to the physics foot.

remarks.para: MountRig parents this helper under PhysicsRig.m_footLf. SetArtOutputAvatar assigns its local position from the avatar’s stored toeLfLocal vector, the measured foot-to-toe displacement expressed in the calibrated foot frame.

The saved foot frame points forward along the foot-to-toe direction flattened perpendicular to the avatar’s up direction, with up taken from the avatar’s calibration root. The stored offset still keeps all three distance components, normally in meters; flattening chooses the frame’s forward axis rather than removing the measured vertical displacement.

The artToeLf helper adds the model’s toe-axis correction, and late output copies its world pose to the visible humanoid toe bone. The setup position is a saved avatar measurement; this helper is not a live ground-contact detector. Reconfiguring the avatar can replace its local position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._backLfRb
member.summary: Cached of the rear-left wheel, supplying mass and the engine-audio spin estimate.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object mass and lets physics move and rotate it. Start, Unity's setup call before this component's first frame update, finds this body on the same object as backLf and stores it here. It sets the body's maximum angular velocity to 300 radians per second; one complete turn is about 6.28 radians.

The rear-left body's angular velocity, its spin vector in radians per second, is also compared with the main body's spin to estimate wheel speed for engine audio. This estimate can rise while a wheel spins in the air; it is not the chassis's speed over the ground.

The cache is captured during Start, not looked up again each frame. Changing backLf later does not automatically replace this body reference. Supply a wheel object with both the joint and a Rigidbody before setup; the update expects the cached body to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._lastBackLfPressure
member.summary: Stored rear-left pressure slot that the ATV's own setup and update code leave unchanged.

remarks.para: This is not an automatically refreshed previous-frame contact measurement. The ATV constructor, Start, Update, and UpdateSkid do not read or fill this slot. Reading it therefore returns the stored value, initially zero unless another caller writes it; changing it does not change the contact or sound calculations in those methods.

The update reads the current rear-left sensor directly instead. Its pressureKgs value is a contact load expressed as an equivalent mass in kilograms, calculated from collision impulse, elapsed physics time, and vertical gravity. The ATV does not establish a measurement unit or a sampling time for this separate stored slot.

Its pressureKgs value is a contact load expressed as an equivalent mass in kilograms, calculated from collision impulse, elapsed physics time, and vertical gravity. The ATV does not establish a measurement unit or a sampling time for this separate stored slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._lastNormedSpeed
member.summary: Stores the most recent wheel-spin speed ratio supplied to the engine audio, relative to .

remarks.para: The ratio is n = r * length(a - b) / v. Here r is wheelRadius in metres; a is the cached rear-left wheel body's angular-velocity vector in radians per second; b is the main body's angular-velocity vector in radians per second; length means the size of the whole three-part vector; and v is maxSpeed, the configured full-throttle rolling speed in metres per second. The result n is unitless. With r = 0.32 m, relative spin of 10 rad/s, and v = 8 m/s, n = 0.4.

This measures wheel spin relative to the chassis, including all spin directions, rather than the chassis's forward travel. A spinning wheel can raise it even with little vehicle movement. The saved ratio is not clamped to 1, so it can exceed 1; the sound component clamps its own speed input when choosing audio settings.

Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. On an awake update with a registered rider and _motorRunning already true, the engine sound receives the new ratio and its change rate (new n - saved n) / dt before the new n is saved here. dt is the current frame's scaled game-time duration in seconds; the rate is normalized-speed change per game second, not metres per second squared. Slow motion reduces dt for the same real frame duration. The first update that sets _motorRunning skips this ratio refresh, and sleeping updates leave it unchanged. Exit cleanup resets it to zero when stopping a tracked motor or clearing a nonzero saved throttle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._lastThrottleSet
member.summary: Remembers the last processed throttle written to the two rear-wheel spin targets.

remarks.para: This is a unitless value from -1 to 1: positive and negative values request opposite wheel-spin directions, and zero requests no driven spin. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. It is saved after both rear joints receive their target velocities during Update; it is not a measurement of force, actual wheel speed, or a separate physics-frame sample.

A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. That rider's right thumbstick supplies unitless sideways input x and forward/back input y. The code first forms u = y + sign(y) * (1 - abs(x)) * (x*x + y*y), clamps u into -1 to 1, then saves t = sign(u) * u*u here. Here t is the shaped throttle made from the registered rider's right thumbstick: x is sideways and y is forward/back, and the ATV reshapes the pair into a unitless value from -1 to 1. Forward input along y gives positive t; a neutral stick gives 0. sign chooses -1 for a negative number and +1 otherwise; abs means size without the sign. For example, x = 0 and y = 0.5 produce u = 0.75 and t = 0.5625. The extra shaping makes the response different from copying y directly.

If the seat has no registered rider and this saved value is nonzero, the next awake update sets both rear spin targets to zero and clears this value and the saved normalized audio-speed value. Updates while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody is sleeping leave the saved throttle untouched.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._mapSkid
member.summary: Keeps the audio player that starts, moves, fades, and stops the ATV's single tire-contact sound loop.

remarks.para: Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled, and UpdateSkid is this component's routine for starting, moving, fading, or stopping the shared loop. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. The constructor creates this ManagedAudioPlayer, a helper that owns a sound source and its playback settings. Update chooses the wheel with the greatest skidMag, its relative contact-point speed in metres per second, then passes that wheel's pressurePoint and normalized load to this player through UpdateSkid. pressurePoint is the strongest-impulse world contact point shifted by the wheel Rigidbody's movement since Unity's FixedUpdate physics-step callback last saved its position. All wheels share this one player rather than having one loop each.

The sound starts when q = s * p is greater than 0.1, where s is the selected wheel's skidMag in metres per second and p = 4 * L / M is a unitless load multiplier. L is that wheel's kilogram-equivalent contact load and M is the sum, in kilograms, of the masses of mainBody, frontAxle, steeringWheel, and the four cached wheel Rigidbodies. The rider's stored avatar mass (RigManager._avatar._massTotal) is added only when driverSeat has a valid registered Seat._rig, the player's RigManager (the object holding their controls and avatar), and that rig has a valid avatar reference. With no registered rider, the calculations use vehicle mass alone. A registered rider must have an avatar reference; if it is missing, this update fails before calculating the load. When starting a stopped player, the code requests the skidPavement clip as a loop at the ATV object's local origin. Later playing updates adjust its volume and pitch and move its local position toward the selected contact point, converted from world coordinates into the ATV object's own coordinates.

While the loop plays, target volume is clamp(q*q*0.01, 0, 1), where clamp means limiting a result to that range. Volume moves toward that target by at most 4 * dt per update; when q is 0.1 or smaller, it fades toward zero by at most 6 * dt and stops after reaching zero. dt is the frame's scaled game-time duration in seconds, so slow motion makes those fades advance more slowly per real second. The source-position blend uses 2 * dt each update rather than an exact arrival deadline. Pitch depends on contact speed and the game's time scale. When mainBody's chassis Rigidbody is sleeping, Update stops a playing skid loop immediately and returns before sensor, input, motor, or material work; this branch does not use the volume fade described above.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._motorRunning
member.summary: Tracks whether the ATV has entered its motor-audio state for a registered rider.

remarks.para: Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. During an awake update, when a valid registered rider is stored, the ATV sets _motorRunning true, requests StartMotor on its sound component, and then applies inSeatMaterial to the chosen collider. This happens once while the flag remains true, even if the current throttle is zero. It tracks that transition; it does not check that an audio clip successfully started or that a physical engine is producing force.

When an awake update finds no registered rider and _motorRunning is true, it calls StopMotor, clears _motorRunning, and then applies outOfSeatMaterial. A sleeping mainBody chassis Rigidbody skips these rider checks and retains the flag. Writing the flag yourself does not immediately start or stop sound or apply a material; it changes which branch a later update takes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv._steeringHinge
member.summary: Stores the physics joint created to connect the steering-wheel body to the front axle.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a connection whose settings restrict movement between two physics bodies. Start, Unity's setup call before the first update, adds this joint to the assigned steering-wheel object when that wheel exists. It disables automatic connected-anchor placement, uses the wheel object's local up direction as its primary axis and local right as its secondary axis, and connects it to frontAxle with the connected anchor at the axle object's local origin.

For setup, the steering-wheel object is briefly rotated to match the front axle and then restored to its saved world rotation. The code locks the joint's angular X motion, which is rotation about the joint's primary axis. It does not make that axis a freely turning hinge. The ATV Update does not read the steering-wheel angle or write a steering target through this stored joint.

This reference is created once during Start. Replacing it later does not recreate the connection or reapply the setup; replacing steeringWheel or frontAxle does not automatically reconnect the joint already created.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.backLf
member.summary: Identifies the rear-left wheel's physics joint and receives its requested drive speed.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection whose settings control which movements and rotations are allowed and which targets its motor tries to reach. Assign the joint on the actual wheel object, with a Rigidbody and a Collider, the shape that detects contact.

During Start, Unity's setup call before the first update, the ATV caches the Rigidbody on this joint's object, sets its maximum spin to 300 radians per second, and sets that object's collider contact offset to 0.005 metres, or 5 millimetres. The contact offset is the small separation at which physics begins preparing contacts; it is not the wheel radius.

Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. While a registered rider is assigned, Update writes this joint's targetAngularVelocity as (w, 0, 0), where w = -t * maxSpeed / wheelRadius. Here t is the shaped throttle made from the registered rider's right thumbstick: x is sideways and y is forward/back, and the ATV reshapes the pair into a unitless value from -1 to 1. Forward input along y gives positive t; a neutral stick gives 0. maxSpeed is the configured full-throttle rolling speed in metres per second, wheelRadius is the wheel radius in metres, and w is the requested spin in radians per second. The X direction follows the joint's target-coordinate settings. The joint's configured drive and the physics contacts determine how much of that request is achieved.

When the seat has no registered rider and the saved throttle was nonzero, the update resets both rear joints' spin targets to zero. This requests no driven spin; it does not instantly remove existing wheel momentum. Set maxSpeed and wheelRadius to positive values before driving, since the calculation divides by wheelRadius.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.backLfStaySensor
member.summary: Supplies rear-left wheel contact load, relative contact speed, and sound position to the ATV.

remarks.para: Assign the CollisionStaySensor belonging to this wheel. It gathers physics contact information. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. When that Rigidbody is awake, the ATV calls this sensor's UpdateSensor along with the other three before reading results. Sensor results refresh only when physics time has advanced; calling it again in the same physics step retains the published values.

pressureKgs is a kilogram-equivalent contact load: the size of the accumulated contact impulse divided by the elapsed physics seconds and the magnitude of gravity's vertical acceleration. An impulse is force added up over time, measured in newton-seconds. The result is a load expressed as an equivalent mass in kilograms, not pressure in pascals or a raw force in newtons. skidMag is the size of the measured velocity at the contact relative to the contacted body's motion, in metres per second; pressurePoint is the world position of the strongest-impulse contact, shifted by the wheel sensor Rigidbody's movement since Unity's FixedUpdate physics-step callback last saved that body's position. The sensor measures wheel velocity at the shifted point and subtracts the contacted body's point velocity at the original contact point. If the contacted Collider has no Rigidbody, its velocity is treated as zero, so skidMag counts it as standing still.

The ATV compares all four skidMag values and picks the greatest. It passes that wheel's contact point and load to the single skid-sound player. The load multiplier is p = 4 * L / M, where L is this selected wheel's pressureKgs in kilograms and M is the sum, in kilograms, of the masses of mainBody, frontAxle, steeringWheel, and the four cached wheel Rigidbodies. The rider's stored avatar mass (RigManager._avatar._massTotal) is added only when driverSeat has a valid registered Seat._rig, the player's RigManager (the object holding their controls and avatar), and that rig has a valid avatar reference. With no registered rider, the calculations use vehicle mass alone. A registered rider must have an avatar reference; if it is missing, this update fails before calculating the load. This multiplier is unitless. For example, L = 50 kg with M = 200 kg gives p = 1. The four loads also contribute to the engine-audio load estimate.

The sensor measures contacts with other objects; this component does not require a pavement material or filter its reads using isGrounded. Assign all four sensors even if one wheel is currently off the ground.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.colliderToMaterialSwap
member.summary: Chooses the contact shape that receives or on a motor-audio state transition.

remarks.para: A Collider is an object's shape for detecting physical contact. The assigned shape receives inSeatMaterial on the transition into the registered-rider motor-audio state and outOfSeatMaterial on the transition out. A physics material controls friction and bouncing. Only this chosen collider's sharedMaterial reference is replaced; the component does not swap every wheel's material.

Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. The start sequence sets _motorRunning true, requests the start sound, then applies the in-seat material. The stop sequence requests the stop sound, clears _motorRunning, then applies the out-of-seat material. These sequences run during awake Update callbacks and use seat registration rather than a fully-seated test. Simply replacing this collider field or one of the material references does not immediately perform a swap. Assign a valid collider before those transitions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.driverSeat
member.summary: Selects the whose registered rider supplies the ATV's throttle input and motor-audio state.

remarks.para: A registered rider here is the player's RigManager, the object grouping the rider's controls, avatar and body, stored in this Seat's _rig reference. Register assigns it during seat entry and DeRegister clears it. The ATV checks this registered RigManager. It does not require the seat's seatedPercent to reach 1 or test its fully-seated flag. Registration can begin during seat entry, so a registered rider can already supply input before the seating blend finishes.

Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. In an awake update, a valid registration leads to the rider's controller rig and right controller's thumbstick. Its sideways and forward/back axes are reshaped into a signed, unitless throttle from -1 to 1, and both rear-wheel joints receive the requested spin speed. Registration also starts the tracked engine-audio state and applies the configured in-seat material on that transition.

When the seat's registration is cleared, a later awake update stops the tracked engine audio and applies the out-of-seat material. If the saved throttle was nonzero, it also resets both rear-wheel spin targets and the saved throttle/speed values. The assigned Seat, controller chain and avatar must exist for the corresponding reads; assigning an empty seat is different from leaving driverSeat null.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.frontAxle
member.summary: Supplies the front axle's physics body for the steering-wheel connection and vehicle mass calculation.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object mass and lets physics move it. During Start, Unity's setup call before the first frame update, an assigned steering wheel receives a new physics joint connected to this axle body. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. Each awake vehicle update includes this body's mass, in kilograms, in the total counted vehicle mass. That total weights the contact load and audio calculations. The ATV's own Update does not apply a steering torque or build suspension forces on this reference. Assign the axle body before setup; replacing it afterward does not reconnect the existing steering-wheel joint.
