member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.mainBody
member.summary: Provides the chassis sleep state, mass, and rotation reference for the ATV's control and sound update.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives the chassis physical mass and motion. Update first checks whether this body is sleeping, meaning physics considers it at rest and has suspended its simulation work. While it sleeps, the ATV stops an active skid sound and skips its sensor, rider, wheel-target, engine-audio and material updates. The saved throttle, speed ratio, and motor flag can therefore remain unchanged until an awake update.

While awake, this body's mass in kilograms contributes to the counted vehicle mass. Its angular velocity, the three-part spin vector in radians per second, is subtracted from the rear-left wheel body's angular velocity to estimate relative wheel spin for engine audio. Its orientation also supplies the coordinate conversion used during that estimate.

The ATV's own Update sends throttle spin targets to the two rear-wheel joints. It does not directly add a throttle force or steering torque to this chassis body. Assign a valid main body before the component runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.maxSpeed
member.summary: Sets the rolling-speed scale for full-throttle rear-wheel targets and engine-audio speed normalization.

remarks.para: Measured in metres per second. A registered rider here is the player's RigManager stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can register it before the player is fully seated. With t as the shaped throttle made from the registered rider's right thumbstick (sideways x and forward/back y reshaped into -1 to 1; forward y gives positive t and a neutral stick gives 0), and wheelRadius r in metres, the rear joint's requested X spin is w = -t * maxSpeed / r radians per second; its other two target components are zero. One full turn is about 6.28 radians. For example, maxSpeed = 8 m/s, r = 0.32 m, and t = 1 give w = -25 rad/s. The joint's target-coordinate settings choose how its X direction is interpreted.

This is a requested wheel-speed scale, not a hard cap on the chassis's forward motion. Slipping, airborne wheels, slopes, outside pushes, and the joint's configured drive can make actual movement differ. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. Changing maxSpeed is picked up on the next eligible awake update, without resizing any wheel.

Engine audio also divides the estimated rear-left relative wheel speed by maxSpeed. That estimate is wheelRadius multiplied by the size of the wheel's spin relative to chassis spin; it is not measured chassis travel. Supply a positive maxSpeed and wheelRadius: these calculations divide by them, and the code does not repair zero or negative settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.motorSfx
member.summary: Receives engine start, stop, and changing wheel-speed/load information for the ATV's motor sounds.

remarks.para: Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. In an awake update, a registered rider starts the tracked motor-audio state: the ATV sets _motorRunning true, calls this component's StartMotor, and then applies the in-seat material. A later awake update with no registered rider calls StopMotor before clearing _motorRunning and applying the out-of-seat material. The calls request configured audio; they do not start or stop a separate physical engine or prove that a clip played.

After the initial start transition, UpdateMotor receives three values. Speed is the unitless ratio of estimated rear-left wheel rolling speed to maxSpeed, the configured speed scale in metres per second. The estimate uses wheel radius in metres times relative wheel/chassis spin in radians per second. Acceleration is the change in that ratio divided by the frame's scaled game-time duration in seconds, giving normalized-speed change per game second rather than physical acceleration in metres per second squared. Load is the sum of the four sensors' kilogram-equivalent contact loads divided by M, a unitless ratio. M is the sum, in kilograms, of the masses of mainBody, frontAxle, steeringWheel, and the four cached wheel Rigidbodies. The rider's stored avatar mass (RigManager._avatar._massTotal) is added only when driverSeat has a valid registered Seat._rig, the player's RigManager (the object holding their controls and avatar), and that rig has a valid avatar reference. With no registered rider, the calculations use vehicle mass alone. A registered rider must have an avatar reference; if it is missing, this update fails before calculating the load.

The sound component clamps its own speed input into 0 to 1 and uses it to choose idle or moving sounds and adjust volume, pitch and audible distance. Load distinguishes loaded and unloaded audio, and the speed-change rate affects acceleration/deceleration audio. Pitch also responds to the game's time scale, so slow motion can lower it. Updates while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody is sleeping skip these engine-audio calls. Assign an initialized MotorSFX component before driving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.outOfSeatMaterial
member.summary: assigned to when the tracked motor-audio state stops for the assigned .

remarks.para: A PhysicMaterial sets how a Collider, an object's contact shape, responds to friction and bouncing. These effects come from the material's configured values and the other contacting surface; the field itself is an asset reference rather than a friction number.

Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. A registered rider is the player's RigManager (the object holding that player's control and avatar references) stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can store it before the rider is fully seated. An awake update with no registered driver calls StopMotor while _motorRunning is true, clears _motorRunning, and then assigns this material as colliderToMaterialSwap's sharedMaterial. The component does not apply it just because an initially empty seat has never started the motor state.

Changing this reference does not immediately change the collider. It is read again on the corresponding state transition; inSeatMaterial is used for the opposite transition. Updates while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody is sleeping skip the rider and material checks. The material swap does not reset existing wheel momentum.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.skidPavement
member.summary: Provides the sound clip requested when the ATV starts its tire-contact loop.

remarks.para: The clip is read when the shared skid-sound player is stopped and weighted contact speed exceeds its threshold. Weighted speed is s * p: s is the greatest wheel-sensor skidMag in metres per second, and p is that wheel's kilogram-equivalent contact load divided by one quarter of M. M is the sum, in kilograms, of the masses of mainBody, frontAxle, steeringWheel, and the four cached wheel Rigidbodies. The rider's stored avatar mass (RigManager._avatar._massTotal) is added only when driverSeat has a valid registered Seat._rig, the player's RigManager (the object holding their controls and avatar), and that rig has a valid avatar reference. With no registered rider, the calculations use vehicle mass alone. A registered rider must have an avatar reference; if it is missing, this update fails before calculating the load. The threshold is strictly greater than 0.1; equality belongs to the fade/stop branch.

Despite the name, the ATV does not check that the contacted surface is pavement or select clips by surface material. The configured clip can be requested for qualifying contacts with any surface the sensors report. Playback starts as a loop at the ATV object's local origin; subsequent playing updates adjust its volume/pitch and move its source toward the chosen contact point.

Replacing this reference while the loop already plays does not immediately replace its clip. It is read again the next time the stopped player starts a loop. Assign a playable clip and keep the shared skid player initialized.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.steeringWheel
member.summary: Identifies the steering-wheel physics body for a connection created during vehicle setup.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's physical mass-and-motion component. If this wheel exists during Start, the setup call before the first update, the ATV adds a ConfigurableJoint, a physics connection, to its object and connects it to the assigned front axle. The wheel is briefly given the axle's world rotation while the joint is configured, then restored to its original world rotation.

The joint's primary axis follows the wheel object's local up direction and its secondary axis follows local right. Setup locks rotation about the joint's primary axis. The ATV script contains no code that reads this wheel's angle to request steering or applies steering torque to the chassis. The wheel is physically joined to frontAxle by the setup joint; any steering effect depends on how surrounding joints are configured, which these Atv methods do not establish.

A registered rider here is the player's RigManager stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can register it before the player is fully seated. The update counts this body's mass in kilograms alongside the chassis, axle, four cached wheel bodies, and that rider's stored avatar mass. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. Although Start can return without creating a joint when the wheel is missing, the awake update still expects this body for its mass calculation. Replacing it after Start does not rebuild the existing joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Atv.wheelRadius
member.summary: Converts between requested rolling speed and wheel spin, and between relative wheel spin and the engine-audio speed estimate.

remarks.para: The configured radius is measured in metres; the constructor starts it at 0.32 m. A wheel's radius is the distance from its centre to its outer surface, half its diameter. This number is used in calculations and does not resize the wheel's Collider, its physical contact shape, or its visible model.

A registered rider here is the player's RigManager stored in driverSeat's Seat._rig reference; seat entry can register it before the player is fully seated. The two rear joints receive requested X spin w = -t * v / r radians per second, where t is the shaped throttle made from the registered rider's right thumbstick (sideways x and forward/back y reshaped into -1 to 1; forward y gives positive t and a neutral stick gives 0), v is maxSpeed in metres per second, and r is this radius in metres. At v = 8 m/s, r = 0.32 m and t = 1, w = -25 rad/s. The target's X direction follows the joint's target-coordinate settings, and the actual spin depends on its drive and contacts.

For engine audio, estimated rolling speed is r * length(a - b), where a and b are the rear-left wheel and chassis angular-velocity vectors in radians per second and length means vector size. The result is metres per second and can be nonzero while the wheel spins without much ground travel. Set r to match the real wheel radius and keep it positive; a larger radius requests less spin for the same rolling-speed setting. Update is Unity's callback once per frame while this component is enabled. Here, an awake update means Update ran while mainBody's chassis Rigidbody was not sleeping; Unity can put a nearly still Rigidbody to sleep to reduce physics work. Changes are read in eligible awake updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.ambMus
member.summary: The sound-playing component whose clip, volume and playback are changed by this fade controller.

remarks.para: Assign an AudioSource before using the fade methods. FadeIn replaces its sound clip and starts playback; AttenuateCurrent adjusts its volume and can start a stopped source; FadeOut and UpdateFade can stop it. This entry controls one source, while Audio2dManager combines several entries for overlapping ambience or music transitions.
Replacing this reference during a fade makes subsequent UpdateFade calls act on the new source using the already stored target and speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.clip
member.summary: Remembers the sound clip most recently supplied to FadeIn.

remarks.para: FadeIn stores the clip here and also assigns it to ambMus, the AudioSource component that plays the sound. Changing this stored reference by itself does not change the source's clip. FadeOut retains it, so this value does not prove that the sound is still playing; inspect the source for live playback state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.fadePerSec
member.summary: Sets how quickly UpdateFade moves the source volume toward its target, in volume units per real second.

remarks.para: Source volume normally runs from 0 for silence to 1 for full source volume. A speed of 0.2 changes it by 0.2 per second, so a difference of 0.6 takes about 3 seconds of frame updates. UpdateFade chooses the direction from the target, so this speed should be nonnegative.

AttenuateCurrent replaces the speed with the absolute target-to-current volume difference divided by its positive duration. FadeIn uses the larger of 0.04 and target volume divided by its positive duration. FadeOut uses the larger of 0.04 and the previous requested target divided by its positive duration. These methods overwrite a manually chosen speed when starting their gradual fades. Changing this field alone does not set isFading.
During some music transitions, Audio2dManager multiplies an entry’s stored fade speed by 3.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.fadeTarget
member.summary: The requested source volume that UpdateFade moves toward.

remarks.para: For ordinary source volume, 0 means silence and 1 means full source volume; it is not a decibel value or a playback-progress fraction. For example, a target of 0.25 requests one quarter of the source's volume setting, without promising one quarter of perceived loudness.

AttenuateCurrent limits its target argument to 0 through 1. FadeIn ultimately stores its supplied target without retaining its preliminary clamp, so callers should supply a value in that range. FadeOut sets this target to zero. Assigning this field alone does not change current volume, calculate a new speed, or set isFading; it redirects later UpdateFade calls using the stored speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AmbAndMusic.isFading
member.summary: Tells Audio2dManager to keep advancing this entry's fade each frame.

remarks.para: The gradual fade methods set this flag to true; their immediate paths clear it. UpdateFade clears it after the source volume approximately reaches fadeTarget, before stopping playback if that volume is zero or lower.

This is a fade-update flag, not a test of whether a clip is playing. Clearing it pauses the manager's volume updates without stopping the sound. Setting it alone does not choose a target or speed, and a direct call to UpdateFade ignores the flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._curAmb
member.summary: Selects which ambience entry receives same-clip volume changes and acts as the outgoing entry for the next cue.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based index into ambAndMusics. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, starts it at 0. New ambience clips rotate the selected index through 0, 1, 2 and back to 0 so the old source can fade out as the next fades in. Older sources can still be audible, so this index is not a list of all playing ambience.
Changing the index by itself does not start a sound. Later cue calls inspect the selected source and can use it as the outgoing source; keep the normal indices and populated entries intact.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._curMus
member.summary: Selects the music entry inspected by music cues and StopMusic.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based index into ambAndMusics. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, starts it at 3. New music clips rotate through entries 3, 4, 5 and back to 3, allowing the previous source to fade out while the next starts. An older source can remain audible during that transition.
Changing the index alone does not play a track; it redirects later cue, stop and intro-to-loop operations to a different source. Keep the normal music indices and assigned entries intact.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._isOverride
member.summary: Makes regular music requests update the saved cue instead of replacing override playback.

remarks.para: CueOverrideMusic sets this flag before starting its special music cue. StopOverrideMusic and the timed-release sequence clear it before trying to restore regular music. It describes control state, not whether an override source is actually playing.

While true, CueMusic remembers regular settings and returns without applying them. StopMusic clears the remembered regular clips rather than stopping the override. Changing this field alone does not start or stop a source or schedule restoration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._loopPending
member.summary: Identifies the sequence waiting to switch a music intro into its looping clip.

remarks.para: This coroutine is work Unity pauses and resumes across frames. The intro cue stores its handle here after starting it. It waits for the intro length minus the requested transition fade, in real seconds, then reads the selected source’s current volume and calls ordinary CueMusic with the loop clip, that volume, looping enabled, and both fade times set to the transition fade. It clears this handle after that call.

Cancellation has separate gates. CueMusicLoopWithIntro rejects a timestamp older than _timecodeMusic before saving its cue fields. The timestamped ordinary CueMusic overload saves its regular-cue fields first, then calls CueMusicInternal only when override is off. There, an older timestamp returns before the single-clip cancellation check. During override, ordinary CueMusic saves the cue fields and skips both the internal timestamp check and cancellation check. These timestamps order requests; the overloads that generate their own timestamp use real seconds since startup. With override off, CueMusicInternal cancels _loopPending only after the selected source’s clip differs; a same-clip request returns unchanged or only adjusts volume. CueMusicLoopWithIntro has a separate two-clip check: override returns before it; with override off, a matching intro or loop clip returns or adjusts volume without cancelling, and cancellation occurs only when both differ. An accepted non-override StopMusic request also cancels the routine. During override, StopMusic clears the remembered regular clips and returns without stopping this pending routine.

At handoff, ordinary CueMusic saves loop-only regular-cue settings: the loop clip, no intro, the handoff volume, and the transition fade for both fade times; it also clears the cached intro-transition fade. If override is still active, that wrapper skips CueMusicInternal, so the handoff updates the remembered cue and clears _loopPending without starting loop playback then. With override off, the handoff can start the loop. Assigning null by itself loses the stored handle without cancelling the running sequence; only the accepted cancellation branches described above cancel this coroutine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overrideCallback
member.summary: Stores the timed-release sequence most recently created for an override music cue; see .

remarks.para: A coroutine is code that Unity pauses and resumes across frames. CueOverrideMusic assigns and starts this sequence when timed release is requested. It waits in real time, clears override control, then attempts to restore the saved regular cue. A stored reference does not prove the sequence is still running: normal completion does not clear this field.

StopOverrideMusic stops the stored sequence and clears this reference when an override is active. Starting another timed override overwrites the field without first stopping the older sequence, so the field does not account for every sequence that could still be running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenFadeInTime
member.summary: Remembers the requested fade-in time of the regular music cue to restore after an override.

remarks.para: This is in real seconds. A restored single clip uses it to change source volume toward the saved target; an intro cue uses it while starting the intro. Source fades advance per rendered frame. Changing this cache affects later restoration, without changing a fade already in progress.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenFadeOutTime
member.summary: Remembers the requested outgoing-source fade time for restoring regular music after an override.

remarks.para: This is in real seconds. Restoration passes it as the outgoing music source's fade-out request. The underlying fade calculates speed from that source's previous target volume, with a minimum speed, so this is not a guarantee of the exact elapsed fade time. Editing the cache affects later restoration.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenHasIntro
member.summary: Chooses whether override release restores a single regular clip or a regular intro followed by a loop.

remarks.para: CueMusic clears this flag; CueMusicLoopWithIntro sets it. False selects the saved single clip. True selects the intro-plus-loop path, which requires both saved clips to be available. The automatic intro-to-loop handoff calls ordinary CueMusic, so it writes this flag false before override gating and leaves only the loop clip for later restoration. Changing it alone does not start or stop music.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenLoop
member.summary: Remembers whether the saved single regular music clip should repeat when restored.

remarks.para: A true value requests repeating playback for the restored single clip; false requests one pass. CueMusic stores its loop argument here, and the intro-plus-loop cue sets it true. The intro restoration path uses its own intro-then-loop behavior. Editing this cache does not change a source's currently applied loop setting.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenLoopTransitionFade
member.summary: Remembers the requested overlap time between a saved regular music intro and its looping clip.

remarks.para: This is in real seconds. When restoring an intro cue, the manager starts its loop after intro length minus this transition time, then requests this duration for the incoming and outgoing source fades. For a 10-second intro and a 2-second transition, the loop request begins after about 8 real seconds. Frames and the fade-speed calculation affect exact timing. A single-clip CueMusic clears this cache to zero, and the automatic intro-to-loop handoff does the same before the ordinary CueMusic call is gated by override mode.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenMusicClip
member.summary: Remembers the regular music clip to restore when override control is released.

remarks.para: For a single-clip cue this is that clip; for an intro-plus-loop cue this is the looping clip. Regular requests can update it while override music continues. It is not the override clip or a test of current playback. StopMusic clears it while an override is active, preventing ordinary restoration from that saved cue.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenMusicIntro
member.summary: Remembers the intro belonging to the regular intro-plus-loop cue that can be restored after an override.

remarks.para: CueMusicLoopWithIntro stores the intro here. A single-clip CueMusic clears it. Restoration needs this intro and the saved looping clip to be available. Before the automatic intro-to-loop handoff, restoring that cue can begin its intro again; when the handoff calls ordinary CueMusic, it clears this cache and leaves only the loop clip. This cache does not track how far playback had progressed. StopMusic clears it while an override is active.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._overridenTargetVol
member.summary: Remembers the source-volume target for regular music restored after an override.

remarks.para: Ordinary source volume is a linear setting from 0 for silence to 1 for full source volume; it is not a decibel value. Restoration passes this value into the saved cue's volume fade. For example, 0.25 requests one quarter of the source volume setting, without guaranteeing one quarter of perceived loudness. Editing this cache does not immediately change an existing source's volume.
These settings belong to the regular cue saved by CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro. Override release reads them later; a new regular cue can overwrite them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._timecodeAmbience
member.summary: Stores the ordering timestamp against which ambience requests are checked.

remarks.para: This is a request-order number, normally real seconds since startup from the overloads that generate their own timestamp. A request strictly below this stored value is ignored; an equal value is accepted. Supplying a future timestamp can suppress later automatically timestamped requests until real time catches up. It is not a playback position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager._timecodeMusic
member.summary: Stores the ordering timestamp against which music requests are checked.

remarks.para: This is a request-order number, normally real seconds since startup from the overloads that generate their own timestamp. A request strictly below this stored value is ignored; an equal value is accepted. Supplying a future timestamp can suppress later automatically timestamped requests until real time catches up. It is not a playback position.

The regular single-clip CueMusic method saves the restoration settings before the internal timestamp check, and skips that internal call during override control. Therefore this timestamp does not prove that every remembered regular cue passed the ordering check. Accepted StopMusic requests also update it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.ambAndMusics
member.summary: Holds the six sound-source fade controllers used for overlapping ambience and music cues.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, replaces this array with six new entries and child AudioSource components, which play sounds. Indices 0 through 2 handle ambience; 3 through 5 handle music. Sources begin in 2D mode, with looping on and automatic startup playback off. Music cue methods can later change looping.

Cue transitions rotate within each group of three, allowing one source to start while others fade out. Update advances every entry whose isFading flag is true. Replacing the array later does not create sources or reroute them; keep at least the six expected, fully assigned entries for the manager's fixed-index operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.fadeRoutine
member.summary: Stores the handle for the mixer's reverb-transition sequence.

remarks.para: A coroutine handle identifies work Unity continues over several frames. FadeToNewReverb stops the old stored sequence before starting and recording a new one. StopFadeRoutine cancels it and clears this field. The sequence's normal completion does not clear the handle, so a non-null value does not prove a fade is still running.
This handle does not control ambience or music source-volume fades. Assigning null alone does not stop the running sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.minFadeTime
member.summary: Sets the minimum game-time duration chosen for a new reverb transition.

remarks.para: The duration is in game seconds: slow motion increases the corresponding real time. For example, a 0.35-game-second fade takes about 0.7 real seconds at half game speed while frame updates continue.

FadeToNewReverb uses this value directly when the new fourth reverb entry, normally the DecayTime setting in seconds, is smaller than its captured current value. Otherwise it uses the increase in that setting, limited to 5 seconds and raised to this minimum. A minimum above 5 seconds takes precedence. The constructor initializes this field to 0.35; changing it affects later transitions, not the duration already captured by a running sequence. Supply a positive value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.mixer
member.summary: The audio mixer whose exposed reverb values this manager reads and blends.

remarks.para: An audio mixer combines sound channels and applies effects. LoadMixers selects the configured asset and assigns output groups to the ambience and music sources after loading completes. Reverb fades read and write named parameters on this mixer.
Changing this reference alone does not reassign existing sources' output groups. A running reverb sequence reads the field on each frame, so replacing it redirects subsequent reverb parameter writes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.prevReverbObj
member.summary: Remembers the preset reference that was replaced by the latest FadeToNewReverb call.

remarks.para: The call copies the old reverbObj here before assigning its new target. This is a preset reference, not a snapshot of mixer values. The fade itself begins from tempData, the captured current mixer values, so interrupting a transition does not make it restart from this older preset.
The inspected FadeToNewReverb and full reverb sequence do not use this field to calculate the blend. Editing it therefore does not redirect those calculations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.reverbObj
member.summary: Supplies the named reverb parameter targets for the current mixer transition; see .

remarks.para: Reverb is the lingering reflected sound that helps a space sound like a room or hall. FadeToNewReverb assigns this preset and captures current mixer values before starting the transition. The frame sequence reads this preset's names and values each frame; it is the destination, not proof that the mixer has already reached it.

Changing this reference during a fade can redirect later writes, but does not recapture the starting values or choose a new duration. Use FadeToNewReverb to begin a transition with a fresh capture. Keep the preset's parameter order and count aligned with tempData.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dManager.tempData
member.summary: Stores the mixer values captured as the starting point of a new reverb transition; see .

remarks.para: The constructor allocates 14 floats. FadeToNewReverb reads the current mixer value for each parameter named by the destination preset and stores it at the matching index. Values retain each parameter's units; this is not an array of volume fractions.

The frame sequence blends from these saved values toward reverbObj's targets. Changing an element during a running fade changes that parameter's starting value for later frames, which can cause a jump. The fourth captured value also helps choose the duration when a fade starts. Keep the array and preset entries aligned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio2dPlugin.Audio2dManager
member.summary: Provides the shared background ambience and music manager created by the audio plugin.

remarks.para: Before a level loads, the plugin checks whether its stored manager still exists. If it does not, it creates a GameObject, an object in the Unity scene, and attaches the Audio2dManager script to it as a component. The plugin marks that object to survive scene changes and reuses the same manager for later levels.

The getter returns the stored reference but never creates a manager. It may be null before the plugin's first level-load callback, the routine the level-loading system invokes before a new level loads. A manager reference does not guarantee that the separate asynchronous mixer loading, work that can finish later, has completed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio3dManager.ambience
member.summary: Provides the mixer channel for ambient background sounds.

remarks.para: A mixer channel routes a sound through that channel's volume controls and audio effects. Pass this group as mixerGroup to a playback method to select the Ambience channel. Choosing a group does not play a clip or change which clip was selected.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio3dManager.audio_Master
member.summary: Stores a slider-style master input, then attempts updates to the three exposed mixer parameters.

remarks.para: The input is a slider-style number, not a direct volume multiplier. An exposed mixer parameter is a named mixer setting that scripts can update. The code passes 90 × sqrt(input / 10) − 80 to the corresponding exposed parameter: input 0 passes −80, 2.5 passes −35, and 10 passes +10. The number's unit and audible effect depend on how the mixer asset configures that exposed parameter. If it is a group-volume control, these values are decibels and a greater nonnegative input requests a louder level; we have not inspected the mixer asset to see how it uses this setting.

The manager initializes this stored input to 8, but loading saved player settings can replace it. The getter returns the stored input, not a measurement of the mixer's current output. sqrt means square root. The code does not clamp input to 0 through 10; a negative input does not produce an ordinary real square root.

Setting any of the three properties stores its own input, then attempts to update all three exposed parameters named channel_Master, channel_Music, and channel_SFX from their stored inputs. It ignores each AudioMixer.SetFloat success result and returns no acceptance status. The runtime settings and loaded mixer asset must be available, and each parameter name must be exposed for its write to take effect. These are mixer-parameter requests, not per-source volume settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.Audio3dPlugin.Audio3dManager
member.summary: Provides the shared for mixer channels and reusable sound playback.

remarks.para: Before a level loads, the plugin creates this manager if its stored reference is missing or destroyed, and marks its object to survive scene changes. A live existing manager is reused.

The getter returns the stored reference without creating it. It can be unavailable before the plugin's first level-load callback, the routine invoked by the loading system. Obtaining the reference does not prove that asynchronous mixer loading, work that can finish later, has completed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.Cache
member.summary: Provides the shared lookup from Unity scene objects (GameObjects) to their registered components.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity scene object this component is attached to. The getter creates an empty component cache, a lookup table, if none exists yet. Each player registers itself in Awake, Unity's initialization callback, and removes itself when destroyed. Audio3dManager uses this table to find the AudioPlayer on a sound object returned by a spawn request.
Cache membership is not a list of sounds currently playing. Pool deinitialization stops playback and clears the clip without removing the component from this lookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared object-to-audio-player lookup table used by Cache.

remarks.para: Cache creates and stores a new table when this reference is null. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, registers each player; OnDestroy removes it and clears this reference when the table becomes empty. Pool deinitialization does not remove the registration.
Replacing or clearing this field alone does not re-register existing players. Use Cache to obtain the shared lookup; its entries describe registered components, rather than live playback state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultDopplerLevel
member.summary: Saves the source's Doppler-effect strength for later pool initialization.

remarks.para: Doppler is the pitch shift heard when a sound source and listener move toward or away from each other. This is a unitless strength setting: 0 disables that shift, while 1 requests its normal strength. It is captured from the source during Awake, Unity's initialization callback, and written back by OnPoolInitialize.
Changing the saved value affects that later restoration; it does not immediately change the source's current Doppler setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultLoop
member.summary: Saves whether the source should repeat its clip when playback does not supply a loop choice.

remarks.para: True requests repeating playback; false requests one pass. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures this setting from the source. OnPoolInitialize restores it, and both Play overloads use it when isLooping is omitted.
Changing this saved value alone does not change whether the current clip repeats; a later pool initialization or Play call applies it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultMinDistance
member.summary: Saves the near-source distance setting used when playback or attenuation omits a distance.

remarks.para: This distance is measured in meters from the AudioSource, the component that plays sound, to the Audio Listener, the scene component that receives it. Within it, the source does not get louder as the listener moves closer (for example, a 2-meter minimum distance). Farther away, how the volume fades depends on the source's rolloff setting (its distance-to-volume curve) and spatialBlend (how much 3D audio processing affects the sound).

Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures it from the source. OnPoolInitialize restores it; Play and Attenuate use it when minDistance is omitted. Editing this saved value does not immediately change the live source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultMixerGroup
member.summary: Saves the mixer channel used when a Play call does not supply a group.

remarks.para: A mixer group routes sound through shared volume controls and effects. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures the source's current group. OnPoolInitialize restores it, and Play chooses it when mixerGroup is missing or points to a destroyed Unity object.

Changing this saved reference does not reroute a source immediately. It affects later pool initialization or playback calls using the fallback. The group does not by itself choose a clip or make the sound positional.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultPitch
member.summary: Saves the source pitch restored during pool initialization.

remarks.para: Pitch is a unitless playback ratio: 1 is the clip's normal pitch and speed, and 0.5 requests half-speed playback with a lower pitch. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures the source's pitch; OnPoolInitialize writes this saved value back. Editing it affects that later restoration.

Play and Attenuate use _defaultVolume instead of this saved pitch when their pitch argument is omitted. Changing _defaultPitch therefore does not change that fallback; supply pitch explicitly when you need a particular playback ratio.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultSpatialBlend
member.summary: Saves the source's 2D-to-3D mix restored during pool initialization.

remarks.para: This unitless setting runs from 0 for 2D sound without position-based placement to 1 for fully 3D sound; intermediate values combine them. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures it, and OnPoolInitialize restores it. Editing the saved value alone does not change the source immediately.
Both Play overloads use a fixed 0.98 when spatialBlend is omitted, rather than this saved value. SetSpatialBlend changes the live source but does not update this saved pool setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._defaultVolume
member.summary: Saves the source-volume fallback, which also becomes the pitch fallback when pitch is omitted.

remarks.para: Source volume is a unitless gain setting: 0 is silent and 1 is full source volume. It is separate from mixer-channel decibels and does not guarantee a proportional change in perceived loudness. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures the source value; OnPoolInitialize restores it.

Play and Attenuate use this value when volume is omitted. They also use it when pitch is omitted, where it becomes a playback ratio. For example, a saved volume of 0.5 produces pitch 0.5 if no pitch is supplied. Editing the cache affects later fallback uses, rather than immediately changing the current source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._hasStartedPlaying
member.summary: Enables the per-frame pool-return check after a Play request.

remarks.para: For a single clip, Play sets this flag before stopping the old source, assigning the new clip and calling Play on the source. The array overload sets it after confirming the array is nonempty, but still before source setup. This records a request, rather than confirmed successful playback.

Update uses this flag when game timeScale is positive and the object is active, and requests pool return when the source reports not playing. Pool deinitialization clears the clip before clearing the flag. Stop leaves the flag set, allowing that later check. Clearing the flag manually prevents this normal automatic return without stopping the sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._highPitchRange
member.summary: Declares a pitch ratio of 1.12, with no playback-control role found in the inspected methods.

remarks.para: Pitch ratios compare playback speed and pitch with the original clip: 1 is normal. Passing 1.12 explicitly as a pitch would request 12% faster, higher-pitched playback. The declaration itself does not make AudioPlayer choose that pitch.

The complete AudioPlayer Play overloads and Attenuate do not use this constant to choose a random pitch. The inspected Audio3dManager world-point playback wrapper instead randomizes from the caller's pitchRng argument, a half-width around the requested pitch. These observations cover the listed playback methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._lowPitchRange
member.summary: Declares a pitch ratio of 0.88, with no playback-control role found in the inspected methods.

remarks.para: Pitch ratios compare playback speed and pitch with the original clip: 1 is normal. Passing 0.88 explicitly as a pitch would request 12% slower, lower-pitched playback. The declaration itself does not make AudioPlayer choose that pitch.

The complete AudioPlayer Play overloads and Attenuate do not use this constant to choose a random pitch. The inspected Audio3dManager world-point playback wrapper instead randomizes from the caller's pitchRng argument, a half-width around the requested pitch. These observations cover the listed playback methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer._source
member.summary: Assigns the sound-playing component used for this player's playback and pool lifecycle.

remarks.para: An AudioSource plays the clip and holds its volume, pitch, looping, distance and mixer settings. Assign it before Awake, Unity's initialization callback, because that routine captures its settings as the defaults for pool reuse. The source property returns this same component.

Replacing this reference later directs subsequent player operations to the new source, while the saved defaults still come from the earlier capture. Pool initialization can therefore apply the old source's settings to the replacement. A source reference by itself does not confirm that a clip is playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.AudioPlayer.source
member.summary: Returns the assigned component that plays this player's sound.

remarks.para: Play, Stop, Attenuate and pool callbacks act on this AudioSource. The getter simply returns _source and does not find or create a source. Editing the returned component changes its live settings without updating the defaults captured during Awake, Unity's initialization callback.

Later Play calls or pool initialization can overwrite those edits. Missing Play or Attenuate pitch uses the saved volume as a pitch ratio; missing Play spatial blend uses 0.98 instead of the saved spatial blend. Inspect this source's actual playback state to learn whether a sound is currently playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.runConcrete
member.summary: The default clip bank randomly sampled by for movement values of 4 or more.

remarks.para: This array is selected when runOverride is absent or destroyed. A live runOverride replaces the entire bank with its audioClips array. Supply a nonempty array of playable clips; there is no empty-bank fallback.

The concrete name describes the intended sounds. PlayStep does not test the floor material. Changing this array changes the choices for the next running call, without changing a clip already playing or the movement-based volume and pitch calculations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.runOverride
member.summary: Replaces the default running clip bank used by .

remarks.para: For a supplied movement value of 4 or more, an existing override asset supplies its audioClips array instead of runConcrete. AudioVarianceData is an asset holding a list of sound clips here; it does not provide volume or pitch variation settings. Random selection and the movement-based volume calculation still happen in PlayStep.

The override is checked on each call, so replacing it affects later steps. An absent or destroyed asset selects runConcrete; an existing asset with a null or empty clip array causes an error instead of trying that default bank.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.volumeMult
member.summary: Multiplies the volume calculated for each newly requested footstep.

remarks.para: This is a unitless multiplier applied when PlayStep sets the AudioSource volume. A value of 0 requests silence, 0.5 halves the calculated source volume, and 1 leaves it unchanged. It does not change pitch, the chosen clip bank, or a source's volume immediately when the field is edited.

Let x be the caller's movement value, m be volumeMult, and clamp01(y) mean limiting y to 0 through 1. The requested volume is m × (0.05 + 0.65 × clamp01(x / 4)) for x below 4, or m × (0.3 + 0.5 × clamp01((x - 4) / 50)) for x of 4 or more. These are unitless source-volume values, not decibels or a promise of perceived loudness. For example, x = 2 and m = 0.5 request volume 0.1875. PlayStep applies no separate clamp to m.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.walkConcrete
member.summary: The default clip bank randomly sampled by for movement values below 4.

remarks.para: This array is selected when walkOverride is absent or destroyed. A live walkOverride replaces the entire bank with its audioClips array. Supply a nonempty array of playable clips; there is no empty-bank fallback.

The concrete name describes the intended sounds. PlayStep does not test the floor material. Changing this array changes the choices for the next walking call, without changing a clip already playing or the movement-based volume and pitch calculations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.FootstepSFX.walkOverride
member.summary: Replaces the default walking clip bank used by .

remarks.para: For a supplied movement value below 4, an existing override asset supplies its audioClips array instead of walkConcrete. AudioVarianceData is an asset holding a list of sound clips here; it does not provide volume or pitch variation settings. Random selection and the movement-based volume calculation still happen in PlayStep.

The override is checked on each call, so replacing it affects later steps. An absent or destroyed asset selects walkConcrete; an existing asset with a null or empty clip array causes an error instead of trying that default bank.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._Id
member.summary: Remembers the pool ID of the player adopted by the latest completed spawn.

remarks.para: A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

Spawn completion records this ID before requesting playback. Stop, property access and reuse checks compare it with the player's current ID. A mismatch makes the wrapper treat the reference as stale; this number is a pool identity value, not a clip time, array index or Unity object instance number. Stop does not clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._ap
member.summary: Stores the pooled AudioPlayer that this wrapper most recently adopted.

remarks.para: A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

After successful spawn adoption, this reference supplies the source for playback, volume, pitch, distance, movement and Stop. It can remain stored after stopping or pool return. Check the ID as well as the reference before treating it as the currently owned sound object. Replacing this field alone does not update _Id or apply the stored settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._apIncoming
member.summary: Marks a pending spawn request that may still be adopted when it finishes.

remarks.para: A playback routine sets this flag before starting a spawn when no matching player is available. While it remains true, further requests update the stored settings instead of starting another spawn. The finishing routine checks it before adopting the returned object, then clears it after Play, or after the random sample-position assignment in a loop variant.

Stop clears the flag before stopping an existing matching source. This is request state, not proof that an object already exists or sound has started. If no matching player exists, isPlaying reports this flag and the editable properties expose the pending settings. The flag is shared by requests; it does not identify a particular spawn operation or cancel the pool task.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._clip
member.summary: Stores the sound clip selected for the latest playback request.

remarks.para: The playback routines save their selected clip here, and a spawn reads it after its wait before calling AudioPlayer.Play. A newer request during that wait can therefore replace the clip the incoming player receives.

The clip property returns this stored reference while a matching player or pending request exists; it does not read the live AudioSource's clip or prove that playback is active. Editing _clip alone does not replace a clip already assigned to that source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._localPosition
member.summary: Stores the requested sound position: relative to for local playback, or in world coordinates for world playback.

remarks.para: Local playback stores coordinates relative to _parent: X is its right direction, Y its up direction and Z its forward direction. At parent scale 1, one unit is one meter; parent rotation and scale change the world placement. World-point playback also uses this field, but stores meters along the world axes and clears _parent.

Local spawning converts the stored point to world coordinates before the wait, then reapplies the latest local point after attaching the completed object. World spawning takes the point before the wait and does not reapply later changes. The localPosition property can move a matching live source, but a direct edit to this backing field only changes stored coordinates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._looping
member.summary: Stores whether the next applied playback request should repeat the clip.

remarks.para: One-shot playback routines write false; loop routines write true. Spawn completion reads this flag after its wait and passes it to AudioPlayer.Play: true repeats the clip, false plays one pass. A newer request while spawning can change that eventual choice.
Editing this field alone does not change a live source's loop setting. The loop spawn variants also jump to a random sample position, but still read this stored flag rather than forcing it to true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._minDistance
member.summary: Stores the near-distance reference in meters exposed by while a matching player or pending request exists.

remarks.para: This distance is measured from the source to the audio listener. For the source's ordinary distance falloff, it sets the near region before volume starts decreasing; it is not a maximum hearing distance. For example, 2 means a two-meter near-distance reference. The audible result also depends on spatial blend, the source's falloff settings and mixer controls.

Playback routines overwrite this stored value with the settings of the latest request, and spawn completion reads it after its wait. The public minDistance property returns this cache while a matching player or pending request exists, otherwise it returns 0. A direct edit to this backing field changes only stored data; it does not call the live source setter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._mixerGroup
member.summary: Stores the audio channel requested for the sound when playback is applied.

remarks.para: An audio mixer group routes sound through shared effects and volume controls. Playback routines store the requested group; the spawn routines read it after the wait and pass it to AudioPlayer.Play. A null or destroyed supplied group makes AudioPlayer use its startup default group.

Editing this field alone does not reroute a live source. A later playback request or spawn adoption applies it. Mixer routing is separate from spatial blend, which controls how strongly position affects the sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._parent
member.summary: Stores the Transform that local playback will attach its sound object to.

remarks.para: A Transform holds position, rotation and scale. The local point is measured from this parent using its own axes, so the attached sound follows the parent as it moves. Local spawning requires a parent to convert the point to world coordinates before its wait, then uses the current stored parent again when adopting the object.
World-point playback clears this field and detaches the source. Editing _parent alone does not reattach an already managed source; local playback or local spawn adoption performs that change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._pitch
member.summary: Stores the final playback-speed and pitch ratio exposed by while a matching player or pending request exists.

remarks.para: Pitch is a unitless playback-speed ratio: 1 is normal, 0.5 plays at half speed with lower pitch, and 2 plays at twice the speed with higher pitch.

Playback routines overwrite this stored value with the settings of the latest request, and spawn completion reads it after its wait. The public pitch property returns this cache while a matching player or pending request exists, otherwise it returns 0. A direct edit to this backing field changes only stored data; it does not call the live source setter.

For ordinary single-clip playback and loop requests, the stored ratio is p × (0.25 + 0.75 × t), where p is the chosen input pitch ratio and t is Unity's unitless game time scale at the request. Optional pitch variation can first choose p randomly. Thus p = 1 and t = 0.5 store 0.625. The adjustment is captured at the call, not updated continuously as time scale changes. The overloads with alternate slow-motion clip banks use their own adjustment when those clips are selected. Direct pitch-property assignments store the supplied ratio without time-scale adjustment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._spatialBlend
member.summary: Stores how much position should affect the next applied sound, from 0 for 2D to 1 for fully 3D.

remarks.para: This is a unitless mix: 0 uses nonpositional playback, 1 uses positional panning and the source's distance behavior, and intermediate values combine those modes. The common playback-call default is 0.98, mostly positional.

Playback routines save the value, and spawn completion passes the current stored value to AudioPlayer.Play after the wait. Editing the field alone does not change a live source. It does not change mixer routing or the sound object's coordinates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._timecode
member.summary: Does not control the playback position in the inspected ManagedAudioPlayer playback and spawn routines.

remarks.para: Those complete routines do not read or write this stored float. Editing it therefore does not seek the sound through these paths. This observation covers the class's playback methods, property accessors and four spawn routines; it does not establish that every possible external caller ignores the field.

The loop paths instead choose a random integer sample frame and assign it directly to AudioSource.timeSamples after Play. A sample frame is one time position across all channels. Its time in seconds is n / f, where n is the frame index and f is the clip's sampling frequency in frames per second. For example, 24,000 / 48,000 is 0.5 seconds. The unused float has no verified unit in these paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer._volume
member.summary: Stores the source-volume level exposed by while a matching player or pending request exists.

remarks.para: Volume is a unitless source level: 0 requests silence, 0.5 is half the source level and 1 is the ordinary full level. It is not decibels or a guarantee of perceived loudness.

Playback routines overwrite this stored value with the settings of the latest request, and spawn completion reads it after its wait. The public volume property returns this cache while a matching player or pending request exists, otherwise it returns 0. A direct edit to this backing field changes only stored data; it does not call the live source setter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.clip
member.summary: Returns the stored requested clip while a matching player or a pending spawn exists.

remarks.para: A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

Otherwise this getter returns null. It reads _clip, not the live AudioSource.clip. It can therefore expose a clip during spawning, after Stop while the same player ID still matches, or after an external source edit. Use isPlaying for the separate playback/request check; a non-null clip alone does not mean sound is audible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.isPlaying
member.summary: Reports the matching source's playback flag, or a pending spawn when no matching player exists.

remarks.para: A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

If a matching player exists, the getter returns its AudioSource.isPlaying flag. Otherwise it returns _apIncoming. A pending request can therefore produce true before any clip begins. When an old matching source exists, its own playback flag takes priority over the pending flag.

This is not a test of whether the player hears sound: source volume can be zero, mixer controls can mute it, and positional sound may be far from the listener. Stop clears the pending flag and stops a matching source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.localPosition
member.summary: Reads stored coordinates and can move a matching source; local playback measures them relative to .

remarks.para: A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

The getter returns the stored vector while a matching player or pending request exists, otherwise (0, 0, 0). It does not read the live Transform position. The setter moves a matching source using Transform.localPosition and updates the stored vector; with only a pending spawn it stores the vector; with neither it ignores the change.

A Transform holds position, rotation and scale. For local playback, coordinates use the parent's right, up and forward axes. At parent scale 1, (0, 1, 0) places the source one meter above the parent; rotation and scale affect its world placement. World-point playback detaches the source, so its local coordinates are then world coordinates in meters. The setter uses the source's actual current parent rather than reattaching it to the stored _parent.

A local spawn applies the latest stored local point after its wait. A world spawn has already submitted its point before the wait and does not reapply later stored edits, so a pending setter change is not guaranteed to move that world spawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.ManagedAudioPlayer.minDistance
member.summary: The requested near-distance reference for positional sound, in meters.

remarks.para: This distance is measured from the source to the audio listener. For the source's ordinary distance falloff, it sets the near region before volume starts decreasing; it is not a maximum hearing distance. For example, 2 means a two-meter near-distance reference. The audible result also depends on spatial blend, the source's falloff settings and mixer controls.

A matching player means that _ap still exists and its current pool ID equals the stored _Id. A pool reuses sound objects for later requests, so a reference alone does not prove that it still belongs to this wrapper.

The getter returns the stored _minDistance value, rather than reading the live source. With no matching player and no pending spawn, it returns 0. The setter applies the value to a matching source and stores it; with only a pending spawn, it stores it for that completion. With neither, the setter ignores the change.

A later playback call supplies and stores its own settings, so this property is not a permanent default for all future calls. Directly editing the live AudioSource can make it differ from this cached getter.

remarks.para: Pitch is a unitless playback-speed ratio: 1 is normal, 0.5 plays at half speed with lower pitch, and 2 plays at twice the speed with higher pitch.

Setting this property applies the supplied ratio directly. The single-clip playback and loop calls adjust their initial pitch for game time scale before storing it, so the cached ratio can already include that adjustment. This property does not apply that adjustment again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.AmbientMixerGroup
member.summary: Routes ambience through the mixer channel assigned to entries 0 and 1 during initialization.

remarks.para: An audio mixer group is a channel for shared volume controls and effects. Awake assigns this reference to those AudioSources when the array has at least four entries. The clips then play through that route; it does not select a clip or control the crossfade by itself.
Changing this field after setup does not automatically update the sources' assigned groups. Edit their output groups separately if an already prepared source needs a new route.

remarks.para: An audio mixer group is a channel for shared volume controls and effects. Awake assigns this reference to those AudioSources when the array has at least four entries. The clips then play through that route; it does not select a clip or control the crossfade by itself.
