member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._curAmb
member.summary: Selects the ambience entry being treated as current by cue and stop operations.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based array index into ambAndMusics, not a clip ID or a count. Awake starts it at 0. The normal ambience pair is entries 0 and 1. CueAmbience fades the current slot out and switches to the other slot when it needs a different clip.

The new index is stored before the incoming clip is faded in. During a crossfade, the previous slot may still be audible, so current does not mean it is the only playing source. Changing this number alone does not move clips or start a fade; an invalid index can make later array access fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._curMus
member.summary: Selects the music entry being treated as current by cue and stop operations.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based array index into ambAndMusics, not a clip ID or a count. Awake starts it at 2. The normal music pair is entries 2 and 3. CueMusic and CueMusicLoopWithIntro fades the current slot out and switches to the other slot when it needs a different clip.

The new index is stored before the incoming clip is faded in. During a crossfade, the previous slot may still be audible, so current does not mean it is the only playing source. Changing this number alone does not move clips or start a fade; an invalid index can make later array access fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._isOverride
member.summary: Makes ordinary music cues save a restoration request instead of changing the current music.

remarks.para: While true, CueMusic and CueMusicLoopWithIntro write the saved regular-music fields and return. StopMusic clears the saved main and intro clips instead of fading the currently playing override. Ambience cues do not use this gate.

CueOverrideMusic first requests music through CueMusic, optionally starts its release coroutine, then sets this flag true. StopOverrideMusic and the timed release clear it before attempting the saved regular-music cue. Clearing the flag alone does not stop a source or restore a clip; those later operations must also run.
A true flag describes the override mode, not proof that a clip successfully started or is audible. Releasing with no valid saved clip clears the mode without necessarily stopping the current music.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._loopPending
member.summary: Stores the started coroutine waiting to change an intro into its repeating music clip.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume across frames. CueMusicLoopWithIntro stores this handle after starting a wait of introLength - transitionFade real-time seconds. Here introLength is the intro clip's length in seconds and transitionFade is the overlap duration in seconds. For a 10-second intro and a 2-second overlap, the loop cue is requested after an approximately 8-second real-time wait, on a resumed frame. This wait is unaffected by game time scale.

On resuming, the routine samples the current music source volume and calls ordinary CueMusic with that volume, equal fade-in and fade-out transition durations, and looping enabled; it then clears this handle. A different music cue or non-override StopMusic can stop the stored routine and clear it. While override mode is active, StopMusic only clears the saved regular clips and returns, so it does not stop this pending routine. That call replaces the deferred regular request with the loop clip alone only if override mode is still active at handoff; if override mode has ended, CueMusic cues live playback and leaves the saved fields unchanged. Setting this field directly does not start or stop a routine.

If override mode is active when the wait finishes, the cue can become a saved regular-music request instead of immediate playback. The actual volume fades use scaled game time, even though this wait uses real time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overrideCallback
member.summary: Stores the resumable routine that releases a timed music override.

remarks.para: This IEnumerator is a routine object whose steps Unity runs as a coroutine across frames. CueOverrideMusic creates it when timed release is requested, with releaseTime = clipLength - fadeOutTime. clipLength is the supplied clip's length in seconds and fadeOutTime is the supplied fade-out duration in seconds. The routine waits until its starting scaled game time plus releaseTime is reached, then clears override mode before requesting any valid saved regular music.

This deadline uses scaled game seconds, so pause or slow motion delays release in real time. For a 10-second clip and a 2-second fade-out setting, release is due after 8 scaled game seconds, checked on a coroutine frame. Playback pitch and whether the source is actually playing are not used to calculate that deadline.

StopOverrideMusic stops this stored routine and clears the field. Normal completion does not clear the field, so a non-null reference alone does not prove that the routine is still running. Editing the field does not itself schedule the routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenFadeInTime
member.summary: Stores the fade-in duration for the saved regular-music request, in scaled game seconds.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

It is recorded by a regular cue during override mode and passed back to the restored cue. A positive duration prepares a gradual source-volume change; zero or a negative duration requests immediate volume application. For example, 2 means a nominal two-game-second fade-in, evaluated frame by frame. Editing it changes future restoration, not the fade already running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenFadeOutTime
member.summary: Stores the fade-out duration for the saved regular-music restoration, in scaled game seconds.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

The restoration cue uses it to fade out the music slot being replaced. A positive duration fades its current volume toward zero; zero or a negative duration stops that outgoing source immediately. It is not the timed override release deadline. Editing it does not change a fade rate already calculated.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenHasIntro
member.summary: Selects whether the saved regular-music request restores a plain clip or an intro followed by a loop.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

During override mode, CueMusic writes false and clears the saved intro; CueMusicLoopWithIntro writes true and saves both clips. False selects plain CueMusic when the saved main clip exists. True requires both saved main and intro clips for the intro-and-loop restoration. If this handoff resumes while override mode is still active, CueMusic writes false and clears the saved intro, so only the loop clip is remembered. If override mode has ended, the handoff cues live music and leaves this saved field unchanged. This bit records the requested form; it does not test whether an intro has finished playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenLoop
member.summary: Stores whether the saved regular-music request should repeat after restoration.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

CueMusic saves its requested loop value. CueMusicLoopWithIntro saves true. A plain restoration passes this setting to the source: true repeats the clip, false plays one pass. With an intro request, the intro is requested as one pass and the later loop cue repeats. Editing this stored bit alone does not change the current source's loop setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenLoopTransitionFade
member.summary: Stores the intro-to-loop overlap duration for the saved regular-music request, in seconds.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

When requested during override mode, an intro request saves this value and a plain request clears it to 0. Restoration passes it to the intro path. If the intro length is L seconds and this overlap is F seconds, the loop coroutine requests its cue after L - F real-time seconds. That cue uses F scaled game seconds for both outgoing and incoming volume fades. For example, L = 10 and F = 2 wait about 8 real seconds, then request two-game-second fades. The automatic handoff clears this value to 0 only if override mode is still active when the wait ends; otherwise it cues live playback and leaves this cached value unchanged. These clocks differ when game time scale is changed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenMusicClip
member.summary: Stores the main regular-music clip requested during an override for later restoration.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

A plain request stores its clip; an intro-and-loop request stores the loop clip here and the intro separately. Release only attempts restoration when the necessary clips exist. StopMusic during an override clears this reference and the intro instead of stopping the override. Changing this field does not replace a live AudioSource clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenMusicIntro
member.summary: Stores the intro clip for the regular music requested during an override.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

When requested during override mode, CueMusicLoopWithIntro saves this clip and the main loop clip; ordinary CueMusic clears this reference and selects the plain-clip mode. An intro restoration requires both saved clips and the flag to select intro mode. The automatic handoff clears this reference only if override mode is still active when the wait ends; otherwise live playback changes and this cached intro remains. StopMusic during override mode clears both. This is not automatically a snapshot of the clip that was playing before the override began.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX._overridenTargetVol
member.summary: Stores the requested source-volume target for regular music restored after an override.

remarks.para: Despite the overriden name, this belongs to the saved regular-music request made while _isOverride is true. It does not describe the override clip currently playing. CueMusic or CueMusicLoopWithIntro records it instead of changing playback. When the override is released, the restoration path reads these saved settings to request that regular music.

The value is a unitless source-volume level: 0 requests silence, 0.5 is half the source level and 1 is the ordinary full level. It is not decibels or a promise of perceived loudness. The restored cue uses it to set up a volume fade or immediate application. Editing the saved value does not attenuate the currently playing override.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.ambAndMusics
member.summary: Holds the two ambience slots and two music slots used to crossfade between clips.

remarks.para: Entries 0 and 1 are the ambience pair; entries 2 and 3 are the music pair. Each AmbAndMusic entry holds an AudioSource, assigned clip, fade flag, target volume and fade rate. An AudioSource is Unity's component for playing sound clips. A new clip can fade in on one source while the previous source fades out on the other.

The constructor allocates four empty entry references, so valid entries must be supplied before Awake prepares their sources. At least four entries are needed for both pairs. Update visits all entries, including extras, but ordinary cues still use the fixed pairs. Array replacement after Awake does not automatically prepare sources or reroute their mixer groups.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.fadeRoutine
member.summary: Stores the handle of the started reverb transition so it can be stopped or replaced.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can resume over several frames; this handle identifies the started transition. FadeToNewReverb stops any previous stored handle, captures current mixer parameters, starts the new transition and saves its handle. StopFadeRoutine stops it and then clears the field.

The transition changes mixer reverb parameters, not the music or ambience sources' volume-fade flags. Normal coroutine completion leaves this field stored, so non-null does not guarantee ongoing work. Editing the handle alone does not start or stop the routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.minFadeTime
member.summary: Sets the minimum nominal reverb transition duration, in scaled game seconds.

remarks.para: The constructor sets 0.35 seconds. This applies to mixer reverb transitions, not the music and ambience source-volume fades.

Let C be the captured current DecayTime and T the new target DecayTime, both in seconds; DecayTime describes how long the reverb tail persists. Let m be minFadeTime in seconds. If C is greater than T, the chosen duration D is m. Otherwise D is the larger of m and the smaller of the absolute difference |C - T| and 5 seconds. For example, changing C = 1 to T = 3 uses D = 2 with the default m = 0.35; changing C = 3 to T = 1 uses D = 0.35.

The routine uses scaled game time, so pause suspends progress and slow motion lengthens the real-time wait. D is calculated when the transition starts; editing m later does not change that running deadline. Completion occurs on resumed frames, not at an exact wall-clock instant.

Keep this value positive. The setup does not validate it independently. If the resulting duration is zero, the time-mapping helper produces progress 0, so the coroutine can keep yielding without reaching its completion condition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.mixer
member.summary: Supplies the audio mixer whose exposed reverb parameters are captured and changed by transitions.

remarks.para: An audio mixer combines sound routes and applies shared effects. FadeToNewReverb reads exposed parameters by the new preset's names, saves their starting values in tempData, and the reverb coroutine writes interpolated values back to this mixer. Assign a valid mixer with the required exposed parameter names before requesting the transition.

This reference is separate from the source routing groups applied in Awake. Changing mixer alone does not reroute music sources or copy a preset into them. During a running transition the routine reads this current reference again, so replacing it redirects later writes while retaining the old captured starting values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.prevReverbObj
member.summary: Remembers the preset reference that was the target before the latest reverb request.

remarks.para: FadeToNewReverb copies the old reverbObj reference here before assigning the new target. It is a preset reference, not a snapshot of the mixer's actual current parameter values. During an interrupted transition, those actual values can lie between presets.

The inspected transition uses tempData, captured from the mixer, as its starting values; it does not blend from prevReverbObj or restore it when stopped. Editing this field alone has no mixer effect through these inspected transition routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.reverbObj
member.summary: Holds the target reverb preset whose named parameter values the transition moves toward.

remarks.para: Reverb is the lingering reflected sound that makes a room sound spacious or enclosed. FadeToNewReverb stores the requested AudioReverbData asset here, captures current mixer values by its parameter names, and starts a gradual transition. Assign a valid preset with the parameter layout expected by the 14-value starting buffer; the fourth entry is DecayTime in the standard layout and helps choose the duration.

The coroutine reads this current preset's names and target values on each step while retaining the starting buffer and deadline captured at setup. Directly changing this field during a fade changes later targets without taking a new snapshot; assigning it while idle does not start a transition. Use FadeToNewReverb when the new target should be applied with fresh setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Audio.MusicAmbience2dSFX.tempData
member.summary: Stores the mixer parameter values captured at the start of a reverb transition.

remarks.para: The constructor allocates 14 float slots. FadeToNewReverb fills them from the mixer using the new preset's parameter names and matching array order. These are starting values, not target values or a copy of prevReverbObj. Each slot keeps its parameter's own unit; this array has no single common unit. In the standard preset, index 3 is DecayTime in seconds.

For each named parameter, the coroutine writes A + (B - A) × p, where A is its captured value from this buffer, B is its current target value from reverbObj, and p is elapsed scaled game time divided by the chosen duration, limited to 0 through 1. A and B use that parameter's unit; p is unitless. Halfway through, p = 0.5 gives the midpoint between A and B.

The buffer must match the preset's array length and order for this capture-and-apply path. Changing a stored slot during a transition changes its later starting value; it does not recapture the mixer. Stopping the routine leaves the buffer stored and the mixer at its last written values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip._physRig
member.summary: The avatar physics rig whose torso colliders and body-shape measurements provide this grip's contact surface.

remarks.para: A collider is the invisible shape the physics system uses to check contacts and collisions.

Assign the PhysicsRig belonging to the avatar this grip should follow. ValidateGripScore searches the relevant colliders on its PhysTorso, while chest, spine, and pelvis hover targets also use the rig's Avatar measurements to follow the shaped torso surface.
AvatarGrip's Awake and Start do not find or assign this reference. The contact calculation requires the assigned rig and the body colliders used by the chosen bodyRb mode.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip._targetColliders
member.summary: A saved mesh-collider list that the inspected AvatarGrip contact methods do not use.

remarks.para: A mesh collider is an invisible physics contact shape made from a mesh.

ValidateGripScore chooses colliders from _physRig.torso according to bodyRb. OnHandHoverUpdate uses its saved contact data and the avatar's body measurements. Neither method reads this array, so adding colliders here does not extend those contact searches.
The inherited Grip.Start separately gathers Collider components on this GameObject into gripColliders. That automatic list is a different field; it is not populated from _targetColliders.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip.bodyRb
member.summary: Chooses the body region and nearby torso colliders used to calculate the hand's contact point for this grip.

remarks.para: A collider is the invisible shape used for physics contacts. The hand target is the desired position and rotation that the physical hand tries to reach.

Head and Neck both use the torso's head mesh collider in this implementation. Chest considers the chest and upper-spine colliders. Spine considers upper spine, lower spine, pelvis, and chest. Pelvis considers the pelvis and lower-spine colliders. The calculation compares nearby surface points to choose the contact it will use.

Chest, Spine, and Pelvis also choose different conversions between body-relative contact coordinates and the shaped avatar torso. Body-relative coordinates express the saved contact relative to that body part; hover updates can rebuild the target in the scene as the body moves. They use those coordinates to place and orient the hand target on the surface. The constructor initially selects Pelvis.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AvatarGrip.genericHandStates
member.summary: Runtime contact records kept separately for each hand while this grip chooses and updates its hand target.

remarks.para: A hand target is the position and rotation the game wants the physical hand to reach. Body-relative coordinates are measured relative to the body; world-space coordinates place the result in the scene.

ValidateGripScore creates a record when it first assesses a hand and saves the chosen surface point and outward direction. These are body-relative contact data, not the final hand pose in world space. Torso modes adjust them using the avatar's measured body offsets.

OnHandHoverUpdate reuses the record to build a world-space position and rotation for the hand target. For the shaped torso paths, it also caches the maximum soft-surface displacement length in meters calculated by the shape helper; this is generated data, not a softness setting. Attached-hand updates and joint-configuration updates require that hand to have a record in this dictionary.
The constructor creates the empty dictionary; contact validation fills and refreshes it during use. Treat its entries as generated state rather than authored grab-point settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BallisticPassthrough.Normal
member.summary: Gets this object’s forward direction in scene coordinates, used to decide which surface hits can pass through.

remarks.para: This is the Transform’s positive Z direction, the blue forward axis, after the object’s rotation is applied. A Transform stores a scene object’s position and rotation. The returned vector is normalized, meaning its length is 1: it describes a direction and has no distance unit. Scene coordinates use the axes of the whole level, rather than axes fixed to the object.

The getter reads the current direction each time, so rotating the object changes the result immediately. It does not store or return the surface normal from the latest bullet hit. A hit’s surface normal is the direction perpendicular to the particular face that was struck.

When isPassthrough is false, the hit test compares that face’s normal with this forward direction. It allows passthrough only when their dot product, the sum of their matching X, Y and Z components multiplied together, is greater than zero. In plain terms, the face normal must point partly forward; an exactly sideways or backward normal fails. When isPassthrough is true, the direction test is bypassed.

For example, if this forward direction is (0, 0, 1), a face normal of (0, 0, 1) passes, while (0, 0, -1) and (1, 0, 0) do not. These are illustrative directions, not a required orientation for every object.

member.returns: The object’s current normalized forward direction, expressed in the whole scene’s axes; this is not the struck face’s normal.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BallisticPassthrough.isPassthrough
member.summary: When true, permits projectile-hit skipping regardless of which way the struck face points; false keeps the directional test.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape. Projectile checks for this component on the collider’s own GameObject, the Unity scene object carrying that shape and its components. True makes the passthrough test accept that hit without comparing directions. It is a stored input read when the hit is evaluated, rather than a report of what the last projectile did.

False does not turn passthrough off completely. A hit can still be skipped when its surface normal, the direction perpendicular to the struck face, points partly along this object’s forward positive Z axis. Both directions use the whole scene’s coordinates. Their dot product must be greater than zero: matching directions pass, opposite directions fail, and an exactly sideways face gives zero and fails. Rotating the object changes this directional behavior.

For a hit accepted by the passthrough loop, Projectile continues its line-of-travel search before sending that hit’s ordinary attack message or doing its penetration-resistance processing. This switch does not disable the collider or change whether the player and other physical objects collide with it.

The inspected Projectile update skips at most four hits in one update, one step of the game’s ongoing work. A further hit found after that goes to ordinary hit handling. True therefore does not promise an unlimited chain of ignored surfaces. Place this component on the same GameObject as the shape you want that projectile search to recognize.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.CapsuleCollider
member.summary: Selects the capsule collider whose shape and orientation define the barrel’s available grab regions.

remarks.para: This is the same reference exposed by _capsuleCollider and CapsuleCollider. The barrel's zone checks read its center, radius, height, axis direction, rotation, and world scale to choose a hand target and a ring, side, edge, cap, or short-barrel pose. Assign it before the grip is used; the checks expect a valid collider.

The collider's direction chooses its long local axis: X, Y, or Z. Rotating its GameObject rotates that axis in the world. With curve override off, the checked half-span is scaled height divided by 2, minus the scaled radius. For example, height 1 and radius 0.2 at scale 1 give a half-span of 0.3 meters, locating the two grip-end regions 30 cm from the collider center.
The property setter only replaces the reference. Zone checks use the new collider when they next run; setting the property does not resize a collider or immediately move an attached hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip._grabConfig
member.summary: Keeps each hand’s latest zone decision and the position and rotation selected for its prospective grab.

remarks.para: Entries are created as hands are checked. ValidateGripScore calls CheckZones and stores whether the zone is valid; hover updates use that result to choose a target or restore the default hand pose. Stored data includes which region was chosen, world-space grip and handle positions, the surface normal, and a position/rotation relative to the collider-centered frame.

These are calculated results. Zone checks overwrite the region flags and target data, and Awake replaces the entire dictionary. Editing an entry is not a persistent way to change the barrel’s configured shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip._grabDistance
member.summary: Sets the shared squared-distance limit used to reject a hand that is too far from a proposed barrel handle.

remarks.para: This value is compared directly with a world-space distance squared, so its unit is square meters. The actual distance limit is its square root. For example, 0.01 allows 0.10 meters, or 10 cm; the class initializer’s 0.02 corresponds to about 14.1 cm, not 2 cm.

The checked zone branches accept equality and reject larger squared distances. This is static data shared by BarrelGrip instances, so changing it affects their later zone checks. Other region and hand-orientation conditions must still pass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip._maxCapHeight
member.summary: Sets the inward radial offset of the hand target when a very short barrel is grabbed across its ends.

remarks.para: In the short-barrel, or sandwich, branch, the target’s distance from the barrel axis is the chosen end radius minus this value. Increasing it tucks the target farther toward the axis. It is measured in meters; with radius 0.20 and this value 0.025, the target lies 0.175 meters from the axis before the collider’s rotation and center place it in the world.

The audited branch separately decides that a barrel is short when its checked half-span is below 0.025 meters. Changing _maxCapHeight does not change that branch threshold. This field is static and affects the later sandwich calculations of all BarrelGrip instances.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip._ringPadding
member.summary: Sets the shared border width used to distinguish the barrel’s middle, end-face interior, and rim regions during grab checks.

remarks.para: Zone checks subtract this distance from the checked half-span and from the selected end radius. Increasing it widens the near-end band along the barrel and makes the inner disk of an end smaller, giving its border more room. The resulting branch also depends on enabledCaps and the hand’s position and orientation.

This is a distance in meters, applied after the collider’s shape has been converted to scaled distances. For example, a checked half-span of 0.30 and padding 0.05 put the middle-to-end boundary 0.25 meters from the center. The initializer uses 0.05 meters; this is shared static data rather than a value per barrel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.barrelHandStates
member.summary: Stores the last selected barrel pose and finger-wrap radius separately for each hand.

remarks.para: A valid zone branch writes a state containing a radius, HandPose, and the region’s two stored break-force values. Hover and attached updates apply the cached pose and radius to the hand animator; an attached update also copies that pose into the inherited handPose field.

The dictionary is created by the constructor and populated by zone checks. These are cached results, not the settings that define all future grabs. A later successful zone choice replaces the entry; a rejected zone does not necessarily remove its old state. The audited update routines use radius and pose but do not apply the two cached break-force values to a joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.capHandPose
member.summary: Chooses how the fingers are posed when grabbing the inner face of an enabled cap.

remarks.para: Zone checks copy this HandPose into the selected hand’s barrelHandStates entry. Later hover and attached updates apply it to that hand’s animator. The accompanying finger-wrap radius is a stored pose radius of 0.02 meters; the pose choice and radius together determine the displayed grip.
Changing this reference changes later zone selections. A hand already using a cached state can keep its previous pose until that state is refreshed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.capMaxBreakForce
member.summary: Stores the maximum break-force value copied into a hand’s cached cap-grab state.

remarks.para: When a zone check selects this region, it copies the value into the corresponding break-force slot in barrelHandStates. Changing the field changes what is stored on a later selection.

The audited BarrelGrip hover and attached updates use the cached radius and pose, while its joint updater adjusts angular drives and rotation limits without applying this cached break-force value. A joint is the physics connection holding the hand to the object. Changing this field therefore has no verified effect on how much pulling breaks that connection in those routines; no working tuning range or force unit was established for this stored value. Consumers outside the audited routines, including mods, were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.enabledCaps
member.summary: Chooses which end faces and their outer edges can be grabbed as capped ends.

remarks.para: PositiveCap is the end along the capsule collider’s positive long axis, and NegativeCap is the opposite end. That axis comes from CapsuleCollider.direction and the collider object’s rotation, not a fixed world direction. Combine the flags to enable both ends; zero enables neither cap.

At an enabled end, zone checks can choose capHandPose for the inner face or edgeHandPose around its border. When that end is not capped, the near-end rim branch instead uses ringHandPose and ringThickness. Side and short-barrel decisions have their own conditions, so these flags do not simply disable every kind of grab at an end.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.heightAndRadiusCurve
member.summary: When isCurveOverride is enabled, defines the barrel’s checked axial span and the radii used to place hand targets along its side.

remarks.para: The curve’s horizontal coordinate is an axial position measured from the negative end, in the collider’s local distance units. Its vertical value is an absolute radius in those units, not a multiplier. At object scale 1 these are meters. The last key’s horizontal coordinate sets the full checked span, with half that distance on each side of the collider center.

The first key’s value supplies the negative-end radius, and the last key’s value supplies the positive-end radius. Between them, the side-grab branch samples at the hand’s signed axial distance from the center plus half the checked span, adjusted back for the scale along the axis. Radius outputs are multiplied by the largest scale perpendicular to that axis.

For example, with scale 1, first key (0, 0.20), and last key (0.60, 0.10), the checked ends are 30 cm each side of center, with radii 20 cm at the negative end and 10 cm at the positive end. A hand 10 cm toward the positive end samples the curve at 0.40. Use a first horizontal coordinate of zero for this from-end convention; the code does not subtract the first key’s coordinate from the last one.

The enabled override requires a nonempty curve. It changes grab calculations without reshaping the actual CapsuleCollider or visible mesh. Region padding, cap flags, hand orientation, and distance checks still determine whether a proposed grab is accepted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.isCurveOverride
member.summary: Switches barrel grab calculations from the capsule’s dimensions to heightAndRadiusCurve’s axial span and radius profile.

remarks.para: When false, the checked half-span is the scaled capsule height divided by 2 minus the scaled capsule radius. When true, the last curve key’s horizontal coordinate supplies the full span, and the curve’s endpoint values supply the two end radii; side grabs also sample the curve between the ends.

Assign a nonempty heightAndRadiusCurve before enabling this flag. The collider still supplies the center, orientation, axis direction, and scale. The override changes later hand-target and zone calculations, without resizing the collider or mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BarrelGrip.ringThickness
member.summary: Sets the finger-wrap radius and inward axial placement of a hand gripping an uncapped end rim.

remarks.para: For the ordinary uncapped-rim branch, this is copied directly into the hand’s pose radius. It is a distance in meters: 0.02 means a 2 cm finger-wrap radius, not a dimensionless thickness multiplier.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.Type
member.summary: Stores the XR controller-family selection used by input-specific processing.

remarks.para: XR means the virtual-reality device system. XRControllerType identifies families such as OculusTouch, Index, ViveWands and WindowsMR; it is an enum selection, not a bit mask or a headset pose.

OpenController updates this value from the selected XR device during input caching, then uses it to choose input and finger/grip processing. The base getter simply returns the stored selection, and the protected setter changes it. A fresh base component has numeric 0, OculusTouch, from zero-initialized storage; this alone does not prove that a device was detected.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController._haptor
member.summary: Stores the component reference assigned to this controller.

remarks.para: A Haptor is a component that prepares vibration feedback for controller interactions. The public haptor getter returns this stored reference directly; it does not search the scene or create a missing component. A missing assignment therefore produces a null reference.

Assigning the reference does not by itself send vibration. Haptor’s sending routine uses its own device_Controller setting to call that controller’s HapticAction implementation. The BaseController HapticAction hook is empty, so an assigned component alone does not guarantee vibration. Check that both the component reference and its device-controller setting describe the intended setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.contRig
member.summary: References the controller rig that groups this controller with the player’s other tracked inputs.

remarks.para: A rig is the group of objects representing the player’s tracked head and hands. ControllerRig.OnAwake needs both leftController and rightController references to complete setup and enters an error path if either is missing. If the left reference exists, OnAwake assigns its contRig first, then assigns the right controller; thus a missing right reference follows the error path after the left assignment. OpenController reads this reference when checking whether menu taps are disabled and when evaluating gestures relative to the rig’s head and hand references.

Assign a rig before those input-specific routines run; their inspected paths require it and do not silently find another rig. Changing the reference affects later processing rather than moving the controller or immediately refreshing its cached buttons.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.handedness
member.summary: Selects which hand’s XR input an input-specific controller reads.

remarks.para: The enum choices are UNDEFINED, LEFT, RIGHT and BOTH. OpenController’s inspected input and vibration routines route LEFT to the left XR device and RIGHT to the right one; UNDEFINED or BOTH do not request both devices in those routines.

Changing this stored selection does not transfer a held object or immediately refresh cached input. The selected device is used when later input or vibration routines run. The base component’s empty update and vibration hooks do not read a device themselves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController.haptor
member.summary: Returns the Haptor component reference assigned to this controller.

remarks.para: A Haptor is a component that prepares vibration feedback for controller interactions. The public haptor getter returns this stored reference directly; it does not search the scene or create a missing component. A missing assignment therefore produces a null reference.

Assigning the reference does not by itself send vibration. Haptor’s sending routine uses its own device_Controller setting to call that controller’s HapticAction implementation. The BaseController HapticAction hook is empty, so an assigned component alone does not guarantee vibration. Check that both the component reference and its device-controller setting describe the intended setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BillOfMaterials.AllComponents
member.summary: Returns the live name-to-component lookup that this bill of materials uses to resolve blueprint references.

remarks.para: A component is a Unity part attached to an object, such as code for a switch. A key is a text label for one registered component. This property returns the same collection as Components, rather than a copy or a search through every component in the scene.

For example, if the collection maps "doorSwitch" to a switch component, resolving that key returns that stored component. Changing that entry through this dictionary changes what a later lookup finds. The label is the configured dictionary key; it is not automatically treated as an object name or a path through the scene.

The collection must be supplied before resolution. A missing key returns null, meaning no component reference was found, and takes the resolver’s diagnostic path. A missing collection is a different setup problem: the resolver requires the collection itself to exist. Reading this property does not create it or restore any blueprint connections.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BillOfMaterials.Components
member.summary: Stores the keyed Unity component collection used by and blueprint reference resolution.

remarks.para: A component is a Unity part attached to an object. This collection pairs text keys with component references, so the blueprint code can request a particular part by its configured label. KeyedComponents is a dictionary that can save these pairs with Unity scene or prefab data; a prefab is a reusable object setup.

The getter and AllComponents expose the same stored collection. The setter only replaces that reference; it does not find components, populate entries, or apply wiring. The bill-of-materials constructor does not allocate the collection, so saved setup or setup code must provide it before the resolver is called.

For example, an entry "doorSwitch" can point to the switch component on a spawned door. Blueprint connection restoration can then use that key to obtain the part it needs. Adding or replacing an entry changes future lookups, but does not itself reconnect an already restored signal connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.Blueprint.spawnables
member.summary: Lists the objects that a blueprint spawner should create and their positions and orientations relative to that spawner.

remarks.para: Each SpawnData entry contains a crate reference, which identifies the object asset to spawn, and a SimpleTransform, which stores a position and rotation. Position is an offset in Unity scene units. Rotation is a quaternion, a set of four numbers representing an orientation.

During a spawn, the record’s position is rotated by the spawner’s orientation and added to the spawner’s world position. The record’s rotation is combined with that orientation. World position means a location in the whole scene. For example, an offset of (2, 0, 0) places an object two Unity units along the spawner’s right direction; turning the spawner also turns that offset. The inspected placement calculation uses position and rotation, without multiplying the offset by the spawner’s scale.

The spawner reads this array during startup and again when asked to spawn the blueprint. Assign the array and valid crate references before those reads. The spawn path checks the references, starts asynchronous creation, waits for the objects to be returned, and then restores the saved signal connections. Asynchronous work can finish later, so starting the request does not mean all objects already exist.

The saved connection endpoints use numbered entries in the spawned group. Keep this ordering consistent with the saved wiring when editing the recipe. Changing the recipe supplies data for later reads; it does not reposition objects already created by the inspected spawn path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.Blueprint.voidLogicConnection
member.summary: Describes the signal wires that the spawner restores between the blueprint’s newly created objects.

remarks.para: VoidLogic is the game’s system for passing signals between components. A component is a behavior attached to a spawned object. Each edge describes a wire from one component’s output to another’s input. Its endpoints identify a spawned object by its spawn-entry number, use the saved string key as the label that the spawned object’s BillOfMaterials uses to find the component, and select a numbered output or input port.

For example, a wire can connect a button component on entry 0 to a door’s input on entry 1. Those entries need matching components under the saved keys and compatible output and input ports. Assign the edges array even when there are no wires; an empty array restores successfully, while an unassigned array is an error in the inspected restoration method.

The spawner waits for the object creation tasks before applying these wires. It keeps the new group inactive during that setup and activates it only after restoration reports success. If restoration reports failure, it requests destruction of the group instead. Merely assigning this saved connection value does not wire an existing group.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner.Blueprint
member.summary: The saved object layout and logic wiring used when this component creates a new group of objects.

remarks.para: The asset stores object choices, positions and rotations relative to the spawner, and logic connections that let those objects send signals to one another. Awake, Unity’s component initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), starts preparing the object assets. An explicit SpawnBlueprint or SpawnBlueprintAsync request creates a new copy of the layout.

Saved position offsets are measured in meters. The spawning path rotates each offset by the spawner’s world rotation and adds the spawner’s world position, then combines the saved rotation with that world rotation. For example, at an unrotated spawner position of (10, 0, 0) m, a saved offset of (0, 0, 2) m requests an object at (10, 0, 2) m. This path does not multiply the offset by the spawner’s scale.

Assign a nonnull blueprint with usable crate references and initialized object and connection arrays before initialization. Changing this property only replaces the saved reference: it does not prepare the new assets, start a spawn, or update existing spawned objects. Keep the reference stable during a pending spawn request; restoration rereads Blueprint after the object spawns complete and can otherwise use different wiring from the object list already requested.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner.ShouldSpawn
member.summary: Optional true-or-false decision called before a blueprint spawn request creates any objects.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. When ignoreCondition is false, the spawning routine calls this callback once at the start of that request. True permits the request and false stops it before creating the new parent object. With no callback assigned, the request is permitted.

For example, a mod can assign a callback that returns whether a door is unlocked. That value is checked when spawning starts; changing it while the asynchronous request waits does not cancel that request. Asynchronous work can pause for assets and continue in later frames.

Passing true for ignoreCondition skips the callback entirely. DebugSpawnBlueprint uses false and therefore respects it. Awake, Unity’s component initialization routine, prepares blueprint assets without consulting this condition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.BlueprintSpawner._Blueprint_k__BackingField
member.summary: Serialized storage for the same blueprint reference exposed by Blueprint.

remarks.para: Serialized storage means Unity can save this assignment in a scene or prefab, an object template. The blueprint describes which objects to create, their relative positions and rotations, and the logic connections used to send signals between them. The Blueprint getter and setter read and write this same reference.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), starts registering its object assets. Writing this field afterward does not repeat that preparation or modify objects already spawned. Assign a usable blueprint before initialization, and keep it stable while a spawn request is waiting: the restoration stage reads the current reference again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.SpawnData.crateRef
member.summary: Selects the spawnable asset that BlueprintSpawner should create for this saved entry.

remarks.para: A spawnable crate is an asset description for an object that can be created in the scene. This reference identifies that crate by its barcode, the asset’s unique identifier. It is not a reference to an object that has already been created. The separate transform value supplies this entry’s position and rotation relative to the spawner.

During Awake, the routine Unity calls for initialization, BlueprintSpawner reads each entry’s crate reference and starts registration with AssetSpawner, the object spawning system. When a blueprint spawn is requested, it checks that each reference is assigned and resolves to a crate before starting that entry. An absent or unresolved reference takes the inspected spawner’s failure path; it is not treated as an empty entry to skip.

The spawn routine passes the selected crate reference to AssetSpawner together with the computed scene position and rotation. Assigning this field alone does not create anything. Changing which crate is stored in a blueprint entry also does not replace an already created object through these spawn routines; it changes the selection available to a later spawn request.
For example, two entries can identify the same crate and give different transform offsets. They request separate objects from the same asset description at those two placements.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Blueprints.SpawnData.transform
member.summary: Stores this entry’s position offset and rotation relative to the blueprint spawner.

remarks.para: This is a SimpleTransform value: three position coordinates and a rotation stored as a quaternion, Unity’s four-number representation of an orientation. It is a saved value, rather than a live Unity Transform component. The position coordinates are distances in meters along the spawner’s axes: X is right, Y is up and Z is forward. The quaternion components are unitless rotation data, not three angles measured in degrees.

BlueprintSpawner first creates a group object at the spawner’s scene position and rotation. For this entry, it rotates the saved position offset by that group’s rotation and adds the group’s position. It also combines the group’s rotation with the saved rotation. The resulting position and orientation are passed to AssetSpawner as the object’s scene placement. Scene coordinates use the axes of the whole level; the saved offset instead uses the spawner’s axes.

For example, position (2, 0, 0) means two meters to the spawner’s right, not the scene position (2, 0, 0). Turning the spawner turns that offset. Position (0, 0, 0) places the object at the spawner’s position; an identity rotation, meaning no extra turn, aligns it with the spawner’s rotation.

SimpleTransform contains no scale value. The inspected placement calculation does not multiply the position offset by the spawner’s scale. BlueprintSpawner copies this record’s placement into its spawn operation; later editing the saved value does not continuously move the already created object through these routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.armLfExtension
member.summary: Controls the left shoulder-to-palm reach as a fraction of the avatar's reference arm reach.

remarks.para: This is a unitless ratio. Capture computes extension = distance / referenceReach. distance is the shoulder-to-palm distance in metres; referenceReach = eyeHeight * shoulderToPalmFraction. eyeHeight is the avatar's stored eye-height length in metres, and shoulderToPalmFraction is its stored unitless shoulder-to-palm length as a fraction of that height. The producer reads those stored measurements when it captures the pose.

Applying the pose multiplies this value by the destination avatar's referenceReach to place the palm along the saved arm direction. For example, extension 0.8 with referenceReach 0.75 m requests a 0.60 m reach from the shoulder. This describes the whole reach, not an elbow angle.

Normal capture limits the upper value to 0.99999 to keep the requested reach just below the reference length. Writing the field or using an unclamped blend can produce larger values; the field itself does not enforce that capture limit.
This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.armLfRotationInChest
member.summary: Sets the left shoulder-to-palm direction and arm bend reference relative to the chest.

remarks.para: A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers rather than three angles in degrees. Identity means no added rotation.

Capture builds an orientation whose forward axis points from the left shoulder toward the palm. Its other axes use the elbow's orientation to preserve the arm's bend reference. It then expresses that orientation relative to the chest by removing the chest's world rotation. This is a whole-arm reach orientation rather than simply the upper-arm bone's measured rotation.

Applying the pose combines the destination chest orientation with this saved orientation, then places the palm along its forward axis at the saved arm-extension distance. For example, turning the chest while keeping this value and the extension fixed turns the requested palm reach with the chest.
This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.handSeparation
member.summary: Controls palm spacing relative to palm size and arm length when hand proximity is applied.

remarks.para: This is a unitless proximity value. Let d be the distance between palm centres in metres, r the sum of their directional palm extents in metres, and a the avatar's stored arm length in metres. Each directional extent comes from that palm's size bounds and its orientation toward the other hand, so turning a palm can change r.

Capture computes clamp(d / r, 0, 1) + max((d - r) / a, 0). clamp limits its number to the given lower and upper bounds; max selects the larger number. If r is zero, the first term is zero instead of dividing by r. A value of 1 means the palm centres are separated by the combined directional extents. Below 1, their size bounds overlap along that direction. Above 1, the extra part records the gap as a fraction of arm length.
For example, d = 0.10 m and r = 0.20 m give 0.5. If d = 0.50 m, r = 0.20 m, and a = 0.60 m, the result is 1.5. Values are not limited to 1.

Applying proximity rebuilds a requested centre distance using the destination avatar's hand sizes and arm length: r * min(value, 1) + a * max(value - 1, 0). Here value is this field, and r and a are the destination measurements just defined. The method adjusts both palms about their current midpoint along the saved palm-to-palm direction.

The adjustment fades between value 1 and 1.5 unless the two-handed strength keeps it active: at two-handed strength 0, value 1 applies the full spacing adjustment and value 1.5 or greater applies none; strength 1 keeps the full adjustment active. This does not guarantee the final visible or physical hand spacing, because later pose and bone processing can affect it. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.headPosition
member.summary: Positions the reconstructed head relative to the rig object using skull-height units.

remarks.para: Controller capture subtracts the rig object's world position from the head's world position, turns that displacement into the rig object's axes with InverseTransformDirection, and divides it by the avatar's skull-height reference length. InverseTransformDirection changes the axes without applying transform scale. The length used for this conversion is the avatar's stored skull-height reference length, measured in metres. The rig divides position components by that length when capturing this pose; one pose unit represents one such reference length. These saved values do not automatically change if the avatar measurements change later.

For example, a head displacement of 1.5 m along the rig's positive Y axis with a reference length of 2 m gives (0, 0.75, 0). This is relative to the rig object, whose axes can differ from the body root's axes.

RemapRig multiplies the saved components by the destination avatar's skull-height length, then uses the rig object's TransformPoint to place the reconstructed head. TransformPoint converts a local point to world space using the object's position, rotation and scale. A scaled rig therefore also scales that reconstruction. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.headPositionInRoot
member.summary: Saves the head's offset from the body reference in that reference's axes and skull-height units.

remarks.para: Controller capture subtracts the centerOfPressure world position from the head world position. It converts that displacement into the centerOfPressure axes with InverseTransformDirection, which changes axes without applying transform scale, then divides by the avatar's stored skull-height reference length. The centerOfPressure transform is the body's reference position and axes. The length used for this conversion is the avatar's stored skull-height reference length, measured in metres. The rig divides position components by that length when capturing this pose; one pose unit represents one such reference length. These saved values do not automatically change if the avatar measurements change later.

For example, a head 1.6 m above that reference along its positive Y axis with a reference length of 2 m is stored as (0, 0.8, 0). Rotating the reference changes the local components even if the head stays at the same world point.

The separate headPosition value uses the rig object's origin and axes. Use this value when inspecting or blending a head offset from the body root. CopyPose, LerpPoseUnclamped and AddPose preserve or combine this saved vector; editing it does not itself move the head.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.legLfExtension
member.summary: Controls the left leg's hip-to-adjusted-toe reach as a fraction of the avatar's usable leg length.

remarks.para: This value has no units. Capture divides the distance from the left hip to an adjusted point on that foot by usableLegLength. The adjusted point is the foot position plus its rotated local toe offset, with the stored toe-height adjustment subtracted from its vertical component and its forward component halved.

usableLegLength = upperLength + lowerLength - (leftToeY - toeHeight). upperLength and lowerLength are the avatar's stored upper- and lower-leg lengths, leftToeY is the left toe offset's vertical component relative to the foot, and toeHeight is the stored vertical toe-height adjustment. All four quantities are lengths in metres. Both legs use this same length derived from the left toe measurements, including the right leg.

Applying the pose multiplies extension by usableLegLength, reaches that far along the saved leg direction, and removes the rotated adjusted-toe offset to recover the foot position. For example, 0.8 with a usable length of 1 m requests a hip-to-adjusted-toe distance of 0.8 m.

Capture does not cap this ratio at 1. A value above 1 can be recorded when the measured reach exceeds that reference length. The stored ratio describes reach rather than a knee bend angle. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.legLfRotationInRoot
member.summary: Sets the left hip-to-adjusted-toe direction and leg bend reference relative to the body root.

remarks.para: A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers rather than three angles in degrees. Identity means no added rotation.

The body root here is the rig's centerOfPressure transform: the reference position and axes from which the body pose is described. Capture removes that reference's world rotation, so the saved orientation is relative to those axes.

Capture builds a reach orientation whose forward axis points from the left hip to the adjusted toe point. That point includes the foot's rotated toe offset, subtracts its vertical toe-height adjustment, and halves the forward toe-offset component. The knee's orientation supplies the bend reference around that direction.

Applying the pose combines the destination root rotation with this orientation, reaches forward by leg extension times usable leg length, then accounts for the foot's toe offset to position the foot. Turning this orientation therefore changes the requested leg reach direction rather than directly supplying a knee angle.
This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.palmRtToLfDirInRoot

Capture measures the vector from the right palm centre to the left palm centre, divides by its length, and removes the root's world rotation. Normal captured values therefore have length 1 and no distance units.

Applying hand proximity rotates this direction into the destination root's world orientation and places the palms on opposite sides of their current midpoint along it. An ordinary unclamped pose blend does not normalize this vector again; AddPose does normalize its blended result. This is a saved pose value. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.rootPosition

remarks.para: In controller capture, the body reference is the centerOfPressure transform. The saved value is that transform's localPosition divided by the avatar's skull-height reference length. localPosition is the position relative to its actual parent transform, expressed in the parent's axes. The length used for this conversion is the avatar's stored skull-height reference length, measured in metres. The rig divides position components by that length when capturing this pose; one pose unit represents one such reference length. These saved values do not automatically change if the avatar measurements change later.

For example, localPosition (0, 0.2, 0) with a reference length of 2 m becomes (0, 0.1, 0). Copying, blending and adding poses operate on this stored scaled value; they do not turn it into a world position.

Setting the value edits pose data without immediately moving the body root. RemapRig's inspected early update copies and combines this field but rebuilds the actual body-reference position from the reconstructed body rather than simply assigning this value as its world position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.rootRotation
member.summary: Controls the body-reference transform's orientation relative to its parent when the pose is applied.

remarks.para: A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers rather than three angles in degrees. Identity means no added rotation.

Controller capture saves the centerOfPressure transform's localRotation. That transform is the body's reference position and axes, and localRotation is relative to its actual parent. This field is therefore a parent-relative orientation, which can differ from the transform's world orientation.

RemapRig applies the saved orientation as the destination centerOfPressure transform's local rotation. For example, a parent-relative turn in this value turns the body reference within its parent; rotating the parent itself also changes the resulting world orientation.

The other fields ending in RotationInRoot describe segment orientations relative to the body root's axes. This field supplies that root's own local orientation. Setting it stores data; the rig applies it during pose processing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.spineInPalmLfNormed
member.summary: Describes the direction from the left palm toward its torso reference, used to measure palm size and near-body correction strength.

remarks.para: This three-component vector has no distance units. Capture takes the displacement from the palm centre to the selected torso reference point, turns it into the palm's own axes, and normalizes it: divides by its length to describe direction. Very small displacements become zero; otherwise the captured vector has length 1.

The torso reference is selected from the head, chest, spine and hip sections according to the palm's height. The vector points toward that selected point rather than along the spine bone. For example, (0, 0, 1) means the torso point lies along the palm's positive-Z direction.

Applying torso proximity uses the vector with the palm's size bounds to choose its extent toward the body. Its forward/back component also influences the positional correction strength when the saved proximity strength is below 1. LerpPoseUnclamped does not normalize the blended vector again; AddPose does. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

Capture takes the displacement from the palm centre to the selected torso reference point, turns it into the palm's own axes, and normalizes it: divides by its length to describe direction. Very small displacements become zero; otherwise the captured vector has length 1.

The torso reference is selected from the head, chest, spine and hip sections according to the palm's height. The vector points toward that selected point rather than along the spine bone. For example, (0, 0, 1) means the torso point lies along the palm's positive-Z direction.

Applying torso proximity uses the vector with the palm's size bounds to choose its extent toward the body. Its forward/back component also influences the positional correction strength when the saved proximity strength is below 1. LerpPoseUnclamped does not normalize the blended vector again; AddPose does. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.spineRotationInRoot
member.summary: Saves the spine, the lower trunk section orientation relative to the body root so the rig can shape the torso's bend.

remarks.para: A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers rather than three angles in degrees. Identity means no added rotation.

The body root here is the rig's centerOfPressure transform: the reference position and axes from which the body pose is described. Capture removes that reference's world rotation, so the saved orientation is relative to those axes.

Applying the pose combines the destination root's orientation with this saved orientation. For example, turning that root while keeping this value fixed carries the spine, the lower trunk section around with the body.
This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.timestamp
member.summary: Marks the controller pose's frame-start game time so pose interpolation can compare samples.

remarks.para: The value is a double-precision time in seconds on Unity's game clock. At frame start, the head input device records Time.timeAsDouble. After its early-update capture, the controller copies that device update time into this pose. It is a frame time rather than a stopwatch measurement of the moment each individual bone was read.

InterpRig uses currentTime - previousTime as the sample interval. Here currentTime and previousTime are the current and previous pose timestamps in seconds. For a positive interval, its blend factor is (fixedTime - previousTime) / (currentTime - previousTime), where fixedTime is Unity's physics-step game time in seconds. A physics step is one scheduled simulation update. The resulting blend factor has no units and is not clamped; for a nonpositive interval that method uses 1.

CopyPose copies this time. AddPose and LerpPoseUnclamped leave the destination timestamp unchanged, so blending or adding pose data does not itself mark a new capture. For example, timestamps 10.00 s and 10.02 s with fixedTime 10.01 s give blend factor 0.5. Keep sample times on the same game clock when constructing poses for interpolation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.torsoHandLfInSpine

remarks.para: A quaternion stores orientation as four numbers rather than three angles in degrees. Identity means no added rotation.

Capture chooses a torso reference orientation according to the palm's position along the head, chest, spine and hip sections. It removes that reference's world rotation from the palm's world rotation and stores the result. The reference can blend between body sections, so it is not always the literal spine bone's transform.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.torsoSinHandLf
member.summary: Sets the left palm's direction around the torso cross-section when its near-body position is rebuilt.

remarks.para: The two components are a direction, not angles or distances. Capture converts the palm's displacement from its selected torso reference into that reference's axes, takes its X and Z components, and divides them by their horizontal length. The stored Vector2.x is the X component; Vector2.y represents Z, the forward/back component, rather than vertical height.

The selected reference follows the palm's saved torso height through the head, chest, spine and hip sections. Applying torso proximity uses this direction and the destination torso extents to build a candidate palm position around that cross-section. For example, (1, 0) selects its positive-X side and (0, 1) its positive-Z side.

Ordinary captured directions have length 1. LerpPoseUnclamped blends the components without normalizing them; AddPose normalizes its blended two-component direction. The field name does not mean you should put sine angles in radians into its components. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.torsoTHandLf
member.summary: Controls how strongly the left palm's near-torso position is adjusted to the destination body shape.

remarks.para: This is a unitless proximity strength computed from the palm's clearance from the torso after accounting for its size and the avatar's soft-body extents. Normal capture gives 0 for a palm far from the torso and stronger values as it approaches; a palm slightly inside the computed extent can produce values up to about 1.05.

Applying torso proximity builds a replacement palm position using the destination torso shape. Below 1, the helper reduces the strength according to the palm-to-torso direction in the palm's own axes, then squares and clamps that strength before moving the palm toward the replacement. Thus 0 normally gives no positional correction, and 1 gives the full candidate positional offset. This is not elapsed time or a guaranteed collision-free hand position.

A negative stored value makes ApplyTorsoProximity skip this hand's own correction branch. A two-handed adjustment can still carry a correction from the other hand. Pose addition and unclamped blending can create values outside the normal capture range. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BodyPose.torsoYHandLf
member.summary: Selects the height and orientation of the torso reference used to correct the left palm's pose.

remarks.para: This is a unitless, piecewise height coordinate. Capture projects the palm against the line from the upper torso reference toward the hips, then remaps it through the avatar's torso sections. Applying torso proximity uses that coordinate to build a matching reference point and orientation from the destination head, chest, spine and hip setup.

Values around 0 select the upper torso reference, 0.5 the adjusted spine reference, and 1 the hip reference. Intermediate values blend between the section references, with additional changes at the quarter points. Values below 0 and above 1 select sections toward the head or below the hips. This is not a height in metres, a world Y position, or a time in seconds.

This height choice determines the frame for the saved radial hand direction and hand orientation, so those values can follow a differently sized torso. For example, keeping 0.5 while changing avatars selects the new avatar's middle torso reference rather than retaining the old avatar's world height. This is a saved pose value. Capturing another pose refreshes it; setting it edits the saved data. The rig must apply the pose before a bone or palm moves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.GrabConfiguration.corner
member.summary: Stores a corner selector in the hand’s grab record, but native zone checking does not fill it with the chosen corner.

remarks.para: The inspected BoxGrip.CheckZones keeps this value unchanged while calculating the grab position, rotation, surface direction and mode flags. The inspected score and hover consumers use those calculated values rather than reading this selector, so it is not a reliable report of the corner the hand is grabbing.

Changing this cached selector does not enable a corner or select a new grab target in those paths. BoxGrip.enabledCorners is the separate setting that allows particular corners; CheckZones must calculate a valid target from the hand’s current position.
