remarks.para: This is the overall permission for the face mode. The selected region must also be included in enabledFaces. A successful selection uses faceHandPose and saves the mode’s pose radius for later hand updates.

Setting it false rejects a selected face contact; it does not resize the box or force the same contact to become another mode. Other modes have their own permissions, masks and geometric selection conditions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.canBeSandwichedGrabbed
member.summary: Allows a hand to use the sandwich pose around a sufficiently thin section of the box.

remarks.para: This mode represents one hand gripping around a thin dimension across opposing sides of the box. CheckZones assesses one Hand at a time; it does not require a second hand to squeeze the other side.

The box dimensions must meet the relevant sandwichSize comparison, and the hand’s location and direction determine the alignment. The selected outward directions must also be allowed by enabledFaces. A success saves sandwichHandPose with a computed span for the hand animator. This switch grants permission; it does not make a thick box thin.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.cornerHandPose
member.summary: The HandPose used to align and animate a hand after a corner grab is selected.

remarks.para: CheckZones reads this pose’s neutral handle: the saved reference describing how the grabbed object fits in the hand. It uses that reference while constructing the target position/rotation and saves the pose with cornerHandPoseRadius in boxHandStates.

Hover and attached-hand updates apply the saved pose and radius to the hand animator. Changing the asset affects the alignment and fingers of future selections; it does not change the enabled region mask or physical collider dimensions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.cornerHandPoseRadius
member.summary: Sets the corner grab’s pose-size input and inward offset from the geometric corner, in meters.

remarks.para: CheckZones subtracts this distance along the corner’s normalized three-axis diagonal from the corner position when making the target. For an illustrative radius of 0.03 meters, the total shift along that diagonal is 3 cm; it is not 3 cm separately on every axis.

The value is saved with cornerHandPose and sent to SetCylinderRadius during hover and attachment. The animator divides it by its cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize, so the finger pose uses size relative to that hand scale. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh the cache; SetHandSize must run again. It is not the radius of a sphere for detecting nearby hands; edgePadding and the hand’s box-relative position select the region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.edgeHandPose
member.summary: The HandPose used to align and animate a hand after a edge grab is selected.

remarks.para: CheckZones reads this pose’s neutral handle: the saved reference describing how the grabbed object fits in the hand. It uses that reference while constructing the target position/rotation and saves the pose with edgeHandPoseRadius in boxHandStates.

Hover and attached-hand updates apply the saved pose and radius to the hand animator. Changing the asset affects the alignment and fingers of future selections; it does not change the enabled region mask or physical collider dimensions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.edgeHandPoseRadius
member.summary: Sets the edge grab’s pose-size input and offset into the box from the edge, in meters.

remarks.para: CheckZones offsets the contact by this distance along the normalized direction across the selected edge’s adjoining faces, while retaining its position along the edge. For an illustrative 0.03 meters, the total inward shift is 3 cm along that direction.

The saved value also accompanies edgeHandPose in hover and attached-hand updates. SetCylinderRadius divides it by the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize, for finger-pose sizing. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh the cache; SetHandSize must run again. This value is not a proximity detection radius: edgePadding and the hand’s position decide whether the contact is an edge region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.edgePadding
member.summary: Sets how far inside the outer boundaries the face interior ends and edge/corner regions begin.

remarks.para: The value is in meters and is shared across all three axes. CheckZones uses each half-size minus edgePadding/2 as the dividing threshold. For an illustrative box width of 1 meter and padding of 0.10 meters, the X threshold is 0.45 meters from the center, leaving 5 cm next to each outer side.

Crossing one such boundary can select a face, crossing two can select an edge, and crossing three can select a corner, with thin-section sandwich conditions and enabled masks also involved. Increasing positive padding moves these thresholds farther inward. The method uses the value directly; it does not resize the physical collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.enabledCorners
member.summary: Chooses which individual box corners may accept a nearby grab.

remarks.para: This is a flags mask: combine the desired corners with the bitwise OR operator to allow several. For example, PositiveXPositiveYPositiveZ enables the corner on the positive side of all three axes. Zero allows none for the corresponding selection.

The axes follow the referenced collider’s rotation. Turning the object turns these allowed regions with it. canBeCornerGrabbed must also permit the corresponding mode; adding a flag does not force every nearby hand to select that region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.enabledEdges
member.summary: Chooses which individual box edges may accept a nearby grab.

remarks.para: This is a flags mask: combine the desired edges with the bitwise OR operator to allow several. For example, PositiveXPositiveY enables the edge where the positive X and positive Y faces meet, running along Z. Zero allows none for the corresponding selection.

The axes follow the referenced collider’s rotation. Turning the object turns these allowed regions with it. canBeEdgeGrabbed must also permit the corresponding mode; adding a flag does not force every nearby hand to select that region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.enabledFaces
member.summary: Chooses which individual box faces may accept a nearby grab.

remarks.para: This is a flags mask: combine the desired faces with the bitwise OR operator to allow several. For example, PositiveX enables the face on the positive X side of the box. Zero allows none for the corresponding selection.

The axes follow the referenced collider’s rotation. Turning the object turns these allowed regions with it. canBeFaceGrabbed must also permit the corresponding mode; adding a flag does not force every nearby hand to select that region.

The sandwich path also checks enabledFaces against its selected outward direction. These permissions for nearby contacts are separate from forceGrabFace and forceGrabTop, which choose the force-pull alignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.faceHandPose
member.summary: The HandPose used to align and animate a hand after a face grab is selected.

remarks.para: CheckZones reads this pose’s neutral handle: the saved reference describing how the grabbed object fits in the hand. It uses that reference while constructing the target position/rotation and saves the pose with faceHandPoseRadius in boxHandStates.

Hover and attached-hand updates apply the saved pose and radius to the hand animator. Changing the asset affects the alignment and fingers of future selections; it does not change the enabled region mask or physical collider dimensions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.faceHandPoseRadius
member.summary: Sets the size input used to shape the fingers for a face grab, in meters.

remarks.para: CheckZones saves this value with faceHandPose. Hover and attached-hand updates send it to SetCylinderRadius, which divides by the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied from the avatar’s handSizeMult by SetHandSize, so the pose is evaluated relative to that hand scale. Changing the avatar’s multiplier later does not itself refresh the cache; SetHandSize must run again.

Unlike the edge and corner radii, the inspected face branch does not use this value to move the contact target. It does not enlarge the face’s grab zone or set how far away a hand may be detected. The contact comes from the face geometry, pose handle and allowed region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.forceGrabFace
member.summary: Chooses the primary box-side direction used to place and orient the force-pull hand target.

remarks.para: UpdateForcePullTransform converts this single face into its outward unit direction in the collider’s axes. It places the target along that direction using the scaled box half-size and applies the force-pull inward adjustment. This is a fixed authored alignment, rather than the nearest face to the approaching hand.

Use one face value, with forceGrabTop on a perpendicular axis. Although Faces supports bit masks for enabledFaces, this direction converter accepts only a single face; a combination produces a zero vector instead of combining directions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.forceGrabTop
member.summary: Chooses the second box direction that controls the force-pull hand target’s roll and pose size.

remarks.para: After aligning with forceGrabFace, UpdateForcePullTransform rotates the target to match this top direction, accounting for the hand’s side. The direction follows the collider’s axes, not world up. Use one face on an axis perpendicular to the primary face; a face mask is not a valid combined direction.

The box half-size along this axis is also saved as the force-pull pose’s radius. If it is below 0.05 meters, it determines how far the target is moved inward from the primary side: 0.05 minus that half-size. Changing this setting can therefore change both target rotation and the distance/size calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.sandwichHandPose
member.summary: The hand pose used for a one-hand grip around a thin section and for force-pull alignment.

remarks.para: A sandwich selection means the hand grips across opposing sides of a thin part of the box. It does not require both hands. CheckZones uses this pose’s neutral handle to align the target and saves the pose with a calculated cross-section span for later hover and attached-hand animation.

Awake, Unity’s initialization routine for this component, also uses this as the inherited initial handPose. UpdateForcePullTransform explicitly selects it regardless of whether ordinary CheckZones accepted a sandwich region; that path computes its own pose radius from forceGrabTop. Assign a usable pose for both of these consumers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BoxGrip.sandwichSize
member.summary: Sets the thickness threshold used when considering one-hand sandwich grabs.

remarks.para: CheckZones compares each full scaled box dimension with this value in meters. A dimension must be strictly smaller to qualify for the corresponding thin-section branches. For an illustrative threshold of 0.12 meters, a 0.10-meter dimension passes, whereas a 0.12-meter dimension does not. This comparison uses full thickness, not the center-to-face half-size.

The hand’s location, projected direction and other dimensions decide which branch is selected; it is not a promise that every grab on a box with one thin axis becomes a sandwich grab. canBeSandwichedGrabbed and the relevant enabledFaces directions must also allow it. The field does not compare two hands or measure the player’s hand span.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CameraSettings.cam
member.summary: Caches the attached found when this component initializes.

remarks.para: A Camera is the component that supplies a view of the scene. A component is a part attached to a scene object. Awake, the routine Unity calls when initializing this component, looks for a Camera on the same scene object and saves its reference here. A cache is a saved reference reused later; reading this field does not search for the camera again. GetComps also replaces this cached reference when called.

The rendering-option writes in this component's setup code go to cameraData, the separate URP component holding extra options for the attached camera. URP means Universal Render Pipeline, Unity's system for drawing the scene. Those writes use that saved data reference rather than looking up data through cam.

For example, assigning a camera from another scene object here does not also replace cameraData or turn the three rendering switches on for that other camera. Changing this reference only changes what the field stores; keep the two cached references matched to the camera you intend to configure.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CameraSettings.cameraData
member.summary: Caches the attached URP UniversalAdditionalCameraData that receives the dithering, post-processing and invalid-number-filter settings.

remarks.para: URP means Universal Render Pipeline, Unity's system for drawing the scene. UniversalAdditionalCameraData is a separate component holding extra rendering options for a Camera. Awake, the routine Unity calls when initializing this component, finds it on the same scene object and saves its reference here. GetComps can refresh that saved reference when called; reading this field does not perform a new lookup.

Awake sets three true/false switches on this object to true: dithering, renderPostProcessing, and stopNaN. The separate ChangeSettings method sets those same switches to true again whenever it is called. Dithering uses a small noise pattern to make visible color bands less obvious. Post-processing applies image effects after the scene is drawn. NaN means “not a number,” an invalid result from a calculation; stopNaN requests the renderer's filter for such pixel values.

URP reads these options when preparing rendering data. The stored switches describe requested settings, rather than proving that an image has already received every effect. For example, graphics support can make URP skip the invalid-number filter even though stopNaN is true. The available image effects and rendering path also affect what is actually drawn.

Provide this URP component before Awake. The setup only searches for it; it does not add a missing one, and attempting the switch writes with no data component fails. Replacing this reference only stores the new reference; it does not automatically apply the three switches to the new object.

For example, changing the saved data object's dithering switch to false after Awake lets later rendering-data preparation read false. A later ChangeSettings call can set it back to true. That edit does not itself redraw the camera's image, and replacing cameraData is a different operation from editing the options on the object it already references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator._externalActuator
member.summary: Stores the companion that can evaluate circuit inputs and call this actuator's action through a callback.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine connected to be called by another object. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the actuator replaces this companion's actuate callback with its own Actuate routine before setting up inputs. Start, Unity's startup callback before the first frame update, then performs the initial evaluation on the companion when one is assigned.

Writing this field directly only changes the reference. Use the externalActuator property to also install the callback and immediately initialize the new companion. The field itself does not reconnect an existing callback or input network.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator._inputs
member.summary: Stores the circuits RecursiveUpdate refreshes before calling this actuator's action.

remarks.para: The circuits are visited in array order. Without an ExternalActuator, SetInputs registers this actuator on each input circuit or on that input's assigned externalCircuit; writing this array directly bypasses registration and removal work. With a companion, a SetInputs overload replaces the companion's input list but links only this actuator's new empty list, so it does not register the companion on the new inputs and may leave its old circuit registrations behind. Use an empty array for no inputs. A null array or null entry is not safely ignored by the update and connection routines.

When an ExternalActuator is assigned, the SetInputs overloads store the requested inputs on the companion and leave this actuator's array empty. The old companion registrations are not unlinked by that owner-side SetInputs call. The base class does not combine input numbers; a derived Actuate routine decides what those numbers mean.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator._updateFixedTime
member.summary: Stores the physics timestamp most recently assigned to this actuator by an update or initialization call.

remarks.para: The unit is seconds on Unity's physics clock, not a frame count or a delay. RecursiveUpdate writes the supplied time before refreshing inputs; InitializingUpdate writes the current fixedTime before Actuate. The constructor starts this field at -1.

This is a single-precision floating-point value. Writing it directly does not run Actuate, and RecursiveUpdate does not check this actuator's stored time to prevent another action at the same timestamp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator._updateSeed
member.summary: Stores the unitless marker supplied for this actuator's most recent initialization pass.

remarks.para: InitializingUpdate writes this before calling Actuate with initialization enabled. Startup supplies a random marker; the constructor starts the field at -1. A normal RecursiveUpdate does not change or test this marker, so editing it is not a way to force or suppress a normal action in the inspected base implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator.externalActuator
member.summary: Connects an companion to this actuator's action and immediately performs the companion's initial evaluation.

remarks.para: Assigning the property first stores the companion, replaces its actuate callback with this actuator's Actuate routine, and then initializes the companion at the current physics time with a random marker. A callback is a routine another object calls to perform or report an action. Existing listeners on the new companion are replaced, rather than added to.

Provide a valid companion. Assigning null stores null and then fails while trying to install the callback; it is not a safe disconnect operation. Replacing a companion also does not clear the previous companion's callback or rebuild input connections.

The companion stores the timestamp and marker for this initial call. Merely forwarding that call to this actuator's Actuate routine does not update this actuator's own updateFixedTime or updateSeed fields.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator.updateFixedTime
member.summary: Reports the physics timestamp last stored on this actuator by an update or initialization call.

remarks.para: The unit is seconds on Unity's physics clock, not the duration of the action. The constructor's initial value is -1. The value is stored as a single-precision float and converted to double when read; that conversion does not recover precision already lost.

RecursiveUpdate records the time before updating input circuits or running Actuate, so it does not prove the action finished successfully. A companion can forward an action without updating this actuator's timestamp; in that case this value can describe an earlier direct call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.Actuator.updateSeed
member.summary: Reports the unitless marker stored for this actuator's most recent initialization pass.

remarks.para: InitializingUpdate stores the supplied marker before running the initial action. Startup supplies a random value, and the constructor's initial value is -1. RecursiveUpdate neither changes nor tests this marker in the inspected base implementation; it is initialization metadata, not a setting for the action's strength or update rate.
An ExternalActuator stores its own marker when it initializes and forwards the action. That forwarding alone does not refresh this actuator's marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.AddCircuit._input
member.summary: Stores the circuit list whose calculated output numbers are added together.

remarks.para: The node adds each circuit's inlineValue, meaning its calculated output rather than its unprocessed sensor reading. For example, input outputs 0.25, 0.50 and -0.10 produce a sum of 0.65. The result is not clamped to 0 through 1. Any physical unit comes from the connected signals; this node does not convert units.

SetupInputs connects this stored array to the evaluated input list. Replacing this field directly does not rebuild those connections; assign the input property or call SetupInputs afterward. Use an empty array for no inputs and valid circuit objects for all entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.AddCircuit.input
member.summary: Selects the circuits whose calculated output numbers are added together, and rebuilds their connections when assigned.

remarks.para: For example, input outputs 0.25 and 0.50 give 0.75; connecting the same circuit twice counts its output twice. The node adds inlineValue, each circuit's calculated output, without clamping or unit conversion. An empty array gives 0 on the next calculation. Assigning the array rebuilds connections but does not immediately calculate the sum.

The getter returns the stored array itself, not a cleaned copy. Editing entries in that array can change which signals are read without rebuilding the circuit registrations. Assign the property again or call SetupInputs to rebuild those connections. A null array or null entry is not a safe substitute for an empty array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController._buttonMode
member.summary: Selects how physical button movement becomes a circuit signal, with the same behavior as .

remarks.para: ClickUp produces a 1 pulse on release after a press; ClickDown produces it on pressing; Toggle switches between 0 and 1 on successive presses; ContinuousDown stays at 1 while the button is logically pressed; ContinuousFloat reports the adjusted travel reading from 0 to 1.

Toggle also changes the physics joint's allowed travel and resting target. A joint is the connection that limits motion between physical objects. Changing this field only changes the selected mode: it does not clear the two stored latches or restore a joint changed by Toggle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController._charged
member.summary: Stores the remembered pressed state in click and held modes, or the latched on/off state in Toggle mode.

remarks.para: In ClickUp, ClickDown and ContinuousDown, an adjusted travel reading above 0.9 sets this true, and a reading below 0.1 clears it. Values between those boundaries preserve the remembered state, so small movements do not repeatedly count as a new press or release.

In Toggle mode, this is the on/off latch: it changes on an armed press and stays unchanged when the button is released. The separate _toggleCharged flag says whether another press is allowed to flip it. ContinuousFloat returns the travel reading without consulting either latch.

This is stored state, not a measurement of the button's current position. Editing it directly can change the next sensor result and transition path without moving the button or applying Toggle's matching joint changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController._depressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sound choices requested when a threshold-based button mode detects a release.

remarks.para: One entry is chosen randomly and requested at this component's world position. The inspected request uses volume 0.8 and base pitch 1.0. Audio3dManager leaves the volume at 0.8 and scales pitch by 0.75 × Time.timeScale + 0.25 before asynchronous playback; Time.timeScale is Unity’s game-speed multiplier, so pitch is 1.0 at the normal value 1 and changes with the time scale. Releasing means the adjusted travel reading falls below 0.1 after a recognized press; Toggle requests this sound when release rearms its next press, even though the on/off output stays latched.

ContinuousFloat bypasses these transition sounds, and initialization does not request them. An empty array requests no sound; a null array is not safely ignored by the audio helper. The request does not guarantee that sound playback has already started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController._pressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sound choices requested when a threshold-based button mode detects a press.

remarks.para: One entry is chosen randomly and requested at this component's world position. The inspected request uses volume 0.8 and base pitch 1.0. Audio3dManager leaves the volume at 0.8 and scales pitch by 0.75 × Time.timeScale + 0.25 before asynchronous playback; Time.timeScale is Unity’s game-speed multiplier, so pitch is 1.0 at the normal value 1 and changes with the time scale. Pressing means the adjusted travel reading rises above 0.9 after the mode has been rearmed. Toggle requests this sound both when switching on and when switching off.

ContinuousFloat bypasses these transition sounds, and initialization does not request them. An empty array requests no sound; a null array is not safely ignored by the audio helper. The request does not guarantee that sound playback has already started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController._toggleCharged
member.summary: In Toggle mode, records whether a press is allowed to flip the stored on/off state.

remarks.para: When true, an adjusted travel reading above 0.9 flips _charged and clears this flag. The next reading below 0.1 sets this flag true again without changing _charged, so holding the button down cannot keep toggling it. The constructor starts this flag at true.

This flag means ready for another toggle, rather than currently on. ClickUp, ClickDown, ContinuousDown and ContinuousFloat do not consult it in their inspected sensor paths. Switching buttonMode does not reset it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.buttonMode
member.summary: Selects whether button motion produces a click pulse, a latched toggle, a held signal, or a continuous travel value.

remarks.para: ClickUp reports 1 when a recognized press is released. ClickDown reports 1 when pressing is recognized. These are pulses in the sampled circuit signal, not timed animations: the normal following sensor read clears the pulse to 0. Their duration depends on when the sensor is read.

Toggle changes between 0 and 1 on each armed press. Releasing rearms the next press without changing the output. Switching on halves the joint's linear limit and target position and shifts its attachment point; switching off reverses those changes. The physics joint is the connection controlling the button's allowed movement, so Toggle affects physical travel as well as its output number.

ContinuousDown reports 1 after a press and retains it until release is recognized. ContinuousFloat reports the adjusted travel reading from 0 to 1 and bypasses press/release sounds. The other modes use readings above 0.9 for pressing and below 0.1 for releasing; the gap preserves their remembered state.

Assigning a mode only stores the selection. It does not reset _charged or _toggleCharged, recalculate the output immediately, or undo joint changes made by Toggle. These are sensor values; an upstream CircuitSocket input, when connected, multiplies the value to form the final circuit output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.downThreshold
member.summary: The fixed 0.9 boundary that the adjusted travel reading must exceed to recognize a press in the threshold-based modes.

remarks.para: The compared reading is clamp(1.04 × (x + L) / (2 × L) − 0.02, 0, 1). Here x is the button's signed displacement in meters along the Servo's joint X direction, and L is the current joint linear limit in meters, the allowed distance each way from the joint's center. Clamp means restricting the result to 0 through 1. The fraction (x + L) / (2 × L) runs from 0 at the negative limit to 1 at the positive limit. The 1.04 multiplier and 0.02 subtraction have no units.

Consequently this is about 88.46% of raw end-to-end travel, rather than exactly 90%. For a current L of 1 cm, giving 2 cm total travel, pressing is recognized just beyond about 1.769 cm from the negative end. Equality at the stored 0.9 boundary does not trigger a press. Toggle uses the joint limit currently installed, which changes when it switches state; ContinuousFloat does not use this boundary.
This is a compile-time constant, not a configurable threshold field. The formula requires a nonzero joint travel limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ButtonController.upThreshold
member.summary: The fixed 0.1 boundary that the adjusted travel reading must fall below to recognize a release in the threshold-based modes.

remarks.para: The compared reading is clamp(1.04 × (x + L) / (2 × L) − 0.02, 0, 1). Here x is the button's signed displacement in meters along the Servo's joint X direction, and L is the current joint linear limit in meters, the allowed distance each way from the joint's center. Clamp restricts the result to 0 through 1. The raw travel fraction (x + L) / (2 × L) is 0 at the negative limit and 1 at the positive limit. The 1.04 multiplier and 0.02 subtraction have no units.

The boundary is therefore about 11.54% of raw end-to-end travel, rather than exactly 10%. With a current L of 1 cm, giving 2 cm total travel, release is recognized below about 0.231 cm from the negative end. Equality at the stored 0.1 boundary does not release or rearm the button. The gap between release and press boundaries stops small movements from repeatedly switching the state.

Toggle releases to rearm another toggle while leaving its on/off state unchanged, and its current joint limit can differ from the original limit. ContinuousFloat does not use this boundary. This is a compile-time constant, not a configurable threshold field; the formula requires a nonzero travel limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.CircuitSocket._input
member.summary: Stores the circuit whose calculated output multiplies this socket's sensor reading.

remarks.para: For example, a local sensor reading of 0.5 and an input output of 0.2 produce 0.1. The connected number is inlineValue, meaning the input's calculated output. No valid input means no multiplier, so the socket returns its sensor number unchanged.

SetupInputs resolves an assigned input's externalCircuit companion and rebuilds the connection. Replacing this raw field alone does not perform that work; use the input property or call SetupInputs afterward. This is a numeric signal connection, not a target orientation for the joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.CircuitSocket._rb
member.summary: Stores the physics body whose sleeping state determines whether the socket's automatic physics-step update evaluates its circuit.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for an object moved by the physics simulation. When this body is sleeping at rest, the socket skips its automatic check. When it is awake and the Servo joint exists, FixedUpdate asks the circuit to evaluate at Unity Time.fixedTime, the time at the start of the current FixedUpdate, measured in seconds since the game started.

Reset keeps an existing valid reference or searches this object and then its children. The reference is not rediscovered every step; a null stored body is not safely skipped. Replacing it changes which body's sleeping state controls the automatic check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.CircuitSocket._servo
member.summary: Provides the physics joint that this socket checks before automatic evaluation and that derived physical sensors can measure.

remarks.para: A joint is the connection controlling motion between physical objects. The base FixedUpdate checks that this Servo's joint exists after finding the Rigidbody awake, then asks the circuit to evaluate. A derived ButtonController also measures displacement along that joint to obtain its sensor value.

Reset keeps an existing valid Servo or searches this object and then its children. The reference is stored for later updates, and a null Servo is not safely skipped on the awake-body path. Changing this field changes the joint available to these checks and derived measurements.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.CircuitSocket.input
member.summary: Selects the circuit whose calculated output multiplies this socket's sensor number, rebuilding the connection when assigned.

remarks.para: The getter returns the configured source's externalCircuit companion when one exists, otherwise the configured source itself. The setter stores the source and calls SetupInputs. Assigning no valid source clears the incoming connection; the socket then returns its sensor number unchanged.

For example, a sensor reading of 0.5 multiplied by input inlineValue 0.2 gives output 0.1. inlineValue means the source's calculated output. Assignment rebuilds links but does not immediately sample or publish a new result. The signal's units and range depend on the source and sensor, and no 0-to-1 limit is imposed here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ExternalCircuit._input
member.summary: Stores the source whose own calculated output multiplies the sensor number when no calculation callback is assigned.

remarks.para: For example, sensor number 0.5 multiplied by this source's inlineValue 0.2 gives 0.1. inlineValue is the source's calculated output. With no valid source, the fallback passes the sensor number through unchanged. With an inlineCalculate routine assigned, that routine supplies the output instead.

SetupInputs can connect the source's externalCircuit companion, but fallback multiplication reads this stored source directly, so its cache can be older than the connected companion's output. Replacing the raw field does not rebuild the connection; use the input property or call SetupInputs afterward.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ExternalCircuit.initialize
member.summary: Optional routine that supplies the starting sensor number when this circuit's network initializes.

remarks.para: This is a callback, a routine called by the circuit to obtain a value. It takes no arguments and returns a float whose units and range depend on the sensor. Without it, Initialize returns 0. Network initialization then stores that sensor number and passes it to the output calculation.

Changing this field does not immediately run initialization. Another circuit that uses this object as its externalCircuit installs its own Initialize routine here, replacing the previous callback, during its setup or companion assignment. Initialization can run again after startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ExternalCircuit.inlineCalculate
member.summary: Optional routine that turns the supplied sensor number into the circuit's output, replacing the default input multiplication.

remarks.para: The callback, a routine called to process a value, receives the current sensor float and returns the calculated output float. Its units and range depend on the calculation. Without it, InlineCalculate multiplies the sensor by the configured source's own inlineValue, or passes the sensor through if no valid source exists.

Assigning this routine does not calculate or publish an output immediately. Another circuit using this object as its externalCircuit can replace the routine with its own InlineCalculate during setup or companion assignment. The callback's caller stores its returned number in this object's output cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ExternalCircuit.input
member.summary: Selects the connected source and rebuilds its links on assignment; its own output also supplies the fallback multiplier when no calculation routine is assigned.

remarks.para: The getter returns the configured source's existing externalCircuit companion when present, otherwise the source itself. The setter stores the configured source and calls SetupInputs. A missing or destroyed source clears the incoming connection.

Fallback InlineCalculate reads the originally stored source's own inlineValue cache, not the resolved getter result. For example, sensor value 0.5 and configured-source output 0.2 give 0.1, even if a connected companion currently has a different output. With no valid source the sensor passes through unchanged.
An assigned inlineCalculate callback supplies the output instead of that fallback. Assignment changes connections without immediately sampling or publishing a result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ExternalCircuit.readSensor
member.summary: Optional routine that obtains the next sensor number from the physics timestamp and previous reading.

remarks.para: This callback, a routine called to obtain a value, receives a double timestamp in seconds on Unity's physics clock and the previous sensor float. It returns the next sensor float, whose units and range depend on the sensor. Without it, ReadSensor retains the previous number.

Normal circuit evaluation invokes it before refreshing incoming circuits. Changing this field does not sample immediately. Another circuit using this object as its externalCircuit can replace the callback with its own ReadSensor during setup or companion assignment; this object's evaluation still stores the returned number in its own sensor cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ValueCircuit.Value
member.summary: Selects the constant sensor and output number and requests a circuit evaluation when assigned.

remarks.para: The getter returns the configured number, rather than the last published inlineValue. For example, setting 0.5 supplies a signal of 0.5 when the circuit is evaluated. Negative numbers and values above 1 are not clamped; the connected calculation determines what the number means and which units it represents.

The setter stores the number first, then asks this circuit or its externalCircuit companion to update at the current physics time. If that object's stored timestamp is already current, the update is skipped. Value can therefore show the new setting while inlineValue still contains an older published number, until a later eligible evaluation occurs.
The constructor starts the configured number at 1, although serialized object settings can differ. Reading Value does not itself evaluate or publish anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Circuits.ValueCircuit._value
member.summary: Stores the constant number returned by this node's initialization and sensor reads, then passed through as its calculated output.

remarks.para: For example, 0.5 supplies a constant signal of 0.5 on evaluation. The code does not clamp it to 0 through 1 or convert units; its meaning comes from the circuit connected to it. The constructor sets it to 1, while serialized settings can replace that value.

Writing this raw field changes the configuration without requesting evaluation. Use the Value property to also request an update, or call UpdateCircuit after changing the field. That request still obeys the physics-timestamp guard, so configuration changes do not always immediately replace the cached output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.OnSignificantCollisionEnter
member.summary: Holds callbacks run when an enter flag, an impulse flag and the selected contact's signed velocity threshold all qualify.

remarks.para: A callback is a method called to report a result; add a listener here before processing collisions. ProcessCollisionHaul calls it immediately with the reusable RelevantCollision object when normal dot relativeVelocity is at least impactVelocityThresh. normal is the unit contact direction, relativeVelocity is world-space relative speed in metres per second, and dot is the sum of their matching components multiplied together. Equality qualifies; sideways speed alone does not.

The enter flag means any collected collision began contact. The payload's detailed contact instead comes from the collision with the largest individual impulse, which can be a different contact, including a stay. Its totalImpulse includes the collected impulses from all contacts.

The argument is the collector's reusable RelevantCollision object, not a fresh copy. It holds the summed impulse from the collected contacts and the details of the individual collision with the largest impulse. Its point is in world coordinates, the level's shared axes, in metres; its normal is a direction with no units, and its relativeVelocity is in metres per second along those same axes. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body; the payload's rigidbody is the other body and can be null for a static surface. Copy any values you need to keep during the callback, a method called when the collector reports a collision: processing later clears totalImpulse and rigidbody, and future contacts overwrite the other details.

In the scaling overload, the callback runs before the new _pressureSensor value is saved. After it returns normally, the enter and impulse flags are cleared, then the impulse data is cleared. This callback is not a UnityEvent; it is an Action delegate that stores methods to call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.OnSignificantCollisionStay
member.summary: Holds callbacks run during processing when no enter flag is set and an impulse flag is present.

remarks.para: A callback is a method called to report a result; add a listener here before processing collisions. A stay means continuing contact. Unlike enter reporting, this branch does not compare velocity with impactVelocityThresh.

The argument is the collector's reusable RelevantCollision object, not a fresh copy. It holds the summed impulse from the collected contacts and the details of the individual collision with the largest impulse. Its point is in world coordinates, the level's shared axes, in metres; its normal is a direction with no units, and its relativeVelocity is in metres per second along those same axes. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body; the payload's rigidbody is the other body and can be null for a static surface. Copy any values you need to keep during the callback, a method called when the collector reports a collision: processing later clears totalImpulse and rigidbody, and future contacts overwrite the other details.

Processing keeps the impulse flag after a stay, even though it clears totalImpulse and rigidbody. Another processing call can therefore run this callback without a fresh contact and with zero impulse and a null rigidbody. It is not a guarantee of one callback per new physical contact or per rendered frame. The scaling overload saves its new _pressureSensor value after the callback returns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.collider
member.summary: The other collision shape from the report with the largest impulse.

remarks.para: A Collider is the shape Unity uses to detect contact, such as a box around a crate. This reference comes from the selected collision report, so it identifies the object hit by the collector side of that collision.

The collector selects the report with the largest impulse magnitude, meaning the size of the collision push. A later report of equal strength keeps the earlier selection. The total accumulated impulse can also include reports involving other colliders.

The collector reuses this collision record. Processing does not clear this reference, so reading it later can show a collider from an earlier collection. Copy the reference during the collision callback, the function called when the collector reports a collision, if you need to remember that event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.colliderSelf
member.summary: The collision shape on the collector side at the selected report's first contact.

remarks.para: A Collider is the shape Unity uses to detect contact. This reference is copied from the first contact in the collision report with the largest impulse magnitude, meaning the size of the collision push. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection.

An object can have several colliders. This tells you which shape actually took part in that contact; it is not a lookup of whichever Collider is attached beside the collector component. For example, a vehicle can report its wheel collider rather than its body collider.
Processing leaves this reference stored, and the same collision record is reused. Copy it during the collision callback, the function called to report the collision, before keeping it for later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.iP
member.summary: The surface settings supplied with the collision report selected by the collector.

remarks.para: ImpactProperties is a component that holds a reference to surface data and other impact settings on an object. The collector stores the ImpactProperties argument passed with the report whose impulse has the largest magnitude, meaning the size of its collision push. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection.

The ordinary collision-enter and collision-stay callbacks, functions Unity calls when contact begins or continues, look up ImpactProperties through its component cache for the other collision object. They submit the collision only when that lookup finds a live component. A direct CollectCollision call can instead pass null, meaning no component reference.

Processing leaves this reference stored while clearing the impulse total and the other object's physics-body reference. The record is reused, so an old surface reference can remain between collections. Copy it during the reporting callback if you need the surface for that event later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.normal
member.summary: The world-space surface direction at the selected report's first contact, used to test collision-enter speed.

remarks.para: A surface normal points straight out from a surface. This is a direction with no distance units, expressed using the scene's world axes rather than the object's own rotated axes. For example, (0, 1, 0) points up. The collector copies Unity's normal from the first contact in the report with the largest impulse magnitude; equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection.

For the collision-enter test, the collector calculates s = nx * vx + ny * vy + nz * vz. Here nx, ny and nz are this normal's world-axis components, and vx, vy and vz are the selected report's relative linear velocity components in world units per second. With Unity's unit-length normal, s is the signed velocity along that direction, also in world units per second. The enter event can run when s reaches or exceeds impactVelocityThresh, the collector's configured speed threshold. This uses the sign, rather than the absolute speed.

The collector does not change this normal when correcting an impulse's direction. Processing also leaves it stored in the reused collision record, so copy it during the reporting callback if you need that event's direction later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.point
member.summary: The world-space position of the selected report's first contact, suitable for placing an impact effect.

remarks.para: World space measures position from the scene's origin using the scene's axes. The components are distances in Unity world units, normally metres when one unit represents one metre. For example, (2, 1, 0) is two units along world X and one unit up; it is not an offset from the object's centre.

The collector copies the first contact point from the collision report with the largest impulse magnitude, meaning the size of its collision push. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection. This is neither an average of the contacts nor a point representing every contribution to the accumulated impulse. CollisionSFX converts this world position to its own local space when placing an impact sound.

Processing leaves this position stored while the collision record is reused. Copy the value during the collision callback, the function called to report a collision, before scheduling an effect for later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.relativeVelocity
member.summary: The relative linear velocity copied from the collision report with the largest impulse.

remarks.para: Relative linear velocity describes how the two objects move compared with each other. Its components use world axes and Unity world units per second, normally metres per second when one world unit is one metre. A magnitude of 3 therefore means a relative linear speed of three world units per second.

The collector copies Unity's collision-wide relativeVelocity from the selected report. It does not calculate a velocity at the individual contact point or add the extra point motion caused by a body rotating. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection.

The collision-enter test multiplies the X, Y and Z velocity components by the corresponding components of the selected contact's surface normal, the direction perpendicular to its surface, and adds the results. It compares that signed speed along the normal with the collector's impactVelocityThresh speed setting. For an upward normal (0, 1, 0), velocity (2, 3, 0) produces a tested value of 3 world units per second.
Processing leaves this velocity stored in the reused record. Copy it during the reporting callback, the function called with collision data, to preserve that event's value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.rigidbody
member.summary: The other object's physics body from the report selected by the collector, or null if it has no Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for an object whose mass and motion are handled by physics. This reference belongs to the other side of the report with the largest impulse magnitude, meaning the size of the collision push. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection. A static wall can have a Collider, its collision shape, without having a Rigidbody, so null does not mean no collision occurred.

The collector clears this reference after its normal collision-processing callbacks return. The callbacks are functions called to report the collected collision, and they receive the collector's reused record. Copy this reference while handling the callback if you need to identify that body later; keeping the record itself will not preserve it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.separation
member.summary: The signed distance between the collision shapes at the selected report's first contact.

remarks.para: The value uses Unity distance units, normally metres when one world unit is one metre. Negative means the shapes overlap at that contact; zero means no gap at that point; positive means a gap. For example, -0.01 represents about one centimetre of overlap when one unit is one metre. This is a distance, not a velocity or an impulse.

The collector copies the first contact's separation from the report with the largest impulse magnitude, meaning the size of its collision push. Equal-strength reports keep the earlier selection. It does not search all contacts for the deepest overlap.

Processing leaves this distance stored in the reused record. Copy it during the collision callback, the function called to report the collision, if you want to retain that event's overlap measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision.totalImpulse
member.summary: The vector sum of collision impulses collected since the previous processing reset.

remarks.para: An impulse is the push accumulated over a short time, measured as a change in momentum. With metres and kilograms, its units are newton-seconds, equivalent to kilogram-metres per second. This world-space vector has both direction and size; it is not a force in newtons.

Each collected report supplies Unity's Collision.impulse, which already combines the impulses from all of that report's contact points. The collector ignores a report whose squared impulse magnitude is zero. When the other object has a live Rigidbody, Unity's physics body component, the collector reverses that report's impulse if it points opposite the first contact's surface normal, the direction perpendicular to the surface. Reports without another Rigidbody keep their original impulse direction.

The collector then adds the corrected vectors component by component, including reports weaker than the one chosen for the other contact details. For example, corrected impulses (2, 0, 0) and (0, 3, 0) produce (2, 3, 0) newton-seconds. The contact details come from the second report because its impulse magnitude is larger. Contributions pointing in opposite directions can cancel instead of increasing the total size.

The total is available during the collector's processing callback, the function called to report the collision. After that callback returns, processing resets the total to zero. The record is reused, so copy the vector during the callback to retain it. The collection interval follows calls to the collector's processing methods; this field does not itself measure the elapsed time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._collisionStay
member.summary: Stores the companion CollisionStay component reference found on the same scene object during Reset.

remarks.para: A component is a piece of behaviour attached to a Unity scene object. CollisionStay receives Unity's continuing-contact notifications and passes them to its assigned collector with isEnter set to false, provided the other object has ImpactProperties, its material/impact information.

Reset is Unity's editor setup call when a component is added or reset. The collector's Reset finds CollisionStay on the same object; CollisionStay's own Reset separately finds its collector there. Set up both references when configuring the object. Assigning this reference alone does not set the companion's collector reference or enable its component. This is a stored component reference, rather than a list of callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._collisionWithImpulse
member.summary: Records that a collected collision had a nonzero impulse and enables a reporting branch during processing.

remarks.para: Impulse is the push delivered over a contact, in newton seconds. CollectCollision sets this flag when the incoming impulse has a positive squared magnitude, the sum of its x, y and z components squared. It stays true when later contacts are weaker or when their summed vectors cancel to zero; it records that an individual impulse occurred.

With _isEnter true, processing uses this flag to allow the enter-threshold test, then clears both flags after the reporting branch returns normally. With _isEnter false, this flag selects stay reporting and is retained. Later processing can therefore report a stay even when the reusable payload's summed impulse has already been cleared.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._highestImpulseSqrMag
member.summary: Stores the largest individual squared impulse collected since the previous processing call to choose which contact supplies the detailed payload.

remarks.para: For an impulse J = (x, y, z), x, y and z are its world-axis components in newton seconds. The squared magnitude is x*x + y*y + z*z, in (newton seconds)². A new collision replaces the selected contact details only when its squared magnitude is strictly larger than this value. Equal strengths leave the earlier contact selected.

Every collected nonzero impulse is added to the summed totalImpulse, even when it does not win this comparison. For example, two equal-strength contacts both contribute to the sum but the first supplies the point, normal, relative velocity and other contact details. Processing resets this maximum to zero after the reporting branch returns normally.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._isEnter
member.summary: Records that at least one collected collision began contact, selecting the enter branch for the collected group of contacts.

remarks.para: CollectCollision sets this flag before checking the impulse when isEnter is true. It does not clear it when a later collision is a stay, and the strongest selected contact can therefore be a stay even while this flag is true.

Processing attempts enter reporting only when the impulse flag is also true. That branch clears both flags after the callback returns normally, even if the velocity threshold prevented a callback. An enter with zero impulse can leave this flag true through processing; a later nonzero impulse can then use the enter branch. It is not a description of the selected contact alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._pressureSensor
member.summary: Stores the world-space summed impulse after the caller's scaling, updated by .

remarks.para: World space uses the level's shared x, y and z axes. The scaling overload saves totalImpulse * divByNewtons after any callback returns, then clears the reusable impulse data. totalImpulse is the summed contact impulse in newton seconds, and divByNewtons is the caller's supplied multiplier. No impulse flag makes this overload save zero. The one-argument overload leaves this field unchanged.

The multiplier determines the units: 1 / dt converts impulse to average force in newtons, where dt is the duration in seconds. PhysicsRig, the component that simulates the player's physical body, instead supplies 1 / (m * g * dt), where m is the avatar's total mass in kilograms, g is the absolute vertical gravity acceleration in metres per second squared and dt is the configured physics-step duration in seconds. A physics step is one update of Unity's physical simulation. An avatar is the player's in-game body. That path stores a unitless fraction of body weight; a value of 1 in a direction represents an average force equal to that weight.

For example, an upward impulse of 2 newton seconds, a 0.02-second step, a 10-kilogram avatar and gravity of 10 metres per second squared produce 1 upward through PhysicsRig's scale. A callback, a method called to report the collision, reads the previous pressure value because the new one is saved after the callback returns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._relCol
member.summary: Stores the reusable collision payload: summed impulse from all collected contacts plus details from the strongest individual collision.

remarks.para: The collector creates one RelevantCollision object during construction and keeps updating it. CollectCollision adds each nonzero impulse to totalImpulse in world coordinates, the level's shared axes, in newton seconds. If the other object has a Rigidbody, Unity's component for a physically simulated body, an impulse pointing against the first contact's normal is reversed before addition. Opposing accumulated vectors can cancel.

Only a strictly stronger individual impulse replaces the details. These include the other collider and this object's collider, relative velocity in world metres per second, first contact point in world metres, unit contact normal, separation in metres, other Rigidbody and supplied ImpactProperties material/impact information. Equal strengths keep the earlier details. A collider describes the shape that can make physical contact.

Both reporting callbacks receive this same object reference. After they return normally, processing zeros totalImpulse and sets rigidbody to null, retaining the other details. Copy values during a callback, a method called to report a collision, if you need to keep that collision's data for later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector._stayEnabled
member.summary: Stores a stay-reporting flag that the collector's collection and processing methods do not consult.

remarks.para: Changing this stored value does not change the branch used by CollectCollision or either ProcessCollisionHaul overload. Those methods route reporting using _isEnter and _collisionWithImpulse instead.

CollisionStay, the companion component that forwards Unity's continuing-contact notifications, also does not test this flag in its Reset or OnCollisionStay methods. Configure and enable that component itself to receive its notifications; writing this field alone does not enable it. These methods provide no automatic switch-off when a body is culled, or skipped from simulation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.impactVelocityThresh
member.summary: Sets the minimum signed speed along the selected contact normal for enter reporting, in metres per second.

remarks.para: ProcessCollisionHaul compares normal dot relativeVelocity with this value when both enter and impulse flags are present. normal is the selected contact's unit direction in world space, the level's shared axes, and relativeVelocity is relative movement in metres per second along those same axes. Dot means multiplying matching components and adding them; this keeps the speed along the normal and its sign.

Equality qualifies. For example, normal = (0, 1, 0) and relativeVelocity = (3, 2, 0) give 2 metres per second, so a threshold of 2 qualifies. A velocity of (3, -2, 0) gives -2 and does not qualify at that threshold, despite the same overall speed. Stay reporting does not use this threshold. Changing it affects the next enter test; it does not change the physical collision or the strongest-contact selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.OrderInPool
member.summary: Stored integer carried with the attack; the inspected combat paths do not use it to order or recycle attacks.

remarks.para: The projectile-hit, punch, crablet mount-attack and inspected rigidbody-projectile messages leave this value at 0. Their forwarding routines copy it along with the other attack data. GenericAttackReceiver and EnemyDamageReceiver do not read it when deciding how to react.

For example, assigning 3 changes the integer carried in that message, but those receivers do not process it as the third attack or choose a reusable projectile slot from it. A pool is a supply of objects kept for reuse; this field does not request a pool operation in those inspected paths. Any ordering convention needs sending and receiving code that explicitly agrees to use it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.attackType
member.summary: Damage-category flags that receivers can test to accept an attack or choose its damage response.

remarks.para: Flags are independent on/off bits, like several checkboxes in one number. The named values are Piercing = 1, Blunt = 2, Fire = 8, Slicing = 16, Stabbing = 32 and None = 64. These are category identifiers, not damage amounts. Combining Piercing and Fire with the bitwise OR operator gives 1 | 8 = 9. The default integer 0 contains no bits; the named None value is 64, not 0.

GenericAttackReceiver sends the damage amount to its configured callbacks when at least one incoming bit matches its accepted flags. A callback is a routine called to report the received attack. By contrast, EnemyDamageReceiver chooses its special category multiplier only when this entire value equals its configured category. Combined flags therefore need not trigger that exact-match branch. Changing the category does not calculate a new damage amount inside Attack itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.backFacing
member.summary: Sender-provided back-face flag that makes the inspected player and enemy health paths skip this attack.

remarks.para: A back face means the reverse side of a surface. Attack does not calculate this flag from the hit angle or from which side of a character was struck: the code making the message supplies it. The inspected projectile, punch, crablet and blade-withdrawal messages set it to false.

When this is true, Health.OnReceivedDamage skips its attack response, and EnemyDamageReceiver skips its damage calculation and forwarding. With false, their other conditions still decide the result. It is therefore not a promise of extra damage for hitting a character from behind, and it does not automatically reverse normal or direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.collider
member.summary: Hit collision shape supplied to receivers for surface effects and critical-hit checks.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape Unity uses to test contact with objects. Projectile and punch messages copy the shape they hit into this field. EnemyDamageReceiver compares it with its configured critical-hit shapes, so supplying the matching shape can change the damage multiplier when critical hits are enabled.

ImpactProperties can use this shape's attached Rigidbody, the component that gives an object simulated mass and motion, to parent a surface-mark effect so it follows that body. It also passes the collider to the surface-mark generator after the effect object arrives. Some attacks, such as the inspected crablet mount attack, leave this reference empty. Setting collider does not by itself select the recipient of ReceiveAttack; the sender separately chooses which scene object receives the message.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.damage
member.summary: Incoming damage amount before the receiving code applies its own rules.

remarks.para: This is a floating-point number in game damage units, not a force in newtons or damage per second. The sender calculates it before delivery. Receivers can multiply it, reject the attack, or report it to another routine instead of directly subtracting it from health.

For example, GenericAttackReceiver reports damage = 10 unchanged to its callbacks when the attack category matches; a callback is a routine called when the attack is reported. An enemy receiver can instead multiply 10 by a configured unitless factor of 2 and pass 20 to its health routine. Its enabled-damage, alive and back-face checks must also pass. Changing this field changes the incoming amount, not a guaranteed final loss of health.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.direction
member.summary: Trajectory vector supplied to orient impact effects and influence some hit reactions.

remarks.para: A vector is three X, Y and Z numbers describing a direction and a length. The inspected projectile and melee senders express this vector using world axes, the axes of the level. It is not automatically a speed in meters per second or a unit-length arrow. Projectile hits copy their travel direction; punches use a scaled arrow opposite the surface normal; the inspected crablet mount attack sends (0, 0, 0).

ImpactProperties normalizes a copy, giving it length 1 when possible, to orient particle effects. It also uses the part along the surface to orient a surface mark. The PowerLegs character hit path scales direction and passes it to a physics push at the attack position, so magnitude can matter to that receiver. For example, (0, 0, 2) points along the same positive world Z axis as (0, 0, 1), but has twice the length. Attack stores the numbers; assigning them alone does not move an object or apply a force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.normal
member.summary: Surface-facing vector supplied to orient impact particles and surface marks.

remarks.para: A surface normal is an arrow perpendicular to a surface: for an upward-facing flat floor, (0, 1, 0) points straight up. The inspected collision and projectile producers copy the hit's normal in world space, meaning the level's axes. It is an orientation vector, with no distance or speed unit; its usual length is 1.

ImpactProperties uses it to orient particles and make a surface mark face the hit. The sender is responsible for supplying the appropriate vector; Attack does not measure the surface. A noncollision sender can choose another reference, as the crablet mount attack does with a character transform's forward arrow. PlayerDamageReceiver converts a copy of normal into that body part's local axes before passing it to Health, so that later copy is no longer in the original world frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.origin
member.summary: Attack position supplied for impact effects, hit reactions and position-based damage queries.

remarks.para: This is a point, not an arrow. Standard projectile and punch messages put the hit position here, expressed in world space, the level's coordinates, with lengths in Unity world units, meters at the usual meter scale. It therefore often means where the impact happened rather than where the projectile was fired.

ImpactProperties requests its particles and surface mark at this point. RigidbodyProjectile centers its blast-recipient search and distance checks on it. For example, a hit at world (2, 1, 3) supplies that point even if the shooter stands elsewhere. PlayerDamageReceiver converts a copy into coordinates relative to the receiving body part before forwarding it to Health. Choose a position in the frame expected by the receiving path; Attack does not perform that conversion itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.Attack.proxy
member.summary: The initiating character's carried for source identification and possible AI threat updates.

remarks.para: A TriggerRefProxy is a component that groups references and identity information for a character, including its root scene object, body references and team information. A projectile copies the proxy supplied when it was set up; a punch tries to obtain the proxy from its hand's configured character-reference object. This identifies the source of the attack, rather than the object receiving it.

In the inspected PowerLegs character hit path, this reference can be passed to AddThreat, which increases the recorded threat for that character and can change the selected target. AI means the game's computer-controlled character behavior. That reaction has other conditions; providing a proxy does not guarantee retaliation. The inspected crablet mount attack leaves this field empty. Setting it does not choose the message's recipient or automatically calculate team-friendly damage rules.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.Count
member.summary: Stores a controller counter separate from the impact manager's active hit count.

remarks.para: The hit path in AddToHitArray updates impactManager's own count and write position, then UpdateArray sends that manager count to the materials. It does not use this Count field as the number of recorded hits.

The inspected controller initialization, reset, hit/cut addition, cache/material refresh, renderer collection and visibility routines do not read or write this field. In particular, ResetHits clears the manager's counter rather than this one. Editing Count does not add or remove hits through those paths; inspect impactManager.count for the count they actually upload.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.Count_CUT
member.summary: Selects the cut-list slot replaced when AddToCutArray receives another cut after the list is full.

remarks.para: While CutPoint contains fewer than eight entries, AddToCutArray appends a matrix and leaves this index alone. Once there are eight entries, it replaces CutPoint[Count_CUT], then advances the index or wraps it back to zero after the last slot. It calls UpdateArray afterward. With eight entries and an index of 2, the next cut replaces the third entry and the index becomes 3.

This is an array/list index, not a count of pending cuts. NumberOfCuts is the cached list size. ResetHits clears the list but leaves this replacement index unchanged, so refilling a previously cleared list does not necessarily restart replacement at its first slot.

Changing it affects a later replacement, not the current matrix data or material appearance. Keep it within the full list's valid indices, normally 0 through 7; the replacement operation does not clamp an invalid index before using it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.CutPoint
member.summary: Stores the cut-effect matrices that AddToCutArray appends or replaces and UpdateArray copies into CutPos.

remarks.para: A matrix is a table of numbers encoding an effect's position, orientation and shape. VisualDamageReceiver.GibletEllipsoidGenerate supplies matrices derived from a cut ellipsoid, a stretched sphere used to describe a cut region. This list is the recorded cut data, rather than a queue emptied after each material refresh.

The normal addition path appends until there are eight entries, then replaces existing slots using Count_CUT. ResetHits clears the list. UpdateArray records its current size in NumberOfCuts and copies it by index to CutPos without removing entries.

Editing a list matrix directly changes the source data for a later UpdateArray call; it does not immediately change CutPos or a material. Direct list edits can bypass the eight-entry addition limit. With the constructed eight-slot CutPos, a larger list can cause that later copy to fail. UpdateArray itself does not upload cut matrices to the shader.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.CutPos
member.summary: Stores the array into which UpdateArray copies the currently recorded cut matrices.

remarks.para: A matrix is a table of numbers encoding an effect's position, orientation and shape. The constructor creates eight slots here. UpdateArray copies CutPoint[0] into slot 0, and so on, using the list's current size as NumberOfCuts. Slots beyond that count keep their previous contents.

ResetHits clears the source list and makes the cached count zero through UpdateArray; it does not erase the old matrices in this array. Changing a copied slot directly can be overwritten by the next refresh when that index still exists in CutPoint.

This is a cut cache. The inspected UpdateArray material loop uploads impactManager's hit array and count, rather than CutPos. Replacing this array alone does not build cuts or send them to materials, and it must have enough slots for a later copy of the source list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.ElipsoidMatricesID
member.summary: Caches the integer shader key for _ElipsoidMatrices.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback for this component, fills this value by calling Shader.PropertyToID with _ElipsoidMatrices. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. A shader is a material's drawing program, and this integer is a lookup key identifying drawing data under that matrix-array property name; it is not the data value, a count, a distance or a size multiplier.

A matrix is a table of numbers encoding position, orientation and shape; an ellipsoid is a stretched sphere. UpdateArray prepares a cut cache, but its checked material loop does not upload the cut matrices or cut count using this key. The inspected controller's UpdateArray does not read this controller field for its hit upload. Editing it alone does not alter that operation or create visual damage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.Renderers
member.summary: Selects the renderers whose material instances receive this controller's recorded hit data.

remarks.para: A renderer draws an object's mesh, and its materials describe how its surfaces look. UpdateArray visits all materials on every entry here, asking impactManager to write the hit matrix array and active count. The materials need a compatible damage shader, the drawing program that interprets those values. Assigning a renderer does not guarantee a visible effect with an unrelated shader.

isLODVisible also scans this array, but UpdateArray performs its upload regardless of that query. collectSkins replaces the selection with skinned mesh renderers on this object and active children; those renderers draw meshes animated by bones. The controller's Awake, Unity's initialization callback, prepares shader keys rather than automatically running collectSkins. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action.
