member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.hitScaleFactor
member.summary: Multiplies the shape scale encoded for new hits generated by VisualDamageReceiver.ReceiveAttack.

remarks.para: VisualDamageReceiver converts an accepted attack into a matrix, a table of numbers describing its visual position, orientation and shape, before passing it to AddToHitArray. This factor multiplies all three scale components in that new matrix; it does not multiply the attack's health-damage value or move the hit center.

For this receiver path, the encoded scale is (20 × h × f, 20 × h × f, 5 × h × f). Here h is hitScaleFactor, a dimensionless multiplier; f is the dimensionless response to d, the incoming Attack.damage value. For d at or below 0.5, f is 1.33. Otherwise, f is 1 divided by (0.8 × d + 0.8) after that expression is limited to the range 0.8 through 1.25. These are encoded matrix scale factors, not a wound radius in metres.

For example, keeping the same accepted attack and changing h from 1 to 2 doubles the encoded scale components for the next generated hit. It leaves already stored matrices unchanged. The constructor starts this field at 1, but an object's saved configuration can supply another value. The checked receiver does not clamp h, and the shader determines how the encoded matrix changes the visible mark.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.impactManager
member.summary: Stores the hit matrices and active count that UpdateArray sends to materials.

remarks.para: This is a data manager, not a component that spawns particles or applies health damage. A matrix is a table of numbers encoding a visual effect's position, orientation and shape. The controller constructs a manager with 32 matrix slots. AddToHitArray fills its next slot, advances a wrapping write position and keeps its active count at no more than 32.

UpdateArray sends the manager's full matrix array to EllipsoidPosArray and then its active count to _NumberOfHits on each configured material. ResetHits sets the manager's count and write position to zero without erasing all old matrix slots. The controller's Count and NumberOfHits fields are separate from this manager count.

Replacing this reference changes the data source for later additions, resets and uploads. The replacement must be a valid initialized manager. Editing its stored data or using its own add/clear routines does not automatically refresh the controller's materials; use the corresponding controller refresh when needed. CutPoint and CutPos are separate cut storage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Combat.VisualDamageController.meshScaleFactor
member.summary: Multiplies the position coordinates in hit matrices created by VisualDamageReceiver.ReceiveAttack.

remarks.para: The receiver first converts the attack's world hit point, a position in the scene, through its current Transform and saved original position, rotation and scale. That reconstructs a point in the controller's original mesh pose, so a mark can be located using the mesh setup rather than simply storing the moving receiver's world position. A Transform holds an object's position, rotation and scale.

A matrix here is a 4-by-4 table of numbers representing position, rotation, and scale. In ReceiveAttack, the receiver multiplies the reconstructed vector by meshScaleFactor before storing the result as the new hit matrix's position. The factor is dimensionless: it scales the position coordinates encoded in that matrix. For example, changing it from 1 to 2 doubles each encoded coordinate for the next hit along the same direction. This is a coordinate example, not a promise of twice the physical distance in metres. The code performs no metre conversion or controller-scale normalization, so physical frame and world-space distance depend on the configured Transform scales.

This factor scales the new matrix's position, while hitScaleFactor supplies its shape-scale multiplier. It does not resize the Transform or alter already recorded hit matrices. The constructor starts it at 1, but saved configuration can override that starting value. The checked receiver does not clamp it. This describes the inspected ReceiveAttack path; GibletEllipsoidGenerate constructs its cut matrix separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Console.TokenParseContext.EligibleCommands
member.summary: Selects the command wrappers whose declared names can be returned by console command-name conversion and suggestions.

remarks.para: This is a HashSet: a collection that keeps each command wrapper only once and does not promise a particular order. A wrapper pairs a command object with its declared names. The set starts empty when the context is constructed. The console plugin adds discovered command wrappers during its startup scan and subsequent scans of newly loaded code.

The command-name converter and suggestion converter read the wrappers currently in this set and inspect their declared names. For example, if only a help-command wrapper is present, those converters cannot return a spawn-command wrapper absent from the set. Adding or removing a wrapper changes the candidates for a later conversion or suggestion request.

The collection itself can be changed even though the field is declared readonly. The inspected command converter enumerates the set without removing entries as it consumes names; the caller can narrow the candidate set explicitly when needed. Its Convert result is an iterable sequence, meaning the search runs as you read the returned results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Console.TokenParseContext.ExpectedTypes
member.summary: Holds the caller’s ordered type expectations in the context passed to token converters and object describers.

remarks.para: Each entry is a type description, such as Int32 for a whole number or String for text. For example, an array containing those two types records a whole-number expectation followed by a text expectation. An empty array records no expected types; the built-in console plugin uses an empty array for its shared context.

The constructor keeps the array object you supplied rather than making a copy. Changing an entry in that original array therefore changes the entry seen through this field. The field is declared readonly, but the contents of the array can still change.

This array supplies information for a consumer that chooses to read it. The inspected built-in command-name converter and its suggestion method do not read the array, so supplying a number type here does not make those methods parse a number or filter their command names by that type. The context constructor itself performs no validation or conversion of the entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Console.TokenParseContext.SoftSuggestionLimit
member.summary: Sets the match-count threshold after which the command-name suggestion converter skips further non-exact matches.

remarks.para: The unit is a returned match entry, which pairs a command wrapper with one of its declared names. This is a count, not a time or a percentage. The constructor default is 20. Exact matches, names beginning with the entered text, and names containing its letters in order all increase the same counter when they are added. Different names on one command can count as separate entries.

A non-exact alias is considered only while that counter is less than the limit. Exact aliases are checked before that gate, so an exact alias can raise the total above the limit when it appears first in a wrapper's alias order. Once the counter reaches the limit, the first non-exact alias on that wrapper ends the scan of its remaining aliases; a later exact alias in that same list can be skipped. For example, with a limit of 2, an exact alias and a partial entry can fill the count. A later wrapper whose exact alias appears before its first non-exact alias can raise the total to 3; if that exact alias follows a non-exact alias, it is skipped.

A limit of 0 or a negative value prevents non-exact suggestions. Exact aliases can still be added when encountered before a non-exact alias in a wrapper's list, but a prior non-exact alias can stop that wrapper before its later exact aliases. The constructor stores the value unchanged. Candidates come from a set with no promised order, so a small limit does not guarantee which partial names are included. This is the behavior of ConsoleCommandWrapperConverter.SuggestConversions; the field does not impose a universal limit on every custom converter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.LineMaterial

remarks.para: A material controls how a surface or line looks, such as its color and texture. On a successful creation path, the tool adds a LineRenderer, Unity’s component for drawing a line, and assigns this material to it. The line joins the two created attachment markers; it is not the aiming laser or a line created on trigger-down.

ConstraintTracker updates the line’s endpoints as the attached objects move. The tool creates a line with a configured width of 0.05 meter at each end. Replacing this field affects later created lines; it does not reassign the material on lines already created.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer._gO1
member.summary: Stores the object used to attach and track constraint endpoint 1.

remarks.para: The first successful trigger-down raycast stores this reference. A raycast is a straight-line check for a collision shape. If the hit has a MarrowBody, the game’s physics-body component, the stored object belongs to that body; otherwise it is the hit collider’s object. A collider is Unity’s collision shape.

Release uses the first object to find a ConstraintTracker in Remove mode. A tracker is the component that remembers the connection and its drawn line. Creation adds trackers to both selected objects so the tool can later find that connection for removal.

This is stored selection data, not a fresh test of what the tool currently points at. Endpoint rearrangement exchanges the two object references. Editing the reference alone does not move an existing anchor or rebuild a connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer._mb1
member.summary: Stores the Marrow physics body for endpoint 1, or no body for an endpoint treated as fixed in the world.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody is the game’s component for a simulated object; a Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives it physics motion. On a successful trigger-down hit, the tool looks up a MarrowBody from the hit Rigidbody’s object and stores it here.

If no MarrowBody is found, the reference is null and the endpoint is treated as a world anchor, a fixed attachment point in the level. Creation requires at least one Marrow body and rejects a pair containing the same body. When only the first endpoint has a body, release moves that body into the second slot and clears the first slot before creating the joint.

Release uses the stored direction to face an attachment marker along that normal. With a body, the marker’s rotation is relative to that body’s object; without a body, it uses world orientation. Endpoint rearrangement exchanges the two normal slots.

The normal input handlers capture the first hit normal but do not capture a second hit normal into this field. With a selected MarrowBody, the game’s physics-body component, the world hit is converted to a position relative to that body’s transform. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer._raycastMissedOnDown
member.summary: Blocks the normal held-input and release actions after the first trigger-down raycast misses.

remarks.para: A raycast is a straight-line check for a collider, Unity’s collision shape. Trigger-down sets this flag true if that first check hits nothing within maxRange on layerMask, and sets it false after a hit. While it is true, the grip-update handler skips both PrimaryButtonHold and PrimaryButtonUp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.breakforce
member.summary: Sets the force limit copied into newly prepared constraint joints before they can break.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits how simulated bodies move. This value is copied into the new joint configuration’s breakForce setting, in newtons. Raising it allows a stronger connection; lowering it makes the force limit easier to exceed. It is not a distance, a damage amount, or the separate twisting-force limit called breakTorque.

The constructor sets it to 100,000,000 newtons. Changing it affects future connection configurations, not joints already created. For example, choosing 1,000 newtons gives a new connection a much lower force limit than the constructor default; it does not itself apply a force or break an existing connection.

The configuration is applied when the Marrow joint builds its underlying Unity joint. This requires the participating Marrow bodies to be active and enabled; a stored configuration alone does not prove that a live physics connection has already been built.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.firePoint

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.firePoint2

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation, and scale. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.icon

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s setup call before normal updates, gets a MeshRenderer from this object and saves its material in iconMat. A MeshRenderer draws an object’s visible surface, and a material controls that surface’s appearance. Start then hides the icon and both laser objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.iconMat

remarks.para: A material controls a rendered object’s color and texture. Start, Unity’s setup call before normal updates, obtains the icon’s MeshRenderer material and stores it here. A MeshRenderer draws the icon’s visible surface.

After the mode-cycle input changes mode, the tool sets this material’s texture offset. The horizontal offset is the numeric mode value multiplied by approximately 0.1428571, one seventh of the texture width; the vertical offset is zero. Both offsets are unitless texture coordinates. For example, mode value 1 shifts horizontally by about one seventh, and value 0 returns to zero.

This expects a texture laid out as seven mode images across its width. Assigning mode directly does not run this display update. Replacing icon later does not recache its material, and writing iconMat alone does not assign that material back to the icon’s renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.layerMask

remarks.para: A layer is a category assigned to scene objects. This mask is a set of on/off bits selecting those categories, rather than one layer number. Both the first trigger-down cast and the second held-input cast pass the mask to Unity’s physics raycast, a straight-line collision check.

For example, excluding a scenery layer stops new selection checks from hitting collision shapes on that layer. A mask value of zero selects no layers. Changing it changes later raycasts; it does not erase already stored endpoint data or remove existing constraints.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.maxRange

remarks.para: A raycast checks for a collision shape along a straight line. A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation, and scale.

For example, a range of 10 meters lets a new selection cast reach an included collision shape 8 meters in front of its firing point, while a shape 12 meters away is beyond that configured reach. Increasing the value permits farther selections; it does not change the length or strength of a constraint already created.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.mode
member.summary: Selects the connection behavior, or removal, used when the current selection is released.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits simulated movement. The modes are Tether, which limits endpoint separation; Weld, which locks relative position and rotation; BallSocket, which locks position while allowing rotation; Elastic, which gives the separation limit a spring effect; EntangleRotation, which locks relative rotation while permitting position movement; and EntagleVelocity, which uses resistance to relative movement while leaving the position and rotation axes free. Remove looks for a tracked connection on the first selected object and requests its cleanup.

The mode-cycle input advances through these seven modes and wraps from Remove to Tether. It requests mode audio and updates the icon’s texture offset. The current value is read on release, so changing modes during a selection changes what that release attempts.

Assigning the field directly does not play the mode sound, update the icon, create or remove a connection, or change existing joints. Creation needs at least one selected Marrow body, the game’s simulated-body component, and rejects two endpoints on the same body. Remove deletes a selected ConstraintTracker connection rather than every physics joint on the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.modeSFX
member.summary: Supplies the sound-clip collection passed to the audio system when the player cycles constraint modes.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a saved sound recording. The mode-cycle input first changes the mode, then passes this entire clip array to the 3D audio system at the tool’s local origin, and afterwards updates the icon. The local origin is position (0, 0, 0) relative to the tool’s transform.

The tool does not index this array with the selected mode number; it is a collection for the audio request, not an automatic one-clip-per-mode table. Assigning this array or assigning mode directly does not play a sound. These clips are separate from the grab, lock, release, and stop requests sent through sfx.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.sfx
member.summary: References the sound controller receiving the tool’s selection, connection-lock, release, and detach-stop requests.

remarks.para: After a successful first selection, the tool calls this controller’s Grab method. After the creation path has made its joint and trackers, it calls GravLocked and then Release. Remove mode and release paths rejected because both bodies are missing or identical still reach Release without a lock request.

Detaching the hand calls StopSound after hiding the aiming objects. These are requests to the sound component; the field itself does not create or remove a physics joint, a connection limiting simulated movement. Mode-cycle audio uses modeSFX through the separate 3D audio system.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Constrainer.triggerGrip
member.summary: Connects the tool to hand-attachment and held-input events so it can select endpoints and create or remove constraints.

remarks.para: A Grip is the handle component a player’s hand attaches to. OnEnable, Unity’s call when the component becomes active, registers callbacks for hand attachment, detachment, and updates while attached. A callback is a function saved to run when an event occurs. OnDisable removes those registrations.

Attachment shows the first laser and icon. Attached updates read the hand/controller input to cycle modes and run the trigger-down, held, and release actions. Detachment hides the icon and both lasers, stops sound, and clears the missed-first-cast flag.

Provide this grip before enabling the tool. Replacing the reference while enabled does not move the already registered callbacks to the new grip automatically. Holding the grip alone does not guarantee a valid raycast or a created constraint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.attachPoint
member.summary: Supplies this end’s moving marker position for the constraint’s visual line.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. The Constrainer normally creates a separate endpoint helper at its selected attachment location, parenting it to the selected object when appropriate so that the marker moves with that object. The tracker reads its world position for the drawn line; with several trackers on an object, Constrainer.SelectConstraint also uses these positions to choose which constraint the tool is pointing toward.

Moving this helper changes the visual endpoint on the next line refresh. The tracker’s drawing routines do not copy that position into the physical joint’s anchors, so this is not a live control for moving the physics connection. SetupTracker stores the supplied reference, while ordinary updates read its current position.

Use a dedicated helper object for this reference. DeleteConstraint destroys its entire GameObject, not just its Transform; assigning the original constrained object’s Transform would make that object a deletion target. Line updates require this reference and the counterpart’s attachment to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.isHost
member.summary: Enables this tracker’s automatic refresh of the shared visual line.

remarks.para: When true, the tracker’s per-frame Update routine writes the two line endpoints only if lineRenderer.isVisible is true, meaning Unity reports that renderer as visible. When false it skips this automatic drawing work. A host still needs a valid renderer, counterpart and attachment transforms; the flag does not create them.

The Constrainer creates a pair that shares one line renderer and sets one tracker’s host flag. This lets one end refresh the shared drawing. SetupTracker itself does not assign isHost, so set it explicitly when assembling a pair through that routine.

This flag does not determine ownership of the physics joint. Both trackers can delete the constraint, and Update checks for a missing or destroyed joint before the host test. Explicit UpdateLines also ignores this flag and the visibility test. Changing it stores the drawing flag rather than transferring a physics connection to another body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.joint
member.summary: Identifies the connection that this tracker monitors and removes.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives movement between bodies. The Constrainer creates the selected connection and stores the same MarrowJoint on both endpoint trackers. Its movement rules belong to that joint; the tracker does not select a new constraint mode or rebuild a connection when this reference changes.

The per-frame Update routine requests DeleteConstraint if this joint is missing or has been destroyed. DeleteConstraint also requests destruction of a still-valid stored joint while removing the paired endpoint helpers. The joint’s own OnDestroy routine disconnects its bodies and removes the underlying Unity connection.

Keep this reference consistent on both trackers. Assigning another joint changes what this tracker watches and can destroy, without updating otherTracker or its reference. Setting it to null is not simply a way to disable drawing: the next Update attempts to remove this tracker’s constraint helpers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.lineRenderer
member.summary: Provides the two-endpoint drawing shared with the other .

remarks.para: A LineRenderer is Unity’s component for drawing a line through configured positions. The Constrainer creates one renderer with two positions and supplies that same component to both trackers. Endpoint writes use the attachment transforms’ world positions; use world-space rendering, since the tracker does not convert them to line-local coordinates.

The host’s automatic Update refreshes the line only when the renderer reports itself visible. Calling UpdateLines explicitly writes both positions without those host or visibility checks. Either path requires a valid renderer and attachment pair; a missing renderer is not safely optional for a host or a direct UpdateLines call. A nonhost can skip automatic line work, and deletion can skip an absent renderer.

Changing this reference does not create a renderer, set its position count or update the counterpart’s reference. DeleteConstraint requests destruction of this component. The visual line is feedback for the connection; it does not provide the physics constraint itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ConstraintTracker.otherTracker
member.summary: Links to the whose attachment supplies the opposite visual endpoint.

remarks.para: The Constrainer creates two trackers and points each at the other. They share the same MarrowJoint and line renderer, but have separate attachment helper transforms. UpdateLines reads this counterpart’s attachment world position for vertex 0 and this tracker’s position for vertex 1. A vertex is an endpoint of the drawn line.

Deleting this end also targets the counterpart’s attachment GameObject and tracker component. It does not recursively call the counterpart’s DeleteConstraint. A GameObject is the Unity scene object containing that helper. An existing counterpart therefore needs a valid attachment reference for both drawing and paired deletion.

Assigning another tracker changes where the line reads its opposite endpoint and which tracker its deletion can remove. It does not automatically create a reciprocal link, make the joint references match, or connect different objects in physics. Set up the complete pair rather than changing this link alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.IsMenuTapDisabled
member.summary: Stops the normal controller menu-tap detector from processing short presses while the flag is true.

remarks.para: OpenController normally records when the mapped menu button goes down and reports a menu tap when it is released in less than 0.2 seconds of unscaled time. Unscaled time counts real elapsed seconds even when the game is slowed. The detector uses one short press-and-release; it does not require a double tap.

When this flag is true, OpenController skips that detection block. It also skips the block that would clear a previous menu-tap pulse, so enabling the flag does not guarantee an already cached pulse becomes false. The controller's normal input caching and grip calculation still run.

The UI rig refreshes this flag from the popup menu's activated state, so a manual change can be replaced by a later UI update. The mapped physical button depends on the controller type; this does not universally disable every menu input.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.IsPaused
member.summary: Whether this rig's latest early update has suspended its normal input and tracking work.

remarks.para: The base early update sets the effective pause state when the shared pause request is true, MarrowGame is not initialized, or the current level-loading session is not DONE. OpenControllerRig skips its normal polling/pose work while this state is true, and RigManager returns before its later early-update passes.

IsPaused reads this cached per-rig result. Its protected setter instead changes the static request shared by all ControllerRig instances; each rig computes its own result on its next base early update. Clearing the shared request therefore does not bypass initialization or loading conditions. Writing _isPausedFinal directly is temporary because that calculation replaces it.
The input getters can still return the previous cached button and axis values while paused. This property does not itself call TimeManager or pause every Unity system.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._axisPrimary
member.summary: The processed two-dimensional movement input supplied to the locomotion rig. Read through .

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. Touchpad devices have additional mappings.

A deadzone is the small region around a stick’s centered position whose deflection is treated as no input. Where MagnitudeRemapAxis is used, overall stick magnitude means the radial distance of the X/Y pair from center; that helper compares it with a lower threshold and linearly rescales the vector magnitude between configured thresholds. Separately, a configured AnimationCurve selects the movement-direction angle; it does not do the magnitude remap. The normal VR path then rotates movement into the center-of-pressure reference orientation, the orientation of the rig’s balance-reference transform. These stored components are unitless sideways and forward/back movement input in that frame, not velocity in meters per second.

RemapRig uses this vector with GetPrimaryAxisDirty to calculate movement. An active seat can take over the input: its base handler captures both offered axis vectors, and when the handler takes the input, OpenControllerRig clears both axis vectors to zero and clears the movement-active flag. The getter does not clamp components or promise a universal −1-to-1 range.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._axisPrimaryDirty
member.summary: Whether the primary movement input passes the current device path's activity test. Read through .

remarks.para: In normal OpenControllerRig paths this activity flag is set from stick magnitude and the device-specific deadzone, not by comparing frames. Overall stick magnitude is the radial distance of the X/Y pair from center; a deadzone is the small centered region ignored as input. In the undefined-controller branch, for example, X² + Y² must be greater than 0.01, equivalent to radial magnitude greater than 0.1. Other device paths use MagnitudeRemapAxis: it applies a lower threshold and linearly rescales the vector between configured thresholds, rather than evaluating an AnimationCurve response curve. The activity thresholds vary by device.

A steadily held stick can keep this true while its position is unchanged. RemapRig receives it as inputPressed for movement. If an active seat takes the offered input, OpenControllerRig clears this flag and both axis vectors. GetPrimaryAxisDirty only reads the cached flag; it does not consume or reset it.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._axisSecondary
member.summary: The control vector used to calculate turning and virtual body-height input.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. Touchpad devices have additional mappings.

On the secondary axis, X is sideways and supplies turning; Y is up/down and can supply signed virtual height input. Both are unitless. abs(Y) measures vertical amount without direction, and abs(X) measures sideways amount without direction. Height input requires the strict gate abs(Y) > 0.2 and abs(X) < 0.65; within it the value is sign(Y) × clamp((abs(Y) − 0.2) / 0.8, 0, 1), where sign preserves up/down direction and clamp limits the amount to 0..1. With X = 0, Y = −0.6 gives −0.5; Y = 0.6 gives 0.5. A large sideways value can therefore turn while suppressing height input.

Device-specific touchpad processing can synthesize the secondary jump-button state. This cached vector itself does not move the avatar; OpenControllerRig derives other input caches and RemapRig consumes them.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._crouch
member.summary: The signed input for lowering or raising the virtual body, separate from the player physically bending down. Read through .

remarks.para: On normal OpenControllerRig input, the secondary-axis X component is sideways and Y is up/down; both are unitless. abs(Y) measures the vertical amount without its direction, while abs(X) measures sideways amount without its direction. Input is accepted only when abs(Y) > 0.2 and abs(X) < 0.65. Then the value is sign(Y) × clamp((abs(Y) − 0.2) / 0.8, 0, 1): sign(Y) supplies the up/down direction and clamp limits the normalized amount to 0..1. With X = 0, Y = −0.6 gives −0.5 and Y = 0.6 gives 0.5; otherwise the cached value is zero. The bounds are strict, so equality does not pass.

RemapRig later uses this signed input for virtual body height: negative requests a lower target and positive requests a higher one. In CrouchHold, the per-update adjustment bound scales with 2 × deltaTime × the input amount × avatar agility; deltaTime is elapsed scaled game time in seconds, and avatar agility scales how quickly the height target can change. Current body height, physical support, and other height limits can restrict the result. This is a unitless adjustment request, not a distance or permanent height percentage.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._crouchInput
member.summary: Whether the secondary axis currently requests a virtual body-height adjustment. Read through .

remarks.para: On normal OpenControllerRig input, secondary-axis X is sideways and Y is up/down; both are unitless. abs(Y) measures how far the input moves vertically without regard to whether it is positive or negative. The cached flag is true only when abs(Y) > 0.2 and abs(X) < 0.65, for either vertical direction. For example, (0, −0.6) passes, while (0.7, −0.6) fails because the sideways amount is too large. This reports an input request, not the avatar’s current height or whether the player physically crouched.
RemapRig receives this flag alongside the signed value from GetCrouch for its later body-height calculation; the flag alone does not move the avatar.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._isPaused
member.summary: The shared pause request checked by ControllerRig instances when calculating their effective pause state.

remarks.para: The protected IsPaused setter writes this static flag. Setting it true makes each instance become effectively paused on its next base early update; it is not private to the rig whose setter was used. OpenControllerRig uses this request as part of its platform-pause handling.

Setting it false only releases this request. The rig can remain paused while the game is not initialized or its level-loading session is not DONE. IsPaused returns the calculated _isPausedFinal value, not this flag directly; direct writes do not immediately refresh that value or call the audio/time pause handlers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._lastBodyPose
member.summary: The stored BodyPose object available alongside the rig's current pose data. Read through .

remarks.para: A BodyPose packages joint orientations, limb-extension amounts, hand/torso relationships, root/head positions, and a timestamp. The constructor creates an object for this storage. lastBodyPose returns the same reference held by _lastBodyPose; reading it does not make a copy or capture the current joints.

Assigning lastBodyPose replaces that reference without applying its contents to the skeleton. If code needs a stable snapshot, it must copy the pose values rather than merely save another reference to the same object. No automatic refresh of this storage was verified in the audited ControllerRig and OpenControllerRig early-update methods, so do not assume the name guarantees the previous frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._primaryAButton
member.summary: Whether the primary role's mapped face-button input is held in the cached sample.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. Touchpad devices have additional mappings.

The normal controller path uses its A-button input, but the physical mapping depends on the device; some touchpad paths synthesize the secondary button from a gesture. This is a logical action state, so it is not guaranteed to mean the button labelled A on every controller.
The time-control routine separately receives the Down and Up edges. Holding this cached value true is not the same as repeatedly pressing the slow-motion control.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._primaryAButtonDown
member.summary: Whether the primary role's mapped face-button input is newly pressed in the cached sample.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. Touchpad devices have additional mappings.

The normal controller path uses its A-button input, but the physical mapping depends on the device; some touchpad paths synthesize the secondary button from a gesture. This is a logical action state, so it is not guaranteed to mean the button labelled A on every controller.

Down marks the press transition and Up marks the release transition. Holding the button for several updates keeps the held state true without producing a new Down each update. These edge values belong to the input sample, not to each getter call.

OpenControllerRig passes the Down edge to its time-control routine, which can request a decrease in time scale when the time-control conditions allow it. Time scale is the multiplier for the scaled game clock: 1 is normal speed and 0.5 advances scaled time at half speed; unscaled time is unaffected. This edge requests the conditional TimeManager step and does not itself set the final time scale.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._primaryAButtonUp
member.summary: Whether the primary role's mapped face-button input is newly released in the cached sample.

remarks.para: Primary and secondary are control roles, not fixed left and right hands. In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. The normal controller path uses its A-button input, but the physical mapping depends on the device; some touchpad paths synthesize the secondary button from a gesture. This is a logical action state, so it is not guaranteed to mean the button labelled A on every controller.

Down marks the press transition and Up marks the release transition. Holding the button for several updates keeps the held state true without producing a new Down each update. These edge values belong to the input sample, not to each getter call.

On a normal OpenControllerRig update, this release arms the pending time-control return only when the current time-scale step is positive. The routine sets its deadline to Time.unscaledTime + 0.25 seconds. Continued primary-stick TOUCH refreshes it to the current unscaled time + 0.25 seconds. On a later no-touch update after the deadline has passed, the routine requests TimeManager.TOGGLE_TIMESCALE. This cached edge does not establish the visible slow-motion duration by itself.

A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._primaryStick
member.summary: Whether the primary role's mapped stick or touchpad control is pressed in the cached sample.

In OpenControllerRig, ordinary right-handed thumbstick controls use the left controller for primary movement and the right controller for secondary turning, height adjustment, and jumping; the handedness setting swaps them. This is the mapped primary stick-button or touchpad-button held state. It records the device’s button report; moving the axis sideways alone is separate. Down marks the press transition and Up marks the release transition. Holding the button for several updates keeps the held state true without producing a new Down each update. These edge values belong to the input sample, not to each getter call.
RemapRig uses the held state to charge its jump pose and the Up state to request Jump. Jump checks jumpEnabled before starting; reading this cache alone does not make the player jump.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig._smoothTwist
member.summary: The turning-angle change, in degrees, calculated for the current controller update. Read through .

remarks.para: OpenControllerRig writes this for both smooth turning and the smoothed release of a snap-turn request. In the smooth path it combines the smoothed sideways input, turn-speed setting, update duration, and time-scale correction. It is a per-update angle, not a torso bend, an absolute facing direction, or degrees per second.

RemapRig applies this angle around its up direction, pivoting at the physical rig's center-of-pressure position (its balance-reference point) when the player has no active seat. For example, a value of 2 requests a 2-degree turn for that update, before any other queued rotation. A snap turn can spread its requested angle over multiple updates.

The normal supported OpenControllerRig device paths update this cache in their unpaused early-update input pass. Reading it does not poll the device or clear the value. A paused rig can retain the last cached value, so check IsPaused before treating it as current input. Other ControllerRig subclasses can provide different input sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.lastBodyPose
member.summary: The stored BodyPose object available alongside the rig's current pose data.

remarks.para: A BodyPose packages joint orientations, limb-extension amounts, hand/torso relationships, root/head positions, and a timestamp. The constructor creates an object for this storage. lastBodyPose returns the same reference held by _lastBodyPose; reading it does not make a copy or capture the current joints.

Assigning lastBodyPose replaces that reference without applying its contents to the skeleton. If code needs a stable snapshot, it must copy the pose values rather than merely save another reference to the same object. No automatic refresh of this storage was verified in the audited ControllerRig and OpenControllerRig early-update methods, so do not assume the name guarantees the previous frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.leftController
member.summary: The assigned controller input component for the physical left hand.

remarks.para: GetController with LEFT returns this already assigned reference. During ControllerRig.OnAwake initialization, the rig reads its leftController field and writes this rig into the controller’s contRig field, the controller’s reference back to its owning rig. OnAwake initializes that backlink; it does not assign leftController, so this reference must already be supplied before initialization.

This field always identifies the physical left side even when primary and secondary control roles swap. Replacing it later does not automatically write the new controller’s contRig backlink or transfer old input state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ControllerRig.rightController

remarks.para: GetController with RIGHT returns this already assigned reference. During ControllerRig.OnAwake initialization, the rig reads its rightController field and writes this rig into the controller’s contRig field, the controller’s reference back to its owning rig. OnAwake initializes that backlink; it does not assign rightController, so this reference must already be supplied before initialization.

This field always identifies the physical right side even when primary and secondary control roles swap. Replacing it later does not automatically write the new controller’s contRig backlink or transfer old input state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.RadiusCurve
member.summary: When variableRadius is enabled, sets the radius used for grab scoring and the hand's finger pose at different points along the cylinder.

remarks.para: The vertical axis is an absolute radius in meters, not a multiplier of Grip.radius. A flat curve at 0.03 gives a uniform 3 cm radius; a flat curve at 1 means a 1-meter radius.

For an attached hand, the horizontal input is its target position relative to targetTransform, measured along primaryMovementAxis. With primaryMovementAxis = (0, 0, 1), X = 0 is the center and X = 0.10 is 10 cm toward the positive end. This is distance, not a 0-to-1 percentage. A curve rising from 0.02 at X = -0.10 to 0.04 at X = 0.10 makes the hand pose wrap around a thicker section toward that end.

Grab scoring samples the prospective grab's local Z coordinate, limited to -limit through +limit, rather than measuring along an arbitrary primary axis. Keep the primary axis aligned with local Z and target scale at 1 for the same distance convention in both uses. The curve does not replace Grip.radius in every cylinder calculation; the large-radius hand-offset calculations still use that field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip._constraintJoints
member.summary: Stores each attached hand’s helper for keeping its physics connection aligned with the cylinder.

remarks.para: OnJointAttached creates and adds a helper, skeleton and joint updates read it, and OnDetachedFromHand removes it. Each helper works with a ConfigurableJoint, the physics connection controlling relative motion. This is runtime state, rather than a list of cylinder meshes or possible grabs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip._isJointPositionFree
member.summary: Tracks attached hands currently allowed to slide along the cylinder.

remarks.para: FreeJoint adds a hand; LockJoint and detachment remove it. IsJointFree also requires the same hand in _isJointRotationFree and a radius below _maxRadius. The length limit and hand-width clearance still constrain sliding; membership does not permit movement away from the cylinder.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip._isJointRotationFree
member.summary: Tracks attached hands currently allowed to turn along with the cylinder’s free-grip state.

remarks.para: FreeJoint adds a hand; LockJoint and detachment remove it. IsJointFree requires both free-state sets and a radius below _maxRadius. Other joint angular limits still apply, so this flag does not mean every rotation is unrestricted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip._maxRadius
member.summary: Sets the radius threshold used to choose ordinary free-grip handling or large-cylinder handling.

remarks.para: This is a radius in meters, not the largest value sampled from RadiusCurve. IsJointFree requires Grip.radius to be strictly smaller than this threshold; above it, target and grab calculations use their large-radius paths. Raising it makes more cylinder radii eligible for the ordinary free state, provided the hand has both free-state flags. It does not resize the cylinder.
The constructor initializes it to about 0.078 m. This is private runtime configuration, and the audited code does not recalculate it as a maximum of the variable-radius curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.aspectRatio
member.summary: No oval-shape behavior was verified for this field in the audited cylinder code.

remarks.para: The constructor sets it to 1, but the audited methods do not read it when choosing hand orientation, scoring grabs, or configuring joints. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to make the grip prefer one angle or become oval. No working units or tuning range were established. This finding covers all 33 unique CylinderGrip method bodies and the audited PropFlashlight, CylinderElectronicGrip2, CylinderFuseGrip, and PropLeverSwitch methods. Other game classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.dynamicFriction
member.summary: No gameplay effect was verified for this field in CylinderGrip or the audited game subclasses.

remarks.para: The audited code sets an initial value but does not read this field to resist sliding or configure a joint. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to make the hand slide more or less easily. This finding covers CylinderGrip, PropFlashlight, CylinderElectronicGrip2, CylinderFuseGrip, and PropLeverSwitch; code outside those classes, including mods, was not exhaustively checked. No working units or useful tuning range were established.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.handWidth
member.summary: Stores half the hovering avatar’s measured palm width, in meters, for keeping the hand inside the cylinder ends.

remarks.para: For example, an 8 cm measured palm width stores 0.04. With limit 0.20, the ordinary held-hand center can travel 0.16 m each way because the game subtracts this half-width. If limit is smaller, ordinary center travel becomes zero and short-cylinder placement rules apply.

The hover update replaces this field with Avatar._palmSize.x × 0.5. The full measured width is the distance between the left index and little finger root pivots, with the ring finger root used instead if the little finger root is missing. It measures bone pivots rather than a visible mesh’s bounding-box width. It is one cached value on the grip, not a separate value for every hand; changing it manually can be overwritten on the next hover update. Despite the name, it is a half-width, not the full width.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.hasCapA
member.summary: Marks the cylinder's positive local Z end as capped when scoring possible grabs, and helps position the hand on very short cylinders.

remarks.para: With limit = 0.20 and target scale 1, this end is 20 cm along targetTransform's blue Z axis. Enabling the cap increases the score penalty for a proposed grab beyond that end, making it less preferred. Normal held-hand travel is limited at both ends even when this cap is off; this is not a switch for unlimited sliding.

When the cylinder is shorter than half the avatar's hand width, this cap can select an end offset for the hand target. The held-target calculation swaps hasCapA and hasCapB when the grip is flipped. A second attached hand can take over the positioning constraint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.hasCapB
member.summary: Marks the cylinder's negative local Z end as capped when scoring possible grabs, and helps position the hand on very short cylinders.

remarks.para: With limit = 0.20 and target scale 1, this end is 20 cm opposite targetTransform's blue Z axis. Enabling the cap increases the score penalty for a proposed grab beyond that end, making it less preferred. Normal held-hand travel is limited at both ends even when this cap is off; this is not a switch for unlimited sliding.

When the cylinder is shorter than half the avatar's hand width, this cap can select an end offset for the hand target. The held-target calculation swaps hasCapA and hasCapB when the grip is flipped. A second attached hand can take over the positioning constraint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.ignoreFlipOnZ
member.summary: Keeps the hand target in its normal end-for-end orientation instead of flipping it when grabbing from the opposite axial direction.

remarks.para: With false, grab scoring can record isZFlipped when the proposed hand direction opposes the cylinder’s primary direction. With true, it does not choose that flipped state. The recorded state also affects neutral target orientation and which cap the held-hand solver treats as each end.
This chooses a target orientation for a possible grab. It does not set a twist speed or remove the joint’s rotation limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.limit
member.summary: Sets the cylinder's half-length in meters and limits how far the hand target can slide from its center.

remarks.para: With limit = 0.20, the cylinder extends 20 cm each way from targetTransform's center, giving a nominal length of 40 cm. The held hand's center normally stops short of each end by half the avatar's hand width, so the whole hand fits. Its travel distance each way is the larger of zero and limit minus that half-width. With a half-width of 4 cm, this example allows 16 cm of travel each way.

Held travel follows primaryMovementAxis in targetTransform's orientation. Grab scoring separately uses targetTransform's local Z coordinate and its TransformPoint conversion; the example assumes a target scale of 1. A second hand can further restrict travel so the hands do not overlap. Very short cylinders use hasCapA and hasCapB to choose the hand's end offset instead of ordinary sliding.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.rotationalFrictionMult
member.summary: No rotation-resistance effect was verified for this field in the audited cylinder code.

remarks.para: The constructor sets it to 1, but the audited methods do not read it when setting joint drives or slide-helper resistance. Actual resistance calculations use controller squeeze, avatar grip strength, and other quantities. Changing this field is therefore not a verified way to make turning harder. No working units or tuning range were established. This finding covers all 33 unique CylinderGrip method bodies and the audited PropFlashlight, CylinderElectronicGrip2, CylinderFuseGrip, and PropLeverSwitch methods. Other game classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.staticFriction
member.summary: No gameplay effect was verified for this field in CylinderGrip or the audited game subclasses.

remarks.para: The audited code sets an initial value but does not read this field to resist hand movement or configure a joint. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to make a stationary hand stick more strongly. This finding covers CylinderGrip, PropFlashlight, CylinderElectronicGrip2, CylinderFuseGrip, and PropLeverSwitch; code outside those classes, including mods, was not exhaustively checked. No working units or useful tuning range were established.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CylinderGrip.variableRadius
member.summary: Enables RadiusCurve for choosing the cylinder radius used by grab scoring and the attached hand’s finger pose.

remarks.para: When true, RadiusCurve must be assigned. Its output is an absolute radius in meters, not a multiplier. With the usual unit local-Z primary axis and target scale 1, the curve input is signed axial distance from targetTransform’s center: 0.10 is 10 cm toward its positive end.

With false, these paths use Grip.radius. Turning the option on does not replace that field everywhere: large-radius positioning and the initial hover pose still read the base radius. A flat curve at 0.03 requests a 3 cm radius in the curve-controlled paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData.Name
member.summary: Returns the cartridge name used for ammo-inventory lookups, filling from the Unity asset name when needed.

remarks.para: If the stored name is null or empty, reading this property copies the asset's current Unity object name into the stored name and returns it. Awake, Unity's setup method when this asset is loaded, performs the same check. Reading this property can therefore fill a missing name even though it has no setter.

A nonempty stored name is returned unchanged. For example, once an asset named RoundA has supplied that cached name, renaming the asset to RoundB does not refresh the stored value. Clearing the stored name lets a later read fill it again. Whitespace is not treated as an empty name by this check.

The inspected ammo inventory saves a mapping from this text to an ammo-group name when registering cartridge groups. Later additions use the text to find the shared group count; an unmapped cartridge uses a count for its data object instead. Choose a stable name before registration. Changing it afterward does not rebuild the already saved mapping. An ammo group is a configured set of cartridge assets with one shared ammo total. If a second group registers a cartridge with the same name, the inventory keeps the first name-to-group mapping, so later additions using that name go to the first group's total. If the second group registers after the name already has a count, registration moves the current count to the second group's total but leaves the name mapped to the first, so later additions by name still update the first group. Use distinct names for cartridges in different groups.
The name can be a readable label or caliber identifier, such as 9mm. This getter treats it as text; it does not calculate bullet size, speed, or damage from the label.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData._name
member.summary: Stores the cached cartridge name returned by and used to look up its ammo group.

remarks.para: This is text, rather than a numerical caliber measurement. Awake, Unity's setup method when the asset is loaded, and the Name getter both fill a null or empty value from the asset's Unity object name. They leave any nonempty value unchanged.

The fallback is cached. Renaming the Unity asset afterward does not replace a nonempty stored name. For example, assigning CustomRound here makes later Name reads return CustomRound until this value is changed or cleared.

The inspected ammo inventory records this name when registering cartridge groups and looks it up again when adding ammo. Set the intended name before registration; editing this field later does not update the inventory's saved name-to-group mapping. An ammo group is a configured set of cartridge assets with one shared ammo total. If a later group reuses a name, the saved mapping stays with the first group, so new additions by name still go there. When a count already exists, registering the later group can move that count to its total without changing the mapping. Use different names for cartridges in different groups.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData.cartridgeCaseSpawnable
member.summary: Selects the spawn settings for the spent casing ejected by a gun.

remarks.para: A Spawnable contains a crate reference identifying the object template to create, plus spawn-policy settings. A template is a saved object setup that can be copied into the scene. This setting normally identifies the empty spent casing, such as a brass shell; its actual appearance comes from the chosen asset.

When a gun ejects a cartridge, an unspent round selects the intact-round setting instead. A spent round selects this setting. More precisely, the inspected ejection method uses the case setting for every nonempty state other than Unspent, provided the gun still has cartridge data.

The gun copies the selected Spawnable into its spawn request. The object is requested at the gun's shell spawn point, using that point's world position and orientation. Replacing this field afterward affects later requests, rather than changing the value already copied into that request.

Spawn work can pause and continue later. The gun clears its chamber without waiting for unfinished spawn work, so an empty chamber does not prove that a casing was successfully created. After a successful spawn, the gun expects a FirearmCartridge component, the part that controls the spawned round or casing, before applying its ejection motion and sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData.cartridgeSpawnable
member.summary: Selects the spawn settings for an intact cartridge ejected before it has been fired.

remarks.para: A Spawnable contains a crate reference identifying the object template to create, plus spawn-policy settings. A template is a saved object setup that can be copied into the scene. This setting represents the complete unfired round, including its bullet and case, rather than the flying projectile alone.

The inspected gun ejection method chooses this setting while its cartridge state is Unspent. For example, ejecting a loaded round without firing requests this intact-round object; ejecting after a shot normally requests the spent-case setting instead. No cartridge spawn is requested when the chamber is empty or its cartridge data is missing.

The selected Spawnable value is copied when the request begins. The gun requests the object at its shell spawn point's world position and orientation. Replacing this setting affects later requests and does not replace a value already captured for unfinished spawn work.

The gun clears the chamber without waiting for unfinished spawn work. Creation may finish later, and the request alone does not prove success. A successfully created object needs the FirearmCartridge component, the part controlling a round's ejection motion and sound, for the inspected completion path to use it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData.projectile
member.summary: Selects the projectile asset and flight, emission, and damage settings sent to the gun's projectile emitter.

remarks.para: When a gun fires its chambered cartridge, it passes this ProjectileData reference to the emitter, the system requesting the flying bullet objects. The emitter uses the gun's fire point as their starting reference: its position is the muzzle location, and its forward direction is the aiming direction. The cartridge and spent-case object settings serve separate ejection requests.

The profile's startVelocity is the initial simulated speed in metres per second, and mass is the simulated mass in kilograms. For example, 0.01 kilograms is 10 grams. Successful bullet setup copies those values and the attack-type category into the bullet's simulation data. The inspected setup does not assign that mass to a Rigidbody, Unity's component for moving an object through physics.

The emission mode chooses the launch pattern. In the inspected emitter, Point requests one centered projectile regardless of count. Cone requests that centered projectile plus additional scattered projectiles up to the requested count; count 5 requests one centered and four extra objects. Cone's radius controls the extra starting offsets in metres across a disk perpendicular to the aiming direction, and angle controls their spread in degrees. The other mode values, including Sphere, return without a spawn request in this emitter.

Bullet setup can finish after the firing request. Replacing this reference affects later shots; a bullet already given a profile keeps that earlier profile reference and its copied initial speed, mass, and attack type. Changing the earlier profile's damageMultiplier can still affect a later hit because the bullet reads that value when preparing its hit message.

The hit message uses damage = (currentSpeed / initialSpeed) × damageMultiplier. Here damage is the unitless attack-strength number sent to the target, currentSpeed is the bullet's speed at the hit in metres per second, initialSpeed is its saved starting speed in the same units, and damageMultiplier is the profile's unitless damage setting. At half the starting speed with multiplier 2, the message's damage value is 1. The target decides how that message changes its health. Use a positive starting speed because this calculation divides by it.

The gun also reads this profile's mass, starting speed, and count when calculating its recoil strength before emission. Changes to those settings can therefore change the gun's kick as well as projectile behavior. In particular, Point still requests one projectile even though the gun's recoil calculation reads count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.LootTableData.items
member.summary: Configures the ordered loot entries whose cumulative percentages decide which spawnable is returned.

remarks.para: Each entry pairs percentage, a number without physical units, with a spawnable description. The description identifies the object template to load and the pool policy, the rules for limiting and reusing spawned objects. GetLootItem reads this array when called; editing an entry affects later selections and does not itself create an object.

The roll is a whole number from 1 through 99. Starting at a total of 0, each entry wins for rolls greater than the previous total and at most the total after adding its percentage. Array order determines which object owns each range. For percentages 20 and 30, the first wins rolls 1–20, the second wins 21–50, and rolls 51–99 select no entry.

The method does not normalize the percentages. Zero covers no rolls, decimal boundaries can make the actual chance differ from the number's name, and large early totals can prevent later entries from winning. Keep the array assigned; a missing array causes an error. An assigned empty array yields an empty description.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.MagazineData.platform
member.summary: Text label checked against a weapon’s magazine socket to decide whether the magazine can enter it.

remarks.para: In AmmoSocket’s insertion check, the incoming magazine’s MagazineState supplies this MagazineData. The socket compares this platform string with its own platform string and rejects a different value. An AmmoSocket is the weapon’s magazine insertion point; MagazineState holds the item’s current ammunition and its settings reference.

This method has an earlier special-case return too: if the socket platform matches a separate string constant, it returns before comparing the magazine’s platform or reaching the later capacity checks. The native body does not identify that constant’s text.

For example, if you choose the label rifle_A for a magazine, use the same text on its matching socket. Passing this comparison still leaves the socket’s other insertion checks, such as available capacity. Set the label during weapon and magazine setup; it is a name with no physical units.
AmmoSocket is marked obsolete in the game’s metadata. This describes its verified insertion check; it does not establish the compatibility rules of every other socket implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.MagazineData.rounds
member.summary: Configured magazine capacity in whole cartridges, used when loading or refilling its ammunition state.

remarks.para: A cartridge is one round of ammunition. MagazineState.Initialize caps a requested starting count at this capacity, and Refill replaces the loaded list with this many cartridges. SetCartridge also caps its requested count, while AddCartridge limits how many it can add. Use a nonnegative whole number; capacity 0 produces an empty refill.

For example, with capacity 30, initialization requesting 50 cartridges loads 30. A partly used magazine can have 7 cartridges left while rounds remains 30. The live loaded count is MagazineState.AmmoCount, which counts its current cartridge list.

Changing this setting does not itself refill or remove existing cartridges. Initialization, refill and later count-changing calls read the capacity when they run. Reducing it below an existing loaded count does not make AddCartridge remove the excess; that method only adds when there is room.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.MagazineData.spawnable
member.summary: Selects the magazine item that inventory and forced-loading routines request from the object spawner.

remarks.para: A Spawnable contains a crate reference identifying a saved item and a policy for creating or reusing copies. A crate here is an asset description of the item to create. InventoryAmmoReceiver.SwitchMagazine registers and copies this setting into its magazine-switch request. AmmoSocket.ForceLoadAsync also reads it when requesting a magazine.

The force-loading operation can wait for spawning to finish. It then looks for the Magazine component, the attached part that handles the item’s ammunition, initializes it and inserts its plug. Merely assigning spawnable does not establish that an item has already appeared or been inserted.

Use a crate configured as the intended magazine item, with its Magazine and MagazineState references set up. ForceLoadAsync takes capacity from the returned item’s own MagazineState.magazineData. Changing the selected crate does not automatically copy this asset’s platform or rounds into that returned item’s settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.AttackType
member.summary: Sets the attack category copied into each projectile's later hit report.

remarks.para: Projectile setup copies this value into that projectile. When it hits something, its attack report includes the copied category so the receiving object can decide how to handle the hit. Changing the data asset afterward does not change the category already copied into a launched projectile.

The named flags are Piercing, Blunt, Fire, Slicing, Stabbing and None. Flags are category bits that can be combined. For example, Piercing labels the report as a piercing attack; this field does not itself select a flight direction or make the projectile pass through a wall. The default is None, which is a category value and does not prevent this projectile code from sending a hit report.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.angle
member.summary: Controls how far additional CONE projectiles can turn away from the emitter's forward direction, in degrees.

remarks.para: CONE first requests one projectile straight forward. For each additional request, it picks a random sideways direction in the emitter's right-and-up plane, then turns forward toward it by a random limit from 0.1 times angle to angle. The angle is converted from degrees to radians for that calculation. For example, angle 20 gives additional requests turn limits from 2 to 20 degrees; it is not a 20-degree angle shared equally on both sides.

The turn is toward a sideways direction, so a large limit does not require the projectile to turn past that direction. The resulting orientation follows the emitting transform, an object's position and orientation record. POINT does not read this field, the centre CONE request stays straight, and SPHERE has no emission branch in this build.
The editor slider shows 0 through 180 degrees. That slider range is not a runtime check in the emitter. The field is read while each additional CONE request is calculated.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.count
member.summary: Controls the total number of spawn requests in CONE emission, including its first centre projectile.

remarks.para: With CONE and a count of 4, the emitter requests one straight projectile from the centre and three additional projectiles with random starting offsets and turns. POINT always requests one projectile and ignores count. SPHERE, and other unhandled emission values, request none in the inspected emitter.

CONE makes the first request before testing the additional-copy loop, so even a count of zero or a negative value still requests that first projectile. The editor slider shows 1 through 10, but the emitter does not clamp larger runtime values to 10.

This is a unitless count of requests, not a guarantee of successfully created projectiles. Spawning runs asynchronously, meaning it can finish later while the game continues. Asset availability and the spawned object's required Projectile component still determine the outcome. Changing this asset does not add or remove objects that have already spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.damageMultiplier
member.summary: Scales the damage number sent in a projectile's hit report, using its current speed relative to its saved starting speed.

remarks.para: At impact, the report's damage is (currentSpeed / startingSpeed) times damageMultiplier. currentSpeed is the projectile's current flight speed in metres per second. startingSpeed is the baseline speed copied from startVelocity during setup, also in metres per second. Their ratio and this multiplier have no physical units; the result is a game damage number, rather than a force in Newtons.

For example, if the starting speed is 100 metres per second, the impact speed is 50 metres per second and the multiplier is 2, the reported damage is 1. At unchanged speed the reported damage is 2. The object receiving the hit decides how that number affects its health or other behavior.

The default multiplier is 1. The projectile reads this field from the data asset when it builds each hit report, so a change can affect an already launched projectile's later hit. Mass is used separately for impact pushes and is not a factor in this damage formula. This code does not clamp the multiplier or protect this division from a zero starting speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.emissionType
member.summary: Chooses which emission pattern handles the configured .

remarks.para: POINT requests one projectile at the emitting transform's centre, facing its forward direction. CONE requests that same centre projectile, then adds random copies until the configured count is reached. Those additional copies can start within a disk in the emitter's right-and-up plane and turn away from forward according to angle.

For example, CONE with count 4 requests one straight centre projectile and three spread projectiles. POINT with count 4 still requests only one. SPHERE is a declared option, but the complete emitter in this build has no branch that spawns its spherical pattern; that value requests no projectile.

The default field value is POINT. The emitting transform is an object's position and orientation record; its local axes turn with that object. Each request starts a separate asynchronous spawn, so requesting a pattern does not prove every copy has finished spawning.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.mass
member.summary: Sets the mass, in kilograms, copied into a projectile's impact-momentum calculations.

remarks.para: The default is 1 kilogram. Projectile setup copies this mass into its own stored value. Changing the data asset after launch does not change the copied mass of that projectile.

The projectile combines mass in kilograms with current speed in metres per second to calculate momentum, in kilogram-metres per second, which is also Newton-seconds. An impulse is a push that changes momentum. If the projectile is configured to apply its remaining impact force and hits a Rigidbody, a body moved by Unity physics, this momentum helps determine that push.

For example, a 0.2-kilogram projectile at 20 metres per second has momentum 4 Newton-seconds. For a hit that stops it completely, the inspected push path applies twice that amount, 8 Newton-seconds, along its flight direction, when that optional impact-push setting is enabled.

This setup path stores the value for projectile calculations; it does not assign a Rigidbody's mass. In the inspected flight and hit code, this mass does not control falling acceleration or appear in the damage-number formula.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.radius
member.summary: Sets the maximum starting offset for additional CONE projectiles, measured in metres from the emission centre.

remarks.para: Each extra CONE request picks a random point inside a unit disk, a circle filled with points up to distance 1 from its centre, and multiplies its two coordinates by radius. The offset lies in the emitter's right-and-up plane and turns with the emitter. For example, radius 0.1 allows extra projectiles to begin up to 10 centimetres from the centre, rather than all beginning exactly 10 centimetres away.

The centre CONE projectile and the single POINT projectile start at the centre and ignore radius. This field describes an emission offset, not the size of a bullet or the width of its collision test. The complete Projectile flight code uses line-based raycasts to test its travel.

The editor slider shows 0 through 1, but the emitter does not enforce that range at runtime. The calculated offset is stored as a local position relative to the emitter, using its Transform (position, orientation, and scale); the emission rotation is stored relative to the same Transform. When SpawnAsync starts, it converts that local position and rotation to a world position and rotation before requesting the object, then waits for the spawn result. If the result has a Projectile component, SetBulletObject uses the current emitter Transform and saved local pose again to place the projectile. Changes to the emitter's position, orientation, or scale while the request is pending can therefore affect the projectile's final position and rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.spawnable
member.summary: Supplies the used for each projectile spawn request.

remarks.para: A spawnable identifies an item crate, the asset containing the object template to create, and carries its spawning-policy data. Projectile registration passes this value to the shared asset spawner to prepare it. Emission passes it to that spawner for each requested copy; registration alone does not create a launched projectile.

Spawning is asynchronous: loading or obtaining the object can finish later while the game continues. After the spawner returns an object, the emitter looks for a Projectile component on it.
