If that component is present, the emitter supplies this data asset and starts the projectile's flight setup. An object without that component is not initialized as a Projectile by this path.

For example, assign a crate whose object has a Projectile component to make these mass, speed and hit settings take effect through the emitter. Changing the spawnable does not replace already created objects, and a request is not a success report.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData.startVelocity
member.summary: Sets a projectile's initial flight speed and saved damage baseline, in metres per second.

remarks.para: This is a speed number, not a three-component direction vector. The default is 1 metre per second. Setup copies it into the projectile's starting-speed baseline and current speed; the flight direction comes from the projectile's final forward orientation.

Update skips a finished projectile, one that has reached its impact-particle limit, or one not enabled to simulate; it also skips a second call in the same game frame (one pass through the game's Update loop). On an eligible update, the projectile tests a travel distance of current speed times that frame's game-time duration, then advances along its current direction when no hit intercepts. Speed is in metres per second and duration is in seconds, so the travel distance is metres. For example, 100 metres per second over 0.02 seconds gives 2 metres of travel before collision effects.

Bullet drop, when enabled on the spawned Projectile, can change its current speed and direction as gravity is applied. The copied starting speed stays as the baseline in the hit formula currentSpeed / startingSpeed times damageMultiplier. Changing this asset after launch does not replace the copied speeds of an already initialized projectile.

The normal ProjectileEmitter path does not pass an emitting Rigidbody into flight setup. Other callers of SetBulletObject can add that body's velocity to the initial speed calculation; a Rigidbody is a body moved by Unity physics. This number therefore need not remain the projectile's speed throughout its flight.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.SpawnPolicyData.groupByCrate
member.summary: Gives each crate its own spawn-policy budget when true, or lets different crates share a budget when false.

remarks.para: A newly constructed SpawnPolicyData settings object initializes this flag to true. This is the runtime constructor default; a serialized settings asset can store a different value.

A crate is the stored item definition that identifies what to spawn. The game chooses a policy using this settings asset and the spawn request’s groupID, an optional numeric label used to separate groups of requests. With this flag true, the crate’s identifying barcode is also included, so different crates have separate tracked counts and reuse choices. With it false, requests using the same settings asset and groupID can share those counts and choices across different crates.

For example, with maxSize = 2, meaning a threshold of two tracked spawns including pending requests, two different crates can each reach that threshold when grouping is enabled. With grouping disabled, they share the threshold. GROW can still exceed it. Different settings assets or different group IDs remain separate.
This flag is read when a later request chooses its policy. Changing it does not move objects already tracked by an existing policy into the newly selected group, or despawn them immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.SpawnPolicyData.maxSize
member.summary: Number of tracked spawns, including pending requests, at which the policy starts applying its selected limit rule.

remarks.para: This is an object count, with no distance or time units. Before a request, the policy adds its successfully spawned objects still being tracked to requests still awaiting completion. If that total is below maxSize, it requests another object. At equality or above, it applies mode. GROW still allows the request; the reuse rules try to remove an existing tracked object first, while REUSENONE returns no object.

For example, with maxSize = 2, one tracked object plus one pending request already reaches the threshold. It does not have to wait for the second object to finish spawning. This is a policy-group threshold, rather than a cap on every object allocated or stored by the underlying pool, which keeps objects available for later reuse.

Changing it affects later request checks and does not immediately remove excess objects. Zero or a negative value sends even an empty group to the selected limit rule; it is not an automatic unlimited setting. A reuse rule cannot make a replacement when that group has no tracked object to remove.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.SpawnPolicyData.mode
member.summary: Chooses what a new spawn request does when the policy’s tracked count plus pending requests reaches maxSize.

remarks.para: maxSize is the threshold number of tracked objects and pending requests. Below it, the ordinary policy requests an object regardless of this selection. At or above it, GROW allows another request, so the threshold is not a hard cap. REUSENONE returns no object. REUSEOLDEST selects the first still-tracked successful spawn; REUSENEWEST selects the last. Successful objects enter that list after their requests complete, so this order follows completion rather than the objects’ original creation dates.

A reuse selection first calls the old object’s recycle notification, then despawns it through AssetSpawner, then requests the desired item from its pool. A notification is a callback, a routine called to report an action. This can affect an item still in the scene. With no tracked object available, the reuse rule returns no object, even if pending requests already fill the budget.

The requested item need not be the exact same Unity scene object that was removed: different crates can share a policy when groupByCrate is false, and each crate has its own underlying pool of reusable objects. Changing mode affects later requests; it does not itself start a request or remove existing objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.SpawnPolicyData.skipDisable
member.summary: Skips the pool’s final GameObject.SetActive(false) call when this policy despawns the object.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object. This setting is read during policy-managed despawning, including the removal performed by a reuse rule. With false, the pool calls SetActive(false) at the end. With true, it skips that final call. Earlier despawn and deinitialize callbacks run before this point and may change the object’s active state, so the setting does not guarantee that it remains active. The pool still performs despawn and cleanup notifications and moves the object from the pool’s spawned list to its available-for-reuse list; this is not a way to keep it counted as a managed spawn.

The order is despawn notification, cleanup of its registered pool behaviors, removal from the spawned list, addition to the reusable list, then deactivation when this option is false. A notification is a callback, a routine called to report an action; the despawn and cleanup callbacks run before the final deactivation decision and may change the object’s active state. The policy removes the object from its own tracked list after that pool operation returns.

Changing this flag affects later despawns using this policy; it does not activate or deactivate existing objects immediately. Objects spawned while bypassing the policy use the ordinary pool despawn path instead, so they do not use this setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Spawnable.crateRef
member.summary: Selects the warehouse crate whose asset the spawner will create or reuse.

remarks.para: This reference holds a barcode, the text identifier for an entry in the warehouse, BONELAB's asset catalog. A spawnable crate describes a prefab: a saved Unity object that can be copied into the scene. Assigning this reference chooses that asset; it does not create a scene object.

AssetSpawner.Register starts preparing the pool for this barcode and loading the crate's asset. A pool keeps objects that can be returned and reused instead of making a new copy each time. Register starts work that may finish later; a valid barcode alone does not prove that preparation has finished.

When spawning, AssetSpawner looks up the referenced crate and its registered pool. A missing crate or unavailable pool can produce no spawned object. For example, choose a crate for a basketball, prepare its pool, and then submit this Spawnable to the spawner to obtain a basketball instance. Check the completed spawn result before using that instance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Spawnable.policyData
member.summary: Selects the pool policy that limits outstanding spawns and decides whether another request grows the group, reuses an object, or produces no object.

remarks.para: This is a reference to a settings asset, not a count of currently spawned objects. AssetSpawner applies it when policyData exists and the spawn call's ignorePolicy argument is false. With no settings asset, or with ignorePolicy set to true, that call spawns directly from the crate's pool.

maxSize is a count of objects, with no distance or time unit. The ordinary policy compares this limit against the number of objects it tracks plus requests that are still waiting to finish. Below the limit it requests another object. At or above the limit, GROW still permits another spawn; REUSEOLDEST retires the first tracked object before requesting a replacement; REUSENEWEST retires the last tracked object; and REUSENONE produces no object. Reuse needs a tracked object to retire. The underlying pool may supply an already returned object, so requesting a replacement does not promise a particular object's identity.

For example, with maxSize set to 2 and mode set to REUSENONE, two outstanding spawns fill that policy's allowance. A third request produces no object until an earlier object is returned. With GROW, a third request remains allowed, so maxSize is not a hard cap in that mode.

AssetSpawner shares a runtime policy by the settings asset and the spawn call's groupID. groupID is an integer label for a group, not an object count. When groupByCrate is true, the crate's barcode also separates those groups. With groupByCrate false, different crates using the same settings and groupID can share the allowance. The runtime policy keeps the settings asset reference and reads its limit, mode, and skipDisable settings when needed.

skipDisable controls the return step: when true, returning an object to this pool skips switching its Unity GameObject inactive. A GameObject is Unity's container for an object and its components. The return still performs the pool's return notifications and bookkeeping. This setting does not hide an object based on its distance from the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge._isStatic
member.summary: Records the mode checked when MakeStatic and MakeDynamic disable or enable shellSfx.

remarks.para: True makes MakeStatic skip its change; false makes MakeDynamic skip its change. When switching modes, each method changes this flag before changing the enabled setting of shellSfx. OnPoolDeInitialize clears a true flag and enables that sound component.

This flag does not measure whether the cartridge is motionless or whether its Rigidbody, Unity’s physics component, is fixed in place. It also does not continually read shellSfx.enabled. Changing the flag directly does not change the sound component, and changing the sound component directly does not update the flag. For example, a true flag can coexist with a casing still moving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge._poolee
member.summary: Selects the pool component that receives this cartridge’s callback registration during Awake.

remarks.para: Poolee connects an object to the system that reuses spawned objects. Awake, Unity’s initial component setup call, registers this cartridge with the assigned reference so that its pool lifecycle functions can be called. The reference must be filled beforehand; Awake does not look it up.

This is a registration reference, not a live test of whether the object currently belongs to reusable pool storage. Changing it after Awake does not move the existing registration. Despawn follows the inherited marrowEntity reference and that entity’s Poolee instead. For normal setup, these references should refer to the same object’s intended pool lifecycle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.renderers
member.summary: Lists the visual components whose extra hide setting is changed by SetRenderActive and cleared during pool cleanup.

remarks.para: A renderer draws an object’s visible shape. SetRenderActive(false) sets forceRenderingOff to true on every entry, preventing those renderers from drawing. SetRenderActive(true) clears that extra hide setting. OnPoolDeInitialize calls the latter so the cartridge does not carry this hide setting into reuse.

For example, include both the casing renderer and any separate bullet renderer if both should follow these visibility changes. The array is read on each call rather than copied into a separate cache. It starts empty, which makes these calls do nothing; an assigned array must contain valid renderer references.

Clearing forceRenderingOff does not override a renderer’s own disabled state or an inactive scene object, so it does not guarantee visible pixels by itself. MakeStatic and MakeDynamic change the sound-component mode and leave this array’s visibility settings alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.shellSfx
member.summary: Supplies the shell sound component enabled or disabled by cartridge mode changes and called for ejection sound after a gun completes a cartridge spawn.

remarks.para: ShellSFX stores and plays casing impact and ejection sound effects. Reset, Unity’s editor setup call when adding or resetting a component, finds this component on the same scene object and stores it here. Awake does not find or replace it.

MakeStatic disables the component when entering static mode; MakeDynamic enables it when leaving that mode. Pool deinitialization enables it if the cartridge’s static-mode flag was true. These methods require a valid reference when performing the enable or disable.

In the inspected gun spawn sequence, the gun first waits for a successful spawned object, applies its cartridge launch movement and spin, then calls ShellEject on this sound component. A spawn request alone is not that completed sound call. The component’s enabled setting and direct sound-method calls are separate; this field is not an audio-volume value.

In the inspected Gun.SpawnCartridge sequence, the gun waits for a spawned object and gets its cartridge component, disables that cartridge’s colliders, applies ForceInDirection, and then calls ShellEject through this reference. A later delay comes before the collider re-enable call. If shellSfx is empty, execution fails at ShellEject and this sequence does not reach that later re-enable call. Reset can leave shellSfx empty when the same object has no ShellSFX, so this ejection path requires a valid reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.startAxisSpeed
member.summary: Scales the additional world-space spin applied by ForceInDirection, before randomized variation and inherited host spin.

remarks.para: The base value is in radians per second when the supplied startRotationAxis is a unit direction, meaning a vector of length 1. A radian measures rotation; one complete turn is about 6.28 radians. The construction default is 100 radians per second, about 16 turns per second, before random variation. World-space here means the scene’s shared X, Y, and Z frame, not axes relative to a parent. The linked MarrowEntity (the component grouping the cartridge’s gameplay and physics pieces) must have an anchor body that supplies a Rigidbody, and the supplied hostRigidbody must be non-null. If either required Rigidbody is missing, the native method fails before setting this spin.

For each world X, Y or Z component, the added angular velocity, meaning rotation per second, is that component of startRotationAxis multiplied by startAxisSpeed, a shared random multiplier from 1 to 2, and a component-specific multiplier from 0.75 to 1.25. The method adds the host Rigidbody’s world angular velocity and writes the result to the cartridge’s Rigidbody, Unity’s component for simulated physical motion. These are the same random multipliers used for the additional launch velocity during that call.

For example, with no host spin, startAxisSpeed 100, a rotation axis of (0, 1, 0), shared multiplier 1.5 and Y multiplier 1, the resulting Y spin is 150 radians per second. The axis is used at its supplied length, without being made length 1. Changing the field affects later ForceInDirection calls, rather than immediately changing a casing’s current spin.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge.startSpeed
member.summary: Scales the additional world-space launch velocity applied by ForceInDirection, before randomized variation and inherited host motion.

remarks.para: The base value is in Unity world units per second when the supplied startDirection is a unit direction, meaning a direction vector of length 1. It equals metres per second only if this scene uses one Unity world unit per metre. The construction default is 2. ForceInDirection reads this field at the time of the call and writes velocity to the cartridge’s Rigidbody, Unity’s component for simulated physical motion; it does not apply a continuing force each frame. World-space here means the scene’s shared X, Y, and Z frame, not axes relative to a parent. The linked MarrowEntity (the component grouping the cartridge’s gameplay and physics pieces) must have an anchor body that supplies a Rigidbody, and the supplied hostRigidbody must be non-null. If either required Rigidbody is missing, the native method fails before setting this velocity.

For each world X, Y or Z component, the added velocity is that component of startDirection multiplied by startSpeed, a shared random multiplier from 1 to 2, and a separate random multiplier for that component from 0.75 to 1.25. The host Rigidbody’s movement at the cartridge’s world position is then included, so a moving or rotating gun can add to the launch velocity. The component-specific multipliers also vary the direction slightly.

For example, with a stationary host, startSpeed 2, a direction of (1, 0, 0), shared multiplier 1.5 and X multiplier 1, the resulting X velocity is 3 Unity world units per second (3 m/s only if this scene uses one Unity world unit per metre). The method uses the supplied direction’s length as-is, so a length of 2 doubles its contribution. Changing the field later affects the next call, rather than rewriting an already moving casing’s velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.OnFlyEnabled
member.summary: Provides a shared no-argument notification called after a FlyingGun component enables its grip handlers.

remarks.para: OnEnable subscribes the triggerGrip attachment handler, then the detachment handler, then the held-update handler. After all three subscriptions it invokes this static Action if it is assigned. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; listeners here are being told the component has enabled.

It does not mean a hand has grabbed the gun, that the trigger is pressed or that no-clip was enabled. OnEnable does not change _noClipping before this notification. Every enabled instance uses the same static delegate, so the call has no instance or hand argument.
Use += to add a listener alongside existing listeners and -= to remove it when finished. Assigning a new delegate with = replaces the previous listeners.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._directionVel
member.summary: Stores a vector reset on grip attachment, without a verified steering role in the audited FlyingGun code.

remarks.para: OnTriggerHandAttached sets it to Vector3.zero. The complete checked FlyingGun class, its one-frame delay iterator and release callback do not pass it to a direction-smoothing calculation.

Steering instead updates _smoothedDirection with Vector3.RotateTowards. Changing _directionVel is therefore not an established way to change steering responsiveness here. This finding does not cover external game components or mods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._host
member.summary: Caches the gun's interaction host for physics mass and gun-entity collision handling.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, finds the InteractableHost on the same GameObject and stores it here. A callback is a routine Unity or game code calls to perform or report an action.

The held movement calculation reads its Rigidbody mass. No-clip methods use its MarrowBody/Marrow entity to toggle the gun's trackers and colliders. The other hand's held host is also compared with this reference so the gun itself is excluded from that extra held-object mass term.
Changing this cache does not transfer grip subscriptions or move the FlyingGun component. A valid host is required by the checked movement and collision-toggle paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._lastFixedTime
member.summary: Stores the scaled physics-time timestamp last copied by attachment or a completed held update.

remarks.para: The value comes from Time.fixedTime, in seconds on Unity's scaled physics clock. Attachment initializes it, and the held update writes it again after the movement, sound and three-ring rotation work succeeds.

No read that paces movement or computes a time difference from this field was found in the complete checked FlyingGun methods and delay/release routines. The movement uses Time.deltaTime directly. It is a stored timestamp rather than a configured update interval.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._noClipping
member.summary: Records whether the gun's no-clip collision-toggle path has completed enabling that state.

remarks.para: EnableNoClip disables the gun entity's trackers/colliders where applicable, then every cached player body's collision detection, then sets this true. DisableNoClip enables those systems first and clears the flag last. Grip attachment sets the flag false after the grab sound request.

The held toggle uses this flag to choose enabling versus disabling. Setting the boolean alone does not change any collisions, so it can become inconsistent with the physics state. canNoClip controls permission to enter through normal input; it is separate from this calculated state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._playerRbs
member.summary: Caches the player rig bodies whose collision detection is changed by no-clip.

remarks.para: The first trigger-grip attachment with no usable cache builds a 13-element array from that hand's physics rig: feet, knee, five torso/head bodies and both hands' hand/upper-arm/lower-arm bodies. These are Rigidbody components participating in the player's physics simulation.

EnableNoClip sets their detectCollisions false and DisableNoClip sets it true. Flight movement applies velocity changes through explicit rig references, rather than looping over this array to drag the player.

After grip detachment, a coroutine waits one frame, calls DisableNoClip and only then clears the array. A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue over several frames. The array is a cache for the attached player rig; replacing it changes the bodies affected by future collision toggles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._ringAngularDisplacement
member.summary: Stores a speed-driven animation value that controls the decorative rings' spin rates.

remarks.para: Every held update replaces it with 0.98 times its old value plus _targetSpeed. This is a numerical animation accumulator, not the total angle the rings have turned. The 0.98 multiplier keeps 98 percent of the old value per update, so its growth/decay depends on update count.

After updating it, the code computes a base spin rate of 90 plus 3 times this value, in degrees per second. Here 90 is the baseline degrees-per-second rate, and 3 converts each unit of this animation value into another 3 degrees per second. Ring A and C use that rate; ring B uses -0.5 times it, half as fast in the opposite direction.

For example, starting at 0 with a smoothed speed value of 10 produces an accumulator of 10 and a 120-degree-per-second base rate on that update. This field changes visual rotation, not the player's flight velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._smoothedDirection
member.summary: Stores the world-space direction gradually used for the desired flight velocity.

remarks.para: Attachment initializes it from the normalized whole-body velocity. While trigger pull is positive, held updates turn it toward firePoint.forward; otherwise they turn it toward the current whole-body velocity direction. Steering uses Vector3.RotateTowards with a maximum angular step of 14 radians per second times Time.deltaTime and no allowed magnitude change.

The desired velocity is this vector times _targetSpeed, before the later velocity-smoothing and gravity-compensation calculations. Its direction is in world axes, not gun-local axes. Later held updates overwrite changes made here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._targetAcceleration
member.summary: Stores the current acceleration state used while smoothing the flight speed.

remarks.para: Mathf.SmoothDamp receives this field by reference while updating _targetSpeed, so the calculation writes it after each step. Because the smoothed quantity is meters per second, this speed-change state is meters per second squared.

On attachment it is initialized from the player's whole-body acceleration projected along the whole-body velocity direction. Clearing it removes that scalar speed-smoothing momentum; later updates calculate it again.
It is not a requested thrust force or an acceleration target the code eases toward. The speed goal is calculated separately from maxSpeed and the trigger exponent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun._targetSpeed
member.summary: Stores the smoothed speed used to build the desired flight velocity.

remarks.para: The units are meters per second. Attachment initializes it from the magnitude of the player's whole-body velocity. The held update smooths it toward maxSpeed times triggerPull raised to speedCurveExponential, using a 0.35-second SmoothDamp time scale, _targetAcceleration by reference, and the frame duration.

triggerPull is the hand's dimensionless trigger amount. The exponent is dimensionless; maxSpeed supplies meters per second. For an illustrative maxSpeed of 10, pull 0.5 and exponent 2, the goal is 2.5 meters per second, while this stored speed approaches that goal over updates.

This is the smoothing output rather than the unsmoothed trigger goal. It also feeds the ring-animation accumulator. The later whole-body velocity calculation can differ because of steering, velocity smoothing, gravity compensation and collisions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.canNoClip
member.summary: Allows the normal held-input toggle to enter collision-free movement.

remarks.para: When the controller reports the mode-toggle button, an inactive no-clip state can be enabled only if this flag is true. An already active state can still be disabled when it is false.

Setting it false does not immediately restore collisions; it is read when that button path runs. The direct EnableNoClip method does not read it, and simply grabbing the trigger grip does not enable no-clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.firePoint
member.summary: Supplies the forward world direction the gun steers toward while the trigger is pressed.

remarks.para: With a positive trigger pull, the held update reads this transform's forward vector for its steering target. Releasing the trigger selects the current whole-body velocity direction instead.

The audited movement path does not apply force at this transform's position. It applies velocity changes to the player's rig bodies. Moving this transform without changing its orientation does not change the steering direction through this read.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.maxSpeed
member.summary: Scales the trigger-derived speed goal for the flight calculation.

remarks.para: It is meters per second. The goal is maxSpeed times triggerPull raised to speedCurveExponential: triggerPull is the hand's dimensionless amount, and the exponent is dimensionless. At pull 1 with a positive exponent, the goal equals maxSpeed.

For an illustrative maxSpeed of 10, half pull gives a goal of 5 meters per second with exponent 1, or 2.5 with exponent 2. The gun smooths its speed toward the goal with a 0.35-second time scale before computing desired velocity.

This is a goal scale rather than a hard clamp on the player's measured velocity. Existing motion, steering, gravity compensation, smoothing and contact physics also affect movement; attachment can initialize the stored speed above this value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.ringA
member.summary: Spins a decorative ring around its local Y axis at the shared animation rate. Driven by .

remarks.para: Each attached-grip update first sets the shared driver to 0.98 times _ringAngularDisplacement plus _targetSpeed. The 0.98 is a dimensionless retention per update; _targetSpeed is the smoothed flight-speed value. The driver is animation state, not an angle.

The base rate is 90 + 3 times that updated driver, in degrees per second: 90 is the baseline rate and 3 supplies 3 degrees per second for each driver unit. This ring adds base rate times frame seconds to its local Y rotation.

The animation runs on held updates even with zero trigger pull; the baseline can keep the ring spinning. The checked code does not establish which assigned ring is physically inner, middle or outer. All three references must be valid for the complete rotation path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.ringB
member.summary: Spins a decorative ring around its local Y axis at half the shared rate in the opposite direction. Driven by .

remarks.para: Each attached-grip update first sets the shared driver to 0.98 times _ringAngularDisplacement plus _targetSpeed. The 0.98 is a dimensionless retention per update; _targetSpeed is the smoothed flight-speed value. The driver is animation state, not an angle.

The base rate is 90 + 3 times that updated driver, in degrees per second: 90 is the baseline rate and 3 supplies 3 degrees per second per driver unit. This ring multiplies that rate by -0.5 and by frame seconds, then adds the resulting local Y rotation.

The animation runs on held updates even with zero trigger pull; the baseline can keep the ring spinning. The checked code does not establish which assigned ring is physically inner, middle or outer. All three references must be valid for the complete rotation path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.ringC
member.summary: Spins a decorative ring around its local Y axis at the shared animation rate. Driven by .

remarks.para: Each attached-grip update first sets the shared driver to 0.98 times _ringAngularDisplacement plus _targetSpeed. The 0.98 is a dimensionless retention per update; _targetSpeed is the smoothed flight-speed value. The driver is animation state, not an angle.

The base rate is 90 + 3 times that updated driver, in degrees per second: 90 is the baseline rate and 3 supplies 3 degrees per second for each driver unit. This ring adds base rate times frame seconds to its local Y rotation.

The animation runs on held updates even with zero trigger pull; the baseline can keep the ring spinning. The checked code does not establish which assigned ring is physically inner, middle or outer. All three references must be valid for the complete rotation path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.sfx
member.summary: Provides the flight tool's grab/drop, no-clip-toggle and held-trigger audio behavior.

remarks.para: Attachment calls Grab, which plays a grab sound and starts its hum loop. Detachment immediately calls GravDrop to stop the loop and request a drop sound; collision restoration waits for the separate one-frame cleanup.

Normal input requests Release after enabling no-clip and Grab after disabling it, so those sound requests occur after _noClipping changes. Direct EnableNoClip/DisableNoClip do not make those sound calls.

During held updates, a positive trigger pull selects GravPull and otherwise GravRelax. Those methods update the sound helper's pull state and target hum volume; they do not spawn a new sound every held frame. A valid GravGunSFX with its own audio setup is required.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.speedCurveExponential
member.summary: Changes how strongly partial trigger pulls reduce the flight-speed goal.

remarks.para: The goal is maxSpeed times triggerPull raised to this exponent. maxSpeed is meters per second, while triggerPull and this exponent are dimensionless. For inputs between 0 and 1, exponent 1 is linear and larger positive exponents reduce partial-pull goals.

For an illustrative maxSpeed of 10 and pull 0.5, exponent 1 requests 5 meters per second, exponent 2 requests 2.5, and exponent 3 requests 1.25. The speed output is then smoothed; this field is not an AnimationCurve asset.
The Inspector shows a range of 1 through 3, but the checked calculation does not clamp the field to that range at runtime. The ordinary pull formula itself is not a velocity cap.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun.triggerGrip
member.summary: Supplies the hand events that initialize the player cache and drive held flight updates.

remarks.para: OnEnable subscribes attachment, detachment and attached-update callbacks. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Attachment builds the player-body cache and initializes movement from current player velocity; held updates read the reporting hand's trigger amount to control speed and aim direction.

Detachment plays the drop sound immediately and starts a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. After one frame it re-enables collisions and clears the player-body cache. Releasing the grip stops these attached updates rather than instantly setting the player's velocity to zero.

OnDisable removes the three subscriptions. Reassigning triggerGrip while enabled does not automatically move existing subscriptions, and OnDisable alone does not perform the delayed detachment cleanup in its checked body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._grip
member.summary: The same-object Grip that supplies the object host, force-pull target transforms, and interaction callbacks.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s startup routine; a GameObject is the scene object carrying the components. A cached reference is stored for later use. Target transforms describe desired positions and rotations, and interaction callbacks are routines called to perform or report interaction actions. Start gets this reference through the Grip component cache on the GameObject. Enable and Disable subscribe or unsubscribe on it; CoPull asks it for the shape-specific target and watches its hand-attached and force-pull-complete events.
Changing this reference after setup does not move existing subscriptions or refresh a running coroutine’s saved host. Treat it as an initialized cache, not a way to retarget an active pull.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._isDoneSnatching
member.summary: Records that the target hand’s snatch has finished, allowing the pull coroutine to clean up.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. The hand joint is the physics connection that holds the hand to the object. CoPull clears it at startup. OnForcePullComplete sets it only for _pullToHand. While it is true, the coroutine settles motion toward the hand and removes its two completion subscriptions; it ends after its accumulated physics time since startup exceeds 0.1 seconds.
Setting this flag manually does not attach the hand or finish a joint. The game sets it after Grip’s snatch sequence finishes attaching the hand’s joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._isEnabled
member.summary: Records whether this component has registered its far-hover handlers on the grip through and .

remarks.para: Handlers are routines registered to be called for distant-targeting events; subscriptions are those registrations. Start is Unity’s startup routine, and OnEnable is the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled. Enable sets it after adding the three event subscriptions and FarHover option; Disable clears it after removing them. Start and OnEnable normally request registration.
Changing the flag alone does not subscribe or unsubscribe events. It also does not report whether a pull is running; use the pull lifecycle and tracked resources for that distinction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._isStartAttaching
member.summary: Records that the target hand has begun attaching, so the pull can finish despite release or increased separation.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. Maximum separation is the predicted world-space distance from the object’s center of mass (its balance point) to the hand-derived target. That target is computed from the hand/grip positions and rotations plus the hand point’s movement over the physics step. The strict cutoff is about 7.8 metres: the 6-metre reference length multiplied by the unitless factor 1.3 with float precision. GrabLock is the hand flag that still makes this routine abort. CoPull clears it at startup, and OnStartAttach sets it when the reporting hand matches _pullToHand. Once true, the coroutine bypasses the secondary-button-held and maximum-separation cancellation checks. GrabLock still cancels the pull.
The flag also changes how strongly the object’s rotation velocity follows the hand during the remaining pull. It is a reported stage, not a command that begins attachment by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip._pullToHand
member.summary: The hand currently targeted by the force-pull coroutine.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. These grip notifications carry a Hand argument. Hover lock holds the hand’s chosen interaction target, storing it in AttachedReceiver; the joint is the temporary physics connection. CoPull stores it at startup. Completion and attachment callbacks compare their hand argument with this reference; attachment by a different hand aborts the original pull. Cancellation and ordinary completion clear it.
This is a lifecycle record. Changing it while a pull runs does not replace the coroutine’s own saved hand, its hover lock, or the joint’s connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.maxForce
member.summary: Sets the force budget used to accelerate and brake the object during a force pull, before its mass-based multiplier.

remarks.para: The base value is in newtons. Each physics pass multiplies it by the host’s numerical mass in kilograms, limited to 0.1 through 1.1 for that multiplier. For an illustrative maxForce of 200, masses of 0.5 kg and 2 kg produce budgets of 100 and 220 newtons respectively.

For a positive finite maxForce, the solver reserves up to half of that budget for upward gravity compensation, then uses the remainder for movement and braking calculations. Raising it increases the budget for those corrections. The routine separately changes velocity and rotation velocity directly, so this is not a guaranteed maximum speed or a limit on every motion adjustment.

The routine reads this field during the pull, so changing it can affect later physics passes. No safe tuning range or field clamp is established; the mass multiplier’s clamp is not a clamp on maxForce itself. Zero, negative or nonfinite values are not safely clamped and can make budget divisions or corrections invalid.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.maxSpeed
member.summary: No speed-limiting effect was verified for this field in the audited ForcePullGrip methods or its pull coroutine. See for the force-budget setting.

remarks.para: The constructor is creation-time code supplying initial field values. A pull coroutine is a sequence continuing over several frames between physics updates; its state-machine body is the code that resumes that sequence. The class constructor initializes this value, but the complete audited class and CoPull state-machine body do not read it when calculating pull motion. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to cap how fast a pulled object moves in those routines.

The actual solver applies force and also changes velocity directly. No working units or useful tuning range were established for this unused setting. External code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.pullCoroutine
member.summary: The saved handle used to avoid duplicate pulls and stop the pull when another hand takes the object.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; its handle is the reference Unity returns so code can stop that sequence.
Pull and the far-hover update store the StartCoroutine result here. A nonnull value prevents those routines from starting another pull. Cancellation or ordinary completion clears it.

This is bookkeeping rather than a live query of Unity’s coroutine scheduler. CancelPull clears it without calling StopCoroutine, and starting CoPull manually does not automatically save its handle here. Keep the handle before cancellation if you need to stop the scheduled coroutine yourself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.state
member.summary: Reports whether this component is idle, being targeted at a distance, or running a force pull.

remarks.para: The host is the physical object owning this grip. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; this pull sequence continues between physics updates. The joint is a temporary connection between bodies in Unity’s physics simulation. IDELING is 0, LONGHOVERING is 1, and PULLING is 2. Begin/end far-hover callbacks change idle/targeting status only while the host is unattached; CoPull sets PULLING on startup; cancellation and ordinary completion restore IDELING.
Setting this value does not start, stop, or clean up a pull. It is a status field, not proof that a coroutine or joint exists or has been removed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.tempJoint
member.summary: The temporary physics connection added to the hand’s rigidbody object during a force pull and connected to the object’s host rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object simulated physics motion. CoPull creates this ConfigurableJoint with all three translation and all three rotation axes set to Free, allowing translation and rotation on those axes, and automatic connected-anchor placement disabled, so Unity does not automatically choose the connection point on the other body. A joint is a connection between objects in Unity’s physics simulation. The routine also drives the pull through explicit force and velocity changes.

CancelPull destroys the joint and sets this field to null. Ordinary completion destroys it immediately but does not explicitly clear the stored field, so it can retain a reference to a destroyed Unity object. Do not treat a stored reference alone as proof that a usable joint still exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.ModIOManager
member.summary: Selects the manager whose mod.io client looks up files for mod.io download targets.

remarks.para: Before a mod.io file lookup, DownloadMod reads this manager and its ModIOAPI client, then requests the target's game ID, mod ID, and file ID. Assign an initialized manager with a ready client before starting that lookup; a null manager or client cannot carry out the request.
Assigning this reference changes which manager a later lookup uses. The setter only stores the reference; it does not sign in, initialize the client, or start a download.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.ModSettingsJSON
member.summary: Holds the settings object that WriteModSettings saves, including the serialized rejected-file records.

remarks.para: JSON is a text format for named values; this JObject is the editable in-memory object before it becomes file text. It can remain null even after LoadModSettings finishes if the file is missing, blank, or does not contain an object. WriteModSettings does nothing while it is null.

A valid object loaded from disk replaces this reference. AddInvalidModFile and RemoveInvalidModFile copy their dictionary into the mod.io.invalid_mods entry before saving. Editing that JSON entry does not itself update the separate invalidMods dictionary; LoadModSettings converts a saved entry back into the dictionary on a later load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.ModSettingsPath
member.summary: Gives the path to mod_settings.json, the downloader settings file read by and replaced by .

remarks.para: The path combines Unity's persistentDataPath with the filename mod_settings.json. persistentDataPath is the game's folder for data kept between runs, so the directory depends on the platform and user. It is not the mod's Unity project folder.
Reading this property only constructs the path; it does not create the file or load its contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.VerboseLogging
member.summary: Always returns false in this game build.

remarks.para: This read-only property is a fixed result, so it cannot be switched on to request detailed downloader logging. Its value does not guarantee that the downloader emits no messages: ordinary errors and status messages are separate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader.invalidMods
member.summary: Stores one rejected mod.io file ID for each mod, allowing subscription checks to skip that same file. saves this mapping through the settings helper.

remarks.para: The key identifies a mod and the value identifies one of its uploaded files. A check skips the mod when the current platform's file ID equals the saved value. For example, mod 101 mapped to file 9001 matches that file; a newer file 9002 does not match and can still pass this particular check.

This is the live in-memory dictionary. GetInvalidMods returns a copy. Subscription downloads also take their own copy after loading settings, so changing this dictionary does not change a download run's existing snapshot.

LoadModSettings replaces this dictionary from a saved mod.io.invalid_mods entry, or clears it when a loaded settings object lacks that entry. AddInvalidModFile and RemoveInvalidModFile copy changes back into ModSettingsJSON before saving. Direct dictionary edits alone are neither synchronized to the JSON nor saved by WriteModSettings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.BeginUserInitiatedLogin
member.summary: Lets a callback prepare the login interface before checks saved credentials.

remarks.para: A callback is a function subscribed to run when an event happens. LogIn invokes this event before calling LoadAndCheckLogin, even if saved credentials will turn out to be valid. For example, a callback can show a login-in-progress panel before the token check begins.

The callback receives no parameters and returns a UniTask, an asynchronous operation that the login method can wait for. The method waits for the event delegate's returned task before checking credentials.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.CompleteUserInitiatedLogin
member.summary: Lets a callback react when token restoration or a successful device-login response signs this manager in.

remarks.para: A callback is a subscribed function. It receives no parameters and returns an asynchronous UniTask. The manager waits for the event delegate's returned task.

In LogIn, successful token restoration sets IsLoggedIn before this callback runs. If a callback is present, the method waits for it, then cancels and replaces the receive-loop cancellation source. With no callback, that restoration shortcut finishes without resetting the source.

For a WebSocket login-success response, success means its numeric Code equals 200. The manager first sets IsLoggedIn to true, applies the received access token to the REST client, updates ModSettingsJSON, and writes the settings file. It then invokes this callback on Unity’s main thread, where Unity normally updates game objects. If a callback is subscribed, the response handler waits for its returned task; when no callback is subscribed, it proceeds directly. In either case it cancels the receive loop. If a subscribed callback throws, the error path also cancels the loop, invokes the failure callback if present, and rethrows. A file-write error occurs before this completion callback can run.

For example, this callback can close the login panel and show the subscribed-mods controls. A later callback error can trigger the failure event even though the flag and token were already set, so the event order matters.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.FailUserInitiatedLogin
member.summary: Lets a callback react to a caught login error or a device-login response whose result code is not 200.

remarks.para: A callback is a subscribed function. This event receives no parameters, including no error object, and returns an asynchronous UniTask. The manager waits for the event delegate's returned task. For example, a callback can replace a login-in-progress panel with a retry message.

When LogIn catches an error in its login-check or handshake work, it invokes this event before passing the caught exception to the debug logger. A visible log message depends on Marrow debug logging being enabled for that thread. The WebSocket response handler also invokes it when a login-success response has a Code other than 200.

If a completion callback throws while processing an otherwise successful WebSocket response, the response handler cancels the receive loop, invokes this failure callback if present, then rethrows the error. The login flag, applied access token, and saved file have already been updated by then. None of these inspected failure-event paths clears IsLoggedIn merely because the event fires.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.IsLoggedIn
member.summary: Reports the login-success flag stored by this manager.

remarks.para: The flag becomes true when LoadAndCheckLogin successfully validates a token or when the WebSocket response handler receives a login-success response with code 200. Unity's OnDisable, the method called when this component is disabled, sets it to false before cancelling work and disposing the clients.

Reading this property does not contact mod.io, check token expiry, or check the WebSocket connection. A failed LoadAndCheckLogin call returns false without clearing an earlier true value. For example, a previous successful login can leave this flag true even if a later token test fails.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModIOAPI
member.summary: Provides the mod.io REST client whose active access token is set when login succeeds.

remarks.para: REST requests are ordinary HTTP requests sent to query a service. This client performs mod.io requests such as querying a mod file. Unity's OnEnable, called when this component becomes enabled, creates a new client for BONELAB game ID 3809 before starting the saved-token check.

Successful saved-token restoration or a device-login response places the user's access token in this client's Context.AccessToken. The request context is the group of settings supplied with API requests. Token validation instead uses a temporary context, so testing a candidate token alone does not alter the live client.

OnDisable, called when the component becomes disabled, disposes this client. The property still holds that disposed object until the next enable creates a replacement. Merely having a non-null client here is therefore not proof that it is ready to make requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModIOApiKey
member.summary: Stores the game API key copied into temporary requests that test a user access token.

remarks.para: The API key identifies the game's API access, while the separate access token identifies the signed-in user. ValidateAccessToken copies this key together with the candidate user token into a new request context, the group of settings supplied to that authenticated-user request.

This value is serialized configuration, so Unity can save it with the component. Its getter reads the stored string. Setting the storage does not itself rebuild a client or copy the key into the REST client's active context. In the inspected enable and login methods, validation copies the current key when each token test is started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModIOGameId
member.summary: Returns 3809, the BONELAB game identifier passed to this manager's mod.io clients.

remarks.para: This is a numeric identifier, with no physical unit. The getter always returns 3809 in this build. During OnEnable, which Unity calls when this component becomes enabled, the manager passes that number to both its REST client and its WebSocket client so their requests target BONELAB.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModIOSettingsPath
member.summary: Returns the full path to mod_settings.json in Unity's persistent data directory.

remarks.para: The persistent data directory is the game's folder for files kept between runs; its location depends on the device. The getter combines that directory with the filename mod_settings.json. It only calculates the path and does not create or read the file.

The login loader reads this file, and a successful device-login response saves the access token here under mod.io.access_token. This is also the settings filename used by ModDownloader for its invalid-mod-file records.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModIOWebSocketAPI
member.summary: Provides the WebSocket client that exchanges device-login requests and responses with mod.io.

remarks.para: A WebSocket is a connection that lets the server send messages back after the initial request. OnEnable, which Unity calls when this component becomes enabled, creates this client for BONELAB game ID 3809 and subscribes the manager's message callback.

Creating the client does not establish a connected socket. If saved-token restoration fails, LogIn connects it, starts the receive loop, and sends the device-login request. Later messages can prompt the player with a code or apply a successful login token.

OnDisable, called when this component becomes disabled, unsubscribes the message callback and disposes the client. The property retains the disposed reference until the next enable replaces it, so a non-null value alone does not show whether a live connection exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.ModSettingsJSON
member.summary: Stores the in-memory settings object loaded for login and updated before saving a new access token.

remarks.para: A JSON object is a collection of named values, such as mod.io.access_token. After waiting for LoadModSettings, LoadAndCheckLogin assigns that result here, including null for a missing, blank, or non-object file. This happens before token validation completes.

When a WebSocket login succeeds with response code 200, the manager creates an empty object if this property is null, replaces its mod.io.access_token value with the received token, and writes the whole object to mod_settings.json. Existing other entries remain in that object.

This is a stored object, not a fresh file read each time the getter runs. Changing it in memory does not by itself save the file or apply the token to the REST client. For example, editing the token text here alone does not perform login.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.RequestUserCodeEntry
member.summary: Lets a callback display the code and login page supplied by a mod.io device-login response.

remarks.para: A callback is a function subscribed to run when this event happens. The manager invokes it after moving to Unity's main thread, where Unity normally updates the game interface. It passes a DeviceLoginResponseContext containing Code, the text code to show the player; LoginUrl, the login-page address; and DateExpires, the expiry timestamp measured in seconds since 00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970.

For example, a callback can show the supplied code beside a button that opens LoginUrl, letting the player complete authorization on that page. This event reports the server's prompt; its return value is not a code entered by the player.

The callback returns an asynchronous UniTask, and the response handler waits for the task returned by the event delegate. Receiving this prompt does not set IsLoggedIn; a later successful login response supplies the access token.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager._enableCTS
member.summary: Stores the cancellation source that stops this manager's login work when the component is disabled.

remarks.para: A cancellation source owns a token, a signal that asks asynchronous work to stop. OnEnable, called when Unity enables this component, creates this source and starts LoadAndCheckLogin with its token. Manual login and token-restoration calls link their caller token with this enable token, so either caller cancellation or disabling the component can stop the work.

OnDisable, called when Unity disables this component, cancels this source and replaces the stored source with a new one before disposing the API clients. Cancelling requests that work stop; it does not make the existing clients ready for another login. The next enable creates fresh clients and cancellation sources.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager._receiveLoopCTS
member.summary: Stores the cancellation source whose token can stop the WebSocket receive loop started for device login.

remarks.para: The receive loop waits for incoming server messages. A cancellation source supplies a token that asks this asynchronous loop to stop. OnEnable, called when Unity enables this component, creates the source. When LogIn starts a receive loop, it links this token with the caller's cancellation token and the enable token, so any of the three can request a stop.

After a successful WebSocket login response, the manager invokes the completion callback and waits for its returned task before cancelling this source; that response path also cancels it when the callback throws. The already-logged-in shortcut in LogIn cancels and replaces the source after a completion callback, but performs no such reset when there is no completion callback.

OnDisable, called when Unity disables this component, cancels and replaces the source before disposing the clients. When the receive-loop helper finishes normally, it disposes its separate linked source and installs a new receive-loop source. Replacing the stored source alone does not start another receive loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModIOModTarget.GameId
member.summary: Selects the mod.io game ID passed to the downloader’s file-information request.

remarks.para: This is a stored signed 64-bit identifier, with no measurement unit. Together with ModId, the mod’s identifier, and ModfileId, the downloadable release’s identifier, it selects the file whose information the downloader requests from mod.io.

The GameId getter reads the configured value; it does not always return BONELAB’s ID. For a BONELAB target, 3809 is the game ID used by the manager’s client setup. Set this target’s ID before starting a download. The downloader reads all three target IDs when building its GetModfile request; changing storage later does not rewrite an already-sent request.
Pack writes the value as gameId in JSON. Unpack replaces it when that stored property is present and convertible to a signed 64-bit integer; a missing gameId leaves the previous value unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModIOModTarget.ModId
member.summary: Selects the mod whose file information the downloader requests from mod.io.

remarks.para: This stored signed 64-bit identifier has no measurement units. It identifies the mod within the game selected by GameId. ModfileId then chooses a particular file release of that mod. The downloader passes these three configured numbers together to GetModfile.

Set the ID before starting the download. Writing this property only changes the target’s stored value; the request reads it when the download begins. Pack saves it as modId, and Unpack replaces it only when a convertible modId property is present. For example, changing the selected mod requires a matching file-release ID for that mod.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModIOModTarget.ModfileId
member.summary: Selects the specific file release requested for this mod.io download target.

remarks.para: A mod can have several uploaded file releases. This stored signed 64-bit ID identifies the one requested by the downloader; it has no measurement unit and is separate from a version label such as 1.2. GameId identifies the game and ModId identifies the mod that owns this release.

The downloader passes this value as the file ID in GetModfile, alongside the stored game and mod IDs. Set it before starting a download. For example, choosing an older release means storing that older release’s file ID; changing a version label elsewhere does not change this request input.

Pack saves the value as modfileId. Unpack replaces it when that property is present and convertible to a signed 64-bit integer; a missing property keeps the old value. Changing the stored ID alone does not download or install anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Author
member.summary: Stores the author credit saved with this mod listing.

remarks.para: Pack writes this string to the author property in JSON, and Unpack replaces it when that property is present. For example, an author string such as ExampleCreator travels with the saved listing.
The getter returns stored text. It does not fetch the repository page or verify who created the mod. A missing author property during Unpack leaves the old value unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Barcode
member.summary: Identifies the mod’s content bundle when the menu matches this listing to an installed pallet.

remarks.para: A Barcode holds a text identifier. A pallet is the bundle of assets belonging to a mod. While parsing repository listings, the mod menu compares this Barcode with each installed pallet’s barcode to find the matching installed bundle. Changing this identifier can therefore change which installed pallet is associated with the listing.

Pack writes Barcode.ID as the barcode string in JSON. Unpack creates a new Barcode from a present stored barcode string; a missing property keeps the existing object. Pack requires the Barcode object to be non-null. Reading this property does not scan or install the bundle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Description
member.summary: Stores the descriptive text included when the listing is saved or loaded.

remarks.para: Pack writes this string as description in JSON, and Unpack converts a present description property back to a string. For example, the text can describe what the mod adds or how to use it.

The property returns the current stored text. It does not fetch a fresh repository page. A missing description property during Unpack leaves the old description unchanged, so a partially loaded listing can contain metadata from an earlier load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Repository
member.summary: Returns the repository last associated with this listing while that repository object is still available.

remarks.para: A repository is a catalog containing mod listings. This association is held through a weak reference: the listing can point back to the catalog without keeping that catalog object alive by itself. If no other code keeps the repository alive, the runtime may release it and this getter can return null.

Assigning Repository creates the weak-reference wrapper on first use and changes its target on later assignments. The getter also returns null when no wrapper exists or when it cannot recover its target.

For example, retaining a listing after its repository has been released does not guarantee that listing.Repository still returns the catalog. The listing’s Pack and Unpack methods do not save or restore this association.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Targets
member.summary: Stores the named download targets that lookups and target selection use for this listing.

remarks.para: The dictionary maps a text target name to a ModTarget object describing how to obtain the mod’s content. A mod.io target can identify a particular uploaded file; another target type can identify a download URL. GetTargetListing looks up a name and checks its requested type. The target resolver checks names in its configured preference order and selects the first usable target of the requested type.

The getter returns the stored dictionary itself. Adding or removing an entry changes later target lookups. A new listing creates an empty dictionary. Setting Targets to null leaves nothing for GetTargetListing or targetNames to read and those operations can fail.

Pack saves named references to the target objects. When Unpack finds a targets property, it replaces this dictionary before reconstructing entries; when that property is absent, the existing dictionary remains. Some reconstructed entries can hold null if their stored reference cannot be resolved. A name appearing in targetNames therefore does not guarantee a usable target object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.ThumbnailUrl
member.summary: Supplies the listing image address copied into the mod menu unless the selected target provides a valid thumbnail override.

remarks.para: A thumbnail is the small preview image beside a mod. When the menu builds a view model, the prepared data for a menu row, it begins with this ThumbnailUrl. A non-empty target thumbnail override replaces it when that override is a valid absolute URL, an address containing its own scheme and location.

The menu row can reuse an image cached under the chosen URL, or fetch the image asynchronously, allowing the game to continue while the request waits. Reading ThumbnailUrl alone does not fetch an image. Editing this listing property after the row’s data has been built does not change the URL already copied into that row.

Pack saves this string as thumbnailUrl. Unpack replaces it when present and otherwise keeps the old value. For example, setting a new image URL changes what the next menu-data rebuild starts from, while the selected target’s valid override can still take priority.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Title
member.summary: Supplies the mod name copied into a repository menu row.

remarks.para: When the menu parses repository listings, it copies Title into the row’s prepared text. Updating this property afterward changes the listing’s stored name but does not automatically replace that already-copied row text.

Pack writes this string as title in JSON, and Unpack replaces it when a stored title property is present. For example, renaming a listing changes the name used when the menu data is built again. A missing title property during Unpack keeps the existing text.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.Version
member.summary: Provides the stored version label that the menu can display for this listing.

remarks.para: This is text, such as 1.2.3, with no measurement units. A newly constructed listing starts with the label 0.0.1. Pack writes it as version in JSON; Unpack replaces it when present and keeps it unchanged when the property is missing.

The menu cell first uses a non-null version from its pallet, the installed bundle of mod assets. If that version is unavailable, it tries this listing’s non-null Version; if neither is available, the cell uses its fallback text.

Changing this label only changes stored metadata. It does not choose a different uploaded mod.io file. A mod.io target has a separate numeric ModfileId that identifies the file release requested by the downloader.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing._repository
member.summary: Stores the weak-reference wrapper read and updated by the Repository property.

remarks.para: A weak reference points to an object without keeping that object alive by itself. Repository creates this wrapper when first assigned and updates its target on later assignments. Its getter tries to recover the repository from this wrapper and returns null if none is available.

The wrapper can still exist after its repository target has been released. A non-null _repository therefore does not guarantee a live catalog. For example, code can keep the listing while other code stops retaining the repository. Pack and Unpack leave this association untouched.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing.targetNames
member.summary: Returns a new set copied from the current target names.

remarks.para: Each call copies the keys in Targets into a new HashSet, a collection that stores each name once. It is a snapshot made at the time of the getter call. Changing the returned set does not add or remove entries in Targets, and later changes to Targets do not update an earlier returned set.

For example, clearing a saved targetNames set leaves the listing’s target dictionary unchanged. Read targetNames again to get the current names. Targets must be non-null; a new listing starts with an empty dictionary.
This lists keys even when an entry’s target value is null. The target resolver uses the set to check whether any names exist, then performs separate typed lookups to find a usable target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GenericGrip._targetColliders
member.summary: Chooses the collider shapes checked when looking for a surface this hand can grab.

remarks.para: A collider is the shape Unity uses for collision and surface tests. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, replaces this list with colliders found on the grip object and its active children. During Start, Unity’s first active-frame setup routine, colliders whose attached Rigidbody differs from the host’s Rigidbody are removed when the grip has a physics host; a Rigidbody is an object moved by the physics simulation.

ValidateGripScore considers the listed shapes, chooses a candidate near the hand handle, then raycasts that collider to get a real hit point and surface direction. A non-convex MeshCollider uses the hand-handle position as its candidate instead of a closest-point query; the raycast still has to hit.
Editing the list after startup changes the shapes considered by later score checks. The inspected joint setup uses the grip and hand configuration rather than reading this list directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GenericGrip.genericHandStates
member.summary: Stores each checked hand’s latest surface-hit and hand-handle data for later hover alignment.

remarks.para: ValidateGripScore creates a record when a hand is first checked, then updates its raycast-hit flag, surface point, surface direction and saved hand-handle pose. A successful calculation converts those positions and directions into the GenericGrip transform’s local frame so the target can follow a moving object.

OnHandHoverUpdate reads the record and turns it back into a world-space hand target. A failed score can leave partial data in the record, so use the normal score-then-hover flow rather than treating every stored record as a valid grab. The dictionary can include hands that are not holding the object; attachedHands is the separate held-hand list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.Cache
member.summary: Finds a from the GameObject it is attached to, so hand interaction can look up the grip without searching its components again.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine for this component, registers this grip; OnDestroy removes it when the component is destroyed. Disabling the component does not remove this cache entry, so finding a grip here does not prove it is available to grab. The getter creates the shared cache if it does not yet exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.IsInteractionDisabled
member.summary: Reports whether this grip has its local interaction switch disabled or its Unity component is inactive or disabled.

remarks.para: Ordinary close-hover updates reject a grip in either condition. This query does not include the host object’s separate interaction switch, and the override hover path can bypass these local checks. It does not release an already attached hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared GameObject-to- lookup behind Cache.

remarks.para: Cache creates this storage when it is missing. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine for this component, adds entries; OnDestroy removes them when the component is destroyed; the storage can return to null when no entries remain. Prefer Cache when looking up a grip, because the backing field itself can be null. Cache membership does not indicate whether interaction is enabled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip._gripDistance
member.summary: Stores the current distance allowance read by CylinderGrip and SphereGrip when judging a possible grab.

remarks.para: The distance is in meters: for example, 0.05 means a 5 cm allowance. CylinderGrip compares the hand’s gap from its cylinder surface, while SphereGrip compares the palm’s gap from the sphere. TargetGrip compares the controller handle’s distance from its target point using gripDistanceSqr, the cached current allowance multiplied by itself, in square metres. These are additional shape-specific acceptance checks, not the radius of the hand’s initial search for nearby objects.

This backs gripDistance, the current allowance. Directly changing _gripDistance does not update gripDistanceSqr, so TargetGrip can keep using an old allowance. Set gripDistance instead when changing the current distance. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), initializes both values from defaultGripDistance, the starting allowance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip._handStates
member.summary: Keeps a separate interaction record for each hand, including hover/attachment flags, pose selection, and an active snatch sequence moving the hand onto the grip.

remarks.para: GetHandState creates a record when the hand has none, even if it is only being queried and is not holding the object. A new record copies handPose, the saved hand-and-finger pose, and radius, the size in metres used for hand wrapping and connection placement; later edits to those Grip fields do not automatically update an existing record. Detach and unattached hover-end cleanup remove records. This dictionary is therefore broader than attachedHands, the list of hands holding the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip._isInteractionDisabled
member.summary: Stores the local switch that DisableInteraction sets and EnableInteraction clears.

remarks.para: Ordinary close-hover updates reject this grip while the switch is true. IsInteractionDisabled also checks whether the Unity component is active and enabled. Changing this field does not immediately detach an existing hold, and forced interaction paths can bypass it. Use DisableInteraction or EnableInteraction for the normal change; EnableInteraction also restores the inherited receiver-enabled flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip._marrowEntity
member.summary: Stores the this grip registers with for interaction-handler cleanup.

remarks.para: SetEntity stores the entity and registers this grip with it; OnDestroy unregisters from the stored entity. A MarrowEntity is the game-object record this grip registers with so its interaction handlers can be cleaned up. Assigning this field directly changes the reference without performing that registration. It is separate from the inherited host, which supplies physics-body and object-control information.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.additionalGripColliders
member.summary: Adds extra collider shapes to the hand’s temporary collision exclusions alongside while gripping this object.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used to detect physical contact. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation; the host supplies this object’s physics body and colliders. For example, a collider on a child object can be included so it does not push the attached hand away. GetSubColliders replaces this array with colliders gathered from this grip and its descendants.

Hand.PrepareJoint includes these alongside gripColliders when there is no Rigidbody-backed host. The host-collider ignore/unignore paths also include non-trigger additional colliders. Listing a collider here does not by itself make that shape a valid grab location.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.angVelocityHistory
member.summary: Keeps recent spin velocities of the joint’s connected Rigidbody for calculating release spin.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation; the joint is the physics connection holding the hand and object together. Each entry is a world-axis angular-velocity vector in radians per second. Its direction gives the axis of spin and its length gives the spin speed; for example, a length of about 6.28 means one revolution per second. Attached-hand updates record it in the slot matching velocityHistory, the matching linear-velocity sample array that shares this slot index, without subtracting the player’s whole-body velocity.

The release calculation combines recent directions and uses the largest sampled angular speed, rather than an ordinary arithmetic average. The linear throw multiplier does not multiply this spin result. Held updates overwrite slots; ClearHistory repeatedly zeroes only the current slot in this implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.attachedHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners when Grip begins recording a hand as attached.

remarks.para: A physics joint is the connection that holds the hand and object together. The argument is the hand being attached. OnAttachedToHand marks its state active, then invokes this delegate before setting the ATTACH flag and before adding the hand to attachedHands. A listener should not expect those later steps to have happened yet. This notification is distinct from OnJointAttached, which registers the physics joint with the object-control solver.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.attachedHands
