member.summary: Lists hands that Grip’s attachment routines, called when a hold begins or ends, have recorded as holding this grip.

remarks.para: A physics joint is the connection that holds the hand and object together. OnAttachedToHand adds a hand after firing attachedHandDelegate; OnDetachedFromHand removes it after firing detachedHandDelegate. GetHand returns the first entry, which is list order rather than a calculated dominant hand. Adding or removing entries yourself does not attach or detach a physics joint and can leave the other interaction records inconsistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.attachedUpdateDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners during each held-hand update after pose, squeeze, and available joint settings have been updated.

remarks.para: A physics joint is the connection holding the hand and object together. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation. The argument is the hand being updated. Motion history is sampled when the hand has a joint connected to a Rigidbody. This delegate fires before that same update checks whether to release the hold, so receiving it does not guarantee the hand remains attached afterward. This notification occurs when the game calls the OnHandAttachedUpdate routine, not a promise of one call per rendered frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.defaultGripDistance
member.summary: Sets the starting grab-distance allowance copied into gripDistance, the current allowance, during Unity initialization.

remarks.para: It is measured in meters. For example, 0.05 starts with a 5 cm allowance; the exact comparison depends on the grip subclass’s shape or target. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), also calculates gripDistanceSqr, the cached current allowance multiplied by itself, in square metres, from this value. Changing defaultGripDistance after Awake does not change the current allowance automatically; set gripDistance for a runtime change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.detachedHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners when Grip begins cleaning up a hand’s attachment.

remarks.para: The argument is the departing hand. OnDetachedFromHand marks its state inactive, then invokes this delegate before removing its ATTACH flag, cached target/state, and attachedHands entry. A listener can therefore still see those records during the notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.farHoverBeginHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies registered code when OnFarHandHoverBegin is called for a hand beginning distant targeting of this grip.

remarks.para: The argument is the hand doing the distant targeting. The base OnFarHandHoverBegin routine, called to handle distant targeting, forwards this notification; it does not itself start a snatch, the sequence moving the hand onto the grip, attach the hand, or set a grip-state flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.farHoverEndHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies registered code when OnFarHandHoverEnd is called for a hand ending distant targeting of this grip.

remarks.para: The argument is the hand that was targeting the grip. The base OnFarHandHoverEnd routine, called to handle the end of distant targeting, only forwards this notification; it does not itself cancel a snatch, the sequence moving the hand onto the grip, or detach an attached hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.farHoverUpdateHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners when OnFarHandHoverUpdate is called for a hand targeting the grip from a distance.

remarks.para: The argument is that hand. The base OnFarHandHoverUpdate routine, called to handle distant targeting updates, forwards the notification without starting or completing a pull. Notification frequency follows calls to that routine; it is not guaranteed to match rendered frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.forcePullCompleteDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners after a snatch finishes its attachment sequence or after hand collision detection is restored during cancellation.

remarks.para: A listener is registered code called at the notification. The argument is the hand involved. The normal CoSnatch completion restores hand collision detection and clears its active coroutine list before notifying. A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames and can pause and resume. CancelSnatch also notifies after stopping and clearing a recorded active sequence, detaching, and restoring hand and forearm collision detection; it does nothing when no sequence is recorded. It restores the previously ignored host collider pairs through UnignoreHostColliders after the notification, so listeners run before that part of cleanup.
A notification alone does not prove success or that an object reached the hand. In the audited base snatch, the skeleton hand moves toward the grip, while the quick path skips that wait.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.gripColliders
member.summary: Holds colliders on this grip’s own GameObject that the hand may temporarily ignore while attaching.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used to detect physical contact. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation; the host supplies this object’s body and colliders. Start, Unity’s startup routine called before this component’s first update, replaces this array with GetComponents<Collider> from the grip’s GameObject; it does not collect child objects. GetSubColliders fills additionalGripColliders separately.

For a grip without a Rigidbody-backed host, Hand.PrepareJoint ignores collisions between these colliders and the hand’s colliders, alongside additionalGripColliders. A Rigidbody-backed host has its own collider handling. These arrays participate in collision exclusion; they do not by themselves define the subclass’s complete grab-scoring shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.gripDistance
member.summary: Sets the current distance allowance used by specialized grips to reject grab candidates that are too far from their shape or target.

remarks.para: The distance is in meters: for example, 0.05 means a 5 cm allowance. CylinderGrip compares the hand’s gap from its cylinder surface, while SphereGrip compares the palm’s gap from the sphere. TargetGrip compares the controller handle’s distance from its target point using gripDistanceSqr, the cached current allowance multiplied by itself, in square metres. These are additional shape-specific acceptance checks, not the radius of the hand’s initial search for nearby objects.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), copies defaultGripDistance, the starting allowance, into gripDistance, the current allowance. Later, set gripDistance to change the current allowance and keep gripDistanceSqr synchronized. The property setter does not clamp the value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.gripDistanceSqr
member.summary: Caches gripDistance × gripDistance, where gripDistance is the current grab-distance allowance in meters.

remarks.para: TargetGrip rejects a hover candidate when the controller handle’s squared distance from its target exceeds this value. Its units are square meters: a 0.05 m distance gives 0.0025 m². Awake, Unity’s initialization routine for this component, and the gripDistance setter calculate it. Changing this field alone can make TargetGrip’s distance limit disagree with the value CylinderGrip and SphereGrip read; set gripDistance to update both.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.gripOptions
member.summary: Combines switches for multiple-hand holds, toggled release, distant targeting, and transferring a hold to a new hand.

remarks.para: MultipleHands allows the same held object to remain a hover candidate for the other hand. SwitchHands makes Hand.AttachObject force-detach existing hands before recording the new hold. These are different choices: allowing two hands to hold an object and transferring a hold have different results.

FarHover enables the grip’s distant-hover route when the hand’s other targeting conditions pass. ToggledGrip changes the held-update release logic; Vive wand controls use a button latch, a remembered true/false button flag that prevents the initiating press from immediately toggling the object free, while other controller paths still consult their release state. Combine flags to request multiple options. These options do not replace the grip subclass’s distance and angle checks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.gripTargetsInBaseTarget
member.summary: Stores each hand’s desired handle position and rotation relative to targetTransform.

remarks.para: The position is a meter offset in the target’s rotated coordinate frame; the rotation is relative to that frame. These SimpleTransform values contain no scale. GetTargetInWorld rotates and translates a stored value to produce a world-space target. Moving or rotating targetTransform therefore moves the stored targets with it.

This can contain hover targets as well as held-hand targets. GetTargetInBase creates a zero-position, identity-rotation entry if the hand has none, meaning the base target’s own pose. Use SetTargetInBase or SetTargetInWorld to change the desired pose; the stored value does not directly move the physical hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.handPose
member.summary: Supplies the default hand-pose asset used to shape the fingers and position the grip connection inside the hand.

remarks.para: Pose selection also supplies the swing and twist limits: swing tilts away from the primary grip direction, while twist turns around it. A hand can have a separate pose override in its HandToGripState.

GetHandState copies this asset into a newly created hand record. Changing handPose later does not automatically replace existing cached selections or begin a new animation. Use SetHandPose for a particular hand to update its selection and request the normal pose transition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.handleAmplifyCurve
member.summary: Adds a wrist-dependent rotation to the two-hand object-control calculation.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is signed sideways wrist bend in degrees, calculated from the avatar hand and forearm orientations. It is not the controller's squeeze input. The vertical axis is a rotation amount in degrees, not a multiplier. primaryMovementAxis is the target-relative main/forward direction, and secondaryMovementAxis is the reference-up direction in that same target-relative frame. The magnitude is limited to the grip's swing limit, then stored as a rotation around the third direction formed by secondaryMovementAxis crossed with primaryMovementAxis. Positive curve values use the opposite of that direction; negative values use that direction.

A flat curve at 0 adds no rotation. A value of 10 at a wrist bend of 20 degrees requests a 10-degree correction, provided the swing limit allows it. The two-hand solver applies the inverse of this stored correction to the controller's handle rotation before deciding the object's target rotation. Other limits and blending can affect the final movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.hasStartedToGrip
member.summary: Tracks the initial held-button latch used by a Vive-wand ToggledGrip hold.

remarks.para: A latch is a remembered true/false button flag. OnAttachedToHand sets this latch for that control mode. Held updates use it so the press that began the hold does not immediately toggle the object free, then clear it after the initial button state has passed. This is one grip-wide input latch, not a measurement of finger closure or whether the physics joint has finished attaching.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.hoverBeginHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners when the one-argument OnHandHoverBegin routine, called to handle the start of close hover, begins handling a hand.

remarks.para: The argument is the hovering hand. OnHandHoverBegin(hand) fires this delegate before its two-argument overload sets the HOVER flag and starts the skeleton-hand hover behavior. Calling the two-argument overload directly does not fire this delegate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.hoverEndHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners when a hand’s close-hover behavior ends.

remarks.para: The argument is the departing hand. The base OnHandHoverEnd routine, called to handle the end of close hover, ends the skeleton-hand hover behavior, fires this delegate, then clears the HOVER flag. It keeps pose/state information if the hand remains attached; otherwise it restores the default pose and removes the hover hand state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.hoverUpdateHandDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners after an accepted one-argument close-hover update has applied its finger-curl override.

remarks.para: The argument is the hovering hand. This delegate fires only when the internal OnHandHoverUpdate(hand, false) check succeeds; that check includes component availability and controller grab/release state. The two-argument overload does not fire this delegate itself. There is no unconditional every-rendered-frame notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.ignoreGripTargetOnAttach
member.summary: Serialized switch whose attachment effect was not found in the audited base Grip, common grip subclasses, or Hand attachment paths.

remarks.para: The Inspector description suggests choosing the original rather than virtualized grip target, but the audited code does not read this field. Changing it is not a verified way to change attachment behavior. This conclusion covers Grip, CylinderGrip, SphereGrip, TargetGrip, BoxGrip, BarrelGrip, GenericGrip, AvatarGrip, WorldGrip, and the examined Hand attachment/collision setup; other subclasses or mods may behave differently.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.isThrowable
member.summary: Controls whether an ordinary release uses the hand joint’s short soft-cleanup period or requests quick cleanup.

remarks.para: A physics joint is the connection holding the hand and object together. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation. For a non-static grip, true allows the normal approximately 0.08-second joint-cleanup sequence; false requests quick cleanup. Static grips also request quick cleanup. The hand stops holding the object before that temporary joint is eventually destroyed.

False does not prevent throwing: the ordinary release path can still calculate and assign the Rigidbody’s linear and angular release velocities. This flag is therefore not a reliable “make this object unable to fly” switch. The native constructor initializes it to true, but serialized content can supply another value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.maxBreakForce
member.summary: Sets the upper force threshold for breaking a 's hand joint at full controller squeeze.

remarks.para: A joint is the physics connection holding the hand to the object. Raising this endpoint lets a fully squeezed grip withstand a larger pull. It is measured in newtons before the avatar's grip-strength multiplier and the physics-step correction of 0.012 seconds divided by the step duration.

The game blends from minBreakForce at squeeze 0 to maxBreakForce at squeeze 1. For endpoints 100 and 300, full squeeze gives 300 newtons when avatar strength is 1 and the physics step is 0.012 seconds. Controller squeeze is the player's 0-to-1 input, not the avatar's strength. The update requires minBreakForce to differ from positive infinity and maxBreakForce to be greater than minBreakForce; equal endpoints do not set a constant threshold.

The native Grip constructor initializes both endpoints to positive infinity, so this optional squeeze-driven update is skipped by default and leaves the joint’s existing threshold alone. Serialized content can supply different values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.minBreakForce
member.summary: Sets the lower force threshold for breaking a 's hand joint when the controller squeeze is 0.

remarks.para: A joint is the physics connection holding the hand to the object. Lower thresholds let that connection break under a smaller pull. This endpoint is in newtons before scaling. The game blends from minBreakForce to maxBreakForce as controller squeeze rises from 0 to 1, then multiplies by the avatar's grip-strength value and a physics-step correction of 0.012 seconds divided by the step duration. Controller squeeze and avatar strength are separate quantities.

For minBreakForce = 100 and maxBreakForce = 300, half squeeze gives 200 newtons when avatar strength is 1 and the physics step is 0.012 seconds. This update only runs when minBreakForce is not positive infinity and maxBreakForce is greater than minBreakForce. Otherwise it leaves the joint's existing threshold unchanged.

The native Grip constructor initializes both endpoints to positive infinity, so this optional squeeze-driven update is skipped by default and leaves the joint’s existing threshold alone. Serialized content can supply different values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.primaryMovementAxis
member.summary: Sets the grip's main direction for twisting, cylinder travel, and the hand's physics connection to the object.

remarks.para: The vector is relative to targetTransform's orientation, not the world's axes. Use a unit vector, meaning a direction with length 1: (0, 0, 1) points along the target's blue Z axis; (1, 0, 0) points along its red X axis. Turning targetTransform turns this direction in the world. This is a direction, not a distance or speed.

For cylinder and sphere grips, this also defines the forward direction of the coordinate frame used to limit hand targets. A hand target is the position and rotation the game wants the hand to reach; the physical hand can lag behind it. Cylinder grab scoring separately assumes the target's local Z axis, so changing this vector alone does not reorient every part of cylinder grabbing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.priority
member.summary: Weights this grip’s hover-selection score: smaller values generally make an eligible grip easier to choose over nearby alternatives.

remarks.para: The hand combines geometry, orientation, motion, and this weight, then chooses the lowest valid score. A weight of 1 leaves this factor neutral; 2 doubles this part of the score and tends to make the grip less preferred. These are unitless examples, not distances or guaranteed rankings.

Zero does not bypass the subclass’s acceptance checks or availability conditions, and equal scores do not guarantee this grip wins. The Inspector range is an editing hint; the audited runtime does not clamp this field to that range.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.radius
member.summary: Sets the grip's size for the hand pose, and affects cylinder and sphere grip scoring and large-radius hand offsets.

remarks.para: The radius is a center-to-surface distance in meters. For example, 0.03 represents a 3 cm radius, or 6 cm diameter. The hand pose uses it to choose how the fingers wrap around the grip. CylinderGrip and SphereGrip also use it when judging a possible grab, so changing it can change which nearby positions are accepted or preferred.

Large grips use extra hand-target offsets; a target is where the game wants the hand to be, not necessarily where the physical hand already is. SphereGrip's force-pull target moves along the third direction, secondaryMovementAxis crossed with primaryMovementAxis, by the amount radius exceeds its internal hand-size threshold. The direction reverses between hands. With primary (0, 0, 1) and secondary (0, 1, 0), that direction is the target's local X axis. The radius is not the hand's hover-search sphere radius.

GetHandState copies radius into a new hand record’s poseRadius, which held updates pass to the pose animator. Changing radius later affects direct shape checks, but does not automatically refresh an existing record’s poseRadius.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.secondaryMovementAxis
member.summary: Sets the grip's reference up direction and the second axis of the hand's physics connection, alongside .

remarks.para: The vector is relative to targetTransform's orientation. With primaryMovementAxis = (0, 0, 1), use (0, 1, 0) for the target's green Y axis as up. These directions define how cylinder and sphere hand targets are oriented and limited. Use unit vectors at right angles to each other; changing this direction turns the frame around the primary direction.

The third direction is secondaryMovementAxis crossed with primaryMovementAxis: with the example above it is (1, 0, 0). SphereGrip uses that third direction for its large-radius force-pull offset. This vector does not set a separate movement speed or distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.targetTransform
member.summary: Defines the grip’s base position and orientation for desired handle targets.

remarks.para: If it is missing, Awake, Unity’s initialization routine for this component, uses its own Transform, which stores its position, rotation, and scale. Per-hand targets are stored relative to this base, so moving or rotating it moves the desired targets in the world. Grip’s SimpleTransform conversions use position and rotation without scale; a shape subclass can separately use scale in its geometry checks.

A handle target is the grip connection point the hand should reach, not always the center of the physical hand. Hand-pose offsets and grip limits contribute to the final desired hand pose, and the physical hand can lag behind that pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.velocityHistory
member.summary: Keeps recent object velocities relative to the player’s whole-body movement for calculating release velocity.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in Unity’s physics simulation; the joint is the physics connection holding the hand and object together. The player physics rig simulates the player’s physical body. Each entry is a world-axis vector in meters per second. When an attached hand has a live joint connected to a Rigidbody, Grip records that body’s world velocity minus the player physics rig’s whole-body velocity. New samples overwrite old slots in a circular array; angular samples use the matching slot in angVelocityHistory.

The release calculation combines recent sample directions, uses the largest sampled speed rather than an ordinary arithmetic average, applies the linear throw multiplier, and adds whole-body velocity back. This is recorded motion, not a force or an impulse. Held updates overwrite recorded slots. ClearHistory in this implementation repeatedly zeroes only the current slot, rather than clearing the whole array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip.velocityHistoryIndex
member.summary: Identifies the newest recorded slot shared by the linear and angular velocity histories.

remarks.para: When recording connected-body motion, the index advances by one and wraps to zero at the array length, then both arrays receive a sample at that index. The release calculation walks backward from it to read recent samples. This is an array position, not elapsed time or a release impulse.
Changing the index yourself does not move samples and can make the release calculation read the wrong history. ClearHistory does not reset this index; it repeatedly writes zero to this one slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.Cache
member.summary: Stores guns registered during Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) so game code and mods can find their components from their GameObjects.

remarks.para: This is a ComponentCache, not a list of only currently spawned guns. A gun is added in Awake and removed in OnDestroy; returning it to the object pool does not remove it here. The cache is created on first access and its static reference is cleared when the last registered gun is destroyed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.MagazineState
member.summary: Holds the magazine data and cartridge list that the gun actually feeds rounds from.

remarks.para: For a removable magazine, assigning a non-null state also marks the gun as having a magazine; assigning null clears that flag. When internalMagazine is assigned, this setter ignores the incoming value because Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) creates the internal state.

The socket assigns removable-magazine state before calling OnMagazineInserted and clears it after calling OnMagazineRemoved. Setting this property alone does not run those sound/art callbacks (routines called to carry out actions or report events) or physically insert a magazine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnMagazineEjectDelegate
member.summary: Receives requests to eject the magazine from controller input or the gun's automatic slide-lock path.

remarks.para: With isMagEjectOnEmpty disabled, Update invokes it when the trigger-grip controller reports magazine-eject input. With that option enabled, SlideLocked invokes it instead. AmmoSocket subscribes EjectMagazine during its setup.

There are no callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) arguments. This is an ejection request, not a notification that a magazine has already detached; it can run when no magazine is available to eject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnSlideGrabbed
member.summary: Notifies listeners after the slide controller begins manual control and records the slide's firing-block state.

remarks.para: There are no callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) arguments. The callback wired in Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) first enters slide override and applies allowFireOnSlideGrabbed, then invokes this delegate. Calling SlideGrabbed directly only sets the blocking flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnSlideReleased
member.summary: Notifies listeners when the slide controller ends manual control on a gun using a non-manual fire mode.

remarks.para: There are no callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) arguments. The wired release callback resumes any permitted timed animation and clears the slide-grab blocking flag before invoking listeners. It skips this delegate in manual fire mode. Calling SlideGrabbedReleased directly does not invoke it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.OnSlideUpdate
member.summary: Receives the slide controller's reported pull fraction after that value has been saved for the gun's manual animation.

remarks.para: The float argument is slide travel: 0 is forward and 1 is fully pulled back. For example, 0.5 means halfway through the pull. The callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) forwards controller reports; it is not an unconditional event every rendered frame.
Calling UpdateSlidePercentage directly stores the same input but does not invoke this delegate. A listener can use these reports to match custom camera shake or sound to slide travel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._ammoInventory
member.summary: Supplies the reserve-ammunition limit for magazine feeding and loses one matching round when OnFire runs.

remarks.para: OnTriggerGripAttached copies the current shared AmmoInventory instance into this reference when the player grabs the trigger grip. AmmoCount combines its matching-cartridge count with the magazine count; OnFire spends the chambered cartridge's reserve ammo.

Changing this reference changes those subsequent checks and deductions. A later trigger-grip attachment can replace it again. Without an inventory reference, AmmoCount uses its 999-round reserve fallback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared gun ComponentCache used by Cache, Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) registration, and destruction cleanup.

remarks.para: This field is static, shared by all guns. Cache creates it when needed, and OnDestroy clears it when the registry becomes empty. Replacing it with an empty cache loses the registrations already recorded there.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._chamberedCartridgeArt
member.summary: Keeps the spawned visual round attached at chamberedCatridgeGameObject so the gun can show a live chambered cartridge.

remarks.para: UpdateMagazineArt prepares this object and _hasChamberedCartArt records that it exists. UpdateArt shows it for UNSPENT and hides it for an empty chamber or spent case. It is separate from chamberedCartridge, which stores the ammunition data.
The art can stay allocated while hidden. Cleanup returns it through the gun's art-despawn path; changing this reference alone does not update the matching presence flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._chamberedCartridgeCaseArt
member.summary: Keeps the spawned empty-case visual attached at chamberedCaseGameObject for a round that has been fired but not ejected.

remarks.para: UpdateArt shows it when cartridgeState is SPENT and hides it when the chamber is empty or contains an unfired round. _hasChamberedCaseArt records whether this art object has been prepared, even while its renderers are hidden.
This is display art held inside the gun, separate from the loose case spawned during ejection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._chargingHandleHelperRenderer
member.summary: Selects the renderer (the Unity component that draws the visual hint) that flashes when the gun needs its action charged or its locked slide released.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) copies chargingHelperHighRes into this reference. CheckGunRequirements selects it for a charging hint, and the hint coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames) temporarily enables and blinks it. Its transform also locates the charging-handle area for the configured collision-triggered slide release.
Replacing this selected reference redirects those later hint and collision-position checks. It does not change the slide controller's travel geometry.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._hasChamberedCartArt
member.summary: Records that the chambered live-round art was prepared and can be shown or hidden by the gun.

remarks.para: True does not mean the round is visible or ready to fire: UpdateArt also checks cartridgeState. This flag is set after UpdateMagazineArt attaches the art and cleared when that art is released. Keep it consistent with _chamberedCartridgeArt; true with a missing object makes art updates fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._hasChamberedCaseArt
member.summary: Records that the chambered empty-case art was prepared and can be shown or hidden by the gun.

remarks.para: True does not mean a spent case is visible: UpdateArt shows this object only for SPENT. UpdateMagazineArt sets the flag after attachment, and art cleanup clears it. Keep it consistent with _chamberedCartridgeCaseArt; true with a missing object makes art updates fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._hasMagState
member.summary: Records whether a removable-magazine state is assigned, which HasMagazine uses when there is no internal magazine.

remarks.para: The MagazineState setter updates it from whether _magState is non-null. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) also sets it when creating an internal magazine state. It is not a flag saying the state was refreshed this frame, and it does not mean ammunition remains.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._hasNextCartArt
member.summary: Records that the next-round art object has been prepared for the magazine feed position.

remarks.para: The object is shown only while HasMagazine is true and AmmoCount is positive. It can remain allocated but hidden when ammo runs out. Keep this flag consistent with _nextCartridgeArt; the gun uses it before trying to change that object's visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._isSlideGrabbed
member.summary: Blocks a shot while a slide grab that disallows firing is active.

remarks.para: SlideGrabbed and the wired controller grab callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) set this to the opposite of allowFireOnSlideGrabbed. Release clears it. Consequently, this is a firing-block flag rather than a complete record of whether a hand is touching the slide.
Fire refuses a shot when it is true, and CompleteSlidePull also clears isFiring when it is true. Changing allowFireOnSlideGrabbed after the grab does not recompute this stored flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._isUpdatingArt
member.summary: Prevents a second magazine-art update from starting while the current asynchronous update is still preparing its objects.

remarks.para: UpdateMagazineArt sets this before spawning art and clears it at the successful end. A competing call exits; it does not queue another refresh or wait for the first one. Manually leaving this true makes later calls skip their art work.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._magState
member.summary: Stores the actual magazine data and cartridge list consumed when the gun loads its next round.

remarks.para: MagazineState returns this same object. PullCartridge limits and removes rounds from its list, and instant loading refills it. It is not a previous-frame copy used to detect changes.
Writing this field directly bypasses the MagazineState setter's _hasMagState update and internal-magazine guard. Prefer that property when changing removable-magazine state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._magazineHelperRenderer
member.summary: Selects the renderer (the Unity component that draws the visual hint) that flashes when the gun needs a magazine or more usable magazine ammunition.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) copies magazineHelperHighRes into this reference. CheckGunRequirements chooses it when no magazine or usable magazine ammo is available and chamberedCartridge is absent. The blink coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames) enables it temporarily, changes its material appearance each frame, then disables it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._nextCartridgeArt
member.summary: Keeps the spawned visual round at nextCartridgeGameObject to show ammunition waiting to feed from the magazine.

remarks.para: It is shown only while a magazine is present and AmmoCount is positive. This object is separate from the cartridge data in the magazine and from the art for a round already chambered.
UpdateMagazineArt prepares it; magazine-removal cleanup releases it and clears _hasNextCartArt. Its presence alone does not guarantee a round can be fired.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._waitForEOF
member.summary: Provides the reusable end-of-frame wait used before applying gun animation-completion effects.

remarks.para: The constructor creates this WaitForEndOfFrame object. The completion coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames) yields it before running the finished slide-pull or slide-return logic, so reaching an animation endpoint does not perform all of that work immediately in the same call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun._wasInstaLoaded
member.summary: Marks the instant-loading path so the next magazine-insertion callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) can skip insertion audio and apply configured instant charging.

remarks.para: InstantLoadAsync sets it before refilling or awaiting the socket. OnMagazineInserted clears it after any isCharged work. If no insertion callback occurs, it can remain true; it is not a reliable indicator that a magazine has finished spawning or is currently loaded.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.allowFireOnSlideGrabbed
member.summary: Allows a slide grab to leave the shot-blocking flag clear, so holding the slide does not by itself prevent firing.

remarks.para: The value is sampled when SlideGrabbed or the slide-controller grab callback (a routine called to carry out an action or report an event) runs. False sets _isSlideGrabbed, which Fire later checks; true leaves that block clear. The normal slide, hammer and cartridge requirements still apply.
Changing this option while a grab is already active does not automatically recompute _isSlideGrabbed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.ammoSocket
member.summary: Connects the gun to physical magazine insertion, removal, instant loading, and magazine-ejection requests.

remarks.para: AmmoSocket assigns itself to this field during Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up). For a removable magazine it supplies MagazineState before calling OnMagazineInserted, then calls OnMagazineRemoved before clearing the state. It can also add cartridge data to an internal magazine.

InstantLoadAsync uses this socket with defaultMagazine when assigned. MakeStatic and MakeDynamic use its current magazine host to disable or enable collision shapes. An internal-magazine gun can still have a socket; this reference is not guaranteed to be null for that setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.animationState
member.summary: Records the gun animation state most recently selected by its animation methods or manual slide update.

remarks.para: The gun's own code changes this during automatic playback, manual override, pooling and slide-lock handling. It can be a reversed variant even though animator uses the same clip as its forward counterpart.
Assigning this field alone does not move the slide visual or perform completion effects. SetAnimationState displays a chosen clip position; PlayAnimationState also advances it over time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.animator
member.summary: Displays the gun's neutral, slide-pull, slide-return and slide-lock clips at positions selected by Gun.

remarks.para: An Animator is the Unity component that displays animation clips. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) sets its speed to zero; Gun advances the chosen clip position itself using timed coroutines (action sequences that pause and continue across frames) or manual slide travel. Setting an ordinary playback speed is therefore different from changing the gun's firing-cycle timing.

The gun uses layer 0 and cached state-name hashes. Culling here means temporarily disabling the entity's gun/display work: the cull handler disables the Animator while retaining its controller state, and the uncull handler re-enables it when the entity is active again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.blinkHighlightCoroutine
member.summary: Tracks the temporary reload/charging hint blink so CheckGunRequirements does not start overlapping hints.

remarks.para: The hint enables the selected helper renderer (the Unity component that draws the visual hint), updates its material brightness across frames using unscaled elapsed time, then disables it and clears this handle after about one second. Unscaled time means the hint timing is not multiplied by the game's time-scale setting.
Assigning null does not stop a running coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames); it only removes the handle that prevents another hint from starting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.cachedVelocity
member.summary: Stores the gun's last captured world movement velocity for the spawned muzzle flare to inherit.

remarks.para: The vector is meters per second along world X, Y and Z. For example, (1, 0, 0) means moving at 1 meter per second toward world positive X; turning the gun does not rotate this coordinate frame.

Fire refreshes it when it can obtain the gun's Rigidbody (Unity's component for simulated physics movement). SpawnFlareAsync reads it after the flare finishes spawning and assigns it to that flare's Rigidbody velocity. It is a cached value, not a continuously updated movement measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.cartridgeState
member.summary: Records whether the chamber is empty, holds an unfired round, or holds a spent case.

remarks.para: NONE means empty, UNSPENT means a live round, and SPENT means a fired round's case is still present. PullCartridge sets UNSPENT after loading; a successful Fire changes it to SPENT; EjectCartridge clears it to NONE.
The state selects chamber art and controls shot/dry-fire behavior. It is separate from chamberedCartridge, which holds the round's data; changing only one can leave the gun inconsistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.chamberedCartridge
member.summary: Holds the ammunition definition for the round or spent case currently in the chamber.

remarks.para: The data supplies ProjectileData, the projectile definition and settings passed to the static ProjectileEmitter.Emit routine, together with full-round and empty-case spawnables and reserve-ammo identity. PullCartridge assigns it, and EjectCartridge clears it. After firing, the same data remains while cartridgeState is SPENT, so this reference does not by itself mean a live round is ready.
Changing the data alone does not update cartridgeState or recreate the stored chamber art.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.chamberedCaseGameObject
member.summary: Provides the attachment position and rotation for the spawned visual of a spent case still inside the gun.

remarks.para: UpdateMagazineArt uses this object's transform when attaching _chamberedCartridgeCaseArt. The spawned case art is then shown for SPENT and hidden for other cartridge states. This reference is the attachment object, not the loose case launched by EjectCartridge.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.chamberedCatridgeGameObject
member.summary: Provides the attachment position and rotation for the spawned visual of a live round in the chamber.

remarks.para: UpdateMagazineArt attaches _chamberedCartridgeArt at this object's transform, and UpdateArt shows it while cartridgeState is UNSPENT. This object marks the art's location; chamberedCartridge holds the ammunition data.
The API preserves the game's spelling of Catridge in this member name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.chargingHelperHighRes
member.summary: Supplies the charging-handle hint renderer (the Unity component that draws the visual hint) selected when the gun awakens.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) activates its GameObject and copies it into _chargingHandleHelperRenderer. Pool initialization disables that selected renderer until a hint needs to flash it. CheckGunRequirements uses the hint to show that the hammer needs cocking or the slide needs releasing.
The selected reference is copied during setup; replacing chargingHelperHighRes later does not perform that copy again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.chargingHelperLowRes
member.summary: Holds the alternate charging-handle helper whose GameObject Gun.Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) disables during setup.

remarks.para: The checked setup selects chargingHelperHighRes for the active hint instead. The HighRes/LowRes names alone do not establish an automatic distance-based switch; no such switch is claimed here. Changing this reference does not reassign _chargingHandleHelperRenderer.
A helper renderer is the Unity component that draws this visual hint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.defaultCartridge
member.summary: Supplies the starting cartridge definition for the gun's internal magazine state.

remarks.para: When internalMagazine is assigned, Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) creates MagazineState and places this definition in its cartridge-data slot. Refilling and later feeding use that state. Its projectile spawnable is also registered during setup.
It is not the live chambered-cartridge field. Replacing defaultCartridge after setup does not automatically replace the existing MagazineState definition or chamberedCartridge.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.defaultMagazine
member.summary: Chooses the magazine definition requested when InstantLoadAsync force-loads an assigned ammo socket.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this component is being set up) registers its spawnable when the definition is present. Pool initialization starts instant loading when isLoaded is enabled; merely assigning defaultMagazine does not insert or spawn a magazine immediately.
This definition does not replace an existing internalMagazine. A missing ammo socket skips the force-load request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.entity
member.summary: Registers this gun for MarrowEntity culling changes that temporarily disable or restore its component and animation work.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups an object's game and physics parts. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) registers Gun as an event handler on this reference; OnDestroy unregisters it. Culling here means temporarily disabling this component and its Animator work when the entity is marked culled. Gun keeps the animation-controller state, then re-enables both when it receives the uncull notification. This entry does not assume which visibility or other criterion caused that state.
Replacing this field after Awake does not move the already-created event registration to the new entity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.fireCurve
member.summary: Shapes how quickly the timed slide-pull animation moves through its clip.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time divided by the remaining pull-animation duration: 0 is the start of that segment, 0.5 is halfway through its time, and 1 is its end. The vertical axis is an animation-progress blend fraction, limited to 0 through 1 before it is applied. It is not seconds, bullet speed, or damage.

For a pull starting at 0, a curve value of 0.2 at horizontal 0.5 displays 20% of the clip halfway through the segment. A straight line from (0, 0) to (1, 1) gives even progress. For a sequence starting at 0.5, the same curve value blends from that midpoint toward 1 rather than restarting at 0.

The configured pull duration is fireDuration times pullAnimationPerc: fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds, and pullAnimationPerc is the unitless share of that period assigned to the pull. A curve that never reaches its final progress can end its time without running the full-pull completion logic. Manual slide override uses the hand's pull fraction directly instead of this curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.fireDuration
member.summary: Stores the cached base firing period in seconds, which the independent pull and return shares use to calculate segment durations.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) calculates this base period as 60 divided by roundsPerMinute, the configured rate in rounds per minute. Timed slide pull lasts fireDuration times pullAnimationPerc; return lasts fireDuration times returnAnimationPerc. fireDuration is in seconds, while pullAnimationPerc and returnAnimationPerc are independent unitless duration shares. The full timed pull-plus-return duration is fireDuration times (pullAnimationPerc plus returnAnimationPerc); the shares are not forced to total 1. For an illustrative 600 rounds per minute, fireDuration is 0.1 seconds; shares 0.2 and 0.8 give a 0.02-second pull and 0.08-second return, totaling 0.1 seconds for those particular shares.

This base period is neither a single pull duration nor the bullet's travel time; it equals the full timed pull-plus-return duration only when the two shares total 1. Awake overwrites an earlier assignment. Changing roundsPerMinute later does not automatically recalculate this field, and manual fire mode still relies on physical action handling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.fireMode
member.summary: Chooses whether the gun cycles automatically and whether one trigger press may fire repeatedly.

remarks.para: MANUAL fires at most once per press and leaves the hammer uncocked after a shot; the slide/action must be operated again. SEMIAUTOMATIC starts the automatic slide cycle but blocks another shot until the press latch is reset. AUTOMATIC starts that cycle and allows further shots while the trigger stays pressed, once the slide and hammer are ready again.

All modes still require the shot's slide, hammer and live-cartridge conditions. Manual mode also changes controller freezing and empty-slide-lock behavior, so switching modes is more than changing an animation label.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.firePointTransform
member.summary: Places and aims projectile emission and the spawned muzzle flare, and locates where recoil is applied to the gun.

remarks.para: Its position and rotation are read in world (the scene coordinate frame) space. OnFire passes the transform and the chambered cartridge's ProjectileData definition/settings to the static ProjectileEmitter.Emit routine; SpawnFlareAsync uses its position and rotation for the muzzle effect. Fire uses its world forward/right directions and position for the recoil impulse (a brief transfer of momentum that pushes the gun for recoil).

Moving this transform therefore changes more than visible flash placement: it also changes the emission reference and the recoil application point. Its coordinates are not measured relative to the player's head.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.fireSpeedHash
member.summary: Stores the Animator identifier calculated from the name FireSpeed during Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up).

remarks.para: An Animator hash is a numeric identifier for a named parameter or state, not a speed value. No later use of this field was found in the complete audited Gun methods, including its animation coroutines (action sequences that pause and continue across frames); changing it is not a verified way to change shot cadence. External classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.gunSFX
member.summary: Provides gunshot, dry-fire, grip, magazine and slide sounds, with controller vibration for several action sounds.

remarks.para: Gun calls the appropriate GunSFX method when firing, handling an empty chamber, grabbing the trigger grip, inserting/removing a magazine or completing slide movement. The audio clips are configured on that GunSFX component; the gun does not use this reference to store ammunition or projectile data.
Loose casing audio comes from the spawned FirearmCartridge's ShellSFX. Many Gun paths expect gunSFX to be assigned; null is not a general mute option.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.hammerState
member.summary: Records whether the hammer is ready to strike the cartridge: COCKED permits a shot; UNCOCKED prevents it.

remarks.para: A hammer is the part of the firing action that strikes the round. Charge and CompleteSlidePull set COCKED. Manual-mode OnFire and an empty-chamber dry fire set UNCOCKED. Pool initialization resets it before any configured charging work.
Setting COCKED alone does not load a cartridge or return the slide forward. Fire checks those conditions separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.hasFiredOnce
member.summary: Remembers that the current trigger press has already been used, preventing repeat shots in manual and semiautomatic modes.

remarks.para: Fire sets it when accepting a shot/dry-fire attempt, and also when trigger input releases a locked slide instead of firing. AUTOMATIC ignores this repeat-shot block. CeaseFire clears it, and the normal Update clears it when trigger input falls below 0.3.
This is a press latch, not a special opening-sound selector. Pool initialization clears it too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.host
member.summary: Connects the gun to its physical object and attached hands for recoil, feedback and grip notifications.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost groups the grips and physical object a hand can hold. Fire uses its GameObject to find the gun's physics body, reads that body's movement and applies recoil, then sends feedback to its attached hands. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) also subscribes to its grab/drop notifications.

OnFire uses the host's trigger proxy when proxyOverride is absent or invalid. Here the proxy is a reference included with projectile hit reports: it is saved in Projectile, copied to Attack.proxy and sent to the hit object's ReceiveAttack routine. Cartridge-art packing and shell launch also rely on the host's body, so assigning only a visual object is not sufficient.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.internalMagazine
member.summary: Configures the gun to keep its own magazine state instead of adopting a removable magazine's state.

remarks.para: During Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up), the gun creates MagazineState from this magazine definition and defaultCartridge. HasMagazine then returns true for the internal-magazine setup even when it has no rounds. The MagazineState setter ignores replacements while this definition is assigned.

An AmmoSocket can still supply rounds to an internal magazine: its insertion path adds cartridge data to the existing state. This field is setup data, not the list of rounds currently remaining. Changing it after Awake does not automatically rebuild that list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isCharged
member.summary: Requests automatic cocking and chamber loading during the gun's configured spawn or instant-load path.

remarks.para: In the configured charging paths, enabling this option calls the charging operation: slide forward, hammer cocked, old chamber contents ejected, and a new magazine round pulled if one is available. It is checked during pool initialization, existing-magazine instant loading, and the instant-load insertion callback (a routine called to perform an action or report an event).

It is not the current ready-to-fire state and Fire does not test it as that state. Use hammerState, slideState and cartridgeState to inspect those separate conditions. Changing it alone does not immediately chamber a round.

During initial Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) setup, this flag also causes MagazineState.Refill when HasMagazine is true. That operation clears and rebuilds the existing/internal magazine's cartridge list to its configured capacity. This initial refill is a separate effect from cocking the hammer and attempting to load the chamber during the later configured charging paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isFiring
member.summary: Marks an active firing request/cycle, which slide-completion logic uses when deciding sounds and when to stop firing.

remarks.para: Fire can set this before its later readiness checks refuse the shot, so true does not prove a projectile was emitted. Charge and SlideRelease clear it. CompleteSlidePull clears it for a blocked slide grab; CompleteSlideReturn clears it when the trigger-press latch has ended.
CeaseFire clears press latches without directly clearing this field. It can remain true while the automatic slide cycle continues.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isLoaded
member.summary: Requests instant ammunition loading when the gun is initialized from its object pool.

remarks.para: OnPoolInitialize starts InstantLoadAsync when this option is true. With it false, initialization can still run Charge when isCharged is enabled, using any available magazine state.
This is a spawn/loading option, not a live test of whether the magazine contains rounds. Changing it after initialization does not immediately refill ammunition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isMagEjectOnEmpty
member.summary: Requests magazine ejection from the slide-lock path instead of the controller's normal magazine-eject input path.

remarks.para: When true, SlideLocked invokes OnMagazineEjectDelegate; AmmoSocket normally subscribes its EjectMagazine method. In ordinary cycling, reaching that path depends on the empty-chamber and isSlideLockedOnEmpty conditions. The flag alone does not directly remove a magazine as soon as its count reaches zero.
When false, Gun.Update accepts the controller's eject input and invokes the same delegate. The socket also uses this option when deciding whether its magazine proxy grip is interactable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isSilenced
member.summary: No suppression effect was verified for this flag in the audited Gun and GunSFX methods.

remarks.para: The complete checked Gun class and GunSFX class do not read it to change shot volume, choose suppressed clips, change projectiles or disable the muzzle flare. GunSFX.GunShot passes its configured fire/fireSlow banks and fixed audio arguments to the sound player.

This is a finding about those audited methods, not proof that no other game code or mod can use the field. No working tuning range, quieter-sound guarantee or enemy-hearing effect is established here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isSlideLockedOnEmpty
member.summary: Allows the completed slide-pull path to hold the slide open when a magazine is present but no round was chambered.

remarks.para: The first empty-lock decision requires a non-manual fire mode. With the option disabled, the completed pull instead proceeds toward the return path. This is checked after ejection and an attempt to pull the next cartridge, so the final chamber state determines the empty condition.

When no manual override is active, a later lock decision checks the magazine/chamber/option again without repeating the fire-mode test. It does not lock merely because the magazine list became empty while a live round is already chambered. Locked-open state also enables the configured magazine-ejection request and later SlideRelease behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isSlideOverride
member.summary: Lets saved manual pull travel position the slide animation during Gun.Update.

remarks.para: While active, overridePerc is the unitless manual slide-pull fraction: 0 means fully forward/returned and 1 means fully pulled back. Update samples the pull clip at overridePerc and the return clip at 1 minus overridePerc. Clip position is also unitless, with 0 at the beginning and 1 at the end; subtracting the manual fraction reverses that progress. Automatic completion uses a manual-position branch instead of immediately starting a normal return coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames). SlideOverride sets this flag; SlideOverrideReleased clears it after selecting any timed continuation.
This flag does not by itself block shots or mean that a hand is physically holding the slide. _isSlideGrabbed records that separate firing block.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isSlideReleaseOnCollision
member.summary: Allows a strong enough collision near the charging-handle helper to release a locked-open slide.

remarks.para: The slide must already be LOCKED. The collision impulse (momentum transferred by the collision, measured in newton-seconds) magnitude must exceed 1 newton-second, and the first contact point must be less than 0.08 meters (8 cm) from the selected charging-handle hint renderer's transform position. That renderer is the Unity component drawing the visual charging-handle hint. The distances use world (the scene coordinate frame) positions.

For example, a contact 10 cm from that helper fails the distance test even if the impact is strong. Exact equality at 8 cm or impulse 1 does not pass. Passing the tests calls SlideRelease, which tries to feed a round and return the slide. The helper reference must be valid for this path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isTriggerPressed
member.summary: Remembers an accepted trigger press across frames until release or CeaseFire clears it.

remarks.para: Fire sets it when the slide-grab rules allow a firing request. Gun.Update clears it when the controller trigger drops below 0.3; CeaseFire also clears it. CompleteSlideReturn checks it to decide whether a firing cycle should stop.
It is not a one-frame edge signal. It can stay true while the trigger is held, including when a later shot-readiness check rejects firing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isTriggerPulled
member.summary: Tracks the gun's pressed/released trigger state using separate press and release thresholds.

remarks.para: In the normal controller Update path, both input above 0.5 and a clear isTriggerPulledOnAttach latch are required to enter the press branch. That branch calls Fire first, then, if isTriggerPulled was false, sends press-click feedback and writes it true. Input above 0.5 alone does not make that write while the attachment latch is set. Input below 0.3 clears it. The gap keeps small input changes from repeatedly switching the state; for example, 0.4 preserves the previous state.
This flag also prevents repeated press/release click feedback. It is not the raw trigger input value and changing it alone does not fire a round.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.isTriggerPulledOnAttach
member.summary: Blocks normal trigger-driven firing when the trigger was already held as the trigger grip was grabbed.

remarks.para: OnTriggerGripAttached sets this latch if controller input is greater than 0.3. Gun.Update skips its trigger-driven Fire call while the latch is true and clears it once input falls below 0.3, requiring a release before a fresh press can fire.
Calling Fire directly bypasses this Update-only attachment check. Pool initialization resets the latch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.lastCompletedAnimation
member.summary: Remembers the animation endpoint already handled so holding at that endpoint does not repeat its completion work.

remarks.para: SetAnimationState and manual Update write this when a recognized forward or reversed endpoint is reached. Completion work is scheduled for the end of the frame, so the stored value can be updated before the slide-loading effects have run.

Sampling a different animation before its endpoint resets this to NONE. Repeated samples of the already-recorded state do not reset it automatically. Setting it to the current endpoint state can suppress completion handling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.leftOverTime
member.summary: Carries extra elapsed animation time into the next timed segment so frame timing does not discard it.

remarks.para: The value is seconds. CoPlayAnimation starts its elapsed timer from this field and writes elapsed time minus its segment duration when it finishes. Gun.Update subtracts Time.deltaTime from a positive remainder on later frames, setting a nonpositive remainder to zero.

For an illustrative segment ending with a 0.004-second remainder, the next timed segment can start 4 milliseconds ahead if it begins before that remainder is consumed. This is animation scheduling state, not extra bullet flight time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.magazineHelperHighRes
member.summary: Supplies the magazine hint renderer (the Unity component drawing this visual magazine hint) selected when the gun awakens.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) activates its GameObject and copies it into _magazineHelperRenderer. Pool initialization disables that renderer until CheckGunRequirements starts a blink, guiding the player toward a missing or unusable magazine.
Replacing this setup reference later does not automatically replace the selected renderer that the hint code uses.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.magazineHelperLowRes
member.summary: Holds the alternate magazine helper whose GameObject Gun.Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) disables during setup.

remarks.para: The checked setup selects magazineHelperHighRes for the active hint. No automatic distance-based switch is established by the audited Gun methods. Changing this field does not reassign _magazineHelperRenderer.
A helper renderer is the Unity component that draws this visual magazine hint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.muzzleFlareSpawnable
member.summary: Chooses the pooled visual effect started at firePointTransform when OnFire emits the shot.

remarks.para: A spawnable is an asset definition used to create an object, not an object already in the scene. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) registers this definition, and SpawnFlareAsync requests it at the firing point's world (the scene coordinate frame) position and rotation.

The spawned effect is expected to have a Rigidbody, Unity's component for simulated physics movement. Once loading finishes, that body receives cachedVelocity, the gun movement speed and direction saved by Fire in meters per second; this cache is read after loading, so it can have changed since the spawn request. This field does not choose the bullet projectile; the chambered cartridge supplies ProjectileData, the definition/settings used by static ProjectileEmitter.Emit, for that separate request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.muzzleVelocity
member.summary: Supplies the fallback recoil number used by Gun.Fire when chambered cartridge data is missing.

remarks.para: The Inspector describes this setting as meters per second, but the checked fallback branch multiplies its numeric value by 0.01 when calculating recoil. For a normal cartridge with an emitter, Fire uses that emitter's mass, velocity and projectile count instead.

Gun.OnFire does not pass this field to ProjectileEmitter.Emit, so overriding this field is not a verified way to change bullet launch speed. Missing cartridge data also leaves later firing work without its required definition; the fallback branch does not make such a setup a valid firearm.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.neutralHash
member.summary: Selects the Animator state used when the gun displays its neutral pose.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites this with Animator.StringToHash("Neutral"). A hash is the numeric identifier Unity uses to find that named state. SetAnimationState and pool initialization use it on animator layer 0; it is not a progress fraction or playback speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.nextCartridgeGameObject
member.summary: Provides the attachment position and rotation for art showing the next round waiting in the magazine.

remarks.para: UpdateMagazineArt attaches _nextCartridgeArt at this object's transform. The art is shown while HasMagazine is true and AmmoCount is positive. This reference marks the art's location; it is separate from the magazine cartridge data and the spawned visual round.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.onFireDelegate
member.summary: Notifies listeners after OnFire starts projectile-emission and muzzle-flare spawn requests, before either object is guaranteed ready.

remarks.para: The callback (a routine called to perform an action or report an event) argument is this Gun, allowing a listener to identify which gun fired. In the normal Fire path, cartridgeState is already SPENT before OnFire starts. OnFire removes one matching reserve round when _ammoInventory is assigned, starts the projectile-emission request, starts the flare-spawn request, then invokes this notification. Both spawn tasks can still be pending; GunShot audio and UpdateArt follow the notification in Fire. A dry fire or an ordinary rejected Fire attempt does not reach it.

Use it to react to the shot request in the normal firing path; it does not confirm that projectile spawning succeeded or completed. Subscribe without replacing existing listeners, and remove your subscription when your mod no longer needs it. Direct calls to OnFire can also invoke this callback, bypassing Fire's readiness checks and its SPENT/recoil writes; OnFire itself does not make those state changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.otherGrips
member.summary: Lists the gun's extra grips that become interactable while the trigger grip is held.

remarks.para: OnTriggerGripAttached enables interaction for every grip in the array. OnTriggerGripDetached disables them and forcibly detaches their hands; pool initialization also disables and detaches them.

The array is processed as configured rather than automatically gathering every non-trigger grip. Populate it with the support or action grips that should follow this holding rule. The checked loops expect a valid array and valid grip entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.overridePerc
member.summary: Stores the manual slide-pull fraction used while isSlideOverride is active.

remarks.para: 0 means fully forward and 1 means fully pulled back; 0.5 is halfway through the pull. Gun.Update uses it directly for a pull clip and uses 1 minus it for a return clip. The slide-controller update callback (a routine called to perform an action or report an event) and UpdateSlidePercentage write it.

SlideOverride initializes it for non-manual modes from whether the slide is already locked; SlideOverrideReleased resets it to zero. Assigning the field alone does not activate override, immediately sample the Animator or invoke OnSlideUpdate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.playAnimationStateCoroutine
member.summary: Tracks the timed gun-animation coroutine (an action sequence that pauses and continues across frames) so a new sequence can stop the previous one.

remarks.para: PlayAnimationState and the automatic slide-lock/return paths stop the saved coroutine before starting a replacement. CoPlayAnimation clears this handle, the saved reference used to stop the running sequence, when its sequence finishes, and pool deinitialization stops all coroutines.
Setting this field to null is not the same as stopping playback; the coroutine can continue after its handle is lost.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.proxyOverride
member.summary: Supplies an alternate trigger proxy, the reference included with projectile hit reports, to static ProjectileEmitter.Emit in place of the host's default proxy.

remarks.para: OnFire chooses this reference when it is a valid Unity object; otherwise it uses the proxy stored by host. The selected reference is saved in Projectile, copied into Attack.proxy when the projectile reports a hit, and sent as part of that report to ReceiveAttack on the hit object. This verified role does not promise team, hearing or credit behavior.
It does not redirect the player's trigger input in the checked Gun.Update path. That input is still obtained from triggerGrip's controller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.pullAnimationPerc
member.summary: Sets the share of the cached firing-cycle time assigned to timed slide pull.

remarks.para: This is a duration fraction, not the current clip position. The pull segment uses fireDuration times pullAnimationPerc: fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds, and pullAnimationPerc is its unitless pull-duration share. For fireDuration = 0.1 seconds and pullAnimationPerc = 0.2, a full timed pull lasts 0.02 seconds.

Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) also uses it to calculate pullAnimationSpeed. It does not automatically adjust returnAnimationPerc, the independent unitless return-duration share, to make the two shares total 1. Manual slide override uses overridePerc for position instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.pullAnimationSpeed
member.summary: Stores the setup calculation roundsPerSecond, the cached rate in rounds per second, divided by pullAnimationPerc, the unitless share of the base period assigned to the pull segment.

remarks.para: The calculated value is inverse seconds. For an illustrative 10 rounds per second and pull share 0.2, it is 50 per second, the reciprocal of a 0.02-second pull segment.

Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites this field. No later reader was found in the complete audited Gun methods and animation coroutines (action sequences that pause and continue across frames); those timed animations use fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds, and the unitless pullAnimationPerc duration share directly. Changing this cached value is therefore not a verified way to speed up the pull. External classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.returnAnimationPerc
member.summary: Sets the share of the cached firing-cycle time assigned to timed slide return.

remarks.para: It is a duration fraction, not current animation progress. A return segment uses fireDuration times returnAnimationPerc: fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds, and returnAnimationPerc is its unitless return-duration share. For fireDuration = 0.1 seconds and share 0.8, a full return lasts 0.08 seconds.

The automatic return and release-continuation paths use this share. It is independent of pullAnimationPerc, the unitless pull-duration share; the checked code does not force the two shares to total 1. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) also uses it to calculate returnAnimationSpeed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.returnAnimationSpeed
member.summary: Stores the setup calculation roundsPerSecond, the cached rate in rounds per second, divided by returnAnimationPerc, the unitless share of the base period assigned to the return segment.

remarks.para: The calculated value is inverse seconds. With illustrative values 10 rounds per second and return share 0.8, it is 12.5 per second, the reciprocal of a 0.08-second return.

Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites it. No later reader was found in the complete audited Gun methods or animation coroutines (action sequences that pause and continue across frames); the checked return paths calculate duration from fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds, times the unitless returnAnimationPerc duration share. Changing this field is not a verified way to change the return speed. External classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.returnCurve
member.summary: Shapes timed forward slide return and the reversed-pull continuation after an interrupted manual pull.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time divided by that remaining animation segment's duration. The vertical axis is a blend fraction, limited to the 0-to-1 interval before changing the clip position. For a forward return starting at 0, a value of 0.7 at horizontal 0.5 advances 70% through the return clip halfway through its time.

The interrupted-pull continuation uses SLIDEPULLREVERSED with this curve: as the curve rises from 0 to 1, the pull clip moves backward toward its starting position. Manual override itself positions clips directly and does not evaluate this curve.

Timed return duration comes from fireDuration times returnAnimationPerc: fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds, and returnAnimationPerc is its unitless return-duration share. Ending below the needed endpoint can leave the slide-completion logic untriggered; the elapsed timer ending alone does not force the clip to that endpoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.roundsPerMinute
member.summary: Sets the firing rate used during Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) to calculate the automatic slide cycle's cached timing.

remarks.para: Awake divides by 60 to get roundsPerSecond, the cached rate in rounds per second, then takes its reciprocal for fireDuration, the cached base firing period in seconds. Thus fireDuration equals 60 divided by the configured rounds-per-minute value. For example, 600 rounds per minute gives 10 rounds per second and a 0.1-second base period. pullAnimationPerc and returnAnimationPerc are independent unitless duration shares: full timed pull plus return lasts fireDuration times (pullAnimationPerc plus returnAnimationPerc). The shares are not forced to total 1; illustrative shares 0.2 and 0.8 give 0.02 seconds of pull and 0.08 seconds of return, totaling 0.1 seconds for those shares.

Changing this field after Awake does not automatically refresh those cached timing values. A configured rate also does not bypass an empty chamber, an unready slide or the once-per-press rule for manual/semiautomatic modes. The checked setup divides directly and supplies no protective clamp for zero or negative rates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.roundsPerSecond
member.summary: Stores roundsPerMinute divided by 60 when the gun awakens.

remarks.para: The unit is rounds per second; 600 rounds per minute produces 10. Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) uses that result to calculate fireDuration and the two animation-speed values, overwriting any earlier assignment. fireDuration is the cached base firing period in seconds of game time, equal to 1 divided by roundsPerSecond. pullAnimationSpeed and returnAnimationSpeed are segment rates in inverse seconds, calculated as roundsPerSecond divided by pullAnimationPerc or returnAnimationPerc respectively. Those two shares are independent unitless duration multipliers and are not forced to sum to 1.

The checked later animation paths use the cached duration and segment shares, not this field as a continuously sampled rate control. Updating roundsPerSecond alone after setup does not automatically rebuild those values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.shellOrientationTransform
member.summary: Chooses the directions used to launch and spin loose ejected cartridges and cases.

remarks.para: After the loose object has spawned, SpawnCartridge reads this transform's world right direction as the launch direction and world up as the added spin axis. World directions are expressed in the scene coordinate frame. Turning the transform changes those world directions. The FirearmCartridge adds the host body's motion plus its own configured launch/spin speeds with random variation.
This does not supply the spawned case's initial rotation: shellSpawnTransform supplies both initial position and rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.shellSpawnTransform
member.summary: Places and orients the loose cartridge or case when ejection spawning begins.

remarks.para: Before awaiting the spawn result, SpawnCartridge reads this transform's world position and rotation for the spawn request. World means the scene coordinate frame, rather than coordinates relative to the gun or player. shellOrientationTransform separately supplies launch and spin directions after the object appears.
Moving it changes the ejection origin; rotating it changes the object's initial orientation. It does not place the visual round that remains attached inside the chamber.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slideLockDuration
member.summary: Sets the duration in seconds of the timed slide-lock animation.

remarks.para: SlideLocked and PlayAnimationState use this as the full lock-animation duration; starting partway through a timed sequence shortens the remaining segment. For example, 0.1 means a tenth of a second for the full animation.
