This is not a timer that automatically unlocks the slide. The logical slide remains LOCKED until another action such as SlideRelease changes it, even after the lock animation finishes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slideLockedHash
member.summary: Selects the Animator clip used for locked-slide visuals, including the reversed lock animation.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites it with Animator.StringToHash("SlideLocked"). A hash is Unity's numeric lookup identifier. SetAnimationState uses it on layer 0; the progress value determines which point of that clip is shown.
Changing this identifier selects different visual state lookup; it does not itself change slideState to LOCKED.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slidePullHash
member.summary: Selects the Animator clip used for forward and reversed slide-pull visuals.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites it with Animator.StringToHash("SlidePull"). The same clip is sampled at different normalized positions for forward and reversed motion, including manual override. Normalized clip position is a unitless fraction: 0 is the beginning and 1 is the end.

This is a state identifier, not a speed. Changing the identifier alone does not load a round or cock the hammer. Completion of a full forward pull cocks the hammer (makes it ready to strike), ejects the old cartridge and attempts to feed another; completing a reversed partial pull only marks the slide RETURNED.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slideReturnHash
member.summary: Selects the Animator clip used for forward and reversed slide-return visuals.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) overwrites it with Animator.StringToHash("SlideReturn"). SetAnimationState and manual slide Update sample this clip on layer 0. The selected position comes from timed animation progress or 1 minus overridePerc. overridePerc is the unitless manual slide-pull fraction: 0 means fully forward/returned and 1 means fully pulled back. The sampled clip position is unitless too, with 0 at its beginning and 1 at its end, so 1 minus the manual fraction reverses that progress.
It is a lookup identifier, not the return duration or the logical slide state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slideState
member.summary: Records where the gun's action is in its pull/return cycle and whether firing can proceed.

remarks.para: RETURNED is fully forward and is the slide state Fire requires for a shot. PULLING means a rearward stroke is underway; PULLED means its rear endpoint has been reached; RETURNING marks a forward-motion state; LOCKED holds the action open.

The gun's completion, override, loading and release methods update this separately from animationState. A slide-lock release tries to load a round and start return; assigning this state field alone does not move the Animator, chamber ammunition or cock the hammer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.slideVirtualController
member.summary: Turns the slide hand's movement into manual slide travel and grab/release notifications for this gun.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) subscribes the gun to this controller's travel, pull, grab and release callbacks (routines called to perform actions or report events). Travel is reported as a fraction from forward to fully pulled; the gun saves it for manual animation. Grabbing enters override and applies the slide-grab firing block; release resumes allowed timed movement and clears that block.

The controller uses its configured track direction and the hand/control payload, not panels as a substitute for a hand grip. Manual fire mode can freeze it after a full pull and unfreeze it on a shot or dry fire.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.triggerGrip
member.summary: Provides the held controller whose trigger input drives this gun's normal firing and magazine-eject input.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) subscribes to its hand-attachment callbacks (routines called to perform actions or report events). Attachment captures the current AmmoInventory, enables otherGrips and can block a trigger already held down. Detachment disables and releases those other grips.

Gun.Update returns early without a valid triggerGrip, and only reads trigger input when this grip can supply a controller. Direct scripted Fire calls have their own readiness checks and are separate from this controller-input path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.weaponSlot
member.summary: Connects the gun to WeaponSlot notifications that disable or enable its inserted magazine's collision shapes.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity's initialization routine, called while this gun component is being set up) subscribes MakeStatic to the slot component's static notification and MakeDynamic to its dynamic notification. Those gun callbacks (routines called to perform actions or report events) find the magazine host through ammoSocket and change that host's colliders, when one exists.

This is a component reference supplying those notifications, not a field containing the player's currently occupied holster location. Replacing it after Awake does not automatically rebuild the event subscriptions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.CanFireGun
member.summary: Reports whether the manager currently allows the normal held-trigger input path to request a shot.

remarks.para: Gun.Update consults this permission when GunManager.HasInstance is set. EnableGunFire and DisableGunFire change the same stored value. It is permission only: true does not mean a particular gun has ammo or is mechanically ready.
A direct Gun.Fire call bypasses this manager check in the audited Gun implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.HasInstance
member.summary: Records that a GunManager registered itself as the singleton during Awake.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine called to initialize this component. The singleton is the shared manager referenced by Instance. OnDestroy is the callback called when this component is destroyed.

Awake sets this flag when it accepts a new Instance. The audited OnDestroy removes fire subscriptions but does not clear HasInstance or Instance, so this field is not a continuously recomputed test that the Unity object is still valid.
Gun uses this flag before accessing the singleton for input permission and grab/drop reports. Keep it consistent with Instance when changing singleton state from a mod.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager.Instance
member.summary: Stores the GunManager accepted as the singleton during Awake.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine called to initialize this component. The singleton is the shared manager referenced by Instance. OnDestroy is the callback called when this component is destroyed.

A new manager registers itself only when the previous Unity instance compares as missing; otherwise Awake logs a duplicate-manager error and leaves the existing reference. Gun uses the singleton for its normal input-permission check and grab/drop reports.
The audited OnDestroy removes subscriptions but leaves this static reference and HasInstance unchanged. Holding a reference here does not by itself prove the Unity component is still alive.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._canFireGun
member.summary: Stores the permission read by CanFireGun to gate normal trigger-driven Gun.Update firing.

remarks.para: DisableGunFire sets it false and EnableGunFire sets it true. Changing it does not chamber rounds or affect the mechanical readiness checks in a direct Gun.Fire call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._gunDroppedCallbacks
member.summary: Stores listeners called for releases of tracked guns by hands whose rigs match _playerTag.

remarks.para: Each Action is registered code that the manager calls with the releasing Hand and Gun; these are the listeners stored in this list. OnGunDropped invokes them before decreasing the grab count, including when another tracked hand still holds the gun.

Registration adds a list entry and unregistration removes an entry. Duplicate registrations are not filtered; they can produce repeated calls. Avoid changing this list while the manager is iterating it.
_playerTag is the manager's configured matching rule for the entity belonging to the hand's physics rig. It is not automatically a local-player lookup or a test of the gun's tag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._gunFireCallbacks
member.summary: Stores listeners that receive a Gun when the manager forwards its fire notification.

remarks.para: The normal forwarding subscription exists while at least one matching grab is counted. This is not a scan of every gun in the scene; a gun never accepted by OnGunGrabbed has no manager subscription from that path.
RegisterGunFireCallback adds to this list without deduplicating. OnGunFire invokes each entry, so duplicate listeners run repeatedly. Avoid changing the list during that iteration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._gunGrabCount
member.summary: Counts accepted grab notifications for each gun, keeping fire forwarding subscribed until its last counted release.

remarks.para: The dictionary maps Gun to an integer. OnGunGrabbed first adds a missing gun with zero, then increments; a matching release decrements and removes the entry at zero or below. Only hands passing _playerTag participate.

For two accepted grabs, a release changes 2 to 1 and keeps the fire subscription; the next changes 1 to 0 and removes it. The counter does not store distinct hand identities, so duplicate grab reports can leave an extra count.
_playerTag is the manager's configured matching rule for the entity belonging to the hand's physics rig. It is not automatically a local-player lookup or a test of the gun's tag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._gunGrabbedCallbacks

remarks.para: Each Action is registered code that the manager calls with the grabbing Hand and Gun; these are the listeners stored in this list. OnGunGrabbed invokes the list before increasing the count or installing a first-grab fire subscription. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager._playerTag

remarks.para: OnGunGrabbed and OnGunDropped obtain Hand.manager.physicsRig.marrowEntity and test it with this MarrowQuery. A query is a configured rule for matching tagged entities. A nonmatch skips listeners and bookkeeping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX._gunshotMap
member.summary: Stores the reusable ManagedAudioPlayer used by GunShot.

remarks.para: When the GunSFX object is created, its constructor creates this playback helper; the helper obtains the actual AudioPlayer when needed. GunShot passes the normal and slow gunshot lists, current world position and playback settings to it. The helper keeps or obtains an AudioPlayer and submits the shot there. If no valid AudioPlayer is ready, playback can begin on a later frame while one is being obtained. Further requests during that wait replace the saved clip and playback settings, rather than queueing a separate sound for every call.

This is a playback object, not a table mapping gun events to sounds. Other GunSFX methods use Audio3dManager directly. Setting it to null prevents GunShot from making its required player call; it does not disable just one clip set.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX._host
member.summary: Caches the local InteractableHost used to find held hands for controller vibrations.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s one-time setup routine before this enabled component’s first frame update, gets InteractableHost from this GunSFX GameObject and stores it here. That host is the component that tracks attached hands. SlidePull, SlideRelease, MagazineInsert, MagazineDrop, SlideLock and DryFire then iterate its attached hands and vibrate each available controller Haptor after requesting audio. A Haptor is the controller’s vibration helper.

This cache does not subscribe to grip events or decide which sound to play. If the host is absent, those audio calls can still run but their vibration loop is skipped. Assigning a different host changes which held hands receive that feedback; Start replaces the cache with the component found locally.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.dryFire
member.summary: Supplies the normal clip variations for the empty-trigger click.

remarks.para: DryFire randomly chooses one clip and plays it at the GunSFX transform’s local origin. The click reports an attempted empty shot; the sound list does not check or alter ammunition.

dryFireSlow is considered when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less. A time scale of 1 is normal game speed, while 0.5 is half speed. An empty slow list falls back to the normal clips with time-dependent pitch adjustment.
Use an empty array to disable this sound. The playback helper returns for an empty normal list, including when a slow list is populated; a null normal array is not checked safely.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.dryFireSlow
member.summary: Supplies the slow-time alternate recordings for the empty-trigger click.

remarks.para: The slow-motion list is considered when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less. A time scale of 1 is normal game speed, while 0.5 is half speed. An empty slow list falls back to the normal clips with time-dependent pitch adjustment.

The normal dryFire list must be nonempty. Unlike GunShot’s managed-player path, this local playback helper randomly indexes the selected slow list using its own length, so it does not require an equal number of normal and slow clips.

Use an empty array to fall back to the normal recordings. A null slow array is not safe when time scale is 0.51 or less. Playback occurs at the gun’s local origin and also receives pitch adjustment based on slowed time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.fire
member.summary: Supplies the normal gunshot variations randomly selected by GunShot.

remarks.para: GunShot reads this list on each call and requests playback at the GunSFX transform’s current world position through _gunshotMap. The sound is an audio effect; changing the clips does not change damage, projectile speed or recoil.

The slow-motion list is considered when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less. A time scale of 1 is normal game speed, while 0.5 is half speed. An empty slow list falls back to the normal clips with time-dependent pitch adjustment.

This list’s length supplies the random index even when fireSlow is chosen. Keep a nonempty slow list at least as long as this one, preferably with corresponding variants at each index. Use an empty array to disable this sound. The playback helper returns for an empty normal list, including when a slow list is populated; a null normal array is not checked safely.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX.fireSlow

remarks.para: The slow-motion list is considered when Time.timeScale is 0.51 or less. A time scale of 1 is normal game speed, while 0.5 is half speed. An empty slow list falls back to the normal clips with time-dependent pitch adjustment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.Animator
member.summary: The pose animator that supplies this avatar's hand, wrist and handle poses.

remarks.para: Requires a valid manager and virtualHeptaRig; returns null when those are unavailable, before checking the cache. An existing live _animator is reused. On a left/right cache miss, finds the corresponding HandPoseAnimator in manager.physicsRig.artOutput and caches it in _animator. That lookup additionally requires initialized physicsRig and artOutput references; missing either does not use the null-return fallback. SetManager does not clear this cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.AttachedReceiver
member.summary: The receiver reserved for this hand while hover selection is locked.

remarks.para: HoverLock copies the current near-hover receiver here and clears the near/far hover targets. HoverUnlock clears this reference. GetGripInHand uses it to find a Grip and return that grip's target in hand-local coordinates.

This reference alone does not prove a GameObject or physics joint is attached. Changing it does not run AttachObject or the receiver's attachment callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action); HasAttachedObject checks the current attached GameObject and GrabLock instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.Cache
member.summary: Shared lookup table that finds a Hand component by its GameObject.

remarks.para: Created when first requested. Awake (Unity's initialization routine) registers each initialized hand; OnDestroy removes it and clears the cache reference when no entries remain. Query this for an existing Hand rather than assuming every GameObject has one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.Controller
member.summary: The controller input source assigned to this hand's left or right side.

remarks.para: On first access, asks manager.controllerRig for the controller matching handedness and caches it in _controller. Returns null if the manager or controller rig is unavailable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.GrabLock
member.summary: Makes HasAttachedObject report that the hand is occupied, even when no current attached GameObject exists.

remarks.para: SetGrabLock sets this flag. AttachObject clears it only after successfully finding a HandReciever for the new object. If that lookup fails, currentAttachedGO is stored but this flag is left unchanged. Changing this flag alone does not create a joint or select a receiver; hoverLocked separately controls hover searches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.HoverSphereRadius
member.summary: Radius in metres of the near-hover search around the palm.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering searches a sphere of this radius, centred ahead of the predicted palm by 0.8 times the radius. Increasing the radius expands the region that can supply near-hover candidates and moves the sphere centre farther forward; candidate validation and scoring still decide the winner.

For example, a radius of 0.1 means ten centimetres, with the sphere centre shifted eight centimetres forward from the predicted palm. This is a physics overlap query, not the size of the collider component.

The native constructor initializes it to 0.09 metres; scene or prefab data can supply another value. The setter copies the number without a runtime clamp. Far-hover aiming also places its aim-cone reference behind the predicted palm, along the far aim direction: reference = predictedPalm − farAimDirection × (3.04 × radius). Here predictedPalm is the estimated palm position in world coordinates: current world palm position + Controller.GetRelativeVelocityInWorld() × 0.015 seconds. The controller value is its cached velocity relative to the head, expressed along world axes in metres per second, from the latest controller physics update. Multiplying it by 0.015 seconds gives the predicted world displacement in metres. radius is this value in metres, farAimDirection is a unit direction vector, and 3.04 is a unitless multiplier, so the displacement is in metres. The broad far-query capsule has its own 1-metre radius.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.HoveringReceiver
member.summary: The near interaction target currently selected for this hand, with callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action) when that selection changes.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering picks it from enabled and eligible nearby receivers. Assigning a different receiver first calls the old receiver's OnHandHoverEnd with this Hand, then the hand's onRecieverHoverEnd event with the old receiver. It stores the new receiver, calls that receiver's OnHandHoverBegin with this Hand, then invokes the hand's onRecieverHoverBegin event with the new receiver. Assigning the same receiver causes no transition callbacks.

OnPhysRigUpdate calls the selected receiver's OnHandHoverUpdate with this Hand after the search. HoverLock clears this near target while reserving it in AttachedReceiver. Writing _mHoveringReceiver directly bypasses the transition callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.Skeleton

remarks.para: On first access, asks manager.virtualHeptaRig for the SkeletonHand matching handedness and caches it in _skeleton. Returns null if the manager or virtual skeleton rig is unavailable.

The controller wrist/handle helpers use its world transform and OffsetTransform to compute targets, including the skeleton's displacement and rotation corrections. These targets can differ from the physical hand's current transform.

member.summary: Suppresses held-object trigger input until a trigger already held during attachment has been released.

remarks.para: After successfully finding a HandReciever for the new object, AttachObject sets this when the controller's primary interaction button is already held. If receiver lookup fails, currentAttachedGO is still stored but this filter is left unchanged. While true, SetIndexButtonAndTrigger sets down, up and held states to false and the analog axis to zero. This prevents the grabbing press from immediately activating the newly held object.
EarlyUpdateHeldObjectInputs clears it after observing that the controller button is no longer held. That release poll still contains the suppressed values; the next poll can supply normal input.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand._mHoveringReceiver
member.summary: Stores the near-hover target selected by .

remarks.para: UpdateHovering selects this receiver and OnPhysRigUpdate calls its OnHandHoverUpdate. The property setter also sends hover-end and hover-begin callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action) when changing targets; writing this field directly skips those callbacks.
HoverLock moves the current target into AttachedReceiver and clears this field through the property. HoverUnlock permits a future search to choose another target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand._skeleton
member.summary: Cached virtual SkeletonHand used for tracked wrist transforms and interaction offsets.

remarks.para: Skeleton fills this reference from the hand's manager and handedness when it is missing or destroyed. Reading the field directly does not perform that lookup.
A live cached reference is reused. SetManager does not clear it, so changing the manager alone does not force this field to switch to the new rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand._upperarmJoint
member.summary: Extra physics connection from a held object's host to this hand's upper-arm Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a configurable physics connection; a Rigidbody is an object whose movement Unity physics calculates. AttachIgnoreBodyJoints creates the ConfigurableJoint on the held host's GameObject and connects it to the corresponding arm Rigidbody when the host has a Rigidbody. It initially sets all position and rotation axes to Free.

This is an additional held-object connection, rather than the arm's own driving joint. DetachIgnoreBodyJoints and completed grab-joint release destroy it and clear the reference; replacing the reference alone does not reconfigure the connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.collider
member.summary: The hand shape checked for overlap with the released grip when separating the hand from an object.

remarks.para: During grab-joint release, the coroutine (a sequence that continues over several frames) compares this collider with the first entry in lastGrip.gripColliders. If they overlap, it moves the physical hand along the separation direction, with the correction limited to 0.1 metres.

This is separate from m_HandColliders, the array used to ignore hand/object collision pairs. EnableCollider and DisableCollider toggle collision detection on rigidbodies rather than changing this collider's enabled flag. A Rigidbody is an object whose movement Unity physics calculates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.farHoverEnabled
member.summary: Allows distant force-pull target searches when no near-hover receiver qualifies.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering first requires an available controller and unlocked hover. It only considers its far-search branch when this is true and near selection found no candidate, and aim-alignment checks must still pass before the query. The native constructor enables it, though scene/prefab data and gameplay code can change it.

Setting it false does not immediately clear the previous receiver. A subsequent UpdateHovering that passes the controller and hover-lock gates prevents distant selection and clears the previous far-hover target through its setter. Changing the flag alone does not run a search or cancel an already active force-pull coroutine (a sequence that continues over several frames); ForcePullGrip handles that lifecycle separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.farHoverLayerMask
member.summary: Chooses which GameObject layers the distant-target capsule search can see.

remarks.para: A layer mask is a set of allowed Unity layers. UpdateHovering supplies this mask to the far-hover overlap query; excluding an object's collider layer prevents that collider from entering the far-search candidate list.

The search still checks aiming, receiver permissions, grip eligibility and obstacles afterwards. This mask does not change force-pull speed, grab distance or near-hover selection. The native constructor includes all layers, but serialized data can override that value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.farHoveringReciever
member.summary: The distant interaction receiver selected for force-pull hover, with callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action) when that target changes.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering fills this only when no near target qualifies and the far-search checks succeed. When the value changes, its setter first calls the previous receiver's OnFarHandHoverEnd with this Hand, then stores the new reference, then calls the new receiver's OnFarHandHoverBegin with this Hand. It does not invoke the hand's near-hover begin/end delegates.

OnPhysRigUpdate calls OnFarHandHoverUpdate on the selected receiver with this Hand. HoverLock clears this selection. Assigning a receiver changes the hover target and sends those callbacks, but does not itself start a pull or attach the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.handedness
member.summary: Selects which side of the player rig supplies this hand’s controller, skeleton and hand animator.

remarks.para: Left selects the left-side references and Right selects the right-side references. SetManager also uses this choice when registering the hand’s inventory slot. Set the side to match the physical hand being configured.

Controller, Skeleton and Animator keep the references they find on their first lookup. Changing handedness afterward does not automatically replace those cached references, so this is a setup choice rather than a way to swap a running left hand into a right hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.hoverLayerMask
member.summary: Chooses which collider layers the hand searches when selecting a nearby hover target.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape, and a layer is a Unity category used to filter those shapes. A trigger collider reports overlaps without acting as a solid obstacle. The nearby search is a sphere around the palm reference and includes trigger colliders. A collider must be on a layer included in this mask before its receiver can be considered. For example, excluding the layer used by an interactable’s collider prevents that collider from being found by this search.

This is a mask of allowed layers, not a distance or a receiver list. The candidate still has to pass the receiver and grip checks. The distant capsule search uses farHoverLayerMask instead, so this field alone does not disable far targeting of the same object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.hoverLocked
member.summary: Stops the hand’s nearby and distant hover-target search while the current grab keeps its receiver locked.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering returns without searching while this flag is true. HoverLock saves the current nearby receiver as AttachedReceiver, sets the flag and clears the nearby and far hover selections. HoverUnlock clears the flag and AttachedReceiver so normal searching can resume.
Use HoverLock and HoverUnlock to perform those coordinated changes. The flag by itself does not create or remove the physics joint, and it is separate from GrabLock, which controls grab input.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.ignoredRecievers
member.summary: Receivers that the nearby hover search must skip even when their colliders are in range.

remarks.para: This HashSet is a collection that stores each receiver at most once. Add a receiver to it to exclude it from the nearby candidate selection, and remove it when it should become eligible again. The constructor creates an empty set; the physical rig also adds selected body receivers during setup.

This set filters receiver selection, rather than turning off physical collisions. The inspected far-hover search does not consult it, and adding an already held receiver does not itself detach the object. m_IgnoredColliders has a different purpose: remembering physics collision pairs to restore on release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.joint
member.summary: The active physics joint connecting this hand to the object it has attached.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint connects two bodies and controls how far they may move or turn relative to each other. The hand’s normal attachment path first prepares tempJoint, then AttachJoint moves that reference here and applies the receiver’s joint settings.

DetachJoint clears this reference and tempJoint and schedules the joint component for teardown. A null value therefore means this field has no active connection, even though a joint component captured for delayed destruction may briefly remain. Assigning a reference here alone does not perform the receiver callbacks (routines called to perform or report attachment changes), collision changes or other attachment setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.jointStartRotation
member.summary: Records the connected body’s starting orientation relative to the hand while preparing an attachment joint.

remarks.para: PrepareJoint calculates inverse(hand Rigidbody rotation) multiplied by connected-body rotation. This describes how the connected body is turned when viewed in the hand’s rotation frame. With no connected body, it stores the inverse of the hand’s world rotation instead.

This is a Quaternion, a representation of rotation, rather than three angles in degrees. It starts as the identity rotation and is replaced when PrepareJoint calculates a new connection. Changing the stored value does not directly rotate either Rigidbody. The inspected release routines do not use it to restore the object’s orientation on release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_ColliderArraySize
member.summary: The fixed capacity of 128 collider entries allocated for the hand’s reusable hover-search buffer.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity’s initialization routine) uses this constant to allocate m_OverlappingColliders. Both the nearby sphere search and distant capsule search reuse that array, avoiding a new array for each search.

This is a compile-time constant, not a live buffer-size setting. Each query supplies a count saying how many entries are valid for that search; the whole array is not a list of 128 current targets. When more colliders are present than the buffer can hold, this buffer cannot contain them all.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_CurrentAttachedGO
member.summary: The GameObject recorded as this hand’s currently attached object.

remarks.para: AttachObject first detaches the previous recorded object, then stores the new one. When its cached HandReciever is found, that receiver is notified and onRecieverAttached is invoked. The reference can still be stored when no receiver is found, so a non-null value alone does not guarantee that an attachment callback, a routine called to report or respond to attaching the object, occurred.

DetachObject clears the reference and the hand slot’s current item before notifying the old receiver. This object bookkeeping is separate from the ConfigurableJoint connection managed by AttachJoint and DetachJoint. Use the attachment methods to update those related states and notifications rather than replacing this field alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_FarHoveringReciever
member.summary: The receiver currently selected by the hand’s distant hover search.

remarks.para: The hand considers distant candidates when its nearby search has not selected an acceptable receiver and farHoverEnabled is true. This reference represents a candidate for far interaction; it does not mean the object is already attached.

Use farHoveringReciever to change the selection with the receiver’s far-hover begin/end notifications. Writing this stored field directly skips those notifications. The onRecieverHoverBegin and onRecieverHoverEnd Actions belong to nearby hover and are not fired by the far-hover property.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_HandColliders
member.summary: The hand colliders whose collisions with a grabbed object can be temporarily ignored.

remarks.para: IgnoreHostColliders and joint preparation pair each collider in this serialized array with the object’s eligible colliders and call Physics.IgnoreCollision. Release restores those pairs using m_IgnoredColliders. Include the physical hand colliders that should stop colliding with a held object.

Awake (Unity’s initialization routine) does not automatically gather this array in the inspected Hand implementation. These are collision-pair participants, not the hover-search results. The separate EnableCollider and DisableCollider methods toggle Rigidbody collision detection rather than enabling or disabling every entry in this array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_IgnoredColliders
member.summary: Remembers object colliders whose collisions with the hand must be restored when its joint is detached.

remarks.para: IgnoreHostColliders and joint preparation add colliders after ignoring their collision pairs with m_HandColliders. DetachJoint restores those pairs and clears the list. The same collider can be recorded more than once; this is bookkeeping for physics changes, not a set of nearby targets.

Adding an entry to the list alone does not call Physics.IgnoreCollision. UnignoreHostColliders restores the matching pairs but does not remove their entries from this list. Receiver filtering for nearby hover belongs to ignoredRecievers instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_IsWarmup
member.summary: Keeps the hand’s rig and runtime-skeleton updates paused until the level-load routine releases startup warmup.

remarks.para: The runtime skeleton is the character model’s animated bone structure. The constructor sets this flag true. OnLevelLoad sets it false; this is a scene-loading condition, not a countdown of a fixed number of frames.

OnPhysRigUpdate and OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate skip their work while it is true. That also suppresses onRTSkeleFixedUpdateDelegate. Setting it false allows those update paths to run; it does not itself attach an object or simulate extra warmup frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.m_OverlappingColliders
member.summary: The reusable array receiving collider results from the most recent nearby or distant hover query.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity’s initialization routine) allocates 128 entries. UpdateHovering fills the same array with the nearby sphere query and, when needed, the distant capsule query. The count returned by the current query determines which entries the search examines.

Entries beyond that count can remain from an earlier query. Do not treat the entire array as the colliders currently inside the palm’s sphere, or as a permanent target list. Filling or editing the array yourself does not update HoveringReceiver or farHoveringReciever; the next physics query replaces the relevant results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.manager
member.summary: Connects this hand to the player rig that supplies its controller, skeleton, avatar animation and inventory.

remarks.para: PhysicsRig setup calls SetManager for both hands. SetManager stores this reference and registers slot with that manager’s inventory using the hand’s side. Controller, Skeleton and Animator then look up their side-specific references through the manager and cache them.

Use SetManager for initialization rather than assigning manager alone, so the slot registration also occurs. Already cached controller, skeleton and animator references are not automatically cleared when this reference changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onAnchorUpdate
member.summary: An Action called before UpdateAnchor writes a joint’s hand-side anchor position.

remarks.para: This Action holds subscribed routines, which are called to report the requested update. The arguments are this Hand and the requested anchor point in the joint object’s local coordinates. This is a position relative to that object’s origin and axes, not a world position, a distance moved or a rotation. The callback runs before joint.anchor is assigned, so reading the joint inside the callback can still return the old anchor.

The overload that uses this hand’s current joint skips the call when there is no joint. Writing joint.anchor directly bypasses this Action. Add a routine with += and remove it with -= to receive notifications without replacing other subscribers; this is a C# Action, not an Inspector UnityEvent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onConnectedAnchorUpdate
member.summary: An Action called before UpdateConnectedAnchor converts and writes the joint’s anchor on the connected side.

remarks.para: This Action holds subscribed routines, which are called to report the requested update. The arguments are this Hand and the requested connected-anchor position. With a connected Rigidbody, a physical body, the point uses that body’s origin and orientation. Body scale means a unitless size factor on each axis: 1 means normal size and 2 means twice that size. UpdateConnectedAnchor may divide the request’s components by their matching body scale factors before storing connectedAnchor, so the callback receives the original request rather than necessarily the final stored local coordinates. With no connected Rigidbody, the anchor is a world position.

The callback runs before the assignment. The overload using this hand’s current joint skips the call when that joint is absent, and writing connectedAnchor directly bypasses the Action. Add a routine with += and remove it with -=; this is a C# Action rather than an Inspector UnityEvent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onRTSkeleFixedUpdateDelegate
member.summary: An Action called after this hand’s held-grip runtime-skeleton update once startup warmup has ended.

remarks.para: The runtime skeleton is the character model’s animated bones. This Action holds routines to call during their runtime-skeleton update. OnRTSkeleFixedUpdate first forwards the update to the recorded attached object’s Grip when one is found, then invokes this parameterless Action. It can also run for an empty hand; holding an object is not required.

No callback occurs while m_IsWarmup is true; OnLevelLoad clears that flag when startup loading finishes. The call belongs to the hand’s runtime-skeleton update phase, rather than every rendered frame. Add and remove routines with += and -=; there is no Hand argument, so retain the hand reference when subscribing if your handler needs it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onRecieverAttached
member.summary: An Action reporting the receiver found when AttachObject records an object on this hand.

remarks.para: The Action calls subscribed routines to report the attachment. The argument is the attached HandReciever. AttachObject first detaches any previous recorded object, stores the new GameObject, calls that receiver’s OnAttachedToHand, and then invokes this Action. The callback can therefore read the newly stored attached object.

If the object has no matching cached receiver, the GameObject can still be recorded but this Action is not invoked. This reports object/receiver attachment bookkeeping, not an automatic notification for every assignment to joint. Add a routine with += and remove it with -=.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onRecieverDetached
member.summary: An Action reporting the receiver removed when DetachObject clears this hand’s recorded attachment.

remarks.para: The Action calls subscribed routines to report the removal. The argument is the previous HandReciever. DetachObject clears m_CurrentAttachedGO and the slot’s item first, calls that receiver’s OnDetachedFromHand, clears matching hover/attached receiver state, and then invokes this Action. The old receiver is supplied as the argument even though the current-object field has already been cleared.

The callback requires a matching cached receiver for the old object. Clearing a joint reference alone does not directly fire this Action. AttachObject detaches a previous object before recording its replacement, so changing held objects can report a detach followed by an attach. Add a routine with += and remove it with -=.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onRecieverHoverBegin
member.summary: An Action reporting the new receiver when this hand’s nearby hover selection changes to it.

remarks.para: The Action calls subscribed routines to report the new hover selection. The argument is the newly selected HandReciever. The HoveringReceiver setter calls the new receiver’s OnHandHoverBegin before invoking this Action. Selecting the same receiver again does not fire another begin callback.

When switching from one receiver to another, the old receiver’s end notifications occur first. A cleared selection has no new receiver and produces no begin call. Far-hover selection uses its own receiver callbacks and does not invoke this Action. Add a routine with += and remove it with -=.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.onRecieverHoverEnd
member.summary: An Action reporting the old receiver when this hand clears or replaces its nearby hover selection.

remarks.para: The Action calls subscribed routines to report the removal. The argument is the previous HandReciever. The HoveringReceiver setter calls that receiver’s OnHandHoverEnd and then this Action before replacing the stored nearby selection. While this handler runs, HoveringReceiver can therefore still refer to the old receiver.

There is no end call when the previous selection is null or the same receiver is selected again. Switching targets reports this end before the new receiver’s begin. Far-hover changes do not invoke this Action. Add a routine with += and remove it with -=.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.otherHand
member.summary: The opposite hand used to check whether an object is already held by the player’s other hand.

remarks.para: Nearby selection compares a candidate with otherHand’s recorded attached object and allows sharing only when the grip permits the corresponding two-hand use. Far selection excludes the other hand’s attached object from its candidates.

Connect this reference to the opposite Hand on the same rig. It lets the searches coordinate object ownership; it is not a second physics joint and does not automatically make every object support a two-hand grab.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.palmPositionTransform
member.summary: The palm reference whose position and orientation the hand uses when finding nearby contact targets.

remarks.para: UpdateHovering uses this Transform’s world position for the near search and its orientation in approach tests. Grip implementations such as BoxGrip and GenericGrip also read the palm reference to evaluate where the hand approaches the object.

Moving or rotating this reference changes the measured palm origin or facing direction. It does not directly move the hand’s Rigidbody. The controller/hand-pose handle and the selected grip target also participate in final hand placement, so this Transform is not unconditionally the joint’s anchor point.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.physHand
member.summary: The PhysHand component providing this hand’s physical arm/hand behavior and grip-force settings.

remarks.para: Awake (Unity’s initialization routine) gets this component from the same GameObject as Hand and caches it here. Hand.SetGripStrength writes the physical hand’s grip multiplier, and the held-grip update also supplies controller grip strength to it. Release and joint-break handling use its physical-hand helpers.

Hand manages receiver selection, attachment state and callbacks, routines called to perform or report interaction changes; PhysHand supplies the separate physics behavior. Assigning another reference here does not move that component or rebuild the physical rig. Normal setup obtains the matching component during Awake (Unity’s initialization routine).

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.playerLayerMask
member.summary: Layers that the distant-hover visibility ray skips so the player’s own colliders do not block a target.

remarks.para: A layer is a Unity category used to filter physics shapes. A trigger collider reports overlaps without acting as a solid obstacle. The far-target visibility test raycasts using the inverse of this mask. A layer included here is therefore excluded from that obstacle test. The ray also ignores trigger colliders.

For example, putting the player’s body colliders on a layer included in this mask keeps those colliders from counting as obstructions in this test. Including a wall layer in this mask also makes the visibility ray ignore that wall. The field does not set the allowed nearby/far candidate layers; hoverLayerMask and farHoverLayerMask do that.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.rb
member.summary: The Rigidbody on this hand’s GameObject, cached for its physical pose, velocity and collision control.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the body Unity’s physics simulation moves and collides. Awake (Unity’s initialization routine) gets and stores it from the same object. Joint preparation reads its rotation to record jointStartRotation, and hover scoring uses its velocity relative to candidate objects. EnableCollider and DisableCollider also change this Rigidbody’s collision-detection setting.
This reference gives interaction code access to the physical hand body. Changing the reference alone does not transfer the hand’s components, receiver state or prepared joints to another object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.slot
member.summary: The inventory slot that tracks the grippable item currently associated with this hand.

remarks.para: SetManager registers this slot in the rig’s inventory using the hand’s side. When AttachObject finds a Grip with a host, it records that host’s GameObject in the slot, then calls the slot’s insertion routines. DetachObject calls the removal routines while the old item is still stored, then clears it. Both insertion and removal routines receive this InventorySlot as their sole argument. These routines let inventory code respond to the change; insertion routines see the new item, while removal routines can still read the departing item.

This connects hand-held item bookkeeping to the inventory system. It is not the ConfigurableJoint that physically holds the object, and replacing the slot reference does not automatically register the replacement or transfer an already stored item.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.tempJoint
member.summary: The newly created attachment joint while the normal grab path is preparing it for activation.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection controlling how two bodies may move or turn relative to each other. CreateConfigurableJoint adds one to the hand’s GameObject and stores it here. PrepareJoint fills its connection details and collision-ignore state. AttachJoint then moves the reference to joint, clears tempJoint and applies the receiver’s joint configuration.

This is staging for ordinary attachment, rather than a special path that bypasses normal grabbing. DetachJoint can also tear down this prepared joint when no active joint is available, and clears both references while the captured component is being destroyed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand.triggerRefProxyObject
member.summary: The object supplying a character reference for this hand’s melee attacks and ordinary held-object attachment.

remarks.para: HandSFX.PunchAttack looks for a TriggerRefProxy component on this object and puts that component into the attack message. A TriggerRefProxy describes a character through references such as its root object, body parts and team. The attack message carries this source reference alongside the damage and contact point.

Receiving enemy code can use that reference to identify the attacker: the inspected PowerLegs hit response adds threat for the supplied character, and its sensor can change which character it targets. Changing this object therefore changes the source reference found for later hand attacks; it does not select the struck collider or set the attack damage.

Ordinary Grip attachment also passes this GameObject to the held host’s SetProxy routine. For an InteractableHost, a successful TriggerRefProxy component lookup copies that character reference into the host’s own stored proxy. Editing the Hand field later does not itself refresh an already copied host reference. If a supplied object lacks the component, the host leaves its existing proxy unchanged.

With no object or no TriggerRefProxy component on it, the attack carries no source proxy. The Hand hover queries themselves use palmPositionTransform and their own trigger-inclusion settings; this reference does not define their hover origin.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.HandleSpace
member.summary: Returns the rotation that gives the pose's handle its forward and up directions.

remarks.para: It uses primaryAxis as forward and secondaryAxis as up. For example, primaryAxis=(0,0,1) and secondaryAxis=(0,1,0) produce an unrotated handle frame. The directions belong to the local pose convention, rather than pointing toward a world location.

HandPoseAnimator combines this rotation with the left or right handle rotation stored in poseData when calculating how a hand and handle fit together. Changing the axes therefore changes handle alignment. This property calculates a rotation on each read; it contains no position offset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseDataGroup.poseArray
member.summary: Finger and handle samples blended for different hand rotations at this group's grip size.

remarks.para: Each sample's nativePry identifies its hand rotation using signed coordinates in degrees. These are the animator's rotation lookup coordinates, rather than conventional Euler X/Y/Z angles. The animator uses those coordinates to blend finger rotations and handle placement for the current hand orientation, then blends corresponding samples between neighboring size groups.

Use the same sample count and rotation ordering in every group. The rotation lookup is built from the first group's coordinates, and size blending pairs samples by array index; it does not search another group for a matching rotation.

Provide populated arrays. The neutral hand/handle calculations read the first sample of the first group directly, so that entry also supplies the pose's neutral placement reference. Changing a sample affects hand shape and placement, rather than the object's collision shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseDataGroup.radius
member.summary: The grip-size sample point, in metres at the reference hand's scale, for selecting this group's poses.

remarks.para: SetCylinderRadius divides a supplied world grip size by the animator's cached unitless hand-size scale factor, which scales the fixed reference hand to the avatar. SetHandSize copies the factor from Avatar.handSizeMult and computes and stores its reciprocal for this conversion. Later Avatar edits affect the conversion only after SetHandSize runs again. The resulting size is compared with these group values. For example, a 0.03-metre grip size and a cached hand-size scale factor of 2 produce a lookup size of 0.015 metres.

Keep groups in increasing radius order. The animator blends between the neighboring groups for an intermediate size and uses an endpoint group outside the available sizes. Changing this value moves where these samples are selected; it does not resize the held collider.
The supplied size comes from the grip's pose-fitting code. It need not be the measured radius of a literal cylinder: BoxGrip's sandwich grab, for example, supplies the selected box thickness.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.leftArtToRigSpace
member.summary: Shared left-hand reference rotation that maps local forward to up, and local up to left.

remarks.para: The static initializer builds this quaternion with an up-facing forward direction and a left-facing up direction. It is shared by all HandPose assets, rather than belonging to one pose.

HandPoseAnimator's pose solving and hand/handle conversions do not apply this field in the inspected runtime implementation. Changing it does not change those calculations. The pose's leftOffsetRotation is the field read when adjusting the tracked left wrist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.leftOffsetRotation
member.summary: Adjusts the tracked left wrist's orientation while this pose is active.

remarks.para: HandPoseAnimator.WristOffset selects this quaternion for a left hand. Hand.GetControllerWristTransform and SkeletonHand.ProcessTransform combine it with the controller/skeleton wrist rotation, changing the wrist orientation used to position the hand.
A quaternion stores a rotation, rather than a distance or four separate angles. This field does not directly replace the finger rotations or handle positions stored in poseData.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.poseData
member.summary: Supplies the finger and handle poses blended to fit different grip radii and hand rotations.

remarks.para: Each group contains a radius used for pose fitting and an array of pose samples. For a cylinder, radius means the distance from its center to its surface, half its diameter. HandPoseAnimator selects the neighboring radius groups, blends corresponding samples between them, then blends for the current hand rotation and finger opening. These samples affect hand appearance and handle placement; they do not resize the object's collider.

Radii are compared in the reference hand's scale: SetCylinderRadius divides the supplied world radius by the avatar's hand-size scale factor, which scales the reference hand to that avatar. As an example, a 0.03-metre input radius and a scale factor of 2 produce a reference-hand lookup radius of 0.015 metres.

Keep the groups in increasing radius order. Values outside the available radii use an endpoint group. Corresponding sample indices must describe the same hand rotation in each group: the animator builds its rotation lookup from the first group and pairs samples by index across groups.

SetHandPose prepares lookup caches when switching to this asset. Editing an already active array does not itself rebuild the cached sample layout. Supply a nonempty group array with populated sample arrays; the inspected setup and handle-conversion paths index their first entries directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.primaryAxis
member.summary: Sets the local direction treated as forward when orienting this pose's handle.

remarks.para: HandleSpace builds a rotation with this vector as its forward direction and secondaryAxis as its up direction. Changing the direction reorients the handle calculations used to fit the hand to a grip; it is a direction, not a position or a distance.

A newly constructed pose starts with (0,0,1), the local forward direction. Together with secondaryAxis=(0,1,0), this gives an unrotated pose frame. These are the pose's handle directions; Grip has its own separate axis settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.rightArtToRigSpace
member.summary: Shared right-hand reference rotation that maps local forward to down, and local up to left.

remarks.para: The static initializer builds this quaternion with a down-facing forward direction and a left-facing up direction. It is shared by all HandPose assets, rather than belonging to one pose.

HandPoseAnimator's pose solving and hand/handle conversions do not apply this field in the inspected runtime implementation. Changing it does not change those calculations. The pose's rightOffsetRotation is the field read when adjusting the tracked right wrist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.rightOffsetRotation
member.summary: Adjusts the tracked right wrist's orientation while this pose is active.

remarks.para: HandPoseAnimator.WristOffset selects this quaternion for a right hand. Hand.GetControllerWristTransform and SkeletonHand.ProcessTransform combine it with the controller/skeleton wrist rotation, changing the wrist orientation used to position the hand.
A quaternion stores a rotation, rather than a distance or four separate angles. This field does not directly replace the finger rotations or handle positions stored in poseData.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.secondaryAxis
member.summary: Sets the local up reference that determines the handle's twist around its forward direction.

remarks.para: HandleSpace uses primaryAxis as forward and this vector as up. Keeping forward fixed while changing the up reference rotates the handle around that forward direction, changing how the hand is turned around the grip.

A newly constructed pose starts with (0,1,0), the local up direction. This is an orientation reference, rather than an angular limit; twistRotationLimit separately supplies the allowed physical twisting angle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.swingRotationLimit
member.summary: Sets the hand's angular allowance for tilting away from the held handle, in degrees.

remarks.para: Grip.GetSwingLimit reads this value from the hand's selected pose. CylinderGrip.UpdateJointConfiguration installs it as the physics joint's two sideways angular limits. A joint is the physics connection that keeps the hand and held object together; larger limits allow more tilt in those directions.
The pose constructor sets 30 degrees. This changes allowed rotation, rather than finger curl or the grip's search distance. Grip implementations can override how they use the pose's allowance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.twistRotationLimit
member.summary: Sets the hand's angular allowance for twisting around a grip, in degrees.

remarks.para: Grip.GetTwistLimit reads this value from the hand's selected pose. CylinderGrip adds its own twistLimit and installs the result as positive and negative limits around the physics joint's twist axis. Larger totals allow more rotation around that axis.

The pose constructor sets 30 degrees. For example, a 30-degree pose allowance plus a 10-degree CylinderGrip twistLimit installs limits of -40 and +40 degrees. This controls physical freedom to rotate; secondaryAxis instead defines the pose handle's up direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.wristOffset
member.summary: Stores a wrist-offset vector that the inspected runtime pose and handle calculations do not apply.

remarks.para: Changing this vector does not shift the handle in HandPoseAnimator.GetHandleInHand, GetHandInHandle, their neutral variants, or the tracked-wrist calculations in Hand.GetControllerWristTransform and SkeletonHand.ProcessTransform. Those paths use the poseData handle positions and the side-specific offset rotations.

To change the calculated hand/handle placement, use the corresponding handle data in poseData. To change the tracked wrist's orientation, use leftOffsetRotation or rightOffsetRotation. The inspected code does not establish units or a coordinate frame for this unapplied vector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.WristOffset
member.summary: Returns the selected pose's left or right rotation correction for the tracked wrist.

remarks.para: For a left hand it reads leftOffsetRotation; for a right hand it reads rightOffsetRotation. With no active pose it returns the identity rotation, which adds no rotation.

Hand.GetControllerWristTransform and SkeletonHand.ProcessTransform combine this correction with the tracked controller/skeleton orientation. Despite its name, this is a quaternion, Unity’s value representing a 3D rotation, rather than a position offset; it does not return HandPose.wristOffset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._currentIndex
member.summary: The index finger's smoothed curl input used to blend its open and closed shapes.

remarks.para: Normally 0 means open and 1 means closed. SetFingers approaches the input or a queued override using a frame-duration smoothing fraction; this field stores the current result, rather than the unsmoothed target.

BlendOpenPose clamps this input to 0..1 and maps it between _minIndex and _maxIndex, the curl fractions selected for fully open and fully closed input. Changing this field affects a later solve; a subsequent SetFingers call can update it again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._currentPoseData
member.summary: Stores the calculated finger rotations and handle placements used by the hand animator.

remarks.para: SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle replace this structure with the sample result adjusted for current finger curls; SolvePose can also blend an active asset transition. ApplyPoseToTransforms reads its finger rotations, and GetArtHandleInHand reads its side-specific visual handle.
Changing the stored data can affect a later apply or getter, but the next solve calculates and overwrites it again.

member.summary: The thumb's smoothed curl input used to blend its open and closed shapes.

remarks.para: Normally 0 means open and 1 means closed. SetFingers approaches the input or a queued override using a frame-duration smoothing fraction; this field stores the current result, rather than the unsmoothed target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._dataArray
member.summary: Stores pose samples after blending between the selected grip-size groups.

remarks.para: Each entry corresponds to one hand-rotation sample, rather than one finger or one size group. RefreshRadius blends matching sample indices from the lower and upper groups for samples with positive weight; the weighted pose blend then combines the contributing entries.
SetHandPose allocates this array for the selected asset's sample layout. It is an intermediate calculation buffer, so later radius refreshes can overwrite edited entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._datapoints
member.summary: Stores the hand-rotation coordinates used to choose how much each pose sample contributes.

remarks.para: SetHandPose copies nativePry from every sample in the first grip-size group. Each sample contains a rotation-axis direction multiplied by its turn angle in degrees, expressed in the pose’s handle-axis convention. First rotate the axis-times-angle vector using the pose's primaryAxis as forward and secondaryAxis as up. If its components are x, y and z in degrees, LEFT uses pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z; RIGHT uses pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z. These are the rotation coordinates compared with the vector produced by ApplyRotationAnimationBlend, rather than world positions or conventional Euler X/Y/Z angles.

The angular weighting code compares the current rotation coordinates with these points. Other size groups must use the same sample ordering because the size blend pairs them by index. SetHandPose rebuilds the array when switching assets.

The pose's handle-axis convention uses pose.primaryAxis as forward and pose.secondaryAxis as up. After that rotation, the axis-times-angle components x, y and z in degrees map as LEFT pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z and RIGHT pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._handSizeMult
member.summary: Unitless scale factor copied by the last call to adjust the fixed reference hand to the avatar's hand size.

remarks.para: SetHandSize copies the avatar's handSizeMult. A factor of 2 makes reference bone and returned handle-position distances twice as large; 1 leaves those distances at reference size.

SetHandSize uses it to position the assigned finger segments. GetHandInHandle, GetHandleInHand and their Neutral variants multiply their returned positions by this cached factor. GetArtHandleInHand returns its stored art-handle position directly. Changing the stored factor alone does not reposition bone transforms already configured by SetHandSize.
This value stays cached from that last call. Later Avatar hand-size edits take effect here only after SetHandSize runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._handSizeMultInv
member.summary: Reciprocal of , used to compare world grip sizes with the reference-hand pose samples.

remarks.para: SetHandSize stores 1 divided by _handSizeMult, the factor that scales the fixed reference hand to the avatar. SetCylinderRadius multiplies the supplied world grip size by this reciprocal before the pose lookup.

For example, a hand-size factor of 2 gives a reciprocal of 0.5, so a 0.03-metre grip size becomes 0.015 metres at the reference hand's scale. Writing _handSizeMult alone does not recalculate this separate cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._lastPitch
member.summary: Records the pitch lookup coordinate from the most recent pose solve.

remarks.para: SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle copy their current pitch coordinate into this field after calculating the pose. This is the X/pitch component of the pose-lookup rotation vector: a rotation-axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in degrees, expressed in the pose frame obtained by rotating the axis-times-angle vector with pose.primaryAxis as forward and pose.secondaryAxis as up; if its components are x, y and z in degrees, LEFT uses pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z and RIGHT uses pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z, so the cached pitch is x for both hands after that rotation. It is not a world position or a conventional Euler angle.
The inspected HandPoseAnimator methods do not read this cache to skip solving. Editing it does not select another sample or prevent those methods from evaluating the pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._lastPose
member.summary: Remembers the asset whose lookup was prepared by SetHandPose.

remarks.para: Successful selection stores the current asset here, and the solve methods compare pose with this reference. It is an identity marker, rather than the old asset whose data is blended during a transition; _transitionCache stores that starting shape.
Writing pose directly can leave this reference and the prepared lookup out of sync. Select assets through SetHandPose; manually changing this marker does not rebuild the sample arrays.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._lastRadius
member.summary: Remembers the grip-size lookup value last used to refresh the neighboring sample groups.

remarks.para: The value is a length in metres at the reference hand's scale. The solve methods compare radius with this cache; a change recalculates the lower/upper size group indices, interpolation fraction and contributing samples.
SetHandPose invalidates the cache when switching assets. Writing it to match radius prematurely can suppress that size-change refresh, rather than changing the actual grip size.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._lastRoll
member.summary: Records the roll lookup coordinate from the most recent pose solve.

remarks.para: SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle copy their current roll coordinate into this field after calculating the pose. This is the Y/roll component of the pose-lookup rotation vector: a rotation-axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in degrees, expressed in the pose frame obtained by rotating the axis-times-angle vector with pose.primaryAxis as forward and pose.secondaryAxis as up; if its components are x, y and z in degrees, LEFT uses pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z and RIGHT uses pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z, so the cached roll is y for LEFT and -y for RIGHT after that rotation. It is not a world position or a conventional Euler angle.
The inspected HandPoseAnimator methods do not read this cache to skip solving. Editing it does not select another sample or prevent those methods from evaluating the pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._lastYaw
member.summary: Records the yaw lookup coordinate from the most recent pose solve.

remarks.para: SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle copy their current yaw coordinate into this field after calculating the pose. This is the Z/yaw component of the pose-lookup rotation vector: a rotation-axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in degrees, expressed in the pose frame obtained by rotating the axis-times-angle vector with pose.primaryAxis as forward and pose.secondaryAxis as up; if its components are x, y and z in degrees, LEFT uses pitch=x, roll=y, yaw=-z and RIGHT uses pitch=x, roll=-y, yaw=z, so the cached yaw is -z for LEFT and z for RIGHT after that rotation. It is not a world position or a conventional Euler angle.
The inspected HandPoseAnimator methods do not read this cache to skip solving. Editing it does not select another sample or prevent those methods from evaluating the pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._magCache
member.summary: Stores the magnitudes of the cached hand-rotation sample vectors for the angular weighting calculation.

remarks.para: SetHandPose calculates each magnitude from the corresponding _datapoints vector. A magnitude is a vector’s length, calculated as sqrt(x*x + y*y + z*z), where x, y and z are that sample’s rotation coordinates in degrees. The coordinates describe a rotation-axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in the pose’s hand/handle convention. Their vector length therefore measures the amount of rotation in degrees, rather than a grip radius or hand length.
CalculateWeightsPolar reads them when deciding each sample's contribution. They must remain consistent with _datapoints; switching assets through SetHandPose rebuilds both caches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._maxIndex
member.summary: The index curl fraction selected when its current input is fully closed.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless blend fraction, rather than an index into the size samples. BlendOpenPose maps that finger's clamped input between _minIndex and _maxIndex. A blend fraction of 0 selects the open shape and 1 selects the closed shape.
The initial value is 1. For example, setting this endpoint to 0.8 makes a fully closed input use 80% of the closed-finger shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._openPose
member.summary: Stores the fixed open-finger reference blended against the selected grip's closed-finger samples.

remarks.para: Awake, the routine Unity calls when initializing the component, and Initialize fill its finger rotations with the reference open shape. BlendOpenPose uses it at every grip size according to the current curls, rather than only when a size lies outside the available groups.
Changing its finger data changes the open side of subsequent finger blends. The closed sample supplies the retained handle data, so this field is not a fallback handle-placement asset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._palmLfPosOffset
member.summary: Caches the avatar's left palm-alignment correction.

remarks.para: SetHandSize copies this positional correction from the avatar. The calibrated hand frame means displacement coordinates measured from the avatar’s hand-bone origin, rotated into the game’s reference hand orientation using the measured finger geometry. This correction is the reference palm-center displacement minus the measured palm-center displacement, in metres, so it aligns the measured palm center with the game’s reference hand.

The inspected HandPoseAnimator methods store this cache but do not apply it to their bone posing or hand/handle calculations. Writing it does not move the palm through those methods, and another SetHandSize call replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._radMaxIndex
member.summary: Index of the upper grip-size group selected for the current pose lookup.

remarks.para: The index selects an entry in the active HandPose's poseData array. When radius changes, the solve recalculates both bounding group indices and _radiusT, the fraction between those groups; matching sample indices are then blended.
At an endpoint both indices can select the same group. This is cached lookup state, rather than a finger number or size in metres.

member.summary: Index of the lower grip-size group selected for the current pose lookup.

remarks.para: The index selects an entry in the active HandPose's poseData array. When radius changes, the solve recalculates both bounding group indices and _radiusT, the fraction between those groups; matching sample indices are then blended.
