member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._radiusT
member.summary: Blend fraction between the currently selected lower and upper grip-size groups.

remarks.para: DetermineMinMax calculates this dimensionless fraction from radius: 0 selects the lower group and 1 selects the upper group. RefreshRadius uses it to blend corresponding pose samples.
The solve recalculates it when the grip-size lookup value changes. Changing this fraction alone does not choose new group indices or change the object's collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._transitionCache
member.summary: Stores the hand shape captured at the start of a pose transition.

remarks.para: SetHandPose and ForceBlend reset transition progress, then copy _currentPoseData here. SolvePose blends from this snapshot toward its newly calculated pose while the transition is active.
This holds pose data, rather than a reference to an old asset. Editing it changes the transition's starting shape, and starting another transition replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._transitionFloat
member.summary: Progress of the current pose transition, normally from 0 at its start to 1 when complete.

remarks.para: SetHandPose and ForceBlend reset progress to 0. SolvePose advances it by the frame duration divided by _transitionTime, the transition's total duration in seconds, then blends from the saved starting shape while progress is below 1.
A nonpositive duration makes SolvePose finish the transition. SolvePoseForHandle does not advance this progress.

Transition durations are game-time seconds. SolvePose advances progress using Unity Time.deltaTime, the time elapsed since the previous frame in game-time seconds, so changing the game’s time scale changes how quickly the blend advances in real time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._transitionTime
member.summary: Total duration, in seconds, used to advance a pose transition.

remarks.para: SetHandPose or ForceBlend stores the requested duration. While a blend is active, SolvePose advances progress by frame duration divided by this value. It does not count this field down as time remaining.
A larger positive duration makes progress advance more slowly; zero or a negative duration makes the next SolvePose complete the transition.

Transition durations are game-time seconds. SolvePose advances progress using Unity Time.deltaTime, the time elapsed since the previous frame in game-time seconds, so changing the game’s time scale changes how quickly the blend advances in real time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator._vec_ijCache
member.summary: Stores relationships between pairs of hand-rotation samples for the angular weighting calculation.

remarks.para: SetHandPose prepares one pair entry for every ordered sample pair. For i == j, it stores Vector2.zero (both components are 0), and CalculateWeightsPolar skips these self-pairs; the formulas below apply only when i and j are distinct. For sample indices i and j, X = (mag_j - mag_i) / ((mag_j + mag_i) / 2), a unitless relative difference between their vector lengths. Each mag is the length of that sample’s rotation vector in degrees; the vector is an axis direction multiplied by the turn angle in the pose’s hand/handle convention. Y is twice the angle between the two vector directions, in degrees. For ordinary finite samples that angle is nonnegative in either pair order: reversing the pair does not make Y negative. These describe rotation samples, rather than scene positions.
CalculateWeightsPolar reads the cached pairs while calculating sample contributions. They are prepared for the selected asset, rather than cleared and rebuilt during every solve.
The pose's hand/handle convention uses pose.primaryAxis as forward and pose.secondaryAxis as up, with the selected hand's rotation-coordinate sign convention.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.debugCountSolveIterations
member.summary: Enables console logging of the angular weighting work and elapsed calculation time.

remarks.para: CalculateWeightsPolar logs its sample-pair comparison count and elapsed time in microseconds when this flag is true. This helps inspect the cost of evaluating the pose; it does not select another pose or change the calculated sample weights.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.defaultHandPose
member.summary: Pose asset selected during initialization and by SetDefaultHandPose.

remarks.para: Awake, the routine Unity calls to initialize this component, and Initialize select it through SetHandPose with a transition lasting 0.1 game-time seconds. SolvePose uses Time.deltaTime, elapsed game-time seconds for the frame, so the blend’s real-time speed follows the game’s time scale. SetDefaultHandPose selects it again through the same routine.
The pose is also used to recognize the default thumb-blending behavior. A null active pose does not automatically substitute this asset during SolvePose; that method returns without solving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.hand2Art
member.summary: The visual hand transform whose position anchors hand-to-handle placement calculations.

remarks.para: A Transform supplies a scene object's position and rotation. GetHandInHandle measures this transform's world position relative to handle, then adjusts that local offset for the pose axes and the animator’s cached unitless hand-size factor, copied by the last SetHandSize call; later Avatar edits affect this calculation only after SetHandSize runs again.
Assign the intended visual hand root. SetArtRefs fills finger-base references but does not assign this field; the inspected solve/apply methods do not move this root.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.handedness
member.summary: Chooses the left or right finger setup, handle data and wrist rotation correction.

remarks.para: SetArtRefs chooses that side's humanoid finger-base bones, SetHandSize uses that side's reference positions, and the handle getters select its saved placement data. It also determines which wrist rotation correction is returned.
Choose LEFT or RIGHT to match the hand being driven before setting up its references and size. A different value does not provide a usable left/right handle result in the inspected placement getters.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.handle
member.summary: Transform that receives the solved handle's local position and rotation within the hand setup.

remarks.para: SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle place it using the selected side's calculated handle data. A Transform stores a scene object’s position and rotation; its local position is a metre offset from its parent using the parent’s axes, and its local rotation is orientation relative to that parent. GetHandleInHand reads its local position, while GetHandInHandle uses it to measure the visual hand's relative offset.

Assign a handle transform in the intended hand hierarchy. It acts as a placement helper; changing it does not itself attach a held object or make a physics joint; a physics joint is a simulated connection between bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.hoverFingers
member.summary: Allows the thumb's base rotation to blend toward its closed shape while using a nondefault pose.

remarks.para: In BlendOpenPose, a nondefault pose with this flag false keeps the closed sample's thumb-base rotation. When true, the base blends from open toward closed using the thumb curl fraction plus 0.25, making it partly closed at zero input when the curl endpoints have their default values of 0 and 1.

The thumb's remaining segment bends and the other fingers still use their normal curl fractions. The default pose blends the thumb base normally regardless of this flag; the flag does not enable or disable hand-hover detection.

remarks.para: SetArtRefs assigns the left or right humanoid index-base bone according to handedness. SetHandSize positions it, and ApplyPoseToTransforms writes the solved base rotation in the bone's local coordinates, relative to its parent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.index2
member.summary: Receives the pose for the index finger’s second segment. Assign this segment separately; fills only the first segments.

remarks.para: ApplyPoseToTransforms replaces this transform’s localRotation with Quaternion.AngleAxis(angle, Vector3.forward), using the current blended index2 angle in degrees. Quaternion.AngleAxis creates a quaternion, Unity’s value for a rotation, from an angle and an axis. Here the parent frame means the parent object’s axes, so this bends around that parent’s positive Z direction. For example, an angle of 45 gives a 45-degree local rotation; the visible bend direction depends on the skeleton’s axes.

Assign the matching index finger segment for this animator’s handedness. SetArtRefs fills only the five first-segment references and does not fill this field. ApplyPoseToTransforms expects this reference to exist; it does not search the base bone’s children to find it.

SetHandSize replaces this transform’s local position using a fixed reference-hand segment distance scaled to the avatar’s hand size. Local position is the distance from the parent object’s origin, measured along that parent’s axes in Unity distance units, normally meters; parent scale can affect its world distance. Ordinary pose application replaces its local rotation. This is the second driven transform in the pose rig, independent of any anatomical naming used by the model.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.kDirScale
member.summary: Doubles the angular component of the pose solver’s comparison between sample directions.

remarks.para: The compiled constant is 2 and has no distance or time unit. The polar solver compares both the direction of the pitch/roll/yaw angle vector and its length. That length measures the amount of requested rotation in angle space. It stores the angular separation between two sample directions multiplied by 2 and applies the same factor to the requested direction’s angular offset when calculating weights.

For example, a signed angular separation of 30 degrees contributes an angular component of 60 in that comparison. It is combined with a separate relative difference between angle-vector lengths. This member describes a constant compiled into the calculation, rather than a per-hand setting read from an instance during each solve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.overrides
member.summary: Temporarily replaces individual finger-curl inputs for the next SetFingers call.

remarks.para: The five array slots are thumb, index, middle, ring and little finger, in that order. A negative value lets that finger use its normal SetFingers input. A value of 0 or greater replaces the input once, then SetFingers writes -1 back into that slot. Call CurlOverride before each update when the override should continue.

These are dimensionless curl inputs: with the default remapping, the normal finger blend uses 0 for the open pose and 1 for the sampled grip pose. SetFingers eases the current curl toward the chosen input using Clamp01(Time.deltaTime × 20), so an override is a target rather than an instant bone rotation. A frame is one game update. Time.deltaTime is that frame’s elapsed scaled game time in seconds, following the game’s speed setting rather than necessarily matching wall-clock time; 20 is the interpolation rate per second, and Clamp01 limits the resulting interpolation fraction to 0 through 1.

Before blending, each eased current curl is limited to 0 through 1, then rescaled between that finger’s unitless minimum and maximum blend limits, normally 0 and 1. In remappedCurl = minimum + (maximum − minimum) × clampedCurrentCurl, clampedCurrentCurl is the eased current curl limited to 0 through 1; minimum and maximum are the finger’s blend limits. All those values are unitless. The thumb base has a special rule when pose differs from defaultHandPose, the animator’s default asset. If hoverFingers is off, it keeps the sampled thumb-base rotation. If hoverFingers is on, it blends from the open rotation toward the sampled rotation using the current remapped thumb curl plus 0.25, limited to 0 through 1. This uses the current curl after easing and remapping, rather than instantly applying the newly requested override target. The added 0.25 is a unitless blend offset, so a remapped curl of 0 still gives a quarter blend toward the sampled thumb base in this case.

Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, allocates a new five-element array. Its initial entries are 0, so the first SetFingers call consumes zero overrides unless CurlOverride changes them first. Keep five valid slots; the native methods index all five directly. Values above 1 are stored as targets, although later finger blending clamps the current curl before its remapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.pitch
member.summary: Chooses the pitch coordinate used to blend authored finger and handle poses.

remarks.para: This is the requested X coordinate in HandPose.PoseData.nativePry angle space, in degrees. SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle compare the full (pitch, roll, yaw) vector with the asset’s sample points and calculate how much each sample contributes. Changing it affects the next pose solve; it does not directly assign a wrist rotation.

ApplyRotationAnimationBlend can overwrite these coordinates from a requested rotation: it multiplies the rotation axis by its angle in degrees, rotates that vector using the asset’s HandleSpace orientation then reverses the Z (yaw) coordinate’s sign for the left hand or the Y (roll) coordinate’s sign for the right hand. Pitch is the X coordinate. HandleSpace is the orientation chosen by the asset’s primary and secondary axes. These coordinates are not ordinary Euler angles, meaning separate turns around a Unity transform’s X, Y and Z axes.

For example, pitch = 30 requests the 30-degree pitch sample coordinate. The result depends on the sample layout and the other two coordinates. The Inspector range of -90 to 90 is an editing aid; these runtime fields and the pose solver do not clamp the stored value to that range.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.pose
member.summary: Identifies the HandPose asset whose samples and caches drive this animator.

remarks.para: Switch assets by calling SetHandPose(newPose, transitionTime) while pose still names the previous asset. That method saves the current pose for a transition, resets angle coordinates, builds the new sample caches and records the new asset in both pose and _lastPose. transitionTime is a duration in scaled game seconds; the default is 0.1. Scaled time follows the game’s speed setting rather than necessarily matching wall-clock seconds. SolvePose advances the saved transition when called, using the elapsed game time for that update. SolvePoseForHandle calculates its handle pose without advancing or applying this saved asset transition in the inspected implementation. The configured duration does not guarantee an exact completion frame.

Assigning this field directly changes only the reference. The solve methods notice a difference from _lastPose and try to call SetHandPose, but SetHandPose returns immediately when its argument already equals pose. A direct assignment can therefore leave caches for the old asset, rather than automatically starting a transition. Calling SetHandPose with that same asset after the assignment also encounters this guard.

The asset needs radius groups and samples; lookup points come from its first radius group and matching samples across groups are paired by index. If pose is null or destroyed, SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle return before solving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.radius
member.summary: Chooses the reference-hand grip size used to blend the asset’s radius groups.

remarks.para: A radius is the distance from a round handle’s center to its outside, half its diameter. This field is compared with HandPose.PoseDataGroup.radius values in the pose’s reference-hand distance units, normally meters. Larger values select pose samples authored for larger handles; the runtime uses those samples rather than calculating finger contact with a cylinder.

SetHandSize caches the avatar’s handSizeMult and its reciprocal in this animator. That unitless multiplier compares the avatar’s hand size with the reference hand: 1 is reference size and 1.5 is 50 percent larger. The reciprocal is 1 divided by that multiplier. SetCylinderRadius accepts a handle radius in game distance units and multiplies it by the cached reciprocal. With a cached multiplier of 1.5, a 0.03-meter handle therefore stores radius = 0.02 meters for sample lookup. Changing the Avatar’s hand-size value alone does not update this conversion; call SetHandSize again to capture a changed hand size. Assigning radius directly bypasses the conversion.

The next solve blends the two surrounding radius groups. For example, radius 0.015 lies halfway between groups authored at 0.01 and 0.02. Values outside the available groups use an endpoint group. Author groups in increasing radius order with matching sample layouts; the Inspector range of 0 to 2 does not clamp this field at runtime.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator.weights
member.summary: Stores how much each authored angle sample contributes to the current pose blend.

remarks.para: Each array slot corresponds to the same sample index in the first radius group and in the radius-interpolated sample cache. Values are dimensionless proportions: a weight of 0 excludes a sample, while weights of 0.75 and 0.25 give two active samples 75 percent and 25 percent of the blend. The polar weight solver normalizes its nonzero total so the active weights sum to 1.

SetHandPose creates this array to match the number of lookup points. SolvePose and SolvePoseForHandle recalculate its values from pitch, roll and yaw, then RefreshRadius uses positive weights to refresh the required samples between grip-size groups. BlendPose reads the weights to combine finger rotations, bend angles and handle placement.

This is working data owned by the solver. Assigning an arbitrary array or weights does not replace the sample caches and can be overwritten by the next solve. The normal solve still calculates angle weights on each call; its reuse of radius-interpolated sample data is a separate optimization.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.Cache
member.summary: Shared lookup table that finds a component by its GameObject.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds components. This lookup maps that scene object to its registered receiver.

Created when first requested. The base Awake routine, Unity's initialization callback (a routine called during component setup), registers the receiver. OnDestroy removes its entry and clears the cache reference when no entries remain.
Hand uses this lookup to resolve hover and held-object receivers. It tracks registered components; it does not search the scene for every live receiver whenever the property is read.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.HandJointConfig
member.summary: Reusable settings applied while preparing and finalizing a hand's grab joint.

remarks.para: Created on first access if _handJointConfig is null, then reused. A joint connects the hand and object in the physics simulation. The configuration contains anchors, the points on the hand and object where the connection meets; movement/rotation permissions; drives, the spring strength and damping that pull toward a target; limits, the allowed movement and rotation ranges; and break thresholds, the pulling force or twisting strength that breaks the connection. Spring strength controls how strongly the connection pulls toward its target; damping resists that movement to reduce bouncing.

Anchor positions use metres relative to the object holding the joint and its connected physics body; with no connected body, the connected anchor uses world coordinates. Automatic connected-anchor configuration can calculate that anchor, so the stored coordinates need not remain its final live position. Movement limits use metres, rotation limits use degrees, break force uses newtons (N), and break torque uses newton-metres (N·m). For torque to break the joint, the rotation axis where the twist is applied must be Locked (no turning) or Limited (turning only within its allowed range); a Free axis supplies no rotational constraint. For example, 0.05 metres is 5 centimetres, and 30 degrees is one-twelfth of a full turn; these are unit examples, not default settings.

Hand.PrepareJoint applies the configuration while preparing a grab, and Hand.AttachJoint applies the final movement settings before OnJointAttached. Reading this property or editing the stored object does not itself apply settings to an existing joint; the code applying the configuration must run.
This is joint configuration rather than a replacement hand pose. The grab setup obtains the neutral handle pose separately from the Grip's hand state and hand animator.

Useful before treating GetHostTransform's result as a real object transform, since that method returns an identity transform when no host is assigned: position (0, 0, 0), at the world origin, with a rotation that adds no turn.

remarks.para: Returns false with no Host; otherwise delegates to Host.HasRigidbody. A Rigidbody is Unity's simulated physical body, which can receive forces and connect to physics joints.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.IsEnabled
member.summary: Whether this receiver currently passes the local and host interaction-permission checks. and change the local permission.

remarks.para: The getter combines the local _isEnabled flag with the host's permission: with a host, it is true only when the local flag is true and Host.IsInteractionDisabled is false. Without a host, it returns the local flag.

The setter changes only the local flag. For example, setting IsEnabled to true while the host is disabled still makes the getter return false. EnableInteraction and DisableInteraction change that same local flag.

Hand.UpdateHovering checks this for near and far candidates. Changing it does not itself release an attachment or immediately send target-transition callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action).

The hand's far search checks both properties, plus its own farHoverEnabled flag, grip eligibility, aim and obstruction tests. A true value here is permission to be considered, not proof this receiver is the selected target or that a force pull is active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever.IsStatic

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever._handJointConfig
member.summary: Cached grab-joint settings exposed by .

remarks.para: Created on first access if _handJointConfig is null, then reused. A joint connects the hand and object in the physics simulation. The configuration contains anchors, the points on the hand and object where the connection meets; movement/rotation permissions; drives, the spring strength and damping that pull toward a target; limits, the allowed movement and rotation ranges; and break thresholds, the pulling force or twisting strength that breaks the connection. Spring strength controls how strongly the connection pulls toward its target; damping resists that movement to reduce bouncing.

Anchor positions use metres relative to the object holding the joint and its connected physics body; with no connected body, the connected anchor uses world coordinates. Automatic connected-anchor configuration can calculate that anchor, so the stored coordinates need not remain its final live position. Movement limits use metres, rotation limits use degrees, break force uses newtons (N), and break torque uses newton-metres (N·m). For torque to break the joint, the rotation axis where the twist is applied must be Locked (no turning) or Limited (turning only within its allowed range); a Free axis supplies no rotational constraint. For example, 0.05 metres is 5 centimetres, and 30 degrees is one-twelfth of a full turn; these are unit examples, not default settings.

Hand.PrepareJoint applies the configuration while preparing a grab, and Hand.AttachJoint applies the final movement settings before OnJointAttached. Reading this property or editing the stored object does not itself apply settings to an existing joint; the code applying the configuration must run.
This is joint configuration rather than a replacement hand pose. The grab setup obtains the neutral handle pose separately from the Grip's hand state and hand animator.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever._isEnabled
member.summary: The receiver's local permission to participate in hand interaction, enabled by .

remarks.para: EnableInteraction sets it true and DisableInteraction sets it false; the native receiver constructor initializes it true. IsEnabled additionally checks whether the assigned host disables interaction.

Changing this field does not toggle the receiver component's enabled switch in Unity, the MonoBehaviour.enabled property. A true local flag can still produce IsEnabled = false when the host blocks interaction, and the change itself sends no hover-transition callback (a routine called to perform or report an action).

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.VelocityPitchCurve
member.summary: A stored speed-to-pitch curve that the inspected HandSFX sound methods do not use.

remarks.para: The complete HandSFX setup, frame/physics updates, collision handlers and explicit playback methods do not read this reference. They do not evaluate this curve or start the stored whoosh clip, and Grab selects grab rather than grabBig.

Assigning or changing this reference alone does not enable that sound or alter the pitch calculations in those routines. This is a bounded statement about HandSFX’s methods; external scripts can retain their own use for a public field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._collisionCollector
member.summary: The assigned component that gathers physical contacts and reports the contact HandSFX should process.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, subscribes the impact-enter and ongoing-contact routines to this collector. FixedUpdate and Update ask it to process accumulated data; the collector selects its relevant contact rather than this field holding every raw Unity collision.

Assign the collector used by this hand before initialization. HandSFX does not automatically find it in Awake or Start. Changing the reference later does not transfer the existing event subscriptions; setup and teardown use the assigned collector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._enemyLayer
member.summary: The cached numeric ID of the named enemy collision group, without a reader in the inspected HandSFX methods.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s routine after initial setup, looks up the numeric ID of a named collision group and stores it here. A collision layer groups scene objects so code can select which groups a contact belongs to.

None of the complete HandSFX methods inspected reads this cache. PunchAttack instead checks meleeAttackMask, the set of allowed collider layers. Changing this saved number therefore does not alter that inspected attack test or make it an enemy-only test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._fixedRan
member.summary: Marks physics work waiting for the hand-sound update to process.

remarks.para: FixedUpdate is Unity’s physics-step routine; awake means the Rigidbody is active in physics calculations. An awake FixedUpdate sets this true. If it was already true, that physics step also processes contacts and refreshes the relative-speed sample. Update is Unity’s rendered-frame routine; it requires true and processes contacts first. After the collector calls the contact routines and the velocities are read, Update clears the pending flag, then stores the new squared hand-versus-chest speed.

The flag stays true while the collector calls the sound routines. A sleeping Rigidbody is temporarily inactive in physics calculations until awakened, so it skips the work and does not clear the flag. The flag is generated scheduling state, not a switch for enabling whoosh sounds.
A Rigidbody is an object’s body in Unity’s physics simulation. The sample is squared hand-minus-chest world speed, in square meters per square second (m²/s²).

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._lastHandChestVelSqMg
member.summary: The cached squared speed of the physical hand relative to the physical chest.

remarks.para: The value is the squared length of hand velocity minus chest velocity, measured in world coordinates. Velocity is in meters per second, so this is in square meters per square second. For example, a relative speed of 2 meters per second gives 4; it is not itself a speed of 4 meters per second.

FixedUpdate and Update replace it after processing the collector, so the routines the collector calls when it reports a contact use the previous cached sample during that processing. The impact branch requires at least 0.64, equivalent to a relative speed of 0.8 meters per second. PunchAttack further rejects samples below 0.9. Changing it directly can affect those tests until a later sample replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._lastImpulse
member.summary: The impulse magnitude saved by the last impact accepted by the collector’s repeat-impact check.

remarks.para: The value is in newton-seconds, representing collision push delivered over time. CheckImpact compares a new magnitude with this value while _nextImpactTime is still ahead. A weaker new hit is rejected, but an equal or stronger hit can be accepted before that deadline.

An accepted check replaces this value and advances the deadline by 0.25 unscaled seconds. It is not updated for every collision, and it is not a force in newtons or the normalized intensity passed into PunchAttack.
Unscaled seconds are elapsed real-time seconds, unaffected by slow motion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._lastRelVelPlane
member.summary: The saved world-space velocity along the contact surface used to measure how sliding motion changes.

remarks.para: The contact routine projects relative velocity onto the surface plane, removing motion into or away from the surface. This stored vector is in meters per second along that plane. Enter processing can initialize it; ongoing contact compares its new projected velocity with this previous sample.

The ongoing-contact routine divides the difference by the physics-step duration to estimate acceleration, then overwrites this field before calling Slide. It is the previous processed contact sample, rather than a guaranteed previous rendered-frame value or a hand-local position.
The physics-step duration is in seconds. Dividing this world velocity difference, measured in meters per second, by that duration estimates acceleration in meters per square second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._mapImpact
member.summary: The reusable playback handle for this hand’s impact, punch, slap and backhand sounds.

remarks.para: The constructor creates a ManagedAudioPlayer here. Its actual audio player can be obtained later through asynchronous spawning, meaning the request can wait while the sound-playing object is created. The handle keeps the requested sound, volume and pitch; OnSignificantCollisionEnter uses it to play at this hand’s local origin, so the sound follows the hand.
These routines request non-looping clips. Reusing the handle can replace or retrigger the sound; it is generated playback state rather than an authored audio-clip bank.

If a valid audio player is already available, playback is requested on it directly. Otherwise a playback request can wait for setup; the handle’s existence alone does not mean a sound is currently playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._mapSlide
member.summary: The reusable playback handle for this hand’s slide and scrape sounds.

remarks.para: The constructor creates a ManagedAudioPlayer here. Its actual audio player can be obtained later through asynchronous spawning, meaning the request can wait while the sound-playing object is created. The handle keeps the requested sound, volume and pitch; Slide uses it to play at this hand’s local origin, so the sound follows the hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._nextImpactTime
member.summary: The unscaled-time deadline used to filter weaker repeated impact sounds.

remarks.para: This is an absolute time in seconds on Unity’s unscaled clock, which keeps its real-time rate during slow motion. An incoming impulse weaker than _lastImpulse is rejected while the deadline is ahead; equal or stronger impulses can still pass.

Start initially sets it five seconds ahead. BodySlot and ForcePull set it 0.2 seconds ahead after requesting their audio. Grab and Drop set it 0.2 seconds ahead only after finding the attached hand’s Controller, even when that Controller has no Haptor vibration sender. An accepted collision check sets it 0.25 seconds ahead. These assignments replace the deadline. It is not a guaranteed quiet period for every impact.
_lastImpulse is the raw collision-push magnitude saved by the last accepted repeat-impact check, measured in newton-seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._nextSlideTime
member.summary: The earliest unscaled time at which a new scrape-clip playback request is allowed.

remarks.para: Slide compares this absolute time in seconds with Unity’s unscaledTime. Issuing a playback request sets it to that clock plus 0.3 seconds. A new request also requires estimated contact acceleration squared of at least 400 square meters per fourth-power second, equivalent to an acceleration magnitude of 20 meters per square second. The normal contact routine calculates it from the change in surface-parallel world velocity divided by the physics-step duration in seconds; passing the time check alone does not produce a sound. A newly needed audio player can still be loading after the request advances this deadline.

While a clip is already playing, its volume and pitch are adjusted before this start gate. This field therefore limits new playback, rather than throttling every slide-audio adjustment. Slow motion does not stretch the unscaled 0.3-second deadline.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._physHand
member.summary: The assigned physical-hand component connecting these sounds to the correct hand, chest and avatar measurements.

remarks.para: Contact routines use its Hand to check whether an object or temporary joint is attached and to obtain the controller for vibration and input. They use its PhysicsRig for chest velocity, the player’s own body list and avatar measurements.

HandSFX’s inspected Awake and Start do not automatically fill this serialized reference. Assign the PhysHand belonging to the same hand. It supplies the context for sound and attack calculations; changing it alone does not move the hand’s physical body.
The temporary joint is a physics connection prepared during grabbing. Awake and Start are Unity setup routines: Awake initializes the component, and Start runs after its initial setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX._rb
member.summary: The hand Rigidbody cached for velocity samples, sleep checks and mass-dependent sound and attack calculations.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the body moved and collided by Unity’s physics simulation. Start is Unity’s setup routine after initialization; it gets this Rigidbody from the same GameObject as HandSFX. A GameObject is the scene object that carries components. FixedUpdate and Update read its whole-scene velocity vector in meters per second and skip processing when it is sleeping, meaning temporarily inactive in physics calculations until awakened.

Impact, scrape and attack code also read its mass in kilograms to turn a collision push into a response relative to the hand’s weight. Start overwrites this cache; changing the reference does not move the HandSFX component or automatically reconnect its collector and PhysHand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.backhand
member.summary: The ordinary-speed clip choices for a backhand impact sound.

remarks.para: The open-hand branch uses this bank for the opposite, sufficiently negative side alignment with the contact. OnSignificantCollisionEnter makes the choice after its empty-hand, motion and impulse checks. Slap and backhand distinguish which side of the hand meets the surface. The comparison uses the hand object’s right axis, reversed for a right hand, against the direction pointing into the surface. A comparison above 0.2 selects slap and below -0.2 selects backhand; the middle range uses fallbackImpact.

The audio player randomly chooses one clip. At timeScale 0.51 or below it can use backhandSlowMo instead when that alternate bank has clips; an empty alternate bank falls back to this bank. Keep both arrays assigned and the ordinary bank nonempty for the dual-bank routine to run. The sound asset does not set attack damage.
timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 0.5 is half speed, and 0 pauses game time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.backhandSlowMo
member.summary: Alternate clip choices for backhand playback when game timeScale is 0.51 or below.

remarks.para: The same collision branch that chooses backhand supplies this array to the audio player. When slow enough and this array has clips, the player chooses one of them randomly. Otherwise it falls back to the ordinary backhand array.

Keep both arrays assigned, and the ordinary backhand array nonempty, for this dual-bank routine to play anything. An empty alternate array is supported. These are alternate sound assets, rather than a field that activates slow motion. The audio player applies its slow-motion pitch adjustment too.
timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 0.5 is half speed, and 0 pauses game time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.bodySlot

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.fallbackImpact

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX.forceGrab

member.summary: A stored floating-point value with no effect in the audited HeadSFX vocal and contact paths.

remarks.para: No read or write of this field appears in the inspected HeadSFX constructor, initialization, vocal playback, collision-enter/stay or sensor-update methods. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._lastHeadChestAngVelSqMg
member.summary: Caches how quickly the head rotates relative to the chest, squared, for headbutt detection.

remarks.para: AfterFixedSensorUpdate stores the squared length of head angular velocity minus chest angular velocity, using world-space vectors measured in radians per second. This cache is therefore in rad²/s². A headbutt requires a value strictly above 6, equivalent to a relative angular-speed magnitude above about 2.45 rad/s, as well as the other impact and layer checks.

The sensor method processes contacts before overwriting this cache, so those contact routines see the previously stored value. Changing the cache can affect those checks until the sensor calculation replaces it; it does not rotate the head.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._lastImpactTime
member.summary: Stores an initialization timestamp that does not control the audited headbutt filter.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s first active-frame setup routine, sets this to Unity’s unscaled-time clock plus 5 seconds. That clock is measured in seconds since game startup and is unaffected by slow motion. No later read appears in the inspected HeadSFX methods.
Changing this value does not add an impact grace period to those paths. Their active quarter-second impulse filter uses _lastImpulse and _nextImpactTime instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._lastImpulse
member.summary: Remembers the summed impulse magnitude accepted by the head impact filter, so weaker follow-up impacts can be skipped.

remarks.para: The stored magnitude is in N·s, equal to kg·m/s: the size of the contact’s change in momentum. OnSignificantCollisionEnter passes this field by reference to CollisionCollector.CheckImpact. Before _nextImpactTime, a new magnitude strictly below this value is rejected; an equal or larger one is accepted. After that deadline, even a weaker impact can pass.

An accepted check overwrites this field with the new magnitude and sets the deadline to the unscaled-time clock plus 0.25 seconds. Acceptance happens before the additional headbutt checks, so this is not necessarily the impulse of a headbutt that played a sound. Raising it can suppress weaker contacts until the deadline; lowering it can allow them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._lastJumpEffort
member.summary: Stores the unscaled-time timestamp used to keep jump grunts at least two seconds apart.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s first active-frame setup routine, records the current unscaled-time clock here. JumpEffort skips a grunt until current unscaled time minus this value reaches 2 seconds; the unscaled clock advances normally during slow motion.

An eligible JumpEffort attempt updates this timestamp before configuring the mouth source and playing. It therefore records an accepted attempt rather than proof that the sound finished or even that later playback setup succeeded. Moving it into the future delays grunts; moving it back can allow an earlier attempt.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._lastRelVelPlane
member.summary: Stores the contact’s relative motion along the surface, after removing motion through the surface.

remarks.para: OnSignificantCollisionEnter projects the contact’s relative velocity onto the plane perpendicular to its world-space contact normal. The stored vector uses world axes and has units of m/s. For example, sliding sideways along a wall remains in this vector, while velocity straight into the wall is removed. If the normal’s squared length is too small for division, the relative velocity is stored without that projection.

The value is stored after processed contacts, but self contacts and contacts rejected by the impact-strength filter return without replacing it. No reader appears in the inspected HeadSFX methods, and their continuing-contact routine is empty; this cache does not itself play sliding audio.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._mapImpact

remarks.para: The HeadSFX constructor creates this helper. After the headbutt checks and a successful attack-dispatch attempt, the contact routine asks it to play a random headbutt clip at this component’s local origin, using the hard-interaction mixer and the optional slow-motion bank. The sound follows this component’s transform rather than the mouth AudioSource.

Replacing this field changes which managed player receives later headbutt playback requests. This component’s OnDestroy routine removes contact registrations but does not call Stop on this player. The field does not identify a map or provide a special modded-audio path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._nextImpactTime
member.summary: Sets the unscaled-time deadline before which the impact filter rejects an impulse weaker than its saved magnitude.

remarks.para: This is an absolute timestamp in seconds on Unity’s unscaled-time clock, which slow motion does not slow down. CollisionCollector.CheckImpact receives this field by reference from the head contact routine. While the current clock is strictly before it, an impulse smaller than _lastImpulse is rejected; equal or stronger impulses are still accepted.

An accepted check replaces the timestamp with current unscaled time plus 0.25 seconds and saves the new impulse magnitude. Setting it into the future prolongs weaker-impact suppression, but does not prevent an equal or stronger impact or guarantee a headbutt.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._physRig

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. The PhysicsRig controls the character’s physical body. Vocal helpers read its current avatar sound data on each call, head contacts use its selfRbs set to exclude the character’s own rigidbodies, and AfterFixedSensorUpdate uses its torso’s chest Rigidbody for the relative-rotation measurement.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is an object controlled by Unity’s physics simulation. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, replaces this reference with the Rigidbody on the same scene object as HeadSFX. Its mass in kg scales attack and impact-audio strength; its rotation orients the contact-facing check, and its angular velocity is compared with the chest’s.
Changing this reference later redirects those measurements to the replacement body. It does not change the PhysicsRig’s chest reference or automatically move the audio source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX._speachEnd
member.summary: The game-time deadline used to report speaking and block the vocal helpers.

remarks.para: This is an absolute timestamp in seconds on Unity’s game-time clock. isSpeaking is true exactly while current game time is less than this value. Slow motion makes that clock advance more slowly, so the same deadline interval lasts longer in real time. This field is not a measurement of AudioSource playback.

Speak normally stores current game time plus the requested clip’s length before playing. If Speak is called with playDelayed while this deadline is still in the future, it instead adds the new clip’s length to the existing deadline and returns without playing or queueing that clip. The jump and damage vocal helpers check this field but do not extend it.
Setting it into the future blocks those helpers until the game-time clock reaches it; setting it to the current time or earlier clears that gate even if mouth audio is still audible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.bigDamage
member.summary: Fallback clips for the heavy-damage vocal when the current avatar has no bigPain sound-data asset.

remarks.para: BigDamageVocal selects the current avatar’s bigPain audioClips array when that sound-data asset exists; this component’s array is used only when the asset is missing. The PhysicsRig and its current avatar must exist. Changing this array therefore affects later calls only while that fallback is selected. An empty selected bank produces no sound, and an empty avatar bank does not fall back here; a null selected array is invalid.

An eligible call chooses a random clip, updates the mouth filter and plays through mouthSrc. It is skipped while game time is before the speech-blocking deadline, and playing a clip does not extend that deadline. Another eligible vocal can replace the sound on the same source.
BigDamageVocal plays at volume 1. This sound helper does not itself change the character’s health or body state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.isSpeaking
member.summary: Reports whether the speech-blocking game-time deadline is still in the future.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.meleeAttackMask
member.summary: Chooses which scene-object layers are allowed to receive this head’s blunt attack.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. A layer is Unity’s numbered category for a scene object; a LayerMask stores a set of those categories. BluntAttack tests the layer of the struck collider’s scene object. A collider is the physical shape used to detect contact. If its layer is excluded, the attack returns false before receiver dispatch, and the headbutt sound is not requested.

Including a layer permits that part of the check but does not guarantee an attack: the contact-enter routine also checks relative motion, impact strength, contact facing and head-versus-chest rotation. The receiver routine is attempted on the collider’s Rigidbody scene object, which can be a different object from the collider itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.mouthLowPass
member.summary: The assigned filter whose custom cutoff curve is rebuilt when a mouth vocal starts.

remarks.para: A low-pass filter removes higher frequencies and makes a sound more muffled. UpdateLowPass rebuilds this filter’s distance curve from the mouth source’s facing direction relative to the main camera: facing the camera uses a higher near curve level than facing away. The farther curve end has one quarter of the near level.

Assign the filter before vocal playback. The update happens while Speak or a vocal helper prepares playback, so changing its curve can be overwritten by the next eligible call. Moving the camera alone does not continuously rebuild the curve during a clip. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, does not find this filter automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.mouthSrc
member.summary: The assigned AudioSource that plays speech and the jump, damage, dying, death and recovery vocals.

remarks.para: An AudioSource plays a sound clip from a scene object. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, sends this source’s output to the npcVocals audio mixer group, which controls the vocal audio channel. Assign the source beforehand; HeadSFX does not find it automatically.

Each eligible vocal replaces the source’s selected clip and volume/pitch before starting it. SmallDamageVocal also sets its near-source volume distance in metres. UpdateLowPass uses this source’s world position and forward direction to rebuild the assigned mouth filter’s distance curve.

The headbutt impact sound uses _mapImpact, a separate managed player at this component’s origin. Changing mouthSrc changes the source read by later vocal calls but does not rerun the initialization mixer assignment or move the assigned filter to the new object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX.proxy

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.UsageSettings.Default
member.summary: Returns a settings value with all six usage multipliers set to zero.

remarks.para: Applying this value with Health.SetUsage makes the hips, spine, left/right arm and left/right leg usage contributions zero when Health.UpdateMuscleStates applies them. It does not provide a set of normal-strength values merely because its name is Default.

The six-argument constructor has optional arguments of 1, which are separate from this property's zero-filled result. To explicitly preserve the other strength factors, construct new Health.UsageSettings(1f, 1f, 1f, 1f, 1f, 1f), then change whichever usage multiplier you need.
This is a returned value copy. Changing its fields does not affect a Health component until you pass the value to SetUsage; applying it does not itself delete joints or make body parts immovable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._accelSanGravMag
member.summary: Stores the horizontal acceleration magnitude used by the animation rig to calculate movement lean.

remarks.para: This is measured in meters per second squared from the supplied world X and Z acceleration components. It is a magnitude, so it has no left/right direction. For example, components (3, 4) give a magnitude of 5. The calculation ignores world Y; it does not subtract a gravity vector from all three components.

AnimationRig.BodyVelocity replaces this cache when it processes movement. If the supplied horizontal speed is zero, that routine clears both the speed and acceleration magnitudes, even if a nonzero acceleration was supplied. Its acceleration contribution to lean is weighted and limited separately, so 5 here does not mean a 5-degree lean.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._angularVelocity
member.summary: Stores the smoothed turning rate of the input rig’s body-support facing direction.

remarks.para: This is a signed rate in degrees per second. BodyVelocity compares the previous and current centerOfPressure forward vectors, chooses the turn’s sign using _playerUp, and divides the angle by deltaTime. It then blends the saved rate toward that result with a fraction limited to 0 through 1, calculated as 10 × deltaTime.

The rate is updated only when deltaTime is positive. For example, a 9-degree heading change over 0.1 seconds gives a 90-degrees-per-second target before that blending. Writing this calculated value does not turn the rig. AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled clears it and resets the facing history.
Here deltaTime is the supplied time step in seconds, and _playerUp is the configured world up direction used to choose the sign of the turn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._copToVelLerp
member.summary: Stores a smoothed, folded and speed-weighted movement/facing angle used in additional chest and pelvis twist.

remarks.para: This is in degrees, not a 0-to-1 blend weight. BodyVelocity obtains a signed angle from the world X/Z movement direction to the world X/Z components of centerOfPressure.forward, then folds and speed-weights it before smoothing, using _copToVelVel as the saved rate. When horizontal speed is zero, its target is zero.

This is calculated history: BodyVelocity replaces it, and AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled clears it and its rate. AnimationRig’s additional chest and pelvis calculations use this angle when forming their twist corrections. Suppression, permitted twist and further smoothing also affect the applied pose, so this cache does not equal the final twist or directly turn a physics body.

BodyVelocity first folds a signed angle strictly above +110 degrees by subtracting 180 degrees, or strictly below −110 degrees by adding 180 degrees. Exactly +110 and −110 stay unchanged. It then multiplies the folded angle by clamp01(speed / avatarPelvisHeight × 0.46), where speed is horizontal speed in metres per second, avatarPelvisHeight is the avatar’s stored pelvis reference height in metres, clamp01 limits a number to 0 through 1, and 0.46 is the routine’s built-in numerical factor. For example, +150 becomes −30 degrees and −150 becomes +30 degrees before that weighting; zero speed gives a zero target. SmoothDamp gradually eases the saved angle toward that target while updating its saved angular rate.

avatarPelvisHeight is the saved hips-bone height above the avatar animation root. RefreshBodyMeasurements rebuilds this setup proportion from eye height; BodyVelocity reads the rig/avatar cache, not a live pelvis measurement. The signed angle compares world-X/Z movement direction with centerOfPressure facing expressed locally; its horizontal speed and angle are not vertical displacement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._copToVelVel
member.summary: Keeps the angular smoothing rate for .

remarks.para: The units are degrees per second. BodyVelocity passes this value by reference to SmoothDamp while smoothing the folded, speed-weighted movement/facing angle; SmoothDamp updates the rate for the next calculation.

It is not movement speed in meters per second. Changing it changes smoothing history rather than turning a transform directly. AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled clears it along with _copToVelLerp; the rate can affect additional chest and pelvis twist through the next smoothed _copToVelLerp value, with suppression, permitted twist and further smoothing still determining the applied pose.

BodyVelocity first folds a signed angle strictly above +110 degrees by subtracting 180 degrees, or strictly below −110 degrees by adding 180 degrees. Exactly +110 and −110 stay unchanged. It then multiplies the folded angle by clamp01(speed / avatarPelvisHeight × 0.46), where speed is horizontal speed in metres per second, avatarPelvisHeight is the avatar’s stored pelvis reference height in metres, clamp01 limits a number to 0 through 1, and 0.46 is the routine’s built-in numerical factor. For example, +150 becomes −30 degrees and −150 becomes +30 degrees before that weighting; zero speed gives a zero target. SmoothDamp means gradual easing toward a target with a saved rate; passing the rate by reference means the routine may overwrite this stored value.

avatarPelvisHeight is the saved hips-bone height above the avatar animation root, rebuilt by RefreshBodyMeasurements from eye height. BodyVelocity reads that rig/avatar cache, not a live pelvis. The smoothing rate remains an angle rate in degrees per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._deviaHandLf
member.summary: Stores the left wrist’s signed sideways bend, exposed by .

remarks.para: The value is in degrees, calculated from the solved hand and forearm orientations. It describes how far the wrist bends sideways relative to the arm; it is not controller squeeze, hand position, or a 0-to-1 weight.

ApplyArms replaces this value when it applies the solved arms. Grip.SolveHandleAmplify reads the corresponding value from the virtual body rig as the input to handleAmplifyCurve, which can add a wrist-dependent correction to two-hand object control. Other grip settings and limits affect that correction. Editing the cache alone does not rotate the wrist, and a later ApplyArms calculation replaces the edit.

This angle is measured before ApplyArms’s later wrist rotation limit, so the cached measurement can differ from the final visible wrist pose. The cache is written before that later limit and the final hand position/rotation writes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._deviaHandRt

remarks.para: The value is in degrees, calculated from the solved hand and forearm orientations. It describes how far the wrist bends sideways relative to the arm; it is not controller squeeze, hand position, or a 0-to-1 weight.

ApplyArms replaces this value when it applies the solved arms. Grip.SolveHandleAmplify reads the corresponding value from the virtual body rig as the input to handleAmplifyCurve, which can add a wrist-dependent correction to two-hand object control. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._elbowLimitCurve
member.summary: Adds a pose-dependent upper-arm rotation to adjust where the solved elbows point.

remarks.para: The curve’s horizontal input is the signed angle in degrees between the upper arm’s forward direction and the direction from the shoulder toward the computed sternum point, after ignoring their components along the shoulder-to-hand axis. Its vertical output is a correction angle in degrees. It is not controller squeeze or a physical joint-force limit.

SolveArms applies this correction when the upper arm’s forward direction is less than 60 degrees from the shoulder-to-computed-sternum direction before those components are ignored. It uses the full curve output through 45 degrees, then fades it to zero at 60 degrees using 1 − clamp((angle − 45) / 15, 0, 1). For example, a 10-degree output at a 52.5-degree outer angle gives a 5-degree correction before other pose operations.

The correction rotates the upper arm about the solver’s chosen swivel axis, with matching left/right handling. A flat curve at zero adds no correction in this step. It affects elbow placement around the arm direction rather than setting the elbow’s bend angle directly.

The sternum is the breastbone at the middle front of the chest. The computed sternum point comes from the chest pose and avatar reference offsets. The shoulder-to-hand direction is the projection and swivel axis, rather than the sternum reference used for the curve input and outer gate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._lastAngularFwd

remarks.para: This is the input rig’s centerOfPressure forward vector in world space, a direction rather than a position or angle. BodyVelocity compares it with the current forward vector to calculate signed turning rate and rotate the saved leaning direction.

BodyVelocity stores the current forward vector here after that comparison, including when deltaTime is not positive. AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled replaces the history with the facing direction rotated by the teleport’s rotation, so the next comparison does not use the old heading unchanged.
Here deltaTime means the supplied time step in seconds; storing the new facing history is separate from the turning-rate and leaning-direction work that requires a positive step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._leanRetainer
member.summary: Stores a smoothed movement-related angle that contributes to additional chest and pelvis bending.

remarks.para: BodyVelocity chooses the larger of 3.5 × speed / avatar eye height and 0.7 × acceleration magnitude / avatar eye height as its target. Speed is in meters per second, acceleration in meters per second squared, and eye height is the avatar’s stored eye-height reference in metres. These calibrated numerical terms form the routine’s movement-related target, which the additional chest and pelvis calculations use as degrees. It is not a distance or a guaranteed 0-to-1 percentage.

SmoothDamp moves this cache toward the target using _leanVelocity as its saved rate. BodyVelocity updates it again, and AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled clears the saved angle. AnimationRig’s additional chest and pelvis calculations combine this angle with their smoothed posture, suppression and baseline terms before rotating about the aligned chest/pelvis right direction. It contributes to the resulting bend without equalling the final body angle.

SmoothDamp gradually eases this angle toward the target and also updates its saved rate. These later pose calculations can replace or limit the contribution; writing the cache does not directly set a simulated body’s rotation.

Eye height is the current avatar’s stored eye-midpoint height above the Animator root; BodyVelocity reads the current Avatar field. Speed and acceleration here are world-X/Z horizontal magnitudes, and both are zero when horizontal speed is zero.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._leanVelocity
member.summary: Keeps the angular smoothing rate of the movement-related angle in .

remarks.para: BodyVelocity passes it by reference to SmoothDamp, which changes it while the movement-related angle approaches its target. Its units are degrees per second; it is not the avatar’s movement speed.

Changing it affects the stored smoothing history. It can affect additional chest and pelvis bending through the next smoothed _leanRetainer angle; other posture, suppression and limit terms still affect the final pose. The audited AnimationRig.Teleport zeroVelocity block clears _leanRetainer but does not clear this rate.

SmoothDamp means gradual easing toward a target while updating a saved rate. Passing this value by reference means the routine can overwrite it; it is history for that angular calculation rather than a constant body-turn command.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._leftHandTwist
member.summary: Keeps the left arm’s signed twist history while the rig chooses where its elbow should point.

remarks.para: This is an angle in degrees around the shoulder-to-hand direction. SolveArms passes it to ElbowIsNot, which compares projected arm and wrist directions and accumulates a signed angular correction. The history helps choose the arm’s swivel, meaning the way the elbow moves around that direction.

It is not a quaternion or a squeeze input. Changing it can affect the next arm solution’s elbow direction, rather than directly rotating the hand transform. ElbowIsNot updates it again, and reduces same-direction winding as its calculation approaches its internal 177-degree reference; that reference is not a proven clamp on the stored angle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._neckTiltCurve
member.summary: Shapes the counter-rotation used as the head or chest approaches a permitted spine bend.

remarks.para: The horizontal input is a unitless ratio: the measured tilt angle divided by the avatar’s permitted angle for that bend direction. Input 1 means the measured tilt equals that reference angle. The vertical output is also a ratio, which the solver multiplies by the reference angle to obtain a counter-rotation; it is not a degree angle by itself.

SolveChest and SolvePelvis evaluate this curve when the input ratio is greater than 0.8; at or below 0.8 they use the ratio directly. For example, with a 40-degree reference, input 1 and output 0.8 produce a 32-degree counter-rotation at that stage. The rotation opposes the measured bend axis; the final orientation combines it with the other pose terms.

Despite the name, both chest and pelvis solving use this correction curve, as do AnimationRig’s additional posture calculations. These branches do not clamp its output to 0 through 1. Changing the curve changes the correction response rather than changing the avatar’s stored range-of-motion angles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._neutFemurLf
member.summary: Sets the left thigh’s neutral orientation in a generated base body pose.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion relative to the pose’s root orientation. GenerateBasePose copies it into legLfRotationInRoot in its output BodyPose. A quaternion represents orientation; its four components are not four degree angles.

Changing it changes that reference rotation in subsequently generated base poses. It is not a live measurement of the thigh’s world rotation. The audited SolveLegs routine calculates legs from its foot/ankle targets without reading this neutral field directly, so changing it is not a verified direct override of that leg solver.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._neutHumLf
member.summary: Sets the left upper arm’s neutral orientation relative to the chest for arm pose calculations.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion: an orientation, not a distance or a single degree angle. SolveArms combines it with the chest’s world rotation to form the neutral shoulder reference used while choosing the elbow’s direction. Turning this reference can change the preferred arm swivel while hand targets and the other arm constraints still determine the final pose.

GenerateBasePose also copies it into armLfRotationInChest in the generated BodyPose. It is a reference orientation rather than a reading of the arm’s current world rotation. For example, an identity quaternion would align this reference with the chest; this is an example, not the constructor’s configured orientation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._playerUp
member.summary: Sets the world direction treated as up when the rig solves body posture and measures turning.

remarks.para: This is a direction vector, not a height or gravity strength. The constructor starts it from world up. For example, (0, 1, 0) points along the world’s positive Y axis; a direction with length 1 keeps the height projections expressed as ordinary distances.

SolveChest and SolvePelvis project head/chest displacement along this direction when choosing their posture curves, and use it as an orientation reference. SolveFeetCenter and SolveLegs also use it in body/leg placement, while AnimationRig.BodyVelocity uses it to choose the sign of a heading change.

Changing it changes those reference calculations when they next run; it does not change Physics.gravity. BodyVelocity still removes world Y from velocity and acceleration and uses world up for its basic lean target, so this field alone does not rotate every movement calculation into a different gravity frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._rightHandTwist

remarks.para: This is an angle in degrees around the shoulder-to-hand direction. SolveArms passes it to ElbowIsNot, which compares projected arm and wrist directions and accumulates a signed angular correction. The history helps choose the arm’s swivel, meaning the way the elbow moves around that direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._sacrumUpOffsetCurve
member.summary: Sets the height-dependent pelvis posture used when placing the lower spine below the chest.

remarks.para: The sacrum is the base of the spine near the pelvis. The curve’s vertical value is a posture angle in degrees, not an upward movement distance. SolvePelvis uses that angle to turn its up reference around the chest-aligned right direction before building the pelvis pose.

In SolvePelvis, the horizontal input is chest height above the rig’s root along _playerUp, divided by the avatar’s chest height, then limited to 0 through 1. Input 0.5 represents half that reference height. An output of 20 at 0.5 requests a 20-degree posture angle at that stage; it does not raise the pelvis 20 meters.

AnimationRig.AdditivePelvis adds spineCrouchOffset and the supplied physKneeOffset before height division, then calls SolveSacrumUpOffset; the helper evaluates and blends posture curves without clamping that height input. GenerateBasePose derives its input from the requested skull height and extrapolated neck offset, then limits it to 0 through 1. CalibratePlayerBodyScale moves the second key’s horizontal position for the avatar while retaining its vertical value; it creates a new key without carrying over the old tangents, and requires that key to exist.

The rig root is the base Transform holding the rig, and _playerUp is its configured world up direction. spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are distance corrections in metres for spinal crouch and physical-knee height. The stored chestHeight reference is the setup neck-bone height: complete setup reads neck world Y minus the Animator-root world Y and divides by eyeHeight; it is not the chest-joint height. RefreshBodyMeasurements rebuilds this calibrated metre proportion. AdditivePelvis initially samples the baseline from the input rig’s neck height; its later helper receives supplied chest height above the animation root plus both distance corrections, divided by chest reference height. GenerateBasePose uses clamp01((skullHeightWeight × skullHeight + extrapolatedNeckOffset.y) / chestHeight): skullHeightWeight is the unitless requested skull-height multiplier, skullHeight and chestHeight are the stored joint reference heights in metres, and extrapolatedNeckOffset.y is the neck displacement in metres along that base-pose local frame’s Y axis.

GenerateBasePose uses skullHeight as the head-bone world-Y height above the animation root in the setup proportion; RefreshBodyMeasurements refreshes that stored value. The sacrum setup denominator therefore uses the corrected neck/eye-height calibration rather than a live chest-joint measurement each solve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._t1UpOffsetCurve
member.summary: Sets the height-dependent upper-spine posture used when placing the chest below the head.

remarks.para: T1 is the upper end of the chest’s spine. The curve’s vertical value is a posture angle in degrees, not an upward distance in meters. SolveChest uses it to rotate its up reference around the head-aligned right direction before constructing the chest pose.

In SolveChest, the horizontal input is head height above the rig’s root, measured along _playerUp, divided by the avatar’s skull height. An input of 0.5 means half that reference height. For example, an output of 30 at input 0.5 requests a 30-degree posture angle at that stage; other bend limits and pose calculations affect the final chest.

SolveChest does not clamp this normalized height before evaluating the curve. AnimationRig.AdditiveChest adds spineCrouchOffset and the supplied physKneeOffset before dividing by skull reference height and calling SolveT1UpOffset; that helper evaluates and blends posture curves without clamping the height input. GenerateBasePose instead samples this curve at input 1. CalibratePlayerBodyScale moves the second key’s horizontal position for the avatar while retaining its vertical value; it creates a new key without carrying over the old tangents, and requires that key to exist.

The rig root is the base Transform holding the rig, and _playerUp is its configured world up direction. spineCrouchOffset and physKneeOffset are distance corrections in metres for spinal crouch and physical-knee height. The skull height denominator is the avatar’s stored skull-joint reference height in metres, rather than skull thickness. AdditiveChest’s helper input uses the supplied head height above the animation root along that up direction, plus both distance corrections, divided by that skull reference height.

The stored skullHeight is the setup head-bone world-Y height above the Animator/animation root, refreshed as a proportion by RefreshBodyMeasurements. SolveChest uses that saved setup reference; it is not a fresh live tracked-head height read on every solve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._velLerp
member.summary: Stores the smoothed world direction toward which movement makes the animation rig lean.

remarks.para: This is a direction with length 1, not a velocity in meters per second. BodyVelocity starts its desired direction from world up, adds contributions from horizontal acceleration and squared horizontal speed, smooths toward that direction, and normalizes the result. For example, (0, 1, 0) is upright; a direction with a horizontal component represents a tilt.

The smoothing uses a 0.3-second response-time parameter and keeps its rate in _velLerpAccel. When the supplied deltaTime is positive and the input rig turns, BodyVelocity first rotates the saved direction by the change in heading around world up. AnimationRig uses the returned direction as _dragUp for its additional chest and pelvis posture calculations; other pose terms and limits still affect the final body.
BodyVelocity replaces this value. AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled resets it to world up, but does not clear _velLerpAccel in the audited reset block.

The response-time parameter controls gradual easing, rather than promising arrival at the target exactly 0.3 seconds later. Actual filter updates advance using the supplied deltaTime time step in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._velLerpAccel
member.summary: Keeps the smoothing rate for the leaning direction in .

remarks.para: Vector3.SmoothDamp reads and updates this vector while moving the saved direction toward the next desired direction. Its components describe change in the direction’s components per second; they are not physical acceleration in meters per second squared.

Changing this history can change the next smoothing step, but it does not push a physics body (an object moved by the physics simulation). BodyVelocity updates it again. Its final direction is normalized after smoothing, so this rate should not be treated as an exact derivative of the normalized output. The audited AnimationRig.Teleport zeroVelocity block resets the direction but leaves this rate untouched.
SmoothDamp gradually eases the saved value toward a target while reading and updating a saved rate; that rate can influence the next filtering step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._velSanGravMag
member.summary: Stores the horizontal movement speed used by the animation rig to calculate lean.

remarks.para: The value is in meters per second: the length of the supplied world X/Z velocity, with world Y omitted. Components (3, 4) therefore give 5 meters per second, regardless of vertical movement. BodyVelocity uses its square in one contribution to the desired leaning direction.

AnimationRig.BodyVelocity replaces it on each calculation, and sets it to zero when horizontal speed is zero. AnimationRig.Teleport with zeroVelocity enabled also clears it. Writing the cache does not change the physical body’s velocity; the next calculation uses its supplied movement again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._velSanGravNormal
member.summary: Stores the movement direction used for the animation rig’s speed-dependent lean.

remarks.para: While moving horizontally, this is a unit vector in world space: the world X/Z velocity divided by horizontal speed, with Y set to zero. A unit vector has length 1 and describes direction rather than speed. Velocity (3, 0, 4), for example, produces (0.6, 0, 0.8).

At zero horizontal speed, BodyVelocity instead copies the input rig’s centerOfPressure forward direction. That is the facing direction of the rig’s body-support reference; it is not necessarily a horizontal vector. The cache is recalculated by BodyVelocity, so changing it is not a lasting movement-direction override.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._wristRelaxLerpLf
member.summary: Stores the smoothed left-arm swivel angle used to relax the wrist while solving the elbow.

remarks.para: This is an angle in degrees, not a 0-to-1 relaxation weight. ElbowIsNot builds a target from the wrist/arm orientation and neutral shoulder reference, then uses SmoothDamp to approach it. The matching _wristRelaxVelLf keeps the angular smoothing rate.

The smoothing response-time parameter is (1.08 − elbowWeight) × 0.12 seconds; for example, an elbow weight of 0 gives 0.1296 seconds. After storing the smoothed angle, the solver can blend its returned angle toward a tracked elbow direction when elbowWeight is positive. The cache therefore need not equal the final angle applied to the arm. SolveArms updates it on later calculations.

Here elbowWeight is the influence of the left tracked-elbow direction: in the returned-angle blend, 0 selects the solved wrist-relaxation angle and 1 selects the tracked-elbow result. This does not establish a runtime clamp on supplied weights. SmoothDamp gradually eases the angular value while updating a saved rate. Its calculated response time is not a guaranteed completion duration; actual updates use the supplied deltaTime in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._wristRelaxLerpRt

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig._wristRelaxVelLf

remarks.para: The value is in degrees per second. SolveArms passes it to ElbowIsNot, where SmoothDamp reads and updates it while moving _wristRelaxLerpLf toward a pose-dependent swivel angle. It is not the hand’s physical movement speed.

Changing this history can change the next relaxation step.
