member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig.accelLeanWeight
member.summary: The built-in factor of 0.33 for the acceleration contribution to the animation rig’s leaning direction.

remarks.para: BodyVelocity multiplies horizontal acceleration magnitude by this factor and divides by g = max(abs(world-Y gravity acceleration), 1.62 metres per second squared). It caps that contribution at 0.422 before adding it along the acceleration direction to the desired up direction.

For example, acceleration 3 meters per second squared and a gravity reference of 10 metres per second squared give 3 × 0.33 / 10 = 0.099 before the cap. That is a contribution to a direction calculation, not a 0.099-degree lean. Speed, smoothing, normalization and the posture solvers also affect the result. This is a compiled constant, not a mutable per-rig tuning field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig.dragWeight
member.summary: An original source constant fixed at 2, with no per-avatar stored tuning value.

remarks.para: The original declaration is a protected const float. A constant means a value built into the compiled program rather than a changing number stored separately on each avatar. This declaration has no per-instance field offset; it is therefore different from the rig’s stored inputs and smoothing caches.

The checked HeptaRig methods, AnimationRig.BodyVelocity, OpenControllerRig.UpdateHeptaBody and GameWorldSkeletonRig.OnUpdate do not establish a separate named effect or working units for this constant. Both dragWeight and pACdProduct equal 2, and the compiled calculations combine numeric constants, so a matching number does not identify which name supplied it. Treat this as a fixed source declaration, not a verified control for drag force, a particular coefficient product or avatar-specific tuning.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig.leftHandDevia
member.summary: Reports the left wrist’s signed sideways bend for wrist-dependent grip calculations.

remarks.para: This returns the value stored in _deviaHandLf. It is an angle in degrees, calculated by ApplyArms from the solved hand and forearm orientations. It does not recalculate the arm or report controller squeeze.

Grip.SolveHandleAmplify uses this wrist measurement from the virtual body rig as handleAmplifyCurve’s horizontal input when calculating a correction for two-hand object control. A reading of 20 means a cached signed 20-degree sideways wrist-bend measurement, not 20 percent input; the curve and grip’s swing limit determine the resulting correction.

This angle is measured before ApplyArms’s later wrist rotation limit, so the cached measurement can differ from the final visible wrist pose. The cache is written before that later limit and the final hand position/rotation writes.

member.summary: Reports the right wrist’s signed sideways bend for wrist-dependent grip calculations.

remarks.para: This returns the value stored in _deviaHandRt. It is an angle in degrees, calculated by ApplyArms from the solved hand and forearm orientations. It does not recalculate the arm or report controller squeeze.

Grip.SolveHandleAmplify uses this wrist measurement from the virtual body rig as handleAmplifyCurve’s horizontal input when calculating a correction for two-hand object control. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig.sDisplaceDegreesToXzMult
member.summary: The built-in factor of 0.00485 used to limit sideways spine displacement from its permitted tilt.

remarks.para: LimitSpinePosition multiplies the permitted tilt angle in degrees by this factor, the spine segment’s length, and an available-motion factor. It limits the tracked offset’s local X/Z distance to that result. X/Z are the local frame of the spine offset passed to the routine, not necessarily the world’s horizontal axes.

The available-motion factor is limited to 0 through 1 and depends on how much of the permitted tilt and twist is already used. For example, a 30-degree tilt reference, 0.5-meter segment and factor 1 give a maximum local X/Z displacement of 30 × 0.00485 × 0.5 = 0.07275 meters. The constant alone is not a meter-per-degree distance: segment length also scales the result. It is compiled into the calculation, not a mutable per-rig setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig.sDisplaceDegreesToYMult
member.summary: The built-in factor of 0.62 used for the vertical correction after limiting a spine offset.

remarks.para: LimitSpinePosition calculates the correction as (r / length)² × 0.62 × length × (alignment + 1). Here r is the limited local X/Z distance in metres, length is the spine segment’s length in metres, and alignment is the dot product of that local displacement direction with the bend-reference direction. The result is a distance along the same local frame’s Y axis.

For example, r = 0.1 meters, length = 0.5 meters and alignment = 1 give a Y correction of 0.0248 meters, or 2.48 cm. Alignment −1 makes that correction zero. The factor is unitless; it is not a fixed 0.62-meter lift or a degree angle. It is a compiled constant rather than a mutable per-rig setting.

The bend-reference direction comes from LimitSpineRotation: reference up expressed in the target spine frame, using its normalized X/Z direction and near-zero fallback. Alignment is the unitless measure of how that direction and the local displacement direction line up: for unit directions, 1 means the same direction, 0 means perpendicular and −1 means opposite.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.Colliders
member.summary: The collision shapes exposed by this grippable's body.

remarks.para: A collider describes a shape used in collision tests. InteractableHost returns its MarrowBody collider array, also used by EnableColliders and DisableColliders. The hand code uses these shapes when managing collision exclusions during a grab.
The getter returns the configured array rather than searching the hierarchy for every collider on each call. A host body and its array must be configured.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.HasRigidbody
member.summary: Reports whether the host's MarrowBody is configured to have a Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object's motion in the physics simulation. InteractableHost checks that its MarrowBody exists and then returns that body's HasRigidbody flag.
This does not test whether the body is awake or its GameObject is active. Rb can still return null when this host is marked IsStatic, so check the returned Rigidbody before using it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.IsAttached
member.summary: Reports whether any grip registered with the host currently has an attached hand.

remarks.para: InteractableHost checks each registered Grip's hand list and returns true if one is nonempty. It does not simply read the host's HandCount value, so manually editing attachment bookkeeping is not a substitute for a complete grab or release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.IsFarHoverEnabled
member.summary: Reports whether the host allows its receivers to report distant hand targeting. Change it through or .

remarks.para: Far hover is targeting from a distance before the hand holds the object. HandReciever reads this host flag to report that far-hover availability. EnableFarHover sets it true; InteractableHost also provides DisableFarHover to clear it.
A true value is permission for targeting, not proof that a hand is currently hovering or that a force pull has started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.IsInteractionDisabled
member.summary: Reports the host-level flag that blocks hand receiver availability.

remarks.para: A hand receiver handles hover and grab actions. Its IsEnabled check requires this flag to be false as well as its own enabled state. DisableInteraction sets the flag and EnableInteraction clears it.

The flag does not describe collider enabled states or whether a hand is already holding the object. Changing it through the interaction methods does not itself release hands or toggle collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.IsPulling
member.summary: Reports whether one of the host's force-pull grips is currently pulling toward a hand.

remarks.para: InteractableHost checks its registered ForcePullGrip components for the PULLING state. Merely targeting the object from a distance, or already holding it, does not by itself make this value true. Reading the property does not start or cancel a pull.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.IsStatic
member.summary: Marks whether the host should be handled as fixed geometry by the interaction code.

remarks.para: In InteractableHost this is a stored flag. A true value makes Rb return null, prevents its optional player-body joint creation during AttachHand, and makes the grip release request quick hand-joint cleanup.
Setting the flag alone does not change a Rigidbody's movement constraints, make it kinematic or run a release. Configure the object's actual physics separately when it needs to stay immovable.

A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object’s movement and rotation in the physics simulation. Kinematic means movement is controlled by code instead of ordinary physics forces; this interaction flag does not enable that mode itself.
A joint is a simulated connection between two physics objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.Rb
member.summary: Returns the Rigidbody this host exposes for movable-object interaction, or null.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody represents an object's motion in the physics simulation. InteractableHost returns its body's Rigidbody only when IsStatic is false, a body reports HasRigidbody, and that body can supply the component.
A static host returns null even if its body reports HasRigidbody. Check the returned reference before reading or changing its physics properties.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable.VirtualController
member.summary: The shared controller that tracks the host's holding hands and their grips.

remarks.para: A hand/grip pair records which hand is holding which Grip. The grip attachment routine registers that pair with this controller, and release removes it. Multiple hands on the same host can therefore share its pair tracking.
InteractableHost returns its configured controller reference. This property is not the physical VR controller and does not itself apply a force or create a joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable.OnSlideGrabbed
member.summary: Notifies listeners when hand control of the slide begins, after its travel bookkeeping is initialized.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This Action holds no-argument listener routines; use += to add one and -= to remove it. Assigning with = replaces existing listeners rather than moving or grabbing the slide.

In the checked SlideVirtualController implementation, OnVirtualControllerStart calculates the slide direction in the grip-handle frame, resets the current travel distance and last movement values, then invokes this notification if assigned. It does not clear the pulled-endpoint latch in that start method.

Gun subscribes during Awake, Unity's initialization callback, to begin manual slide override and its configured firing restriction. The interface exposes notifications; it does not implement those gun actions itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable.OnSlidePulled
member.summary: Notifies listeners when the standard controller first reaches its full-pull endpoint.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. In SlideVirtualController, the solver stores the new travel distance and sends OnSlideUpdate first. If normalized travel reaches 1 and the pulled latch was false, it sets _slideIsPulled true before invoking this no-argument Action.

It does not repeatedly notify on every solve while the slide remains fully pulled. Returning all the way clears the latch after the return notification; ending the hand-control session also clears it.

Gun's subscribed routine uses this endpoint to play the manual pull sound when appropriate and handle release from a locked slide. Add listeners with += so that existing gun listeners remain installed; calling the Action yourself only sends a notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable.OnSlideReleased
member.summary: Notifies listeners when the hand-control session for the slide ends.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The checked SlideVirtualController.OnVirtualControllerEnd clears _slideIsPulled before invoking this no-argument Action, so its listeners observe that latch already false.

Releasing the hand is different from the slide physically reaching its returned position. This notification does not require normalized travel to be zero and does not also invoke OnSlideReturned in that end method.

Gun listens to release its manual animation override and clear its slide-grab firing restriction. Use += and -= for listener lifetime; assigning with = replaces the other listeners. The interface itself does not perform the mechanical return.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable.OnSlideReturned
member.summary: Notifies listeners when the standard controller reaches zero travel after having reached full pull.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. SlideVirtualController first stores the new distance and sends OnSlideUpdate. It invokes this no-argument Action only when normalized travel is at or below zero and _slideIsPulled is still true.

The return notification occurs before the controller clears _slideIsPulled. Its listeners therefore see the old true latch during the call. A partial pull that never set that latch does not produce this return notification merely by moving back to zero.
This is an endpoint notification during the solver, not the hand-release notification. Add listeners with += and remove them with -=; replacing the Action can remove existing subscribers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable.OnSlideUpdate
member.summary: Reports the standard controller's normalized slide travel so the gun can update its animation.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This Action<float> receives travel distance divided by pullDistance. In SlideVirtualController, travel is the calculated movement along the slide path, and pullDistance is the configured length representing full pull, measured in the same controller coordinate units. Their ratio is dimensionless: 0 is returned, 1 is fully pulled and 0.5 is halfway.

For an illustrative full travel of 0.05 length units and current travel 0.025 in the same frame, the argument is 0.5; it is not meters, speed or time. The standard solver clamps distance between zero and pullDistance before division, assuming a positive nonzero pullDistance.

The solver stores the distance before invoking this callback, then checks whether to send OnSlidePulled or OnSlideReturned and change their latch. Gun stores the reported value for its later animation update. It can report the same value on consecutive solves, and the interface itself does not promise a frame/update frequency.
Use += to add a listener alongside the gun's own routine and -= when it should stop listening. Assigning the delegate or invoking it does not physically move the slide.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.Cache
member.summary: Provides a shared GameObject-to-ImpactProperties lookup, creating the cache when first needed.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components. A collider is the shape Unity uses for collision tests.

Awake, Unity's initialization callback, adds this component with its GameObject as lookup key. OnDestroy removes that pair and clears _cache when it becomes empty. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action.

A Rigidbody is Unity's component that moves an object through physics. The Projectile consumer obtains ImpactProperties from the hit Rigidbody's GameObject, or the collider's GameObject for a static hit, through this cache. It avoids repeating that component lookup for every hit.

This is a lookup helper, not a guaranteed list of only currently enabled or spawned objects. The registration lifecycle follows initialization/destruction. Changing the static backing field can replace the shared lookup used by other callers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.SurfaceDataCard
member.summary: Selects the warehouse surface card used for resistance values and lazy impact-effect data loading. See .

remarks.para: The penetration coefficient is unitless: it has no physical units. On a successful passage through the hit surface, the projectile multiplies it by starting speed to calculate speed loss. Starting speed and that speed loss are in meters per second; this coefficient is not itself a speed.

The reference identifies a SurfaceDataCard asset by its warehouse data-card identity, the game’s asset-library lookup key. Its penetration coefficient and megapascal value are read directly by the resistance getters. The penetration coefficient controls how much projectile speed is lost during a successful passage; the megapascal value is hardness in MPa (newtons per square millimeter), which supplies force opposing stabbing. With normal positive spring settings and a nonnegative tip area, increasing hardness lowers the unclamped initial-depth target. The final depth is limited to zero through maxDepth, the tip’s configured maximum penetration depth in meters, so it can stay unchanged at either limit. Its separate SurfaceData asset supplies impact/decal spawn definitions, decal material entries and particle tint.

SurfaceDataCard and _surfaceDataCard expose the same reference. Setting the property only stores the new reference; it does not reset _isSetup, _isSurfaceDataLoaded or _cachedSurfaceData. Resistance getters can therefore read the new card while an already prepared visual response still uses the old cached effect data.

Setup tries this card first and falls back to legacy surfaceData if no usable effect asset results. Changing the reference is not an automatic reload or a command to apply its PhysicMaterial to colliders.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared lookup used to find ImpactProperties by GameObject. See .

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components.

Cache creates this ComponentCache if the field is null. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, registers this object/component pair; OnDestroy removes it and clears the static field once the lookup is empty. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action.

It serves hit lookups such as Projectile's surface lookup. Replacing or clearing it changes the cache shared by all instances and does not cause already initialized instances to run Awake again automatically. It is not an enabled-object list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties._cachedSurfaceData
member.summary: Stores the resolved effect-data asset used for particle effects and decal selection. See .

remarks.para: A decal is a mark on a surface, such as a bullet hole. Asset registration prepares each configured object template for later creation or reuse by the pool.

Setup fills it from the SurfaceDataCard asset when available, otherwise from legacy surfaceData. It writes this reference before marking _isSurfaceDataLoaded. The attack response then uses its spawn definitions, particle tint and bullet/blunt decal arrays.

The resistance getters read the current card/legacy reference directly, rather than reading this cache. Replacing SurfaceDataCard alone does not replace this effect-data reference or reset setup. Assigning this field alone also does not register its spawn assets or establish matching flags.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties._isSetup
member.summary: Records that the surface setup attempt has finished, so later attacks can skip repeating it.

remarks.para: When newly resolved data is usable, setup stores _cachedSurfaceData before setting _isSurfaceDataLoaded. If data is already marked loaded, it reuses that cache. It then awaits preparation of the impact-effect asset followed by the decal asset and sets _isSetup true last. Pool registration asks the reusable-object system to prepare each configured effect or decal object template for later spawning.

An attempt with neither usable card data nor legacy data also sets this true at the end. It therefore means the attempt finished, not that a valid surface was loaded. ReceiveAttackAsync skips setup when this flag is true.

Setting it true yourself can skip needed loading/registration. Clearing it permits a later setup attempt, but that attempt can still reuse a cache already marked loaded; it is not by itself a complete replacement-data reload. No readiness event is raised by the checked flag write.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties._isSurfaceDataLoaded
member.summary: Records whether setup resolved a usable effect-data object, including the legacy fallback.

remarks.para: A decal is a mark on a surface, such as a bullet hole. Pool registration prepares the configured effect and decal object templates for later spawning. Setup stores _cachedSurfaceData first and then writes this flag from that Unity object's validity. It can become true before that registration finishes and before _isSetup becomes true.

It is not specifically proof that the warehouse card loaded successfully: legacy surfaceData can also produce true. GetMaterialFromAttack returns an empty entry when false, and the attack response finishes without effects when false.
Assigning true does not load an asset or populate the cache. If the flag and _cachedSurfaceData disagree, later methods can fail when accessing the expected data.

On a successful passage through the hit surface, the projectile multiplies it by starting speed to calculate speed loss. Starting speed and that speed loss are in meters per second; this coefficient is not itself a speed.

The reference identifies a SurfaceDataCard asset by its warehouse data-card identity, the game’s asset-library lookup key. The penetration coefficient controls how much projectile speed is lost during a successful passage; the megapascal value is hardness in MPa (newtons per square millimeter), which supplies force opposing stabbing. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.decalType
member.summary: Chooses whether the surface response skips decals or requests a decal projected onto the attacked collider.

remarks.para: A decal is a surface mark, such as a bullet hole; a collider is the shape Unity tests for collisions.

None (-1) skips the decal step after the impact-effect object has been processed; it does not suppress that particle-effect request. Collider (0) requests bulletDecalSpawnable and, when a DecalProjector and hit collider are available, builds the selected decal on that collider.

A Rigidbody is Unity's component that moves an object through physics. For a collider with an attached Rigidbody, the spawn request supplies the Rigidbody transform as parent, making the decal follow that object's position and rotation. A static hit supplies no parent through this path. The checked response only tests for None, so other numeric values also enter the decal path, although Collider is the other defined enum value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.megaPascalModifier
member.summary: Multiplies the reported surface hardness used by stabbing calculations. See .

remarks.para: It is a dimensionless multiplier. MPa means megapascals, or newtons per square millimeter, the hardness units used here. GetMegaPascals chooses the current card's megaPascal value, the legacy value if the card cannot be resolved, or a base 100 MPa with neither; all three multiply by this field. An illustrative modifier 2 turns a base 50 MPa into 100 MPa.

In the checked stab setup, the resulting hardness multiplied by the tip area in square millimeters supplies an opposing force in newtons. With normal positive spring settings and a nonnegative tip area, increasing hardness lowers the unclamped initial-depth target. The final depth is limited to zero through maxDepth, the tip’s configured maximum penetration depth in meters, so it can stay unchanged at either limit. That value is cached in the new stab joint and later contributes to depth-dependent damping. The stab joint is a physics connection holding the blade to the struck object; damping resists their relative motion.

Changing it updates later hardness queries/new stab setup, rather than rewriting an existing joint's cached hardness. It does not change GetPenetrationResistance, which provides the separate projectile coefficient. This field is public but hidden in the Inspector in the inspected layout.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.surfaceData
member.summary: Provides the legacy surface asset used when the warehouse card cannot supply the needed data.

remarks.para: A decal is a mark on a surface, such as a bullet hole.

PenetrationResistance is a unitless coefficient: on successful projectile passage it multiplies the starting speed, in meters per second, to calculate speed loss in meters per second. megaPascal is hardness in MPa, newtons per square millimeter; higher hardness opposes stabbing. With normal positive spring settings and a nonnegative tip area, increasing hardness lowers the unclamped initial-depth target. The final depth is limited to zero through maxDepth, the tip’s configured maximum penetration depth in meters, so it can stay unchanged at either limit.
Setup copies it into _cachedSurfaceData if loading/resolving the card did not produce usable effect data. Its impact/decal spawn definitions, tint and decal arrays then provide the visual response.

The resistance getters also fall back to its PenetrationResistance and megaPascal values when the card cannot be resolved. Assigning it alone does not refresh an already prepared effect cache or rerun asset registration.

The field is marked obsolete in the inspected class; SurfaceDataCard is the warehouse reference used first. The two data sources have separate direct-number and cached-effect consumers, so changing one need not immediately change both behaviors.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.OnSignificantCollision
member.summary: Reports a collision that passes the first contact’s normal-velocity test, before the sound cooldown is checked.

remarks.para: Listeners receive the Collision, then a strength V in metres per second. With a nonzero collision impulse, V = impulse magnitude / _mass: impulse is momentum change in kilogram-metres per second, and _mass is this component’s cached mass in kilograms. For example, an impulse of 8 kg·m/s with cached mass 2 kg reports V = 4 m/s.

A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in physics. When impulse is zero, V comes from the relative approach velocity along the first contact’s normal, the direction perpendicular to that contact surface. If the other object has a Rigidbody, that velocity is multiplied by otherMass / (otherMass + _mass), a unitless mass share. otherMass is the other collision body’s current mass in kilograms; otherwise the unweighted normal velocity is used. The initial minVelocity test uses the normal velocity before this strength calculation.

The callback, a routine called to report an action, runs before updating either the component’s or manager’s last-strength/time values, and before clip selection, audio, controller vibration or blunt-attack delivery. Listeners therefore see the previous gate state; they can receive this report even when the later sound gate rejects the collision.

The ordinary Unity collision-entry path reaches this report only when the component is active and enabled and its cached Marrow entity is not hibernating. Hibernating is Marrow’s temporary sleeping/frozen physics state. A direct call to ImpactSound performs the velocity/report/gate sequence itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._altColliders
member.summary: Caches whether alternate impact-surface filtering was enabled during setup.

remarks.para: Initialize sets this to true when altImpactColliders has at least one entry. With the flag true, a collision compares the first contact’s collider on this object against that array, then can choose altImpact if a match has a nonempty clip set. A false flag skips the alternate search.

This stores the array’s empty/nonempty status, not the hit collider. Changing entries in an already enabled array affects later searches, because those searches read the array itself. Making an initially empty array nonempty does not update this flag automatically; setup must be refreshed or the cache updated explicitly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._host
member.summary: Caches the interactable object that supplies held hands and grabber information for impact effects.

remarks.para: Start looks up InteractableHost on this component’s same GameObject. After a collision sound request, the collision path finds each hand holding that host and sends controller hit vibration. JointBreakFx likewise sends vibration after requesting break audio.

The collision-generated blunt attack also takes its proxy, the object representing the last grabber for attack attribution, from this host. This is a cached setup reference; changing the object hierarchy does not itself repeat Start’s lookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._lastImpactImpulse
member.summary: Stores the last accepted local collision strength for the sound-delay comparison.

remarks.para: Despite its name, ordinary collision processing stores a speed V in metres per second, normally collision impulse magnitude divided by cached mass. During the local 0.24-second delay, a smaller strength is rejected while an equal or greater strength can pass. A passing local check overwrites this value before requesting playback.

Start initially stores 100,000,000 as a startup suppression value. DestructionEvent and JointBreakFx multiply the current stored value by 10 before requesting sound, to suppress smaller following collisions during their local 0.3-second delay. When a manager handles ordinary collision gating, that path updates the manager’s separate strength instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._mapImpact
member.summary: Holds the managed audio player that requests ordinary collision sounds at contact points.

remarks.para: The component constructor creates this player. After the collision passes its gate and chooses clips, it requests a random clip at the first contact’s world-space position, through the impact mixer. The managed player keeps track of its pooled audio player so repeated requests can move/update an existing managed playback source or request one from the pool.

Collision volume is clamp(V / velocityClipSplit, 0, 1), where V is the collision strength in metres per second, normally collision impulse magnitude divided by this component’s cached mass, with a normal-velocity fallback when impulse is zero. Normal velocity is relative speed perpendicular to the first contact surface, weighted by the other body’s mass share when present. velocityClipSplit is the soft/hard speed boundary in metres per second and the ratio is unitless. clamp limits volume to the range 0 through 1. The minimum-distance input is numerically sqrt(V / velocityClipSplit), used in metres by the 3D audio player; sqrt means square root. Minimum distance is the near-distance setting the 3D audio system uses when making a sound quieter as the listener gets farther away. Pitch starts from _pitchMod, a unitless base multiplier with 1 meaning normal pitch, varies randomly by ±0.25, and receives the audio helper’s game-time-scale adjustment. Destruction and joint-break requests use their own audio-helper calls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._marrowBody
member.summary: Caches the Marrow body whose entity can suppress automatic collision effects while hibernating.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in physics. Hibernating is Marrow’s temporary sleeping/frozen physics state. Initialize finds this body on the cached Rigidbody’s GameObject when a Rigidbody is present. In the ordinary OnCollisionEnter path, a present MarrowBody supplies its entity’s IsHibernating flag. If hibernating, the path skips ImpactSound, including the collision report, audio, vibration and blunt-attack attempt.

If this cached body is absent, that path has no Marrow hibernation check, although it still requires the component to be active and enabled. This check belongs to the Unity collision-entry wrapper; calling ImpactSound directly goes into its processing routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._mass
member.summary: Caches this object’s mass in kilograms for collision strength and blunt-damage calculations.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in physics. Initialize copies the same GameObject’s Rigidbody.mass, or stores 20 kilograms without a Rigidbody. With nonzero collision impulse, reported strength is V = impulse magnitude / _mass, giving metres per second. Impulse magnitude is the amount of momentum change, measured in kg·m/s. With zero impulse and another Rigidbody, the normal approach velocity is weighted by otherMass / (otherMass + _mass). otherMass is the other collision body’s current mass in kilograms; normal velocity is the relative speed perpendicular to the first contact surface.

The blunt-attack calculation also reads this cached mass. Changing Rigidbody.mass later does not itself refresh _mass; Initialize is the setup routine that copies it again. Editing this cache changes the later calculations without changing the Rigidbody’s physical mass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._minVelSquared
member.summary: Stores the setup-time square of the minimum normal impact velocity.

remarks.para: Initialize writes minVelocity × minVelocity, so its units are (metres per second) squared. For example, minVelocity = 0.5 m/s gives a cached value of 0.25 (m/s)².

In the complete audited ImpactSFX setup, startup, collision, local-gate, joint-break, destruction and pitch methods, and the ImpactSfxManager methods, this cache is not read. The collision threshold reads minVelocity directly. Editing _minVelSquared therefore does not change that audited threshold; this is a statement about these paths, not every possible caller in the game.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._nextImpactTime
member.summary: Stores the end of this component’s local collision-sound delay on the scaled physics clock.

remarks.para: Measured in Time.fixedTime seconds, the physics clock affected by game speed. A local collision check rejects an impact only if the clock is still earlier than this time AND its strength is smaller than _lastImpactImpulse. Equal or stronger impacts can pass before the time expires.

Start writes the current physics time plus 2 seconds. Accepted local collisions write current physics time plus 0.24 seconds; DestructionEvent and JointBreakFx write plus 0.3 seconds. These writes precede their audio requests. Ordinary collisions with a valid manager use its separate unscaled-time delay instead of this local field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._pitchMod
member.summary: Stores the current base pitch for collision and joint-break playback.

remarks.para: This is a unitless pitch multiplier: 1 is normal pitch before the random variation and game-speed factor. Initialize copies pitchMod here. SetPitchMultiplier can replace it with its size-related calculated value; assigning pitchMod alone later does not automatically refresh this cache.

Collision and joint-break audio varies this base randomly by ±0.25, then multiplies it by 0.75 × T + 0.25. T is the unitless game time scale, with 1 meaning normal speed. For a cached base of 1 at normal speed, the helper requests a pitch from 0.75 to 1.25. DestructionEvent separately starts from base pitch 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX._rb
member.summary: Caches the Rigidbody on this same GameObject for setup of impact processing.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody supplies the object’s physical mass and motion. Initialize finds this reference, copies its mass into _mass, and looks up MarrowBody on the Rigidbody’s object. Without a Rigidbody, the cached mass uses the 20-kilogram fallback.

The later impact strength calculation reads the saved _mass and the Collision’s impulse/relative velocity; it does not refresh the own-body mass just because Rigidbody.mass changes. The other object’s Rigidbody, read from the Collision, is a separate reference used by the zero-impulse weighting and blunt-attack condition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.altImpact
member.summary: Provides alternate sound clips for impacts on the special colliders.

remarks.para: After the velocity and sound-delay tests pass, a collision whose first contact’s thisCollider matches an entry in altImpactColliders can use this set. ThisCollider means the collider on this component’s side of the collision. The cached _altColliders switch must also be enabled, and this clip array must be nonempty.

A matching nonempty alternate set takes priority over the ordinary soft/hard choice, regardless of the velocity split. Otherwise the path falls back to impactSoft or impactHard. A random clip plays at the first contact’s world point with the same strength-based volume and cached pitch as ordinary impacts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.altImpactColliders
member.summary: Lists colliders on this object that can select the sounds.

remarks.para: The collision path compares the first contact’s thisCollider, the collider on this object’s side, with these references. It does not select by the other object’s material or by every contact in the collision. A matching entry selects altImpact only when that sound set is nonempty; otherwise ordinary soft/hard selection remains available.

Initialize caches whether this list has any entries in _altColliders. Editing references while that switch is true changes later comparisons, but making an initially empty list nonempty does not update the cached switch automatically. Keep an existing array, which can be empty, because setup reads its length.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.bluntAttack
member.summary: Enables collision processing to send a blunt attack after a qualifying impact sound request.

remarks.para: The ordinary collision path must first pass the contact-normal minVelocity test and its local or shared sound gate. After choosing/requesting sound and sending held-hand vibration, it checks this flag. A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in physics. A true flag still requires the other object to have a Rigidbody, its collision GameObject to have ImpactProperties, and the calculated excess strength to be nonnegative. A valid cached host supplies the last grabber’s proxy for attribution.

The damage is D = 0.2 × m × (V − 10 × u). Here m is _mass in kilograms, V is the derived collision strength in metres per second, normally collision impulse magnitude divided by cached mass, and u is minVelocity, the normal-speed threshold in metres per second. The fixed 10 creates the higher speed margin for attacks; the fixed 0.2 converts the resulting quantity to game damage. Because this attack requires another Rigidbody, its zero-impulse V is d × otherMass / (otherMass + m), where d is signed relative approach speed perpendicular to the first contact surface, in metres per second, and otherMass is the other body’s current mass in kilograms. This path does not read bluntDamageMult. If V − 10 × u is negative, it sends no attack.

For an illustrative cached mass of 2 kg, minVelocity = 0.5 m/s and V = 8 m/s, damage is 0.2 × 2 × (8 − 5) = 1.2. This example assumes the other gates pass. The delivered payload is a Blunt attack with its origin at the first world contact point, the contact normal and an opposite-normal direction; it is sent to attack receivers on the collision GameObject. ReceiveAttack on this component is a separate empty base handler.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.bluntDamageMult
member.summary: Exposes a stored multiplier that the audited collision-damage path does not apply.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes this value to 1. In the complete audited ImpactSFX and ImpactSfxManager methods, the collision-generated blunt attack instead uses the fixed coefficient 0.2 times its calculated excess momentum-like strength. It does not read bluntDamageMult there, so changing this field does not scale damage in that path.

This scope covers the saved class and manager methods, including collision processing; it is not a claim about every game script or derived class. bluntAttack controls whether that outgoing collision attack is attempted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.destruction
member.summary: Provides the preferred clip set when DestructionEvent requests this object’s break sound.

remarks.para: DestructionEvent chooses a random clip here if this array is nonempty. If empty, it tries impactHard, then impactSoft. Playback is at this component’s world position through the hard-interaction mixer. Assignment of these clips is sound configuration; DestructionEvent’s caller performs the actual object destruction.

The routine also updates local collision-sound suppression before requesting audio. input is the unitless loudness argument supplied to DestructionEvent. Its volume input produces playback volume 0.3 + 0.7 × input and minimum distance max(input, 1) metres, while pitch starts from 1 with random variation and game-speed adjustment. Minimum distance is the near-distance setting used by 3D audio when making sound quieter as the listener gets farther away. Changing pitchMod does not alter that separate destruction base pitch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.impactHard
member.summary: Provides ordinary collision clips at or above the soft/hard speed split, plus fallback break clips.

remarks.para: After a collision passes its velocity and sound-delay tests, and no eligible alternate clip set was selected, V >= velocityClipSplit chooses this set if it is nonempty. V is the derived speed in metres per second, normally impulse magnitude divided by cached mass; velocityClipSplit is also in metres per second. Equality selects hard clips. An empty hard set falls back to impactSoft.

A random chosen clip plays at the first contact’s world position. Volume is clamp(V / velocityClipSplit, 0, 1); the unitless ratio also supplies sqrt(ratio) as the minimum-distance value in metres. clamp limits volume to the range 0 through 1, and sqrt means square root. Minimum distance is the near-distance setting the 3D audio system uses when making a sound quieter as the listener gets farther away. OnJointBreak and DestructionEvent additionally use this set when their preferred break/destruction sets are empty, before trying impactSoft.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.impactSoft
member.summary: Provides ordinary low-strength collision clips and the final fallback for hard or break sounds.

remarks.para: After velocity and sound-delay tests pass, and no eligible alternate set was selected, V < velocityClipSplit chooses this set. V is the derived collision speed in metres per second, normally impulse magnitude divided by cached mass, and velocityClipSplit is the soft/hard boundary in metres per second.

It is also used when impactHard is empty, or when the preferred joint-break/destruction set and hard fallback are empty. A nonempty set supplies a random clip. An empty selected set makes the audio helper return without sound; in ordinary collision processing, later vibration/attack checks can still continue. A missing array reference is not treated as the same thing as an existing empty array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.jointBreak
member.summary: Provides the preferred clips for Unity’s joint-break notification.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation. OnJointBreak chooses this set if it is nonempty, otherwise impactHard and then impactSoft. The helper requests a random clip at this component’s world position with jointBreakVolume and cached _pitchMod, through the hard-interaction mixer. jointBreakVolume is unitless playback volume; _pitchMod is the unitless base pitch multiplier, with 1 meaning normal pitch. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, or Initialize copies that pitch value from pitchMod; SetPitchMultiplier can replace the cached value afterwards.

With a clip set, the helper raises local collision-sound suppression before requesting audio and then sends hit vibration to held hands. The breakForce argument is ignored by this implementation. An existing but empty final fallback results in no sound or vibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.jointBreakVolume
member.summary: Sets the unitless playback volume and near-distance setting for joint-break audio.

remarks.para: JointBreakFx sends this value directly as sound volume. The same number also produces a minimum distance of max(jointBreakVolume, 1) metres for the 3D audio player. Minimum distance is the near-distance setting the 3D audio system uses when making a sound quieter as the listener gets farther away, separate from the volume amount. For example, 0.5 requests volume 0.5 and minimum distance 1 metre; 2 requests volume 2 and minimum distance 2 metres.

The constructor initializes it to 1; serialized component settings may replace that initial value. The native helper does not clamp this field before passing volume to the audio system. It does not change the force needed to break a joint or scale the hand-vibration call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.manager
member.summary: Selects an to share an impact-sound gate across registered ImpactSFX components.

remarks.para: ImpactSfxManager.Start assigns itself to the components in its impactSfxes array. With a valid manager, ordinary collision processing compares against that manager’s last accepted strength and next time. Thus one registered piece’s hit can suppress a smaller hit from another piece during the shared 0.24-second window.

The shared clock uses unscaled seconds, independent of game time scale. Without a manager, this component uses its own gate on Time.fixedTime, the scaled physics clock. Both rules reject only when still inside the window AND the new speed-like strength is smaller than the previous one; an equal or greater value can pass immediately.

OnSignificantCollision fires before this gate, so sharing the manager does not suppress that earlier report after the velocity test. DestructionEvent and JointBreakFx write the component’s local delay values separately; those local writes do not become the manager’s shared delay.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.minVelocity
member.summary: Sets the minimum relative approach speed along the first contact’s normal for collision effects.

remarks.para: Measured in metres per second. ImpactSound takes the Collision’s relative velocity component along the first contact’s normal, the direction perpendicular to that surface. A value below minVelocity returns before OnSignificantCollision, sound gating, audio, held-hand vibration or blunt-attack processing. At equality the collision passes this initial test.

This signed normal-speed test occurs before calculating the reported strength from collision impulse and cached mass. A mostly sideways sliding motion can therefore have a large total speed but fail the normal-speed test. For an illustrative setting of 0.5 m/s, normal approach 0.3 m/s fails, while 0.5 m/s reaches the next stages.

The blunt-attack formula also uses 10 × minVelocity as its higher strength margin. The constructor’s initial minVelocity is 0.5 m/s; serialized settings may replace it. Initialize saves its square in _minVelSquared, but the audited collision path reads the live minVelocity directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.pitchMod
member.summary: Supplies the setup-time base pitch for ordinary collision and joint-break sounds.

remarks.para: A unitless pitch multiplier: 1 is normal pitch, values above 1 raise pitch and values below 1 lower it before playback’s random variation and game-speed factor. The constructor initializes this input to 1; serialized settings may replace it.

Initialize copies pitchMod into the internal _pitchMod cache. Later assigning pitchMod alone does not update the saved playback pitch. SetPitchMultiplier recalculates that cache using pitchMod for inputs other than exactly 3; its exact-3 special case stores 1. Repeating Initialize resets the cache to this public input.

The collision and joint-break audio helpers randomly vary the cached pitch by ±0.25 and then multiply it by 0.75 × T + 0.25, where T is the unitless game time scale, 1 meaning normal speed. DestructionEvent has its own base pitch of 1. The audited blunt-damage calculation does not use pitchMod.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX.velocityClipSplit
member.summary: Sets the speed boundary between ordinary soft and hard impact clips and scales collision loudness.

remarks.para: Measured in metres per second. After the initial normal-speed and sound-delay tests, V < velocityClipSplit selects impactSoft; V >= velocityClipSplit selects a nonempty impactHard, otherwise impactSoft. V is the derived strength, normally impulse magnitude divided by cached mass, not necessarily the object’s total travel speed. A matching nonempty alternate set takes priority over this choice.

The unitless ratio R = V / velocityClipSplit also sets playback volume clamp(R, 0, 1), and supplies sqrt(R) as the numeric minimum-distance input in metres for the 3D audio player. clamp limits volume to the range 0 through 1; sqrt means square root. Minimum distance is the near-distance setting the 3D audio system uses when making a sound quieter as the listener gets farther away. For an illustrative split of 8 m/s, V = 2 m/s gives soft selection, volume 0.25 and minimum distance 0.5 metres. V = 8 m/s gives hard selection if available, volume 1 and minimum distance 1 metre.

The constructor initializes the split to 8 m/s; serialized settings may replace it. The native path divides by the configured split without a runtime input clamp. This setting does not replace the earlier minVelocity test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController.Grip
member.summary: Reports the analog grip-squeeze reading from the bound input action.

remarks.para: The normal scale is unitless: 0 means no squeeze and 1 means full squeeze; 0.5 represents half of the input range, not half a newton. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController.GripForce
member.summary: Reports the grip-force value supplied by the bound input action.

remarks.para: ControllerActionMap copies this float directly; it does not convert it into newtons or kilograms or enforce a range. The input binding and device determine the scale. This reading is separate from Grip, the ordinary grip-squeeze amount.

For Index controllers, OpenController, the player's input handler, combines this reading with finger and trigger input when calculating grabbing strength. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController.GripVelocity
member.summary: Stores a grip-change value, but the inspected controller action map does not calculate it.

remarks.para: The complete checked XRController and ControllerActionMap methods expose storage for this value without calculating a change in Grip or assigning time units to it. Do not rely on it as grip change per second on that path. No functional range or physical unit was established.

OpenController, the player's input handler, calculates its own separate grab-change rate from its newly solved grab value minus the previous value, divided by unscaled frame time in seconds. That calculation does not populate this property.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController.IndexFinger
member.summary: Reports ControllerActionMap's cached estimate of index-finger curl.

remarks.para: ControllerActionMap updates this cached estimate after an input update. It is a unitless curl amount: 0 means open and 1 means curled, not an angle in degrees. A later update replaces a value you write.

The calculation adds Trigger, the analog trigger-pull reading, to a smoothed touch contribution, then limits the sum to 0 through 1. The touch contribution moves toward 0.3 while TriggerTouched is true and toward 0 otherwise, by at most 10 × unscaledDeltaTime per update. unscaledDeltaTime is the previous frame's duration in seconds, unaffected by slow motion. For example, a trigger reading of 0.5 and a settled touch contribution of 0.3 give curl 0.8.

OpenController, the player's input handler, calculates separate finger values from controller input and, where available, hand-tracking data. Its inspected finger-processing methods do not read these five XRController curl caches, so writing this property alone does not change those separate values on that path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController.Joystick2DAxis

remarks.para: The normal unitless control scale has (0, 0) at the center and each component between -1 and 1. remarks.para: XRController starts with Undefined, meaning no recognized controller type yet. ControllerActionMap can update the type when it identifies an input device. OpenController, the player's input handler, uses this selection to remap Vive face-button input and to choose grip and finger calculations for Oculus Touch, Index, Vive Wands and Windows MR. Changing this stored selection changes those code paths, not the physical controller.

The enum also includes OculusTouchPro. The inspected ControllerActionMap device-identification path selects Undefined, Oculus Touch, Index, Vive Wands or Windows MR; it does not select OculusTouchPro. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.AngularVelocity
member.summary: Stores how quickly the device is rotating, as a vector supplied by the input provider.

remarks.para: For standard OpenXR tracking input, this is radians per second. The vector points along the rotation axis expressed in tracking-origin coordinates, and its length gives the rotation speed. The tracking origin is the reference point and axes chosen by the VR runtime. A length of about 3.1416 radians per second corresponds to 180 degrees per second.

ControllerActionMap copies the bound action's vector directly, without converting it to degrees or calculating a difference between Rotation values. The reading is cached; it is not a fresh hardware query or a command to spin the controller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.Characteristics

OnFrameStart uses these flags only when _xrDevice is invalid. Changing them while the existing handle is valid does not immediately replace that device.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.IsConnected
member.summary: Reports the stored connection flag in the base implementation; subclasses can perform a different connection check.

remarks.para: XRDevice's base getter simply returns its cached true/false value. XRController and XRHMD instead check whether Unity considers _xrDevice valid. Connection and IsTracking are separate: a recognized device handle does not guarantee usable position and rotation tracking.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.IsTracking
member.summary: Reports whether the input provider has marked this device as tracked.

remarks.para: The base implementation returns a cached true/false value. ControllerActionMap copies its tracked input action into this flag; reading it does not poll tracking hardware. This is separate from having a valid device handle, and false does not clear stored Position or Rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.Position
member.summary: Stores the current device position that readers can use to place the headset or controller.

remarks.para: The normal XR pose uses meters in tracking-origin coordinates, relative to the reference point and axes chosen by the VR runtime. For example, X = 0.20 means 20 cm along that tracking frame's positive X axis. It is not automatically a world-space point in the game.

The getter returns a cached value. ControllerActionMap.Refresh replaces it from the input pose, using its configured pointer-to-palm offset when the direct palm-pose feature is unavailable. Writing this value does not move the physical device; a later pose update can replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.Rotation
member.summary: Stores the current device orientation as a quaternion in the tracking frame.

remarks.para: A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Its components are unitless and are not separate X, Y and Z angles in degrees. On the normal XR-input path, the orientation is relative to the VR runtime's tracking-origin axes, rather than automatically to the game world.

The getter returns a cached value. ControllerActionMap.Refresh replaces it from the palm pose, or from the pointer pose combined with the configured orientation offset. Writing it changes the stored orientation until another update replaces it; it does not rotate the physical device.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.UpdateTime
member.summary: Stores the scaled game-time timestamp used as the newer endpoint when blending device poses.

remarks.para: OnFrameStart sets it from Unity's timeAsDouble, in seconds since the game started. Scaled means that the game's time-speed setting affects the clock; this is not a date or wall-clock timestamp. For example, 12.5 means 12.5 seconds on that game clock.

The timestamp advances at frame start even when the device handle is invalid and no new pose was received. GetPoseAtFixedTime uses it together with _lastUpdateTime; changing this value changes the pose-blending interval, not when the tracking hardware actually sampled a pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice.Velocity
member.summary: Stores the linear motion reading supplied by the input provider.

remarks.para: For standard XR device input, the vector is meters per second in the tracking-origin frame: the reference point and axes chosen by the VR runtime. For example, (1, 0, 0) is movement at 1 meter per second along that frame's positive X direction. It is not automatically the player's total world-space movement.
ControllerActionMap copies the bound action's three-number vector directly. XRDevice does not calculate this value by subtracting positions, and reading it does not obtain a new sensor sample.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice._lastPosition
member.summary: Stores the position saved by Refresh as the starting point for time-based pose blending.

remarks.para: This is a copy of Position at the last call to the base Refresh implementation, not necessarily the previous input sample or previous rendered frame. It has the same units and coordinate frame as Position: on the normal XR path, meters in tracking-origin coordinates, the VR runtime's reference point and axes. The next Refresh replaces it.

When UpdateTime is later than _lastUpdateTime, GetPoseAtFixedTime blends from this position to Position. At the older timestamp it returns this position; halfway between the timestamps it returns the midpoint. For example, saved X = 0 and current X = 0.20 give X = 0.10 halfway through that interval. Requested times outside the interval can extend beyond these endpoints.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice._lastRotation
member.summary: Stores the orientation saved by Refresh as the starting point for time-based pose blending.

remarks.para: This is a copy of Rotation at the last call to the base Refresh implementation. A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation; its components are unitless, not angles in degrees. On the normal XR path it uses the VR runtime's tracking-origin axes. The next Refresh replaces it.

When UpdateTime is later than _lastUpdateTime, GetPoseAtFixedTime blends from this orientation to Rotation using Quaternion.LerpUnclamped. That means the blend amount is not restricted to the interval between the saved and current orientations. If the timestamp interval is zero or negative, the method returns the current pose instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice._lastUpdateTime
member.summary: Stores the frame-start timestamp that becomes the older endpoint for time-based pose blending.

remarks.para: OnFrameStart copies the old UpdateTime here before setting UpdateTime to the new scaled game time. Both timestamps use seconds since game start, affected by the game's time-speed setting. This is frame-start history, not a guaranteed tracking-sensor sample time.

GetPoseAtFixedTime uses blend amount = (requestedTime - oldTime) / (newTime - oldTime), where requestedTime is its requested game-clock time in seconds, oldTime is this saved timestamp, and newTime is UpdateTime in the same units. A requested time halfway between the endpoints gives 0.5. The amount is not clamped; when newTime is not later than oldTime, the method returns the current pose instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice._xrDevice
member.summary: Holds the Unity XR device handle selected for validity checks and device-specific operations.

remarks.para: A handle is the value Unity uses to identify a particular device. OnFrameStart keeps it while Unity considers it valid; if invalid, it searches using Characteristics and takes the first matching result. An empty search does not supply a replacement. XRController and XRHMD use this handle for their IsConnected check.
Selecting a handle does not itself fill Position, Rotation, button values or tracking status. Those readings are updated separately by the input handlers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice._xrDevices
member.summary: Stores the temporary results of searching Unity for devices matching Characteristics.

remarks.para: OnFrameStart passes this list to Unity's device search only when the selected _xrDevice handle is invalid. If there are results, it takes the first one as the selected handle. This is a search-results buffer, not a list that is kept current while the selected handle remains valid.
Adding or removing a list entry alone does not select a different active device. The next device search can replace the list contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD.IsConnected
member.summary: Reports whether Unity considers this headset's XR device handle valid.

remarks.para: This queries the selected device handle. It does not prove the headset is currently tracking its position and rotation, and it does not test whether someone is wearing it. Tracking and IsUserPresent are separate readings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD.IsUserPresent
member.summary: Reports headset presence, treating an unavailable presence reading on a valid device as present.

remarks.para: An invalid device returns false. For a valid device, a successful presence-feature read returns the reported true/false value; a failed read returns true. For example, a connected headset that cannot provide this feature is treated as present. A true result therefore does not prove a person is wearing the headset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD.LeftGazeConfidence
member.summary: Stores an optional left-eye gaze-confidence value; the inspected headset input methods do not populate it.

remarks.para: The complete inspected XRHMD and HmdActionMap methods expose storage for this float without producing a live confidence reading or using it for a gameplay decision. The getter and setter do not limit its range. A working 0-to-1 interpretation was not established in those methods; the code supplying the value must define its meaning. This finding does not cover every external game or mod caller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD.LeftGazePosition
member.summary: Stores an optional left-eye gaze position; the inspected headset input methods do not populate live gaze positions.

remarks.para: The complete inspected XRHMD and HmdActionMap methods only initialize, read or write this storage. No producer or consumer in those methods establishes its units, coordinate frame, or whether it is an eye location or a point being looked at. The original world-space interpretation was not verified.

The getter returns the stored three-number vector without a coordinate conversion or sensor query. Writing it changes storage rather than the headset's actual eye tracking. The meaning of a supplied value depends on its writer; this finding does not cover every external game or mod caller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD.LeftGazeRotation
member.summary: Stores an optional left-eye gaze orientation; the inspected headset input methods do not populate live gaze orientations.

remarks.para: A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation; its components are unitless, not separate angles in degrees. The getter and setter copy the stored quaternion directly, without querying an eye tracker or changing the headset's physical gaze.

The complete inspected XRHMD and HmdActionMap methods initialize this storage but do not supply live eye-gaze updates or use it for gameplay. They do not establish which coordinate frame a supplied orientation belongs to, so it should not be assumed to use world axes. This finding does not cover every external game or mod caller.

remarks.para: A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation; its components are unitless, not separate angles in degrees. The getter and setter copy the stored quaternion directly, without querying an eye tracker or changing the headset's physical gaze.

The complete inspected XRHMD and HmdActionMap methods initialize this storage but do not supply live eye-gaze updates or use it for gameplay. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand.IndexCurl
member.summary: Reports a normalized estimate of index-finger bend derived from tracked bone orientations.

remarks.para: HandActionMap calculates this cached, unitless amount from three local bone orientations after an input update. The calculated scale runs from 0 for low bend to 1 for high bend. Reading the property does not obtain a fresh tracking sample, and another hand-processing update replaces a value you write.

For the proximal, intermediate and distal bones: the finger's base, middle and outer segments, it compares the direction each bone calls up with its parent's up direction. It averages those three alignment scores, then converts that average to one bend angle A in radians. An alignment score is 1 for the same direction, 0 for a right angle and -1 for opposite directions. This is an angle calculated from average alignment, not the arithmetic average of three joint angles.

The calculation is curl = clamp((A - 0.2) / 1.4, 0, 1). A is the bend angle above in radians; 0.2 radians is the zero-curl endpoint and 1.4 radians is the interval from zero to full curl. clamp means limiting the result to 0 through 1. For example, A = 0.9 radians gives curl 0.5. Radians are angle units; about 3.1416 radians equals 180 degrees.
The property setter itself does not enforce this range. Failed or missing bone input can leave cached data, so the value alone is not proof of fresh tracking.

When OpenController, the player's input handler, selects its hand-tracking path, it reads this curl as part of the player's finger and grab calculations. Its later processing can change the final value; this property is an input to that path rather than a direct command for the visible finger angle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand.Positions
member.summary: Stores hand-bone positions relative to their parent bones on the HandActionMap path.

remarks.para: HandActionMap creates 26 entries, indexed by HandBone. Entries 1 through 25 are rebuilt from tracked bone positions after hand processing. Each is a displacement in meters from the parent bone, expressed in the parent's corrected orientation. For example, (0, 0.03, 0) means 3 cm along that parent frame's positive Y direction, not a world-space point.

A parent bone is the preceding segment in the hand's skeleton. For finger metacarpals, the parent here is the hand root; later segments use the preceding segment of that finger. Carpals uses the root, and ThumbMetacarpal uses Carpals.

The array's Root entry is not filled by the inspected HandActionMap processing; the root's tracked pose is written into the inherited XRDevice Position and Rotation instead. The getter returns the stored array reference, not a copy. Editing an entry changes this cache, but later processing can overwrite it.

XRHand's base constructor does not allocate these arrays; HandActionMap does. GetHandBone reads the supplied hand's matching position and rotation entries, so both arrays must exist and contain the requested index. Failed or missing bone input can leave old or initial values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand.Radii
member.summary: Stores optional per-bone radius values, but the inspected HandActionMap does not populate them.

remarks.para: HandActionMap allocates 26 float entries indexed by HandBone. The complete inspected XRHand and HandActionMap methods do not fill these entries from tracking or use them to size bones or collisions. No working units or physical-radius effect was established in those methods. This finding does not cover every other provider or mod.

The getter returns the stored array reference without copying it. XRHand's base constructor does not allocate the array; the 26-entry allocation belongs to HandActionMap. GetHandBone reads position and rotation arrays and does not read Radii.
