member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand.Rotations
member.summary: Stores hand-bone orientations relative to their parent bones on the HandActionMap path.

remarks.para: HandActionMap creates 26 entries, indexed by HandBone, and fills entries 1 through 25 during hand processing. A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of orientation; its components are unitless and are not separate angles in degrees. These orientations are relative to the corrected parent-bone frame rather than the game world.

A parent bone is the preceding segment in the hand's skeleton. For finger metacarpals, the parent here is the hand root; later segments use the preceding segment of that finger. Carpals uses the root, and ThumbMetacarpal uses Carpals.

The array's Root entry is not filled by the inspected HandActionMap processing; root orientation is written into inherited XRDevice.Rotation instead. HandActionMap also reads these local rotations when calculating finger curl. The getter returns the array reference, so entries are shared with the cache; later processing can replace edited values.

XRHand's base constructor does not allocate the array. HandActionMap allocates it before receiving tracking data, so an allocated array alone does not guarantee valid orientations. GetHandBone also needs the matching Positions entry, and failed bone input can leave old or initial values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand.ThumbCurl
member.summary: Reports a normalized estimate of thumb-finger bend derived from tracked bone orientations.

remarks.para: HandActionMap calculates this cached, unitless amount from three local bone orientations after an input update. The calculated scale runs from 0 for low bend to 1 for high bend. Reading the property does not obtain a fresh tracking sample, and another hand-processing update replaces a value you write.

For the thumb metacarpal, proximal and distal bones: the thumb's base, middle and outer segments, it compares the direction each bone calls up with its parent's up direction. It averages those three alignment scores, then converts that average to one bend angle A in radians. An alignment score is 1 for the same direction, 0 for a right angle and -1 for opposite directions. This is an angle calculated from average alignment, not the arithmetic average of three joint angles.

The calculation is curl = clamp((A - 0.77) / 0.13, 0, 1). A is the bend angle above in radians; 0.77 radians is the zero-curl endpoint and 0.13 radians is the interval from zero to full curl. clamp means limiting the result to 0 through 1. For example, A = 0.835 radians gives curl 0.5. Radians are angle units; about 3.1416 radians equals 180 degrees.
The property setter itself does not enforce this range. Failed or missing bone input can leave cached data, so the value alone is not proof of fresh tracking.

The inspected OpenController hand-tracking path calculates its thumb input from controller touch readings instead of reading this ThumbCurl cache. No direct thumb-animation effect from writing this property was verified in that path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand._isFullUpdate
member.summary: Stores the full-update request flag, which has no verified update-control effect in the inspected HandActionMap.

remarks.para: In the complete inspected XRHand and HandActionMap methods, the flag is stored but HandActionMap never reads it before updating bone arrays and finger curl. Changing it therefore does not stop or start those updates on that provider. This finding does not cover every other provider or mod.
XRHand initializes it to true; StartFullUpdate writes true and StopFullUpdate writes false. The flag records a request, not proof that an update actually ran or that hand tracking is available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Body
member.summary: The MarrowBody on this host's own GameObject, which supplies its physics-body and collider information.

remarks.para: On first access, or if the stored component has been destroyed, it asks the shared MarrowBody lookup cache for that GameObject and stores the result. This is not a parent-or-child search. It can be null if no matching body is available. A Rigidbody, the Unity component for simulated mass and motion, is obtained separately through Rb.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Cache
member.summary: Shared lookup table for finding an InteractableHost by its GameObject.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, adds each host; OnDestroy removes it. Reading Cache creates an empty table if one does not exist yet. The table records registered components, so an empty table does not prove no uninitialized host exists in a scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Colliders
member.summary: The host uses the colliders listed by its MarrowBody; EnableColliders and DisableColliders toggle those shapes.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape the physics system detects. This returns the body's array directly rather than collecting every descendant collider. The body must exist; this getter does not provide an empty-array fallback for a missing body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.HasRigidbody
member.summary: Whether a MarrowBody exists for this host and its HasRigidbody flag is true.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody supplies simulated mass and motion. This reads the body's recorded flag; it does not inspect Rigidbody.isKinematic or the host's IsStatic flag. It can therefore be true while Rb returns null, especially when IsStatic has been set to true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.IsAttached
member.summary: Whether any grip recorded for this host currently has a hand in that grip's attachment list.

remarks.para: This checks the grips, rather than the host's _hands list read by HandCount. Normally the grab process updates both, but directly changing one list can make IsAttached and HandCount disagree.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.IsFarHoverEnabled
member.summary: Permission for this host to be selected by the hand's distant-target search.

remarks.para: Distant hovering is aiming at an object beyond direct grabbing range, as a first step toward force pulling. EnableFarHover and DisableFarHover change this flag. A true value still requires an enabled receiver and the search's other grip, direction and visibility checks. It is permission, not a report that a hand is currently aiming at or pulling the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.IsInteractionDisabled
member.summary: When true, makes this host's hand receivers fail their normal enabled check and keeps them out of hand targeting.

remarks.para: DisableInteraction sets it true; EnableInteraction sets it false. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, also clears it during setup. It does not switch off colliders, release existing grips or report whether the GameObject is active. An individual receiver can still be disabled when this flag is false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.IsPulling
member.summary: Whether any force-pull grip recorded for this host has its state set to PULLING.

remarks.para: This reads the grip's state flag. It does not measure object velocity or prove that the object has reached a hand or completed a grab. With no recorded force-pull grips it returns false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.IsStatic
member.summary: Tells interaction code to treat this host as a stationary target instead of supplying a movable Rigidbody.

remarks.para: Start, Unity's startup callback, sets this to the opposite of HasRigidbody. Reset in the editor instead copies the GameObject's Static setting. Assigning it later only changes this flag: it does not freeze the Rigidbody, the component for simulated mass and motion.

While true, Rb returns null and AttachHand skips the optional player-body collision-ignore joints. Releasing grips also uses the quick path. Set it to match the intended interaction setup rather than treating it as a direct physics freeze command.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.LastGrabbedProxy
member.summary: The player-or-entity reference kept as attribution for the object's latest registered grab.

remarks.para: SetProxy stores the TriggerRefProxy from the supplied GameObject and stops any earlier sleep-check coroutine, a sequence that can pause across frames. RemoveProxy can retain this reference after release until the Rigidbody sleeps, meaning the simulation stops actively updating a settled object.

This is not proof that the object is still held. On an object whose own activeSelf flag is false, RemoveProxy clears it immediately; on an active host with no reported Rigidbody, the sleep check does not clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.Rb
member.summary: The Rigidbody this host exposes for moving-object interaction, or null when it is treated as static or no body is reported.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object simulated mass and motion. This only returns the MarrowBody's stored Rigidbody when IsStatic is false and the body reports HasRigidbody. Setting IsStatic true hides the body through this property without removing or freezing the actual Rigidbody.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.VirtualController
member.summary: For a movable host, combines its holding hands and grips to calculate a target pose for object control.

remarks.para: A target pose is the position and rotation the game wants the object to reach; the physical object can lag behind. The controller records hand-and-grip pairs as grips attach and removes them as grips detach. The host creates a controller during construction, and ClearAttachedHandsForDespawn clears its pair list before reuse.

Grips use this host controller when IsStatic is false and HasRigidbody is true. Static or bodyless hosts use the player rig's controller instead. Changing this reference does not transfer the previous controller's recorded pairs to a replacement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._chestJoint
member.summary: Extra physics connection that lets the held object overlap the player's chest without collision.

remarks.para: A joint connects two simulated bodies. AttachHand creates this connection when ignoreBodyOnGrab is true, IsStatic is false and the pelvis connection is missing. It connects that player body part to the host's exposed Rigidbody and leaves every movement and rotation direction free.

The final DetachHand schedules removal and clears the stored reference. DestroyJoints removes the full set immediately only when HasRigidbody is true and the pelvis connection exists. This is separate from the hand-to-grip joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._fpGrips
member.summary: The setup list checked for distant-pull state and returned by GetForcePullGrip.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, collects ForcePullGrip components from this object and descendants, stopping before any child with its own InteractableHost. GetForcePullGrip returns the first entry; IsPulling checks whether any entry reports PULLING. Adding a component later does not automatically append it to this list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._grips
member.summary: The setup list of places the hands can hold on this host, checked for attachment and released by ForceDetach.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, collects Grip components from this object and descendants, stopping before any child with its own InteractableHost. GetGrip returns the first entry, IsAttached checks their recorded hands, and ForceDetach asks each grip to release. It is not rebuilt automatically when a grip is added later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._hands
member.summary: Host attachment records that determine HandCount and GetHand results.

remarks.para: AttachHand appends to this list before notifying listeners. DetachHand removes one matching entry before its notification and cleans up the optional body joints when the list becomes empty. Adding the same hand twice creates duplicate records.
IsAttached instead checks the grip lists, so directly editing this list does not by itself make or break a physical grab. ClearAttachedHandsForDespawn clears it without detach notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._headJoint
member.summary: Extra physics connection that lets the held object overlap the player's head without collision.

remarks.para: A joint connects two simulated bodies. AttachHand creates this connection when ignoreBodyOnGrab is true, IsStatic is false and the pelvis connection is missing. It connects that player body part to the host's exposed Rigidbody and leaves every movement and rotation direction free.

The final DetachHand schedules removal and clears the stored reference. DestroyJoints removes the full set immediately only when HasRigidbody is true and the pelvis connection exists. This is separate from the hand-to-grip joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._lastHand
member.summary: Stores the last recorded Hand reference returned by GetLastHand.

remarks.para: DetachHand writes the supplied hand here before removing its list entry and notifying listeners, provided the host list was nonempty. It does not require the hand actually to be in the list. AttachHand and the despawn list cleanup do not update or clear this value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost._marrowBody
member.summary: Cached MarrowBody from this host's own GameObject, supplying collider and Rigidbody information.

remarks.para: Body fills this reference on demand from the shared MarrowBody lookup table when it is missing or destroyed. Colliders uses its configured shape array; HasRigidbody reads its body flag; Rb returns its stored Rigidbody only when IsStatic is false. A Rigidbody gives an object simulated mass and motion.
This is cached component information, rather than a new scan of every child body on each access.

remarks.para: A joint connects two simulated bodies. AttachHand creates this connection when ignoreBodyOnGrab is true, IsStatic is false and the pelvis connection is missing. It connects that player body part to the host's exposed Rigidbody and leaves every movement and rotation direction free.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.checkForSleepCoroutine
member.summary: Handle kept so a new grab or proxy-removal request can stop the previous wait for physics sleep.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues across frames. RemoveProxy stores the handle when it starts CoCheckForSleep; SetProxy stops and clears it when a valid new proxy is stored. RemoveProxy also stops and clears an earlier handle before starting again.
The sleep sequence clears LastGrabbedProxy when the body settles. It does not clear this handle on its own when it finishes, so a nonnull handle does not prove the sequence is still running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.ignoreBodyOnGrab
member.summary: When true, grabbing a nonstatic host creates extra connections that stop the object colliding with the player's torso and locomotion body.

remarks.para: AttachHand creates six physics joints for pelvis, spine, chest, neck, head and the locomotion knee body if the pelvis connection is missing. A joint connects two simulated bodies. These connections leave all motion and rotation directions free, while ignoring collisions between the connected bodies.

This is read when attaching. Changing it while an object is already held does not remove existing connections; normal final detachment, DestroyJoints or ForceDetach performs their cleanup. It does not turn off the object's colliders for the rest of the world.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.manager
member.summary: Links this host to the group controller that tracks grabs across several hosts.

remarks.para: InteractableHostManager.Start, Unity's startup callback, assigns this reference on each configured host and subscribes to the host's attachment and detachment delegates. Those routines forward host-and-hand notifications and add or remove the host in the manager's grabbedHosts list.
Assigning this field alone does not install those delegate subscriptions. The group controller must also be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.onHandAttachedDelegate
member.summary: Called with this host and the hand just added to its attachment records.

remarks.para: A delegate holds callbacks: routines called to report an action. AttachHand first appends the hand, then invokes this delegate, then creates the optional player-body collision-ignore joints. Listeners see the new HandCount before those extra joints are created.

In the normal grip attachment path, this callback also runs before LastGrabbedProxy is refreshed and before the grip's hand list is updated. IsAttached may still show the earlier grip state. It does not reject duplicate hand entries, so repeated AttachHand calls can produce repeated notifications. The group manager also subscribes here during its startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost.onHandDetachedDelegate
member.summary: Called with this host and the hand passed to DetachHand after the removal attempt.

remarks.para: DetachHand first saves the supplied hand as GetLastHand, then removes one matching entry from the host list, then calls this delegate. A delegate holds callbacks, meaning routines called to report an action. These callbacks run before cleanup of the optional player-body joints when the last recorded hand leaves.
No callback occurs if the host list was already empty. Otherwise the callback can occur even if the supplied hand was not found in that list. The group manager subscribes here during its startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.grabbedHosts
member.summary: Attachment records that can contain the same host once for each holding hand.

remarks.para: The manager creates an empty list during construction. OnHandAttached appends one host after its notification, and OnDetachedHand removes one matching entry after its notification. For example, a box held with both hands normally appears twice; releasing one hand leaves one box entry.

This is bookkeeping, not a unique set or a fresh check of which objects are physically held. During a manager callback it still shows the state before that callback's list update. Directly changing the list does not create or release a grip. The group collision, interaction and release methods visit hosts instead of this list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.hosts
member.summary: The configured group whose collision shapes, hand-targeting permission and held grips this manager can change together.

remarks.para: Reset in the Unity editor fills this array with InteractableHost components on this object and its children. Start, Unity's startup callback called before the component's first frame update, assigns this manager to each host and subscribes to its attach and detach notifications.

Startup also reads each host's Rigidbody mass. A Rigidbody gives an object simulated mass and motion. The inspected startup path requires nonstatic hosts with valid reported bodies and stored Rigidbody references; it does not skip an unsuitable entry. Supply a nonnull array with no missing hosts or an empty array for an empty group.

The group methods read this array when called, including hosts not currently grabbed. Replacing the array later changes their targets, but does not move the subscriptions installed during Start from the old hosts to the new ones.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.onHandAttached
member.summary: Callbacks receiving the host and attaching hand before the manager adds that host to grabbedHosts.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action. OnHandAttached invokes these callbacks with the supplied host first and hand second, then appends the host to the manager list. In the normal subscribed host path, the host's own HandCount already includes that hand, while grabbedHosts still shows its earlier state.
A second hand attaching to the same object produces another notification and another host entry. These callbacks report attachments; assigning them does not make a hand grab an object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager.onHandDetached
member.summary: Callbacks receiving the host and detaching hand before the manager removes one matching grabbedHosts entry.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action. OnDetachedHand passes the supplied host first and hand second. In the normal subscribed host path, the host has already attempted to remove the hand and recorded GetLastHand, while grabbedHosts still has its earlier contents until these callbacks return.
The callbacks run even if there is no matching entry in grabbedHosts. They report a release; assigning them does not physically detach a hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.CONTACT_UPDATE_DISTANCE_SQR
member.summary: The squared position-change threshold used before moving and rotating the contact anchor.

remarks.para: It is initialized to the square of 0.001 meters: approximately 0.000001 square meters, corresponding to a one-millimeter displacement. SetPositionAndRotation compares the requested world position with the anchor Rigidbody’s current world position, using the squared distance between them.

A difference smaller than this threshold skips the entire update, including the requested rotation. A rotation-only request therefore gets skipped if its position stays unchanged. Equality with the threshold is sufficient to update. The value is a squared distance, not a time interval or an angle; The class initializes it once as a static readonly value.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body; this check uses the separate anchor body’s current position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact.Transform
member.summary: Returns the host-attached anchor position and rotation in scene coordinates.

remarks.para: The result is a SimpleTransform value containing a position and rotation. Its position is the host’s world position plus _anchorPosition rotated by the host’s world rotation. Its rotation is the host’s world rotation followed by _anchorRotation, the stored host-relative anchor orientation. The calculation uses no scale, so scaling the host does not multiply the offset in this result.

This is calculated from the host and the stored anchor on every read. It can differ from the separate kinematic anchor body’s current pose after SetPositionAndRotation has moved that body along a path. Modifying the returned value does not move either object.
The returned world position and saved anchor offset distances are in meters. Kinematic means code controls the separate anchor’s position and rotation instead of forces moving it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._anchorPosition
member.summary: The saved anchor offset from the host’s origin, expressed in the host’s axes.

remarks.para: Construction takes anchorPosition, rounds each component to the nearest 0.001-meter step, stores it here, and assigns the same vector to the joint’s connectedAnchor on the host. For example, an input X of 0.0124 meters becomes approximately 0.012 meters.

The Transform getter rotates this stored offset by the host’s world rotation and adds the host’s world position; that getter does not multiply by host scale. This is a readonly native setup value. Changing it through the proxy later changes the getter’s calculation but does not repeat construction or automatically update the joint’s separately stored connectedAnchor.
The joint is the physics connection between the separate anchor body and the host; connectedAnchor is its attachment point on the host.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._anchorRotation
member.summary: The saved orientation of the anchor relative to the host body.

remarks.para: Construction copies anchorRotation here and combines it with the host’s world rotation to place the new anchor object. The Transform getter uses the same combination on every read, so the reported anchor orientation turns with the host.

This quaternion represents a rotation; it is not three angles in degrees. The native field is readonly after setup. It is separate from _startRotation, the relative-orientation snapshot used by disabling and spring stabilization; changing this proxy value does not recompute that snapshot or directly turn the anchor physics body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._disabledRotation
member.summary: The contact anchor’s saved world orientation, restored when the contact is enabled.

remarks.para: Construction fills this cache with the newly created anchor’s world rotation. Every Disable call overwrites it with the anchor Transform’s current world rotation before resetting and deactivating that object.

Enable activates the scene object first, then restores this orientation to both its Transform and Rigidbody. The saved value is in scene coordinates. It is not automatically refreshed while disabled or recalculated from the host’s later rotation; another Disable call overwrites it. It stores rotation only, so it does not restore a saved position.
A Transform stores a scene object’s position and rotation; a Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._hostBody
member.summary: The existing Rigidbody whose motion is constrained by this contact’s separate anchor body.

remarks.para: The constructor receives this body and assigns it as the contact joint’s connectedBody. The joint itself is added to the newly created contact scene object. A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body, which supplies motion and rotation to the physics simulation.

The host’s current world pose and saved anchor values determine the Transform getter’s reported anchor pose. Disable and spring stabilization also read its rotation. Destroy removes the contact’s owned anchor object and joint while leaving this host object in the scene.
The joint is the physics connection between this host and the separate anchor. A pose means position plus rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._joint
member.summary: The physics connection between the contact’s kinematic anchor and the existing host Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint can permit, limit or stop sliding and turning on its axes, and use spring/damper drives to push toward a desired pose or speed. Construction adds this component to the contact’s new scene object and connects it to _hostBody. Its main X axis is local right and its secondary axis is local up at setup.

FreeDirection and LimitDirection change sliding along X. The drive setters tune restoring strength, resistance and force caps, and SwingTwistSpringStabilization supplies a rotation target. This readonly native reference points to the contact-owned component that Destroy removes.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. The anchor is kinematic, meaning code sets its position and rotation instead of forces moving it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._rigidbody
member.summary: The separate kinematic anchor body that code positions to guide the host’s motion.

remarks.para: Construction creates a new scene object, adds this Rigidbody, sets isKinematic to true, and places it at the host-attached anchor pose. Kinematic means code controls its position and rotation while the physics joint constrains the connected host against it.

The joint is on this same new object. SplineJoint updates its pose along the line path through Contact.SetPositionAndRotation. Enable and Disable activate or deactivate this object and manage its rotation; Destroy removes this object. The constructor creates it independently of the existing host body.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body, which participates in the simulation of motion and contacts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._startRotation
member.summary: The anchor’s initial rotation relative to the host, saved as the reference orientation for later calculations.

remarks.para: Construction calculates inverse(host world rotation) multiplied by the newly created contact’s world rotation. This expresses the contact’s starting orientation in the host’s frame, so it is a relative quaternion rather than a frozen world orientation.

Disable combines the host’s current world rotation with this snapshot before deactivation. SwingTwistSpringStabilization uses it when comparing the current contact and host orientations, keeping the initial rotational offset in that calculation. The native field is readonly; it is not recomputed each frame when the host turns.
A quaternion stores a rotation. Inverse here means undoing the host’s world rotation so the contact’s starting orientation is measured in the host’s axes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact._worldToJointSpace
member.summary: The cached axis-frame rotation used to express the spring target in the joint’s own directions.

remarks.para: Construction builds this quaternion from the joint’s normalized axis and secondaryAxis, completing a perpendicular three-axis frame. The constructor sets those first two directions to local right and local up, so the resulting reference is the identity rotation for that setup.

Despite the field name, this is not refreshed from either object’s world rotation. SwingTwistSpringStabilization uses its inverse while working in joint axes and combines it back into the resulting target rotation. It is a readonly setup cache; editing it through the proxy does not rebuild the joint’s axis or secondaryAxis.
A quaternion stores a rotation. A normalized direction has length 1. Identity means no rotation, and using the inverse undoes this cached frame rotation.
The joint is the physics connection between the host and the separate anchor. Its frame means its own X, Y and Z directions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._angXDrive
member.summary: Saved settings for driving the joint's rotation about X axis.

remarks.para: The settings contain spring strength for turning toward the target, damping for controlling relative rotational motion, and a maximum strength for that turning force.

CopyFrom captures angularXDrive; CopyTo reapplies it only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Unity uses this drive when the joint's rotationDriveMode is X and YZ. Restoring this cache does not choose that mode or change the target rotation.
Clear zeros the live drive but retains the snapshot. Editing this saved value affects a later restoration, and capturing again overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._angXMotion
member.summary: The saved rule for rotation about the joint's X axis, reapplied when the joint is restored.

remarks.para: Locked blocks rotation about this axis, Limited uses the joint's existing angular limits, and Free allows rotation without those limits. The field selects a mode; it does not store an angle in degrees.

CopyFrom reads angularXMotion into this field. CopyTo restores it only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Clear frees the live joint's rotation without changing this saved mode. Editing the cache affects a later restoration; capturing again replaces the edited value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._attachedBody
member.summary: The other physics body that the joint should reconnect to when its saved settings are restored.

remarks.para: CopyFrom saves the joint's connectedBody here; it is the other Rigidbody in the connection, rather than the body carrying the joint component. A Rigidbody represents an object's motion in the physics simulation.

CopyTo restores this connection only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Clear sets the live joint's connectedBody to null while keeping this saved reference. Changing the cache chooses the body used by a later restoration, and another capture replaces it.
A saved null value is valid: a joint with no connected Rigidbody connects to a fixed point in the world instead. Its movement still depends on the restored motion modes and drives.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._hasBeenCopied
member.summary: Allows the saved settings to be restored after a joint snapshot has been captured.

remarks.para: CopyFrom sets this flag true after saving the connected body, six motion modes and six drives. CopyTo returns without changing the joint when it is false; a newly created snapshot starts with the flag false.

Clear and CopyTo do not reset the flag. It also does not block a new CopyFrom: every capture replaces the stored settings. Setting it false therefore prevents restoration, rather than preventing another capture.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._slerpDrive
member.summary: Saved settings for driving the joint's rotation about all three axes together.

remarks.para: The settings contain spring strength for turning toward the target, damping for controlling relative rotational motion, and a maximum strength for that turning force.

CopyFrom captures slerpDrive; CopyTo reapplies it only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Unity uses this drive when the joint's rotationDriveMode is Slerp. Restoring this cache does not choose that mode or change the target rotation.
Clear zeros the live drive but retains the snapshot. Editing this saved value affects a later restoration, and capturing again overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._xDrive
member.summary: Saved settings for the joint's force that moves the object along its X axis.

remarks.para: The settings hold spring strength, damping and a maximum force. The spring pulls toward the drive target, damping resists the difference from the target motion, and the maximum force caps how strongly the drive can push.

CopyFrom captures xDrive; CopyTo reapplies it only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Clear zeros the live drive while retaining this snapshot. Editing this cache changes the next restoration, rather than immediately moving the object; another capture overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo._xMotion

remarks.para: Locked blocks movement along this axis, Limited uses the joint's existing distance limit, and Free allows movement without that limit. This is a motion mode, not a distance in metres.

CopyFrom reads the live joint's xMotion into this field; CopyTo writes it back only when _hasBeenCopied is true. Clear makes the live joint free to move without changing this saved mode. Editing the field changes a later restoration, and another CopyFrom replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager.Instance
member.summary: Gets the EntityManager plugin used for registering entities and looking them up by tag.

remarks.para: On the first access with no cached manager, the getter asks MarrowPlugins for its EntityManager plugin. A successful lookup is stored in _manager, and later accesses return that cached object. If the plugin lookup fails, the getter can return null and a later access can try again. It does not create an EntityManager or search the scene for a component.

Use this to reach RegisterEntity and the tag lookup methods once the plugin is available. Check for a null result when accessing it before that availability is established. A level-load registry clear empties the manager's collections and does not clear this cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager._entities
member.summary: Stores the distinct entities that have been registered with this manager.

remarks.para: This set records membership, with one entry per entity. RegisterEntity adds membership before indexing tags; UnregisterEntity removes it before removing tag entries. An empty tag list does not prevent membership. This is not an automatically discovered list of every object in the scene, nor does membership alone prove that an entity is currently visible or active.

The set and _tagIDToEntity are separate collections. Editing this set directly does not update the tag lists. Removing an entity here first also makes a later UnregisterEntity return early, leaving any tag entries behind. Use the registration methods to keep membership and lookups together. The level-loading callback clears this set before clearing the tag dictionary.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager._manager
member.summary: Caches the EntityManager plugin returned by .

remarks.para: When this reference is null, Instance attempts to retrieve the plugin from MarrowPlugins and caches a successful result here. When it is non-null, Instance returns it directly. Replacing this reference therefore redirects later Instance calls to the supplied manager; it does not copy or clear the old manager's registered entities.

Setting the reference to null allows a later Instance access to retry plugin lookup. This does not dispose of the previous manager or clear its collections. Normal level-load cleanup keeps this reference and clears the collections on that manager instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager._tagIDToEntity
member.summary: Stores each tag barcode ID and the ordered list of entities indexed under that ID.

remarks.para: Each string key is a BoneTag barcode ID, the tag asset's identifier rather than its display name. RegisterEntity reads the entity's current tag references and appends an entry for each. AddEntityToTag can also append directly. These lists can contain duplicate entries and can disagree with the entity's current Tags if the tags are edited without updating registration.

TryGetEntitiesWithTag exposes the stored list through a read-only-list interface; it is the existing list rather than a separate snapshot, and that method does not filter despawned entities. TryGetFirstEntityWithTag walks the list in order and skips IsDespawned entries. A read-only interface limits editing through that interface; it does not freeze the list while the manager changes it.

Editing or replacing this dictionary changes the lookup index, without editing _entities membership or the entities' own tags. Normal removal deletes a key when its list becomes empty. The level-loading callback clears the dictionary after clearing _entities.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowCollisionManager._colBsToRemove
member.summary: Temporarily holds partner colliders while one collider’s managed ignores are removed.

remarks.para: A Collider is a shape used by the physics simulation to detect contact. ClearManagedIgnoresFor(A) walks the recorded partner set for collider A, restores collisions between A and each partner, and adds those partners to this shared working list. It then clears and removes A’s own lookup entry.

A second pass through the list removes each A/partner count and removes A from each partner’s reverse lookup. This keeps the cleanup steps separate from the first set traversal. The list is cleared after that pass. These entries are cleanup references; this operation does not destroy the collider objects.

The static initializer creates the list, and the after-level-unload callback also clears it. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The list describes work within a cleanup call, rather than a permanent list of colliders to delete later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowCollisionManager._colliderToColliderMap
member.summary: Records each collider’s partner colliders so their managed collision ignores can be cleaned up.

remarks.para: The dictionary maps collider A to a set of partners such as B and C. A set stores each partner once, even when several requests ask to ignore the same pair. A newly registered pair normally gets both directions, A → B and B → A. The number of overlapping requests is kept separately in _ignoreCounts.

When the final balanced release restores an A/B pair, ClearLookups removes B from A’s set and A from B’s set; it removes a dictionary entry when that collider’s set becomes empty. This is a cleanup index, not a direct query of Unity’s physical collision state. Normal use should balance each managed ignore request with its release; use IsIgnored for the manager’s pair-registration query.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowCollisionManager._ignoreCounts
member.summary: Counts overlapping requests to keep a collider pair from colliding.

remarks.para: The key is an integer hash, a lookup number calculated from the two collider references after ordering them by their Unity instance IDs. Thus A/B and B/A use the same pair key. The stored integer is a unitless request count, not a force, distance, or duration.

ManagedIgnore(A, B, true) increments the count. For the first registered request it stores the count and both partner lookups, then calls Physics.IgnoreCollision(A, B, true). Further requests increase the count without repeating that physics call. A false request subtracts one; while a positive count remains, collisions stay ignored.

For example, two true requests give count 2. One false request leaves count 1 and keeps the ignore. The next false request stores count 0, restores physical collisions, removes the count entry and clears both partner lookups. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.AnchorBody
member.summary: Gets the cached body used as the positioning reference when teleporting this entity.

remarks.para: ValidateBodies and ValidatePoseCache select this reference. Their scan starts from the current selection: it takes the first candidate if no anchor exists, then replaces a Rigidbody-backed anchor only with a Rigidbody-backed body of strictly greater mass. The chosen reference is therefore usually a heavy body, but this getter does not calculate the current heaviest body on demand. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated mass and motion. The mass compared in this scan is measured in kilograms.

Equal masses keep the existing selection. An existing heavier anchor can remain even if a later rebuilt Bodies array excludes it. Teleport uses the anchor’s reference pose to position the other bodies together. Merely reading this property does not refresh any selection or pose cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Bodies
member.summary: Provides the body components that this entity moves and manages together.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody manages one part of the object’s physics, including its Rigidbody and associated collision shapes. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that simulates an object’s motion and response to forces. MarrowEntity visits this array to teleport the parts, freeze or restore their physics, change collision participation and recalculate mass.

Bodies returns the stored array itself, rather than a fresh copy or a search of the hierarchy. Entity validation rebuilds this array from the configured body and Rigidbody components under the entity.

The default-pose and teleport caches use the same index order as this array. Changing its order or length after initialization does not rebuild those caches and can make later operations use the wrong body pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Cache
member.summary: Looks up registered MarrowEntity components by the GameObject that owns them.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity object carrying the entity component. This shared cache maps that object to its registered components so callers can find the entity without repeatedly searching for it. Cache creates the shared cache when it is first needed.

Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, adds this entity under its own GameObject. OnDestroy removes it, and clears the shared cache reference when no entries remain. The cache is not restricted to objects that are currently active or visible.

Cache.Get(gameObject) returns the first registered entry, or null if none is stored. Cache.TryGet(gameObject, out entity) reports success or failure and supplies that entry on success. These lookups use the specified object’s registration; they do not search its children for an entity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsCollidersEnabled
member.summary: Records whether normal solid-collider participation has been enabled for the entity.

remarks.para: A solid collider is a shape that participates in physical contacts. EnableColliders(false) saves the enabled state of the bodies’ solid colliders and disables them. EnableColliders(true) restores those saved states, so a collider that was already disabled stays disabled.
This stored flag is the entity’s logical setting, not a fresh check of every collider. Ghost mode can temporarily disable the actual colliders while this flag remains true.

The property setter and backing field only store the flag. Use EnableColliders to update the bodies. Writing the flag first can make EnableColliders return early because it sees the requested value already stored, leaving the collider components unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsCulled
member.summary: Reports whether culling is requested for this entity.

remarks.para: Culling is the game suspending an entity’s normal processing. When the request is resolved, MarrowEntity requests physics hibernation for culling, disables its configured MarrowBehaviour components and calls its registered culling routines.

This reads the requested state, not a confirmation that the manager has resolved the request or applied all of its effects. Notifications and component changes can follow later. It is not a fresh check of GameObject.activeSelf, physics motion or camera visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsDespawned
member.summary: Reports whether returning the entity to its inactive pool state is requested.

remarks.para: Despawn asks the associated Poolee to return the object to its pool for later reuse. Pool cleanup requests despawning through the inactivity manager. This flag is separate from IsDestroyed: a pooled object can remain allocated for a later spawn.

This reads the requested state, not a confirmation that the manager has resolved the request or applied all of its effects. Notifications and component changes can follow later. It is not a fresh check of GameObject.activeSelf, physics motion or camera visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsDestroyed
member.summary: Marks the entity as destroyed for its remaining lifecycle handlers.

remarks.para: OnDestroy, Unity’s routine called when this component is destroyed, sets this marker after removing the entity from its shared component cache and before unregistering it from the entity manager. The entity’s managed active-state handler returns without further activity changes when the marker is true.

This differs from returning an object to a pool: a despawn request is reported by IsDespawned. Setting this marker yourself only changes the stored value; it does not call Unity’s destruction routine, return the object to its pool or run the cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsGhosting
member.summary: Records whether the entity has entered its ghost physics mode.

remarks.para: Ghost(true) disables the bodies’ tracker objects, solid colliders and trigger colliders, and makes bodies that have a Rigidbody kinematic. A kinematic Rigidbody is moved by code rather than pushed around by ordinary simulated forces. The transition also clears culling registrations and removes each registered runtime-joint entry before calling its Destroy routine. That routine requests destruction only when the joint’s IsCreatedAtRuntime flag is true; registration alone does not set that flag.

Ghost(false) restores saved collider and trigger enabled states, requests tracker restoration through the entity-wide permission, and sets the bodies’ Rigidbodies to isKinematic=false so ordinary forces can move them. It does not restore an earlier individually saved kinematic setting. Ghost also passes the change to externally packed entities. These operations do not change the normal collider, trigger or tracker permission flags to match the temporary ghost state.

Ghost stores this marker before changing bodies or calling joint-destruction routines, so listeners can see the new marker while that work is still running. The property setter and backing field merely store the marker. Call Ghost to apply the mode. If you set the marker first, Ghost called with that same value can return without changing any bodies. This flag is not a guarantee that the renderers have become transparent or invisible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsHibernating
member.summary: Reports whether a recorded reason currently asks the entity’s bodies to keep their physics frozen.

remarks.para: Hibernation pauses body motion without destroying the entity. Hibernate adds or removes a reason such as Default, Culling or Loading. The entity is considered hibernating while one or more of those recorded reasons remain; removing Culling alone does not wake it if Loading is still recorded.

The normal Hibernate transition freezes or restores the managed bodies only when the combined state changes between having a reason and having none. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that simulates an object’s motion and response to forces. For a Rigidbody, the freeze saves its physics settings, locks motion and puts it to sleep.

This getter checks the entity’s recorded reason flags. It is not Unity’s Rigidbody.IsSleeping check and does not detect every possible reason that an individual body is motionless. Change hibernation with Hibernate rather than writing _hibernationFlags directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsHidden
member.summary: Reports whether managed hiding is requested for this entity.

remarks.para: Hide(true) requests hiding and Hide(false) requests restoration. Applying hiding normally deactivates the entity’s GameObject, the Unity object containing its components. The immediate-apply option can change GameObject activity before the manager sends the hide notifications.

This reads the requested state, not a confirmation that the manager has resolved the request or applied all of its effects. Notifications and component changes can follow later. It is not a fresh check of GameObject.activeSelf, physics motion or camera visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsInactive
member.summary: Reports whether hiding, culling or despawning is requested for the entity.

remarks.para: This is true if any of the three requested reasons is present. For example, clearing a hide request still leaves it true if a culling request remains. It is false before the entity’s inactivity-status object has been initialized.

This reads the requested state, not a confirmation that the manager has resolved the request or applied all of its effects. Notifications and component changes can follow later. It is not a fresh check of GameObject.activeSelf, physics motion or camera visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsTrackersEnabled
member.summary: Records whether the entity permits its body tracking objects to be active.

remarks.para: A Tracker links a body’s collision shape to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity references. A collision shape is a collider used for physics detection, and a GameObject is the Unity scene object holding the tracker’s components. EnableTrackers changes this permission and updates those tracker GameObjects across the bodies. After an object changes from active to inactive, OnDeactivate calls its registered disable routines with the tracker’s collider.

Body-level tracker enabling also checks this entity-wide permission. Ghost mode can force the tracker objects off even while the stored permission remains true, so this flag does not report every tracker’s current GameObject activity.

The property setter and backing field only store the permission. Use EnableTrackers for the update across bodies. Setting the flag directly first can make that method skip its work because the stored value already matches. Disabling trackers through the method also clears the entity’s zone-culling registrations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.IsTriggersEnabled
member.summary: Records whether normal trigger-collider participation has been enabled for the entity.

remarks.para: A trigger collider detects overlaps instead of pushing objects apart. EnableTriggers(false) saves the enabled state of the bodies’ trigger colliders and disables them. EnableTriggers(true) restores the saved states rather than forcing every trigger on.
This stored flag is not a check that every trigger is currently active. Ghost mode can force trigger colliders off while this normal setting remains true.

The property setter and backing field only store the flag. Use EnableTriggers to change the components. Writing the flag before calling that method with the same value can cause its early-return check to skip the actual trigger update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Joints
member.summary: Provides the configured physics connections whose settings the entity can save and restore.

remarks.para: A joint connects bodies in Unity’s physics simulation, allowing movement or turning according to its settings. These MarrowJoint components represent the entity’s configured ConfigurableJoint connections; this array does not mean that the connected bodies are immovable.

Joints returns the stored array. Validation rebuilds it from the joint components under the entity. SetPhysicsDefaults records their current joint configuration, and pool cleanup restores saved settings. RuntimeJoints is the separate collection used for connections added during play.
Replacing an array entry only changes which component the entity manages. It does not create or connect a new Unity joint by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.RuntimeJoints
member.summary: Lists the extra physics connections registered with the entity during play.

remarks.para: A joint is a connection between bodies in the physics simulation. RuntimeJoints exposes the entity’s current internal list through a read-only collection interface: callers can inspect its entries, and later additions or removals remain visible through that collection.

The entity’s joint-registration routines avoid duplicate entries and remove registered joints. Entering ghost mode removes each registered entry before calling its Destroy routine. That routine requests destruction only when the joint’s IsCreatedAtRuntime flag is true; AddRuntimeJoint registration does not set that flag. Pool cleanup separately asks Unity to destroy each registered MarrowJoint component, whose OnDestroy cleanup requests destruction of its underlying physics joint. Removal from the list is not a completed-destruction check. The configured Joints array is separate; the ghost-mode loop walks the runtime list instead.

The internal _runtimeJoints collection is lifecycle bookkeeping. Putting a component into it does not itself create its Unity physics connection; removing an entry alone does not perform the cleanup carried out by the entity’s ghost or pool routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.ScaleRatio
member.summary: Stores the relative volume multiplier used when recalculating the entity’s body masses.

remarks.para: This number has no units. Pool initialization calculates it by multiplying current localScale.x / originalScale.x, current localScale.y / originalScale.y and current localScale.z / originalScale.z. Each originalScale component is the saved size multiplier on that axis; localScale is the current size multiplier relative to the entity’s parent.

A value of 1 means the original volume. For example, doubling all three dimensions gives 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, rather than 2. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that simulates an object’s motion and response to forces. Hibernation freezes the body’s physics. For an ordinary active body with a Rigidbody that is not hibernating, ResetMass uses this multiplier with its saved reference mass in kilograms; a 1-kilogram reference body and multiplier 8 gives 8 kilograms.

Pool initialization recalculates this value only when at least one current local-scale component differs from its saved reference component by more than 0.00000011920929, a unitless difference. Equality and smaller differences leave the stored multiplier unchanged. Pool cleanup restores the original localScale and resets the multiplier to 1. It is not recalculated on every property read.

Changing this value alone does not change Transform.localScale or immediately update a Rigidbody’s mass. Mass recalculation is a separate operation, and packed or hibernating bodies have additional handling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.Tags

remarks.para: This is a TagList of BoneTag references, rather than Unity’s single GameObject tag string. MarrowQuery can test these labels to decide whether an entity matches its selection rules, including rules that exclude a tag.

Replacing this reference changes the list returned to tag consumers. It does not resize the entity or apply a physics state change.

During unhide application, it updates activity first and then calls OnEntityUnhide. Hide with doApplyImmediately=true can change GameObject activity earlier, before these queued notifications. The receiver routines take no arguments. The manager stores applied bookkeeping only after its application notification routines return.
Unhiding removes only the hide reason. Other inactivity reasons can still leave the entity disabled when the restoration routines run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._hostEntity
member.summary: Stores the entity reference recorded from the host body during packing.

remarks.para: Packing makes one MarrowBody share the host body’s physics arrangement. In this Pack implementation, the host body must belong to the receiving entity, and this field is assigned that host body’s Entity reference. Do not assume from the name that it always points to a separate parent entity.

The root GameObject is the Unity scene object holding this entity component. The managed active-state handler treats a valid entity reference here as a reason to keep the root GameObject active for a culling-only state. Hide and despawn can still disable it. Unpack and pool cleanup clear the stored reference.
Writing this reference alone does not pack bodies, reparent their transforms or transfer mass. The Pack and Unpack operations carry out those changes and maintain the related body and entity lists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._inactiveStatus
member.summary: Stores the requests, processing stages and notifications for the entity’s managed inactivity.

remarks.para: This is an InactiveStatus object, not a single bitfield. It holds separate requested, resolved and applied hide/cull/despawn flags. Requested means asked for; resolved means the manager has accepted the current request; applied means its application handlers have been processed.

InitializeInactiveState creates this object and connects the entity’s culling, hiding and despawning routines. Public IsHidden, IsCulled, IsDespawned and IsInactive read its requested flags, while the active-state handler uses its resolved flags.

Its notification routines are called to report transitions and receive this status object plus a bool for whether their reason is entering or leaving. The manager sets that reason’s completed flag before an entering resolve notification, which runs before resolved is copied from requested. Application notifications receive the corresponding resolved bool and run before applied is copied from resolved. Separate completed flags remember the entering notifications that ran. Leaving resolve notifications wait until no hide, cull or despawn request remains and the manager has drained its request/application queues; the relevant completed flag is cleared before the leaving routine is called. The manager processes changes through queues. Replacing the reference or editing its flags directly does not perform the wiring, enqueue the normal transition or update all affected components. Use the entity and manager transition routines for those effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._isDisableOnCullPrevented
member.summary: Allows a culled entity’s root GameObject to remain active when managed activity is applied.

remarks.para: A GameObject is Unity’s object carrying the entity component. PreventDisableOnCull changes this stored flag. The managed active-state handler uses it when deciding whether culling should deactivate that object.

This applies to the culling reason. Hiding or despawning can still deactivate the object. Culling can still freeze body physics, disable the configured MarrowBehaviour components and notify culling receivers even if the root GameObject stays active.

Changing the flag alone does not immediately run the active-state handler or undo those culling effects. Packed-entity relationships are additional reasons the handler can keep a culled root object active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._joints
member.summary: Provides the configured physics connections whose settings the entity can save and restore.

remarks.para: A joint connects bodies in Unity’s physics simulation, allowing movement or turning according to its settings. These MarrowJoint components represent the entity’s configured ConfigurableJoint connections; this array does not mean that the connected bodies are immovable.

Joints returns the stored array. Validation rebuilds it from the joint components under the entity. SetPhysicsDefaults records their current joint configuration, and pool cleanup restores saved settings. RuntimeJoints is the separate collection used for connections added during play.
Replacing an array entry only changes which component the entity manages. It does not create or connect a new Unity joint by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._originalScale
member.summary: Stores the entity’s reference local scale for the volume calculation in and for pool restoration.

remarks.para: This Vector3 contains dimensionless X, Y and Z size multipliers relative to the entity Transform’s parent. Validation captures the current Transform.localScale as this reference; it is not a vector of world lengths in metres.

Pool initialization performs the volume calculation only when at least one current local-scale component differs from its saved reference component by more than 0.00000011920929, a unitless difference. Equality and smaller differences leave the stored ScaleRatio unchanged. When the condition passes, it multiplies the three current/reference component ratios to calculate ScaleRatio, the relative volume used by mass recalculation. For example, current (2,2,2) and original (1,1,1) gives volume ratio 8.

Pool cleanup writes this saved vector back to Transform.localScale and restores ScaleRatio to 1. Changing only the saved reference does not immediately resize the entity; it changes the baseline and later restoration target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._parasites
member.summary: Lists external entities whose bodies have been packed into this entity’s bodies.

remarks.para: A packed body is attached into a host body’s physics arrangement. Pack adds the external body’s owning entity here when that body is not part of this entity’s own Bodies array, avoiding duplicate entries. This is not a list of every child GameObject in the Unity hierarchy.

The root GameObject is the Unity scene object holding an entity component. The entity passes ghost-mode and hibernation transitions to these packed entities. Their presence also lets the managed active-state handler keep the host root active for culling alone. Pool cleanup despawns the listed entities through their Poolee components.
Unpack removes an external entity when no remaining packed body from it is found. Adding or removing a list entry yourself does not perform the actual body packing or unpacking.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._poolee
member.summary: Connects the entity to the pool that can spawn, clean up and reuse it.

remarks.para: Pooling returns an object for later reuse instead of destroying and reconstructing it each time. Validation finds the Poolee on this entity’s GameObject and adds one if missing, storing the resulting component here.

Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, registers the entity as a poolable component with this Poolee. MarrowEntity.Despawn forwards to it; pool initialization and cleanup then manage inactivity, trackers, body arrangements, saved physics settings and scale.
This is a component reference, not the requested despawn flag or a pool identifier. Replacing the reference alone does not register the entity with the new component or carry out a despawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._poseables
member.summary: Lists registered routines notified after the entity writes a body pose.

remarks.para: Each receiver implements IMarrowEntityPoseable.OnWritePose. A pose describes the positions and rotations of the entity’s body parts. WritePose first places the bodies using the supplied pose relative to the entity’s current world position and rotation, then calls these receivers so their own systems can respond.

ReadPose only captures the body transforms in the examined path; it does not notify this list. RegisterEventHandler avoids duplicates and does not immediately call OnWritePose, and UnregisterEventHandler removes the receiver.
The list does not store the body poses themselves. The supplied pose array and the bodies must use corresponding indices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._runtimeJoints
member.summary: Lists the extra physics connections registered with the entity during play.

remarks.para: A joint is a connection between bodies in the physics simulation. RuntimeJoints exposes the entity’s current internal list through a read-only collection interface: callers can inspect its entries, and later additions or removals remain visible through that collection.

The entity’s joint-registration routines avoid duplicate entries and remove registered joints. Entering ghost mode removes each registered entry before calling its Destroy routine. That routine requests destruction only when the joint’s IsCreatedAtRuntime flag is true; AddRuntimeJoint registration does not set that flag. Pool cleanup separately asks Unity to destroy each registered MarrowJoint component, whose OnDestroy cleanup requests destruction of its underlying physics joint. Removal from the list is not a completed-destruction check. The configured Joints array is separate; the ghost-mode loop walks the runtime list instead.

The internal _runtimeJoints collection is lifecycle bookkeeping. Putting a component into it does not itself create its Unity physics connection; removing an entry alone does not perform the cleanup carried out by the entity’s ghost or pool routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._tags
member.summary: Provides the entity’s tag labels for systems that select or classify objects.

remarks.para: This is a TagList of BoneTag references, rather than Unity’s single GameObject tag string. MarrowQuery can test these labels to decide whether an entity matches its selection rules, including rules that exclude a tag.

Tags returns the existing TagList. Tag matching reads the list’s cached tag identifiers. If you edit the list’s tag entries directly after that cache has been built, call TagList.UpdateCache to rebuild it so subsequent matches use the edited labels.
Replacing this reference changes the list returned to tag consumers. It does not resize the entity or apply a physics state change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity._teleportTransformCache
member.summary: Holds the computed world poses for every body during one teleport operation.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, allocates one SimpleTransform entry for each body. Teleport calculates all destination positions and rotations into this array before it changes any body Transform. This keeps one moved body from changing the reference frame used to calculate another body’s destination.

The positions in this scratch array are world-space distances, normally metres; the quaternions are world orientations. Teleport either preserves the current arrangement relative to the anchor body or uses each body’s initial entity-relative arrangement when doResetPose is true.

The entries are overwritten by the next teleport and match the Bodies array by index. This is working storage, not the entity’s saved default-pose cache and not a cache of hierarchy reparenting operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.allHibernationSources
member.summary: Stores the mask representing all three defined hibernation reasons.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes this to 7: Default=1 for an ordinary explicit freeze request, Culling=2 for suspended processing, and Loading=4 for level loading, combined together. Combining the flags means choosing all three reason bits; it is not a duration or intensity.

This mask is separate from _hibernationFlags, which records the reasons currently keeping the entity frozen. The examined Hibernate, ClearHibernation and pool-restoration routines operate on that active-reasons field, so changing this combined mask alone does not pause or resume the bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntityPose.bodyPoses
member.summary: Stores each entity body's position and rotation relative to the entity's own position and orientation, in body-array order.

remarks.para: Each SimpleTransform contains a position vector and a rotation quaternion, a value describing orientation rather than three angle values. Position offsets are in meters along the entity's right, up and forward axes; they are not absolute scene coordinates or offsets from each body's immediate parent. For example, position (1, 0, 0) places that body 1 meter to the entity's right when the pose is applied. Turning the entity turns that offset with it.

MarrowEntity.ReadPose replaces this array with one entry for each entity body and captures those relative poses. WritePose uses the entity's current scene position and rotation to place the bodies, then notifies registered pose handlers. The data stores position and rotation, not body scale or velocity; the relative conversion uses the entity's rotation and position without its scale.

Keep entries in the same order as the target entity's Bodies array. The apply routine matches by array index, not by body name: fewer entries update only that prefix, while extra entries can exceed the body array and fail. Changing or assigning this array alone does not immediately move the bodies; it changes the data for a later pose application.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.BodyA
member.summary: Identifies the body whose GameObject hosts the Unity ConfigurableJoint.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection that can restrict or drive relative movement between physical bodies, or between a body and the fixed scene.

This body supplies the position/rotation captured by ReadJointSpace and temporarily used by WriteJointSpace. BodyA must be valid for construction. The CreateJoint/OnBodyEnable path waits for it to be active/enabled; a direct Build call does not check that state. CreateJoint and assigned-joint setup register this connection with the body for enable/disable notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.BodyB
member.summary: Identifies the other participating body, or no body for a connection to the fixed scene.

remarks.para: Build connects its Rigidbody when it has one; a Rigidbody is Unity's component for simulated physics movement. With BodyB assigned and ConfiguredInWorld false, joint reference poses are measured relative to this body's scene position and rotation. Enable processing waits for an assigned BodyB to be active/enabled.
It remains the saved MarrowBody reference even while disabling clears the engine joint's connectedBody. SwapBodies does not exchange the stored BodyA and BodyB references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.ConfiguredInWorld
member.summary: Reports whether the engine joint uses scene coordinates for its target configuration.

remarks.para: World/scene coordinates are the fixed scene frame rather than coordinates that turn with a body. This flag also makes ReadJointSpace and WriteJointSpace use the scene frame instead of BodyB as their reference.

For a valid engine joint it reads configuredInWorldSpace. When that joint is missing, it reads the fallback flag in _cjTempInfo, which is a separate configuration object, rather than the full saved default. This getter does not change the configuration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.HasConfigJoint
member.summary: Reports whether the saved Unity ConfigurableJoint still counts as a valid engine object.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection that can restrict or drive relative movement between physical bodies, or between a body and the fixed scene.

It uses Unity object-validity comparison, so a destroyed joint can fail this check even while an old reference value remains stored. It does not build a missing joint or report that both bodies are enabled or that the connection is unbroken in every other sense.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.IsCreatedAtRuntime
member.summary: Selects runtime removal/break handling instead of the scene-joint rebuild policy.

remarks.para: breakForce is the force break threshold in newtons. Setting it to infinity prevents force alone from exceeding that threshold; the turning-force break threshold, breakTorque in newton-meters, is not changed by this cleanup policy.

CreateJoint sets this true before assigning configuration and bodies. Destroy acts only when it is true. If the engine joint disappears, cleanup invokes break listeners and removes the runtime component when true, but rebuilds from the saved scene configuration with infinite breakForce when false.
Changing this flag does not create a joint or change its bodies; it changes which removal/recovery policy later code takes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.StartRotation
member.summary: Stores the captured orientation of BodyA relative to BodyB or the fixed scene. See .

remarks.para: ReadJointSpace writes this quaternion, an orientation value rather than three angles. It uses BodyB as reference only when that body exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it captures BodyA's scene rotation. The same captured value is written into the default configuration's startRotation.

It is a cache distinct from _jointSpace. Assigning it alone does not move a body, update the other orientation caches or make RestoreStartRotation apply that new value; that routine uses the separately stored pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.SwapBodies
member.summary: Reports the Unity joint's reversed body-role setting without exchanging the stored BodyA and BodyB references.

remarks.para: This reverses the order in which Unity processes the two physical bodies, which can change joint motion. Changing that setting does not exchange the saved body references or anchors, the points where the connection attaches.

With a valid engine joint this reads swapBodies; otherwise it reads the separate _cjTempInfo fallback flag. WriteJointSpace briefly toggles the live setting and restores it while refreshing the joint reference.
This is a reported configuration choice, not an operation that swaps the MarrowBody fields or physically moves the bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.ToJointSpace
member.summary: Stores the orientation of the joint axes calculated from the saved default axis and secondaryAxis. See .

remarks.para: The saved axis and secondaryAxis directions are relative to BodyA's local frame, which turns with that body. ToJointSpace is the quaternion describing that local joint-axis orientation.

ReadJointSpace obtains this quaternion from _defaultConfigJointInfo.GetJointSpace. The primary axis supplies the joint X direction; the secondary axis is used with cross products, which make a direction perpendicular to two given directions, to form the remaining perpendicular directions. A quaternion describes that orientation, not a speed or an angle limit.
This is a calculated cache, not a continuously updated read of the live joint axes. Changing live axes alone does not recalculate it; ReadJointSpace refreshes it and the paired inverse together.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.ToJointSpaceFromDefault
member.summary: Stores the captured starting orientation composed with the saved joint-axis orientation.

remarks.para: The saved axis and secondaryAxis directions are relative to BodyA's local frame, which turns with that body. ToJointSpace is the quaternion describing that local joint-axis orientation. In StartRotation × ToJointSpace, the starting quaternion describes BodyA's captured orientation in the chosen BodyB-or-fixed-scene reference frame; multiplication composes it with this local axis orientation.

ReadJointSpace calculates StartRotation multiplied by ToJointSpace. A quaternion is an orientation value, not three angle values. StartRotation is BodyA's captured orientation relative to BodyB only when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is relative to the fixed scene. ToJointSpace is the quaternion orientation constructed from the saved default axes. Multiplication composes those rotations; it is not scaling an angle value.
This quaternion is recalculated when joint space is read. Assigning it alone does not change the bodies, the engine joint or the other cached orientations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.ToJointSpaceInv
member.summary: Stores the inverse of the cached joint-axis orientation, for reversing that orientation conversion. See .

remarks.para: The saved axis and secondaryAxis directions are relative to BodyA's local frame, which turns with that body. ToJointSpace is the quaternion describing that local joint-axis orientation. This inverse quaternion reverses that orientation conversion.

ReadJointSpace calculates Quaternion.Inverse(ToJointSpace), where ToJointSpace is the orientation built from the saved default axis and secondaryAxis. These are quaternion orientation values, not measured distances or playback fractions.
Assigning this cache alone does not update ToJointSpace or the engine joint. Recapturing joint space refreshes the related orientation caches together.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._bodyB
