member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._cjTempInfo
member.summary: Supplies fallback world-space and reversed-body-role flags when the live Unity joint is missing.

remarks.para: World coordinates are fixed scene coordinates, rather than directions that turn with a body. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._configurableJoint
member.summary: Holds the Unity physics connection that this component builds, configures and temporarily neutralizes. See .

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint connects a physics body to another body or the fixed scene, with separately chosen movement modes, targets and drives. HasConfigJoint tests whether this saved Unity object is still valid; TryGetConfigurableJoint returns that validity result and the reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._defaultConfigJointInfo

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._disableJointInfo
member.summary: Saves the connected body, six movement modes and six drive settings for restoration after body disabling.

remarks.para: Drives act like motors that push or turn the physical bodies toward position, rotation or movement-speed targets.

When _hasBeenEnabled is true, OnBodyDisable clears that guard first. If a valid engine joint exists, it copies the connected body, six motion modes and six drives into this snapshot, then frees the motions, zeros the drives and disconnects the connected body. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._doResetConnectedAnchor

remarks.para: A connected anchor is the point where the connection attaches on its connected side. Automatic connected-anchor configuration means Unity calculates that point.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._hasBeenEnabled

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._jointBreakActions

remarks.para: A callback is registered code called to report or carry out an action. After the Update wait, cleanup invokes these callbacks while IsCreatedAtRuntime is true, then clears the list and requests component removal. Scene-joint repair does not dispatch this list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._jointDestroyActions

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint._jointSpace
member.summary: Stores BodyA's captured reference position and rotation relative to BodyB or the fixed scene.

remarks.para: The reference is BodyB's scene position and rotation when BodyB exists and ConfiguredInWorld is false; otherwise it is the fixed scene frame. Position is in meters. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint.angularXDriveBase
member.summary: Supplies the saved spring, damping and force-cap values multiplied by SetAngularXDrive.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection between bodies, and a drive acts like a motor pushing or turning them toward a target. Torque means turning force. Orientation error is the difference from the wanted orientation, and angular velocity means turning speed and direction; its error is the difference from the wanted angular velocity. Angular X and Y/Z refer to the configured joint axes, which need not match the fixed scene axes.

The drive turns the joint toward its rotation/angular-velocity target. Spring supplies restoring torque for orientation error, damper responds to angular-velocity error and maximumForce caps torque. The selected rotationDriveMode chooses Slerp or the angular X/YZ drives; this setter does not change that mode. For angular driving, the force cap is a torque in newton-meters; spring and damper are the engine's angular restoring and damping coefficients.

A JointDrive is a three-value settings structure. SetAngularXDrive multiplies its positionSpring, positionDamper and maximumForce by separate unitless factors. For example, factor 0.5 applies half the corresponding baseline value. Assigning this property or calling SetAngularXDriveBase changes that future baseline; it does not apply a drive until SetAngularXDrive or a separate engine-joint operation runs.
The full saved default configuration and the body-disable snapshot are separate stores. Capturing or applying that full configuration does not automatically synchronize this baseline.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager.Instance
member.summary: Returns the registered overlap-manager plugin, caching the first successful lookup.

remarks.para: This manager aggregates collider contacts into object-level enter and exit notifications. The getter consults Marrow’s plugin registry when its cached reference is empty; it does not create a new manager by itself.

With the plugin registry available, a failed lookup leaves the result null and can be tried again on a later read. Once a manager is found, subsequent reads return that cached reference. The getter expects the plugin registry itself to be available during game startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager._getComponentsTriggerCache
member.summary: Temporarily holds the trigger components that will receive a newly recorded enter or exit.

remarks.para: When an object-level pair begins or ends, the manager gathers all OverlapTrigger components on the trigger’s own GameObject into this reused list. It queues a notification for each component, then clears the list. It does not search the trigger’s child hierarchy through this collection.

The list is working storage for notification recipients, not the collection of other objects currently overlapping the trigger. Its contents are replaced and cleared by later contact processing, so it is not persistent trigger configuration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager._helperPairLookup
member.summary: Keeps reverse associations so disabling an overlapping object can clean up every trigger that recorded it.

remarks.para: The key is the other, overlapping GameObject. Its value is a set of trigger GameObjects associated with that object. This is the reverse direction from _overlapCounts, whose outer key is the trigger object.

The first contact for a pair adds the trigger object to this set. If the other object has neither an OverlapTrigger nor an OverlapStateHelper, the manager adds an OverlapStateHelper to it; that helper reports when the object is disabled so recorded overlaps can be cleared.

The last reported contact exit removes the trigger from the set. DisableOverlap uses these reverse associations to clear the disabled object’s positive pair counts and queue the corresponding exits. Removing an association does not destroy the helper component, and an empty set can remain until later object cleanup.
Changing this dictionary directly does not update the count dictionary or event queue. Use the normal enter, exit and disable operations to keep those related records consistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager._manager
member.summary: Stores the manager instance returned by successful plugin lookup.

remarks.para: Instance fills this shared reference from Marrow’s plugin registry when it has not already found a manager. A stored reference directs later callers to that manager’s overlap records and event queue.

Changing this reference alone does not construct a manager’s collections or change its registration with the update loop. Update registration occurs in each manager’s constructor and is removed by its finalizer, so replacing the lookup reference does not unsubscribe a previously registered manager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager._overlapCounts
member.summary: Counts the reported collider contacts for each trigger-object and other-object pair.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape Unity uses to detect contacts between objects. The outer key is the GameObject holding the trigger; the inner key is the other GameObject reported by the contact. The integer counts outstanding contact reports, not distance, elapsed time or an object’s size. Multiple colliders on the same other GameObject can contribute to the same object-level pair.

For example, two enter reports for that same pair raise its count to 2 but queue only the first object-level enter notification. One exit reduces it to 1 and produces no exit notification; the last exit reduces it to 0 and ends the pair.

The first enter creates the pair, queues enter records for the trigger components, then increments its count. An exit decrements the count first; when none remains, it removes the helper association, queues exits and removes the inner pair entry. OnMarrowUpdate delivers these notifications later, so recipients see bookkeeping that may already include newer reports.

These are records maintained from reports, not a fresh overlap scan. DisableOverlap can clear recorded contacts when an object is disabled even if it has not physically moved away. Editing the counts alone does not maintain the helper associations or send notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.OverlapTriggerManager._triggerEvents
member.summary: Stores enter and exit notifications until the game update loop delivers them.

remarks.para: Each record contains its event type, receiving OverlapTrigger component and the other GameObject. Enter means the first recorded contact began an object-level pair; exit means the last contact ended or the pair was cleared. These are saved notification arguments rather than physical Collider references.

OnMarrowUpdate removes records in queue order and calls OnOverlapEnter or OnOverlapExit on the saved trigger, passing the other object. These callbacks are routines called to report the overlap change. Multiple trigger components on one trigger GameObject each receive their own queued record.

The dictionaries are updated by the enter, exit or disable processing before delivery. Clearing an object’s recorded overlap does not remove already queued notifications. Both an enter and its later exit can therefore be waiting for the same drain.
Changing this queue does not change the contact counts. Events added during a drain can be delivered before that drain ends; the queue does not enforce a fixed one-frame delay.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.PolyLineData.polyVerts
member.summary: Stores the ordered sampled positions and directions that PolyLine uses for path queries.

remarks.para: Each PolyLineVert contains a position, a tangent along the path, a normal describing its orientation, and forward/backward directions used by the lookup routines. Positions are in the consuming PolyLine Transform's local frame: relative to that object rather than fixed world coordinates. Position lengths use Unity distance units; the direction vectors describe orientation, not extra positions.

PolyLine.GetPointAtIndex converts a stored position to world space through its Transform and converts tangent and normal directions using its orientation. Moving, rotating, or scaling that Transform therefore changes where the stored local points appear in the scene. For example, local position (1, 0, 0) is one local distance unit along the PolyLine's X direction, with world placement determined by that Transform.

The query methods differ in their output frame. GetNearestPoint converts its world input to local coordinates for the search but returns the stored local position, tangent, and normal directly. GetNearestPointFromIndex instead converts its outputs to world space. Interpret each result in the frame returned by that particular method.

During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, PolyLine selects its stored-table mode if this array is non-null and nonempty, then keeps the same array reference. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Editing an entry in that shared array can affect later queries, including other initialized components sharing it; replacing the asset's array leaves an already initialized component holding its old reference.

Supply ordered, valid vertex entries and consistent direction data and segmentResolution. A nonempty array only passes the startup test; it does not prove the geometry is complete or suitable for every query. Changing the resolution or totalDistance does not create, reorder, or repair these entries. An empty table does not make the inspected nearest-point and linear-distance methods generate replacement samples from the spline.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.PolyLineData.segmentResolution
member.summary: Selects the nominal local step that PolyLine uses to estimate which stored samples to search.

remarks.para: This is a choice from SegmentResolution, not a directly editable float length. SegmentDistance maps Millimeter, Centimeter, Decimeter, and Meter to 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, and 1 Unity distance unit respectively. The metric names apply when one unit represents one meter; Transform scaling can change world distances between the stored local points.

PolyLine's linear-distance lookup divides the requested local distance by the cached step to estimate a sample index, then examines the stored vertex geometry. A smaller step means more nominal intervals for the same distance, but changing this choice alone does not add samples or improve an unchanged table. For example, choosing Centimeter for vertices prepared at Meter spacing gives a 0.01 step alongside the old one-unit table, so the metadata no longer matches the geometry.

PolyLine copies the selected step during Awake, Unity's initialization callback; a callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Later edits change what SegmentDistance returns on this asset but do not update that initialized component's cached step. Prepare a table and resolution that agree before the component initializes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.PolyLineData.totalDistance
member.summary: Stores the total-distance metadata supplied with this sampled-path asset.

remarks.para: This is a stored number, rather than a live sum of the distances between polyVerts. PolyLine copies it into its own cached total-distance field during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Editing the asset later does not update that cached scalar automatically.

The inspected PolyLine methods GetNearestPoint, GetNearestPointFromIndex, GetPointAtIndex, and GetPointAtLinearDistance determine their positions from the vertex table and do not use this cached total-distance value to stretch or regenerate that table. Changing totalDistance alone therefore does not move their stored path points or repair a mismatched sampling step.

Use the distance convention with which this metadata was prepared. The checked asset method and startup-copy path do not measure this value, establish its authoring frame, or convert it for a scaled Transform. It should not be treated as a freshly measured world-space path length merely because the PolyLine was moved or scaled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings._initialPos
member.summary: Stores the parent-relative position used by the optional enable-time pose reset.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) captures transform.localPosition here. Its coordinates are local Unity distances relative to the current parent, so parent scale and movement affect the corresponding world position. It is not a continuously updated spawn-world position.

OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) restores it only when resetOnEnable is true, then synchronizes the Rigidbody’s world position. Changing this cache changes the next reset position; it does not immediately teleport the body. With an unchanged parent of scale 1, adding 0.1 to local X moves the next reset 10 cm along the parent’s X direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings._initialRot
member.summary: Stores the parent-relative orientation used by the optional enable-time pose reset.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) captures transform.localRotation as a quaternion, which represents one orientation with four components rather than four separate degree angles. OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) restores that local orientation when resetOnEnable is true and synchronizes the resulting world rotation to the Rigidbody.

Changing this cache affects the next reset, not the body’s current rotation. If the parent turns between initialization and re-enabling, restoring the same local quaternion produces a correspondingly turned world orientation. The identity quaternion means aligned with the parent; it is an example rather than a guaranteed captured value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings._nativeMass
member.summary: Stores the initialized Rigidbody mass used as the baseline for scale-based mass adjustment.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) reads the Rigidbody’s mass in kilograms before this component’s OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) scaling. With scaleMass true, each enable assigns this value times the product of the object’s world-scale components. Each component is a unitless size multiplier including scale inherited from parents. For example, a baseline of 2 kg at scale (2, 2, 2) requests 16 kg.

Editing the baseline does not immediately change the body’s mass. It affects the next OnEnable scaling; with scaleMass false that path does not read it. Each enable starts from this saved baseline rather than compounding the current mass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.collidersToIgnore
member.summary: Lists the other collision shapes paired with localColliders when applying collision ignores.

remarks.para: Start (the routine Unity calls for this component’s first startup) requires a nonnull array and enables ignoring for these pairs when it is nonempty. Provide a nonnull collidersToIgnore array before Start, even when no pairs should be ignored; use an empty array for that case. A null array causes a null-reference failure during startup. IgnoreColliders can later enable or clear the same listed pairs. Other game code, including spawn decorators, can replace this list and call IgnoreColliders immediately.

Assigning a new array alone does not change physics. Call IgnoreColliders(true) to apply the new pairs, and clear old pairs before removing them if they should collide again. The routine requires valid localColliders and collider entries; it does not search for missing local shapes or disable all collisions on this object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.comOverride
member.summary: Specifies the balance-point reference that Start (the routine Unity calls for this component’s first startup) and SetCenter convert into the body’s center of mass.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale; rb is the cached reference to the Rigidbody physics component.

The routines use this Transform’s world position, then convert it through the cached Rigidbody’s transform. Its own localPosition is not copied directly, so it can be under a different parent. Moving the balance point changes how the body balances and rotates without moving its visible transform.

Start applies it once when both references exist. To apply a later movement or replacement of the override, call SetCenter. Missing override leaves that operation unchanged. The world-to-local conversion includes scale, whereas Unity’s centerOfMass uses position and rotation without scale; for a scaled body, the physical center need not coincide exactly with the marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.disableITCalc
member.summary: Keeps the initialized inertia tensor and center of mass as explicit values for a non-kinematic body.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion. A kinematic body has its movement controlled by scripts instead of ordinary physics forces. The center of mass is the body’s balance point.

During Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization), if this flag is true and the Rigidbody is not kinematic, the routine reads the current inertia tensor and center of mass and assigns the same values back. This preserves their current numbers while making them custom values instead of values Unity automatically derives from the attached collider shapes.

An inertia tensor describes resistance to rotation; this flag is unrelated to controller input or an “interaction tensor.” The later iTensorMult adjustment can still change the tensor, and Start (the routine Unity calls for this component’s first startup) or SetCenter can replace the center of mass. Changing the flag later does not restore automatic calculation; the Rigidbody’s reset APIs are needed for that.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.drawCom
member.summary: No center-of-mass drawing was verified for this flag in the audited RigidbodySettings class.

remarks.para: The complete audited class has no drawing or gizmo routine that reads this flag. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to display a center-of-mass marker through this component. This finding covers RigidbodySettings’s native methods only; other code and mods were not exhaustively checked.
The flag also does not choose the center-of-mass location in those routines. Use comOverride and SetCenter for that verified operation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.iTensorMult
member.summary: Scales the body’s resistance to rotation when Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) applies its inertia tensor.

remarks.para: The inertia tensor describes how hard it is to accelerate rotation around each principal axis of the body, meaning its reference directions for measuring rotational inertia. Awake multiplies all three current tensor components by this unitless factor unless it is approximately 1. For example, 2 doubles each component; ordinary torque (twisting force) then needs twice as much rotational effort for the same acceleration. A factor of 0 writes zero tensor components, which Unity treats as infinite rotational inertia, rather than zero resistance. To restore automatic collider-based calculation, use Rigidbody.ResetInertiaTensor instead of using 0 as a reset.

The constructor initializes the multiplier to 1. This is an initialization adjustment, not a continuously applied effect: changing the field later does not update the tensor. Manually repeating Awake can multiply an already scaled tensor again. The VelocityChange helpers, the two float SetVelocity/SetAngularVelocity overloads, add a spin-speed change directly, so this factor does not scale their requested change like an ordinary force torque.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.ignoreHierarchy
member.summary: Makes startup ignore collisions between the colliders on this object and its active children.

remarks.para: A collider is the shape physics uses to detect contact.

Start (the routine Unity calls for this component’s first startup) gathers these colliders and enables collision ignoring for the gathered pairs when the flag is true. This can include colliders belonging to child bodies; it is not restricted to the cached rb or the localColliders array.

Changing the flag after Start does not update existing collision pairs. Call IgnoreHierarchy to apply the operation at a later time; that method always enables ignoring, even if this flag is false. Clearing the flag does not restore pairs that were already ignored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.localColliders
member.summary: Supplies this component’s side of the collider pairs processed by IgnoreColliders and the startup ignore list.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Each collider here is paired with every entry in collidersToIgnore. These are collision shapes, not necessarily every shape belonging to the cached Rigidbody. The complete audited RigidbodySettings class reads this array but does not automatically gather or assign it from the hierarchy.

Provide valid collider entries before applying the ignore operation. For example, 2 entries here and 3 ignored colliders create 6 pairs. Changing the array alone does not update physics; apply IgnoreColliders again. Pairs removed from the list are not automatically restored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.maxAv
member.summary: Sets the requested spin-speed limit applied to the Rigidbody during Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization), with a minimum of 60 radians per second.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake assigns the larger of this value and 60 to Rigidbody.maxAngularVelocity. For example, 30 still applies 60, while 100 applies 100. One radian per second is about 57.3 degrees per second; this controls the physics spin limit, not a constant target spin.

The constructor initializes the field to 60, but configured instances can hold other values. Changing this field after Awake does not automatically update the Rigidbody’s limit; OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) does not reapply it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.rb
member.summary: Caches the physics body that receives this component’s settings and movement helpers.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) finds the Rigidbody on the same object. OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) looks it up again if the cached reference is missing, and returns if no body exists. The velocity helpers instead require the cache to exist; they do not perform that lookup.

Changing this reference redirects later body operations, but the stored mass and pose still belong to the initialization capture until updated separately. OnEnable’s pose reset uses this component’s transform before synchronizing the cached body, so pointing the cache at an unrelated object can mix two objects’ state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.resetOnEnable
member.summary: Restores the saved local position and rotation whenever this component becomes enabled.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

Awake (Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to perform initialization) captures the pose in _initialPos and _initialRot. With this flag true, OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) restores that parent-relative pose and writes the resulting world position and rotation to the Rigidbody. A changed parent can change where the object returns in the world.

With the flag false, the enable routine preserves the current pose but still sets linear and angular velocity to zero. Changing the flag while the component is already enabled does not reset the body immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.RigidbodySettings.scaleMass
member.summary: On each enable, scales the saved Rigidbody mass by the object’s effective world-scale volume.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

When true, OnEnable (the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled) assigns _nativeMass × lossyScale.x × lossyScale.y × lossyScale.z. Here _nativeMass is the initially captured mass in kilograms, and each lossyScale component is a unitless size multiplier including scale inherited from parents. For a 2 kg baseline, uniform scale 2 produces 16 kg; a scale (2, 1, 1) produces 4 kg. Doubling all three dimensions multiplies the requested mass by 8, not 2.

The calculation uses the raw scale components, without an absolute-value correction in this routine. When false, OnEnable leaves mass alone. Toggling the flag or changing scale while already enabled does not run this calculation immediately. OnEnable still clears both velocities with either flag value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.AnchorRotation
member.summary: Calculates the local orientation of the contact layout from the configured primary and secondary directions.

remarks.para: A quaternion is an orientation value that represents a rotation. Normalizing rescales a nonzero direction to length one without turning it. These vectors are unitless directions, not distances.

_axis becomes the layout’s X direction along the path, and _secondaryAxis supplies its up reference. For each direction, the getter divides by its length only when that length is greater than 0.00001; at or below the threshold it uses a zero vector, including for a small nonzero input. It then builds the remaining perpendicular directions; increasing a vector’s length does not increase contact spacing.
This is a quaternion in the body’s local coordinate frame. It depends on the configured directions, not on the existing contacts’ positions or the body’s current world rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.FrontContact
member.summary: Returns the unrotated offset for the front half of the configured contact layout.

remarks.para: _anchor is the layout-centre offset in metres along the body’s local axes.

The vector is (_size.y / 2, 0, 0), where _size.y is the full configured front/back spacing in metres; dividing by two gives half that spacing. For example, spacing 1 metre gives (0.5, 0, 0) metres: a 0.5-metre layout-X offset, or 50 centimetres.

This is a layout-frame offset. It contains neither the configured anchor offset nor a world position on the path. AnchorRotation is the calculated orientation that turns layout X/travel, Y/up and Z/side coordinates into the body’s own local axes. To form a local anchor position, rotate it by AnchorRotation and add _anchor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.RightContact
member.summary: Returns the unrotated offset for the side half of the configured contact layout.

remarks.para: _anchor is the layout-centre offset in metres along the body’s local axes.

The vector is (0, 0, _size.x / 2), where _size.x is the full side-to-side spacing in metres; dividing by two gives half that spacing. For example, spacing 0.4 metres gives (0, 0, 0.2) metres: a 0.2-metre layout-Z offset, or 20 centimetres.

This is a layout-frame offset, not an existing contact’s world position. AnchorRotation is the calculated orientation that turns layout X/travel, Y/up and Z/side coordinates into the body’s own local axes; rotate it by AnchorRotation and add _anchor to obtain the corresponding local anchor offset. Four uses this side spacing for its rectangular layout.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint.Size
member.summary: Returns the full configured contact spacing from as a vector in the anchor layout’s axes.

remarks.para: The result in metres is (_size.y, 0, _size.x): X is front/back spacing, Y is zero, and Z is side-to-side spacing. _size is the saved two-component layout size in metres. This getter rearranges those values; it does not measure a collider, apply body scale, or find the current contacts’ world separation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint._anchor
member.summary: Chooses the body-relative center of the contact layout and the location from which the solver follows the path.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. _anchor is the layout-centre offset in metres along the body’s local axes.

The offset is expressed in the body’s local axes. One uses it as the contact anchor; Two and Four place their anchor points around it using the configured spacing and axis orientation. Attach copies the resulting offsets into the generated contact joints, rounded to approximately millimetre steps.

Changing this after attachment changes subsequent solver query positions but does not move the connected-anchor copies already installed in those joints. Query placement uses TransformPoint and therefore includes body scale; GetContactOriginInWorld and the Contact’s setup pose use rotation and translation without scaling this offset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint._angularXDrive
member.summary: Stores the restoring strength, damping and torque cap for twist around the path direction.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint._axis
member.summary: Chooses which body-local direction acts as the layout’s X axis for travel and twist along the path.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. Normalizing rescales a nonzero direction to length one without turning it. These vectors are unitless directions, not distances.

AnchorRotation divides this vector by its length only when that length is greater than 0.00001; at or below the threshold, including a small nonzero input, it uses a zero vector. It combines the result with _secondaryAxis, the local up reference, to orient the contact layout. Its length is not a speed or spacing multiplier. Use a meaningful direction distinct from the secondary direction so the frame can be formed.

One uses the configured anchor and applies the angular and sideways-motion restrictions directly. Two uses _size.y for a front/back pair; Four also uses _size.x for side spacing. remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body whose movement and rotation Unity physics simulates.
A Contact is a generated physics body joined to the main Rigidbody; the joint constrains how the two bodies can move relative to each other.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback—a routine Unity calls to prepare the component—creates the list and Attach appends the chosen layout. The solver uses fixed list indices for One, Two or Four, while refresh, enable, disable and destruction operations visit every stored entry.

Replacing or removing entries does not destroy their generated objects automatically, and adding an entry does not change _contactCount. Keep the list consistent with the layout; otherwise some contacts can remain outside solver updates or expected entries can be missing.

remarks.para: This is an integer index into the selected PolyLine’s stored vertex array, not a distance, time, or normalized progress from zero to one. Attach initializes it from a nearest-point query; Solve and its two-point helper overwrite it with a later nearest-sample result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint._forward
member.summary: Stores the shared reference direction used to offset Four’s contact targets sideways.

remarks.para: Multiplying this unitless direction by that metre-valued spacing produces an offset in metres.

The class initializes it to (0, 0, 1), a unit direction. Four rotates this vector by the calculated path orientation and multiplies it by half of _size.x, the configured full side-to-side distance in metres, then adds and subtracts that offset for its two side targets.

It has no distance units and is shared by all SplineJoint instances. Changing its direction changes the direction of the side offsets, while changing its length scales their separation. Despite its name, it supplies the sideways layout direction here rather than the tangent used to travel along the path.

A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. A drive applies push/pull force or turning force through that joint to move toward a target. DampenContactDrive is the record of damping strength and the force cap. The damping coefficient is newtons of force per metre-per-second speed error (N·s/m). A newton (N) is a unit of push/pull force.

positionDamper corrects desired minus current relative speed, in N·s/m; maximumForce caps the resulting drive force in newtons. With a zero target speed the damper resists travel, while a nonzero _linearXDriveSpeed—the saved requested relative path speed in metres per second along contact X, the path direction—can make it propel the body. A drive is the joint motor applying push/pull force toward the requested relative speed: the coefficient determines how strongly it corrects speed error, and the cap limits that correction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.SplineJoint._size
member.summary: Sets the front/back and side-to-side spacing of the generated contact layout.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated helper physics body. A physics joint connects it to the main Rigidbody, the body Unity physics simulates, and limits how the two bodies move relative to each other. _size.y is the full front/back distance in metres; _size.x is the full side-to-side distance in metres.

The component names are easy to misread: y is the full front/back spacing along layout X; x is the full side-to-side spacing along layout Z. Two uses y, and Four uses both. Attach offsets each end or side by half its corresponding spacing around _anchor, the layout-centre offset in metres in the body’s local axes, rotated by AnchorRotation—the calculated orientation that turns layout X/travel, Y/up and Z/side coordinates into those body-local axes. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.Body
member.summary: Gets the body whose zone overlap counts are updated when this tracker enters or leaves a zone.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody groups one physics body and its associated shapes and saved settings. Validate assigns this reference from the supplied body; the Body getter returns the same stored reference without searching the object hierarchy.

An active zone uses the reference as its body-count key. Several trackers belonging to the same body contribute to one overlap count, so a body’s entry is reported when its first tracker enters and departure when its final tracker leaves. The zone also requires hasBody and hasEntity to be true.

Assigning this reference later does not refresh hasBody, the snapshot taken by Awake (Unity’s initialization routine), or transfer existing zone counts to a new body. A missing reference can be null; the stored flag and the reference should not be assumed to stay synchronized automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.Cache
member.summary: Gets the shared lookup that finds registered Trackers from their GameObjects.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, registers each tracker under its own GameObject. A zone receives an overlapping collider, takes that collider’s GameObject and queries this cache to find the tracker’s body and entity references. This links a physics overlap to the game’s ownership and zone-count bookkeeping.

The getter creates a new empty cache when _cache is null; it does not scan the scene to register every Tracker. Trackers that have not run their registration are consequently not guaranteed to be present. OnDestroy removes the tracker and clears the shared reference if the cache becomes empty. A disabled tracker can remain registered until destruction.
A collider is an invisible physics shape. A GameObject is a scene object that holds components such as the Tracker and collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.Collider
member.summary: Gets the tracker’s selected overlap-detection shape, also supplied to its disable-notification routines. The owning and are stored separately: a body groups one physics unit and its shapes, while an entity groups the object’s bodies and interaction state.

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible physics shape. Validate finds or creates the required shape on the tracker’s own GameObject, sets it as a trigger that reports overlaps without blocking movement, and stores the selected component here. This is the tracker shape, rather than the owning body’s Rigidbody or its whole collection of solid colliders.

OnDeactivate passes this stored collider to every registered notification routine. A zone uses its GameObject to look up this Tracker in Cache and process the corresponding departure. Collider returns the stored reference without finding a new component each time.

Replacing the reference alone does not configure the new shape, change the owner references or update the cache key. If it points to a collider on another GameObject, the zone’s lookup uses that other object and may fail to find this tracker.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physics movement.

member.summary: The registered routines called with this tracker’s collider when OnDeactivate reports deactivation.

remarks.para: Each callback is a routine registered to perform or report an action. AddDisableCallback appends a routine, and RemoveDisableCallback removes one matching entry. The list allows duplicate registrations. OnDeactivate invokes it from last entry to first, passing the currently stored Collider as the sole argument. A collider is an invisible physics shape.
