member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.hasBody
member.summary: Records whether the Body reference existed when Awake ran, and helps gate zone overlap processing.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization routine. After registering the tracker in Cache, it sets this Boolean using Unity’s existence check on the stored Body reference. This is a snapshot, not a getter that checks the current reference every time.

An active zone requires both hasBody and hasEntity before accepting this tracker’s entry or processing its departure. If either flag is false when the zone receives a new entry, that entry is ignored. Changing a flag to false after the tracker was counted does not remove its existing counts and can prevent normal exit processing from clearing them. Validate and later owner assignment do not refresh these flags.
Setting this flag alone does not supply a missing Body reference or re-process existing overlaps. Keep the flag and stored owner reference consistent when arranging tracker setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Tracker.hasEntity
member.summary: Records whether the Entity reference existed when Awake ran, and helps gate zone overlap processing.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization routine. After registering the tracker in Cache, it sets this Boolean using Unity’s existence check on the stored Entity reference. This is a snapshot, not a getter that checks the current reference every time.

An active zone requires both hasBody and hasEntity before accepting this tracker’s entry or processing its departure. If either flag is false when the zone receives a new entry, that entry is ignored. Changing a flag to false after the tracker was counted does not remove its existing counts and can prevent normal exit processing from clearing them. Validate and later owner assignment do not refresh these flags.
Setting this flag alone does not supply a missing Entity reference or re-process existing overlaps. Keep the flag and stored owner reference consistent when arranging tracker setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.center
member.summary: Offsets the center of a Sphere or Capsule detection volume along the tracker’s own axes.

remarks.para: A tracker’s collider is an invisible shape used to detect overlaps. For Sphere and Capsule preparation, center is a distance vector in Unity distance units (metres under Unity’s physics convention), measured from the tracker’s origin along its local X, Y and Z directions. It is an offset, rather than an absolute position in the scene. The Bounds and Box branches obtain their centers from the MarrowBody’s bounds instead of reading this field. The body bounds are the enclosing box calculated from the body’s gathered ordinary collision shapes. They provide a center offset relative to the body and full X, Y and Z lengths, rather than an absolute position in the scene.

Preparation calculates localCenter.x = center.x / sx, and likewise for Y and Z. Here localCenter is the offset written to the collider in its local distance units, center is this configured distance vector, and sx, sy and sz are the unitless components of the tracker Transform’s lossyScale: its effective scale after its parents are included. For positive, nonzero scales, the division compensates for that scale. For example, with scale (2, 2, 2), center (0, 1, 0) produces collider center (0, 0.5, 0), placing it one distance unit along the tracker’s up direction after scaling.

The preparation comparison uses the lengths of the old and proposed center vectors, rather than comparing their individual coordinates. It writes the proposed center only when those lengths differ by more than 0.0001 local distance units. Thus an existing center (1, 0, 0) and a proposed center (0, 1, 0) have the same length and this preparation leaves the old center in place, even though their directions differ. Changing this stored field alone does not rerun preparation or move a live collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.direction
member.summary: Chooses the local axis along which a Capsule tracker extends.

remarks.para: A capsule is a cylinder with rounded half-sphere ends. XAxis (0) makes its length run along the tracker’s local X direction, YAxis (1) along local Y, and ZAxis (2) along local Z. These directions turn with the tracker; local Y is the tracker’s up direction and need not point upward in the scene. This setting is passed to the CapsuleCollider during Capsule preparation. The Sphere, Box and Bounds branches do not use it.

For example, a capsule intended to follow a rod can use the rod’s local long axis. The height field controls its total length including the rounded ends, and radius controls its thickness. Selecting another direction rotates that long-axis choice without swapping the stored height and radius. The native new-settings constructor initializes direction to XAxis; serialized content can replace that value. Writing direction later changes the stored setting and does not itself rotate a live collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.height
member.summary: Supplies the nominal total length of a Capsule detection volume, including its rounded ends.

remarks.para: This distance is used only by the Capsule preparation branch. Increasing it increases the proposed capsule length along direction, the tracker-local X, Y or Z axis chosen for its long direction. Height is measured in Unity distance units (metres under Unity’s physics convention). It describes the full capsule, rather than just the cylindrical middle. The native new-settings constructor initializes height to 2; a serialized entry can contain another value.

Preparation proposes localHeight = height * k, where localHeight is the length sent to CapsuleCollider in its local distance units, height is this configured total length, and k = max(1 / sx, 1 / sy, 1 / sz). The values sx, sy and sz are the unitless components of the tracker Transform’s lossyScale, its effective scale including its parents. The reciprocal-scale multiplier k is unitless. It uses all three scale components, rather than only the axis selected by direction. These examples assume positive, nonzero scale: height 2 at scale (2, 2, 2) proposes localHeight 1; at scale (1, 2, 4), k is 1 and the proposed localHeight is 2.

Unity also scales the resulting collider with its Transform, so the configured number is not an unconditional promise of the final world-space length under unequal scales. Preparation writes a new collider height only when the existing and proposed values differ by more than 0.0001 local distance units. Assigning this field does not immediately resize an already prepared tracker; its settings must be applied through preparation again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.isActive
member.summary: Includes this settings entry when a MarrowBody generates its configured trackers.

remarks.para: GenerateTrackers skips this entry when isActive is false. When it is true, generation can reuse a matching child Tracker or create one, then prepare its collider using this entry. A Bounds entry also requires the body’s gathered ordinary collider array to contain at least one collider. Box, Sphere and Capsule entries can pass this particular gate without ordinary colliders. The native new-settings constructor initializes isActive to true; serialized content can choose otherwise.

This is a configuration-inclusion flag, rather than a report of an existing tracker GameObject’s current active state. Setting it to false does not itself disable that object. A later generation pass skips the entry and removes unused candidate child trackers, while candidates used by other included entries can remain. Separate MarrowBody tracker-enable handling controls the objects’ active state during gameplay. For example, an optional Sphere entry can be excluded before regeneration without changing the stored radius or center.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.layer
member.summary: Selects the tracker category used to choose and configure a generated tracker’s Unity physics layer.

remarks.para: The supported category values are Entity (1), Being (2) and Observer (4), from TrackerLayers. Generation maps them to the actual Unity layer indices EntityTracker (26), BeingTracker (27) and ObserverTracker (28). A Unity physics layer is a numbered group used by collision and overlap filtering; this field stores the category value that selects that group. For example, assign Entity’s category value 1 to select EntityTracker, rather than assigning the final layer index 26 here.

GenerateTrackers looks for a reusable direct child Tracker on the mapped layer and creates a child when none is available. Tracker preparation then assigns the corresponding layer for these supported values. Use one category value per entry: this consumer compares exact values, so combining Entity and Being into 3 does not select both categories. The native new-settings constructor initializes layer to 1. Changing the field later does not itself reassign an existing GameObject’s layer or rerun tracker generation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.radius
member.summary: Supplies the nominal center-to-surface distance for a Sphere tracker or the rounded thickness of a Capsule tracker.

remarks.para: Radius is a length in Unity distance units (metres under Unity’s physics convention). A sphere is round in every direction; a capsule uses this radius for its rounded ends and cross-section. Increasing it increases the proposed collider radius when these shapes are prepared. The Bounds and Box preparation branches do not read this field. The native new-settings constructor initializes radius to 0.5; serialized content can replace that value.

Preparation proposes localRadius = radius * k, where localRadius is the radius sent to the collider in its local distance units, radius is this configured distance, and k = max(1 / sx, 1 / sy, 1 / sz). Here sx, sy and sz are the unitless components of the tracker Transform’s lossyScale, the effective scale after including its parents; k is a unitless reciprocal-scale multiplier. For positive, nonzero scale (2, 2, 2), radius 0.5 proposes localRadius 0.25. Scale (1, 2, 4) instead gives k = 1 and proposes localRadius 0.5.

Unity then scales the collider with its Transform. Unequal scales therefore need not produce a final world-space radius equal to this stored number. Preparation writes the proposed radius only when it differs from the current collider radius by more than 0.0001 local distance units. Changing the settings field alone does not resize a live collider; the preparation path must apply it again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.size
member.summary: Stores box dimensions, although the inspected Tracker preparation obtains Box dimensions from the body’s bounds instead.

remarks.para: This is the stored setting intended to describe box dimensions, but the inspected generation and preparation paths do not use it to set the detection box. Its name alone does not establish a physical-unit contract for this unused input. The body bounds are the enclosing box calculated from the body’s gathered ordinary collision shapes. They provide a center offset relative to the body and full X, Y and Z lengths, rather than an absolute position in the scene. In Tracker.Validate’s Box branch, the proposed collider size comes from MarrowBody.Bounds divided component by component by the tracker’s effective Transform scale. The Bounds branch also uses MarrowBody.Bounds, directly. Neither of these two branches reads this stored size vector.

Consequently, setting size to (1, 2, 1) does not make the inspected MarrowBody generation and Tracker preparation paths produce that requested box. Their result follows the body bounds and their shape-specific scale handling. This conclusion is limited to these inspected consumers; it does not establish that no other code can read the field. Writing this setting does not itself rebuild or resize a live tracker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettings.type
member.summary: Chooses which collider shape is prepared for this tracker settings entry.

remarks.para: Bounds (0) prepares a box from MarrowBody.Bounds. The body bounds are the enclosing box calculated from the body’s gathered ordinary collision shapes. They provide a center offset relative to the body and full X, Y and Z lengths, rather than an absolute position in the scene. Box (1) also prepares a box from those bounds, with center and size divided by the tracker’s effective scale along each axis; the inspected Box branch does not use this entry’s center or size fields. Sphere (2) prepares a round collider from center and radius. Capsule (3) prepares a cylinder with rounded ends from center, radius, height and direction. Prepared shape branches mark the collider as a trigger: an invisible volume for detecting overlaps instead of a solid surface that pushes other objects away.

During MarrowBody generation, the entry must have isActive true. Bounds also requires at least one gathered ordinary collider on the body; the other three type values pass that particular gate without one. Generation reuses a suitable child tracker or creates a child, then preparation reuses a collider of the needed class or adds one. A matching collider object can therefore remain while its settings are applied. The native new-settings constructor initializes type to Bounds. Assigning type alone changes the stored choice and does not immediately replace a live collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettingsGroup.layers
member.summary: Stores the group's declared tracker-category mask; generation uses each settings entry's own layer.

remarks.para: TrackerLayers is a set of flags naming Entity, Being, and Observer categories. Flags form a mask: category choices that can be combined in one value. A collider is a physics shape, and a collision layer is a Unity category used to filter which objects can interact. This field stores the group-level declaration of those categories. They correspond to separate tracker collision layers, which let physics filtering distinguish detection categories.

In the inspected MarrowBody.GenerateTrackers path, this mask is not used to choose which entries are generated or which collision layer a generated tracker receives. That path reads settings and each active entry's layer instead. For example, an active entry marked Observer is processed as an Observer tracker even if this group mask says Entity.

Changing this mask alone does not replace the settings array, regenerate tracker objects, or retarget an existing collider. To change the category used by that generation path, prepare the individual entry's layer and run the body's corresponding validation or generation operation. The constructor initializes the group declaration to Entity alongside its single Entity settings entry; later field edits do not repeat that construction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.TrackerSettingsGroup.settings
member.summary: Stores the individual detection-volume settings that MarrowBody processes when generating trackers.

remarks.para: A collider is a physics shape used to detect contacts. A direct child is an object immediately one level beneath the body. Each TrackerSettings entry describes one candidate volume: whether it is active, its tracker category, and its shape and dimensions. GenerateTrackers processes active entries, reusing a direct child tracker with the matching category layer or creating a new one, then applies the entry through Tracker.Validate. The resulting tracker is stored in the body's _trackers array.

Bounds means the recorded enclosing box of the body's gathered physics shapes. Bounds entries use that box and are processed only when ordinary body colliders were gathered. The checked Tracker.Validate Box branch also uses this recorded body box, with object-scale adjustment, rather than the entry's size; Sphere and Capsule use the entry's configured measurements. Active explicit Box, Sphere, or Capsule entries can be processed without ordinary colliders. Generated collider branches use triggers, which detect overlapping objects rather than form solid surfaces. Existing Plug-layer trackers are retained separately from the configured entries.

This array supplies generation; assigning a new array or editing an entry alone does not immediately rebuild existing tracker GameObjects or their collider geometry. Prepare a valid group, array, and non-null entries before the body's validation path calls generation. The generator may remove unused direct child tracker candidates while preparing its result.

For example, an active Sphere entry marked Being can request a spherical detection volume on the Being tracker layer when generation applies it. Changing only group.layers does not create that entry. Constructing a new TrackerSettingsGroup initially supplies one active Bounds entry marked Entity; this array can subsequently be authored differently.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig._lastFixedTime
member.summary: Stores the physics-clock time at which OnUpdate last refreshed the saved animated skeleton.

remarks.para: The value is a double in seconds, using Time.fixedTimeAsDouble. OnAwake initializes it during RigManager’s Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to perform initialization). OnUpdate replaces it only after copying the animation rig’s supported transforms into lastRig.

OnUpdate skips that copy while the current physics time is less than or equal to the saved value. For example, after the marker reaches 1.02 seconds, another frame with physics time 1.02 keeps the saved skeleton; a later time of 1.04 permits a new copy. These times are illustrative, not a fixed game timestep.

This is not the interpolation fraction or a timer that changes the physics clock. Editing it changes when the snapshot refresh passes its check. OnFixedUpdate calculates interpolation timing from the controller rig’s current and previous pose timestamps, without updating this marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig._lastRig
member.summary: Supplies the saved skeleton used as the earlier transform endpoint for physics-step interpolation.

remarks.para: World positions are measured in metres.

This is a reference to a configured Rig object, not an automatically selected previous player or avatar. OnUpdate copies supported transforms from manager.animationRig into this rig after physics time advances. OnFixedUpdate blends from these stored transforms toward the current animation rig’s transforms.

Keep its required skeleton transforms assigned. The stored centerOfPressure reference, pelvis and both hands use scene world positions and rotations; the other supported body transforms store parent-relative rotations. SetAvatar adjusts its skeleton positions for the avatar’s proportions alongside this interpolation rig.
Changing the reference redirects later snapshot copies and interpolation reads; it does not clone a previous pose into the new object immediately. The lastRig property returns this same reference.
A Transform stores an object’s position and rotation. Here centerOfPressure is the rig reference whose position and orientation anchor this body snapshot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig._lastUpdateBodyPose
member.summary: Keeps the older of the two remapped pose samples blended during a physics update.

remarks.para: A BodyPose groups body orientations, limb-extension values and other pose data. OnEarlyUpdate first copies the contents of _updateBodyPose into this buffer, before replacing _updateBodyPose with the latest manager.remapHeptaRig.bodyPose. The constructor creates a separate object for each buffer.

OnFixedUpdate blends from this older sample toward _updateBodyPose into this rig’s bodyPose. It uses the controller rig’s current and previous timestamp difference to choose the fraction, and that fraction is not limited to 0 through 1. It can therefore extend beyond the two samples rather than always stay between them.

Editing this buffer can change the next interpolated pose contents, but the next OnEarlyUpdate replaces them. Keep it assigned and distinct from _updateBodyPose; if both references point to the same object, capturing the new sample also overwrites the older sample. Editing its timestamp alone does not set the interpolation fraction.

Pose timestamps in the controller and these buffers are times in seconds. The blend fraction is unitless: 0 selects the older sample, 1 the newer and 0.5 halfway. A fraction outside that range continues the blend past one of the samples rather than keeping the result between them. The controller times choose the fraction; the buffer timestamps remain part of the copied contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig._updateBodyPose
member.summary: Keeps the newest remapped pose sample used by the physics-step interpolation.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate copies this buffer into _lastUpdateBodyPose first, then fills it from manager.remapHeptaRig.bodyPose. That source contains the tracked body pose adapted to the avatar’s proportions. The constructor creates a BodyPose object for this buffer; a BodyPose groups rotations, limb-extension values and other pose data.

OnFixedUpdate uses this as the newer endpoint when blending into this rig’s bodyPose. The time fraction comes from controller pose timestamps and can be outside 0 through 1. The buffer’s own timestamp is copied with its contents but is not the clock reference used to calculate that fraction.

Changing this sample can change the next blended pose and will be replaced by the next early capture. Keep this and _lastUpdateBodyPose as distinct assigned objects; sharing one object loses the old/new distinction.

Pose timestamps in the controller and these buffers are times in seconds. The blend fraction is unitless: 0 selects the older sample, 1 the newer and 0.5 halfway. A fraction outside that range continues the blend past one of the samples rather than keeping the result between them. The controller times choose the fraction; the buffer timestamps remain part of the copied contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InterpRig.lastRig
member.summary: Returns the configured saved skeleton used as the earlier endpoint when interpolating animated body transforms.

remarks.para: World positions are measured in metres.

This returns _lastRig directly, without making a copy or selecting another rig. OnUpdate fills the referenced rig with the animation rig’s supported transforms once physics time advances. OnFixedUpdate then blends from that saved skeleton toward the current animated skeleton.

The reference does not mean “the avatar used before the last avatar swap.” Its centerOfPressure reference, pelvis and both hands represent saved scene world positions and rotations; its other supported body rotations are local to their parents. The rig and its required transforms must already be configured.
A Transform stores an object’s position and rotation. Here centerOfPressure is the rig reference whose position and orientation anchor this body snapshot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.bodySlots
member.summary: Lists body holster containers whose placement settings can be mirrored for weapons and tools.

remarks.para: A SlotContainer describes where a holster is attached to the player body. SlotContainer.Awake, Unity's initialization callback, saves degreesFromCenter as the starting angle, then marks the container ready before optional child setup. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Later flips restore or negate that saved angle; directly editing degreesFromCenter does not update the saved starting value. FlipSlot sends its first Boolean choice to ready entries here; it restores or negates each flippable container's originally cached degreesFromCenter angle. The angle is in degrees around the body, and changing it supplies settings for placement rather than moving the object inside FlipSlot.

PhysicsRig.SetBodySlot processes this array to position its containers using the avatar and each container's settings. Keep entries valid; unready containers are skipped by FlipSlot, while null arrays and null entries are not silently skipped. Editing this array does not by itself register names in m_InventorySlots or insert weapons into its slots.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.m_InventorySlots
member.summary: Maps registered names to the objects used for insertion and removal subscriptions.

remarks.para: RegisterSlot creates this dictionary when first needed and keeps the first slot for each name. The subscription and unsubscription methods search it for an exact registered name. With a valid dictionary, a missing name is ignored; before any dictionary exists, those methods are not safe no-ops. Register your slot before attaching listeners.

This lookup is separate from bodySlots and specialItems, which list containers for body placement. Editing it does not move holsters or move stored items. Listeners are attached to the slot objects themselves: replacing or clearing an entry does not detach listeners from the previous object or transfer them to a replacement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Inventory.specialItems
member.summary: Lists utility holster containers whose forearm side is selected separately from body slots.

remarks.para: This is the separate container group intended for special utility holsters, such as keycard storage. That grouping alone does not check which item is inserted. A SlotContainer describes where a holster is attached to the player body; it is separate from the InventorySlot that stores an item reference and reports changes.

FlipSlot applies its second Boolean choice to ready entries: true sets bodyRegion to the left forearm, false to the right forearm. It does not check flippable in this group or mirror the cached body-slot angle. PhysicsRig.SetBodySlot later uses the configured region to place the container. Supply valid arrays and entries; assigning this group does not register a name or place an item in a slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.itemGameObject
member.summary: The scene GameObject currently recorded in this slot.

remarks.para: For a Hand’s slot, attachment code records the gripped object’s host GameObject here. This is the actual object reference, not a warehouse crate description or asset identifier.

Insert reports an old live item before replacing this field, then reports insertion after storing the new value. Remove reports the old item before clearing this field. Both listeners receive the InventorySlot and read this field for the relevant item.

Assigning this field directly changes the record without sending those notifications or making a physical connection. Use the slot routines when you need their reporting behavior. Direct insertion into a slot holding a live item requires a removal listener; its replacement path does not guard an absent slotRemoveEvent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.slotInsertEvent
member.summary: Insertion callbacks called after Insert stores the new item reference.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Each routine receives this InventorySlot, not the inserted GameObject directly. Read the supplied slot’s itemGameObject for the new item.

When replacing a live item, the removal report runs before the old reference is replaced; the insertion report runs afterward. Insert does not check that its new GameObject is nonnull before sending an assigned insertion callback.

Use add_slotInsertEvent and remove_slotInsertEvent to add or remove a listener. Registering does not replay the current item or insert anything. Registering the same callback more than once can call it more than once; keep your registration and removal balanced.
The exposed field holds the combined routines. Replacing it directly replaces the stored callback chain rather than inserting an item.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InventorySlot.slotRemoveEvent
member.summary: Removal callbacks called while the slot still records the old live item.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Each routine receives this InventorySlot, not the old GameObject directly. Read the supplied slot’s itemGameObject during the callback to inspect the item being removed.

Remove sends this report only for a live recorded item and an assigned callback, then clears the field after the report returns. Insert into an occupied slot reports removal before replacing the item; that insertion path requires this callback to be assigned.

Use add_slotRemoveEvent and remove_slotRemoveEvent to add or remove a listener. Registering does not immediately report or remove the current item. Repeated registration of the same routine can create repeated calls, so balance registrations and removals.
The exposed field holds the combined routines. Replacing it directly changes the callback chain without clearing the item or disconnecting a grab.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager.__c__DisplayClass7_0.et
member.summary: Temporarily stores the found while selecting an export table for an object.

remarks.para: A scene export table holds named references to Unity objects, so a lookup can identify the object through that table. This field belongs to a compiler-made helper used by FindSuitableExportTableForObject. For a component, a piece of behavior attached to a Unity scene object, the lookup first stores the table found on that object or its parents. If none is found there, a callback, a routine called to perform a search step, checks top-level scene objects with the required name and writes their SceneExportTable component into this field when found.

The lookup copies the successful reference to its output. This is temporary search storage, rather than a setting that registers a table or changes its exported objects. Use FindSuitableExportTableForObject for the lookup; changing this helper field can change the stored result but does not start the search.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager._exportTableOfLastResort
member.summary: Supplies the fallback table used when choosing an export table for an unindexed Unity object that is not a Component.

remarks.para: A Component is an item attached to a GameObject, such as a Light or script. FindSuitableExportTableForObject uses this fallback for other live Unity objects when its cached object-to-ID lookup has not supplied a table. Component objects take its parent or scene-table search path instead.

The manager's setup leaves this reference null until a table is supplied. Setting it changes future table-selection calls; it does not load that table's exports, index its objects, or link waiting references. TryGetObject resolves IDs from its caches and does not consult this fallback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager._sceneExportIndex
member.summary: Maps each indexed object ID to the SceneExportTable recorded as its owner for object queries and linking callbacks.

remarks.para: The key is an exported object's ID string, such as door-switch-01. It is not a scene name. Several IDs can point to the same scene table. LoadTable adds each ID only when it is not already present, so an existing owner wins a duplicate-ID conflict.

TryGetObject, reverse ID queries, and the subscription linking pass use this table entry after finding an object or ID in the paired caches. Removing only the owner entry can make those calls fail with a missing-key error. Register updates object caches without adding an owner here; UnloadTable and VacuumLinks remove owner entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager._sceneIdsByObject
member.summary: Stores the reverse object-to-ID lookup that uses to identify already-indexed objects.

remarks.para: This dictionary pairs a Unity object reference with its exported ID text. LoadTable and Register write it. TryGetIdForObject uses the ID to return the corresponding owner table, and late-reference serialization uses that result to save an object's ID for later lookup.

One object has one stored reverse ID. If the same object is indexed under several IDs, the latest reverse write replaces the earlier reverse ID while the forward cache may still contain several IDs for that object. Editing this dictionary alone does not update those forward entries or their owner tables.

UnloadTable removes keys for the objects in the table's current exports. VacuumLinks attempts to remove destroyed keys, with its collection-modified failure path. Its blank-ID cleanup does not remove a reverse key for an object that is still alive.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager._sceneObjectsById
member.summary: Stores the ID-to-object cache read by typed object queries and subscription linking passes.

remarks.para: Each key is an exported object's ID text and each value is the object reference saved when LoadTable or Register indexed it. A matching ID lets TryGetObject check the object's type or lets the linking pass deliver it to waiting references.

This is stored lookup state. Changing a table's exports or destroying an object does not automatically refresh the corresponding entry. UnloadTable and VacuumLinks remove entries explicitly, and multiple ID strings can point to one object.

Writing an entry here alone does not run linking callbacks or create the matching table-owner and reverse-ID entries. A lookup can find an object here and then fail because its owner-table entry is missing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.LateReferences.LateReferenceManager._subscriptions
member.summary: Groups waiting late-reference instances by the target ID that a later linking pass will try to resolve.

remarks.para: The key is the reference's UniqueId text at the time it was added. The value is a set of reference instances waiting under that ID. AddSubscription creates or extends a group; adding the same instance to the same group does not duplicate it.

LinkSubscribedLateReferences leaves a group in place when its ID is missing from the object cache. When the ID is found, it calls the group's references and then removes the whole group after their callbacks return. The group can be removed even when a typed reference rejected the cached object's type.

Clearing this dictionary discards waiting work. Changing a queued reference's UniqueId does not move its existing entry. Table loading, registration, and changes to this dictionary do not by themselves start a linking pass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._firstCartridgeArt
member.summary: Stores the loaded first cartridge display object so later refreshes can show or hide it.

remarks.para: Initialization stores this reference after a successful first-model spawn, marker alignment and attachment to the magazine. The object is decorative art: it does not represent an extra usable round.

When refreshes are allowed and the first display marker exists, zero stored rounds requests this object hidden; one or more requests it shown. Insertion hiding requests it hidden regardless of count. A missing reference is skipped.

Pool cleanup clears the reference. Replacing it changes which existing object later visibility operations target; it does not spawn or position an object. Newly loaded art is initially activated without a final count check.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._isArtHidden
member.summary: Suppresses count-based cartridge display refreshes while the magazine’s exposed rounds should stay hidden.

remarks.para: Insertion hiding sets this flag before issuing hide requests. Ejection showing clears it before refreshing the models. Pool setup also clears it.

True makes CheckBulletArt() return without touching the models. Setting the flag by itself does not hide or show any object. For example, setting it false allows a later refresh but does not perform that refresh.

The flag records the suppression rule, not a visibility measurement. A pending show/hide request or an initialization that activates newly loaded art can leave actual visibility different from the flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._isInitalized
member.summary: Prevents another initialization from starting after the first initialization attempt begins.

remarks.para: The spelling is part of the API. InitializeAsync sets this flag before it changes the round list or requests visual models. True therefore includes both loading in progress and a finished attempt.

A new initialization call returns without replacing ammunition or waiting for the earlier load while this is true. Failure does not automatically clear it. Await the task returned by the original call to know whether that setup finished successfully.
Pool cleanup clears the flag after plug cleanup. Pool setup does not clear it itself. Changing this flag alone does not load art or prepare the magazine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._isMagazineClaimed
member.summary: Makes later grab handling skip this magazine’s first-claim receiver registration and inventory credit.

remarks.para: Claim() sets this flag. Grab handling also sets it after available receiver registration or inventory credit, and player-pouch magazine creation marks its finished magazines claimed. Pool setup clears it.
The grab handler can still search for and cache a missing ammo receiver before checking the flag. Once the flag is true, it skips the registration and credit block.

The inventory credit uses configured magazine capacity, magazineState.magazineData.rounds, in whole rounds. This flag does not measure ammunition, prove that a transfer happened, or say which hand currently holds the object. Setting it directly changes that later grab behavior without transferring anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._lastAmmoInventory
member.summary: Caches the available ammo inventory credited by this magazine’s first unclaimed grab.

remarks.para: When the magazine is unclaimed and the shared player ammo inventory exists, grab handling stores that inventory here before adding ammunition to it. The amount is the configured magazine capacity in whole rounds, even for a partly empty magazine.

The cartridge type comes from the magazine state: its last stored cartridge when present, otherwise its configured cartridge settings. The field records an inventory reference, not a running count or proof of a completed credit.
Pool setup clears this cache. Assigning another reference alone does not add or remove ammunition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._lastAmmoInventoryReceiver
member.summary: Caches the player’s ammo-pouch receiver so grab registration and pool cleanup can track this magazine.

remarks.para: When this cache is missing, grab handling searches the grabbing hand’s player rig, the collection of objects controlling that player, for an ammo receiver and stores the first one found. The search happens even when the magazine is already claimed.

An unclaimed grab registers the magazine with an available cached receiver. On pool cleanup, an available cached receiver is asked to remove this magazine from its active-magazine list. That tracking list is separate from the ammunition count.
Pool setup clears the cache. Writing a different reference does not register or unregister anything immediately, but changes the receiver targeted by later grab or cleanup operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine._secondCartridgeArt
member.summary: Stores the loaded second cartridge display object so later refreshes can show or hide it.

remarks.para: Initialization stores this after the second-model spawn succeeds, its second marker exists and ignoreSecondBulletSpawn is false. The model is decorative and does not add ammunition.

When refreshes are allowed and the first display marker exists, fewer than two stored rounds requests this object hidden; two or more requests it shown. Insertion hiding requests it hidden only if the second display marker exists. A missing reference is skipped.
Pool cleanup clears the reference. Changing the cached object does not spawn or position it. Newly loaded art is activated without checking whether two rounds are currently stored.

For cartridge objects with a MarrowEntity, the group that manages their physical parts, visibility goes through its hide/show request. Other cartridge objects use GameObject activation directly. A request or flag does not prove that the object has already finished becoming visible or hidden.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.ammoPouchOffset
member.summary: Sets a pouch display magazine’s position and rotation relative to its pouch marker.

remarks.para: This SimpleTransform is stored position and rotation data, not a scene Transform component. During the ammo receiver’s pouch-display creation, the magazine’s interaction host is parented to an ammo display marker and receives this local position and rotation.

Position components are meters along the parent marker’s local X, Y and Z axes. For example, (0, 0.02, 0) places the host two centimeters along that marker’s upward Y direction. It follows the marker’s orientation rather than the world’s axes.
Rotation is a quaternion, four numbers that describe an orientation rather than four angles in degrees. Identity rotation (0, 0, 0, 1) aligns the host with the marker.

This offset is read when the display is placed. Changing it does not continuously move an already placed display. The inspected hand-magazine creation path uses the hand and grip poses to place the grabbed magazine instead of this offset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.firstCartridgeTarget
member.summary: Provides the scene marker whose position and facing place the first cartridge display model during initialization.

remarks.para: This is a GameObject whose Transform stores its scene position and rotation. A missing marker skips the first-model spawn. After the spawn finishes, initialization reads the marker’s current world position and rotation and applies them to the model before attaching it to the magazine.

World position uses scene axes and meters. For example, moving this marker two centimeters upward before the model finishes loading moves the first model’s starting position by that amount. The marker is an alignment reference; the model is packed into the magazine’s physical object group rather than simply parented to this marker.

The marker must also exist for CheckBulletArt() to refresh either cached model. Changing the marker later does not continuously reposition already attached art, and it does not alter the stored round count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.grip
member.summary: Provides the magazine’s hand-grab point and the grab notification that triggers first-claim inventory work.

remarks.para: Pool setup connects the magazine’s grab handler to this Grip’s attached-hand notification; pool cleanup removes that connection. A notification is a function call made when a hand attaches. A missing grip skips those connections.

For an unclaimed magazine, the handler registers an available player ammo receiver and credits the configured magazine capacity to an available ammo inventory. That count is whole rounds, not necessarily the magazine’s remaining rounds.

The player-pouch hand-spawn path also uses the grip’s pose to place the magazine and attach it to the hand. Replacing this reference after setup does not move the listener from the old grip to the new one automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.ignoreSecondBulletSpawn
member.summary: Skips requesting a second cartridge display model during initialization when true.

remarks.para: Initialization tests this flag when it reaches the second-model stage. That stage also requires secondCartridgeTarget, the marker for the second decorative round. The flag does not reduce magazine capacity or remove ammunition.

If the first model is still loading, a change made before the second-model test can affect whether the second spawn is requested. Once that spawn is already underway, changing this flag does not cancel it.
Changing the flag does not despawn or hide an existing second model. Later CheckBulletArt() uses current round count and the hidden-refresh flag, and does not test this setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.insertPointTransform
member.summary: Stores an insertion-marker Transform reference; the inspected plug-alignment path uses the plug and host poses to position the magazine.

remarks.para: A Transform holds a scene object’s position and rotation. This field can hold a marker reference, but assigning it alone does not seat or move a magazine.

The complete inspected magazine setup and display methods, ammo plug insertion and exit completion, ammo socket loading, and AlignPlug insertion-pose calculation do not read this field. The insertion-pose calculation reads the plug’s own Transform and its interaction host. This is a statement about those methods, not every possible script or mod.
Treat this as stored configuration unless the particular code you are using reads it. Changing the referenced marker has no movement effect through the inspected paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.interactableHost
member.summary: Provides the magazine’s physical interaction group for attaching cartridge art and placing pouch display magazines.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost manages the object’s grab interaction and physical bodies. A physical body is the part whose movement is simulated; a physics joint is a connection that constrains bodies relative to one another.
Cartridge setup uses this host’s main physical body to pack newly aligned decorative rounds into the magazine’s object group. This host must exist for that attachment path to finish.

Pouch display creation disables grabbing on the host, parents its Transform to the ammo display marker, and applies ammoPouchOffset as a local position in meters and a local rotation relative to that marker. The hand-spawn path instead uses the grip and hand poses.
Replacing this reference does not automatically move an existing display or repack existing cartridge objects. Those effects occur when the setup operations run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.isMagazineInserted
member.summary: Records the ammo plug’s last completed insertion or exit transition for this magazine.

remarks.para: The ammo plug sets this true when insertion completes, before calling the magazine’s hiding method. It sets this false when exit completes, before calling the showing method. Pool setup also resets it false.

This is a transition flag, not a check of the magazine’s present position. After writing true and calling OnInsert(), AmmoPlug checks the socket’s IsClearOnInsert predicate. The inspected AmmoSocket override returns true when its assigned Gun’s internalMagazine field is non-null. This field holds a MagazineData object for the Gun’s internal magazine. The predicate does not read the public Boolean despawnOnInsert field. When true, insertion completion clears the plug from the socket and calls DespawnOnJointBreak.OnJointBreak, which despawns the pooled magazine. Calling OnInsert() or OnEject() directly changes display behavior but does not write this flag.
Assigning true does not insert the magazine, hide cartridge art, or connect a physical joint. Use the plug/socket operations for those effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.magazinePlug
member.summary: Provides the that connects the magazine to a gun’s magazine socket or an ammo receiver.

remarks.para: A plug is the magazine-side connector; a socket is the receiving opening, such as a gun’s magazine well. The plug handles alignment and completed insertion or exit transitions.

On completion, the plug writes isMagazineInserted before calling the magazine’s hide or show operation. After that call, AmmoPlug checks the socket’s IsClearOnInsert predicate. The inspected AmmoSocket override returns true when its assigned Gun’s internalMagazine field is non-null. This field holds a MagazineData object for the Gun’s internal magazine. The predicate does not read the public Boolean despawnOnInsert field. When true, insertion completion clears the plug from the socket and calls DespawnOnJointBreak.OnJointBreak, which despawns the pooled magazine.

The ammo socket’s forced-load operation waits for magazine creation and initialization, then uses this plug to force the magazine into its socket. Pool cleanup calls this plug’s despawn cleanup to clear its connection and joint, the physical connection constraining it to the receiving object.
Assigning a different plug reference does not itself insert or eject the magazine. The plug is required for magazine pool cleanup to finish.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Magazine.magazineState
member.summary: Stores the magazine settings, actual cartridge list and ammo-count notification that drive filling and cartridge display.

remarks.para: This is a serializable data object, meaning Unity can save its values with the magazine; it is not a separate scene component. magazineData.rounds is the configured capacity in whole rounds. cartridgeData is the selected ammunition’s settings. The per-cartridge list stores one settings reference for each current usable round.

Initialization replaces that list with the requested number of copies, limited to zero through capacity for a nonnegative capacity. Pool setup refills it using its existing cartridge settings. The current list length is the count used to display zero, one or two decorative rounds.

The ammo-count callback is a function notified after the list changes; its single integer argument is the resulting total in whole rounds. Pool setup subscribes the magazine’s visual-refresh handler, which reads the list’s current count. Cleanup unsubscribes it.
Replacing this state reference alone does not move that existing subscription or load new art. Configure the state and its magazine-capacity settings before setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.AmmoCount
member.summary: Reports the whole-number count of entries currently loaded in this magazine’s ammunition list.

remarks.para: This is a live reading of the backing list length, not the configured magazineData.rounds capacity. It counts every entry, including a null entry. A gun’s separately stored chambered round is not part of this list count.
For example, a magazine with capacity six can report three after loading three rounds. Direct edits to the backing list appear in the next reading, even if they exceed capacity.

Some operations pass this count to onAmmoChange, an optional notification function, but notifications are not automatic for every count change. In particular, ClearMagazine and a successful PullCartridge change the count without calling it. Reading AmmoCount does not send a notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState._cartridges
member.summary: Stores one ammunition-type reference per loaded round; counts these list entries.

remarks.para: The constructor creates an empty list. Initialize, Refill and ClearMagazine clear that same list in place. AddCartridge and an increase through SetCartridge append entries; PullCartridge and a decrease through SetCartridge remove entries from the end. The last remaining entry is the next one taken.

Entries are references to shared CartridgeData assets, which describe ammunition types, rather than spawned round objects. Different entries can refer to different types, and a null entry still counts as one loaded entry.

Directly changing this list bypasses the capacity limits and notifications in the helper methods. AddCartridge requires both this list and magazineData (the magazine configuration, including its round capacity) to be non-null. If either reference is null, it skips the add loop and onAmmoChange notification, then enters a shared failure path rather than returning normally. The body does not show a list-operation exception on that guarded branch, but it also does not make the call a successful no-op. Other methods have their own null handling; do not use null as a supported empty-list state. Keep a valid list. Changes to the default cartridgeData field do not rewrite existing entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.cartridgeData
member.summary: Chooses the default ammunition definition for refills, count increases and additions that have no valid supplied ammunition type.

remarks.para: CartridgeData is a shared data asset describing an ammunition type, including its projectile, round and spent-case assets. Initialize stores its supplied type here. Refill puts this reference in every new entry; an increase through SetCartridge uses it for added entries, and AddCartridge uses it when cart is null or a destroyed Unity object.

Changing this field leaves already loaded entries alone, so a magazine can contain types that differ from its current default. For example, changing the default from A to B while three A entries remain keeps those A entries; adding through SetCartridge then appends B entries, while Refill replaces the whole load with B.

GetCartridgeData returns this default when the list is empty. PullCartridge on an empty list returns null instead. A null default is allowed into the list by fill operations, but each such null entry still counts as a round.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.magazineData
member.summary: Supplies the magazine’s round capacity and its magazine-spawning and firearm-platform configuration.

remarks.para: MagazineData is a shared configuration asset. Its rounds field is the capacity in whole rounds; use a nonnegative value. Initialize limits the starting count to that capacity, AddCartridge limits positive additions, SetCartridge limits a changed target count, and Refill rebuilds the list to that capacity.

These operations read the current configuration when called. Changing this reference or its rounds value does not automatically resize the loaded list or send a count notification. SetCartridge also returns before reading capacity if its requested count already equals the current count.

The asset also contains spawnable, the definition used to create a physical magazine, and platform, a string identifying the firearm family it fits. AmmoSocket compares that platform string when considering an incoming magazine. Storing this field by itself neither spawns a magazine nor loads rounds.
Assign this configuration before filling or adjusting ammunition. Refill clears the old load before checking for a missing magazineData reference, so that failure can leave an empty list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MagazineState.onAmmoChange
member.summary: Receives count notifications from specific magazine operations, passing the actual loaded list count.

remarks.para: This optional Action<int> is a callback: a function, or a chain of registered functions, that is called with one whole-number round count. It supplies no previous count, ammunition type or reason for the call. If no function is assigned, these operations continue without a notification.

Initialize, Refill and AddCartridge call it once after their list work, including calls that leave the count unchanged. SetCartridge skips it when the requested count equals the current count; otherwise it calls it after adjustment, even if the capacity limit leaves the count unchanged.

PullCartridge calls it with zero only on the empty-list path, before returning null. A successful pull sends no notification. ClearMagazine also sends none. GetCartridgeData, AmmoCount reads and direct changes to the backing list or configuration fields do not trigger it.

These notifications run immediately as part of the method call, after the stated list work; they are not queued for another frame. If a listener throws an error, completed list changes are not undone. Magazine registers a listener that updates the visible cartridge models, so missing notifications should not be treated as proof that the load stayed unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.GAME_NAMES
member.summary: Stores the game-name list initialized to a single entry, BONELAB.

remarks.para: The array is a list of strings. At class initialization this build places the same BONELAB text used for the project name in its only entry. Reading it returns the stored list; it does not discover installed games.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.INSTALL_STAGING_DIRECTORY_NAME
member.summary: Provides ModsStaging as the folder name used when forming the mod installation staging path.

remarks.para: Staging means a place for mods being prepared for installation. This value is only the final folder name. The full path combines it with the game’s persistent saved-data folder. PrecachePaths caches that string; the InstallStagingPath getter creates the directory if missing when read.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.MarrowSDK.InstallStagingPath
member.summary: Returns the ModsStaging directory path for mods being prepared for installation and creates the directory if it is missing.

remarks.para: The path combines Application.persistentDataPath, the game’s persistent saved-data folder, with ModsStaging. It is an absolute filesystem path. For example, if that folder were /GameData, the result would be /GameData/ModsStaging. The actual folder and path separator depend on the platform.

PrecachePaths fills the saved path during runtime startup. If the saved path is null or empty, this getter computes and caches it when read. Later reads reuse the saved string. Every read still checks whether the directory exists and tries to create it if missing; filesystem failures can throw an exception.

member.summary: Stores the character list that SanitizeName deletes when cleaning a name.

The list belongs to filename-name cleanup. SanitizeID instead uses its own rule that preserves only ASCII letters A through Z and a through z, digits 0 through 9, and periods. Clearing this cached list makes the next SanitizeName call build it again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectDestructible.__c__DisplayClass52_0.__4__this
member.summary: Keeps the original that owns the spawn callback.

remarks.para: The compiler creates this helper to save information for a callback, a function that runs when the spawner obtains an object. DestroyNoDebris saves its own ObjectDestructible here before choosing loot. This reference points to the original destructible, not to the spawned loot.

When the successful spawn callback runs, it reads this object's current OnLootSpawn event. If that event exists, it sends listeners three values in order: this destructible, the saved spawnable choice, and the newly obtained GameObject. A GameObject is Unity's container for a scene object and its components. The callback does not report a request that finished without an object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectDestructible.__c__DisplayClass52_0.spawnable
member.summary: Stores the loot-table Spawnable choice before AssetSpawner begins its asynchronous object-creation request.

remarks.para: DestroyNoDebris copies the result of its loot table's GetLootItem into this field, checks that choice's crate identifier, and submits it to AssetSpawner. A Spawnable describes the saved asset to use and its optional pool settings; it is not an already spawned object.

If the asynchronous request produces a valid object and the captured owner’s current OnLootSpawn event is non-null, the callback passes this saved choice as the second OnLootSpawn argument, between the original destructible and the resulting GameObject. A GameObject is Unity's container for a scene object and its components. The callback uses the saved choice rather than picking from the loot table again, so listeners can tell which choice produced that result even if the table changes while spawning waits.

For example, if a broken crate chooses an ammo box, this field holds the ammo-box spawn description. The event's third argument is the actual ammo-box object. Saving the description or starting the request does not guarantee that object will be obtained.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectDestructible.__c__DisplayClass54_0.__4__this
member.summary: Remembers which should receive the loot-spawn notification when its requested loot object becomes available.

remarks.para: This is a captured reference: the game saves the existing destructible object in a small callback holder. A callback is code the spawning system calls when it has a result. The holder lets that code find the destructible even when the spawn takes longer than the damage-processing call.

The damage-processing method fills this reference before selecting loot and requesting a spawn. When the spawn callback runs, it reads this object's current OnLootSpawn event and, if that event exists, sends it the destructible, the saved Spawnable description, and the returned GameObject. GameObject means the actual object in the scene. Saving this reference does not copy the destructible's health or save a separate list of event listeners.

For example, a broken crate can request an ammunition pickup. This reference identifies the broken crate in the later notification; the callback's GameObject identifies the ammunition pickup. The reference being filled is not proof that the spawn has completed: an unsuccessful spawn can produce no loot notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectDestructible.__c__DisplayClass54_0.spawnable
member.summary: Saves the selected loot's description so OnLootSpawn can report which loot was requested alongside the returned scene object.

remarks.para: After the destructible reaches its breaking condition, the damage-processing method gets one entry from its loot table and copies that Spawnable value into this callback holder. Spawnable is a small description containing a reference to the asset to spawn and a reference to its spawn-policy settings. A spawn policy controls how the spawning system handles that request. This saved description is separate from the GameObject that may later appear in the scene.

If the saved description passes its validity check, the method registers it with the spawning system and submits the spawn request. The callback later sends this saved value, the destructible, and the returned GameObject to the destructible's current OnLootSpawn event. It does not select another loot-table entry at notification time. For example, if this request selected an ammunition pickup and the loot table later changes to select a battery, the callback still reports the description saved for this request.

The copy stores the two references in the description; it does not make private copies of the referenced asset or policy settings. Changing this holder after a request is submitted can change what its callback reports, but does not change the description already copied into that spawn request. A filled value alone does not guarantee that an object was successfully spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController._localTrackPos
member.summary: Stores a three-number tracking-position value that OpenController’s update does not populate or apply.

remarks.para: The field’s name suggests a local position, meaning coordinates relative to some reference rather than the whole scene. The inspected OpenController methods do not establish that reference frame or a unit conversion, because none of them reads or writes this storage.

Do not treat it as the current controller position or a target that automatically moves a held object. Changing it alone has no position-setting effect in the inspected OnUpdate, finger, grip, or gesture methods. This finding covers this class’s complete methods, not every outside caller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController._localTrackRot
member.summary: Stores a tracking-rotation value that OpenController’s update does not populate or apply.

remarks.para: The value is a quaternion: four numbers Unity uses to represent an orientation, rather than three angles in degrees. The inspected OpenController methods do not establish this storage’s reference frame, because none of them reads or writes it.

Do not treat it as the current controller orientation or a target that automatically rotates a held object. Changing it alone has no rotation-setting effect in the inspected OnUpdate, finger, grip, or gesture methods. This finding covers this class’s complete methods, not every outside caller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController._noFingies
member.summary: Chooses controller-based finger estimates instead of the Index tracked-hand path when true.

remarks.para: ProcessFingers checks this flag only for the Index controller type. With false, a present tracked hand can supply the four finger curls; with true, that branch falls back to trigger, grip, and touch estimates. A missing or untracked hand also falls back.
Finger curls still update, and the thumb remains simulated from touch inputs on either path. The flag does not disable all finger animation or all finger processing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController._runUpdates
member.summary: Stores a Boolean value that does not gate OpenController.OnUpdate.

remarks.para: OnUpdate performs input copying, finger processing, and grip/state tests without reading this value. Setting it to false therefore does not pause that method’s work.

None of the complete OpenController methods inspected reads or writes this field. This finding is limited to this class’s methods; it does not establish how every outside caller might use the exposed storage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.grabThreshold
member.summary: The fixed 0.99 squeeze cutoff for the grabbed-input test.

remarks.para: This is a constant, rather than a configurable live setting. Solved grip is a unitless combined squeeze amount from 0 open to 1 fully closed. OnUpdate marks the grabbed-input state true only when that amount is strictly greater than 0.99; exactly 0.99 does not pass.
Starting a new grab also requires the previous grab latch to be clear. Passing this threshold describes input and does not prove that an object has been held.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenController.releaseThreshold
member.summary: The fixed 0.5 base value for the speed-dependent release cutoff.

remarks.para: This is a constant, rather than a configurable live setting. It is a unitless squeeze amount, with 0 open and 1 fully closed.

The release test uses solved grip, a unitless squeeze amount from 0 (open) to 1 (fully closed), and grip velocity, its change per second. The cutoff is 0.5 + clamp(-0.02 × gripVelocity, -0.4, 0.4). Here 0.02 is a response time in seconds, and clamp keeps its result between the two stated limits. A faster opening movement raises the cutoff; a faster closing movement lowers it. The grip must be strictly below the cutoff.

At zero grip velocity the cutoff is 0.5, so exactly 0.5 does not release. At an opening rate of -10 squeeze units per second it becomes 0.7; at a closing rate of +10 it becomes 0.3. The adjusted cutoff is limited to 0.1–0.9. A one-update release also requires an existing grab latch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.CooledJogTog
member.summary: Reports whether unscaled game time is strictly past the stored jog-toggle deadline.

remarks.para: The getter compares Time.unscaledTime with _jogCoolTime. Both are seconds on the real-time clock, which continues through slow motion. It returns true only when the current time is greater than the deadline; equality still returns false. Reading it does not consume or move that deadline.

OnEarlyUpdate sets the deadline to the current unscaled time plus 0.5 seconds when a primary-stick press changes the traversal state from Walk to Jog. Its later jog-release and settled-input checks use the same deadline together with other input and timing conditions. For example, a deadline of 10.5 seconds is still waiting at 10.5 and has elapsed at 10.6. Those times are illustrative.
A true result does not by itself engage jogging or promise that every gesture is accepted. It is a readiness check against one timestamp, not a remaining-time countdown or a measured running speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.CustomDirection
member.summary: Supplies the transform to select as the movement-facing reference when Custom direction mode is applied.

remarks.para: SetDirectionMasterTransform with Custom copies this reference into directionMasterTransform; OnStart makes the same selection when the saved directionMode is Custom. OnEarlyUpdate later reads the selected transform’s rotation to orient active movement input relative to the body-support reference.

For example, select a separately controlled transform to guide walking by that object’s facing direction. Moving its position does not change this rotation-based direction calculation. Rotating it affects later movement samples; assigning a different CustomDirection object does not automatically replace the already selected reference, so reapply Custom when replacing it.

Supply a valid transform before selection and movement. OnStart changes a missing-Custom saved mode to Head after its initial selection, without selecting a replacement reference again in that branch. This field selects a direction source; it is not a movement vector or a direct command to turn the avatar.

A transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale. The body-support reference is the rig’s center-of-pressure transform, its balance-reference point; that transform’s orientation supplies the body axes used for movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OculusHandOffsetLf
member.summary: Stores the constructor’s fixed left-hand pose preset, separate from the runtime hand-offset fields.

remarks.para: The native constructor fills this readonly SimpleTransform with a position of approximately (−0.04, −0.035, −0.085) and a fixed quaternion rotation. A SimpleTransform contains position and orientation without a scale. The quaternion’s four values describe orientation rather than separate degree angles. These stored numbers alone do not establish physical distance units or an application frame for the unconsumed position preset.

This preset is stored data in the audited build. Across the complete OpenControllerRig native routines checked, there is no read that applies OculusHandOffsetLf to a controller or hand pose. ProcessesWristOffset writes the separate leftHandOffset field instead, and its model-based values differ from this constructor preset.

Do not treat this value as a verified live hand-calibration control merely because its name refers to Oculus. The checked routines do not establish a visible hand shift from changing it. This limit concerns the audited OpenControllerRig implementation; it does not claim that external code can never read the value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.OnPauseStateChange
member.summary: Shared listener action reporting this rig’s platform-pause transitions: true for pausing and false for resuming.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action; listeners here are called from OnEarlyUpdate only when the platform-pause flag changes. Outside the editor, its checked condition combines a connected and tracking headset, user presence and input focus. In this audited build the input-focus helper always returns true, so it does not independently pause the rig for an overlay. Other ControllerRig pause causes, such as level initialization or streaming, do not themselves fire this action.

On entering platform pause, the routine first sets the shared ControllerRig pause request, pauses AudioListener, and sets _isPlatformPaused to true. It then invokes this Action with true if assigned. Only afterward does it call TimeManager.PAUSE and reset the headset/controller tracking states. Listeners therefore see the local flag already true, while those later time/state operations have not yet run.

On resuming, TimeManager.UNPAUSE is called first. Only when Time.deltaTime is positive does it clear the shared pause request, unpause AudioListener, set _isPlatformPaused false and then invoke this Action with false. While the frame delta remains non-positive, the local flag stays true and no false notification is sent.

The action is static and has no rig argument, so one listener list is shared by all OpenControllerRig instances. Use += to add a listener and -= to remove that same listener without replacing others. OnDestroy clears the entire shared Action, including listeners installed elsewhere. The event is a transition report, not an instruction that merely subscribing will pause or resume anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._adaptiveJuice
member.summary: Stores the remaining distance budget for gradually correcting the tracking root’s height.

remarks.para: OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate updates the remaining budget to max(0, previousBudget − deltaTime × eyeHeight × 0.6). previousBudget and eyeHeight are distances in metres; eyeHeight is player’s eye height, deltaTime is elapsed seconds, and 0.6 is the per-second decay rate. The amount spent is previousBudget minus the new remaining budget. Geometric clamping of the height reference happens separately first; the spent distance limits the further move from that clamped reference toward the preferred height. Suitable upright virtual-height input can allow additional movement toward that preferred height, and the clamping contribution can make the total root correction exceed the budget spent.

OnStart seeds a budget of 2 metres in this setup path. SetAvatar raises the budget to at least abs(newEyeHeight − oldEyeHeight) + 0.3 × newEyeHeight, using player’s eye heights in metres before and after recalculation and the extra unitless multiplier 0.3. This helps a size change settle through later updates.

For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 metres and deltaTime of 0.02 seconds, a remaining budget of at least 0.0192 metres can spend 0.0192 metres that call. A smaller positive budget can only supply its remaining amount. Increasing the stored budget allows more future correction while it lasts; it does not directly move the root or apply a spring impulse. The update overwrites this value as it is spent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._adaptiveY
member.summary: Stores the accumulated vertical correction written to the tracking root’s local Y position.

remarks.para: OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate calculates the current pelvis, chest or head reference height along playerUp and compares it with player’s measured body geometry. It first brings an out-of-range reference inside its allowed geometric limits, then limits the further move toward the preferred height by the available correction budget. It adds both the geometric-clamp contribution and that later budget-limited move to this field, then writes it to vrRoot.localPosition.y while keeping that root’s local X and Z positions. Local Y is relative to the root’s parent, normally metres before parent scaling.

This shifts the tracking hierarchy vertically rather than changing an avatar’s mesh height or simply measuring clearance from the floor. The update can replace an externally assigned value through its next correction. SetAvatar also rescales it by newRootScale / oldRootYScale; both are unitless transform scales, so the result remains a local distance.

For example, a stored value of 0.1 represents a 0.1-local-metre Y position of the tracking root at unit parent scale. It is not necessarily a 0.1-metre world-space upward move if the parent is rotated or scaled. Setting the cache alone does not immediately write the transform; the height-update path performs that write.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._averageSkullLocal
member.summary: Keeps a slowly averaged difference between the body-tracking head position and the headset, expressed in the headset’s axes.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyTrack subtracts headset.localPosition from the XR body’s head-bone position, then rotates that difference by the inverse headset.localRotation. The result is a displacement in the headset-oriented tracking frame, normally metres before parent scaling. It is not the head’s world position.

Each permitted body-tracking refresh stores 0.998 × oldAverage + 0.002 × currentDifference. Both vectors are distance-valued differences in that frame and both weights are unitless. The fixed weights are applied per call, so the rate at which the average settles depends on how often refresh runs.

The average minus the current difference, rotated back by the headset’s orientation, corrects chest and pelvis tracker positions when _hasAssignedOffsets is true. The average itself is updated before that flag check. Editing it changes that temporary alignment correction and later samples gradually replace the edit; it is not a command to move the camera.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._chestGimbalOffset
member.summary: Stores a chest vector for which the checked rig implementation does not establish an active smoothing effect.

remarks.para: A Vector3 stores three numeric components. Although this field’s name suggests an offset for chest smoothing, the complete OpenControllerRig native routines checked do not read it into a pose calculation or update it as smoother history. UpdateHeptaBody uses different history fields for its active pelvis and foot smoothing.

Therefore these checked routines do not establish a chest movement change from editing this value, nor physical units or a coordinate frame for it.
