member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._contLfBlend
member.summary: Stores how much saved pose correction remains while the left controller switches between tracked and fallback targets.

remarks.para: A blend calculation uses this unitless correction weight: 1 keeps the full saved difference, and 0 applies the current target directly in that calculation. Position is calculated as targetPosition + savedPositionDifference × blend. targetPosition is the current tracked or fallback controller target in its parent tracking coordinates. savedPositionDifference is the output position minus that target position captured when the target changes. Both positions are local distance vectors, normally metres before parent scaling; blend is the extra unitless multiplier. A quaternion is four numbers describing orientation. Rotation applies the target quaternion followed by the saved rotation correction blended from no correction.

The left controller tracking-state field decides whether the target is the live tracked pose or its fallback. Thus this weight is not simply a percentage of physical tracking quality or always a tracked-pose weight. A target change captures the current difference, starts the weight at 1 and resets its smoothing rate; subsequent updates smooth it toward zero.

When the remaining weight reaches 0.01 or less, the update sets it to zero before changing the transition state to its steady tracked or untracked state. For an illustrative saved X difference of 0.2 metres and weight 0.5, the added X correction is 0.1 metres. The pose update recalculates the weight, so edits are temporary smoother-state changes rather than permanent calibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._contLfOffset
member.summary: Saves the pose difference used to prevent a jump when the left controller changes tracking target.

remarks.para: The transition snapshot stores output.localPosition − targetPosition as its position difference. output is the controller transform being updated; targetPosition and targetRotation are its current tracked or fallback target position and orientation. inverse(targetRotation) means the rotation that undoes that target orientation; multiplying rotations combines them in the shown order. These are in the same parent tracking coordinates, normally metres before parent scaling. Its rotation is inverse(targetRotation) × output.localRotation, a quaternion correction relative to the target orientation. A quaternion describes orientation; its components are not degree angles.

During a transition, the current target position receives this saved position difference multiplied by the remaining blend weight. The target rotation receives the saved correction faded toward no extra rotation. For example, a 0.2-metre local X difference at full weight begins from the previous output rather than immediately jumping that distance to the new target.

This snapshot is refreshed when left controller tracking changes or reverses during a blend. It is distinct from the fixed device-model hand presets and tracker calibration-child poses. Editing it changes a temporary transition correction; a later snapshot can replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._contLfState
member.summary: Records whether the left controller pose is using a tracked target, a fallback target, or a transition between them.

remarks.para: The stored state values are 0: Untracked, 1: Tracked, 2: BlendingToUntracked, and 3: BlendingToTracked. Untracked and Tracked directly apply their corresponding current target while that tracking condition stays the same. These states describe pose handling, not a numerical confidence score.

On a target change, the update captures the current output-to-target difference, initializes the correction blend and rate, then enters the appropriate transition state. Regaining tracking also performs the first blend update before recording BlendingToTracked. Losing it records BlendingToUntracked after the snapshot; its later calls perform the blend.

Continued transitions smooth the correction toward zero. At a remaining weight of 0.01 or less, the weight is set to zero first and the state then becomes Untracked or Tracked. If tracking reverses before completion, a new difference is captured from the current output so the new transition can remain continuous. Platform pause resets the three headset/controller state values after its true pause notification.

The state is maintained by early pose processing; assigning a value does not make the device physically tracked or create a valid fallback pose. Unrecognized state values return without applying the transition helper’s normal pose update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._contLfTime
member.summary: Stores the smoothing duration, in seconds, for fading the left controller’s saved transition correction.

remarks.para: The transition snapshot computes this duration from both the position difference and rotation correction. The position term is 0.02 + 0.1 × clamp01(distanceInMetres) seconds: distanceInMetres is the numeric length of the local position difference expressed in metres, and clamp01 limits that numeric input between zero and one. The rotation term is 0.12 − 0.1 × abs(rotationW) seconds, where rotationW is W, the fourth, unitless component of the saved quaternion. A quaternion is four numbers describing orientation; abs ignores the sign of its input. The larger term is used.

BlendOffset passes the duration to SmoothDamp, which gradually moves the correction weight toward zero while keeping its change-rate history. A larger duration makes that correction settle more slowly for otherwise identical inputs; it is not a timestamp, the age of a device sample, or a fixed delay before tracking resumes.

A new target-change snapshot replaces it. For an illustrative zero position difference and identity rotation correction, whose scalar component is 1, both terms give approximately 0.02 seconds; the native calculation uses floating-point numbers. Editing the duration affects a transition that uses it, but the next snapshot can overwrite the edit. The calculation does not establish a universal caller-side validation rule for arbitrary stored values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._contLfVelocity
member.summary: Keeps the rate-of-change state used while smoothing the left controller’s correction weight.

remarks.para: SmoothDamp updates this float by reference while it moves the unitless blend weight toward zero. Its units are blend units per second, not metres per second: it describes how the correction weight is changing, not the controller’s or headset’s physical linear velocity. There is no position vector or movement direction in this scalar.

A target-change snapshot resets it to zero before later smoothing uses it. Together with the remaining blend and smoothing duration, it affects how the saved pose difference settles. The next smoothing call overwrites it as part of the calculation, so manually assigned values are temporary history edits rather than a command to move the device.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._doubleFlickMem
member.summary: Remembers the primary stick’s previous direction for recognizing a second similar flick. The detector is .

remarks.para: This Vector2 stores the stick’s two unitless input components. The gesture detector compares the new direction with this vector when a stick movement crosses into its high-magnitude state. A second direction less than 50 degrees away and less than 0.25 seconds after the saved time can be treated as a double flick; these tests also use _lastFlickTime and _wasOverFlickThresh. The saved time is a scaled Time.time timestamp in seconds, refreshed on calls when the detector was already in its high-magnitude state, including the call that releases that state. The second-flick test compares the new time with this saved timestamp, rather than measuring from the first high-threshold crossing.

The high threshold is squared magnitude greater than 0.5; the rearm threshold is squared magnitude at most 0.45. These are radial input tests rather than button clicks. OnEarlyUpdate’s matching detector can select Jog on a recognized gesture. The memory is updated as the gesture is processed, so it is neither a movement speed nor a permanent preferred walking direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._footLfGimbalOffset
member.summary: Stores the additive position correction that smooths the left tracked foot target.

remarks.para: The correction is a distance vector in metres along world axes. The solver adds it to the current foot displacement, then adds the moving head-reference position back to obtain the rig foot’s world target. For an illustrative offset (0, 0.02, 0), that target is shifted 2 centimetres along world Y before the body fit uses it.

The smoother accumulates the difference between smoothed and newly measured displacement velocity, fades the correction toward zero using 10 × deltaTime, and limits its magnitude to 0.05 metres in these foot calls. Here deltaTime is elapsed seconds and 10 is the per-second fade rate. These corrections adjust position along world axes; their components are distances rather than rotation angles. This is a positional smoothing correction.

UpdateHeptaBody uses this history for the left foot only in the tracked-body path when both tracked feet are configured. It smooths the foot’s world-space position relative to a moving head reference built from headset position and the player’s rotated skull-camera offset. The vector axes remain world X, Y and Z; subtracting the reference position removes its translation rather than rotating the vector into foot-local axes.

A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for a body controlled by physics. These values are calculated smoother history, not Rigidbody velocity or forces. The positive-delta update overwrites them. For non-positive delta time, the helper returns the current target plus its saved offset without updating the history; this does not make those values a new measurement.

remarks.para: The input rate is (currentDisplacement − previousDisplacement) / deltaTime. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._hasAssignedOffsets
member.summary: Enables use of the configured tracker calibration setup after capture has been requested.

remarks.para: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets this flag true at its beginning, before checking and writing optional tracker calibration children. A true value is therefore not proof that every tracker is assigned, that every child exists, or that the method completed successfully. It is separate from the hand-offset flags and XR body permission.

RefreshBodyTrack still updates its head-alignment average when this is false, but returns before writing the later tracker poses. UpdateHeptaBody also checks this flag together with a connected, permitted body device before using its tracked-body path; otherwise it uses its body-solving fallback.

Clearing the flag skips those uses; setting it alone does not capture alignment poses or grant device permission. Perform CaptureTrackedOffsets with the intended rig pose and a complete hierarchy rather than treating this boolean as a test that calibration is valid.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._hasLeftHandOffset
member.summary: Stores a left-hand flag that the checked rig routines do not use to validate or apply an offset.

remarks.para: The native field is a boolean, but the complete OpenControllerRig routines checked neither set it after capture nor test it before using a hand pose. ProcessesWristOffset writes the separate leftHandOffset preset and clears the XR hand’s full-update mode flag without setting this validity flag. The complete HandActionMap update path checked continues processing hand poses without testing that mode flag. The mode-flag write therefore does not establish that all XR-hand pose updates stop.

A true value therefore is not a verified indication that calibration succeeded, and changing it does not enable hand-offset application through those checked routines. This statement is limited to the audited OpenControllerRig implementation; it does not establish a global absence of external users.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._headsetBlend
member.summary: Stores a headset float for which the checked rig routines do not establish an active pose-transition effect.

remarks.para: This field stores a float, a single number. The complete 37 OpenControllerRig native routines checked do not use this field to calculate or fade the headset pose, and no checked caller passes it as the corresponding argument of ProcessTrackedBlend, SnapshotOffset or BlendOffset. Its name alone does not establish applied physical units, an active smoothing duration or a coordinate frame.

The separate controller transition helper uses a unitless remaining-correction weight: 1 retains its full saved difference and 0 applies its current target in a blend calculation. Its position equation is targetPosition + savedPositionDifference × blend, with targetPosition the current controller target and savedPositionDifference the previously captured output-minus-target distance in the same parent tracking coordinates. For example, a saved X difference of 0.2 local metres at weight 0.5 contributes 0.1 local metres to that controller calculation. Those actual controller arguments establish the calculation; they do not establish that this headset field has the same effect.

The active headset path instead applies the available tracked pose directly and uses _headsetState to request reacquisition alignment. When tracking is unavailable it uses the remembered headset pose and resets that alignment state. The controller helper’s fade-completion threshold, reversal snapshots and transition-duration behavior are not the headset path’s state handling.

For practical use, reading or assigning this stored value does not, through these checked routines, establish a measured headset speed, tracking-confidence percentage, completed calibration, a visible correction or a delay before tracking resumes. No automatic update/reset lifecycle or validated range is inferred from the field name. This limit covers the complete OpenControllerRig implementation inspected; it does not rule out external code reading or writing the field. The separate readonly hand presets and tracker calibration-child poses also remain different storage with their own verified contracts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._headsetOffset
member.summary: Stores a headset position-and-orientation value for which the checked rig routines do not establish an active pose-transition effect.

remarks.para: This field stores a SimpleTransform: three position components and a quaternion, four numbers describing orientation. The complete 37 OpenControllerRig native routines checked do not use this field to calculate or fade the headset pose, and no checked caller passes it as the corresponding argument of ProcessTrackedBlend, SnapshotOffset or BlendOffset. Its name alone does not establish applied physical units, an active smoothing duration or a coordinate frame.

The separate controller snapshot helper stores output.localPosition − targetPosition and inverse(targetRotation) × output.localRotation. output is the controller transform being updated; the target is its current tracked or fallback pose in the same parent tracking coordinates. inverse means the rotation that undoes the target orientation, and multiplying rotations combines them in the shown order. A captured controller X difference of 0.2 local metres is retained at full correction weight and then fades. This field is not a verified argument of that calculation, so those controller units and snapshot rules cannot be assigned to it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._headsetState
member.summary: Records whether the early headset path needs to realign the tracking root after tracking becomes available again.

remarks.para: The checked early-update headset path uses zero to request reacquisition alignment and one after performing it. When the headset is unavailable or not tracked, the routine applies the remembered fallback local position and orientation, then resets this field to zero. These values describe how the rig handles the pose; assigning one does not make the physical device tracked or create a valid fallback pose.

When a tracked headset pose is available, the routine applies that pose first. If this field is zero, it then adjusts vrRoot horizontally and turns it about the headset using the root’s up direction to align with the remembered headset pose. It removes the root’s extra tilt in that alignment path, saves the current headset local pose, and sets this field to one. A transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; vrRoot is the parent tracking transform whose movement carries the tracked hierarchy.

This headset path does not run the controller helper’s BlendingToUntracked or BlendingToTracked fade states, remaining-weight threshold or reversal snapshots. An unrecognized stored state does not prevent the tracked headset pose from being applied: the tracked pose write happens before the zero-state test. A nonzero value skips that special zero-state alignment, rather than calling the controller transition helper.

Platform pause resets this headset state along with both controller states after the true pause notification, preserving the listener-visible event order. Early pose processing maintains it; manually resetting it to zero requests the alignment path on a later available tracked update, subject to the outer pause and device checks. It is neither a tracking-confidence score nor proof that a physical tracker was calibrated. Required headset, tracking-root and remembered-pose references still need to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._isPlatformPaused
member.summary: Records whether this rig’s platform-pause path has entered pause and has not yet completed its resume step.

remarks.para: Outside the editor, OnEarlyUpdate tests headset connection, tracking and user presence together with the input-focus helper. If the combined condition fails and this flag is false, it requests controller pause, pauses AudioListener, sets the flag true, invokes OnPauseStateChange(true), then pauses TimeManager and resets the tracked-state fields. In this build the input-focus helper always reports true, so this flag is not a direct record of a VR overlay being open.

When the combined condition succeeds again, it first calls TimeManager.UNPAUSE. Only with a positive Time.deltaTime does it clear the shared controller pause request, unpause AudioListener, set the flag false and invoke OnPauseStateChange(false). That event is after the flag change in both directions, so listeners see the new value.

This local flag is distinct from ControllerRig.IsPaused, the effective pause result that also accounts for initialization and level streaming. Editing the flag alone does not reproduce its audio, time or shared-request operations and can change which transition branch runs next.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._jogCoolTime
member.summary: Stores an unscaled-time deadline used before some jog-release checks may return to walking.

remarks.para: It is a timestamp in seconds on Time.unscaledTime, not a duration remaining. When a primary-stick press changes traversal from Walk to Jog, OnEarlyUpdate stores current unscaled time + 0.5 seconds. Unscaled time measures real elapsed time even during slow motion.

CooledJogTog and the corresponding early-update checks require current time strictly greater than this deadline; equality has not elapsed. For an illustrative press at 10 seconds, a deadline of 10.5 is still waiting at exactly 10.5. Later jog downgrade also depends on stick release, held/activity state and other timing conditions.

Changing the deadline changes when those checks can pass, without directly selecting Walk or Jog. This half-second deadline is not set by every double-flick branch, so it should not be interpreted as a universal cooldown for all ways of engaging faster locomotion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastChest
member.summary: Startup displacement from the avatar’s head bone to its neck bone, stored in world axes.

remarks.para: OnStart subtracts the head bone’s world position from the neck bone’s world position and stores the result here. This is a relative vector in metres, not the chest’s world position and not a value refreshed every frame. For example, a neck 0.12 metres below the head produces a downward displacement of that size.

The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines contain that startup write but no later use of this vector. Editing it therefore does not adjust the chest through those routines. Actual chest fitting uses the tracked transforms and the body solver; this observation does not establish that every external mod or game routine ignores the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastContLfLocal
member.summary: Remembered left controller pose relative to the head, used to keep the hand placed when tracking is unavailable.

remarks.para: The pose contains a position in metres and a quaternion rotation, which stores orientation rather than three degree angles. OnStart builds it from the left controller’s local pose relative to the headset. During tracked early updates, the rig replaces it with the accepted controller pose expressed relative to the remembered headset position and the filtered, tilt-removed head orientation.

When the left controller is disconnected or reports an unusable rotation, OnEarlyUpdate reconstructs a fallback hand pose from this memory, the remembered headset position and _swungHeadLerp. The positional part is a displacement from the head in that head-oriented frame, not an absolute world location or a controller position in its parent’s axes.

For example, a remembered hand 0.3 metres to the side follows the reconstructed head orientation during fallback instead of being pinned to one world position. A tracked update can overwrite a mod’s edit. This is tracking history and fallback state, not the separate device-to-hand correction stored in leftHandOffset or rightHandOffset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastFixedTime
member.summary: Last physics timestamp for which OnUpdate performed its rig-root correction and saved the previous body pose.

remarks.para: The timestamp is Time.fixedTimeAsDouble in seconds on Unity’s scaled physics clock. OnUpdate only enters its correction block when the current fixed time is strictly greater than this stored value. Several rendered frames can share one physics timestamp, so they do not each repeat that correction.

After adjusting the rig root, the routine records the current fixed timestamp and copies the current body pose into the previous-pose buffer. This marker controls that block; it is not a count of physics steps or the elapsed duration of a step. For example, writing a future timestamp postpones this block until the clock passes it. The checked routine maintains the marker on subsequent successful corrections.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastFlickTime
member.summary: Scaled-time memory used to decide whether two primary-stick flicks are close enough to enable jogging.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate passes Time.time, measured in scaled game seconds, to CheckDoubleFlick. While _wasOverFlickThresh was already true, that helper writes the supplied time here, including on the call that returns the stick below the reset threshold. It is not simply the timestamp of a snap turn.

A new flick can qualify as a double flick when the interval from this stored time is less than 0.25 seconds and the angle to the remembered stick direction is less than 50 degrees. Entering the flick state requires squared stick magnitude greater than 0.5; returning to magnitude squared at or below 0.45 resets it. These are unitless radial stick measurements.

For example, two similarly directed flicks separated by 0.2 scaled seconds can qualify. A successful check does not itself rotate the player. Slow motion changes how quickly the scaled clock advances compared with real time.

A qualifying double flick enables Jog by selecting the jogging state. This successful flick branch does not test the separate jog cooldown and does not alternate jogging on and off; other button, release and idle-stop branches have their own conditions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastFootLf
member.summary: Previous left foot target relative to the moving head reference, used to estimate motion for foot smoothing.

remarks.para: UpdateHeptaBody takes the left foot’s world position, subtracts the current head reference position, and passes that displacement to Rig.Gimbal. The stored vector uses world axes and metres. It is not an absolute foot location: translating the head reference and foot together leaves their relative displacement unchanged.

On a normal Gimbal call with positive time and an enabled offset limit, the helper estimates target velocity from the difference between the new displacement and this history, divided by elapsed seconds. It updates this history to the new displacement and returns that target plus _footLfGimbalOffset, the temporary smoothing displacement.

This field advances when the corresponding body-tracking branch calls the helper, not necessarily on every rendered frame. Editing the history changes the next velocity estimate and can create a transient smoothing correction; it does not permanently place the foot. The checked foot calls limit the correction magnitude to 0.05 metres and use a 0.1-second smoothing time.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastFootRt
member.summary: Previous right foot target relative to the moving head reference, used to estimate motion for foot smoothing.

remarks.para: UpdateHeptaBody takes the right foot’s world position, subtracts the current head reference position, and passes that displacement to Rig.Gimbal. The stored vector uses world axes and metres. It is not an absolute foot location: translating the head reference and foot together leaves their relative displacement unchanged.

On a normal Gimbal call with positive time and an enabled offset limit, the helper estimates target velocity from the difference between the new displacement and this history, divided by elapsed seconds. It updates this history to the new displacement and returns that target plus _footRtGimbalOffset, the temporary smoothing displacement.

This field advances when the corresponding body-tracking branch calls the helper, not necessarily on every rendered frame. Editing the history changes the next velocity estimate and can create a transient smoothing correction; it does not permanently place the foot. The checked foot calls limit the correction magnitude to 0.05 metres and use a 0.1-second smoothing time.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastHeadFwd
member.summary: Remembered horizontal head-facing direction used to measure headset yaw changes.

remarks.para: CheckHeadsetLimits removes head tilt from the headset’s local rotation and transforms the forward direction with the resulting orientation. This unitless direction vector is in the headset’s local tracking axes; it represents facing, not a position or a degree angle.

The routine compares the new direction with this stored direction, gives the angle a sign around up, and divides by unscaled elapsed seconds to obtain yaw speed in degrees per second. It replaces this direction before checking the acceleration limits, even when the speed histories are retained because the sample is rejected.

For example, a 10-degree facing change over 0.02 seconds produces a 500-degree-per-second yaw sample. Editing this vector changes the next comparison, rather than rotating the headset. The constructor initializes it to the forward direction, and later limit checks maintain it.

These rules describe CheckHeadsetLimits when it is called. The checked ordinary OnEarlyUpdate does not call that helper or refresh this history through it; no call occurs in the complete inspected OpenControllerRig class routines. This does not establish that an external caller can never invoke the helper.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastHeadVel
member.summary: Remembered headset velocity used by the tracking-limit check to detect sudden horizontal acceleration.

remarks.para: CheckHeadsetLimits estimates velocity from the headset’s local position minus the remembered headset position, divided by Time.unscaledDeltaTime. The components are metres per second in the headset parent’s tracking axes. The next horizontal acceleration estimate compares the new X/Z velocity with this stored X/Z velocity and divides by unscaled seconds again.

The routine normally stores the new three-component velocity. When horizontal acceleration magnitude exceeds 480 metres per second squared, or absolute yaw acceleration exceeds 100,000 degrees per second squared, it retains the previous velocity instead. Thus this field can hold an older accepted history rather than the most recent raw device sample.

The check separately rejects horizontal speed above 10 metres per second. Vertical velocity can be stored but is not included in those horizontal speed and acceleration tests. Editing the memory affects the next acceleration comparison; the field is not a force, a requested movement speed or a direct headset-position control.

These rules describe CheckHeadsetLimits when it is called. The checked ordinary OnEarlyUpdate does not call that helper or refresh this history through it; no call occurs in the complete inspected OpenControllerRig class routines. This does not establish that an external caller can never invoke the helper.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastHmdInput
member.summary: Startup copy of the rig’s head transform position; the checked OpenControllerRig update paths do not use it as smoothing history.

remarks.para: OnStart copies m_head.localPosition here. This is a position in metres relative to that transform’s parent. The producer does not read a stick axis or convert the value into head-relative control input.

The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines contain no later read of this vector. Changing it therefore does not alter their headset smoothing or fallback. Those paths use _lastHmdLocal and the other tracked-pose state instead. This is a bounded statement about these checked routines, not a claim that external code cannot access it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastHmdLocal
member.summary: Remembered headset pose used when current tracking is unavailable and as a reference for headset reacquisition alignment.

remarks.para: The SimpleTransform contains the headset’s local position in metres and its quaternion orientation relative to the headset parent. A quaternion stores rotation; its four numbers are not four degree angles. OnStart copies the configured headset transform into this memory.

OnEarlyUpdate restores this remembered pose when the XR headset is disconnected or not tracking. With tracking available, it directly applies the current headset pose, performs its tracking-state and root handling, and remembers the resulting local pose for later alignment and fallback. The late camera-render path can refresh the live headset without replacing this memory, so it is not necessarily the pose from the immediately preceding rendered frame.

The public lastHmdLocal property reads or replaces the same memory directly. Writing it does not immediately move the headset or run a tracking check, but changes the reference used by the next early update. For example, replacing its position changes the next calculated displacement and the pose restored if tracking is missing; a later tracked update can overwrite it.

The checked ordinary OnEarlyUpdate does not run headset ProcessTrackedBlend or call the separate CheckHeadsetLimits helper. Its remembered pose is the resulting early-update output, rather than a sample certified by that helper’s motion-limit tests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastPelvis
member.summary: Previous pelvis target relative to the head reference, used by the pelvis motion smoother.

remarks.para: OnStart seeds this vector with the avatar hips’ world position minus its neck’s world position. When UpdateHeptaBody runs a pelvis Gimbal branch, it instead maintains the pelvis target relative to that update’s moving head reference. Both are displacements in metres expressed in world axes, not absolute pelvis locations.

Rig.Gimbal estimates target velocity from the new relative target minus this memory, divided by elapsed seconds. On normal positive-time calls it replaces the memory with the new target and returns that target plus _pelvisGimbalOffset, the temporary smoothing displacement. The pelvis is then placed relative to the current head reference.

Editing this history changes the next velocity estimate and can cause a short-lived correction. It does not permanently move the hips or set their body proportions. The checked pelvis calls use a 0.2-metre correction limit, a 0.05-second smoothing time and a fade rate of 10 per second. History only advances on a branch that actually invokes the helper.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lastTwistVel
member.summary: Remembered headset yaw speed used to check how abruptly the head’s turning speed changes.

remarks.para: CheckHeadsetLimits compares successive tilt-removed head-facing vectors, measures their signed angle around up, and divides by unscaled elapsed seconds. The resulting yaw speed is stored in degrees per second. It is a headset tracking measurement, not the torso’s turn command or the smooth-turn stick filter.

The difference between the newly measured yaw speed and this memory, divided by unscaled seconds, supplies yaw acceleration. If its absolute value exceeds 100,000 degrees per second squared, or horizontal acceleration exceeds 480 metres per second squared, the routine retains the previous speed history. It also checks absolute yaw speed against 2,000 degrees per second.

For example, changing this memory from 0 to 100 degrees per second changes the next acceleration estimate even if the headset pose is unchanged. A successful ordinary check refreshes it; it is not guaranteed to describe the immediately preceding rendered frame.

These rules describe CheckHeadsetLimits when it is called. The checked ordinary OnEarlyUpdate does not call that helper or refresh this history through it; no call occurs in the complete inspected OpenControllerRig class routines. This does not establish that an external caller can never invoke the helper.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._lockViveJump
member.summary: Touchpad latch that prevents the lower middle sector from supplying the secondary jump-hold flag after the upper sector was used.

remarks.para: ProcessSecondaryTouchpad first clears its returned secondaryAButtonHold flag. With unitless horizontal axis magnitude below 0.6, an upward axis above 0.2 sets this latch. A downward axis below -0.2 only returns the hold flag when the latch is false; that accepted lower-sector branch also removes Y from the returned axis.

Horizontal magnitude at or above 0.6 clears the latch. Returning only the vertical axis to the center does not clear it. For example, using the upper middle sector, then moving directly downward, remains blocked until the input reaches either horizontal side sector.

This is a specific secondary-touchpad mapping rule. It does not test every physical Vive button click or disable jumping from every controller. Changing the flag affects the next helper call, and that call can set or clear it again under these exact conditions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._pelvisGimbalOffset
member.summary: Temporary displacement added to the pelvis target to soften sudden changes in tracked motion.

remarks.para: UpdateHeptaBody feeds Rig.Gimbal a pelvis target relative to a moving head reference. This offset uses the same world axes and is measured in metres. The helper returns target plus this offset, and the caller adds the current head reference back to place the pelvis.

On ordinary positive-time calls, the offset accumulates the difference between filtered and raw target velocity over elapsed seconds, fades toward zero at 10 per second, and is limited to a magnitude of 0.2 metres in the checked pelvis branches. The velocity filter uses a 0.05-second smoothing time. This offsets motion temporarily; it is not a permanent avatar hip calibration.

For example, a 0.01-metre upward offset raises that update’s smoothed pelvis target by one centimetre before later filtering changes it. Editing it can affect the next Gimbal result, but the next normal call fades and clamps it. With no positive elapsed time, the helper returns target plus the stored offset without advancing its normal state.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._pelvisGimbalVel
member.summary: Filtered pelvis-target velocity retained by the pelvis motion smoother.

remarks.para: Rig.Gimbal estimates raw velocity from consecutive pelvis targets relative to the moving head reference. It uses Vector3.SmoothDamp to bring this memory toward that raw velocity, with the checked pelvis calls supplying a 0.05-second smoothing time. The vector is metres per second in world axes.

The difference between this filtered velocity and raw target velocity contributes to _pelvisGimbalOffset, the temporary displacement that softens movement. _pelvisGimbleAccel is the separate derivative state used while filtering this velocity. Neither value is a force applied to a Rigidbody.

For example, changing this memory changes how the next accepted pelvis movement is filtered; it does not command the pelvis to move at that speed indefinitely. The Gimbal call updates it when its normal positive-time branch runs. Body branches that do not call the pelvis helper leave this history untouched.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for simulated physical motion; the history here belongs to the velocity-smoothing calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._pelvisGimbleAccel
member.summary: Derivative memory used when smoothing the pelvis-target velocity.

remarks.para: The field keeps its native spelling. Rig.Gimbal passes it by reference to Vector3.SmoothDamp while smoothing _pelvisGimbalVel toward the velocity estimated from successive pelvis targets. Because the smoothed value is a velocity in metres per second, this derivative state is measured in metres per second squared, in world axes.

The checked pelvis calls use a 0.05-second smoothing time. SmoothDamp updates this state on normal positive-time Gimbal calls; it affects how quickly the filtered velocity approaches its new target, which then affects the temporary pelvis offset.

This is internal smoothing state, not a separately measured sensor acceleration or a force that accelerates the avatar’s Rigidbody. Editing it alters the next filtering step, and subsequent calls replace it as the filter continues.

The moving head reference is the headset’s world position plus the tracking avatar’s skull/camera offset rotated by the headset’s world orientation. The positions and offset are in metres, and the resulting point moves as the headset moves or turns.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for simulated physical motion; the history here belongs to the velocity-smoothing calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._player
member.summary: The tracking avatar whose measurements and bones this controller rig uses to fit the player’s tracked body.

remarks.para: This RealHeptaAvatar supplies the body proportions and skeleton used by the controller rig’s body-fitting routines. It is a separate reference from RigManager’s currently equipped game avatar. OnRealHeptaAwake, the rig’s setup routine, assigns it to this rig’s avatar reference, precomputes its measurements from the manager avatar’s eye height in metres, and refreshes its own measurements while copying selected player shape factors into the calibration avatar.

OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate and UpdateHeptaBody use it while fitting torso, arms, pelvis and feet and saving the resulting body pose. SetAvatar updates the existing tracking avatar’s scale and measurements; it does not replace this reference with its argument. Reset can find a RealHeptaAvatar on the same GameObject (Unity scene object) for setup.

The public player getter returns the same stored reference without finding or creating another avatar. Replacing _player alone does not repeat initialization or equip that avatar in RigManager. A replacement needs the skeleton and measurements expected by the body-fitting paths; otherwise those paths can encounter missing references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._secondaryFlickReady
member.summary: Arms one snap-turn request until the secondary axis is returned far enough toward the center.

remarks.para: SnapRotate accepts a false inputPressed argument by setting this flag true before draining any existing turn debt. A true request adds a signed snap angle only when the flag is true; it clears the flag before adding that angle. Keeping the stick deflected therefore does not repeatedly add a new snap on every call.

For secondary thumbstick snap modes 1 through 4, horizontal magnitude below 0.4 rearms it. A new request requires horizontal magnitude at least 0.65 and vertical magnitude below 0.5. All these axis values are unitless. The space between the thresholds provides a buffer against repeated snaps near the edge.

For example, after a right snap, bringing X to 0.3 rearms it; X at 0.5 does not. The constructor sets the flag true, but later input calls control its state. Setting it true manually allows the next eligible request to add debt even if the stick never recentered.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._smoothInput
member.summary: Filtered horizontal turning input from which the rig calculates a smooth-turn angle for the update.

remarks.para: SmoothRotate smooths this stored value toward its supplied axis using a 0.04-second SmoothDamp time; ProcessSecondaryThumbstick uses the same state in smooth mode 5 after applying its horizontal dead zone. The value is unitless stick input, not an angle or a rotation speed. _turnVel is the derivative memory used by this filter.

Smooth-turn output in degrees is filtered input × (48 × degreesPerSnap + 60) × dt / (0.3 × (1 - timeScale) + timeScale). Here degreesPerSnap is the unitless speed setting, the rate in parentheses is degrees per second, dt is the caller’s elapsed seconds, and timeScale is the unitless game-time multiplier. The filter itself uses Time.deltaTime.

For example, with filtered input 0.5, speed setting 2, dt 0.02 seconds and timeScale 1, the update produces 1.56 degrees. This is an illustrative calculation, not a default. A mod’s edit changes the next calculation, but a subsequent smooth-turn call filters and replaces the memory.
Time.deltaTime is scaled elapsed seconds for the current frame. It supplies the smoothing filter’s elapsed time; the separate caller-supplied elapsed time enters the later turn-angle calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._swungHeadLerp
member.summary: Filtered head orientation used to keep remembered controller poses following the head during tracking fallback.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate takes the remembered headset rotation, removes the tilt that points its up direction away from the tracking up direction, and interpolates this memory toward that orientation. Its quaternion stores orientation in the headset’s local tracking frame; it is not a head position, a body yaw speed or four degree angles.

The interpolation factor is 8 × Time.deltaTime, where Time.deltaTime is scaled elapsed seconds and 8 is the rate per second. The native interpolation is unclamped: it does not cap that factor at one. This filtered orientation expresses controller history relative to the head and rotates the remembered displacement and orientation when rebuilding a fallback hand pose.

For example, during temporary controller tracking loss the remembered hand can continue following the head-facing orientation. Changing this memory affects that fallback and the next interpolation; the next ordinary early update recalculates it. It does not by itself rotate the avatar’s torso or camera.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._timeInput
member.summary: Arms a delayed time-scale toggle after an eligible primary-button release.

remarks.para: TimeInput sets this flag after a primary-button-up input when TimeManager reports a positive time-scale step. It records a deadline 0.25 unscaled seconds ahead. While armed, continued touch pushes that deadline forward, so the pending toggle waits until touch stops and the deadline has passed.

When unscaled time is strictly later than _timeInputTimer and touch is false, the routine clears this flag before asking TimeManager to toggle time scale and playing accelTime. A primary-button-down input clears the flag first and can instead request a decrease in time scale, subject to TimeManager’s enable and step checks.

This flag means a toggle is waiting; it does not report that slow motion is currently engaged or that a button is currently held. For example, it can stay true while a thumb remains touching the control even after the button release. Editing it alone does not immediately change global time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._timeInputTimer
member.summary: Unscaled-time deadline for the pending time-scale toggle.

remarks.para: TimeInput writes Time.unscaledTime + 0.25 here when it arms _timeInput after an eligible primary-button release. While the pending input is still touched, it repeatedly moves the deadline to 0.25 seconds after the current unscaled time. This is an absolute clock time in seconds, not an accumulated hold duration.

With touch false, a pending toggle happens only when the current unscaled time is strictly greater than this deadline. Equality does not trigger it. The routine clears _timeInput before toggling time scale and playing accelTime. Global slow motion does not stretch this wait because the deadline uses unscaled time.

For example, a release at unscaled time 12.0 seconds starts with deadline 12.25; continued touch through time 12.4 moves it to 12.65. Setting an earlier deadline affects an already-armed request on the next call, but does not arm one or change time scale by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._trackedChestOffset
member.summary: Stored chest tracker pose that the checked OpenControllerRig paths do not apply as a calibration offset.

remarks.para: This private SimpleTransform stores a position and quaternion orientation. A quaternion is a way to store rotation using four numbers, rather than four angles in degrees. The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render, puck-assignment, offset-capture and body-update routines do not read or write this field. Its name alone therefore does not establish an active calibration effect or the coordinate frame of a consumed pose.

CaptureTrackedOffsets performs actual chest calibration by changing the tracker/output transform relationship and the output transform’s local pose; it does not fill this storage. Assigning a value here does not run that operation or move the chest through the checked body update.

For a mod that needs to calibrate tracking, use the configured tracking transforms and the capture operation after they are assigned. Keep this field separate from that active path. This checked-code limit does not establish that every external caller ignores the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._turnVel
member.summary: Derivative memory for filtering the horizontal smooth-turn axis.

remarks.para: SmoothRotate and smooth-mode ProcessSecondaryThumbstick pass this value by reference to Mathf.SmoothDamp while updating _smoothInput, the unitless filtered stick axis. Because the filtered value is unitless, this derivative is axis units per second, not degrees per second.

The filter uses a 0.04-second smoothing time and Time.deltaTime. The rig then converts the filtered axis into an angle using the speed setting and the caller’s elapsed time. That later angle calculation is separate from this filter state.

Changing this memory affects the next smooth filtering step; it does not directly set angular velocity or instantly rotate the player. A subsequent smooth-turn call updates it. SnapRotate uses the separate _twistDebtVel to smooth queued turn degrees.
Time.deltaTime is scaled elapsed seconds for the current frame. It supplies the smoothing filter’s elapsed time; the separate caller-supplied elapsed time enters the later turn-angle calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._twistDebt
member.summary: Signed snap-turn angle still waiting to be applied.

remarks.para: SnapRotate adds a signed angle in degrees when a new request is armed: modes 1, 2, 3 and 4 choose 15, 30, 45 and 90 degrees. A negative horizontal input adds a negative angle; zero or positive input adds a positive angle. The direct helper uses 15 degrees for other mode values.

Each call smooths this debt toward zero and writes the difference between the old and new debt to _smoothTwist, the degree change for that update. _twistDebtVel is the degrees-per-second derivative memory. The smoothing time is 0.01 + 0.2 / degreesPerSnap seconds, where degreesPerSnap is the unitless speed setting, not the snap angle.

For example, if 30 degrees of debt becomes 24 degrees after the filter step, that update’s output is 6 degrees and 24 remain queued. Opposite requests can reduce existing signed debt. This is queued input rotation, not a measurement of the difference between head and torso facing, and ordinary calls replace it as the turn is applied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._twistDebtVel
member.summary: Derivative memory used while reducing the queued snap-turn angle.

remarks.para: SnapRotate passes this value by reference to Mathf.SmoothDamp when bringing _twistDebt, the remaining angle in degrees, toward zero. The derivative is therefore degrees per second. It is filter state, not a measured torso turning speed or a separate requested snap angle.

The smoothing time is 0.01 + 0.2 / degreesPerSnap seconds; degreesPerSnap is the unitless speed setting. The filter uses caller dt / (0.2 × (1 - timeScale) + timeScale), where dt is elapsed seconds and timeScale is the unitless game-time multiplier. The difference between the old and new debt supplies the degree change for this update.

For example, resetting this derivative while debt remains changes the next smoothing step but does not erase the debt. A subsequent SnapRotate call updates it, including calls that merely rearm another request while the old debt continues to drain.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig._wasOverFlickThresh
member.summary: Latch recording whether the primary stick has entered the radial flick range for jog detection.

remarks.para: CheckDoubleFlick sets this latch when unitless squared stick magnitude is greater than 0.5, corresponding to radial deflection greater than about 0.707. While latched, it updates _lastFlickTime and clears the latch once squared magnitude is at or below 0.45, corresponding to radial deflection at or below about 0.671.

Those different thresholds keep a stick near the boundary from repeatedly counting new flicks. A newly entered flick can qualify for enabling jogging when it occurs within 0.25 scaled seconds of the remembered time and within 50 degrees of the remembered direction.

For example, keeping the stick at magnitude 0.8 leaves it latched; moving to 0.6 clears it so another outward movement can become a new flick. This state belongs to primary-stick double-flick jogging, not secondary-stick snap turning. The helper updates it on later calls.

A qualifying double flick enables Jog by selecting the jogging state. This successful flick branch does not test the separate jog cooldown and does not alternate jogging on and off; other button, release and idle-stop branches have their own conditions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.accelTime
member.summary: Sound played when the pending time-control input toggles time scale. Its companion decrease-time sound is .

remarks.para: Despite its name, this is an AudioClip, not a duration or acceleration number. TimeInput uses it after an armed _timeInput request has lost touch and its unscaled deadline has passed. The routine clears that flag, asks TimeManager to toggle time scale, then requests this clip as a 2D one-shot sound.

The sound’s volume and pitch are calculated from TimeManager’s step after the toggle. It is a cue for that time-control branch, not for avatar movement acceleration, and assigning another clip changes the requested sound rather than the 0.25-second wait. decelTime is the separate clip requested by the accepted decrease-time-scale branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.cameras
member.summary: Stored camera array; the checked late tracking hook chooses Camera.main directly.

remarks.para: The field can hold camera references, but the complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not read this array. OnMarrowReady registers OnBeginCameraRendering with the render pipeline, and that routine compares the incoming camera with Camera.main instead.

Adding a camera to this array therefore does not make the checked hook refresh tracking for that camera or invoke onLastCameraUpdate for it. Conversely, that main-camera path does not require membership in this array. This does not establish that external code never uses the stored references, or that these are the only cameras rendered anywhere in the game.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.curveMode
member.summary: Saved startup choice of which configured touchpad-direction curve becomes active.

remarks.para: OnStart selects touchPadCurve from the configured presets: Linear, Poles, GenesisDpad, Dpad, SmoothGenesis or SmoothDpad. The active curve maps the signed input direction angle in degrees to a new direction angle in degrees while keeping the axis magnitude. Its keys are supplied by the assigned AnimationCurve asset.

Changing curveMode after startup does not immediately replace touchPadCurve. SetTouchPadCurve selects a preset immediately but does not write this stored mode. BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT can select the active curve separately from this startup field when player settings are propagated.

For example, setting the mode to Dpad prepares that startup selection; calling SetTouchPadCurve(Dpad) changes the current reference. A preset name alone does not guarantee a particular curve shape, a thumbstick-wide speed change, or a runtime clamp on the curve’s output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.curve_Dpad
member.summary: Configured curve selected for the Dpad touchpad-direction profile.

remarks.para: OnStart can choose this reference from curveMode, and SetTouchPadCurve(Dpad) chooses it for the active touchPadCurve. Selecting it copies the reference; it does not generate or rewrite the curve’s keys. The selected asset determines the actual response, so the profile name does not by itself prove a particular shape.

TouchPadCurve evaluates the curve with the signed angle from upward axis input, measured in degrees, and uses the returned value as a new angle in degrees. It reconstructs a unitless axis vector with the original magnitude. This changes direction, not directly the amount of stick deflection or a movement speed in metres per second.

For example, if a configured key maps 30 degrees to 45 degrees, an input at the former direction leaves at the latter with the same magnitude. Replacing this preset field after selection does not replace the already-selected touchPadCurve reference; select the preset again. Editing the keys on the active curve object changes what later evaluations use.

It reconstructs a unitless axis vector with the original magnitude. This changes direction, not directly the amount of stick deflection or a movement speed in metres per second.

For example, if a configured key maps 30 degrees to 45 degrees, an input at the former direction leaves at the latter with the same magnitude. Replacing this preset field after selection does not replace the already-selected touchPadCurve reference; select the preset again. Editing the keys on the active curve object changes what later evaluations use.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.decelTime
member.summary: Sound played when time-control input successfully requests a lower time-scale step.

remarks.para: This is an AudioClip rather than a deceleration duration. On primary-button down, TimeInput first clears the pending _timeInput flag. If TimeManager’s slow-time input is enabled and its current step is at most 2, the routine requests DECREASE_TIMESCALE and then plays this clip as a 2D one-shot.

The clip’s volume and pitch are derived from the manager’s step after that request. Replacing the clip changes the sound requested by this branch, not physical avatar deceleration or the wait before a later toggle. accelTime is used by the separate delayed-toggle branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.degreesPerSnap
member.summary: Speed setting used for smooth turning and for how quickly a queued snap turn is applied.

remarks.para: The name is misleading: this unitless setting does not choose the snap angle. Smooth turning calculates its full-input rate as 48 × degreesPerSnap + 60 degrees per second. SnapRotate calculates a smoothing time of 0.01 + 0.2 / degreesPerSnap seconds. snapDegreesPerFrame is the separate mode selector that chooses 15, 30, 45 or 90-degree snaps.

For example, settings 2 and 4 give smooth-turn rates of 156 and 252 degrees per second before axis filtering and time-scale compensation, and snap smoothing times of 0.11 and 0.06 seconds. These are illustrative values. Increasing a positive setting makes smooth turning faster and reduces the snap smoothing time, without changing the selected total snap angle.

The in-game menu cycles the saved speed setting from 1 through 10. That menu range is not a runtime clamp on writes to this field: the native turn helpers use the supplied value directly, including the division. BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT copies its locomotion speed setting here, so a later settings propagation can overwrite a mod’s edit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.directionMasterTransform
member.summary: Cached orientation reference used to turn active movement input into the rig’s movement direction. It is selected by .

remarks.para: OnStart selects this reference from directionMode. Controller mode uses the physical left controller when isRightHanded is true and the physical right controller otherwise; Head uses m_head; Custom uses CustomDirection. SetDirectionMasterTransform can select it again without changing the stored directionMode.

OnEarlyUpdate uses this transform’s orientation together with the body-support orientation to rotate active, unitless movement-axis input. Its position is not a requested destination. For example, with a controller reference, changing the controller’s facing changes the walking direction supplied by the same stick input.

Assigning the reference directly changes the later orientation source; it does not move the avatar at assignment time. The selector and player-settings propagation can replace it. Supply the reference required by the selected path: a missing custom reference at startup changes the saved mode to Head after the attempted selection, but does not immediately recache a head reference in that fallback branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.directionMode
member.summary: Startup choice of the orientation source used for walking direction.

remarks.para: OnStart uses Controller to select the non-dominant physical controller, Head to select m_head, or Custom to select CustomDirection. In Controller mode, isRightHanded true selects physical left and false selects physical right. The selected reference is stored in directionMasterTransform, whose orientation later rotates active movement input.

Changing this field after startup does not automatically select a new reference. SetDirectionMasterTransform chooses the current reference immediately but does not update this mode. BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT also selects the current reference using its own locomotion-direction setting.

For example, writing Head prepares the stored mode, while calling SetDirectionMasterTransform(Head) selects the head now. If startup Custom has no valid reference, OnStart changes this stored mode to Head after its selection attempt; it does not repeat that selection in the fallback branch. Assign the custom transform before startup or explicitly select a valid reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.drawDebugBodyBones
member.summary: Stored debug flag that does not gate the checked OnUpdate bone-line drawing.

remarks.para: The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines contain no read of this flag. In particular, OnUpdate reaches its Debug.DrawLine calls without testing it. Their other execution conditions and required references still apply.

Setting this flag false therefore does not switch off those checked debug-line calls, and setting it true does not force the body update to run. The field’s name is not proof of an active rendering control. This scope does not establish that no external routine or mod reads it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.frequencyMult
member.summary: Stored multiplier initialized to 1 by the constructor, with no reader in the checked OpenControllerRig paths.

remarks.para: The native constructor writes 1 to this field. The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not use it in a frequency calculation or in the Gimbal smoothing parameters. Those smoothing calls supply their own numeric settings.

Changing it therefore does not change the smoothing frequency or display refresh rate through those checked paths. No effect, unit or valid tuning range can be established from its name alone. The constructor write is an initialization fact, not a guarantee about every serialized instance or a claim that external code never reads the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.headset
member.summary: Transform where the rig keeps the tracked headset pose used to position and orient the player’s tracked head.

remarks.para: OnStart copies this transform’s local pose into _lastHmdLocal. OnEarlyUpdate directly applies the current headset/controller-tracking pose when tracking is available, performs tracking-state and root handling, and remembers the resulting local pose; when tracking is missing it restores the remembered pose. Position is in metres relative to the transform’s parent, and rotation is its orientation in that parent’s axes.

The main-camera render path can refresh its rotation close to rendering and updates position on its checked paused branch. Body fitting and tracker calibration also use the headset and its world pose. A transform reference is required by the paths that dereference it; assigning a different object does not itself repeat startup capture or calibration.

For example, moving this transform changes the pose currently held by the rig, but a later tracked update can replace that edit with the XR pose or remembered fallback. It is a tracked output/reference transform, not the XR device object or a free-standing camera-selection field.

The checked ordinary early update does not blend the headset through ProcessTrackedBlend or call CheckHeadsetLimits. That separate helper’s velocity and facing histories therefore do not certify this ordinary pose update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.isRightHanded
member.summary: Chooses which physical controller supplies the primary and secondary input roles.

remarks.para: When true, the rig’s checked input mapping uses physical left for the primary movement/time-control role and physical right for the secondary turn/height role. When false, those roles swap. It does not rename or exchange the physical left and right tracked hand transforms.

Controller movement-direction selection also uses the non-dominant physical controller: left for true and right for false. OnEarlyUpdate can use this flag for its current control mapping, but changing it does not automatically rebuild the cached directionMasterTransform. Reselect that direction reference if it also needs to follow the new handedness.

BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT copies its handedness into this field. In that routine the direction reference is selected before the new handedness is copied, so the cached Controller direction can reflect the earlier flag until selected again. A later settings propagation can overwrite a direct mod edit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.lPointerInPalmOffset
member.summary: Stored left palm-pointer pose that is not applied by the checked controller-rig update paths.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes this SimpleTransform with an identity pose: zero positional offset and no extra rotation. The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not read it to locate an interaction pointer.

Changing the stored pose therefore does not move the pointer through those checked routines. The field’s name does not establish the coordinate frame or an active pointer-calibration contract. It is separate from leftHandOffset and rightHandOffset, which are actually composed with tracked controller poses. This checked-code finding does not establish that every external interaction routine ignores it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.lastHmdLocal
member.summary: Remembered headset pose used when current tracking is unavailable and as a reference for headset reacquisition alignment.

remarks.para: The SimpleTransform contains the headset’s local position in metres and its quaternion orientation relative to the headset parent. A quaternion stores rotation; its four numbers are not four degree angles. OnStart copies the configured headset transform into this memory.

OnEarlyUpdate restores this remembered pose when the XR headset is disconnected or not tracking. With tracking available, it directly applies the current headset pose, performs its tracking-state and root handling, and remembers the resulting local pose for later alignment and fallback. The late camera-render path can refresh the live headset without replacing this memory, so it is not necessarily the pose from the immediately preceding rendered frame.

The public lastHmdLocal property reads or replaces the same memory directly. Writing it does not immediately move the headset or run a tracking check, but changes the reference used by the next early update. For example, replacing its position changes the next calculated displacement and the pose restored if tracking is missing; a later tracked update can overwrite it.

The checked ordinary OnEarlyUpdate does not run headset ProcessTrackedBlend or call the separate CheckHeadsetLimits helper. Its remembered pose is the resulting early-update output, rather than a sample certified by that helper’s motion-limit tests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.leftAdjustDir
member.summary: Stored left controller adjustment direction step that the checked rig routines do not apply.

remarks.para: The field is an integer, but the complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not read it or implement a numeric choice table for it. No meaning for particular numbers or active adjustment axis can be established from the field name.

Setting it therefore does not step the left controller offset through those checked routines. Actual tracked-pose correction uses leftHandOffset, and ProcessesWristOffset can replace that correction with a device preset. Treat this integer separately from that active correction path; this scope does not establish that every external calibration tool ignores it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.leftHandOffset
member.summary: Correction composed with the tracked left controller pose before placing the hand.

remarks.para: OnEarlyUpdate combines a valid XR controller pose with this SimpleTransform. Its positional part is an offset in metres in the controller’s own axes, and its quaternion is the extra orientation relative to the controller. The corrected position is device position plus device rotation applied to offset position; the corrected rotation is device rotation multiplied by offset rotation.

For example, a 0.01-metre offset along the controller’s local right direction shifts the hand one centimetre along that direction, which turns as the device turns. It is not a fixed one-centimetre world-X shift. The correction enters the normal tracking blend, so changing it need not instantly replace the displayed hand pose.

ProcessesWristOffset writes device-specific left and right corrections and stops full XR-hand updating for the recognized device branches. It runs during the main-camera render update, so a direct edit can be overwritten by the next preset refresh. The constructor initializes this correction to an identity pose; that is not a guarantee about its value after setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.leftOffsetBuffer
member.summary: Stored left calibration pose buffer that the checked rig paths do not use to update the hand correction.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes this SimpleTransform to an identity pose: zero positional offset and no extra rotation. The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not read it or copy it into the active hand offset.

Editing this buffer therefore does not calibrate the left hand through those paths. leftHandOffset is the correction actually composed with the tracked controller pose, and ProcessesWristOffset can refresh it from device presets. A consumed coordinate frame or tuning effect for this buffer has not been established; this does not claim that every external calibration tool ignores it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.onLastCameraUpdate
member.summary: Routine called after this rig’s main-camera render update path has finished.

remarks.para: This Action is a callback: a routine called to report or perform an action. OnMarrowReady registers OnBeginCameraRendering with the render pipeline. When that hook receives Camera.main, it processes its late XR and headset update path, then invokes this Action if assigned. Other cameras do not invoke it through this hook.

The call occurs after the attempted device and wrist-offset refresh, but it is not proof that every tracked device produced a fresh pose. The Action is still reached on the main-camera path when the headset tracking branch is skipped. It has no camera argument and belongs to this rig instance.

For example, a mod can use it to update something after the rig’s late pose work and before that camera renders. Assigning the Action stores the routine; it does not invoke it immediately. OnDestroy removes this rig’s pipeline hook. Rendering or invoking the hook repeatedly can call the Action repeatedly, so it is not a once-per-physics-step notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.player
member.summary: The tracking avatar whose measurements and bones this controller rig uses to fit the player’s tracked body.

remarks.para: This RealHeptaAvatar supplies the body proportions and skeleton used by the controller rig’s body-fitting routines. It is a separate reference from RigManager’s currently equipped game avatar. OnRealHeptaAwake, the rig’s setup routine, assigns it to this rig’s avatar reference, precomputes its measurements from the manager avatar’s eye height in metres, and refreshes its own measurements while copying selected player shape factors into the calibration avatar.

OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate and UpdateHeptaBody use it while fitting torso, arms, pelvis and feet and saving the resulting body pose. SetAvatar updates the existing tracking avatar’s scale and measurements; it does not replace this reference with its argument. Reset can find a RealHeptaAvatar on the same GameObject (Unity scene object) for setup.

The public player getter returns the same stored reference without finding or creating another avatar. Replacing _player alone does not repeat initialization or equip that avatar in RigManager. A replacement needs the skeleton and measurements expected by the body-fitting paths; otherwise those paths can encounter missing references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.quickmenuEnabled
member.summary: Allows the UI controller-input path to operate the player’s quick menu.

remarks.para: UIControllerInput.Update reads this flag from the OpenControllerRig after positioning its UI input object at the selected hand. With the flag true, it continues through the controller menu-input path. With it false, it skips that path; if the quick menu is already open, it deactivates it, otherwise it returns.

For example, setting it false stops this checked controller UI path from opening the menu and closes an existing menu on that update. It does not itself disable the controller, remove the menu object or promise to block every direct menu activation from a mod.

BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT copies its own quickmenuEnabled flag here. A later settings propagation can therefore overwrite a direct edit. The flag is checked by the separate UI update, not by every controller-rig input sampling operation.
