member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.snapDegreesPerFrame
member.summary: Selects secondary-thumbstick snap turning or smooth turning; it is a mode number rather than degrees per frame.

remarks.para: In ProcessSecondaryThumbstick, modes 1, 2, 3 and 4 request snaps of 15, 30, 45 and 90 degrees. A snap request needs unitless horizontal magnitude at least 0.65 and vertical magnitude below 0.5. Horizontal magnitude below 0.4 rearms the next request. The queued angle is applied over successive calls by SnapRotate, not all as a fixed per-frame amount.

Mode 5 smooths horizontal input after a 0.4 dead zone and calculates a degree change using degreesPerSnap, the unitless speed setting, elapsed seconds and time scale. Mode 0 and other values do not start either of those turn calculations in this helper; they do not explicitly clear the already-cached _smoothTwist value. A mode change alone should therefore not be treated as erasing a previous turn result.

For example, mode 2 chooses a total 30-degree snap, while changing degreesPerSnap changes how quickly that debt drains. The in-game menu cycles saved mode values 0 through 5 and BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT copies the selected mode here. Neither that menu range nor this field’s name is a runtime clamp or a universal promise about every turning path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.testOffsetDir
member.summary: Stored vector with no offset-testing or visualization consumer in the checked controller-rig paths.

remarks.para: The complete audited OpenControllerRig setup, input, camera-render and body-update routines do not read or write this vector. Its name alone does not establish a debug drawing operation, a consumed direction frame, a distance unit or a movement effect.

Changing it therefore does not test an offset or move a tracked point through those checked routines. Active tracked hand corrections use leftHandOffset and rightHandOffset, while tracking-transition blends use their own stored pose differences. This scope does not establish that every external debugging tool ignores the vector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.touchPadCurve
member.summary: Active curve that remaps controller-input direction while retaining the input’s deflection magnitude. It is selected by .

remarks.para: TouchPadCurve measures the unitless input vector’s angle from upward input in degrees, positive toward the right, evaluates this AnimationCurve with that angle, and treats its output as another angle in degrees. Sine and cosine rebuild a vector at that output direction with the original magnitude. The curve is an angular mapping, not a direct multiplier for movement speed.

For example, a curve that maps 30 degrees to 45 degrees turns an input at the former direction to the latter without changing its magnitude. The assigned curve’s keys determine its shape; a profile label such as Linear does not by itself prove identity mapping.

OnStart and SetTouchPadCurve select this reference from the configured preset fields, and player-settings propagation can select it again. Assigning a different curve changes later evaluations, while editing keys on the current curve changes the same object. The checked evaluator needs an assigned curve and does not provide a verified substitute for a missing one. OnEarlyUpdate uses this mapping when its primary movement-input flag is active, including eligible thumbstick input. Earlier axis preprocessing can change the magnitude; this angular-mapping stage preserves the magnitude supplied to it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedChest
member.summary: Calibrated chest pose reference used when fitting the tracked torso to the avatar.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. This Transform is the body point read by UpdateHeptaBody, separate from trackerChest, which receives the body device’s raw local pose. In the usual configured hierarchy, the calibrated child supplies the body point. CaptureTrackedOffsets edits trackerChest’s first child; it does not automatically assign this field to that child, so the references must be wired consistently.

The tracked torso path requires _hasAssignedOffsets and a connected body-tracking device with permission. When this reference is present, the solver reads its world pose and fits the torso using the player’s body measurements and spine limits. Those positions use world axes and metres. It does not simply copy the marker to every chest bone without limits; when chest tracking is absent, the torso can use its solving fallback.

Presence of this reference also enables chest tracker assignment, refresh and calibration, and selects the chest-based height reference when no tracked pelvis is configured. For example, moving a correctly calibrated chest marker changes the next eligible torso fit; assigning a transform alone does not obtain device data or capture offsets. Set up trackerChest and its child before calling the capture routine.
Body-array entry numbers count from zero: entry 0 is the first element. The stated position and rotation indexes therefore refer to those numbered elements, not physical tracker identifiers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedElbowLf
member.summary: Calibrated left elbow pose used to guide how that arm bends.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. When _hasAssignedOffsets is true and this reference is present, UpdateHeptaBody reads its world right direction and position. It combines that orientation with the displacement from this elbow marker toward the fitted upper-arm point (upper-arm position minus marker position) and the player’s upper-arm length, then supplies a bend-direction hint to SolveArms, the routine computing the arm pose. The hint influences the elbow’s orientation instead of directly copying a marker rotation onto every arm segment.

The position uses world axes and metres; transform.right is the marker’s own positive-X direction expressed in scene axes; it is unitless. The reference upper-arm length is the avatar’s upper-arm segment length in metres. AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack update trackerLowerArmLf for this role, and CaptureTrackedOffsets applies a zero-position, side-specific orientation correction to that tracker’s first child.

For example, rotating the left elbow marker changes the bend-direction hint even without translating it. The calibrated marker and raw lower-arm tracker must be assigned consistently; capture changes the first child’s pose rather than assigning this field. This arm consumer does not separately check whether its stored marker pose was refreshed this frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedElbowRt
member.summary: Calibrated right elbow pose used to guide how that arm bends.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. When _hasAssignedOffsets is true and this reference is present, UpdateHeptaBody reads its world right direction and position. It combines that orientation with the displacement from this elbow marker toward the fitted upper-arm point (upper-arm position minus marker position) and the player’s upper-arm length, then supplies a bend-direction hint to SolveArms, the routine computing the arm pose. The hint influences the elbow’s orientation instead of directly copying a marker rotation onto every arm segment.

The position uses world axes and metres; transform.right is the marker’s own positive-X direction expressed in scene axes; it is unitless. The reference upper-arm length is the avatar’s upper-arm segment length in metres. AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack update trackerLowerArmRt for this role, and CaptureTrackedOffsets applies a zero-position, side-specific orientation correction to that tracker’s first child.

For example, rotating the right elbow marker changes the bend-direction hint even without translating it. The calibrated marker and raw lower-arm tracker must be assigned consistently; capture changes the first child’s pose rather than assigning this field. This arm consumer does not separately check whether its stored marker pose was refreshed this frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedFootLf
member.summary: Calibrated left foot pose read to place the rig’s foot when both tracked foot references are configured.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. UpdateHeptaBody enters this foot-placement block only when both trackedFootLf and trackedFootRt are present. The block follows the point where tracked-torso and fallback-torso solving rejoin; it does not recheck _hasAssignedOffsets, body-device connection or permission. The other required rig parts and matching tracker transforms still need to exist.

The left marker supplies world position in metres and world orientation. Its position is smoothed relative to a moving head reference while keeping world axes, with a 0.05-metre correction limit and a 0.1-second smoothing setting. The moving head reference is the headset’s scene position plus the avatar’s stored skull/camera offset, a local distance in metres rotated by the headset’s orientation. The smoothing setting and elapsed update time guide the motion; arrival is not guaranteed after exactly 0.1 seconds. The solver also reads trackerFootLf’s world position to adjust the output orientation when smoothing changes the marker-to-tracker displacement.

For example, moving the left marker supplies a new foot target on the next body update, but smoothing can temporarily offset that target. CaptureTrackedOffsets can calibrate the corresponding tracker’s first child to the current rig foot. AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack do not fill these foot poses in the checked implementation; an external provider or mod must maintain the configured transforms if live motion is needed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedKneeLf
member.summary: Calibrated left knee pose used to choose that leg’s bend orientation in the tracked-foot block.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. After both tracked feet have been placed, UpdateHeptaBody reads this optional left knee marker’s world right direction and position. It combines them with the hip-to-foot direction, the fitted upper-leg position, the hip-side origin of that leg, and the player’s upper-leg length to build the leg’s orientation. The marker guides bending; it is not simply a world position copied onto the knee joint.

The marker position and reference upper-leg length are in metres, while its right direction is its own positive-X direction expressed in scene axes and is unitless. The hip-to-foot direction runs between the fitted hip point and the placed foot point. This consumer is inside the block that requires both tracked feet; it does not separately recheck body permission, connection or the calibration flag. A missing knee marker skips that side’s optional knee adjustment, subject to the preceding foot path’s requirements.

CaptureTrackedOffsets calibrates trackerKneeLf’s first child from the current rig-leg pose when this role is configured. AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack do not update knee tracker poses here. For example, a mod can provide a maintained knee marker to change the next bend hint, but setting this reference alone does not start a device stream or capture calibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedPelvis
member.summary: Calibrated pelvis pose used to fit the avatar’s hips and choose the pelvis-based height reference.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. This Transform is the calibrated body point, separate from trackerPelvis, which receives the raw body-device pose. CaptureTrackedOffsets edits the raw tracker’s first child to match the current rig pelvis; it does not automatically assign this field to that child. Configure the references consistently before capture.

UpdateHeptaBody uses the pelvis world pose in its eligible tracked-torso branches, then fits it against the avatar’s torso geometry and spine limits. The raw tracker’s world position also helps correct orientation when smoothing changes the marker-to-tracker displacement. Position is measured in metres in world axes. The pelvis Gimbal correction is limited to 0.2 metres and uses a 0.05-second smoothing setting in these branches. Gimbal is the routine smoothing motion and limiting its correction; this parameter does not promise arrival after exactly 0.05 seconds.

The tracked torso route requires _hasAssignedOffsets and a connected body device with permission. Separately, presence of trackedPelvis makes OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate choose the rig-pelvis-based height reference ahead of chest or head. For example, changing a maintained pelvis marker changes the next eligible torso fit; assigning the field alone neither captures offsets nor equips another avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackedShoulderLf
member.summary: Calibrated left shoulder position used to adjust the avatar’s collarbone pose.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. With _hasAssignedOffsets true and this reference present, UpdateHeptaBody reads its world position, converts it into the fitted chest’s local frame, which uses that chest’s origin, directions and scale, and compares it with the tracking avatar’s shoulder geometry. The resulting adjustment is limited by the avatar’s shoulder range, the permitted collarbone angles in degrees, and applied as a collarbone rotation. This guides the shoulder rather than directly moving every arm bone to the marker.

The marker’s world position is measured in metres; the conversion uses the chest’s axes and hierarchy scale. AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack write the raw upper-arm pose into trackerUpperArmLf, while CaptureTrackedOffsets calibrates that tracker’s first child. They do not replace this field with a newly found physical tracker or automatically wire it to the child.

For example, moving the left shoulder reference changes the next eligible collarbone adjustment within its permitted range. Configure the matching tracker and calibrated marker together. The shoulder consumer checks the calibration flag and marker reference here; it does not independently require a fresh device sample at this point, so a stale configured pose can still be read.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackerChest
member.summary: This existing transform receives the body device’s raw chest pose through AssignTrackingPucks; calibrated body fitting uses a separate marker.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. AssignTrackingPucks copies body-array position entry 6 and rotation entry 5 into this transform’s local pose when trackedChest is configured and the body device is connected with permission. Despite the method’s name, it does not find a physical puck, create a transform or replace this field’s reference. The relevant arrays must contain those entries.

RefreshBodyTrack updates this raw pose on its connected, permitted and _hasAssignedOffsets path. Its refresh position includes the head-alignment correction derived from the body device and headset. Local position uses tracking-space metres before parent scaling, and local rotation is orientation in the parent’s axes. Parent scale and rotation can change how that local pose appears in world space.

CaptureTrackedOffsets sets its first child’s local position to the current rig chest point expressed in tracker axes and applies a fixed orientation correction. That child is the calibration helper, which must exist and be wired to the appropriate tracked marker in the rig hierarchy. For example, a mod can supply this raw transform and its calibrated child, then capture offsets from the current rig pose; assigning the reference alone does not calibrate it. Later device refresh can overwrite edits to the raw local pose.

After copying the available raw poses, AssignTrackingPucks calls CaptureTrackedOffsets when its body-device connection and permission checks pass. This capture requires the configured raw trackers, their first children and matching rig references; a missing required object can interrupt the attempt. Assigning this field alone does not run capture, and this setup call does not automatically wire the calibrated marker fields.
Body-array entry numbers count from zero: entry 0 is the first element. The stated position and rotation indexes therefore refer to those numbered elements, not physical tracker identifiers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackerFootLf
member.summary: The checked AssignTrackingPucks path does not copy a raw left foot pose from the body device into this tracker reference.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. With trackedFootLf configured, CaptureTrackedOffsets edits this transform’s first child. It expresses the current rig foot position in tracker-local axes and records the rig foot rotation relative to the tracker. These distances are in tracker-local metres before hierarchy scaling; changing hierarchy scale changes the corresponding scene distances; the rotation is an orientation difference, not a set of degree offsets.

In UpdateHeptaBody’s both-feet block, the solver reads this raw tracker’s world position as well as trackedFootLf’s world pose. When position smoothing changes the displacement from raw tracker to calibrated marker, that change is used to adjust the rig foot’s orientation. Assigning this reference alone does not place the foot; the calibrated marker and required rig references must also be set.

Unlike the checked chest and arm roles, AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack do not copy body-device data into the left foot tracker here. For example, a mod using this pair needs to maintain the raw and calibrated poses through its own provider. Capture snapshots the current calibration child and does not create or discover a physical tracker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackerKneeLf
member.summary: The checked AssignTrackingPucks path does not copy a raw left knee pose from the body device into this tracker reference.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. When trackedKneeLf is configured, CaptureTrackedOffsets takes this transform’s first child and puts the current rig knee point into tracker-local coordinates. It also stores the current rig hip/upper-leg rotation relative to the tracker. The captured position uses tracker-local metres before hierarchy scaling; scale changes the corresponding scene distance. A quaternion is a four-number representation of orientation; this one records the hip/upper-leg orientation relative to the raw tracker.

UpdateHeptaBody reads the configured trackedKneeLf marker, rather than this raw tracker reference directly, to guide leg bending in its both-feet block. Wire the calibrated child and marker consistently; capture does not automatically replace trackedKneeLf with the first child or create missing objects.

The complete checked AssignTrackingPucks and RefreshBodyTrack routines do not copy device data into the left knee tracker. For example, assigning this reference can prepare a calibration setup, but a live knee pose still needs a provider that maintains the relevant transforms. Capture overwrites the child’s calibration when called again.

For example, a mod can supply this raw transform and its calibrated child, then capture offsets from the current rig pose; assigning the reference alone does not calibrate it. Later device refresh can overwrite edits to the raw local pose.

After copying the available raw poses, AssignTrackingPucks calls CaptureTrackedOffsets when its body-device connection and permission checks pass. This capture requires the configured raw trackers, their first children and matching rig references; a missing required object can interrupt the attempt. Assigning this field alone does not run capture, and this setup call does not automatically wire the calibrated marker fields.
Body-array entry numbers count from zero: entry 0 is the first element. The stated position and rotation indexes therefore refer to those numbered elements, not physical tracker identifiers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.trackerUpperArmRt
member.summary: This existing transform receives the body device’s raw right upper-arm pose through AssignTrackingPucks; it is separate from the fitted shoulder and elbow markers.

remarks.para: The _hasAssignedOffsets flag records a calibration attempt: CaptureTrackedOffsets sets it before processing the child objects, so a true value does not prove capture finished successfully or that the current frame supplied fresh device data. A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale; a pose is position plus orientation. Calibration records the correction between a raw tracker and the intended body point. World coordinates use the scene’s axes. Local coordinates use the containing object’s origin and axes; that containing object is the parent. The first child is the object directly beneath a tracker, whose local coordinates use that tracker’s origin and axes. AssignTrackingPucks copies body-array position entry 15 and rotation entry 15 into this transform’s local pose when trackedShoulderRt is configured and the body device is connected with permission. Despite the method’s name, it does not find a physical puck, create a transform or replace this field’s reference. The relevant arrays must contain those entries.

RefreshBodyTrack updates this raw pose on its connected, permitted and _hasAssignedOffsets path. Its refresh position comes from the corresponding body array without the torso head-alignment correction. Local position uses tracking-space metres before parent scaling, and local rotation is orientation in the parent’s axes. Parent scale and rotation can change how that local pose appears in world space.

CaptureTrackedOffsets sets its first child’s local position to the current rig right upper arm point expressed in tracker axes and applies a fixed orientation correction. That child is the calibration helper, which must exist and be wired to the appropriate tracked marker in the rig hierarchy. For example, a mod can supply this raw transform and its calibrated child, then capture offsets from the current rig pose; assigning the reference alone does not calibrate it. Later device refresh can overwrite edits to the raw local pose.

This capture requires the configured raw trackers, their first children and matching rig references; a missing required object can interrupt the attempt. Assigning this field alone does not run capture, and this setup call does not automatically wire the calibrated marker fields.
Body-array entry numbers count from zero: entry 0 is the first element. The stated position and rotation indexes therefore refer to those numbered elements, not physical tracker identifiers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.vrRoot
member.summary: Tracking-root transform adjusted to align the tracked player space with the avatar’s size and movement.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, orientation and scale. This root is a containing object for the configured tracked objects beneath it; its parent is the object containing the root. Parent-local axes follow that parent’s orientation and scale, while world axes are the scene’s axes. SetAvatar writes a uniform, unitless scale to this root. Its scale is avatar.eyeHeight / (player.realWorldHeight / player.heightPercent): avatar.eyeHeight is the supplied avatar’s eye height in metres, player.realWorldHeight is the tracking avatar’s calibrated real-world height in metres, and player.heightPercent is its unitless total-height-to-eye-height ratio: the player’s refreshed total height equals this ratio times its eye height. These are reference measurements for the size conversion, not extra controller-axis input.

OnRealHeptaEarlyUpdate uses the root’s up direction as the body-support reference and adjusts its parent-local Y position using _adaptiveY, the tracked-height correction in local metres. That path preserves local X and Z. Parent rotation and scale affect how a local displacement appears in world space; writing 0.1 metres locally is not guaranteed to mean a 0.1-metre world-up displacement.

The headset-limit handling in OnEarlyUpdate can also shift this root horizontally and turn it around the headset while reconciling the new tracked pose with the remembered pose. For example, moving or scaling the root changes the mapped tracked space for transforms actually beneath it. The code does not prove that every object the rig ever moves is its descendant. Later rig updates can overwrite a direct edit.

For example, if avatar.eyeHeight is 1.6 metres, player.realWorldHeight is 1.8 metres and player.heightPercent is 1.125, the uniform scale is 1.6 / (1.8 / 1.125) = 1. The ratio 1.125 means the player’s total height is 1.125 times its eye height, so dividing that real-world total-height reference by the ratio converts it to an eye-height reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.OpenControllerRig.vrVertState
member.summary: Stored posture enum that the checked controller-rig routines do not use to select a posture.

remarks.para: An enum is a stored choice from a list of named values. This enum lists Stand, Crouch, Sit, Kneel and Prone. The complete audited OpenControllerRig initialization, input, tracking, camera-render and body-update routines contain no read or write of this field. Its name and enum labels do not establish an active crouching or leg-placement control.

Setting it therefore does not switch those checked routines into the named posture. Actual body fitting uses tracked poses, avatar measurements and the rig’s separate movement and height inputs. This bounded code finding does not claim that every external game routine or mod ignores the stored enum, or establish a historical Boneworks origin.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ParticleSpreadManager.Info.direction
member.summary: Incoming direction captured when the manager configured a particle system.

remarks.para: A direction vector is three X, Y and Z numbers describing an arrow. AutoOrient copies its incoming direction into this record without normalizing it, so its length is not guaranteed to be 1. The usual impact caller supplies it using world axes, the level's axes; it is not the current velocity of an individual particle in meters per second.

The manager uses that input to choose a particle system's facing direction and emission angle. Source alignment faces opposite it, Direction alignment faces along it, and Reflected alignment uses its mirror direction across the supplied surface normal. For example, incoming (0, -1, 0) points downward in the world frame.

The manager creates a new record after applying one ParticleSpread component's rotation and emission-angle settings. AutoOrient clears its record list before processing the configured components again. This is a saved setup value, not a measurement updated as individual particles move. Editing the record does not update the particle system through the inspected manager methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ParticleSpreadManager.Info.name
member.summary: Name of the ParticleSpread component captured when this settings record was created.

remarks.para: The manager copies the component's Unity name into the record after applying its settings. This labels which configured particle spread produced the record; it is not a unique ID or a lookup key in the inspected manager methods.

For example, a component named Sparks produces a record labeled Sparks. Renaming that component later does not change an already stored string. AutoOrient replaces the manager's record list on its next call, so a newly made record can capture the new name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ParticleSpreadManager.Info.normal
member.summary: Surface-facing arrow captured when the manager configured a particle system.

remarks.para: A surface normal is an arrow perpendicular to a surface. For an upward-facing flat floor, (0, 1, 0) points up. The usual impact caller supplies a world-space normal, expressed in the level's axes, with no distance or speed unit. The manager copies the supplied X, Y and Z numbers into this record without normalizing them.

The manager uses the input for Surface alignment, reflected direction and the emission-angle calculation. A unit-length normal, an arrow of length 1, is needed for the recorded reflection formula to describe a true mirror bounce. This record describes the setup input rather than a new collision measured from a moving particle.

The manager creates a new record after applying one ParticleSpread component's rotation and emission-angle settings. AutoOrient clears its record list before processing the configured components again. This is a saved setup value, not a measurement updated as individual particles move. Editing the record does not update the particle system through the inspected manager methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ParticleSpreadManager.Info.reflect
member.summary: Calculated mirror direction across the surface described by .

remarks.para: The record contains r = d - 2 × (n · d) × n. Here d is the supplied incoming direction arrow, n is the supplied surface-normal arrow, r is the calculated reflected arrow, and 2 is a unitless numeric factor. The dot product n · d means n.x × d.x + n.y × d.y + n.z × d.z: it measures how much the arrows point along each other.

For a unit-length normal n = (0, 1, 0) and incoming d = (0, -1, 0), the result is r = (0, 1, 0), pointing up. These arrows use the same coordinate frame, normally the level's world axes. The manager does not normalize the inputs or the stored result; the mirror interpretation assumes n has length 1.

Reflected alignment uses this calculation to turn the particle system before the record is added. The manager also records it for other alignment modes. It does not mean that an individual particle has physically bounced, and changing the record does not rotate the particle system through the inspected manager methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ParticleSpreadManager.Info.spread
member.summary: Raw unitless angle-control value captured after the particle system was configured.

remarks.para: The manager calculates spread = C³, meaning C × C × C. C = n · (-d), where n is the supplied surface-normal arrow, d is the supplied incoming direction arrow and -d reverses that direction. The dot product adds the three matching X, Y and Z products. For arrows of length 1, C is 1 for a straight-in hit, 0 for motion along the surface and -1 for motion away from it. This stored value is not an angle in degrees and is not a distance.

To choose the applied emission angle, the manager limits a separate copy to the range 0 through 1; call that copy t. It uses A = MinAngle/2 + ((MaxAngle - MinAngle)/2) × t. MinAngle and MaxAngle are that ParticleSpread component's configured angle limits in degrees, A is the particle system's applied shape angle in degrees, and 2 is a unitless divisor. The record stores the original spread, not t or A.

For example, C = 0.5 gives spread = 0.125. With MinAngle = 20 degrees and MaxAngle = 100 degrees, t = 0.125 and A = 10 + 40 × 0.125 = 15 degrees. With C = -1 the stored spread is -1, but the limited copy t is 0, so those same limits give A = 10 degrees. This is a snapshot of that setup calculation; editing it does not change the already applied angle through the inspected manager methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._angJerkMult
member.summary: Stores the current rotation-strength factor that lets the hand’s joint motors respond harder to a large rotation-following error.

remarks.para: This unitless factor multiplies the rotation-drive maximum-force inputs. The error combines the turning speed needed to reach the desired rotation in one physics step with the speed at which that desired rotation changed; the hand’s actual turning velocity is subtracted from each before the two are added. The normal rotation solver moves it toward 1 at 12 units per second when its combined angular-speed error exceeds 3 radians per second, or toward 0.1 at 8 units per second otherwise. Those are update rates, not a fixed number of frames.

Lower values reduce the maximum drive strength but also increase part of the damping calculation through 1 minus this factor. ClearJerk can lower it immediately. The next arm physics update recalculates it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._armInternalMult
member.summary: Scales both the hand-following force calculation and the maximum strength of the shoulder and elbow joint motors.

remarks.para: This is the stored value exposed by armInternalMult. It is unitless and is multiplied by _forceMultiplier to make the combined arm-strength scale. For example, 0.5 with _forceMultiplier = 1 supplies half the combined scale; it does not promise that every final movement or force is exactly halved.
Changing the value affects later force solving. EarlyUpdateArm refreshes shoulder and elbow motor limits only when the product differs from _lastForceMult.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._armMantle
member.summary: Stores the last calculated assistance weight for pushing the body up with a supported, downward-facing palm.

remarks.para: This is the same unitless 0-to-1 value returned by armMantle. ReadSensors overwrites it with ArmMantle’s result after updating the hand-load estimate. That calculation combines support, the palm’s downward-facing direction, and the hand’s height below the shoulder.

The shoulder muscle calculation multiplies its sideways force limits by 1 + 2 × this value. Thus an illustrative value of 0.25 contributes a factor of 1.5 to those limits. The axes turn with the current shoulder-to-wrist direction; this does not directly add a fixed upward force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._colliding
member.summary: Records whether a substantial collision impulse has been relayed since the last completed arm physics update.

remarks.para: CollisionRelay sets this true when a collision impulse’s squared size is at least 0.00001 newton-seconds squared. In the force calculation, true allows an empty hand to use the load-estimation path instead of being treated as freely moving.

FixedUpdateArm clears it after solving and publishing the accumulated impulse to currentCollision. It is a short-lived report of relayed collision impulses, not a lasting test of whether the hand still touches a surface.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._collisionImpulse
member.summary: Accumulates the world-space collision impulses reported for this hand during the current arm update interval.

remarks.para: Impulse is a push accumulated over time, measured in newton-seconds. CollisionRelay adds qualifying collision vectors here, so several collisions can contribute before the next arm update. ReadSensors uses its world Y component when calculating hand support.

At the end of a non-shutdown FixedUpdateArm, the vector is copied into currentCollision and then cleared to zero. Opposing vectors can cancel; its size is not the sum of the strengths of all contacts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._curlLerp
member.summary: Stores the smoothed finger-curl amount that changes the finger collision box’s pose and shape.

remarks.para: This is unitless, with ordinary curl input ranging from 0 for open fingers to 1 for closed fingers. UpdateColliders moves it toward the requested curl using a blend factor of 20 × frameDuration, limited to 0 through 1; frameDuration is Unity’s deltaTime in seconds.

For example, a 0.02-second update blends 40% of the remaining difference. Changes of 0.01 or less between the requested curl and this cache skip the shape update. Higher curl turns the finger box farther around its local up axis and shortens its local Z length; the side of the hand chooses the rotation sign.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._elbowServo
member.summary: References the that bends the forearm toward its elbow rotation target.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint: a connection between bodies with motors that pull toward a desired position or rotation. UpdateArmTargets supplies the elbow’s local rotation. Its angular X drive is the elbow motor refreshed by EarlyUpdateArm; CalibrateArmJoints positions its connection using the cached upper-arm length.
This stores the configured controller reference. Replacing it does not transfer the old joint’s calibration or reconnect its bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._fingerEnableFlag
member.summary: Stores a pending request to turn finger collisions back on once the finger box has space.

remarks.para: True does not mean that the collider is enabled. EnableFingerCollider sets the request. During UpdateColliders, a clear front-half check against fingerColCheckMask clears it and enables the finger box. DisableFingerCollider immediately disables the box and clears the request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._forceMultiplier
member.summary: Scales the hand-following force calculation and the arm’s shoulder and elbow motor limits.

remarks.para: This unitless value is multiplied by armInternalMult, the second unitless arm-strength scale. That combined product enters FixedUpdateArm’s force and rotation-strength calculations. EarlyUpdateArm also uses it as the maximum-force multiplier for the shoulder and elbow joint motors.

For example, 2 with armInternalMult = 0.5 gives a combined scale of 1. The effect also depends on load, damping, muscle limits, and later drive updates, so it is not a guaranteed multiplier of every final force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._handChestServo
member.summary: References the that controls the hand’s position and rotation relative to the chest.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint: a connection between bodies with motors that pull toward a desired position or rotation. UpdateArmTargets supplies the chest-relative hand rotation and, when forceViaJoint is enabled, position and velocity targets. UpdateArmSupportDrives always updates this connection’s X, Y, and Z position drives. Its rotation drive is selected when monofootEnabled is false.
This stores the configured controller reference. Replacing it does not transfer the old joint’s calibration or reconnect its bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._handRb
member.summary: Supplies the physics body for the hand segment of this arm.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s object that carries mass and responds to forces and collisions. The arm solver applies the hand-following force to this body and reads its position, rotation, velocity, and mass. SetArmMass assigns it 30% of the supplied arm mass.
This is a configured object reference. Replacing it changes which body later operations read or move; it does not automatically rebuild the arm’s joints or collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._handSupported
member.summary: Stores the smoothed hand-load signal that controls friction, relaxation, and mantle assistance.

remarks.para: ReadSensors calculates this unitless signal from accumulated world-Y collision impulse and, when present, the held joint’s world-Y force over the physics step. A caller-supplied normalization factor converts that load measurement into this signal. It is not a collider-contact boolean or a guaranteed 0-to-1 percentage of body mass.

The signal can rise by at most 6 × stepDuration or fall by at most 2 × stepDuration per sensor update, with stepDuration measured in seconds. It affects the palm/finger friction thresholds, rotation relaxation, the force solver’s gravity adjustment, and ArmMantle’s assistance calculation. Later sensor updates overwrite direct edits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._highFriction
member.summary: Stores the material selected for the palm and fingers when squeeze or support calls for high friction.

remarks.para: A physics material controls contact friction and bounce. Awake, the routine Unity calls when it initializes this component, replaces this reference with the palm collider’s current shared material and marks the high-friction mode active. An Inspector assignment made before Awake can therefore be overwritten.

Later squeeze above 0.5 or support above 0.2 selects this material when the high-friction mode is off. The asset’s own settings determine how much friction it actually provides; changing this reference alone does not immediately reassign collider materials.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._isHighFriction
member.summary: Tracks the material-selection routine’s high-friction mode for the palm and fingers.

remarks.para: Awake, the routine Unity calls when it initializes this component, sets this true after saving the palm’s current material as _highFriction. Grip above 0.5 or support above 0.2 can turn the mode on; grip below 0.5 and support below 0.1 can turn it off.

This is a cached decision, not a fresh comparison of collider materials. SetFriction changes this mode before assigning the palm and then the finger materials. Writing the flag does not assign a material, and manually changing a collider’s material can leave it out of sync. SetFrictionLow and SetFrictionNatural clear it after their material assignments, and only when that assignment path runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._jerkedMult
member.summary: Stores the force-strength factor that rises when the requested hand force increases sharply and relaxes when it does not.

remarks.para: The force solver compares newSq, the new position-correction force’s squared size, with oldSq, the saved force vector’s squared size. A force’s squared size is the sum of its X, Y, and Z components squared, measured in newtons squared (N²). Only when newSq is greater than oldSq + 1 N² does this unitless factor move toward 1 at 3.2 units per second. Otherwise it moves toward 0.15 at 4 units per second. For example, oldSq = 100 N² and newSq = 100.5 N² still take the relaxation branch because the increase does not exceed the 1 N² margin.

The shoulder muscle calculation multiplies its directional force limits by this factor. Lowering it weakens those limits until later physics updates raise it again. ClearJerk lowers it to a requested ceiling, and SetHand clears it when zeroVelocity is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastForce
member.summary: Stores the last calculated world-space hand-following force, in newtons, for the next load estimate and force-response update.

remarks.para: This is the solver’s force result, not a reading of the force that a joint actually applied. When the hand is attached to a static target, the direct-force path applies 30% of this vector to the hand while retaining the full vector in this cache. The chest’s physics body receives the opposite full force.

ApplyForce replaces the cache at the end of solving; invalid calculated components can result in a zero vector. The next solve compares its size and uses it with the change in relative hand velocity to estimate effective carried load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastForceMult
member.summary: Stores the last maximum-force multiplier applied by EarlyUpdateArm or UpdateArmDrives.

remarks.para: This unitless cache suppresses repeated drive updates. EarlyUpdateArm compares it with _forceMultiplier × armInternalMult. UpdateArmDrives compares it with its slerpForceMult argument.

Because UpdateArmDrives returns as soon as that force multiplier matches, changing only the spring or damping arguments can be ignored. This cache is not the last physical force, nor proof that every joint currently has the same strength.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastTargetLocalPos
member.summary: Stores the previous desired hand center-of-mass offset from the upper-arm body, expressed along world axes.

remarks.para: The vector is in meters. Although its name says Local, the position-force calculation compares it with the hand’s world center of mass minus the upper-arm’s world position. Its origin is relative to the upper arm, while its X, Y, and Z directions remain world directions.

FixedUpdateArm adds the rotated hand center-of-mass offset to its supplied hand-position target before ApplyForce saves this vector. On the next solve, target change divided by the physics-step duration in seconds supplies the desired relative movement speed. Direct edits can therefore create an artificial target-speed change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastTargetRotation
member.summary: Stores the previous desired world rotation of the hand for calculating how fast its rotation target is moving.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion, Unity’s four-number way of storing an orientation; it is not a four-component angle or a torque. ApplyTorque2 compares the new desired rotation with this saved one and divides the angle change by the physics-step duration to calculate target angular speed.

The solver replaces it after applying the rotation-drive settings. Keep this history consistent with the desired hand pose when changing it, or the next update can interpret the change as rapid target movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastTorqueSqMg
member.summary: Stores the squared size of the torque calculated by the alternate ApplyTorque routine.

remarks.para: The value has squared newton-meter units: a calculated torque of 2 newton-meters has a squared size of 4. ApplyTorque compares a new calculated torque size with this cache to choose how its rotation-strength factor changes, then overwrites the cache.
The normal FixedUpdateArm path calls ApplyTorque2, which does not update or read this cache. Treat it as history for the alternate routine, not a current measurement of the joint’s applied torque.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lastVel
member.summary: Stores the previous hand velocity relative to the upper-arm body for estimating carried load.

remarks.para: The components follow world X, Y, and Z and are in meters per second. ApplyForce begins with the hand’s velocity minus the upper-arm body’s velocity at its own position. When solving the second hand on a static target, it also accounts for the other hand’s saved force. The saved Y component includes the solver’s support-dependent gravity adjustment for that step.

The change from this cache to the next relative velocity, divided by the physics-step duration, supplies acceleration for the effective-load estimate. This is not the hand’s unmodified world velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lowFriction
member.summary: Supplies the material selected for easier sliding of the arm and palm.

remarks.para: A physics material controls contact friction and bounce. SetFrictionLow assigns this asset to the upper-arm mesh, forearm mesh, and palm; it assigns _naturalFriction to the fingers. The squeeze/support selector can instead assign this low-friction asset to both palm and fingers when grip is below 0.5 and support is below 0.1.
Changing this reference alone does not update the colliders. The material’s actual friction settings, rather than its field name, determine how easily contacts slide.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._lowerArmRb
member.summary: Supplies the physics body for the forearm segment of this arm.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s object that carries mass and responds to forces and collisions. Its position and rotation locate the wrist’s attachment point for the muscle-force frame and hand recovery. SetArmMass assigns it 33.3% of the supplied arm mass.
This is a configured object reference. Replacing it changes which body later operations read or move; it does not automatically rebuild the arm’s joints or collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._muscleSpace
member.summary: Stores the turning coordinate frame in which the hand’s directional muscle-force limits are applied.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion, Unity’s four-number orientation value. The shoulder muscle calculation starts from the chest body’s orientation and turns its forward direction to point from the upper-arm body toward the wrist’s forearm attachment point.

MuscleClamp rotates a requested world force into this frame, limits each component with the saved positive and negative force bounds, and rotates it back. The frame changes as the arm moves; its axes are not fixed world axes. It is recalculated by PrepShoulderMuscle during force solving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._naturalFriction
member.summary: Supplies the material restored by SetFrictionNatural and assigned to the fingers by SetFrictionLow.

remarks.para: A physics material controls contact friction and bounce. SetFrictionNatural assigns this asset to the upper arm, forearm, palm, and fingers when its assignment path runs. SetFrictionLow assigns it only to the fingers while the other three shapes receive _lowFriction.
Changing the stored reference does not immediately update a collider. The asset’s actual coefficients determine its friction; the name does not establish a fixed strength.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._shock
member.summary: Stores a temporary increase in hand rotation damping after ClearJerk is called.

remarks.para: This unitless value is set to 1 by ClearJerk. ApplyTorque2 makes its damping multiplier at least 3 times this value, then moves the value toward 0 by 8 × stepDuration on each update; stepDuration is the physics-step length in seconds.
For example, a 0.02-second step reduces 1 to 0.84 after that solve. This is a decaying damping input, not a measured collision force or a factor that lasts exactly one rendered frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._shoulderServo
member.summary: References the that turns the upper arm toward its shoulder rotation target.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint: a connection between bodies with motors that pull toward a desired position or rotation. UpdateArmTargets sets the shoulder target relative to the chest. Calibration sets its base angular X and YZ drives, and EarlyUpdateArm refreshes their maximum-force multipliers.
This stores the configured controller reference. Replacing it does not transfer the old joint’s calibration or reconnect its bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._staticCheatMult
member.summary: Defines the 0.3 scale applied to the hand’s calculated force during a static grab.

remarks.para: The direct-force path applies 30% of its calculated force to the hand at the grab attachment point when the hand is connected to the world or a body moved without physics forces. It still stores the full calculated vector and applies the opposite full force to the chest.
This is a fixed unitless constant, not a runtime tuning field. ReadSensors compensates for the reduced hand-force contribution when it estimates support from a static grab’s joint force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._supportHandServo
member.summary: References the that controls the hand rotation through the rig’s support connection.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint: a connection between bodies with motors that pull toward a desired position or rotation. With monofootEnabled true, UpdateArmTargets calculates the rotation target from the hand and supplied support orientations, and UpdateArmSupportDrives selects this rotation drive. The flag chooses the rig’s single-foot support mode.
This stores the configured controller reference. Replacing it does not transfer the old joint’s calibration or reconnect its bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._upperArmRb
member.summary: Supplies the physics body for the upper arm segment of this arm.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s object that carries mass and responds to forces and collisions. Its position is the origin for hand-following displacement and its velocity is subtracted when estimating relative hand movement. SetArmMass assigns it 36.7% of the supplied arm mass.
This is a configured object reference. Replacing it changes which body later operations read or move; it does not automatically rebuild the arm’s joints or collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._wristServo
member.summary: References the that turns the hand toward its wrist rotation target.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint: a connection between bodies with motors that pull toward a desired position or rotation. UpdateArmTargets supplies the hand’s desired rotation relative to the forearm. ApplyTorque2 changes its angular X and YZ drive strengths and damping. The wrist’s forearm attachment also helps define the hand-force frame.
This stores the configured controller reference. Replacing it does not transfer the old joint’s calibration or reconnect its bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand._xNeg
member.summary: Stores the current negative X bound for the hand’s muscle-force calculation, in newtons.

remarks.para: The X axis belongs to _muscleSpace, a turning orientation based on the chest and the direction from shoulder to wrist; it is not a fixed world axis. The negative bound is the signed lower permitted component, normally a negative number.

PrepShoulderMuscle recalculates this from xNegForce, the configured force magnitude in newtons, together with arm strength, arm extension, motion direction, and the force-response factor. For X and Y it also increases the available strength with mantle assistance. MuscleClamp limits a requested force to this bound after turning it into muscle coordinates. Direct changes are temporary because the next force solve rebuilds the cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.additionalMass
member.summary: Stores the force solver’s estimate of extra effective load that the hand is moving or supporting.

remarks.para: This is measured in kilograms. The solver can estimate it from the saved force divided by the change in relative velocity per second, then subtract the hand body’s mass. Held-object and static-grab states choose different bounds or body-mass estimates, and the value is smoothed before being saved.

It affects the hand-following force and damping calculations. It does not add kilograms to the actual arm bodies: SetArmMass sets their masses from its supplied mass argument. SetHand clears this load estimate, and later force solving can overwrite direct edits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.angDampening
member.summary: Controls angular-velocity damping in the alternate ApplyTorque routine.

remarks.para: Its unit is per second. That routine keeps a fraction of hand angular velocity equal to 1 - stepDuration × angDampening, limited to 0 through 1; stepDuration is the physics-step length in seconds. Larger positive values remove more of the velocity before the routine calculates its torque response.

For an illustrative 0.02-second step and a value of 10, the retained fraction is 0.8. FixedUpdateArm normally calls ApplyTorque2, which does not read this setting. Changing it therefore does not tune the normal path’s wrist joint damping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.armInternalMult
member.summary: Scales the hand-following force calculation and the shoulder and elbow joint strength.

remarks.para: This property directly reads and writes _armInternalMult. It is unitless; the combined arm-strength scale is this value multiplied by _forceMultiplier, another unitless strength scale. For example, 0.5 with _forceMultiplier = 1 supplies half the combined scale.

The setter stores the value without refreshing any joint. The next force solve uses it, and EarlyUpdateArm refreshes shoulder and elbow motor limits when the combined product differs from its saved multiplier. Damping, load, and muscle limits also affect the final force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.armMantle
member.summary: Reports the last assistance weight for pushing the body up with a supported, downward-facing palm.

remarks.para: This reads the cached _armMantle value rather than recalculating it. ReadSensors updates the cache after measuring hand support. The value is unitless and ranges from 0 to 1, combining support, the palm’s downward-facing direction, and the hand’s vertical distance below the shoulder compared with the avatar’s arm length.

The hand muscle calculation increases its sideways force limits by the factor 1 + 2 × this value. For example, 0.25 contributes a 1.5 multiplier. The muscle axes turn toward the wrist, so the result is not a direct upward force or a measurement of climbing progress.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.cLower
member.summary: Supplies the collision shape that lets the forearm bump into other physical objects.

remarks.para: A MeshCollider is an invisible contact shape built from a mesh. CalibrateArmColliders replaces this mesh with one generated from the supplied avatar and makes it convex, meaning it has no inward dents.

SetFrictionLow and SetFrictionNatural assign its contact material. Replacing this reference changes which shape those routines modify; it does not automatically rebuild the joints or recalibrate the shape.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.cUpper

remarks.para: A MeshCollider is an invisible contact shape built from a mesh. CalibrateArmColliders replaces this mesh with one generated from the supplied avatar and makes it convex, meaning it has no inward dents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysHand.currentCollision
member.summary: Reports the accumulated world-space collision impulse from the last completed arm physics update.

remarks.para: This vector is measured in newton-seconds: impulse is the amount of push accumulated over time. CollisionRelay adds qualifying impulses into _collisionImpulse; FixedUpdateArm copies that accumulator here after its force and rotation solves, then clears the accumulator and the collision flag.

It is a vector sum, so opposing collision pushes can cancel. It is not a contact position, surface normal, or Collision object. With shutdown enabled, FixedUpdateArm returns early and leaves this report unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._chestPelServo
member.summary: Stores the longer joint connection whose separation-limit settings are calibrated between chest and pelvis.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint, a connection between simulated body parts. CalibrateJoints sets this joint's attachment points and linear-limit setting using the avatar's geometry; the avatar is the player's in-game body. Attachment points and distance limits use the project's Unity distance scale (often one unit per metre). Anchor vectors are expressed relative to the bodies they attach to; the joint's configured settings determine how it applies the limit.

This is separate from the four adjacent spine servos. The torso's EarlyUpdateSpineJoints, UpdateSpineDrives, UpdateSpineTargets and ZeroTargets methods operate on those four adjacent servos and do not update this longer connection. The joint's own configured movement modes determine how its saved distance limit is enforced.
Assign the intended existing servo and joint before calibration. Replacing this reference alone does not create a connection, apply avatar geometry or copy the old joint's settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._chestRb
member.summary: Stores the simulated chest body whose mass and movement contribute to the torso's physical motion.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body: it stores mass and responds to forces. This reference identifies the chest body used by torso mass assignment, centre-of-mass setup and momentum measurement. The rbChest getter returns this same stored reference.

When SetTorsoMass runs, it sets this body's Rigidbody.mass to 25% of the supplied torsoMass. Unity projects commonly express Rigidbody mass in kilograms; the native code passes this share of the argument. GetTorsoMomentum reads the current mass and world-space velocity in Unity distance units per second; Unity scenes often treat one unit as one metre, but the project sets that scale. World space uses the scene-wide axes. The method contributes mass times velocity to the torso's linear momentum, in mass-units times Unity-distance-units per second (kg·m/s when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). These values are read from the body, rather than fixed by reading this reference.

Assign the intended body before rig setup and torso calibration. PhysicsRig's initial setup copies all five torso bodies into its body set. Replacing this reference later does not automatically update that earlier set or rewire existing physics joints. The reference can be null when setup has not supplied it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._chestSpineServo
member.summary: Stores the joint controller that drives the chest relative to the spine along the internal spine chain.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a physics joint, a connection that applies forces between simulated body parts. CalibrateJoints adjusts its attachment points and saves angular drive settings using the avatar's body size and mass; an avatar is the player's in-game body.

UpdateSpineTargets takes the desired chest rotation relative to the desired spine rotation from its input rig, the group of objects describing the requested body pose. It passes that relative rotation and the update duration in seconds through the servo's local-target helper. For a positive duration, the helper can derive target angular velocity from a changed rotation; with a zero or negative duration it does not write target angular velocity. These are requests for physics to follow, not direct assignments to the body's actual pose.

EarlyUpdateSpineJoints and UpdateSpineDrives apply the saved angular drive with selected strength scales. ZeroTargets writes this joint's neutral rotation target and zero target turning speed. Assign the servo and its joint before calibration; replacing it later does not automatically give it the previous servo's saved drive or starting-rotation setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._headRb
member.summary: Stores the simulated head body whose mass and movement contribute to the torso's physical motion.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body: it stores mass and responds to forces. This reference identifies the head body used by torso mass assignment, centre-of-mass setup and momentum measurement. The rbHead getter returns this same stored reference.

When SetTorsoMass runs, it sets this body's Rigidbody.mass to 13% of the supplied torsoMass. Unity projects commonly express Rigidbody mass in kilograms; the native code passes this share of the argument. GetTorsoMomentum reads the current mass and world-space velocity in Unity distance units per second; Unity scenes often treat one unit as one metre, but the project sets that scale. World space uses the scene-wide axes. The method contributes mass times velocity to the torso's linear momentum, in mass-units times Unity-distance-units per second (kg·m/s when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). These values are read from the body, rather than fixed by reading this reference.

SetTorsoMass also resets this body's inertia tensor from its colliders and multiplies all three values by 1.25. The inertia tensor describes resistance to turning about the body's principal axes; its scale is mass times distance-unit squared (kg·m² when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). This unitless factor changes resistance to turning without multiplying the body's mass again.

Assign the intended body before rig setup and torso calibration. PhysicsRig's initial setup copies all five torso bodies into its body set. Replacing this reference later does not automatically update that earlier set or rewire existing physics joints. The reference can be null when setup has not supplied it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._lastLinearDamperMult
member.summary: Stores a remembered linear-damping value that the torso's own calibration and update methods do not use.

remarks.para: Linear damping means resistance to straight-line movement. This stored float is separate from the angular-damping marker. The complete PhysTorso constructor, calibration methods, target methods and drive-update methods do not read it or save a new value into it.

Writing this field alone therefore does not alter damping through those methods or request a joint refresh. The actual angular refresh checks _lastSpineForceMult and _lastSlerpDamperMult. Do not use this stored value as a reading of the current joint damping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._lastSlerpDamperMult
member.summary: Stores the damping-field value remembered after the four internal spine drives were refreshed.

remarks.para: Both EarlyUpdateSpineJoints and UpdateSpineDrives compare _slerpDamperMult with this unitless saved value, together with a force-scale comparison. If both comparisons match, they return without writing the drives. After all four writes return normally, they copy _slerpDamperMult here.

This is a change marker, not a measurement of actual damping or a record of UpdateSpineDrives' supplied damping multiplier. Changing this storage alone does not apply damping. For example, manually making the marker match the current field can suppress a refresh even though no new base calibration was performed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._lastSpineForceMult
member.summary: Stores the force scale last recorded after all four internal spine drives were written.

remarks.para: The value has no units. EarlyUpdateSpineJoints compares it with _spineInternalMult * _spineForceMult, the product of the current internal-strength and configured torso-strength scales. UpdateSpineDrives instead compares it with its supplied maximum-force scale. Both also check the saved damping marker before deciding to skip a refresh.

After all four servo writes return normally, the method saves its force scale here. Writing this storage does not change any joint by itself and can affect whether the next refresh is skipped. It tracks the scale used for that write, rather than the bodies' current forces or the saved base-drive strength.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._lowFriction
member.summary: Selects the shared contact material assigned to the six torso colliders by SetFrictionLow.

remarks.para: A physics material supplies friction and bounce settings for physical contact. This field stores the configured asset reference; the asset's actual settings determine sliding and bounce, so the field name does not establish a numerical friction value.

SetFrictionLow checks the pelvis collider's shared material against this reference. If it already matches, the method returns without updating the other shapes. Otherwise it copies this reference to pelvis, lower spine, spine, chest, neck and head, in that order. Assign the material and intended collider components before applying it.

Changing this field alone does not change materials already installed on the shapes. For example, supply your chosen low-friction asset here and call SetFrictionLow when the torso should use those contact settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._slerpDamperMult
member.summary: Sets the damping-to-spring scale used when the four internal spine angular drives are calibrated.

remarks.para: This is a unitless number, initially 0.1 before Unity applies saved settings. CalibrateJoints sets each saved angular damping value to its calculated spring value multiplied by this number. A physics joint connects simulated body parts; its angular spring turns toward the requested pose, while damping resists turning to reduce swinging and wobble. Slerp names the joint's combined rotation drive.

EarlyUpdateSpineJoints and UpdateSpineDrives compare this field with _lastSlerpDamperMult as a change marker. Changing it can trigger a refresh, but early refresh applies a damping multiplier of 1 to the saved base drive rather than rebuilding damping from this new number. Run the appropriate calibration step if you need a new saved damping-to-spring relationship.

For example, changing 0.1 to 0.2 before recalibration doubles the saved damping for the same calculated spring. Merely storing 0.2 and calling the early update does not perform that calculation again. Other callers can also give UpdateSpineDrives its own damping multiplier.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso._spineForceMult
member.summary: Scales calibrated internal-spine drive strength and the maximum force applied by later early updates.

remarks.para: This number has no units. The effective scale is _spineInternalMult * _spineForceMult, where _spineInternalMult is the adjustable internal-strength scale and _spineForceMult is the configured torso-strength scale. Both start at 1 in the native constructor, before scene or prefab settings are applied.

CalibrateJoints uses this product while calculating the four adjacent joints' saved angular spring, damping and maximum-force settings from the avatar's size and mass. An avatar is the player's in-game body. A physics joint is a connection that applies forces between simulated body parts; its spring pulls toward a pose, damping resists turning and its force limit caps that drive.

Later EarlyUpdateSpineJoints, unless shutdown is true, multiplies the already saved base maximum force by the current product when it detects a change. It does not recalculate the saved spring or damping. Calibration and later scaling are separate steps, so a scale used during calibration is already present in the saved base values.

For example, after calibration at both scales equal to 1, setting the internal scale to 0.5 makes the next refresh use half the stored maximum force. Calibrating again at 0.5 also changes the saved base settings; do not assume that every update rebuilds them. Neither operation directly changes body mass or collider size.

An avatar is the player's in-game body. PhysicsRig.SetAvatar calls this calibration when setting up a body.

Both friction methods can assign this collider their configured shared material. IgnoreWholeTorsoColliders includes it when ignoring or restoring collisions with another supplied shape or array of shapes. Head and spine shapes also participate in the four self-collision exclusions made by OnAwakeInitialize.

Assign the intended collider before setup and calibration. Replacing this reference alone does not generate its mesh, copy the previous material or transfer previously ignored collision pairs. Mesh vertices are in the assigned mesh's local coordinates and are transformed with the collider object. Their numeric distance scale comes from the project; Unity units are often treated as metres, but this calibration does not establish a conversion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.gChest
member.summary: Stores the chest hand-interaction grip that rig setup excludes from both player hands' nearby grip search.

remarks.para: Stores the chest's grip component, which provides a place and behaviour for hand interaction. PhysicsRig's OnAwake method is the project's rig-setup callback; it copies this reference into both player hands' ignored-receiver sets.

The hand's UpdateHovering method checks that set when choosing a nearby grip candidate and skips a matching receiver. This prevents those player hands from selecting the registered torso grip through that nearby-search path. It does not disable the component globally or prove that all other interaction paths ignore it.

Assign the intended component before rig setup. Replacing this field afterward does not automatically remove the old reference from the hands' sets or register the replacement. A reference stored here is separate from the receiver a hand is currently holding.

remarks.para: Stores the neck's grip component, which provides a place and behaviour for hand interaction. PhysicsRig's OnAwake method is the project's rig-setup callback; it copies this reference into both player hands' ignored-receiver sets.

This is a CylinderGrip, which supplies hand interaction along the avatar's cylindrical neck region. CalibrateTorsoGrips builds a two-key AnimationCurve from avatar geometry values and stores it in CylinderGrip.RadiusCurve. It sets CylinderGrip.limit from a derived distance and writes the inherited Grip.targetTransform.localPosition in that transform's local frame. CylinderGrip.UpdateJointConfiguration sets ConfigurableJoint.linearLimit.limit to max(limit - handWidth, 0). These dimensions use the project's Unity scale; the native methods do not establish a metres conversion. This grip setup is separate from the neck collider's shape setup.

The hand's UpdateHovering method checks that set when choosing a nearby grip candidate and skips a matching receiver. This prevents those player hands from selecting the registered torso grip through that nearby-search path.
