member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.neckCol
member.summary: Supplies the capsule collision shape sized and positioned to the avatar's neck during torso calibration.

remarks.para: A CapsuleCollider is Unity's rounded cylinder collision shape. CalibrateTorsoColliders changes its radius, height and centre using the avatar's neck dimensions; an avatar is the player's in-game body. Radius, height and centre are measured in the collider object's local Unity units and are affected by its transform scale. Unity projects often treat one unit as one metre, but this calibration does not establish that conversion.

Both friction methods can apply their configured shared material to this shape. IgnoreWholeTorsoColliders includes it when changing collision pairs with supplied shapes. OnAwakeInitialize separately disables its collisions with cSpine and cSpineLow, allowing the neck to overlap those parts without pushing against them through those pairs.
Assign this existing collider before PhysicsRig setup and avatar calibration. Reading or replacing the reference does not itself resize a collider, update ignored pairs or perform calibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.rbChest
member.summary: Returns the simulated chest body whose mass and movement contribute to the torso's physical motion.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body: it stores mass and responds to forces. This reference identifies the chest body used by torso mass assignment, centre-of-mass setup and momentum measurement. The getter returns _chestRb directly; it does not search the scene or create a body.

When SetTorsoMass runs, it sets this body's Rigidbody.mass to 25% of the supplied torsoMass. Unity projects commonly express Rigidbody mass in kilograms; the native code passes this share of the argument. GetTorsoMomentum reads the current mass and world-space velocity in Unity distance units per second; Unity scenes often treat one unit as one metre, but the project sets that scale. World space uses the scene-wide axes. The method contributes mass times velocity to the torso's linear momentum, in mass-units times Unity-distance-units per second (kg·m/s when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). These values are read from the body, rather than fixed by reading this reference.

Assign the intended body before rig setup and torso calibration. PhysicsRig's initial setup copies all five torso bodies into its body set. Replacing this reference later does not automatically update that earlier set or rewire existing physics joints. The reference can be null when setup has not supplied it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.rbHead
member.summary: Returns the simulated head body whose mass and movement contribute to the torso's physical motion.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's component for a physically simulated body: it stores mass and responds to forces. This reference identifies the head body used by torso mass assignment, centre-of-mass setup and momentum measurement. The getter returns _headRb directly; it does not search the scene or create a body.

When SetTorsoMass runs, it sets this body's Rigidbody.mass to 13% of the supplied torsoMass. Unity projects commonly express Rigidbody mass in kilograms; the native code passes this share of the argument. GetTorsoMomentum reads the current mass and world-space velocity in Unity distance units per second; Unity scenes often treat one unit as one metre, but the project sets that scale. World space uses the scene-wide axes. The method contributes mass times velocity to the torso's linear momentum, in mass-units times Unity-distance-units per second (kg·m/s when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). These values are read from the body, rather than fixed by reading this reference.

SetTorsoMass also resets this body's inertia tensor from its colliders and multiplies all three values by 1.25. The inertia tensor describes resistance to turning about the body's principal axes; its scale is mass times distance-unit squared (kg·m² when the project uses kg and one unit equals one metre). This unitless factor changes resistance to turning without multiplying the body's mass again.

Assign the intended body before rig setup and torso calibration. PhysicsRig's initial setup copies all five torso bodies into its body set. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.shutdown
member.summary: Skips normal early drive refresh and input-pose target updates while true.

remarks.para: EarlyUpdateSpineJoints and UpdateSpineTargets return immediately when this flag is true. This stops those methods from replacing joint drive settings or pose targets. A physics joint is the connection that applies forces between simulated body parts; existing joints and bodies can continue their physical simulation.

It does not make every torso method return: UpdateSpineDrives, ZeroTargets, friction switching and calibration can still run. PhysicsRig.ShutdownRig sets this flag, applies separate reduced drive settings, then calls ZeroTargets. Writing this flag alone does not perform those extra steps or freeze body position.

For example, set the flag when deliberately taking over torso target control, and supply the drive/target setup that your use requires. Clearing it permits later normal updates; it does not reconstruct the rig, the group of objects representing the player's body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysTorso.spineInternalMult
member.summary: Scales calibrated internal-spine drive strength and the maximum force applied by later early updates.

remarks.para: spineInternalMult reads and writes _spineInternalMult directly. Writing the property stores the number without immediately changing a joint. This number has no units. The effective scale is _spineInternalMult * _spineForceMult, where _spineInternalMult is the adjustable internal-strength scale and _spineForceMult is the configured torso-strength scale. Both start at 1 in the native constructor, before scene or prefab settings are applied.

CalibrateJoints uses this product while calculating the four adjacent joints' saved angular spring, damping and maximum-force settings from the avatar's size and mass. An avatar is the player's in-game body. A physics joint is a connection that applies forces between simulated body parts; its spring pulls toward a pose, damping resists turning and its force limit caps that drive.

Later EarlyUpdateSpineJoints, unless shutdown is true, multiplies the already saved base maximum force by the current product when it detects a change. It does not recalculate the saved spring or damping. Calibration and later scaling are separate steps, so a scale used during calibration is already present in the saved base values.

For example, after calibration at both scales equal to 1, setting the internal scale to 0.5 makes the next refresh use half the stored maximum force. Calibrating again at 0.5 also changes the saved base settings; do not assume that every update rebuilds them. Neither operation directly changes body mass or collider size.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._avgDeltaTest
member.summary: A stored number that the inspected rig setup, pose-switching and movement methods neither update nor use to control the body.

remarks.para: This is a separate floating-point field, a place to store a number that can have a fractional part. In this game build, the complete PhysicsRig methods inspected for initialization, avatar fitting, disabling and re-enabling the rig, teleporting, regular updates, ladder contact and stepping contain no read or write of this field. The constructor assigns no field-specific starting value either.

It is not part of the neighboring saved foot orientation, and the disable and re-enable pose snapshots do not include it. Those operations therefore do not provide an averaging rule, reset point or movement effect for this number.

No speed, distance or time unit has been verified for it. Do not treat its value as an average skid measurement. The actual skidVelocity and skidSpeed readings are separate: after a physics step they report the ball's contact-point velocity relative to the ground, as a world-space vector and its magnitude in metres per second.

This description covers the inspected PhysicsRig class and the supporting routines inspected with it. It does not rule out separate code accessing the field, or another game build using the stored value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._ballLocoEnabled
member.summary: Selects the rolling-ball locomotion path in the rig's update methods.

remarks.para: True makes the active updates use the monofoot, the single rolling ground-support ball and the support body above it, for stepping, support forces and collider maintenance. False skips those ball-locomotion paths. The value describes an enabled mode, not whether the ball is touching the floor.

EnableBallLoco sets this flag before rebuilding support links and enabling monofoot collision detection; DisableBallLoco clears it before undoing that configuration. Writing the field directly changes the branches that updates take, but does not run those setup operations or switch the separate legs' simulation mode. Use the mode-changing methods when the whole configuration needs to change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._cachedChest
member.summary: Saved chest pose that can be restored when the rig is re-enabled.

remarks.para: OnRigDisable overwrites this SimpleTransform with the chest's position and rotation relative to its transform parent, before returning it to the initial setup pose. A transform stores an object's position and orientation; its parent is the object it belongs under in Unity's hierarchy.

The saved position follows the parent's axes and is in Unity distance units, normally metres when the rig and its parents have scale 1, meaning they are not enlarged or shrunk. The saved rotation is a quaternion, a four-number orientation representation whose components are not degree angles.

OnRigEnable with reEnable true applies this saved local pose to the chest. Editing the cache changes the pose that operation will restore; it does not move the body immediately, and the next disable overwrites it. The value is a disable-time snapshot rather than a pose updated on every physics step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._cachedFootLf
member.summary: Saved left foot orientation relative to the left knee, restored when the rig is re-enabled.

remarks.para: OnRigDisable calculates this rotation from the left knee's inverse world orientation and the left foot's world orientation, before restoring the initial leg pose. The inverse orientation undoes the reference part's turn, leaving this part's orientation relative to that reference. World orientation means the direction a part faces in the game world's axes; this stored value instead describes how it faces relative to the left knee.

The value is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Its components have no distance units and are not angles in degrees. It stores a rotation only, with no position or velocity.

OnRigEnable with reEnable true combines the left knee's current world orientation with this value to restore the left foot's world orientation. Editing it changes that next restored orientation rather than immediately rotating the body. The next disable overwrites it with a fresh snapshot.

The saved position follows the parent's axes and is in Unity distance units, normally metres when the rig and its parents have scale 1, meaning they are not enlarged or shrunk. The saved rotation is a quaternion, a four-number orientation representation whose components are not degree angles.

OnRigEnable with reEnable true applies this saved local pose to the left hand. Editing the cache changes the pose that operation will restore; it does not move the body immediately, and the next disable overwrites it. The value is a disable-time snapshot rather than a pose updated on every physics step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._cachedHipLf
member.summary: Saved left hip orientation relative to the pelvis, restored when the rig is re-enabled.

remarks.para: OnRigDisable calculates this rotation from the pelvis's inverse world orientation and the left hip's world orientation, before restoring the initial leg pose. The inverse orientation undoes the reference part's turn, leaving this part's orientation relative to that reference. World orientation means the direction a part faces in the game world's axes; this stored value instead describes how it faces relative to the pelvis.

The value is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Its components have no distance units and are not angles in degrees. It stores a rotation only, with no position or velocity.

OnRigEnable with reEnable true combines the pelvis's current world orientation with this value to restore the left hip's world orientation. Editing it changes that next restored orientation rather than immediately rotating the body. The next disable overwrites it with a fresh snapshot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._climbingKneeJointVelocity
member.summary: Remembers the smoothing motion that helps hanging and climbing targets change gradually.

remarks.para: CheckStep passes this Vector3 by reference to SmoothDamp, a helper that moves a value toward a target while carrying a remembered velocity between updates. The helper reads and rewrites this field. Its components are smoothing velocities in metres per second, not the measured velocity of a physical knee.

During hanging it smooths the knee-to-pelvis joint's target position, so the components follow the joint's coordinate axes. A physics joint is the connection that guides relative movement between simulated parts. During climbing the same field is reused while smoothing the last contact point in world coordinates. It therefore has no single fixed reference frame for every state.

Changing the field changes the carry-over motion in the next smoothing calculation. Setting it to zero removes that remembered motion; it does not stop a Rigidbody, the body Unity actually moves through the physics simulation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._climbingNormal
member.summary: Stores the outward direction of the last climbing contact surface for support placement and ball rolling.

remarks.para: World axes are the fixed directions of the game world, rather than axes that turn with a body part. CheckStep fills this world-space Vector3 from the normal returned by its climbing contact query. A surface normal is a direction perpendicular to the surface, pointing outward. It is normally a unit vector, meaning a direction vector of length 1 with no distance units; for example, (0, 1, 0) points straight up from a level floor.

While hanging or climbing, OnAfterFixedUpdate places the centre of pressure one current ball radius opposite this direction from the monofoot ball's centre. The centre of pressure is the rig's support reference point. ApplyFeetForce also uses the direction to calculate the ball's rolling rotation while climbing.

The value can retain the last recorded direction after a state change; it is not a flag proving the rig is currently climbing. UpdateLadderInfo stores rung data and does not itself refresh this contact normal.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._climbingOffset
member.summary: Metre-valued correction subtracted from the monofoot knee-to-pelvis vertical target.

remarks.para: UpdateKnee subtracts this value from the joint's Y target after adding the crouch and gravity-support terms. A physics joint connects simulated parts; its target is where the controller tries to guide their relative movement. Positive 0.1 therefore reduces the target by 0.1 metres along the joint's Y axis, while a negative value increases it.

This is a target correction, not a direct world-height change or an immediate move of the body. When the step state is not Climbing, ApplyFeetForce moves the value toward zero at 0.1 metres per second using Unity's fixed physics timestep. For example, 0.02 metres eases away over roughly 0.2 seconds of physics updates.
The correction is kept while the Climbing state is active. Setting ladder information alone does not calculate or assign it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._climbingVelocity
member.summary: World-space correction velocity that rolls the locomotion ball along the surface during the Climbing step state.

remarks.para: This is a calculated Vector3, in metres per second along the world X, Y and Z axes. CheckStep derives it from the change in a smoothed climbing support point, adds a small tracking-error correction, removes the component pointing through the surface, and divides the remaining displacement by the physics-step duration in seconds. It describes the correction along that surface; it is not a measurement of the entire body’s velocity or a ladder movement command.

Entering Climbing from the supported Dangle branch clears this velocity. Successful climbing checks then replace it, and ApplyFeetForce uses it with the climbing surface normal to choose the ball’s rolling angular target. Outside Climbing, the ordinary stepping and movement calculation is used instead. A cached value can therefore outlive the state that used it. Read climbingVelocity for this result; changing the stored vector does not move the support point and can be overwritten by the next successful check.

A surface normal is a unitless direction pointing straight out of the contact surface. Removing the normal component leaves the surface-tangent part, so this cached velocity is a world movement correction along the surface, in metres per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._collisionCollectors
member.summary: Body collision collectors that the rig processes after a physics step to report significant contacts. See .

remarks.para: Each CollisionCollector gathers contact information. OnAfterFixedUpdate calls the two-argument ProcessCollisionHaul overload on every entry after updating the hand and head sensors and before updating the whole-body movement measurements. The pelvis rigidbody, the Unity component that stores mass and simulated motion, must be awake for this processing to run. The later shutdown check does not bypass this earlier collector loop.

A collector can call its significant-enter or significant-stay callbacks: a callback is a routine called to report an action, here a collision. Each callback receives the stored RelevantCollision payload, which includes contact point, outward contact normal, relative velocity, total impulse, and the associated body/contact references. On an enter with an impulse, the significant-enter test compares the contact-normal dot relative-velocity value with impactVelocityThresh; the significant-enter callback runs only when that value reaches the threshold. The stay callback follows its separate non-enter path. The callback runs before the collector clears its gathered data. Putting a collector in this array includes it in that processing loop; it does not by itself attach it to a collider or connect a sound listener. Keep the array and its entries valid. An empty array processes no collectors, but a null array or null entry is not skipped safely.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._doubleCooldown
member.summary: Physics-clock deadline before an armed double-jump request can add another upward impulse.

remarks.para: The value is an absolute time in seconds on Time.fixedTime, Unity’s clock for the physics simulation. It is not a countdown or the requested cooldown duration. CheckDoubleJump rejects an otherwise armed request while fixedTime is less than this value; equality is allowed.

On an accepted request, CheckDoubleJump first clears _doubleReady, adds the requested impulse to _monoRemainder, and stores fixedTime plus the supplied cooldown duration here. For example, accepting a request at physics time 12 seconds with a 1-second cooldown records 13, not 1. Readiness must still be established separately; reaching this deadline alone does not arm the jump.

The accepted newtonSecond input is an impulse in N·s, and the destination _monoRemainder stores that impulse for later release. The cooldown field itself is an absolute fixed-physics-clock deadline in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._doubleLaunchWindow
member.summary: Physics-clock deadline used to expire an armed jump when the feet have enough support.

remarks.para: When CheckDoubleJump finds _doubleReady false and footSupported greater than 0.1, it first sets readiness true, then records Time.fixedTime plus 0.5 seconds here and returns false. That call arms the request; it does not launch it. This field stores the resulting absolute time in seconds, not the length of the window or time remaining.

OnAfterFixedUpdate clears readiness only when the physics time is strictly later than this deadline and footSupported is greater than 0.25. At the deadline itself, or with support at or below 0.25, that expiration branch does not clear it. For example, arming at 8 seconds records 8.5; a later supported update can expire it after 8.5. The deadline does not establish a universal airborne time limit, and accepting a jump does not itself refresh this field.

footSupported is a unitless support amount. The native strict comparisons are preserved: support thresholds decide arming/acceptance, while the field stores the absolute fixed-time launch-window deadline in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._doubleReady
member.summary: Whether CheckDoubleJump is armed to consider adding an upward jump impulse.

remarks.para: If this flag is false, footSupported must be greater than 0.1 for CheckDoubleJump to arm it. That call sets the flag true, records a launch-window deadline 0.5 physics seconds ahead, and returns false. If support is at or below 0.1 and the flag is false, it returns false without arming.

An armed request is still rejected before _doubleCooldown. Once that deadline is reached, acceptance clears this flag before adding the requested impulse to _monoRemainder and updating the cooldown deadline. The flag therefore reports permission to try, not proof that a launch happened. OnAfterFixedUpdate can also clear it after the launch-window deadline when footSupported is greater than 0.25. Those support numbers are unitless support amounts; they are not distances or stick input thresholds.

The accepted upward push is an impulse in N·s, not a velocity. CheckDoubleJump adds it to _monoRemainder, which later releases it through the monofoot physics body; the permission flag is set false before that addition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._feetKneeJoint
member.summary: The whose angular target rolls the locomotion ball beneath the knee proxy.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in Unity’s physics simulation and can push them toward a target position or rotation. ApplyFeetForce converts the desired rolling direction into the feet rigidbody’s local axes and writes this joint’s targetAngularVelocity in radians per second. SetAvatar uses Avatar._strengthLower multiplied by 0.35 as a shared strength-based factor: it sets the feet Rigidbody inertia tensor from that factor, this joint’s Slerp damper to the factor multiplied by 9e13, and its maximum force to the factor multiplied by 1000. The avatar pelvis mass is excluded from these feet-body inertia and feet-joint damper/cap settings. Rigidbody means Unity’s physics body that stores mass and simulated motion. The slerp spring drives toward the target orientation; its damper resists angular turning, and max force caps twisting torque in N·m. Under a torque-based angular drive with a conventional SI scene scale (1 Unity distance unit = 1 m, mass in kg, time in seconds), the spring gain has units N·m/rad and damper gain N·m·s/rad. That scale is an assumption, not a scale established by these code paths.

DisableBallLoco sets this joint’s angular target to zero after disabling knee/feet collisions and resetting the step state. This reference must match the rig’s configured feet-to-knee joint; replacing a reference does not configure its connected body, axes or anchors. The native consumers require a valid joint. It controls the ball’s relative rotation, while _kneePelJoint handles the separate knee-to-pelvis position targets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._feetRb
member.summary: The Rigidbody that simulates the locomotion ball’s feet proxy.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for mass, velocity and physical motion. This is the central monofoot feet object, rather than the avatar’s separate left or right foot bone. rbFeet returns this same reference. The rig reads its world position for support, crouch height, casts and climbing, and uses its rotation to express the rolling joint target in local axes.

Reset obtains or adds this component on the feet GameObject. SetBodyMassDistribution assigns it 56.25% of the current monofoot mass budget; the knee receives the other 43.75%. SetAvatar resets its local center of mass, the balance point used by physics, and recalculates its resistance to rotation. EnableBallLoco and DisableBallLoco enable or disable its collision detection. StepFeet and UpdateFootballRadius also change its position, so a manual pose or mass edit can be replaced by those rig operations.

A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. Its world position is in metres at unit scale, velocity is metres per second, and mass is kilograms; the rig uses this reference for the feet body’s simulated motion and mass setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._footHits
member.summary: Reusable array that limits how many contacts a foot sphere cast can examine.

remarks.para: OnAwake, the rig’s initialization routine, creates an array with 32 entries. FootCast supplies it to SphereCastNonAlloc, which writes contacts into the existing array instead of creating a new hit array. FootCast uses footballColCheckMask to choose physics layers, follows Unity’s global trigger-query setting, and filters out rigidbodies listed in selfRbs.

Only the returned hit count is examined; old values outside that count are not fresh contacts. The helper ranks eligible sphere hits by the squared distance from the cast origin to hit.point plus hit.normal times the cast radius, and rejects points extremely near the world origin. Filtering occurs after the physics query, so a full buffer can hide additional eligible hits. The array is not expanded by this helper. Keep it non-null and non-empty: its false-result path still copies slot zero, which is not evidence of a valid hit. A zero-length array is not a safe way to turn foot casting off.

This is a buffer of sphere-cast RaycastHit results. hit.point and the cast origin are world positions in metres, hit.normal is a unitless outward direction, and cast radius is metres. The ranking compares squared distance in m², so it avoids a square root. The helper filters Rigidbody owners and uses Unity trigger-query policy; an empty/false result still has the documented invalid-buffer caveat.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._football
member.summary: The that forms the rolling ball used for monofoot locomotion.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape Unity uses to detect contact with other objects. This sphere is the central locomotion ball, rather than a visible foot mesh. The rig reads its actual radius for ground height, foot/climb casts and knee positioning. footballRadius reads this collider’s current radius; _footballRadius holds the separate requested radius.

UpdateFootballRadius applies the requested radius to this collider, updates the larger knee fender, moves the knee/feet bodies to preserve their relative height, and refreshes the circumference used for rolling. When a checked enlargement is obstructed, it can return before changing the collider. Changing a cached request and changing this collider are therefore different operations. Maintain the configured sphere and related rigidbodies/joints together; swapping this reference alone does not build a working monofoot.

The sphere collider radius is a world distance in metres at unit scale. Rigidbody means the Unity physics body; a physics joint connects bodies and drives their relative target position/orientation, so this collider/body participates in the knee/feet locomotion assembly rather than being only a visual ball.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._footballCircum
member.summary: Cached ball circumference that converts movement velocity into a rolling angular target.

remarks.para: UpdateFootballRadius computes C = 2πr, where r is the requested ball radius being applied in metres and C is circumference in metres. For example, applying a radius of 0.10 metres records a circumference of about 0.628 metres. These are example values, not configured defaults.

ApplyFeetForce divides the movement-derived rolling vector by this circumference and multiplies by 2π to produce the ball joint’s angular target in radians per second. With the same movement vector, doubling this divisor halves that target. This is not a direct walking-speed setting: body motion, support and the joint still matter. A successful radius update replaces the cache. Keep it consistent with the actual ball radius; the calculation supplies no protective minimum for a manually written zero divisor.

π is the unitless circle constant, so 2πr is circumference in metres. The movement-derived rolling vector is a velocity in metres per second, and the physics joint consumes its local angular target in radians per second; the cached circumference is the divisor that relates those quantities.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._footballRadius
member.summary: Requested locomotion-ball radius that may still be waiting to be applied to the collider.

remarks.para: This distance is in metres. SetFootballSize stores r = eyeHeight × 0.055 × max(mult, 1.05): eyeHeight is the avatar’s reference eye height in metres, mult is the extra unitless size multiplier, and r is the requested radius in metres. SetAvatar and EnableBallLoco use a multiplier of 1.3; DisableBallLoco uses 1.05. Those methods can replace a manual request.

SetFootballSize changes this cache rather than immediately resizing the sphere. During enabled ball locomotion, UpdateMonofootColliders compares it with _football.radius and requests UpdateFootballRadius with an obstruction check when they differ. A checked enlargement can be refused, leaving this request different from the actual radius returned by footballRadius. A successful update also changes the fender, knee/feet heights, joint limit/target and cached circumference. Use the actual collider radius when measuring the current ball; do not assume this request has already taken effect.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._impactProperties
member.summary: Body components whose surface material is replaced when the avatar changes.

remarks.para: ImpactProperties describes the physical surface for impacts, including the material data used by impact effects. SetAvatar writes the avatar’s directly assigned SurfaceData into every component in this array. If the avatar has no directly assigned data, it writes _surfaceDataDefault instead. That is a material-reference update, not an impact-strength or sound-volume multiplier.

When the avatar’s surface-data card can be resolved, SetAvatar also requests its asset load. Its completion callback, a routine called to report that the load finished, writes the loaded SurfaceData to every current entry in this array. The earlier direct/default material can therefore be replaced later. Changing the array decides which components receive these assignments; it does not add those components to body objects. A valid empty array is allowed, while null arrays or null entries are not silently ignored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._initialChest
member.summary: Initial local position and rotation restored to the chest when the physics rig is disabled.

remarks.para: OnAwake, the rig’s initialization routine, saves m_chest’s localPosition and localRotation in this SimpleTransform. A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale; this snapshot contains position and rotation only. Both are relative to that object’s parent, rather than world coordinates. Position uses Unity distance units, corresponding to metres at unit parent scale; parent scaling changes the resulting world displacement. Rotation is a quaternion, a four-number orientation rather than degree angles.

OnRigDisable first saves the current pose in the separate cached-pose field, then restores this initial snapshot. OnRigEnable with reEnable true restores the cached pose; it does not use this initial snapshot. Editing this value changes a later disable restoration, not the current pose immediately, and OnAwake replaces it when initialization runs again. For example, adding 0.1 to its local position X changes the next restored position along the parent’s X axis; it is not necessarily a 0.1-metre move along world X.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._kneeAnchorVelocity
member.summary: World-space knee/pelvis tracking correction divided by the physics-step duration.

remarks.para: OnFixedUpdate computes the displacement needed to reconcile the physical pelvis and knee anchor with the input rig, then divides its X, Y and Z corrections by deltaTime in seconds. This Vector3 consequently has metres-per-second units in world axes. It is a calculated correction, rather than the knee Rigidbody’s measured velocity or the local joint anchor position.

The calculation runs in the awake, non-shutdown fixed-update path and replaces this cache. For example, a 0.02-metre correction over 0.02 seconds produces a 1-metre-per-second component. The same routine subsequently handles leash correction and ball locomotion separately, so this earlier cache is not necessarily the final applied movement. Read _kneeRb.velocity when you need the simulated body’s actual world velocity; editing this cache does not move the joint anchor and the next calculation can overwrite it.

The referenced knee anchor is a Unity Rigidbody/physics-body measurement. This cached vector is the tracking correction derived from world displacements divided by the physics-step duration, so its components are metres per second, not a permanent position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._kneeChestServo
member.summary: that drives the knee proxy’s orientation relative to the requested chest orientation.

remarks.para: A Servo controls a ConfigurableJoint, which connects physics objects and pushes them toward target positions or rotations. OnFixedUpdate sets this servo’s rotation target relative to the input chest from the input rig, allowing the support structure to follow the requested body orientation. This is an active rotation drive, not a collision barrier that guarantees the body parts cannot overlap.

CalibrateJoints calculates its base rotation spring, damping and force cap from avatar measurements and the monofoot multipliers. While ball locomotion is enabled, OnEarlyUpdate refreshes its rotation drive with a support-dependent force cap; DisableBallLoco writes zero spring, damping and force through SetSlerpDrive. Keep its configured joint valid. Replacing the Servo reference does not configure a new joint or transfer its base drive settings. The target is a quaternion orientation and target angular rates use radians per second. Under a torque-based angular drive with a conventional SI scene scale (1 Unity distance unit = 1 m, mass in kg, time in seconds), spring gain has units N·m/rad, damper gain N·m·s/rad, and max force is a torque cap in N·m. That scale is an assumption, not a scale established by these code paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._kneeFender
member.summary: The larger sphere collider around the monofoot knee that provides a second contact shape beside the locomotion ball.

remarks.para: A collider is the shape Unity tests for contact. UpdateFootballRadius sets this sphere’s radius to r × 1.0444444, where r is the requested ball radius being applied in metres and 1.0444444 is a unitless enlargement multiplier. Its local center Y is sqrt(fenderRadius² − r²), in metres. For a ball radius of 0.10 metres, the example fender radius is about 0.1044 metres and center height about 0.0301 metres.

When checking an enlargement, the resize routine tests both the ball and fender shapes against footballColCheckMask while ignoring triggers. A blocked test can prevent the whole resize. Climbing also moves the fender’s local horizontal center to follow the knee-to-pelvis offset; leaving Climbing restores its horizontal center to zero while preserving its vertical center. A manual radius or center edit can therefore be replaced. The collider is a contact shape, not a guarantee that clipping is impossible.

fenderRadius is the requested ball radius multiplied by 1.0444444, in metres at unit scale. The centre offset uses sqrt(fenderRadius² − radius²), also metres, in the collider’s local axes; it is a clearance geometry calculation, not a unitless height.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._kneePelJoint
member.summary: The knee-to-pelvis whose targets provide crouch height and horizontal foot stepping.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation and can drive their relative position. UpdateKnee writes the target’s local Y position and velocity for vertical support. HoldStep, ReturnStep and CheckStep manipulate its local X/Z targets for stepping and climbing. These positions use metres and target velocities use metres per second in the joint’s configured local frame, rather than world axes.

SwitchStepState changes its horizontal motion and drive settings before recording the new step state. ReturnStep smooths its horizontal target toward zero; zero means no extra X/Z target displacement in this local frame, not world position zero. kneePelvisJoint returns this same reference. Keep it consistent with _kneePelServo and the configured bodies/anchors. A manual target can be replaced by the next update, and changing this reference alone does not create or reconnect a working joint.

This servo also supplies the knee-to-pelvis joint anchor, vertical support drive and crouch limit. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._kneeRb
member.summary: The Rigidbody that simulates the central monofoot knee proxy and supplies its physical orientation.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for mass, velocity and simulated physical motion. This is the central knee GameObject’s body, rather than either left/right leg’s knee bone. Reset obtains or adds the component on knee, and rbKnee returns the same reference. The rig uses its world rotation to convert stepping and joint targets between local and world directions.

SetBodyMassDistribution assigns it 43.75% of the current monofoot mass budget, with the other 56.25% assigned to _feetRb. EnableBallLoco and DisableBallLoco change its collision detection. StepFeet and UpdateFootballRadius move it alongside the feet body. Fixed updates also set its requested orientation, so a manual pose or mass edit can be replaced by rig updates or recalibration. Keep the reference paired with the knee object and the configured support joints.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body; its mass is in kilograms and its world position/velocity use metres and metres per second. This reference is the central knee body used by the monofoot assembly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._ladderInfo
member.summary: Stored used to place the body’s ladder-support correction relative to a rung.

remarks.para: This is a value-type record, not a nullable ladder component. UpdateLadderInfo copies the supplied record here and sets onLadder to 1. The record contains the source, rung Transform, rung counts and dimensions. A Transform stores position, rotation and scale. The separate onLadder/ladderFade state decides how ladder support fades; the presence of old information here alone is not proof that the player is currently on a ladder.

LadderForce converts the feet’s world position into the rung Transform’s local axes, uses rungWidth to bound its local Z correction, converts back to world coordinates, and changes pelvis velocity with the current ladderFade. It requires a valid rung Transform and configured bodies. ApplyFeetForce moves ladderFade toward the current onLadder signal and clears that signal for subsequent updates. To report a fresh ladder contact, use UpdateLadderInfo; merely changing the stored record does not perform its onLadder assignment.

rungWidth is a local ladder distance in Unity distance units (metres at unit scale); ladderFade is unitless, with 0 meaning no fade and 1 meaning full fade in the checked interpolation. The ladder vectors remain in the ladder’s configured local/world frames as documented by the producer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._lastClimbingPoint
member.summary: Previous smoothed world-space support point used to calculate the next climbing correction.

remarks.para: CheckStep seeds this Vector3 with the detected support point when its Dangle branch enters Climbing. During successful Climbing checks it smooths toward the new contact point, uses the difference from this saved point to calculate _climbingVelocity along the surface, and saves the new smoothed point here. Its X, Y and Z are positions in world metres, not a rung-local coordinate, surface normal or velocity.

For example, moving the support point by 0.01 metres changes the displacement used in the next correction; the final velocity also depends on smoothing, tracking error, surface direction and physics-step duration. This is an internal history value, not a command to teleport the player or cling to a chosen object. The next successful climbing check overwrites it, and outside that path it can remain from an earlier climb.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._lastKneeRotation
member.summary: Knee world orientation saved by ApplyFeetForce so stepping can preserve its joint targets as the knee turns.

remarks.para: ApplyFeetForce records _kneeRb.rotation here. This is a quaternion, a four-number orientation with no degree-angle units. CheckStep compares the saved orientation with the current knee world orientation and rotates the knee-to-pelvis target position into the current knee-local axes. In the Climbing branch it also rotates the target velocity.

The normal fixed-update path calls CheckStep before ApplyFeetForce, so CheckStep uses the orientation left by the earlier ApplyFeetForce call. It is not necessarily the rotation from the previous rendered frame: physics updates and rendered frames can run at different rates, and sleeping or shutdown paths can skip updates. Editing this history can change target rebasing; it does not rotate the Rigidbody immediately and the next ApplyFeetForce replaces it.
The saved rotation is compared against the knee Rigidbody’s current orientation. A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body; the rotation is a quaternion and has no metre or degree-triplet units.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._legsKinematic
member.summary: Whether the rig updates the two leg chains through scripted poses instead of their normal physical limb updates.

remarks.para: Kinematic means movement is controlled by code rather than by ordinary physics forces. KinematicLegs puts both physical leg chains into that mode, then sets this flag true. PhysicalLegs switches them to physical movement, clears the flag, then updates their limb targets. The actual PhysLimb.SetPhysical transition ignores the passed pelvis velocity for the limb-body assignment and sets each body’s world velocity from its centre-of-mass displacement divided by fixedDeltaTime. OnStart also makes them kinematic; RagdollRig clears the flag, while UnRagdollRig restores it.

Early and fixed updates skip the normal leg-limb routines while this flag is true. OnAfterFixedUpdate instead positions the kinematic leg bodies from the requested rig pose and avatar offsets. This flag does not describe the separate locomotion ball’s Rigidbody mode. Use KinematicLegs or PhysicalLegs for a mode transition: changing this bookkeeping flag alone does not perform the body mode changes or assign the limb velocities.

The actual PhysLimb.SetPhysical transition ignores the passed pelvis velocity for the limb-body assignment. It sets each body’s world velocity from its world centre-of-mass displacement divided by fixedDeltaTime, then the rig clears the kinematic flag and updates limb targets. The flag remains a mode switch for code-controlled versus physics-driven legs, not a stored velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._maxStepHeight
member.summary: Avatar-sized upper height limit used when the ordinary foot-step casts consider a ledge.

remarks.para: This distance is in metres. SetAvatar calculates H = 0.61 × (legLength + hipPelvisOffsetY), where legLength is the avatar’s reference leg length in metres, hipPelvisOffsetY is its vertical hip-to-pelvis offset in metres, 0.61 is a unitless proportion, and H is this stored step-height limit. Applying an avatar replaces a manual value.

The relevant CheckStep branches reject a cast height below H × 0.055 or above H, then also test surface direction and other step-state conditions. For an illustrative H of 0.50 metres, that height band is 0.0275 through 0.50 metres, including the boundaries. Increasing H changes both ends of this band; it is not a guarantee the rig can walk onto every ledge of that height. Hand-assisted climbing and other step branches have their own conditions. No general runtime clamp is established for a manually written value.

The cast-height quantity is contact-point world Y plus the actual ball radius minus the feet-proxy world Y, in metres. FootCast’s sphere-cast path and the later H bands use this world-distance height; the sphere follows a swept path rather than testing only its centre.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._monoDamperMult
member.summary: Unitless proportion used to calculate damping for the three monofoot rotation drives during calibration.

remarks.para: CalibrateJoints computes each knee-to-pelvis, knee-to-head and knee-to-chest rotation damper as damper = spring × d. Here spring is that joint drive’s already calculated angular spring gain, and d is this extra unitless damping multiplier. The spring turns the joint toward its target orientation and damping resists its relative angular motion. Under a torque-based angular drive with a conventional SI scene scale (1 Unity distance unit = 1 m, mass in kg, time in seconds), spring gain has units N·m/rad and damper gain N·m·s/rad; that scale is an assumption, not a scale established by these code paths.

For example, using d = 0.2 instead of 0.1 with the same spring doubles the calibrated damper value. This does not double every force or automatically damp all body motion. The vertical knee-to-pelvis drive is calibrated separately without this multiplier. Changing this field alone leaves the existing base drive values unchanged until CalibrateJoints runs again; SetAvatar invokes that calibration. The checked consumers supply no clamp for this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._monoRemainder
member.summary: Remaining upward jump impulse that the monofoot system gradually releases into the pelvis.

remarks.para: This is an impulse amount in newton-seconds, not a movement velocity. An accepted CheckDoubleJump clears readiness, adds its newtonSecond argument to this remainder, and updates the jump cooldown deadline. The discharge calculation runs only for a positive remainder, so a negative stored value is not treated as a downward jump by that branch.

DischargeMono smooths the remainder toward zero using _monoVel as its retained smoothing rate and a 0.2-second smoothing time. The amount removed that step is multiplied by max(0, 10 − pelvisWorldVelocityY) × 0.1, where pelvisWorldVelocityY is the pelvis’s upward world velocity in metres per second, 10 is the upward-speed reference of 10 metres per second, and 0.1 normalizes that numerical speed difference into a unitless factor. The result is applied upward in world space using Impulse force mode. For example, at 5 metres per second upward the multiplier is 0.5; at or above 10 it is zero. The calculation can consume the remainder even when that upward-speed gate suppresses the applied impulse. ApplyFeetForce contains the corresponding positive-remainder discharge path.

The stored remainder is a brief upward impulse in N·s. Impulse force mode changes a Rigidbody’s velocity according to mass, so this value is not itself metres per second; the later release consumes it through the physics body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._monoVel
member.summary: Retained smoothing rate for reducing the remaining upward jump impulse toward zero.

remarks.para: DischargeMono passes this float by reference to SmoothDamp while smoothing _monoRemainder, the remaining impulse in newton-seconds. The smoothing routine updates this rate across physics steps. Its units are impulse per second, newton-seconds per second; it is not the feet’s or pelvis’s velocity in metres per second.

The discharge uses a 0.2-second smoothing time and then applies the impulse removed from the remainder, subject to the pelvis upward-speed gate. Editing this history can change how the next positive remainder is smoothed, but does not directly set walking velocity or apply a force on its own. When the positive-remainder branch does not run, this stored smoothing state need not be refreshed. Use the relevant Rigidbody velocity for actual body motion.

This retained smoothing value accompanies a remaining N·s impulse and is updated by SmoothDamp; it is an impulse-per-second history, not Rigidbody movement velocity. The actual body movement comes from the relevant Rigidbody velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._pelvisForceInternalMult
member.summary: Unitless multiplier shared by the knee-to-pelvis, knee-to-head and knee-to-chest rotation drives.

remarks.para: CalibrateJoints uses the product P = _pelvisForceMult × _pelvisForceInternalMult, where both factors are unitless rotation-drive multipliers. For all three servos, that product scales the calculated base rotation spring, damper and maximum force. These are twisting drives; the vertical knee-to-pelvis support drive is calculated separately without these multipliers. These angular drive gains have conditional torque-based SI dimensions: spring N·m/rad, damper N·m·s/rad, and maximum-force cap N·m, assuming 1 Unity distance unit = 1 m, mass in kg and time in seconds. The code paths do not establish that project scale.

While ball locomotion is enabled, OnEarlyUpdate also multiplies each servo’s base maximum force by the unitless support blend B = (1 − s) × o + s and by P, while retaining its base spring and damper. Here clamp01 means limiting a value to the 0-to-1 range; s is clamp01(left-hand support + feet support + right-hand support), and o is clamp01(overrideKneePelForce), the 0-to-1 fallback factor used when support is low. For example, doubling this field with the other multiplier unchanged doubles that live force-cap multiplier. If you also recalibrate, the base values change too, so the final force cap can scale by the product twice; it is not a single multiplier on every pelvis force.

monofootInternalMult reads and writes this same internal value. A field edit can affect the next enabled EarlyUpdate force cap, while spring and damping need recalibration to change. SetAvatar calls CalibrateJoints. The checked calculations do not clamp these stored multipliers. A value does not by itself guarantee a stable posture or prevent falling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._pelvisForceMult
member.summary: Unitless multiplier shared by the knee-to-pelvis, knee-to-head and knee-to-chest rotation drives.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._returnStepTranslates
member.summary: Internal flag that suppresses ReturnStep’s horizontal movement correction while true.

remarks.para: ReturnStep smooths the knee-to-pelvis joint’s local horizontal target back toward zero. It converts that target’s velocity to world axes, but adds the X/Z correction to _stepDelta only when this flag is false. True therefore does not mean that the return still needs to be wound back; it changes whether that return velocity contributes to the ordinary ball-movement correction.

The hand-assisted foothold branch sets the flag true, while ordinary foot placement and several supported transitions set it false. EnableBallLoco also clears it before selecting ReturnStep. SwitchStepState clears it when leaving an existing ReturnStep state, before recording the destination state. A manual change does not move the feet or reset the joint target, and later transitions can replace it. It is bookkeeping for these step paths rather than a general walking-translation switch.

The knee-to-pelvis physics joint’s target position is a local distance in metres at unit scale, and its target velocity is metres per second. ReturnStep converts the smoothed local correction to world axes before adding it to the world correction state when this flag is false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._skidSpeedTest
member.summary: Internal float whose name does not identify the rig’s verified skid-speed result.

remarks.para: The checked PhysicsRig ground-update path obtains a slip-vector magnitude from PhysGrounder and writes it to skidSpeed. It does not establish this separate float as that measurement or as a tuning threshold. The original claim that a skid detector accumulates speed here is unsupported by these consumers.

No units or gameplay effect are established for _skidSpeedTest by the checked PhysicsRig ground/step/update paths. To read the calculated slipping speed, use skidSpeed, which is in metres per second, and skidVelocity for its world-space direction. Do not substitute this float in a skid-speed display or assume writing it changes ground behavior. This is a bounded account of the audited paths, not a claim that no other code can access the field.

The checked skid result is skidSpeed, a world contact-relative speed magnitude in metres per second; skidVelocity is its world contact-relative vector in metres per second. This separately named field is not treated as that result without a native consumer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepCastBuffer
member.summary: Accumulated world-space movement used to decide when another foot-step cast is needed.

remarks.para: CheckStep adds inputDelta to this Vector3. Its components are accumulated displacement in metres along world X, Y and Z; this is a distance accumulator, not merely unused scratch storage. In relevant branches, a cast is delayed until its squared magnitude reaches the squared threshold based on 1.4 times the actual ball radius. For example, a 0.10-metre radius gives a basic accumulated-distance threshold of 0.14 metres.

The threshold and reset behavior also depend on the current step state. A too-small movement can remain here for a later update; a completed cast attempt or certain climbing transitions clear it. EnableBallLoco clears it too. Opposite movement can cancel earlier accumulated components. Editing the vector affects later cast scheduling but does not perform a cast, move the body or return a hit immediately.

The cast gate uses the squared Vector3 magnitude X² + Y² + Z², in m², against a radius-derived threshold. The 1.4 factor is unitless; the buffer itself accumulates world displacement in metres before the state-specific cast/reset branches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepDelta
member.summary: Accumulated world-horizontal velocity correction removed from the ordinary ball movement calculation.

remarks.para: This Vector2’s X component represents world X and its Y component represents world Z. Both use metres per second, rather than displacement metres. HoldStep adds the input movement velocity while moving the knee-to-pelvis target along that direction. ReturnStep can add its returned joint-target velocity after converting it to world axes, when _returnStepTranslates is false.

In the ordinary movement branch, ApplyFeetForce subtracts these two components from its horizontal movement vector before calculating the ball’s rolling target, separating joint stepping from that ordinary movement. It then clears _stepDelta, including the Climbing path that uses a different rolling calculation. For example, a world-X correction of 0.5 metres per second removes that amount from the X movement used by this calculation. It is transient state consumed per ApplyFeetForce call, not a permanent speed or accumulated step distance.

The knee-to-pelvis physics joint connects the support body and pelvis and its relative target movement contributes to this transient world-horizontal velocity correction. X maps to world X and Y to world Z, both in metres per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepDeltaOverTimeBuffer
member.summary: Deferred horizontal distance that is fed back into ball movement gradually after a foothold adjustment.

remarks.para: This is one Vector2, not an array of past samples. Its X component is world-X distance and its Y component is world-Z distance, in metres. A hand-assisted foothold branch adds a surface-derived adjustment to these components. The saved distance lets that adjustment be spread across later ordinary movement calculations.

ApplyFeetForce moves the vector toward zero by at most 4 × fixedDeltaTime metres per call, where fixedDeltaTime is the physics-step duration in seconds and 4 is the distance-release rate in metres per second. It divides the distance removed that step by fixedDeltaTime and adds that velocity back to the horizontal movement vector. For example, at a 0.02-second step, at most 0.08 metres of the vector’s magnitude is removed, producing at most 4 metres per second from this release. Climbing uses its separate movement branch, so the buffer need not drain there. It is internal deferred movement, not a general smoothing-time setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepOffset
member.summary: Internal float with no established step-height output in the checked foot-step routines.

remarks.para: The checked CheckStep, HoldStep, StepFeet, ReturnStep, ApplyFeetForce and UpdateKnee paths do not establish this field as the current vertical step height. The step implementation instead changes knee/feet world positions and knee-to-pelvis joint targets; ReturnStep retains its two horizontal smoothing components in _stepVel. The old vertical-offset explanation is therefore not supported by these paths.

No reliable unit, update timing or tuning effect is established for this stored float. For live step state, read stepState; for the driven local position, inspect kneePelvisJoint.targetPosition, whose components are distances in the joint’s configured frame. Do not treat this field as a current vertical displacement or change it expecting a verified step-height effect. This limitation applies to the audited routines and is not a whole-game claim that the field can never be accessed.

The checked routines do not establish this scalar as a current vertical displacement. The verified driven quantity is kneePelvisJoint.targetPosition: a local joint distance in metres at unit scale; its configured axes and state drive the actual step transition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepOffsetVelocity
member.summary: Internal float with no established vertical step-smoothing role in the checked foot-step routines.

remarks.para: The checked CheckStep, HoldStep, StepFeet, ReturnStep, ApplyFeetForce and UpdateKnee paths do not establish this field as the speed of a vertical step-height adjustment. The step implementation instead changes knee/feet world positions and knee-to-pelvis joint targets; ReturnStep retains its two horizontal smoothing components in _stepVel. The old vertical-offset explanation is therefore not supported by these paths.

No reliable unit, update timing or tuning effect is established for this stored float. For live step state, read stepState; for the driven local position, inspect kneePelvisJoint.targetPosition, whose components are distances in the joint’s configured frame. Do not treat this field as a current vertical displacement or change it expecting a verified step-height effect. This limitation applies to the audited routines and is not a whole-game claim that the field can never be accessed.

The checked routines do not establish this scalar as a vertical step speed. The verified ReturnStep history is _stepVel and the joint target velocity is metres per second in its configured local frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepState
member.summary: The current foot-placement mode that chooses rolling, holding, returning, dangling, climbing or foothold behavior. See .

remarks.para: The values are NeutralRoll (0), HoldStep (1), ReturnStep (2), Dangle (3), Climbing (4) and Foothold (5). HoldStep advances the knee-to-pelvis horizontal target with input movement; ReturnStep smooths it toward zero. Dangle and Climbing use hand/support checks, while Foothold handles supported placement after those transitions. ApplyFeetForce uses the special surface-tangent rolling velocity only for Climbing.

SwitchStepState restores settings associated with the old state, configures the destination joint motion and drives, and only then records the new value. NeutralRoll locks the joint’s X/Z motion; the other named states use free X/Z motion, with additional drive changes in the holding/climbing paths. stepState returns this field. Writing the enum alone does not run those joint changes or the flag/reset work, so it is not equivalent to a complete state transition. Support and cast results can choose another state during later updates.

The state configures the physics joint’s X/Z axes and drives: NeutralRoll locks those axes, while the moving states free them as documented. The enum is mode bookkeeping; changing it alone does not configure the joint or run transition cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._stepVel
member.summary: Retained two-axis smoothing velocity used when the knee-to-pelvis horizontal target returns toward zero.

remarks.para: ReturnStep passes this Vector2 by reference to SmoothDamp while reducing the joint target’s local X/Z position. Its first component is the local X smoothing velocity and its second is local Z, both in metres per second. They describe the smoothing history, not the feet’s world velocity or the player’s forward/side input.

The smoothing time is 0.05 seconds. Its maximum speed depends on the supplied world-horizontal input velocity and the direction back toward the centered joint target, so this cache alone does not determine return speed. Each return calculation updates it. A manual edit can change the next smoothing result but does not move the joint by itself. Use the Rigidbody velocity for actual world motion, and keep this history consistent if changing the joint target as part of a custom movement routine.

SmoothDamp is gradual target easing with a retained rate; here it operates on the physics joint’s local X/Z target distance. The cached components are metres per second in the joint frame, not the Rigidbody’s world velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._surfaceDataDefault
member.summary: Fallback surface material written onto the body’s ImpactProperties when the avatar has no directly assigned .

remarks.para: SetAvatar selects the avatar’s direct SurfaceData when it is present; otherwise it assigns this fallback reference to every component in _impactProperties. SurfaceData describes the material used for physical impact properties and effects. This field is a material reference, not a default impact force, collision shape or sound-volume value.

If the avatar’s surface-data card resolves and its asset load finishes, the completion callback, a routine called to report the finished load, can later replace those ImpactProperties materials with the loaded data. Changing this fallback alone does not immediately reapply it to the components. It affects a later fallback assignment through SetAvatar, and the rig does not infer or construct a material if the reference is null.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig._torsoSfxManager
member.summary: Torso collision-sound manager enabled for ragdoll motion and disabled when active locomotion is restored. See .

remarks.para: RagdollRig, which puts the legs into physical movement and disables ball locomotion, enables this CollisionSfxManager near the end of its transition. UnRagdollRig restores kinematic leg movement and ball locomotion, then disables it near the end. A ragdoll is the body’s limp, physics-driven state. This reference therefore participates in whether its managed torso impact sounds are permitted during those states.

The manager connects its CollisionSFX entries back to itself during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, meaning the routine Unity calls to initialize that component. Its CheckImpact rejects requests while the manager is disabled and otherwise limits repeated impacts using a 0.3-second unscaled-time deadline, while allowing an equal or stronger impulse through earlier. Unscaled time is the clock unaffected by game time scale. Assigning this rig reference alone does not subscribe it to _collisionCollectors or build its sound-entry list; those are separate setup concerns. The ragdoll transition expects a valid manager.

Kinematic means code-controlled movement rather than ordinary physics integration. The collision manager’s impact quantity is an impulse in N·s, and its unscaled-time deadline is unaffected by the game time scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.artOutput
member.summary: Optional that updates the visible avatar from this physical rig.

remarks.para: OnAwake, the physical rig’s initialization routine, calls ArtOutputAwake on this ArtRig when it exists. SetAvatar also sends it the selected avatar through SetArtOutputAvatar. The physics rig keeps simulating its bodies separately; the ArtRig is the output used to place the visible avatar.

OnLateUpdate calls its ArtOutputUpdate and then ArtOutputLateUpdate only when the pelvis Rigidbody is awake and this reference is present. LateUpdate is the update phase after ordinary frame updates. A sleeping pelvis skips both calls, so this reference does not guarantee a fresh visual update every rendered frame. An absent ArtRig is guarded in these paths. Replacing the reference alone does not perform its initialization or avatar setup; those operations remain necessary for a newly supplied visual rig.

The pelvis reference is a Rigidbody, Unity’s mass-and-motion physics body. Sleeping means the physics body is resting and Unity may pause its simulation updates; the late visual-output update is gated by that awake/sleep state, so this reference does not guarantee a render update every frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.ballLocoEnabled
member.summary: Whether the physics rig is using its central locomotion ball for active movement and support.

remarks.para: The getter returns the rig’s stored mode flag. OnStart sets it true. EnableBallLoco sets it true before changing hand support, enabling knee/feet collision detection, requesting the active ball size and resetting foot placement. DisableBallLoco sets it false before removing the three monofoot rotation drives, changing hand support, disabling those collisions and resetting the step state.

Enabled fixed updates run CheckStep, ApplyFeetForce, the body-mass check and UpdateKnee. Disabled mode skips that ball-movement group; RagdollRig uses DisableBallLoco, while UnRagdollRig uses EnableBallLoco. This flag describes the monofoot movement path, not whether every Rigidbody or the whole rig component is enabled. A mode flag alone is not the full transition: use the transition methods when changing the working rig so their joint, collision and support changes run too.

The central locomotion ball is a Rigidbody-backed physics body. This flag selects the ball movement path; it is not a claim that every Rigidbody or the whole rig component is enabled, and transition methods still perform the joint/collision/support changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.bodyMassNaturalHold
member.summary: Keeps enabled ball locomotion in the NaturalMono mass distribution instead of switching to StableMono as support improves.

remarks.para: NaturalMono puts 12% of the avatar’s total mass into the knee/feet support bodies, while StableMono uses 34%. These names describe mass allocation, not extra applied forces. When this flag is true, the mass-state checker chooses or retains NaturalMono during enabled ball locomotion regardless of the support thresholds that would otherwise select StableMono.

When false, moving from NaturalMono to StableMono requires footSupported at least 0.7, while StableMono stays selected only with support greater than 0.6. Initial selection from Natural or Seated uses the separate 0.65 boundary. Those are unitless support amounts. The flag is considered by later distribution checks, not a command that immediately changes every mass. With ball locomotion disabled, the checker selects Natural or Seated according to whether RigManager has an active Seat; this hold flag does not force those modes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.bodyMassState
member.summary: Selects how the avatar’s mass is divided between its torso, arms, legs and central knee/feet support bodies. See .

remarks.para: The states are Natural (0), NaturalMono (1), StableMono (2) and Seated (3). SetBodyMassDistribution gives the monofoot bodies 2%, 12% or 34% of total avatar mass for the first three states respectively; Seated uses twice the avatar’s per-leg mass. The feet receive 56.25% of that monofoot budget and the knee receives 43.75%. Each arm receives 7.317% of total mass. Torso allocation subtracts the relevant budgets; these changes alter simulated mass, not a force multiplier.

For example, an 80-kilogram avatar in StableMono has a 27.2-kilogram monofoot budget: 15.3 kilograms for the feet and 11.9 for the knee. These are illustrative values. Ball-enabled support checks choose NaturalMono or StableMono with hysteresis; ball-disabled checks choose Natural or Seated based on the actual active Seat. SetAvatar applies the distribution, and changing states through the checker applies it after recording the new state.

Writing this enum alone does not immediately assign Rigidbody masses. The checker can replace it on a later update, or retain the same state without rerunning the mass assignment. Read it as the selected allocation state rather than proof that a manual enum edit has already recalculated every mass.

A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body and mass is measured in kilograms. The support checks use hysteresis: entering and retaining a mass state use different support thresholds, so a boundary crossing does not immediately toggle back and forth.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PhysicsRig.canFall
member.summary: Allows the active ball-locomotion rig to enter its fallen body state through the normal update checks.

remarks.para: A fallen state lets the body use its limp, physics-driven ragdoll motion. In OnUpdate, a sleeping pelvis or shutdown stops the relevant checks, and an active RigManager Seat skips the fall/recovery branch. With automatic falling selected, an enabled ball rig can request the fallen body state when the angle between its physical pelvis up direction and the requested rig’s pelvis up direction is greater than 24 degrees, provided canFall is true.

With ball locomotion already disabled, the automatic recovery test remains available even when this flag is false. It requires the pelvis-direction angle to be less than 17 degrees and the squared world X/Z angular-velocity sum to be less than 25, equivalent to a horizontal angular-speed magnitude below 5 radians per second. These strict thresholds give fall and recovery different boundaries; the angle is relative to the requested pelvis, not necessarily world vertical.

When manualFallenState is selected instead, the branch uses the right controller’s thumbstick-down input to switch modes; this flag still prevents entry from the enabled-ball state while false. Setting canFall true does not immediately trigger a fall, and false does not itself stand the body up or disable every external body-state change.

Angular velocity is turning speed in radians per second; the checked X/Z squared sum is in rad²/s². “Sleeping pelvis” means Unity’s pelvis Rigidbody is asleep, so the automatic fall/recovery checks return early. The stored permission is a gate for the native branch, not an immediate fall command.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PlayerDamageReceiver.bodyPart
member.summary: Labels the body region sent to health with this receiver's attacks and collisions, affecting the normal handler's head-damage multiplier and the region used for optional hit marks.

remarks.para: Set this to the region this receiver represents, such as Head, Chest, or HandLf, the left hand. It is a label, not a measurement or a command to move the collider. The constructor starts with Pelvis; a saved component setting can replace that default. Both attack and collision forwarding read the current value each time they run.

In the normal Health attack handler, also used by Player_Health, Head multiplies incoming damage by 4.1 and every other value multiplies it by 0.6 before requesting a health change. These factors are unitless. For a living player with an attack not marked backFacing, 10 incoming game damage points therefore request 41 points with Head or 6 points with Pelvis. The health component's rules still decide the final result.

When optional visual damage is enabled, the same label selects which avatar region's stored position and rotation offsets the health system uses to place the hit mark. These offsets are separate from this receiver's Transform (its position, rotation, and scale), which supplies the local coordinates sent with the attack; changing the bodyPart label does not reposition the receiver or its collider, or change that conversion. Give the receiver the matching body-part label so a hit can be attributed to the correct region.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PlayerDamageReceiver.health
member.summary: The health component that receives this body part's attacks and enabled collision notifications and decides their damage effects.

remarks.para: During Health.Awake, Unity's one-time startup hook, the health component finds the PlayerDamageReceiver components below the rig's PhysicsRig and assigns itself to each receiver it finds. PhysicsRig is the player-body setup used for physical movement and collisions. This saved reference connects the separate body-part receivers to the same health handler; the receiver does not search for health again on every hit.

ReceiveAttack reads the current reference and sends it a converted attack plus the receiver's bodyPart label. Collision forwarding reads it when the receiver is enabled and sends it the collision plus that same label. Replacing the reference changes the target of later notifications. Leave it assigned before sending a hit: these forwarding methods fail on a missing reference rather than treating the hit as harmless.

This field stores a component reference, not a number of remaining health points. The assigned component's damage and collision handlers control the response. For example, the base Health collision handler does nothing, while another Health implementation can choose its own collision response.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.OnDeathImminent
member.summary: Shared callbacks reporting entry into the Mortal death-save state with true, and the LifeSavingDamgeDealt recovery path with false.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The bool argument reports which transition is being announced. Mortal Dying sets deathIsImminent to true before calling these listeners; it starts the new death animation afterward. LifeSavingDamgeDealt increments playerDeathSaves and clears deathIsImminent before calling them with false, but restores half health afterward. Listeners cannot assume the new timer or recovered health has already been written.
