For example, 0.05 is a requested 0.05-scaled-second gap, about 20 updates per scaled second before frame scheduling. At a constant half-speed time scale, that gap is roughly 0.1 real-world seconds.

For the final overlay fade, each update moves the inner and outer shader controls toward zero by 0.01, so the interval affects the fade's duration as well as its sampling frequency. Regeneration instead samples an elapsed-time blend, so this changes how often health is written rather than its calculated duration.

The initial regeneration wait, death animation and shut-eyes recovery use frame-by-frame time/progress rather than this wait interval. No runtime clamp was found at the two checked wait-construction sites; this value is an interval in seconds, not a damage multiplier or an updates-per-second count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.shutEyeCurve
member.summary: Shapes how the fatal overlay's shut-eyes control moves from its starting value toward 1 as death-animation progress advances.

remarks.para: Scaled seconds are seconds on the game clock, affected by the game's time scale; during slow motion they pass more slowly than real-world seconds. A shader is the material's drawing program.

The horizontal input is unitless death-animation progress. Each frame adds scaled frame seconds / currDeathTime, where currDeathTime is the current duration denominator in scaled seconds. Roughly 0 is the start and 1 is the end when that denominator remains positive.

The curve's vertical output is a unitless blend fraction, limited by the animation to 0 through 1. The shader value written is starting shut-eyes value + (1 - starting shut-eyes value) × clamped curve output. With a starting value of 0 and curve output 0.25, it writes 0.25; with starting value 0.5, the same output writes 0.625.

A curve that rises earlier makes the shader control reach its closed end earlier, but it does not change when progress reaches 1 or the final health check calls Death. This is an overlay shader control, not movement of physical eyelid bones. The curve must be assigned; the routine samples it each frame and does not use routineTickRate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.shutEyesID
member.summary: Selects the shader control _ShutEyes animated toward 1 during fatal health and toward 0 during recovery.

remarks.para: Scaled seconds are seconds on the game clock, affected by the game's time scale; during slow motion they pass more slowly than real-world seconds.

A shader is a material's drawing program; the integer property ID is a key for one setting, not the amount of closure. The constructor looks up "_ShutEyes". The fatal coroutine blends its starting value toward 1 using shutEyeCurve, while CoBrightenDeathSave blends its starting value toward 0 over one scaled second. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames.

ResetVigMaterial writes 0 to the selected property. These are unitless shader control values, not physical eyelid angles or distances. Changing the integer redirects these reads and writes; it does not by itself animate or reopen the overlay. The property block must be applied to the renderer for a buffered change to reach the drawing component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.slowMoOnDeath
member.summary: Allows the first Mortal Dying entry to request a slower global time-scale step.

remarks.para: Dying sets deathIsImminent first, then, if this flag is true, calls TimeManager.DECREASE_TIMESCALE. That request is subject to TimeManager's global slow-motion enable flag and step limit, so this field alone does not guarantee a speed change. Scaled-time death progress and waits can take longer in real time when slow motion is active.

The already-imminent Mortal branch only considers the duration reduction, and the instant-death branch does not make this slow-motion request. Changing this flag during an existing window does not itself change time scale. LifeSavingDamgeDealt, SetFullHealth and checkpoint-respawn startup request the normal time-scale target through TimeManager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.spawnHeroProps
member.summary: A stored hero-prop switch that the inspected Player_Health implementation does not use.

remarks.para: Neither value makes these health routines create or remove hero props: they do not read this switch or spawn the prop_Hero array. It is retained component data, rather than an active on/off control for objects appearing after damage or death.
The separate spawn_points array is active, but it chooses a position and rotation for the object carrying Player_Health during startup. It is not gated by spawnHeroProps.

The complete Player_Health setup, damage, recovery and death methods and their seven continuing routines were inspected. This is a statement about that implementation; external scripts can still use the stored public field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.spawn_points
member.summary: Positions and rotations from which startup chooses where to place the object carrying Player_Health.

remarks.para: Each entry is a Transform: an object’s position, rotation and scale. Start, Unity’s startup routine, and the equivalent STARTDATA method reset health and then copy the selected entry’s world position and rotation onto this component’s own GameObject. World coordinates mean coordinates in the scene; the entry’s scale is not copied.

There is a selection quirk: the code passes the array length minus 1 as the exclusive upper end of its random integer range. With three entries it can choose the first or second, but never the third. One entry selects that entry. An empty array leaves the object’s pose alone; pose means position and rotation. Keep the array and selected entries assigned, because the routine does not treat a missing array or selected Transform as an empty list.

Changing the array after startup does not immediately move the player, and the death checkpoint routine does not select from this array. This array places the health object; it does not supply spawn positions for hero props.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.thr_Impact
member.summary: A stored impact-threshold number that the inspected health damage path does not read.

remarks.para: Changing this value does not establish a minimum hit needed to damage the player in these routines. Player_Health forwards received attack messages to Health, whose damage handling uses the attack’s damage amount. The inherited OnCollision routine has an empty body; it does not compare collision strength with thr_Impact.
The field name and Inspector tooltip do not establish active units or a working threshold. Use the actual attack damage and health-mode controls when changing the behavior of this implementation.

The complete Player_Health setup, damage, recovery and death methods and their seven continuing routines were inspected. This is a statement about that implementation; external scripts can still use the stored public field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.totalRegenDuration
member.summary: The game-time duration used for a full missing-health recovery, shortened when regeneration starts with some health remaining.

remarks.para: After the initial wait, the regeneration coroutine—a sequence that continues over several frames—reads current health and max_Health, the number of health points that represents full health. It chooses a recovery window by mapping health from 0 to max_Health onto durations from totalRegenDuration down to 0.1 seconds. More remaining health therefore gives a shorter window.

For example, with a maximum of 100 health points, 50 points remaining and totalRegenDuration set to 10, the calculated window is 5.05 game-time seconds. This is an illustrative timing calculation. The routine moves health toward max_Health plus 0.5 health points, then finishes and limits it to max_Health once a later check finds it full, so this field does not promise an exact wall-clock completion time.

These are scaled game-time seconds: the clock follows the unitless timeScale multiplier, where 1 is normal speed, 0.5 is half speed, and 0 pauses game time. Slow motion takes more real seconds for the same recovery. The routine snapshots the calculated window after its wait; changing this field during an active recovery does not rebuild that window. The initial wait is separate and uses the wait passed to CoRegenHealth.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.uiTarget
member.summary: A stored UI-position reference that the inspected Player_Health implementation does not follow.

remarks.para: This Transform can hold an object’s position, rotation and scale, but these health routines do not read it, move a canvas toward it, or use it to position the death effect. Changing it alone does not relocate the view effect.

The actual visual setup is MakeVignette: it creates a copy of Vignetter and parents that copy to Unity’s main camera, placing it at the camera’s local origin with no local rotation and unitless scale 1 on each axis, meaning no resizing. That setup does not consult uiTarget.

The complete Player_Health setup, damage, recovery and death methods and their seven continuing routines were inspected. This is a statement about that implementation; external scripts can still use the stored public field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.useMask
member.summary: A stored mask-use flag that the inspected health damage path does not consult.

remarks.para: Turning it on does not make these routines reject attacks by an object’s physics layer or apply msk_Impact. A physics layer is a category assigned to scene objects for collision and lookup rules. Player_Health’s attack routine forwards the message to base Health without reading this flag, and its inherited collision routine does no damage work.
It is saved component data, not an active damage-immunity switch here. The healthMode setting is the actual mode read by the dying logic; useMask does not select that mode.

The complete Player_Health setup, damage, recovery and death methods and their seven continuing routines were inspected. This is a statement about that implementation; external scripts can still use the stored public field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.vigRend
member.summary: The generated renderer that draws the health border and closing-eye effect in the player’s view.

remarks.para: A renderer is the component that draws a visible mesh. MakeVignette creates a copy of Vignetter, takes its SkinnedMeshRenderer from that copy, and stores it here. It parents the copy to the main camera so the effect stays with the view. Running MakeVignette again replaces this cached renderer reference.

Health and dying routines apply a MaterialPropertyBlock to this renderer. This block holds visual settings for this renderer, including border amounts, color and the closing-eye amount, without needing to change a shared material asset. The ordinary health fade enables the renderer while showing feedback and disables it after the healthy border has faded away.

ResetVigMaterial clears the relevant visual amounts and reapplies the block. Changing this cached reference does not move an object or create the effect; later visual writes are sent to whichever renderer is stored here. The generated effect still needs its expected visual properties.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.vignetteRoutine
member.summary: The saved coroutine handle used to stop or replace ordinary health-border fading.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; its handle is the reference Unity returns when starting it. Damage feedback and StartHealthRegnerationAndVignette stop the handle saved here before starting and storing a replacement CoFadeVignette. LifeSavingDamgeDealt also stores a newly started health fade here.

The death-closing sequence uses the separate inherited _deathRoutine handle. The one-second recovery brightening sequence is also started separately. This field therefore does not represent every visual routine running on the component.

Completion and stopping do not clear this field in the inspected routines. A non-null handle can refer to a finished or stopped sequence. Assigning a handle directly only changes the saved reference; it neither starts that sequence nor automatically stops the previous one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.visDebug
member.summary: Enables extra log messages about entering, shortening or escaping the dying state and completing death.

remarks.para: The flag gates Debug.Log calls in Dying, LifeSavingDamgeDealt and Death. A log message is text sent to Unity’s diagnostic log; it is not an object drawn in the scene. Turning the flag off does not stop health changes, the dying timer or the view effect.

This flag does not enable debug shapes for regeneration. Some other messages, including the instant-death branch’s message and UpdateHealth’s messages, are printed independently of this flag, so false does not promise that Player_Health prints no logs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Player_Health.wait_Regen_t
member.summary: The game-time delay passed to normal health regeneration after damage or a death save.

remarks.para: Ordinary damage handling stops the previous regeneration coroutine—a sequence that continues over several frames—and starts a new one with this many seconds to wait. Another accepted damage call can therefore restart the wait. LifeSavingDamgeDealt also uses this field after restoring the player to half of max_Health, the health-point value representing full health.

The waiting loop subtracts Time.deltaTime, the game-time seconds elapsed in each frame, before the health increase begins. These seconds follow the unitless timeScale multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 0.5 is half speed, and 0 pauses game time. For example, a 3-second wait takes about 6 real seconds at a steady half speed. A nonpositive input skips the waiting phase; frame scheduling means the delay is not an exact wall-clock alarm.

The coroutine copies the delay when it is created. Changing this field later does not change a wait already in progress. StartHealthRegnerationAndVignette can instead supply its own regenWait argument, and instant-death mode does not start the ordinary regeneration branch from damage. The recovery window after waiting is calculated separately from totalRegenDuration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay._timeEnabled
member.summary: Stores the Time.time timestamp that starts the current despawn countdown.

remarks.para: OnPoolInitialize writes this value; Update subtracts it from the current Time.time to get elapsed scaled seconds. It is a clock reading since the application started, not a duration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay._wasInitialize
member.summary: Arms the countdown after pool initialization and disarms it just before requesting despawn.

remarks.para: OnPoolInitialize sets it to true. When the timer expires, Update clears it before calling Poolee.Despawn; a later pool initialization arms it again and records a fresh start time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.DespawnDelay.secondsUntilDisable
member.summary: Scaled game-time seconds to wait after pool initialization before this component asks its object to despawn.

remarks.para: The constructor default is 1.0 second. Update compares this value with the elapsed time, Time.time - _timeEnabled, only while _wasInitialize is true and the attached Poolee has a nonzero ID. Zero or a negative value passes on the next update where both gates are met. Unity's time scale controls how quickly the clock advances in real time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._crate
member.summary: Stores the SpawnableCrate asset definition used to load this pool’s template.

remarks.para: The constructor saves the supplied SpawnableCrate reference. Spawn uses that crate definition to request its GameObject asset when this pool has not cached a template. A prefab is a reusable GameObject template; loading the crate asset and creating the pool’s cached template happen in Spawn, not in the constructor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._despawned
member.summary: Tracks Poolee instances returned to the pool and available for reuse.

remarks.para: A Poolee is a component attached to a pooled GameObject. A callback is a routine the game calls at a particular lifecycle moment. Despawn runs the despawn and deinitialization callbacks before appending an accepted instance here. A later Spawn call reuses the first entry in this list when forceInstantiation is false; a forced instantiation skips this reuse path.
The list records pool state, not Unity’s active state. Despawn can leave an object active when skipDisable is true, while still adding it here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._hasTemplateObject
member.summary: Records whether the pool has created its cached template object.

remarks.para: Spawn sets this flag after it loads the crate’s GameObject asset and creates the inactive template copy used for future instantiations. A null asset result leaves the template flag false and that Spawn completes with no Poolee result. This flag is separate from _isTemplateLoading, which marks the pending load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._isTemplateLoading
member.summary: Marks that a pool template asset load is in progress.

remarks.para: The first Spawn that needs a template sets this flag before requesting the crate’s GameObject asset asynchronously. Another Spawn waits until the flag becomes false before it continues to use the template. On the normal load completion path, Pool clears the flag; it does not by itself guarantee that an asset was returned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._objects
member.summary: Tracks the Poolee instances created and managed by this pool.

remarks.para: A Poolee is a component attached to a pooled GameObject. When Spawn creates a new instance from the cached template, it adds that instance here and also marks it spawned. Despawn moves an instance between _spawned and _despawned without removing it from _objects. Clear removes the supplied reference from this list as well as the two state lists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._parentTransform
member.summary: Stores the Transform of the outer holder created beneath the pool’s rootTransform.

remarks.para: A Transform stores a GameObject’s position, rotation, scale and parent. The constructor creates a holder GameObject beneath its rootTransform argument and caches the holder’s Transform here. During template loading, Spawn creates a second inactive GameObject under this holder and places the cached template copy inside that child container; the cached copy is not a direct child of _parentTransform.
This field is not the default parent for every spawned instance. Spawn uses its separate parent argument when it reparents a new or reused instance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._prefabName
member.summary: Caches the loaded template asset’s name for naming the template objects and new instances.

remarks.para: When Spawn successfully loads the source GameObject, it copies that asset’s name into this field. The template-loading path uses the name for both the intermediate container and the cached template copy. When Spawn creates a fresh pooled instance, it uses the name again when naming that copy. Reusing a Poolee from _despawned skips the fresh-instance naming path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._spawned
member.summary: Tracks Poolee instances that this pool currently considers spawned.

remarks.para: Spawn adds the selected new or reused Poolee here before initialization finishes. Despawn checks membership in this list; an instance absent from it is left unchanged. A successful Despawn removes it and adds it to _despawned.
This is the pool’s bookkeeping state, not a direct report of GameObject.activeSelf. For example, skipDisable can leave a despawned GameObject active after its reference has moved out of this list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Pool._templateObject
member.summary: Stores the inactive cached copy made from the crate’s loaded prefab.

remarks.para: A prefab is a reusable GameObject template. After Spawn loads the source GameObject, it creates an inactive container beneath _parentTransform, instantiates the loaded asset inside that container, and stores the inactive copy here. When a new pooled instance is needed, Spawn clones this cached copy. An instance in _despawned can instead be reused.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.SpawnEvents.ID
member.summary: Gets the unsigned 64-bit ID value stored by the associated Poolee.

remarks.para: SpawnEvents reads this value from Poolee.ID; it does not generate or change the ID. It is the pool identity value, not Unity’s instance ID. Poolee clears its ID to zero after its deinitialize callbacks, and IsDespawned checks for that zero value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.SpawnEvents.IsDespawned
member.summary: Gets whether the associated Poolee ID is zero.

remarks.para: The getter returns true exactly when Poolee.ID equals zero. Poolee clears that ID after dispatching its deinitialize callbacks. This property checks the pool ID; it does not check whether the GameObject is active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.SpawnEvents._poolee
member.summary: The serialized Poolee reference used by this component’s pool callbacks, ID properties, and Despawn method.

remarks.para: A Poolee is the component that tracks the pooled object. Reset looks for one on this GameObject or a parent, and Awake uses the stored reference to register this component. The field is serialized, so a scene or prefab can keep an assigned reference. A valid reference is needed before Awake, ID, IsDespawned, or Despawn runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.SpatialBlend
member.summary: Sets the spatial blend requested for movement clips and event sounds: 0 is 2D audio, 1 is fully positional 3D audio, and intermediate values mix them.

remarks.para: This unitless value is passed when a sound starts. Changing it does not update the existing managed sound. The inspector Range presents 0–1; PrismaticSFX does not itself clamp scripted assignments.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._blockJointBreakStop
member.summary: When true, prevents OnJointBreak from stopping the managed movement sound.

remarks.para: OnJointBreak is Unity’s notification that a physics joint connecting bodies has broken. When this flag is false it stops _mapLoop, but does not change _canPlay or permanently disable the component. OnDisable still stops that player; separate audioEvents sounds are not stopped by this callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._canPlay
member.summary: Allows a new modulated clip to start when the managed player is neither playing nor waiting for a sound to arrive.

remarks.para: The constructor sets this true. A non-looping start sets it false; a looping start leaves it unchanged. With a nonempty modulatedClips array, sampling current speed at or below minSpeed rearms it; a sleeping Rigidbody also rearms it. Independent audioEvents do not use this gate.

Awake and Initialize do not reset it, and OnDisable only stops the player. Thus disabling a non-looping sound while this is false does not guarantee another start on re-enable while speed remains above minSpeed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._host
member.summary: Caches the InteractableHost on the same GameObject for feedback to hands holding it.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds components; GetComponent finds a component attached to that object. Awake and Initialize use GetComponent here, without searching parents. An InteractableHost tracks interactions and holding hands. When present, event hits and movement can send controller vibration to those hands; it does not supply the measured Rigidbody velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._lastSpeed
member.summary: Stores the previous awake Update’s measured speed for the next audio-event test.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s per-frame callback. Events use the larger of this value and the current speed, retaining the matching velocity direction from _lastVel when the previous sample is larger. Continuous modulated clips use current speed instead. After event checks, Update replaces this with the current sample, not the selected maximum. Sleeping resets it to zero. Speeds are world units per second, or metres per second in a scene using one Unity unit per metre.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._lastVel
member.summary: Stores the previous awake Update’s measured velocity in world coordinates for audio-event direction tests.

remarks.para: When _lastSpeed exceeds current speed, event checks use this vector with that previous speed; otherwise they use the current vector. This is not a difference between frames or an acceleration. It contains own point velocity minus rb_parent point velocity when that reference is assigned. After event checks it is overwritten by current velocity, and sleeping clears it. Components are world units per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._mapLoop
member.summary: ManagedAudioPlayer that owns the selected modulated clip, whether it loops or plays once.

remarks.para: A ManagedAudioPlayer controls a reusable sound player and can also report a pending sound as playing while that player is being obtained. The constructor creates it. Update adjusts its volume and pitch, and stops it when volume reaches zero; OnDisable and an unblocked OnJointBreak stop it directly. Independent audioEvents use separate sound requests and are not owned by this player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX._rigidbody
member.summary: Caches the Rigidbody on this GameObject for point-velocity measurement and sleeping checks.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a moving body. Awake and Initialize find it on this same scene object, without a parent search. The awake-body branch of Update requires it and velocityTran; it measures velocity at velocityTran’s world position, including motion caused by rotation. A sleeping body skips movement/event sampling, fades managed volume toward zero, rearms _canPlay, and clears the previous speed and velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.audioEvents
member.summary: One-shot sound triggers checked before the continuous modulated clips on each awake Update.

remarks.para: Each AudioEvent needs an eventTran, the Transform defining its position and forward direction, and eventClip choices. Transform means a scene object’s position, rotation and scale. The selected event speed is the larger current/previous sample, with its matching world velocity. The whole event pass requires that speed to be strictly above this component’s minSpeed.

An armed event fires only strictly inside its triggerDistance sphere measured in world units, at or above its own minSpeed, with selected velocity pointing against or perpendicular to eventTran.forward, its world direction along the local positive Z axis. It also requires the measurement point’s local Z in eventTran’s coordinates to be less than twice selected speed times Time.deltaTime. Local Z includes the Transform’s scale; deltaTime is the scaled elapsed seconds for this frame. Equality at the sphere boundary neither fires nor rearms.

The request chooses an eventClip and plays at sourceTran’s local origin. Volume is the event’s own minSpeed-to-maxSpeed fraction clamped to 0–1, with equal endpoints giving zero. After requesting sound and processing any holding-hand vibration, the event is disarmed. While the component speed gate is open, an unarmed event rearms only when the measurement point is strictly outside its sphere. Assign an empty array for no events, rather than null; event and Transform references must be valid.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.loopClips
member.summary: Chooses looping or single-play playback when a modulated clip starts.

remarks.para: True chooses a random clip and repeats it; false chooses a random clip for one play and clears _canPlay, requiring a later low-speed or sleeping sample to rearm another start. Changing this field does not convert a sound already started between loop and single-play modes, though Update reads it to choose later pitch adjustments. It does not affect independent audioEvents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.maxSpeed
member.summary: Upper speed endpoint for the modulated volume target and looping pitch target.

remarks.para: Current speed is mapped from minSpeed–maxSpeed to a clamped fraction from 0 to 1; equal endpoints produce zero. For example, minSpeed 1, maxSpeed 3 and speed 2 give a target fraction of 0.5. Above a normally ordered maxSpeed the target stops increasing. Volume approaches the target rather than jumping immediately. AudioEvent has its own separate speed endpoints. Speeds are world units per second, or metres per second in a scene using one Unity unit per metre.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.minSpeed
member.summary: Lower speed endpoint and strict start threshold for modulated clips.

remarks.para: A current sample must be strictly above this speed to start a modulated clip; at or below it, the volume target is zero and _canPlay is rearmed when modulatedClips is nonempty. Existing volume fades toward zero, so crossing the threshold does not instantly silence a sound. The event pass instead compares the larger current/previous speed against this threshold and then checks each event’s own minSpeed. Speeds are world units per second, or metres per second in a scene using one Unity unit per metre.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.modulatedClips
member.summary: Clip choices for the managed movement sound, selected randomly each time playback starts.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a stored sound asset. Configure a nonnull array of valid clips. A start requires current speed strictly above minSpeed, _canPlay true, and no managed sound already playing or pending. Playback begins at sourceTran’s local origin, initially requesting volume 0.2, with looping controlled by loopClips.

An empty array skips the remaining awake managed-audio updates, including low-speed rearming and volume/pitch adjustment, after event processing and saving current velocity. It does not prevent earlier audioEvents from firing, or the sleeping branch from fading and stopping the managed player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.pitchMod
member.summary: Multiplier applied to requested playback pitch, rather than a speed-response slope.

remarks.para: Pitch is unitless: 1 is the clip’s normal pitch. During awake playback Update, let u be current speed’s clamped minSpeed-to-maxSpeed fraction and t be Time.timeScale clamped to 0–1. Time.timeScale is the game-time rate, with 1 meaning normal speed. Looping pitch approaches (0.85 + 0.3 × u) × (0.5 + 0.5 × t) × pitchMod by at most 0.08 per Update. Non-looping managed pitch is set directly to (0.5 + 0.5 × t) × pitchMod, without the speed factor.

At normal time, the looping target therefore ranges from 0.85 to 1.15 times pitchMod. The initial sound request, including an event sound, passes pitchMod through the audio helper’s separate startup time-scale adjustment; the formulas above describe later managed Update adjustments, not every initial sample.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.rb_parent
member.summary: Optional Rigidbody whose point velocity is subtracted from this body’s velocity at velocityTran.

remarks.para: Both bodies are sampled at the same world position, including velocity caused by their rotation. The subtraction remains a vector in world coordinates; it is not transformed into the parent’s local axes. For example, subtracting a moving platform’s velocity can leave only the object’s movement relative to that platform. Without a live reference, own point velocity is used. Awake and Initialize clear this reference if it is the same Rigidbody as _rigidbody. Speeds are world units per second, or metres per second in a scene using one Unity unit per metre.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.sourceMinDistance
member.summary: Minimum-distance setting requested for movement and event sounds.

remarks.para: This is a distance in world units, or metres when the scene uses one Unity unit per metre. For spatial audio it sets the near region where distance attenuation does not further reduce volume; it is not a hard outer audible radius. The value is passed on new playback requests, so editing it alone does not change the existing managed sound’s setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.sourceTran
member.summary: Transform used as the playback origin for both modulated clips and event sounds.

remarks.para: A Transform describes a scene object’s position, rotation and scale. New sound requests use local position zero on this Transform, placing them at its origin. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PrismaticSFX.velocityTran
member.summary: Transform whose world position is the point used to measure movement and test event triggers.

remarks.para: Assign a valid Transform, which describes a scene object’s position, rotation and scale; Awake does not supply a fallback for this field. GetPointVelocity samples the own Rigidbody at that world position and includes rotation-induced motion. With rb_parent assigned, its velocity at the same point is subtracted. The measurement uses position, not a difference of Transform positions between frames. Event tests also compare this point with eventTran’s world position and convert it into eventTran’s local coordinates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.aggression
member.summary: Sets the enemy's starting anger value when this configuration is applied.

remarks.para: This is a number normally between 0 and 1, and damage reactions can change the live copy afterward. For BehaviourPowerLegs, such as humanoid enemies, it helps choose a response to a target with exactly the same npcType category: below 0.5 chooses the engaged state, while 0.5 or higher chooses the aggressive state. Targets of a different category follow a separate aggressive branch. Setting it to 0 therefore does not make the enemy harmless to every target.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

In this PowerLegs decision update, the aggressive branch can attempt its configured attack animations, subject to combat mode, range, facing and cooldown gates. The engaged branch handles the target without starting that attack routine in this branch. This does not guarantee a hit or set an attack-rate multiplier.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.irritability
member.summary: Stores a copied disposition setting whose effect on anger was not verified in the inspected health and BehaviourPowerLegs code.

remarks.para: The complete SubBehaviourHealth non-event methods and BehaviourPowerLegs hit, collision, and decision-update methods inspected here do not read this value to make the enemy easier to anger. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo and ApplyFrom copy it, but that copying alone provides no verified tuning effect. Other enemy classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.maxAppendageHp
member.summary: Sets how much processed damage each arm or leg can take before its own health is depleted.

remarks.para: The live system stores a separate health fraction for each arm and leg: 1 is full health and 0 is depleted. It divides that limb's processed damage by this value to reduce the fraction. For example, 20 damage points against a value of 100 removes 0.20, or 20% of the limb's full health, after any special damage adjustments.

Lower limb health also reduces how strongly that limb follows its intended body pose. Organic enemies can lose some overall health from limb damage too. A depleted limb does not by itself mean the enemy's overall health is zero. Use a positive value so the damage division makes sense.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.maxHitPoints
member.summary: Sets the damage-point scale for depleting the enemy's overall health and triggering death.

remarks.para: Overall health is stored as a fraction: 1 is full and 0 is depleted. Damage calculations divide their processed damage by this value. For a calculation that subtracts 20 damage points directly, a value of 100 removes 0.20, or 20% of full health. Head hits, blunt-hit reductions, and limb hits have additional rules, so an incoming attack of 20 does not always remove exactly 20 points.

Larger positive values make the same processed damage remove a smaller fraction. Applying this setting does not refill the current health fraction. Use a positive value because the damage calculation divides by it.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.maxStunSeconds
member.summary: Limits how far a hit can push the enemy's stun counters below zero, setting the lower starting point from which physical control recovers.

remarks.para: For positive stunRecovery, the lowest counter value is -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery). Here maxStunSeconds is in scaled game seconds, stunRecovery is the number of counter units regained per game second, and the counter is a number whose normal full value is 1. Values below 0 strongly suppress physical control; between 0 and 1 it gradually returns. Some limbs retain a small minimum strength.

For example, maxStunSeconds = 5 and stunRecovery = 2 allow a lowest counter of -10. With no new hits, recovery nominally takes 5 game seconds to reach 0 and another 0.5 seconds to reach the full value of 1. This is not an exact 5-second timer for complete recovery: updates happen on frames, game time can be slowed, and later hits can delay recovery.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.minHeadImpact
member.summary: Sets the amount subtracted from a collision's processed impact strength before a head hit can stun and damage the enemy.

remarks.para: Stun rejects a strength below this threshold. At exactly the threshold, subtracting it leaves zero strength; a stronger hit uses the excess. For a threshold of 10 and supplied processed strength of 14, the head-hit calculation receives 4. Head hits change the shared spine stun counter rather than a separate head timer.

The supplied strength normally comes from collision impulse, the shove delivered during contact, measured in newton-seconds. Some zero-impulse fallback calculations and enemy-specific collision adjustments use a different scale, so this is a threshold for the processed value, not a universal force reading. Direct Attack damage uses a separate calculation and does not check this threshold.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.
Stun marks recovery active before checking this threshold. A below-threshold hit leaves health and stun counters unchanged, but can still enable recovery updates for existing depressed counters.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.placability
member.summary: Controls how much the qualifying melee-contact path lowers the enemy's anger toward a target of the same npcType category.

remarks.para: BehaviourBaseNav.DealMeleeDamage moves live aggression toward 0 by 0.1 × placability after its qualifying contact path, when its current target and self have exactly matching npcType values. Aggression is the live anger number normally between 0 and 1; placability is a multiplier with no physical unit. For aggression = 0.7 and placability = 2, one such adjustment lowers aggression to 0.5.

A value of 0 stops this particular reduction. The reduction is a fixed step per qualifying contact, not a percentage of the damage actually received by the other object. It does not calm every kind of attack or every target category.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.stunRecovery
member.summary: Sets how quickly depressed stun counters climb back toward 1, restoring the enemy's physical control.

remarks.para: A stun counter is a unitless physical-control recovery number: 1 means recovered, 0 suppresses its stun contribution, and negative values delay its return. Physical control means how strongly a simulated body part follows its intended animation. Limb health and other multipliers still affect final strength, and the limb calculation retains a small minimum contribution before multiplying by that body part’s unitless usage setting, a configured multiplier that scales its strength, so a recovered counter does not guarantee an undamaged limb’s full strength.

The value is counter units per scaled game second. Each active recovery update advances a counter by stunRecovery × deltaTime, where deltaTime is the game seconds elapsed since the previous frame. A counter at 0 with stunRecovery = 2 nominally reaches 1 in 0.5 game seconds if no new hit interrupts it. At 0 this rate provides no recovery increment.

Hits can push a counter as low as -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery), where maxStunSeconds is the configured number of game seconds for the below-zero part of recovery. Raising this rate speeds the climb from a particular counter value but also makes that lowest value more negative. From the lowest value, full recovery nominally takes maxStunSeconds + 1 / stunRecovery game seconds for a positive rate, before frame timing and later hits are considered.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BaseEnemyConfig.HealthSettings.vengefulness
member.summary: Scales how strongly qualifying received damage raises BehaviourPowerLegs' anger toward an attacker of the same npcType category.

remarks.para: In that behavior's surviving-hit reaction, live aggression moves toward 1 by (processed damage / maxHitPoints) × vengefulness, when the attack identifies a proxy with exactly the same npcType value as the enemy. Processed damage is the damage amount returned by the health calculation after its reductions; maxHitPoints is the overall-health damage-point scale; vengefulness is a multiplier with no physical unit. Aggression is the live anger number normally between 0 and 1.

For 10 processed damage, maxHitPoints = 100, and vengefulness = 2, the increase is 0.20, stopping at 1. A value of 0 stops this particular anger increase. The attacker is added to the threat system separately, so this value is not a duration or strength of last-attacker fixation. Other enemy behaviors can have different damage-reaction rules.

These are stored configuration settings. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo copies this value to the enemy's live health system; editing this object alone does not update an enemy that already received its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.OnHierarchyChanged
member.summary: Calls listeners when the base muscle-added or muscle-removed hook is invoked.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to notify other code or let it add work. These callbacks run immediately on this instance and pass no arguments.

Both OnMuscleAdded and OnMuscleRemoved invoke this same field when assigned, with no initialization or enabled check in their base implementation. The callback supplies neither the changed muscle nor a new hierarchy snapshot.

For example, a listener can refresh its own lookup of simulated body parts when told the list changed. This is not a promise that every possible transform-parent change triggers the notification. Adding a listener with += preserves existing listeners; assigning this delegate field replaces its current listeners. A field assignment alone does not run the callback.

The wrapper passes each stage its own copy of this value, so changing the copied attack in one listener does not edit the value passed to the later hook.

Order is OnPreMuscleHit, OnMuscleHitBehaviour, then OnPostMuscleHit, skipping unset callbacks. The wrapper checks initialization, but does not check enabled. The base custom hook is empty. This order describes behaviour handling; it is not a guarantee that physical contact resolution or damage delivery happens before or after this callback.
Adding a listener with += preserves existing listeners; assigning this delegate field replaces its current listeners. A field assignment alone does not run the callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.PuppetEvent.animations
member.summary: Lists the animation changes requested, in array order, when this puppet event is triggered.

remarks.para: Trigger first runs unityEvent, which calls its configured listeners, routines called to handle the notification. It then processes these animation entries in their stored order, before handling the configured behavior switch. Assigning the array alone does not start animations.

Each AnimatorEvent names an animation state, the animation controller’s selected action, and a layer, a separate track of animations that can be mixed with other tracks. The puppet’s target Animator, the component that runs the animated character’s controller, receives the requests. Each entry’s crossfadeTime is a transition duration in seconds: a positive value requests a blend from the current animation into that state, while zero or a negative value requests a direct switch without blending.

For example, crossfadeTime = 0.25 requests a quarter-second blend. Trigger issues the requests without waiting for that blend or animation to finish. A frame is one game update; how many frames the transition takes depends on the Animator’s updates. The configured duration is not a guarantee that this method waits exactly that long.

Use an empty array when this event needs no animation changes. The array, its entries, unityEvent and the target Animator needed for those entries must exist; a null array can fail after the notification has already run. The animation state’s identifier is cached when its entry is initialized. Editing animationState afterward by itself does not refresh that saved identifier; initialize the entry again to update it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase._poolee
member.summary: Stores the pooled-object controller that registers this behaviour for lifecycle callbacks.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages a reusable object in a pool. Awake, Unity’s setup callback when the component loads, keeps an existing valid reference or searches the puppet’s MarrowEntity component for one, then registers this behaviour with it.

This is a cached reference. Assigning it later does not repeat registration automatically. Provide the correct controller before Awake runs; the base pool initialization, spawn and cleanup hooks are empty until a derived behaviour overrides them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase._runtimeAnimatorController
member.summary: Caches the contact animator’s current clip collection when the contact-point tool runs.

remarks.para: A runtime animator controller is the Unity asset that supplies an Animator’s animation clips. GetAnimContactPoint overwrites this cache from contactAnimController at the beginning of each call, then looks for the first clip whose name exactly matches contactAnimName.
Changing this cached field is not how to select a different animator for the next tool call: the tool reads the selected Animator again. A controller and its clip list must exist for the search.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.contactAnimController
member.summary: Selects the Animator object whose animation and bone positions the contact-point tool samples.

remarks.para: An Animator is Unity’s component that plays animation. GetAnimContactPoint reads this animator’s current runtime controller to find the named clip, samples the clip on this animator’s object, and measures contactBoneRef relative to this animator transform.

Its origin, axes and scale define the reported local position. Sampling changes the object’s pose and the tool does not restore its original pose. Assigning this field alone performs no sample; the context-menu tool must run. A usable animator with the selected humanoid bone and a matching clip is required.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.contactAnimName
member.summary: Chooses the clip by exact name when the animation contact-point tool runs.

remarks.para: The tool searches the selected animator controller’s clip list in order and uses the first clip with exactly this name. For example, a name of Walk chooses a clip named Walk, rather than a different name such as WalkSlow.
The string has no distance or time unit. Editing it alone does not sample an animation; GetAnimContactPoint must run. A missing match logs a warning, then the attempted null-clip sample can fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.contactBoneRef
member.summary: Selects the humanoid bone measured by the animation contact-point tool.

remarks.para: This component’s Get Animation Contact Point context-menu helper selects a clip in contactAnimController, the Animator component that plays animation, whose name exactly equals contactAnimName. It then asks that animator for this named humanoid bone. The helper measures the bone position relative to the animator transform’s origin, rotation and scale; the logged coordinates are local Unity units, not a world-space point.

For example, choosing LeftFoot measures that bone at contactPointFrame when the Get Animation Contact Point context-menu helper runs. This is a selection label with no time or distance unit. Setting it alone does not sample the clip or perform a ground-contact test. The selected Animator must supply a usable humanoid bone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.contactPointFrame
member.summary: Selects the numbered animation frame whose bone position the contact-point tool first measures.

remarks.para: This is the animation-frame index used by this component’s Get Animation Contact Point context-menu helper, not a live game-update count. The helper reads clips from this component’s contactAnimController Animator and selects the clip whose name exactly matches contactAnimName. It samples that clip at f / R seconds, where f is this integer and R is that clip’s frames-per-second rate truncated to an integer. For f = 30 and R = 30, the chosen time is 1 second. A usable positive integer frame rate is required.

The chosen point is returned to the tool in the contact animator’s local coordinate frame, whose origin, axes and scale define the coordinates. The tool logs it rather than returning it to its caller. The helper then samples and logs the clip’s numbered frames; it changes the animator’s pose and does not restore its starting pose. Editing this field alone does not perform sampling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.deactivated
member.summary: Stores a deactivation marker separately from the component’s enabled state.

remarks.para: The complete base Activate and Deactivate wrappers inspected here do not set this marker; they dispatch their hooks and callbacks. PuppetMaster.ActivateBehaviour and DeactivateBehaviour instead change enabled before calling those wrappers. A callback is a routine called to add work or report a stage.

The inspected base update wrappers use the initialized flag, muscle-list size and their enabled checks, rather than this marker, to decide their work. The complete PuppetMaster initialization, activation, deactivation, fixed, ordinary, late and read methods inspected here also do not use this behaviour marker as their update gate.

For example, writing true does not by itself disable the component, stop a simulated body part, or dispatch Deactivate. Other derived behaviours or callers can interpret the marker; those were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.forceActive
member.summary: Exposes the stored force-active flag without activating the component when it is written.

remarks.para: The native getter returns the stored Boolean, and the protected setter only stores a new Boolean. Neither operation invokes Activate or changes enabled. For example, writing true is not proof that a disabled component has become enabled.

The complete base fixed, ordinary, late, read, write and transform-correction wrappers inspected here do not consult this flag. Their own initialization, muscle-list and enabled checks still determine dispatch. The complete PuppetMaster initialization, activation, deactivation, fixed, ordinary, late and read methods inspected here do not use this behaviour flag to override those checks.
Other derived behaviours and external callers were not exhaustively checked, so this flag does not have a verified universal keep-active effect in the inspected methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.initiated
member.summary: Controls whether the base behaviour wrappers allow their initialized stages to run.

remarks.para: BehaviourBase.Initiate sets this flag true before OnPreInitiate, then runs OnInitiate and OnPostInitiate. It therefore records that initiation has begun, rather than proving the entire setup completed successfully. A callback is a routine called to notify other code or add work.

The base fixed, ordinary and late update wrappers require this flag and a nonempty simulated-body-part list. The read, write and transform-correction wrappers also require enabled; hit, collision and deactivation wrappers test initialization without the same enabled gate.
Writing true directly does not run setup or callbacks. For example, setting it false makes the initialized base wrappers skip their stages; it does not reset the puppet’s body or health.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBase.puppetMaster
member.summary: Selects the controller whose simulated body parts this behaviour queries and updates.

remarks.para: A PuppetMaster manages the character’s simulated body parts and connects them with its animated character. Its initialization discovers behaviours under its own object, or under its parent when necessary, assigns itself to their puppetMaster fields, and then calls each behaviour’s Initiate.

Base update wrappers read this controller’s muscle list. The animation/body helper methods also use the controller for muscle queries and removal. Base Awake, Unity’s setup callback when a component loads, can read the controller’s MarrowEntity object to find its pool controller, so those references must already be available when that path runs.
Assigning this field later changes which controller subsequent reads use; it does not add the behaviour to the new controller’s discovered behaviour list or rerun setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnDeath
member.summary: Stores the no-argument notification invoked after KillEnd’s navigation and targeting cleanup.

remarks.para: A listener is a callback, a routine called to handle a notification. A UnityEvent stores the routines to call when the notification is sent.

KillEnd invokes it after clearing the path, disabling navigation, resetting roaming records, clearing sensor targets and resetting the overlap counter. The call is skipped when this event reference is null. It does not itself prove the puppet’s physical death is complete or prevent repeated notifications.
The ordinary death sequence arranges the start notification earlier. Calling KillEnd directly does not call OnDeathStart first, and a cleanup failure can prevent this notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnDeathStart
member.summary: Stores the no-argument notification invoked after KillStart disables the melee window and detection sphere.

remarks.para: A listener is a callback, a routine called to handle a notification. A UnityEvent stores the routines to call when the notification is sent.

KillStart clears the attack-window flag, zeroes and disables the sensor sphere, resets its center, then invokes this event if its reference exists. The sphere is an invisible detection shape. A missing sensor/sphere or a listener failure can stop the routine.

Calling that hook does not request actual puppet death or invoke the final OnDeath event. Ordinary death-sequence code calls the start and finish hooks in its intended order; this event is not a once-only latch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.OnPostReactivate
member.summary: Stores the callback run at the end of the base reactivation reset for phase 0, receiving this behavior.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to handle a notification. OnReactivate calls this one with the BehaviourBaseNav object as its single argument after phase 0’s navigation, animation, sensor, sound, health and timing resets.

Immediately before the call, meleeAttackActive is false and _blockCollisionsUntil is Time.time + 3 scaled game seconds, a future deadline for part of collision-reaction processing. A null callback is skipped. Phase 1 and other nonzero phases do not reach this base callback, and an earlier reset failure prevents it.
The health reset depends on the puppet’s current dead flag, so notification alone does not prove the puppet has become Alive. More specific NPC classes can add their own work around this base hook.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._animatedRoot
member.summary: Stores the current animated root-bone offset used to align navigation with the physical body.

remarks.para: It is the first muscle’s animated target world position minus the animated target root’s world position. The X, Y and Z components are distances in meters along the world’s axes; this is a current offset, not accumulated root movement.

OnReadBehaviour refreshes it, and phase-0 reactivation and KillEnd also save that offset. SetNavAgentToPhysics subtracts it from the physical root’s predicted position, so changing it shifts where the navigation object is aligned. The next sampling step can overwrite an edit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._animatedRotVel
member.summary: Stores the animation-derived turn-rate contribution added during navigation prediction.

remarks.para: OnReadBehaviour compares the first animated muscle target’s previous and current local rotations, measured in that bone’s parent axes. A quaternion stores an orientation using four unitless numbers. The shortest change is converted to degrees and divided by deltaTime, the current frame’s elapsed scaled game seconds, affected by slow motion. A frame is one game update.

The stored value is the negative X component of that local rotation rate, in degrees per second. SetNavAgentToPhysics adds it to the stored steering turn rate and multiplies by its prediction time in seconds to produce a turn in degrees around world up, the world Y axis. It is not a direct reading of a physical body’s spinning speed; later animation reads replace the stored estimate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._blockCollisionsUntil
member.summary: Stores the absolute scaled game-time deadline for part of collision-reaction suppression.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

BlockCollisions copies its argument here directly. Setup puts it 1.5 seconds ahead; phase-0 reactivation puts it 3 seconds ahead. In PowerLegs’ qualifying non-hand collision path, Time.time earlier than this value skips investigation, stun and pain reactions; equality permits them. Impact-sound setup and hand melee processing are outside that deadline gate.

For example, at Time.time = 20, a stored value of 22 keeps that path blocked until the clock reaches 22. A stored value of 2 is already expired. This field does not disable physical contacts or all collision effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._cachedDestination
member.summary: Stores the destination saved immediately before the navigation agent is disabled.

remarks.para: The three components are a world-space position in meters. DisableNav copies the agent’s destination here; EnableNav submits this saved position again after enabling the agent.

This is a disable/enable snapshot, not a live record of every SetPath request. It can be stale while the agent is running. Editing it changes the next restored destination, without itself submitting a path or moving the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._cooldownLocoSwitch
member.summary: Stores a scaled game-time deadline read by automatic movement-state transitions.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

Setup and phase-0 reactivation initialize this marker from the current Time.time. In PowerLegs, a positive SwitchLocoState cooldown stores the current time plus that many seconds, and getting-up setup can install its own later deadline.

PowerLegs’ automatic getting-up/fallen/airborne decisions check that deadline alongside support and motion conditions. It is not a remaining-seconds countdown or a universal lock on every explicit SwitchLocoState call. A stored value of 25 at game time 23 represents a deadline two scaled seconds ahead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._currentRotDelta
member.summary: Stores the signed steering angle sampled before turn smoothing.

remarks.para: For path steering in PowerLegs’ Standing and Walking updates, it is the signed angle in degrees from local forward to the selected steering direction using the navigation object’s X/Z axes. Local axes turn with that object; local Z is forward. Control modes can supply a different steering input.

The value is sampled before smoothing toward zero. The smoothing updates _currentRotVel, a turn-rate value in degrees per second that is then applied over the frame’s elapsed scaled game seconds. This is not a remaining angle measured after the body has turned, and later AI updates can replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._currentRotVel
member.summary: Stores the signed steering turn-rate value updated by rotation smoothing.

remarks.para: In PowerLegs, smoothing the requested local steering angle toward zero updates this value by reference. Its units are degrees per second. The angle is measured from navigation-local forward toward the chosen path or control direction; the agent’s turning-speed setting limits that smoothing.

The AI applies this rate times the frame’s elapsed scaled game seconds as a turn around world up, the vertical world Y axis. SetNavAgentToPhysics also combines it with the animated turn contribution for prediction. This stored steering value is not a measured Rigidbody angular velocity; a Rigidbody is a body moved by physics.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._fixedTime
member.summary: Stores the last sampled physics-clock time used to avoid repeating synchronization for the same physics time.

remarks.para: It contains Time.fixedTime in scaled game seconds. A physics step is an update of the physical simulation; a frame is one game update and can occur between physics steps. Setup, enabling and phase-0 reactivation initialize this cache.

OnUpdate only refreshes grounded sensing and synchronizes the agent from physics when the current fixedTime is strictly greater than this saved value, then replaces the cache. It is therefore the last processed physics time, not a duration or a guarantee that a new physics step happened on this frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._forceAiTick
member.summary: Requests that the next eligible AI decision check bypass its usual waiting interval.

remarks.para: In the inspected PowerLegs and turret AiTick implementations, true bypasses the comparison with aiTickFreq, the desired interval in unscaled game seconds. Unscaled time is not slowed by the game’s time scale. When the check enters its decision work, it clears this flag and records the unscaled time of that update.

Writing true does not immediately call AiTick or remove other update/setup conditions. The base AiTick hook is empty; its NPC replacement implements this timing behavior. Setup and phase-0 reactivation clear the flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._homeBound
member.summary: Stores whether a navigation binding has established the saved home position.

remarks.para: Setup and phase-0 reactivation save the agent’s isOnNavMesh result here: whether it currently lies on the walkable-surface map. It is not a geometric test of whether the NPC is inside its home area.

When SetPath or ClearPath tries to rebind an off-map agent, a false value lets a successful bind capture the agent’s current world position as homePosition and set this flag true. While true, that recovery path does not recapture home. The stored flag can outlast the sampled agent state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._investigateTarget
member.summary: Stores either an investigation position or an investigation direction in world coordinates.

remarks.para: When investIsPosition is true, the three numbers describe an absolute world-space point in meters and investigation can submit a path toward that point. When false, the vector supplies a direction in the world’s axes, such as the opposite of a collision’s relative movement; it is not a destination position. A collision caller can supply a relative-velocity vector in meters per second; the facing calculation uses that vector’s direction.

Investigate writes this value only when its state and expired-cooldown checks allow the request. In PowerLegs, a direction is turned into the navigation object’s axes for facing when there is no path. Assigning this field alone does not switch the NPC to Investigate or submit a path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._investigationCooldown
member.summary: Stores the scaled game-time deadline that limits new investigation requests.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

Investigate accepts its timing gate only when Time.time is strictly later than this value. On acceptance it stores the current time plus investForSeconds, the requested investigation duration in seconds. It also refuses those requests while Agroed, Engaged or MindControlled.

PowerLegs’ Investigate decision logic uses an expired deadline, no pending overlap count and no path as conditions for calling its return-to-earlier-state hook. The deadline alone does not force an exact-time return. Phase-0 reactivation resets it to −1, making the ordinary clock comparison already expired.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._isNavAgentStopped
member.summary: Stores the agent’s stopped flag saved before navigation is disabled.

remarks.para: DisableNav copies isStopped here when the agent is on its walkable-surface map; it stores false when off the map. EnableNav restores this value after enabling the component and resubmitting its saved destination.
This is a snapshot, not the current live stopped state. A saved true value makes a later enabled agent remain stopped. Editing the field alone does not immediately halt or resume the agent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._lastAiTickTime
member.summary: Stores the clock marker used by the NPC’s decision-interval check.

remarks.para: PowerLegs and turret AiTick compare current unscaled game time minus this value with aiTickFreq, the desired interval in seconds, unless the forced-decision flag is set. Once permitted, they save the current unscaled time here before their decision work. Unscaled seconds are unaffected by slow motion.

Setup initially writes scaled Time.time + 10, and phase-0 reactivation writes scaled Time.time + 5. Those initial future markers are not timestamps of completed AI ticks and come from a different clock from the later decision writes. It is a stored scheduling marker; changing it can permit or delay the next check, without calling the check immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._lastJumpTime
member.summary: Stores the jump-related clock marker used by more specific NPC movement code.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

Setup and phase-0 reactivation write the current time even without a jump. Crablet’s Jump routine can write a future marker, up to 1.1 scaled seconds later, adjusted by its remaining health and unitless recovery-control factor. That factor is 1 for recovered control and 0 for suppressed control.

PowerLegs’ Jumping update compares the current time minus this marker with 2 seconds before requesting an airborne mode. The exact interpretation therefore belongs to the NPC’s movement code: this field is not reliable proof of when the most recent jump began, nor a command to jump.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._localAnimatedRoot
member.summary: Stores the inverse local rotation sample of the first animated muscle target.

remarks.para: A quaternion represents orientation using four unitless numbers. Local rotation is relative to that animated bone’s parent axes. This sample is the inverse orientation, which undoes that local rotation; it is not a position offset or an angle in degrees.

Phase-0 reactivation initializes it. OnReadBehaviour uses the previous inverse sample with the current rotation to estimate animation turning, then replaces it with the current inverse. SetNavAgentToPhysics combines it with the physical root’s world rotation to remove the saved animation rotation before navigation alignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._navAgent
member.summary: Stores the navigation agent whose planned movement is aligned with this NPC’s animation and physical body.

remarks.para: A NavMesh is the game’s map of walkable surfaces. A NavMeshAgent is the component that plans and follows routes on that map.

OnInitiate gets this component from the behavior object’s parent. It disables the agent’s automatic position, rotation and up-axis updates; the behavior then explicitly synchronizes it with the physical root and the animated target root. Its speeds and positions are navigation state, not guaranteed measured body movement.

The route, destination and stopped-state helpers operate on this existing component. Replacing the reference alone does not repeat setup or copy saved routes, so the required navigation and body references must already be ready.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._preAggroState
member.summary: Stores the earlier decision state requested when the NPC returns from investigation or aggression.

remarks.para: Investigate saves the previous decision state when first entering Investigate. SetAgro, SetEngaged and AddThreat save it when the current state is Rest or Roam. Phase-0 reactivation also stores the current state before requesting Rest.

PowerLegs’ ReturnToPreAgro requests this saved state before clearing target and investigation data. That is a stored decision-mode label, not a physical movement mode; the empty base return hook does not restore either state by itself. A new qualifying request can overwrite the saved label.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._targetDirNormalWorld
member.summary: Stores the unit-length world-space direction from the eye reference toward the selected target’s head.

remarks.para: CheckTarget subtracts the eye position from the head physics body’s position, then divides by the resulting distance to make a unitless direction. World axes keep the same orientation throughout the scene. When that distance is zero, this producer saves a zero vector instead.

This cached direction contributes to facing and visibility decisions in derived AI checks. It is not a world position or movement speed, and it is only refreshed when target logic runs. Some derived routines divide by the distance without CheckTarget’s zero-distance fallback, so the field is not universally guaranteed to hold a unit vector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._targetDirWorld
member.summary: Stores the world-axis displacement from the eye reference to the selected target’s head.

remarks.para: CheckTarget writes target-head world position minus eyeTran world position. The X, Y and Z values are signed distances in meters; their combined length is the target separation. For example, a target 3 meters along world X produces an X component of 3 when the other components match.

Target logic uses the displacement for distance, facing and visibility checks and derives a unit-length direction from it. This is a cached displacement, not a destination point or a velocity. It can retain the previous target’s numbers until another target update rewrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav._time
member.summary: Stores the scaled game-clock time last sampled by the behavior’s update or setup code.

remarks.para: Scaled game seconds follow the game’s time scale, including slow motion. Time.time is the elapsed time on that clock, not a real-world clock or a duration.

OnEnable, OnInitiate and phase-0 reactivation initialize it. OnUpdate replaces it with the current Time.time before calling its AI hooks. A frame is one game update; this cache is a clock timestamp, not the frame’s elapsed deltaTime.

It is separate from the unscaled clock used for AI decision intervals and from _fixedTime, the sampled physics-clock time. Reading or writing this field alone does not advance the game clock or run an update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.accuracy
member.summary: Accuracy tuning value with a declared range of 0–10.

remarks.para: BaseEnemyConfig copies this scalar to and from BehaviourBaseNav. The inspected attack and turret consumers do not connect it to projectile spread, so the range does not define an in-game shot-error formula.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.activeRange
member.summary: Range used to size the sensor vision sphere in Roam state.

remarks.para: On Roam entry, PowerLegs.SwitchMentalState passes (activeRange + 1) / 2 to SubBehaviourSensors.SetVisionSphere, not the raw setting. A vision sphere is the sensor's radius-based sensing volume; this field does not set a wake-up distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.agroColor
member.summary: Emissive glow color while agroed.

remarks.para: It is a Unity Color: red, green, blue and alpha channels used as an HDR/emissive color where the surrounding attributes request it. It is not a position or a gameplay scalar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.agroOnNpcType
member.summary: NpcType bitmask gate for trigger-driven agro.

remarks.para: TriggerRefProxy classifies an object for trigger handling: triggerType identifies its category and npcType holds type flags. A bitmask stores several on/off type flags in one value. A Collider defines an object's collision shape, a Rigidbody is Unity's physics-body component, and a GameObject is a scene object that holds components. OnTriggerEnter, the routine Unity calls when a collider enters the trigger, looks for TriggerRefProxy on the incoming collider's attached Rigidbody GameObject. OnTriggerExit, the routine called when it leaves, instead looks on the Collider's own GameObject. These can be different scene objects. Both routines ignore a proxy equal to sensors.selfTrp, a TriggerRefProxy reference separate from sensors.target (the tracked target). OnTriggerEnter increments triggerCount for Player (triggerType 0) without checking this mask; other trigger types must satisfy (agroOnNpcType & npcType) == npcType before AddThreat. OnTriggerExit decrements triggerCount only when the proxy differs from sensors.selfTrp and triggerType is Player (0). Its nested NpcType condition is redundant with that Player-only check, so the mask is not applied symmetrically to both event paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.throwMaxRange
member.summary: Maximum target distance for the inspected PowerLegs throw-enabled attack path.

remarks.para: This float is a distance threshold in Unity world units. In the inspected BehaviourPowerLegs.TriggerAttack path, this maximum is checked only when enableThrowAttack is on: a target farther than the maximum exits that attack path, while equality passes this check.

A Rigidbody is Unity's physics-body component, and a Transform stores an object's position, rotation, and scale. That path's targetDistance is the world-space distance between the target Rigidbody position and the eye Transform position. Facing, attack-event, cooldown, and state gates still apply, so passing the range check alone does not cause a throw.

This condition is reached only when enableThrowAttack is on and the branch's forward-facing and locomotion-state checks pass. It is one gate in that consumer, not a rule for every derived behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.throwVelocity
