remarks.para: This float is copied between BehaviourBaseNav and BaseEnemyConfig by the inspected ApplyFrom and ApplyTo methods. Those copies do not establish a launch effect or a unit.

A Rigidbody is Unity's physics-body component; its AddForce method applies force to that body. In the inspected BehaviourPowerLegs.Throw spawn callback (the routine called when the projectile has spawned), the spawned projectile's Rigidbody.AddForce input is scaled by the separate BehaviourPowerLegs.throwSpeed field. The reviewed paths do not establish this shared throwVelocity field as that launch scalar.

remarks.para: This int is incremented or decremented only for TriggerRefProxy.TriggerType.Player (enum value 0). The enter and exit handlers skip the proxy that is already the sensors' current target; enter also requires the collider's attached Rigidbody to resolve to a TriggerRefProxy.
Proxy (1) and Npc (2) trigger types do not change this counter. It is therefore not a count of every overlapping trigger or a general count of nearby objects.

remarks.para: This List<Vector3> stores generated roam target positions in Unity world coordinates. In RoamByMode when roamMode is LEGACY, the branch records a candidate after CalculatePath succeeds: it adds entries while the list has fewer than 10, then replaces a random existing entry.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.waypointEvalMode
member.summary: Selects how GetNextWaypoint chooses an index from the Vector3 waypoint array.

remarks.para: LINEAR advances the current index and wraps to the beginning. PING_PONG advances it, then at the end resets the index to 1 and reverses the waypoints array in place. RANDOM chooses a random array index.

RANDOM_MIN_TIME attempts at most as many random index draws as there are entries in the waypoint array, sampling with replacement; the same index may be drawn again while another remains untested. Each index has a Time.time eligibility deadline, the saved game-time at which the normal selection check considers it eligible. Time.time is Unity game time in seconds, affected by Time.timeScale (the game clock's speed setting); wpMinTime is the cooldown interval added to that clock, also in game-time seconds. When a draw finds a missing deadline or one at or before the current time, the method stores Time.time + wpMinTime and returns that index. If all bounded draws hit indices whose deadlines are still in the future, the method returns the last sampled index even though that index is not yet eligible. It can therefore miss an eligible index and return one whose cooldown has not expired. The mode changes index selection for the configured Vector3 array; it does not describe waypointObjects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.waypointObjects
member.summary: GameObject reference array; the inspected waypoint route reads a separate Vector3 array.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a scene object that can hold components, such as physics or rendering behavior. The declared type is GameObject[], an array of references to those scene objects. The inspected WAYPOINTS route in RoamByMode reads positions from the separate Vector3[] waypoints field and passes the selected position to SetPath.

The reviewed setup and route bodies do not show these GameObjects being converted into route positions. This description is limited to the field type and those inspected consumers; it makes no whole-binary absence claim.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.waypoints
member.summary: World-space positions the NPC can roam between.

remarks.para: This is an array of Unity Vector3 world-space waypoint positions. Components use Unity distance units (metres at unit scale); it is the vector data source, distinct from waypointObjects and from usedWPList history.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.wpMinTime
member.summary: Cooldown interval used to make RANDOM_MIN_TIME waypoint indices eligible again.

remarks.para: This float is an interval in Unity game-time seconds, not time spent standing at a waypoint. In RANDOM_MIN_TIME, GetNextWaypoint adds it to the current Time.time to make the selected index's next eligibility deadline.
Time.time is measured in seconds and is affected by Unity's Time.timeScale; changing this interval changes the cooldown clock, not the agent's travel speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.wpTimeLookup
member.summary: Per-index Time.time deadlines used by RANDOM_MIN_TIME waypoint selection.

remarks.para: This Dictionary<int, float> maps a waypoint-array index to an absolute eligibility deadline on the Time.time clock. Its float values are deadlines, not durations or configured per-index wait overrides.

In GetNextWaypoint, a missing key or a deadline at or before the current time makes that random index eligible; the method then stores Time.time + wpMinTime for the next time it can be selected. Unity's Time.time uses seconds of game time and is affected by Time.timeScale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.MasterProps.normalMode
member.summary: Chooses this puppet's normal mode: Active (0) or Unmapped (1).

remarks.para: This field is an enum selection: a named mode value rather than a distance, time, or force. It belongs to the serializable MasterProps settings alongside mappingBlendSpeed, activateOnStaticCollisions, and activateOnImpulse.

The field is stored at the start of the MasterProps data, before the mapping speed value. The verified MasterProps constructor initializes mappingBlendSpeed to 10.0 but does not write normalMode, so it establishes no explicit constructor assignment for this field.

During BehaviourPuppet.OnLateUpdate—the per-frame late-update pass PuppetMaster uses to call this behavior—after the PuppetMaster controller that owns the muscle bodies reports isAlive, the behavior compares normalMode with its saved lastNormalMode. When it detects a change from Unmapped (1) to a different mode, it sets each muscle's extra Muscle.State.mappingWeightMlp multiplier to 1.0, then remembers the selected mode. A muscle here is an individual simulated body segment; mapping moves it toward its animated target pose. Muscle.Map multiplies this extra factor by the muscle's configured Muscle.Props.mappingWeight and the overall weight passed by PuppetMaster to the mapping call. A value of 1.0 is a neutral multiplier in that product; the other weights still affect the final mapping amount, so it does not guarantee full mapping by itself. The update happens in late update, not synchronously when the setting is assigned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.MusclePropsGroup.groups
member.summary: The collection of muscle groups governed by this property configuration block.

remarks.para: A Muscle.Group value is a category label for a puppet body part, such as Hand or Foot. These are labels rather than measurements or directions in the scene, so they have no units or coordinate frame.

GetProps scans the groupOverrides array in order and returns the props value from the first block whose groups array contains the queried category. If no block contains it, GetProps returns the defaults settings. If more than one block lists a category, the first matching block wins.

InGroup is a separate two-category check: it returns true when the two category values are equal or when both appear in the same override block. It does not select settings for one category and does not test a parent/child hierarchy.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.MusclePropsGroup.props
member.summary: The MuscleProps settings used for every category listed in this override block.

remarks.para: MuscleProps is copied configuration data returned by GetProps, not the simulated muscle or its mass. Its three collision-unpin amounts tune falloff: how strongly a collision's unpin effect reaches parent, child, and same-group muscles. Here, unpin means reducing the hold that keeps a simulated muscle near its animation pose. The collision and unpin routines read these amounts when evaluating group falloff; the native evidence verifies them as inputs and does not claim one fixed pin-weight change for every collision.

The bundle also contains minimum and maximum mapping weights. A mapping weight is a unitless 0-to-1 multiplier for how strongly Muscle.Map copies a simulated muscle's pose (its position and rotation) onto its matching animated target (the transform used for that limb's animation). Muscle.Map writes rotation and, when position mapping is enabled, position to the target. BlendMuscleMapping reads those bounds while moving the muscle mapping weight over time using the configured blend speed.

The bundle includes a collider-disable setting and separate PhysicMaterial references for Puppet/GetUp and Unpinned states. A collider is the Unity shape used to detect contacts. A PhysicMaterial is the contact-surface setting applied to a collider. SetState routes later state handling through SetColliders, which reads the selected settings and applies collider material and enabled-state choices. Puppet is the normal pinned mode, GetUp is recovery, and Unpinned is the loosened ragdoll mode.

The amounts and mapping weights described here are dimensionless tuning values, not distances, masses, or positions. MuscleProps also has other fields, including a distance setting and physics-material references, so the bundle has no single unit or coordinate frame. Assigning this field stores configuration; it does not itself run collision handling, update mapping, rebuild groups, or change state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.onLoseBalanceFromPuppet
member.summary: Event raised when SetState leaves normal mode after balance loss.

remarks.para: SetState first invokes the general onLoseBalance event. If that event does not request a behavior switch and the previous state is Puppet, SetState invokes this specialized event before changing the stored state, so listeners see Puppet. In the reviewed Unpinned branch, SetState does not gate this loss-event call on eventsEnabled; that flag gates the separate regain event.

A PuppetEvent is the configured no-argument UnityEvent plus optional Animator and behavior-switch actions. A callback is a routine the event invokes. Trigger invokes the UnityEvent first, then Animator actions, then attempts the configured switch. If switchToBehaviour requests another behavior, SetState stores Unpinned before returning.
This is a transition event, not a value with a physical unit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.onRegainBalance
member.summary: Event raised when SetState changes the stored mode to .

remarks.para: SetState stores Puppet before checking the eventsEnabled gate and triggering this event, so listeners see the new mode.

A PuppetEvent is the configured no-argument UnityEvent plus optional Animator and behavior-switch actions. A callback is a routine the event invokes. Trigger invokes the UnityEvent first, then Animator actions, then may switch behavior. The UnityEvent listeners receive no arguments here.
This is a transition event, not a value with a physical unit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.pinWeightThreshold
member.summary: Inspector setting for the intended pin-weight test after a muscle moves farther from its animated target than Knock Out Distance.

remarks.para: Pin weight is a normalized, unitless value for how strongly a muscle is held toward its animated target. The Inspector tooltip’s intended rule is: after the muscle moves farther than Knock Out Distance, unpin only if its pin weight is below this threshold. The Inspector Range of 0 to 1 guides editing; it is not a runtime clamp.

The complete reviewed OnFixedUpdate, SetState, OnMuscleCollisionBehaviour, GetProps, UnPin, and UnPinMuscle bodies contain no read of this top-level setting. This is a limit of those named bodies, not proof that no consumer exists elsewhere; runtime use is not established here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.regainPinSpeed
member.summary: Top-level pin-recovery setting; its Inspector tooltip describes how quickly muscles regain target pin weight.

remarks.para: The class declares this top-level setting with an Inspector Range of 0.001 to 10. The complete reviewed OnFixedUpdate body does not read it, so those inspected bodies establish neither a runtime effect nor units. The Inspector range is editing guidance, not proof of a runtime clamp.

This field is separate from BehaviourPuppet.MuscleProps.regainPinSpeed, stored within defaults or a group override, and from getUpRegainPinSpeedMlp, a separate GetUp multiplier. OnFixedUpdate calls GetProps into a local buffer but does not read the returned MuscleProps values in that body; this does not establish a consumer for the top-level field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.state
member.summary: Current mode: , , or . Use to coordinate a transition.

remarks.para: This property stores an enum value, not a physical quantity. Puppet is the normal mode in which muscle bodies are held toward the animated target. Unpinned is the physics-driven ragdoll mode with normal pinning released or reduced. GetUp is the recovery mode that aligns the target and blends toward a get-up animation.

The state getter and setter only read or write the stored enum. Call SetState when changing modes: it also updates colliders and muscle weights, resets recovery timers as appropriate, aligns the target, and dispatches transition events. Writing the property directly skips that coordinated work.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.unpinnedMuscleKnockout
member.summary: Serialized option whose Inspector tooltip describes whether zero-pin-weight muscles can contribute to balance loss.

remarks.para: A muscle with zero pin weight has no normal pinning influence toward its animated target. The Inspector tooltip says that setting this option false excludes muscles configured with zero pin weight from unbalancing the puppet.

The complete reviewed OnFixedUpdate, SetState, OnMuscleCollisionBehaviour, GetProps, UnPin, and UnPinMuscle bodies do not read this setting. The literal hook address examined for muscle hits resolves to an unrelated empty stub, so it does not prove a consumer. The documented toggle is the Inspector intent; these reviewed bodies do not establish its runtime effect, and this is not a whole-binary absence claim.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.unpinnedMuscleWeightMlp
member.summary: When SetState enters while PuppetMaster reports the character alive, this unitless multiplier is copied into each muscle’s runtime strength setting.

remarks.para: This is a unitless muscle-strength multiplier. On entry to Unpinned, SetState copies this value into each muscle’s Muscle.State.muscleWeightMlp when PuppetMaster reports isAlive. If PuppetMaster reports not alive, SetState copies PuppetMaster.StateSettings.deadMuscleWeight instead. MusclePdDrive uses the stored muscleWeightMlp when calculating the joint’s slerp drive.

The Inspector Range of 0 to 1 is editing guidance, not a runtime clamp. The reviewed OnFixedUpdate body does not reapply this value each physics step, so changing the setting while already Unpinned is not shown to update live muscle values until another code path copies it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourPuppet.unpinnedTimer
member.summary: Seconds accumulated during ; the recovery delay uses this timer before GetUp can begin.

remarks.para: OnFixedUpdate runs during Unity’s FixedUpdate physics-step callback. It adds Time.deltaTime only when the connected PuppetMaster is active and reports alive, and only while state is Unpinned; Time.deltaTime is measured in seconds. Automatic GetUp also requires canGetUp to be true, this timer to reach getUpDelay, getupDisabled to be false, and the hip Rigidbody’s speed magnitude to be below maxGetUpVelocity. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for a simulated physics body.

SetState resets this timer when entering Unpinned, Puppet, or GetUp. OnReactivate also resets it. Resurrect writes positive infinity while still Unpinned; that satisfies the elapsed-delay comparison, while the other recovery gates still apply. Rigidbody velocity is a world-space Unity-units-per-second value; these bodies do not establish a conversion from the game’s Unity units to metres.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.Props.group
member.summary: The muscle category PuppetMaster uses to select this profile for group-wide weight settings.

remarks.para: The field is stored at the start of the profile data, before mappingWeight, muscleWeight, muscleDamper, and mapPosition. The parameterized constructor writes its argument to this slot.

Categories include Hips, Spine, Head, Arm, Hand, Leg, Foot, Tail, and Prop. This is a category label, not a bone-array index or position; it has no distance, force, or coordinate frame. When the PuppetMaster is initialized, the group-taking SetMuscleWeights overload finds profiles with the matching category and updates their strength, mapping, and damping values. It changes profile settings; it does not itself move a bone.

member.summary: Configuration settings defining weight, damping, group categorization, and position mapping for this muscle.

remarks.para: Muscle.Props configuration value consumed by the drive and mapping paths. It groups per-muscle settings such as weight/damping and mapping categories; it is not the live Rigidbody mass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.rotationRelativeToTarget
member.summary: Initialized rotation offset used to reconstruct the physical bone's orientation from its animated target.

remarks.para: Initiate stores inverse(target.rotation) * transform.rotation, using the animated target and physical bone's world orientations at setup. A Transform stores position and rotation; world orientation is measured in the scene's shared reference frame. MoveToTarget later multiplies the animated target's world rotation by this saved offset to obtain the physical bone's world rotation. The offset is a unitless Quaternion, a representation of orientation, not a continuously measured difference or an angular velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.slerpDrive
member.summary: The joint's rotation-drive settings: spring, damping, and maximum force.

remarks.para: A joint links two physics bodies. Slerp is Unity's smooth blending between rotations; the ConfigurableJoint uses these JointDrive settings to make the muscle follow a target orientation. The spring setting controls the rotation-restoring drive, damping opposes rotational motion, and maximum force caps the drive. MusclePdDrive builds and applies these settings when their cached values change. This is configuration applied to the joint, not a current pose or a measured force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.state
member.summary: Mutable runtime Muscle.State values associated with mapping and joint-drive calculations.

remarks.para: Muscle.State is mutable runtime data, distinct from the serialized Props configuration. The verified mapping path uses mappingWeightMlp; the slerp-drive path scales muscle weight, damping, and maximum force with their State values and adds muscleDamperAdd. The struct also declares immunity and impulseMlp values; this evidence does not name their broader consumers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.target
member.summary: Animated target transform that this physical muscle joint attempts to track and match.

remarks.para: Animated target Transform that the physical muscle attempts to follow. Its pose is an object-owned Unity Transform, not a copy of the current Rigidbody pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetAnimatedPosition
member.summary: Vector3 backing value exposed by the targetAnimatedPosition property.

remarks.para: The property getter and setter copy a Vector3 backing value. Those accessors do not identify who produces the value, which coordinate frame it uses, or how it is consumed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetAnimatedRotation
member.summary: Animated target rotation cached by Read, with its reference frame chosen by the connected-body branches.

remarks.para: A Transform stores position and rotation; a Quaternion is a unitless representation of orientation. With a connected physics body and directTargetParent=true, Read stores target.localRotation, relative to the animated target's immediate parent. With a connected body and false, it stores targetLocalRotation, computed as inverse(targetParentRotation * toParentSpace) * target.rotation. targetParentRotation is the selected animated parent's world rotation; toParentSpace is the initialized offset from that parent to the physical connected body; target.rotation is the animated target's world orientation. With no connected body, only the observed Props.group==0 branch stores the target world rotation; the other observed group branches leave this cache unchanged. MusclePdController later converts this cached pose into the joint's rotation reference for drive calculations, so it is not itself always a local rotation or an angular rate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetLocalRotation
member.summary: Animated target orientation relative to the selected parent's rotation with the initialized connected-body offset applied.

remarks.para: The getter computes inverse(targetParentRotation * toParentSpace) * target.rotation. targetParentRotation is the selected animated parent's world orientation, toParentSpace is the offset established during initialization from that parent to the physical connected body's world orientation, and target.rotation is the animated target's world orientation. World space is the scene's shared reference frame, and a Transform stores an object's position and rotation. This unitless Quaternion (orientation value) expresses the target relative to the combined connected-body reference, rather than relative to the animated parent alone; it need not equal Transform.localRotation. If no connected body exists at initialization, the physical reference used to establish the offset is identity, meaning no rotation, so the initialized combined reference is the world frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetParent
member.summary: Transform reference used as the animated target parent frame.

remarks.para: Initiate selects connectedBodyTarget when it finds the matching parent body target; otherwise it uses target.parent. A Transform stores position and rotation. Its world rotation participates in targetLocalRotation together with toParentSpace, the initialized unitless offset from this animated parent to the physical connected body. The resulting reference includes that physical-body correction rather than only this Transform's animated-parent frame. If it is absent, the target-parent rotation helper returns identity where defined.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetParentRotation
member.summary: Current world rotation of the target's parent transform.

remarks.para: World rotation of targetParent, or identity when targetParent is absent. It is a unitless Quaternion frame basis used by targetLocalRotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.targetRotationRelative
member.summary: Gets the initial target rotation relative to the muscle rigidbody.

remarks.para: Property exposing the cached relative rotation target used by drive/mapping code. It is a Quaternion relationship rather than a world rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.Muscle.toParentSpace
member.summary: Initialized rotation offset from the selected animated parent to the physical connected-body reference.

remarks.para: Initiate computes inverse(targetParentRotation) * ParentRotation. targetParentRotation is the selected animated parent's world orientation, while ParentRotation is the physical connected body's world orientation, or identity (no rotation) if there is no connected body. A Transform stores position and rotation, and world space is the scene's shared reference frame. The targetLocalRotation getter combines targetParentRotation with this saved offset before converting the animated target's world rotation into that reference. This is a unitless Quaternion, an orientation offset; it is not a general conversion of local joint rotations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.isActive
member.summary: Requires an active, enabled component and initiation; a Disabled runtime mode with no mode switch reports true only while a state change is pending.

remarks.para: First requires Behaviour.isActiveAndEnabled: this component must be enabled and the scene object that holds it must be active in the hierarchy. It also requires initiated, the initialization gate set during Initiate; that gate does not guarantee that every setup callback has finished. If either check fails, this getter returns false.

After those checks, when activeMode is Disabled and isSwitchingMode is false, it returns whether the requested state differs from activeState. Here activeMode is the runtime mode currently applied, isSwitchingMode means a mode transition is running, state requests Alive, Dead, or Frozen, and activeState is the lifecycle state currently applied. In every other mode/switch case, it returns true. For example, with Disabled activeMode and no mode switch, requested Dead with activeState Alive returns true while that state change is pending; matching requested and applied states return false. This is a computed Boolean status with no numeric unit or side effect; the getter is not itself the FixedUpdate gate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.muscleDamper
member.summary: The positionDamper of the ConfigurableJoint Slerp drives. Pair it with . Higher values resist pose changes more.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics joint that connects two bodies; its Slerp drive applies torque to make their relative rotation follow a target orientation. A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics-body component. The global positionDamper coefficient is passed to each Muscle update and supplied to the muscle ConfigurableJoint's Slerp drive. MusclePdDrive combines it with the per-muscle Props.muscleDamper and state multipliers before writing JointDrive.positionDamper. This is a drive coefficient, not a normalized 0-to-1 weight; its response depends on the Rigidbody and joint setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.muscleSpring
member.summary: The positionSpring of the ConfigurableJoint Slerp drives. Pair it with .

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics joint that connects two bodies; its Slerp drive applies torque to make their relative rotation follow a target orientation. A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics-body component. The global positionSpring coefficient is passed to each Muscle update and supplied to the muscle ConfigurableJoint's Slerp drive. MusclePdDrive combines it with muscle drive weight before writing JointDrive.positionSpring. This is a drive coefficient, not a normalized weight; its response depends on the damper, Rigidbody, and joint setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.muscleWeight
member.summary: Global muscle drive weight with an Inspector Range of 0 to 1; the runtime path does not clamp the stored value.

remarks.para: The Inspector Range metadata gives this global muscle drive weight an intended range of 0 to 1. OnLateUpdate passes the stored value into each Muscle update, where it scales drive influence together with per-muscle and state multipliers; the inspected runtime path does not clamp it. It is not force in Newtons.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.muscles
member.summary: The s driven by this PuppetMaster, one per ragdoll joint.

remarks.para: An indexed array of Muscle objects, normally one for each prepared ragdoll joint. A Muscle pairs a target bone Transform with a physical Rigidbody and its ConfigurableJoint; its Slerp drive makes the body follow the target. Muscle and targetChildren indices preserve that pairing. Positions are in metres and rotations are Quaternions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.prefabParameters
member.summary: Target Animator parameter values captured at Awake time for later restoration.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback for this component. A dictionary snapshot of the targetAnimator's current parameter values. Awake calls SetParameters(false) to capture them at Awake time, and ReadParameters(false) can restore that snapshot. These are the values present at capture time, not necessarily untouched prefab defaults or values captured before per-instance changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.solverIterationCount
member.summary: Rigidbody.solverIterationCount applied to this puppet's muscles. Higher means stiffer, more accurate solving at greater cost.

remarks.para: An integer count applied to the muscle Rigidbodies' solver iteration setting. Unity uses those iterations during each fixed physics step; more iterations can make joint constraints stiffer and more accurate at additional CPU cost. This is a count, not a frequency or force.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.solvers
member.summary: SolverManager components under targetRoot gathered into the list by Awake before Initiate.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback for this component. Awake gathers SolverManager components under targetRoot into this list before calling Initiate. A SolverManager is a helper component that adjusts a pose, for example with inverse kinematics. OnEnable and OnDisable toggle the separate BehaviourBase and cullableAnimators arrays; the reviewed bodies do not show those callbacks enabling or disabling this solvers list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.state
member.summary: Requested Alive, Dead, or Frozen state; activeState tracks the runtime state while transitions proceed, and Frozen is reached through the delayed freeze path.

remarks.para: The requested State enum: Alive (0), Dead (1), or Frozen (2). activeState tracks the runtime state currently applied, so a request can take time to settle. The normal OnFreezeFlag handler can enter Frozen once Unity’s fixed physics time reaches the stored deadline, measured in seconds; that handler does not test a velocity threshold, and Frozen can later be resurrected; assigning state does not instantly settle every muscle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.stateSettings
member.summary: Controls how killing and freezing play out: freeze timing, what gets disabled, and so on.

remarks.para: The StateSettings value supplies six kill/freeze controls. killDuration is a duration in seconds; deadMuscleWeight and deadMuscleDamper tune the dead-state muscle drive; maxFreezeSqrVelocity is a squared-speed threshold in metres squared per second squared; enableAngularLimitsOnKill and enableInternalCollisionsOnKill control those settings during kill. PreKill uses the kill settings, and CanFreeze checks its time gate and each muscle Rigidbody's squared speed against maxFreezeSqrVelocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetAnimator
member.summary: Animator resolved during Initiate; culling manages its parameters while pose mapping traverses target Transforms.

remarks.para: The Animator resolved and stored during Initiate. Its controller evaluates the animated target and its parameter values are saved/restored by culling code. Pose mapping traverses target Transforms and Muscle entries; it does not use the Animator component itself as a pose buffer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetChildren
member.summary: Target bone Transforms paired one-to-one with muscles in muscle-array order.

remarks.para: UpdateHierarchies builds this array from each Muscle's target Transform in muscles order. Entries therefore correspond one-to-one and by index with muscles; the array is not every Transform under targetRoot. Pose buffers use this same index relationship.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetRoot
member.summary: Root of the animated target whose pose the muscles follow. Usually the NPC's animated avatar itself.

remarks.para: The root Transform of the animated target followed by the physical ragdoll. Where stored or sampled poses use a relative frame, the root entry uses its local pose and child entries are expressed relative to targetRoot; values are not all world-space.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetSampledPositions
member.summary: Target bone positions captured by the last SampleTargetState() call.

remarks.para: SampleTargetState stores targetRoot.localPosition in entry 0 and stores each child position offset in the targetRoot frame. Positions are measured in metres, and BlendToSampledState consumes the array to rebuild the sampled pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetSampledRotations

remarks.para: SampleTargetState stores targetRoot.localRotation in entry 0 and child orientations relative to targetRoot. SampleTargetRotations uses the equivalent root-relative branch. Entries are Quaternions, which encode orientation without degree units.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetStoredPositions

remarks.para: StoreTargetState stores targetRoot.localPosition at entry 0 and each child position offset in the targetRoot frame. SetTargetState composes the saved values back into world positions; positions are measured in metres.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.targetStoredRotations
member.summary: Target bone rotations saved by the last StoreTargetState() call.

remarks.para: StoreTargetState stores targetRoot.localRotation at entry 0 and child rotations relative to the root. SetTargetState composes these Quaternion values back into the hierarchy; Quaternions encode orientation without degree units.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.teleportMoveToTarget
member.summary: Teleport option controlling the later call that snaps muscles to the teleported target.

remarks.para: The Boolean option saved by Teleport for ProcessTeleport. The target hierarchy is transformed and reparented as part of the teleport regardless of this option; when true, the later loop also calls Muscle.MoveToTarget() to snap muscles to their target after teleport.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.teleportPosition
member.summary: World-space teleport destination in metres, applied regardless of teleportMoveToTarget.

remarks.para: The pending world-space destination used by ProcessTeleport's parent/pivot delta calculation. It is measured in metres and is applied as part of the teleport regardless of teleportMoveToTarget, which controls only the later muscle snap loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.teleportRotation

remarks.para: The pending world-space Quaternion used by ProcessTeleport to rotate the parent/pivot and transform stored pose snapshots. It is applied regardless of teleportMoveToTarget; that Boolean separately controls whether muscles are snapped to target after the transform.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.updateJointAnchors
member.summary: Recomputes the joint anchors every cycle. Mapping is more accurate when the target animates bones between the muscle bones. It costs performance.

remarks.para: When enabled, Read and OnLateUpdate call Muscle.UpdateAnchor for each Muscle. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics joint that connects two bodies, and a Transform stores position and orientation. Muscle.UpdateAnchor builds an anchor point in world space, then converts it into the local frame of its stored connectedBodyTarget Transform before writing the joint’s connectedAnchor. This is the frame of that target Transform, rather than the connected physics body’s own Transform. Anchor positions use Unity distance units, equal to metres if one Unity distance unit represents one metre. It can improve tracking when animated target bones lie between muscle bones, costs computation, and does not change the target pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.visualizeTargetAnimation

remarks.para: An Editor-only Scene-view diagnostic for drawing the animated target bone hierarchy. It is separate from visualizeTargetPose, which draws the target pose against the muscle/joint pose. These drawing switches do not change runtime physics or write the simulated Transforms.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.PuppetMaster.visualizeTargetPose

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.OnHeadShot
member.summary: Shared notification sent for a Piercing attack processed against a muscle mapped to Head.

remarks.para: This static callback is a routine called to report the hit across all health instances; it passes no arguments. It runs after that head-hit path changes health and the shared spine stun counter, but before OnNPCDamage, the score increase, and the depleted-health death request. It does not require positive damage, and other attack types mapped to Head do not send it.
This is not proof of a successful kill. Adding listeners with += preserves the other callbacks; assigning a new callback directly replaces them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.OnNPCDamage
member.summary: Shared notification sent when a health object's damage calculation reaches its scoring step.

remarks.para: This is a static callback, meaning a routine called to report an action across all instances. It receives one processed damage amount and no NPC identity. TakeDamage reports its processed attack amount; Stun reports its calculated collision-damage amount. The amount can be 0 and is not always the amount of health actually removed.

Health/counter changes and stunActive = true are visible before listeners run. For a piercing head attack, OnHeadShot runs first. OnNPCDamage then runs before damageScore is increased and before the final depleted-health check requests death. Direct Kill, Resurrect, and field assignments do not send it. Add/remove listeners through the event accessors to preserve other listeners.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.UsageSettings.Default
member.summary: Returns settings with all six pose-driving multipliers set to 0.

remarks.para: After these values are applied, the zeros remove each simulated body part’s rotational-drive contribution toward its intended animated pose. Other physical motion and damping are separate from this contribution.

After SetUsage copies these values and UpdateMuscleStates applies them, the resulting body-region strength multipliers are zero. This does not itself freeze the physical body or apply any settings to an enemy.

To keep the strength calculated from health and stun, construct settings with 1 in every position: UsageSettings(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1). Those values differ from this Default property, which returns zeros.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.aggression
member.summary: Tracks the enemy's live anger level, which some damage reactions raise or lower.

remarks.para: This is a live number normally between 0 and 1, and damage reactions can change it during play. For BehaviourPowerLegs, such as humanoid enemies, it helps choose a response to a target with exactly the same npcType category: below 0.5 chooses the engaged state, while 0.5 or higher chooses the aggressive state. In that same-category aggressive branch, PowerLegs can attempt its configured attack animation when combat, facing, range, cooldown, and other checks pass; the engaged branch tracks or pathfinds without calling TriggerAttack. An animation attempt does not guarantee a damaging hit. Targets of a different category follow a separate aggressive branch. Setting it to 0 therefore does not make the enemy harmless to every target.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.bluntMult
member.summary: Scales the incoming damage points of Blunt attacks before the body-region damage rules.

remarks.para: This multiplier has no physical units: 1 preserves the incoming amount, 0.5 halves it, 2 doubles it, and 0 makes the initial processed amount zero. The health calculation then applies any head, limb, or stun-dependent adjustments, so it is not a direct multiplier of the final lost health fraction. Collision Stun uses a separate calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.cur_arm_lf
member.summary: Stores the left arm's remaining health fraction, which affects its ability to follow its intended pose.

remarks.para: A normal value of 1 means full health, 0.5 means half health, and 0 means depleted. The selected limb's processed damage is divided by maxAppendageHp, its damage-point health scale, before reducing this fraction. Some attack types have additional reductions.

UpdateMuscleStates multiplies this fraction by that limb's and the spine's stun factors. Each factor is its stored stun counter limited to 0–1: 1 means recovered control of the intended pose, and 0 means that control is suppressed. The method keeps a minimum calculated strength of 0.02 before multiplying by that region's usage setting. Usage is a unitless strength multiplier: 1 keeps the calculated strength, 0.5 halves it, and 0 removes it. Zero health therefore does not promise absolutely zero physical strength. Initiate and Resurrect reset it to 1; Kill resets it to 0. Writing the field alone does not invoke those routines or send a damage event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.cur_hp
member.summary: Stores the enemy's overall remaining health fraction; damage routines request death when it becomes depleted.

remarks.para: Normally 1 is full health, 0.5 is half health, and 0 is depleted. Processed overall damage is divided by maxHitPoints, the damage-point scale, before reducing this fraction; head and limb attacks have additional rules. It is overall health rather than a count of torso hit points.

Writing 0 here does not itself call PuppetMaster.Kill or send damage events. Damage routines check this field and request death afterward. Writing 1 does not revive an already-dead physical puppet. Initiate and Resurrect reset the fraction to 1; Kill resets it to 0.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.damageScore
member.summary: Stores a running integer score accumulated by processed damage, with larger weights for spine and head hits.

remarks.para: The scoring path adds int(processed amount × region weight): the weight is 200 for Head, 10 for Spine, and 1 for other groups. These are score units rather than remaining health. For a processed amount of 2, the additions are 400 for a head, 20 for spine, and 2 for a limb. Conversion to int truncates the fractional part of each addition.

OnNPCDamage runs before this score is increased. Initiate, Kill, and Resurrect do not reset it in their inspected implementations. A piercing head's extra health-loss factor of 4.1 is separate from the 200 score weight, so the score is not a count of actual hit points removed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.irritability
member.summary: Stores a copied disposition setting whose effect on anger was not verified in the inspected health and BehaviourPowerLegs code.

remarks.para: The original Inspector tooltip calls this setting “Nonfunctioning”. The verified absence described here is limited to the complete methods listed below, rather than a guarantee about every enemy class or mod.

The complete SubBehaviourHealth non-event methods and BehaviourPowerLegs hit, collision, and decision-update methods inspected here do not read this value to make the enemy easier to anger. BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo and ApplyFrom copy it, but that copying alone provides no verified tuning effect. Other enemy classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.isOrganic
member.summary: Selects the organic damage rules, which let attacks on limbs also reduce overall health.

remarks.para: For an organic arm or leg attack, the calculation reduces overall health by one tenth of processed damage divided by maxHitPoints, the overall damage-point scale, as well as reducing the selected limb's health. A non-organic limb attack skips that overall-health contribution and can reject damage when that limb is already depleted.

Collision spine hits also use different rules: non-organic enemies receive one quarter of the excess-impact counter reduction and use a larger direct collision-damage factor; organic spine collision damage depends on the updated stun factor. This flag chooses these health calculations; it does not change the enemy's model or establish that a limb will be visually severed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.maxAppendageHp
member.summary: Sets how much processed damage each arm or leg can take before its own health is depleted.

remarks.para: The live system stores a separate health fraction for each arm and leg: 1 is full health and 0 is depleted. It divides that limb's processed damage by this value to reduce the fraction. For example, 20 damage points against a value of 100 removes 0.20, or 20% of the limb's full health, after any special damage adjustments.

Lower limb health also reduces how strongly that limb follows its intended body pose. Organic enemies can lose some overall health from limb damage too. A depleted limb does not by itself mean the enemy's overall health is zero. Use a positive value so the damage division makes sense.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.maxHitPoints
member.summary: Sets the damage-point scale for depleting the enemy's overall health and triggering death.

remarks.para: Overall health is stored as a fraction: 1 is full and 0 is depleted. Damage calculations divide their processed damage by this value. For a calculation that subtracts 20 damage points directly, a value of 100 removes 0.20, or 20% of full health. Head hits, blunt-hit reductions, and limb hits have additional rules, so an incoming attack of 20 does not always remove exactly 20 points.

Larger positive values make the same processed damage remove a smaller fraction. Applying this setting does not refill the current health fraction. Use a positive value because the damage calculation divides by it.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.maxStunSeconds
member.summary: Limits how far a hit can push the enemy's stun counters below zero, setting the lower starting point from which physical control recovers.

remarks.para: For positive stunRecovery, the lowest counter value is -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery). Here maxStunSeconds is in scaled game seconds, stunRecovery is the number of counter units regained per game second, and the counter is a number whose normal full value is 1. Values below 0 strongly suppress physical control; between 0 and 1 it gradually returns. Some limbs retain a small minimum strength.

For example, maxStunSeconds = 5 and stunRecovery = 2 allow a lowest counter of -10. With no new hits, recovery nominally takes 5 game seconds to reach 0 and another 0.5 seconds to reach the full value of 1. This is not an exact 5-second timer for complete recovery: updates happen on frames, game time can be slowed, and later hits can delay recovery.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.minHeadImpact
member.summary: Sets the amount subtracted from a collision's processed impact strength before a head hit can stun and damage the enemy.

remarks.para: Stun rejects a strength below this threshold. At exactly the threshold, subtracting it leaves zero strength; a stronger hit uses the excess. For a threshold of 10 and supplied processed strength of 14, the head-hit calculation receives 4. Head hits change the shared spine stun counter rather than a separate head timer.

The supplied strength normally comes from collision impulse, the shove delivered during contact, measured in newton-seconds. Some zero-impulse fallback calculations and enemy-specific collision adjustments use a different scale, so this is a threshold for the processed value, not a universal force reading. Direct Attack damage uses a separate calculation and does not check this threshold.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.minLimbImpact
member.summary: Sets the amount subtracted from a collision's processed impact strength before an arm or leg hit can stun and damage that limb.

remarks.para: Stun rejects a strength below this threshold. At exactly the threshold, subtracting it leaves zero strength; a stronger hit uses the excess. For a threshold of 6 and supplied processed strength of 10, the limb calculation receives 4. The selected arm or leg has its own stun and health values, which affect its physical control.

The supplied strength normally comes from collision impulse, the shove delivered during contact, measured in newton-seconds. Some zero-impulse fallback calculations and enemy-specific collision adjustments use a different scale. This is a threshold for that processed value. Direct Attack damage to a limb does not check this threshold.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.minSpineImpact

The remaining strength affects the spine stun counter and collision damage, with separate organic and non-organic damage rules.

The supplied strength normally comes from collision impulse, the shove delivered during contact, measured in newton-seconds. Some zero-impulse fallback calculations and enemy-specific collision adjustments use a different scale. This field therefore applies to the processed value. Direct Attack damage does not check this threshold.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.muscles
member.summary: Maps each puppet muscle index to a body region for damage and physical control. Each entry is a value.

remarks.para: A physical muscle here is a physics-controlled body part. StunGroup names the body regions to which those parts are mapped for damage and recovery.

muscles[m] is the group chosen by Stun, TakeDamage, and GetStun. Here m is the physical muscle's index, not the numeric StunGroup value. For example, setting the entry for a particular upper-arm muscle to ArmLf sends its damage to the left-arm health and stun values.

UpdateMuscleStates uses the same map for physical-strength updates after handling the first puppet muscle as hips. Supply entries for every visited index: a missing array or out-of-range index fails rather than choosing a safe fallback. Initiate does not build this map.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.pierceMult
member.summary: Scales the incoming damage points of Piercing attacks before the body-region damage rules.

remarks.para: This multiplier has no physical units: 1 preserves the incoming amount, 0.5 halves it, 2 doubles it, and 0 makes the initial processed amount zero. The health calculation then applies any head, limb, or stun-dependent adjustments, so it is not a direct multiplier of the final lost health fraction. Collision Stun uses a separate calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.placability
member.summary: Controls how much the allowed melee-contact path lowers the enemy's anger toward a target of the same npcType category.

remarks.para: The melee path requires a supplied processed impulse or contact strength of at least 1 and a collided object whose layer is included in meleeAttackMask. A layer is a Unity object category, and this mask selects the categories allowed for this melee path. The subsequent anger adjustment follows the damage-delivery attempt and its landing sound; it does not require proof that the other object received damage.

BehaviourBaseNav.DealMeleeDamage moves live aggression toward 0 by 0.1 × placability after its qualifying contact path, when its current target and self have exactly matching npcType values. Aggression is the live anger number normally between 0 and 1; placability is a multiplier with no physical unit. For aggression = 0.7 and placability = 2, one such adjustment lowers aggression to 0.5.

A value of 0 stops this particular reduction. The reduction is a fixed step per qualifying contact, not a percentage of the damage actually received by the other object. It does not calm every kind of attack or every target category.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.stabMult
member.summary: Scales the incoming damage points of Slicing and Stabbing attacks before the body-region damage rules.

remarks.para: This multiplier has no physical units: 1 preserves the incoming amount, 0.5 halves it, 2 doubles it, and 0 makes the initial processed amount zero. The health calculation then applies any head, limb, or stun-dependent adjustments, so it is not a direct multiplier of the final lost health fraction. Collision Stun uses a separate calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.stunActive
member.summary: Allows UpdateStun to advance the stored stun counters toward full recovery.

remarks.para: Stun and TakeDamage set this true before their rejection checks, so true does not prove an accepted hit or complete incapacitation. UpdateStun clears it when all five counters are at least 1. Initiate, Kill, and Resurrect also clear it.

Setting it false stops UpdateStun from changing counters; it does not reset those counters or stop UpdateMuscleStates from using their current values. If you lower a counter directly and expect normal recovery updates, the recovery flag must also allow those updates.
Edited values above 1 also satisfy that completion test. For example, if every counter is 1.2 and the recovery rate is 0, UpdateStun can clear this flag without changing those values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.stunRecovery
member.summary: Sets how quickly depressed stun counters climb back toward 1, restoring the enemy's physical control.

remarks.para: The value is counter units per scaled game second. Each active recovery update advances a counter by stunRecovery × deltaTime, where deltaTime is the game seconds elapsed since the previous frame. A counter at 0 with stunRecovery = 2 nominally reaches 1 in 0.5 game seconds if no new hit interrupts it. At 0 this rate provides no recovery increment.

Hits can push a counter as low as -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery), where maxStunSeconds is the configured number of game seconds for the below-zero part of recovery. Raising this rate speeds the climb from a particular counter value but also makes that lowest value more negative. From the lowest value, full recovery nominally takes maxStunSeconds + 1 / stunRecovery game seconds for a positive rate, before frame timing and later hits are considered.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.stun_arm_lf
member.summary: Tracks how much stun recovery remains before the left arm regains its calculated pose-driving strength.

remarks.para: Pose-driving strength means how strongly a simulated body part tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation. Usage is a unitless multiplier applied to the calculated strength: 1 preserves it, 0.5 halves it, and 0 removes that strength contribution.

This is a counter with no physical unit, not seconds: 1 is fully recovered. Hits reduce it; UpdateStun raises it toward 1 while stunActive is true. Values below 0 keep its stun contribution at 0 until enough recovery updates occur. A value of 0.5 supplies half of this limb's stun factor before other factors are combined.

Physical strength also depends on the spine stun factor, this limb's health fraction, and its usage multiplier. The combined health/stun strength has a 0.02 minimum before usage is applied. For positive stunRecovery, the lowest requested counter is -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery): the first setting is the below-zero interval in game seconds and the second is counter units regained per game second. Initiate, Resurrect, and Kill reset this counter to 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.stun_spine
member.summary: Tracks the shared torso recovery counter that also limits arm and leg pose-driving strength.

remarks.para: A physical muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Pose-driving strength means how strongly a simulated body part tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation. Usage is a unitless multiplier applied to the calculated strength: 1 preserves it, 0.5 halves it, and 0 removes that strength contribution.

This is a number with no physical unit, not seconds: 1 is fully recovered. Both spine and head hits reduce it, and UpdateStun raises it toward 1 while stunActive is true. A normal value of 0.5 halves the spine stun factor and contributes that same factor to each limb's health/stun calculation.

Below 0 the clamped factor is 0. The first physical muscle can receive zero strength, while other mapped spine, head, and limb muscles retain a 0.02 calculated floor before their usage multipliers. For positive stunRecovery, hits move toward -(maxStunSeconds × stunRecovery), where maxStunSeconds is the configured below-zero interval in game seconds and stunRecovery is counter units regained per game second. Initiate, Resurrect, and Kill reset it to 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.usage_arm_lf
member.summary: Scales the pose-driving strength assigned to the left arm; stores this multiplier.

remarks.para: Pose-driving strength means how strongly a simulated body part tries to follow its intended animated position and rotation.

This is a multiplier with no physical unit. A stun counter of 1 means recovered and 0 or below contributes a zero stun factor; a limb health fraction of 1 is full and 0 depleted. A value of 1 keeps the health/stun-based strength, 0.5 halves it, and 0 makes the final strength zero. It does not measure the force or weight currently supported by this body region. UpdateMuscleStates multiplies the spine and matching limb stun factors, each limited to 0 through 1, by that limb's health fraction; limits the result to 0.02 through 1; then multiplies by this value.

SetUsage stores these values, and UpdateMuscleStates later applies them to the physical-muscle strength settings. A direct field edit likewise needs that later update before it affects strength. Stored values are not limited to 0 through 1 by SetUsage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.SubBehaviourHealth.vengefulness
member.summary: Scales how strongly qualifying received damage raises BehaviourPowerLegs' anger toward an attacker of the same npcType category.

remarks.para: This PowerLegs adjustment requires the enemy to survive the hit and the health calculation to return positive processed damage. Blunt hits, the attack category for blunt contact, on physical Hand or Foot muscle groups are excluded. An attack proxy is the scene object identifying the attacker; it must exist and have exactly the enemy’s npcType category for this anger increase.

In that behavior's surviving-hit reaction, live aggression moves toward 1 by (processed damage / maxHitPoints) × vengefulness, when the attack identifies a proxy with exactly the same npcType value as the enemy. Processed damage is the damage amount returned by the health calculation after its reductions; maxHitPoints is the overall-health damage-point scale; vengefulness is a multiplier with no physical unit. Aggression is the live anger number normally between 0 and 1.

For 10 processed damage, maxHitPoints = 100, and vengefulness = 2, the increase is 0.20, stopping at 1. A value of 0 stops this particular anger increase. The attacker is added to the threat system separately, so this value is not a duration or strength of last-attacker fixation. Other enemy behaviors can have different damage-reaction rules.
BaseEnemyConfig.ApplyTo can overwrite this live setting with its configuration value. Editing this field does not by itself reset health, run a damage reaction, or change the enemy's decision state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug.IsAttached
member.summary: Whether this plug currently has an attached socket.

remarks.para: Plug attachment is separate from socket binding: this can be true while IsBound is either true or false. During Attach, the plug sets this flag true and stores _attachedSocket before notifying the socket and then its registered IPlugable components, so those listeners see IsAttached true. During an unbound Detach, the plug clears the flag before notifying its listeners and the socket.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug.IsBound
member.summary: Whether the attached socket has put this plug into its bound state.

remarks.para: Binding is an extra state after attachment. A socket's Bind flow sets this property and disables interaction through the plug's _host; its Unbind flow clears the property and restores host interaction. While bound, Detach does nothing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug.Tags
member.summary: The plug's tag list for the tag checks in a socket's compatibility query; this property implements .

remarks.para: This implements ITaggable and returns the saved _interfaceTags list. It supplies the tag checks in a socket's MarrowQuery, the socket's compatibility rules. If the queried object has a Poolee component (which marks an object kept for reuse by a pool, a system that stores objects for reuse) and the query has crate rules, it can also check that object's crate. The query combines tag and crate results with And (both must match) or Or (either can match). Tags contribute to compatibility but do not attach the plug by themselves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._attachedSocket
member.summary: The selected for the current attachment, or null when there is no current attachment.

remarks.para: The plug stores the selected socket as attachment begins. During detachment it keeps this reference while it notifies registered plugables and the socket, then clears it. The separate _sockets list holds nearby candidate sockets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._host
member.summary: The that reports this plug's hand-grab state and controls its interaction.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost manages interaction for a physical object and reports the state of its hand grips. Awake is Unity's initialization callback for this component; the plug subscribes there to the host's hand-attached notification. That notification reports that a hand has attached to a grip, and the plug's handler enables the component and calls Detach. During candidate validation, the plug checks the host's attached-grip state only for the candidate equal to _lastDetachedSocket, the remembered socket it last detached from. If the host reports any attached grip, that candidate is skipped. Other candidates go directly to the distance-cutoff check without this host check. When a plug attaches, it force-detaches attached hands before creating the physics joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._interfaceTags
member.summary: The saved tag list returned by for a socket's tag-rule checks.

remarks.para: A tag is a label used to describe compatibility. Unity saves this TagList with the plug's scene object or reusable object template. It supplies labels for the tag rules in a socket's MarrowQuery, its compatibility rules. If the plug object has a Poolee component (which marks an object kept for reuse by a pool, a system that stores objects for reuse) and the query has crate rules, the query can also check the object's crate and combine that result with the tag result using And (both required) or Or (either). These checks determine whether a socket tracks the plug as a candidate; this list alone does not attach it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._joint
member.summary: The component created to connect the plug's body to the selected socket's body.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection between two simulated bodies. On attachment, the plug creates a MarrowJoint on its body object and configures it with that body's MarrowBody and the socket's Body. DestroyJoint and Detach ask Unity to destroy this component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._lastDetachedSocket
member.summary: The last this plug detached from, or null if no socket is remembered.

remarks.para: When the plug enters the socket's tracked area, the socket's entry handler checks this reference before waking the plug to search for a connection. This is a temporary re-entry reference, not the currently attached socket.

During FixedUpdate, Unity's routine for physics updates, Validate checks the candidate sockets. It can clear this reference only while checking that same remembered socket, and only when the squared distance between the plug's and socket's world positions is strictly greater than _maxAttachDistSqr. Squared distance adds the squared position differences along the three axes of Unity's shared scene coordinates. The default threshold is approximately 0.0144 world-coordinate units squared, equivalent to a distance of about 0.12 world-coordinate units. Equality does not clear the reference. Scene scale determines those units' physical size; the code does not guarantee a conversion to meters.

The direct-hover handler Plug.OnSocketHoverExit also clears this reference after removing its supplied socket from the candidate list. The separate Socket.OnZoneTrackerExit handler performs cleanup within its own routine when the plug leaves the socket's tracked area; it does not call that direct-hover handler. This area-exit cleanup clears the reference only when the socket's tag-rule list is nonempty, its compatibility query still accepts the plug, the socket is unattached, and it still tracks this plug. It removes the candidate, clears this reference, disables the plug if no candidates remain, and then clears the socket's tracked-plug reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._maxAttachDistSqr
member.summary: The larger squared world-distance threshold used to forget the last detached socket.

remarks.para: The default is approximately 0.0144 world-coordinate units squared, whose square root is about 0.12 world-coordinate units. A world-coordinate unit is one unit in Unity's shared scene coordinates; scene scale determines its physical size, so the code does not guarantee a conversion to meters. Validate compares the squared distance between the plug's and socket's world positions with this threshold and clears _lastDetachedSocket only when checking that same remembered socket and the distance is strictly greater. This is not the ordinary attach cutoff.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._minAttachDistSqr
member.summary: The squared world-distance cutoff for choosing a socket to attach to.

remarks.para: The default is approximately 0.0064 world-coordinate units squared, equivalent to a distance of about 0.08 world-coordinate units. These are positions in Unity's shared scene coordinates; scene scale determines how those units map to physical distance, so the code does not guarantee a conversion to meters. During FixedUpdate, Unity's routine for physics updates, Validate measures the distance from the plug's world position to each candidate socket's world position and chooses the nearest eligible candidate at or below this cutoff. Only the candidate equal to _lastDetachedSocket, the remembered socket it last detached from, is skipped if the host reports a hand attached to one of its grips. Other candidates go directly to the distance comparison without that host check. Squared distance adds the squared differences along the three world-coordinate axes, so the stored value is a squared distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._plugables
member.summary: The registered listeners that receive this plug's socket-attachment callbacks.

remarks.para: A registered IPlugable object is a listener that receives OnSocketAttached(Socket) and OnSocketDetached(Socket). A callback is a routine the plug calls to report an attachment change so other code can respond. Register adds a listener only if it is not already in the list; Unregister removes it. During attachment, the plug notifies the socket first, then calls each listener's attached callback before aligning the bodies or creating the joint. During detachment, it clears IsAttached, calls each listener's detached callback before notifying the socket, and keeps _attachedSocket set through both notification steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug._sockets
member.summary: The sockets this plug currently tracks as attachment candidates; a candidate is not necessarily tag-checked or attached.

remarks.para: When the plug enters a socket’s tracked area, Socket.OnZoneTrackerEnter adds it only when the tag-rule list is nonempty, its MarrowQuery accepts this plug, the socket is unattached, and it is not already tracking another plug. The plug’s own OnSocketHoverEnter handler can also add the supplied socket directly, without repeating those query checks. When the plug leaves the tracked area, Socket.OnZoneTrackerExit performs the cleanup inline; it does not call Plug.OnSocketHoverExit. It removes the socket from this list, clears _lastDetachedSocket, disables the plug when no candidates remain, and clears the socket’s _plugInSocket reference. That area-exit removal occurs only when the socket’s tag-rule list is nonempty, its query still accepts the plug, the socket is unattached, and it still tracks this plug. Plug.OnSocketHoverExit is a separate direct-hover handler with similar candidate and last-detached cleanup. While this list is nonempty, FixedUpdate checks candidates; it does not represent every socket in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.IsAttached
member.summary: Whether this socket marks a plug as attached.

remarks.para: This true/false value belongs to the socket and is separate from Plug.IsAttached and Socket.IsBound. A physics joint is the connector that holds the plug and socket bodies together in the physics simulation. The socket sets this value true before onPlugAttached and clears it before onPlugDetached; the attach callback runs before the plug finishes positioning itself and creating its physics joint.

During Plug.Detach, Plug.IsAttached is cleared and Unity Destroy is requested for the stored joint before Socket.OnPlugDetached clears this flag. It can therefore remain true during the earlier part of the plug detach path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.IsBound
member.summary: Whether the attached plug is bound, with its normal interaction disabled.

remarks.para: A plug can be attached but unbound. Unbind clears this state while leaving IsAttached true, so the plug can then be detached.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.onPlugAttached
member.summary: Callback raised when a starts attaching to this socket.

remarks.para: The callback receives the plug. At this point IsAttached is already true, and registered listeners implementing ISocketable have already received this plug attach notice; those listeners also receive plug detach notices. It runs before the plug finishes creating its physics joint and before an armed auto-bind request is applied. A physics joint is the connector that holds the plug and socket bodies together in the physics simulation.
A callback is a routine the game calls when an action happens; this one reports the plug being attached.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.onPlugBound
member.summary: Callback raised after a plug is bound to this socket.

remarks.para: The callback receives the plug after both bound flags are true and the plug's normal interaction has been disabled. Binding leaves the plug attached.
A callback is a routine the game invokes to report an action; this one reports that the plug was bound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.onPlugDetached
member.summary: Callback raised after the attached plug has detached from this socket.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the game invokes to report an action. Plug.Detach first asks Unity to destroy its stored physics joint, the connector that holds the plug and socket bodies together in the physics simulation. That destroy request does not mean Unity has removed the joint when this callback runs. The socket then clears IsAttached, notifies registered listeners implementing ISocketable (the interface for receiving plug attach and detach notices), and invokes this callback with the plug.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket.onPlugUnbound
member.summary: Callback raised after a bound plug is released but remains attached.

remarks.para: The callback receives the plug after both bound flags are false. IsAttached remains true, so code can call Detach afterward if it wants to remove the plug.
A callback is a routine the game invokes to report an action; this one reports that the plug was unbound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.JumpCurve
member.summary: Controls how the jump sequence tucks and extends the feet pose and changes the extra spine-crouch control.

remarks.para: The horizontal curve axis is jump progress: cycleTime / predictedFlightTime. Both named times are in seconds, so progress has no unit. The cycle clock is reset when push-off is detected; 0.5 is half the predicted duration and 1 is the full predicted duration. The sequence can continue past 1.

The vertical curve axis is a unitless pose amount. It is multiplied by avatar height measurements to make the feet-offset target in metres. It also produces a spine-control target of -0.35 × curveValue, where curveValue is the sampled vertical value. This does not directly set the torso's upward velocity.

The constructor creates keys at (0, 0), (0.3, -0.8), (0.5, -1), (0.75, -0.8), and (1.3, 0). This gives a tucked pose near the middle and recovery later. These are constructor defaults; a saved rig can provide a different curve. Stage 2 ends only when progress is greater than 1.3.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._accelDuckRetainer
member.summary: Stores the smoothed movement-dependent control that adjusts the support point and feet vertically.

remarks.para: The early update rebuilds its target from horizontal movement speed and the saved movement-acceleration magnitude, weighted and divided by the avatar's standing pelvis height. This produces an internal pose control rather than a stored acceleration in metres per second squared.

The control eases toward the target with a shorter smoothing time when increasing (0.1 seconds) and a longer one when decreasing (0.24 seconds). These are response settings, not promises that the target is reached after exactly that many seconds.

The center of pressure is the body's support reference point. This correction changes each object's Y position relative to its parent, along that parent's up axis; one local distance unit maps to one metre in world space when the parent hierarchy has scale 1. It contributes to the local vertical correction of the center of pressure and both feet. Holding the other terms fixed, its contribution is +0.01 × pelvisHeight × heightFraction × control, in metres. Here pelvisHeight is the avatar's standing pelvis height in metres, heightFraction is (pelvisAboveRoot + feetOffset) / pelvisHeight, limited to 0 through 1, and control is this stored value. Here pelvisAboveRoot is the current pelvis height above the rig root projected along the rig's up direction, and feetOffset is the current vertical feet correction. Both are distances in metres, so heightFraction is unitless. It is updated every early update; it is not saved crouching acceleration later restored on standing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._accelDuckVelocity
member.summary: Stores the rate of change used to smooth the movement-dependent vertical pose control.

remarks.para: The early update passes this by reference to the smoother for accelDuckRetainer, so the smoother reads and replaces it on successive updates. It is in internal control units per second, not the rig's movement speed in metres per second.
Changing it changes the next smoothing response of the control that adjusts the support point and feet. It does not directly assign a crouching or jumping body velocity.
