member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._addAdditivePose
member.summary: Stores the extra pose differences calculated from testAdditiveRig and added to the output body pose.

remarks.para: When addWeight is positive, the early update refreshes the test rig, makes an avatar-based neutral reference, and calculates how the test rig differs from that reference. Rotations become changes from neutral, and the pose's position and extension values become differences rather than a second complete standing body.

The head, torso, hand, and leg orientations are expressed relative to the rig root, the parent object representing the body as a whole. Upper-arm orientations are relative to the chest. The rotations are quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Arm and leg extension values are unitless ratios, rather than bone lengths in metres.

These differences are added to the main pose using the individual body-part factors in addWeights. A zero factor ignores that part and a factor of 1 takes its full difference. The addWeight value only enables this calculation when positive; it is not an overall multiplier.
This is a working pose rebuilt on enabled updates. Writing a custom value here does not make it a lasting extra animation, because the next enabled update replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._addSubtractivePose
member.summary: Stores the neutral reference subtracted from testAdditiveRig when making its extra pose contribution.

remarks.para: When addWeight is positive, the neutral-pose generator receives a unitless head-height control and multiplies it by the avatar's stored skull-height measurement, in metres, when calculating its body-height control.

The head, torso, hand, and leg orientations are expressed relative to the rig root, the parent object representing the body as a whole. Upper-arm orientations are relative to the chest. The rotations are quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Arm and leg extension values are unitless ratios, rather than bone lengths in metres.

The test rig's rotations and pose values are compared with this reference to form the extra differences added to the main body pose. Subtracting the neutral reference prevents a second neutral standing pose from being added on top of the first.
This reference is regenerated on each enabled update. It is not a separate subtractive layer that directly removes a pose from the final body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._addWeights
member.summary: Controls how strongly each body part takes the extra pose differences from testAdditiveRig.

remarks.para: These factors are read only when addWeight is positive and the extra pose layer is processed. addWeight acts as an on/off gate here; its positive numeric size does not multiply these factors.

Each factor controls one contribution: 0 ignores its pose difference and 1 takes the full difference. Intermediate factors take a partial contribution. The blend does not clamp these factors, so negative values or values above 1 can reverse or exaggerate differences.

For example, a hand factor of 0 removes that side's hand/arm rotation and arm-extension contribution; 1 keeps its full contribution. Feet factors also scale that side's leg-extension contribution. Position factors affect position differences, while rotation factors affect changes of orientation. A rotation is stored as a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation.

The constructor starts these factors at zero, which ignores the extra differences until they are configured. A saved rig can override those defaults. They are read during each enabled update, rather than copied once by SetAvatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._artificialDelta
member.summary: Stores a two-number vector whose effect on this rig's movement was not verified.

remarks.para: The complete inspected RemapRig methods do not read or update this field. Its name alone does not establish a per-frame artificial movement displacement. Do not rely on it to control that behavior or to report a value kept current by this rig.

No unit, coordinate frame, or refresh timing was established for this stored value. This finding is limited to RemapRig's inspected native methods; other game classes or code added by a mod were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._basePose
member.summary: Stores the avatar-based pose after the enabled input and extra-rig differences have been added.

remarks.para: Each early update first rebuilds a neutral pose from the avatar's stored dimensions. The neutral-pose generator receives a unitless head-height control and multiplies it by the avatar's stored skull-height measurement, in metres, when calculating its body-height control. If their gates are enabled, it then adds the controller's differences from neutral and the test rig's differences from neutral using their separate body-part factors.

The head, torso, hand, and leg orientations are expressed relative to the rig root, the parent object representing the body as a whole. Upper-arm orientations are relative to the chest. The rotations are quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Arm and leg extension values are unitless ratios, rather than bone lengths in metres.

The combined rotations and extension values are copied into this rig's output body pose. The rest of the output begins as a copy of the controller body pose. This stored pose therefore contains the combined result during the update, rather than remaining an unmodified avatar base.

It is regenerated each early update. Its rotations describe orientation, its extension values are ratios, and its normalized position values are pose controls rather than a collection of world-space bone positions in metres.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._baseWeights
member.summary: Stores a set of base-pose factors for which no effect was found in RemapRig's native methods.

remarks.para: The constructor creates this set with all factors equal to 1. However, the complete inspected RemapRig methods do not read it when building the output pose. The input and extra-rig layers use their own factor sets.
Setting this field to zero is therefore not a verified way to disable the base pose. This finding covers the inspected RemapRig methods, not every other game class or code added by a mod.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._crouchSpeedLimit
member.summary: Multiplies the requested movement speed according to the physics body's current pelvis-height ratio.

remarks.para: This is a unitless factor, normally from 0 to 1, not a speed in metres per second. A value of 0.5 halves the speed target before the other movement factors are applied; the actual velocity still eases toward the target.

The movement update recalculates its target from how far the physics pelvis-height ratio is from 1. That ratio is (pelvisY - feetBodyY + supportRadius) / standingPelvisHeight. Here pelvisY is the physical pelvis body's world-Y height, feetBodyY is the feet body's world-Y height, supportRadius is the foot-support sphere's radius, and standingPelvisHeight is the avatar's stored standing pelvis height. All four distances are in metres, so the ratio is unitless. It limits that height difference to a 0-to-1 penalty and subtracts the penalty from 1. A decrease in the stored factor is eased using the update duration and foot-support score; an increase can be immediate.
Because the update replaces this value, assigning a speed cap here does not establish a persistent maximum speed setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._crouchTarget
member.summary: Stores the feet-height target that crouch and recovery calculations move toward.

remarks.para: The target is in metres and is an offset control, not an absolute pelvis height or a 0-to-1 crouch percentage. Crouch calculations build it from the avatar's stored heights and the current neck height above the support point, measured along the rig's up direction.

The feetOffset value eases toward this target using crouchVelocity as the saved rate of change. Jump preparation also reads the target when lowering the pose. Jump starts and later crouch or recovery updates can replace it, so it is a working state value rather than a fixed crouch-height setting.
The support point mentioned here is the center of pressure, the physics body's reference point for support through the ground.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._crouchVelocity
member.summary: Stores the rate of change that the feet-height smoother carries between updates.

remarks.para: It is the smoother's reference value for feetOffset and is measured in metres per second. Crouch, jump-preparation, and ordinary recovery paths read and update it so the feet control changes smoothly.
Starting Jump clears this value before preparing the next pose. It is a smoothing state, rather than a reading of how quickly the physical pelvis or feet are actually moving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._currentAcceleration
member.summary: Stores the horizontal movement rate of change returned by .

remarks.para: Its two components are world X and world Z, in metres per second squared. The second component is not upward acceleration.

The movement update copies the velocity smoother's saved rate of change here, using its full value for ordinary movement or 0.3 of it when consuming a virtual-controller request. This is a reported movement-control value, not a force or a measured physics acceleration.
A seated early update clears it. Teleport clears it only when zeroVelocity is true. The next movement calculation can replace a value written here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._currentVelocity
member.summary: Stores the horizontal movement velocity integrated by the rig and returned by .

remarks.para: This two-number vector uses x for world X and y for world Z, in metres per second. For example, (0, 3) contributes 0.06 metres toward positive world Z during a 0.02-second update.

The movement calculation eases this value toward the target formed from movement input, navigation travel, and any consumed virtual-controller correction. The early update adds velocity multiplied by frame duration to the rig root's world X and Z position.
This excludes vertical movement and does not report a physical body part's velocity. A seated early update clears it, as does Teleport with zeroVelocity true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._dirVel
member.summary: Scales the requested movement speed according to the controller input's forward or backward direction.

remarks.para: The horizontal curve axis is the forward component of the normalized two-number movement input. Normalized means its direction has length 1: -1 is backward, 0 is sideways, and 1 is forward. Diagonal input falls between these values. This axis is in the controller movement frame before it is turned into world-space movement.

The vertical curve axis is a unitless speed multiplier. For example, a value of 0.6 at -1 requests 60 percent of the otherwise calculated backward speed. The result is also multiplied by the avatar-based maximum speed, the crouch-speed factor, and other movement modifiers.

The curve is sampled only for nonzero controller movement input. With no such input, the multiplier remains 1, including when the navigation agent supplies movement. It shapes the target speed; it does not instantly set the current velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._effectiveAcceleration
member.summary: Stores the rate of change retained by the horizontal velocity smoother between movement updates.

remarks.para: The smoother receives this two-number vector by reference while easing currentVelocity toward its target. Since the smoothed quantity is velocity in metres per second, this saved rate of change is in metres per second squared. The components follow world X and world Z.

The movement update copies this into the reported currentAcceleration cache, or copies 0.3 of it when consuming a virtual-controller request. It is internal smoothing state, not a separately applied physics force.
Teleport with zeroVelocity clears currentVelocity and currentAcceleration but leaves this value intact. As a result, that option does not fully reset the movement smoother's state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._feetOffset
member.summary: Stores the metre-valued height control adjusted by crouch, jump preparation, jumping, and ordinary recovery.

remarks.para: The center of pressure is the body's support reference point. This local correction changes each object's Y position relative to its parent, along that parent's up axis; one local distance unit maps to one metre in world space when the parent hierarchy has scale 1. The early update uses changes in this value to adjust the rig root's vertical position, scaled by foot support. It also subtracts this value when building the local vertical correction added to the center of pressure and both feet.

For example, with the other correction terms held fixed, increasing feetOffset by 0.1 contributes an additional -0.1 metres to that local correction. This is a procedural pose control, not an absolute world-space foot height.

Crouch and preparation paths smooth it toward a target; the later jump stages move it toward curve-driven targets with a maximum step based on the update duration. The selected path can replace it each early update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._inAdditivePose
member.summary: Stores the controller body pose's differences from its avatar-based neutral reference.

remarks.para: When inWeight is positive, the early update compares the controller body pose with a freshly generated neutral pose. The differences contain changes in orientation, extension, and pose position rather than another complete standing body.

The head, torso, hand, and leg orientations are expressed relative to the rig root, the parent object representing the body as a whole. Upper-arm orientations are relative to the chest. The rotations are quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Arm and leg extension values are unitless ratios, rather than bone lengths in metres.
The differences are added to the main pose using inWeights for individual body parts. This lets a zero hand factor ignore that side's arm-and-hand contribution while other parts still contribute.

This is rebuilt on each enabled update. inWeight is only tested for being positive; it does not scale the differences itself. A value written into this working pose can be replaced on the next enabled update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._inBasePose
member.summary: Stores the neutral avatar pose used as the reference for extracting controller pose changes.

remarks.para: When inWeight is positive, this reference is generated from the avatar's stored body measurements. The neutral-pose generator receives a unitless head-height control and multiplies it by the avatar's stored skull-height measurement, in metres, when calculating its body-height control.

The head, torso, hand, and leg orientations are expressed relative to the rig root, the parent object representing the body as a whole. Upper-arm orientations are relative to the chest. The rotations are quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of orientation. Arm and leg extension values are unitless ratios, rather than bone lengths in metres.

The controller pose is compared with this reference to form the input differences. Removing the neutral part avoids adding a second standing body pose when those differences are added to the main pose.
This is regenerated on each enabled update. It is not a saved copy of the controller's full pose from before blending.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._inWeights
member.summary: Controls how strongly individual body parts take the controller's changes from the neutral pose.

remarks.para: These factors are read when inWeight is positive. A positive inWeight enables the input-difference layer; changing it from 0.25 to 1 does not change that layer's strength by itself.

Each factor controls one contribution: 0 ignores its pose difference and 1 takes the full difference. Intermediate factors take a partial contribution. The blend does not clamp these factors, so negative values or values above 1 can reverse or exaggerate differences.

For example, a hand factor of 0 removes that side's hand/arm rotation and arm-extension contribution; 1 keeps its full contribution. Feet factors also scale that side's leg-extension contribution. Position factors affect position differences, while rotation factors affect changes of orientation. A rotation is stored as a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation.
The constructor starts these factors at 1. A saved rig can configure different values, and the enabled update reads the current factors each time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._jumpCycle
member.summary: Stores the jump sequence's running clock, which supplies progress to .

remarks.para: Jumping adds the update duration in seconds on each call. Jump may initialize the clock below zero from the current preparation pose, so it is not always a simple time-since-Jump counter.

When leaving support is detected and upward speed passes the required threshold, the clock resets to zero. Later stages sample the curve at cycleTime / predictedFlightTime, where both values are seconds; the resulting progress is unitless.
The stage-1-to-stage-2 transition does not reset this clock. JumpEnd clears the active flag but leaves the saved clock value in place.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._jumpStage
member.summary: Selects which feet-and-spine control step runs during the jump sequence.

remarks.para: Stage 0 is push-off: it extends the feet control and waits for the physics rig's leaving-support report plus enough upward speed. Stage 1 is the first curve-driven airborne pose. Stage 2 is the later curve-driven recovery pose.

Jump selects stage 0. A successful push-off selects stage 1 and resets the cycle clock; stage 1 selects stage 2 after the clock exceeds half the predicted flight duration. Stage 2 ends after progress exceeds 1.3. Here progress = cycleTime / predictedDuration: cycleTime is the running cycle clock in seconds and predictedDuration is the saved predicted flight duration in seconds, making progress unitless.
Charging is handled by a separate preparation method, rather than being a numbered stage here. Stage 2 does not prove the body has landed, and JumpEnd does not reset this saved stage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._jumping
member.summary: Indicates that the jump-pose sequence is active.

remarks.para: Jump sets it to true after invoking the jump event. JumpEnd clears it, and active crouch or jump-preparation processing can clear it too.

The early update uses this flag to choose jump processing. It is a control-state flag, not a ground-contact test: it can become true before the player leaves support, and becoming false does not prove a landing. Setting it alone does not initialize the other jump controls that Jump prepares.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._lastPelvisHeight
member.summary: Stores the previous early update's pelvis height above the support point for crouch-target recovery.

remarks.para: The height is in metres along the rig's up direction. It is the projection of the world-space pelvis-to-center-of-pressure difference onto that up direction; the center of pressure is the body's support reference point.

During ordinary crouch recovery, the early update subtracts this saved height from the current height and divides the difference by the update duration in seconds. The result is the pelvis's vertical movement rate in metres per second, which helps choose how quickly the crouch target returns toward standing. The previous height remains available for that calculation until the update overwrites it with the current height after choosing its crouch or jump control path. This is a recovery input, rather than a landing check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._lfCurlLerp
member.summary: Stores the smoothed left-controller squeeze used to estimate the left hand's clearance from the body.

remarks.para: The value is normally 0 for a released grip and 1 for a full squeeze. It is a unitless squeeze control, rather than a bending weight for the whole limb or a force measured in newtons.

Each early update moves it toward the controller's reported squeeze by a fraction limited to 0 through 1: frameSeconds × smoothingRate. Here frameSeconds is the update duration in seconds and smoothingRate is 20 per second, so their product is a unitless blend fraction. For example, a 0.01-second update moves it 20 percent of the remaining difference toward the new squeeze. The blend fraction is limited; the reported squeeze itself is not clamped here.

The updated value is passed to the avatar's hand-bounds calculation, which estimates the space the hand occupies. Its squeeze-dependent extent then affects hand and torso clearance adjustments. Changing this value can affect those adjustments until the next update smooths it again.

member.summary: Provides navigation travel input and receives the rig's avatar-based navigation settings.

remarks.para: This is a NavMeshAgent, Unity's component for planning and following a route over walkable navigation surfaces. The rig reads the agent's travel velocity as an input to its horizontal movement calculation.

During the rig's OnAwake initialization method, it disables the agent's automatic position, rotation, and up-axis updates. This is a setup hook: a method run when the rig is being prepared for use. The remap rig then controls its own transform, the component storing an object's position, rotation, and scale.

SetAvatar configures the agent's body size, speed, and acceleration. During ordinary updates, a difference greater than 0.5 metres between the agent's internal next position and its transform position makes the rig request repositioning of the agent to the transform position with Warp. The method ignores Warp's success result, so this call does not guarantee that the agent moved.
The inspected setup and update paths require this reference and do not treat a missing agent as an optional no-op. Provide it before initialization and avatar setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._rotationOffset
member.summary: Stores the pending extra rotation submitted by .

remarks.para: It is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of a rotation. It represents an extra turn to apply, not a destination position or a final world heading.

SetRotate replaces this saved rotation and sets the dirty flag. The after-physics update then rotates the remap, animation, interpolated, and virtual rig roots around the interpolated head's skull reference point. This keeps the extra turn centered on that point.

Writing this field alone does not request application; the dirty flag controls whether the rotation step runs. After application, a separate flag requests later removal of the roots' tilt when no active seat is present.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._rotationOffsetDirty
member.summary: Requests application of the saved extra rotation during the next after-physics update.

remarks.para: SetRotate first makes this request flag true, then stores the supplied quaternion, Unity's representation of a rotation. The after-physics update applies that saved extra turn around the interpolated head's skull reference point to four rig roots: remap, animation, interpolated, and virtual.

After applying the turn, the update clears this flag and sets rotationOffsetWasDirty to request later upright cleanup. True means a turn is pending, not that the current roots already have that rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._rotationOffsetWasDirty
member.summary: Records that the rig roots still need upright cleanup after an extra rotation was applied.

remarks.para: Applying a pending rotation sets this flag. On a later after-physics update with no new pending rotation and no active seat, the rig removes the tilt from the remap, animation, interpolated, and virtual roots, keeps their turn around the vertical axis, and clears this flag.
An active seat delays this cleanup, so the flag can remain true across several updates. It is a pending-work flag rather than simply a record of whether the previous frame was dirty.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._rtCurlLerp
member.summary: Stores the smoothed right-controller squeeze used to estimate the right hand's clearance from the body.

remarks.para: The value is normally 0 for a released grip and 1 for a full squeeze. It is a unitless squeeze control, rather than a bending weight for the whole limb or a force measured in newtons.

Each early update moves it toward the controller's reported squeeze by a fraction limited to 0 through 1: frameSeconds × smoothingRate. Here frameSeconds is the update duration in seconds and smoothingRate is 20 per second, so their product is a unitless blend fraction. For example, a 0.01-second update moves it 20 percent of the remaining difference toward the new squeeze. The blend fraction is limited; the reported squeeze itself is not clamped here.

The updated value is passed to the avatar's hand-bounds calculation, which estimates the space the hand occupies. Its squeeze-dependent extent then affects hand and torso clearance adjustments. Changing this value can affect those adjustments until the next update smooths it again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._smoothTwist
member.summary: Stores the extra degrees queued for the rig's next turn.

remarks.para: SetTwist adds degrees to this value. The rotation step adds it to the controller-supplied angle, turns around the physics support point using the rig's up axis, and clears this value after a nonzero turn.
Despite its name, this field is not itself smoothed or a measured torsion angle. An active seat leaves the queue waiting. A total angle of exactly zero also leaves it unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._spineCrouchOff
member.summary: Stores the extra crouch control eased and forwarded by .

remarks.para: This is a unitless pose-control value, not a world height or a measured displacement of the spine. Crouch and jump processing choose its target, and the helper approaches that target in timed steps before copying the changed value to the animation rig's spineCrouchOffset.

For example, a sampled jump-curve value of -1 requests a control target of 0.35. The saved value need not reach that target in the same frame, because the helper limits how fast it changes. Writing this cache directly does not run the helper's copy to the animation rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._timeOfFlight
member.summary: Stores the predicted jump duration calculated when a successful push-off is detected.

remarks.para: The estimate is in seconds: predictedDuration = 2 × upwardSpeed / gravityStrength. Here upwardSpeed is the torso's world-Y speed minus the ground's world-Y speed, in metres per second; gravityStrength is the negative of Physics.gravity.y, in metres per second squared. The calculation assumes downward world-Y gravity.

For example, upwardSpeed of 3 metres per second and gravityStrength of 10 metres per second squared produce 0.6 seconds. This is a simple up-and-down flight estimate, not a timer of how long the body has actually been airborne.

The later stages divide the cycle clock by this estimate to sample the jump curve and choose timed transitions. Obstacles, moving ground, or other forces can make the physical flight differ from it. The estimate is saved at push-off, rather than recalculated every airborne update, and JumpEnd does not clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._vcActive
member.summary: Marks a virtual-controller movement correction as waiting for the movement calculation.

remarks.para: A virtual controller is the software-adjusted hand target used while interacting with a grabbed object; these corrections help keep that target within the object's movement limits. Either SetVcLocomotionLf or SetVcLocomotionRt sets this flag when it stores a hand correction. The movement calculation reads the pending left and right values, clears their saved corrections and constraint data, and finally clears this flag after consuming the request.

On that calculation, the reported currentAcceleration receives 0.3 of the velocity smoother's saved rate of change. The flag does not mean a hand is currently gripping a controller or that the body has already moved.
If movement processing is skipped, such as by the seated early-update path, the flag can remain true while the correction waits. Setting the flag alone does not provide a new correction vector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._vcLocoDeltaLf
member.summary: Stores the pending world-space hand-target correction supplied by the left virtual-controller movement source.

remarks.para: A virtual controller is a software-adjusted hand target used while interacting with a grabbed object. Its movement limits can require this correction between the old and adjusted hand-target positions. The vector is a correction between world-space hand positions, in metres. Its X and Z components contribute direction and numeric size to the horizontal movement request; the stored Y component is not used for horizontal travel. It is not a measured body velocity or a promise to move the root by exactly this displacement.

The left setter replaces this value and marks a request as pending. It does not accumulate repeated calls. The movement calculation combines the left and right corrections with controller input and their constraints, then clears both saved vectors after reading them.

For example, a stored positive world-X correction contributes toward positive world X, but the actual movement still depends on the movement blend and velocity smoothing. If movement processing is skipped, the stored request can remain waiting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._vcLocoDeltaRt

remarks.para: A virtual controller is a software-adjusted hand target used while interacting with a grabbed object. Its movement limits can require this correction between the old and adjusted hand-target positions. The vector is a correction between world-space hand positions, in metres. It is not a measured body velocity or a promise to move the root by exactly this displacement.

The right setter replaces this value and marks a request as pending. It does not accumulate repeated calls. The movement calculation combines the left and right corrections with controller input and their constraints, then clears both saved vectors after reading them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._vcLocoDofLf
member.summary: Selects whether the left virtual-controller movement can take part in direction-based steering. Set it through .

remarks.para: A virtual controller adjusts the tracked hand to obey a held object's movement limits. This integer describes that adjustment; it does not itself grant movement or configure a physics joint, a connection between simulated objects. The movement solver permits its combined-direction steering branch only when both hands' values are either 1 or -1. Other values skip that branch, while the supplied movement adjustments can still affect locomotion.

The value has no physical units. For example, setting both hands to 1 through their locomotion setters permits their supplied directions to influence the requested horizontal heading, provided movement input is pressed and the summed horizontal adjustment is nonzero. Setting either hand to 2 skips this steering branch.

The setter also marks the controller adjustment as pending. During the next movement solve that consumes it, both hand values are reset to -1 and their directions and adjustments are cleared. Writing this property alone does not mark a new adjustment as pending. -1 is therefore also a cleared-state marker, not a count of negative movement axes.

remarks.para: A virtual controller adjusts the tracked hand to obey a held object's movement limits. This integer describes that adjustment; it does not itself grant movement or configure a physics joint, a connection between simulated objects. The movement solver permits its combined-direction steering branch only when both hands' values are either 1 or -1. Other values skip that branch, while the supplied movement adjustments can still affect locomotion.

The value has no physical units. Setting either hand to 2 skips this steering branch.

The setter also marks the controller adjustment as pending. During the next movement solve that consumes it, both hand values are reset to -1 and their directions and adjustments are cleared. Writing this property alone does not mark a new adjustment as pending. -1 is therefore also a cleared-state marker, not a count of negative movement axes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._vcLocoNormalLf
member.summary: Supplies the left virtual controller's world-space direction for steering the requested horizontal movement.

remarks.para: This is a direction rather than a position or speed, so its components have no distance units. Despite the name, the inspected sliding-controller producer supplies its allowed sliding axis, rotated into world space; treating every value as a surface's outward normal would give the wrong meaning.

When movement input is pressed, the combined controller adjustment has a nonzero world X/Z component, and both hand mode values are 1 or -1, the solver combines the two directions and biases the requested heading toward their horizontal direction. World X/Z means the level's horizontal axes, not the hand's own axes. The right direction can be negated temporarily when it points against the left direction, so opposite axis signs can describe the same sliding line.

Supply this with the matching SetVcLocomotionLf call, which also marks an adjustment as pending. The next movement solve that consumes controller adjustments clears both directions to zero. For example, a world direction (1, 0, 0) describes a line along world X; it does not request a speed of 1 meter per second.

remarks.para: This is a direction rather than a position or speed, so its components have no distance units. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig._velocitySanGravMagRetainer
member.summary: Exposes a stored float that the inspected RemapRig implementation does not update or read as a speed measurement.

remarks.para: The complete methods declared on RemapRig contain no reader or writer for this slot. Its name alone does not establish that it holds a current speed, has had gravity removed, or carries a measurement between frames. Changing it has no demonstrated movement effect in those methods; this conclusion does not cover every possible external caller or subclass.

To inspect this rig's calculated horizontal movement, use GetVelocity instead. That returns world X speed and world Z speed in meters per second. For a returned value (3, 4), horizontal speed is 5 meters per second: square each component, add the squares, then take the square root. This measures the rig's movement calculation rather than proving the physics body actually travels at that speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.addWeight
member.summary: Enables the extra rig's additive pose branch when its value is greater than zero.

remarks.para: An additive pose is a set of changes added to a starting body pose, such as extra hand or torso rotation. In the early pose update, any positive addWeight enables updating testAdditiveRig, finding its changes from the stored reference pose, and adding those changes using _addWeights. Zero and negative values skip this branch.

Although the Inspector offers a 0-to-1 slider, this field is only tested as an on/off gate in that branch. For example, 0.1 and 1 enable the same calculation; 0.1 does not make the contribution ten percent as strong. The per-body-part _addWeights entries supply the strength instead: 0 suppresses a part's additive change and 1 applies its full change.

Set up a valid testAdditiveRig and its per-part weights before enabling the branch. The constructor creates zeroed _addWeights, so enabling addWeight alone does not establish a visible contribution. The field is read on each early pose update, rather than copied once during avatar setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.brakingMult
member.summary: Adjusts how quickly horizontal movement eases toward its requested velocity, especially when slowing or changing direction. This response is separate from .

remarks.para: This is a unitless response multiplier. For normal positive settings, the solver blends a response factor between 1 and this value according to current speed and the direction of the requested velocity change. When a virtual-controller locomotion adjustment is pending, it first doubles this value for that solve.

The selected factor divides the base smoothing time of 0.3 seconds and multiplies the acceleration coefficient passed to the smoothing calculation. For example, when the factor reaches 3, its smoothing time is 0.1 seconds. That describes the calculation's response setting, not a promise that the avatar stops exactly 0.1 seconds later.

The separate drag step removes some velocity before smoothing and does not multiply its removal by brakingMult. This field is read during each movement solve; it changes the calculated velocity response rather than directly setting a physics body's drag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.currentMaxVelocity
member.summary: Exposes a stored float that is not the applied movement-speed limit in the inspected RemapRig methods.

remarks.para: The complete methods declared on RemapRig contain no reader or writer for this slot. They build the requested horizontal velocity directly from maxVelocity and movement modifiers without storing the result here. Do not treat this property as a refreshed readout of the current cap. This inspection does not rule out an external caller or subclass assigning its own meaning to the slot.

For example, changing this property to 10 has no demonstrated effect on the movement calculation in those methods. To change the baseline requested walking speed, change maxVelocity; to read the calculated horizontal velocity in meters per second, use GetVelocity. Physics contacts and other forces can still make actual body speed differ.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.doubleJump
member.summary: Lets request an additional upward boost from the physics rig using .

remarks.para: Jump first passes the jumpEnabled check, fires onPlayerJump, starts its normal jump state, and requests its effort sound. Only afterward, when doubleJump is true, does it ask the physics rig to accept a boost with a one-second cooldown. A successful boost request also triggers the double-jump sound.

The physics rig decides eligibility. Its checked method rejects an unarmed request when foot support is at or below 0.1. With support greater than 0.1, the first unarmed request arms the next boost but returns false; a later armed request is accepted when the cooldown has expired, consumes the armed state, and queues the configured boost strength. Foot support is a unitless measure of support under the feet, not a height in meters.

True therefore enables a request path; it does not guarantee another launch, prove that the player is airborne, or immediately change velocity when assigned. False skips this extra request while leaving the normal Jump behavior available if jumpEnabled is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.doubleJumpPower
member.summary: Sets the nominal impulse budget requested for an accepted extra jump while is enabled.

remarks.para: The physics rig accepts this value as newton-seconds, the unit of impulse: force multiplied by time. An impulse changes a body's momentum; it is not a jump height in meters or a velocity in meters per second. The constructor starts this field at 1000, though saved scene settings can replace that value.

Jump passes the current value only when doubleJump is enabled. If the physics rig accepts the request, it adds the value to a remaining boost budget. When the remaining boost budget is positive, later physics work smooths that budget toward zero with a 0.2-second response setting and applies the removed part upward to the torso Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is Unity's component for an object moved by the physics simulation. Zero or negative remaining budgets are not discharged; the request does not clamp this field to a positive range.

The delivered impulse is also reduced according to the torso's current world-Y upward speed, reaching zero at 10 meters per second or faster. The body's mass and other physics conditions affect the result, so 1000 does not promise a fixed rise or a fixed velocity increase. Changing this property after a boost is accepted does not rewrite the already queued budget.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.dragPerSec
member.summary: Removes a fixed amount of calculated horizontal speed before each movement-smoothing step.

remarks.para: For positive values, this moves the current horizontal velocity toward zero without passing through zero. At normal time scale its units are meters per second of speed removed per second, or meters per second squared. It is not a percentage of speed and is separate from a Rigidbody's drag, the physics component's own resistance to motion.

The maximum speed removed in one solve is dragPerSec × dt × s². Here dt is the movement-step time in seconds, and s is Unity's unitless timeScale, where 1 is normal speed and 0.5 is half speed. For example, dragPerSec = 0.2, dt = 0.02, and s = 1 remove at most 0.004 meters per second in that step. With the same dt and s = 0.5, removal is at most 0.001 meters per second.

After this removal, the solver smooths toward the velocity requested by movement input or navigation, so the final speed need not continue falling. The field is read every movement solve. A negative value can move velocity away from zero; this calculation does not clamp the field to a positive range.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.inWeight
member.summary: Enables the controller pose's additive branch when its value is greater than zero.

remarks.para: This branch finds the controller pose's changes from its stored reference pose and adds them to the base pose using _inWeights. A pose describes the body parts' positions and rotations. The constructor starts inWeight at 1, and the field is tested again on each early pose update.

Although the Inspector offers a 0-to-1 slider, this field is only an on/off gate in the inspected branch. For example, 0.1 and 1 both enable the same branch; 0.1 does not mean ten-percent tracking. The _inWeights entries set contributions for individual body parts, where 0 suppresses an additive change and 1 applies its full change.

Zero or a negative value skips that additive branch. It does not disable every controller update: the method still copies controller pose data and performs its later movement and body calculations. To reduce a particular body part's additive contribution, change its per-part input weight rather than relying on a smaller positive inWeight.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.jumpEnabled
member.summary: Allows to start its jump sequence when true.

remarks.para: Jump tests this first. False makes that call return before firing onPlayerJump, setting its jump state, playing the jump-effort sound, or asking for an extra jump. The constructor starts this field at true; a scene or script can change it.

Assigning false does not itself cancel a jump already in progress. The charge, crouch, and ongoing jump calculations have their own conditions, and this field does not block unrelated physics forces from lifting the player. For example, disabling it before calling Jump suppresses that new request, while disabling it after Jump has started does not undo the existing sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.jumpVelocity
member.summary: Controls the foot-extension rate during the first jump stage and the upward-speed threshold for entering the airborne jump stage.

remarks.para: The value is in meters per second. During initial extension, the rig moves its requested feet offset toward a body-size-based target. Its movement rate blends the torso's world-Y velocity relative to the ground with jumpVelocity, using a blend based on the remaining extension. This changes a position target for the body calculation rather than directly assigning the torso Rigidbody's upward velocity. A Rigidbody is the component that lets Unity simulate an object's physical motion.

The same value sets a separate test: the next jump stage begins only when the physics rig reports becoming ungrounded that frame and relative upward speed is greater than jumpVelocity × 0.25. Relative upward speed here is the torso's world-Y speed minus the supporting ground's world-Y speed, both in meters per second.

For example, jumpVelocity = 5 makes that speed test strictly greater than 1.25 meters per second; exactly 1.25 does not pass. Five is also the constructor's starting value, not a guarantee of a 5-meter-per-second takeoff. The ongoing initial-stage calculation reads this field, so changing it during that stage changes subsequent extension steps and the threshold.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.maxAcceleration
member.summary: Sets the baseline rate coefficient for smoothing calculated horizontal velocity toward its movement target.

remarks.para: Because the smoothed quantity is velocity in meters per second, this coefficient has acceleration units: meters per second squared. The solver reduces it when world-Y gravity is weaker than normal Earth gravity, then scales it by the selected braking response and the animation rig's chest-twist suppression factor. Zero vertical gravity leaves five percent of the baseline; gravity magnitude 9.81 meters per second squared or greater uses the full baseline before those other multipliers.

This scaled value is passed to SmoothDamp, a calculation that eases a changing value toward a target while retaining its rate of change. Its limit constrains the target difference used by that smoothing calculation; it is not a direct clamp of measured physical acceleration. Drag, previous smoothing state, collisions, and other forces can make the body's actual acceleration differ.

SetAvatar overwrites maxAcceleration with seven times the avatar's stored unitless agility rating and configures the navigation agent's acceleration as ten times the resulting value. A navigation agent plans motion over walkable areas. Later movement solves read this field live, but a manual edit does not repeat that agent setup. For an agility rating of 1, avatar setup produces a baseline of 7 meters per second squared.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.maxVelocity
member.summary: Sets the baseline requested horizontal movement speed before jogging, posture, direction, and animation modifiers.

remarks.para: The value is in meters per second. With full movement input and all other speed multipliers equal to 1, Walk uses this value and Jog uses twice this value. For example, maxVelocity = 2 requests 2 meters per second for Walk and 4 meters per second for Jog. The horizontal calculation uses the world X/Z plane; it does not cap all physical motion or vertical jumping.

The requested speed is further multiplied by the crouch-speed factor derived from pelvis height and foot support, the direction-speed curve, and an animation factor. The direction curve takes the input's forward alignment: +1 forward, 0 sideways, and -1 backward, and returns a unitless speed multiplier. The animation factor is 1 minus 0.100000024 times the animation rig's unitless chest-twist suppression value. Input strength and the navigation request also affect the final horizontal velocity.

SetAvatar overwrites this field with twice the avatar's stored unitless speed rating, then sets the navigation agent's speed to twice the resulting maxVelocity. Later movement solves read maxVelocity live, but manually editing it does not repeat navigation-agent setup. Physics constraints, forces, and smoothing mean actual body speed can differ from the requested value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.onPlayerJump
member.summary: Calls subscribed routines at the start of an enabled request, before its jump flags and sounds change.

remarks.para: This Action supplies no arguments. It runs synchronously inside Jump: a subscribed routine, also called a callback, runs immediately when the action is invoked. Jump first checks jumpEnabled, invokes this action if present, then marks itself as jumping, resets the jump stage, calculates the starting crouch target, requests the effort sound, and changes the physics rig's mass-hold flag. The optional extra-jump request comes afterward.

This Jump call has not yet written its new jump flags when the notification begins; listener code can change them. The notification does not prove that the player has left the ground, that an extra boost was accepted, or that a landing will follow. Jump does not perform a grounding check before invoking it. For example, a UI routine can respond to the jump request here without treating it as a takeoff report.
A disabled Jump call returns before this action fires. If a subscribed routine throws an exception, the later steps in that call have not yet run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.physicalTwistAlignEnabled
member.summary: Aligns the rig roots toward the physics pelvis's horizontal facing after physics updates when true.

remarks.para: This correction runs while the player is not in an active seat. It compares the physics pelvis and virtual pelvis facing after removing their tilt, using world up, the level's positive Y direction. It allows an angular gap of 2 + 6 × f degrees, where f is the physics rig's unitless foot-support value clamped from 0 to 1. That permits 2 degrees without foot support and 8 degrees at full support.

If the gap is larger than the allowed angle, the method rotates the remapping, animation, interpolation, and virtual rig roots around the virtual pelvis's world position by the excess angle. A root is the parent transform that moves a whole rig together. For example, a 12-degree gap at full support produces a 4-degree correction, leaving the allowed 8-degree gap.

This path directly changes transforms; it does not configure a twist joint, which would be a physical connection between objects. With no active seat, pelvis-based root-position correction still runs whether this flag is true or false. It is checked in each post-physics update rather than applied once during setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.testAdditiveRig
member.summary: Supplies the extra whose pose changes can be added to the remapped body pose.

remarks.para: A rig groups the transforms and pose data representing a body. When addWeight is greater than zero, the early pose update first calls this rig's own early-update routine, then finds its pose changes relative to the stored additive reference pose and adds them using _addWeights. Those per-part weights determine how much each body part contributes; addWeight itself only enables the branch.

This participates in the running remapping calculation, so it is not limited to a standalone preview. SetAvatar also passes the chosen avatar to this rig when the reference is a valid Unity object. Replacing the reference after avatar setup does not automatically configure the replacement with that avatar.

Before enabling the additive branch, assign a valid rig with pose data and configure its per-part weights. For example, enabling only the hand contributions can add hand pose changes while the torso contributions remain zero. The early update does not silently skip a missing rig when addWeight is positive.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.testGazeTarget
member.summary: Replaces the copied controller gaze data with an aim toward this transform's current world position.

remarks.para: A transform supplies an object's position and orientation. When this target is valid, the early pose update reconstructs the avatar's camera point from the current head pose and the avatar's stored head-to-camera offset. It computes the direction from that point to the target, expresses it in the head's local axes, and stores it in eyeGaze together with the distance in meters.

Head-local X means right, Y means up, and Z means forward from the head. The stored direction is unitless and is reshaped for strongly sideways or backward targets; it is not always the raw normalized target direction. The fourth eyeGaze component stores the target distance. This assignment changes gaze data and does not itself rotate the head transform.

The target position is read again on every early pose update. For example, moving a valid target changes the next gaze calculation without rerunning avatar setup. When no valid target is assigned, this rig copies the controller rig's existing gaze data instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.travState
member.summary: Selects a traversal label; Jog doubles the baseline speed in this rig's movement calculation.

remarks.para: The available labels are Walk, Jog, Run, Jump, Leap, Airborne, HandClimb, QuadClimb, and FootClimb. In the inspected ApplyMovement method, only Jog selects the two-times speed multiplier. The other labels take the same baseline-speed branch before the usual posture, direction, and animation modifiers.

For example, choosing Jog with a baseline maxVelocity of 2 meters per second requests 4 meters per second before those other modifiers. Choosing Run does not select a separate faster multiplier in that method. Setting Jump or Airborne here does not call Jump or establish physical grounding; it only changes the stored enum value unless another caller reacts to it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.vertState
member.summary: Selects a body-posture label that changes the standing-height calculations for crouching and feet placement.

remarks.para: The labels are Stand, Crouch, Kneel, Prone, Supine, SitChair, and SitFloor. Prone means lying face down and Supine means lying face up. They describe posture rather than grounded or airborne motion.

CrouchHold and the early pose update use a special Stand branch that derives standing-height allowances from the avatar's leg and torso dimensions. Other labels use the alternative height calculation. This affects the requested feet/crouch offset; assigning a label does not by itself play a kneeling or lying animation or force the physics body into that pose.

For example, changing Stand to Crouch makes the next eligible crouch/height calculation use the non-standing branch. The complete inspected methods do not provide separate posture-specific branches for every non-Stand label, so SitFloor and Prone should not be assumed to select distinct offset formulas here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.avatar
member.summary: Gets the reference stored by this rig.

remarks.para: An avatar describes a body and its measurements. This getter reads this rig's saved avatar reference directly; it does not look up the manager's current avatar each time.

The base SetAvatar hook does not fill or refresh this reference. A specific rig's setup must do so if it needs this property. Changing the manager's avatar is therefore not, by itself, proof that this base property contains the same object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.bodyPose
member.summary: Gets or replaces the object holding this rig's saved pose data.

remarks.para: Pose data describes a body's arrangement, including rotations of body parts and positions. This property holds the data object, rather than sampling bone transforms whenever it is read. Assigning a new object replaces the stored reference; it does not copy its values into the old object or immediately move bones.

A specific rig decides when it fills or reads that data. For example, OpenControllerRig reads its current pose and its saved previous pose during its regular update, but performs the root correction only when Unity's physics clock has advanced past the time saved by its last correction. That clock counts seconds along scheduled physics updates. It corrects the world position and rotation of the root object carrying the whole rig, records the physics time, then copies the current pose into its previous-pose cache for the next comparison. A cache is saved data reused later; regular updates at the same physics time skip this correction and pose copy. That later work is separate from assigning this property.
The base constructor creates a BodyPose object. Code that keeps a reference to the old object will still have that old object after this property is replaced.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.manager
member.summary: Stores the that schedules this rig and connects it to the other player rigs.

remarks.para: During setup, the manager assigns itself to the controller rig, the rigs in its remapping list, and the physics rig before calling their initialization hooks. Specific rigs can follow this reference to find the other rigs and shared avatar settings.
Assigning this reference yourself only changes which manager the rig can read. It does not add the rig to that manager's update list or call any setup hook.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig.rigWeights
member.summary: Gets or replaces the rig's set of multipliers for combining body pose data.

remarks.para: Weights are unitless numbers that control how much a selected body part or root movement contributes when pose-combining code reads them. The set contains separate values for the head, gaze, hands, shoulders, elbows, chest, pelvis, knees, feet, root position, and root rotation.

For a concrete example, when this set is passed to BodyPose.AddPose, rootPosition = 0 ignores the added root-position change, 0.5 adds half of that change, and 1 adds all of it. In that operation rootRotation controls the added orientation by blending from no rotation toward the added rotation, then combining it with the existing orientation. These are pose contributions, not forces or body mass.

Assigning this property replaces the stored weights object. The setter does not blend a pose or move bones, and it does not limit the numbers to 0–1. A specific rig or an explicit pose-combining call must read the weights for them to affect anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.AvatarCrate
member.summary: Gets or stores the avatar crate reference selected for this manager.

remarks.para: An avatar crate is the packaged avatar asset, and its barcode is its identifier. At startup, an inspector override can select a different crate from the calibration avatar. After a successful asynchronous crate switch, this reference is updated to that request’s crate.

Assigning this property only stores the reference; it does not load or equip the avatar. Use SwapAvatarCrate to request that work. Equipping an existing instance with SwapAvatar also does not update this crate reference, so it can describe a different selection from the currently equipped instance.

Asynchronous loading can pause while the asset loads or a pending avatar change finishes, then continue over later frames. A selected crate reference therefore does not show that its body is already equipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.Cache
member.summary: Provides a lookup cache of RigManager components that have been initialized and not destroyed.

remarks.para: A cache is a saved lookup table, so callers can find a manager without repeatedly searching every scene object. The manager adds itself during Awake, Unity’s one-time component setup call, and removes itself when destroyed.

Disabling a manager does not remove it from this cache. A cached entry therefore does not prove that its rig is enabled or receiving updates. Accessing Cache creates the shared cache if it has not yet been created.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.CalibrationAvatar
member.summary: Gets or stores the fallback avatar used to initialize and recover this player rig.

remarks.para: During Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, the manager prepares this avatar and first binds its stages to it. If the current avatar later lacks the required animation avatar data, the early pass queues this fallback again.

Assigning this property only replaces the stored reference; it does not immediately change the worn avatar or rebind the stages. Supply a working calibration avatar before setup. Its crate identifier is configured separately in calibrationAvatarBarcode.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.ControllerRig
member.summary: Returns the input rig that supplies the player’s head, hand, and movement targets.

remarks.para: A rig is a set of body bones and the code that positions them. This is the same component stored in controllerRig. Input targets describe where the player is trying to move; the physical body can lag behind or be blocked by a wall. The manager runs this stage before the remap stages and physics stage.
The controller stage also updates the pause state used to decide whether later rig work runs. Reading this property does not create or update the component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.HasInitialAvatar
member.summary: Records whether startup selected a valid avatar override different from the calibration avatar’s barcode.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, sets this flag from the startup crate selection before launching its asynchronous load. Asynchronous work can continue over later frames, so true does not mean the avatar has finished loading or become the worn body.

This is a startup-selection flag, not a success notification for every later swap. For example, it can already be true while avatar still points to the calibration body and the requested crate is loading.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.OnPostLateUpdate
member.summary: Runs registered callbacks after the manager’s late rig work has finished.

remarks.para: A callback is a function registered to run when this point is reached. The manager first runs the controller, eligible remap stages, and physical rig’s late updates. It then runs the current avatar’s late update if that avatar’s object is active, followed by these callbacks. No arguments are supplied.

The hook is skipped when the controller reports the rig paused. It can still run when the avatar object is inactive, because only the avatar’s own late update is conditional on that activity. It marks a particular order in the frame; it does not guarantee that arbitrary pose changes will remain valid through later game code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.OnPreAvatarEarlyUpdate
member.summary: Runs registered callbacks before this manager processes its early avatar, teleport, and body-state requests.

remarks.para: A callback is a function registered to run at this point. These callbacks receive no arguments and run at the very start of the early per-frame pass, before the fallback-avatar check and before any pending avatar change is applied.

After the callbacks, the manager applies pending avatar, teleport, and body-state work in that order, then updates the controller and later stages. This hook runs before the controller’s pause check, so it is not automatically skipped merely because later pose updates are paused. For example, a SwapAvatar request made here can be considered during this same early pass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatar
member.summary: Stores the avatar instance currently bound to this rig’s stages; it backs .

remarks.para: A completed avatar-switch pass changes this reference after preparing the candidate, then tells the controller, remap stages, physical rig, seat, and health module about that avatar. A pending SwapAvatar request does not immediately replace it.

Writing this storage field directly skips that preparation and notification. Use SwapAvatar for an existing instance or SwapAvatarCrate for a packaged avatar. For scene setup, the inspector’s Avatar Override selects the crate rather than this read-only avatar display.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatarCache
member.summary: Keeps avatar instances by crate barcode so a later cached crate request can reuse an existing body.

remarks.para: A barcode identifies an avatar crate. With the crate-switch cache option enabled, the manager keeps the instantiated Avatar under that key. Switching away can deactivate that cached avatar’s object while retaining it for a later request.

The cached-request path still awaits the crate’s asset-load operation before looking up the instance, so this table does not guarantee that all loading is skipped. When the manager is destroyed, it cleans up its cached avatars and unloads their crates. Treat the entries as stored instances, not proof that each one is currently active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatarCrate
member.summary: Stores the configured avatar crate selection exposed by .

remarks.para: The inspector presents the startup setting as Avatar Override. Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, saves that selection while first preparing the calibration body. A valid different selection can then start an asynchronous crate request: it begins loading and may pause and continue over later frames while the asset loads or the avatar change finishes.

A successful crate request later stores its crate reference here. Writing this field or AvatarCrate at runtime only changes stored selection; it does not start loading or equip a body. An instance-only SwapAvatar request does not refresh it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatarDirty
member.summary: Marks an avatar-switch attempt that the next early per-frame pass must process.

remarks.para: SwapAvatar stores its candidate and sets this flag. The early pass can also set it when replacing an avatar that lacks required animation data with the calibration fallback. After attempting the switch, the flag is cleared, whether the candidate was accepted or rejected.

The asynchronous crate-switch code waits for this flag to clear, then compares its requested instance with the current avatar to decide success. False therefore means the queued attempt has been processed, not that a particular request succeeded.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatarID
member.summary: Stores the string returned by ; the normal avatar-switch paths do not refresh it.

remarks.para: The manager initializes this string when constructed. Equipping a different avatar through SwapAvatar or SwapAvatarCrate does not update this storage, so do not assume it is the worn avatar’s current crate barcode.
Read avatar for the actual equipped instance. AvatarCrate describes the stored crate selection after a successful crate request, but an instance-only swap can leave that selection unchanged too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._avatarOnDeck
member.summary: Stores the avatar candidate to consider when an avatar-switch attempt is pending.

remarks.para: SwapAvatar writes this reference and sets _avatarDirty. In the next early per-frame pass, the manager checks and tries to bind that candidate. Another request before the pass replaces the candidate rather than adding a second queued swap.

A successful pass can leave this reference stored after clearing the pending flag. Its presence alone therefore does not mean a swap is waiting. The current equipped instance is stored separately in avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._bodyState
member.summary: Stores the body mode already applied to the rig, such as OnFoot or Seated; the public accessor is .

remarks.para: The bodyState getter reads this value. Queuing a different mode changes the pending value first; this field changes only after the manager has notified the controller, remap stages, and physical rig.

In the Ragdoll mode, where the body is allowed to move as a physics body, the manager skips the remap array’s early, fixed, after-fixed, and late pose passes. Writing this storage directly skips the stages’ body-mode notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._bodyStateDirty
member.summary: Marks a body-mode request for the next early per-frame pass.

remarks.para: Assigning bodyState sets this flag when the requested value differs from the currently applied mode. The early pass sends the pending mode and previous mode to the stages, records the new applied value, then clears this flag.
It does not mean the body mode has already changed. For example, requesting Seated can leave bodyState reporting OnFoot until that early pass finishes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._bodyStateOnDeck
member.summary: Stores the body mode waiting to be applied while the pending body-state flag is set.

remarks.para: The bodyState setter writes this when its requested value differs from the currently applied mode. The next early per-frame pass uses it to reconfigure the controller, remap stages, and physical rig.

Assigning the already applied mode does not cancel an older pending request. For example, if the applied mode is OnFoot, assigning Seated and then OnFoot before the early pass leaves Seated pending. This stored value is meaningful as a pending request only while _bodyStateDirty is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared lookup cache containing initialized, undestroyed RigManager components.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s one-time component setup call, adds each manager. Destruction removes it, and an empty shared cache is released. Disabling the manager does not remove its entry.

A cache is a saved lookup table. Use Cache to obtain it, because that property creates the table when needed. An entry tells you the manager is registered, not that it is enabled or currently updating.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._calibrationAvatar
member.summary: Stores the fallback body used during startup and recovery from missing avatar animation data; the public accessor is .

remarks.para: The CalibrationAvatar property accesses this reference. Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, prepares it and initially binds the rig stages to it. The early per-frame pass can queue it again when the current avatar lacks required animation-avatar data.

Changing this stored reference does not immediately equip it or recalibrate the stages. For example, replacing it after startup changes the fallback available to a later recovery attempt, rather than instantly changing the worn body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._fixedRan
member.summary: Tracks whether a completed physics-step update still needs its after-fixed processing.

remarks.para: A physics step is a regular simulation interval, which can occur zero, one, or several times during a rendered frame. The manager sets this flag after running its fixed updates. If another fixed step arrives first, it runs the previous step’s after-fixed work before starting the next step.
The ordinary frame update also runs any outstanding after-fixed work, then clears this flag. This coordinates the two update schedules; it does not prevent all but one physics step from running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._leashJoint1
member.summary: Stores the physics connection created on the chest body for a circular player leash.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with adjustable movement limits. LeashPlayerCircle creates this joint, anchors it at the supplied world position, and limits movement on the horizontal X and Z axes using the supplied maximum radius in meters.

UpdateLeashCircle changes the joint’s horizontal damping, meaning resistance to motion, while adjusting the requested horizontal movement. UnleashPlayer requests destruction of this joint and clears its reference. A stored leash flag alone does not prove this connection still exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._leashJoint2
member.summary: Stores an additional leash joint that the leash cleanup code will remove if present.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits a body’s movement. UnleashPlayer checks this reference as well as the first joint, requests destruction of any live connection here, and clears its reference.

The circular-leash setup creates only _leashJoint1. It does not populate this second reference, so a circular leash does not require two joints. Assigning a reference here does not configure a leash for you.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._leashPositionWorld
member.summary: Stores the circular leash’s center in world-space meters.

remarks.para: A physics joint limits how simulated bodies move. Its world anchor is the fixed point in the level that the connection uses. LeashPlayerCircle copies its supplied center here and installs that center as the joint’s world anchor. The feedback updater compares the chest position with this center on the horizontal X/Z plane; height does not contribute to that feedback distance.

Changing this field later changes the feedback calculation but does not move the anchor already installed on the joint. Recreate the leash with LeashPlayerCircle when moving the physical restriction. For example, (0, 0, 5) places the configured center five meters along the world’s positive Z direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._leashRotationWorld
member.summary: Stores an orientation value for leash configuration; the circular-leash routines do not apply it.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion, a four-number representation of a rotation rather than a position or a set of distances. The circular setup uses a world-space center and radius, and its feedback uses the world X/Z plane.
Changing this orientation does not rotate or tilt the circular leash. The circular setup and updater do not read it; do not interpret a stored value here as the current physical joint orientation.
A physics joint is a connection that limits movement in the simulation. Storing an orientation here does not change that connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._leashed
member.summary: Stores the leash status flag returned by .

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits movement in the simulation. Circular-leash setup sets this flag as part of creating the connection, and UnleashPlayer clears it before cleaning up the joint references. The flag is stored state; it is not a fresh check that the physical joint exists or still limits movement.
Writing true does not create a joint, and writing false does not destroy one. Use LeashPlayerCircle and UnleashPlayer so the flag and physical connections are managed together.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._maxBounds
member.summary: Stores the circular leash’s maximum radius in its X component, measured in meters.

remarks.para: A physics joint limits movement in the simulation. LeashPlayerCircle installs this radius as the joint’s movement limit. At setup it computes the squared three-dimensional chest-to-center distance and the squared supplied radius, both in square meters. It rejects the setup when the computed squared distance is greater than the computed squared radius; computed equality passes. These calculations use rounded floating-point numbers, so an ideal geometric boundary is not an exact numerical guarantee.

The feedback updater uses the X value with the inner feedback radius to reduce outward horizontal movement near the edge. The inner radius is the horizontal chest-to-center distance, in meters, at or inside which requested movement is returned unchanged. The circular routines do not use the Y component. Editing X after setup changes feedback but does not update the joint’s installed movement limit; recreate the leash to change that physical limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._minBounds
member.summary: Stores the circular leash’s free-movement feedback radius in its X component, measured in meters.

remarks.para: A physics joint limits movement in the simulation, and its damping resists motion. At or inside this horizontal chest-to-center distance, UpdateLeashCircle returns the requested movement unchanged and clears positive horizontal joint damping. Outside it, the updater varies movement and damping according to distance and whether the requested motion points toward or away from the center.

The outer value is the maximum radius, in meters, installed as the joint’s movement limit by LeashPlayerCircle. This inner value is the start of the feedback region, not a forbidden inner circle. For example, with an inner value of 1 meter and an outer value of 3 meters, standing half a meter from the center is allowed by this feedback. The circular routines do not use the Y component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._queuedDestination
member.summary: Stores the feet position and facing orientation for the pending ordinary Teleport request.

remarks.para: The position is a world-space destination in meters. The orientation is stored as a quaternion, a four-number representation of a rotation, and supplies the facing direction for the move. The position-only Teleport overload keeps an upright version of the current chest-facing direction.

Ordinary Teleport overloads overwrite this stored pose; the last request before the early per-frame pass wins. InternalTeleport applies it, and the early caller then clears the pending flag. TeleportToPose follows a separate immediate path rather than filling this queue.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._reEnable
member.summary: Remembers that this manager has been disabled so its next enable notification can identify a re-enable.

remarks.para: OnDisable sets this flag. OnEnable passes its value to the controller, every entry in remapRigs, and the physical rig, then clears it after those notifications. These are Unity’s calls when a component stops or resumes being enabled.

It does not schedule or perform the enabling itself. For example, after disabling and later enabling the manager, the stages receive true once so they can distinguish that return from their first enable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._teleportQueued
member.summary: Marks an ordinary Teleport request waiting for the next early per-frame pass.

remarks.para: The position-based Teleport overloads store the destination and velocity-reset option before setting this flag. The Transform overload sets the flag first, then copies the destination pose and velocity-reset option. A Transform stores an object’s position and orientation. In the early pass, the manager applies the stored teleport after pending avatar work and before pending body-state work, then clears this flag.

Setting the flag alone does not move the player. Calling InternalTeleport directly applies the stored destination without clearing this flag, and TeleportToPose moves through a separate immediate path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._type
member.summary: Stores the recorded leash shape; circular-leash setup writes Circle.

remarks.para: This is a configuration label, not a command to build a new shape. The circular feedback routine uses its center and radius directly rather than branching on this value.
