Changing the value to Rectangle does not create rectangular bounds or rebuild the physical joint. Use the supported leash setup routine to establish the actual connection.
A physics joint is a connection that limits movement in the simulation. The stored shape label does not rebuild that connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager._zeroVelocity
member.summary: Stores whether the queued teleport requests clearing the rig’s motion.

remarks.para: The ordinary Teleport overloads copy their zeroVelocity argument here. InternalTeleport passes the stored choice to the controller, remap stages, and physical rig’s teleport routines when applying the move.

It is a choice for the queued move, not a report that the body currently has zero speed. For example, true requests a stopped arrival when the teleport is applied; writing this field without a teleport does not stop the body immediately. The manager initializes it to true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.activeSeat
member.summary: References the seat that has registered this player rig, or no seat when that registration is cleared.

remarks.para: Seat registration stores this reference and requests the Seated body mode. Seat removal clears it and requests OnFoot. Those body-mode requests are applied during the manager’s early per-frame pass, so the reference and applied bodyState can temporarily describe different stages of the transition.

The manager forwards seat-specific early and after-physics work to this seat and notifies it when an avatar is rebound. Ordinary teleports exit a registered seat before moving. Assigning this reference by itself does not perform the seat’s physical setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.animationRig
member.summary: References the body-animation stage that adapts its skeleton and body animation to the selected avatar.

remarks.para: When an avatar is installed, this stage adjusts skeleton proportions and calibrates body scale, then gives the avatar to its body-animation component. This lets differently sized avatars provide appropriate poses for later rig stages.

The interpolation stage samples this stage’s bone transforms when blending poses for physics timing. Keep the component connected through the rig setup, including remapRigs when it is part of that update chain; replacing this reference alone does not initialize a new stage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.avatar
member.summary: Returns the avatar instance currently equipped and bound to this rig’s stages.

remarks.para: The native setter is private. Use SwapAvatar to request an existing instance, or SwapAvatarCrate to load a packaged avatar over time. A request can still be pending while this getter returns the old body.

When an avatar candidate is accepted in the early per-frame pass, the manager prepares it and notifies the controller, remap stages, physical rig, seat, and health module. Read this getter when checking which instance actually became equipped; the stored candidate or a crate request’s notification alone does not prove that.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.avatarID
member.summary: Returns a stored avatar-identification string that is not refreshed by the normal avatar-swap methods.

remarks.para: The string is initialized when the manager is constructed. SwapAvatar and SwapAvatarCrate do not change it, so it can remain unchanged while the worn avatar changes.

For example, switching from one crate to another does not make this getter a reliable report of the new crate barcode. Read avatar to check the equipped instance; AvatarCrate gives the stored crate selection after a successful crate request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.bodyState
member.summary: Gets the applied body mode and queues a different requested mode for the next early per-frame pass.

remarks.para: The getter continues reporting the old mode until the manager has notified the controller, remap stages, and physical rig and recorded the new mode. For example, assigning Seated while OnFoot is applied does not instantly make the getter return Seated or register a seat.

The setter compares the request with the applied mode, not with an older pending request. If OnFoot is currently applied, assigning Seated and then OnFoot before the early pass leaves the Seated request pending. Assigning a different unapplied value replaces the stored request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.calibrationAvatarBarcode
member.summary: Stores the crate identifier associated with the configured calibration fallback.

remarks.para: A barcode is an avatar crate’s identifier; this field stores it as text. During Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, the manager builds the calibration crate reference from this string and compares the startup override’s identifier with it.

The comparison decides whether startup has a valid different avatar selection. This string is separate from the CalibrationAvatar instance; replacing that instance does not derive or update its barcode here. Changing the string later does not load or equip an avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.checkpointFwd
member.summary: Stores the world-space facing direction to use for checkpoint teleports.

remarks.para: This vector’s three components are unitless and describe a direction, not a position or an angle in degrees. For example, (0, 0, 1) points along the world’s positive Z axis. The checkpoint teleport combines it with world up to choose an upright facing orientation.

Start, Unity’s call before the component’s first normal update, initializes it from the manager object’s forward direction. The health module reads it together with checkpointPosition when returning the player to the checkpoint. Changing it only changes the saved direction; it does not turn the player immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.checkpointPosition
member.summary: Stores the world-space destination used when the health module teleports the player to a checkpoint.

remarks.para: Coordinates are distances in meters along the world’s X, Y, and Z axes. Start, Unity’s call before the first normal update, initializes this value from the manager object’s world position.

The checkpoint-teleport routine supplies this as the feet destination together with checkpointFwd and requests cleared motion. Some health reset paths use it too, but a health reset does not always imply a checkpoint move. For example, storing (2, 0, 5) prepares a destination two meters along world X and five along world Z; editing it alone does not move the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.controllerRig
member.summary: References the input stage that supplies head, hand, and movement targets for the player rig.

remarks.para: A rig is a set of bones and the code that positions them. This stage carries the player’s requested pose before the physical body resolves collisions. The manager updates it first, then lets the remap stages adapt its pose to the avatar and the physics stage respond.

Its early update also establishes the pause state that stops later pose work. ControllerRig returns this same reference. Replacing the field alone does not run the new component’s startup or avatar setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.interpRig
member.summary: References the stage that blends successive remap and animation poses for physics timing.

remarks.para: Physics simulation steps and rendered frames can occur at different times. This stage keeps previous and newer remap body poses and animation-skeleton transforms, then blends them for the physics update’s timing. That reduces abrupt target-pose changes between samples.

It is not simply a blend between controller targets and collision results. The manager reaches stages through remapRigs during its update chain; this named reference alone does not schedule the component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.inventory
member.summary: References the player’s inventory module, which registers named item slots, looks them up by name, and connects functions to item-added and item-removed notifications.

remarks.para: An inventory slot is a named place that can store an item, such as a holster. Slot registration builds a name-to-slot lookup so inventory operations can address the correct storage location. Subscriptions use that lookup to register a function that runs when an item is added to or removed from the named slot.

This reference lets code reach that inventory module. Setting it does not create slots or move an item by itself; registration and notification subscriptions belong to the inventory routines, and item changes belong to the slot routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.isLeashed
member.summary: Returns the stored leash status flag, rather than checking the current physical connection.

remarks.para: LeashPlayerCircle sets the flag while setting up a circular constraint. UnleashPlayer clears it before removing the stored joints. A physics joint is a connection that limits a body’s movement.

True alone does not prove that the joint is still present or that it has the expected radius. For example, external joint destruction can leave the saved flag unchanged. Use the leash setup and cleanup methods to keep the flag and connections together.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.onAvatarSwapped
member.summary: Runs no-argument callbacks when a crate-switch request reaches the end of its queued avatar-switch attempt.

remarks.para: A callback is a function registered to run at this point. The asynchronous crate request first waits for the pending avatar flag to clear and compares its candidate with the equipped avatar. On success it updates AvatarCrate. It then invokes this hook, followed by onAvatarSwapped2, then the request’s boolean result callback.

This hook can run when the candidate was rejected, so it is not a success guarantee. Earlier failures such as an invalid crate request can exit before these hooks. SwapAvatar for an already instantiated body does not invoke this hook.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.onAvatarSwapped2
member.summary: Runs crate-switch callbacks with the barcode used by the completed queued-switch attempt.

remarks.para: A callback is a function registered to run when this notification occurs. A barcode is the identifier of the requested avatar crate. If the request substitutes a fallback crate, this hook receives that effective request’s barcode. The request waits for the pending avatar attempt to finish, compares the candidate with the equipped instance, and updates AvatarCrate only on success.

The manager invokes onAvatarSwapped first, then this hook, then the request’s boolean result callback. This hook can run even when the candidate did not become equipped, so its barcode does not prove which body is currently worn. Earlier request failures can exit before the hook, and instance-only SwapAvatar does not invoke it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.physicsRig
member.summary: References the simulated body that responds to forces, joint limits, and collisions.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a Unity component that makes a body part move in the physics simulation. Physics joints connect those parts and limit their relative motion; colliders define the shapes that touch the level and objects. This rig coordinates those parts using the pose targets supplied by earlier stages.

The manager forwards fixed simulation updates, avatar setup, body-mode changes, and teleports to this rig. The circular leash creates a constraint on its chest body. Use this reference when you need physical motion or collisions rather than the virtual skeleton’s target pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.remapHeptaRig
member.summary: References the main stage that adapts the controller’s requested body pose to the avatar’s proportions.

remarks.para: Different avatars can have different arm lengths and body sizes. This stage takes the controller pose, adjusts head and hand targets using the avatar’s proportions, and applies movement adjustments such as crouching and body turning.

The interpolation stage samples its body pose, and teleport code uses its chest-facing direction when selecting an upright turn. Its normal manager updates come through remapRigs, so the named reference and the scheduled array must be configured consistently.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.remapRigs
member.summary: Lists the intermediate rig stages that the manager initializes, updates in order, and rebinds when the avatar changes.

remarks.para: The manager visits this array between controllerRig and physicsRig. It forwards setup, enable/disable, avatar and body-mode changes, teleports, and frame or physics-step work to each entry in array order. The serialized field was formerly named inputRigs.

This array schedules the stages; having a separate animationRig, interpRig, or virtualHeptaRig reference does not automatically add that component to the array. In Ragdoll mode the manager skips the array’s early, fixed, after-fixed, and late pose passes, while its ordinary frame-update pass still visits the entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.virtualHeptaRig
member.summary: References the world-space skeleton that supplies pose targets for the simulated body.

remarks.para: World space means coordinates relative to the level, rather than relative to a parent bone. This skeleton represents the avatar’s desired body pose; it is separate from the physics bodies that can be pushed or blocked by collisions.

Avatar setup adjusts its skeleton to the avatar’s proportions. GetPhysInputRig returns this component, and the immediate TeleportToPose path uses its center-of-pressure position, the reference point beneath the target body, when calculating a move. Normal stage updates require the corresponding entry in remapRigs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.worldGrip
member.summary: References the runtime grip handle used when hands grab static level geometry, such as during climbing.

remarks.para: The grip code finds nearby level collision shapes without their own movable physics body, records a suitable grab surface, and supplies the hand’s attachment behavior. A collider is the shape Unity uses to detect contact with a surface.

Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, creates this grip on a separate object, copies worldGripHandPose into its hand-pose setting, and stores it here. The manager destroys that object when the manager is destroyed. Replacing this reference alone does not create or configure a new grip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.worldGripHandPose
member.summary: Provides the default hand shape copied into the world-geometry grip during rig setup.

remarks.para: A HandPose stores a hand’s shape, such as how its fingers are arranged. During Awake, Unity’s one-time setup call, the manager copies this reference into the newly created worldGrip. The grip uses that setting as the starting pose for a hand’s grip state.

This configures the avatar hand’s grip pose; it does not move the real controller. Changing this manager field after setup does not replace the pose already stored on worldGrip or in an existing hand grip state. Update the actual grip’s settings when changing an already initialized grip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable.BakedObjectPath
member.summary: The path string recorded for this object's baked form.

remarks.para: This component stores the path as metadata. Unbake(true) clears it; the assigned Saveable code does not explain the path format or resolve the path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable.Data
member.summary: The string save data stored with this object.

remarks.para: CopyFrom copies this value from another Saveable. Unbake(true) leaves it in place while clearing the path, hash-algorithm name, unique ID, and last-baked record.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable.HashAlgorithm
member.summary: The stored name of the hash algorithm associated with this object's bake metadata.

remarks.para: This property holds a string; the assigned Saveable code does not perform hashing or validate the algorithm name. Unbake(true) clears the stored name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable.LastBaked
member.summary: The string record stored for this object's last bake.

remarks.para: CopyFrom copies this value, and Unbake(true) clears it. The assigned Saveable code does not define the record's format.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable.UniqueId
member.summary: The identifier string stored with this saveable object.

remarks.para: CopyFrom copies the identifier, and Unbake(true) clears it. The assigned Saveable code stores the value but does not generate it or check whether it is unique.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.ChunkBatch.addedChunks
member.summary: Pending components requested for the next scene-loading batch.

remarks.para: A Unity component is a script attached to a level object. A SceneChunk is such a component and may reference zero, one, or several Unity scenes; a Unity scene is a saved group of level objects. The ChunkBatch constructor starts this list empty. The shared SceneLoader manages loaded chunks and later processes pending batches; SceneLoader.Add adds a chunk only when it is not already in this pending list. Editing the list records a request; it does not load a scene by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.PlayerMarker._hasSpawned
member.summary: Records whether OnPlayerSpawned has been called on this marker.

remarks.para: OnPlayerSpawned sets this flag to true before it stores the supplied GameObject and notifies listeners. The inspected OnPlayerDespawn method sends OnDespawn callbacks but does not reset the flag. Treat it as a record that a spawn was reported, not as proof that the player is currently present.
TryGetPlayerGameObject returns this flag as its Boolean result while also copying _playerGameObject to its output argument.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.PlayerMarker._playerGameObject
member.summary: The GameObject most recently stored by OnPlayerSpawned, returned by .

remarks.para: OnPlayerSpawned stores the GameObject passed to it before notifying listeners. TryGetPlayerGameObject copies this stored reference to its output argument and returns _hasSpawned; it does not search the scene for an active player.

OnPlayerDespawn passes its GameObject argument to listeners but does not clear this stored reference or reset _hasSpawned. After that callback, the field can still refer to the last reported player object and the TryGet result can still be true; neither fact means the player is currently spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.PlayerMarker._spawnListeners
member.summary: List of ISpawnListenable objects registered for this marker's spawn and despawn notifications.

remarks.para: The constructor creates this list. RegisterSpawnEventListener adds an object and UnregisterSpawnEventListener removes one matching entry; those registration methods do not themselves send spawn or despawn notifications. Each listener is an object whose class supplies OnSpawn(GameObject) and OnDespawn(GameObject). These callbacks are methods PlayerMarker calls to report the corresponding event, passing its GameObject argument. Registering the same object twice creates two list entries. Unregister removes one matching entry, so any duplicate entry still receives later callbacks until removed separately.

OnPlayerSpawned and OnPlayerDespawn each walk the current list from its first entry to its last and invoke OnSpawn or OnDespawn respectively. OnPlayerSpawned first sets _hasSpawned and _playerGameObject, so listeners can read the updated values during OnSpawn. OnPlayerDespawn does not clear either value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.SceneStreamingManager.Instance
member.summary: Gets the shared SceneStreamingManager plugin instance.

remarks.para: If its static cache is empty, this property asks MarrowPlugins.TryGetPlugin to search the registered plugin list for a SceneStreamingManager and caches the result when found. It does not create a manager with new. If the plugin lookup finds nothing, the property returns null; callers that need to register scene zones require the plugin to be available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.SceneStreamingManager._gameObjectToScenes
member.summary: Lookup table from registered Unity GameObjects to their .

remarks.para: The constructor creates this Dictionary. RegisterSceneZone adds a GameObject key and its SceneChunk; because it uses Dictionary.Add, registering the same key twice fails instead of replacing the old value. UnregisterSceneZone removes a key, and TryGetScenesFromCollider uses the supplied GameObject as the exact lookup key.

SceneChunk.Awake registers the GameObject that holds each configured ZoneCuller, paired with that SceneChunk. SceneChunk.OnDestroy removes mappings for the live cullers in its current array. OnBeforeLevelLoad replaces this whole dictionary with a new empty one, so old mappings are discarded at that callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.SceneStreamingManager._manager
member.summary: Static cache for the SceneStreamingManager plugin instance.

remarks.para: Static means one shared slot for the class rather than one copy per manager instance. Instance checks it first, looks up the plugin through MarrowPlugins when it is empty, and saves a found manager here. If lookup fails, the field remains empty for a later attempt. The constructor initializes the per-instance dictionary but does not write this static cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.Level
member.summary: The resolved LevelCrate for the level reference passed to this session’s constructor.
member.remarks: A LevelCrate is Marrow’s level-content asset record. The constructor stores the supplied LevelCrateReference in _level and resolves Level only when that reference is valid. It does not use the runtime-settings fallback used for LoadLevel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.LoadLevel
member.summary: The resolved LevelCrate used as this session’s load-level content.

remarks.para: A LevelCrate is a level-content asset record. The constructor stores the requested LevelCrateReference in _loadLevel. If that reference is invalid or its crate is unavailable in AssetWarehouse, the game’s crate registry, it tries to obtain a fallback reference from the runtime MarrowSettings instance, the active game-settings object. It logs an error if that fallback is unavailable. LoadLevel can therefore differ from Level.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.Status
member.summary: Records whether this session has started loading and whether it has reached the level-load notification.

remarks.para: StreamStatus values are NONE (0), the newly constructed session before loading starts; LOADING (1), a load in progress; and DONE (2), the level-load callback point. A callback is a routine called at that phase. Load sets DONE before invoking its queued level-load callbacks, and later cleanup continues before Load’s UniTask completion object finishes.
The property accessors only store or return this enum value. Changing Status itself does not run Load’s transitions or dispatch its callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._Status_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the StreamStatus value exposed by the Status property.
member.remarks: This compiler-generated backing field holds NONE (0), LOADING (1), or DONE (2). Setting it directly does not itself run the callback dispatch performed by Load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession.__c.__9
member.summary: The single shared helper object generated by C# for Load. Load uses this object as the target for two yes/no callbacks (small routines called by the wait operation) and caches those callbacks in separate static fields on the generated helper type. If Unity's texture-streaming memory budget is nonzero, the first callback returns yes only when both the streaming-texture loading count and pending-load count are below five. Later, the second callback returns yes only when ZoneManagerPlugin.InactiveManager's inactive-object apply queue—the list of work waiting to be applied—is empty. If ZoneManagerPlugin.InactiveManager is missing, the native path enters its error path. After that wait succeeds, Load marks the session done. Textures are images used on scene surfaces.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._doLevelLoad
member.summary: Stores callbacks waiting for the session’s level-load notification.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the session calls at this phase; these callbacks receive no arguments. AddDoLevelLoadCallback adds one to the stored batch while Status is not DONE. During Load, the session sets Status to DONE, safely invokes any stored callbacks, then clears this batch. A callback registered after Status is already DONE runs immediately instead of being stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._doLevelUnload
member.summary: Stores callbacks registered for this session’s level-unload notification.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine the session calls at a phase; these callbacks receive no arguments. AddDoLevelUnloadCallback adds the supplied routine to this batch and has no Status-based immediate-call branch.

In Load, the session safely invokes any stored unload callbacks and clears this batch after the old-scene unloading steps and loading-music setup, immediately before invoking the pre-persistent-scene-load callbacks. This timing describes Load’s inspected path; the registration method alone does not establish an invocation time or replay callbacks registered later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._doPersistentSceneLoad
member.summary: Stores callbacks for the phase after persistent scenes have loaded.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine Load calls at this phase; these callbacks receive no arguments. Load safely invokes any stored callbacks after persistent-scene loading and its player-marker spawn work, then sets _doPersistentSceneLoadHappened and clears the stored batch. Listeners therefore run before the flag changes.
AddDoPersistentLoadCallback adds callbacks while the flag is false. Once it is true, a newly registered callback runs immediately instead of being stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._doPersistentSceneLoadHappened
member.summary: Marks that Load has passed its persistent-scene-loaded notification phase.

remarks.para: Load first safely invokes any stored _doPersistentSceneLoad callbacks, meaning routines called at this phase, then sets this flag and clears that stored batch. The flag becomes true even if no callbacks were registered; during a callback it has not yet changed.
AddDoPersistentLoadCallback stores callbacks while this flag is false and runs a new callback immediately once it is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._level
member.summary: Retains the LevelCrateReference supplied as the session’s primary level reference.
member.remarks: The constructor resolves the public Level field from this reference when it is valid. This stored reference is kept separately from _loadLevel and is reused by Refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._loadDependencyCount
member.summary: Counts load dependencies registered with this session.
member.remarks: RegisterLoadDependency adds 1 and UnregisterLoadDependency subtracts 1 without a zero floor. Load waits until a generated predicate sees a value below 1; the counter stores no per-dependency identity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._loadLevel
member.summary: Retains the LevelCrateReference used to resolve this session’s load-level crate.
member.remarks: The constructor may replace an invalid or unavailable requested reference with a fallback from the runtime MarrowSettings instance. Refresh passes this stored reference to the new session’s constructor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._persistentQueue
member.summary: The SceneLoadQueue that collects this session’s persistent game-area loading requests.

remarks.para: The constructor creates a new queue. LoadPersistentScenes adds the primary level crate’s main scene asset and every listed extra MarrowScene asset by GUID, each asset’s unique ID. MarrowScene is a scene-asset record; a loaded Scene is a game area.

LoadPersistentScenes starts the queue load, waits for completion, then retrieves the main or root Scene, makes it active through Unity’s SceneManager, and returns it. These assets come from _level, whereas _loadLevel chooses the initial loading scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._playerMarkers
member.summary: Stores PlayerMarker objects that provide the player’s spawn position during Load.

remarks.para: The constructor creates a new list. RegisterPlayerMarker checks for an existing marker before adding, so registering the same marker again does not add a duplicate.

When the runtime player-rig reference has a valid barcode (its crate ID) and the list contains a marker, Load selects the first marker. It reads that marker’s Transform.position, a position in world coordinates, and passes it to the player spawn request. It also supplies that marker’s OnPlayerSpawned and OnPlayerDespawn routines as callbacks, routines called for those actions. This inspected path does not spawn one player at every registered marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._willPersistentSceneLoad
member.summary: Stores callbacks for the phase just before persistent-scene loading starts.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine Load calls at this phase; these callbacks receive no arguments. Load safely invokes any stored callbacks, then sets _willPersistentSceneLoadHappened and clears the stored batch. The callbacks run before that flag changes.
AddWillPersistentLoadCallback adds a callback while the phase flag is false. Once _willPersistentSceneLoadHappened is true, a newly supplied callback runs immediately instead of being stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession._willPersistentSceneLoadHappened
member.summary: Marks that Load has passed the phase just before persistent-scene loading.

remarks.para: Load first safely invokes any stored _willPersistentSceneLoad callbacks, meaning routines called at this phase, then sets this flag and clears that stored batch. The flag becomes true even if no callbacks were registered; during a callback it has not yet changed.
AddWillPersistentLoadCallback stores callbacks while this flag is false and runs a newly registered callback immediately once it is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer._cachedChildScale
member.summary: No effect was verified for this child-scale value in the inspected slot code.

remarks.para: The field is a Vector3, a three-component vector (x, y, z) used here to represent scale, but none of the complete SlotContainer methods inspected reads or writes it. In particular, Return restores the child's local position and rotation from _defaultLocalOffset, not its scale. Other game code outside the inspected slot and rig methods was not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer._cachedDegrees
member.summary: The starting degreesFromCenter angle copied by Awake and used when FlipSagittal restores the saved angle or negates it.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object. This is a cached angle in degrees. Changing degreesFromCenter after Awake does not update the cache, so a later flip can replace that newer value with the angle originally saved.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer._defaultLocalOffset
member.summary: The child's local position and rotation saved by Awake for Return to restore after temporary reparenting.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object. Local position and rotation are measured relative to the child's parent. Return first reparents the child under this container and then restores these saved values. SimpleTransform stores a position and a rotation; it has no scale field. Return writes those two saved values back to the child, so this cache does not restore scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer._inventorySlot
member.summary: The found on child during Awake, refreshed while the slot anchor moves between its avatar and panel parents.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object. This private cached receiver is distinct from the public inventorySlotReceiver field. MoveToTemporaryParent turns this receiver's useOffset setting off and calls UpdateTransform; Return turns it back on and refreshes the transform again. This setting controls whether the receiver applies the slotted item's placement offset: the panel move disables that offset, and returning enables it again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.art
member.summary: The slot's visual object, hidden during a temporary panel move and shown again by Return.

remarks.para: Older prefabs serialized this field under the name hideObject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.bodyRegion
member.summary: Selects which avatar body part holds the slot anchor: the torso or a left/right upper/lower arm or leg.

remarks.para: PhysicsRig.ProcessSlotContainer reparents the slot container to the selected body region and positions it using that region's avatar measurements; the child anchor follows the container. Torso slots also use regionY, degreesFromCenter, and hardDimentions; limb slots use the matching arm or leg position. The available choices are Torso, ArmUpperLf, ArmLowerLf, ArmUpperRt, ArmLowerRt, LegUpperLf, LegLowerLf, LegUpperRt, and LegLowerRt. The suffix Lf means left and Rt means right.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.child
member.summary: The Transform used as the slot's anchor; the physics rig positions it on the selected avatar body region.

remarks.para: A Unity Transform holds an object's position, rotation, and scale. Here, PhysicsRig places this anchor for the torso or a limb. The item-slot panel can temporarily reparent it, and Return restores its saved local position and rotation. Local position and rotation are measured relative to the current parent, which changes during the panel move.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.degreesFromCenter
member.summary: Sets the slot's angle: around the torso for torso slots, or around the slot container's local Z axis for limb slots.

remarks.para: Local position and rotation are measured relative to a Transform's parent. Here the angle rotates the slot container relative to its avatar-body parent; the child anchor follows that container. For a torso slot, 0 degrees faces the front center, +90 and -90 degrees point to opposite sides, and 180 degrees faces the back. For a limb slot, PhysicsRig.ProcessSlotContainer applies this value as a local Z rotation of the container, negating it for right limbs. If flippable is true, FlipSagittal can replace the sign using the angle cached by Awake, Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.flippable
member.summary: Allows to change the slot's angle; when false, that method leaves the angle unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.hardDimentions
member.summary: Sets the width and height of a torso slot's layout footprint, which the physics rig uses to place and face its anchor.

remarks.para: The vector's X component supplies the width and Y supplies the height. The torso layout uses half of each around the slot center to build its placement bounds; it limits the half-width against the avatar's torso width. These values do not check whether the held item fits inside the slot, and they are not used for limb slots.

The layout combines them with avatar torso measurements expressed in meters, so these dimensions use meters as well. The native constructor initializes both components to 0.1, though serialized prefab values may replace that code default.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.inventoryAmmoReceiver
member.summary: The component used by an ammo slot to track magazine and cartridge data.

remarks.para: The receiver's slot handlers add or remove the gun's magazine and cartridge entries and switch the active magazine. This field is the component reference; the receiver performs that ammo bookkeeping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.inventorySlotReceiver
member.summary: The receiver that this container asks to enter UI mode while the slot anchor moves to the item-slot panel, then return when the anchor comes back.

remarks.para: MoveToTemporaryParent calls SendToUI on this reference, and Return calls ReturnFromUI. This is separate from the private _inventorySlot receiver found on child.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.ready
member.summary: Marks that Unity has called Awake; Inventory.FlipSlot checks it before calling this slot's flip methods.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object. It sets this flag before checking whether child exists. A true value therefore does not confirm that the anchor or its receiver was found.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.regionY
member.summary: Sets the unitless vertical placement of a torso slot between avatar torso landmarks; it has no placement effect on limb slots.

remarks.para: The Inspector tooltip describes 0 as between the shoulders and 1 as between the hips. PhysicsRig.ProcessSlotContainer uses this value to interpolate the torso anchor along avatar measurements. The Inspector's 0-to-2 range is not itself a runtime clamp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.rootRb
member.summary: The root Rigidbody reference that PullCordDevice.Awake uses as the connected physics body for its ball joint.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is an object's physics body, and a joint is a physics connection between bodies. PullCordDevice.Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for that object. It reads this reference from its parent SlotContainer while initializing the joint, so the joint can pull against the avatar's root body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip._isJointFree
member.summary: Hands recorded as using free rotational correction for this sphere grip.

remarks.para: Free mode is recorded per hand in _isJointFree. UpdateJointConfiguration later sets that hand joint’s rotational restoring drive to zero while free, or a strong restoring drive while locked. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and the held object; a drive applies spring-like correction toward its target. Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.

FreeJoint inserts a hand before updating anchors and target position. LockJoint removes it before storing a captured target, and OnDetachedFromHand removes it before base detach reports. This set can be changed before the physical joint drive is updated; it is not a list of detached hands.
Direct collection edits affect later membership checks and drive updates but skip the corresponding anchor or target work. Its presence is required by the grip’s free/lock and update routines.
Anchors are the joint’s connection points on the hand and held target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip._maxRadius
member.summary: Radius threshold above which extra handle and target offsets are added for a large sphere.

remarks.para: Large-sphere calculations use excess = max(radius − _maxRadius, 0). radius is the inherited sphere radius in meters, _maxRadius is this grip’s radius threshold in meters, and excess is the resulting meter amount used to scale the chosen unitless direction vector. For illustrative values of radius 0.10 m and _maxRadius 0.04 m, excess is 0.06 m, giving a 6 cm displacement when that direction is a unit vector. This threshold does not clamp the sphere radius.

Force-pull poses and free/locked target setup use the excess length, with direction and sign adjusted for the hand side. It is separate from the inherited radius used to score whether a hand is near the sphere, and from the hard-coded 0.05 m threshold used for secondary-button free-mode behavior.
Changing this stored threshold affects later pose and anchor calculations. It does not resize a collider, clamp radius, or immediately rebuild an already stored target or anchor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip.autoConfigure
member.summary: Stored authoring option; the checked SphereGrip initialization and joint routines do not perform automatic configuration from it.

remarks.para: The complete checked SphereGrip class constructs this field but does not read it in Awake, target solving, hand updates, or joint setup and updates. Those routines also do not overwrite the friction fields according to autoConfigure. The Inspector’s automatic-configuration wording therefore does not establish a runtime adjustment here.

Changing this field does not alter the behavior of those checked routines. Actual verified rotational behavior comes from rotationLimit, the free-hand set, and the live joint configuration. Separate editor or external consumers were not exhaustively audited, so this is not a claim that the field is unused everywhere.
