member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.CurrentTimeScaleStep
member.summary: Gets the currently stored discrete slow-motion step index.

remarks.para: This is an index, not a speed multiplier. The helper-managed levels are 0 through 3; a direct call to STEP_TIMESCALE can store a different integer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.OnSlowTime
member.summary: Notifies subscribers with the current step index as a float.

remarks.para: The audited event calls come from DECREASE_TIMESCALE, TOGGLE_TIMESCALE, and changing slowMoEnabled from true to false. They occur after the step has been written. Disabling slowMoEnabled raises the event before the flag becomes false, so a handler still reads true during that callback. DECREASE_TIMESCALE raises it only when slow motion is enabled, but still raises it at the upper step limit; TOGGLE_TIMESCALE raises it even when the step was already 0. INCREASE_TIMESCALE, direct STEP_TIMESCALE calls, RISE_TIMESCALE, DROP_TIMESCALE, SET_TIMESCALE, RESET_TIMESCALE, PAUSE, and UNPAUSE do not raise it in their audited bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager._controllingTime
member.summary: Marks an active or pending transition of intensity toward a target.

remarks.para: Step, rise, drop, toggle, and slow-motion-disable requests set this flag. While paused, the handler skips the transition update and leaves this flag set, so the transition can remain pending. The handler clears it when current intensity reaches target intensity; RESET_TIMESCALE also clears it when its cached-scale guard allows a reset. This marks a transition in progress or waiting to resume; it is not a general flag for every system that might write Unity timeScale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager._curTimeScale
member.summary: Stores the time scale the manager will apply or restore.

remarks.para: During a slow-motion update it is the reciprocal of the bounded intensity, such as 0.25 for intensity 4. PAUSE overwrites it with Unity's current timeScale before setting Unity timeScale to 0, and UNPAUSE uses the saved value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager._isPaused
member.summary: Records whether TimeManager has paused Unity's scaled game time.

remarks.para: PAUSE sets this before setting Unity timeScale to 0. The transition update skips its work while this flag is true; UNPAUSE clears it before restoring the saved scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager._slowMoEnabled
member.summary: Controls whether the manager applies slow motion, where intensity above 1 means Unity timeScale below 1.

remarks.para: The static initializer starts this flag as true. Changing the slowMoEnabled property to false requests step 0 and intensity 1 before this stored flag changes; changing that property to true only changes the flag. Direct SET_TIMESCALE requests above intensity 1 are ignored while it is false. STEP_TIMESCALE still stores any supplied index and its target intensity; the update can move current intensity toward that target, but does not apply an intensity above 1 as a slower timeScale while this flag is false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.cur_intensity
member.summary: Stores the current unitless slow-motion intensity as it moves toward its target. uses the reciprocal of the bounded intensity.

remarks.para: Intensity 1 means normal speed; intensity 8 means one-eighth speed. The update handler applies Unity timeScale as the reciprocal of this value after bounding the applied intensity between 1 and max_intensity. For example, intensity 4 produces timeScale 0.25.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.cur_timeScaleStep
member.summary: Stores the current discrete step index returned by CurrentTimeScaleStep.

remarks.para: The helper-managed indexes 0, 1, 2, and 3 target intensities 1, 2, 4, and 8. STEP_TIMESCALE can store any integer directly, while INCREASE_TIMESCALE and DECREASE_TIMESCALE keep their selected indexes within 0 through max_timeScaleStep.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.lrp_time
member.summary: Sets the duration used to ease current intensity toward its target.

remarks.para: The initial value is 0.5 seconds. The update handler uses Unity's unscaledDeltaTime, the frame duration that ignores timeScale, to move current intensity toward the target over this duration. Changing this duration affects eased transitions generally, including step, rise, drop, toggle, and slow-motion-disable requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.max_intensity
member.summary: Sets the maximum unitless intensity used for slow motion.

remarks.para: The initial value is 8. Because Unity timeScale is the reciprocal of intensity, that maximum corresponds to 0.125 speed. The update and direct intensity setter bound their applied intensity between 1 and this value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.max_timeScaleStep
member.summary: Sets the highest step index used by the increase and decrease helpers.

remarks.para: The initial maximum is 3, giving helper-managed indexes 0 through 3. Direct STEP_TIMESCALE calls do not use this bound and store their supplied index as-is.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.slowMoEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets whether TimeManager applies slow motion.

remarks.para: The initial value is true. Changing it to false starts a transition toward intensity 1 at step 0 and raises OnSlowTime before the property reports false. Intensity above 1 means a Unity timeScale below 1, so simulation runs more slowly. STEP_TIMESCALE can still store a step and target while this property is false; the update does not apply above-1 intensity as slow motion until enabled. Changing it to true only enables slow-motion application; it does not choose a step or raise the event by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.tar_intensity
member.summary: Stores the unitless intensity that the current transition is moving toward.

remarks.para: Step 0 targets intensity 1, step 1 targets 2, and so on by powers of two; drop targets max_intensity and rise targets 1. Unity timeScale is the reciprocal of the bounded intensity, so larger target intensity means slower simulation time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.tmp_intensity
member.summary: Stores the intensity snapshot used to calculate a transition's movement rate.

remarks.para: When a transition request starts, this is set to current intensity. The update handler compares this starting value with tar_intensity and uses their difference, unscaledDeltaTime, and lrp_time to move current intensity. When the target is reached, it copies current intensity here and clears the transition flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.AddNode.PortMetadata
member.summary: Describes a variable list of numeric inputs and the single Sum output produced by .

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal. The input descriptions use the group name Addends, meaning numbers to add together, with individual labels formatted as Term {0}. The output at index 0 is Sum. The node adds all readable entries in _previousConnections; it is not limited to two inputs.

This property returns descriptions shared by all instances, created once when the class is initialized. The number of actual configured input connections comes from the instance's connection array. Reading the descriptions does not calculate the sum or return its current value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.Deprecated
member.summary: Reports the stored marker that identifies this node as deprecated, meaning obsolete.

remarks.para: The getter reads _deprecated. Reading it does not change connections or request an enable or disable operation. The cached NodeState.Enabled flag, checked before graph calculations, is a separate value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.InputCount
member.summary: Counts the slots in this node's saved input-connection array, including empty slots.

remarks.para: The count is _previousConnections.Length. Input indices start at 0: an array with five slots has indices 0 through 4. An unconnected slot still contributes to the count; this does not count successful signal reads.

The normal constructor creates an empty array, giving a count of 0 before connections are supplied. TryConnectPortToInput can enlarge the array to include a requested index. Connecting index 4 makes room for at least five slots, even if the earlier slots are empty. The getter reads the array length directly; if code replaces _previousConnections with null, the property fails instead of returning 0.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.OutputCount
member.summary: Returns 1 for the base implementation, giving the node one output at index 0.

remarks.para: Derived classes can override this property to declare another output count. It describes the available output slots; reading it does not calculate their signal values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.PortMetadata
member.summary: Describes this node's signal sockets, including their names and input or output arrangement.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal passed between logic components. Each concrete node supplies its own descriptions. For example, AddNode describes a variable list of numeric inputs and a single Sum output.

Descriptions and current signal values are separate. A description may represent a whole variable input group, while InputCount counts this instance's saved connection slots. Use the descriptions to identify sockets and the node's signal state to obtain current output numbers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode.Subgraph
member.summary: Identifies the runtime logic group that holds this node's cached signal state.

remarks.para: A subgraph is a group of connected logic components. Its node lookup table maps each component to an entry in its cached NodeState array. Signal reads use this reference to find the node's saved output numbers.

Assigning this property only replaces the reference. It does not add the node to the new group's lookup table, copy its signal state, or rebuild connections. The reference must agree with the group's runtime tables for signal lookup to succeed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode._deprecated
member.summary: Stores the deprecation marker returned by Deprecated, identifying the node as obsolete.

remarks.para: Setting this Boolean changes what Deprecated reports. The direct field write does not submit an enable, disable, or connection request to the manager. Graph calculations use the separate cached NodeState.Enabled flag to decide whether to run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode._previous
member.summary: Legacy storage for old node references; BaseNode reads input connections from _previousConnections.

remarks.para: The game marks this field obsolete with the message Dead Field: Please remove. BaseNode's inspected connection-access methods read the newer output-port references, which identify both a source node and one of its outputs, instead of reading this array.

Use _previousConnections for current input wiring. This finding describes BaseNode's own native methods; it does not establish that every external migration tool or mod ignores legacy serialized data.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode._previousConnections
member.summary: Holds the output-port reference supplying each of this node's input slots.

remarks.para: Array index 0 supplies input 0, index 1 supplies input 1, and so on. Each reference can identify another node and an output index, or contain an inline constant: a number stored directly in the connection. The number's meaning and units depend on the receiving node.
InputCount counts all slots, including unconnected ones. TryGetInputConnection retrieves a slot's reference; actual signal reads then look up the source's cached output or return the inline number.

For runtime wiring changes, TryConnectPortToInput updates this array and submits a connection-change request to the manager. Writing this array directly changes local storage but does not submit that request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode.PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns descriptions of the Power input and Power output that scales the incoming signal by shaft travel.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Input 0 is Power and output 0 is also Power. The output is a continuous number, not an on/off pressed flag.

Output = incoming Power × p, where p = 1 - d² / L², d is the current world distance in metres between the joint's object and _endTransform, and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. The travel factor p has no unit. For example, input Power 2 and a shaft halfway toward the endpoint along a straight path give p = 0.75 and output 1.5. A missing readable Power input gives output 0; the output is not clamped to the range 0 to 1.
These descriptions are created once when the class is initialized and shared by every ButtonNode. Reading them does not measure the shaft or change its physics or sounds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._buttonShaftCollider
member.summary: Chooses the shaft collision shape whose collisions with _ignoreColliders are disabled during setup.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape Unity uses to detect contact. Assign the collider on the moving shaft, normally the part hands press. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the node disables collisions between this collider and each shape in _ignoreColliders, typically the other parts of the same button prefab (a reusable button template).
Changing this reference later does not run that setup again. The travel reading uses object positions, not the size or contact points of this collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._depressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sounds requested when the button changes from its latched pressed state to released.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a saved sound. On a release transition, the audio manager chooses one clip at random from this array and requests it at this component's current world position. The node then sets _isPressed to false after the request returns; it does not wait for playback to finish or confirm that a sound started. An empty array requests no sound but still allows the flag change. The array must not be null.

Release requires the raw travel value p to be strictly below _lowThreshold while _isPressed is true. Here p = 1 - d² / L², d is the current world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform, and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, between the joint's object and _endTransform, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. The value p has no unit. This transition is checked only while the shaft's Rigidbody, its physics movement component, is awake and the Power output changed by at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. Equality with the threshold does not release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._endTransform
member.summary: Marks the endpoint used to measure shaft travel and configure the joint during setup.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. This marker's current world position is compared with the world position of the joint's object. Coinciding positions give a raw travel value of 1. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, between these positions is cached and their midpoint is used to set the joint's connected anchor, the point on the other body or in the world that the joint connects to.

Later sensor reads use this marker's current position but keep the cached initial distance. Moving the marker after setup therefore changes the measured value without refreshing the joint anchor or travel limit. Put it at the intended fully pressed position before setup, separated from the shaft's starting position; a zero starting distance causes invalid division in the travel calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._highThreshold
member.summary: Sets the raw travel value that must be exceeded to request a press sound and latch _isPressed true.

remarks.para: This threshold has no unit and compares p = 1 - d² / L². Here d is the current three-dimensional world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform, and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. It compares the raw travel factor p, before multiplication by incoming Power. For example, a threshold of 0.95 requires more than about 77.64% of the straight travel toward the endpoint, because the distance is squared. Exactly 0.95 does not pass that threshold.

The node checks this condition only while its Rigidbody, the component that moves the shaft through physics, is awake, _isPressed is false and the final Power output has changed by at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. It requests one of _pressClips and sets the flag true after that request returns. Together with the lower release threshold, this leaves a middle range where the flag stays as it was. This value changes sound and flag decisions; it does not change the joint's travel limit or the output formula.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._ignoreColliders
member.summary: Lists collision shapes that the shaft collision shape stops colliding with during setup.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape Unity uses to detect contact. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the node disables collisions between every collider in this array and _buttonShaftCollider. This keeps the shaft from colliding with the rest of the button prefab (a reusable button template). If hands should still touch the shaft, leave their colliders out of this list.

Use an empty array when there are no pairs to disable. The setup expects an array, so do not leave it null. Editing this list later does not rerun the collision setup, and the inspected ButtonNode code does not automatically restore previously ignored pairs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._initialDisplacement
member.summary: Stores the initial world-space offset from the shaft's joint object to the endpoint for travel measurement.

remarks.para: During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, this vector is set to _endTransform.position minus the position of the joint's object. A vector is three numbers for an offset along the world's X, Y and Z axes; these components are in metres. Its length L is the shaft's initial full three-dimensional distance from the endpoint.

Sensor reads use p = 1 - d² / L², where d is the current world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform and p is the raw travel factor with no unit. The sensor uses this vector's squared length, not its direction, and does not refresh it on each read. For example, an initial distance of 0.04 metres and a current distance of 0.02 metres give p = 0.75. A zero-length vector makes the division invalid. Changing the stored vector changes later readings but does not rebuild the joint settings made during setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._isPressed
member.summary: Stores the latched pressed state that chooses the next press or release sound transition.

remarks.para: This is a remembered sound state, not a fresh physical measurement. OnEnable, Unity's call when the component becomes enabled, resets it to false. During Actuate, when the logic system asks the node to apply its result, a press sound request is followed by setting it true; a release sound request is followed by setting it false. The flag changes after the audio request returns, without waiting for completed playback.

Transitions use p = 1 - d² / L², where d is the current world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, between the joint's object and _endTransform, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. This unitless factor must be strictly above _highThreshold to press or strictly below _lowThreshold to release. The shaft's Rigidbody, its physics movement component, must also be awake, and the final Power output must have changed by at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. For example, incoming Power 0 can keep this flag unchanged even while the shaft moves. Changing the flag directly changes the next sound decision but does not change the continuous Power output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._joint
member.summary: Selects the whose object supplies the shaft position and receives the button's travel settings.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects a moving body to another body or to the world and limits its motion. This ConfigurableJoint's object supplies the Rigidbody, the component that lets physics move the shaft. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the node caches that body's reference and the world offset from the joint's object to _endTransform.

Let L be the initial full three-dimensional distance in metres between those two objects. Setup writes their midpoint as the connected anchor, sets the joint's linear-limit distance to L / 2 and sets its target position to (L / 2, 0, 0) in the joint's target-position coordinates. These target coordinates are relative to the object's local axes, or to the world's axes when the joint's configuredInWorldSpace setting is enabled; this setup does not change that setting. When there is a connected body, the midpoint is converted into that body's local coordinates, measured relative to that body; without one it is a world position. Existing joint axis, motion and drive settings still determine how the shaft can move. The joint's autoConfigureConnectedAnchor setting can also let Unity choose the applied anchor automatically.

Later sensor reads compare the joint object's current world position with _endTransform. Changing the joint reference later changes which position is measured but does not refresh the cached Rigidbody, initial offset or setup settings. Assign a valid joint and endpoint before setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._lowThreshold
member.summary: Sets the raw travel value below which a latched press requests a release sound and clears _isPressed.

remarks.para: This threshold has no unit and compares p = 1 - d² / L². Here d is the current three-dimensional world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform, and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. It compares the raw travel factor p, before multiplication by incoming Power. For example, a threshold of 0.05 releases only when less than about 2.53% of the straight travel remains compressed. Exactly 0.05 does not pass that threshold.

Release is checked only while _isPressed is true, the shaft's Rigidbody, its physics movement component, is awake and the final Power output has changed by at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. The node requests one of _depressClips, then clears the flag after that request returns. Keep this threshold lower than _highThreshold to provide a middle range where small movements do not switch the remembered state. It does not set the physical travel limit or directly change the continuous output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._performedInitialRead
member.summary: Records that a sensor measurement has begun, allowing later reads to skip a resting shaft.

remarks.para: ReadSensors first checks that _rigidBody exists. A Rigidbody is the component that lets physics move an object. If this flag is already true and the body is sleeping, meaning physics has paused it because it is resting, the method returns without changing the saved travel value. When this flag is false, a valid body can be measured even while sleeping.

The method sets this flag true before reading the joint and endpoint positions, so true does not prove the measurement finished successfully. OnEnable, Unity's call when the component becomes enabled, does not clear it. Setting it false permits another measurement with a valid sleeping body, but does not refresh the initial distance cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._pressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sounds requested when an unlatched button crosses its press threshold.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a saved sound. On a press transition, the audio manager chooses one clip at random from this array and requests it at this component's current world position. The node sets _isPressed true after the request returns; it does not wait for completed playback or confirm a sound started. An empty array requests no sound but still allows the flag change. The array must not be null.

Press requires p to be strictly above _highThreshold while _isPressed is false. Here p = 1 - d² / L², d is the current world distance in metres from the joint's object to _endTransform, and L is the initial full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, between the joint's object and _endTransform, cached during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. The value p has no unit. The shaft's Rigidbody, its physics movement component, must also be awake, and the final Power output must have changed by at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. Equality with the threshold does not press.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode._rigidBody
member.summary: Caches the shaft's physics body for deciding whether travel and sound transitions need updating.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that lets Unity physics move an object. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the node gets this body from the GameObject that holds _joint, the joint connecting and limiting the shaft. The reference is cached; later reads do not automatically look it up again.

A missing body makes the sensor leave its saved travel value unchanged. After the first attempted measurement with a valid body, a sleeping body also skips the measurement. Sleeping means physics has paused motion because the body is resting. Sound transitions likewise require an awake body. This reference controls those checks; the actual travel distance is measured from the joint object's world position, rather than from a separate body position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.InputCount
member.summary: Always returns 1 for the volume's single Power input, even when that input has no connection.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic input port is a socket for a numeric signal. This count describes the available socket, rather than counting valid saved connections. The only accepted input index is 0.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the fixed description of the Power input that scales the volume's attack amount and source range.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a numeric signal. Power is input index 0, and this node declares no outputs. Each damage attempt maps Power from the range 0 to 1 into the configured _mapLow to _mapHigh range: _mapLow is the multiplier at Power 0 and _mapHigh is the multiplier at Power 1. Values outside 0 to 1 use the nearest endpoint. These multipliers have no unit.

With mapping endpoints 0 and 1, Power 0.5 halves the base attack amount. When _effectiveDistance is positive, it also halves the allowed source range. An unreadable connection supplies Power 0, which maps to _mapLow; this does not necessarily mean zero damage if that endpoint is nonzero. Speed and distance modifiers can further reduce an attack.

These descriptions are created once when the class is initialized and shared by all instances. The logic system accesses them through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which it reads a node's descriptions. Reading this property does not process a target, change the saved connection or return its current signal value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.Subgraph
member.summary: Gets or assigns the stored reference for this node's connected logic group.

remarks.para: A subgraph is a group of connected logic components managed together. This property stores that group reference directly. Assigning it does not rebuild the group's connection tables, track a new target or apply a damage tick; those operations belong to the logic manager and damage-volume routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._damage
member.summary: Sets the base attack-damage amount that Power and the optional movement modifiers multiply for each target attempt.

remarks.para: The amount is a number of game damage points, not a force or a rate per second. The outgoing amount is D = B × g × m × v × f. Here B is _damage; g is the unitless Power multiplier after mapping input 0..1 to _mapLow.._mapHigh, the configured multipliers at input 0 and 1; m is the caller's multiplier, normally 1 or 0.08 in Update; v is the unitless speed factor, or 1 when speed scaling is skipped; and f is the unitless distance factor, or 1 when distance scaling is off.

For example, B = 10, g = 0.5, m = 1, v = 0.5 and f = 1 send 2.5 damage points. The target's receiver can modify that amount further, such as through its own resistance. This field is read on each attempt. Setting it to 0 does not turn off tracking or the tick routine, and an attempt that reaches dispatch can still send a zero-damage message.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._damageSourceTransform
member.summary: Chooses the live world point used for the source-range check and the direction attached to an attack.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object; it replaces a missing source with this volume's own Transform. Each attempt uses the source's current world position, measured in metres in the scene, and the target body's GameObject position for the range check.

The attack's normal and direction point from the target position toward this source point. Its origin field is the target's world position, rather than this source position. The separate distance-falloff option measures from the volume object, so moving this source does not move that falloff centre. Keep source and target positions separated when a valid direction is needed: zero separation makes the direction calculation divide by zero.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._damageType
member.summary: Sets the attack classification copied into every damage message sent by the volume.

remarks.para: AttackType labels the kind of attack, with choices such as Fire, Blunt or Piercing. It is passed to the target's attack receiver together with the computed damage amount and direction. The volume does not convert this label into a different base amount by itself.

Receivers can interpret the label differently. For example, ObjectDestructible checks its configured resistance bits against this attack type and can multiply the received amount by its own resistance multiplier. Changing this field affects the next dispatched attack; it does not move the trigger or change which bodies are tracked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._effectiveDistance
member.summary: Sets the source-range distance in metres before the Power multiplier scales that range.

remarks.para: When this value E is positive, an attempt is allowed only if d ≤ g × E. Here d is the full three-dimensional world distance, in metres, between _damageSourceTransform's current position and the target body's GameObject position. The unitless factor g is Power mapped from 0..1 to _mapLow.._mapHigh, the configured multipliers at input 0 and 1. Equality with the resulting range passes this check.

For example, E = 4 metres and mapped Power g = 0.5 allow a target up to 2 metres from the source. Zero, or a negative E, skips this range cutoff. That does not turn off the separate distanceMinimum/distanceMaximum falloff measured from the volume object when scaleDamageWithDistance is enabled. Usually choose a source range that covers the trigger volume; being inside the trigger alone does not guarantee passing this test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._lastTickTime
member.summary: Stores the real-time timestamp used to decide when another damage pass becomes eligible.

remarks.para: This is seconds since the application started, from Unity's realtimeSinceStartup clock. Unity's Time.timeScale is the game-speed setting; changing it does not change the realtimeSinceStartup clock. Update, Unity's once-per-game-frame routine, permits a pass when current real time minus this timestamp is at least _tickFrequency, the configured interval in seconds, and there is a tracked physics body.

The timestamp is written at the end of a processed pass, after target processing and dead-body cleanup. It does not mean a target necessarily lost health: all attempts can fail their range or movement checks. Frames that return because there are no tracked bodies or the interval has not elapsed leave it unchanged. Setting an earlier timestamp can make the next frame eligible sooner.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._objectDamageRecievers
member.summary: Caches the destructible receivers found on recognized bodies inside the trigger for the full-strength damage pass.

remarks.para: A trigger is a collision shape that detects entry and exit without blocking movement. Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object; it creates this list. On a body's first recognized entry, the volume checks for an ObjectDestructible on that body's GameObject after the character and player-receiver checks. It adds the object to this list and removes it when the final tracked collider for that body leaves.

A due Update pass, Unity's once-per-frame check of the interval, processes every list entry with caller multiplier 1. The list is a cache used with a separate GameObject-to-Rigidbody lookup, where a Rigidbody is the physics movement component. Adding an entry manually does not create that lookup. If an object remains in the later tracked non-player-body pass, it can also receive a smaller attempt with multiplier 0.08.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._playerDamageRecievers
member.summary: Caches the player damage receivers found on recognized bodies inside the trigger.

remarks.para: A trigger is a collision shape that detects entry and exit without blocking movement. Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a setup routine Unity calls for this object; it creates this list. The volume recognizes a PlayerDamageReceiver on the entering Rigidbody's own GameObject and adds it on the first recognized entry; a Rigidbody is the physics movement component. The entry is removed when the final tracked collider for that body leaves.

A due Update pass, Unity's once-per-frame interval check, processes only the first entry in this list with caller multiplier 1. Its later tracked-body pass skips every body represented by this list, so this list does not mean every listed player receives a full-strength attempt. It works with a separate GameObject-to-Rigidbody lookup; adding entries manually does not register that required lookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._previousConnection
member.summary: Stores the source signal or constant number read as Power for each damage attempt.

remarks.para: An OutputPortReference identifies either a numeric output from another logic node or a number stored directly in the reference. TryConnectPortToInput accepts it for input index 0 and replaces this value before notifying the logic manager. A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal; this volume has only the Power input.

Each attempt reads the reference, with an unreadable input supplying 0. Power is mapped from 0..1 into _mapLow.._mapHigh, the configured multipliers at input 0 and 1. That mapped number multiplies the base damage and, when positive _effectiveDistance enables the source cutoff, its allowed range. Changing this reference does not itself run a damage pass.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume._tickFrequency
member.summary: Sets the real-time interval in seconds between eligible damage passes.

remarks.para: Despite its name, this is a duration, not a count of ticks per second. Update is Unity's once-per-game-frame routine. It runs one pass when at least one physics body is tracked and current real time minus _lastTickTime, the timestamp saved at the end of the previous pass, is at least this interval. Unity's Time.timeScale is the game-speed setting; changing it does not change the realtimeSinceStartup clock.

For example, 0.25 seconds makes a pass eligible after a quarter second, while 1 means one second. Each pass still waits for a game frame, and a late frame produces one pass rather than replaying all missed intervals. The Inspector, Unity's panel for editing component values, offers the range 0.25 to 10 seconds; the runtime comparison does not clamp values assigned directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.associatedRb
member.summary: Chooses the moving body used to measure relative speed when staticVelocityDamage is false.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object physics movement. With staticVelocityDamage false and this reference assigned, the measured velocity is this body's velocity at the volume object's current world position minus the target body's velocity. Point velocity includes motion caused by rotation. The length of that three-component world velocity is the speed, in metres per second, used by the speed-damage limits.

For a train or another fast mover, assign its Rigidbody and leave staticVelocityDamage false to compare its movement at the volume with the target's movement. If staticVelocityDamage is true, the calculation instead uses the target body's own speed and ignores this reference. If the flag is false and this reference is missing, speed scaling is skipped, so the speed factor is 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.distanceMaximum
member.summary: Sets the distance in metres where distance falloff reaches zero and beyond which the attempt is skipped.

remarks.para: This is used only when scaleDamageWithDistance is enabled. Distance r is measured in world space from the volume object's current position to the target Rigidbody.position, where a Rigidbody is the physics movement component. With 0 ≤ a < b, where a is distanceMinimum and b is this distanceMaximum, the damage factor is f = 1 - clamp((r - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Clamp keeps a number between 0 and 1. Thus the full amount remains at r ≤ a, fades between a and b and is zero at r = b; r > b skips dispatch.

For example, minimum 2 metres and maximum 4 metres give half the amount at 3 metres and zero at 4 metres. This centre is the volume object, not _damageSourceTransform. Choose a clearly greater maximum than minimum: nearly equal endpoints use a step, giving full distance factor strictly below the maximum and zero at it. This does not disable the separate Power-scaled source-range check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.distanceMinimum
member.summary: Sets the distance in metres up to which the distance modifier leaves the attack amount at full strength.

remarks.para: This is used only when scaleDamageWithDistance is enabled. Distance r is the full world distance between the volume object's current position and the target Rigidbody.position; a Rigidbody is the physics movement component. With 0 ≤ a < b, where a is this distanceMinimum and b is distanceMaximum, the factor is f = 1 - clamp((r - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Clamp keeps a number between 0 and 1.

At or below a, f is 1. Between a and b it decreases linearly, and at b it is 0; beyond b the attempt is skipped. For example, minimum 2 metres and maximum 4 metres give f = 1 at 2 metres and f = 0.5 at 3 metres. Use clearly separated endpoints. Nearly equal endpoints use a step at the maximum instead of this ramp. The measurement is from the volume object, not the separate attack-source marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.invertVelocity
member.summary: Reverses the speed-damage factor so slow motion keeps more of the attack amount.

remarks.para: This matters only when speed scaling runs: staticVelocityDamage true uses the target Rigidbody's own velocity; with that flag false, an assigned associatedRb supplies its point velocity at the volume position minus the target velocity. A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object physics movement. The speed s is the length of the resulting world velocity in metres per second.

For nonnegative limits a < b, where a is velocityMinimum and b is velocityMaximum, the ordinary factor is v = clamp((s - a) / (b - a), 0, 1); clamp keeps the number between 0 and 1. With this flag enabled the factor becomes 1 - v, and speeds above b skip the attempt. For example, limits 2 and 6 metres per second give full factor at speed 2, half at 4 and zero at 6. Equality with the maximum reaches a zero-factor attack rather than the above-maximum skip.

Choose clearly separated limits. Nearly equal limits use a step: the ordinary factor is 0 at or below the minimum and 1 above it, then inversion reverses that factor. With no speed-scaling branch, this flag has no effect on the amount.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.scaleDamageWithDistance
member.summary: Enables distance falloff measured from the volume object to the target physics body.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object physics movement. When enabled, the calculation uses its current world position and this volume's current world position, in metres. It does not use _damageSourceTransform as the falloff centre. With 0 ≤ a < b, where a is distanceMinimum, b is distanceMaximum and r is their measured world distance, the damage factor is f = 1 - clamp((r - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Clamp keeps a number between 0 and 1.

The factor is 1 through the minimum, fades linearly to 0 at the maximum, and targets beyond the maximum are skipped. For example, minimum 2 metres and maximum 4 metres give half the amount at 3 metres. Use clearly separated limits; nearly equal limits form a step at the maximum. Disabling this flag skips only that falloff calculation. A positive _effectiveDistance still enables a separate source-range cutoff, multiplied by the mapped Power signal.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.staticVelocityDamage
member.summary: Selects the target body's own speed for velocity-based damage instead of relative motion from associatedRb.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object physics movement. With this flag true, speed is the length of the target body's world velocity in metres per second, and associatedRb is ignored. With it false and associatedRb assigned, speed comes from that body's point velocity at the volume's world position minus the target velocity; point velocity includes rotation. With it false and no associated body, speed scaling is skipped.

For nonnegative limits a < b, where a is velocityMinimum, b is velocityMaximum and s is the chosen speed, the ordinary damage factor is v = clamp((s - a) / (b - a), 0, 1); clamp keeps the number between 0 and 1. Speeds below a skip the normal attempt. Enabling invertVelocity uses factor 1 - v instead and skips speeds above b. For example, a = 2 and b = 6 metres per second give half the speed-scaled amount at s = 4. Use clearly separated limits; nearly equal limits use a step rather than this ramp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.velocityMaximum
member.summary: Sets the speed in metres per second where the ordinary velocity modifier reaches full strength.

remarks.para: With nonnegative limits a < b, where a is velocityMinimum and b is this velocityMaximum, the ordinary factor is v = clamp((s - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Clamp keeps a number between 0 and 1. Speed s is the length of the measured world velocity: staticVelocityDamage true uses the target Rigidbody's own velocity; otherwise an assigned associatedRb supplies its velocity at the volume position minus the target's velocity. A Rigidbody is the physics movement component.

For normal scaling, reaching b gives full factor and faster speeds stay at full factor. With invertVelocity enabled, the factor is 1 - v: reaching b gives zero, and speeds above b skip the attempt. For example, minimum 2 and maximum 6 metres per second give half factor at 4. If staticVelocityDamage is false and associatedRb is missing, this speed calculation is skipped. Choose a clearly greater maximum than minimum; nearly equal limits use a step instead of the ramp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume.velocityMinimum
member.summary: Sets the speed in metres per second below which the normal velocity-damage attempt is skipped.

remarks.para: With nonnegative limits a < b, where a is this velocityMinimum and b is velocityMaximum, the ordinary factor is v = clamp((s - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Clamp keeps a number between 0 and 1. Speed s is the length of the chosen world velocity: staticVelocityDamage true uses the target Rigidbody's own velocity; otherwise an assigned associatedRb supplies its velocity at the volume position minus the target velocity. A Rigidbody is the physics movement component.

Normal scaling skips s < a; exactly a passes that gate but has factor 0. With invertVelocity enabled, the factor is 1 - v, so at or below a it stays at full factor; the hard cutoff then skips speeds above b. For example, limits 2 and 6 metres per second give normal factors 0, 0.5 and 1 at speeds 2, 4 and 6. If neither speed branch is configured, this threshold is not applied. Use clearly separated limits; nearly equal limits use a step at the minimum instead of the normal ramp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.Deprecated
member.summary: Reports the stored marker that labels this node as obsolete.

remarks.para: This property reads _deprecated. Reading it does not disable the adapter, change a connection, or run an event. Its value is a marker rather than the current enabled state of this node in the logic graph.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.InputFell
member.summary: Runs its callbacks when a high-state input falls strictly below .

remarks.para: The adapter remembers whether it is in its high state. It enters that state when the input is strictly greater than highThreshold, the upper switching number, and leaves it when the input is strictly less than lowThreshold, the lower switching number. Both thresholds use the same units as the input. Equality with the lower threshold does not cause a fall.

During a qualifying fall, _isHigh is set false before InputFell is invoked. If InputUpdated also qualifies, its callbacks run first and the changed input is saved before the fall. With ordinary callbacks that do not alter the adapter’s fields, InputHeld does not run on that falling actuation.

An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; each such method is a callback. The event is passed this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource (the common interface for a node that supplies an output number), and the input number read for this actuation. The source can be null when the input is an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. The adapter does not clamp that number to 0–1; its units are whatever the source number means.
For example, with highThreshold 0.7 and lowThreshold 0.3, a rise to 0.8 enters the high state; 0.5 keeps it high; 0.2 triggers InputFell once. Staying at 0.2 does not repeatedly trigger this event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.InputHeld
member.summary: Runs its callbacks on each actuation that finishes with the input’s remembered high state still set.

remarks.para: An actuation is the logic system running this node’s effects. The high state starts when the input is strictly greater than highThreshold, the upper switching number, and ends when it is strictly less than lowThreshold, the lower switching number. In between these thresholds, the previous state is kept. Both thresholds use the input’s units. Thus InputHeld can run even when the current number has dropped below highThreshold.

With a valid input reference, this event is checked after InputUpdated, the rise or fall handling, and any first-rise event. It can run on the same actuation as InputRose, and it can run with an unchanged input. It is tied to actuations; it is not a promise of a call every rendered frame. Invalid input references cause the adapter to return without invoking it.

An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; each such method is a callback. The event is passed this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource (the common interface for a node that supplies an output number), and the input number read for this actuation. The source can be null when the input is an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. The adapter does not clamp that number to 0–1; its units are whatever the source number means.

For example, with upper threshold 0.7 and lower threshold 0.3, 0.8 starts the high state. Later actuations at 0.5 still invoke InputHeld. At 0.2 the ordinary fall clears the state and stops held callbacks. Callbacks run before later checks, so a callback that changes _isHigh can change whether InputHeld runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.InputRose
member.summary: Runs its callbacks when a low-state input rises strictly above .

remarks.para: highThreshold is the upper switching number in the input’s units. The adapter must currently be in its low state, with _isHigh false. Equality with the upper threshold does not trigger a rise. Once high, it stays high until the input is strictly below lowThreshold, the lower switching number; intermediate values do not cause another rise.

The adapter sets _isHigh true before invoking InputRose. If InputUpdated qualifies, its callbacks and the saved-input update happen first. On the first rise since initialization, InputRoseOneShot is checked next, then InputHeld is checked. This order assumes callbacks return normally without changing the adapter’s fields.

An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; each such method is a callback. The event is passed this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource (the common interface for a node that supplies an output number), and the input number read for this actuation. The source can be null when the input is an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. The adapter does not clamp that number to 0–1; its units are whatever the source number means.

For example, with upper threshold 0.7 and lower threshold 0.3, going from low to 0.8 triggers a rise. Later 0.9 does not trigger another rise. Dropping to 0.2, then returning to 0.8, allows InputRose again. Initialize, the logic system’s setup call, can start the adapter already high without invoking this event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.InputRoseOneShot
member.summary: Runs its callbacks on the first detected low-to-high rise since the most recent initialization.

remarks.para: A rise means the input is strictly greater than highThreshold, the upper switching number in the input’s units, while _isHigh was false. After _isHigh becomes true and InputRose finishes, this event is eligible only if _hasBeenHigh is false. The adapter sets _hasBeenHigh true after these one-shot callbacks return, even when there are no calls configured for the event.

Initialize is the logic system’s setup call. Every such call resets _hasBeenHigh to false and sets _isHigh from whether the initial readable input is strictly above highThreshold. It does not invoke any of these events. Starting already high therefore does not produce a one-shot rise: the input must later go strictly below lowThreshold, the lower switching number, and rise again. The adapter’s enable and disable routines do not themselves reset this latch.

An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; each such method is a callback. The event is passed this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource (the common interface for a node that supplies an output number), and the input number read for this actuation. The source can be null when the input is an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. The adapter does not clamp that number to 0–1; its units are whatever the source number means.

For ordinary callbacks that do not change fields, the first rise runs InputUpdated if its change test passes, then InputRose, InputRoseOneShot and InputHeld. Later rises omit InputRoseOneShot until initialization resets its latch. Because _hasBeenHigh is written after the callbacks, changing the flag or calling back into the adapter before they finish can affect this sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.InputUpdated
member.summary: Runs callbacks when the input differs from its saved comparison value by more than 0.0001; frequent calls can be expensive. Prefer or when a threshold transition is enough.

remarks.para: Each actuation, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, first checks that the stored input reference is valid. It then reads an input number f and compares it with _priorValue, the last number saved by a qualifying change. The test is abs(f - _priorValue) > 0.0001, where abs means the size of the difference without its sign. The tolerance is in the input’s units. A difference equal to the tolerance does not pass; floating-point arithmetic, the game’s limited-precision number calculations, determines the comparison.

When the test passes, configured InputUpdated callbacks run before _priorValue is replaced by f, and before the high/low threshold checks. The new comparison value is saved even if the event has no calls. Small differences that fail the test do not refresh it, so several small changes can eventually add up to a qualifying difference. Threshold checks still happen even when this event’s test fails.

An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; each such method is a callback. The event is passed this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource (the common interface for a node that supplies an output number), and the input number read for this actuation. The source can be null when the input is an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. The adapter does not clamp that number to 0–1; its units are whatever the source number means.

For example, after saving 0.5, an input of 0.50005 stays below the change tolerance; 0.5002 passes. A callback reading _priorValue sees the older saved number until InputUpdated returns. Initialize, the logic system’s setup call, does not refresh _priorValue. The original performance warning still matters: this event can run the configured methods on every qualifying update, so use the rise/fall events if you only need switching behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.PortMetadata
member.summary: Describes this adapter’s one Power input and its lack of signal output ports.

remarks.para: Input 0 is named Power. An output reference or inline constant, a number stored directly in the reference, supplies it. The adapter reads that number to decide which event lists to invoke; it does not forward a new numeric output. An event list is a collection of callbacks, methods called when a condition is met.

The input can invoke InputUpdated when its change is larger than 0.0001, enter the high state strictly above highThreshold, and leave it strictly below lowThreshold. The change tolerance and thresholds use the input’s units; the adapter does not clamp the number to 0–1. For example, a button supplying 0 and 1 can trigger rise and fall events with upper threshold 0.7 and lower threshold 0.3.

These descriptions are built once for the type and returned from the cached _portMetadata value. They describe the port rather than the current connection, input number or events already fired. IVoidLogicNode is the common node interface, the form through which the logic system accesses a node’s descriptions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.Subgraph
member.summary: Stores the group of connected VoidLogic nodes that this adapter belongs to.

remarks.para: A VoidLogicSubgraph is a connected group processed together, with tables for its nodes and their cached output numbers. This property gets or replaces the stored group reference. Replacing the reference alone does not add the adapter to the new group’s tables, copy cached values or request a connection update.

The logic system invokes enabled actuators, nodes that perform effects, while processing a group that needs an update. That is when this adapter reads its input and chooses its events. For example, moving it to a different group by changing only Subgraph is not a complete graph reconnect; the graph’s node and connection tables must also agree.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter._hasBeenHigh
member.summary: Remembers whether the first-rise opportunity has already been consumed since initialization.

remarks.para: Initialize is the logic system’s setup call. It resets this flag to false even if the readable input starts above highThreshold, the upper switching number in the input’s units. Starting high sets _isHigh, the current high-state latch, without firing a rise or setting _hasBeenHigh true.

On a later low-to-high rise, _isHigh becomes true, InputRose callbacks run, then InputRoseOneShot callbacks are eligible while _hasBeenHigh is false. A callback is a method run by an event. The flag is set true after the one-shot callbacks return, even if the event has no calls. A fall strictly below lowThreshold, the lower switching number, clears _isHigh but does not reset this first-rise flag.

For example, after one rise and a fall, the next rise can invoke InputRose again but omits InputRoseOneShot. A later Initialize call reopens that first-rise opportunity. Turning the adapter off and on does not reset this field in its own enable/disable routines. Changing this flag from a callback can change which later one-shot check runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter._isHigh
member.summary: Remembers whether the input is in the high state, including while its value is between the switching thresholds.

remarks.para: During actuation, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, a false flag becomes true only if the input is strictly above highThreshold, the upper switching number. A true flag becomes false only if the input is strictly below lowThreshold, the lower switching number. Both thresholds use the input’s units. For the usual setup with the lower threshold below the upper one, equality at either boundary and values between them keep the previous state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter._previousConnection
member.summary: Stores the source output reference or inline constant read by this adapter’s input events.

remarks.para: The adapter has one input, index 0. An OutputPortReference records a node and output index, or an inline constant, a number stored directly in the reference. At actuation, when the logic system runs the adapter’s effects, a valid reference is read once and that number is passed to whichever events qualify. The number is not clamped to 0–1; the thresholds and change tolerance use its units.

An invalid reference makes actuation return without running events or refreshing _priorValue, _isHigh or _hasBeenHigh. A reference can be valid yet not have a currently readable cached output, so validity alone is not proof of a successful value read.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter._previousNode
member.summary: Legacy node-reference field marked obsolete by the game.

remarks.para: The game marks it obsolete, as "Dead Field: Please remove". Do not build against this.

The EventAdapter connection methods, Initialize setup and Actuate event processing inspected here read _previousConnection instead. This field is still serialized, meaning Unity can save and load its value, but that does not establish an effect on this adapter’s current input events or prove what external migration code may do with it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter._priorValue
member.summary: Stores the comparison number last accepted by the InputUpdated change test.

remarks.para: During actuation, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, it reads an input number f and tests abs(f - _priorValue) > 0.0001. Here abs is the size of the difference without its sign, and the tolerance is in the input’s units. Only a strictly larger difference passes; the comparison uses the game’s floating-point number precision.

On a passing test, InputUpdated invokes its configured callbacks, methods run by an event, before _priorValue is set to f. The field is saved even if there are no calls. A failing test leaves it unchanged, so it is not necessarily the immediately preceding input sample. For example, from a saved 0.5, samples 0.50005 and then 0.5002 are both compared with 0.5; the second passes and replaces it.

Initialize, the logic system’s setup call, does not refresh this field. An invalid input reference during actuation also leaves it alone. A callback reading it during InputUpdated sees the old comparison number, while rise/fall processing afterward sees the new one when the change test passed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.highThreshold
member.summary: Sets the input number that must be exceeded to enter the high state and trigger .

remarks.para: This is the upper switching number in the same units as the input. During actuation, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, the input must be strictly greater than highThreshold while _isHigh is false to cause a rise. Equality does not qualify. Once high, values between highThreshold and lowThreshold, the lower switching number, keep the state high until the input is strictly below the lower number.

For example, with highThreshold 0.7 and lowThreshold 0.3, 0.7 does not turn a low state on; 0.8 does. A later 0.5 can still invoke InputHeld because the high state is remembered. The constructor starts the upper threshold at 0.95, but saved component settings can supply another value. The input is not restricted to the 0–1 range.

Initialize, the logic system’s setup call, reads this threshold to choose the initial high state without firing a rise event. Changing the threshold later does not itself invoke an event; its effect is considered on a later setup call or actuation. Use a lower switching number below this upper one to leave a stable middle band, preventing repeated switching from small input fluctuations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter.lowThreshold
member.summary: Sets the input number that a high-state input must fall below to trigger .

remarks.para: This is the lower switching number in the same units as the input. During actuation, when the logic system runs this node’s effects, the input must be strictly less than lowThreshold while _isHigh is true to cause a fall. Equality does not qualify. The state is set false before the event invokes its callbacks, methods called by the event.

For example, with lowThreshold 0.3 and highThreshold 0.7, the upper switching number, a rise to 0.8 enters the high state. Dropping to 0.5 or exactly 0.3 keeps it high; 0.2 causes a fall. Use the lower number below the upper one to keep this stable middle band. The constructor starts lowThreshold at 0.05, but saved component settings can supply another value.

Initialize, the logic system’s setup call, chooses the initial state using the upper threshold, not this lower one, and invokes no events. Changing lowThreshold does not immediately clear a high state or fire InputFell; a later actuation with a valid input reference must run the comparison.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AssetWarehouse.OnChanged
member.summary: Runs after AddPallet processes a pallet’s listed crate and data-card contents, but only when its data-card list is present. Use it if any change matters; otherwise, prefer , , or for those specific additions.

remarks.para: In AddPallet, this callback runs after the item-registration loops and before OnPalletAdded only when the pallet’s data-card list is not null. If that list is null, AddPallet skips both callbacks. The audited individual crate/data-card add routines and unload routines do not invoke it, so its name does not mean every possible inventory change is reported. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AssetWarehouse.OnCrateAdded

remarks.para: The barcode identifies the crate description, not a spawned scene object. The add routine writes the typed registry before invoking listeners; it can replace an existing entry with the same key, so this callback is not restricted to brand-new keys.

When AddPallet processes an item whose owning-pallet reference is missing, it fills that reference after this item callback. A listener can therefore run before that particular link is set. Clear removes the subscription.
An invalid barcode can still reach this callback, even though normal TryGet lookup rejects that barcode.

SpawnSpawnableAsync passes it with each pool request, and the handler sends the affected GameObject to ISpawnListenable.OnDespawn.

Replacing this field changes the routine passed to later requests. It does not replace routines already attached to an earlier pooled object. The normal subscription methods manage the listener list without replacing this forwarding routine.

Replacing this field changes the routine passed to later requests. It does not replace routines already attached to an earlier pooled object. The normal subscription methods manage the listener list without replacing this forwarding routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner._spawnedSpawnable
member.summary: A public GameObject slot on the spawner; the checked spawn methods do not fill it with their result.

remarks.para: SpawnSpawnableAsync returns a Poolee and passes its GameObject to onSpawnEvent, but the inspected CrateSpawner spawn wrapper, state machine, and listener handlers do not assign this field. It should therefore not be treated as an automatically maintained latest-spawn result for that path.
Use the asynchronous result or the event argument when code needs the object that a request produced. Assigning this slot alone does not spawn, move, or despawn an object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.crateQuery
member.summary: The source of the inherited Barcode, the warehouse ID used to identify a crate, when is true.

remarks.para: GetCrateReference reads this query's Barcode but does not call RunQuery or read tempBarcode. RunQuery stores a random matching crate's Barcode in tempBarcode; copy that value into Barcode before SetSpawnable when you want to use that result.

The query must be present, and its Barcode must ultimately identify a SpawnableCrate. CrateQuery itself searches Crate descriptions of any type. Replacing this object or changing the query mode requires SetSpawnable to refresh the saved pair.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.manualMode
member.summary: Suppresses this spawner’s automatic spawn request during persistent scene loading while playing; remains callable.

remarks.para: The checked OnPersistentLoad routine calls SpawnSpawnable only when the application is playing and this flag is false. Set it before that scene-load notification to suppress that automatic request.

SpawnSpawnable, ReSpawnSpawnable, and SpawnSpawnableAsync do not test this flag. Other code can still call them directly. Changing the flag does not despawn an existing object or cancel an already started request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.onSpawnEvent
member.summary: Reports a successful pool spawn with this spawner and the resulting scene GameObject.

remarks.para: It receives two arguments: the CrateSpawner that requested the object and the spawned or reused GameObject. It runs only for a nonnull pool result and only when this event object is assigned.

Pool listener callbacks, routines called to report an action, run first inside AssetSpawner. After its wait completes, the spawner removes the scene-load dependency, invokes this event, then completes SpawnSpawnableAsync. A reused object can trigger it; it does not require a new prefab instantiation.
This event does not report despawn or recycling. Use RegisterSpawnEventListener for those lifecycle notifications. The checked routine does not assign _spawnedSpawnable before this event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.playmodePreviewMaterial
member.summary: The material assigned to the preview child’s renderer to control how its mesh is drawn.

remarks.para: A material specifies a surface’s rendering settings, such as shader and appearance. CreateRuntimePreview assigns this one when it is a live Unity object, after starting the mesh load and marking the preview request as generated. It is applied to the preview child rather than the spawned prefab.
Changing this field later does not update the already created renderer automatically. A missing material leaves the renderer without an assignment from this routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.policyData
member.summary: The pool rules saved with the selected crate, controlling capacity, grouping, and what happens when a limit is reached.

remarks.para: The base SpawnPolicyData includes maxSize, a count of tracked active objects plus pending requests, and a rule to grow, reuse the oldest, reuse the newest, or refuse another spawn at the limit. Reuse can recycle an earlier object instead of creating an unlimited number of copies. groupByCrate determines whether the policy grouping includes the crate barcode.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, and SetSpawnable copy this policy object reference into _spawnable. Replacing policyData requires SetSpawnable for later requests to use the new object. The active policy reads the shared data object, so editing its fields can affect later decisions without replacing it.

A null policy takes the checked AssetSpawner path that spawns from the pool without these policy rules. The size is an object count, not a distance or duration; the grow rule does not make maxSize a hard ceiling.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.previewMeshInPlaymode
member.summary: Requests a visual preview child during Awake, separate from the pooled gameplay object.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback. When this flag is true, it calls CreateRuntimePreview, which adds a child with a MeshFilter, the component holding a mesh, and a MeshRenderer, the component drawing it. It requests the selected SpawnableCrate's preview mesh and uses playmodePreviewMaterial when assigned.

The child is parented to the spawner. Its local position of zero adds no position offset from the spawner, its identity rotation adds no extra rotation, and its local scale of one adds no extra scale; it inherits the spawner's transform. This flag is checked during initialization; changing it afterward does not itself create or remove a preview. The checked preview path is runtime code and has no editor-only or Application.isPlaying guard of its own.

A valid crate reference and preview mesh reference are required for the load path. The generated flag can become true before the mesh actually finishes loading. The visual preview does not itself request a pooled prefab spawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.shouldSpawn
member.summary: An optional routine whose false result rejects a spawn request before the pool is called.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This one takes no arguments and returns a yes-or-no decision. For example, a routine can return whether a game objective currently permits another prop.

SpawnSpawnableAsync calls it only after the saved crate reference resolves. Null means no extra decision is required. A false result returns null before a stream dependency is registered or an object is requested. It is checked once at the start, rather than repeatedly while the asynchronous operation waits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.spawnableCrateReference
member.summary: The crate identifier selected for spawning when is false.

remarks.para: A SpawnableCrateReference identifies a prefab description in the warehouse; it is not the scene object. The warehouse must be ready and contain a matching SpawnableCrate for the saved reference to resolve.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, copies this reference into the saved Spawnable pair. Replacing it later requires SetSpawnable before later requests use the new reference. Editing the same shared reference object’s Barcode can also affect that saved reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner.useQuery
member.summary: Chooses whether reference selection uses .Barcode or .

remarks.para: True builds a SpawnableCrateReference from the query’s inherited Barcode; false returns spawnableCrateReference. This selects an identifier source. It does not run a search or automatically use CrateQuery.tempBarcode.

The choice is used when Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, or SetSpawnable builds the saved Spawnable pair. Changing this flag after initialization requires SetSpawnable to refresh that pair before subsequent spawn requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.EntityPose.ColliderBounds
member.summary: The saved box center and half-size recorded for this pose’s collider bounds.

remarks.para: Bounds describes a box by center, its middle point, and extents, the distance from that middle to each face along x, y, and z. Full size is twice the extents: extents (0.5, 1, 0.5), for example, describe size (1, 2, 1) in the same distance units used by Unity Transform positions. This code does not convert them to meters. These values are geometric metadata, not an actual collider component.

Pack writes the stored center and extents, and Unpack can restore them. The checked card code copies these numbers without converting between entity-local and world coordinates; use the box in the coordinate frame in which it was recorded. Changing this field does not resize colliders or recalculate the box from PoseData.
ColliderBounds returns a value copy of _colliderBounds. Editing a temporary returned Bounds does not update the card unless that value is assigned back through the property or stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.EntityPose.PoseData
member.summary: The saved positions and rotations applied to an entity’s physics bodies by MarrowEntityPoseDecorator.

remarks.para: MarrowEntityPose.bodyPoses contains one SimpleTransform per recorded body: a three-number position offset in the same distance units used by Unity Transform positions and a quaternion rotation, a four-number orientation rather than angles in degrees. The offsets and orientations are relative to the entity root’s position and rotation, not each body’s immediate parent.

When applied, the entity rotates each stored offset by its current root rotation, adds its current root position, and combines the root rotation with the stored body rotation. For example, an offset of (0, 0, 0.5) adds 0.5 of those distance units along the entity root’s forward direction. The checked conversion neither converts offsets to meters nor multiplies them by the root’s scale.

Body poses are matched by array index, so the stored order must match the target entity’s body array. More pose entries than available bodies can fail; fewer entries leave the remaining bodies untouched by this loop. The pose object, its array, and each referenced target body must be present.

PoseData and _poseData expose the same object. Changing it alters a later application; the property setter does not apply the pose immediately. The checked card JSON serializer does not write this body array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.EntityPose.PosePreviewMesh
member.summary: The mesh loader reference packed with the card under PosePreviewMesh.

remarks.para: A mesh is the geometry used to draw a shape. This field holds a MarrowAssetT<Mesh> loader reference rather than the mesh or a scene renderer. ExportPackedAssets includes the reference, and packed-asset import can replace it from a saved asset identifier.

PosePreviewMesh and _posePreviewMesh expose the same object. Setting the reference does not load a mesh or display it by itself. The checked ExportPackedAssets requires a nonnull reference object even when no mesh has been loaded; setting this field to null makes that export path fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.EntityPose.Spawnable
member.summary: The SpawnableCrateReference identifying the prefab description associated with this recorded pose.

remarks.para: A prefab is a saved object template. This reference stores its warehouse barcode; it is not a spawned object. Use an arrangement recorded for the same body structure and order when applying the pose to a scene entity.

Pack writes the reference’s Barcode.ID as spawnable, and Unpack can replace this reference from that value. The checked MarrowEntityPoseDecorator applies PoseData to the GameObject reported by its spawner; it does not read this field to choose or spawn a different crate.
Spawnable and _spawnable expose the same reference. Replacing it does not spawn an entity, rebuild PoseData, or reapply a pose to an existing entity.
