member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.Asset
member.summary: In the base implementation, this property returns the current operation’s result when the handle is valid and that result is a Unity object; otherwise returns null.

remarks.para: Load the asset first through LoadAsset or LoadAssetAsync; reading this property does not start a request. This base getter checks handle validity and result type, but does not require IsDone or a successful operation status.

IsDone distinguishes a completed operation from an operation still waiting, but completion alone does not prove a usable asset loaded. Wait for the returned load task and handle its result or failure when code needs the requested asset. A null Asset can mean no valid handle or no compatible Unity object result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.AssetGUID
member.summary: The asset catalog key passed to Addressables when this reference starts a new load.

remarks.para: AssetGUID exposes the stored _assetGUID text, returning an empty string for a null field. Common crate packing writes this identifier when the crate has a nonnull MainAsset reference. DataCard packing writes its asset identifier only when IsBundledDataCard() is true, the DataCardAsset reference is nonnull, and its AssetGUID is nonempty. The identifier is not the warehouse barcode that identifies the crate or card description.

Changing the stored text does not invalidate an existing operation handle. A later load can still reuse that handle and return the old asset. In the base path, releasing the cached handle first lets a subsequent request start a load using the changed key. A field edit alone does not load or release anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.AssetType
member.summary: The cached type description reported by this asset reference; the base getter fills it with UnityEngine.Object when absent.

remarks.para: This is a type object, not the loaded asset. The base getter uses _assetType if already set, and otherwise stores UnityEngine.Object there. It does not inspect Asset.GetType to discover a loaded result’s concrete type.

Packed-asset exporters use the virtual AssetType as part of their reference records. Changing the cached type description does not convert an already loaded object. LoadAssetAsync requests its own generic TObject type; the checked base loading routine does not choose that type from this cached field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.IsDone
member.summary: True when the stored operation handle is valid and reports completion.

remarks.para: An unused or released handle gives false. A completed failed operation can also be done, so this is a completion check rather than a success guarantee. Reading it does not start loading or wait for a task.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.IsLoading
member.summary: True while the stored handle is valid and its operation has not completed.

remarks.para: It is false for an unused or released handle and false after completion. A false value alone does not tell whether the asset was successfully loaded. LoadAssetAsync uses this state to reuse a pending operation instead of starting another request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.LoadTask
member.summary: Returns a default already completed UniTask with a null Unity object result in the base implementation.

remarks.para: The base setter ignores its argument, and the getter does not read OperationHandle. This property therefore does not represent an in-progress load in the base class and does not initiate loading.
Await the task returned by LoadAssetAsync to wait for that request. LoadTask is virtual, so a specialized subclass can provide its own stored task behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset.OperationHandle
member.summary: The cached Addressables operation that supplies the loading state and asset result for this reference.

remarks.para: A handle is a small value identifying an asynchronous operation and its version. The base loader stores it when starting a load; IsLoading and IsDone query it, Asset reads its result, and later load requests reuse it while valid. The no-argument base ReleaseAsset releases it first, then clears the stored handle.

OperationHandle returns a value copy of _operationHandle. Reading a copy does not start another request or create a separate loading operation. Assigning a raw stored handle does not automatically release the previous one or update the identifier.
LoadTask is a separate virtual property. In this base class it returns a default completed task, so use the task returned by LoadAssetAsync when waiting for this operation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset._assetGUID
member.summary: The raw nullable asset-catalog identifier stored for later Addressables loads.

remarks.para: This raw backing field holds the identifier text as supplied and can be null. The get_AssetGUID accessor exposed as AssetGUID is different: it returns String.Empty when this field is null. Common crate packing writes the identifier when a MainAsset reference exists; DataCard packing writes it only for a bundled card with a nonnull asset reference and a nonempty identifier. Neither reading nor changing the field resolves an Addressables key, starts a load, or writes the warehouse barcode.

Changing the stored text does not invalidate an existing operation handle. A later load can still reuse that handle and return the old asset. In the base path, releasing the cached handle first lets a subsequent request start a load using the changed key. A field edit alone does not load or release anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset._assetType
member.summary: The cached type field; direct reads can return null until the base AssetType getter lazily stores UnityEngine.Object.

remarks.para: This field is a cached type object, not the loaded asset. Reading _assetType directly returns its current value, including null; field access does not call AssetType or trigger initialization. The base AssetType getter uses the cached value when present and, when null, lazily stores typeof(UnityEngine.Object). It does not inspect Asset.GetType to discover a loaded result’s concrete type.

Packed-asset exporters use the virtual AssetType as part of their reference records. Changing the cached type description does not convert an already loaded object. LoadAssetAsync requests its own generic TObject type; the checked base loading routine does not choose that type from this cached field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset._operationHandle
member.summary: The cached Addressables operation that supplies the loading state and asset result for this reference.

remarks.para: A handle is a small value identifying an asynchronous operation and its version. The base loader stores it when starting a load; IsLoading and IsDone query it, Asset reads its result, and later load requests reuse it while valid. The no-argument base ReleaseAsset releases it first, then clears the stored handle.

OperationHandle returns a value copy of _operationHandle. Reading a copy does not start another request or create a separate loading operation. Assigning a raw stored handle does not automatically release the previous one or update the identifier.
LoadTask is a separate virtual property. In this base class it returns a default completed task, so use the task returned by LoadAssetAsync when waiting for this operation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.Crates
member.summary: Alternative spawn-crate identities accepted by the query’s crate group.

remarks.para: For MarrowEntity and MarrowBody targets, a nonempty list compares each reference’s Barcode with the SpawnableCrate Barcode recorded by the entity’s Poolee. A Poolee is the component tracking an object created by the spawn pool. Matching any one listed identifier passes this group; missing pool or crate information fails it.
An empty list passes the crate group. This list selects acceptable origins for existing targets; adding a reference does not spawn or load its crate. Keep the list and its entries nonnull.
The checked Matches overloads read this list when called. Replacing or editing it changes their next crate test without calling the query’s Cache method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.TagCrateOperator
member.summary: Chooses whether the tag group and the crate group must both pass, or either group may pass.

remarks.para: And requires both groups to pass. Or requires either group to pass; it does not change the rule that every tag condition must pass within the tag group, or that any listed crate may pass within the crate group.

An empty tag list and an empty crate list each count as a passing group. Therefore Or with either list empty accepts every otherwise valid target. For example, use And with no crate restrictions when you want the tags alone to filter objects.
The matching routines evaluate both groups before combining their results. Or does not make null lists or broken references safe.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.Tags
member.summary: Tag conditions that must all pass for the query’s tag group.

remarks.para: Each TagQuery names a BoneTag identifier. With Invert false, the target must have that tag; with Invert true, the target must lack it. Every listed condition must pass, so requiring tag A and excluding tag B accepts targets with A and without B.

An empty list passes the tag group. These are BoneTag identifiers on the target’s TagList, rather than the separate text tags on a warehouse crate. Keep the list, its entries and their BoneTag references nonnull.
The checked Matches overloads read this list when called. Replacing or editing it changes their next tag test without calling the query’s Cache method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery._crates
member.summary: Stores the same alternative spawn-crate references exposed by Crates.

remarks.para: For MarrowEntity and MarrowBody targets, a nonempty list compares each reference’s Barcode with the SpawnableCrate Barcode recorded by the entity’s Poolee. A Poolee is the component tracking an object created by the spawn pool. Matching any one listed identifier passes this group; missing pool or crate information fails it.
An empty list passes the crate group. This list selects acceptable origins for existing targets; adding a reference does not spawn or load its crate. Keep the list and its entries nonnull.
The checked Matches overloads read this list when called. Replacing or editing it changes their next crate test without calling the query’s Cache method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery._operator
member.summary: Stores the And or Or choice exposed by TagCrateOperator.

remarks.para: And requires both groups to pass. Or requires either group to pass; it does not change the rule that every tag condition must pass within the tag group, or that any listed crate may pass within the crate group.

An empty tag list and an empty crate list each count as a passing group. Therefore Or with either list empty accepts every otherwise valid target. For example, use And with no crate restrictions when you want the tags alone to filter objects.
The matching routines evaluate both groups before combining their results. Or does not make null lists or broken references safe.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery._tags
member.summary: Stores the same required or excluded BoneTag conditions exposed by Tags.

remarks.para: Each TagQuery names a BoneTag identifier. With Invert false, the target must have that tag; with Invert true, the target must lack it. Every listed condition must pass, so requiring tag A and excluding tag B accepts targets with A and without B.

An empty list passes the tag group. These are BoneTag identifiers on the target’s TagList, rather than the separate text tags on a warehouse crate. Keep the list, its entries and their BoneTag references nonnull.
The checked Matches overloads read this list when called. Replacing or editing it changes their next tag test without calling the query’s Cache method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.crateQuickLookup
member.summary: Distinct alternative crate identifiers accumulated by Cache.

remarks.para: Cache adds identifiers from crate references without clearing old entries. Removing a condition from its list does not remove its identifier here.

The checked MarrowBody, MarrowEntity and ITaggable Matches overloads use the condition lists instead of this query set. Editing this set alone does not change their matching result. Their tag membership tests use the target’s TagList cache, not this set.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.tagExclusionQuickLookup
member.summary: Distinct excluded BoneTag identifiers accumulated by Cache.

remarks.para: Cache adds identifiers from inverted tag conditions without clearing old entries. Removing a condition from its list does not remove its identifier here.

The checked MarrowBody, MarrowEntity and ITaggable Matches overloads use the condition lists instead of this query set. Editing this set alone does not change their matching result. Their tag membership tests use the target’s TagList cache, not this set.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery.tagQuickLookup
member.summary: Distinct required BoneTag identifiers accumulated by Cache.

remarks.para: Cache adds identifiers from non-inverted tag conditions without clearing old entries. Removing a condition from its list does not remove its identifier here.

The checked MarrowBody, MarrowEntity and ITaggable Matches overloads use the condition lists instead of this query set. Editing this set alone does not change their matching result. Their tag membership tests use the target’s TagList cache, not this set.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Pallet.ChangeLog.version
member.summary: The release-version label for this individual note; changing it does not change the pallet’s own Version.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.Active
member.summary: Stored active flag in the manifest’s installation metadata.

remarks.para: Pack and Unpack preserve this flag as active, and CopyTo copies it. A newly constructed record starts with the flag true before any pallet has been loaded.

The setter only changes this boolean. It does not invoke a warehouse load/unload operation or switch Addressables locators, so the flag alone is not a reliable test that content is currently available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.Catalog
member.summary: The live Addressables resource locator associated with this pallet’s catalog.

remarks.para: A resource locator maps asset-loader identifiers to locations from which Addressables can obtain assets. This is separate from warehouse Barcode lookup and from CatalogPath, the catalog’s file path.

Warehouse pallet loading assigns a successfully obtained locator, and UnloadPallet removes that locator when it removes the tracked catalog. Replacing this field alone does not add or remove a locator in Addressables.
This runtime reference is shared by CopyTo but is not written or restored by manifest Pack/Unpack.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.CatalogPath
member.summary: File path identifying the pallet’s Addressables content catalog.

remarks.para: The catalog describes where its assets can be found; this path is separate from the pallet-description JSON file and the manifest file. Warehouse manifest setup stores the catalog path used by loading.
Changing this string does not load a new catalog. Pack and Unpack preserve it as catalogPath; CopyTo copies it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.EXTENSION_NAME
member.summary: The manifest filename suffix, manifest, used after a separating period.

remarks.para: For example, a pallet barcode Maker.PuzzlePack becomes Maker.PuzzlePack.manifest in the default manifest path. This identifies the installation record; the pallet content description uses a different JSON filename.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.InstalledDate
member.summary: Recorded installation-time text, using UTC Unix milliseconds when set by SetInstalledDateToNow.

remarks.para: The helper stores an integer count of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as a string. For generated values, an increase of 1000 means one second later. This is wall-clock time, not game elapsed time or a frame count.

The ordinary setter accepts text, and Unpack restores text without validating that format. The helper can overwrite the value repeatedly; it does not enforce a one-time installation record. Pack preserves it as installedDate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.ManifestPath
member.summary: The manifest record’s own file path, computed and cached on first read when needed.

remarks.para: If the stored path is null or empty and Pallet is a live Unity object, the getter builds the runtime Mods-folder path from that pallet’s Barcode and .manifest, then stores it. Without a live Pallet, it returns the current empty or null value.
Once nonempty, this path is returned unchanged even if the pallet or barcode changes. Clear it before another read if you want the default path recomputed from the current Pallet.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest.ModListing
member.summary: Optional mod-repository listing data associated with this installed pallet.

remarks.para: The listing describes the package with information such as creator, version, thumbnail URL and platform targets. It is separate from the loaded Pallet description.

Pack includes a reference to a nonnull listing, and Unpack attempts to resolve a present listing reference through the object store. If resolution reports failure, the current listing is cleared to null; a missing key leaves it unchanged. Warehouse manifest setup can attach a supplied listing or retain a stored one. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.Barcode
member.summary: The warehouse lookup identifier for this description.

remarks.para: The warehouse is the game’s catalog of registered descriptions. Crate, data-card and pallet references use this Barcode’s ID string to find registered descriptions. It is separate from the asset-loader identifiers used to load their prefabs, scenes or sound assets.

Assigning a new Barcode only changes this object’s stored reference. It does not rekey existing warehouse entries or load content. Complete identifier setup before registration, or explicitly manage registration when changing identities.

GenerateBarcode creates or replaces an absent or invalid Barcode before calling the derived generator. Base Pack requires both a Barcode object and an output JSON object before it writes the ID and other metadata. Unpack replaces the Barcode object only when a barcode field is present.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.Description
member.summary: Explanatory text stored with the warehouse description.

remarks.para: Pack writes it as description, and Unpack replaces it only when that field is present. For example, it can describe what a content item contains or how a player uses it.
The base setter only stores this metadata. Editing it does not rebuild or load the item’s actual prefab, scene or audio asset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.PackedAssets
member.summary: The reusable list of supporting-asset reference groups used by export and packing code.

remarks.para: Each PackedAsset entry has a title naming the group, an asset reference, and an optional list of sub-asset references with their own titles. These references identify supporting assets to the loader. The getter returns the actual list, so it can be edited despite having no public setter. The base ExportPackedAssets clears it and returns it empty; overrides can rebuild it from the derived description’s references.

PackJsonPackedAssets calls the virtual export before serializing the list, so manually added entries can be overwritten during packing. For example, MonoDisc exports its AudioClip reference and GameObjectCrate exports its preview-mesh reference.

These entries identify assets and groups; they do not themselves contain every loaded game object or a saved bundle file. Inspect them after the appropriate export when you need the current supporting references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.Redacted
member.summary: Marks a crate for exclusion from lists filtered to hide redacted descriptions.

remarks.para: For example, AssetWarehouse.FilterCrates with NonRedactedCrateFilter removes entries whose Redacted flag is true. The checked filters that also enforce unlock requirements reject redacted entries even when the unlock condition passes.

Changing the flag only stores it. It does not remove warehouse registration or alter an already spawned object. The checked CrateSpawner spawn path does not enforce it; list filtering and direct spawning are separate operations.
Pack and Unpack preserve the flag as redacted. A menu needs to use the corresponding filtering rule and refresh its displayed list to reflect that rule.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.Title
member.summary: The human-readable label for this warehouse description.

remarks.para: For example, SpawnGun uses a selected spawnable crate’s Title as its item text. This label is separate from the warehouse Barcode used to identify the content.

The setter only stores the text; it does not automatically regenerate the Barcode or update an already displayed label. Crate, data-card and pallet generators use the title when building identifiers, while a valid existing ID can be preserved unless generation is forced.
Pack writes title. A present title during Unpack updates both the stored title and this Unity object’s name; a missing title leaves them alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable.Unlockable
member.summary: Marks a crate as requiring a player unlock in filters that enforce unlock requirements.

remarks.para: This is a requirement flag, not the player’s current unlocked state. The checked filters obtain the active save’s unlock count for the crate’s Barcode separately.

For example, FilterCrates with UnlockedNotUnlockableAndNotRedactedFilter removes an unlockable crate when that count is less than one. With a recorded unlock, that unlock condition passes; Redacted can still exclude it. With Unlockable false, this filter does not require a recorded unlock.

Changing this flag does not grant or remove a saved unlock. Its setter only stores the flag, and Pack/Unpack preserve it as unlockable. The checked CrateSpawner spawn path does not enforce this flag, so it is not a universal barrier to direct spawning.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.ScannableReference.Scannable
member.summary: Resolves a live registered warehouse description using this reference’s Barcode.
member.returns: The registered description, or null when lookup cannot resolve it.

remarks.para: AssetWarehouse is the game’s catalog of Scannable descriptions. This base getter returns null before that catalog is ready or when the identifier cannot resolve to a live data entry. It checks the primary registry and supported old-barcode aliases; it does not wait for loading or start an asset load.

The base getter looks up the broad Scannable category and does not consult virtual ScannableType. Accessing this member through the base reference can therefore return a crate, data card or pallet. Use a typed reference’s own typed getter when you require a particular category.

The result is the catalog’s description/data entry. Its main asset is separate: a prefab is a saved reusable object template, and a scene object is an instance placed in a level. This lookup returns neither the loaded template nor a spawned scene object.

The base Scannable getter does not consult this virtual property and still requests the broad Scannable category, which includes crates, data cards and pallets. A declared category alone is therefore not a type check on that base getter’s result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagList.CachedTagBarcodes
member.summary: The distinct BoneTag identifiers available to cached tag-membership tests.

remarks.para: MarrowQuery’s target-tag tests use this set to decide whether required or excluded tags are present. The entries are Barcode identifiers from BoneTagReference objects, not loaded BoneTag assets.
The getter performs the first build when initialCache is false. Later Tags edits are not noticed by the getter automatically; call UpdateCache(false) to refresh from the lists.

The actual set is returned, so edits affect membership tests using it. A rebuild clears and repopulates the set, overwriting those manual cache edits. Replacing the set does not reset initialCache; setting it to null after initialization can therefore leave the getter returning null until you rebuild.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagList.InheritTags
member.summary: Optional object supplying a TagList whose references can be merged into this list.

remarks.para: When rebuilding, this list first asks the source’s TagList to initialize if needed, then appends source tag references missing from its own Tags list. It keeps the same reference objects rather than creating copies.

Inherited entries become part of the local Tags list. Removing a tag from the source or setting InheritTags to null does not remove previously copied entries here. To remove an inherited entry, first make sure the source no longer supplies it or set InheritTags to null. Then remove its retained reference from this list’s Tags and call UpdateCache(false). If the source still supplies the entry, refreshing adds it again.

Assigning a source only stores it; call UpdateCache(false) after changing an already initialized list. That refresh initializes the source only if needed, rather than forcing every already initialized ancestor to rebuild.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagList.Tags
member.summary: The local BoneTag references from which cached tag membership is built.

remarks.para: The getter returns the actual list, so you can add or remove references despite Tags having no public setter. References name BoneTags by Barcode; they are separate from the text tags used on pallet or crate descriptions.
Inheritance refresh can append source references to this list. Those entries remain local afterward, so clearing InheritTags does not restore an earlier local-only list.
After edits, call UpdateCache(false) before relying on CachedTagBarcodes or MarrowQuery target-tag results. An already initialized cache otherwise keeps its previous membership.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagQuery.BoneTag
member.summary: The naming the tag whose presence or absence this condition tests.

remarks.para: This reference’s Barcode holds the tag’s identifying ID. MarrowQuery compares it with TagList.CachedTagBarcodes, the set of tag IDs stored by the target’s TagList for matching. It checks the ID rather than loading the BoneTag description; use a nonnull reference with the intended tag ID. After changing the target’s tag list, call that TagList’s UpdateCache(false) to rebuild its set before matching again.
Changing this reference changes the next checked MarrowQuery match without calling MarrowQuery.Cache. Invert determines whether that identifier must be present or absent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagQuery.Invert
member.summary: Chooses whether this tag condition requires the tag to be absent instead of present.

remarks.para: BoneTag.Barcode holds the selected tag’s identifying ID. False requires that ID in the target’s TagList.CachedTagBarcodes, the stored set of tag IDs used for matching; true requires it absent. After editing the target’s tag list, call that TagList’s UpdateCache(false) to rebuild the set before matching again.

For example, a required tag A and an inverted tag B require A to be present and B absent. Every condition in MarrowQuery.Tags must pass for the combined tag-rule result to pass. TagCrateOperator then combines this result with the separate crate-matching result, which tests the query’s listed crate references.

This negates one tag condition, not the entire MarrowQuery result. With TagCrateOperator set to Or, a passing crate-matching result can still accept an object whose combined tag-rule result fails. Changing this flag affects the next checked match without calling MarrowQuery.Cache.

It checks the ID rather than loading the BoneTag description; use a nonnull reference with the intended tag ID. After changing the target’s tag list, call that TagList’s UpdateCache(false) to rebuild its set before matching again.
Changing this reference changes the next checked MarrowQuery match without calling MarrowQuery.Cache. Invert determines whether that identifier must be present or absent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagQuery._invert
member.summary: Unity saves this Exclude boolean with the condition; Invert exposes the same value to require the tag’s absence instead of its presence.

remarks.para: BoneTag.Barcode holds the selected tag’s identifying ID. False requires that ID in the target’s TagList.CachedTagBarcodes, the stored set of tag IDs used for matching; true requires it absent. After editing the target’s tag list, call that TagList’s UpdateCache(false) to rebuild the set before matching again.

For example, a required tag A and an inverted tag B require A to be present and B absent. Every condition in MarrowQuery.Tags must pass for the combined tag-rule result to pass. TagCrateOperator then combines this result with the separate crate-matching result, which tests the query’s listed crate references.

This negates one tag condition, not the entire MarrowQuery result. With TagCrateOperator set to Or, a passing crate-matching result can still accept an object whose combined tag-rule result fails. Changing this flag affects the next checked match without calling MarrowQuery.Cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.HandToGenericGripState.isRaycastHit
member.summary: The result of the most recent surface ray test, which the hover update checks before rebuilding the hand's grip target.

remarks.para: A raycast tests whether a straight line meets a collider, a shape the physics system detects. ValidateGripScore chooses a nearby collider without an attached Rigidbody, the component for simulated mass and motion, then tests a ray up to 0.25 meters long against that shape. It stores that ray test's true or false result here.

This flag alone does not mean a grip was accepted or a hand has attached. After a hit, scoring also checks the surface normal, the direction pointing out of the surface. Its direction-agreement score with world up, the scene's positive Y direction, must be at least 0.75. This score is called a dot product: 1 means the directions line up, 0 means they are at right angles, and -1 means they point opposite ways.

The other required direction-agreement score is at least 0.5 between the direction into the surface, opposite its outward normal, and the back-of-hand direction. Scoring derives that hand direction from the handle's rotated right axis, reversing it for the other hand. These scores have no length or angle units. Rejecting either direction check leaves a true ray-test result in this flag.

Scoring also leaves this flag unchanged when it finds no eligible collider to raycast, so it can retain an older true result. The hover callback, a routine run for a hand considering this grip, skips rebuilding its target when the stored flag is false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.HandToGenericGripState.targetColliderCount
member.summary: How many entries in the per-hand collider buffer came from the latest nearby-surface query.

remarks.para: ValidateGripScore runs a sphere query around the hand's palm and writes the number of results here. A collider is a shape the physics system detects. The query ignores triggers, colliders used to detect overlaps, and applies a layer filter to select which categories of objects it checks. The normal buffer has space for 16 colliders, so this is a count of returned entries, not proof that every nearby shape was found.

This count is taken before the grip rejects colliders with an attached Rigidbody, the component for simulated mass and motion. It can therefore include movable-body shapes. For example, a count of 3 means only entries 0, 1 and 2 of the 16-slot buffer belong to this query; later slots can contain older values.

When the hand's stored hit flag allows a hover update, the grip copies this many entries from each recorded hand into its additionalGripColliders array, a list of collider shapes for the hand to ignore. Later hand attachment code uses those shapes to disable collision pairs with the hand; building this list during hover does not itself disable those collisions. The count does not report the number of hands attached or the number of accepted grip surfaces.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.HandToGenericGripState.worldHandleTransform
member.summary: Working copy of the hand's handle pose whose rotation helps aim the surface-grip target.

remarks.para: A pose is a position and rotation. ValidateGripScore first copies the hand's current world handle pose here, with position in meters along the scene's axes and rotation stored as a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of orientation.

On the accepted surface path, it converts this pose into the WorldGrip object's frame: position becomes an offset from that object in its rotated axes, and rotation becomes relative to the object. This pose conversion ignores object scale, so the position offset remains in meters. If surface validation fails, this conversion is not reached and the field can still contain the initial world pose. Its name does not guarantee one fixed coordinate frame.

The hover update expects the accepted, relative rotation. It combines that rotation with the object's current world rotation, then turns the hand to line up with the surface. It places the target at the separately stored raycastPoint; this field's position is not the surface contact point. The pose is a saved value from scoring, not a live Transform component or proof that the hand has grabbed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.genericHandStates
member.summary: Stores each scored ’s surface-hit data and nearby colliders for later hover updates.

remarks.para: The dictionary is created empty in the WorldGrip constructor, the setup that runs when a new WorldGrip object is created. ValidateGripScore adds a tracking record the first time it scores a particular hand, then fills that record with the hand handle, nearby collider results and raycast-hit flag. Each record starts with a buffer for 16 collider references; targetColliderCount identifies how many entries from the start of that buffer belong to the recorded query.

A collider is an invisible collision shape; a raycast tests a line against those shapes. A surface normal points straight out of a surface. The hand handle is the hand’s grip-reference position and orientation.

On the accepted-surface path, the hit point, surface normal, back-of-hand direction and hand-handle transform are converted into coordinates relative to this WorldGrip object. Positions describe distances in metres; normals and hand-facing vectors describe directions. The hover update later uses those saved values to reconstruct a world target.

These records describe scoring and cached geometry, not which hands are currently attached. For example, two hands scored near the same tabletop have separate target data. The hover update also gathers nearby colliders from all dictionary entries, even entries whose hit flag is false. A true hit flag records a raycast hit and does not by itself prove that every later surface-score check passed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.ignoreColliders
member.summary: Provides the temporary collider list copied into the grip’s additional hand-collision exemptions.

remarks.para: A collider is the invisible shape used for contact and collision tests. This list starts empty in the WorldGrip constructor. When a hover update has a recorded hit for its hand, the update clears the list, adds each tracked hand’s nearby collider results up to that hand’s recorded count, and copies the list into additionalGripColliders.

The list can contain results from both hands and repeated references to the same collider. It is rebuilt from the scoring records, so hand-written changes to the list are replaced by the next eligible hover update. A hover update with no stored hand entry or a false hit flag returns before rebuilding it.

During hand-joint preparation, the additionalGripColliders array is used when ignoring collisions between the hand’s collision shapes and the grip’s nearby shapes on the static-attachment path. This helps the hand occupy its grip point without being pushed away by that surface. Copying this list prepares the inputs for that later step; the list itself does not switch Unity collision checks on or off.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.cur
member.summary: Records whether this zone link is active for this activator through either its primary or secondary role.

remarks.para: An activator is an entity, such as the player, whose zone entry is accepted by ZoneLink.activatorTags. This flag belongs to one activator and one link; it does not say whether every object in the zone is enabled. A primary link is the link selected by the manager from the activator's active zones. Its outgoing linked neighbors become secondary links.

The manager compares the old cur with nxt, copies nxt into cur, and calls the link's OnEnter or OnExit when the value changes. These callbacks let listeners respond to zone activation. Switching between primary and secondary can leave cur true, so the combined enter callback does not repeat just because the role changed. Writing cur directly does not call these methods immediately; it changes the old value the next zone-state solve compares with its rebuilt nxt, so it can suppress a later OnEnter/OnExit notification if the values match or cause one if they differ.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.curPri
member.summary: Records whether this link is the manager's selected primary zone link for this activator.

remarks.para: The activator is the entity responsible for activating the zone, such as the player. When zones overlap, the manager uses its active-zone stack to choose a primary link; this flag does not simply mean the entity touches the zone's trigger.

During a state solve, nxtPri replaces curPri. A false-to-true change calls OnPrimaryEnter; a true-to-false change calls OnPrimaryExit. The combined cur flag can stay true if the link remains active as a secondary neighbor. Treat this as the manager's recorded result: assigning it yourself does not invoke a primary callback and can change what the next comparison detects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.curSec
member.summary: Records whether this link is active as an outgoing linked neighbor of this activator's selected primary link.

remarks.para: For example, if link A lists B in its outgoing zone links and A becomes primary for the player, B becomes secondary even though the player need not be inside B. This lets a linked area respond before it becomes the primary area. Being merely in the same connected group is not enough: the solve uses the primary link's outgoing neighbors.

The manager copies nxtSec into curSec and calls OnSecondaryEnter or OnSecondaryExit when the value changes. A secondary exit can happen while cur remains true because the same link is becoming primary. These are role flags, not mutually exclusive enum values; the solver sets the two channels separately. Writing curSec directly does not call listeners immediately; it changes the old value compared with the next rebuilt nxtSec, so it can suppress a later OnSecondaryEnter/OnSecondaryExit notification if they match or cause one if they differ.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.nxt
member.summary: Holds the combined primary-or-secondary activation result being calculated before the manager applies it to .

remarks.para: The manager clears this flag for the connected group being solved, then sets it for the selected primary link and that link's outgoing neighbors. It compares the finished result with cur to decide whether to send OnEnter or OnExit.

This is working state inside the solve, not an instruction scheduled for the next Unity frame. The solve applies it before returning. Setting nxt yourself does not activate objects or send events, and a later solve for the group recalculates it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.nxtPri
member.summary: Holds whether this link is being selected as primary in the current activation calculation.

remarks.para: The manager clears nxtPri for the connected group, then sets it on the chosen active link for this activator. Primary means the manager's selected active area, rather than every zone the entity overlaps.

The same solve copies it into curPri, then calls registered listeners’ OnPrimaryEnter or OnPrimaryExit methods if the value differs from the previous curPri result. This is a calculated flag, not a request to make this zone primary on the next frame. Editing it does not update the active-zone stack, and the next solve can overwrite it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState.nxtSec
member.summary: Holds whether this link is being activated as an outgoing neighbor of the chosen primary link in the current calculation.

remarks.para: For example, with a link from A to B, choosing A as primary sets B's nxtSec and nxt to true for that activator. A link farther along a chain is not automatically secondary merely because it belongs to the same connected group.

The manager clears and rebuilds this flag while solving the group, then copies it into curSec and calls registered listeners’ OnSecondaryEnter or OnSecondaryExit methods when the result changes. It is applied during the solve, not after a fixed number of frames. Assigning it yourself does not notify listeners or change the graph of zone links.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnCullApply
member.summary: Receives changed culling flags during the manager's Apply pass so the handler can update the object's culling response.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and its resolved culling boolean: true for culled, false for cleared. It runs only when the culling bit differs between resolved and applied. The manager records applied after the apply callbacks; it does not wait for any asynchronous work a handler starts.

For a standard MarrowEntity, GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds its components and has an activeSelf state. This handler normally turns that object off for a Cull request unless disable-on-cull is prevented or host/parasite conditions keep it active. Physics hibernation and MarrowBehaviour disabling occur separately in OnCullResolve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnCullResolve
member.summary: Receives the beginning of requested culling and the later release of its recorded inactive state.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and an inactive boolean. Resolve sends true when culling newly enters its requested state and its recorded completed flag is not already set. Complete sends false after all Hide, Cull, and Despawn requests clear and the resolved Cull flag is clear. In Update, completion also waits until the manager's resolve and apply queues empty.

A callback is a routine the manager calls for a processed status change. For a standard MarrowEntity, true hibernates rigid bodies (physics bodies), disables its MarrowBehaviour components (the entity's game-behavior components), and notifies cull handlers. False releases the Culling hibernation source, enables those components, and notifies uncull handlers. Clearing Cull while Hide remains requested can postpone this false callback, and another hibernation source can keep physics asleep after Culling is released.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnDespawnApply
member.summary: Receives changes to the resolved despawned-state flag so the handler can update lifecycle notifications and activation.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and a boolean: true means the Despawn flag is set; false means it is clear. The manager calls it when that bit differs between resolved and applied, then records the resolved mask as applied after the apply callbacks.

A Tracker is a per-collider component associated with a body; it stores its Collider and registered deactivation actions. For a standard MarrowEntity, when entering Despawn this handler sends despawn notifications, calls OnDeactivate on each associated Tracker, then checks GameObject activation. OnDeactivate invokes registered Collider-action listeners; it does not disable the Tracker or its Collider. When clearing Despawn, activation is checked before spawn notifications. The handler itself does not remove the entity from or obtain it from an object pool.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnDespawnResolve
member.summary: Receives the beginning of a requested despawned state and the later release of its recorded inactive flag.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and an inactive boolean. Resolve sends true for a newly requested Despawn channel that is not already recorded in completed. Complete sends false only when all three requested inactive channels are clear and resolved no longer contains Despawn. Clearing this channel while Hide or Cull remains requested does not release it here.

A callback is a routine the manager calls for a processed status change. An object pool is the game's reuse system for objects removed from active play. This callback slot supplies no pool operation by itself. Attach a routine if your status needs a response at this phase; leaving it empty does not stop the manager from recording and processing the channel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnHideApply
member.summary: Receives changes to the resolved hiding flag so the handler can hide or show the object.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and its resolved Hide boolean: true for hidden, false for cleared. It runs only when that bit differs between resolved and applied, and the manager updates applied after the apply callbacks.

A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components and has an activeSelf state. For a standard MarrowEntity, the callback notifies hide or unhide listeners and checks GameObject activation. Showing does not override a remaining Cull or Despawn flag. A custom status can implement a different response in this callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.OnHideResolve
member.summary: Receives the beginning of requested hiding and the later release of its recorded inactive flag.

remarks.para: The arguments are this status and an inactive boolean. Resolve sends true for a newly requested Hide channel not already recorded in completed. Complete sends false only after all requested Hide, Cull, and Despawn channels are clear and resolved no longer contains Hide.

For example, clearing Hide while Cull is still requested can send a false hide-apply callback without releasing this resolve callback yet. These two phases therefore have different timing; neither attaching a handler nor changing the callback field queues a request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.applied
member.summary: Records the resolved flags after the manager has dispatched the apply callbacks for changed channels.

remarks.para: Apply compares this mask with resolved to decide which callbacks need to run, then copies resolved here. It advances even when a callback is unassigned, and it is not an acknowledgement that asynchronous work launched by a callback finished. Writing it yourself can suppress a later changed-channel callback without performing that callback's object effect.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.completed
member.summary: Remembers which inactive resolve channels have been entered and still need their later false resolve callback released.

remarks.para: Resolve sets a channel's bit before sending its true OnHideResolve, OnCullResolve, or OnDespawnResolve callback. Complete clears the bit before sending false, after all requested inactive channels are clear and that channel's resolved bit is clear. The bits can be recorded even if no callback is assigned.

Despite the name, this is not a copy of applied or a signal that all work is finished. For example, it can still contain Cull after the culling request clears because Hide remains requested. Direct edits change which resolve callbacks are suppressed or released.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.request
member.summary: Holds the desired combination of Hide, Cull, and Despawn flags that the manager should process.

remarks.para: The status's Hide, Cull, and Despawn methods change one bit here, and the IsActive/IsHidden/IsCulled/IsDespawned queries read this mask. These changes are immediate bookkeeping, independent of whether the object's callbacks have run.

Use the manager's request methods when you need to change the flag and queue processing together. Assigning request directly does not add the status to a queue. Combining Hide | Cull requests both channels; None requests no inactive channel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus.resolved
member.summary: Records the request most recently accepted by the manager's Resolve pass and supplies the target flags for Apply.

remarks.para: Resolve compares request with this mask, handles newly entered inactive resolve channels, and records the current request here. Apply compares resolved with applied to choose the callbacks and their boolean arguments. This is pipeline state, not a separate guarantee about the object's actual activation or pool state.
A later queued request can overwrite it on another Resolve pass. Directly editing it can change or bypass callback comparisons without correctly updating the other masks and queues.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.RecycleDecorator._crateSpawner
member.summary: Selects the whose recycle listener list receives this decorator while enabled.

remarks.para: A CrateSpawner manages crate creation and recycling. Assign it before enabling this component: OnEnable adds this decorator to that spawner, and OnDisable removes it from the current reference. Changing the field while enabled does not move the existing registration.
OnRecycle is the method the spawner calls with the recycled GameObject, the Unity scene object it recycled. This is that object, not this decorator's own GameObject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.SpawnDecorator._crateSpawner
member.summary: Selects the CrateSpawner whose spawn and despawn notifications this decorator receives.

remarks.para: OnEnable subscribes using this reference and OnDisable removes the subscription using the reference then present. Assign it before enabling. Changing it by itself does not move an existing subscription; remove the old subscription before replacing the reference.
The GameObject passed to OnSpawn or OnDespawn is the object involved in that notification, not this spawner's GameObject. Registration does not replay earlier spawns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._bodyListeners
member.summary: Holds the listeners receiving this zone's body enter and exit reports.

remarks.para: Use matching RegisterZoneEventListener and UnregisterZoneEventListener overloads to maintain the list. Registration prevents duplicates and does not replay existing overlaps. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; these listeners supply enter and exit callbacks.

The first tracker for a body causes OnZoneBodyEnter after its count is stored. The last exit removes its count entry before OnZoneBodyExit. Enter runs after tracker enter; exit runs after entity exit when applicable and before tracker exit. Avoid null entries and editing the list during its enumeration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._bodyOverlapCounts
member.summary: Counts the accepted overlapping trackers belonging to each physical body.

remarks.para: A body is a physical part of an entity. Each new tracker increments its body's count; the first stores 1 and sends body enter. An exit decrements the count, removing the body entry and sending body exit when the result is below 1.

For example, two different trackers belonging to one body can give it a count of 2. The first to leave reduces it to 1 without a body exit; the last removes the entry and causes exit. These are accepted-tracker counts, not collision contacts, meters, or seconds. Let the zone maintain them rather than assigning values independently.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._deferredTriggerExitTracker
member.summary: Stores the single tracker whose exit was postponed because enter reports were still being dispatched.

remarks.para: ProcessTriggerExit writes this reference and sets _isTriggerExitDeferred when _isProcessingEnterEvents is true. Another deferred request overwrites the same reference; this is not a queue of every exit.

At the normal end of enter processing, the zone clears the enter flag, processes the saved exit in the same call, then clears the deferred flag and reference. Exit listeners reached through this path can still observe the deferred flag as true until that exit returns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._entityListeners
member.summary: Holds the listeners receiving this zone's entity enter and exit reports.

remarks.para: Use matching RegisterZoneEventListener and UnregisterZoneEventListener overloads to maintain the list. Registration prevents duplicates and does not replay existing overlaps. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; these listeners supply enter and exit callbacks.

The first tracker for an entity causes OnZoneEntityEnter after its count is stored. The last exit removes its count entry before OnZoneEntityExit. Enter runs after tracker and applicable body enter; exit runs before applicable body exit and tracker exit. Avoid null entries and editing the list during its enumeration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._entityOverlapCounts
member.summary: Counts the accepted overlapping trackers belonging to each whole entity.

remarks.para: An entity can contain several bodies and collision shapes. Each newly accepted tracker increments its entity's count; the first stores 1 and sends entity enter. An exit decrements it, removing the entry and sending entity exit when the result is below 1.

For example, different body parts of one object can keep its entity count above zero after one part leaves. Entity exit waits for its last counted tracker. These are tracker counts, not body counts or collision-contact counts. Changing the dictionary alone does not create a matching overlap or notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._isProcessingEnterEvents
member.summary: Is true during accepted-tracker enter processing, causing exit requests to be postponed until that processing finishes.

remarks.para: The tracker is added to _trackerOverlap before this becomes true. Tracker enter listeners run first, followed by body count updates and any first-body enter, then entity count updates and any first-entity enter. Those listeners see this flag true.

Normal completion clears it before processing the saved deferred exit. This coordinates routines calling back into the zone during a report; assigning it manually can alter exit handling without creating an overlap.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._isProcessingExitEvents
member.summary: Records that counted tracker-exit processing is underway.

remarks.para: An immediate exit removes the tracker from _trackerOverlap before setting this true. Entity and body exit reports, followed by tracker exit, occur while it is true; normal completion clears it after tracker listeners finish.

In the audited Zone lifecycle this flag is written and cleared but is not checked to block or defer another exit. Postponement uses _isProcessingEnterEvents instead. Do not treat this flag as a general reentrancy lock or an exit request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._isTriggerExitDeferred
member.summary: Records that an exit is waiting in the single saved tracker slot while enter processing finishes.

remarks.para: ProcessTriggerExit first saves _deferredTriggerExitTracker, then sets this true when the enter-processing flag is true. Multiple requests replace the saved tracker rather than accumulating a queue.

After enter reports finish, the enter flag is cleared, the saved exit runs synchronously, then this flag becomes false and the saved reference is cleared. It remains true during that exit's reports. It does not mean waiting for the next frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._trackerExitBuffer
member.summary: Temporarily holds a copy of recorded trackers for OnDisable cleanup.

remarks.para: OnDisable copies _trackerOverlap here, attempts ProcessTriggerExit on valid Unity entries, then clears this list. The copy lets exits remove trackers from the live set without invalidating the set enumeration.

This buffer is separate from postponed exits during enter dispatch, which use the single _deferredTriggerExitTracker reference. Editing the buffer alone does not send reports or remove recorded overlaps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._trackerListeners
member.summary: Holds the listeners receiving this zone's tracker enter and exit reports.

remarks.para: Use matching RegisterZoneEventListener and UnregisterZoneEventListener overloads to maintain the list. Registration prevents duplicates and does not replay existing overlaps. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; these listeners supply enter and exit callbacks.

OnZoneTrackerEnter runs after set insertion and setting _isProcessingEnterEvents true, but before body and entity count updates. OnZoneTrackerExit runs after removal and both count updates while _isProcessingExitEvents is true. Avoid null entries and editing the list during its enumeration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone._trackerOverlap
member.summary: Contains the unique trackers whose trigger overlaps this zone has accepted and not yet removed.

remarks.para: A tracker associates a collision shape with a body and entity. Acceptance requires a tracker found in the collider GameObject cache, an enabled and active zone, and tracker flags reporting both body and entity. Adding the same tracker again is ignored, even if more trigger reports reach the zone.

The set is updated before tracker enter and exit reports. Body and entity counts group its trackers separately, with first-count enter and last-count exit. This is recorded state, not a fresh physics query. Direct set edits do not update counts or send notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneChunkLoader.chunks
member.summary: Lists the SceneChunks this link requests when it becomes the selected primary link.

remarks.para: A SceneChunk groups one or more scene layers that the scene streamer manages as one loadable chunk. Primary means the zone manager selected this link by priority for an entity accepted by the linked ZoneLink's activatorTags filter in its connected group of zone links.

Configure a nonnull array with valid chunk references before activation. The callback requests each entry; the shared loader suppresses duplicate entries within its pending batch, but requests are not guaranteed to all enter one batch. An empty array makes no requests.

The shared loader reconciles a desired active set. Include every chunk this area needs to retain, because earlier active chunks omitted from that set can be unloaded before new chunks load. Changing the array alone does not load or unload scenes, and leaving primary activation does not automatically unload this array.

For each SceneChunk, the load step sets IsChunkLoaded to true, updates its ZoneCullers (components that manage entities and level assets in the chunk's zone), calls registered IChunkLoadable.OnChunkLoad handlers, and then fires the configured onChunkLoad event. These are per-chunk readiness signals; they do not make the request synchronous.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents._hasZoneEntered
member.summary: The component-wide flag that controls whether OnEnter attempts the optional one-shot event.

remarks.para: After the regular enter event returns, OnEnter checks this flag. If it is still false, OnEnter runs the optional one-shot event and writes the flag true after its listeners return, even if the event is absent. This flag records the one-shot gate; it is not a count of current occupants or a per-entity record.

OnExit and ZoneItem's inherited enable and disable methods do not clear it. Setting it false allows a later qualifying OnEnter call to try the one-shot event again; assigning either value alone sends no event. Regular listeners can change the flag before its check, and nested entry before its final write can affect whether the event repeats.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.onZoneEnter
member.summary: The optional event for each Zone entity-enter report that passes the inherited activatorTags filter, receiving the whole .

remarks.para: The event receives the whole entering MarrowEntity, not its individual Collider or the Zone component. A Tracker links one Collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity. The Zone groups Tracker overlaps by entity and reports entity enter when the first accepted tracked collider for that entity is counted; additional colliders do not create additional entity-enter reports while the count remains above zero.

activatorTags is a MarrowQuery filter configured with tag and crate rules. ZoneItem checks it before forwarding the report. Registering ZoneItem after an overlap began does not replay that earlier enter. OnEnter invokes this regular event before checking _hasZoneEntered, and its listeners can change the flag before the one-shot check. Attached callbacks are routines the event calls; they can, for example, start a sound or record progress.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.onZoneEnterOneShot
member.summary: The optional enter event run when _hasZoneEntered is still false after the regular enter event returns.

remarks.para: It receives the same whole MarrowEntity as onZoneEnter. OnEnter writes _hasZoneEntered true only after this event's listeners return, so they normally see the earlier false value. A nested entry before that write can invoke the event again.

The flag is shared by this ZoneEvents component across all entities; it is not once per entity and is not reset by exit or disable. OnEnter writes it true after the first eligible check even when this event is absent. Adding listeners later does not replay that attempt. A callback is a routine the event calls to perform or report an action.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.onZoneExit
member.summary: The optional event for each accepted Zone entity-exit report, carrying the whole .

remarks.para: A Tracker links one Collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity. The Zone reports entity exit when its last tracked collider leaves or is removed during Tracker or Zone cleanup; this report can therefore occur without physical movement. Before forwarding the report, ZoneItem checks the current activatorTags MarrowQuery, which uses its configured tag and crate rules. Calling OnExit directly bypasses that filter.
OnExit invokes this event without changing _hasZoneEntered. Exit does not rearm the one-shot enter event; listeners supply any cleanup action they need.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.Priority
member.summary: Returns the stored unitless rank used to choose this link against other active links in the same connected group.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone enter report passed this link's activatorTags query. A connected group is the set of ZoneLinks joined by configured connections, following incoming or outgoing connections. For each activator and connected group, the manager keeps active links in a priority-ordered list (called a stack in the code); the highest-ranked link at the top is primary.

Larger values win within that activator's group list. Equal-priority links are inserted after existing equals, so the most recently inserted equal link becomes the selected primary only when that tied rank is the highest active rank in the group. A newer link at a lower tied rank does not displace a higher-ranked active link. Different connected groups can have separate primary links.

This property reads the same value as priority. Sorting happens when links are inserted into the list; changing the field alone does not reorder a list already built. ZoneCuller also copies a link's rank when its own culler record is registered.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink._onActivatorDespawn

remarks.para: Its type is Action<GameObject>: a callback, meaning a routine called to perform or report an action, accepting a GameObject when invoked. No registration, assignment, or invocation of this field was found in the audited 21 ZoneLink methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink._zone
member.summary: Selects the Zone trigger area whose whole-entity overlap reports supply potential activators for this link.

remarks.para: This reference can be configured in the Inspector; Reset fills it from the same GameObject. OnEnable subscribes and OnDisable removes the subscription using the reference then present. Assign a valid Zone before enabling.

A Collider is a shape Unity checks for trigger contact. Its GameObject is the scene object that holds its components. A Tracker is the component the Zone finds on that GameObject; it links the Collider to a MarrowBody (the physical body) and a MarrowEntity (the larger in-game entity that can have multiple bodies).

The Zone accepts collider reports only while the GameObject carrying the Zone is active in the scene and the Zone component is enabled, and when the Tracker has both body and entity links. It counts distinct Trackers for each entity, reports enter for the first counted Tracker, and reports exit when the last counted Tracker is removed. Tracker or Zone cleanup can also produce an exit without physical movement. This link tests activatorTags on those reports before requesting activation or deactivation. Changing _zone alone does not transfer subscriptions or clear earlier manager state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink._zoneLinkListeners
member.summary: Holds listeners for an activator's combined link activation, where either primary or secondary activity keeps the link active.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed this link's activatorTags query. For that activator and connected group, primary is the highest-ranked active link and secondary links are its direct outgoing neighbors; combined activity means either role is active. A callback is a routine registered to run when a state changes. These listeners receive OnZoneLinkEnter when combined activity changes from false to true and OnZoneLinkExit when it changes back. The argument is the activator entity. Switching from primary to secondary while still combined-active does not produce another combined enter or exit.
In normal manager dispatch, all three new link flags for that activator are stored before callbacks begin. Combined callbacks run before changed primary and secondary callbacks for the same link.

The matching RegisterLinkEventListener overload adds without deduplication or replay; repeated registrations produce repeated calls. Registering while combined activity is already true does not immediately call the new listener with that current state. Unregister removes one occurrence. Use valid listeners, since dispatch does not skip null entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink._zoneLinkPrimaryListeners
member.summary: Holds listeners for this link becoming or ceasing to be the selected primary for an activator in one connected group.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed this link's activatorTags query. A connected group is the set of links joined through their configured incoming or outgoing connections. For each activator and group, the manager orders active links by priority; the highest-ranked link at the top is primary.
A callback is a routine registered to run when a state changes. Primary listeners receive the activator entity, not a special 'primary entity' type.

In normal manager dispatch, new combined, primary, and secondary flags are stored before callbacks. Changed combined callbacks run first, then primary, then secondary for this link. Direct OnPrimaryEnter or OnPrimaryExit calls only dispatch the list and do not perform that selection. Registering after this link is already primary does not immediately call the new listener with the current state. Unregister removes one occurrence, and dispatch requires valid list entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink._zoneLinkSecondaryListeners
member.summary: Holds listeners for secondary activation from a selected primary link to its direct outgoing neighbors.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed the selected link's activatorTags query. A connected group is links joined through one or more configured incoming or outgoing connections. For that activator and connected group, primary means the highest-ranked active link. Its direct outgoing neighbors are secondary; they can receive that activator even when it is not physically inside each neighbor's Zone.

A callback is a routine registered to run when a state changes. In normal manager dispatch, all three new link flags are stored first; changed combined and primary callbacks run before secondary callbacks for this link. Direct secondary-dispatch calls do not calculate graph activity.

Registration adds without deduplication. Registering after a link is already secondary does not immediately call the new listener with the current state. Unregister removes one occurrence, and null listener entries are not skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.activatorTags
member.summary: Filters which reported MarrowEntity values the link manager accepts as activators for this link.

remarks.para: An activator is the reported MarrowEntity that passes this link's query. A MarrowQuery supplies matching rules. Marrow tags classify entities, and crate identities identify the warehouse asset an object was spawned from. All listed tag checks must pass; any listed crate can satisfy its group. And requires both groups, while Or allows either. Empty groups count as matching, so an empty group with Or can make the query permissive.

Both Zone enter and exit wrappers test the current query. A changed match result can therefore allow entry but suppress its later deactivation report. A valid query object is required; assigning null is not a pass-all filter. Changing the query alone does not rescan existing overlaps or replay reports. An accepted activator need not be the player.

If an exit still passes the current query, ZoneLink asks the manager to deactivate the link with its allow-orphan option. When this is the only active link left for that activator in the group, the manager can retain its selected state after the entity leaves the Zone. This is the last-entry orphan case, not a rule for every Zone exit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.priority
member.summary: Stores the input rank exposed through for selecting a primary link within a connected group.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed this link's activatorTags query. A connected group is the set of ZoneLinks joined through one or more configured incoming or outgoing connections. For each activator and group, the manager keeps active links in a priority-ordered list; the highest-ranked link at the top is primary.

The rank is unitless: larger values take precedence for that activator's group, and the newest equal-priority insertion becomes primary only when those links tie at the highest active rank in the group. A newer insertion at a lower tied rank cannot outrank a higher-ranked active link. For example, active links with ranks 2 and 5 select 5 when they belong to the same group; this is an illustrative choice, not a default.

Priority and this field expose the same integer. It is read for stack insertion, so assigning a new value alone does not sort existing lists again or send role callbacks. Existing ZoneCuller records keep the priority copied when they registered.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink.zoneLinks
member.summary: Lists the directed outgoing links that can become secondary when this link is primary for an activator.

remarks.para: An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passed the selected link's activatorTags query. A connected group is links joined through one or more configured incoming or outgoing connections. A primary is the highest-ranked active link for that activator in one connected group. Its direct outgoing neighbors are secondary.

For example, a configured connection A to B lets B become secondary while A is primary for an activator, even if that entity is not physically inside B. It does not automatically add the reverse connection B to A. Secondary activation follows direct outgoing neighbors rather than recursively activating the entire group.

The manager groups links using incoming and outgoing connections for primary selection. Configure a nonnull array with valid links before Awake. Awake is Unity's initialization callback, the routine called to set up the component. An empty array registers this link without adding outgoing connections from this array, though other links can connect to it.

Editing this array alone does not reconcile the connections already registered. Destruction removes the link from the manager's connection graph and recalculates roles only in groups reached from an activator's remaining active links. If this was that activator's only active link in its group, its former secondary neighbors keep their secondary and combined-active flags and receive no exit callback (a routine called to report leaving that state) from this teardown. Combined-active means primary or secondary activity for the same activator. Former neighbors disconnected from every remaining active link can also be missed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ChestEllipseNegZ
member.summary: Sets the back-side depth of the avatar’s chest at the underbust level for body geometry and measurements.

remarks.para: Increasing this positive magnitude makes that side of the generated body collision shape project farther out. It is a fraction of eye height, not meters. For an eye height of 1.6 m, an example value of 0.05 supplies a nominal 0.08 m center-to-edge size. Negative local z points backward. The avatar’s body orientation defines these directions, not the world’s fixed axes.
Use a positive depth magnitude for the back side. The geometry builder applies the backward sign; entering a negative value does not mean “backward”.
The corresponding torso-curve point sits at UnderbustY. That position is a fraction along the upper-chest-to-hips segment. Changing the size does not move this point up or down.
ComputeMass also reads this part of the torso shape when estimating body mass. Updating the dimensions can therefore change later mass calculations as well as geometry.

This setter changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; setting the property does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.HandSchematic.DefaultLf
member.summary: Returns the fixed reference left-hand measurements used when fitting the model’s finger bases to the game’s hand rig.

remarks.para: The result contains five finger-base vectors and two joint-to-joint distances for each finger, in metres. ArtRig compares the measured left-hand base positions with these reference positions multiplied by handSizeMult, the avatar’s hand-size scale factor that scales the fixed reference hand to this avatar.

The opposite hand uses DefaultRt: its base vectors have opposite signs and its segment distances are the same. Each getter constructs a new value from fixed constants, so changing your returned struct does not change future reference values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.HeadTop
member.summary: Sets the distance from eye level to the top of the head as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: For an avatar with eye height 1.6 m, an example value of 0.068 represents 0.1088 m above the eyes. Initial precomputation uses 1 + HeadTop as the ratio of full standing height to eye height. The skull collision-mesh generator and body drawing guides also use this input.

This setter changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; setting the property does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

Changing HeadTop after initial precomputation does not itself update the cached overall-height ratio. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses that cached ratio, so it is not a substitute for repeating the model setup when this relation must change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.OnRefreshBodyMeasurements
member.summary: Runs subscribed callbacks after RefreshBodyMeasurements has replaced the derived dimensions, mass and stat ratings.
