member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.OnWriteTransforms
member.summary: Runs subscribed callbacks when the avatar’s UpdateBlender hook is called during the rig’s late update.

remarks.para: The base UpdateBlender implementation invokes this parameterless Action and performs no other work. RigManager calls the hook for the active avatar after updating its rigs when the avatar GameObject is active and rig updates are not suspended. AvatarExtension subscribes its own transform-writing hook here.
This is a place for additional visual bone adjustments. It does not signal that new body measurements were calculated. Use += and -= for subscription; assigning a new Action replaces other callbacks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.PreComputed
member.summary: Records whether the base parameterless PrecomputeAvatar routine has already finished measuring this avatar.

remarks.para: When true, that routine returns immediately without refreshing its bone or dimension caches. It changes to true at the end of successful precomputation. This is a Boolean guard, not a container of computed data.

Clearing it allows the next base precomputation to run again. That operation restores the Animator’s default pose and replaces measurements and orientation corrections; clearing the flag alone does not rebuild anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._acLfLocal
member.summary: Stores the calculated left collarbone segment from its inner joint toward the shoulder blade.

remarks.para: This approximates the distance from the sternoclavicular joint at the chest to the acromioclavicular joint at the outer shoulder. The vector is in meters, in the Animator root's orientation. Adding it to the corresponding scLocal offset gives the outer-shoulder location relative to the neck. The art rig uses this segment to position its shoulder-blade helper.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._acRtLocal
member.summary: Stores the calculated right collarbone segment from its inner joint toward the shoulder blade.

remarks.para: This approximates the distance from the sternoclavicular joint at the chest to the acromioclavicular joint at the outer shoulder. The vector is in meters, in the Animator root's orientation. Adding it to the corresponding scLocal offset gives the outer-shoulder location relative to the neck. The art rig uses this segment to position its shoulder-blade helper.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._agility
member.summary: Stores the calculated movement-response score used to set how quickly the movement rig can change velocity.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless score. RemapRig.SetAvatar sets its base acceleration to 7 × agility in meters per second squared: how much movement velocity can change each second. An attached navigation agent receives ten times that value. For example, an illustrative agility of 1 produces a base setting of 7 meters per second squared and a navigation setting of 70. ApplyMovement scales the base setting for gravity and movement conditions, so those numbers are not guaranteed momentary acceleration. The base speed target uses speed instead.

ComputeBaseStats calculates agility from the avatar's head and leg proportions. It is a generated result and RefreshBodyMeasurements overwrites it. RemapRig keeps its own acceleration value after avatar assignment, so editing this field alone does not update that cached setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._ankleEllipse
member.summary: The oval cross-section used to calculate the avatar's ankle end of the lower leg shape and generated collision geometry.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. XBias and ZBias are dimensionless fractions of the matching radius. The center offsets in meters are XBias × XRadius × eyeHeight and ZBias × ZRadius × eyeHeight. A bias of zero centers the opposite surface extents; an illustrative bias of 0.5 moves their center half a radius, or 2.4 cm with the radius example above. The left limb mirrors the X direction.

The limb-shape calculation blends this section with the calf section as it moves along the limb. These values describe generated geometry; they do not resize the imported visible mesh. Physics calibration builds meshes from the shape descriptions and installs them in collision components, so editing the description alone does not replace an already generated collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armLength
member.summary: Stores the combined upper-arm and forearm length plus half the wrist-to-hand segment, in meters.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates this from armUpperLength + armLowerLength + half of carpalLength. It does not include the shoulder/collarbone segment, and it differs from the full shoulder-to-palm reach. The movement rig uses the individual segment measurements and related reach values to fit arms to an avatar.
This is a calculated cache, not an independent setting for all the arm bones. Changing it does not update its component lengths or normalized proportions, and a refresh can overwrite it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armLowerLength
member.summary: Stores the measured distance from the right elbow to the wrist or humanoid hand, in meters.

remarks.para: When wristRt is supplied, the segment ends at that wrist; otherwise it ends at the right humanoid hand bone. RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as _armLowerPercent × eyeHeight. Changing this cache alone does not update that proportion, and a later refresh replaces the change. The limb solver and generated forearm geometry use this length.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armLowerPercent
member.summary: Stores the measured forearm length divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: The source is the right lower-arm bone to wristRt when that reference exists; otherwise it ends at the right humanoid hand bone. This is a fraction, so 0.18 with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters gives 0.288 meters. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies it by eyeHeight to update armLowerLength.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armPercent
member.summary: Stores the combined arm length as a fraction of eyeHeight.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as _armUpperPercent + _armLowerPercent + half of _carpalPercent. The carpal term is the wrist-to-humanoid-hand segment. This differs from shoulderToPalmPercent, which includes the full carpal segment and an additional palm offset.

This is a generated sum, not an independent input controlling the three segment lengths. The same refresh updates armLength from the segment lengths; writing _armPercent alone does not resize those segments.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armUpperLength
member.summary: Stores the measured distance from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone, in meters.

remarks.para: This is the upper-arm joint-to-joint length, rather than the visible mesh's outer length. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates it as _armUpperPercent × eyeHeight; changing this cache alone leaves the stored proportion unchanged. The shape generators and movement rig use the measured segment length when constructing arms and solving reach.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._armUpperPercent
member.summary: Stores the measured upper-arm length divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar measures from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone. This is a fraction: 0.20 with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters gives 0.32 meters. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies it by eyeHeight to update armUpperLength and uses it in combined reach and strength calculations.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._c1HeightPercent
member.summary: Stores the humanoid head bone's standing height as a fraction of eyeHeight.

remarks.para: Both heights are measured above the Animator root. A fraction of 0.90 means 90%, not 0.90%. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies this value by eyeHeight to update skullHeight; this does not measure the visible skull's size.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._calfEllipse
member.summary: The oval cross-section for the middle section of the avatar's lower-leg collision shape.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. XBias and ZBias are dimensionless fractions of the matching radius. The center offsets in meters are XBias × XRadius × eyeHeight and ZBias × ZRadius × eyeHeight. A bias of zero centers the opposite surface extents; an illustrative bias of 0.5 moves their center half a radius, or 2.4 cm with the radius example above. The left limb mirrors the X direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._carpalLength
member.summary: Stores the measured wrist-to-humanoid-hand distance, in meters.

remarks.para: This segment is measured using wristRt and the right humanoid hand bone; it is zero when no separate wrist reference is available. RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as _carpalPercent × eyeHeight. It contributes fully to shoulderToPalmPercent, while combined armLength includes half this segment.
It is a cache derived from the stored proportion. A direct edit can be replaced by a refresh and does not update the proportion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._carpalPercent
member.summary: Stores the wrist-to-hand segment length divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar measures wristRt to the right humanoid hand bone when a wrist reference exists. Without it, this segment is zero. The fraction is converted to carpalLength in meters by RefreshBodyMeasurements. It also contributes to the combined arm and shoulder-to-palm reach calculations.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._cervicalHalfLocal
member.summary: Stores the vector from the head pivot halfway toward the neck pivot, for placing the game’s neck skeleton.

remarks.para: The vector is half of Neck.position minus Head.position, in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s axes. It is an offset from the head, not the midpoint’s absolute position. For an upright model it normally points downward.

The game skeleton uses negative two times this vector to place the head relative to the neck: it doubles the length and reverses the direction. Precomputation derives it from the humanoid bones; it does not follow the player’s head movement each frame.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._cervicalRom
member.summary: Controls how much of the player’s neck bending and twisting the skeleton solver allows.

remarks.para: The four components are angular ranges in degrees: X for forward bend, Y for twist, Z for sideways bend, and W for backward bend. The solver blends the bend limit between these directions, so this is not four independent clamps applied directly to a Transform.

The neck’s Y value also determines its share of total spine twist: the neck (cervical) Y value divided by the sum of the neck, chest-section (thoracic), and lower-spine (lumbar) Y values. Increasing that share directs more of the twist into the neck. These ranges guide the skeleton solver; they do not directly set physical joint limits.

The corresponding public property reads this same Vector4. These are input settings rather than bone measurements. Skeleton-solving functions read them when calculating the pose; changing them does not directly assign a Unity joint limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._chestHeight
member.summary: Stores the humanoid Neck pivot’s height above the Animator root, in metres.

remarks.para: The cached ratio comes from the Neck bone’s world Y position minus the Animator root’s world Y position, divided by eyeHeight. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies that ratio by eyeHeight.
This is the height of the upper end of the torso used in body calculations. It is not chest thickness, chest circumference, or a live measurement of the animated Chest bone.
RefreshBodyMeasurements replaces this derived value using cached proportions. Writing it does not alter those proportions or immediately rebuild the rig’s collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._chestToShoulderPerc
member.summary: Stores the right upper-arm pivot’s sideways distance from the Chest pivot as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: The producer subtracts Chest.position from RightUpperArm.position, rotates that offset into the Animator root’s axes, and divides its X component by eyeHeight. This is a signed sideways distance, not the full three-dimensional distance.

For example, 0.1 with a 1.6-metre eye height gives a 0.16-metre sideways offset. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses the ratio to calculate clavicleLength, which helps the solver place the shoulders. Precomputation replaces the cached ratio from the humanoid bones.

Writing it changes the clavicleLength calculated by the next RefreshBodyMeasurements. PrecomputeAvatar replaces it with the measured right-side offset. Existing physical joints and visible bone lengths require their setup calculations to be repeated.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._chinY
member.summary: Sets the eye-level-to-chin distance used to shape the lower head, as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: Use a positive distance magnitude. For an eye height of 1.6 m, an example value of 0.08 represents 12.8 cm below eye level. Skull geometry applies the downward sign; this is not a world Y coordinate.

It also helps choose where the jaw sample lies on the torso outline between the head and neck. Larger values place the lower head farther down in generated geometry; they do not move the model’s existing jaw bone.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._clavicleLength
member.summary: Stores the sideways Chest-to-right-upper-arm distance used when positioning the shoulders, in metres.

remarks.para: This equals chestToShoulderPercent multiplied by eyeHeight. The source measurement is the X component in the Animator root’s axes; it is not the full length along a clavicle bone.
The shoulder solver uses it when estimating shoulder reach. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this cached result, so changing the model’s bones and recalibrating is what changes the measurement.
RefreshBodyMeasurements replaces this derived value using cached proportions. Writing it does not alter those proportions or immediately rebuild the rig’s collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._clavicularRom
member.summary: Sets how far the shoulder solver can move the clavicle section forward, backward, upward, and downward to reach the hands.

remarks.para: X is forward, Y is backward, Z is upward, and W is downward, all in degrees. The solver combines the direction values when deciding how much shoulder motion can help an arm reach its target.

Larger values allow more shoulder movement in that direction before the arm-reach calculation treats the pose as beyond that range. This guides the calculated skeleton pose rather than setting a physical joint’s angular limits.

The corresponding public property reads this same Vector4. These are input settings rather than bone measurements. Skeleton-solving functions read them when calculating the pose; changing them does not directly assign a Unity joint limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._crotchBottom
member.summary: Sets how far generated pelvis geometry and body guides extend below the hip center, as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: Use a positive downward-distance magnitude. With eye height 1.6 m, an example value of 0.04 supplies 6.4 cm of extension below the hips. This is relative to the hip center, not the floor or world origin.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._elbowEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the elbow in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the upper-arm profiles and the elbow, forearm, and wrist profiles. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. With an eye height of 1.6 metres, a radius of 0.03 produces a 4.8-centimetre half-width before the mesh-generation scale is applied. XBias and ZBias shift the cross-section by a fraction of its radius.

The generated shape is used by colliders, which are the surfaces that objects hit in the physics simulation. The same profiles contribute to estimated limb mass. Changing this field only stores the profile; the collider must be calibrated again and body measurements refreshed to update those results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._ellipseNegZ
member.summary: Stores the generated back-side distance profile used to sample the avatar’s torso surface.

remarks.para: The curve’s horizontal input is the body-path coordinate: 0 is the sternum/upper-chest reference and 1 is the hip-center reference. For example, 0.35 samples 35% of the way down that torso segment. Negative inputs describe the head/neck region; the generated forehead sample is at −1.4. This is not a time in seconds.

The vertical output is a size divided by eye height, not meters or a strength multiplier. A sample output of 0.05 represents a nominal 8 cm center-to-edge distance at an eye height of 1.6 m. GetTorsoEllipseInMeters multiplies the sample by eye height before returning the physical size.

The profile includes a correction for the measured spine’s forward/backward curve. Its positive output describes the distance on this side of that centerline. The back-side geometry applies the backward sign; an output for the back profile is not a world Z position.

The game uses these profiles to sample the avatar’s body outline, including when fitting hand targets to its torso. A hand target is where the game wants the hand to reach; the physical hand can lag behind it. Editing the profile does not deform the imported visible mesh or automatically rebuild every collider.

RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the curve from the stored shape inputs and cached spine curve, replacing a manually assigned curve. Use the cross-section inputs when a change should survive that refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._ellipseZ
member.summary: Stores the generated front-side distance profile used to sample the avatar’s torso surface.

remarks.para: The curve’s horizontal input is the body-path coordinate: 0 is the sternum/upper-chest reference and 1 is the hip-center reference. For example, 0.35 samples 35% of the way down that torso segment. Negative inputs describe the head/neck region; the generated forehead sample is at −1.4. This is not a time in seconds.

The vertical output is a size divided by eye height, not meters or a strength multiplier. A sample output of 0.05 represents a nominal 8 cm center-to-edge distance at an eye height of 1.6 m. GetTorsoEllipseInMeters multiplies the sample by eye height before returning the physical size.

The profile includes a correction for the measured spine’s forward/backward curve. Its positive output describes the distance on this side of that centerline. This is an extent relative to the body’s curve, not a world Z position.

The game uses these profiles to sample the avatar’s body outline, including when fitting hand targets to its torso. A hand target is where the game wants the hand to reach; the physical hand can lag behind it. Editing the profile does not deform the imported visible mesh or automatically rebuild every collider.

RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the curve from the stored shape inputs and cached spine curve, replacing a manually assigned curve. Use the cross-section inputs when a change should survive that refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._eyeHeight
member.summary: Stores the calibrated eye level above the Animator root, in meters, used to scale the avatar’s normalized body measurements.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar finds the midpoint of the model’s eye bones, or eyeCenterOverride, and subtracts the Animator root’s world Y position. This is a model calibration value, not the player’s current headset Y position or crouched height.

RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies stored limb and height ratios by this value to obtain lengths in meters. Shape builders also multiply normalized radii by it. For example, a radius ratio 0.03 becomes 4.8 cm at eye height 1.6 m.

Writing a different eye height changes the scale used by later calculations, but does not itself rescale the imported mesh or recalibrate a mounted physics body. RefreshBodyMeasurements updates derived caches; rig setup separately installs collision shapes, joint settings and artwork alignment. Another PrecomputeAvatar replaces the measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._eyeHeightPercent
member.summary: Stores the normalized eye-height reference, which precomputation sets to 1.

remarks.para: The model’s body measurements use eyeHeight itself as the reference length, so eyeHeight divided by that reference is 1. This is a ratio and does not need to be multiplied by 100 before it is used.
The constructor has an initial value before calibration, but PrecomputeAvatar replaces it with 1. It does not report eye height divided by total avatar height.
Renderer bounds setup also reads this reference when calculating the body’s visibility box. Writing it does not move the eyes; the next PrecomputeAvatar restores the calibrated reference value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._eyeLfLocal
member.summary: Stores the calibrated offset from the head pivot to the left eye, for placing the eye relative to the head.

remarks.para: The offset is in metres and uses the Animator root’s axes at calibration. It is calculated from the eye position minus the Head position, rather than being a world position or the eye Transform’s own localPosition.
Rig setup uses this offset to place its eye reference relative to the head. It is cached from the model, so it does not report the player’s current gaze or eye movement.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._footLength
member.summary: Stores the calibrated three-dimensional distance from the right Foot pivot to the right toe landmark, in meters.

remarks.para: The cached right toe vector records the complete toe-bone displacement from the Foot pivot. RefreshBodyMeasurements takes its three-dimensional magnitude, including the vertical component; this is not a ground-plane projection.

This is a distance between bone reference points. It does not include the heel behind the Foot pivot or measure the full rendered shoe. Writing the cache does not resize the shoe or collision shape, and the next RefreshBodyMeasurements replaces it from the stored toe vector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._forearmEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the middle of the lower arm in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the elbow, forearm, and wrist. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. With an eye height of 1.6 metres, a radius of 0.03 produces a 4.8-centimetre half-width before the mesh-generation scale is applied. XBias and ZBias shift the cross-section by a fraction of its radius.

The generated shape is used by colliders, which are the surfaces that objects hit in the physics simulation. The same profiles contribute to estimated limb mass. Changing this field only stores the profile; the collider must be calibrated again and body measurements refreshed to update those results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._ghLfLocal
member.summary: Stores the final offset in the left shoulder chain, from the outer collarbone reference to the upper-arm pivot.

remarks.para: This is a calculated segment vector in meters, expressed in the Animator root’s calibration axes. The inner shoulder offset (sc), middle collarbone offset (ac) and this final offset (gh) add up from the neck to the upper-arm pivot. It is not an absolute world position.
HeptaRig.CalibratePlayerBodyScale adds this to the middle shoulder offset when placing the upper-arm pivot in the game’s skeleton. This fits the shoulder chain to the avatar’s measured proportions.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

remarks.para: This is a calculated segment vector in meters, expressed in the Animator root’s calibration axes. The inner shoulder offset (sc), middle collarbone offset (ac) and this final offset (gh) add up from the neck to the upper-arm pivot. It is not an absolute world position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._handSizeMult
member.summary: Stores how large the measured hand is relative to the game’s reference hand, for finger fitting and grab-search size.

remarks.para: A pivot is a bone’s reference point. Proximal means the finger’s base bone near the palm; intermediate is the middle bone, and distal is the end bone. These measurements use the distances between those reference points.

The calculation adds the first two measured segments of the left index finger and the span between the bases of the left index finger and thumb, then divides by the 0.12762-meter reference. A result of 1 has the reference size; 1.2 is 20% larger by this measurement.

ArtRig uses the multiplier when comparing the model’s fingers with the reference hand. PhysicsRig also sets its hand grab-search radius to 0.09 metres times this value. Precomputation calculates the multiplier from bones, so it is not an independent hand-size setting.

This is the same stored result read by handSizeMult. HandPoseAnimator.SetHandSize copies it into its own scale cache, and physics setup copies it into the grab-search radius. Changing the field alone does not repeat those setup operations; PrecomputeAvatar will replace the value from measured bones.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._hasUpperChest
member.summary: Stores whether calibration found a humanoid UpperChest bone, which changes how the game splits the torso skeleton.

remarks.para: With that bone, the cached torso offsets use the actual UpperChest-to-Chest segment. Without it, precomputation splits the Neck-to-Chest distance into two equal segments to supply the missing section.
This is a calculated result of the humanoid bone lookup. It does not create an UpperChest bone or enable one in the Animator.

This is a cached lookup result, not a switch that adds a humanoid bone. Writing it changes which later branches are selected without supplying the corresponding measured bone/segment data; keep it consistent with calibration. PrecomputeAvatar replaces it from the Animator lookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._headEllipseNegZ
member.summary: Sets the back-side depth of the avatar’s forehead for body geometry and measurements.

remarks.para: Increasing this positive magnitude makes that side of the generated body collision shape project farther out. It is a fraction of eye height, not meters. For an eye height of 1.6 m, an example value of 0.05 supplies a nominal 0.08 m center-to-edge size. Negative local z points backward. The avatar’s body orientation defines these directions, not the world’s fixed axes.
Use a positive depth magnitude for the back side. The geometry builder applies the backward sign; entering a negative value does not mean “backward”.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._headEllipseX
member.summary: Sets the side-to-side half-width of the avatar’s forehead for body geometry and measurements.

remarks.para: Increasing this value makes that section of the generated body collision shape wider. It is a fraction of eye height, not meters. For an eye height of 1.6 m, an example value of 0.05 supplies a nominal 0.08 m center-to-edge size. Local x points sideways; this is one half of the full width. The avatar’s body orientation defines these directions, not the world’s fixed axes.
ComputeBaseStats also calculates intelligence from this value divided by 0.044, so this is both a shape input and an input to that cached rating.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._headTop
member.summary: Sets the distance from eye level to the top of the head as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: For an avatar with eye height 1.6 m, an example value of 0.068 represents 0.1088 m above the eyes. Initial precomputation uses 1 + HeadTop as the ratio of full standing height to eye height. The skull collision-mesh generator and body drawing guides also use this input.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

Changing HeadTop after initial precomputation does not itself update the cached overall-height ratio. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses that cached ratio, so it is not a substitute for repeating the model setup when this relation must change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._height
member.summary: Stores the avatar’s calculated full height, including its configured head-top allowance, in metres.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates height as eyeHeight multiplied by heightPercent. Precomputation sets heightPercent to 1 plus HeadTop, so the full height is the calibrated eye level plus that normalized allowance above the eyes.
For example, eyeHeight of 1.6 metres and HeadTop of 0.068 give height of 1.7088 metres. This is a body-model estimate, not a mesh-bounds measurement or the player’s current crouched height.
RefreshBodyMeasurements replaces this derived value using cached proportions. Writing it does not alter those proportions or immediately rebuild the rig’s collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._heightPercent
member.summary: Stores the ratio that converts calibrated eye height into the avatar’s calculated full height.

remarks.para: Precomputation sets this to 1 plus HeadTop. HeadTop is the allowance above eye level relative to eyeHeight: an example value of 0.068 gives a ratio of 1.068.

RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies the ratio by eyeHeight to calculate height. This is a dimensionless ratio, not a percentage written on a 0-to-100 scale, and it is recalculated from HeadTop during precomputation.

Writing this ratio changes the next height calculation performed by RefreshBodyMeasurements, but does not scale the rendered mesh or the mounted physical body by itself. PrecomputeAvatar replaces it with 1 + HeadTop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._highHipY
member.summary: Sets where the upper hips cross-section sits along the upper-chest-to-hips body outline.

remarks.para: This is a segment fraction: 0 is the sternum/upper-chest end and 1 is the hip-center end. Larger values move the cross-section down toward the hips. For example, 0.35 places it 35% of the way from the upper chest to the hips; it is not 0.35 meters or 35% of the avatar’s standing height.

The torso width, front-depth and back-depth curves use this value as their horizontal coordinate for this cross-section. It also partitions the cached spine-segment offsets during initial precomputation. Changing it does not move the Animator’s bone itself.

Writing this field changes the stored shape input only. Generated torso curves and physical collision shapes are prepared by the measurement and rig-calibration routines; changing the field does not rebuild a mounted rig or deform the visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._hipOffsetPercent
member.summary: Stores the displacement from the humanoid Hips pivot to the midpoint of the upper-leg pivots, divided by eye height.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar averages the left and right upper-leg bone positions, subtracts the Hips bone position, rotates the difference into the Animator root’s axes, and divides by eye height. The result is a three-component ratio, not a position in meters or a 0-to-100 percentage.

hipPelvisOffset multiplies this stored vector by eye height to return meters. For example, a Y component of −0.02 at eye height 1.6 m means the upper-leg midpoint is 3.2 cm below the Hips pivot. Torso/joint calibration uses the offset to align the pelvis geometry and anchors with that leg center.
Writing the vector changes the offset returned by the property, but does not move existing bones or joint anchors automatically. PrecomputeAvatar replaces it from the model.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._intelligence
member.summary: Stores the avatar’s calculated intelligence rating, based on its forehead width.

remarks.para: ComputeBaseStats replaces this value with ForeheadEllipseX divided by 0.044. Both widths are measured relative to eye height, so the result has no physical unit. For example, a forehead half-width ratio of 0.044 produces a rating of 1; 0.066 produces 1.5. These are examples, not prefab defaults.

The intelligence property reads this same stored value. Writing here changes what that property reports until the next stat calculation. No effect on player controls or enemy decision-making was established in the audited Avatar, PhysicsRig.SetAvatar and ArtRig code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._jawLocal
member.summary: Stores the calibrated offset from the Head pivot to the humanoid Jaw pivot, in metres.

remarks.para: When a humanoid Jaw bone exists, precomputation subtracts Head.position from Jaw.position and rotates the vector into the Animator root’s axes. The value is therefore an offset from the head rather than the Jaw Transform’s own localPosition.
This is a cached model landmark. Reading it does not measure the current mouth opening, and it is only populated by this bone-measurement path when a Jaw bone is available.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._l1Local
member.summary: Stores the torso segment from UpperChest to Chest, used when fitting the game’s spine to the avatar.

remarks.para: The vector is in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s calibration axes. With an UpperChest bone it is Chest.position minus UpperChest.position. Without one, it is half of Chest.position minus Neck.position, supplying a substitute segment.
The anatomical-style name does not identify an actual first-lumbar vertebra bone. ArtRig uses this cached segment together with the other torso offsets to place and bend its spine.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._l1OffsetZ
member.summary: Stores the UpperChest-to-Chest section’s forward/backward deviation from the straight torso reference, divided by eye height.

remarks.para: GenerateSpineCurve first forms a straight line between the sternum and hip-center references. This value is the section’s Z displacement away from that line, normalized to eyeHeight. Positive and negative values describe opposite directions along the avatar’s forward axis.

For example, 0.01 at an eye height of 1.6 metres represents a 1.6-centimetre deviation. This is a calculated spine-shape result, not an absolute world Z coordinate; regenerating the spine curve replaces it.

This field is a calculated deviation, separate from the generated spineZ curve. Writing it does not edit that curve’s keys or reposition a spine bone. GenerateSpineCurve replaces it from its input segment vectors.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._l1Y
member.summary: Stores where the UpperChest-to-Chest section ends along the torso’s sternum-to-hip span.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless fraction of the vertical span from the calculated sternum reference toward the hip-center reference. Zero is the sternum end and one is the hip end. A value of 0.5 would be halfway down that span; it is not a Y coordinate in metres or a fraction of total avatar height.

GenerateSpineCurve calculates it from the cached torso segments and endpoint offsets. The art-rig spine calculations use these fractions when sharing a bend between the torso sections. Regenerating the spine curve replaces the cached result.
This field is the cached value read by the matching property. Changing it does not update the measured segment vectors or regenerate the spine curve. GenerateSpineCurve replaces it from those inputs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._l3Local
member.summary: Stores the torso segment from Chest to Spine, used when fitting the game’s lower spine to the avatar.

remarks.para: This is Spine.position minus Chest.position, in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s calibration axes. It is a segment offset, not an absolute position of a third-lumbar vertebra.
Precomputation measures the offset from the humanoid bones. ArtRig combines it with the neighboring torso segments to place the spine and distribute its bend.

PrecomputeAvatar replaces this cached value when it measures the model. Writing it changes the stored result used by later consumers; it does not remeasure bones or immediately recalibrate an already mounted physics rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._legLowerLength
member.summary: Stores the calibrated shin length in metres, for fitting the game’s leg and collision shapes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._lumbarRom
member.summary: Controls the lower spine’s contribution to bending and twisting when the game solves the player’s torso pose.

remarks.para: The components are angular ranges in degrees: X for forward bend, Y for twist, Z for sideways bend, and W for backward bend. The pelvis solver adds the lower-spine and chest-section bend ranges when deciding how far the torso can lean.

Y also participates in distributing total spine twist between the neck, chest, and lower spine. Increasing it gives the lower spine a larger share. These values guide the skeleton pose calculation; they do not directly configure a physical joint’s limits.

The corresponding public property reads this same Vector4. These are input settings rather than bone measurements. Skeleton-solving functions read them when calculating the pose; changing them does not directly assign a Unity joint limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._massArm
member.summary: Stores the calculated mass estimate for one arm, in kilograms.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.
This is the estimate for one limb. The total includes two arms and two legs.
PhysicsRig redistributes arm mass from total body mass during setup, so this value is not simply the sum of the current arm Rigidbodies’ masses.

This is the same stored estimate read by the corresponding mass property. Writing it changes the cache only; it does not call Rigidbody.mass setters or keep the other mass estimates consistent. ComputeMass, including the call inside RefreshBodyMeasurements, replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._neckEllipseNegZ
member.summary: Stores the back-side depth at the neck level for the generated body outline and collision shape.

remarks.para: This is a positive depth magnitude divided by eyeHeight. The builder supplies the backward direction; a negative input is not required to select the back side. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, a value of 0.05 gives a nominal 0.08-meter depth. Z follows the avatar’s forward/backward direction rather than a fixed world axis.

The torso-depth builder accounts for the spine curve’s center displacement when turning this shape input into a radius. It is therefore a contour dimension used by the builder, not a bone’s Z coordinate or a promise that every local section has exactly this radius after alignment.

The field stores a shape input. RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the outer torso curves from the stored inputs, while physical calibration installs generated collision shapes. Editing it alone does not replace an existing collider or deform the imported visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._palmLfLocalPerc
member.summary: Stores the measured left palm-center offset from the hand bone, divided by the left hand’s index-to-thumb span.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar averages the thumb, index and ring fingers’ first-joint positions to approximate the palm center, subtracts the hand bone’s position, and rotates the displacement into the game’s calibrated hand orientation. This frame accounts for the model’s hand alignment; it is not a world position or necessarily the imported hand bone’s own local axes.

The three components are fractions of handSize.y, which is the distance between the left index and thumb finger roots. They are not fractions of eyeHeight. The palmLfLocalScaled getter multiplies by that span to return meters: for an illustrative span of 0.08 meters, a component of 0.5 becomes 0.04 meters.

PhysicsRig.SetAvatar adds the scaled measured offset to the separate ArtOffsets palm-position correction when placing the physical hand target. The stored measurement alone is therefore not the final hand-target position. PrecomputeAvatar generates it; changing the field does not rebuild the correction or move an already configured target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._palmOffsetLength
member.summary: Stores the length of the left hand’s calculated palm-alignment correction, in meters.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar calculates an ArtOffsets.palmLfPosOffset vector that shifts the measured palm center toward the game’s reference hand alignment. This field is the magnitude of that correction: how far it shifts, without the direction.

It is not the distance from the wrist to the palm, the magnitude of palmLfLocalScaled, or an average of the two hands. PhysicsRig.SetAvatar uses the correction vector together with the scaled palm measurement when positioning its hand target. Changing this scalar alone does not change that vector or move the target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._palmSize
member.summary: Stores two measured spans between the left hand’s finger roots, in meters.

remarks.para: X is the distance from the left index finger’s first joint to the little finger’s first joint, or to the ring finger’s first joint if the little-finger bone is missing. Y is the distance from the left index finger’s first joint to the thumb’s first joint. These are straight distances between bone pivots, not the palm mesh’s bounding box or the fingers’ total lengths.

PrecomputeAvatar calculates this Vector2 and handSize returns it. The Y span is also the scale used to convert both hands’ stored palm-center fractions back to meters. For example, an illustrative Y span of 0.08 meters converts a normalized palm component of 0.5 to 0.04 meters.

This is generated measurement data. Changing it alone leaves the measured finger schematic, palm-position corrections and already configured physical hand targets inconsistent; it does not resize the visible model.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._pelvisHeight
member.summary: Stores the measured height of the humanoid hips bone above the Animator root, in meters.

remarks.para: This is the pelvis joint's standing height, not the thickness or total size of the pelvis. RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as sacrumHeightPercent × eyeHeight. For an eye height of 1.6 meters and a proportion of 0.55, the result is 0.88 meters. The example values are illustrative.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.
Changing this cached height does not update its normalized height proportion. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates the height from that proportion, replacing a direct edit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._sacrumHeightPercent
member.summary: Stores the hips bone's standing height divided by the avatar's eye height.

remarks.para: This is a fraction, not a number from 0 to 100: 0.55 means 55% of eyeHeight. Both heights are measured above the Animator root. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies this fraction by eyeHeight to produce pelvisHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._shoulderToPalmPercent
member.summary: Stores the arm's calculated reach from the upper-arm joint to the palm, divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: It includes the upper-arm, forearm and wrist-to-hand segment lengths, plus the palm offset used by the hand pose. It is a fraction: multiply by eyeHeight to get reach in meters. For example, 0.40 with eyeHeight = 1.6 gives 0.64 meters.

The body-proportion solver divides a tracked hand distance by this reach to describe how far an arm is extended, then multiplies by the destination avatar's reach when applying that pose. This helps the same motion fit characters with different arm lengths.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

For an upright root, X is sideways, Y is up, and Z is forward. PrecomputeAvatar rotates the world-space head-minus-eye difference into this root orientation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._speed
member.summary: Stores the avatar's calculated movement-speed score used to set the movement rig's walking and jogging targets.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless score, not meters per second. RemapRig.SetAvatar sets its base movement speed to 2 × speed. Its movement update doubles that target in the Jog traversal state, before applying other movement factors such as crouching. An attached navigation agent is assigned a speed of 4 × speed.

For an illustrative score of 1, those base walking and jogging targets are 2 and 4 meters per second. The final motion can differ because of inputs, pose restrictions and physics. ComputeBaseStats derives this score from body size, mass and leg shape; RefreshBodyMeasurements can overwrite a direct edit, and assigning the avatar updates the movement rig's cached targets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._spineHighHipsToS3Perc
member.summary: Stores the calculated displacement from the high-hips level to the hip-center reference, divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: This is a Vector3 segment, not a single length. Its axes follow the Animator root’s orientation; a downward segment has negative Y on an upright avatar. The chest reference uses the upper-arm bone midpoint and the hip reference uses the upper-leg bone midpoint. The intermediate levels divide this span using UnderbustY, WaistY and HighHipsY, with the spine curve supplying their forward/backward bend.

The spineHighHipsToS3 getter multiplies each component by eyeHeight to return meters. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, a Y component of -0.10 becomes a 0.16-meter downward displacement. The rig combines the segments to place the torso and build its collision geometry.
PrecomputeAvatar generates these related segments. Editing one stored segment does not update its neighbors or rebuild the physical rig, so they can cease to describe one consistent body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._spineZ
member.summary: Stores the generated curve that places the torso’s center forward or backward at each level of its body outline.

remarks.para: The curve’s input is a position along the chest-to-hip span: 0 is the chest/shoulder-center reference, 1 is the hip-center reference, and negative values extend above the chest. This input is not elapsed time. Its output is a signed forward/backward displacement divided by eyeHeight; positive points forward in the avatar’s body orientation. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, an output of 0.01 means 1.6 cm forward.

GenerateSpineCurve constructs this curve from the torso shape. At UnderbustY it uses 0.2 times the difference between the front and back depths; at WaistY and HighHipsY it uses 0.4 times those differences. The chest and hip reference points have zero displacement. The same routine also calculates the separate t7, l1 and l3 landmark fractions and deviations, which are not the curve’s direct keyframe values.

PrecomputeAvatar stores the curve. The torso-depth curve builders and body mesh generators use it to account for the center’s forward/backward placement. Replacing it does not update already generated outer-depth curves, spine segments or collision meshes; RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the outer torso curves using the stored spine curve, and physics calibration prepares the physical shapes.

member.summary: Stores the neck-to-shoulder-center displacement as a fraction of eyeHeight.

remarks.para: The shoulder-center reference is the midpoint between the left and right upper-arm bones. PrecomputeAvatar subtracts the neck bone’s position, rotates the displacement into the Animator root’s orientation, and divides each component by eyeHeight. This is a Vector3 displacement, not a single percentage or chest thickness.

The sternumOffset getter multiplies the vector by eyeHeight to return meters. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, a Y component of -0.02 means 3.2 cm downward from the neck in that root orientation. The torso and shoulder calculations use this reference when joining their chains.
PrecomputeAvatar generates the measurement. Changing it does not update the related spine segments or rebuild a mounted rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._strengthGrip
member.summary: Stores the calculated strength multiplier for holding and turning objects with the physical hand.

remarks.para: This is separate from the controller's squeeze input. PhysHand.CalibrateJoints uses it to configure the hand's rotational drive and maximum wrist torque. CylinderGrip also multiplies its squeeze-dependent joint break threshold by this score, so a stronger avatar can withstand a larger pull before that hand connection breaks.

It is a dimensionless body-derived score, not a force in newtons. ComputeBaseStats calculates it from body mass, size, hand size and wrist shape; RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates it. Existing arm settings may need recalibration after changing the stored result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._strengthLower
member.summary: Stores the avatar's calculated strength multiplier for the physical legs; physics setup also uses it to set the foot body's resistance to spinning.

remarks.para: The score is dimensionless. ComputeBaseStats calculates it from body mass, eye height, thigh shape and leg proportions. PhysLimb.CalibrateLimbJoints uses it to scale the leg joints’ springs, damping and force allowances. PhysicsRig.SetAvatar also sets each component of the foot body's inertia tensor to 0.35 × strengthLower. An inertia tensor describes how difficult it is to turn a physical object: larger values need more torque for the same angular acceleration.

This is a generated result, not a direct walking-speed setting. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates it. The verified foot-body effect occurs when the avatar is assigned to the physics rig; changing the cached score alone does not immediately change an already configured rigidbody.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._strengthUpper
member.summary: Stores the avatar's calculated arm-strength multiplier used to configure the physical arms and hands.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless score, not a force in newtons. PhysicsRig supplies it to PhysHand.CalibrateJoints, which scales the arm's force values and the springs, damping and force allowances used by its shoulder, elbow and wrist connections. A physics connection keeps two simulated body parts together and drives them toward their target pose.

Higher values give those configured drives more strength; the final ability to move an object also depends on its mass and the rest of the solver. ComputeBaseStats calculates the score from body mass, size and arm proportions. RefreshBodyMeasurements recomputes it, so editing a stored result can be overwritten, and existing configured joints need updating to use a new score.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._t1HeightPercent
member.summary: Stores the humanoid neck bone's standing height divided by the avatar's eye height.

remarks.para: The name refers to the upper-spine reference, but the measured source is the neck bone. The denominator is eyeHeight, not the model's total height. For example, 0.85 means the neck joint is 85% as high as the eye-center measurement. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses it to calculate chestHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._t7Local
member.summary: Stores the measured upper-spine segment leading down from the neck toward the upper chest, in meters.

remarks.para: With an UpperChest bone, this is UpperChest position minus neck position, rotated into the Animator root's orientation. Without UpperChest, the game uses half the chest-minus-neck vector. It is a segment displacement, not a world position or a localTransform.position value.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._t7OffsetZ
member.summary: Stores the calculated forward/backward deviation of the upper-spine landmark from a straight chest-to-hips line.

remarks.para: GenerateSpineCurve subtracts the straight line's Z value at t7Y from the measured landmark's Z value. Both are divided by eyeHeight, so this result is a fraction of eye height, not a distance in meters. For example, 0.02 corresponds to 3.2 cm when eyeHeight is 1.6 meters; positive Z follows the Animator root's forward direction.
This is a cached calculation result. GenerateSpineCurve overwrites it; writing it alone does not move a bone or rebuild the spine curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._t7Y
member.summary: Stores the calculated fraction locating the upper-spine landmark along the chest-to-hips span.

remarks.para: This is a fraction of the generated spine's vertical span, not a Y coordinate in meters or a percentage from 0 to 100. The chest/shoulder-center reference is 0 and the hip-center reference is 1. GenerateSpineCurve calculates the value from the measured spine segments and reference offsets.
This is a cached geometry result. GenerateSpineCurve overwrites it; writing it alone does not rebuild the curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._thighUpperEllipse
member.summary: Stores the oval cross-section used to calculate the avatar's upper thigh shape and generated collision geometry.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. XBias and ZBias are dimensionless fractions of the matching radius. The center offsets in meters are XBias × XRadius × eyeHeight and ZBias × ZRadius × eyeHeight. A bias of zero centers the opposite surface extents; an illustrative bias of 0.5 moves their center half a radius, or 2.4 cm with the radius example above. The left limb mirrors the X direction.

The limb-shape calculation blends this section with the knee section as it moves along the limb. These values describe generated geometry; they do not resize the imported visible mesh. Physics calibration builds meshes from the shape descriptions and installs them in collision components, so editing the description alone does not replace an already generated collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._thoracicRom
member.summary: Stores the upper-spine bending allowances, in degrees, used when the movement rig solves the torso pose.

remarks.para: The four components are X = bending forward, Y = turning around the spine, Z = bending sideways, and W = bending backward. For example, X = 45 gives a 45-degree forward-bending allowance; these values are angles, not fractions or distances.

The solver combines the forward, sideways and backward allowances with the lower-spine allowances and blends them according to the bend direction. The Y component also determines how much of the body's turning is assigned to the upper spine relative to the neck and lower spine. They guide the solved pose rather than defining four independent Unity physics-joint limits.
Changing these stored allowances changes what the torso pose solver reads. It does not move a bone immediately or configure a physical joint by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._tippyToeExt
member.summary: Stores the calculated extra leg-and-foot reach beyond the measured standing arrangement, in meters.

remarks.para: The calculation uses the right leg. It starts with the sum of the upper- and lower-leg lengths minus the straight hip-to-foot distance, then adds twice the sum of the foot-to-toe distance and that offset's vertical component. This includes spare reach from straightening the leg and rotating the foot; it is not simply the toe bone's height.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.
The audited measurement, proportion and leg-solver code establishes this geometry result, but does not establish a separate live movement control for changing this value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._toeHeight
member.summary: Stores the right toe bone's standing height above the Animator root, in meters.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar subtracts the Animator root's world Y coordinate from the right toe bone's world Y coordinate. This is a measured bone height, not the toe mesh's thickness or a live distance from the floor. The body-proportion calculations use it with each foot-to-toe offset to reconstruct leg placement.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._toeLfLocal
member.summary: Stores the measured offset from the left humanoid foot bone to its toe bone, in the game's calculated foot frame.

remarks.para: The vector is in meters. The frame points forward along the ankle-to-toe direction after removing its component along the Animator root's up direction; its up direction follows the root. This means it is not necessarily the imported foot bone's local axes. The leg solver uses this offset when bending the foot for extra reach, and the body-proportion calculation combines its vertical component with toeHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._toeRtLocal
member.summary: Stores the measured offset from the right humanoid foot bone to its toe bone, in the game's calculated foot frame.

remarks.para: The vector is in meters. The frame points forward along the ankle-to-toe direction after removing its component along the Animator root's up direction; its up direction follows the root. This means it is not necessarily the imported foot bone's local axes. The leg solver uses this offset when bending the foot for extra reach, and the body-proportion calculation combines its vertical component with toeHeight.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._underbustY
member.summary: Stores where the underbust/chest cross-section sits between the chest/shoulder-center and hip-center references.

remarks.para: This is a segment fraction: 0 is the upper chest reference and 1 is the hip reference, so larger values place the section farther down the torso. For example, 0.35 means 35% of the way down this span, not 0.35 meters or 35% of standing height. The references use the upper-arm and upper-leg bone midpoints.

The width, front-depth and back-depth curve builders use this value as the horizontal coordinate of the section. Initial avatar precomputation also uses it to divide the generated spine segments, and GenerateSpineCurve uses it to position a centerline keyframe.

Changing it does not move an Animator bone. RefreshBodyMeasurements rebuilds the outer contour curves, but it does not regenerate the stored spine curve and related measured segment chain. Those dependent calculations and physical calibration must agree with the new outline before it describes a consistent mounted body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._upperarmEllipse
member.summary: Stores the oval cross-section used to calculate the avatar's upper arm shape and generated collision geometry.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. XBias and ZBias are dimensionless fractions of the matching radius. The center offsets in meters are XBias × XRadius × eyeHeight and ZBias × ZRadius × eyeHeight. A bias of zero centers the opposite surface extents; an illustrative bias of 0.5 moves their center half a radius, or 2.4 cm with the radius example above. The left limb mirrors the X direction.

The limb-shape calculation blends this section with the elbow section as it moves along the limb. These values describe generated geometry; they do not resize the imported visible mesh. Physics calibration builds meshes from the shape descriptions and installs them in collision components, so editing the description alone does not replace an already generated collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._vitality
member.summary: Stores the avatar's calculated durability score, used to set maximum health.

remarks.para: Health.SetAvatar sets maximum health to 10 × vitality. For example, an illustrative vitality of 1 gives 10 health points and 2 gives 20. When the old maximum is positive, it preserves the fraction of health remaining: switching from 5 out of 10 to a 20-point maximum gives 10 out of 20.

ComputeBaseStats derives vitality from body mass, eye height and the measured chest-to-hips span. It is a generated score, not the current health value. RefreshBodyMeasurements can replace a direct edit; the health component updates its maximum when SetAvatar runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._waistEllipseNegZ
member.summary: Stores the back-side depth at the waist level for the generated body outline and collision shape.

remarks.para: This is a positive depth magnitude divided by eyeHeight. The builder supplies the backward direction; a negative input is not required to select the back side. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, a value of 0.05 gives a nominal 0.08-meter depth. Z follows the avatar’s forward/backward direction rather than a fixed world axis.

The torso-depth builder accounts for the spine curve’s center displacement when turning this shape input into a radius. It is therefore a contour dimension used by the builder, not a bone’s Z coordinate or a promise that every local section has exactly this radius after alignment.
The corresponding body-outline point is located at WaistY. Changing the size changes the contour at that level, not its vertical placement.

The field stores a shape input. RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the outer torso curves from the stored inputs, while physical calibration installs generated collision shapes. Editing it alone does not replace an existing collider or deform the imported visible mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar._waistEllipseX
member.summary: Stores the waist’s side-to-side half-width used to generate the body outline and collision shape.

remarks.para: This is a fraction of eyeHeight, not meters or the full width. For an illustrative eye height of 1.6 meters, a value of 0.05 gives a 0.08-meter half-width, or 0.16 meters across. X follows the avatar’s sideways direction rather than a fixed world axis.
The corresponding body-outline point is located at WaistY. Changing the size changes the contour at that level, not its vertical placement.

The field stores a shape input. RefreshBodyMeasurements regenerates the outer torso curves from the stored inputs, while physical calibration installs generated collision shapes. Editing it alone does not replace an existing collider or deform the imported visible mesh.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.acLfLocal
member.summary: Reports the middle segment of the calculated left shoulder chain, used to place its outer collarbone reference.

remarks.para: The vector is a segment offset in meters, expressed in the Animator root’s axes. It connects the end of the inner collarbone section to the outer collarbone reference; it is not the complete neck-to-shoulder position. Add scLfLocal on the left or scRtLocal on the right to obtain that reference’s full offset from the neck. The remaining gh segment reaches the upper-arm pivot.

PrecomputeAvatar estimates the shoulder’s three segments from the upper-arm position relative to the neck and a reference shoulder model. ArtRig.SetArtOutputAvatar copies this middle segment into the left scapula reference’s localPosition. It helps align the visual shoulder and arm with the game’s body rig. The getter reads the cache rather than repeating the estimate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.acRtLocal
member.summary: Reports the middle segment of the calculated right shoulder chain, used to place its outer collarbone reference.

remarks.para: The vector is a segment offset in meters, expressed in the Animator root’s axes. It connects the end of the inner collarbone section to the outer collarbone reference; it is not the complete neck-to-shoulder position. Add scLfLocal on the left or scRtLocal on the right to obtain that reference’s full offset from the neck. The remaining gh segment reaches the upper-arm pivot.

PrecomputeAvatar estimates the shoulder’s three segments from the upper-arm position relative to the neck and a reference shoulder model.
