The getter reads the cache rather than repeating the estimate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.agility
member.summary: Reports the calculated agility rating used by RemapRig to set how quickly its movement speeds up.

remarks.para: The calculation compares the combined upper- and lower-leg lengths, divided by eye height, with the reference ratio 0.506831. It also compares the square root of intelligence with 1. Ratios close to those reference proportions give a larger rating; it is not a measured walking speed or an angle.
For example, leg ratios adding to 0.506831 and a forehead half-width ratio of 0.044 produce a rating of 1. The getter reads a cache; ComputeBaseStats and RefreshBodyMeasurements replace it.

When RemapRig adopts the avatar, it stores a base movement-acceleration limit of 7 × agility meters per second squared and sets its navigation agent’s acceleration to 70 × agility in the same units. Acceleration is how quickly velocity can change: a rating of 1 gives base settings of 7 m/s² and 70 m/s². ApplyMovement uses the first setting to limit how quickly its smoothed movement velocity approaches the target, with further adjustments for gravity and movement conditions; these settings do not guarantee that acceleration at every moment.

Larger ratings let that rig change speed more quickly; its top-speed setting is calculated separately from the speed stat. These are copied during avatar setup, so changing the rating does not automatically update an already configured movement rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.agro
member.summary: Holds an optional voice-clip asset for aggression; automatic playback was not verified in the audited player sound code.

remarks.para: AudioVarianceData contains an array of AudioClips. Assigning it stores a clip list; it does not make the avatar attack, change enemy hostility or play a sound immediately.

All 19 distinct native HeadSFX methods were audited. They read several other Avatar vocal fields, including bigEffort for jumping and bigPain for large damage, but no read of agro was found there. Code outside HeadSFX, including other game systems or mods, was not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.animator
member.summary: Supplies the humanoid skeleton that Avatar measures and later writes visible bone poses to.

remarks.para: An Animator provides a model’s named human bones, such as hips, head, elbows and hands. PrecomputeAvatar resets it to its default pose, asks it for those bone transforms, and measures them to fit the game’s rig. Its transform supplies the root position and orientation for measurements.

Assign the Animator belonging to this avatar’s model, with a valid humanoid bone mapping. Changing the reference after precomputation does not automatically replace the cached artTransforms, measurements or rotation corrections.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ankleEllipse
member.summary: Sets the ankle-end thickness and cross-section bias of the generated lower-leg shape.

remarks.para: SoftEllipse has XRadius and ZRadius, plus XBias and ZBias. The radii are center-to-edge sizes divided by eye height. With eye height 1.6 m, an example radius 0.03 gives 4.8 cm before the bias adjustment. Each bias has no unit and shifts the section center by that fraction of its matching radius: a bias of 0.5 shifts it by half a radius, adding that amount to one side’s extent and subtracting it from the other. The X shift is mirrored on the left leg. Bias changes thickness distribution, not limb length.

GenerateLegLowerMesh uses this as its ankle-end section, alongside the calf and knee sections, and PhysLimb uses that mesh for lower-leg collision. The setter replaces the stored SoftEllipse; it does not rebuild an existing collider or stretch the visible ankle mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.armLength
member.summary: Reports the measured upper-arm-to-hand chain length, including half the wrist-to-hand segment, in meters.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements computes armUpperLength + armLowerLength + half the carpal length. The upper segment runs from upper-arm bone to lower-arm bone; the lower segment runs from lower-arm bone to the chosen wrist reference. The extra half segment reaches partway from that wrist toward the hand bone.

This excludes the collarbone/shoulder span and finger lengths. It is a cached dimension used to fit the avatar to the body rig, not the full fingertip-to-fingertip wingspan. The armPercent property expresses the same convention relative to eye height.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.armLowerLength
member.summary: Reports the elbow-to-wrist-reference distance in meters, as last refreshed from measured proportions.

remarks.para: Initial precomputation measures from the right humanoid lower-arm bone to wristRt when that override is present, or to the right Hand bone otherwise, then stores that length relative to eye height. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies the ratio by eye height. The wrist-to-hand segment is stored separately as carpalLength, so it is not included here.

ComputeMass uses this dimension for the lower-arm estimate. ArtRig.SetArtOutputAvatar also positions its wrist references using this length. The getter returns a cache rather than the arm’s current animated distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.armPercent
member.summary: Reports armLength divided by eye height, using the game’s upper-arm + lower-arm + half-carpal convention.

remarks.para: This is a unitless ratio, not a value from 0 to 100. An armLength of 0.72 m with eye height 1.6 m gives 0.45, meaning 45% of eye height. It excludes the collarbone span and fingers.
RefreshBodyMeasurements adds the stored upper-arm and lower-arm ratios plus half the wrist-to-hand ratio. Reading it does not change or recalculate the avatar’s size.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.armUpperLength
member.summary: Reports the upper-arm bone-to-elbow distance in meters, as last refreshed from measured proportions.

remarks.para: Initial precomputation measures the distance between the right humanoid upper-arm and lower-arm bones and stores it relative to eye height. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies that ratio by eye height to produce this length.

This is a cached geometric measurement, not a strength multiplier. ComputeMass uses it to estimate upper-arm mass, and rig setup uses it when positioning the body and artwork. Reading the property does not remeasure a bent or animated arm.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.artOffsets
member.summary: Stores rotation corrections that align the game’s body-rig pose with the avatar model’s original bone orientations.

remarks.para: Different models can point a bone’s local axes in different directions even when the body looks the same. PrecomputeAvatar captures those differences in this object; ArtRig.ApplyRotationOffsetsToRig applies them when adopting the avatar. They help the displayed mesh follow the physical skeleton without unwanted twists.

Awake creates an ArtOffsets object and initial precomputation fills it. These corrections differ from artTransforms, which holds the actual bones, and poseOffsets, which stores pose-relative transforms. Replacing the object after setup does not automatically repeat rig alignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.artTransforms
member.summary: Stores references to the model’s humanoid bones so the art rig can write the visible avatar pose.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar fills this object from Animator.GetBoneTransform: hips, spine, chest, head, eyes, arms, legs and fingers. ArtRig.ArtOutputLateUpdate reads these references and sets their poses to follow the solved body rig. They are the model’s actual Transform objects, not copies of positions.

Assigning or replacing this object does not discover bones or calculate the corrections needed for a different skeleton. Bone discovery and alignment occur during precomputation. Missing required references can prevent rig setup or pose output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bigEffort
member.summary: Supplies the avatar-specific voice clips used by HeadSFX.JumpEffort when the player jumps.

remarks.para: HeadSFX chooses a random clip from this AudioVarianceData asset’s audioClips array. If the asset is absent, it falls back to its own jumpEffort clip array. Assigning an asset does not play it immediately.

The audited jump-vocal path skips playback while another speech interval is active and limits attempts to one every 2 seconds of unscaled time. It plays through the mouth AudioSource at volume 0.2 and adjusts pitch for time scale. This path reads the clip list, not extra volume or pitch settings on the asset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bigPain
member.summary: Supplies the avatar-specific voice clips used by HeadSFX.BigDamageVocal for a large-damage reaction.

remarks.para: HeadSFX randomly selects one clip from the asset’s audioClips array. If the asset is absent, it uses its own bigDamage clips. This changes the voice sound selected for that reaction; it does not change how much damage the avatar takes.

The audited path waits until the current speech interval has ended, plays through the mouth AudioSource at volume 1, and adjusts pitch for time scale. Assigning the asset does not itself trigger a pain reaction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bodyMeshes
member.summary: Lists the visible body renderers whose skinning bounds are prepared around the avatar’s hips.

remarks.para: A SkinnedMeshRenderer draws a mesh that bends with its bones. Put the avatar’s body clothing and other body parts here, except separately assigned head and hair renderers. During PrecomputeAvatar, the game changes each listed renderer’s root bone to the humanoid hips and enlarges its local bounds. Bounds tell Unity when an animated mesh might be visible; an incorrect box can make parts disappear as the body moves.

The first body renderer also supplies a position reference during setup. Use empty arrays for absent optional head or hair parts; PrecomputeAvatar iterates all three arrays. Head and hair arrays have separate hiding behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bulgeAbdomen
member.summary: Sets the extra shape protrusion on the front of the abdomen, including how much of it belongs to rigid or soft body geometry.

remarks.para: This SoftBulge describes depth and shape around an apex, meaning the point that sticks out farthest. Its vertical shape is evaluated from UnderbustY to HighHipsY on the torso path. The apexZ depth is a fraction of eye height: with eye height 1.6 m, an example 0.02 supplies a 3.2 cm depth scale before its shape falloff.

GetSoftTorso splits the bulge displacement using rigidity: the rigid part uses rigidity and the separate soft displacement uses 1 − rigidity. Increasing depth therefore changes the body outline supplied to generated collision geometry, rather than deforming the imported visible mesh by itself.

ComputeMass also includes apexZ in its chest or pelvis estimate. Changes can affect the next mass calculation as well as geometry. Generated colliders and an already mounted rig require their own calibration; replacing this object does not rebuild them immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bulgeBreast
member.summary: Sets the extra shape protrusion on the front of the chest, including how much of it belongs to rigid or soft body geometry.

remarks.para: This SoftBulge describes depth and shape around an apex, meaning the point that sticks out farthest. Its vertical shape is evaluated from sternum 0 to UnderbustY on the torso path. The apexZ depth is a fraction of eye height: with eye height 1.6 m, an example 0.02 supplies a 3.2 cm depth scale before its shape falloff.

GetSoftTorso splits the bulge displacement using rigidity: the rigid part uses rigidity and the separate soft displacement uses 1 − rigidity. Increasing depth therefore changes the body outline supplied to generated collision geometry, rather than deforming the imported visible mesh by itself.

ComputeMass also includes apexZ in its chest or pelvis estimate. Changes can affect the next mass calculation as well as geometry. Generated colliders and an already mounted rig require their own calibration; replacing this object does not rebuild them immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.bulgeGroin
member.summary: Changes the front of the pelvis contour used to fit hand positions to the avatar’s body.

remarks.para: Adds a shaped protrusion to the high hips downward section of the torso model used when mapping the player’s hands onto the avatar. The bulge’s size, position, and rigidity determine its contribution to that surface. This does not reshape the avatar’s rendered skin mesh.

Rigidity divides the displacement between two outputs: rigidity times the displacement is part of the rigid outline, while one minus rigidity times it is the separate soft displacement. Zero puts it in the soft output; one puts it in the rigid outline.

Bulge depth is a fraction of eye height. A depth of 0.02 on an avatar with an eye height of 1.6 metres represents 3.2 centimetres before the bulge’s position and shape weights are applied. This is an example, not a recommended setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.c1HeightPercent
member.summary: Reports the head bone’s height above the Animator’s root as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: This is calculated from the humanoid Head bone’s world Y position minus the Animator root’s world Y position, divided by eyeHeight. It is a ratio: 0.9 means 90% of eye height, not 0.9 metres or 0.9%.

Despite the vertebra-style name, this measures the Head pivot. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies it by eyeHeight to obtain skullHeight. Precomputation replaces the cached ratio from the model’s bones.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.calfEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the widest part of the lower leg in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the knee, calf, and ankle. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. With an eye height of 1.6 metres, a radius of 0.03 produces a 4.8-centimetre half-width before the mesh-generation scale is applied. XBias and ZBias shift the cross-section by a fraction of its radius.

The generated shape is used by colliders, which are the surfaces that objects hit in the physics simulation. The same profiles contribute to estimated limb mass. Setting this property only stores the profile; the collider must be calibrated again and body measurements refreshed to update those results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.carpalLength
member.summary: Reports the distance between the right wrist override and the humanoid right Hand pivot, in metres.

remarks.para: Precomputation measures this extra wrist-to-hand segment only when wristRt is assigned. Without that override, this calculated length is zero and the whole elbow-to-Hand distance is treated as the forearm.

RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the cached proportion back to metres and includes half of this length in the total arm-length calculation. It is a measured result, rather than a setting that creates or stretches a wrist bone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.carpalLf
member.summary: Chooses an optional left wrist-area bone that the art rig moves between the forearm and hand.

remarks.para: ArtRig solves a separate wrist-area transform from the wrist and hand poses, then applies the avatar’s calibration offset. During late output, it copies that helper’s world position and rotation to this bone when the reference is assigned.

This reference chooses the visual output bone; it does not set the measured wrist-to-hand length. PrecomputeAvatar obtains that scalar length from the separate right wrist override. An unassigned reference skips this optional output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.carpalRt
member.summary: Chooses an optional right wrist-area bone that the art rig moves between the forearm and hand.

remarks.para: ArtRig solves a separate wrist-area transform from the wrist and hand poses, then applies the avatar’s calibration offset. During late output, it copies that helper’s world position and rotation to this bone when the reference is assigned.

This reference chooses the visual output bone; it does not set the measured wrist-to-hand length. PrecomputeAvatar obtains that scalar length from the separate right wrist override. An unassigned reference skips this optional output.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.cervicalHalfLocal
member.summary: Reports the vector from the head pivot halfway toward the neck pivot, for placing the game’s neck skeleton.

remarks.para: The vector is half of Neck.position minus Head.position, in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s axes. It is an offset from the head, not the midpoint’s absolute position. For an upright model it normally points downward.
The game skeleton negates and doubles this offset to place the head relative to the neck. Precomputation derives it from the humanoid bones; it does not follow the player’s head movement each frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.cervicalRom
member.summary: Controls how much of the player’s neck bending and twisting the skeleton solver allows.

remarks.para: The four components are angular ranges in degrees: X for forward bend, Y for twist, Z for sideways bend, and W for backward bend. The solver blends the bend limit between these directions, so this is not four independent clamps applied directly to a Transform.

The neck’s Y value also determines its share of total spine twist: the neck Y value divided by the sum of the neck, chest-section, and lower-spine Y values (cervicalRom, thoracicRom, and lumbarRom). Increasing that share directs more of the twist into the neck. These ranges guide the skeleton solver; they do not directly set physical joint limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.chestHeight
member.summary: Reports the humanoid Neck pivot’s height above the Animator root, in metres.

remarks.para: The cached ratio comes from the Neck bone’s world Y position minus the Animator root’s world Y position, divided by eyeHeight. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies that ratio by eyeHeight.
This is the height of the upper end of the torso used in body calculations. It is not chest thickness, chest circumference, or a live measurement of the animated Chest bone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.chestToShoulderPercent
member.summary: Reports the right upper-arm pivot’s sideways distance from the Chest pivot as a fraction of eye height.

remarks.para: The producer subtracts Chest.position from RightUpperArm.position, rotates that offset into the Animator root’s axes, and divides its X component by eyeHeight. This is a signed sideways distance, not the full three-dimensional distance.

For example, 0.1 with a 1.6-metre eye height gives a 0.16-metre sideways offset. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses the ratio to calculate clavicleLength, which helps the solver place the shoulders. Precomputation replaces the cached ratio from the humanoid bones.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.clavicleLength
member.summary: Reports the sideways Chest-to-right-upper-arm distance used when positioning the shoulders, in metres.

remarks.para: This equals chestToShoulderPercent multiplied by eyeHeight. The source measurement is the X component in the Animator root’s axes; it is not the full length along a clavicle bone.
The shoulder solver uses it when estimating shoulder reach. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this cached result, so changing the model’s bones and recalibrating is what changes the measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.clavicularRom
member.summary: Sets how far the shoulder solver can move the clavicle section forward, backward, upward, and downward to reach the hands.

remarks.para: X is forward, Y is backward, Z is upward, and W is downward, all in degrees. The solver combines the direction values when deciding how much shoulder motion can help an arm reach its target.

Larger values allow more shoulder movement in that direction before the arm-reach calculation treats the pose as beyond that range. This guides the calculated skeleton pose rather than setting a physical joint’s angular limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.dead
member.summary: Chooses this avatar’s voice clips when the player dies.

remarks.para: HeadSFX.DeathVocal reads the current avatar’s AudioVarianceData and randomly selects a clip from its audioClips array. Supply a nonempty clip array. A missing avatar bank uses the HeadSFX component’s fallback bank; an assigned bank with no clips produces no clip.
An existing spoken clip can suppress this vocal until it finishes. Assigning the bank chooses audio; it does not change the player’s health state or start playback immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.dying
member.summary: Chooses this avatar’s voice clips when the player enters the dying state.

remarks.para: HeadSFX.DyingVocal reads the current avatar’s AudioVarianceData and randomly selects a clip from its audioClips array. Supply a nonempty clip array. A missing avatar bank uses the HeadSFX component’s fallback bank; an assigned bank with no clips produces no clip.
An existing spoken clip can suppress this vocal until it finishes. Assigning the bank chooses audio; it does not change the player’s health state or start playback immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.elbowEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the elbow in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the upper-arm profiles and the elbow, forearm, and wrist profiles. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. With an eye height of 1.6 metres, a radius of 0.03 produces a 4.8-centimetre half-width before the mesh-generation scale is applied. XBias and ZBias shift the cross-section by a fraction of its radius.

The generated shape is used by colliders, which are the surfaces that objects hit in the physics simulation. The same profiles contribute to estimated limb mass. Setting this property only stores the profile; the collider must be calibrated again and body measurements refreshed to update those results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeCenterOverride
member.summary: Provides the world position used as the avatar’s eye center during initial measurement.

remarks.para: Without this transform, PrecomputeAvatar takes the midpoint between the Animator’s left and right eye bones. An override makes models with no eye bones measurable and can place the view reference correctly on unusual heads. When eye bones do exist, the game still records them for eye animation.

The measured eye height is this center’s world Y minus the Animator root’s world Y, in meters. Setup also records the head bone’s displacement from that eye center to align the visible head with the tracked view. Place the transform at the desired eye center before the first precomputation; changing it afterward does not automatically rebuild those cached measurements.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeHeight
member.summary: Reports the calibrated eye level above the Animator root, in metres, and supplies the scale for the avatar’s normalized body measurements.

remarks.para: Precomputation finds the eye or eye-override position and subtracts the Animator root’s world Y position from its world Y coordinate. It is a measurement of the model during calibration, not the current headset height.

Body radii and many proportions are stored relative to this value. For example, a normalized radius of 0.03 becomes 0.048 metres at an eye height of 1.6 metres. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses eyeHeight to convert cached proportions to physical lengths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeHeightPercent
member.summary: Reports the normalized eye-height reference, which precomputation sets to 1.

remarks.para: The model’s body measurements use eyeHeight itself as the reference length, so eyeHeight divided by that reference is 1. This is a ratio and does not need to be multiplied by 100 before it is used.
The constructor has an initial value before calibration, but PrecomputeAvatar replaces it with 1. It does not report eye height divided by total avatar height.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeLfLocal
member.summary: Reports the calibrated offset from the head pivot to the left eye, for placing the eye relative to the head.

remarks.para: The offset is in metres and uses the Animator root’s axes at calibration. It is calculated from the eye position minus the Head position, rather than being a world position or the eye Transform’s own localPosition.
Rig setup uses this offset to place its eye reference relative to the head. It is cached from the model, so it does not report the player’s current gaze or eye movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeOffset
member.summary: Moves the visible avatar head backward relative to its tracked view, by a fraction of avatar eye height.

remarks.para: PlayerAvatarArt subtracts eyeHeight × eyeOffset from the head-placement offset’s local Z component, then rotates that offset with the tracked head orientation. Thus the direction follows the head, rather than a fixed world axis. A larger positive value moves the artwork farther backward along that orientation’s Z axis.

The value has no unit: it is a fraction, not meters. For an avatar whose eye height is 1.6 m, an example value of 0.05 produces a 0.08 m adjustment. This affects rendered-head placement; it does not replace eyeCenterOverride’s measured eye position. The Inspector range is not a runtime clamp in the audited placement function.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.eyeRtLocal
member.summary: Reports the calibrated offset from the head pivot to the right eye, for placing the eye relative to the head.

remarks.para: The offset is in metres and uses the Animator root’s axes at calibration. It is calculated from the eye position minus the Head position, rather than being a world position or the eye Transform’s own localPosition.
Rig setup uses this offset to place its eye reference relative to the head. It is cached from the model, so it does not report the player’s current gaze or eye movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.footLength
member.summary: Reports the distance from the right Foot pivot to the Toe landmark, in metres.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements takes the magnitude of the cached right foot-to-toe offset. The offset is expressed in a calculated foot frame, but keeps the full three-dimensional displacement, including any height difference between the pivots.

This measures the distance between the selected pivots. It does not include the heel behind the Foot pivot and is not a measurement of the rendered shoe’s full length. It is a cached model measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.footstepsJog
member.summary: Chooses this avatar’s faster footstep clips when the locomotion system plays a step.

remarks.para: Locomotion.SetAvatar copies this AudioVarianceData reference into both feet’s running override slots. PlayStep randomly selects a clip from the override’s audioClips array; if there is no override asset, it uses the footstep component’s own clip array.

The player locomotion caller scales its supplied movement-speed value by 0.906 divided by the avatar’s calculated leg length in metres. Normal steps pass that scaled value to PlayStep; the transition from ungrounded to grounded passes twice the value. PlayStep selects the walking bank below 4 and the running bank at or above 4. For the same supplied speed, shorter legs therefore reach the running bank sooner. Assign a nonempty clip array: an empty assigned override does not fall back to the component clips and can fail with an array-index error when a step is played. Reassigning this avatar field after setup requires the overrides to be copied again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.footstepsWalk
member.summary: Chooses this avatar’s slower footstep clips when the locomotion system plays a step.

remarks.para: Locomotion.SetAvatar copies this AudioVarianceData reference into both feet’s walking override slots. PlayStep randomly selects a clip from the override’s audioClips array; if there is no override asset, it uses the footstep component’s own clip array.

The player locomotion caller scales its supplied movement-speed value by 0.906 divided by the avatar’s calculated leg length in metres. Normal steps pass that scaled value to PlayStep; the transition from ungrounded to grounded passes twice the value. PlayStep selects the walking bank below 4 and the running bank at or above 4. For the same supplied speed, shorter legs therefore reach the running bank sooner. Assign a nonempty clip array: an empty assigned override does not fall back to the component clips and can fail with an array-index error when a step is played. Reassigning this avatar field after setup requires the overrides to be copied again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.forearmEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the middle of the lower arm in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the elbow, forearm, and wrist. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ghLfLocal
member.summary: Reports the final offset in the left shoulder chain, from its clavicle section to the upper-arm pivot.

remarks.para: This is a calculated vector in metres, expressed in the Animator root’s calibration axes. The shoulder is split into several offsets; the inner collarbone offset, middle collarbone offset, and this final shoulder offset together reconstruct the upper-arm position relative to the neck.

It is a segment offset rather than the shoulder’s absolute position from the Animator root. HeptaRig combines this with the middle collarbone offset when placing the upper-arm attachment in the player skeleton. Changing the cache alone does not move an already calibrated attachment; calibration must use it again. Precomputation replaces the cached value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.ghRtLocal
member.summary: Reports the final offset in the right shoulder chain, from its clavicle section to the upper-arm pivot.

remarks.para: This is a calculated vector in metres, expressed in the Animator root’s calibration axes. The shoulder is split into several offsets; the inner collarbone offset, middle collarbone offset, and this final shoulder offset together reconstruct the upper-arm position relative to the neck.

It is a segment offset rather than the shoulder’s absolute position from the Animator root. HeptaRig combines this with the middle collarbone offset when placing the upper-arm attachment in the player skeleton. Changing the cache alone does not move an already calibrated attachment; calibration must use it again. Precomputation replaces the cached value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.hairMeshes
member.summary: Lists hair renderers that can be hidden while still casting shadows.

remarks.para: PlayerAvatarArt.DisableHair changes each listed renderer to ShadowsOnly: the hair stops appearing directly but can still produce a shadow. EnableHair restores ordinary shadow casting. This differs from the head list, whose hide operation disables its renderers entirely.
PrecomputeAvatar gives these renderers the humanoid head as their root bone and prepares head-sized visibility bounds. Include separate hair renderers here; use an empty array when none exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.handSchematicLf
member.summary: Describes the left hand’s measured finger layout so the game can fit its hand rig to the model.

remarks.para: The schematic stores finger-root positions and distances between finger joints in metres. PrecomputeAvatar fills it from the humanoid finger bones in a calibrated hand coordinate frame.

A finger root is its base bone near the palm. A pivot is a bone’s reference point. The measured segments run from the proximal base bone to the intermediate middle bone, then from the middle bone to the distal end bone; they do not measure beyond that last pivot to the fingertip.

ArtRig compares the finger-root offsets with the game’s reference hand, scaled by handSizeMult, when correcting the finger positions. Replacing a schematic only changes the stored data; setup must use it again to update the rig. The inspected hand-bound calculation uses handSize and palm measurements separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.handSchematicRt
member.summary: Describes the right hand’s measured finger layout so the game can fit its hand rig to the model.

remarks.para: The schematic stores finger-root positions and distances between finger joints in metres. PrecomputeAvatar fills it from the humanoid finger bones in a calibrated hand coordinate frame.

A finger root is its base bone near the palm. A pivot is a bone’s reference point. The measured segments run from the proximal base bone to the intermediate middle bone, then from the middle bone to the distal end bone; they do not measure beyond that last pivot to the fingertip.

ArtRig compares the finger-root offsets with the game’s reference hand, scaled by handSizeMult, when correcting the finger positions. Replacing a schematic only changes the stored data; setup must use it again to update the rig. The inspected hand-bound calculation uses handSize and palm measurements separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.handSize
member.summary: Reports two measured hand landmark distances, in metres, used to size hand shapes and palm offsets.

remarks.para: A pivot is a bone’s reference point. Proximal means the finger’s base bone near the palm; intermediate is the middle bone, and distal is the end bone. These measurements use the distances between those reference points.

X is the distance from the left Index proximal pivot to the left Little proximal pivot, across the finger bases; if the humanoid Little proximal bone is absent, precomputation uses the Ring proximal pivot instead. Y is the distance from the left Index proximal pivot to the left Thumb proximal pivot. Y is a reference span across the palm, not the full length from wrist to fingertip.

The left-hand Y value scales the normalized palm positions for both hands. The collision calibration also uses these dimensions. Precomputation derives the measurements from the humanoid bones; they are calculated results, not size sliders.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.handSizeMult
member.summary: Reports how large the measured hand is relative to the game’s reference hand, for finger fitting and grab-search size.

remarks.para: A pivot is a bone’s reference point. Proximal means the finger’s base bone near the palm; intermediate is the middle bone, and distal is the end bone. These measurements use the distances between those reference points.

The calculation adds the left Index proximal-to-intermediate distance, Index intermediate-to-distal distance, and the Index-to-Thumb base span, then divides by a 0.12762-metre reference. A result of 1 has the reference size; 1.2 is 20% larger by this measurement.

ArtRig uses the multiplier when comparing the model’s fingers with the reference hand. PhysicsRig also sets its hand grab-search radius to 0.09 metres times this value. Precomputation calculates the multiplier from bones, so it is not an independent hand-size setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.hasUpperChest
member.summary: Reports whether calibration found a humanoid UpperChest bone, which changes how the game splits the torso skeleton.

remarks.para: With that bone, the cached torso offsets use the actual UpperChest-to-Chest segment. Without it, precomputation splits the Neck-to-Chest distance into two equal segments to supply the missing section.
This is a calculated result of the humanoid bone lookup. It does not create an UpperChest bone or enable one in the Animator.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.headImpactHard
member.summary: Stores an avatar hard head-impact sound bank; the inspected player collision playback does not select it.

remarks.para: The inspected RigManager and physics/art/input rig avatar setup do not copy this bank into the collision sound components. HeadSFX, HandSFX, and CollisionSFX select their own component or surface sound data in the collision paths examined.
Assigning this field alone therefore does not change those inspected player impact sounds. Other or custom consumers have not been established for this bank.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.headImpactSoft
member.summary: Stores an avatar soft head-impact sound bank; the inspected player collision playback does not select it.

remarks.para: The inspected RigManager and physics/art/input rig avatar setup do not copy this bank into the collision sound components. HeadSFX, HandSFX, and CollisionSFX select their own component or surface sound data in the collision paths examined.
Assigning this field alone therefore does not change those inspected player impact sounds. Other or custom consumers have not been established for this bank.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.headMeshes
member.summary: Lists separately rendered head parts that the player-avatar system can hide from view.

remarks.para: PlayerAvatarArt.DisableHead sets these renderers’ enabled state to false; EnableHead turns them back on. A renderer draws the visible mesh, so this controls visibility rather than deleting the head bone or its collision shape. A head built into the body’s single mesh cannot be hidden separately through this list.

PrecomputeAvatar gives each listed renderer the humanoid head as its root bone and prepares head-sized visibility bounds. Assign renderers, not Mesh assets, and use an empty array when the model has no separate head renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.height
member.summary: Reports the avatar’s calculated full height, including its configured head-top allowance, in metres.

remarks.para: RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates height as eyeHeight multiplied by heightPercent. Precomputation sets heightPercent to 1 plus HeadTop, so the full height is the calibrated eye level plus that normalized allowance above the eyes.
For example, eyeHeight of 1.6 metres and HeadTop of 0.068 give height of 1.7088 metres. This is a body-model estimate, not a mesh-bounds measurement or the player’s current crouched height.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.heightPercent
member.summary: Reports the ratio that converts calibrated eye height into the avatar’s calculated full height.

remarks.para: Precomputation sets this to 1 plus HeadTop. HeadTop is the allowance above eye level relative to eyeHeight: an example value of 0.068 gives a ratio of 1.068.

RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies the ratio by eyeHeight to calculate height. This is a dimensionless ratio, not a percentage written on a 0-to-100 scale, and it is recalculated from HeadTop during precomputation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.highFallOntoFeet
member.summary: Stores an avatar landing sound bank; no playback use was found in the inspected player footstep and step-state paths.

remarks.para: The inspected locomotion avatar setup copies footstepsWalk and footstepsJog into the foot sound overrides, but does not copy this bank. FootstepSFX.PlayStep chooses between those overrides, and the inspected PhysicsRig.SwitchStepState does not play this bank.
Assigning this field alone does not add a landing sound in those paths. A use in another or custom component has not been established.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.hipPelvisOffset
member.summary: Reports the offset from the humanoid Hips pivot to the midpoint between the two upper-leg pivots, for placing the game’s pelvis.

remarks.para: The vector is in metres and uses the Animator root’s calibration axes. Precomputation measures the midpoint of LeftUpperLeg and RightUpperLeg, subtracts the Hips position, and stores it normalized to eyeHeight; this property returns it multiplied by eyeHeight.

The game skeleton uses the result to position its pelvis reference, and physics setup includes its vertical component in step-height calculations. It is not a world position or the width between the hips.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.intelligence
member.summary: Reports the forehead-width-based rating last calculated by ComputeBaseStats.

remarks.para: The rating is ForeheadEllipseX / 0.044. ForeheadEllipseX is a center-to-side distance divided by avatar eye height, so this is a relative rating, not a distance. A ratio of 0.044 gives intelligence 1; increasing it to 0.066 gives 1.5.

This reads the same value as _intelligence and does not calculate it on demand. RefreshBodyMeasurements also recalculates stats. The audited code establishes how the rating is produced; it does not establish an effect on player controls or enemy decision-making.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.jawLocal
member.summary: Reports the calibrated offset from the Head pivot to the humanoid Jaw pivot, in metres.

remarks.para: When a humanoid Jaw bone exists, precomputation subtracts Head.position from Jaw.position and rotates the vector into the Animator root’s axes. The value is therefore an offset from the head rather than the Jaw Transform’s own localPosition.
This is a cached model landmark. Reading it does not measure the current mouth opening, and it is only populated by this bone-measurement path when a Jaw bone is available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.kneeEllipse
member.summary: Sets the width, depth, and sideways shift of the knee in the avatar’s generated collision shape.

remarks.para: The limb surface blends between the upper-leg profiles and the knee, calf, and ankle profiles. XRadius and ZRadius are half-widths divided by eyeHeight. With an eye height of 1.6 metres, a radius of 0.03 produces a 4.8-centimetre half-width before the mesh-generation scale is applied. XBias and ZBias shift the cross-section by a fraction of its radius.

The generated shape is used by colliders, which are the surfaces that objects hit in the physics simulation. The same profiles contribute to estimated limb mass. Setting this property only stores the profile; the collider must be calibrated again and body measurements refreshed to update those results.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.l1Local
member.summary: Reports the torso segment from UpperChest to Chest, used when fitting the game’s spine to the avatar.

remarks.para: The vector is in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s calibration axes. With an UpperChest bone it is Chest.position minus UpperChest.position. Without one, it is half of Chest.position minus Neck.position, supplying a substitute segment.
The anatomical-style name does not identify an actual first-lumbar vertebra bone. ArtRig uses this cached segment together with the other torso offsets to place and bend its spine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.l1OffsetZ
member.summary: Reports the UpperChest-to-Chest section’s forward/backward deviation from the straight torso reference, divided by eye height.

remarks.para: GenerateSpineCurve first forms a straight line between the sternum and hip-center references. This value is the section’s Z displacement away from that line, normalized to eyeHeight. Positive and negative values describe opposite directions along the avatar’s forward axis.

For example, 0.01 at an eye height of 1.6 metres represents a 1.6-centimetre deviation. This is a calculated spine-shape result, not an absolute world Z coordinate; regenerating the spine curve replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.l1Y
member.summary: Reports where the UpperChest-to-Chest section ends along the torso’s sternum-to-hip span.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless fraction of the vertical span from the calculated sternum reference toward the hip-center reference. Zero is the sternum end and one is the hip end. A value of 0.5 would be halfway down that span; it is not a Y coordinate in metres or a fraction of total avatar height.

GenerateSpineCurve calculates it from the cached torso segments and endpoint offsets. The art-rig spine calculations use these fractions when sharing a bend between the torso sections. Regenerating the spine curve replaces the cached result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.l3Local
member.summary: Reports the torso segment from Chest to Spine, used when fitting the game’s lower spine to the avatar.

remarks.para: This is Spine.position minus Chest.position, in metres, rotated into the Animator root’s calibration axes. It is a segment offset, not an absolute position of a third-lumbar vertebra.
Precomputation measures the offset from the humanoid bones. ArtRig combines it with the neighboring torso segments to place the spine and distribute its bend.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.l3OffsetZ

remarks.para: GenerateSpineCurve first forms a straight line between the sternum and hip-center references. This value is the section’s Z displacement away from that line, normalized to eyeHeight. Positive and negative values describe opposite directions along the avatar’s forward axis.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.legLowerLength

remarks.para: Precomputation measures the distance between the humanoid LowerLeg and Foot pivots and stores it divided by eyeHeight. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies the cached proportion by eyeHeight to produce this length.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.lumbarRom
member.summary: Controls the lower spine’s contribution to bending and twisting when the game solves the player’s torso pose.

remarks.para: The components are angular ranges in degrees: X for forward bend, Y for twist, Z for sideways bend, and W for backward bend. The pelvis solver adds the lower-spine and chest-section bend ranges when deciding how far the torso can lean.

Y also participates in distributing total spine twist between the neck, chest, and lower spine. Increasing it gives the lower spine a larger share. These values guide the skeleton pose calculation; they do not directly configure a physical joint’s limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.massArm
member.summary: Reports the calculated mass estimate for one arm, in kilograms.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.
This is the estimate for one limb. The total includes two arms and two legs.
PhysicsRig redistributes arm mass from total body mass during setup, so this value is not simply the sum of the current arm Rigidbodies’ masses.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.massChest
member.summary: Reports the calculated mass estimate for the chest section, in kilograms.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.

PhysicsRig uses this estimate when calibrating the forces that hold the head and torso joints at their target rotations. A joint connects body parts in the physics simulation. The actual torso Rigidbody masses use a separate distribution of the torso’s mass budget; this cached estimate is not assigned directly as one part’s physical mass. Recalculating this value alone does not recalibrate an already configured joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.massHead
member.summary: Reports the calculated mass estimate for the head, in kilograms.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.
The head estimate is the mass left after subtracting chest, pelvis, two arms, and two legs from the total; it is not calculated from skull volume alone.

PhysicsRig uses this estimate when calibrating the forces that hold the head and torso joints at their target rotations. A joint connects body parts in the physics simulation. The actual torso Rigidbody masses use a separate distribution of the torso’s mass budget; this cached estimate is not assigned directly as one part’s physical mass. Recalculating this value alone does not recalibrate an already configured joint.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.massTotal
member.summary: Reports the calculated mass estimate for the whole avatar, in kilograms.

remarks.para: ComputeMass estimates mass from the avatar’s measured size and configured body profiles, then applies its mass-normalization calculation. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates this result along with the body stats. It is a cached calculated value, not a mass slider.

PhysicsRig uses the total when distributing mass to its Rigidbodies, the objects moved by the physics simulation. More physical mass makes the body harder to accelerate with the same force. Individual body-part masses depend on the rig’s distribution calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.neck2
member.summary: Chooses an optional extra neck bone that follows halfway between the art rig’s neck and head.

remarks.para: During ArtOutputLateUpdate, the bone receives the midpoint of the neck and head helpers’ world positions and a halfway blend of their world rotations. This shares their motion with an extra neck section on models that provide one.
Assign the model’s intended extra neck bone; an unassigned reference skips this output. This reference does not supply a second neck-length measurement to PrecomputeAvatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.palmLfLocalScaled
member.summary: Reports the measured left palm-center offset in metres, for placing the hand’s physical target.

remarks.para: Precomputation estimates the palm center from the thumb, index, and ring finger-base positions relative to the Hand pivot, in the calibrated hand coordinate frame. This property multiplies the stored normalized offset by handSize.Y, the left index-to-thumb base span.

PhysicsRig.SetAvatar adds palmLfPosOffset to this value when placing the left hand target. The returned offset is therefore one part of the final alignment, rather than the target’s complete position or a world-space palm location.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.palmLfPosOffset
member.summary: Reports the correction added to the measured left palm offset to align the physical hand target with the game’s reference hand.

remarks.para: The correction is in metres in the calibrated hand frame. Precomputation compares the measured normalized palm center with a fixed reference palm center, then scales their difference by handSize.Y.

PhysicsRig.SetAvatar adds this correction to palmLfLocalScaled and copies the sum into the left hand target’s local position. Reading or changing the stored correction does not automatically reposition an already configured target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.palmOffsetLength
member.summary: Reports the length of the left palm-alignment correction, in metres.

remarks.para: Precomputation takes the magnitude of the left palmLfPosOffset vector. It does not use the right-hand correction, average the hands, or measure the distance from the wrist to the palm.

A larger result means the measured left palm center needs more positional correction to match the game’s reference hand. It is a cached measurement of that correction, rather than a separate hand-placement setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.pelvisHeight
member.summary: The measured height of the humanoid hips bone above the Animator root, in meters.

remarks.para: This is the pelvis joint's standing height, not the thickness or total size of the pelvis. RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as sacrumHeightPercent × eyeHeight. For an eye height of 1.6 meters and a proportion of 0.55, the result is 0.88 meters. The example values are illustrative.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.poseOffsets
member.summary: The precomputed transforms describing the model's bones and the game's measured body-pose references.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar fills offsets for the pelvis, spine, chest, neck, head, arms, hands, legs and feet from the measured humanoid rig. It uses the first body mesh's Transform as the reference when that mesh exists, otherwise the Animator root, and converts measured displacements into that reference's orientation.

This is generated rig data, not a list of arbitrary extra movements to add each frame. Replacing or changing entries does not rerun avatar measurement. Keep the complete initialized object when using PrecomputeAvatar, because that routine writes into its entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.recovery
member.summary: The avatar's clip collection for the player's recovery vocalization.

remarks.para: HeadSFX.RecoveryVocal randomly chooses an audioClips entry from this collection and plays it through the mouth AudioSource. A missing collection falls back to HeadSFX's recovery clips. Calling the method still requires the audio source and a usable clip array; an empty assigned collection does not mean “use the fallback.”
Playback is skipped while HeadSFX's speech-blocking time is active. Assigning this field chooses the available voice clips; it does not itself trigger recovery or heal the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.requiredBonesOrRefsMissing
member.summary: A stored validation flag that the audited runtime avatar setup does not use to decide whether measurement can proceed.

remarks.para: The name describes missing required bones or references, but Avatar.Awake, Reset, PrecomputeAvatar and RefreshBodyMeasurements do not read or update this flag in the audited binary. Setting it to false does not supply a missing bone, and setting it to true does not make those methods skip measurement.
Those setup methods still use their actual Animator, bone and mesh references. Editor validation and code outside the audited runtime methods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.sacrumHeightPercent
member.summary: The hips bone's standing height divided by the avatar's eye height.

remarks.para: This is a fraction, not a number from 0 to 100: 0.55 means 55% of eyeHeight. Both heights are measured above the Animator root. RefreshBodyMeasurements multiplies this fraction by eyeHeight to produce pelvisHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.sacrumLocal
member.summary: The measured offset from the humanoid spine bone to the hips bone, in meters.

remarks.para: The vector uses the Animator root's orientation. On an upright model it usually points downward, so its Y component is negative. It is a segment between two bones, not the hips' position relative to the whole avatar. The spine setup combines it with the other spine segments to recover the torso layout.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.scLfLocal
member.summary: The calculated offset from the neck reference to the inner end of the left collarbone.

remarks.para: This approximates the sternoclavicular joint: the place where the collarbone meets the chest. It is measured in meters and expressed in the Animator root's orientation. PrecomputeAvatar estimates it from the neck and upper-arm bone positions rather than requiring an extra bone at that joint. The movement rig uses it to place the shoulder chain.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.scapulaLf
member.summary: An optional extra bone for the left shoulder blade that the art rig can move with the shoulder.

remarks.para: Assign the model's shoulder-blade Transform before measuring and mounting the avatar. PrecomputeAvatar records its alignment with the calculated shoulder chain; ArtRig applies the solved shoulder-blade position and rotation to it. A Transform is a scene object's position, rotation and scale.

The output checks whether this extra bone exists before using it. It is distinct from the humanoid shoulder and upper-arm bones, and changing this reference does not measure or rebuild the avatar by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.shoulderToPalmPercent
member.summary: The arm's calculated reach from the upper-arm joint to the palm, divided by eyeHeight.

remarks.para: It includes the upper-arm, forearm and wrist-to-hand segment lengths, plus the palm offset used by the hand pose. It is a fraction: multiply by eyeHeight to get reach in meters. For example, 0.40 with eyeHeight = 1.6 gives 0.64 meters.

The body-proportion solver divides a tracked hand distance by this reach to describe how far an arm is extended, then multiplies by the destination avatar's reach when applying that pose. This helps the same motion fit characters with different arm lengths.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.skullCameraLocal
member.summary: The offset from the measured eye center to the humanoid head bone, in the Animator root's orientation.

remarks.para: The vector is in meters and points from the camera/eye position toward the head joint. It is not a world position or an offset in the head bone's own rotated axes. For an upright root, X is sideways, Y is up, and Z is forward. PrecomputeAvatar rotates the world-space head-minus-eye difference into this root orientation.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.skullHeight
member.summary: The measured height of the humanoid head bone above the Animator root, in meters.

remarks.para: Despite the name, this is the head joint's height, not the skull's top-to-bottom size. RefreshBodyMeasurements calculates it as c1HeightPercent × eyeHeight. The head bone can sit below the visible top of the model.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.smallEffort
member.summary: An avatar audio-clip slot whose automatic mild-effort playback was not verified in the audited player code.

remarks.para: This stores an AudioVarianceData collection, whose audioClips array supplies possible sounds. Assigning the collection does not play a clip by itself.

The audited Avatar measurement setup, PhysicsRig.SetAvatar and HeadSFX initialization, vocal and collision methods do not read this slot. The player’s JumpEffort method reads bigEffort, not smallEffort. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked, so this finding does not prove the slot is unused everywhere.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.smallPain
member.summary: The avatar's clip collection for the player's smaller damage vocalization.

remarks.para: HeadSFX.SmallDamageVocal randomly chooses one audioClips entry and plays it through the mouth AudioSource. If this collection is missing, it uses HeadSFX's smallDamage clips. An empty assigned collection skips playback rather than selecting that fallback.

The audited player vocal method ignores damage amounts below 0.25 and skips while its speech-blocking time is active. The supplied damage amount also controls volume, up to 1. Assigning clips changes the available voice sounds; it does not cause damage or decide when gameplay calls the vocal method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.speed
member.summary: The avatar's calculated movement-speed score used to set the movement rig's walking and jogging targets.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless score, not meters per second. RemapRig.SetAvatar sets its base movement speed to 2 × speed. Its movement update doubles that target in the Jog traversal state, before applying other movement factors such as crouching. An attached navigation agent is assigned a speed of 4 × speed.

For an illustrative score of 1, those base walking and jogging targets are 2 and 4 meters per second. The final motion can differ because of inputs, pose restrictions and physics. ComputeBaseStats derives this score from body size, mass and leg shape; RefreshBodyMeasurements can overwrite a direct edit, and assigning the avatar updates the movement rig's cached targets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.spineHighHipsToS3
member.summary: The calculated displacement from the high-hips level to the hip-center reference, in meters.

remarks.para: This is a Vector3 segment, not a single length. Its axes follow the Animator root's orientation; for an upright avatar, a downward segment has negative Y. The chest reference is based on the upper-arm bone midpoint and the hip reference on the upper-leg bone midpoint. The intermediate levels divide that span using the avatar's torso proportions and add the spine curve's forward/backward bend.

The rig combines these segments to position the torso. The getter converts the stored proportion to meters by multiplying by eyeHeight. It returns calculated geometry; changing a backing proportion without rebuilding the related rig measurements can leave the body inconsistent.

remarks.para: This is a Vector3 segment, not a single length. Its axes follow the Animator root's orientation; for an upright avatar, a downward segment has negative Y. The chest reference is based on the upper-arm bone midpoint and the hip reference on the upper-leg bone midpoint. The intermediate levels divide that span using the avatar's torso proportions and add the spine curve's forward/backward bend.

The rig combines these segments to position the torso. The getter converts the stored proportion to meters by multiplying by eyeHeight. It returns calculated geometry; changing a backing proportion without rebuilding the related rig measurements can leave the body inconsistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.sternumOffset
member.summary: The measured offset from the neck bone to the midpoint between the two upper-arm bones, in meters.

remarks.para: The game uses that midpoint as its chest/shoulder-center reference. The vector uses the Animator root's orientation. It is not the thickness of the chest or a mesh vertex displacement. The value comes from the stored proportion multiplied by eyeHeight and helps position the torso and shoulder chains.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.strengthGrip
member.summary: The calculated strength multiplier for holding and turning objects with the physical hand.

remarks.para: This is separate from the controller's squeeze input. PhysHand.CalibrateJoints uses it to configure the hand's rotational drive and maximum wrist torque. CylinderGrip also multiplies its squeeze-dependent joint break threshold by this score, so a stronger avatar can withstand a larger pull before that hand connection breaks.

It is a dimensionless body-derived score, not a force in newtons. ComputeBaseStats calculates it from body mass, size, hand size and wrist shape; RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates it. Existing arm settings may need recalibration after changing the stored result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.strengthLower
member.summary: The avatar's calculated strength multiplier for the physical legs; physics setup also uses it to set the foot body's resistance to spinning.

remarks.para: The score is dimensionless. ComputeBaseStats calculates it from body mass, eye height, thigh shape and leg proportions. PhysLimb.CalibrateLimbJoints uses it to scale the leg joints’ springs, damping and force allowances. PhysicsRig.SetAvatar also sets each component of the foot body's inertia tensor to 0.35 × strengthLower. An inertia tensor describes how difficult it is to turn a physical object: larger values need more torque for the same angular acceleration.

This is a generated result, not a direct walking-speed setting. RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates it. The verified foot-body effect occurs when the avatar is assigned to the physics rig; changing the cached score alone does not immediately change an already configured rigidbody.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.strengthUpper
member.summary: The avatar's calculated arm-strength multiplier used to configure the physical arms and hands.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless score, not a force in newtons. PhysicsRig supplies it to PhysHand.CalibrateJoints, which scales the arm's force values and the springs, damping and force allowances used by its shoulder, elbow and wrist connections. A physics connection keeps two simulated body parts together and drives them toward their target pose.

Higher values give those configured drives more strength; the final ability to move an object also depends on its mass and the rest of the solver. ComputeBaseStats calculates the score from body mass, size and arm proportions. RefreshBodyMeasurements recomputes it, so editing a stored result can be overwritten, and existing configured joints need updating to use a new score.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.surfaceData
member.summary: Selects the collision-surface data assigned to the avatar’s body surface providers when the physics rig adopts it.

remarks.para: SurfaceData describes how a material responds to contact and attacks, including penetration resistance, impact effects and decal references. A surface provider makes that data available on the body’s collision shapes; the renderer’s visible Material is a separate object.

PhysicsRig.SetAvatar copies a valid surfaceData reference into every body surface provider. If it is absent, the rig uses its default surface data. Changing the Avatar field later does not by itself repeat that assignment. A surfaceDataCard load can assign data afterward through its completion callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.surfaceDataCard
member.summary: Lets the physics rig load the avatar’s body surface data from a warehouse SurfaceDataCard.

remarks.para: During PhysicsRig.SetAvatar, a valid card reference is resolved and its SurfaceData asset is loaded. When loading completes, the callback assigns the loaded data to all of the rig’s body surface providers. This allows the collision material data to come from a packaged warehouse asset.

The rig also immediately assigns surfaceData, or its default surface if that field is absent. The card callback can therefore replace that initial choice later. A missing or unresolved card does not supply a replacement. Changing this reference after setup does not automatically start another load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.t1HeightPercent
member.summary: The humanoid neck bone's standing height divided by the avatar's eye height.

remarks.para: The name refers to the upper-spine reference, but the measured source is the neck bone. The denominator is eyeHeight, not the model's total height. For example, 0.85 means the neck joint is 85% as high as the eye-center measurement. RefreshBodyMeasurements uses it to calculate chestHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.t7Local
member.summary: The measured upper-spine segment leading down from the neck toward the upper chest, in meters.

remarks.para: With an UpperChest bone, this is UpperChest position minus neck position, rotated into the Animator root's orientation. Without UpperChest, the game uses half the chest-minus-neck vector. It is a segment displacement, not a world position or a localTransform.position value.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.t7OffsetZ
member.summary: The calculated forward/backward deviation of the upper-spine landmark from a straight chest-to-hips line.

remarks.para: GenerateSpineCurve subtracts the straight line's Z value at t7Y from the measured landmark's Z value. Both are divided by eyeHeight, so this result is a fraction of eye height, not a distance in meters. For example, 0.02 corresponds to 3.2 cm when eyeHeight is 1.6 meters; positive Z follows the Animator root's forward direction.
This is a cached calculation result. GenerateSpineCurve overwrites it; writing it alone does not move a bone or rebuild the spine curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.t7Y
member.summary: The calculated fraction locating the upper-spine landmark along the chest-to-hips span.

remarks.para: This is a fraction of the generated spine's vertical span, not a Y coordinate in meters or a percentage from 0 to 100. The chest/shoulder-center reference is 0 and the hip-center reference is 1. GenerateSpineCurve calculates the value from the measured spine segments and reference offsets.
This is a cached geometry result. GenerateSpineCurve overwrites it; writing it alone does not rebuild the curve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.thighUpperEllipse
member.summary: The oval cross-section used to calculate the avatar's upper thigh shape and generated collision geometry.

remarks.para: A cross-section is the shape seen if the limb were sliced across its length. XRadius and ZRadius are fractions of eyeHeight, not meters: with eyeHeight = 1.6 meters, an illustrative radius of 0.03 gives 4.8 cm from the center to the surface, or 9.6 cm across when unbiased. XBias and ZBias are dimensionless fractions of the matching radius. The center offsets in meters are XBias × XRadius × eyeHeight and ZBias × ZRadius × eyeHeight. A bias of zero centers the opposite surface extents; an illustrative bias of 0.5 moves their center half a radius, or 2.4 cm with the radius example above. The left limb mirrors the X direction.

The limb-shape calculation blends this section with the knee section as it moves along the limb. These values describe generated geometry; they do not resize the imported visible mesh. Physics calibration builds meshes from the shape descriptions and installs them in collision components, so editing the description alone does not replace an already generated collider.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.thoracicRom
member.summary: The upper-spine bending allowances, in degrees, used when the movement rig solves the torso pose.

remarks.para: The four components are X = bending forward, Y = turning around the spine, Z = bending sideways, and W = bending backward. For example, X = 45 gives a 45-degree forward-bending allowance; these values are angles, not fractions or distances.

The solver combines the forward, sideways and backward allowances with the lower-spine allowances and blends them according to the bend direction. The Y component also determines how much of the body's turning is assigned to the upper spine relative to the neck and lower spine. They guide the solved pose rather than defining four independent Unity physics-joint limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.tippyToeExtension
member.summary: The calculated extra leg-and-foot reach available beyond the avatar's measured standing arrangement, in meters.

remarks.para: The calculation uses the right leg. It starts with the sum of the upper- and lower-leg lengths minus the straight hip-to-foot distance, then adds twice the sum of the foot-to-toe distance and that offset's vertical component. This includes spare reach from straightening the leg and rotating the foot; it is not simply the toe bone's height.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.
The audited measurement, proportion and leg-solver code establishes this geometry result, but does not establish a separate live movement control for changing this value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.toeHeight
member.summary: The right toe bone's standing height above the Animator root, in meters.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar subtracts the Animator root's world Y coordinate from the right toe bone's world Y coordinate. This is a measured bone height, not the toe mesh's thickness or a live distance from the floor. The body-proportion calculations use it with each foot-to-toe offset to reconstruct leg placement.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.toeLfLocal
member.summary: The measured offset from the left humanoid foot bone to its toe bone, in the game's calculated foot frame.

remarks.para: The vector is in meters. The frame points forward along the ankle-to-toe direction after removing its component along the Animator root's up direction; its up direction follows the root. This means it is not necessarily the imported foot bone's local axes. The leg solver uses this offset when bending the foot for extra reach, and the body-proportion calculation combines its vertical component with toeHeight.

This is a stored result of avatar measurement, not a live reading of the moving bone. PrecomputeAvatar creates these measurements; calculating them again can replace a direct change to the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.vitality
member.summary: The avatar's calculated durability score, used to set maximum health.

remarks.para: Health.SetAvatar sets maximum health to 10 × vitality. For example, an illustrative vitality of 1 gives 10 health points and 2 gives 20. When the old maximum is positive, it preserves the fraction of health remaining: switching from 5 out of 10 to a 20-point maximum gives 10 out of 20.

ComputeBaseStats derives vitality from body mass, eye height and the measured chest-to-hips span. It is a generated score, not the current health value. RefreshBodyMeasurements can replace a direct edit; the health component updates its maximum when SetAvatar runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.wristLf
member.summary: An optional left wrist bone that the art rig aligns and drives with the solved arm.

remarks.para: PrecomputeAvatar uses this reference’s orientation when calculating the left arm’s art alignment. ArtRig can update the bone during output. Reset initially copies the humanoid left hand bone into this slot when it exists, and a custom model can supply its separate wrist Transform.

The shared cached forearm and wrist-to-hand lengths are measured on the right side using wristRt. Changing wristLf does not change those scalar length measurements. Assign the model’s references before measuring and mounting the avatar; replacing this Transform alone does not rebuild the art alignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar.wristRt
member.summary: The right wrist bone used to split the measured forearm from an optional wrist-to-hand segment.

remarks.para: With a separate wrist reference, PrecomputeAvatar measures elbow-to-wrist as the lower arm and wrist-to-humanoid-hand as the carpal segment. Without that reference, it measures elbow-to-hand and uses a zero carpal segment. Reset initially copies the humanoid hand bone into this slot when that bone exists; a custom rig can provide a separate wrist bone.
ArtRig can update this bone during output. Assign references before measuring and mounting the avatar; replacing the Transform alone does not recalculate limb lengths.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain
member.summary: Connects an NPC's navigation and combat controller to its physics puppet, death notifications, and spawn-group lifecycle.

remarks.para: The physics puppet is the NPC's simulated body, with connected parts that can fall as a ragdoll. Callbacks are routines called to perform or report an action. behaviour makes the navigation and combat decisions; puppetMaster controls the physical body. This brain exposes the behaviour's mental state, records death and resurrection, forwards callbacks with itself as the argument, and stores a configuration override. The arena entrance timer can request the puppet's death if entrance takes too long.

NPCs may be pooled: the same object can be reused for later spawns. Pool initialization connects puppet notifications and may clear the configuration override; deinitialization disconnects those notifications and clears onDeathDelegate and onResurrectDelegate. Use the lifecycle when setting references and subscribing to callbacks.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain.SpawnGroupEvent
member.summary: Unity event carrying an AI brain and an ignore flag to listeners of .

remarks.para: The first argument identifies the brain that raised the event. The second is the boolean supplied to SpawnGroupIgnore: SpawnGroup's listener adds that brain to its ignored set for true and removes it for false. Raising this event does not itself despawn the NPC or remove it from the group's living and dead collections.

AIBrain.Awake creates a new event and stores it in OnGroupDeregister. Attach runtime listeners after that initialization. A SpawnGroup installs its listener when the NPC spawns and removes it when the NPC despawns. Other listeners can give the same flag their own behavior.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.Encounter
member.summary: Coordinates NPC spawn groups, their completion progress, and a temporary music cue for an encounter connected to a zone.

remarks.para: Configure spawnGroups before initialization. Awake prepares their cancellation slots and manual spawners; Start gathers assets and optional toggles. WarmupEncounter can create an initial NPC population, while StartEncounter runs the ordinary population loops. Zone entry caches the entering entity and starts the encounter; zone exit requests PauseEncounter.

Completion records an event and prevents another start until reset.
