The base early update calculates a cached pause state from the shared pause request, game initialization, and level-loading status. OpenControllerRig uses it to skip normal input/tracking work, and RigManager uses it to stop its later early-update rig passes. Getters return the current caches; they do not clear button edges or guarantee a fresh sample while paused.

Here Transform means Unity’s scene object component carrying position, rotation and scale. A Transform frame may be local to a parent or expressed in world coordinates; it is not itself a Rigidbody or a velocity.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.AttackType
member.summary: Classifies a hit so receiving components can select which attacks to react to and how to process their damage.

remarks.para: These are unitless flags: independent on/off bits that can be combined. The named values are Piercing 1, Blunt 2, Fire 8, Slicing 16, Stabbing 32 and None 64. The name describes the kind of hit, while the separate Attack.damage value carries its amount. None is a set bit, not value 0.

The | operator combines flags. For example, Piercing | Blunt has value 3. GenericAttackReceiver is a component that responds to incoming attacks; its configured attackType filter accepts a hit if any bit overlaps. A filter of 3 therefore accepts Piercing or Blunt, then calls its registered event actions with the incoming damage value. A filter of 0 accepts neither.

Each consumer chooses how to interpret the stored value. Enemy_Health.OnReceivedDamage compares the whole incoming value with its configured mod_Type, the category for a special damage multiplier. A combined value of 3 does not exactly match Piercing 1 in that method. Combining flags therefore does not guarantee that every damage or effect routine treats them as separate categories.

Assign the category when constructing the hit, and configure the receiving component’s filter or special-damage category before it handles the hit. A category assignment is stored data; the receiving code performs the event or damage response when the attack arrives.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.CartridgeData
member.summary: Links a cartridge's ammo-lookup name, projectile settings, intact-round object, and spent-case object.

remarks.para: This is a ScriptableObject: a Unity asset storing shared settings without being a scene object itself. Guns and ammo systems reference it to describe a round. Its projectile profile selects the flying bullet's emission, flight, and damage settings; its two Spawnable values identify object templates and spawn-policy settings for intact-round and spent-case objects.

The stored name falls back to the asset's Unity object name during Awake, Unity's setup method when the asset is loaded, or a later Name read if it is still empty. Ammo-group registration saves a mapping using that name. A readable caliber label is still text and does not determine the projectile's physical settings.

Firing and ejection have separate effects. A gun passes the projectile profile to its emitter when firing. Ejecting an unfired round selects the intact cartridge, while ejecting a spent round selects the case. These requests can finish later; their settings and the gun's chamber state do not prove that a spawn completed successfully.

For example, two cartridge assets can use different projectile profiles while selecting the same casing template. Choose stable names before registering ammo groups, and provide appropriate projectile and ejection assets before those paths use them. Changing this shared configuration does not automatically replace objects already created from it.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.LootTableData
member.summary: A saved Unity settings asset that rolls a random description from its entries.

remarks.para: This is a ScriptableObject, a Unity asset that stores settings independently of a scene object. It pairs each possible object description with a percentage number and lets a caller select one. A spawnable description holds the object-template reference and pool policy, the rules for limiting and reusing spawned objects; selection does not create that object.

GetLootItem chooses a whole-number roll from 1 through 99 and searches cumulative percentage ranges in array order. The percentages have no physical units and are not automatically adjusted to total 100. For example, one entry with percentage 50 wins rolls 1–50, while 51–99 return an empty description. The result is not guaranteed to identify a usable object.

In the inspected ObjectDestructible destruction paths, a breakable object asks this table for a description, checks whether that description is valid, then requests its object at the assigned spawn target. That later request is separate from this asset's selection operation and can finish later.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.MagazineData
member.summary: Saved magazine settings for capacity, socket compatibility and the item requested when a magazine is spawned.

remarks.para: A ScriptableObject is a Unity asset that stores reusable settings. Create this asset through Variables/Magazine Item in Unity’s asset-creation menu, then assign it to the magazine or weapon configuration that needs it.

rounds is the capacity in whole cartridges. platform is the text label checked by the inspected AmmoSocket insertion path. spawnable identifies the saved magazine item and its spawning policy. For a 30-round magazine, choose rounds 30, matching magazine/socket platform text, and a crate configured with the intended Magazine behavior.

The current loaded ammunition belongs to MagazineState, which keeps its own cartridge list and references this settings asset. Editing the asset changes the configuration read by later operations; it does not itself refill a magazine, request a new item or insert one into a weapon.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.ProjectileData
member.summary: A shared data asset that configures projectile spawn requests, flight setup, hit reporting and emission patterns.

remarks.para: As a ScriptableObject, this is a Unity data asset that components can share; it is not itself a flying object. The spawnable identifies the item template. The emitter requests its objects, and a successfully returned object with a Projectile component receives the flight settings.

Mass in kilograms, starting speed in metres per second and attack category are copied during each projectile's setup. The damage multiplier is read from the shared asset when a hit report is built. Editing a shared asset can therefore affect later hits differently from already copied flight settings.

POINT requests one straight projectile. CONE requests a straight centre projectile plus random additional copies using count, angle in degrees and radius in metres. SPHERE has no spawning branch in the inspected emitter. For example, CONE with count 4, angle 20 and radius 0.1 requests one centre projectile and three extra projectiles starting within 10 centimetres of the centre and using turn limits from 2 to 20 degrees.

The count, angle and radius sliders shown in Unity's editor are configuration aids; the emitter does not enforce those ranges as runtime limits. Spawn requests can finish later and are not a guarantee that all configured copies were created.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.SpawnPolicyData
member.summary: Reusable settings for grouping spawn requests, choosing a tracked-object limit rule, and deciding whether returned objects are deactivated.

remarks.para: This is a ScriptableObject, a Unity asset that stores settings rather than a scene object. Assign it to a Spawnable’s policyData or a CrateSpawner’s policyData before requesting a spawn. A pool stores objects for reuse instead of creating and destroying a copy every time. The policy tracks successful spawns and pending requests above that pool; its maxSize is a threshold for those counts, not a limit on all stored copies.

groupByCrate determines whether each crate, the stored definition of an item, gets its own policy within the same settings asset and groupID. A groupID is an optional numeric label supplied with a spawn request. mode chooses whether reaching the threshold grows the group, removes its oldest or newest tracked spawn before requesting another, or returns no object. skipDisable controls the final GameObject deactivation when returning an object, while cleanup and bookkeeping still happen.

The running policy keeps a reference to this settings asset. Later spawn checks read maxSize and mode, and later policy-managed despawns read skipDisable. Editing those settings does not immediately resize the group or change objects already in the scene. Changing groupByCrate changes later policy selection without regrouping already tracked objects. Requests made with ignorePolicy true bypass these rules.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Spawnable
member.summary: Describes the asset and optional pool policy to use for a spawn request.

remarks.para: crateRef identifies the saved asset in the warehouse, BONELAB's asset catalog. policyData optionally chooses how a group handles its spawn allowance and reuses objects. A pool stores objects that can be returned and used again. This small data structure describes a request; it is not the spawned object.

For example, combine a basketball crate reference with a policy that allows two outstanding basketballs, prepare the crate's pool, and submit this data to AssetSpawner. The spawn call supplies the placement separately. Assigning the fields or calling IsValid does not create a basketball.

Spawning may need to wait for asset loading. Starting a request is different from receiving a successfully completed result: the spawner can finish with no object if it cannot resolve the crate or pool, or the policy refuses another spawn. Use the completed result or the successful spawn callback, a function the spawner calls after obtaining an object, before accessing the spawned object.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Data.Weight
member.summary: Names three weight categories: , , and .

remarks.para: An enum is a set of named choices. These choices have category codes LIGHT = 0, MEDIUM = 1, and HEAVY = 2. The numbers have no physical unit and do not specify kilograms or a multiplier. Choosing a label does not itself alter an object’s physics mass.

For example, a Weight variable set to Weight.HEAVY identifies the heavy category, and a comparison with Weight.HEAVY recognizes that choice. This enum does not define mass boundaries between the categories or automatically run a collision or movement rule.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.DebugDraw
member.summary: Editor drawing helpers whose static drawing routines produce no output in the inspected game build.

remarks.para: The checked text, line, circle, transform and log drawing methods are marked for the Unity editor and all resolve to an empty implementation in this game build. They do not draw a world-space guide or on-screen message there. An editor implementation is not available in that inspected code.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FirearmCartridge
member.summary: Controls an ejected firearm cartridge’s launch settings, shell sound-component mode and renderer hide settings across pool reuse.

remarks.para: The cartridge works with a MarrowEntity, the component grouping its gameplay and physics parts, and with Poolee, the component connecting it to reusable spawned objects. Awake, Unity’s initial component setup call, registers the cartridge for pool callbacks. Its Despawn method forwards through the linked MarrowEntity.

ForceInDirection sets movement and spin on its Rigidbody, Unity’s component for simulated physical motion. It combines the host object’s movement with randomized contributions from the live startSpeed and startAxisSpeed settings. Their defaults are 2 Unity world units per second and 100 radians per second when their supplied direction vectors have length 1. The linear speed is 2 m/s only if this scene uses one Unity world unit per metre.

MakeStatic and MakeDynamic toggle a flag and the enabled setting of the shell sound component. Those names do not mean these methods freeze or unfreeze the physical object. Pool cleanup clears that flag and enables the sound component if needed, then clears the extra hide setting on the listed renderers. For example, a hidden casing can have that hide setting cleared for reuse without resetting its configured launch speeds.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.FlyingGun
member.summary: Moves the player through trigger-controlled flight and offers a separate optional no-clip toggle.

remarks.para: While its trigger grip is held, it smooths a speed goal from trigger amount, turns a world direction toward the muzzle's forward direction when pressing the trigger, and applies velocity changes to the player rig with gravity compensation. The firePoint position is not a force origin.

The no-clip toggle changes the cached player bodies' collision detection and, where applicable, the gun entity's trackers/colliders. Releasing the grip starts one-frame-delayed collision cleanup, while the drop sound starts immediately.
OnFlyEnabled is a static component-enable notification after grip subscriptions, not proof of a trigger press or active no-clip. The rings and sound helper provide held visual/audio feedback.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip
member.summary: Lets a free object’s grip be targeted at a distance and brought into the player’s hand through force grab.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s startup routine; a GameObject is a scene object carrying components, and the host is the physical object owning the grip. Start finds the Grip on the same GameObject, enables far hovering on its host, and subscribes to the grip’s distant-hand events. Input qualifies when the primary interaction button is pressed this update while secondary is held, or secondary is pressed this update while primary is held. That combination starts a physics-step pull toward the hand’s shape-specific handle target, the desired hand/object position and rotation.

The pull locks that hand’s targeting, applies motion corrections, then uses the grip’s snatch sequence to finish attachment. A snatch is the near-hand sequence that attaches the hand’s physics connection to the object. If another hand takes the object, the original pull is stopped and cleaned up. Configure the Grip and host physics references before using this component; Enable alone does not start a pull.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ForcePullGrip.GripState
member.summary: Reports whether a force-pull grip is idle, targeted from a distance or actively pulling toward a hand.

remarks.para: The values are IDELING (0), LONGHOVERING (1) and PULLING (2). Far-hover begin selects LONGHOVERING for an unattached host; CoPull selects PULLING when it begins; far-hover end or pull cleanup returns to IDELING in the corresponding paths.

Use ForcePullGrip.state to observe these stages. Writing a state value alone does not start a pull, create a physics joint (a connection between simulated bodies) or enable the component: the native state setter only stores the value. LONGHOVERING has no built-in waiting-time requirement in the far-hover begin/end routines.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModDownloader
member.summary: Downloads and installs mod content, and manages saved records of rejected mod.io files.

remarks.para: A pallet is a package of mod content such as objects, avatars, or levels. DownloadMod fetches the selected target, unpacks the downloaded archive, and installs the pallet. Its task must complete successfully before the download and installation can be treated as finished.

The settings helpers remember a rejected upload by pairing its mod ID with its file ID. Subscription checks can skip that same upload while allowing a different file for the mod to be considered. These records are saved in mod_settings.json, separate from the downloaded content.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager
member.summary: Connects BONELAB to mod.io, restores saved login tokens, and runs device-code login when the player needs to authorize the game.

remarks.para: This is a Unity component, an object whose lifecycle methods run as the game enables or disables it. When enabled, it creates a REST client for ordinary HTTP API requests and a WebSocket client for later server login messages, both for BONELAB game ID 3809. It then starts checking saved credentials asynchronously without waiting for the check to finish.

An access token is a string identifying a signed-in user. The manager reads one from mod_settings.json in Unity's persistent data directory, where files survive between runs. LogIn first tries token restoration; if that fails, it starts the device-code exchange and lets event callbacks update the login interface. A callback is a subscribed function run when an event happens.

For example, login can begin with a progress panel, then show the server's code and login URL, then close the panel after a response with code 200. On that successful response, the manager sets its stored login flag, applies the token, saves the settings, and then runs the completion callback. Sending the request alone does not complete this sequence.

Disabling this component clears the login flag, requests cancellation of ongoing work, and disposes both clients. The stored IsLoggedIn value reports earlier success; reading it does not ask mod.io to revalidate credentials.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.ModIOManager.UserCodePromptHandler
member.summary: Defines a callback that receives the mod.io login code and page address so the game can show them to the player.

remarks.para: A callback is a function subscribed to run when an event happens. This type is the callback for RequestUserCodeEntry. The manager calls it on Unity’s main thread, where Unity normally updates game objects and the interface, when a device-login response arrives.

Its loginResponseContext parameter contains Code, the text code to show; LoginUrl, the address of the login page; and DateExpires, the expiry time measured in seconds since 00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970. For example, a callback can show the code beside a button opening the supplied login page so the player can authorize the game there.

The callback returns UniTask, an asynchronous operation, and the response handler waits for the task returned by the event delegate. This task can represent preparing the prompt interface. It is not a player-entered code or proof that login succeeded. The prompt response does not set IsLoggedIn; a later successful response supplies the access token identifying the signed-in user.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModIOModTarget
member.summary: Describes a mod.io file release so Forklift can request its information and download it.

remarks.para: A download target holds the details telling the downloader where content should come from. This target stores GameId, the game’s numeric ID; ModId, the mod’s numeric ID; and ModfileId, the numeric ID of one uploaded file release. The downloader passes all three stored values to mod.io’s GetModfile request.

For example, a BONELAB target can use game ID 3809 plus the selected mod’s ID and its desired release’s file ID. Each ID is a signed 64-bit number identifying an object, with no measurement units. The target also carries the inherited thumbnailOverride string, which Pack saves alongside these IDs.

Pack adds these values to JSON for saving through an object store. Unpack loads available properties from the stored object; missing properties leave previous values unchanged. Creating or editing this description alone does not start a download.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Forklift.Model.ModListing
member.summary: Describes a repository mod so the menu can show it, match installed content, and select a download target.

remarks.para: A listing stores the mod’s barcode, title, description, author credit, version label and preview-image URL. The barcode is a text identifier used to match the listing to a pallet, the bundle of assets belonging to the mod. These values are metadata; the target dictionary holds the separate instructions for obtaining that content.

Targets maps names to download-target objects. The resolver checks its configured preference order to find a usable target. For example, a mod.io target can specify an uploaded file by game, mod and file IDs. The menu copies the title and chosen image URL into row data, and its version display can use the listing’s label.

Pack saves metadata and object-store references to named targets. Unpack restores available fields and rebuilds Targets only when the targets property is present. Repository is a weak association with the source catalog, so retaining the listing alone does not keep that catalog alive.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GenericGrip
member.summary: Lets a hand find a grab target on collider surfaces instead of using one fixed handle location.

remarks.para: The grip gathers collider shapes during startup. Its score check finds a candidate near the hand handle and raycasts that shape from the palm, using a ray length of half the avatar’s measured arm length. A hit and the subsequent hand-facing test are required for that checked candidate.

Each hand has its own cached surface point and orientation data. Hover updates use that cache to place and turn the hand target on the moving object, then run the usual Grip hover behavior. Configure the object’s colliders and physics host before startup so the intended surfaces survive the host-Rigidbody filter.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GenericGrip.HandToGenericGripState
member.summary: Stores one hand’s last surface-contact and handle-pose measurements so a GenericGrip can align that hand with the object.

remarks.para: GenericGrip keeps a separate entry for each Hand in genericHandStates. ValidateGripScore finds a nearby collider surface, casts a ray toward it and records the hit point, outward surface direction, hand-back direction and handle pose. A handle pose is the position and rotation of the reference point used to align a gripping hand.

After an accepted hit, raycastPoint is relative to the GenericGrip transform, while raycastNormal and backOfHandNormal are directions expressed in that transform’s axes. Directions describe orientation rather than a distance. The field named worldHandleTransform is also converted to a grip-relative position and rotation in the accepted-hit path, despite its name.

OnHandHoverUpdate transforms the saved point and directions back into world space and turns the hand’s saved handle orientation toward the surface before setting the hand’s world target. Keeping the successful measurements relative to the grip lets that target follow the object as it moves and turns.

isRaycastHit records whether the collider ray test hit. The later grip-score calculation can still reject the contact because the hand faces the wrong way, without clearing that flag. Use the full grip validation result rather than treating the flag alone as proof of a usable grab. Repeated validation replaces these measurements; the cache does not create a collider or physics joint.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Grip
member.summary: A hand interaction point that supplies desired handle poses, per-hand grip state, and the lifecycle of holding and releasing an object.

remarks.para: Grip is the shared foundation for shape-specific grips such as CylinderGrip, SphereGrip, and TargetGrip. A subclass decides how its shape accepts hover candidates and can configure the joint: the physics connection that keeps the hand and object together. Several base configuration hooks deliberately do nothing.

The base class stores separate hand targets and pose selections, handles snatch and attachment callbacks, and records connected-body motion for ordinary release velocity. A snatch is the sequence moving a hand onto the grip; an attachment callback is a routine called to handle a hold beginning or ending. A desired target is where the hand should reach; it is distinct from the physical hand’s current pose and from directly moving the scene object.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun
member.summary: Coordinates a firearm's magazine feeding, chamber and hammer states, trigger input, slide movement, shot effects and animated cartridge art.

remarks.para: The main pieces have separate jobs: AmmoSocket handles physical magazine interaction, MagazineState holds magazine rounds, CartridgeData supplies the loaded round's projectile/ejection definitions, and GunSFX plays action sounds. Gun combines them into a firing cycle.

For a normal shot, the slide must be forward, the hammer cocked and the chamber hold an unfired round; a request can still fail those checks. Non-manual modes animate the action automatically. Manual mode needs the player to work the action again. Pool initialization applies isLoaded/isCharged as loading options; those flags are not current readiness reports.

For shot notifications, onFireDelegate receives this gun after projectile emission starts. Fire attempts, animation state and physical hand input are distinct, so changing one flag or visual alone does not complete the whole firing setup.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.AnimationStates
member.summary: Selects the gun's supported visual action clips and their forward or reversed playback direction.

remarks.para: Selecting an animation is separate from directly changing the logical slide state. SetAnimationState displays a clip position; PlayAnimationState advances a timed sequence.

Normalized clip position is a fraction: 0 is the clip beginning and 1 its end. Forward variants complete at 1; reversed variants complete at 0. Some completed sequences schedule chamber/hammer/slide work for the end of the frame. FIRE and FIRERETURN are present in the enum but are not handled as clip selections in the audited Gun methods.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.CartridgeStates
member.summary: Distinguishes an empty chamber, a live round and the spent case left after firing.

remarks.para: Gun.cartridgeState controls shot versus dry-fire behavior, chamber art, and whether ejection uses the full-round or empty-case object. It is separate from chamberedCartridge, which holds ammunition definitions; assigning only the enum does not create matching data or run a loading/ejection operation.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.HammerStates
member.summary: Records whether the gun’s hammer is ready to strike the chambered round.

remarks.para: The hammer is part of the firing action, separate from the round and slide position. Gun.hammerState uses UNCOCKED and COCKED for readiness checks; selecting an enum value alone does not load a round or animate a slide stroke.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Gun.SlideStates
member.summary: Tracks whether a gun's slide is ready for firing, in a pull or return phase, or locked open.

remarks.para: The slide is the moving part pulled back during the gun's loading cycle. Gun.slideState records logical steps in that cycle; the separate animation state and slide override, which means manual position control, govern the visible movement. The override amount is a unitless position fraction: 0 is the forward/start endpoint and 1 the rear pull endpoint. The forward-return animation uses 1 minus this amount, and the gun does not universally clamp arbitrary assignments to the endpoint range. The logical state and visible direction need not match at every moment.

Assigning a state alone does not eject or load a cartridge, cock the hammer, or play a slide sound. Those actions belong to the gun's transition methods. Fire requires RETURNED before its ordinary firing checks can proceed.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunManager
member.summary: Collects grab, release and firing notifications for guns held by matching player rigs, and supplies the normal trigger-input firing permission.

remarks.para: The first accepted grab subscribes to Gun.onFireDelegate, the gun's firing-notification event, so the manager can forward that notification. Counts allow two hands to hold one gun while keeping one forwarding subscription; the last counted release removes it. _playerTag chooses which rigs qualify.

Listeners are registered code called for these reports: grab/drop listeners receive Hand and Gun; fire listeners receive Gun. These notifications report game actions rather than performing physical grabs or shots. EnableGunFire and DisableGunFire gate the normal Gun.Update input path; direct Fire calls bypass that manager check.
_playerTag is the manager's configured matching rule for the entity belonging to the hand's physics rig. It is not automatically a local-player lookup or a test of the gun's tag.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.GunSFX
member.summary: Provides audio and controller-vibration feedback for gun handling and firing events.

remarks.para: Configure clip arrays for gunshots, empty-trigger clicks, grip grabs, slide movement and magazine changes. Each method requests one randomly chosen clip for its event; the gun or other calling code decides when those events occurred. This component does not launch bullets, move the slide or insert magazines itself.

GunShot uses its retained _gunshotMap player at a world position. Handling sounds use local positions parented to the gun. DryFire, SlideLock, slide movement and magazine methods also send short vibrations to hands attached to the InteractableHost cached in Start. This host tracks attached hands. Unity runs Start once before this enabled component’s first frame update; it gets the host from this GameObject and stores that reference.

fireSlow, dryFireSlow and slideLockFireSlow are alternate lists for Time.timeScale of 0.51 or less. Time.timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed and 0.5 is half speed. Empty alternate arrays fall back to normal recordings; normal arrays must be nonempty for sound. GunShot uses the normal array length for its slow-list index, while the two local playback events use the slow array’s own length. GunError is an empty native hook.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand
member.summary: Manages a player hand’s nearby and distant receiver selection, held-object state and attachment joints.

remarks.para: A Hand links the controller and hand animation to the physical hand components. It searches for eligible receivers near the palm, can choose a distant target, records the attached GameObject and hand inventory item, and prepares a ConfigurableJoint: the physics connection used to hold an object.

PhysHand and the Rigidbody supply the physical hand behavior, while Hand coordinates the interaction state. Its public Actions hold subscribed routines that report nearby hover changes, receiver attachment/removal, runtime-skeleton updates and requested anchor updates. The runtime skeleton is the character model’s animated bones. The anchor Actions run before their joint positions are written, rather than reporting every possible direct change to a joint.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose
member.summary: A reusable Unity asset that supplies finger poses, handle alignment, wrist rotation corrections and angular freedom for a hand grip.

remarks.para: Assign it to a Grip's handPose or select it for a particular hand with Grip.SetHandPose. HandPoseAnimator blends its samples for grip size, hand rotation and finger opening, then applies the resulting finger rotations. The handle data also determines how the hand and held object fit together.

The pose axes orient that handle frame, the left/right offset rotations adjust tracked wrist orientation, and the swing/twist limits supply physical rotation allowances. These settings control different parts of the grab; changing a finger sample does not by itself change the object's collider or the physics joint's angular limits.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseData
member.summary: Defines one authored hand pose that the animator can blend with neighboring poses and grip sizes.

remarks.para: The sample stores a quaternion, four numbers representing orientation, for each finger’s first driven bone and degree-valued Z-axis bend angles for the next two bones. Those bends use the axes of the bone’s parent, the bone or object it is attached under. It also stores the handle’s placement relative to each hand, reverse neutral hand placement, and separate handle placement for the visible art hands.

nativePry locates the sample in the solver’s pitch/roll/yaw angle coordinates, in degrees. PoseDataGroup holds samples for one handle radius: the distance from a round handle’s center to its outside, using local Unity distance units, normally meters. The animator blends corresponding samples between radius groups, then blends the finger rotations and handle placements using the requested angle coordinates; controller curl and transitions can modify the final pose.

All radius groups need matching sample order because the runtime pairs samples by index and takes the lookup coordinates from the first group. The neutral handle getters also read the first sample of the first radius group. These fields describe authored pose data; the animator writes the selected results to its finger and handle transforms.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPose.PoseDataGroup
member.summary: A set of finger and handle samples for one grip size in a HandPose asset.

remarks.para: HandPoseAnimator blends between size groups and between hand-rotation samples within them, letting the hand fit differently sized grips while retaining the intended placement. Each group stores its size point in radius and its pose samples in poseArray.

Keep groups sorted by size and use matching sample layouts across them. Grip size is adjusted using the animator's cached unitless hand-size factor, which scales the fixed reference hand to the avatar, so a larger avatar can use the same reference-hand pose data. SetHandSize copies that factor from Avatar.handSizeMult and computes and stores its inverse. Later Avatar edits affect this size conversion only after SetHandSize runs again.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandPoseAnimator
member.summary: Blends authored grip poses and controller finger curl, then writes the result to one hand’s finger transforms. Uses samples and matching .

remarks.para: Use one animator per hand and set handedness to match its transforms. A transform stores a bone’s position, rotation and scale; its local values are relative to its parent in the finger skeleton. Angle sample coordinates and later-segment bend angles use degrees. Reference-hand distances use Unity distance units, normally meters, and finger curl is a unitless input toward the open or sampled grip pose. A HandPose asset supplies finger rotations and handle placements for different reference-hand grip sizes and pitch/roll/yaw angle coordinates. The solver chooses and blends those samples; it does not detect finger contact against the held object’s collider, its physics shape.

SetHandPose builds sample caches and starts an asset transition. SetHandSize captures the avatar’s unitless hand-size factor and its reciprocal, meaning 1 divided by that factor. The factor compares linear hand size with the reference hand: 1 is reference size and 1.5 is 50 percent larger. SetCylinderRadius converts a handle’s radius by multiplying it by that saved reciprocal. Changing the Avatar’s hand-size value alone does not refresh the conversion; run SetHandSize again to capture the new factor. ApplyRotationAnimationBlend supplies angle coordinates, and SetFingers updates smoothed per-finger curl. SolvePose or SolvePoseForHandle prepares the pose, and ApplyPoseToTransforms writes local finger rotations. These are separate calls, so changing an input alone does not immediately move the bones.

Assign all three driven transforms for every finger. SetArtRefs obtains only the five first segments from a Unity Animator; it does not populate the later segments. SetHandSize also changes the finger transforms’ local positions to the scaled reference-hand layout. Those positions and the local pose axes must suit the rig used for this hand.

Awake is Unity’s initialization routine; here it allocates the curl-override array, creates the open finger pose and selects defaultHandPose. The hand rig drives subsequent updates. Switch assets through SetHandPose rather than assigning pose directly, because the method’s equality guard can otherwise leave the old sample caches in place.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever
member.summary: Receives a hand's hover, held-object and joint notifications for an owning grabbable object.

remarks.para: Its callback methods are routines called to perform or report an interaction action. The ten base hover, held-object, attachment and detachment notification hooks are empty; receiver types such as Grip provide their own hover selection and grabbing behavior. Other base routines perform setup, permission changes or grip scoring.

Host supplies the object's physics and permissions. IsEnabled controls whether automatic hand searches can consider this receiver, and HandJointConfig supplies settings for a grab joint, the physics connection between hand and object.
The game spells this type "HandReciever". The spelling is part of its code name.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandSFX
member.summary: Produces hand contact, melee, grab, release, force-pull and inventory-slot sounds, with collision-based controller vibration.

remarks.para: Its assigned CollisionCollector gathers contacts. HandSFX processes those contacts across physics and rendered-frame updates, filters held-hand and repeated impacts, and selects impact, fist, slap, backhand or scrape audio. A collider is the invisible physics shape that supplies those contact points and directions.

The explicit Grab, Drop, BodySlot and ForcePull methods are sound notifications for actions performed by other interaction code; they do not perform the grab, release, storage or pull themselves. PunchAttack can separately send a blunt attack message to contacted receivers.

Several retained settings are inactive in the inspected implementation, including whoosh, VelocityPitchCurve and grabBig. The updates here do not play a movement-whoosh loop. Scrapes use non-looping managed playback with contact-triggered retriggers and volume/pitch adjustment.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeadSFX
member.summary: Plays the character’s mouth vocals and turns qualifying head contacts into blunt attacks with separate impact audio.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics component for a simulated body. An AudioSource is the scene component that plays audio clips.

The PhysicsRig is the character’s simulated body. Its current avatar can supply jump-effort, pain, dying, death and recovery sound banks; the corresponding arrays on HeadSFX are fallbacks when those sound-data assets are missing. Double-jump audio uses its own bank. Eligible vocal calls select random clips and play them through the assigned mouth AudioSource.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, finds the Rigidbody on this scene object, routes the assigned mouth source to the vocal mixer and registers contact callbacks on the assigned collision collector. A callback is a routine called to report an action, such as a contact. Assign the PhysicsRig, mouth source, mouth low-pass filter and collision collector before using the relevant paths; the audio references are not found automatically.

The speaking flag follows a game-time deadline rather than actual source playback. Vocal helpers check the deadline but do not extend it themselves. The mouth low-pass filter is refreshed when playback is prepared and depends on facing the main camera. Headbutt detection separately checks self contacts, impulse, velocity, facing, cached relative head rotation and the collider’s layer; it attempts attack receiver dispatch before requesting impact audio.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Health.HealthMode
member.summary: Selects the player's damage-to-death and recovery rules through .

remarks.para: Player_Health interprets these values when handling damage and entering its dying sequence: Invincible skips that death transition, Mortal allows the ordinary grace period and recovery, and InsantDeath uses the special countdown and skips ordinary post-hit regeneration. Invincible still permits damage to reduce health.

The selection is a rule input, not a command to heal, kill or revive. SetHealthMode only stores the selected value; it does not reset health, flags or a running coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames. The player's explicit recovery methods perform their own state changes.

These effects come from Player_Health's inspected methods. The base Health damage and death methods do not themselves branch on healthMode, so another Health-derived component can implement different behavior. The name InsantDeath is spelled that way in the game's code.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HeptaRig
member.summary: Builds avatar body poses by solving the spine, arms and legs from body targets and the avatar’s proportions.

remarks.para: A target is the position and rotation a body part should reach. The rig uses head, hand and foot targets, segment lengths and permitted bend angles to calculate the intermediate chest, pelvis, elbow and knee poses. It can also extract a pose from one set of body proportions and apply it to another.

Its curves control particular posture corrections, while many underscored fields store calculated angles, directions or smoothing history. Those caches are not all direct controls for the physical body. CalibratePlayerBodyScale adjusts the rig to the supplied avatar; later solving uses the resulting geometry and reference curves.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGrippable
member.summary: Common operations and status checks for an object that hand receivers can target and hold.

remarks.para: An interface lets hand and grip code work with a host through the same operations: register or release hands, inspect physics and held/pulling states, and control interaction availability and collision shapes. A hand receiver handles a hand's hover and grab actions; a Grip defines a holding location and behavior.

InteractableHost is the built-in implementation described in the member remarks. It keeps host-wide hand/grip tracking; the individual grip and hand routines manage the actual grab connections. Freeze and Unfreeze use that implementation's auxiliary-joint behavior rather than guaranteeing that a Rigidbody becomes immovable.

A Rigidbody is the component that represents an object’s movement and rotation in the physics simulation. A joint connects two objects in that simulation. The auxiliary joints are additional player-body connections managed by InteractableHost.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.IGunSlideable
member.summary: Connects slide-handling controllers to listeners for hand control, normalized movement and pull/return endpoints.

remarks.para: Its properties hold callbacks: routines called to perform or report an action. Four notifications take no arguments; OnSlideUpdate takes a normalized travel value in the standard SlideVirtualController implementation. Adding a listener does not implement physical slide movement.

Gun subscribes during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. Those listeners update its animation and manual slide state. Use += and -= to share these Action properties with existing subscribers; assignment with = replaces the current list.

The checked controller stores travel before sending its movement update. It sets the pulled latch before the full-pull notification, but clears it after the returned-endpoint notification. Ending hand control clears that latch before the release notification. Other implementations define their own movement and notification scheduling; the interface contains no native method bodies.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties
member.summary: Supplies a hit surface's visual-response data, decal behavior and resistance values.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components. Pool registration asks the reusable-object system to prepare each configured effect or decal object template for later spawning.

PenetrationResistance is a unitless coefficient: on successful projectile passage it multiplies the starting speed, in meters per second, to calculate speed loss in meters per second. megaPascal is hardness in MPa, newtons per square millimeter; higher hardness opposes stabbing. With normal positive spring settings and a nonnegative tip area, increasing hardness lowers the unclamped initial-depth target. The final depth is limited to zero through maxDepth, the tip’s configured maximum penetration depth in meters, so it can stay unchanged at either limit. A decal is a surface mark, a collider is a shape Unity tests for collisions, and a prefab is an object template whose components can add behavior.

It registers a GameObject lookup during Awake, Unity's initialization callback, and removes that entry on destruction. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The first attack response lazily resolves surface data and registers the effect/decal pool assets.

Incoming attacks request an impact-effect object, optional particle tint/spread setup and, unless disabled, a collider-projected decal. This response is separate from health damage and any extra behavior contained in the effect prefab.

Its penetration getter supplies the projectile coefficient, while its megapascal getter supplies hardness scaled by megaPascalModifier for stabbing. SurfaceDataCard is preferred, with legacy surfaceData as fallback. Changing the reference alone does not invalidate the cached visual response.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactProperties.DecalType
member.summary: Chooses whether an impact surface requests a decal mark or skips the decal stage.

remarks.para: None is the disabled decal option; Collider enables spawning a surface decal and giving its projector the reported hit collider. A decal is a visual mark placed on a surface, such as an impact spot. A collider is the shape Unity uses to detect hits, and the DecalProjector component places the mark onto that shape. This choice is stored on ImpactProperties rather than on the hit collider itself.

The handler can wait over later frames for surface data and spawned effects. It checks the choice after its particle stage, so None does not suppress that earlier work. Enabled decals still depend on the required surface asset, hit collider and projector being available.

For an enabled decal, the spawn request uses the hit collider’s attached physics body as its parent when one exists; the collider remains the separate projection target. The enum has no duration, scale or damage units and does not itself erase existing marks.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ImpactSFX
member.summary: Turns qualifying physical collisions into sound, held-hand vibration and optional outgoing blunt attacks.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody gives an object mass and motion in physics; an InteractableHost identifies the hands holding it. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, caches the same-object Rigidbody/MarrowBody, mass and sound settings. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Start later finds the host and installs the component’s local startup sound delay.

The ordinary collision-enter path requires an active, enabled component and no hibernating cached Marrow entity. Hibernating is Marrow’s temporary sleeping/frozen physics state. ImpactSound first tests the relative approach speed along the first contact’s surface normal against minVelocity. The surface normal is the direction perpendicular to that contact surface; minVelocity is the signed approach-speed threshold in metres per second. It then calculates a speed-like strength, reports OnSignificantCollision, and checks the component’s or manager’s delay rule. That report happens before the gate values change and can occur even when sound is later suppressed.

After passing the gate, it updates the last strength and next time, chooses alternate/soft/hard clips, and requests a random sound at the first world contact point. Next it sends hit vibration to held hands, then can deliver an outgoing Blunt attack when bluntAttack and the additional target/strength conditions pass. Assigning sounds or enabling that flag alone does not guarantee an effect for every collision.

OnJointBreak requests break audio at this component’s world position and held-hand vibration. DestructionEvent requests destruction audio and updates local suppression; its caller handles actual destruction. ReceiveAttack is an empty base handler, so receiving an attack is not itself the collision-audio trigger. Public configuration and private setup caches have different refresh times, described on their entries.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRController
member.summary: Holds a VR controller's pose and cached button, stick, touch and finger input for the game's input handlers.

remarks.para: XRController stores readings; subclasses such as ControllerActionMap fill them from Unity input actions. Reading an input property does not ask the controller for a new measurement or clear its value. With ControllerActionMap, button Down and Up flags describe the current input-processing pass and are reset before the next pass.

Trigger and Grip normally use a unitless 0-to-1 scale, from released to fully squeezed. The two-dimensional control axes normally use -1 through 1 on each component around center (0, 0); they describe the control surface, not world-space motion. The cached finger values are estimates of curl from 0 (open) to 1 (curled), and can be calculated from buttons and squeeze rather than actual finger tracking.
IsConnected checks whether Unity's device handle is valid. Tracking status is separate: a valid handle does not guarantee that the controller's current position and rotation are being tracked.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRControllerType
member.summary: Chooses the hardware family used for controller-specific button mappings, finger estimates and grab-input calculations.

remarks.para: ControllerActionMap sets this selection when it identifies a device. OpenController, the player's input handler, reads it to decide how to process the available inputs. This is a choice of input-handling code, not a measurement of tracking quality or proof that every input feature is available.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRDevice
member.summary: Holds a VR device's cached position, orientation, motion and tracking state, and manages the handle used to identify it.

remarks.para: A pose combines position and orientation. Subclasses supply input readings; the base getters return stored values. OnFrameStart can find a device and advance timestamps, while Refresh saves pose history. These are separate operations, so a new timestamp does not by itself mean a new hardware pose was received.

On normal XR input paths, positions use meters in the VR runtime's tracking-origin frame, the reference point and axes chosen for tracking. Orientations use quaternions, Unity's four-number representation of rotation. Applying the tracking origin's scene transform is a separate step when world-space coordinates are needed.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHMD
member.summary: Represents a VR headset with cached pose and motion readings, a device-validity check and a user-presence query.

remarks.para: Unity input actions are configured inputs that deliver values such as headset position and rotation. HmdActionMap uses them to supply headset position and orientation. A pose is a position together with an orientation. IsConnected checks device validity, while IsUserPresent separately reads the headset's presence feature and assumes present if that feature cannot be read on a valid device.

The left/right gaze members provide optional storage. No live eye-gaze population or gameplay consumer was verified in the complete inspected XRHMD and HmdActionMap methods. These members do not establish that eye tracking is available.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Input.XRHand
member.summary: Holds tracked hand-bone poses and calculated finger-bend inputs for the player's hand-processing code.

remarks.para: A bone is one segment of the hand's skeleton; a pose is its position and orientation. HandActionMap supplies parent-relative bone arrays and calculates unitless curl amounts from 0 to 1. The player input handler can use four finger-curl values when its hand-tracking path is selected, then further adjust them.

XRHand's base constructor sets the full-update request flag but does not allocate the bone arrays. HandActionMap allocates 26-entry arrays indexed by HandBone and updates positions and rotations when it processes available hand data. Cached or allocated data alone does not prove a fresh tracking update succeeded.

The inspected HandActionMap does not check the full-update request flag and does not populate Radii. StartFullUpdate and StopFullUpdate therefore do not control its bone/curl updates in that checked path.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost
member.summary: Groups an object's grips, hand attachment records, distant-target permissions and physics-body access.

remarks.para: A grip describes a place and pose for a hand to hold. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, the host collects grips on itself and descendants, stopping at children with their own host. For a movable host, its virtual controller combines the holding hands to calculate a target pose, the position and rotation the held object should reach.

Host flags control how interaction code treats the object; they do not directly freeze its physics or disable its colliders. If ignoreBodyOnGrab is enabled, the host also manages extra collision-ignore joints between the held object and the player's torso and locomotion body. A joint connects two bodies in the physics simulation.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHostManager
member.summary: Groups interactable hosts so their collider settings, hand-targeting permission and hand release can be controlled together.

remarks.para: An interactable host groups an object's grips, the places and poses where hands can hold. This manager uses its hosts array for group commands and subscribes to those hosts' hand notifications during Start, Unity's startup callback before the first frame update.

It forwards the host and hand to listeners, then updates grabbedHosts. That list records attachments rather than unique objects: two hands on one object can produce two entries. The callbacks therefore see the manager list before the corresponding update.

Set up a nonnull hosts array with valid entries. Startup expects each host to expose a nonstatic Rigidbody, the component for simulated mass and motion, because it also totals their mass. The collision and interaction commands do not themselves release a held hand; ForceDetachAll requests release separately.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.ArtCull
member.summary: An obsolete component that adds no ArtCull-specific visibility or culling behavior.

remarks.para: Culling means leaving objects out of rendering when they do not need to be drawn. Despite its name, this class does not implement that decision or add a decorative-art registration step. Its only declared method is ordinary inherited construction.

The game marks ArtCull as obsolete and explicitly says it does nothing and is no longer required. When maintaining old content, this component is a leftover to remove rather than a setting for when an object should disappear from view.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Contact
member.summary: Creates and controls a physics anchor that can guide a Rigidbody along a SplineJoint’s path.

remarks.para: A contact connects an existing host Rigidbody to a separately created anchor GameObject, meaning the scene object that holds components. The anchor Rigidbody and ConfigurableJoint are components on that object. The Rigidbody is kinematic, so code controls its pose; the ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection that can restrict or drive sliding and turning. SplineJoint uses one or more such anchors and moves them along its line path to guide the host.

Construction stores an anchor offset and orientation relative to the host, rounds the offset to millimeter steps, and creates the anchor at that pose. The joint’s X direction is its travel axis; Y/Z settings govern sideways movement. Twist is turning around X, and swing is tilting sideways. The drive methods set desired speeds or the strength of spring, damping and force limits; they do not directly set the host’s velocity.

Transform reports the saved anchor attached to the host in scene coordinates, which can differ from the movable anchor Rigidbody’s actual pose. Disable/Enable temporarily remove and restore the contact object’s active connection, preserving world rotation; Destroy removes the generated object and its joint while retaining the host. SplineJoint owns the update sequence; Contact itself is a helper object rather than a component with its own frame update.
A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. A pose means a position together with a rotation.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.ContactCount
member.summary: Chooses the one-, two-, or four-contact constraint layout that a SplineJoint creates for following its path.

remarks.para: A Contact is a generated controlled physics body joined to the object’s main Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is a body simulated by Unity’s physics system; the joint constrains movement between the bodies while the spline solver updates the contact targets. A spline is a curved path. This enum selects a constraint layout rather than the number of collision events, collider touch points or gripping hands.

One uses the anchor itself and applies the configured angular motion to that contact. Two spreads contacts to the front and back using size.y. Four adds side-to-side spread using size.x, producing a rectangle. The anchor is the connection position relative to the body, and its layout directions come from the configured axis and secondary axis. Those size dimensions describe configured spacing in Unity distance units along those directions; one unit represents one meter when the scene uses that convention. Initial contact creation rotates and translates the offsets without applying body scale. Runtime local-to-world path queries include scale through TransformPoint, while Four's lateral target width uses size.x directly after world rotation. These are different steps, so changing body scale does not uniformly rescale the complete layout; changing contact count alone supplies no automatic spacing or strength increase.

SplineJoint.Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, builds the contact list. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. OnEnable and OnDisable enable or disable the existing contacts; they do not recreate them for a changed count. Select the layout before initialization, because a later count change can make the solver expect list entries that were never built.

While its main Rigidbody is not sleeping, SplineJoint.Update solves the selected layout and requests target updates. Sleeping means physics has temporarily stopped updating a resting body. One, Two and Four are exclusive choices, not flags to combine.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DampenContactDrive
member.summary: Groups the damping coefficient and force cap used for a contact's linear speed drive.

remarks.para: The checked SplineJoint consumer applies these two values to each Contact's ConfigurableJoint.xDrive. A joint connects bodies through a physics constraint; here its local X drive tries to match the configured linear X target speed.

positionDamper measures the force requested for a speed difference, in N·s/m (newton-seconds per meter), and maximumForce caps the drive in newtons. That speed difference is the chosen speed minus the current relative speed, meaning how fast the connected bodies move past each other along the connection’s X direction, in meters per second. This struct has no positionSpring setting, so it describes the damper/cap pair rather than a complete position-spring configuration.

It is a value type containing numbers. Constructing it, changing a copy or boxing a copy does not create or reconfigure a joint by itself. SplineJoint copies its stored pair into contacts when setting them up and when refreshing their configuration. Its live SetLinearXDrivePositionDamper and SetLinearXDriveMaxForce methods apply their supplied arguments to current contacts without saving them in this pair; a later refresh can restore the stored values.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.DisabledJointInfo
member.summary: Keeps the motion modes, drive strengths and connected body needed to restore a temporarily freed physics joint.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation. Save its state with CopyFrom, temporarily free it with Clear, then restore with CopyTo. Clear makes all six movement/rotation modes Free, sets all six drives to zero and clears connectedBody; it does not destroy or disable the joint component.

MarrowJoint uses this sequence when its bodies are disabled and enabled. It captures before clearing on disable; when the required bodies are active again, it restores an existing joint from the saved settings or builds a joint if none exists.

This is a partial snapshot. It does not capture anchors, target position/rotation, numerical limits or rotationDriveMode. Capturing again overwrites the saved values, and restoration only runs after _hasBeenCopied has been set by a capture.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.EntityManager
member.summary: Registers objects and keeps tag lookup lists for gameplay code that needs to find them.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity represents a gameplay object with its tag data and entity state. This manager is a Marrow plugin with a registered-entity set and a dictionary of tag barcode IDs to entity lists. Instance retrieves and caches the plugin. The registry is populated by registration calls; it does not automatically discover every scene object.

MarrowEntity normally registers during Awake, Unity's initialization callback, and unregisters during OnDestroy, Unity's destruction callback. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Registering makes the object findable by its current tag references. Before loading a level, the manager clears membership first and tag lookups second; clearing this registry does not itself remove the objects from the game.

For example, gameplay code can use a crate BoneTag to find a crate entity after registration. TryGetFirstEntityWithTag returns the first entry not marked for despawn, while TryGetEntitiesWithTag returns the stored list without that filter. First is insertion order, not a distance ranking. Tag keys are exact barcode IDs; they are not display-name searches.

Changing an entity's tags does not automatically refresh the index. Unregister while the old tags are present, change the tags, then register again. Calling RegisterEntity twice without unregistering does not refresh an existing member. Direct edits to the backing collections or tag helpers can separate membership from lookup entries, so the tag index is not proof that the object's current tags still match.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.Handedness
member.summary: Chooses a left side, right side, both sides or neither for Marrow hand operations.

remarks.para: The defined values are UNDEFINED = 0, LEFT = 1, RIGHT = 2 and BOTH = 3. A rig is the group of objects representing the player’s body and controls; a skeleton hand is the hand-bone representation, separate from its controller and its physical collision hand. A Hand stores its side with this enum, and rig APIs use it to choose which controller, skeleton hand or physical-hand operation to access.

Support for BOTH depends on the method. PhysicsRig.ResetHands accepts it and processes both sides, right before left, when no reset is already running. ResetHands starts a new selection only when no hand reset is already running. A call during an existing reset is ignored: it does not replace that reset’s selection or queue another reset. GetController and GetSkeletonHand require one side and return null for BOTH or UNDEFINED.
This is a hand selection, not a count of attached hands or a promise of simultaneous action. For example, obtaining both controller references requires separate LEFT and RIGHT lookups.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.HibernationBodyInfo
member.summary: Preserves selected Rigidbody settings so a temporarily hibernating body can resume its earlier state.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody represents an object's motion in the physics simulation. MarrowBody captures this snapshot before freezing all its movement/rotation axes and forcing it to sleep; unhibernating restores the settings through CopyTo.

CopyFrom always saves inertia, constraints, sleep threshold and sleeping state, but saves velocities only for an awake body. CopyTo restores the common settings, then either sleeps the body or restores its saved velocities and wakes it.

This snapshot does not contain position, rotation, mass or inertia-axis orientation. After CopyTo, the full MarrowBody unhibernate path also requests mass and inertia recalculation on the root body reached through Host links. It is not a complete restoration of every physics property.
Each Host link points to another MarrowBody; the root is the last body in that chain, with no further Host.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityCullable
member.summary: Defines the two routines a component uses to pause and resume its work with a ’s culling state.

remarks.para: Culling suspends an entity’s normal processing while it is inactive. MarrowEntity’s culling handler requests or releases physics hibernation, changes its configured MarrowBehaviour components’ enabled state, and then calls OnEntityCull or OnEntityUncull on registered implementations. Physics hibernation pauses the simulated bodies while a pause reason remains. MarrowBehaviour components are the entity’s configured game-script components. The pause notification runs while a new culling request is processed, before the resolved state is stored and before the later GameObject activation stage. A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components. The manager sets the completed-cull flag before the pause notification and clears it before the resume notification; this bookkeeping is separate from recording and applying the resolved state. The resume notification waits for completion after all hide, cull and despawn requests have cleared and queued changes have finished; clearing culling alone need not resume the work.

Register the receiver with MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler and remove it with UnregisterEventHandler when it should stop receiving these calls. Registration avoids duplicate entries but does not immediately report the current state. The interface itself has no routine bodies; each implementing component decides which of its own systems to pause and restore.

An Animator is the Unity component that runs animations. A practical pair pauses an animator while keeping its animation state, then re-enables it on restoration, as the Gun implementation does. These culling notifications are separate from the interface used to report entity hiding and from pool despawning. They can also run when the entity prevents GameObject disabling on cull, because notification processing is separate from the later GameObject activation decision.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityDespawnable
member.summary: Gives components paired notifications for preparing a 's spawn and cleaning up its despawn.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups an object's game and physics parts. Implement both methods, then register that implementation with the entity's matching RegisterEventHandler overload; implementing the interface alone does not add it to the listener list. The entity ignores a duplicate registration of the same handler. Use UnregisterEventHandler when that relationship ends.

The two callbacks are routines called to report or carry out work for a lifecycle transition. A tracker links a collision shape, the shape Unity uses to detect contact, to the entity’s physics parts. A GameObject is Unity’s object that holds components. OnEntityDespawn runs before its trackers send deactivation notifications and before its activation state is recalculated; OnEntitySpawn runs after its activation state is recalculated. Physical tracker disabling can occur earlier during OnPoolDeInitialize, before the queued despawn transition is applied. These calls are part of applying the requested despawn state, so a request can be queued before your handler runs. For example, pair a spawn-time effect reset with despawn-time cleanup.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityHideable
member.summary: Defines the paired routines a component uses to react to a MarrowEntity’s managed hiding and restoration.

remarks.para: MarrowEntity’s managed hide state normally deactivates its GameObject, the Unity object containing the entity and its components. OnEntityHide lets your component pause or clean up its own work for that transition; OnEntityUnhide lets it restore that work. Each implementation decides what it needs to change.

Register an implementation with MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler and remove it with UnregisterEventHandler when it should stop receiving these calls. Registration avoids duplicate entries and does not immediately report the current state. Implementing the interface by itself does not put an object into this registered list.

The inactivity manager resolves requests and then applies hide-state changes. During hide application, MarrowEntity notifies receivers before its own active-state update; during unhide application, it updates activity before notifying them. Hide(..., doApplyImmediately=true) can change GameObject activity earlier, before those notifications. Other inactivity reasons can keep the object disabled after unhide.

These routines report managed hide transitions. They are separate from the culling interface that reports suspended entity processing and from despawn notifications. Calling one of these routines yourself does not change the entity’s managed hide flag.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.IMarrowEntityPoseable
member.summary: Receives a notification after a MarrowEntity applies body positions and orientations from a stored pose.

remarks.para: A pose records how the entity's body parts are arranged. This interface supplies OnWritePose, a callback: a routine called to perform or report an action. The entity first applies the supplied pose entries to its body transforms, which hold their positions and orientations, then notifies the handlers registered for this interface. The notification lets a handler react to that newly placed arrangement.

Implementing the interface alone does not add the handler to this entity's pose-handler list. Use the IMarrowEntityPoseable overload of MarrowEntity.RegisterEventHandler to add it and the matching UnregisterEventHandler to remove it. Repeated registration of the same handler is ignored. The entity calls handlers in list order during WritePose, after the body-transform loop, rather than on a later frame.

For example, a component that keeps its own copy of a body's position could refresh that copy in OnWritePose, after the saved body placement has been written. The callback supplies no pose argument, and it does not mean that the next physics step has finished. A shorter input pose changes only its matching initial body entries; notification does not promise that every body was changed. The inspected ReadPose capture path does not issue this notification.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowCollisionManager
member.summary: Manages overlapping requests to ignore collisions between pairs of collider shapes.

remarks.para: A Collider describes a shape used for physics contact. ManagedIgnore(A, B, true) asks the physics system to stop collisions between shapes A and B and records one request. The manager counts repeated requests so that one caller releasing its request does not restore collisions while another caller still needs the pair ignored.

For example, after two ignore requests, the first ManagedIgnore(A, B, false) leaves one request and keeps the ignore. The second release restores collisions and removes the pair’s count and both partner lookups. These counts and lookup collections are static, so they are shared by manager instances. IsIgnored reports the manager’s pair registration, not every ignore set directly through Unity.

MarrowBody uses this manager when ignoring its collider pairs. Its CleanupIgnoredCollisions calls ClearManagedIgnoresFor for each body collider; that cleanup restores all recorded pairs for a collider regardless of their request counts and removes their shared records. The partner map and temporary list let it clean both directions without losing the partner references.

After level unload, the plugin callback clears the count dictionary, partner map and working list in that order and returns a completed task. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. That unload callback clears bookkeeping; explicit per-collider physical restoration happens in ClearManagedIgnoresFor. Balance ordinary true/false requests and use the manager methods so the records and physics calls follow the same path.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity
member.summary: Groups an object’s physics parts so they can be moved, suspended and returned to a pool as one entity.

remarks.para: Bodies contains the managed physical parts, and Joints contains their configured physics connections. A Rigidbody simulates a body’s motion; a joint connects bodies with movement and turning rules. The entity can teleport its parts together, change their collision and tracking participation, and restore saved arrangements and settings during pool reuse.

Its tag labels allow query systems to classify the object. Registered cull, hide, despawn and pose receivers perform their own component-specific work when the corresponding transitions are processed. RegisterEventHandler adds those receivers; merely implementing an interface does not insert it into the entity’s registered list.

Managed inactivity keeps separate requested, resolved and applied states. IsHidden, IsCulled, IsDespawned and IsInactive read the requests, so they can change before notifications and component updates finish. Physics hibernation is separately tracked by its own reason flags.

Use Ghost, EnableColliders, EnableTriggers, EnableTrackers and Hibernate when you need their effects across the bodies. The similarly named status properties and backing fields store bookkeeping; changing a flag alone does not carry out those transitions. ScaleRatio is a cached volume multiplier for mass recalculation, not a method that resizes the object.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity.HibernationSources
member.summary: Identifies independent reasons that keep a Marrow entity’s physics hibernating.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component that gives an object simulated movement and rotation. An entity groups Marrow physics bodies. Hibernation saves and pauses their physics state; bodies with a Rigidbody have movement and rotation frozen and are put to sleep. The named reason bits are Default = 1, Culling = 2 and Loading = 4. They can be combined with |, such as Culling | Loading. Their numbers identify flags and have no physical unit.

These are independent reason flags, not request counts. Hibernate(true, source) adds the selected reason bits; Hibernate(false, source) removes only those bits. The entity’s flags change first. Its body pause/restore work runs only when the overall state changes between no active reason and at least one active reason.

With Culling | Loading set, removing Loading leaves Culling, so the bodies remain paused. Removing Culling afterwards leaves no active reason and restores their saved state. IsHibernating reads whether the entity has an active reason. Default is also an active reason; a zero mask is the no-reason state even though this enum has no named zero member.

A reason bit is not a counter: adding Culling twice still sets the same bit, and one removal clears it. Different systems should use their matching reason when releasing hibernation so they leave the others’ reasons in place. The ordinary culling path changes the reason before enabling/disabling configured behaviours, the entity’s script components, and reporting cull/uncull handlers; loading completion removes the Loading reason.

Restoration returns saved body settings and the prior sleeping/awake state, so it need not make an already sleeping body move. These reasons describe physics hibernation; their surrounding culling and loading callers perform the additional lifecycle work described on each value.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntityPose
member.summary: Saves an entity's body arrangement so it can be applied at the entity's current position and orientation.

remarks.para: This is pose data, not a group of live Transform components. bodyPoses holds each body's relative position in meters and its rotation quaternion, an orientation value. MarrowEntity.ReadPose captures bodies relative to the entity's position and rotation; WritePose reconstructs their scene positions and rotations using the entity's current position and rotation.

A saved pose can therefore keep the same arrangement when the entity is moved or turned. Its body order must match the target entity's Bodies array. Creating the object or changing its data does not apply the pose by itself, and this data contains no per-body scale or movement velocity.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowJoint
member.summary: Manages a configurable physics connection, its saved reference/settings and its body-enable or break lifecycle.

remarks.para: Update is a stage of the game's repeated frame processing. breakForce is the force break threshold in newtons. Setting it to infinity prevents force alone from exceeding that threshold; the turning-force break threshold, breakTorque in newton-meters, is not changed by this cleanup policy.

A joint is a physics connection that can restrict relative movement or use motor-like drives to push bodies toward position/rotation and velocity targets. BodyA hosts the Unity ConfigurableJoint; BodyB is the other body, or absent for a connection to the fixed scene. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, captures an assigned joint. CreateJoint sets up a runtime connection and can wait for the bodies to be enabled before construction.

The full default configuration, body-disable snapshot, reference pose and six drive baselines are separate stores. Disabling saves/neutralizes the connection and enabling restores or rebuilds it. Drive-scaling methods use unitless factors on the saved baselines; changing a baseline does not immediately write the live drive.

Missing scene joints are rebuilt after a deferred Update check with infinite breakForce.
