A proportion such as 0.25 is one quarter of its reference measurement, not 25 distance units. A Vector3 is three X/Y/Z values. C, T, L, and S identify the cervical (neck), thoracic (chest), lumbar (lower-back), and sacral (pelvis) spine regions; the number identifies a vertebra within that region. A scapula is a shoulder blade, an acromion is its outer shoulder tip, and the glenohumeral joint is the shoulder joint. The SC, AC, and GH labels mark successive neck-to-scapula, scapula-to-acromion, and acromion-to-joint reference vectors.

PrecomputeAvatar receives a standing eye height in meters and scales reference distances by eyeHeight / _eyeHeightDefault. For example, if the reference eye height is 1.60 m and the reference total height is 1.75 m, an input eye height of 1.70 m gives a scale of 1.0625 and a computed total height of about 1.86 m. The heightPercent setting is a unitless total-height-to-eye-height ratio; the refresh formula is height = heightPercent × eyeHeight.

RefreshBodyMeasurements recalculates derived heights and segment lengths from eyeHeight and their proportions, rebuilds torso curves, recomputes mass and base stats, then invokes OnRefreshBodyMeasurements if subscribed. A callback is a registered method the avatar calls to report that refresh. The overload that accepts a calibration Avatar copies only selected chest, waist, hip, and sternum shape values into that argument when it is non-null; it then always invokes the inherited refresh dispatch. A null argument skips only the selected-value copy. This is a one-way selected-value copy, not a full avatar copy. The SetPlayerInseam and SetPlayerWingspan overrides have empty native bodies in this build, so their parameters do not update these measurements.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Plug
member.summary: A tracker that finds a nearby compatible socket, aligns the plug, and connects their physics bodies.

remarks.para: A Unity component is data or behavior attached to a scene object (called a GameObject in Unity). This plug implements ITaggable, so its Tags list supplies labels for the tag rules in a socket's MarrowQuery, the socket's compatibility rules. The query can also check a pooled object's crate when it has a Poolee component; a pool is a system that stores objects so they can be reused, and a Poolee marks an object managed by that system. And requires both the tag and crate results, while Or accepts either. When the plug enters a socket's tracked area, the socket's entry handler adds it only when tag rules are configured, the query accepts it, the socket is unattached, and the socket tracks no other plug. The plug's hover-enter handler can also add a candidate directly, so being a candidate does not prove the tag query passed or that attachment occurred.

FixedUpdate is Unity's callback on physics updates. While the plug is unattached and has candidates, it checks the host's attached-grip state only for the candidate equal to _lastDetachedSocket, the remembered socket it last detached from. It skips that candidate if the host reports a hand attached to one of its grips; other candidates go directly to the distance-cutoff comparison. It then chooses the nearest eligible socket whose world position is within the default 0.08 world-coordinate units of the plug's position. The plug's and socket's Transform.position values are their locations in Unity's shared world-coordinate frame; scene scale determines how these coordinate units map to real distances, so 0.08 does not guarantee 0.08 meters. Attach first sets the plug's IsAttached flag and stores _attachedSocket. The socket then marks itself attached, notifies its registered ISocketable objects (objects registered to receive socket notifications) and its configured event (a notification other code can subscribe to), and calls Bind automatically if autobind is configured. Plug next calls its registered IPlugable callbacks. A callback is a routine one component calls to report a change so another can respond; these listeners see the plug already marked attached, and may see IsBound true if the socket's automatic bind ran. Only after these notifications does Plug align the body transforms, force-detach attached hands, create a MarrowJoint connecting the plug and socket physics bodies, disable the host's distant-hover interaction (far-hover), and stop its own search. A joint is a physics connection between bodies.

When a hand-attached notification arrives from the host, the plug enables itself and calls Detach. Detach proceeds only when the plug is attached and unbound: it clears IsAttached, asks Unity to destroy the physics joint, calls registered plug listeners before notifying the socket, remembers the last socket, and then clears _attachedSocket. If the socket is bound, Detach returns without changing the attachment. A socket can be configured to call Bind automatically during its attachment notifications, so IsAttached and IsBound describe separate parts of the lifecycle.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Redacted.Socket
member.summary: A receiving slot that registers nearby objects as candidates; later, a Plug checks its candidate sockets, chooses a valid one, and begins attaching. The socket can bind an attached plug separately.

remarks.para: A Zone reports when tracked objects enter or leave its trigger area. While enabled, this socket registers for those reports. When a Plug enters, this socket considers it only if its MarrowQuery has at least one tag rule and accepts the plug, this socket is unattached, and it is not already tracking another plug candidate. MarrowQuery is a filter that checks the plug's tags and the ID for its associated content crate. And requires both the tag check and crate check to pass; Or accepts either check. With no crate IDs configured, the crate check defaults to passing, so Or can accept a plug even when its tags do not match.

Entering the trigger only makes a plug a candidate. On a later physics update, the plug checks its candidate sockets and starts attaching to a valid one. The attach callback runs at the start of that operation: it reports state changes before the plug has finished lining up with the socket and creating a physics joint. A physics joint is a connector that holds two bodies together in the simulation.

Binding is an extra state after attachment: it disables the plug's normal interaction. To release a bound plug, call socket.Unbind(); socket.Detach(); in that order. This socket can also notify registered ISocketable listeners and its four plug callbacks. An ISocketable listener is registered code implementing the interface to receive plug attach and detach notices.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig
member.summary: Extends to combine controller body poses with calculated movement, jump and crouch targets, and corrections from the physics rig.

remarks.para: A rig groups a body's transforms and pose data. The early pose update combines controller input with optional additive pose changes, updates horizontal movement, and adjusts body positions for jumping and crouching. The post-physics update reconciles rig roots with the simulated body, including optional pelvis-facing alignment.

Its movement values describe targets and calculations, so they are not always reports of the physics body's actual motion. Jump requests notify listeners before changing jump state, and optional extra boosts still require acceptance by the physics rig. Several settings are read each update, while SetAvatar copies the avatar's movement ratings into this rig and configures its navigation agent during setup.

For example, a custom movement script can set a baseline speed and call Jump, but collisions, support, smoothing, and the extra-jump cooldown still affect the resulting motion. Configure the associated controller, avatar, physics rig, and navigation references before running the remapping updates.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RemapRig.TraversalState
member.summary: Labels stored in RemapRig.travState; the inspected movement calculation gives Jog a speed boost and treats the other values alike.

remarks.para: These are mutually exclusive choices, not flags that can be combined. Their integer values are identifiers, with no meters-per-second units. The names do not automatically report the player's current speed, grounding, jumping or climbing state.

In the complete inspected ApplyMovement body, Jog doubles maxVelocity, the base horizontal speed setting in meters per second, before body-pose and movement-direction adjustments and acceleration smoothing. All other defined values follow its unboosted calculation. Choosing Run therefore does not select a greater sprint multiplier there.

The inspected OnEarlyUpdate, Jump, JumpCharge, Jumping and JumpEnd bodies manage actual jumping through controller input and separate jump flags/stages. They do not start a jump by selecting the Jump enum value. These findings cover those methods; other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Rig
member.summary: Provides shared bone references, saved pose data, and update hooks for rigs coordinated by .

remarks.para: A rig is a set of transforms representing a body. A transform stores position, rotation, and scale. The controller rig starts from player input, remapping rigs adapt the body arrangement, and the physics rig handles the body's physical side; the manager calls their hooks in a coordinated order.

This base class can find or create its main bone references, sample poses, and smooth target values. Its initialization, frame, physics, avatar-change, body-state, and teleport hooks are empty. A derived rig overrides those hooks to supply the behavior for its particular job.
Saved pose and weight objects are data. Replacing them does not itself move the body; movement depends on the specific rig code that reads and applies them.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager
member.summary: Coordinates the player’s input targets, avatar pose stages, and simulated body, including avatar changes, body modes, teleports, and movement leashes. Its modules include , , and .

remarks.para: A rig is a set of body bones and the code that positions them. The controller stage supplies requested poses, the intermediate stages adapt them to the avatar, and the physics stage moves the body through the level. The manager calls these stages in order and tells them when the avatar or body mode changes.

Many requests take effect in its early per-frame pass. That pass invokes the pre-update hook, applies pending avatar, teleport, and body-mode work in order, then runs pose stages. A physics step is a regular simulation interval; the manager coordinates its fixed-step and after-fixed work with ordinary frame updates. Late updates finish the poses before the post-late hook.

Stored configuration and pending requests do not always describe the currently applied body. For example, SwapAvatar queues an existing instance, AvatarCrate assignment only stores a crate reference, and the leash status flag does not check a live physics joint. Read the applied avatar and bodyState when checking which requests have taken effect.

An update hook is a registered callback, a function the manager runs at the named point in its update work. A physics joint is a connection that limits simulated movement; a saved status flag does not test whether that connection currently exists.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.RigManager.BodyState
member.summary: Selects normal walking, seat use, active ragdoll, or reduced-control ragdoll for the player’s body.

remarks.para: The values are OnFoot = 0, Seated = 1, ActiveRagdoll = 2, and Ragdoll = 3. They are mode choices, not amounts or measurements. ActiveRagdoll keeps active body control with physical legs; Ragdoll weakens that control so the body can fall more freely.

Setting RigManager.bodyState queues a change when the requested value differs from the current state. During the next EarlyUpdate, the early part of a game frame, the manager sends the new and previous modes to the controller rig, each pose-remapping rig, and the physics rig, in that order. A pose-remapping rig translates tracked head and hand movement into a body pose. The current state is changed only after those calls finish.

For example, after requesting Ragdoll from OnFoot, reading bodyState immediately can still return OnFoot. The physical setup also depends on the previous mode: entering Ragdoll from OnFoot enables physical legs before weakening control, while entering it from ActiveRagdoll only weakens control. Seat registration and release must handle their own physical connection.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Saveable
member.summary: A Unity component that keeps an object's string save data and its saved identity and bake metadata together.

remarks.para: Its five stored strings are copied together by CopyFrom. Unbake(true) clears the path, hash-algorithm name, identifier, and last-baked record while retaining Data; Unbake(false) leaves them unchanged.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.ChunkBatch
member.summary: Groups SceneChunk components (scripts attached to level objects) into the requested set for the shared scene loader to keep loaded.

remarks.para: A Unity scene is a saved group of level objects. A SceneChunk component may reference zero, one, or several scenes; its scene list can be empty. The shared SceneLoader manages loaded chunks and processes each requested set. It compares the requested chunks with chunks it already has loaded: requested chunks already loaded are kept, newly requested chunks are prepared to load, and previously loaded chunks omitted from the request are prepared to unload. For example, if chunks A and B are loaded and a batch requests B and C, B is kept, C is prepared to load, and A is prepared to unload. Editing a batch records the request; the loader processes it later.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.PlayerMarker
member.summary: Marks a player spawn location in a scene and coordinates spawn lifecycle events with registered listeners.

remarks.para: PlayerMarker is a MonoBehaviour, a script component attached to a Unity GameObject. A GameObject is an object in a scene that holds components. PlayerMarker stores the latest player GameObject it is told about and notifies registered listeners when spawn or despawn is reported. A listener is an object whose class supplies OnSpawn(GameObject) and OnDespawn(GameObject); a callback is a method PlayerMarker calls to report an event.

Awake is Unity's initialization callback, the routine Unity calls when it initializes this component. PlayerMarker checks the current SceneStreamer session. SceneStreamer is Marrow's static scene-streaming service; its StreamSession stores the current loading status and a list of PlayerMarker components. When that session's Status is StreamStatus.LOADING, Awake adds this marker to the session's list only if the list does not already contain it. If Status is another value, Awake returns without adding the marker. This session list is separate from _spawnListeners, which contains event listeners.

When OnPlayerSpawned receives a GameObject, it sets _hasSpawned to true and stores that reference before walking _spawnListeners in order and calling each listener's OnSpawn callback with the same object. OnPlayerDespawn walks the current listener list and calls OnDespawn with its argument, but the method leaves the stored reference and flag unchanged. Register and unregister affect later notifications; registering does not replay an earlier spawn, and unregister removes only one matching entry, so duplicate entries can still receive later notifications.

TryGetPlayerGameObject outputs the stored reference and returns _hasSpawned. For example, after a spawn notification it returns true and the reported GameObject; after a despawn notification it can still return true with that same reference because this class does not reset either field on despawn.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.SceneStreamingManager
member.summary: Plugin that maps scene-zone GameObjects to the they belong to.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components. A plugin here is a registered service that can receive level-load callbacks; this class is not a Unity GameObject component. Its Instance property looks up the plugin through MarrowPlugins. Each SceneChunk groups one or more scene layers for streaming. When a SceneChunk initializes, it registers the GameObject for each configured ZoneCuller with itself as the mapped SceneChunk. When that SceneChunk is destroyed, it unregisters the current live culler GameObjects.

RegisterSceneZone adds a new mapping, UnregisterSceneZone removes one, and TryGetScenesFromCollider passes the supplied GameObject directly as the dictionary key. It returns the lookup's Boolean result; the out SceneChunk receives the mapped value on a match and null on a miss. Despite the method name, it does not accept a Collider or search a parent object. Before a level load, the plugin replaces the map with an empty dictionary. These methods maintain the lookup; they do not themselves load or unload the scene layers.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamSession
member.summary: Coordinates loading a level, its persistent scene content, and player-marker spawn work for one streaming session.

remarks.para: A session retains separate primary-level and load-level crate references, with a resolved LevelCrate, a level-content asset record, for each when available. Load uses the load-level reference for the loading scene; persistent scenes come from the primary-level reference. The session owns a persistent-scene queue, registered player-marker list, four callback batches for level load/unload and before/after persistent-scene loading, and an integer load-dependency counter.

A callback is a routine the session calls at a loading phase. For persistent-scene phases, Load invokes any stored callbacks before setting the phase flag, then clears the batch; callbacks added after the flag is set run immediately. Level-load callbacks run after Status becomes DONE.

Load returns a UniTask, a completion object callers can await so their routine continues when the operation finishes. Loading can pause across frames, and post-notification cleanup continues after DONE before this completion object finishes. Refresh creates a new session from the two stored references rather than resetting this object.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SceneStreaming.StreamStatus
member.summary: Reports the stage reached by a StreamSession's level-load routine.

remarks.para: StreamSession holds the state and callbacks used while a level's scenes are loaded. A level-load callback is a routine registered for the loader to call at a particular point. The status values are codes, not a percentage or elapsed-time measure: NONE is the new-session default, LOADING is written when the load routine starts its scene-load path, and DONE is written after the main scene-load waits.

After writing DONE, the routine invokes level-load callbacks that were registered earlier. A callback registered after DONE is invoked immediately. The load routine continues afterward, so DONE marks a stage in the process; it does not guarantee that Load has returned or that all callback work is complete.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer
member.summary: Defines where an avatar's inventory slot sits and moves its anchor into or out of the item-slot panel.

remarks.para: The child Transform is the slot anchor. PhysicsRig positions it on the selected body region; torso slots use a vertical setting, an angle, and footprint dimensions. When the item-slot panel opens, MoveToTemporaryParent reparents the anchor and hides the slot art. Return restores the saved local position and rotation, shows the art, and restores receiver state.
The rootRb reference also lets PullCordDevice connect its ball joint to the avatar's root Rigidbody.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SlotContainer.BodyRegion
member.summary: Selects which body area an inventory attachment uses when the character rig places it.

remarks.para: A SlotContainer is the scene component for one body-slot or special-item attachment. Inventory stores these containers in its bodySlots and specialItems arrays. The bodyRegion value records which body area to use. PhysicsRig is the character rig component that positions them: it chooses a matching rig transform (the torso, shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee) as the container's parent, then sets a local position using the Avatar's position for that body area. Here, Avatar is the character component that supplies body measurements and placement points. Torso placement uses Avatar torso measurements. Lower arm means forearm; lower leg means calf. The enum stores the placement choice; it does not move the container by itself.

PhysicsRig.SetBodySlot processes the configured body-slot and special-item containers. SlotContainer.FlipSpecialItem selects value 2 (left forearm) when its Boolean is true and value 4 (right forearm) when false. This enum does not describe item categories or promise that a particular scene has every rig parent configured.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SphereGrip
member.summary: A sphere-shaped grab target with per-hand locked or free rotational correction and limited handle swing.

remarks.para: The inherited radius defines the sphere used to score a nearby hand. Desired hand targets use the center for a small sphere and excess-radius offsets for a large one. The inherited rotationLimit bounds the target and joint’s permitted swing; it is measured in degrees. The hand pose also has a separate swing allowance returned by GetSwingLimit.

Free mode is recorded per hand in _isJointFree. UpdateJointConfiguration later sets that hand joint’s rotational restoring drive to zero while free, or a strong restoring drive while locked. A joint is a physics connection between the hand and the held object; a drive applies spring-like correction toward its target. Free mode preserves the position connection and still permits the configured angular limits to constrain rotation.

A host with a Rigidbody and radius at most 0.05 m, or 5 cm, can switch to free correction when its secondary interaction button is released and lock again when pressed. State is recorded first, anchors or desired targets are updated next, and the live joint drive is updated through the held-hand configuration routine.

Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to prepare the component. It performs base grip setup and pose caching, but the checked runtime class does not consume the autoConfigure or friction authoring fields. Force-pull and target helpers return poses; their coordinate frames matter, including GetNeutralTargetInWorld’s host-relative position case.
The host is the grippable object that owns this grip. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for an object’s mass and physical motion.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager
member.summary: Controls Unity's scaled game speed, stepped slow motion, pause, and restoration of the previous time scale.

remarks.para: Unity timeScale is a unitless multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 0.5 advances scaled game time at half speed, and 0 stops scaled time. TimeManager represents slow motion with an intensity whose reciprocal becomes timeScale; it eases transitions using unscaled frame time, the duration of a frame unaffected by timeScale. It sets fixedDeltaTime to timeScale divided by the recommended physics frequency, meaning physics steps per second, so fixedDeltaTime is the number of seconds per physics step.

Step helpers use indexes 0 through 3 by default, corresponding to timeScale values 1, 0.5, 0.25, and 0.125. PAUSE saves the current scale before setting it to 0, and UNPAUSE restores that saved value.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.TimeManager.SlowTime
member.summary: Defines a callback signature for TimeManager's slow-time notifications: one method that receives the selected step as a float.

remarks.para: A callback is a method the game calls to send a notification. Unity's Time.timeScale setting controls how quickly scaled game time runs. This delegate carries a unitless step number used by TimeManager, not a duration or that speed setting. Its Invoke method calls the handler attached to this delegate.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.AddNode
member.summary: Produces one output containing the sum of every input number it can read.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic node is a logic component connected to other components through signal ports. On each calculation, this node starts at zero, reads all entries in its configured input array, and adds the available values. A connection that cannot provide a value is skipped. An empty input array produces zero.

For example, inputs 0.4, 0.7, and -0.2 produce 0.9. The result is not limited to the usual 0-to-1 signal range: 0.8 plus 0.8 produces 1.6. The node adds raw numbers without converting units; if all inputs are lengths in meters, the sum is also in meters.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.BaseNode
member.summary: Common base for logic components that accept incoming signals and publish numeric outputs.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic node is a logic component connected to others through signal ports. This base stores input connections, reports their slot count, and forwards Unity initialization, enable, disable, and destruction routines to the logic manager.

Concrete node types supply port descriptions and implement Initialize to prepare their signal state and Calculate to produce their output. For example, AddNode adds its readable input values into one Sum output. Subgraph identifies the connected group holding the cached output state.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.ButtonNode
member.summary: Turns the travel of a physical button into a continuous VoidLogic Power signal and press or release sound requests.

remarks.para: VoidLogic joins components with signal sockets. This node has one Power input and one Power output. It measures the full three-dimensional world distance d, in metres, from the shaft's joint object to _endTransform. During Awake, Unity's initialization callback, it caches the initial full three-dimensional world distance L in metres. The raw travel factor is p = 1 - d² / L², with no unit, and output = incoming Power × p. For example, moving halfway toward the endpoint on a straight path gives p = 0.75; input Power 2 then gives output 1.5. No readable input gives output 0. The value is not clamped, and the starting distance must be nonzero.

A Rigidbody is the component that lets physics move the shaft. After the first attempted measurement with a valid body, the sensor skips further measurements while that body sleeps, meaning physics has paused it because it is resting. Setup configures the physics joint, which connects and limits the shaft, using the starting distance and midpoint, and disables collision pairs listed in _ignoreColliders. Later movement is still governed by the joint's existing axis, motion and drive settings.

The remembered _isPressed flag is separate from the continuous output. During Actuate, when the logic system asks this node to apply its result, it requests a press sound above _highThreshold or a release sound below _lowThreshold, using the raw factor p and strict comparisons. These checks require an awake body and a Power output change of at least 0.0001 since the previous calculation. The flag changes after the sound request returns, without waiting for playback; empty clip arrays allow silent flag transitions. Enabling the component resets the flag to false.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.DamageVolume
member.summary: Tracks bodies entering a trigger and sends periodic attacks scaled by a VoidLogic Power input, speed and optional distance falloff.

remarks.para: A trigger is a collision shape that detects entry and exit without blocking movement. Entering colliders need an attached Rigidbody, the component that gives an object physics movement. Colliders tagged NoDamage are ignored. Recognized targets include living character muscle bodies, player damage receivers and destructible objects. Multiple colliders on one body share tracking until its final collider leaves.

Update is the routine Unity calls once per game frame. It waits until the configured _tickFrequency interval, in real-time seconds, has elapsed and at least one body is tracked. A due pass processes the first player-list entry with multiplier 1, every destructible-list entry with multiplier 1, then remaining tracked non-player bodies with multiplier 0.08. A destructible still present in that final pass can get an additional smaller attempt. The timestamp is saved at the end; slow frames do not replay missed intervals.

Power is the sole signal socket, input 0. Each attempt maps its number from 0..1 into _mapLow.._mapHigh, the configured multipliers at inputs 0 and 1; values outside 0..1 use the nearest endpoint and unreadable input supplies 0. The mapped factor multiplies _damage, the base amount in game damage points. It also multiplies a positive _effectiveDistance, the source cutoff in metres. That cutoff compares the target GameObject position with _damageSourceTransform's current world position; zero effective distance skips only this cutoff.

Speed scaling either uses the target body's own world speed when staticVelocityDamage is true, or relative point velocity from associatedRb when that flag is false and that body exists. Speed is in metres per second; the factor ramps from 0 at velocityMinimum to 1 at velocityMaximum, with invertVelocity reversing it. Without either speed branch it uses factor 1. Optional distance falloff instead measures from the volume object to the target body and fades from full at distanceMinimum to zero at distanceMaximum, both in metres. Use nonnegative, clearly separated limits.

An accepted attempt sends an Attack, a damage message containing the final amount, attack type, target world position as origin and a direction and normal pointing toward the source marker. Target receivers may further modify the amount or reject it; entering the trigger is not a guarantee of lost health.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.VoidLogic.EventAdapter
member.summary: Turns a VoidLogic input number into UltEvent callbacks for changes, rising, holding and falling.

remarks.para: An UltEvent is a list of methods to call; a method called by an event is a callback. This adapter has one Power input at index 0 and no numeric output ports. The input comes from a source output reference or an inline constant, a number stored directly in the connection. Each invoked event receives this adapter, the source as IVoidLogicSource, the common interface for a node that supplies an output number, and the number read for that actuation. The source can be null for an inline constant. The number is not clamped to 0–1; the thresholds and change tolerance use its units.

An actuation is the logic system running this node’s effects, rather than a guaranteed call on every rendered frame. With a valid reference, it first compares the input f with _priorValue, the last saved qualifying number. If abs(f - _priorValue) > 0.0001, where abs means difference size without its sign, InputUpdated callbacks run and then f is saved. Smaller changes do not refresh the saved number, but the threshold tests still run. Frequent change callbacks can be expensive; use rise/fall callbacks if you only need a switch.

The high state starts strictly above highThreshold, the upper switching number, and ends strictly below lowThreshold, the lower switching number. For the usual setup with the lower number below the upper, values between them keep the previous state. With upper 0.7 and lower 0.3, a low state reading 0.8 rises, a later 0.5 stays high, and 0.2 falls. Equality at the boundaries does not switch the state.

On an ordinary first rise, InputUpdated runs first if its change test passed; the saved number is then updated, _isHigh becomes true, InputRose runs, InputRoseOneShot runs if _hasBeenHigh is false, _hasBeenHigh becomes true, and InputHeld runs if _isHigh remains true. On an ordinary fall, the qualifying change handling comes first, _isHigh becomes false, then InputFell runs. These events run synchronously, so their callbacks finish before the next step. Empty event lists are skipped while the corresponding state changes still happen. Callbacks that change fields or call back into the adapter before returning can change later checks and event flow.

Initialize is the logic system’s setup call. It sets _isHigh according to whether the initial readable input is strictly above the upper threshold and resets _hasBeenHigh false, without running events or refreshing _priorValue. Starting already high does not immediately trigger a rise or one-shot event; it can invoke InputHeld on later actuations. A one-shot rise needs a later fall and rise in that case. The adapter’s enable/disable routines do not themselves reset the one-shot flag. An invalid reference during actuation skips all events and preserves its saved number and flags.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AssetWarehouse
member.summary: Keeps track of available content packages, their item descriptions, and the catalogs needed to load their assets. selects the warehouse used for shared queries.

remarks.para: A pallet is a package, such as the built-in game content or an installed mod. Its crates describe items such as props, avatars, or levels; data cards describe other package content. Registering these descriptions makes them discoverable by barcode, the identifier used for lookup. It does not spawn every described object into the scene.

Use AssetWarehouse.Instance for the selected warehouse. Initialization selects it before its startup loading pass finishes, so use OnReady or await InitAsync before relying on the complete initial inventory. The callbacks on this class report registration steps; they are not a general notification for every unload or direct dictionary edit.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Crate
member.summary: Describes a loadable content item for a , including its barcode, display information, asset reference, and tags.

remarks.para: A crate is a description that lets the warehouse find and load content. A GameObject is a Unity object that can be placed in a scene; a prefab is a reusable GameObject template, and a scene is a loaded level with its GameObjects. For example, a SpawnableCrate can identify a prop prefab, while a LevelCrate identifies a scene. The crate itself is the description, not an object already placed in the scene. Loading the referenced asset and creating a scene instance are separate operations.
Derived crate types choose the main asset reference and the kind of Unity object they manage. A pallet is the package containing these descriptions.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.CrateSpawner
member.summary: Requests pooled scene objects from a SpawnableCrate at this component's position and rotation in the overall scene, rather than relative to its parent.

remarks.para: A SpawnableCrate describes a prefab, which is a saved object template. The pool can create a copy or reuse an available copy; the crate description itself is not that scene object. SpawnSpawnable starts a request, while SpawnSpawnableAsync lets code wait for and inspect the result.

Awake, Unity's initialization callback, builds a saved Spawnable pair from the chosen crate reference and policyData. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. SetSpawnable rebuilds that pair after configuration changes.

The persistent scene-load callback automatically requests a spawn while playing unless manualMode is true. Code can also request a spawn directly. The optional shouldSpawn routine can reject a request, and the pool policy can limit or reuse objects.
With useQuery true, the chosen reference comes from crateQuery.Barcode. The checked reference-selection path does not run the query or copy its tempBarcode result.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.EntityPose
member.summary: A warehouse data card recording an entity’s body arrangement, associated spawnable template, and packed mesh reference.

remarks.para: An entity can contain several physics bodies. PoseData is the saved list of body positions and rotations relative to the entity’s root, so the arrangement can be placed at another world location. This is a saved arrangement rather than an animation timeline.

MarrowEntityPoseDecorator resolves this card when its spawner reports a spawned object, finds the object’s MarrowEntity, and applies PoseData to that entity’s indexed bodies. The card and spawned object must resolve, and the pose must suit that entity’s body order. Simply assigning a card field does not reposition an existing object.

DataCardAsset is this card’s loader reference to its saved asset. Because the card reports bundled=true, the warehouse loads the actual card through that reference. This is separate from PoseData, the saved list of body positions and rotations, and Spawnable, the associated template’s warehouse ID. Checked JSON Pack stores the card asset identifier, spawnable identifier, collider-bound numbers, and packed mesh reference rather than serializing the body-pose list.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.GenericCrateReference
member.summary: A reference for looking up a registered record. GenericCrateReference accepts any subtype of Crate.

remarks.para: A Barcode is the identifier used for this lookup. Crate is the common base type for the warehouse's crate records, so a list of GenericCrateReference values can refer to different crate kinds. SpawnableCrateReference and AvatarCrateReference restrict the result to their own crate types.

The inherited Crate property asks AssetWarehouse, the game's catalog of registered content, for a matching record only after its ready flag is true. It returns null when lookup fails. TryGetCrate returns true and places the matching live Crate in its output parameter; otherwise it returns false and sets that parameter to null. Lookup can fail when the warehouse is not ready, the Barcode is invalid or empty, neither the current nor old registry yields a live match (for example, because the registered Unity object was destroyed), or the matching object is not a Crate.

A resolved Crate is warehouse catalog data. Its MainAsset property points to a separate MarrowAsset; resolving the reference does not load that asset or create an in-game object. MarrowQuery.Crates is one concrete use: when MarrowQuery.Matches checks a MarrowEntity, it looks on that entity's GameObject for a Poolee component, reads its SpawnableCrate, and compares that crate's Barcode with the listed references' Barcodes. In this path, Poolee is an attached Unity component that supplies the object's SpawnableCrate reference.

The empty constructor uses an empty Barcode marker. Passing a Barcode stores that same object; passing barcode text creates a Barcode from the text. These constructors set up the reference and do not register crate content.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowAsset
member.summary: An asset-loader identifier with a cached asynchronous loading handle, used to obtain Unity assets such as prefab templates or meshes.

remarks.para: The identifier is passed to Unity Addressables, the system that finds and loads assets by a key. It is separate from a warehouse Crate or DataCard Barcode. The reference and loaded asset are also separate from a spawned scene copy.

LoadAssetAsync returns a task to wait for. Repeated requests reuse this reference’s pending or completed handle rather than starting another load while that handle is valid. ReleaseAsset(true) or the no-argument protected release can release the cached operation; the boolean overload with false does nothing.

The base LoadTask property is a default completed task, not the active operation. Use the task returned by LoadAssetAsync to wait for a requested load. Concrete asset-reference subclasses can override the virtual properties and release behavior.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MarrowQuery
member.summary: Filters tagged targets using required or excluded BoneTags and alternative spawn-crate identities.

remarks.para: The tag group requires every TagQuery condition to pass. The crate group accepts any listed spawn-crate Barcode. TagCrateOperator combines the two group results with And or Or. For example, a required tag A and excluded tag B plus crate X, combined with And, accepts an object from X only if it has A and lacks B.

Each empty group passes. A new query therefore accepts valid targets, and Or with either group empty bypasses restrictions in the other group. Use And for a query that only restricts tags or only restricts crate identity.

MarrowEntity matching uses the entity’s TagList and pool origin. MarrowBody matching uses the body’s own TagList, but takes the pool origin from its owning entity. For an ITaggable that is a Unity MonoBehaviour (a script component attached to a GameObject, the Unity object that carries components), a nonempty crate list passes only when that GameObject has a Poolee (a component that records which spawnable crate created an object managed by the game’s reuse pool) with a live SpawnableCrate (the crate record for that object), and the crate’s Barcode (BONELAB’s crate ID) matches one listed reference. If no Poolee is found, its SpawnableCrate is missing or destroyed, or no listed ID matches, the crate group fails. An ITaggable that is not a MonoBehaviour bypasses this crate-origin check, so its crate group passes. TagCrateOperator combines the tag and crate group results.

ZoneItem uses an entity query when an entity enters a zone and forwards the entry only when Matches succeeds. The query itself returns a decision; it does not spawn objects or dispatch the zone’s action.

The three checked Matches overloads read the live condition lists. Cache merely adds identifiers to separate query sets without clearing them, and is not needed for list changes to affect those matches. Target tag membership still comes from the target’s own TagList cache.

Supply nonnull condition lists and valid entries and target tag data. Both groups are evaluated before the operator combines them; an otherwise passing Or group does not protect broken inputs in the other group.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.MonoDiscReference
member.summary: A reference that stores the barcode used to find a data card in BONELAB’s Warehouse.

remarks.para: AssetWarehouse is the game’s catalog of barcode-addressed data cards. A DataCard stores information about an item; MonoDisc is the card record for a sound track. A barcode identifies this card record, not the sound file.

The inherited DataCard lookup runs only when AssetWarehouse’s ready flag is set. It returns a MonoDisc only when the barcode is valid, a matching card is in the catalog, and that card has the requested MonoDisc type; otherwise DataCard is null. TryGetDataCard reports whether it found the card and supplies it. Lookup checks the current barcode registry, then a second registry for older barcode aliases. A reference made with the parameterless constructor starts with Barcode.EmptyBarcode, which is not a usable lookup identifier.

The card’s AudioClip is separate from its barcode. AudioClip is Unity’s sound data. The MonoDisc’s MarrowAssetT<AudioClip> property is a reference object whose AssetGUID is the identifier used to find that sound. In the verified ZoneAmbience path, the zone ambient-sound code resolves the card, loads the clip asynchronously, waits for it, then asks the audio manager to play it as ambience. Constructing or resolving this reference only finds the card; it does not load or play the sound.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.OnSpawnEvent
member.summary: Reports a successful spawn, carrying the requesting spawner and the resulting scene GameObject.

remarks.para: A listener is a callback: a routine called to perform or report an action. A GameObject is a Unity scene object that can hold components. The first argument identifies which spawner requested the object; the second is the resulting GameObject to inspect or configure. The object can be reused from a pool, so this event does not imply a freshly created instance.

CrateSpawner reaches this event only if its crate reference resolves (its spawnable-crate lookup succeeds) and its optional shouldSpawn callback returns true (when one is set). It asks AssetSpawner, the game's spawn helper, to get the object from a pool. A pool keeps objects available for reuse and returns a Poolee component on the GameObject; that component stores the object's pool callbacks. Before the request, CrateSpawner adds one to the load-dependency count, an integer on the current level-streaming session. When a live Poolee is returned, AssetSpawner first runs the spawn callback passed by CrateSpawner: its OnPooleeSpawn forwarder calls ISpawnListenable.OnSpawn with the GameObject on every registered spawn listener added with RegisterSpawnEventListener. AssetSpawner then calls IPoolable.OnPoolSpawn on each IPoolable registered with the Poolee. IPoolable is the pool's interface for its initialize, spawn, and deinitialize callbacks. After the spawn operation returns, CrateSpawner subtracts one from the current session's load-dependency count, even when no live object resulted. It then invokes this event only if its onSpawnEvent object exists and the returned Poolee passes Unity's live-object check, and completes its own SpawnSpawnableAsync task afterward. Thus the registered spawn listeners run before IPoolable.OnPoolSpawn and before this event.
The checked path skips this event if no live object results. Use the supplied GameObject to access the result; this path does not populate the spawner's exposed _spawnedSpawnable field.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Pallet.ChangeLog
member.summary: A release-note record in a pallet’s ChangeLogs list, containing a version label, short heading and detailed explanation of changes.

remarks.para: For example, an entry can identify version 1.2.0, use Added puzzles as its title, and describe the new levels in text. These strings describe the release; creating an entry does not install an update or change the pallet’s Version.

Pallet.Pack converts the pallet into a JSON data object in memory, storing each entry’s version, title and text in the changelogs array in list order. JSON is a text-based format for storing named values and lists; Pack does not write a file. Pallet.Unpack reads that JSON data back into the pallet. A present changelogs array clears and refills the existing ChangeLogs list, so a present empty array clears all notes. A missing array leaves the current notes in place.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletManifest
member.summary: An installation record holding a pallet’s identifiers, file paths, version, date metadata and runtime references.

remarks.para: The record links a stored pallet Barcode with an optional live Pallet description, Addressables catalog locator and mod listing. Constructing or restoring the record does not load or register that content.

Pack/Unpack preserve stored paths, version, date strings and Active, but do not preserve Pallet, Catalog or ManifestPath. Pack stores a reference to a nonnull listing. Unpack attempts to resolve a present listing reference through the object store: successful resolution supplies the listing, resolution that reports failure clears it to null, and a missing key leaves the current listing unchanged. The manifest’s own file path can be computed lazily from a live Pallet.

Copying shares the pallet, Barcode and catalog references. The stored Active flag is separate from an actual warehouse load/unload operation, and the date helpers record UTC wall-clock Unix milliseconds rather than game time.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.PalletReference
member.summary: Identifies a record in the game's catalog by Barcode, its lookup ID. A Pallet record lists content such as crates and data cards.

remarks.para: The Pallet getter and TryGetPallet resolve the registered description after warehouse readiness. IsValid only checks the identifier’s empty/placeholder rules; it does not confirm registration or content availability.

Barcode identifies the Pallet record in AssetWarehouse, the game's catalog. Package file paths locate files on disk, while Unity asset-loader IDs tell the loader which content to find; those serve separate purposes from this record's lookup ID. For example, PalletDependencies stores these references to name other pallets; simply constructing a reference does not load a dependency’s content.
The empty constructor starts with the empty barcode marker, which needs replacement before lookup can succeed. Sharing a Barcode object shares its later ID changes too.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.Scannable
member.summary: The shared description base for warehouse crates, data cards and pallets.

remarks.para: A Scannable carries a warehouse Barcode, a readable title/description, stored filtering flags and supporting asset references. It describes content; the main prefab, scene or sound asset and any spawned instances are separate objects.

The warehouse is the game’s catalog of registered descriptions; it finds them by Barcode. Loading content, spawning it and packing its description are separate operations supplied by derived types and their consumers.

Base Pack writes the description data to JSON only after it has both a Barcode object and an output JSON object. Unpack restores only fields present in the saved data; missing fields leave the existing values alone.

The base PreloadAssets does no loading, and the base ExportPackedAssets clears and returns an empty supporting list. Derived implementations can provide different behavior, so those method names alone do not guarantee that content is ready.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.ScannableReference
member.summary: The shared base for references that name warehouse descriptions by Barcode.

remarks.para: AssetWarehouse is the game’s catalog of registered Scannable descriptions. Each Scannable is a catalog data entry describing content; it is separate from a loaded prefab (a reusable object template) or a spawned object placed in a scene.
The empty constructor starts with the empty barcode marker. Supply a usable warehouse identifier before expecting lookup to succeed; construction itself does not find or load content.

IsValid checks identifier markers, while the Scannable getter resolves a registered description after AssetWarehouse readiness. Those are different tests: a plausible identifier can exist without any registered item.

The base getter accepts any registered Scannable category. Typed crate, card and pallet references provide their own typed lookups. Obtaining a description is separate from loading its main asset or creating a scene object.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.SpawnableCrate
member.summary: Describes a saved prefab that a can place in the scene.

remarks.para: A prefab is a saved reusable object template. This crate is a data record for AssetWarehouse, the game's content catalog. Its Barcode object holds the ID used to look up that record; its inherited MainAsset is a separate reference used to load the prefab. Loading MainAsset retrieves the template. Crate.CreateCrate creates the record; creation alone should not be taken as proof that it is registered in the catalog. Looking up the record does not spawn it either.

For example, CrateSpawner resolves a SpawnableCrateReference and sends its saved reference and optional pool policy to AssetSpawner. The CrateSpawner's own Transform supplies the world-space position and rotation that determine where the requested object appears. A pool keeps scene objects for reuse after they are returned. The ordinary spawn policy sets a limit on the number of objects in its group and a rule for reaching that limit: allow the group to grow, return an already spawned object to the pool for reuse, or produce no object. A successful request can therefore reuse an object instead of making a fresh copy. The crate must resolve, the spawner's optional shouldSpawn check must allow the request, and AssetSpawner needs a registered pool for that crate.

CrateSpawner.SpawnSpawnableAsync returns a task; await that task to receive its Poolee result when the request finishes. A Poolee is the component that manages the scene object's pool lifecycle. Use that component's GameObject to access the object. When the result is still a live Unity object (it exists and has not been destroyed), an assigned onSpawnEvent receives the spawner and that GameObject before the spawner's task completes.

Inherited PreviewMesh points to separate mesh geometry that CrateSpawner can load for its visual preview; it is not the gameplay prefab. ColliderBounds stores a box's center and extents, the distances from its center to the faces along x, y, and z, in the same distance units used by Unity positions. The checked bounds accessors and Pack/Unpack paths copy these numbers without moving or resizing collider components or converting between local and world coordinates. Those paths do not establish the frame in which the box was recorded.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.SpawnableCrateReference
member.summary: A warehouse Barcode reference that resolves to a record for the spawn system.

remarks.para: A Barcode object holds the ID that AssetWarehouse, the game's content catalog, uses to find a registered SpawnableCrate record. The inherited Crate getter and TryGetCrate require the warehouse to be ready and the matching registered crate to be a non-destroyed Unity object of the requested type. A valid Barcode alone does not prove that record exists. Lookup does not wait for startup: on failure, Crate returns null and TryGetCrate returns false with a null output.

The record's MainAsset points to a prefab, a saved reusable GameObject template. Its AssetGUID is the separate identifier that Unity's asset loader uses to find that template; it is not the crate's catalog Barcode. Creating or resolving this reference does not itself load the template or spawn an object.

CrateSpawner combines this reference with optional SpawnPolicyData and sends the request to AssetSpawner. A pool keeps returned scene objects for later reuse. The ordinary spawn policy sets a limit on the number of objects in its group and a rule for reaching that limit: allow the group to grow, return an already spawned object to the pool for reuse, or produce no object. A matching registered pool is also needed; resolving the crate alone does not create one.

CrateSpawner.SpawnSpawnableAsync returns a task; await that task to receive its Poolee result when the request finishes. A successful result is a Poolee component that manages the scene object's pool lifecycle, and the object may have been reused. Access its GameObject, or use the GameObject supplied to the spawner's successful onSpawnEvent.
The empty constructor starts with a placeholder Barcode ID that the warehouse treats as invalid. Replace it with the registered crate ID before lookup can succeed.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagList
member.summary: Holds an object’s BoneTag references and the cached identifiers used to test its tag membership.

remarks.para: For example, MarrowQuery checks an entity or body’s TagList cache to require tag A or exclude tag B. The source references name BoneTag descriptions by Barcode; updating this cache does not load those descriptions.

A new list starts with empty Tags and an empty identifier set. The first CachedTagBarcodes read builds the set. After changing an initialized list, call UpdateCache(false) to keep matching results aligned with the references.

InheritTags supplies another object’s list, whose references are copied into this list during refresh. Those copied entries persist in the local list after detaching the source; inheritance is not a temporary view that automatically removes old tags.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.TagQuery
member.summary: One tag rule that a MarrowQuery checks against a target object, requiring a selected tag to be present or absent.

remarks.para: Set BoneTag to a nonnull reference for the selected tag. Its Barcode holds the tag’s identifying ID. MarrowQuery compares that ID with TagList.CachedTagBarcodes, the set of tag IDs stored by the target’s TagList for matching. With Invert false, the set must contain the ID; with Invert true, it must lack it.

Every condition in MarrowQuery.Tags must pass for the combined tag-rule result to pass. TagCrateOperator combines this result with the separate result of matching the query’s listed crate references: And requires both results to pass; Or requires either one. This condition alone does not guarantee that the whole query rejects or accepts an object.

Creating or editing a condition does not search a scene or load a tag asset. Matches reads the current condition directly, so editing BoneTag or Invert does not require MarrowQuery.Cache. After changing the target’s tag list, call that TagList’s UpdateCache(false) to rebuild its stored set before matching again.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip
member.summary: A that finds nearby world surfaces and supplies a surface point and hand orientation for grabbing them.

remarks.para: Its scoring routine searches nearby colliders, the invisible shapes used for contact tests, and selects a surface candidate without an attached Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that lets physics move an object using mass, forces and collisions. A collider with any attached Rigidbody is skipped as a candidate here, even if that body is configured to stay still.

Scoring caches geometry separately for each hand. The hover update uses the recorded surface point and surface-facing directions to place that hand’s target. Accepted cached geometry is relative to the WorldGrip object; converting the point back to world coordinates gives a position in metres.

The attachment configuration locks position and permits limited rotation. A physics joint is the connection that imposes those restrictions on the hand. After attachment, the saved hand pose supplies the angle limits. The current controller grip input and the avatar’s stored grip-strength multiplier set how strongly the joint pulls the wrist toward its target orientation. This pulling effort is the rotation-drive strength. The avatar is the character’s body model, and its stored multiplier is a unitless strength scale. For example, this can provide a grip point on static tabletop geometry while letting the wrist turn within the pose’s allowed angles.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.WorldGrip.HandToGenericGripState
member.summary: Keeps one hand's candidate surface, nearby collider results and handle pose for a .

remarks.para: WorldGrip looks for environmental surfaces a hand can hold. It creates a separate state record the first time it scores this grip for a hand, then reuses that record for later scoring and hover updates. A collider is a physics detection shape. Construction allocates a 16-slot collider buffer; scoring fills its first targetColliderCount entries and records the result of a surface ray test. Entries after that count can still hold older values.

A hover update, a routine run while a hand considers the grip, uses the saved surface point and orientation to set a target pose: the position and rotation the grip wants the hand to reach. The record is candidate information, not proof of an attached hand. Its hit flag can retain an older result when no eligible collider is found, and its handle pose is converted from world coordinates to the grip's frame only on the accepted path. Coordinates in that frame describe offsets from the grip's origin, measured along its rotated axes.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ActiveZoneState
member.summary: Tracks one activator's primary, secondary, and combined activation results for one zone link, so the manager can send enter and exit callbacks when those results change.

remarks.para: An activator is an entity, such as the player, accepted by a ZoneLink's activatorTags; activatorTags is the link's filter for which entities may activate it. The manager keeps a separate state for each activator/link pair. Primary is the link chosen from that entity's active-zone stack, the manager's list of active links kept in priority order; secondary links are the chosen link's outgoing neighbors. A connected group is the set of links the graph groups together through zone connections. Combined activation is true for either role.

The nxt flags are calculation results and the cur flags record the applied results. The manager clears and rebuilds the nxt flags, copies them to cur, then dispatches combined, primary, and secondary callbacks for changed channels. This happens as part of the state solve. It is not a timer or a promise to apply a change on the next frame.

For example, if the manager selects A as primary and A links to B, A is primary and B is secondary for that activator; B need not contain the activator. Both are active in the combined channel. A role change can produce primary or secondary callbacks without another combined enter. A listener is a script registered to hear about zone changes; its callback is the method the manager calls to report a changed channel. A GameObject is a Unity object in the scene. Changing these booleans directly does not enable or disable a GameObject or invoke those methods; use the zone manager’s activation operations to change its tracked state.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ISpawnListenable
member.summary: Receives a CrateSpawner's notifications when it spawns or despawns an object that the game manages for reuse.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity object in the scene. A pooled object is one the game's object pool manages so it can be reused. A listener is an object that implements this interface and registers with a CrateSpawner to receive later notifications. RegisterSpawnEventListener(ISpawnListenable) adds the listener to the spawner's list; registering the same listener again does not add a duplicate. Call UnregisterSpawnEventListener(ISpawnListenable) to remove it. A callback is a method the spawner calls to report an event; this interface's callbacks are OnSpawn(GameObject) and OnDespawn(GameObject).

OnSpawn and OnDespawn receive the GameObject involved in the notification, not the CrateSpawner's own GameObject. For example, OnSpawn can set up an effect on a newly spawned prop, and OnDespawn can clear a reference to it when it leaves play. Registering subscribes to later callbacks only; it does not immediately report objects that already spawned. Recycling uses a separate IRecycleListenable.OnRecycle(GameObject) callback.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneBodyListenable
member.summary: Receives zone entry and exit notifications for individual physical bodies, with multiple tracked colliders counted as one body membership.

remarks.para: Register with the Zone's RegisterZoneEventListener overload for IZoneBodyListenable and remove the listener with the matching UnregisterZoneEventListener when finished. Adding the same listener twice is ignored, and registration does not announce bodies that already overlap the zone.

In Unity, a component is a piece of data or behavior attached to a GameObject. A Tracker is the component the Zone looks up on a collider's GameObject; it links that collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity. The Zone counts distinct Trackers, while repeated callbacks for one Tracker are deduplicated. For example, two distinct Trackers linked to colliders on the same body produce one body enter when the first accepted overlap arrives and one body exit when the last counted overlap is removed. A multi-part entity can contain several bodies, so use IZoneEntityListenable when you want a single notification for the whole entity. Zone disable cleanup or Tracker GameObject deactivation can also produce exits.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkListenable
member.summary: Receives per-activator changes in a zone link's combined primary-or-secondary activation.

remarks.para: Register once with the ZoneLink's RegisterLinkEventListener overload for IZoneLinkListenable and remove the listener with the matching UnregisterLinkEventListener when finished. Registration adds another list entry each time, so duplicate registrations can repeat callbacks. It does not replay an existing active state.

Use these notifications when an area should respond both as the activator's selected primary link and as an outgoing neighbor of that primary link. Use IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable or IZoneLinkSecondaryListenable for changes to a specific role. Use IZoneEntityListenable on a Zone for direct entity overlap instead.

For both callbacks, the manager writes the combined state for that link and activator before dispatching: enter follows a write to active, and exit follows a write to inactive. A trigger entry starts activation only when the source ZoneLink’s activatorTags query accepts the entity; activatorTags is that source link’s filter for which entities it accepts. After a matching source entry activates the graph, the manager can notify that source’s outgoing linked neighbors as secondary links without the entity entering those neighbors’ triggers or their own activatorTags queries running.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable
member.summary: Receives changes in whether a zone link is the selected primary link for a particular activator.

remarks.para: Register once with the ZoneLink's RegisterLinkEventListener overload for IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable and remove it with the matching UnregisterLinkEventListener when finished. Duplicate registration adds duplicate list entries and can repeat callbacks; registration does not replay existing state.

Use this channel to react to the manager's selected area for an entity such as the player. For example, an area can stay active as a neighboring secondary link while losing the primary role. Use IZoneLinkListenable for the combined state: the link is active either as the selected primary or as an outgoing linked secondary neighbor. Use IZoneEntityListenable on a Zone for direct physical overlap of an entity with that Zone.
The manager updates the activator’s selected-primary state before dispatching either primary enter or primary exit, so listener code sees the new role from inside the callback.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.IZoneLinkSecondaryListenable
member.summary: Receives changes in a link's activation as an outgoing neighbor of an entity's selected primary zone link.

remarks.para: Register once with the ZoneLink's RegisterLinkEventListener overload for IZoneLinkSecondaryListenable, then use the matching UnregisterLinkEventListener when finished. Duplicate registration adds more list entries and can repeat callbacks. Registration does not replay an existing secondary state.

Use this channel when a neighboring area should react before it becomes the entity's selected primary area. Use IZoneLinkPrimaryListenable for the selected-primary role, or IZoneLinkListenable for activation through either role. These callbacks report changes per activator, such as the player; secondary is the link's role for that activator.

A callback is a method the manager calls to notify a listener. During a state solve, the manager applies the new secondary state before calling either method: it writes true before secondary enter and false before secondary exit, so listener code sees the updated value.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStates
member.summary: Defines the bit-mask values for independent Hide, Cull, and Despawn requests stored in an InactiveStatus; the enum does not apply them.

remarks.para: These constants are masks: None=0, Hide=1, Cull=2, Despawn=4, and All=7. The bitwise OR operator combines bits, so Hide | Cull = 3 requests both channels and All = 1 | 2 | 4. In InactiveStatus, request is what code asks for; resolved is the request the Resolve stage has processed; applied is the state after Apply handlers run; completed records channel activations processed by Resolve that have not yet been released. Resolve sets a channel's completed bit before checking whether its resolve callback exists and calling it with true (on), so a set bit does not prove a callback ran. Update processes Resolve and then Apply; only when both queues of waiting statuses are empty does it release recorded channels whose request bits are all clear and whose resolved flag is off. It clears the completed bit before checking whether the resolve callback exists and calling it with false (off). A callback is a routine the manager or entity calls to report or perform a state change.

For a standard MarrowEntity, the GameObject is its Unity scene object; Hide and Despawn apply handlers reconcile that object's active state. The standard entity registers a resolve callback for Cull only; its Hide and Despawn resolve callbacks are absent, so those completed bits are set and cleared without resolve calls. Cull adds or removes one hibernation source, meaning a reason for suspending physics, and can disable MarrowBehaviour scripts, attached components that run parts of the entity's game behavior. Rigidbody freezing occurs on the aggregate hibernation transition for MarrowBody instances with HasRigidbody, while another source can keep physics asleep. Culling may leave the GameObject active when culling is prevented or host/parasite attachment conditions apply. Custom InactiveStatus callbacks choose their own response. Use InactiveObjectManager's request methods to change and queue a status together; the enum value alone does not combine or apply a status.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.InactiveStatus
member.summary: Stores an object's requested and processed hide, cull, and despawned flags together with callbacks that implement its response.

remarks.para: The three inactive channels are independent. request is the desired state, resolved is the state prepared for application, and applied is the state recorded after apply callbacks. completed remembers entered inactive resolve channels until their later release; it is not a final applied-state snapshot.

Use InactiveObjectManager's Hide, Cull, or Despawn methods to update and queue a request. The same-named methods on this status only edit request, and its Is... queries report request rather than actual object state. Clear erases all four masks without reversing object effects.

A callback is a routine the manager calls during the status pipeline; an apply callback receives this status and a resolved-channel boolean, while a resolve callback receives true when an inactive channel begins and false later when all requests clear and completion can run. For a standard entity, a GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components and has an activeSelf state.

The callbacks determine the object effect; the status itself has no GameObject reference or object-pool entry to operate on. An object pool is the game's reuse system for retaining objects for later use. Use InactiveObjectManager.Hide, Cull, and Despawn with false to release requested channels through normal callbacks. Clear zeros all four masks without callbacks; after effects have run, later false requests may then generate no apply or completion work. Use Clear only when resetting bookkeeping without reversing lifecycle effects.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.RecycleDecorator
member.summary: Base component for responding when a recycles one of its objects. Override to react to it.

remarks.para: A CrateSpawner manages crate creation and recycling. A GameObject is the Unity scene object passed to this callback, and OnRecycle is the method the spawner calls to report that object. The base OnRecycle does nothing; a derived decorator can play an effect or update its own tracking.
Recycle notifications are separate from ordinary spawn and despawn notifications. This decorator registers with its assigned spawner while enabled and removes the current registration when disabled.

Assign _crateSpawner before enabling and keep the reference consistent until disabling removes the subscription. If you override OnEnable or OnDisable, retain their base registration work when you want this subscription lifecycle.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.SpawnDecorator
member.summary: A base component that subscribes to spawn and despawn notifications while enabled. Override or to respond.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Here, the spawner reports spawning or despawning by calling the matching override with the affected GameObject. The base callbacks do nothing; a derived component could, for example, attach its own effect or stop work associated with that object.

Assign a valid _crateSpawner before OnEnable subscribes. OnDisable removes this listener without despawning objects. Keep the reference consistent across those calls, because assigning another spawner alone leaves the old subscription in place. Registration suppresses duplicates but does not replay past spawn state. Recycling uses the separate IRecycleListenable channel.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.Zone
member.summary: A trigger area that records overlapping trackers, groups them by body and entity, and reports enter and exit changes to registered listeners.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used for collision detection. A Tracker connects that shape to a physical body and its whole entity. The zone accepts cached trackers only while enabled and active and only when they report both body and entity; unrelated collider objects are not automatically tracked.

Listeners implement IZoneBodyListenable, IZoneEntityListenable, or IZoneTrackerListenable and register through the appropriate overload. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Tracker reports describe each accepted tracker; body and entity reports describe the first and last counted overlaps for their shared object. Registration prevents duplicates within each list but does not replay earlier enters.

On entry the tracker is recorded and the enter flag is set before tracker callbacks. Body count and any body-enter callback follow, then entity count and any entity-enter callback. The flag is cleared before processing the one saved deferred exit. On immediate exit the tracker is removed, the exit flag is set, entity and body counts are reduced with any last-overlap exits, then tracker exit runs before the exit flag clears.

Awake is Unity's initialization callback, the routine called to set up this component; it prepares tracker-disable reporting. Disabling a tracker or the zone can produce cleanup exits without physical movement. Exit requests during enter processing use one overwriteable tracker slot and run at the end of the same enter call.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneChunkLoader
member.summary: Requests configured scene chunks when its zone link becomes an activator's selected primary link.

remarks.para: A ZoneLink's activatorTags field is a filter that decides which entering entities it accepts. Its zoneLinks connections form a connected group, and the manager uses link priority when selecting a primary link for an accepted activator in that group. A callback is a routine invoked in response to a link report. Before enabling this component, assign its inherited ZoneLink reference, configure its chunks array, and select the event reports it should receive. The native constructor selects both Primary and Secondary event options by default.

The primary callback starts each SceneChunk request and returns without waiting for loading to finish. A loader batch is the set of chunks the shared scene loader wants active in one pass; requests may be queued or divided across batches. Chunks omitted from its desired active set can be unloaded before newly requested chunks load.

A SceneChunk groups one or more scene layers as a loadable chunk. When a chunk's load step runs, it sets IsChunkLoaded to true, updates its ZoneCullers (components that manage entities and level assets in the chunk's zone), calls registered IChunkLoadable.OnChunkLoad handlers, and then fires its configured onChunkLoad event. Watch these per-chunk signals to observe loading; activation does not guarantee immediate scene availability.
This type has no automatic unload action when the link later stops being primary.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents
member.summary: Turns a Zone's entity-overlap reports into regular enter, component-wide one-shot enter, and exit events carrying the whole MarrowEntity.

remarks.para: A Collider is a shape Unity uses to detect overlap. A Tracker links one Collider to its MarrowBody and MarrowEntity; the MarrowEntity is the whole in-game entity. Zone counts these tracked overlaps by entity, reporting enter for its first accepted tracked collider and exit after its last tracked collider leaves or cleanup removes it. Multiple colliders on one entity therefore do not create multiple entity-enter events.

ZoneItem registers to receive Zone reports while enabled and unregisters while disabled. Its inherited activatorTags is a MarrowQuery filter configured with tag and crate rules; ZoneItem checks that filter for both enter and exit reports. Configure the inherited Zone reference and filter before enabling. Registering after an overlap began does not replay it, and direct OnEnter or OnExit calls bypass the filter.

Each event calls its attached listener routines (callbacks), which can perform actions such as playing a sound or recording progress. The regular enter event runs before the one-shot flag check. If the flag remains false, the one-shot event runs before the flag is set true. This flag is shared across all entities, is written after one-shot listeners return even if that event is absent, and is not reset by exit or enable/disable. A nested entry before the write can invoke the one-shot event again; the events themselves do not move or remove an entity.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneEvents.ZoneEventCallback
member.summary: A serializable UltEvent carrying the affected to ZoneEvents enter or exit listeners.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This event stores the callbacks to invoke and passes them the whole entering or exiting entity, rather than its collider or the zone object.

The same event type is used for regular enter, one-shot enter, and exit. The containing ZoneEvents component decides when each one fires. In its enter path, regular listeners run before the one-shot guard check, and one-shot listeners run before the guard becomes true; this event container itself does not enforce one-shot behavior.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.ZoneLink
member.summary: Connects filtered Zone entity reports to per-activator primary, secondary, and combined activation states in a directed link network.

remarks.para: A Zone is the trigger area that turns accepted Collider contacts into whole-entity enter and exit reports. A Collider is a shape Unity checks for trigger contact. Its GameObject is the scene object holding its components. A Tracker links that Collider to a MarrowBody (one physical body) and a MarrowEntity (the larger in-game entity that can group bodies).

An activator is the MarrowEntity whose Zone report passes a link's activatorTags query; it need not be the player. For each activator, the manager groups links joined through incoming or outgoing configured connections and keeps active links in a priority-ordered list. The highest-ranked link at the top of that list is primary. Its direct outgoing neighbors are secondary for the same activator; secondary status does not recursively spread through every connected link. A link is combined-active while it is either primary or secondary.

Configure _zone, activatorTags rules, outgoing zoneLinks, and priority before Awake. Awake is Unity's initialization callback, the routine called to set up this component; it registers directed connections. OnEnable separately subscribes to the Zone's whole-entity overlap reports, which the query filters. A late Zone listener receives no immediate enter report for an entity already inside. The Zone accepts collider reports only while its GameObject is active in the scene and the Zone component is enabled, and when a Tracker has both body and entity links. It counts distinct Trackers for an entity and emits enter for the first counted Tracker and exit after the last; disabling a Tracker or Zone can also trigger cleanup exits.

A callback is a routine registered to run when a state changes. The manager stores new combined, primary, and secondary flags before dispatching changed combined callbacks, then primary, then secondary for a given link. Listeners supply game responses such as culling, streaming, or audio; activation does not mean every object in the Zone is immediately enabled. Link-state listener registrations permit duplicates. A listener registered after its state is already active gets no immediate current-state call.

When an accepted Zone exit passes the current query, the manager's allow-orphan path can keep the only remaining active link for that activator after the entity leaves the trigger area. This orphaned state is conditional, not the outcome of every Zone exit. OnDisable removes entity reports without tearing down the connection graph; OnDestroy removes this link from the manager's connection graph and recalculates roles only in groups reached from an activator's remaining active links. If this was that activator's only active link in its group, its former secondary neighbors keep their secondary and combined-active flags and receive no exit callback from this teardown. Former neighbors disconnected from every remaining active link can also be missed. Disabling the component does not itself synthesize an entity exit.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.VRMK.Avatar
member.summary: The component on a character model that turns its humanoid bones and body-shape settings into measurements for the game's movement and physics rigs.

remarks.para: The model supplies bones, meshes and optional helper bones. PrecomputeAvatar measures that rig, calculates reference offsets and initializes body proportions; RefreshBodyMeasurements converts stored proportions to physical sizes and recalculates mass and strength scores. The shape methods can generate the collision geometry that physics calibration installs.

Many members are calculated results or cached values, while shape descriptions and bone references are setup inputs. Changing a cached value does not automatically rebuild every rig or collision shape that used it. The component also supplies avatar-specific sound collections to player audio code.
